title: Genesis 1: The Creation of Light and Mankind
text: Genesis Study · Genesis 5-8 → Genesis 1: The Creation of Light and Mankind Read the chapter → Genesis 1 Introduction This reading covers Genesis 1 through 4 straight through. When you deal with Genesis you are dealing with an illustrated story; the pictures in it stand for something, and every teaching is backed with a precept. Genesis 1:1-2 - This darkness is not a symbol for sin; it is real darkness. In the beginning everything was black. Genesis 1:3 - This light came before the sun, the moon, and the stars, which were not made until the fourth day. It is the light you see in the morning sky before the sun comes up. - There is light in the sky when the sun is not out; the Most High made that light first. The light is twelve hours and the darkness is twelve hours, and afterward He made the sun as the greater light to rule the day. - What exactly that first light was is not declared; what is declared is that He commanded a fair light so that His work might appear. Genesis 1:1 coincides with 2 Esdras 6. Precepts: - 2 Esdras 6:38-40 The Most High commanded a fair light on the first day so that His work might appear. Genesis 1:5 - The day begins in the evening. The day begins when it is dark and it ends when it is dark. Genesis 1:6-8 - The firmament is the sky. It divides the waters below from the waters above; space is water up there. Genesis 1:14-19 - On the fourth day the Most High created the sun, the moon, and the stars to give light upon the earth and make a brighter light upon it. - The sun is the greater light; it was made brighter than the light created on the first day, which is how it rules over the day. Genesis 1:26-27 - Notice it says let them have dominion. The Most High did not create just one man; the man spoken of here is mankind. - The words created he him point to a particular person, who begins to be described in Genesis 2. Male and female created he them is mankind. Genesis 1:28 - The Most High blessed mankind here, just as He blessed the whales, the fowls, and the cattle before them. Genesis 1:29 - The herb was created for meat, that is, for food. Genesis 1:31 - Everything He made was very good according to the Most High; snakes and jellyfish included. He created everything for His own purpose. Genesis 2: Adam, the Chosen of the Most High Read the chapter → Genesis 2 Genesis 2:1-3 - This is the first Sabbath that you read about in the scriptures. The Most High blessed the seventh day and sanctified it. Genesis 2:4-6 - Chapter 2 is the manner of creation. It goes back through what you read in chapter 1 and gives you more detail on certain things. Genesis 2:7 - Here is the detail on how man was formed: the Most High formed him of the dust of the ground. - The breath of life is talking about the commandments. - This is Adam, the chosen. Out of all the people the Most High created on the earth, He had a favorite from the beginning. Genesis 2:8-14 - The Most High planted the garden eastward in Eden and put the chosen man there. - The river Gihon is the Blue Nile; it compasses the whole land of Ethiopia. Genesis 2:16-17 - Some of these trees are literal trees, and some of these trees represent men. Precepts: - Mark 8:24 Scripture uses trees to represent men. Genesis 2:18-20 - The Most High looked at the women on the earth and there was no help meet right for Adam. This again shows there were more people on the earth than Adam alone. Genesis 2:21-23 - The Most High created Eve from Adam because there was no woman on the earth right for him at that time. Genesis 3: The Craftiness of Your Enemy Read the chapter → Genesis 3 Genesis 3:1 - Chapter 3 deals with the craftiness of your enemy. - This is not a literal snake. Another word for serpent is deceiver; the serpent is Satan. You know it is not a literal serpent because serpents do not speak. Precepts: - 2 Corinthians 11:14 Satan transforms himself, which is how the serpent is Satan in disguise. Genesis 3:4-5 - Satan taught Eve doctrine. She had been taught that if she broke the commandments of the Most High she would die; the serpent now taught her that she would not die. - The same doctrine is taught today: that your eyes will be opened and you do not have to keep the commandments and you will not die. If you leave the commandments you are going to die. Genesis 3:6 - Any time scripture speaks of good for food like this, it is talking about good to learn. - The fruit she ate was the lies. She was enticed to break the commandments of the Most High, then she went and taught her husband the same thing the serpent taught her, and he broke the commandments as well. Precepts: - Hosea 10:13 The fruit of lies is eaten; the fruit Eve ate was the lie she was taught. Genesis 3:7 - They were not literally naked; nakedness represents sin. They were in sin. - Remember this is an illustrated story. The fig leaves and aprons represent them trying to cover their transgressions. Precepts: - Job 31:33 Adam covered his transgressions; the fig leaves are that covering. - Lamentations 1:8 Jerusalem sinned and her nakedness was seen; nakedness is sin. Genesis 3:8 - The trees of the garden here are people. Adam and his wife tried to hide their sins among the other people that were in the garden with them. Precepts: - Ezekiel 31:8 The trees in the garden of God are men among whom a man may seek to hide. Genesis 3:9 - The Most High was not looking for Adam as though He could not find him; He was calling Adam to examine himself. - Adam had started to separate himself from the Most High by covering and hiding his sins, and the Most High already knew what he had done. Genesis 3:12-13 - Adam blamed Eve for his sin, and in saying the woman whom thou gavest he blamed the Most High also. Then Eve blamed the serpent; they played the blame game. Genesis 3:14 - The cattle and the beasts of the field here are the nations. - Going on the belly and eating dust means the serpent was brought to a very low estate, made like a vagabond upon the earth. Cain became a vagabond upon the earth, and so did Esau. Precepts: - Isaiah 49:23 The nations lick up the dust, showing the low estate spoken to the serpent. - Micah 7:16-17 The nations shall lick the dust like a serpent, proving the cattle and beasts are the nations. - Ecclesiastes 3:18 The sons of men are themselves called beasts. Genesis 3:15 - This is a prophecy. It is not talking about the serpent and Eve; the woman is the nation of Israel. - The woman does not plant seed; the man plants seed. The Most High is saying He will put enmity between Satan's seed and Israel's seed, and that enmity remains. - Christ was to come from the woman. Revelation 12 explains this verse. - Bruising the heel is making Israel stumble. When a serpent strikes at your heel you stumble; Satan makes Israel stumble through evil communication and corrupting good manners. - It shall bruise thy head is spoken to the serpent: Christ was going to come and destroy the works of Satan. Precepts: - Jeremiah 3:2 The Most High speaks to Israel as the woman. - Romans 16:20 The Most High bruises Satan under the feet of His people; that is the bruising of the head. Genesis 3:16 - Your desire, your learning, your desire of anything was to be to your husband, and he shall rule over thee. - This is one of the first commandments given, alongside be fruitful and multiply, the Sabbath, and the commandment not to eat of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. - Sisters, if you do not allow your husband to rule over you, it does not matter what else you keep; you are not entering the kingdom without fulfilling this. Precepts: - 1 Corinthians 14:34 The women are commanded to be under obedience, as the law says from the beginning. Genesis 3:17-19 - Because Adam hearkened to his wife and broke the commandment, the ground was cursed for his sake; in sorrow and sweat he would eat of it all his days. Genesis 3:21 - This is animal sacrifice to cover the sins. This is where the Most High ordained the sacrificial law; this is when they started to sacrifice. - The first sacrifice is twofold. A literal lamb was slain here to clothe Adam and his wife, and that lamb slain from the foundation of the world represents Christ, slain for our sins. Precepts: - Isaiah 61:10 The Most High clothes His saints with righteousness, as Adam was clothed to cover sin. - Leviticus 16:27 The sin offering yields skins, as the Most High made coats of skins to cover sin. - Revelation 13:8 The Lamb was slain from the foundation of the world; Christ is that Lamb. Genesis 3:22-24 - The man was driven out of the garden to till the ground from whence he was taken, and the way of the tree of life was kept. Genesis 4: Cain, Abel, and the Sons of the Wicked Read the chapter → Genesis 4 Genesis 4:1-2 - Here is the birth of trade and of religion with Cain and Abel: Abel a keeper of sheep, Cain a tiller of the ground. Genesis 4:3-5 - The Most High had respect to Abel's offering and not to Cain's, and Cain was wroth. - Remember the earth was cursed in chapter 3, so it was hard to get fruit out of the ground; that is part of why Cain was angry. Genesis 4:7 - The Most High is calling Cain to repent. Cain knew that the Most High required animal sacrifice, because the sacrificial law was ordained at Genesis 3:21. - If Cain would not repent, sin lay at the door; he would become subject to Satan and Satan would rule over him. Genesis 4:8-9 - When Cain talked with Abel, Abel was trying to get Cain to repent. Abel was a prophet. Precepts: - Matthew 23:35 Christ counts righteous Abel with the blood of the prophets, proving Abel was a prophet. Genesis 4:11-12 - Cain was cursed from the earth and made a fugitive and a vagabond, the same low estate spoken of the serpent in chapter 3. Genesis 4:14-15 - Every one that findeth me shall slay me is proof in the pudding, like we brought out in Genesis 1, that there were more people on the earth than Adam's household. - The mark set upon Cain changed him; at the beginning Cain looked like everybody else, and the Most High marked him so that any finding him would not kill him. Genesis 4:16-17 - Cain found his wife in the land of Nod; there were already people on the earth during the time of Adam. - Cain built a city, and you do not build a city for three people; this is more proof that the earth was peopled. - The lands in those days were named after men, which is why the land was called Nod. - Cain called the city after the name of his son, as the wicked call their lands after their own names. Precepts: - Psalms 49:11 The wicked call their lands after their own names, as Cain named the city after Enoch. Genesis 4:19 - This is the first time you read about a man taking multiple wives, and it is the sons of the wicked who did it. In the beginning it was one wife. - When you read about the sons of God in Genesis 5 you do not read about them taking multiple wives; only the sons of the wicked. Genesis 4:22 - An instructor of every artificer in brass and iron: these men started making weapons. This is the first you read about weapons being created. Genesis 4:23-24 - Lamech was murdering men; Satan was working with the sons of the wicked. - Lamech knew the commandment thou shalt not kill was in force in his day; that is why he appealed to Cain's sevenfold, saying seventy and sevenfold. They knew the commandments during that time. Genesis 4:25-26 - Seth was appointed another seed instead of Abel. Through Seth men began to call upon the name of the Lord; they started to worship the Most High and keep the commandments, while the line of Cain went on in evil and wickedness. That is why the Most High chose the line of Seth. --- Topics: Clean and Unclean Meats · Esau and Edom · Sacrifice and Atonement · The Feasts of the Most High · The Sabbath Genesis Study · Genesis 5-8 →

title: Genesis 13: The Peacemaker and the Promise
text: ← Genesis 9-12 · Genesis Study · Genesis 17-20 → Genesis 13: The Peacemaker and the Promise Read the chapter → Genesis 13 Introduction This reading covers Genesis 13 through 16. Genesis is the book of the genetics and the genealogy: it shows how Israel comes from the lineage of Shem, and where every other nation finds its beginning. Genesis 13:1-2 - When the scriptures speak of our forefathers being rich, it is not carnal wealth. Abram was rich in cattle, silver, and gold: livestock, land, and the things that take care of a family. That is true wealth. - We have to be retaught what wealth is: build houses, dwell in them, plant gardens, and eat the fruit of them, and learn to provide for ourselves. Precepts: - Jeremiah 29:5 Build houses and plant gardens and eat the fruit of them; that is the wealth the Most High teaches. Genesis 13:5-7 - Lot was Abram's nephew: Terah begat Abram, Nahor, and Haran, and Haran begat Lot. - Their substance was so great they could not dwell together. That substance came from Egypt, where Pharaoh entreated Abram well for Sarai's sake and gave him sheep, oxen, servants, and camels; the maidservants from Egypt are where Hagar comes from. Precepts: - Genesis 11:27 Haran begat Lot; Lot was Abram's nephew. - Genesis 12:16 Pharaoh gave Abram livestock and menservants and maidservants; this is where the household's wealth and Hagar came from. Genesis 13:8-9 - Abram said, Let there be no strife, for we be brethren. That was the spirit of Abram: he would de-escalate and look for solutions. If you go left I go right; if you go right I go left; you cannot argue with that. - Be solution minded and fix problems using the scriptures; blessed are the peacemakers. Precepts: - Matthew 5:9 Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called the children of God; Abram was a peacemaker. Genesis 13:10-13 - Lot lifted up his eyes and chose the well watered plain of Jordan, fertile like the garden of the Lord, and pitched his tent toward Sodom. Toward Sodom became in Sodom; Genesis 14:12 shows Lot dwelt in Sodom. - The men of Sodom were wicked and sinners before the Lord exceedingly: they were lawless, without principles, and given to sexual freedom. That is why the city was overthrown. Precepts: - Genesis 14:12 Lot dwelt in Sodom; pitching toward Sodom ended with dwelling in it. Genesis 13:14-17 - The Most High reiterated the promise He made when Abram first entered the land: unto thy seed will I give this land, and thy seed shall be as the dust of the earth. - This is the same covenant language spoken over the children of Israel: as the sand of the sea which cannot be measured nor numbered. Precepts: - Genesis 12:7 Unto thy seed will I give this land; the promise was made at Abram's first altar. - Hosea 1:10 The number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea; they shall be called the sons of the living God. Genesis 14: The War of the Kings and Melchizedek Read the chapter → Genesis 14 Genesis 14:1-3 - Four kings, the Mesopotamian kings, made an allegiance against five kings; this was a world war, nations and kingdoms making alliances to war against other nations. Shinar is modern day Iraq. - The king of Bela is the one king whose name is not given; Bela is the city, which is Zoar. The vale of Siddim is the salt sea, known today as the Dead Sea. Genesis 14:4-11 - The five kings served Chedorlaomer twelve years and rebelled in the thirteenth; the four kings defeated them and took the goods of Sodom and Gomorrah. - The vale of Siddim was full of slimepits: bitumen, tar, petroleum. The same region is rich in oil to this day. Genesis 14:12-16 - Because Lot dwelt in Sodom he was carried away captive with his goods, and one that escaped told Abram the Hebrew. - Abram armed his trained servants, three hundred and eighteen, born in his own house. That tells you Abram trained them: he was a warrior fit for battle who knew how to conduct war, nothing like the frail figure in the whitewashed images. - He divided his men and moved by night; that is military strategy. With three hundred and eighteen men and his three confederates he smote four kingdoms and brought back Lot, the goods, and the people. - The victory of battle stands not in the multitude of an host; strength comes from heaven. Whether with many or with them that have no power, the battle is not yours but God's; our forefathers proved it, as when Asa cried to the Lord and a million Ethiopians fell before Judah and Benjamin. Precepts: - 1 Maccabees 3:18-19 It is no hard matter for many to be shut up in the hands of a few; the victory of battle standeth not in the multitude of an host. - 2 Chronicles 20:15 Be not afraid by reason of this great multitude; the battle is not yours, but God's. - 2 Chronicles 14:9-11 Asa rested on the Lord against a thousand thousand Ethiopians; it is nothing with the Lord to help, whether with many or with them that have no power. Genesis 14:18-20 - Melchizedek king of Salem brought forth bread and wine; Salem goes into Shalom, peace, so he is the king of peace, and he was the priest of the Most High God. - Abram paid tithes to Melchizedek. This is way before the Levitical priesthood; the twelve tribes were not yet born. For the order of Melchisedec, study Hebrews 7 and John 8:56. Genesis 14:21-24 - The king of Sodom asked only for the persons and offered Abram all the goods, and Abram refused from a thread even to a shoelatchet, lest the king of Sodom say, I have made Abram rich. He would not give him that satisfaction. - The young men's portion was not refused: Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre fought, and they earned their portion. Genesis 15: The Covenant and the Four Hundred Years Read the chapter → Genesis 15 Genesis 15:1-4 - Abram asked what the Lord would give him, seeing he went childless and the steward of his house, Eliezer of Damascus, stood to inherit everything. - The word came: This shall not be thine heir; he that shall come forth out of thine own bowels shall be thine heir. The Most High prophesied children to Abram out of his own seed. Genesis 15:5-6 - Look now toward heaven and tell the stars: so shall thy seed be. Abram believed the Lord, and it was counted to him for righteousness. - Righteousness is immortal, and righteousness is defined by the law: it shall be our righteousness if we observe to do all these commandments. Abram's faith showed itself in his works. Precepts: - Wisdom of Solomon 1:15 Righteousness is immortal; the righteous seed endures forever. - Deuteronomy 6:25 It shall be our righteousness if we observe to do all these commandments; righteousness goes into keeping the laws. - Romans 4:1-3 Abraham believed God and it was counted unto him for righteousness; his faith was shown in his works. Genesis 15:9-12 - Abram divided the heifer, the goat, and the ram, and drove the fowls from the carcases; he was offering sacrifice. - When the sun went down a deep sleep and a horror of great darkness fell on Abram: he was about to receive a vision of future prophecy. The Most High speaks in a dream, in a vision of the night, and reveals His secret to His servants the prophets. Precepts: - Job 33:15-16 In a dream, in a vision of the night, He openeth the ears of men and sealeth their instruction. - Amos 3:7 The Lord God revealeth His secret unto His servants the prophets. Genesis 15:13-16 - Know of a surety: thy seed shall be a stranger in a land that is not theirs, shall serve them, and be afflicted four hundred years. This prophecy was fulfilled in Egypt; the sojourning of the children of Israel in Egypt was four hundred and thirty years, and the four hundred was an approximation of that time. - This verse is not the doctrine about America and 1619. The northern kingdom's captivity on this side began in 1492, and by that counting the years pass four hundred and Israel is still in captivity and still scattered this day; the prophecy of Genesis 15:13 was fulfilled at the Exodus. - They came out with great substance: the children of Israel required jewels of silver and gold and raiment of the Egyptians, and they spoiled Egypt as they left. - The twelve tribes scattered among the nations today, the people called Blacks, Hispanics, and Native Americans, are the seed this covenant history belongs to. - Abram himself would go to his fathers in peace and be buried in a good old age; and the seed would return in the fourth generation, for the iniquity of the Amorites was not yet full. Precepts: - Acts 7:6 His seed should sojourn in a strange land, in bondage, and be evil entreated four hundred years. - Exodus 12:40-41 The sojourning of the children of Israel in Egypt was four hundred and thirty years, and it ended the selfsame day; the prophecy was fulfilled at the Exodus. - Baruch 3:8 Israel is yet this day in captivity, scattered for a reproach; the scattering did not end on a four hundred year clock. - Exodus 12:33-36 Egypt urged them out in haste, and the Lord gave the people favour, and they spoiled the Egyptians; they came out with great substance. Genesis 16: Hagar and Ishmael Read the chapter → Genesis 16 Genesis 16:1-2 - Hagar was Sarai's Egyptian handmaid, from the servants Pharaoh gave in Genesis 12:16. - Sarai, restrained from bearing, gave her maid to Abram that she might obtain children by her. Genesis 16:3-6 - When Hagar conceived, her mistress was despised in her eyes. Hagar got high minded; she stopped submitting because she carried Abram's child. - Sarai laid the wrong on Abram, and Abram answered, Behold, thy maid is in thy hand. He did not say my wife; he had no attachment to Hagar. His sole purpose was the seed, not multiple wives. - Abram kept the laws of the Most High. Do not use this account to justify taking multiple wives; the purpose here was the promised inheritance, and Sarai dealt with her maid as mistress over her. Genesis 16:7-9 - The angel of the Lord found Hagar by the fountain in the way to Shur and sent her back: Return to thy mistress, and submit thyself under her hands. Humble yourself and go back. Genesis 16:10-12 - Ishmael would be a wild man, his hand against every man and every man's hand against him, and he would dwell in the presence of all his brethren. - Ishmael became the ancestor of the nomad desert tribes inhabiting the area from the Sinai desert across the Negev to southern Jordan, and the Arabs venerate Ishmael as their forefather; Muslim tradition holds that Ishmael and Hagar are buried at the Kaaba in Mecca. The reference work Who's Who in the Bible lays this history out. - They dwell in the presence of all their brethren to this day, nation beside nation through that whole region. Genesis 16:15-16 - Abram was fourscore and six years old, eighty six, when Hagar bare Ishmael. Ishmael was Abram's firstborn, but the covenant did not go to Ishmael; the covenant goes through the twelve tribes of Israel. --- Topics: Esau and Edom · Sacrifice and Atonement · The Covenant · The Priesthood ← Genesis 9-12 · Genesis Study · Genesis 17-20 →

title: Genesis 17: The Covenant Sealed in the Flesh
text: ← Genesis 13-16 · Genesis Study · Genesis 21-24 → Genesis 17: The Covenant Sealed in the Flesh Read the chapter → Genesis 17 Introduction This reading covers Genesis 17 through 20. Abraham is a righteous example all across the board: faith, obedience, hospitality, leadership, and immediate action on the commandments of the Most High. Genesis 17:1 - At ninety and nine years old Abram was commanded to walk before the Most High and be perfect. There is no age excuse; Christ said nothing new in Matthew 5:48, for the command to be perfect was given thousands of years before. - Perfect according to the scriptures means to walk in His statutes and keep His commandments; that is how Israel perfects itself. Precepts: - 1 Kings 8:61 A perfect heart is one that walks in His statutes and keeps His commandments; that is the meaning of be thou perfect. Genesis 17:4-6 - When the Most High began dealing with Abram on a covenant level, his name was changed: Abram became Abraham, a father of many nations, and kings would come out of him. - Father of many nations does not mean everybody is spiritually a child of Abraham. The same promise was passed down the seed line: Jacob's name was changed to Israel and told a nation and a company of nations and kings would come out of his loins. - The blessing of all men and the covenant were made to rest upon the head of Jacob and divided among the twelve tribes. Kings come out of that seed, including Christ, the King of kings. Precepts: - Genesis 35:10-11 The same covenant words passed to Jacob, named Israel: nations and kings out of his loins. - Ecclesiasticus 44:19-23 The blessing of all men and the covenant rested on the head of Jacob and was divided among the twelve tribes. Genesis 17:7 - The covenant is with Abraham's seed after him, and seed is literal offspring, not a spiritual metaphor. The Most High promised to be a God to Abraham and to his seed after him. Precepts: - Isaiah 41:8 Israel is the servant, Jacob the chosen, the seed of Abraham; Israel is the nation that carries the seed of Abraham. Genesis 17:10-14 - Circumcision is the token of the covenant: every man child circumcised at eight days, and the uncircumcised soul cut off from his people. - Abraham received circumcision as a seal of the righteousness of the faith he had yet being uncircumcised. He believed and obeyed first, and circumcision sealed it; likewise a brother can come into the truth, get built up in the faith, and then go through with the process. - It still has to be done. A covenant is a contract with terms; the covenant was confirmed to Jacob for a law, and circumcision is one of the laws within the covenant. Precepts: - Romans 4:11 Circumcision was a seal of the righteousness of the faith Abraham had yet being uncircumcised. - Genesis 15:6 Abraham was counted righteous before circumcision was implemented; faith and obedience came first. - 1 Chronicles 16:15-17 Be mindful always of His covenant, confirmed to Jacob for a law; the covenant carries terms. Genesis 17:15-19 - Sarai's name was changed to Sarah, and she shall be a mother of nations; those are the same nations of the covenant, and she and Abraham had one child together, Isaac. - Abraham fell on his face and laughed in his heart: shall a child be born to a hundred year old man, and Sarah bear at ninety? The Most High read his thought and named the child from it: Isaac means he will laugh. Genesis 17:20-21 - Ishmael received a blessing: fruitful, multiplied exceedingly, twelve princes, a great nation. But the word to Abraham was kings shall come out of thee, and the covenant passes to Isaac: my covenant will I establish with Isaac. - Not all who are of Abraham's seed are the children; in Isaac shall thy seed be called. Ishmael was born of the flesh, of Sarai's plan, with no word from God ordaining it; the children of the promise are counted for the seed. Precepts: - Romans 9:7-9 In Isaac shall thy seed be called; the children of the flesh are not the children of God, but the children of the promise are counted for the seed. Genesis 17:23-27 - The selfsame day Abraham circumcised every male of his house, himself at ninety and nine and Ishmael at thirteen. That is the righteous example: he received the commandment and performed it the same day. Genesis 18: The Promise of Isaac and the Cry of Sodom Read the chapter → Genesis 18 Genesis 18:1-8 - The three men who stood by Abraham were angels of the Lord, and they had bodies: their feet were washed with water, they rested under the tree, and they did eat. Be careful how you deal with people, for some have entertained angels unawares. - Abraham hastened to serve them. He commanded his household; he told Sarah, Make ready quickly. That is the level of his hospitality and his leadership. Genesis 18:9-15 - Sarah was barren from the beginning and it had ceased to be with her after the manner of women; she laughed within herself at the promise of a son. - The Lord answered the thought she never spoke: Wherefore did Sarah laugh? She denied it out of fear, and He said, Nay, but thou didst laugh. The Most High sees what is within the mind. - Is any thing too hard for the Lord? The barren woman is made a joyful mother of children. Through faith Sarah received strength to conceive when she was past age, and Abraham, as good as dead at a hundred, staggered not at the promise but was strong in faith, fully persuaded that what He had promised He was able to perform. Precepts: - Genesis 11:30 Sarai was barren from the beginning; she had no child. - Psalms 113:9 The Most High makes the barren woman a joyful mother of children. - Hebrews 11:11-12 Through faith Sara received strength to conceive past age, because she judged Him faithful who had promised; of one as good as dead sprang as many as the stars. - Romans 4:19-21 Abraham considered not his own body now dead nor the deadness of Sarah's womb; he staggered not at the promise through unbelief. Genesis 18:17-19 - The Lord said, I know Abraham, that he will command his children and his household after him. The man is the leader who makes the rules and keeps his house in the way of the Lord. - What makes a great husband and father is commanding the household in the way of the Lord, to do justice and judgment. Where men walk away from justice and judgment, they cannot properly command their household. Genesis 18:20-21 - The cry of Sodom and Gomorrah was great and their sin very grievous. The iniquity of Sodom was pride, fulness of bread, and abundance of idleness; she strengthened not the hand of the poor and needy, was haughty, and committed abomination. - The same iniquities fill the land that is spiritually called Sodom today: pride, wealth, idleness from morning to night, and abomination made law. Precepts: - Ezekiel 16:49-50 The iniquity of Sodom: pride, fulness of bread, abundance of idleness, and abomination committed before the Most High. Genesis 18:23-33 - Abraham drew near and negotiated with the Most High because his nephew Lot dwelt in Sodom; that is why he pleaded for the city. - Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right? Abraham reasoned from fifty righteous down to forty and five, forty, thirty, twenty, and ten, and the Lord said, I will not destroy it for ten's sake. Below ten there was no more negotiating, and the Lord went His way. Precepts: - Genesis 13:12 Lot dwelt in the cities of the plain and pitched toward Sodom; his dwelling there is why Abraham interceded. Genesis 19: The Destruction of Sodom Read the chapter → Genesis 19 Genesis 19:1-3 - Lot sat in the gate and pressed the two angels into his house, because he knew the men of Sodom. He made them a feast, and they did eat; angels have bodies and functions like men. Genesis 19:4-5 - The men of Sodom, old and young, all the people from every quarter, compassed the house and demanded the men, that we may know them. To know in scripture is to lie with: Rebekah was a virgin, neither had any man known her. - The whole city, both small and great, was given to this wickedness. Precepts: - Genesis 24:16 Neither had any man known her proves that to know means intercourse. Genesis 19:6-11 - Lot went out and said, I pray you, brethren, do not so wickedly. This is Genesis, way before Leviticus 18; sodomy was already wickedness and already unlawful before the law was written at Sinai. - They pressed on Lot to break the door, and the angels smote them with blindness, small and great, so that they wearied themselves to find the door. Genesis 19:12-17 - Lot's sons in law took him as one that mocked, and they perished. When the warning comes, treating it as a joke is death. - While Lot lingered, the angels laid hold on his hand, the Lord being merciful to him. Then the instruction: Escape for thy life; look not behind thee; escape to the mountain. Genesis 19:18-25 - The angel told Lot, Haste thee, for I cannot do any thing till thou be come thither. The destruction waited on the righteous being brought out, the same way the angels in Revelation 7 hold the four winds until the servants of God are sealed. - When Lot entered Zoar, the Lord rained brimstone and fire on Sodom and Gomorrah. Those cities are set forth for an example, suffering the vengeance of eternal fire; what was done there on a small scale is done in spiritual Sodom on a greater scale, and the example stands. - Just Lot was delivered, a righteous man vexed from day to day with the filthy conversation and unlawful deeds of the wicked. A righteous man cannot be at home with that conduct. Precepts: - Jude 1:7 Sodom and Gomorrah, giving themselves to fornication and going after strange flesh, are set forth for an example, suffering the vengeance of eternal fire. - 2 Peter 2:6-8 The cities were made an example unto those that after should live ungodly, and just Lot was delivered. Genesis 19:26 - Lot's wife looked back, against the instruction, and became a pillar of salt: a standing monument of an unbelieving soul. - Remember Lot's wife: three words among the weightiest in the scriptures. As it was in the days of Lot, they ate, drank, bought, sold, planted, and builded until the day the fire fell; so shall it be in the day when the Son of man is revealed. If you find yourself reminiscing after the old life, remember Lot's wife. Precepts: - Wisdom of Solomon 10:6-7 The standing pillar of salt is a monument of an unbelieving soul; the wasteland that smoketh is a testimony to this day. - Luke 17:28-32 As it was in the days of Lot, so shall it be in the day the Son of man is revealed; remember Lot's wife. Genesis 19:30-38 - Lot's daughters thought Sodom had been the whole world and no man was left on the earth to give them seed, so they made their father drink wine and lay with him; he perceived not when they lay down nor when they arose. - Do not take any wayward idea from this: uncovering the nakedness of thy father is against the laws of the Most High. It was unlawful then and it is unlawful now. - The firstborn bare Moab, father of the Moabites, and the younger bare Benammi, father of the Ammonites, unto this day. In this teaching those nations are identified with the peoples known today as the Chinese and the Japanese. Precepts: - Leviticus 18:7 The nakedness of thy father and mother thou shalt not uncover; incest is against the law of the Most High. Genesis 20: Sarah and Abimelech Read the chapter → Genesis 20 Genesis 20:1-2 - Abraham said again, She is my sister, as he had done entering Egypt, for fear the men of the place would kill him for his wife's sake; Sarah was still that fair to look upon even at ninety. Precepts: - Genesis 12:11-13 The saying began at Egypt: they will kill me, but save thee alive; say thou art my sister. Genesis 20:3-7 - God came to Abimelech in a dream: Behold, thou art but a dead man, for the woman is a man's wife. Adultery was sin in Genesis, way before Exodus 20:14; the Most High said, I withheld thee from sinning against me. - Abimelech had acted in the integrity of his heart, and the Most High withheld him from touching her. Restore the man his wife, for he is a prophet, and he shall pray for thee. Genesis 20:9-13 - Abimelech called it what it is: a great sin. Adultery is one of the weightier matters; there is no animal sacrifice that atones for it. - Abraham thought, Surely the fear of God is not in this place. And technically she was his sister: the daughter of his father but not of his mother, who became his wife; the sister saying was their agreement in every strange land. Genesis 20:17-18 - Behind the scenes the Lord had fast closed up all the wombs of the house of Abimelech because of Sarah; when Abraham prayed, God healed them. - The same happened with Pharaoh before. The Most High plagues a household over the prophet's wife; He does not play about that. Precepts: - Genesis 12:17 The Lord plagued Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai; it happened both times she was taken. --- Topics: Sacrifice and Atonement · The Covenant · The Feasts of the Most High ← Genesis 13-16 · Genesis Study · Genesis 21-24 →

title: Genesis 21: Isaac the Child of the Promise
text: ← Genesis 17-20 · Genesis Study · Genesis 24-27 → Genesis 21: Isaac the Child of the Promise Read the chapter → Genesis 21 Introduction This reading covers Genesis 21 through 24: the birth of Isaac, the offering on Moriah, the death of Sarah, and the taking of a wife for Isaac from Abraham's own kindred. Genesis 21:1-6 - The Lord visited Sarah as He had said, and she bare Isaac at the set time. Abraham was a hundred years old, and he circumcised Isaac at eight days as commanded. - God hath made me to laugh: Isaac's name means he will laugh, for the story of a hundred year old father and a ninety year old mother is a joyful and comical thing. Genesis 21:8 - The great feast the day Isaac was weaned was not a birthday celebration. Weaned means finished being breastfed, and the mothers gave their children suck about three years; Abraham was celebrating Isaac coming off his mother's breast at around three years old. Precepts: - 2 Maccabees 7:27 The mothers gave their sons suck three years; being weaned was a milestone at about that age, not a birthday. Genesis 21:9-13 - Sarah saw the son of Hagar mocking and said, Cast out this bondwoman and her son; the son of the bondwoman shall not be heir with Isaac. - It was grievous to Abraham because he loved his firstborn, but God said, Hearken unto her voice, for in Isaac shall thy seed be called. Sarah was on point; Isaac is the child of the promise. - Ishmael would still be made a nation, because he was Abraham's seed. Genesis 21:14-19 - When the water was spent, Hagar cast the child under a shrub and wept, thinking he would die of thirst. God heard the voice of the lad and opened her eyes to a well of water. - The lad could not die there; the prophecy of chapter 16 stood over him, that he would become a great nation. Genesis 21:20-21 - Ishmael dwelt in the wilderness and became an archer; he learned the skills of combat and war, according to his nature. - The word over his lineage stands: a wild people, his hand against every man and every man's hand against him, dwelling in the presence of all his brethren in the Middle East. His mother took him a wife out of Egypt. Precepts: - Genesis 16:11-12 The prophecy over Ishmael's posterity: a wild man, his hand against every man, dwelling in the presence of all his brethren. Genesis 21:22-32 - Abraham reproved Abimelech over a well his servants had taken violently, and they made a covenant; the seven ewe lambs stood as a witness that Abraham digged the well. - The place was called Beersheba, which means the well of the oath, because there they sware both of them. Genesis 22: The Offering of Isaac Read the chapter → Genesis 22 Genesis 22:1-3 - God did tempt Abraham: Take now thy son, thine only son Isaac. Ishmael was alive, but the Most High counted Isaac the only son, because Ishmael was born of the flesh, of a plan the Lord never spoke, while Isaac was the child of the promise. - Abraham rose up early in the morning and went. No hesitation, no debating with the word; that is obedience. Genesis 22:7-8 - Isaac asked, Where is the lamb for a burnt offering? Abraham answered, My son, God will provide himself a lamb. He trusted the Most High with what was missing. Genesis 22:9-12 - Abraham bound Isaac, laid him on the altar, and stretched forth his hand with the knife; the angel called out of heaven in the midst of it: Lay not thine hand upon the lad. - Now I know that thou fearest God. The fear of God is proved in obedience; they that fear the Lord will not disobey His word. - Abraham's inner faith carried him: he accounted that God was able to raise Isaac up, even from the dead, since the promise stood in Isaac who had no children yet. Faith and the commandments go together; you cannot have one without the other. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 2:15 They that fear the Lord will not disobey His word; Abraham's fear was proved by his obedience. - Hebrews 11:17-19 By faith Abraham offered up Isaac, accounting that God was able to raise him up even from the dead. Genesis 22:13-14 - Once the obedience was fulfilled, God provided the sacrifice: a ram caught in a thicket by his horns, offered in the stead of his son, just as Abraham had told Isaac. Abraham called the place Jehovahjireh: in the mount of the Lord it shall be seen. Genesis 22:15-18 - By myself have I sworn, saith the Lord: in multiplying I will multiply thy seed as the stars of the heaven and as the sand upon the sea shore, and thy seed shall possess the gate of his enemies. - The seed possessing the gate of his enemies is part of the covenant: the seed of Jacob shall possess the remnant of Edom and of all the heathen, and Edom shall be a possession. That is why all nations cannot be inside this covenant; the covenant has Israel possessing their enemies. - In thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed: those nations are the nations of Israel, the twelve tribes. Precepts: - Amos 9:11-12 The tabernacle of David is raised up, that they may possess the remnant of Edom and of all the heathen. - Numbers 24:17-18 A Star out of Jacob and a Sceptre out of Israel; Edom shall be a possession, and Israel shall do valiantly. Genesis 23: The Death of Sarah Read the chapter → Genesis 23 Genesis 23:1-2 - Sarah lived an hundred and seven and twenty years, and died in Kirjatharba, the same is Hebron, in the land of Canaan; Abraham came to mourn and to weep for her. Genesis 23:14-20 - Ephron offered the field freely, but Abraham insisted on paying, and weighed four hundred shekels of silver, current money with the merchant. The field of Machpelah and its cave were made sure unto Abraham for a possession of a buryingplace, and there he buried Sarah. Genesis 24: A Wife for Isaac Read the chapter → Genesis 24 Genesis 24:1-4 - Abraham made his eldest servant swear that he would not take a wife for Isaac of the daughters of the Canaanites, but go to Abraham's country and kindred. The Most High never condoned marrying into the other nations; the custom was kept from the beginning, way before Moses and Deuteronomy 7:3. Precepts: - Tobit 4:12 Take a wife of the seed of thy fathers, as Noah, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob did from the beginning, and their seed shall inherit the land. Genesis 24:7 - Abraham told the servant, The Lord God of heaven shall send His angel before thee. He trusted the oath would be fulfilled because the Most High goes before the errand. Genesis 24:12-16 - The servant prayed for a sign at the well: the damsel who offers to draw for the camels also is the one appointed. Before he had done speaking, Rebekah came out. - Rebekah was very fair to look upon, a virgin, neither had any man known her: undefiled and beautiful, the kind of wife the forefathers had from the beginning. Genesis 24:26-27 - When the sign came to pass exactly, the servant bowed his head and worshipped the Lord: I being in the way, the Lord led me to the house of my master's brethren. Genesis 24:58-60 - Rebekah said, I will go. Her family blessed her: Be thou the mother of thousands of millions, and let thy seed possess the gate of those which hate them. - The covenant narrows again here: it runs through Rebekah's children, and of her two sons it is Jacob who carries it, for Esau sold his birthright. The covenants in Genesis cannot be broken. Genesis 24:63-65 - Isaac went out to meditate in the field at the eventide; that was a custom of the forefathers, showing the Lord was dealing with them long before the law was written at Sinai. - When Rebekah saw Isaac she lighted off the camel, and she took a vail and covered herself. The four mothers covered their heads with actual material as a sign of submission; that is the custom 1 Corinthians 11 goes into. Genesis 24:66-67 - Isaac brought Rebekah into his mother's tent, and she became his wife, and he loved her; and Isaac was comforted after his mother's death, for he received a righteous wife like unto his mother. --- Topics: Esau and Edom · Sacrifice and Atonement · The Covenant · The Feasts of the Most High ← Genesis 17-20 · Genesis Study · Genesis 24-27 →

title: Genesis 24: A Wife From the Kindred
text: ← Genesis 21-24 · Genesis Study · Genesis 28-31 → Genesis 24: A Wife From the Kindred Read the chapter → Genesis 24 Introduction This reading covers Genesis 24 through 27: the marriage of Isaac, the two nations in Rebekah's womb, the wells of Isaac, and the blessing that passed to Jacob. Genesis 24:3-4 - The Most High does not deal with marriage into the other nations among His chosen. Abraham made his servant swear not to take a wife for Isaac of the daughters of the Canaanites; these laws were in place long before Moses reiterated them. - The reason is given in the law itself: they will turn away thy son from following me, that they may serve other gods. Solomon is the prime example; he loved women of the other nations, went into their gods, and had to repent and bring it back. - The forefathers arranged marriages. The building block of a strong nation is a strong family, and a strong family comes from marriage, not from young men and women left to their own accord. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 7:3-4 Make no marriages with the nations, for they will turn away thy son from following the Most High to serve other gods. Genesis 24:12-20 - The servant asked a sign, and before he had done speaking Rebekah came out: very fair, a virgin, and kind. She gave a stranger drink and drew for all his camels; that kind and easily entreated spirit is the pattern for the daughters of Israel. Genesis 25: Two Nations in the Womb Read the chapter → Genesis 25 Genesis 25:1-6 - Abraham took Keturah and had more sons, but Abraham gave all that he had unto Isaac; to the sons of the concubines he gave gifts and sent them away eastward from Isaac. The inheritance followed the child of the promise. Genesis 25:7-10 - Abraham lived an hundred threescore and fifteen years and died in a good old age, as it was prophesied to him; his sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the cave of Machpelah with Sarah. Genesis 25:12-18 - The generations of Ishmael list twelve princes according to their nations, exactly as the Most High promised in Genesis 17:20. Ishmael lived an hundred and thirty and seven years and died in the presence of all his brethren. Genesis 25:20-21 - Isaac was forty years old when he took Rebekah to wife. Brothers waiting on a wife, be patient and stay virtuous; Isaac waited forty years, and the Most High had the right sister appointed. - Isaac intreated the Lord for his wife because she was barren, and the Lord was intreated of him; Rebekah conceived. Genesis 25:22-23 - The children struggled together within her, and the Lord gave Rebekah the prophecy: two nations are in thy womb, one people stronger than the other, and the elder shall serve the younger. - The whole scripture is good set against evil: the godly against the sinner, Jacob against Esau, righteousness against sin. Two powerful forces were being born into the earth, and the struggle began in the womb. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 33:14-15 Good is set against evil and the godly against the sinner; all the works of the Most High are two and two, one against another. Genesis 25:24-26 - The first came out red, all over like an hairy garment, and they called his name Esau. The scriptures describe the man because a nation comes from him; this teaching identifies Esau's seed with the red, hairy, melanin-lacking people of the world today. - Jacob's hand took hold on Esau's heel, and that is prophecy: Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth. When Esau's rulership is done, Jacob comes into power; that is how we know the times. Precepts: - 2 Esdras 6:7-9 Jacob's hand held first the heel of Esau; Esau is the end of the world and Jacob the beginning of it that followeth. Genesis 25:27-28 - Esau was a cunning hunter, a man of the field; Jacob was a plain man, dwelling in tents. The Most High gives you the characteristics of the man so the nation can be known. - Isaac loved Esau because he did eat of his venison, but Rebekah loved Jacob, because the Lord had told her the prophecy that the younger was the chosen. Genesis 25:29-34 - Esau sold his birthright for red pottage; therefore was his name called Edom, red. He said, What profit shall this birthright do to me, and sware it away for a meal. - Thus Esau despised his birthright. Jacob is called a supplanter, but the supplanting was of the Holy Ghost; Esau gave the birthright away himself. Genesis 26: The Wells and the Envy of the Philistines Read the chapter → Genesis 26 Genesis 26:1-5 - In the famine Isaac was told, Go not down into Egypt; the oath sworn to Abraham was performed unto Isaac: seed as the stars, all these countries, and in thy seed shall all nations of the earth be blessed. - In thy seed shall all nations be blessed does not put everybody in the covenant. The seed is Christ, and the children of the prophets and of the covenant are Israel, scattered into every nation; through Christ scattered Israel in all kindreds of the earth receives repentance and comes back to the Father. - The reason the oath stood: because Abraham obeyed my voice, and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws. Precepts: - Galatians 3:16 The promise was to Abraham and his seed, which is Christ. - Acts 3:25-26 Ye are the children of the prophets and of the covenant; unto you first God sent His Son to bless you in turning every one from his iniquities. - Amos 2:11 The Most High raised up prophets of the sons of Israel; the children of the prophets are Israel. Genesis 26:7-11 - Isaac said of Rebekah, She is my sister, fearing the men of the place, and Abimelech saw Isaac sporting with Rebekah his wife and knew. - Take the lesson from the sporting: love your wife, play with your wife, keep the flirting and the freshness in the marriage. Give her love, attention, and affection all the days. Genesis 26:12-16 - Isaac sowed and received in the same year an hundredfold, and the man waxed great until he became very great; and the Philistines envied him and stopped the wells with earth. - The nations envy the prosperity of Israel. It is not for anything done to them; the blessing itself is what is hated. Genesis 26:17-22 - Isaac digged again the wells of his father and the herdmen strove for Esek and Sitnah; he removed and digged Rehoboth, and they strove not: for now the Lord hath made room for us. Genesis 26:26-31 - Abimelech came saying, We have done unto thee nothing but good, though his people had stopped the wells and sent Isaac away. Isaac answered plainly: Wherefore come ye to me, seeing ye hate me? - Isaac was not simple; he separated from the people that hated him rather than assimilating among them, and he dealt with their covenant with open eyes. The words can be like butter while war is in the heart. Genesis 26:34-35 - Esau at forty took wives of the Hittites, and they were a grief of mind unto Isaac and to Rebekah. He went straight against the fathers' law of marrying within the kindred; that is the nature of the vessel. Genesis 27: The Blessing of Jacob Read the chapter → Genesis 27 Genesis 27:1-4 - Isaac's eyes were dim so that he could not see, and the Lord allowed that blindness for a purpose: so that the blessing could pass to Jacob. What looks like evil can be for good, as Joseph's slavery in Egypt was for good. Genesis 27:5-13 - Rebekah heard and moved for Jacob because she carried the word from the Lord: the elder shall serve the younger. She knew the blessing belonged to Jacob by prophecy, and she took the curse upon herself: Upon me be thy curse, my son; only obey my voice. Genesis 27:14 - His mother made savoury meat, such as his father loved. Rebekah knew exactly how her husband loved his food and made it to that standard; sisters, learn to prepare it such as he loveth. Genesis 27:15-23 - Rebekah put Esau's raiment on Jacob and the skins of the kids of the goats upon his hands and neck, and Isaac discerned him not: the voice is Jacob's voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau. Genesis 27:28-29 - The blessing is rulership of the earth: the dew of heaven, the fatness of the earth, plenty of corn and wine; let people serve thee, and nations bow down to thee; be lord over thy brethren; cursed be every one that curseth thee, and blessed be he that blesseth thee. Genesis 27:34-38 - Esau cried with a great and exceeding bitter cry and begged, Bless me, even me also, O my father. But he had already sold the birthright and never dealt rightly with Jacob about it; he wanted the blessing anyway. - Esau found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears. He that despised the birthright for one morsel of meat was rejected when he would have inherited the blessing. Precepts: - Hebrews 12:16-17 Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright, was rejected and found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears. Genesis 27:39-40 - Esau's portion: the fatness of the earth and the dew of heaven from above, and by thy sword shalt thou live. Esau's kingdoms have gotten what they have through war; his living is by the sword, by ever more advanced weaponry, and the nations are overcome and awed by it. - And it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck: this is the time period now, where Esau has the dominion and rules first, and when his rule is done, Jacob comes into power. Precepts: - Revelation 13:13-14 He maketh fire come down from heaven in the sight of men and deceiveth them that dwell on the earth by those wonders; the sword Esau lives by. Genesis 27:41-46 - Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing and purposed in his heart to slay him, the same hatred Cain had for Abel. Good against evil runs from the beginning of the book to the end. - Rebekah sent Jacob to Laban her brother until Esau's fury turned away, and said she was weary of her life because of the daughters of Heth: if Jacob take a wife of the daughters of the land, what good shall my life do me? Marrying the sons and daughters within the kindred is a weighty matter to the mothers of Israel. --- Topics: Esau and Edom · Idolatry · The Covenant · The Feasts of the Most High ← Genesis 21-24 · Genesis Study · Genesis 28-31 →

title: Genesis 28: The Charge and the Vow at Bethel
text: ← Genesis 24-27 · Genesis Study · Genesis 32-35 → Genesis 28: The Charge and the Vow at Bethel Read the chapter → Genesis 28 Introduction This session read Genesis 28 through 31 straight through and then opened the key points of each chapter. The recording of part one ends with the chapter 28 teaching; the teaching on chapters 29 through 31 in these notes comes from the part two recording of the session. Genesis 28:1-4 - Isaac called Jacob, blessed him, and charged him: Thou shalt not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan; arise, go to Padanaram, to the house of Bethuel, and take a wife of the daughters of Laban. - The fathers from the beginning, Noah, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, married wives of their own kindred and were blessed in their children. Abraham gave the same charge for Isaac, and Isaac gives it to Jacob; the instruction was kept in the family line from the beginning. - With the charge came the blessing of Abraham, passed now to Jacob and his seed: to be fruitful, to multiply into a multitude of people, and to inherit the land promised to Abraham. Precepts: - Tobit 4:12 The fathers from the beginning married wives of their own kindred; take a wife of the seed of thy fathers. - Genesis 24:2-4 Abraham made his servant swear the same charge for Isaac: no wife of the daughters of the Canaanites, but of his own kindred. Genesis 28:5 - Jacob was sent to Laban, the son of Bethuel the Syrian, the brother of Rebekah. Rebekah herself was born to Bethuel, son of Milcah, the wife of Nahor, Abraham's brother; the family line was kept in place, generation after generation going back to their own kindred. Precepts: - Genesis 24:15 Rebekah was born to Bethuel, son of Milcah, wife of Nahor, Abraham's brother; the marriages stayed within the kindred. Genesis 28:6-9 - Esau saw that the daughters of Canaan pleased not Isaac his father, but instead of following Jacob's path he went to Ishmael and took Mahalath to add to the wives he had. He answered his father's grief by doing his own thing. - Esau had already taken Hittite wives that were a grief of mind unto Isaac and Rebekah, and his generations show wives of the daughters of Canaan. He was hardheaded from the beginning; that is the spirit of the wicked, who hate instruction and cast the words of the Most High behind them. Precepts: - Genesis 26:34-35 Esau's Hittite wives were a grief of mind unto Isaac and Rebekah. - Genesis 36:2-3 Esau's generations confirm he took wives of the daughters of Canaan and of Ishmael. - Psalms 50:16-17 Unto the wicked God saith, Thou hatest instruction, and castest my words behind thee; that is Esau's spirit. Genesis 28:20-22 - Jacob vowed a vow: if God will be with me, and keep me in this way, and give me bread to eat and raiment to put on, so that I come again to my father's house in peace, then shall the Lord be my God; the stone set for a pillar shall be God's house, and of all that thou shalt give me I will surely give the tenth unto thee. - A vow to the Most High is not to be made lightly. When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; better not to vow than to vow and not pay. Jacob vowed and rolled with the Most High, and he paid his vow. Precepts: - Ecclesiastes 5:4-6 When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay. Genesis 29: Bone and Flesh in Haran Read the chapter → Genesis 29 Genesis 29:1-4 - Jacob went on his journey out of the land of Canaan and came into the land of the people of the east. On the map he goes north out of Canaan and then east to Haran in Padanaram; that is why the men at the well answer him, Of Haran are we. - This is the same ground the family had already covered. Isaac charged Jacob to go to Padanaram to the house of Bethuel, and generations earlier Terah had brought Abram from Ur of the Chaldees up along the Euphrates, and they came unto Haran and dwelt there. Precepts: - Genesis 28:1-2 Isaac charged Jacob to arise and go to Padanaram to the house of Bethuel; that is where Jacob was headed. - Genesis 11:31 Terah took Abram from Ur of the Chaldees to go into Canaan, and they came unto Haran and dwelt there; Jacob's road runs back to the family's old dwelling. Genesis 29:5 - Jacob asks, Know ye Laban the son of Nahor, and the men of Haran know him. Terah begat Abram, Nahor, and Haran, so Laban dwells in that area because the family remained there when Terah stopped at Haran. - This ties the family line together: Abraham first journeyed from Ur of the Chaldees northwest to Haran, and now Jacob comes up from Canaan northeast to Haran. Because of the way Jacob traveled, he went back home and is dwelling amongst family. Precepts: - Genesis 11:26-27 Terah begat Abram, Nahor, and Haran; Laban is of Nahor's line, so Jacob has come to his own people. Genesis 29:14-15 - Laban said unto Jacob, Surely thou art my bone and my flesh. In the scriptures that phrase means we are family; Jacob abode with him a month, and Laban, because Jacob was his brother, asked what his wages should be. Precepts: - Judges 9:1-2 Abimelech told his mother's brethren, Remember also that I am your bone and your flesh; the phrase declares, we are family. - 2 Samuel 19:12 Ye are my brethren, ye are my bones and my flesh; further proof that bone and flesh speaks of kindred. Genesis 29:16-18 - Leah was tender eyed, but Rachel was beautiful and well favoured, and Jacob loved Rachel. He had already run to roll the stone from the well's mouth, watered her flock, and kissed her when she came out with the sheep; his eyes were fixed on her from the start. - Do not be hasty to credit somebody based on their looks. Of course you want somebody you are attracted to, but commending a person for beauty alone gets a lot of people in trouble. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 36:22 A man loveth nothing better than the beauty of a woman; that is what Jacob saw in Rachel. - Ecclesiasticus 11:2 Do not be hasty to credit somebody for their beauty or their outward appearance. Genesis 29:20 - Jacob served seven years for Rachel, and they seemed unto him but a few days for the love he had to her. That is how fine she was to him: with six and a half years still left, it felt like a couple of days. - Men gather gold and silver and every goodly thing, then let all those things go and fix their eyes fast on a woman comely in favour and beauty. Many run out of their wits for a woman and become servants for their sakes; Jacob became a servant fourteen years, because he was deceived and served another seven. Precepts: - 1 Esdras 4:18-22 Men let gold and silver go and fix their eyes fast on a comely woman; by this ye must know that women have dominion over you. - 1 Esdras 4:25-26 Many have run out of their wits for women and become servants for their sakes; Jacob served fourteen years for Rachel. Genesis 29:30-31 - Jacob loved Rachel more than Leah and served with Laban yet seven other years. When the Lord saw that Leah was hated, he opened her womb; but Rachel was barren. Jacob was showing more favor to Rachel because he was more attracted to Rachel. - Favour is deceitful and beauty is vain. You are not going to look the same at seventy that you did at twenty-five; our days are threescore years and ten, or by reason of strength fourscore, and outside a handful who retain a semblance of their youth, the looks fade along the way. A woman that feareth the Lord, she shall be praised. Precepts: - Proverbs 31:30 Favour is deceitful and beauty is vain, but a woman that feareth the Lord, she shall be praised. - Psalms 90:10 Our days are threescore years and ten, or by reason of strength fourscore years; the beauty of youth does not last the span. Genesis 30: Trouble in the Flesh and a Righteous Hire Read the chapter → Genesis 30 Genesis 30:1-2 - Rachel saw that she bare Jacob no children, envied her sister, and told Jacob, Give me children, or else I die. Jacob's anger was kindled against her: Am I in God's stead, who hath withheld from thee the fruit of the womb? Jacob was not the problem; he was having no trouble producing children. - Their arguing is the trouble in the flesh the scriptures speak of. If thou marry, thou hast not sinned, but such shall have trouble in the flesh: it is not all going to be sweet all the time. Rachel's trouble in the flesh was that she envied her sister and could not bear children, and she took it out on Jacob. Precepts: - 1 Corinthians 7:28 They that marry have not sinned, but such shall have trouble in the flesh; in marriage there will be some hard times. Genesis 30:14-18 - Reuben found mandrakes in the field in the days of wheat harvest and brought them unto his mother Leah. Rachel asked for them, and Leah answered, Is it a small matter that thou hast taken my husband? and wouldest thou take away my son's mandrakes also? So Rachel granted, He shall lie with thee to night for thy son's mandrakes. - When Jacob came out of the field in the evening, Leah went out to meet him: Thou must come in unto me, for surely I have hired thee with my son's mandrakes. He lay with her that night, and she bare a son and called him Issachar. - The mandrake is a flower with several uses; it was used medicinally and as an aphrodisiac, a help for those having problems conceiving. That is why the sisters set such a price on them. Genesis 30:22-24 - God remembered Rachel, hearkened unto her, and opened her womb; she conceived and bare a son and called his name Joseph, saying, God hath taken away my reproach. - It was not the mandrakes that gave her the child; it is only coincidence that the baby came after she had them. The Most High is the one who showed her mercy and opened up her womb, for he maketh the barren woman to keep house and to be a joyful mother of children. Precepts: - Psalms 113:1-2 Praise ye the Lord, O ye servants of the Lord; blessed be the name of the Lord from this time forth and for evermore. - Psalms 113:9 He maketh the barren woman to keep house and to be a joyful mother of children; the Most High is the one who opened Rachel's womb. Genesis 30:27-30 - Laban asked Jacob to tarry: I have learned by experience that the LORD hath blessed me for thy sake. Laban understood that with Jacob in his household he was increasing, and he offered to appoint Jacob his wages. - Jacob answered that Laban knew how he had served him and how the cattle fared with him: it was little which thou hadst before I came, and it is now increased unto a multitude; the LORD hath blessed thee since my coming. And now, when shall I provide for mine own house also? A man looks to provide for his own house. Genesis 30:31-36 - Jacob said, Thou shalt not give me any thing. He asked no gift, only terms: he would keep feeding Laban's flock, and the speckled, spotted, and brown cattle among the sheep and goats from that day forward would be his hire. - That refusal is the spirit our forefathers rolled in. We have to come back to these scriptures and to the understanding of who we are, because our people are lost and have fainted from that spirit; we cannot roll in a handout spirit, and when we repent we have to conduct ourselves as men and provide for our own houses, for the Most High provides. - So shall my righteousness answer for me in time to come: Jacob set terms that could be checked in the open. Every one that was not speckled and spotted among the goats and brown among the sheep would be counted stolen with him. Judge me on my works; my word is my bond. He said it because he knew they were going to have something bad to say about his increase. - Laban agreed, then removed that same day the he goats that were ringstraked and spotted, all the speckled and spotted she goats, and the brown among the sheep, and gave them into the hand of his own sons, setting three days' journey between himself and Jacob. Precepts: - Genesis 14:21-23 After the war Abram told the king of Sodom, I will not take from a thread even to a shoelatchet, lest thou shouldest say, I have made Abram rich; the Most High was his provider, and that is the spirit of the forefathers. Genesis 31: The Return Home and Laban's Idols Read the chapter → Genesis 31 Genesis 31:1-2 - Jacob heard the words of Laban's sons, saying, Jacob hath taken away all that was our father's, and of that which was our father's hath he gotten all this glory; and Jacob beheld the countenance of Laban, and behold, it was not toward him as before. - Remember, Laban had just acknowledged, I have learned by experience that the LORD hath blessed me for thy sake; now he is looking at Jacob sideways because of what his sons said. That is exactly why Jacob said, So shall my righteousness answer for me: he dealt righteously in the open so his dealings would be his answer. Genesis 31:3 - The LORD said unto Jacob, Return unto the land of thy fathers, and to thy kindred; and I will be with thee. The command to go home came with the promise of the Most High's presence. Genesis 31:17-19 - Jacob rose up, set his sons and his wives upon camels, and carried away all his cattle and all the goods he had gotten in Padanaram, to go to Isaac his father in the land of Canaan; he was returning home. - Laban went to shear his sheep, and Rachel had stolen the images that were her father's. Remember what we read in Proverbs about beauty: yes, she was fine, but she was a thief. She might have been a fine thief, but she was a thief. Precepts: - Proverbs 31:30 Favour is deceitful and beauty is vain; Rachel's beauty did not keep her from being a thief. Genesis 31:30-32 - Laban overtook Jacob and asked, Wherefore hast thou stolen my gods? That question tells you what Laban was: Laban was an idolater. - The scriptures prove it. Your fathers dwelt on the other side of the flood in old time, even Terah, the father of Abraham and the father of Nachor, and they served other gods. Laban was of the house of Nahor, an idolater just like his fathers. That is why the Most High told Abram to get out from his country and from his kindred: he separated Abram because of what he had set up for Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and for us, that we not be idolaters. - Jacob answered that he went away because he was afraid Laban would take his daughters from him by force, and said, With whomsoever thou findest thy gods, let him not live. For Jacob knew not that Rachel had stolen them. Precepts: - Joshua 24:2 Your fathers dwelt on the other side of the flood in old time, even Terah the father of Abraham and the father of Nachor, and they served other gods; Laban came of that idolatrous house. - Genesis 12:1 The Most High told Abram, Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred; he separated Abram from the idolaters. --- Topics: Esau and Edom · Idolatry · The Covenant ← Genesis 24-27 · Genesis Study · Genesis 32-35 →

title: Genesis 32: Wrestling Until the Blessing
text: ← Genesis 28-31 · Genesis Study · Genesis 36-39 → Genesis 32: Wrestling Until the Blessing Read the chapter → Genesis 32 Introduction This reading covers Genesis 32 through 35: Jacob's return, the wrestling at Peniel, the meeting with Esau, the matter of Dinah, and the renewing of the name Israel at Bethel. Genesis 32:1-2 - The angels of God met Jacob as he departed from Laban, and he said, This is God's host, and called the place Mahanaim, which means two hosts or camps. - When the scriptures speak of the Lord of hosts, the hosts are the armies of angels that stand before Him. Precepts: - 2 Esdras 8:21 Before the throne of the Most High the hosts of angels stand with trembling; the host Jacob saw was the angels. Genesis 32:3-7 - Jacob sent messengers to Esau, and they returned saying Esau was coming with four hundred men, and Jacob was greatly afraid and distressed. - His fear was rightful: the last word he had of Esau was that Esau purposed in his heart to slay him once their father's mourning came. The hatred began at the blessing, and the scriptures show in Ezekiel that the hatred never ended. - The violent man imagines mischiefs in his heart and is continually gathered together for war; that is what Jacob understood was coming toward him. Precepts: - Genesis 27:41-42 Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing and said in his heart, I will slay my brother Jacob; that was the last report Jacob had. - Psalms 140:1-2 Deliver me from the evil man, preserve me from the violent man, which imagine mischiefs in their heart; Jacob's prayer fit the psalm. Genesis 32:9-12 - Jacob prayed humbly: I am not worthy of the least of all the mercies; deliver me from the hand of my brother. He was not too proud to confess his fear to the Most High. - He pleaded the covenant: thou saidst, I will make thy seed as the sand of the sea. That is the pattern for our prayers; plead the promise made to the fathers and ask the Most High to remember His covenant. Genesis 32:13-20 - Jacob sent droves of livestock ahead as a present, spaced apart, each servant instructed what to say. He said, I will appease him with the present that goeth before me. He moved strategically to soften Esau before they met face to face. - What he did was scriptural: a man's gift maketh room for him, and bringeth him before great men. Precepts: - Proverbs 18:16 A man's gift maketh room for him; the present went before Jacob to make room. Genesis 32:24-26 - Jacob was left alone, and there wrestled a man with him until the breaking of the day; the man had to touch the hollow of Jacob's thigh and put it out of joint, because Jacob would not be beaten. - With his thigh out of joint Jacob still held on: I will not let thee go, except thou bless me. That is faith with works. Cleave unto the Most High and depart not away, that thou mayest be increased at thy last end. - That is the spirit to carry through hardship: fight the good fight of faith and lay hold on eternal life the way Jacob laid hold and would not let go. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 2:3 Cleave unto Him and depart not away, that thou mayest be increased at thy last end; hold on until the blessing. - 1 Timothy 6:12 Fight the good fight of faith; lay hold on eternal life as Jacob laid hold until he was blessed. Genesis 32:27-28 - Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel: for as a prince hast thou power with God and with men, and hast prevailed. Israel means a prince that has power with God. - The God of Israel is He that giveth strength and power unto His people; He is the power source. When Israel went astray and served other gods, the name and the power were taken, and the nations called the people by every other name. Returning to the Most High is how the power returns, not carnal weapons of warfare. Precepts: - Psalms 68:35 The God of Israel is He that giveth strength and power unto His people; the power of the name is from Him. Genesis 32:29-30 - The man would not give his name, but he blessed Jacob there, and Jacob called the place Peniel: for I have seen God face to face, and my life is preserved. - The one Jacob wrestled was an angel: by his strength he had power with God, yea, he had power over the angel, and prevailed. The word God, Elohim, is plural, which clears up the passages where men are said to have seen God and yet no man hath seen the Father. Precepts: - Hosea 12:3-4 Jacob had power with God; he had power over the angel, and prevailed; the wrestler was an angel. Genesis 32:31-32 - The sun rose upon him and he halted upon his thigh; therefore the children of Israel eat not of the sinew which shrank, which is upon the hollow of the thigh, unto this day. Genesis 33: The Meeting With Esau Read the chapter → Genesis 33 Genesis 33:1-4 - Jacob bowed himself to the ground seven times as he came near, and Esau ran, embraced him, fell on his neck, and kissed him, and they wept. - That embrace is not proof that the hatred was gone. Jacob had prayed for deliverance, and when a man's ways please the Lord, He maketh even his enemies to be at peace with him; the Most High put that peace on Esau in that moment. - The same prayer belongs to us: pray for all that are in authority, that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness, keeping the commandments until Christ returns. Precepts: - Proverbs 16:7 When a man's ways please the Lord, He maketh even his enemies to be at peace with him; that is what happened with Esau. - 1 Timothy 2:1-2 Pray for all in authority, that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty. Genesis 33:5-11 - Jacob presented the children which God graciously gave thy servant, and urged the present on Esau until he took it. Receiving the gift sealed the peace; Jacob wanted the assurance. Genesis 33:12-16 - Esau offered to travel together and to leave some of his four hundred men, and Jacob declined both, pleading the tender children and the young flocks: I will lead on softly. He stayed wise and kept his distance, and Esau returned that day to Seir. Genesis 33:17-20 - Jacob journeyed to Succoth, which means booths, built him an house, and made booths for his cattle; the forefather was industrious. - At Shalem he bought a parcel of a field for an hundred pieces of money and erected an altar, and called it Elelohe-Israel: God, the God of Israel. Genesis 34: Dinah and the Zeal of Simeon and Levi Read the chapter → Genesis 34 Genesis 34:1-2 - Dinah, Jacob's only daughter, went out to see the daughters of the land without supervision, and Shechem the son of Hamor took her, and lay with her, and defiled her. This was stranger rape. - The lesson stands for every generation: keep watch over the daughters. Have a care of their body; do not give overmuch liberty; the father wakes for the daughter and the care for her takes away sleep. Everything the children do should have supervision, especially in this age. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 7:24 Hast thou daughters? have a care of their body, and shew not thyself cheerful toward them. - Ecclesiasticus 26:10 If thy daughter be shameless, keep her in straitly, lest she abuse herself through overmuch liberty. - Ecclesiasticus 42:9-11 The father waketh for the daughter when no man knoweth; keep a sure watch, lest she be defiled and made a reproach. Genesis 34:3-7 - Shechem's soul clave to Dinah after he defiled her; he did it backwards, taking first and loving after. That is the world's pattern, not righteousness. - When Jacob's sons heard, the men were grieved and very wroth, because he had wrought folly in Israel in lying with Jacob's daughter, which thing ought not to be done. The laws were in place and kept long before they were written in stone at Sinai. Genesis 34:8-10 - Hamor proposed the exact opposite of the law: make ye marriages with us, give your daughters unto us, and take our daughters unto you, and dwell with us, and become one people. Assimilation and intermarriage is the offer the nations always make, and it is the offer the law forbids. Genesis 34:13-24 - The sons of Jacob answered deceitfully: every male of the city must be circumcised before they would consent. Hamor and Shechem persuaded the whole city, reasoning that the wealth of Jacob's house would become theirs; every male was circumcised. Genesis 34:25-29 - On the third day, when they were sore, two of the sons, Simeon and Levi, took each man his sword, came upon the city boldly, and slew all the males; they took Dinah out, spoiled the city, and carried away the substance and the households. - Two men do not take a city alone. The sword of Simeon was given of God to take vengeance of the strangers that defiled the maid; they were moved with the zeal of the Most High, and He was behind the judgment. Precepts: - Judith 9:2-4 O Lord God of my father Simeon, to whom thou gavest a sword to take vengeance of the strangers who defiled the maid; the vengeance was ordained of God, and they were moved with His zeal. Genesis 34:30-31 - Jacob was troubled: ye have made me to stink among the inhabitants of the land, and I being few in number. He feared the nations round about gathering against his house. - The brothers answered, Should he deal with our sister as with an harlot? There shall be no whore of the daughters of Israel; the daughters of Israel are not to be handled so, and the sons of Israel did not go for it. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 23:17 There shall be no whore of the daughters of Israel; the answer of Simeon and Levi stood on that law. Genesis 35: Bethel and the Twelve Sons of Israel Read the chapter → Genesis 35 Genesis 35:1-4 - Before going up to Bethel, Jacob told his household, Put away the strange gods that are among you, and be clean. The strange gods were there because Rachel had stolen her father's images and hidden them, sitting on them when Laban searched. - Idolatry hidden in the household must be put away before you can stand at Bethel. Rachel finally gave up the images, and Jacob hid them under the oak by Shechem. - From Eve to Rachel the scriptures warn how sin enters through the household; of the woman came the beginning of sin. Sisters, stay in the spirit and guard against the serpent's beguiling as the mothers were beguiled. Precepts: - Genesis 31:19 Rachel had stolen the images that were her father's; that is where the strange gods in the household came from. - Genesis 31:34-35 Rachel hid the images in the camel's furniture and sat upon them, and Laban found them not. - Ecclesiasticus 25:24 Of the woman came the beginning of sin; the warning runs from Eve through the mothers.
