Genesis 35:5 - The terror of God was upon the cities round about, and they did not pursue after the sons of Jacob. What Jacob feared after Shechem never came, because the angel of the Lord encamps round about them that fear Him and delivers them. Precepts: - Psalms 34:7 The angel of the Lord encampeth round about them that fear Him, and delivereth them. Genesis 35:9-11 - God appeared to Jacob again and confirmed it: thy name shall not be called any more Jacob, but Israel shall be thy name. Be fruitful and multiply; a nation and a company of nations shall be of thee, and kings shall come out of thy loins. - The nation and company of nations of Abraham's covenant is Israel, plain and clear, and kings come out of Israel's loins. Christ washed us from our sins and made us kings and priests unto God; the men of Israel are kings in the sight of the Most High. - Israel once had mighty kings who ruled over countries beyond the river, and tribute and custom were paid unto them. The kings failed when they forsook the law, and their power was given to a strange nation; that is why the kings of the scriptures are not known as black kings today. When the King of kings returns He restores the crowns, and He sets crowns on the heads of the great multitude on mount Sion. Precepts: - Revelation 1:5-6 Christ washed us from our sins and hath made us kings and priests unto God. - Ecclesiasticus 49:4-5 All except David, Ezekias, and Josias were defective and forsook the law; therefore their power was given unto others, and their glory to a strange nation. - Ezra 4:20 There have been mighty kings over Jerusalem which ruled over all countries beyond the river, and tribute and custom was paid unto them. - 2 Esdras 2:42-43 A great people whom none could number stood on mount Sion, and one taller than all the rest set crowns upon every one of their heads. Genesis 35:12 - The land given to Abraham and Isaac was promised to Jacob and his seed: the land of Canaan, which is northeast Africa, the land the Most High named when He brought Israel out of Egypt. Precepts: - Leviticus 25:38 I am the Lord which brought you out of Egypt, to give you the land of Canaan; that is the land of the promise. Genesis 35:16-20 - Rachel travailed in hard labour and died bearing her second son; she called him Benoni, but his father called him Benjamin, the son of the right hand. He was the twelfth son, and Jacob set a pillar upon Rachel's grave in the way to Ephrath, which is Bethlehem. Genesis 35:22 - Reuben went and lay with Bilhah, his father's concubine, and Israel heard it. That is fornication such as is not so much as named among the Gentiles, that one should have his father's wife. - The judgment followed him: forasmuch as he defiled his father's bed, his birthright was given unto the sons of Joseph, and the genealogy is not reckoned after the birthright. The firstborn lost the birthright over it. Precepts: - 1 Corinthians 5:1 That a man should have his father's wife is fornication not so much as named among the Gentiles. - 1 Chronicles 5:1 Reuben was the firstborn, but because he defiled his father's bed his birthright was given unto the sons of Joseph. Genesis 35:27-29 - Isaac gave up the ghost at an hundred and fourscore years, old and full of days, and his sons Esau and Jacob together buried him. --- Topics: Esau and Edom · Idolatry · The Covenant · The Priesthood ← Genesis 28-31 · Genesis Study · Genesis 36-39 →

title: Genesis 36: The Generations of Esau, Who Is Edom
text: ← Genesis 32-35 · Genesis Study · Genesis 40-43 → Genesis 36: The Generations of Esau, Who Is Edom Read the chapter → Genesis 36 Introduction This reading covers Genesis 36 through 39: the generations of Esau, Joseph the dreamer sold into Egypt, Judah and Tamar, and Joseph in Potiphar's house. Genesis 36:1 - Now these are the generations of Esau, who is Edom. Esau is Edom, and this teaching identifies Edom with the people called the white man today. - Esau came out of the womb red, all over like an hairy garment; his blood could be seen through his skin for lack of melanin, and his name Esau goes into wasted away. Jacob was not described, because Jacob looked like everyone from Adam down to his time; the man of melanin needed no description. - Esau was called Edom, which means red, because he sold his birthright for that same red pottage. Precepts: - Genesis 25:24-26 The first came out red, all over like an hairy garment; the twins were two nations, polar opposites. - Genesis 25:30 Feed me with that same red pottage; therefore was his name called Edom, which is red. Genesis 36:2-5 - Esau took his wives of the daughters of Canaan and of Ishmael. He was the first of the Edomites; there were no women of his nation yet, so his lineage began through those wives. Genesis is Bereshith, the beginning of nations. Genesis 36:6-8 - Esau went from the face of his brother because their riches were more than that they might dwell together, the same as with Abram and Lot in Genesis 13. Esau was rich at this time, out of the house of Isaac and Abraham. - Thus dwelt Esau in mount Seir. Mount Seir is the clefts of the rock; the vision of Obadiah speaks to Edom as thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, whose pride hath deceived him. Precepts: - Obadiah 1:3 The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee, thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock; that is Edom in mount Seir. Genesis 36:9-11 - Esau is the father of the Edomites in mount Seir, and his grandson Teman, son of Eliphaz, is identified in this teaching with Germany; the reference work Edom and Germany lays that connection out. - The prophecy over Teman stands: the wise men shall be destroyed out of Edom and understanding out of the mount of Esau, and the mighty men of Teman shall be dismayed. Much of the world's science and weapons technology has come out of Germany, and the word says that wisdom will be destroyed. Precepts: - Obadiah 1:8-9 The wise men of Edom and the mighty men of Teman shall be destroyed, that every one of the mount of Esau may be cut off. Genesis 36:12 - Timna was concubine to Eliphaz, and she bare Amalek. Amalek came of a concubine, a lesser wife, which is why the word bastard is studied here: in the scriptures it means a child of incest or one born outside the proper marriage. - The word says a bastard shall dwell in Ashdod, and Ashdod is the area of modern day Tel Aviv; this teaching places the line of Amalek dwelling there today. Precepts: - Zechariah 9:6 And a bastard shall dwell in Ashdod; the prophecy names the place where that seed sits. Genesis 36:15-19 - These were the dukes of the sons of Esau: dukes are the chiefs of their tribes, the leaders of the families of Edom. Genesis 36:20-30 - The sons of Seir the Horite inhabited the land before Esau; the Horites were the original dwellers of mount Seir. - The Lord destroyed the Horims from before the children of Esau, and they succeeded them and dwelt in their stead, as Deuteronomy records. Precepts: - Genesis 14:6 The Horites were in their mount Seir already in Abraham's day. - Deuteronomy 2:22 The Lord destroyed the Horims from before the children of Esau, and they dwelt in their stead. Genesis 36:31 - These are the kings that reigned in the land of Edom before there reigned any king over the children of Israel. Israel had no king until Saul, whom the Lord sought out when Israel asked for a king like the nations, in 1 Samuel 8 and 9. Genesis 37: Joseph the Dreamer Read the chapter → Genesis 37 Genesis 37:1-2 - Joseph brought unto his father the evil report of his brethren. That was law, not tale bearing: if a soul hear swearing and be a witness and do not utter it, he shall bear his iniquity. The law was already around, and Joseph kept it. Precepts: - Leviticus 5:1 A witness that does not utter what he has seen bears his own iniquity; Joseph uttered the evil report according to that law. Genesis 37:3-4 - Israel loved Joseph more than all his children, the son of his old age, and made him a coat of many colours; and his brethren hated him and could not speak peaceably unto him. - That is real hatred among brothers, and the same spirit is on Israel today, where a brother cannot even receive a shalom in peace. Genesis 37:5-8 - Joseph dreamed, and the sheaves of his brethren made obeisance to his sheaf. The Lord speaks by the prophets in visions and similitudes; the vision of dreams is the resemblance of one thing to another, as the likeness of a face to a face. - His brethren understood the dream, that he should reign over them, and hated him yet the more for his dreams and for his words. Precepts: - Hosea 12:10 The Most High multiplies visions and uses similitudes by the ministry of the prophets. - Ecclesiasticus 34:3 The vision of dreams is the resemblance of one thing to another; the sheaf stood for Joseph and the sheaves for his brethren. Genesis 37:9-10 - In the second dream the sun, the moon, and the eleven stars made obeisance to Joseph. Jacob interpreted it at once: shall I and thy mother and thy brethren indeed come to bow down ourselves to thee? - The same figures mark Israel: the woman clothed with the sun with a crown of twelve stars is the daughter of Zion, the nation of Israel, and the twelve stars are the tribes. - The dream came true. In the famine the whole house of Jacob came down to Joseph in Egypt, and he placed them in the best of the land and nourished them with bread; they bowed to the one the Most High had set over them. Precepts: - Revelation 12:1 The woman clothed with the sun, with the moon under her feet and a crown of twelve stars, figures Israel and her tribes. - Jeremiah 6:2 The daughter of Zion is likened to a comely and delicate woman; the woman of the vision is Israel. - Genesis 47:11-12 Joseph placed his father and his brethren in the best of the land and nourished them; the dream was fulfilled. Genesis 37:11 - His brethren envied him, but his father observed the saying. Envy consumes a man, and such a man shall have no fellowship with wisdom; when envy takes over, wisdom leaves. Precepts: - Wisdom of Solomon 6:23 Consuming envy has no fellowship with wisdom; the brothers' envy put wisdom away from them. Genesis 37:18-20 - When they saw him afar off, they conspired against him to slay him: Behold, this dreamer cometh. That is the same spirit Cain had, and the same spirit Esau had. - Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer. Inner hatred, given room, plots death; that is why the law says thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart. Precepts: - 1 John 3:15 Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer, and no murderer hath eternal life abiding in him. Genesis 37:21-28 - Reuben delivered him out of their hands: cast him into this pit, but lay no hand upon him; he meant to return him to his father. - Judah said, What profit is it if we slay our brother and conceal his blood? They sold Joseph to the Ishmaelites, the people known today as the Arab man, for twenty pieces of silver, and they brought him into Egypt. Genesis 37:29-36 - The brothers dipped the coat in the blood of a kid and let their father believe an evil beast had devoured Joseph. They dealt falsely and lied, against the law: ye shall not steal, neither deal falsely, neither lie one to another. - Jacob could not see the lie because the thing was of the Lord. As Joseph told them later, ye thought evil against me, but God meant it unto good, to save much people alive; had Joseph never gone down to Egypt, the whole house of Israel would have died in the famine. - The Midianites sold him in Egypt to Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh and captain of the guard. Precepts: - Leviticus 19:11 Neither deal falsely, neither lie one to another; the brothers broke that law before their father. - Genesis 50:20 Ye thought evil against me, but God meant it unto good, to save much people alive. Genesis 38: Judah and Tamar Read the chapter → Genesis 38 Genesis 38:1-7 - Judah took the daughter of Shuah and had Er, Onan, and Shelah; and Er, Judah's firstborn, was wicked in the sight of the Lord, and the Lord slew him. Genesis 38:8-10 - Onan was told to go in unto his brother's wife and raise up seed to his brother, and he refused, spilling it on the ground, and the Lord slew him also. - The sin was refusing to raise up seed to his brother, not the act itself; do not build a doctrine on the wrong point. What happened here later became law: the husband's brother raises up the name of the dead, and he that refuses has his shoe loosed and his face spat in, and his house carries the reproach. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 25:5-9 The brother's duty to raise up a name in Israel became law, and the refuser bore public reproach; Onan refused that duty. Genesis 38:11-19 - Judah promised Tamar to Shelah and did not perform it. When she saw Shelah was grown and she was not given to him, she put off her widow's garments, covered herself with a vail, and sat where Judah would pass. - Judah thought her to be an harlot because of the attire; the scriptures show a harlot was always known by her dress, as the woman with the attire of an harlot and subtil of heart. - She took his signet, bracelets, and staff as a pledge, and conceived by him. Precepts: - Proverbs 7:10 There met him a woman with the attire of an harlot, and subtil of heart; the attire spoke before she did. Genesis 38:24-26 - When Judah heard Tamar was with child by whoredom he said, Bring her forth, and let her be burnt. A woman promised in the covenant that plays the harlot and brings an heir by another disobeys the law of the Most High, and her reproach is not blotted out; that is why the judgment was so heavy. - Then she produced the signet, bracelets, and staff, and Judah acknowledged them: She hath been more righteous than I, because that I gave her not to Shelah my son. And he knew her again no more. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 23:22-26 The wife that brings in an heir by another disobeys the law of the Most High and leaves her memory to be cursed; that standard is why Judah called for judgment. Genesis 38:27-30 - Twins were in her womb: the midwife bound a scarlet thread on the hand of the first, but his brother broke forth first and was called Pharez, and after him came Zarah with the scarlet thread. - Judah's line went down into Egypt in the end, and Judah died there with his brethren; and Joseph died, and all his brethren, and all that generation. Precepts: - Exodus 1:6 And Joseph died, and all his brethren, and all that generation; Judah ended his days in Egypt. Genesis 39: Joseph in Potiphar's House Read the chapter → Genesis 39 Genesis 39:1-6 - The Lord was with Joseph in his captivity, and his master saw that the Lord made all that he did to prosper; Potiphar made him overseer over his house, and the Lord blessed the Egyptian's house for Joseph's sake. - The Most High deals with His people even in captivity and gives them compassion before them who carried them captive; the favor on Joseph is the pattern of that prayer. Precepts: - 1 Kings 8:50 Give them compassion before them who carried them captives; the Lord gave Joseph that compassion in Egypt. Genesis 39:7-9 - His master's wife cast her eyes upon Joseph and said, Lie with me; and he refused: how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God? - Adultery was known as sin from the beginning, long before Sinai. Abraham kept the commandments, statutes, and laws; and Abimelech rebuked Isaac because one of the people might have lain with his wife and brought guiltiness upon them. The nations themselves knew adultery brought guilt. Precepts: - Genesis 26:5 Abraham obeyed my voice, and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws; the laws are nothing new. - Genesis 26:10 Abimelech knew lightly lying with another man's wife would have brought guiltiness upon them; adultery was known sin. Genesis 39:10-12 - She spake to Joseph day by day, and he hearkened not. Then she arranged the empty house, caught him by his garment, and he left his garment in her hand and fled. - That is the example: flee from sin as from the face of a serpent, for if thou comest too near it, it will bite thee; the teeth thereof are as the teeth of a lion. Joseph knew thirty more seconds of entertaining her would be the bite. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 21:1-2 Flee from sin as from the face of a serpent; come too near and it will bite thee. Joseph fled. Genesis 39:13-18 - When she saw he was fled, she lied and cried that the Hebrew came in to mock her, holding his garment as evidence. - The scriptures warn of that spirit: the woman whose heart is snares and nets and her hands as bands; whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her. The lips of a strange woman drop as an honeycomb, but her end is bitter, and her ways are moveable; the same mouth that flattered turns and accuses. Precepts: - Ecclesiastes 7:26 The woman whose heart is snares and nets, and her hands as bands; whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her, as Joseph escaped. - Proverbs 5:3-6 The lips of a strange woman drop as an honeycomb, but her end is bitter as wormwood; her ways are moveable. Genesis 39:19-20 - When his master heard the words of his wife, his wrath was kindled and he put Joseph into the prison. He did not seek understanding, for jealousy is the rage of a man: he will not spare in the day of vengeance, nor regard any ransom. Precepts: - Proverbs 6:32-35 Jealousy is the rage of a man; he will not spare in the day of vengeance nor regard any ransom; that is why no plea could reach Potiphar. Genesis 39:21-23 - But the Lord was with Joseph, and shewed him mercy, and gave him favour in the sight of the keeper of the prison, and everything in the prison was committed to Joseph's hand. - Everywhere Joseph went the favor followed, because the Most High was ordering his steps the whole way, so that Joseph would stand where he could save the whole house of Israel alive. --- Topics: Esau and Edom · The Covenant ← Genesis 32-35 · Genesis Study · Genesis 40-43 →

title: Genesis 40: Do Not Interpretations Belong to God
text: ← Genesis 36-39 · Genesis Study · Genesis 44-47 → Genesis 40: Do Not Interpretations Belong to God Read the chapter → Genesis 40 Introduction This is a reading session: Genesis 40 through 43 were read straight through, with exposition gathered at the verses below. The reading covers the butler and the baker's dreams in the prison, Pharaoh's two dreams and Joseph's exaltation over Egypt, the first journey of Joseph's brethren to buy corn, and Benjamin brought down at the second journey. Questions were taken at the end of the reading; none produced affirmed teaching beyond what is entered under the verses. Genesis 40:8 - We have dreamed a dream, and there is no interpreter of it. Joseph answered on another level: do not interpretations belong to God? Interpretations do belong to God. - Daniel stood in the same understanding in Babylon; the king confessed that Daniel's God is a God of gods and a revealer of secrets. Joseph already understood that these things belong to the Most High. Precepts: - Daniel 2:47 Your God is a God of gods and a revealer of secrets; the same God that gave Joseph interpretations gave them to Daniel. Genesis 40:9-13 - The chief butler's dream: a vine with three branches that budded and brought forth ripe grapes, pressed into Pharaoh's cup. Joseph interpreted it at once: the three branches are three days, and within three days Pharaoh would restore the butler to his butlership. Genesis 40:16-19 - The chief baker's three white baskets were also three days, but his end was hanging on a tree with the birds eating his flesh from off him. - Both men saw variations of three, and in both dreams the three stood for three days. The dream is not always what is seen: the vision of dreams is the resemblance of one thing to another, even as the likeness of a face to a face. You may see yourself steal a piece of bread in a dream, and the meaning is that somebody will steal something from you in the days ahead; one thing resembles another. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 34:3 The vision of dreams is the resemblance of one thing to another; the threes in both dreams stood for three days. Genesis 40:20-23 - On the third day, Pharaoh's birthday, it happened just as Joseph laid it out: the chief butler was restored unto his butlership again, and the chief baker was hanged. - Birthdays are heathen customs, and wicked things take place at them: at this birthday feast a man was put to death before everybody, and on Herod's birthday the daughter of Herodias danced and John the Baptist was beheaded. - Yet did not the chief butler remember Joseph, but forgat him. Precepts: - Matthew 14:6-8 On Herod's birthday the dancing pleased him, and the head of John the Baptist was demanded in a charger; another wicked occurrence on a birthday. Genesis 41: Pharaoh's Dreams and Joseph's Rise Over Egypt Read the chapter → Genesis 41 Genesis 41:1-8 - After two full years Pharaoh dreamed: seven well favoured kine eaten up by seven ill favoured ones, and seven good ears devoured by seven thin ears blasted with the east wind. He saw different variations of the number seven, as the butler and the baker saw variations of three; the dream is a resemblance of one thing to another. - His spirit was troubled, and none of the magicians and wise men of Egypt could interpret the dreams unto Pharaoh. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 34:3 The vision of dreams is the resemblance of one thing to another; the sevens in Pharaoh's dreams resembled seven years. Genesis 41:15-16 - Pharaoh told Joseph he had heard he could understand a dream to interpret it, and Joseph gave all the praise to the Most High: it is not in me; God shall give Pharaoh an answer of peace. - The Most High reveals his secrets to his servants, and the secret of the Lord is with them that fear him. That is why the interpretation was with Joseph and not with the magicians of Egypt. Precepts: - Amos 3:7 The Lord God revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets. - Psalm 25:14 The secret of the Lord is with them that fear him; the Most High shows those things unto his servants. Genesis 41:32-36 - The dream was doubled unto Pharaoh twice because the thing is established by God, and God will surely bring it to pass. - Joseph did not stop at the interpretation; he gave the counsel: take up the fifth part of the land in the seven plenteous years and store it up, so Egypt could ration food through the years of famine. That shows what was on Joseph: he was wise, understanding, and diligent. - A prudent man foresees the evil coming and makes preparation so he is not consumed in it; the simple pass on and are punished. There is treasure and oil in the dwelling of the wise, but a foolish man spends it up; spending irrationally is a spirit of folly. Precepts: - Proverbs 22:3 A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself; that prudent spirit was on Joseph. - Proverbs 21:20 There is treasure to be desired in the dwelling of the wise, but a foolish man spendeth it up. Genesis 41:38-39 - Can we find such a one as this is, a man in whom the Spirit of God is? Israel has always been a wise and understanding people: Joseph in Egypt, Daniel in ancient Babylon, up until this day, a people responsible for many inventions and cunning arts. - The children of Israel brought to Babylon were skilful in all wisdom, cunning in knowledge, understanding science, and able to stand in the king's palace to give counsel; and they were taught the tongue of the Chaldeans, for we have the capability to understand multiple languages as well. Precepts: - Daniel 1:3-4 Children of Israel skilful in all wisdom and understanding science stood in the king's palace; the same spirit that was in Joseph. Genesis 41:40-44 - Pharaoh set Joseph over his house and over all the land of Egypt; only in the throne was Pharaoh greater. Without Joseph no man lifted up his hand or foot in all Egypt: nothing moved unless Joseph decreed it. - The Most High called for the famine and sent a man before them, even Joseph: sold for a servant, his feet hurt with fetters, laid in iron until the time that his word came; then the king loosed him and made him lord of his house, to bind his princes at his pleasure and teach his senators wisdom. Whether prince or common man, Joseph could bind any man in Egypt. Precepts: - Psalm 105:16-22 He sent a man before them, even Joseph, who was sold for a servant; the king made him lord of his house, to bind his princes at his pleasure and teach his senators wisdom. Genesis 41:45 - Pharaoh called Joseph's name Zaphnathpaaneah and gave him Asenath the daughter of Potipherah priest of On to wife. These heathens always like to change our names; that is one reason America is called spiritual Egypt, because they do the same thing that ancient Egypt did. Genesis 41:50-52 - Joseph called the firstborn Manasseh, forgetting, for God had made him forget all his toil and all his father's house; and the second called he Ephraim, fruitful, for God had caused him to be fruitful in the land of his affliction. - Ephraim was the second born, yet Ephraim possessed the kingship: the first king of the Northern Kingdom, Jeroboam, was of the tribe of Ephraim, not of Manasseh. Ephraim is the head tribe of the Northern Kingdom. - Jacob set that in place. When Joseph saw his father lay his right hand upon Ephraim's head it displeased him, and he tried to move it to Manasseh's head; but Jacob refused and said, his younger brother shall be greater than he; and he set Ephraim before Manasseh. Precepts: - Genesis 48:17-20 Jacob refused to move his right hand from Ephraim's head, saying the younger brother shall be greater; he set Ephraim before Manasseh. Genesis 41:53-57 - The seven years of dearth began to come, according as Joseph had said. Another word for dearth is famine: no food, no sustenance to nourish the body. - The dearth was in all lands, but in all the land of Egypt there was bread, because Joseph had stored up the seven years of plenty. All countries came into Egypt to Joseph for to buy corn. Precepts: - Acts 7:11 There came a dearth over all the land of Egypt and Chanaan, and our fathers found no sustenance; dearth is famine. Genesis 42: Joseph's Brethren Bow Down in Egypt Read the chapter → Genesis 42 Genesis 42:1-3 - Jacob saw that there was corn in Egypt and said unto his sons, why do ye look one upon another? Get you down thither, and buy for us from thence, that we may live, and not die. - This is a repeating thing in our history: when famine came, the fathers moved toward Egypt for sustenance and nourishment. There was a famine in Abram's days and he went down into Egypt, and another famine in Isaac's days, when the Lord told him not to go down. Precepts: - Genesis 12:9-10 There was a famine in the land, and Abram went down into Egypt to sojourn there, for the famine was grievous. - Genesis 26:1-2 In the famine of Isaac's days the Lord appeared unto him and said, go not down into Egypt; the pattern of famine and Egypt runs through the fathers. Genesis 42:4 - Jacob sent not Benjamin with his brethren; lest peradventure means perhaps mischief befall him. Benjamin was the youngest boy, and he was Rachel's son: Rachel died in hard labour bearing him, calling him Benoni as her soul was departing, but his father called him Benjamin. - Jacob loved Rachel more than Leah, and Rachel was barren for years; she brought forth only Joseph and Benjamin. With Joseph presumed dead, Benjamin was the last son Jacob had of his beloved wife, so he would not let him go down. Precepts: - Genesis 35:16-19 Rachel travailed in hard labour and died bearing Benjamin, and was buried in the way to Ephrath, which is Bethlehem. - Genesis 29:30-31 Jacob loved Rachel more than Leah, and Rachel was barren; Joseph and Benjamin were the only sons she brought forth. Genesis 42:7-9 - Joseph knew his brethren, but made himself strange unto them and spake roughly unto them; and they knew him not. Time had passed, and they supposed he was dead or a slave; they never expected their brother to be set as second in command and ruler over Egypt. - They also knew him not because he blended in among the Egyptians: Israel is black as night, just like the ancient Egyptians. When Jacob died, the Canaanites saw the mourning company and took them all for Egyptians; all twelve tribes looked like the people of Egypt. - And Joseph remembered the dreams which he dreamed of them. The sheaves that made obeisance to his sheaf were now his brethren bowing down themselves before him with their faces to the earth. Precepts: - Genesis 50:10-11 The Canaanites saw the mourning and said, this is a grievous mourning to the Egyptians; the twelve tribes were mistaken for Egyptians. Genesis 42:15-16 - Hereby ye shall be proved: ye shall not go forth hence, except your youngest brother come hither. Joseph pressed for Benjamin because that was his own mother's son, his baby brother, whom he wanted to see. Genesis 42:21-24 - We are verily guilty concerning our brother, in that we saw the anguish of his soul when he besought us, and we would not hear. Their conscience was activated; they knew this distress had come upon them for what they did to their brother Joseph, not knowing Joseph stood before them. - Reuben answered them, spake I not unto you, saying, do not sin against the child? Reuben was the one who would not have Joseph slain, but said to sell him not and lay no hand on him. - They knew not that Joseph understood them, for he spake unto them by an interpreter. He spoke to them in the tongue of the Egyptians and heard every word they said in their own tongue; we have the capacity to understand many languages. - He turned himself about from them and wept, for he heard everything they said; then he returned, and took from them Simeon, and bound him before their eyes. Genesis 42:35-38 - Every man's bundle of money was in his sack, and they were afraid; and Jacob their father said, me have ye bereaved of my children: Joseph is not, and Simeon is not, and ye will take Benjamin away. - My son shall not go down with you; his brother is dead, and he is left alone. If mischief befell Benjamin by the way, Jacob's gray hairs would go down with sorrow to the grave: he would die of a broken heart, for Benjamin was the last son he had of Rachel. Genesis 43: Benjamin Brought Down to Egypt Read the chapter → Genesis 43 Genesis 43:8-10 - Judah stood surety for the lad: of my hand shalt thou require him; if I bring him not unto thee, and set him before thee, then let me bear the blame for ever. - Except we had lingered, surely now we had returned this second time. Judah reasoned with his father: had Benjamin been sent at the first, they would have been down to Egypt and back already with food. Genesis 43:11-14 - Israel yielded: carry down the man a present of the best fruits in the land, a little balm, a little honey, spices, and myrrh, nuts, and almonds. - Take double money in your hand, and carry again the money that was brought back in your sacks; peradventure it was an oversight. Jacob would not keep what was not his: return it and be guiltless. - And God Almighty give you mercy before the man. Jacob committed the outcome to the Most High: if I be bereaved of my children, I am bereaved. Genesis 43:29-31 - Joseph lifted up his eyes and saw his brother Benjamin, his mother's son, and said, God be gracious unto thee, my son. His bowels did yearn upon his brother, and he entered into his chamber and wept there; then he washed his face, and went out, and refrained himself. Genesis 43:32 - The Egyptians might not eat bread with the Hebrews, for that is an abomination unto the Egyptians. The same thing showed up back in the 1900s in America: colored only and whites only, no seat at the same table; they fashioned themselves after ancient Egypt. - Esau patterns himself after the former kingdoms. He learns how to govern and oppress by studying the kingdoms that were before him: ancient Babylon, ancient Greece, ancient Rome, ancient Egypt. They search out iniquities and accomplish a diligent search; nothing they do is accidental, everything follows the blueprint of the kingdoms that came before them. Precepts: - Psalm 64:5-6 They search out iniquities; they accomplish a diligent search; the oppressor studies the former kingdoms and follows their blueprint. Genesis 43:33-34 - They sat before him, the firstborn according to his birthright and the youngest according to his youth, and the men marvelled one at another. - Benjamin's mess was five times so much as any of theirs. Joseph gave all of them provision, but he made sure his baby brother was well taken care of: Benjamin was his mother's son and had nothing to do with him being sold. And they drank, and were merry with him. --- Topics: Esau and Edom · The Covenant · The Priesthood ← Genesis 36-39 · Genesis Study · Genesis 44-47 →

title: Genesis 44: The Cup in Benjamin's Sack and Judah's Surety
text: ← Genesis 40-43 · Genesis Study · Genesis 48-50 → Genesis 44: The Cup in Benjamin's Sack and Judah's Surety Read the chapter → Genesis 44 Introduction This reading covers Genesis 44 through 47: the silver cup planted in Benjamin's sack, Joseph made known unto his brethren, Israel's going down into Egypt with threescore and ten souls, and the family planted in Goshen through the famine years. The session opens back at Genesis 43:30-34 to bring the account up to speed: the Egyptians might not eat bread with the Hebrews, for that is an abomination unto the Egyptians; even while Israel sojourned in Egypt the Lord put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel, as Exodus 11:7 shows. The exposition after the reading draws out the characteristics of Joseph: forgiveness, favor, righteousness, mercy, and perseverance through adversity. Genesis 44:1-2 - Joseph commanded his steward to fill the men's sacks with food, return every man's money, and put his own silver cup in the sack's mouth of the youngest. The cup was planted so Joseph could hold Benjamin for a short period of time; he was not seeking harm, he was drawing out word of his father Jacob and whether he was yet alive. Genesis 44:11-13 - The steward searched, beginning at the eldest and leaving at the youngest, and the cup was found in Benjamin's sack; they rent their clothes and returned to the city. Benjamin found with the cup gave Joseph cause to hold him, and it set the stage for Judah to speak the whole history. Genesis 44:27-29 - Thy servant my father said unto us, Ye know that my wife bare me two sons: that is Jacob speaking of Rachel, who bare Joseph and Benjamin, the eleventh and twelfth sons. - Ye shall bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to the grave: Jacob never got over Joseph being taken away. Sorrow kills; give not over thy mind to heaviness, for the gladness of the heart is the life of man, and losing Benjamin also would have brought their father to the grave. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 30:21-23 Remove sorrow far from thee, for sorrow hath killed many; losing Benjamin would have killed Jacob. Genesis 44:30-34 - Judah became surety for the lad unto his father, and offered to abide instead of the lad as a bondman: let the lad go up with his brethren. He knew his father's life was bound up in the lad's life, and he would not see the evil come on his father. - Joseph in all of this was interrogating his brothers about the whereabouts and welfare of their father; holding Benjamin was the device that drew it out of Judah. Genesis 45: Joseph Made Known unto His Brethren Read the chapter → Genesis 45 Genesis 45:1-3 - Joseph made himself known, and his brethren could not answer him, for they were troubled at his presence. They could not recognize their own brother: he was sold as a teenager, and he stood before them now a grown man in his years. - He was also clothed in the customs of Egypt: shaved, in Egyptian raiment, decked out as the second in command, and he had made himself strange to them and spoken by an interpreter though he understood their tongue. - This does not prove the Israelites looked like the Egyptians; the peoples were all dark people. The change was his age, his dress, and the customs of the land he ruled in. Precepts: - Genesis 42:7-8 He made himself strange unto them and spake roughly; Joseph knew his brethren, but they knew not him. - Genesis 42:23 He spake unto them by an interpreter, though he understood every word. - Genesis 41:14 He shaved himself and changed his raiment; Joseph had taken on the customs of Egypt as second in command. Genesis 45:4-8 - Be not grieved nor angry with yourselves: it was not you that sent me hither, but God. The Most High sent Joseph before them to preserve life and to save the whole house of Israel by a great deliverance; had he not been in Egypt, they would have died in the famine. - Joseph kept the law of forgiveness: forgive thy brother not until seven times, but until seventy times seven. His own brothers sold him into slavery, and he forgave them; that is the law Israel must keep with one another today. - The famine itself was called by the Most High, and the man was sent before them, even Joseph, sold for a servant, whose feet they hurt with fetters. The fetters and the iron are the prison where the king's prisoners were bound. Precepts: - Matthew 18:21-22 Not until seven times, but until seventy times seven; the law of forgiveness Joseph showed his brethren. - Acts 7:9-10 The patriarchs, moved with envy, sold Joseph into Egypt; but God was with him, delivered him out of all his afflictions, and made him governor. - Psalms 105:15-18 Touch not mine anointed; he called for a famine and sent a man before them, even Joseph, whose feet they hurt with fetters. - Genesis 39:20 The fetters and the iron of the psalm are the prison where the king's prisoners were bound. Genesis 45:25-28 - Joseph is yet alive, and he is governor over all the land of Egypt. Everything Egypt was at that point in time came through the influence of Joseph; the prosperity of that land was the favor the Lord had with Israel. - The word of the Lord tried Joseph. Until the time that his word came he sat in the prison; then the king sent and loosed him, made him lord of his house and ruler of all his substance, and Joseph taught his senators wisdom. He was the teacher in Egypt, second in command, a king in all but title. - To go from prison to governor is favor: the Lord causes the enemy to entreat his remnant well in the time of evil. Keep the commandments, for rulers are not a terror to good works. - These are the characteristics of Joseph: my son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation; set thy heart aright and constantly endure, and make not haste in time of trouble. Do not be quick to leave the truth or find excuses in the time of trouble. Gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity. - Better is the end of a thing than the beginning thereof: he began sold into slavery and put in prison under false pretenses, and the end of the thing was governor of Egypt, a father to Pharaoh. In the day of prosperity be joyful, but in the day of adversity consider the days that were good, and be patient in spirit: read the Bible more, study more, pray more, apply more. - If thou faint in the day of adversity, thy strength is small. When trials come, read the afflictions of the forefathers and the attributes they had in those times, and apply them: forgiveness, favor, righteousness, mercy. There is no other way into the kingdom but through tribulation. - Jacob knew there was corn in Egypt because Joseph had already told Pharaoh exactly what to do to save up in the time of tribulation; when Jacob heard, he sent out the fathers. Applying these attributes makes better men, women, brothers, and sisters, to bring forth the nation unto the kingdom of God. Precepts: - Psalms 105:19-24 The word of the Lord tried him; the king loosed him and made him lord of his house, to teach his senators wisdom; then Israel also came into Egypt. - Jeremiah 15:11 Verily I will cause the enemy to entreat thee well in the time of evil; that favor took Joseph from prison to governor. - Romans 13:3 Rulers are not a terror to good works; do that which is good, and thou shalt have praise of the same. - Ecclesiasticus 2:1-6 Prepare thy soul for temptation and constantly endure; Joseph was gold tried in the fire. - Ecclesiastes 7:8 Better is the end of a thing than the beginning thereof; the patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit. - Ecclesiastes 7:14 In the day of prosperity be joyful, but in the day of adversity consider; the Most High set the one over against the other. - Acts 14:22 We must through much tribulation enter into the kingdom of God, as our forefather Joseph did. - Proverbs 24:10 If thou faint in the day of adversity, thy strength is small; the strength applied to the Bible is small. - Acts 7:11-14 There came a dearth over all the land, and when Jacob heard that there was corn in Egypt, he sent out our fathers; Joseph's saving carried the family. - Luke 17:20-21 The kingdom of God cometh not with observation; put on these attributes to bring forth the nation unto that kingdom. Genesis 46: Israel Comes into Egypt, Threescore and Ten Souls Read the chapter → Genesis 46 Genesis 46:26-27 - All the souls of the house of Jacob which came into Egypt were threescore and ten. A score is twenty, so three score is sixty, and ten more makes seventy souls. Genesis 46:31-34 - Joseph instructed his brethren to tell Pharaoh their trade hath been about cattle from their youth, both they and also their fathers, that they might dwell in the land of Goshen; for every shepherd is an abomination unto the Egyptians. - There is history behind that instruction. Somewhere between the fifteenth and seventeenth dynasties Egypt was ruled by the Hyksos, called the shepherd kings, a group of Canaanites or Hittites that occupied the land; the Egyptians did not deal with shepherds. - Naming their trade set Israel apart in Goshen, which was fertile land, and the favor Joseph had was bestowed upon him through Pharaoh to give them that land. Genesis 47: Goshen, the Famine, and the Fifth Part Read the chapter → Genesis 47 Genesis 47:1-6 - Joseph presented five of his brethren, and they answered as instructed: thy servants are shepherds, both we and also our fathers. Pharaoh gave the best of the land: in the land of Goshen let them dwell, and men of activity among them were made rulers over his cattle. Genesis 47:11-12 - Joseph placed his father and his brethren in the best of the land, in the land of Rameses, and nourished them with bread. Goshen and the land of Rameses are the exact same place. - Rameses was the king at the time Israel left Egypt, and Moses wrote the first five books of the Bible; he wrote the place under the name of his own day. In the bush the Most High manifestly revealed himself to Moses, showed him the secrets of the times and the end, the beginning to the end, and the words were written again with Esdras. Precepts: - 2 Esdras 14:3-6 Moses was shown the secrets of the times and the end; that is how the land carried the name Rameses in the writing. Genesis 47:13-20 - When money failed in the land, the Egyptians gave their cattle for bread, and the next year their bodies and their lands; so the land became Pharaoh's. Pharaoh got everybody in servitude off the business dealings of Joseph and the favor the Lord had with him. Genesis 47:23-26 - Joseph gave the people seed and made it a law over Egypt: give the fifth part unto Pharaoh, and four parts are your own for seed of the field, for your food, and for your households and little ones. - Joseph teaches how to save money: pay the fifth part, and lay up for the years of trouble. That wisdom is how Egypt got through the famine, and it is the same perseverance to practice now in times of tribulation. Genesis 47:27-31 - Israel dwelt in the country of Goshen, had possessions therein, and grew and multiplied exceedingly. Jacob lived in Egypt seventeen years, so the whole age of Jacob was an hundred forty and seven years. - Jacob made Joseph swear to carry him out of Egypt and bury him in the burying place of his fathers. By faith Jacob, when he was a dying, blessed both the sons of Joseph; and by faith Joseph made mention of the departing of the children of Israel and gave commandment concerning his bones. Hebrews 11 is the hall of faith, the faithful men of the sons of God, a chapter to read. - Neither was there a man born like unto Joseph, a governor of his brethren, a stay of the people, whose bones were regarded of the Lord. To grow in spirit and be like him, put on the spirit of the forefathers. Precepts: - Hebrews 11:21-22 By faith Jacob blessed the sons of Joseph, and by faith Joseph gave commandment concerning his bones. - Ecclesiasticus 49:15 No man was born like unto Joseph; put on the spirit of the forefathers. --- Topics: The Priesthood ← Genesis 40-43 · Genesis Study · Genesis 48-50 →

title: Genesis 48: Ephraim and Manasseh Blessed as Sons of Israel
text: ← Genesis 44-47 · Genesis Study · Exodus 1 → Genesis 48: Ephraim and Manasseh Blessed as Sons of Israel Read the chapter → Genesis 48 Introduction This session is a reading session, marked (READ), covering Genesis 48 through 50 and Exodus 1: Jacob blessing Ephraim and Manasseh, the prophecies over the twelve tribes for the last days, the burial of Jacob and the death of Joseph, and Israel under a new king in Egypt. The reading moved straight through with brief teaching and no questions, and the full twelve-tribe breakdown of Genesis 49 was reserved for its own class; the tribe identifications given in the reading are recorded here. The Exodus 1 portion received its own teaching and is written in its own chapter file. Genesis 48:1-2 - Word came to Joseph, Behold, thy father is sick, and he took with him his two sons Manasseh and Ephraim to visit Jacob; and Israel strengthened himself and sat upon the bed. Genesis 48:3-6 - Jacob rehearsed to Joseph how God Almighty appeared unto him at Luz in the land of Canaan and blessed him, promising to make him a multitude of people and to give the land to his seed after him for an everlasting possession. - Thy two sons Ephraim and Manasseh, as Reuben and Simeon, they shall be mine. Jacob took Joseph's sons as his own, so the blessings that came upon Jacob's sons came upon Ephraim and Manasseh also; they became children of Israel, partakers of the same promises as the rest of the sons of Jacob. Genesis 48:7 - Jacob told Joseph where his mother was buried: Rachel died by him in the land of Canaan in the way of Ephrath, which is Bethlehem, and he buried her there. Genesis 48:8-14 - The eyes of Israel were dim for age, so that he could not see, and he kissed and embraced Joseph's sons: I had not thought to see thy face, and lo, God hath shewed me also thy seed. - Joseph set Manasseh toward Israel's right hand and Ephraim toward his left, but Israel stretched out his right hand and laid it upon Ephraim the younger, guiding his hands wittingly, for Manasseh was the firstborn. Genesis 48:15-16 - Jacob blessed Joseph: God, before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac did walk, the God which fed me all my life long unto this day, the Angel which redeemed me from all evil, bless the lads; and let my name be named on them. - By that word Joseph's sons carried the name of Israel and grew into a multitude in the midst of the earth. Genesis 48:17-19 - It displeased Joseph, and he held up his father's hand to move it to Manasseh the firstborn; but Jacob refused: I know it, my son, I know it. Manasseh also shall become a people and shall be great, but truly his younger brother shall be greater than he, and his seed shall become a multitude of nations. - Ephraim was set above Manasseh because Ephraim became the head of the Northern Kingdom of Israel. Genesis 48:20-22 - In thee shall Israel bless, saying, God make thee as Ephraim and as Manasseh; and he set Ephraim before Manasseh. - Behold, I die: but God shall be with you, and bring you again unto the land of your fathers. Jacob prophesied the return of Joseph's seed to the land of Israel, and gave Joseph one portion above his brethren, which he took out of the hand of the Amorite with his sword and with his bow. Genesis 49: What Shall Befall the Twelve Tribes in the Last Days Read the chapter → Genesis 49 Genesis 49:1-2 - Gather yourselves together, that I may tell you that which shall befall you in the last days. These blessings are twofold: they speak to what would come upon each tribe in their day and in the last days, and they help determine who the tribes are and where they would be found today. Genesis 49:3-4 - Reuben is the so-called Seminole Indian today. Reuben, thou art my firstborn, the beginning of my strength: the firstborn is the father's posterity, and the excellency of dignity and the excellency of power belonged to him; the Seminoles were great warriors. - Unstable as water: the Seminoles were nomads, always moving around, as the scripture said. - Thou shalt not excel: Reuben would not excel as the firstborn, because he went up to his father's couch. His birthright was given unto the sons of Joseph because he defiled his father's bed, and the genealogy is not to be reckoned after the birthright. Precepts: - 1 Chronicles 5:1 Reuben's birthright was given unto the sons of Joseph because he defiled his father's bed. Genesis 49:5-7 - Simeon is the so-called Dominican and Levi the so-called Haitian today. Simeon and Levi are brethren: all the tribes of Israel are brethren, but these two in particular were to dwell together, and they share the same island, Hispaniola. - Instruments of cruelty are in their habitations: the witchcraft practiced on that island, such as the voodoo of Haiti. O my soul, come not thou into their secret: because of those practices the Most High does not unite them, and the two nations stay divided on the island even though Levi helped free Simeon from slavery. - For in their anger they slew a man: when their sister was defiled at Shechem, they told all the men of the city to be circumcised, and while the men were sore they slew every male of the city. Simeon and Levi did not play. - I will divide them in Jacob, and scatter them in Israel: Levi had no whole portion but cities scattered throughout all the tribes; and as Judah was scattered to the four corners of the earth, so was Levi, for Judah, Benjamin, and Levi make up the southern kingdom. Precepts: - Genesis 34:24-25 The men of Shechem were circumcised, and on the third day, when they were sore, Simeon and Levi slew all the males; that is the anger Jacob cursed. Genesis 49:8-12 - Judah is the so-called American Black man today. Judah, thou art he whom thy brethren shall praise: Judah was the first to bring out this truth that we are the nation of Israel, and the great majority of the teachers of this truth today are of the kingdom of Judah. - Thy hand shall be in the neck of thine enemies: Judah sits right in the neck of the enemy's kingdom, right up under Esau here in America, in his politics and his government, always in a key position. - Thy father's children shall bow down before thee: Judah is the top tribe in the awakening today, for the Lord saves the tents of Judah first. - Judah is a lion's whelp: from the prey, my son, thou art gone up. The movements that stood up against the enemy in this land, that was Judah rebelling; then he stooped down and couched as an old lion, content, and only the Most High shall rouse him up. - The sceptre shall not depart from Judah, nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh come: Shiloh means the peaceful one, Christ, who comes from the tribe of Judah, and unto him shall the gathering of the people be. - Binding his foal unto the vine is the prophecy of Christ riding into Jerusalem upon the colt; and he washed his garments in wine and his clothes in the blood of grapes runs ahead to Christ returning from Bozrah with dyed garments, treading the winepress, to destroy Israel's enemies. - His eyes shall be red with wine: Christ drank wine, so much that men called him a winebibber, but he was never drunken. Precepts: - Zechariah 12:7 The Lord shall save the tents of Judah first, that the glory of the house of David do not magnify itself against Judah. - Zechariah 9:9 Thy King cometh riding upon an ass, and upon a colt the foal of an ass; the foal bound unto the vine is that prophecy. - Isaiah 63:1-3 He that cometh from Bozrah with dyed garments has trodden the winepress alone; the garments washed in the blood of grapes look ahead to that day. - Matthew 11:19 The Son of man came eating and drinking, and they said, Behold a winebibber; yet he never was drunken. Genesis 49:13 - Zebulun is the so-called Mayan Indians today, from Guatemala down to Panama. Zebulun shall dwell at the haven of the sea, and he shall be for an haven of ships: the Panama Canal sits in his land, built to shorten the trip around the world, and the ships of the earth must come through and dock there. - His border shall be unto Zidon: as Zebulun dwelt by the sea in ancient Israel, so he dwells by the sea now; it was going to be the same, nothing different. Genesis 49:14-15 - Issachar is the so-called Aztec Indian, the Mexican of today. Issachar is a strong ass: a hard worker, given over to hard work and known over the earth for labor. - Couching down between two burdens: the two burdens are North America and Mexico, and the tribe sits pressed between them at the border, under the immigration laws, with even their children detained. - He saw that rest was good, and the land that it was pleasant: Mexico is a beautiful land. - He bowed his shoulder to bear, and became a servant unto tribute: hired out for cheap labor, and that labor is used to undercut and compete with Judah in the market. Genesis 49:16-18 - Dan shall judge his people, as one of the tribes of Israel. Dan shall be a serpent by the way, an adder in the path, that biteth the horse heels, so that his rider shall fall backward: Dan was like an ambush to the enemies, a powerful tribe that did not play. - The tribe of Dan was absorbed into the other tribes, and chiefly into Benjamin; that is part of why Benjamin had so many slave revolts, and successful ones. Genesis 49:19 - Gad is the so-called North American Indian, the Native American, today. Gad, a troop shall overcome him: the United States cavalry led by Andrew Jackson overcame Gad. - But he shall overcome at the last: in the last days the tribe of Gad rises back up, as you see it rising now. Genesis 49:20 - Asher is the so-called Incan Indians of South America, dwelling in the places from Colombia on down. Out of Asher his bread shall be fat, and he shall yield royal dainties: Asher is known for resources, an abundance of natural riches in his land. - The blessing of Moses says the same of Asher: let him dip his foot in oil. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 33:24 Let Asher be blessed with children and dip his foot in oil; the fatness of his bread is the abundance of his resources. Genesis 49:21 - Naphtali is the so-called Indians of Argentina and Chile today. Naphtali is a hind let loose: he giveth goodly words, and the capital of Argentina carries that mark, for Buenos Aires means good airs, goodly words. Genesis 49:22-26 - Joseph is a fruitful bough, even a fruitful bough by a well: Joseph, blessed in his sons Ephraim and Manasseh, is the so-called Puerto Ricans and Cubans today, a fruitful people. - Whose branches run over the wall: the Spaniards built a wall in Puerto Rico to keep themselves separate, but the daughters went over the wall and mixed themselves among the people; interracial marriage ran high, and that is why a great part of them favor Esau today. - The archers have sorely grieved him, and shot at him, and hated him: the Spanish conquistadors. But his bow abode in strength, and the arms of his hands were made strong by the hands of the mighty God of Jacob. - The blessings of thy father have prevailed above the blessings of my progenitors: they shall be on the head of Joseph, on the crown of the head of him that was separate from his brethren; these are the blessings Ephraim and Manasseh received in Genesis 48. Genesis 49:27 - Benjamin is the so-called Jamaican today. Benjamin shall ravin as a wolf: loud when he communicates, quick to anger, fierce; in the morning he shall devour the prey, and at night he shall divide the spoil. - With Dan absorbed into him, Benjamin was dangerous in captivity; his slave revolts were plenty, and they were successful. Genesis 49:28-33 - All these are the twelve tribes of Israel, and their father blessed them, every one according to his blessing. The blessings tell who the tribes are and where they would be found in the last days. - Jacob charged them to bury him with his fathers in the cave of the field of Machpelah, which Abraham bought of Ephron the Hittite for a possession of a buryingplace, where Abraham and Sarah, Isaac and Rebekah, and Leah lie buried. - When Jacob had made an end of commanding his sons, he gathered up his feet into the bed, and yielded up the ghost, and was gathered unto his people. Genesis 50: The Burial of Jacob and the Forgiveness of Joseph Read the chapter → Genesis 50 Genesis 50:1-3 - Joseph fell upon his father's face, and wept upon him, and kissed him, and commanded the physicians to embalm his father; forty days were fulfilled for the embalming, and the Egyptians mourned for Israel threescore and ten days. Genesis 50:4-6 - Joseph asked leave of Pharaoh according to the oath his father made him swear, to bury him in the grave he had digged in the land of Canaan; and Pharaoh said, Go up, and bury thy father, according as he made thee swear. Genesis 50:7-11 - All the servants of Pharaoh, the elders of his house, and all the elders of the land of Egypt went up with Joseph and his brethren and his father's house, with chariots and horsemen, a very great company. - The Canaanites saw the mourning in the floor of Atad and said, This is a grievous mourning to the Egyptians; wherefore the place was called Abelmizraim, which means the mourning of the Egyptians, beyond Jordan. - The Israelites and the Egyptians were compared as looking like one people, because the Egyptians are black and the Israelites are black. The Bible dictionary defines Ham as the progenitor of the dark races, and Egypt was of Ham; the people sitting in that land today are not the true ancient Egyptians of the scriptures. Genesis 50:12-14 - His sons did unto him according as he commanded them, and carried him into the land of Canaan, and buried him in the cave of the field of Machpelah before Mamre; and Joseph returned into Egypt, he and his brethren, and all that went up with him. Genesis 50:15-21 - When Joseph's brethren saw that their father was dead, they said, Joseph will peradventure hate us, and will certainly requite us all the evil which we did unto him; for they had sold him as a slave into Egypt. They sent a messenger pleading forgiveness and fell down before his face: Behold, we be thy servants. - Joseph wept and answered, Fear not: for am I in the place of God? But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive. And he comforted them and spake kindly unto them, and nourished them and their little ones. - Joseph had a real forgiving spirit. The lesson is to always be forgiving: sometimes people do evil against you, but the Most High means it unto good for you, so keep that spirit of forgiveness when people do certain things. Genesis 50:22-26 - Joseph dwelt in Egypt and lived an hundred and ten years, and saw the children of Ephraim of the third generation; the children of Machir the son of Manasseh were brought up upon Joseph's knees. - Joseph took an oath of the children of Israel: God will surely visit you, and ye shall carry up my bones from hence. So Joseph died, and they embalmed him, and he was put in a coffin in Egypt. - That is why no Egyptologist can show you the mummy of Joseph, the tomb of so famous a man: when Israel fled out of the land of Egypt they took the bones of Joseph with them, according to that oath. Precepts: - Exodus 13:19 Moses took the bones of Joseph with him, for Joseph had straitly sworn the children of Israel to carry his bones away with them. --- Topics: Esau and Edom ← Genesis 44-47 · Genesis Study · Exodus 1 →

title: Genesis 5: The Book of the Generations of Adam
text: ← Genesis 1-4 · Genesis Study · Genesis 9-12 → Genesis 5: The Book of the Generations of Adam Read the chapter → Genesis 5 Introduction This reading covers Genesis 5 through 8, read straight through, with the key points opened after the reading. The 365 reading is to give faith through hearing the word of the Most High. Romans 10:17 - The daily reading of the scriptures gives faith through hearing the word of the Most High. Genesis 5:1-2 - The words made he him speak of the first Adam. This Adam was made in the likeness of God, a direct descendant of the Most High. - Male and female created he them, and called their name Adam: they were not that Adam; these were the other people on the earth. When the Most High creates a fish He does not create only a salmon; there is mackerel and tuna and all types of fish. In the same way, He created Adam and He created the other people. - Chapter 5 is the direct lineage of Adam. That lineage is the sons of God you read of in chapter 6, and the later chapters of Genesis tie the Israelites directly to the lineage of Adam through Shem. - When Christ said, Ye are gods, He was saying we come from that line of Adam. Precepts: - Genesis 1:26-27 The man made in our image, created he him, is the first Adam; male and female created he them is the other people. - Luke 3:36-38 Christ's lineage on his mother's side runs back through Seth to Adam, the son of God. Genesis 5:24 - Enoch walked with God and was not: the Most High took him up, and Enoch did not taste death, the same way Elijah did not taste death. Precepts: - 2 Kings 2:9-11 Elijah was taken up by a whirlwind into heaven; that is what it means that God took Enoch. - Acts 1:9 Christ was taken up and received in a cloud; taken up means received by the Most High. Genesis 5:32 - Noah was five hundred years old here, and he was six hundred when the flood came (Genesis 7:6), so Noah preached for around a hundred years, give or take. Genesis 6: The Sons of God and the Preparing of the Ark Read the chapter → Genesis 6 Genesis 6:1-2 - The men who began to multiply on the face of the earth were of the other nations; they were not the direct descendants of Adam. The sons of God are the lineage of Adam laid out in chapter 5; that is the distinction between the sons of God and the daughters of men. - The law against marrying into the other nations began here in Genesis. It was already known, and Moses had to reiterate that same law to the children of Israel when they came over Jordan. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 7:3 Moses reiterated to the sons of God the law against taking wives of the other nations. Genesis 6:3 - Here the Most High shortened the lifespan of man to a hundred and twenty years. In chapter 5 the forefathers lived seven, eight, and nine hundred years. Genesis 6:4 - The giants in the earth came from the sons of God intermingling with the other nations, and the children born to them became mighty men of renown. - The angels which kept not their first estate are these same men of Genesis 6:4; they came from the lineage of Adam, and their first estate was sons of God. Another word for angel is messenger. Precepts: - Jude 1:6 The angels left their first estate as sons of God, and the Most High reserved them unto judgment. Genesis 6:8-9 - Noah found grace in the eyes of the Lord; he was a just man and perfect in his generations, and Noah walked with God. - Without Noah none of us would be here; Shem, Ham, and Japheth repopulated the earth after the flood. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 44:17-18 Noah was found perfect and righteous and was left as a remnant unto the earth when the flood came. Genesis 6:14 - The ark was a literal boat, made of gopher wood. Genesis 6:21 - At this time the animals were vegetarian; that is why the Most High explained to Noah to gather food for himself, for his family, and for the animals, and why the animals did not eat one another on the ark. Genesis 6:22 - Noah did all that the Most High commanded him by faith. Up to that time rain had never been seen; it takes faith to build an ark for a thing that has never happened. - While the ark was preparing, Noah was a preacher of righteousness, telling his people to repent, and the longsuffering of the Most High waited for them to repent. - Eight souls were saved by water; the ones that were actually in the water died, so this is not talking about getting baptized. - As Noah prepared the ark to the saving of his house, we must prepare our households for when Christ comes back; that takes the same faith. In the days of Noah they were eating, drinking, and marrying until Noah entered the ark and there was no more chance to repent; so shall the coming of the Son of man be. We have to put on the spirit of Noah. Precepts: - Hebrews 11:1 Faith is the evidence of things not seen; with Noah the thing not seen was rain. - Hebrews 11:6-7 By faith Noah, warned of God of things not seen as yet, moved with fear and prepared an ark to the saving of his house. - 1 Peter 3:20 The longsuffering of God waited in the days of Noah while the ark was preparing, and eight souls were saved by water. - 2 Peter 2:5 Noah was the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness. - Matthew 24:37-39 As the days of Noah were, so shall also the coming of the Son of man be. Genesis 7: The First Rain and the Flood Read the chapter → Genesis 7 Genesis 7:2-3 - The dietary law was not yet instituted, but the Most High had already defined what was a clean beast and what was an unclean beast, all the way back in Genesis; Moses reiterated that law to the children of Israel. - Today this gets confused with the doctrine that says I can eat all things through Christ who strengthens me, and that is not true; the laws were instituted for us to discern between the unclean and the clean. - The beasts went in male and female to keep seed alive upon the face of all the earth, so that they could repopulate once the earth dried up; nature itself tells you what we should and should not be doing. Precepts: - Leviticus 11:45-47 The law of the beasts makes a difference between the unclean and the clean, the beast that may be eaten and the beast that may not be eaten. - Ezekiel 44:23 The people are taught to discern between the unclean and the clean; that is what the laws were instituted for. Genesis 7:4 - Up until this point it had never rained on the earth; a mist went up from the earth and watered the ground. Understand the faith Noah had to have, being told to build an ark because it was going to rain, a thing that had never happened. Precepts: - Genesis 2:5-6 The Most High had not caused it to rain upon the earth; a mist watered the whole face of the ground. Genesis 7:11 - The great deep is the seas, the rivers, and the oceans. The windows of heaven are the sky, the firmament, and their opening is the rain. - This is the first time it ever rained on the earth, and when the rain came it came with destruction. Genesis 7:21-23 - This was the first time the Most High destroyed the earth for the wickedness that was being done. The flood came because they despised the commandments; destruction came because of sin. - Of them that dwelt in the world only Noah and his household were left, of whom came all righteous men: through Shem's seed to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and through their line the Israelites. - The breath of life is twofold. One is the commandments, which were given to Adam; the other is the breathing life, the oxygen. Here everything on the dry land that breathed died; the fish were not touched. Precepts: - 2 Esdras 3:8-11 The flood came upon them that despised the commandments, and Noah alone was left with his household, of whom came all righteous men. - 2 Esdras 3:5 The Most High breathed into Adam the breath of life; that breath is the commandments. - Proverbs 7:2 Keep my commandments, and live; the commandments are the breath of life. Genesis 8: The Earth Dried and the Covenant Read the chapter → Genesis 8 Genesis 8:2 - The windows of heaven being stopped and the rain from heaven being restrained shows you that the windows of heaven refer to the rain. Genesis 8:20-22 - Noah built an altar and offered burnt offerings of every clean beast and every clean fowl, and the Most High smelled a sweet savour and said He would not again curse the ground any more for man's sake. - An everlasting covenant was made with Noah that all flesh should perish no more by a flood. Before it was water; the next time it is going to be fire, so let us get our minds right. --- Topics: Clean and Unclean Meats · Sacrifice and Atonement · The Covenant ← Genesis 1-4 · Genesis Study · Genesis 9-12 →

title: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow
text: ← Genesis 5-8 · Genesis Study · Genesis 13-16 → Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow Read the chapter → Genesis 9 Introduction This reading covers Genesis 9 through 12, read with precepts as the chapters go. The laws you meet in these chapters stand from the beginning, long before Moses. Genesis 9:1 - Noah and his sons were told to replenish the earth after the flood, and the earth is replenished with righteous children; a multitude of ungodly children profits nothing. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 16:1-3 One just child is better than a thousand ungodly; replenish the earth with righteous seed. Genesis 9:2 - The fear and dread of man upon the beasts is not how it was in the beginning, and not how it will remain; the original relationship between man and the animals will be restored. Precepts: - Isaiah 11:6-9 The wolf dwells with the lamb and a little child leads them; the animals return to their original state when things are set back in order. Genesis 9:3 - This is the introduction of man eating meat. The Most High did not give man a new stomach; the body was already made for it and it lay dormant until after the flood. - Having the liberty to eat meat does not mean eating without balance; be not too greedy upon meats, for excess of meats brings sickness. - The law of what may be eaten was already understood; you could not eat everything. The doctrine that says you can pray over anything and eat it is a seducing spirit and a doctrine of devils. - Fish is meat; all flesh is not the same flesh, but the flesh of beasts, of fishes, and of birds are all flesh. Every creature of God is good for what it was made for, and it is sanctified by the word of God, and the word that sanctifies what may be eaten is the dietary law. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 37:27-31 Be not unsatiable in any dainty thing nor too greedy upon meats; excess of meats bringeth sickness. - Leviticus 11:46-47 The law of the beasts makes a difference between the beast that may be eaten and the beast that may not be eaten. - 1 Timothy 4:1-5 Commanding to abstain from meats is a doctrine of devils; the creature is sanctified by the word of God, which is the dietary law. - 1 Corinthians 15:38-39 All flesh is not the same flesh; there is flesh of beasts, of fishes, and of birds, so fish is meat. Genesis 9:4 - The law against eating flesh with the blood was given to Adam and is still in place with Noah; the word is true from the beginning. Precepts: - Psalms 119:160 The word is true from the beginning, and the righteous judgments, the laws, endure for ever. - 2 Esdras 3:4-8 Adam was given the breath of life, the commandments, and a commandment to love the way of the Most High; the peoples after him despised the commandments. Genesis 9:5 - The Most High requiring blood at the hand of every beast is animal sacrifice, still in place with Noah, passed down generation to generation. - The judgment for sin has always been death. When Eve sinned and caused Adam to sin, either they had to die, or something had to stand in their place; the blood of the animal stood in for them. - That is the scapegoat: it takes the wrongdoings, mistakes, and faults of others and places them on the animal. That is why Cain and Abel were bringing offerings, because they knew of the sacrifice from Genesis 3. Precepts: - Genesis 3:21 The coats of skins were the first sacrifice; the beast stood in place of Adam and Eve. - Genesis 4:3-5 Cain and Abel brought offerings, proving the sacrifice was known and passed down. - Leviticus 16:8-10 The scapegoat is presented alive to make an atonement, standing in for the faults of others. Genesis 9:6 - Whoso sheddeth man's blood, by man shall his blood be shed: life for life. This law is way before Moses, so it cannot be dismissed as the law of Moses. - The laws were never done away with; Christ came not to destroy the law but to fulfil, and not one jot or tittle passes from the law. Precepts: - Matthew 5:17-18 Christ came not to destroy the law or the prophets; not one jot or one tittle shall pass from the law. Genesis 9:9-11 - The covenant established here is with Noah, his seed, and every living creature: all flesh shall never again be cut off by the waters of a flood. - This is a general covenant with all flesh. The covenant with Israel is found in Jeremiah 31. Genesis 9:12-13 - The bow in the cloud, the rainbow, is the token of the covenant between the Most High and the earth; it compasses the heaven about with a glorious circle, and His hands bended it. - The world has taken that same bow, the token of the covenant, and turned it into the symbol of sodomy. The spiritual eyes will see what that means: the great city is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 43:11-12 Look upon the rainbow and praise Him that made it; the hands of the Most High bended it. - Revelation 11:8 The great city is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt; the place that flies the bow as a symbol of sodomy identifies itself. Genesis 9:14-15 - The waters shall no more become a flood to destroy all flesh. The next time the destruction is not water but fire, when the day of the Lord comes and the elements melt with fervent heat. Precepts: - 2 Peter 3:9-10 The Lord is longsuffering, not willing that any should perish; but the day of the Lord will come, and the elements shall melt with fervent heat. Genesis 9:18-19 - Shem, Ham, and Japheth went forth out of the ark and the whole earth was overspread from them. Ham dwelt in what is called Africa; Shem in the land mass toward Arabia; Japheth went into Europe. - Ham is the father of Canaan, and Canaan dwelt in the land later called the land of Israel. That is how you know the land of Israel is a part of Africa; the maps separate Israel from Africa so that the connection is not made. Genesis 9:20-23 - Noah was still perfect and righteous. A just man falleth seven times and riseth up again; one fall does not undo righteousness. - Understand Noah's heart: he preached repentance for around a hundred years, and everyone he knew outside his house drowned. Strong drink is for him that is ready to perish and wine for those of heavy hearts; Noah drank too much, but he remained righteous in the eyes of the Most High. - Ham saw the nakedness of his father and did not cover him; Shem and Japheth went backward and covered their father without looking. The commandments concerning nakedness were being applied; Leviticus 18 opens those laws. Precepts: - 2 Peter 2:5 Noah was the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness. - Ecclesiasticus 44:17-18 Noah was found perfect and righteous and was left as a remnant unto the earth. - Proverbs 24:16 A just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again. - Proverbs 31:6-7 Wine is for those of heavy hearts, to remember misery no more; that was Noah after the flood. Genesis 9:24-27 - Noah was asleep, so how did he know what his younger son had done? The Most High speaks to man in a dream, in a vision of the night, and reveals His secret unto His servants the prophets; Noah was a preacher of righteousness, and the Lord told him. - Cursed be Canaan: a servant of servants unto his brethren. - Blessed be the Lord God of Shem: it was revealed that the Messiah and the righteous seed would come through Shem. Precepts: - Job 33:14-16 God speaks in a dream, in a vision of the night, and seals the instruction of men. - Amos 3:7 The Lord God reveals His secret unto His servants the prophets. Genesis 10: Shem, Ham, Japheth, and Nimrod Read the chapter → Genesis 10 Genesis 10:1-5 - The sons of Japheth settled what became Europe. Ashkenaz is a Hebrew name for Germany; Tarshish is Spain; Kittim is Rome; Javan is Greece; you can see Meshech, Tubal, and Magog on the old maps. - These were the isles of the Gentiles, divided in their lands, every one after his tongue. Genesis 10:6-7 - The sons of Ham: Cush is Ethiopia; Mizraim is Egypt; Phut is Libya, to the left of Egypt; and Canaan is the land where Jerusalem sits. - Ham inhabited what is known as Africa, and Canaan's land is the land of Israel; so the land of Israel is part of Africa. - The Israelites are of Shem, not of Ham; the children of Israel are Shemites scattered among the children of Ham in Africa. Genesis 10:8-11 - Cush begat Nimrod, the mighty hunter, and the beginning of his kingdom was Babel, Erech, Accad, and Calneh in the land of Shinar; Shinar is what is known as Iraq. Out of that land Asshur, the Assyrians, built Nineveh. - History records that Nimrod was the first king of Nineveh; the name Nineveh means the habitation of Ninus, which was Nimrod. He was the first mortal deified at his death, the father of the gods, and that pagan practice of deifying kings spread from Mesopotamia to Egypt and beyond. - Nimrod, his queen Semiramis, and her child Tammuz became the first pagan trinity, and their worship spread under different names through every nation: Baal, Bel, Zeus, Jupiter, Ra, Thor; Ishtar, Ashtaroth, Isis, Diana. - Sunday sacredness, Christmas, the Christmas tree, Easter, the Easter egg, and Good Friday have their origin in that Babylonian sun worship, not in the Old and New Testaments. This is why the scriptures must be studied precept upon precept, so ancient paganism mixed in is not mistaken for the truth. - The origins of these places, Babel, Erech, Accad, Shinar, still sit on the eastern side of the world, which is why the history reads like a fairy tale to a people carried to the western side with none of it to see. Genesis 10:15-19 - The border of the Canaanites reached unto Sodom and Gomorrah, and Admah and Zeboim; when Sodom and Gomorrah were destroyed, those cities went into destruction with them. Deuteronomy names the cities together. Genesis 10:21 - Shem is the father of all the children of Eber, and Eber is where the name Hebrew comes from. Genesis 11: Babel and the Separation of the Nations Read the chapter → Genesis 11 Genesis 11:1-4 - The whole earth was of one language, and they journeyed from the east to the plain of Shinar. Coming from Jerusalem eastward lands you in Shinar, in Babylon. - They built the tower so they would not be scattered abroad; the fear of the flood was still on them, and they wanted to make themselves a name. Genesis 11:5-9 - The people being one was not going to produce righteousness; nothing would be restrained from what they imagined to do, and it would be evil, so the Most High confounded their language and scattered them. - There has never been a doctrine of all nations holding hands as one in the scriptures.
