The Most High divided the nations their inheritance and separated the sons of Adam, setting the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Israel. - The man of sin opposes this: he exalts himself above all that is called God, gathers all nations to himself as one, and deifies himself, making God and the Messiah after his own image. That is the same thing Nimrod did in the land of Shinar. - After Babel the Most High sent every family back to where it was supposed to be: Ham to his place, Shem to his, Japheth to his. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 32:7-9 The Most High divided the nations and separated the sons of Adam by the number of the children of Israel; Jacob is His portion. - 2 Thessalonians 2:3-4 The man of sin exalts himself above all that is called God, sitting as God; the spirit of Nimrod all over again. Genesis 11:10-13 - Watch the lifespans in the generations of Shem: five hundred years, then four hundred, then two hundred, then down past one hundred and nineteen with Nahor. The word of Genesis 6:3 is taking hold on man's days. - Each of these generations begat sons and daughters for hundreds of years; the earth is being populated again all through this chapter. Genesis 11:27-32 - Haran begat Lot and died before his father Terah in Ur of the Chaldees. Ur means fire in the etymology, and the Chaldees is Babylon; Abram was born and called out of that area. - Lot was a just man. To be just means to do that which is lawful and right, a commandment keeper; righteous Lot was vexed from day to day with the unlawful deeds of the wicked. Precepts: - Ezekiel 18:5 A just man is one that does that which is lawful and right. - 2 Peter 2:7-9 Just Lot was a righteous man, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked. Genesis 12: The Calling of Abram Read the chapter → Genesis 12 Genesis 12:1 - The Most High called Abram to get out of his country, from his kindred, and from his father's house. He called Abraham alone, and blessed him, and increased him. - Some hold back from repenting because of what family or friends may say. Do not let your kindred hold you back from being blessed and increased; when the Most High calls you out, you have to go. - Confessing Christ before men means something. When Christ asked, Whom say ye that I am, Peter confessed, Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God; whoever confesses Him before men, He confesses before His Father, and He came to set a man at variance against his own household for the truth's sake. Precepts: - Isaiah 51:2 The Most High called Abraham alone, and blessed him, and increased him. - Matthew 10:32-37 Confess Christ before men though it set you at variance with your own household; he that loveth father or mother more than Him is not worthy of Him. - Matthew 16:13-16 Peter confessed, Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God; that confession means something. Genesis 12:2-3 - In thee shall all families of the earth be blessed is not talking about everybody. The children of the prophets and of the covenant are Israel, and Israel would be scattered into all nations of the earth; through Abraham's seed the kindreds of the earth are blessed because scattered Israel gets the chance to repent and return, circumcised or not. Precepts: - Acts 3:25-26 Ye are the children of the prophets and of the covenant made with Abraham; unto you first God sent His Son to bless you in turning you from your iniquities. - Amos 2:11 The Most High raised up prophets from the sons of Israel; the children of the prophets are the children of Israel. Genesis 12:4-5 - Abram departed at seventy and five years old, with Sarai and Lot, into the land of Canaan; Canaan is northeast Africa. Genesis 12:10-13 - Sarai was around the same age as Abram, about ten years apart, and she was still a very fair woman to look upon in her sixties. Genesis 12:17-20 - The Lord plagued Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai, and Pharaoh sent Abram away with his wife and all that he had. The Most High protected the household of Abram in Egypt. --- Topics: Clean and Unclean Meats · Idolatry · Sacrifice and Atonement · The Covenant · The Priesthood ← Genesis 5-8 · Genesis Study · Genesis 13-16 →

title: Exodus 1: A New King Over Egypt Which Knew Not Joseph
text: ← Genesis 48-50 · Exodus Study · Exodus 2-5 → Exodus 1: A New King Over Egypt Which Knew Not Joseph Read the chapter → Exodus 1 Introduction This chapter comes from the same reading session as Genesis 48 through 50, marked (READ). The reading covered the children of Israel multiplying after Joseph, the new kingdom that arose and oppressed them, the godliness of the midwives in saving the men children alive, and Pharaoh's charge to cast the sons into the river. Exodus 1:1-7 - All the souls that came out of the loins of Jacob were seventy souls, for Joseph was in Egypt already; and Joseph died, and all his brethren, and all that generation. - The children of Israel were fruitful, and increased abundantly, and multiplied, and waxed exceeding mighty, and the land was filled with them. Israel had those babies; the nation did not cast away its children, and the increase was the blessing. Exodus 1:8-14 - Now there arose up a new king over Egypt, which knew not Joseph: this is not merely one king but a new kingdom arising, the eighteenth dynasty. - Come on, let us deal wisely with them, lest they multiply and join our enemies: the same wise dealing works on Israel in America today, through movements set up to redirect the people, through Planned Parenthood, and through the prison industrial complex; but the enemy did not count on Christ returning, restoring the nation, and bringing us back to the commandments of God. - They set over them taskmasters to afflict them with their burdens, and they built for Pharaoh treasure cities, Pithom and Raamses; but the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and grew. - The Egyptians made the children of Israel to serve with rigour, and made their lives bitter with hard bondage, in morter and in brick and in all manner of service in the field. Exodus 1:15-21 - The king of Egypt commanded the Hebrew midwives, Shiphrah and Puah, to kill every son born upon the stools and save the daughters alive; but the midwives feared God, and did not as the king of Egypt commanded them, but saved the men children alive. - The midwives answered Pharaoh that the Hebrew women are not as the Egyptian women, for they are lively, and are delivered ere the midwives come in unto them; the daughters of Israel are not as the women of the nations. - Because the midwives feared God, God dealt well with them and made them houses; the Most High blessed the women who saved the children of Israel alive, and the people multiplied and waxed very mighty. Exodus 1:22 - Pharaoh then charged all his people, saying, Every son that is born ye shall cast into the river, and every daughter ye shall save alive. --- ← Genesis 48-50 · Exodus Study · Exodus 2-5 →

title: Exodus 10: The Most High Hardens Pharaoh to Shew His Signs
text: ← Exodus 6-9 · Exodus Study · Exodus 14-17 → Exodus 10: The Most High Hardens Pharaoh to Shew His Signs Read the chapter → Exodus 10 Introduction This reading covers Exodus 10 through 13: the plagues of locusts and darkness, the death of the firstborn announced and executed, the institution of the Lord's Passover and the feast of unleavened bread, Israel thrust out of Egypt after 430 years, the sanctifying of the firstborn, and the pillar of cloud and fire leading the people. The session opens with a precursor from Proverbs 21 and Romans 9: the things that were written aforetime were written for our learning, and the Most High is in absolute control of the kings of the earth. Exodus 10:1 - The Most High hardened the heart of Pharaoh and of his servants so that he might show his signs and exemplify his power in the earth. After he brought down Egypt and delivered the people, every nation feared Israel and the God of Israel. - The king's heart is in the hand of the Lord; he turns it whithersoever he will. He is in control of the mind of the kings of the world, so there is no need to worry over who becomes president or who gets put in office; either way the Most High is in control. - The scripture said to Pharaoh, Even for this same purpose have I raised thee up, that I might show my power in thee, and that my name might be declared throughout all the earth. He has mercy on whom he will have mercy, and whom he will he hardeneth. - The potter has power over the clay, of the same lump to make one vessel unto honour and another unto dishonour. Some nations are honourable, which are the Israelites, and some are dishonourable; Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated. The vessels of wrath were fitted to destruction, endured with much longsuffering so the Most High could show how powerful he is; that is why Esau had to be set on such a high level, so that when he brings these people down all will know God is truly all powerful. - The same holds in spiritual Egypt today: the Most High will harden the hearts of the rulers of this kingdom so they will not let Israel go and will continue to oppress, because in the affliction the people will seek him early. It does not matter who is voted into office; whoever sits in the seat, the Most High turns him about like the rivers of water. - The things that were written aforetime were written for our learning, and the thing that hath been is that which shall be. That is why so many similarities appear between the captivities: this captivity carries the marks of Egypt, of Babylon, and of the Greeks, because these things must come to pass. Precepts: - Proverbs 21:1 The king's heart is in the hand of the Lord; he turns rulers whithersoever he will, no matter who is voted in. - Romans 9:15-18 He has mercy on whom he will have mercy; Pharaoh was raised up for this same purpose, that the Most High might show his power in him. - Romans 9:19-22 The potter has power over the clay to make one vessel unto honour and another unto dishonour; the vessels of wrath were fitted to destruction. - Romans 9:13 Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated; Jacob is the honourable vessel and Esau the dishonourable. - Romans 15:4 The things written aforetime were written for our learning; the history of Egypt teaches this captivity. - Ecclesiastes 1:9 The thing that hath been is that which shall be; the captivities repeat their patterns. - Hosea 5:15 In their affliction they will seek me early; the oppression is used to wake the people up. Exodus 10:2 - The fathers are to tell in the ears of their sons and their sons' sons what things the Most High wrought in Egypt. That is what Israel does every year at the Passover, giving honour to the things he did in Egypt and the way he delivered the people out of the hand of the oppressors. - The same deliverance will be told again: it shall no more be said, The Lord liveth that brought up the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt, but, The Lord liveth that brought them up from the land of the north, out of Babylon the Great where the people sit today. Precepts: - Jeremiah 16:14-15 No more Blessed be the Lord that brought Israel out of Egypt, but out of the land of the north; the greater exodus is still ahead. Exodus 10:3-6 - Moses went in to Pharaoh with a staff and an ultimatum: how long wilt thou refuse to humble thyself? Let my people go, or tomorrow, in twenty four hours, the locusts come into thy coast. - The locusts would cover the face of the earth so no one could see the ground, eat the residue that escaped the hail, and fill the houses of Pharaoh, of his servants, and of all the Egyptians, such as neither their fathers nor their fathers' fathers had seen. Exodus 10:7-11 - Pharaoh's own servants pleaded with him: how long shall this man be a snare unto us? Knowest thou not yet that Egypt is destroyed? - Moses answered that all would go, young and old, sons and daughters, flocks and herds, for we must hold a feast unto the Lord. The Most High loves to see Israel gathered together in unity; that is why so many feast days bring the nation together to honour him. - Pharaoh offered to let only the men go, and Moses and Aaron were driven out from his presence. Precepts: - Psalm 133:1 Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity; the feasts gather the nation. Exodus 10:12-15 - The hail with fire wrapped in it had already destroyed much; now the locusts came on an east wind to clear out the remaining crops, even all that the hail had left. - The locusts covered the face of the whole earth so that the land was darkened; there were so many that they blocked out the sun. They ate every herb and all the fruit of the trees, and there remained not any green thing in all the land of Egypt. Exodus 10:16-17 - When the judgment got real, Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron in haste and confessed, I have sinned against the Lord your God and against you. Everything had been eaten by the locusts, and now he begged that this death only be taken from him. Exodus 10:18-20 - Moses entreated the Lord, and a mighty strong west wind took away the locusts and cast them into the Red Sea; there remained not one locust in all the coasts of Egypt. - But the Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, so that he would not let the children of Israel go. The Most High is in ultimate control even of the devil; he is the omnipotent master of all existence, and nothing can be done outside his will. Exodus 10:21-23 - Moses stretched forth his hand toward heaven, and there was thick darkness in all the land of Egypt three days, even darkness which may be felt. They saw not one another, neither rose any from his place. - But all the children of Israel had light in their dwellings; the Most High put a difference between his people and the Egyptians. Exodus 10:24-26 - After three days of darkness Pharaoh called for Moses: go, serve the Lord, only let your flocks and your herds be stayed. Go, but leave all your possessions in Egypt. - Moses refused: our cattle also shall go with us, there shall not an hoof be left behind. Not a hoof, a hair, or a heifer would stay in Egypt, for thereof must Israel take to serve the Lord, and we know not with what we must serve the Lord until we come thither. Exodus 10:27-29 - The Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart yet again, and Pharaoh threatened Moses: see my face no more, for in that day thou seest my face thou shalt die. After the rivers turned to blood, the hail with flaming fire, the locusts, and the darkness, Pharaoh still thought he was in a position to give out threats. That is the deceivableness of the strong delusion: God sends it so that they should believe a lie. - The same delusion falls on Israel when the people go reprobate in their sins: believing the Sabbath begins when the sun comes up, that anything can be eaten on Passover, or that the leaven to be put away is only the heart. Sin blinds. - Moses answered, Thou hast spoken well, I will see thy face again no more. Precepts: - 2 Thessalonians 2:11 God shall send them strong delusion, that they should believe a lie; Pharaoh was deceived into thinking he could threaten the servant of God. Exodus 11: The Death of the Firstborn Announced Read the chapter → Exodus 11 Exodus 11:1 - The Most High already knew what was going down: yet will I bring one plague more upon Pharaoh and upon Egypt. This last plague would end it, and when Pharaoh let the people go he would thrust them out hence altogether, with the quickness. Exodus 11:2-3 - Every man and woman was to borrow of their neighbours jewels of silver and jewels of gold, and the Lord gave the people favour in the sight of the Egyptians. - Moses was very great in the land of Egypt, in the sight of Pharaoh's servants and in the sight of the people; he had a good report. Israel in spiritual Egypt must deal the same way: have the respect of the people, and if people despise you, let it be because they hate God and the word you teach, not because you are in wickedness, shady dealings, deceit, or disrespect. Exodus 11:4-6 - About midnight the Lord would go out into the midst of Egypt, and all the firstborn in the land would die, from the firstborn of Pharaoh on his throne to the firstborn of the maidservant behind the mill, and all the firstborn of beasts. - There would be a great cry throughout all the land of Egypt, such as there was none like it, nor shall be like it any more. Exodus 11:7 - Against the children of Israel not a dog would move his tongue, that ye may know how that the Lord doth put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel. - A difference had to be shown because Israel and the Egyptians looked alike. Moses was mistaken for an Egyptian, Paul was mistaken for an Egyptian, Joseph was mistaken for an Egyptian by his own brothers, and at Jacob's funeral the mourners were called Egyptians because no one could tell the difference. - The difference was made plain in the plague itself: the houses whose firstborn died were shown not to be his people. Precepts: - Exodus 2:19 The daughters of Reuel said an Egyptian delivered us; Moses was taken for an Egyptian. - Acts 21:38 The chief captain took Paul for that Egyptian; Israel resembled the Egyptians in appearance. - Genesis 50:11 The Canaanites saw the mourning and called it a grievous mourning to the Egyptians; Jacob's family blended in with the Egyptians among them. Exodus 11:8-10 - All Pharaoh's servants would come down and bow to Moses, saying, Get thee out, and all the people that follow thee; and Moses went out from Pharaoh in a great anger. - Pharaoh would not hearken, that the wonders of the Most High might be multiplied in the land of Egypt. He is in control of the leaders of every country, presidents, governors, senators, congressmen, and mayors alike; whoever gets in the seat, he twists and turns them about like the river. Exodus 12: The Lord's Passover Read the chapter → Exodus 12 Exodus 12:1-2 - This month shall be unto you the beginning of months, the first month of the year. The month is Abib, the month in which Israel came out of Egypt. - Abib in the Bible dictionary is the pre-exilic name for the first month of the year; after the exile the name was changed to Nisan, and it falls between March and April. So the new year begins in the springtime, around March and April, not on January the first in the dead of winter; that is another lie taught in Babylon. Precepts: - Exodus 13:4 This day came ye out in the month Abib; the exodus month is the first month of the year. Exodus 12:3-5 - In the tenth day of the month every man was to take a lamb according to the house of his fathers; if the household was too little for the lamb, he and his neighbour next unto his house were to take it according to the number of the souls. - The lamb was to be without blemish, a male of the first year, taken from the sheep or from the goats. This is a foreshadowing: the feast days and sacrifices are a shadow of things to come, but the body is of Christ. - The lamb without blemish and without spot points to Christ, who was sinless, verily foreordained before the foundation of the world but manifest in these last times for the nation of Israel. Precepts: - Colossians 2:16-17 The meat, drink, holydays, and sabbaths are a shadow of things to come, but the body is of Christ; the Passover lamb was a precursor of him. - 1 Peter 1:19-20 The precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot, foreordained before the foundation of the world. Exodus 12:6-8 - The whole assembly of the congregation of Israel was to kill the lamb in the evening, and take of the blood and strike it on the two side posts and on the upper door post of the houses. - The flesh was to be eaten that night, roast with fire, with unleavened bread and with bitter herbs. That is the Passover menu in layman's terms: lamb roast with fire, unleavened bread, bitter herbs; no fried chicken, no birthday cake, no mashed potatoes and gravy, none of the thirteen herbs and spices. Exodus 12:9-11 - Eat not of it raw, nor sodden at all with water: do not boil it, but roast it with fire, the head with the legs and the purtenance thereof, and let nothing of it remain until the morning; what remains is burned with fire. - It was to be eaten with loins girded, shoes on the feet, and staff in hand, in haste: it is the Lord's passover, and that very night Israel was leaving Egypt. Exodus 12:12-13 - The Lord would pass through the land that night and smite all the firstborn of man and beast, and against all the gods of Egypt he would execute judgment. Each plague put an Egyptian god to shame: when he smote the land with darkness he showed that the sun god Ra is no god at all, for the God of heaven and earth blotted out the sun three days. Israel had to learn that those gods are nothing, because the nation was about to come out and serve the one true God. - The blood was a token upon the houses: when I see the blood, I will pass over you. That is where the term Passover comes from; the houses with the blood on the doorposts were passed over from death while the firstborn of Egypt were slain. Exodus 12:14 - This day is a memorial, a feast to the Lord throughout your generations, kept by an ordinance for ever. It was not done away; even in the New Testament the Passover is still kept: Christ our passover is sacrificed for us, therefore let us keep the feast. The lamb of the Passover represents Christ, and the apostle's instruction is to keep the feast, not to spiritualize it away. Precepts: - 1 Corinthians 5:7-8 Christ our passover is sacrificed for us; therefore let us keep the feast, with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth. Exodus 12:15-17 - Seven days shall ye eat unleavened bread; even the first day the leaven is put out of the houses, and whosoever eats leavened bread from the first day until the seventh, that soul shall be cut off from Israel. - The first day and the seventh day are holy convocations; no manner of work is done in them save that which every man must eat, meaning the food may be cooked. - The feast of unleavened bread is observed because in this selfsame day the Most High brought the armies of Israel out of Egypt. He deals with armies, and when he brings Israel out of this place he is bringing out an army again: when the spirit of life enters them and they stand upon their feet, great fear falls on them which see them, for they stand up an exceeding great army, not choir boys. Precepts: - Revelation 11:11 The spirit of life from God entered into them and they stood upon their feet, and great fear fell upon them which saw them. - Ezekiel 37:10 The breath came into them, and they lived, and stood up upon their feet, an exceeding great army; that is why they fear. Exodus 12:18-20 - In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month at even, ye shall eat unleavened bread, until the one and twentieth day of the month at even. The Passover begins and ends at even because the day begins and ends at even; it is not difficult. - Sin puts blinders on: when you hate your brother you are in darkness and cannot see what the scripture plainly says. Many fell away from the truth over this very point of the day beginning at evening. - For seven days no leaven is found in the houses; whoever eats that which is leavened, whether stranger or born in the land, is cut off from the congregation of Israel. Precepts: - 1 John 2:11 He that hateth his brother is in darkness and knoweth not whither he goeth, because darkness hath blinded his eyes. Exodus 12:21-23 - The elders were to draw out a lamb for their families and kill the passover, take a bunch of hyssop, dip it in the blood in the bason, and strike the lintel and the two side posts; the hyssop bush was used like a paintbrush to paint the blood of the lamb over the doorposts. - None of you shall go out at the door of his house until the morning: stay inside, for the Lord passes through to smite the Egyptians, and where he sees the blood he will pass over the door and will not suffer the destroyer to come in to smite you. - The destroyer was Christ, the almighty word of God. In the quiet silence of that night the almighty word leaped down from heaven out of the royal throne as a fierce man of war into the midst of the land of destruction, and standing up filled all things with death. The Egyptians cried for the children that were bewailed; master and servant, king and common person suffered after one manner, and the dead were too many to bury. Upon the destruction of the firstborn they acknowledged this people to be the sons of God. Precepts: - Wisdom of Solomon 18:10-16 The almighty word leaped down from heaven as a fierce man of war; the destroyer in Egypt was the word of God. - John 1:1 The Word was with God, and the Word was God; Christ is the almighty word that slew the firstborn in Egypt. Exodus 12:24-28 - This thing is an ordinance to thee and to thy sons for ever, kept even when Israel comes into the land the Lord promised. When the children ask, What mean ye by this service? the answer is, It is the sacrifice of the Lord's passover, who passed over the houses of the children of Israel in Egypt when he smote the Egyptians and delivered our houses. - The feast days commemorate the Most High delivering his people and bringing judgment on their enemies; that is the same pattern the feast of dedication commemorates. The people bowed the head and worshipped, and the children of Israel went and did as the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron. Exodus 12:29 - At midnight the Lord smote all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh that sat on his throne unto the firstborn of the captive in the dungeon, and all the firstborn of cattle. Even the prisoners' firstborn died, and Pharaoh's own son died. - In this Christ showed that Osiris and Isis, the supposed Egyptian gods of life and death, control neither life nor death. Unto God the Lord belong the issues from death; the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob is the God of salvation, and he alone brings forth death. Precepts: - Psalm 68:20 He that is our God is the God of salvation; and unto God the Lord belong the issues from death, not to the idols of Egypt. Exodus 12:30-33 - Pharaoh rose up in the night, he and all his servants and all the Egyptians, and there was a great cry in Egypt, for there was not a house where there was not one dead. - The last time Pharaoh saw Moses he threatened to kill him if he ever saw his face again; now he called for Moses and Aaron by night, saying, Rise up, get you forth from among my people, go, serve the Lord as ye have said, take your flocks and your herds, and bless me also. Touch not mine anointed, and do my prophets no harm; the man who thought he could threaten the servant of the Most High had a complete change of tone. - The Egyptians were urgent upon the people to send them out of the land in haste, for they said, We be all dead men. Precepts: - Psalm 105:15 Touch not mine anointed, and do my prophets no harm; Pharaoh's threat against Moses could not stand. Exodus 12:34-36 - The people took their dough before it was leavened, their kneadingtroughs bound up in their clothes upon their shoulders. - As Moses had said, they borrowed of the Egyptians jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and raiment; the Lord gave the people favour in the sight of the Egyptians, so that they lent them what they required, and they spoiled the Egyptians. They took everything. Exodus 12:37 - The children of Israel journeyed from Rameses to Succoth, about six hundred thousand on foot that were men, beside children. Israel departed from Rameses in the first month; the exodus is tied to Rameses by name. Precepts: - Numbers 33:3 They departed from Rameses in the first month, on the fifteenth day of the first month, on the morrow after the passover. Exodus 12:38 - A mixed multitude went up also with them, and flocks and herds, even very much cattle. The mixed multitude that left with Israel were not to be among the children of Israel as rulers. - The law sets the order: bondmen and bondmaids are to be of the heathen round about and of the strangers that sojourn among you; they are a possession and an inheritance for the children. But over the brethren, the children of Israel, ye shall not rule one over another with rigour. Precepts: - Leviticus 25:44-46 The bondmen are of the heathen and the strangers, a possession for ever; but over your brethren the children of Israel ye shall not rule with rigour. Exodus 12:39-42 - They baked unleavened cakes of the dough brought out of Egypt, for it was not leavened, because they were thrust out of Egypt and could not tarry, neither had they prepared any victual. - The sojourning of the children of Israel who dwelt in Egypt was four hundred and thirty years, and at the end of the four hundred and thirty years, even the selfsame day, all the hosts of the Lord went out from the land of Egypt. - It is a night to be much observed unto the Lord for bringing them out from the land of Egypt: this is the Passover night, which all the children of Israel are to observe in their generations. Exodus 12:43-51 - This is the ordinance of the passover: no stranger eats of it. A bought servant may eat when he is circumcised; a foreigner and an hired servant shall not eat thereof. When a stranger will keep the passover of the Lord, let all his males be circumcised, and he shall be as one born in the land; one law is to the homeborn and to the stranger. - It is eaten in one house, none of the flesh carried outside, neither shall ye break a bone thereof. That also goes to Christ, the Passover lamb, whose bones were not broken on the cross. - Thus did all the children of Israel as the Lord commanded Moses and Aaron, and the selfsame day the Lord brought them out of the land of Egypt by their armies. Precepts: - John 19:36 These things were done that the scripture should be fulfilled, A bone of him shall not be broken; Christ is the Passover lamb. Exodus 13: By Strength of Hand the Lord Brought Us Out Read the chapter → Exodus 13 Exodus 13:1-2 - Sanctify unto me all the firstborn, whatsoever openeth the womb among the children of Israel, both of man and of beast: it is mine. The firstborn belong to the Most High. Exodus 13:3-4 - Remember this day, in which ye came out from Egypt, out of the house of bondage; for by strength of hand the Lord brought you out from this place, and no leavened bread is eaten. - This day came ye out in the month Abib: the first month of the year, falling at the first new moon of the spring. Exodus 13:5-10 - When the Lord brings Israel into the land of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, a land flowing with milk and honey, this service is kept in this month: seven days of unleavened bread, and in the seventh day a feast to the Lord, with no leaven seen in all thy quarters. - Thou shalt shew thy son in that day, saying, This is done because of that which the Lord did unto me when I came forth out of Egypt. It is a sign upon thine hand and a memorial between thine eyes, that the Lord's law may be in thy mouth. - Thou shalt therefore keep this ordinance in his season from year to year: the Passover is kept every year. Exodus 13:11-13 - All that openeth the matrix is set apart unto the Lord; the matrix is the womb. Every firstling that cometh of a beast which thou hast, the males are the Lord's. - Every firstling of an ass is redeemed with a lamb, and if not redeemed its neck is broken; and all the firstborn of man among thy children shalt thou redeem. Exodus 13:14-16 - When thy son asketh thee in time to come, saying, What is this? thou shalt say, By strength of hand the Lord brought us out from Egypt, from the house of bondage: when Pharaoh would hardly let us go, the Lord slew all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, therefore the firstborn are sacrificed or redeemed. - The children must be taught the righteousness of why the feast is kept. Ask the children of this land why they keep Christmas and they answer that Santa Claus is coming down the chimney; Israel's children are to be taught the works of the Most High instead. - It is for a token upon thine hand and for frontlets between thine eyes, for by strength of hand the Lord brought us forth out of Egypt. Exodus 13:17-18 - When Pharaoh let the people go, God led them not through the way of the land of the Philistines, although that was near, lest peradventure the people repent when they see war and return to Egypt. Israel would have been fearful at the sight of the Philistine army and turned back. - The people felt a false security in Egypt: in the wilderness they murmured for the fish, the leeks, the onions, and the garlick of Egypt and loathed the light bread; and when the Assyrians came, Israel again ran down to Egypt for help. The same spirit holds the people in America today: a little job, government assistance, a car, food from the store, and they never want this kingdom to come down. But the Most High has something much greater in store: the world, the earth, and many mansions. - So God led the people about, through the way of the wilderness of the Red Sea, and the children of Israel went up harnessed out of the land of Egypt. Precepts: - Numbers 11:5 We remember the fish, the cucumbers, the melons, the leeks, the onions, and the garlick; the people longed for Egypt in the wilderness. - Numbers 21:5 Our soul loatheth this light bread; the murmuring shows the false comfort Israel took in Egypt. - Isaiah 30:1-2 Woe to the rebellious children that walk to go down into Egypt to strengthen themselves in the strength of Pharaoh; Israel kept running back to Egypt for safety. - John 14:2 In my Father's house are many mansions; the Most High has something far greater in store than the false security of this captivity. Exodus 13:19 - Moses took the bones of Joseph with him, for Joseph had straitly sworn the children of Israel, saying, God will surely visit you, and ye shall carry up my bones away hence with you. Exodus 13:20-22 - They took their journey from Succoth and encamped in Etham, in the edge of the wilderness. - The Lord went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud to lead them the way, and by night in a pillar of fire to give them light, to go by day and night. He took not away the pillar of the cloud by day, nor the pillar of fire by night, from before the people. --- Topics: Esau and Edom · Idolatry · Sacrifice and Atonement · The Feasts of the Most High · The Priesthood · The Sabbath ← Exodus 6-9 · Exodus Study · Exodus 14-17 →

title: Exodus 14: The Salvation of the Lord at the Red Sea
text: ← Exodus 10-13 · Exodus Study · Exodus 18-21 → Exodus 14: The Salvation of the Lord at the Red Sea Read the chapter → Exodus 14 Introduction This reading covers Exodus 14 through 17: the Red Sea opened and the Egyptians overthrown, the song of Moses, the manna and the sabbath proved in the wilderness, and the first war with Amalek. The session was a straight reading with brief commentary and questions afterward; the answers are folded in under the verses they belong to. Exodus 14:1-5 - The Most High is not done with the Egyptians. He destroyed their firstborn and brought Israel out, but He kept one more judgment in store for that wicked nation, and He will do the same to the wicked nation that has done the same things to Israel today. - The heart of Pharaoh and of his servants turned as soon as the people were gone: why have we done this, that we have let Israel go from serving us? The oppressor does not release his slaves gladly. Exodus 14:10-12 - At the first sight of the Egyptians marching, Israel lost all faith. The Lord had done miracle after miracle before their eyes and brought them out with an high hand, yet at the first sign of danger they said He brought them out to die. Our people have always been a rebellious people of little faith: a very froward generation, children in whom is no faith. - Let us alone, that we may serve the Egyptians: that is the same word our people speak today. Why are you stirring up trouble, why tell us to come out of the ways of Babylon; let us alone to serve the slave master, because serving him feels easier than having faith in the Most High. - The same spirit was in Israel in the days of Christ: if we let him thus alone, all men will believe on him, and the Romans shall come. The fear of the oppressor outweighed belief in the miracles. - In captivity the people wax old in mind and will not depart: woe to the bloody city, the prey departed not. Israel was the prey in Egypt and did not want to leave, the same as now. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 32:20 A very froward generation, children in whom is no faith; that is the record over Israel. - John 11:47-48 If we let him thus alone the Romans shall come; the same spirit feared the oppressor more than the Most High. - Nahum 3:1 The prey departed not; in captivity the people wax old in mind and will not leave. Exodus 14:13-14 - Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of the Lord. The Egyptians whom ye have seen today, ye shall see them again no more for ever; that sounds like the same word that will stand over Babylon. - The Lord shall fight for you, and ye shall hold your peace. The battle was never Israel's to win by strength. Exodus 14:19-22 - The angel of God that went before the camp, the angel in the chariot whom we know to be Christ, removed and went behind them, standing between the camp of Egypt and the camp of Israel. - The pillar was a cloud and darkness to the Egyptians but gave light by night to Israel, so that the one came not near the other; Egypt could not see clearly where they were going. - The Lord caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind all that night; Israel went through on dry ground, and the waters were a wall on the right hand and on the left. Exodus 14:23-28 - In the morning watch the Lord troubled the host of the Egyptians and took off their chariot wheels, so that they said, Let us flee from the face of Israel, for the Lord fighteth for them. - Moses stretched out his hand and the sea returned in his strength. All that water that had stood up as a wall came down on the Egyptians, their chariots, and their horsemen, and consumed them. All praises to the Most High for loving His children enough to save us by such a mighty salvation. Exodus 14:29-31 - Israel saw the Egyptians dead upon the sea shore and saw the great work of the Lord, and the people feared the Lord and believed the Lord and His servant Moses. - The Lord who brought us out the first time with great signs and wonders will save Israel out of this captivity the same way; that is why the brothers and sisters must have faith in these last days, because a trial is the true test of faith. - We have to accept that our salvation was their destruction. The Red Sea opened for Israel and closed on Egypt in the same hour; whoever hates that the Most High saves one nation by destroying the others will have to come to grips with it. - Even the ground testified: where water stood before, dry land appeared, and a green field came up out of the violent stream; grass sprang up at the bottom of the sea for the people to pass. Precepts: - Wisdom of Solomon 18:6-8 The salvation of the righteous and the destruction of the enemies were accepted together; the Lord glorified Israel by punishing the adversary. - Wisdom of Solomon 19:6-12 Creation itself was fashioned anew to keep the children without hurt; a green field out of the violent stream, and afterward the quails, which come later in the wilderness. Exodus 15: The Song of Moses: The Lord Is a Man of War Read the chapter → Exodus 15 Exodus 15:1-3 - Then sang Moses and the children of Israel this song unto the Lord. The whole chapter is a song and a prophecy, speaking not only of the coming out of Egypt but in the future tense as well. - The Lord is a man of war: the Lord is His name. He loves war against His enemies; our carnal minds cannot fathom it, but the word says what it says. He mustereth the host of the battle: He brought the Babylonians, the Persians and Medes, the Greeks, and the Romans against Israel, and He has stood in the midst of the wars of the nations ever since. Precepts: - Isaiah 13:4 The Lord of hosts mustereth the host of the battle; He is a man of war. Exodus 15:14-16 - The people shall hear and be afraid; the dukes of Edom shall be amazed, trembling shall take hold of the mighty men of Moab, and the inhabitants of Canaan shall melt away. This goes into the future, when the nations would hear what the Lord had done for Israel. - Fear and dread fall upon them by the greatness of His arm till the people pass over which the Lord purchased. Exodus 15:20-21 - Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took a timbrel, and all the women went out after her with timbrels and with dances, answering the song: sing ye to the Lord, for he hath triumphed gloriously. - The prophetesses guided the women, teaching the young women to be sober and to love their husbands, and Miriam had her part in bringing Israel out of Egypt by keeping the sisters in order; that is the charge on the older sisters today toward the younger. Exodus 15:23-26 - At Marah the waters were bitter, and the people murmured; the Lord shewed Moses a tree, which when he had cast into the waters, the waters were made sweet. - There He made a statute and an ordinance, and there He proved them: hearken diligently to the voice of the Lord thy God, do that which is right in His sight, and keep all His statutes, and none of the diseases of Egypt will be put on thee: for I am the Lord that healeth thee. Exodus 16: Manna From Heaven and the Sabbath Proved Read the chapter → Exodus 16 Exodus 16:1-3 - The whole congregation murmured against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness: would to God we had died by the hand of the Lord in Egypt, when we sat by the flesh pots. The Lord commanded Moses to bring the people out, and when things got tough they made it his fault. - That is us today. When the deliverance does not come easy, the people turn on the man sent to them instead of trusting the Most High who sent him. Exodus 16:4-5 - Behold, I will rain bread from heaven for you; and the people shall gather a certain rate every day, that I may prove them, whether they will walk in my law, or no. The Lord proves His people by the daily portion. - On the sixth day they were to prepare twice as much as they gathered daily; that word becomes important later in the chapter. Exodus 16:6-8 - Your murmurings are not against us, but against the Lord. Moses and Aaron were nobody of themselves; complaining against the leadership the Most High sets is murmuring against the Most High Himself. - That is a heavy point for today. A man says he has no problem with the Bible, only with leadership, but it was the word coming out that made him mad; the Lord hears every murmur of the complainers and doubters. Exodus 16:13-18 - At even the quails came up and covered the camp, and in the morning the manna lay like a small round thing, small as the hoar frost. They said one to another, It is manna: for they wist not what it was. - An omer is a measure, a portion, like measuring cups of flour; every man gathered according to his eating, an omer for every man. He that gathered much had nothing over, and he that gathered little had no lack. Exodus 16:19-21 - Moses said, Let no man leave of it till the morning; some hearkened not and left it, and it bred worms and stank, and Moses was wroth with them. - They gathered it every morning, and when the sun waxed hot it melted; the portion was for the day the Lord gave it. Exodus 16:22-30 - On the sixth day they gathered twice as much, and Moses said, Tomorrow is the rest of the holy sabbath unto the Lord: bake that which ye will bake today. This is the scripture we always use to show that we do not cook on the sabbath; everything is prepared friday before sundown, and the leftovers are eaten the next day. - What was laid up did not stink, neither was there any worm therein, because the Lord had given the bread of two days on the sixth day; the same manna that bred worms on other nights was preserved for the sabbath. - Some of the people still went out on the seventh day to gather and found none, and the Lord said, How long refuse ye to keep my commandments and my laws? The sabbath was already binding in the wilderness. - Abide ye every man in his place on the seventh day is about not going out to gather food on the sabbath. Some foolish Israelites read verse 29 out of context and say you never have to leave your house or join a congregation on the sabbath; that is not what it says. The sabbath is a holy convocation, a large gathering, in all your dwellings, and we are to come together on it. - For the brothers and sisters far from a congregation: you may have to travel and you may have to be the firstfruits in your area. The first assemblies met in houses, and that is how camps start; a man will drive hours to a club, so drive for the truth, and the Lord honors that faith. Precepts: - Leviticus 23:1-3 The seventh day is a sabbath of rest, an holy convocation in all your dwellings; Exodus 16:29 does not undo the gathering. - Romans 16:3-5 Greet the church that is in their house, and Epaenetus the firstfruits of Achaia; congregations begin with the diligent few. - Matthew 6:33 Seek ye first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things shall be added; the Lord sees the sacrifice it takes to get to the congregation. Exodus 16:31-36 - The house of Israel called the name thereof Manna: like coriander seed, white, and the taste of it like wafers made with honey. An omer is the tenth part of an ephah. - Aaron laid up an omer of manna before the Testimony, to be kept for generations, that they may see the bread wherewith the Lord fed Israel in the wilderness. The manna that spoiled overnight on other days was preserved for generations; that is the power of the Most High. - Israel ate manna forty years, until they came unto the borders of the land of Canaan. - Stop reading over the power in these books with the colonizer's picture of the fathers in mind. Esau paints our fathers as a backward people in rags, but the Most High shewed mighty wonders through Genesis and Exodus; stop believing that image. Exodus 17: Water Out of the Rock and War With Amalek Read the chapter → Exodus 17 Exodus 17:1-4 - At Rephidim there was no water, and the people did chide with Moses: wherefore is this that thou hast brought us up out of Egypt, to kill us and our children and our cattle with thirst? At the first sign of trial the people jumped off the Lord's bandwagon again, the same as we do today when tribulation comes. - Moses cried unto the Lord, What shall I do unto this people? they be almost ready to stone me. They were ready to kill the prophet over water, blaming the brother for what only the Most High controls; we have to build our faith up like Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, who trusted the Lord even when trials came. Exodus 17:5-7 - The Lord stood before Moses upon the rock in Horeb; Moses smote the rock, and water came out of it in the sight of the elders of Israel. - He called the place Massah and Meribah, temptation and chiding, because they tempted the Lord, saying, Is the Lord among us, or not? That is wickedness: He had just made Egypt dark, slain their firstborn, and sent His angel in the chariot to guide us, and the people still asked whether He was with them. The mercy of the Most High in bearing that is beyond us. Exodus 17:8-13 - Then came Amalek, and fought with Israel in Rephidim. Amalek was the first nation to come against Israel after Egypt; Amalek was Esau's grandson, born to Eliphaz of Timna the concubine, a duke in the land of Edom. - When Moses held up his hand, Israel prevailed; when he let down his hand, Amalek prevailed. Aaron and Hur stayed up his hands until the going down of the sun. Moses was about eighty years old holding a rod above his head all day; the fathers were mighty men, stronger than we are today. - The sign shewed the people whose hand their life was in: Moses is the man to hearken to, so do not speak against him. And Joshua discomfited Amalek with the edge of the sword; Joshua was a mighty warrior even then. Precepts: - Genesis 36:12 Timna bare to Eliphaz Amalek; Amalek is the grandson of Esau, a duke of Edom. Exodus 17:14-16 - Write this for a memorial in a book, and rehearse it in the ears of Joshua: for I will utterly put out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven. Moses wrote it, and Deuteronomy 25 is that rehearsal: remember what Amalek did unto thee by the way. - Amalek smote the hindmost, all that were feeble, when Israel was faint and weary, and he feared not God. He did not meet the mighty men in the front; he went to the back to slay the women, the children, and the old ones. That same spirit works against the nation's young and old today. - The Lord hath sworn that the Lord will have war with Amalek from generation to generation. By the time Moses rehearsed it in Deuteronomy, forty years had passed and the children of Amalek had done nothing themselves; hundreds of years after that the Lord sent Saul by Samuel to smite Amalek for what was done coming out of Egypt. God be true and every man a liar: the nations do not get away with what they did to His people, and the judgment carries to the seed. - Saul did not finish Agag's line, and in Esther's day Haman the Agagite of that same seed rose against Israel; the war truly runs from generation to generation. - Today that seed says they are Jews and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan, robbing Israel of identity and prospering off the oppression. The Lord says He will make them come and worship before thy feet, and to know that I have loved thee. - The whole world is set up between Jacob and Esau, and Esau is the end of this world, the so-called white man, with Amalek leading; it is not speaking of the Arab man, for if Ishmael had a rulership still to come, Israel would have another captivity to enter, and Christ has already redeemed us from the curse of the law. - The enmity was set from the garden between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed. They bruised Christ's heel, but at the end of the world Jacob bruises the head: the God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 25:17-19 Remember what Amalek did, how he smote the hindmost, the feeble, the faint and weary, and feared not God; thou shalt blot out his remembrance. - 1 Samuel 15:1-3 Hundreds of years later the Lord remembered what Amalek did to Israel in the way from Egypt and sent Saul to destroy Amalek utterly. - Isaiah 14:21-22 Prepare slaughter for his children for the iniquity of their fathers; the name and remnant are cut off, so none escape by saying it was only the forefathers. - Revelation 2:9 The blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan; the Most High knows the lie, and Israel in tribulation and poverty is rich. - Revelation 3:9 The synagogue of Satan will be made to come and worship before Israel's feet, and to know that the Most High loved Israel. - 2 Esdras 6:7-9 Jacob's hand held first the heel of Esau; for Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth. - 2 Esdras 6:10 Nothing stands between the heel and the hand; the world passes straight from Esau's end to Jacob's beginning. - Genesis 3:15 Enmity is set between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed; the battle between Esau's seed and Israel stands until the end. - Romans 16:20 The God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly; Jacob bruises the head at the end of the world. --- Topics: Esau and Edom · Idolatry · Sacrifice and Atonement · The Feasts of the Most High · The Priesthood · The Sabbath ← Exodus 10-13 · Exodus Study · Exodus 18-21 →

title: Exodus 18: Jethro's Counsel and Righteous Leadership
text: ← Exodus 14-17 · Exodus Study · Exodus 22-25 → Exodus 18: Jethro's Counsel and Righteous Leadership Read the chapter → Exodus 18 Introduction This reading covers Exodus 18 through 21: Jethro's counsel to Moses and the structure of righteous leadership, the covenant at Mount Sinai, the Ten Commandments, and the judgments set before Israel. Each chapter is read through, then the highlighted portions are opened with precepts. Exodus 18:1-6 - Jethro the priest of Midian, Moses' father in law, heard all that God had done for Moses and for Israel, and came to Moses in the wilderness with Zipporah and her two sons, Gershom and Eliezer. - Jethro is the same man called Reuel in Exodus 2: the priest of Midian whose seven daughters Moses helped at the well, and who gave Moses Zipporah his daughter. Reuel and Jethro are one person. - Exodus 2 also holds one of the color scriptures: the daughters told their father an Egyptian delivered them out of the hand of the shepherds. Moses, an Israelite, was taken for an Egyptian, because Israel looked like the Egyptians. - Jethro was not an Israelite; he and his kindred were not of the tribes. Precepts: - Exodus 2:16-22 The priest of Midian gave Moses Zipporah his daughter, and she bare Gershom; Reuel is Jethro, and the daughters took Moses for an Egyptian. Exodus 18:9-11 - Jethro rejoiced for all the goodness which the Lord had done to Israel, and confessed, now I know that the Lord is greater than all gods, for in the thing wherein they dealt proudly he was above them. - Other non-Israelites came to that same knowledge. All the gods of the nations are idols, but the Lord made the heavens; give unto the Lord the glory due unto his name. - Naaman the Syrian, healed of his leprosy in Jordan, confessed that there is no God in all the earth but in Israel. His faith was so strong he vowed to offer neither burnt offering nor sacrifice unto other gods, and asked pardon for even bowing in the house of Rimmon with his master. - Nebuchadnezzar came to praise and extol and honour the King of heaven, for those that walk in pride he is able to abase. The heathen understand that the Most High is greater than all other gods; it is our people that want a god that does not look like them. Precepts: - Psalms 96:5-8 All the gods of the nations are idols, but the Lord made the heavens; give unto the Lord the glory due unto his name. - 2 Kings 5:1 Naaman, captain of the host of Syria, was a mighty man in valour, but he was a leper. - 2 Kings 5:14-18 Naaman dipped seven times in Jordan and was clean, and confessed there is no God in all the earth but in Israel; a heathen vowed to sacrifice to no other god but the Lord. - Daniel 4:37 Nebuchadnezzar praised and extolled the King of heaven, whose works are truth, and those that walk in pride he is able to abase. Exodus 18:15-16 - The people came to Moses to inquire of God; he judged between one and another and made them know the statutes of God and his laws. That responsibility is Moses' seat. - The scribes and the Pharisees sat in Moses' seat, which is why their words were to be observed but their works not followed, for they say and do not. Precepts: - Matthew 23:2-3 The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses' seat; observe what they bid, but do not after their works. Exodus 18:20 - Thou shalt teach them ordinances and laws, and shalt shew them the way wherein they must walk and the work that they must do. That is the work done today when the laws of the Most High are taught in the streets and online: shewing the people the ways they must walk and the work they must do. Exodus 18:21-22 - Able men, such as fear God, men of truth, hating covetousness, were set as rulers of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens. This is the structure of righteous leadership the Most High established: captains and officers over the tribes, offices never heard in the church. - The judges were charged to hear the causes between brethren and judge righteously, without respect of persons, not afraid of the face of man, for the judgment is God's. The hard causes went up to Moses, as the hard matters today go to the high-ranking officers and ultimately the bishop, while the smaller matters are judged by the lower-ranking officers. - Judgment did not pass away with the Old Testament. He that is spiritual judgeth all things, and the spiritual man is the man that keeps the commandments. The saints shall judge the world, so brethren should judge the smallest matters among themselves instead of going to law before the unjust; only matters of life and death under today's system go outside. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 1:15-17 Captains over thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens, and officers among the tribes, charged to judge righteously and not respect persons, for the judgment is God's. - 1 Corinthians 2:15 He that is spiritual judgeth all things; the spiritual man keeps the commandments. - 1 Corinthians 6:1-2 The saints shall judge the world; do not go to law before the unjust when you are able to judge the smallest matters. Exodus 19: The Covenant at Mount Sinai Read the chapter → Exodus 19 Exodus 19:1-2 - In the third month after going forth out of Egypt, Israel departed from Rephidim, came into the wilderness of Sinai, and camped before the mount. The journeys are recorded in Numbers 33: Israel departed from Rameses on the fifteenth day of the first month, on the morrow after the Passover, and later pitched in the wilderness of Sinai. - Israel went forth out of Egypt with their armies. The tribes are armies, for the Lord is a man of war; Israel has always been at war and is at war today, a spiritual war. - Moses wrote their goings out by the commandment of the Lord. The Lord gave the word, and great was the company of those that published it; so the claim that another people wrote the scriptures falls, for Moses wrote what God commanded him to write. Precepts: - Numbers 33:1-4 These are the journeys of Israel by their armies, and Moses wrote their goings out by the commandment of the Lord, departing from Rameses on the morrow after the Passover. - Numbers 33:15 They departed from Rephidim and pitched in the wilderness of Sinai, the same arrival Exodus 19 records in the third month. - Exodus 15:3 The Lord is a man of war; the tribes came out as armies. - 2 Corinthians 10:3-4 Though we walk in the flesh, we do not war after the flesh; the war Israel fights today is spiritual. - Psalms 68:11 The Lord gave the word; great was the company of those that published it. Moses published what the Lord commanded. Exodus 19:5-8 - If ye will obey my voice indeed, and keep my covenant, then ye shall be a peculiar treasure unto me above all people, a kingdom of priests, and an holy nation. - Moses laid all these words before the elders, and all the people answered together, all that the Lord hath spoken we will do. Right there Israel made a covenant, an agreement, with the Most High. Exodus 19:12-13 - Bounds were set round about the mount: whosoever touched it, whether beast or man, was to be stoned or shot through, and no hand was to touch it. - The Most High is serious about that charge. When the oxen shook the cart, Uzzah put forth his hand to the ark of God and took hold of it, and the anger of the Lord was kindled and he smote him there, for the stranger that came nigh the priests' office was to be put to death. Every family of the priesthood had its own responsibility in the tabernacle service, and none could transgress against another's charge; what the world later called unions came from that order. - When the trumpet sounded long they were to come up to the mount. The trumpets were made for the calling of the assembly and for the journeys of the camps, and trumpets still gather the congregation at the new moons and at the start of classes. - That trumpet in the mount was not blown by Moses, for Moses was down among the people sanctifying them; the trumpet came from heaven. Precepts: - 2 Samuel 6:3-7 Uzzah put forth his hand to the ark when the oxen shook it, and God smote him there for his error; the Most High is serious about what is not to be touched. - Numbers 3:10 Aaron and his sons waited on the priest's office, and the stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death. - Numbers 10:1-2 The two trumpets of silver were made for the calling of the assembly and for the journeys of the camps. Exodus 20: The Ten Commandments Read the chapter → Exodus 20 Exodus 20:4-5 - An image in itself is not the sin, except for that white image of the beast; making images to bow down to them and serve them is the transgression, for the Lord thy God is a jealous God. - Visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation: Israel is yet this day in captivity, scattered for a reproach and a curse, according to all the iniquities of the fathers which departed from the Lord. Right now Israel is paying for the sins of the fathers; that is why the people are scattered to the four corners of the earth. Precepts: - Baruch 3:8 We are yet this day in our captivity, scattered for a reproach, according to all the iniquities of our fathers which departed from the Lord our God. Exodus 20:6 - And shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love me, and keep my commandments. Judith recounted how the Most High tried the fathers for the examination of their hearts: he tried Abraham and Isaac, and Jacob in Mesopotamia of Syria keeping the sheep of Laban, serving twenty years with his wages changed and given Leah when he looked for Rachel. - In Judith's day there was no tribe, family, people, nor city that worshipped gods made with hands, as had been aforetime; for that cause she trusted the Lord would not despise the nation. Mercy rests on them that know none other God, not Allah, not Buddha, not a white Jesus. Precepts: - Judith 8:25-27 The Lord tried Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob for the examination of their hearts, and scourgeth them that come near unto him, to admonish them. - Judith 8:18-20 The fathers were given to the sword for idolatry, but a generation that knows none other god can trust he will not despise the nation. Exodus 20:8-11 - Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy. The word says remember because Israel would forget it: in this captivity the people were forced to serve other gods and their religions, and the Sabbath was lost through forced conversion. - Look up the blue laws, also known as Sunday laws; they help give understanding of why the Bible says remember the Sabbath day. Precepts: - Jeremiah 17:4 Thou shalt serve thine enemies in the land which thou knowest not; the captivity brought forced service to other gods. - Deuteronomy 28:64 Scattered among all people, there shalt thou serve other gods, wood and stone; that is how the Sabbath was forgotten. - 1 Kings 8:47 If they bethink themselves in the land whither they were carried captives, and repent; the remembering begins in the captivity. Exodus 20:25-26 - An altar of stone was not to be built of hewn stone, for lifting up a tool upon it pollutes it; neither go up by steps unto the altar, that thy nakedness be not discovered thereon. - This scripture helps explain pants, precept upon precept. The priests were given linen breeches to cover their nakedness from the loins even unto the thighs when they came near the altar, and Israel was called in this same reading to be a kingdom of priests, so do not be simple and say that law was only for Aaron and his sons. - Those breeches were made for men and not for women, as the law of the garments also shows. Precepts: - Exodus 28:42-43 Linen breeches to cover their nakedness, from the loins even unto the thighs, upon Aaron and his sons at the altar, a statute for ever. - Exodus 19:6 Ye shall be unto me a kingdom of priests; the priests' standard belongs to the whole nation. - Deuteronomy 22:5 The woman shall not wear that which pertaineth unto a man; the breeches pertain to the man. Exodus 21: The Judgments Set Before Israel Read the chapter → Exodus 21 Exodus 21:2-6 - If thou buy an Hebrew servant, six years he shall serve, and in the seventh he shall go out free for nothing. If he came in by himself he goes out by himself; if he were married when he came in, his wife goes out with him. - Deuteronomy repeats the same judgment for a Hebrew man or a Hebrew woman sold unto thee. Nehemiah 5 shows how brethren came into servitude: in the dearth some mortgaged lands, vineyards, and houses to buy corn, some borrowed money for the king's tribute, and some brought their sons and daughters into bondage. The brother that waxes poor is not to be compelled to serve as a bondservant, but as an hired servant, and not ruled over harshly. - If the master gave him a wife and she bare him sons or daughters, the wife and her children are the master's, and he goes out by himself; he did not bring them in. His two choices are to go out alone, or to plainly say, I love my master, my wife, and my children, have his ear bored through with an aul at the door post, and serve his master for ever. - Zedekiah's covenant in Jeremiah confirms the law in the prophets: every man was to let his Hebrew manservant and maidservant go free at the appointed release. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 15:12 An Hebrew man or an Hebrew woman sold unto thee serves six years, and in the seventh year thou shalt let him go free. - Nehemiah 5:1-5 In the dearth the people mortgaged lands and borrowed for the king's tribute, and brought their sons and daughters into bondage; that is how brethren came into servitude. - Leviticus 25:39-40 Thy brother that is waxen poor and sold unto thee shall not serve as a bondservant, but as an hired servant, unto the year of jubile. - Jeremiah 34:8-10 Zedekiah made a covenant to proclaim liberty, that every man let his Hebrew manservant and maidservant go free; the law of release stood in the prophets. Exodus 21:7-11 - If a man sell his daughter to be a maidservant, she shall not go out as the menservants do. The reason is that her master betrothed her to himself, or unto his son; she is a wife, not a six-year servant, so the release of the menservants does not apply to her. - If she please not her master who hath betrothed her to himself, he must let her be redeemed; he has no power to sell her unto a strange nation, seeing he hath dealt deceitfully with her. The deceit is that he betrothed her to himself and then would not deal with her, keeping her to himself when she could have been another man's wife. - If he take him another wife, her food, her raiment, and her duty of marriage shall he not diminish; the duty of marriage is the marriage bed. If he lay with her, she belongs to him and he cannot send her away; and if he do not these three unto her, then shall she go out free without money. He must take care of her. Exodus 21:13-14 - If a man lie not in wait, but God deliver him into his hand, a place was appointed whither he shall flee. That is the case of the slayer that kills his neighbour ignorantly, as when a man hews wood with his neighbour and the axe head slips from the helve and lights upon him that he die: he flees to the appointed city and lives, lest the avenger of blood overtake him while his heart is hot, for he was not worthy of death, having hated him not in time past. - But if a man come presumptuously upon his neighbour to slay him with guile, thou shalt take him from mine altar, that he may die. Men would run and grab the horns of the altar, but wilful murder found no refuge there. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 19:4-6 The slayer that kills his neighbour ignorantly, as when the axe head slips from the helve, flees to the city of refuge and lives, for he was not worthy of death. Exodus 21:18-19 - If men strive and one smite another so that he keep his bed, he that smote him shall pay for the loss of his time and shall cause him to be thoroughly healed. That is restitution: paying for the time the man was down and could not work and provide for his family. That is what the court system calls a civil suit today. Exodus 21:20-21 - If a man smite his servant with a rod and he die under his hand, he shall surely be punished; but if he continue a day or two, he shall not be punished, for he is his money. - The wisdom writings teach not to be ashamed of much correction of children, nor of making the side of an evil servant to bleed. An evil servant that will not get right could be corrected physically, so long as he was not killed. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 42:1, 5 Be not ashamed of much correction of children, nor to make the side of an evil servant to bleed. Exodus 21:22-25 - If men strive and hurt a woman with child so that her fruit depart from her, this judgment covers the miscarriage: if no mischief follow, he is punished as the woman's husband lays upon him and the judges determine; and if any mischief follow, then life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, wound for wound. Exodus 21:28-29 - If an ox gore a man or a woman that they die, the ox is stoned and his flesh not eaten, and the owner is quit. But if the ox were wont to push with his horns in time past, and it hath been testified to his owner, and he hath not kept him in, and it kill a man or a woman, the ox is stoned and his owner also put to death. - Most do not have oxen today, but the same judgment reaches the yard dogs, the pit bulls, German shepherds, and rottweilers. If the dog has bitten before and it was reported to you, and it gets out again through a snapped chain or a breach in the fence and mauls or kills somebody, the scripture holds the owner responsible unto death; that is why animal control writes the ticket and warns you to keep your dogs in. - The law is slack right now, as Habakkuk says, so many punishments worthy of death in the scriptures, like rape or this judgment, come out today as a fine or a slap on the hand. Precepts: - Habakkuk 1:4 The law is slacked, and judgment doth never go forth; that is why death-worthy offences draw light penalties today. --- Topics: Clean and Unclean Meats · Idolatry · Sacrifice and Atonement · The Covenant · The Feasts of the Most High · The Priesthood · The Sabbath ← Exodus 14-17 · Exodus Study · Exodus 22-25 →

title: Exodus 2: The Birth of Moses
text: ← Exodus 1 · Exodus Study · Exodus 6-9 → Exodus 2: The Birth of Moses Read the chapter → Exodus 2 Introduction This reading covers Exodus 2 through 5: the birth of Moses and his flight to Midian, the angel in the burning bush, the three signs given to Moses and the circumcision of his son, and the first appearance before Pharaoh with the answer, Let my people go. The session opened with prayer out of Psalms 56, be merciful unto me, O God, for man would swallow me up; in God I have put my trust, I will not fear what flesh can do unto me; and with thanksgiving for the reawakening prophesied in Ezekiel 37, that the people of the Most High will return unto Him and stand upon their feet, an exceeding great army. Exodus 2:1 - A man of the house of Levi took to wife a daughter of Levi. These are Amram and Jochebed, the father and mother of Moses, Aaron, and Miriam. Precepts: - Exodus 6:20 Amram took him Jochebed to wife, and she bare him Aaron and Moses; the scripture names the parents of Moses. Exodus 2:2 - The woman conceived and bare a son, and when she saw him that he was a goodly child, she hid him three months. Goodly means the child was exceeding fair; there was something special about this child from his birth. Precepts: - Acts 7:20 In which time Moses was born, and was exceeding fair, and nourished up in his father's house three months. - Hebrews 11:23 By faith his parents hid him, because they saw he was a proper child, and they were not afraid of the king's commandment. Exodus 2:3-4 - When she could no longer hide him, she took for him an ark of bulrushes, daubed it with slime and with pitch, and laid it in the flags by the river's brink. Bulrushes are the river reeds known as cattails. - His sister Miriam stood afar off, to wit what would be done to him. The movie tellings of this account do not give the full details; to get a full understanding of what happened in the days of Moses you have to read the scriptures. Exodus 2:5-6 - The daughter of Pharaoh sent her maid to fetch the ark, and when she had opened it she saw the child, and the babe wept. She had compassion on him and said, This is one of the Hebrews' children. - She knew the child was a Hebrew and no Egyptian because the Most High put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel; though both peoples were dark of skin, this was a child of the chosen nation. Precepts: - Exodus 11:7 The Lord doth put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel. - Psalms 50:2 Out of Zion, the perfection of beauty, God hath shined; she saw this was of the chosen vessel of the Lord. Exodus 2:7-9 - Miriam was crafty. She offered to call a nurse of the Hebrew women, and Pharaoh's daughter sent the maid, who called the child's own mother, and wages were paid her to nurse him. - So Moses was raised in his first years by his actual mother; the Most High allowed it, all praises to Him. Exodus 2:10 - The child grew, and he became the son of Pharaoh's daughter. She called his name Moses, which means drawn out, because she drew him out of the water. - So Moses grew up as an Egyptian, although he was a Hebrew. Exodus 2:11-12 - When Moses was grown he went out unto his brethren the Israelites and looked on their burdens, and he spied an Egyptian smiting an Hebrew, one of his brethren. Moses knew the Israelites were his brothers; he knew he was not of the Egyptian lineage and that there was something different about him. - He looked this way and that way, and when he saw that there was no man, he slew the Egyptian and hid him in the sand. He did not just marvel at the oppression; he used his position for his people, unlike many who hold a position of power today and will not risk it for their people. Moses is the ultimate revolutionary, as Christ is. Precepts: - Ecclesiastes 5:8 If thou seest the oppression of the poor, and violent perverting of judgment, marvel not at the matter: for he that is higher than the highest regardeth; the Most High sees the oppression. Exodus 2:13-14 - The second day two men of the Hebrews strove together, and he that did the wrong answered, Who made thee a prince and a judge over us? intendest thou to kill me, as thou killedst the Egyptian? When a people is oppressed they take the oppression out on one another, and brothers become their own enemies; the same spirit answers correction among Israel today, pointing the finger at the one who corrects. - Moses feared, and said, Surely this thing is known. Exodus 2:15 - When Pharaoh heard this thing, he sought to slay Moses; but Moses fled from the face of Pharaoh and dwelt in the land of Midian. - Moses gave up his whole upbringing and position. By faith he refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter, choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season. In Egypt his head was shaved, his beard cut, his dress and customs Egyptian; he laid all of it down to be what he was called to be, an Israelite. - The same claim stands now: the remnant does not want the names of the captivity but the natural heritage of Israel, esteeming the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures of this land. Precepts: - Hebrews 11:24-27 By faith Moses refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter, esteemed the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures in Egypt, and forsook Egypt, not fearing the wrath of the king. Exodus 2:16-20 - The priest of Midian had seven daughters, and the shepherds drove them from the troughs; but Moses stood up and helped them, and watered their flock. Moses was a man of war, not a weak man. - The daughters told their father, An Egyptian delivered us out of the hand of the shepherds. They took Moses for an Egyptian by his dress, by how he carried himself, and by his skin: Moses was a very dark-skinned man, the same color as the Egyptians. Israel was always being mistaken for Egyptians. - Reuel the priest of Midian is the same man called Jethro, the father in law of Moses. Precepts: - Acts 21:37-39 The chief captain took Paul for that Egyptian which made an uproar; Paul answered, I am a man which am a Jew of Tarsus; the Israelites were mistaken for Egyptians. - Genesis 42:7-8 Joseph knew his brethren, but they knew not him; an Israelite in Egyptian dress passed for an Egyptian. Exodus 2:21-22 - Moses was content to dwell with the man, and he gave Moses Zipporah his daughter. She bare him a son, and he called his name Gershom: for he said, I have been a stranger in a strange land; Gershom means stranger. - Zipporah and her family were Midianites, not Israelites; Moses married a woman of the land where he dwelt those forty years. Exodus 2:23-25 - In process of time the king of Egypt died, and the children of Israel sighed by reason of the bondage, and they cried, and their cry came up unto God, as Israel cries in this captivity today. - God heard their groaning, and God remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob. The bondage itself was prophesied to Abraham: his seed would be a stranger in a land not theirs and be afflicted four hundred years, and afterward come out with great substance. That prophecy is about Egypt, not a date of release in this present day. - God had respect unto them. The Most High has respect unto one nation, Israel: He is in the midst of Israel, and His people shall never be ashamed. - Respect unto His chosen is not respect of persons. Within Israel there is no respect of persons: the Most High renders to every man according to his deeds, tribulation and anguish upon every soul that doeth evil, of the Jew first and also of the Gentile, the southern kingdom and the northern kingdom that was Hellenized; but glory, honour, and peace to every man that worketh good. The nation is chosen above the nations, and all Israel shall be saved through the Deliverer out of Sion. Precepts: - Genesis 15:13-14 Thy seed shall be a stranger in a land that is not theirs, and shall serve them four hundred years; and afterward shall they come out with great substance. - Joel 2:27 Ye shall know that I am in the midst of Israel, and that I am the LORD your God, and none else: and my people shall never be ashamed. - Wisdom of Solomon 4:15 His grace and mercy is with his saints, and he hath respect unto his chosen. - Isaiah 44:1 Yet now hear, O Jacob my servant; and Israel, whom I have chosen. - Romans 2:6-11 God will render to every man according to his deeds, to the Jew first and also to the Gentile: for there is no respect of persons with God. - Romans 11:26 And so all Israel shall be saved: there shall come out of Sion the Deliverer, and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob. Exodus 3: The Angel in the Burning Bush Read the chapter → Exodus 3 Exodus 3:1-6 - Moses kept the flock of Jethro his father in law and led it to the backside of the desert, to Horeb the mountain of God; and the angel of the LORD appeared unto him in a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush, and the bush was not consumed. - The voice out of the bush said, Draw not nigh hither: put off thy shoes from off thy feet, for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground; I am the God of thy father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob. - The precepts identify that angel. Stephen recounts that the angel which appeared in the bush sent Moses to be a ruler and a deliverer; Joshua met the captain of the host of the LORD, who gave him the same command, Loose thy shoe from off thy foot; and the captain of their salvation, made perfect through sufferings, is Jesus Christ.
