Precept upon precept, the angel in the burning bush was Christ. - The same angel went before Israel out of Egypt: Behold, I send an Angel before thee; beware of him, and obey his voice, provoke him not, for my name is in him. Precepts: - Acts 7:30-36 There appeared to Moses in the wilderness of mount Sina an angel of the Lord in a flame of fire in a bush; him did God send to be a ruler and a deliverer by the hand of the angel which appeared to him in the bush. - Acts 7:37-38 This is that Moses which said, A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you of your brethren, like unto me; he was in the church in the wilderness with the angel which spake to him in the mount Sina. - Joshua 5:13-15 The captain of the host of the LORD said to Joshua, Loose thy shoe from off thy foot; for the place whereon thou standest is holy; the same command given at the bush. - Hebrews 2:9-10 Jesus was made a little lower than the angels for the suffering of death, the captain of their salvation made perfect through sufferings; the captain of the Lord's host is Christ. - Exodus 23:20-23 Behold, I send an Angel before thee, to keep thee in the way; obey his voice, provoke him not; for he will not pardon your transgressions: for my name is in him. - God is a Spirit, and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth; yet He has a celestial, angelic body, not flesh of this earth. The Ancient of days has a garment and the hair of his head like the pure wool; that is how man could be made in His image. - Christ was not reincarnated when he came in the flesh. He took not on him the nature of angels, but the seed of Abraham, made like unto his brethren, born a man so that he could die for the nation of Israel, for an angel cannot die. Precepts: - John 4:24 God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth. - 1 Corinthians 15:39-40 There are celestial bodies, and bodies terrestrial; the Most High has an angelic celestial body. - Daniel 7:9 The Ancient of days did sit, whose garment was white as snow, and the hair of his head like the pure wool; He has form and body, not of this earth. - Hebrews 2:16-17 He took not on him the nature of angels; but he took on him the seed of Abraham, and in all things it behoved him to be made like unto his brethren. Exodus 3:7-10 - The LORD said, I have surely seen the affliction of my people which are in Egypt, and have heard their cry by reason of their taskmasters; for I know their sorrows; and I am come down to deliver them out of the hand of the Egyptians. - He is come down to bring them up unto a land flowing with milk and honey, the place of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites. That was the best land on earth, and when the Lord restores His people it will be so again. - Come now therefore, and I will send thee unto Pharaoh, that thou mayest bring forth my people the children of Israel out of Egypt. Exodus 3:11-12 - Moses said unto God, Who am I, that I should go unto Pharaoh? This shows the humility of the forefathers: none of them sought the position they were given. The Lord chose Moses because He saw the spirit that was in him. - Certainly I will be with thee; and this shall be a token unto thee: ye shall serve God upon this mountain. Exodus 3:13-15 - God said unto Moses, I AM THAT I AM: thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel, I AM hath sent me unto you. The Lord God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Jacob: this is my name for ever, and this is my memorial unto all generations. - Christ spoke to that very name: Verily, verily, I say unto you, Before Abraham was, I am. He was telling them he was the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob who met Moses at the bush. Precepts: - John 8:58 Jesus said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Before Abraham was, I am; Christ identified himself with the I AM of the bush. Exodus 3:16-18 - Go, and gather the elders of Israel together, and say unto them, The LORD God of your fathers hath surely visited you, and hath seen that which is done to you in Egypt; and I will bring you up out of the affliction of Egypt unto a land flowing with milk and honey. - They shall hearken to thy voice; and thou and the elders shall say unto the king of Egypt, The LORD God of the Hebrews hath met with us: let us go, we beseech thee, three days' journey into the wilderness, that we may sacrifice to the LORD our God. Exodus 3:19-20 - I am sure that the king of Egypt will not let you go, no, not by a mighty hand; and I will stretch out my hand, and smite Egypt with all my wonders. The Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart so that the deliverance would come with wonders, destroying the idols of Egypt in the sight of Israel and of Egypt; the Most High is not one to be played with. Exodus 3:21-22 - I will give this people favour in the sight of the Egyptians: and it shall come to pass, that, when ye go, ye shall not go empty; every woman shall borrow of her neighbour jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and raiment, and ye shall spoil the Egyptians. - It happened exactly the way it was spoken: after the firstborn of Egypt were slain, the Egyptians lent Israel what they required, and they spoiled the Egyptians. Precepts: - Exodus 12:35-36 The children of Israel borrowed of the Egyptians jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and raiment; and the LORD gave the people favour, so that they lent unto them such things as they required: and they spoiled the Egyptians. Exodus 4: The Three Signs and the Covenant of Circumcision Read the chapter → Exodus 4 Exodus 4:1 - Moses answered, But, behold, they will not believe me, nor hearken unto my voice. Moses knew the spirit of his people: Israel is impudent, hardhearted, and stiffnecked, a rebellious house that does not like to listen even when shown precept upon precept. - The word to Ezekiel is the same commission: Israel is not a people of a strange speech and hard language; had the prophet been sent to such, they would have hearkened; but the house of Israel will not hearken. Go, get thee to them of the captivity, and speak unto them, whether they will hear or whether they will forbear. That stubbornness is itself a mark of who the Israelites are among the nations today. Precepts: - Ezekiel 3:4-9 The house of Israel will not hearken unto thee, for they are impudent and hardhearted; fear them not, though they be a rebellious house. - Ezekiel 3:10-11 Go, get thee to them of the captivity, unto the children of thy people, and speak unto them, whether they will hear, or whether they will forbear. Exodus 4:2-5 - The first sign: the rod cast on the ground became a serpent, and Moses fled from before it; he caught it by the tail and it became a rod in his hand. - The sign was given that they may believe that the LORD God of their fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, hath appeared unto thee. Israel would not believe on a man's word alone; it took a miracle, because we were a people of little faith. Exodus 4:6-8 - The second sign: Moses put his hand into his bosom, and when he took it out, his hand was leprous as snow; he put it in again, and it was turned again as his other flesh. - This was a miracle precisely because Moses was a very dark-skinned man; the daughters of the priest of Midian had taken him for an Egyptian. The hand came out white as snow and went back to his natural dark skin; had he been white already there would have been no sign in it. - If they will not believe the first sign, they will believe the voice of the latter sign; the magicians of Egypt could imitate serpents, but not this. Exodus 4:9 - The third sign: if they will not believe the first two, take of the water of the river and pour it upon the dry land, and the water shall become blood upon the dry land. Exodus 4:10-12 - Moses said, O my Lord, I am not eloquent, but I am slow of speech, and of a slow tongue. Moses did not stutter, as is commonly taught; he was not fluent in the Hebrew tongue. He was learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians and mighty in words and in deeds, but he grew up in Pharaoh's house speaking the Egyptian language and then spent forty years in Midian, and a language moves on in forty years. - The LORD answered, Who hath made man's mouth? Now therefore go, and I will be with thy mouth, and teach thee what thou shalt say. Precepts: - Acts 7:22 Moses was learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and was mighty in words and in deeds; he had no speech impediment. - 2 Corinthians 11:6 Though I be rude in speech, yet not in knowledge; Paul said the same of himself. Exodus 4:13-17 - Moses pressed, Send, I pray thee, by the hand of him whom thou wilt send; and the anger of the LORD was kindled against Moses. Is not Aaron the Levite thy brother? I know that he can speak well; he spoke the Hebrew of the people fluently. - Aaron shall be thy spokesman unto the people: he shall be to thee instead of a mouth, and thou shalt be to him instead of God. Moses stood as God in this instance, speaking through Aaron his prophet, who interpreted to the people. - And thou shalt take this rod in thine hand, wherewith thou shalt do signs. Exodus 4:18-23 - Moses returned to Jethro his father in law and asked leave, and Jethro said, Go in peace. The LORD said, Go, return into Egypt: for all the men are dead which sought thy life; the Pharaoh of chapter 2 had died. - Moses took his wife and his sons and returned to the land of Egypt, and Moses took the rod of God in his hand. The LORD told him, Do all those wonders before Pharaoh which I have put in thine hand: but I will harden his heart, that he shall not let the people go. - Thou shalt say unto Pharaoh, Thus saith the LORD, Israel is my son, even my firstborn. Israel was not the first nation created; it was among the last. But Israel is the first nation the Most High chose, the apple of His eye from Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob down. If thou refuse to let him go, behold, I will slay thy son, even thy firstborn. Exodus 4:24-26 - By the way in the inn, the LORD met him, and sought to kill him, because Moses had not circumcised his son. Zipporah took a sharp stone, cut off the foreskin of her son, and said, Surely a bloody husband art thou to me: bloody because of the circumcision she had to perform herself. - This shows the laws did not begin at Sinai. Circumcision was the covenant given to Abraham for every man child in his generations, on the eighth day, and the uncircumcised man child whose flesh is not circumcised, that soul shall be cut off from his people: he hath broken my covenant. That is why Moses was worthy of death. Precepts: - Genesis 17:9-14 Every man child among you shall be circumcised, he that is eight days old, for an everlasting covenant; the uncircumcised man child shall be cut off from his people; he hath broken my covenant. - Leviticus 12:1-3 In the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised; the law Moses himself later carried to Israel. - The covenant still stands. A son of Israel must be circumcised; and a man that comes to the truth grown must still be circumcised, even at forty, fifty, or sixty years, as Abraham himself was circumcised at ninety and nine, and as Paul circumcised Timothy, whose father was a Greek. Nothing that defileth enters the kingdom. - The Egyptians did not practice circumcision; they were a nation of uncleanness, and the covenant was between the Lord and Israel: after the doings of the land of Egypt, wherein ye dwelt, shall ye not do. Precepts: - Genesis 17:23-24 Abraham was ninety years old and nine when he was circumcised; the covenant is kept at any age. - Acts 16:1-3 Paul took Timothy, whose father was a Greek, and circumcised him because of the covenant. - Leviticus 18:3 After the doings of the land of Egypt, wherein ye dwelt, shall ye not do; Egypt did not keep the covenant of circumcision. - Revelation 21:27 There shall in no wise enter into it any thing that defileth; the unclean do not enter the kingdom. - Colossians 3:5-6 Mortify therefore your members, fornication, uncleanness; for which things' sake the wrath of God cometh on the children of disobedience. - Romans 2 does not do away with circumcision of the flesh. Circumcision verily profiteth if thou keep the law: the Jews who grew up circumcised and keeping the law, yet broke it, made their circumcision uncircumcision; and the uncircumcised of the cast-off northern kingdom who keep the righteousness of the law are counted as circumcised. Circumcision of the heart is putting away the evil of the doings, as the prophets say, take away the foreskins of your heart; the scribes and Pharisees were clean on the outside of the cup but full of iniquity within. Precepts: - Romans 2:25-29 Circumcision verily profiteth, if thou keep the law; he is a Jew, which is one inwardly, and circumcision is that of the heart; it speaks to lawbreaking, not to ending the covenant of the flesh. - Jeremiah 4:4 Circumcise yourselves to the LORD, and take away the foreskins of your heart, ye men of Judah; because of the evil of your doings. - Deuteronomy 10:16 Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart, and be no more stiffnecked. - Matthew 23:25-28 Ye make clean the outside of the cup, but within ye are full of hypocrisy and iniquity; the outward show is not the covenant. Exodus 4:27-31 - The LORD sent Aaron into the wilderness to meet Moses, and he met him in the mount of God and kissed him; Aaron believed right away. Moses told Aaron all the words of the LORD and all the signs. - Aaron spake all the words which the LORD had spoken unto Moses and did the signs in the sight of the people, and the people believed: and when they heard that the LORD had visited the children of Israel, and that he had looked upon their affliction, they bowed their heads and worshipped. After a long time in which the Lord had not been dealing with them, He finally heard their prayers. Exodus 5: Let My People Go Read the chapter → Exodus 5 Exodus 5:1-2 - Moses and Aaron went in and told Pharaoh, Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, Let my people go, that they may hold a feast unto me in the wilderness. That feast was the Passover. - Pharaoh said, Who is the LORD, that I should obey his voice to let Israel go? I know not the LORD, neither will I let Israel go. The Lord had already said He would harden Pharaoh's heart. Exodus 5:3 - They said, The God of the Hebrews hath met with us: let us go, we pray thee, three days' journey into the desert, and sacrifice unto the LORD our God; lest he fall upon us with pestilence, or with the sword. Exodus 5:4-5 - The king of Egypt said, Wherefore do ye, Moses and Aaron, let the people from their works? get you unto your burdens. That is the standing complaint of the oppressor: the prophets are pulling the people from their labor and getting their hopes up that their God will deliver them. Exodus 5:6-9 - Pharaoh commanded the taskmasters the same day: ye shall no more give the people straw to make brick; let them go and gather straw for themselves; and the tale of the bricks ye shall lay upon them, ye shall not diminish ought thereof. For they be idle; therefore they cry, saying, Let us go and sacrifice to our God. - Let there more work be laid upon the men, that they may labour therein; and let them not regard vain words. The same tactic runs in this captivity: burdens are increased and extra wages dangled for working the Sabbath and the feast days, to wear the people down so they will not regard the words of the Most High. - The work of the Lord is the true calling over any occupation held in Babylon: consider the Apostle and High Priest of our profession, Christ Jesus; fight the good fight of faith, lay hold on eternal life, whereunto thou art also called, and hast professed a good profession before many witnesses. Precepts: - Hebrews 3:1 Consider the Apostle and High Priest of our profession, Christ Jesus; the work of the Lord is the profession of the called. - 1 Timothy 6:12 Fight the good fight of faith, lay hold on eternal life, whereunto thou art also called, and hast professed a good profession before many witnesses. Exodus 5:10-14 - The people were scattered abroad throughout all the land of Egypt to gather stubble instead of straw, and the taskmasters hasted them, saying, Fulfil your works, your daily tasks, as when there was straw. Fewer resources, the same production and the same deadline: the pattern of oppression has not changed in this captivity. - The officers of the children of Israel, which Pharaoh's taskmasters had set over them, were beaten. Israelites were set as officers over their own people, so that the anger of the oppressed lands on their own brother, the supervisor they can see, instead of on the power above him; it has always been an agenda, and it is the same one today. - This place is the same house of bondage in the spirit: the great city is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt, and the afflictions Egypt laid on Israel are the same tactics laid on Israel here. Precepts: - Revelation 11:8 The great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified. Exodus 5:15-19 - The officers of the children of Israel came and cried unto Pharaoh, saying, Wherefore dealest thou thus with thy servants? There is no straw given unto thy servants, and they say to us, Make brick: and, behold, thy servants are beaten; but the fault is in thine own people. - Pharaoh answered, Ye are idle, ye are idle: therefore ye say, Let us go and do sacrifice to the LORD. The charge of idleness is the standing answer to any who would go serve God, whether it is the three days' journey or keeping the Sabbath and the new moons now. - The officers did see that they were in evil case. That is when they realized no appeal to Pharaoh would deliver them; deliverance was not coming from Egypt. Precepts: - John 11:47-48 The chief priests and Pharisees said, If we let him thus alone, the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation; men set over the people fear losing their place more than they love the deliverer. Exodus 5:20-21 - They met Moses and Aaron and said, The LORD look upon you, and judge; because ye have made our savour to be abhorred in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of his servants, to put a sword in their hand to slay us. - The people blamed the deliverers for the increase of affliction. It is the same spirit that meets the truth today, preferring quiet assimilation to deliverance; the enemy turns up the pressure precisely because the truth is being spoken. Exodus 5:22-23 - Moses returned unto the LORD, and said, Lord, wherefore hast thou so evil entreated this people? why is it that thou hast sent me? For since I came to Pharaoh to speak in thy name, he hath done evil to this people; neither hast thou delivered thy people at all. - Affliction can increase when the truth first goes forth, and the deliverer himself can be shaken by it. Walk in wisdom under that pressure and hold the tongue where wisdom requires, without letting go of the work. - Have the faith to see ahead. The work of the Lord grows from a handful over many years because He sees the faith of those who endure, though at the time they cannot yet see what it will become. --- Topics: Clean and Unclean Meats · Idolatry · Sacrifice and Atonement · The Covenant · The Feasts of the Most High · The Priesthood · The Sabbath ← Exodus 1 · Exodus Study · Exodus 6-9 →

title: Exodus 22: The Civil Laws of Restitution
text: ← Exodus 18-21 · Exodus Study · Exodus 26-29 → Exodus 22: The Civil Laws of Restitution Read the chapter → Exodus 22 Introduction This reading covers Exodus 22 through 25: the civil laws of restitution, the laws of righteous judgment and the three feasts in the year, the blood of the covenant sworn at Sinai, and the pattern of the tabernacle with the ark, the table, and the candlestick. The session opens on Matthew 5:17, that Christ came not to destroy the law but to fulfil, so the mind is right going into the reading: these laws still apply, though some are in a different form or in suspension because of the captivity and because of what Christ took away. Exodus 22:1 - If a man steal an ox or a sheep and kill it or sell it, he restores five oxen for an ox and four sheep for a sheep. We are in a different situation where we do not keep oxen and sheep, but the principle of restitution still applies among brothers and sisters in the body: if something is stolen, the law written here governs the payback. Do not be stealing. Precepts: - Matthew 5:17-18 Christ came not to destroy the law or the prophets but to fulfil; not one jot or tittle passes from the law till all be fulfilled. Exodus 22:2-4 - If a thief be found breaking up means breaking in. He entered your home and you defended yourself and he died: that is what is called self-defense today, and no blood is shed for him, meaning there is no judgment. The judgment was already passed in the breaking in. - If the sun be risen upon him, the thief got away, and there shall be blood shed for him means there shall be a judgment; then the verse gives the judgment. He makes full restitution, and if he have nothing he is sold for his theft: not sold into slavery, but into work servitude until he pays off the debt of what he stole. - If the theft be found in his hand alive, he restores double. Verse three covers the thief who already got rid of what he stole; verse four covers the one still holding it. Exodus 22:5-6 - These are self-explanatory: if a man lets his beast feed in another man's field or vineyard, he makes restitution of the best of his own field and vineyard; and he that kindles a fire that consumes another man's corn surely makes restitution. Exodus 22:7-9 - If a man deliver money or stuff to his neighbor to keep and it be stolen, the thief found pays double. If the thief be not found, the master of the house is brought unto the judges, to see whether he put his hand unto his neighbor's goods, whether he was part of a scheme to deceive the owner out of his goods. - For all manner of trespass, whether for ox, ass, sheep, raiment, or any lost thing, both parties come before the judges, and whom the judges condemn pays double unto his neighbor. Exodus 22:10-11 - If a beast delivered to a neighbor to keep die or be hurt or driven away, no man seeing it, an oath of the Lord is between them both. In layman's terms he swears: I did not take the stuff, I did not set you up, I do not know where it is. The owner accepts the oath and the matter ends there; it is not to be spoken of again. - Paul uses this civil law to show how the Most High is unchangeable. An oath for confirmation is the end of all strife; God confirmed his counsel by an oath, and by two immutable things, that it is impossible for God to lie and that he will not take back what went out of his mouth, we have strong consolation. The same way, once the oath of this law is applied, the matter is over. Precepts: - Hebrews 6:16-18 An oath for confirmation is to men an end of all strife; God, willing to shew unto the heirs of promise the immutability of his counsel, confirmed it by an oath. Exodus 22:12-15 - If the thing kept be stolen from him, he makes restitution; if it be torn in pieces, he brings it for witness and does not make it good. - If a man borrow ought of his neighbor, ought meaning anything, and it be hurt or die with the owner not present, he surely makes it good. You borrowed it, it got messed up, you owe the man. - But if the owner be with it, or if it be an hired thing, it came for its hire. If you came to plow a man's field for ten shekels with your own donkey and your donkey breaks his leg, you cannot expect the owner to pay for your own faulty equipment; the same as a business loan today, the property owner is not liable when your own equipment breaks down. Exodus 22:16-17 - If a man entice a maid that is not betrothed and lie with her, he shall surely endow her to be his wife; he has to sign the papers. He is at fault for not going through the proper channels of marriage, and she is at fault for being enticed and laying down. - The proper channel was that the father married off the daughter. To marry thy daughter is to perform a weighty matter, for the father gives her over to that man for the rest of her life and is out of all watching over her; so she is to be given to a man of understanding, one keeping the commandments as a wise man. In our own land the daughter went from her father's house to a husband's house with the blessing of the father. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 7:25 Marrying off the daughter was the father's weighty matter; she was given to a man of understanding. - If her father utterly refuse to give her unto him, he does not agree with the backdoor marriage, the man still pays money according to the dowry of virgins. Genesis 34 gives the example with Dinah: Shechem and his father Hamor begged Jacob for her and offered never so much dowry, for Shechem understood the union was not supposed to take place, the Hebrews with the Hamites. - The dowry of virgins was fifty shekels of silver, paid by the man who laid hold on a damsel not betrothed, and she became his wife whom he could not put away all his days. And if a husband afterward brought up an evil name upon a virgin of Israel, saying he found her not a maid, the tokens of her virginity, the cloth from the bedchamber her father kept, were spread before the elders; the man was chastised and amerced in an hundred shekels of silver for the false report. Precepts: - Genesis 34:11-12 Shechem offered never so much dowry and gift for Dinah; the dowry stood even where the union was wrong. - Deuteronomy 22:28-29 The man that lay with a damsel not betrothed gave her father fifty shekels of silver, and she became his wife; that is the dowry of virgins. - Deuteronomy 22:17-19 The tokens of virginity were spread before the elders, and the man that brought up an evil name on a virgin of Israel was amerced in an hundred shekels of silver. Exodus 22:18-20 - Thou shalt not suffer a witch to live: witchcraft goes into horoscopes, palm readings, and all things of that nature. - Whosoever lieth with a beast, bestiality, shall surely be put to death. - He that sacrificeth unto any god save unto the Lord only shall be utterly destroyed. Exodus 22:21 - This is twofold, and first and foremost the stranger is your brother from a different area, our own people. Leviticus 25 shows it: if thy brother be waxen poor, though he be a stranger or a sojourner, sojourn meaning travel, thou shalt relieve him that he may live with thee. A brother of another tribe who falls on hard times and travels down to live with you is that stranger; neither vex him nor oppress him, for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt. Precepts: - Leviticus 25:35-37 If thy brother be waxen poor, though he be a stranger or a sojourner, relieve him; take no usury of him, and lend him not thy victuals for increase. Exodus 22:22-24 - Ye shall not afflict any widow or fatherless child. A wife without a husband already has a hard life, and a son or daughter without a father the same; do not make their life harder than it already is. - If thou afflict them in any wise and they cry unto the Most High, he will surely hear their cry, and his wrath shall wax hot: he will kill you with the sword, and your own wives shall be widows and your children fatherless. That is the Lord's plain warning against mistreating those less fortunate. Exodus 22:25 - Usury means interest. You cannot charge your brother or sister interest: if you lend twenty dollars, you get twenty dollars back, nothing more, nothing less; no little bit more off the top. This is the same law read in Leviticus 25:36-37. Exodus 22:26-27 - If thou take thy neighbor's raiment to pledge, deliver it unto him by that the sun goeth down, for that is his covering only; wherein shall he sleep? The tunics and overcoats worn then were also sleeping garments to keep a man warm at night, especially the poor. - A well-off man does not have to work for you; this speaks of the less fortunate who extend their services for money and give what is most valuable to them, their raiment, as the pledge. If he cries unto the Most High, he will hear, for he is gracious. Exodus 22:28 - Thou shalt not revile the gods means do not hate or speak evil of your leaders. The word gods here is the leaders over you: the Most High says in the psalm, I have said, Ye are gods, and all of you are children of the Most High, speaking of us. - Acts 23 is the example: when Paul spoke against the high priest, they that stood by said, Revilest thou God's high priest? And Paul answered, I wist not, brethren, that he was the high priest: for it is written, Thou shalt not speak evil of the ruler of thy people, quoting this very verse. Precepts: - Psalms 82:5-6 They know not, neither will they understand; I have said, Ye are gods, and all of you are children of the Most High. - Acts 23:1-5 Paul, rebuked for reviling God's high priest, cited this law: it is written, Thou shalt not speak evil of the ruler of thy people. Exodus 22:29-30 - Thou shalt not delay to offer the first of thy ripe fruits and of thy liquors, and the firstborn of thy sons shalt thou give unto me. The firstborn sons that opened the matrix were consecrated unto the Lord, and the father redeemed them back from the priest with shekels. - Likewise with the oxen and the sheep: seven days the firstling stayed with his dam, his mother, and on the eighth day it was given. The Lord did not want it too young, taken as soon as it popped out; it had to be its appointed time with the mother, then brought to the priest. Exodus 22:31 - Ye shall be holy men unto me: neither shall ye eat any flesh that is torn of beasts in the field; ye shall cast it to the dogs. This is twofold, and the dogs are the strangers of other nations, the aliens and foreigners. - Always get the context of the law, because sometimes the stranger is your brother and sometimes it is literally the other nations. Deuteronomy 14:21 doubles this law: that which dieth of itself thou shalt give unto the stranger that is in thy gates, or sell it unto an alien, for thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God. Cast the torn flesh to the other nations; ye shall not eat it, because ye are holy people. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 14:21 That which dieth of itself is given to the stranger in thy gates or sold to an alien; thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God. Exodus 23: Righteous Judgment, the Three Feasts, and the Angel of the Covenant Read the chapter → Exodus 23 Exodus 23:1-2 - Thou shalt not raise a false report, nor put thine hand with the wicked to be an unrighteous witness: basically, thou shalt not lie. If you did not see it, do not make up a story like you were there; keep your mouth shut. - Thou shalt not follow a multitude to do evil. Enter not into the path of the wicked; sinners entice, saying come with us, cast in thy lot among us, but walk not thou in the way with them, for their feet run to evil and make haste to shed blood. Many of our young men's lives end short because they follow a multitude to do evil. To be in the midst of the singing, like the whole school hollering fight, fight, fight, is to be in the multitude the Most High warns of; a soul without knowledge of the laws of God hastes with his feet and sins. Precepts: - Proverbs 4:14-17 Enter not into the path of the wicked; they sleep not except they have done mischief, and they drink the wine of violence. - Proverbs 1:10-15 If sinners entice thee, consent thou not; walk not thou in the way with them, for their feet run to evil. - Proverbs 19:2 That the soul be without knowledge, it is not good; and he that hasteth with his feet sinneth. - Isaiah 59:6-7 The works of sinners are works of iniquity; their feet run to evil, and they make haste to shed innocent blood. - Neither shalt thou speak in a cause to decline after many to wrest judgment: once the judgment has been passed by the leaders, do not speak out against it to sway people's opinion in a different direction. The judgment is God's; whoever sits in leadership, at the end of the day it comes from the Most High, so to sway people against it is to go against God. When a Romans 16:17 marking is put out in your congregation, follow it, because it ultimately comes from God. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 1:17 Ye shall not be afraid of the face of man, for the judgment is God's. - Romans 16:17 Mark them which cause divisions and offences contrary to the doctrine, and avoid them; once put out, that judgment is followed. Exodus 23:3 - Neither shalt thou countenance a poor man in his cause. This deals with judgment: do not be a respecter of persons because a man is poor, as if he is automatically wrong when he brings a matter against a rich man. The judges were charged to hear the small as well as the great. - In this corrupt system in Babylon, how innocent or guilty you come out depends on how much lawyer you can afford. Our law was holy and righteous because none of that made a difference: either you were right or you were wrong, whether poor or rich. The Pharisees learned the ways of the heathen and began respecting persons, which the book of James speaks against. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 1:16-17 Judge righteously between every man and his brother; ye shall not respect persons in judgment, but hear the small as well as the great. Exodus 23:4-5 - If thou meet thine enemy's ox or his ass going astray, thou shalt surely bring it back to him again; if thou see the ass of him that hateth thee lying under his burden, thou shalt surely help with him. This enemy that hates you is your brother, your own nation, not the other nations as Matthew 5:44 is misconstrued to mean. - Deuteronomy 22:1-4 proves it, saying the same law with thy brother in the place of thine enemy: thou shalt not see thy brother's ox or sheep go astray; in any case, no matter how you feel, bring them again unto thy brother. And if thou know him not, keep it in thine own house until thy brother seek after it. He is still your brother even if you never grew up with him; that is real love for your own people. - Deuteronomy means the second law; it speaks the law plain in case you did not understand it here. Keep Deuteronomy 22:1-4 and Leviticus 19:17-18 in your hip pocket with this verse. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 22:1-4 Thou shalt not see thy brother's ox go astray and hide thyself; in any case bring it again to thy brother, even a brother thou knowest not, and help him lift his ass or his ox when it is fallen. - Leviticus 19:17-18 Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart, nor bear grudge against the children of thy people, but love thy neighbour as thyself. - Matthew 5:44 Love your enemies: read with Exodus 23:4-5 and Deuteronomy 22:1-4, the enemy to be loved and helped is the brother of thine own nation that hates thee. Exodus 23:6-8 - Thou shalt not wrest the judgment of thy poor in his cause: verse six explains verse three again in case you did not catch it, do not be partial in judgment. - Keep thee far from a false matter; the innocent and righteous slay thou not, for the Most High will not justify the wicked. - Thou shalt take no gift, for the gift blindeth the wise and perverteth the words of the righteous: do not take a bribe when it comes to judgment; be upright and honest. Exodus 23:9 - Also thou shalt not oppress a stranger, for ye know the heart of a stranger, seeing ye were strangers in the land of Egypt. This is speaking about us, as Exodus 22:21 already laid out with Leviticus 25:35. Exodus 23:10-11 - Six years thou shalt sow thy land, but the seventh year thou shalt let it rest and lie still, that the poor of thy people may eat, and the beasts of the field after them; likewise the vineyard and the oliveyard. That is mercy from the Lord: in the seventh year the land itself fed the poor. - The seventh year ties into the count of the jubilee: seven sabbaths of years to the forty-ninth year, and in the fiftieth year no plowing of the land, which the law takes up later. Exodus 23:12 - Six days do thy work, and on the seventh day rest, that thine ox and thine ass may rest, and the son of thy handmaid and the stranger may be refreshed. The stranger here can be another nation working for you: they too get their due rest on the sabbath. - When the Lord sets Israel back up to rule, the nations will kick and scream at first, but once these laws are applied there will be righteousness reigning over the earth like they have never seen, and all will be refreshed on the sabbath, spiritually and physically. Exodus 23:13 - Make no mention of the name of other gods is not saying you cannot pronounce the names Buddha, Allah, Krishna, Ra. Christ himself named Beelzebub, the chief of the devils, a name derived from the Philistine god of Ekron, and Christ did no sin; so the verse cannot mean the bare saying of a name. - The Lord says this same thing three ways in this one chapter, and the other two places show the meaning: verse 24, thou shalt not bow down to their gods nor serve them nor do after their works; and verses 32 and 33, thou shalt make no covenant with them nor with their gods, for if thou serve their gods it will surely be a snare unto thee. Make no mention means do not learn how to serve and worship them. - Joshua and Deuteronomy double it: neither make mention of the name of their gods, nor cause to swear by them, neither serve them, nor bow yourselves unto them; and if thy brother or son or wife entice thee secretly, saying, Let us go and serve other gods, thou shalt not consent. Wherever you are, do not go trying to find out how the nations worship their gods. Precepts: - Matthew 12:25-27 Christ said, If I by Beelzebub cast out devils, by whom do your children cast them out? He mentioned the name of another god and did no sin. - Joshua 23:6-8 Neither make mention of the name of their gods, nor cause to swear by them, neither serve them, nor bow yourselves unto them, but cleave unto the Lord your God. - Deuteronomy 13:6-8 If thy nearest kin entice thee secretly, saying, Let us go and serve other gods, thou shalt not consent unto him nor hearken unto him. Exodus 23:14-17 - Three times thou shalt keep a feast unto me in the year: all the males appeared before the Lord God three times in the year. - The feast of unleavened bread is the Passover, kept in the time appointed of the month Abib, the first month of the year, as it is written, the feast of unleavened bread drew nigh, which is called the Passover. - None shall appear before me empty: you could not come empty-handed. You brought the tenth of your oil, your wine, whatever was required, for the priests to replenish the storehouses. - The feast of harvest, the firstfruits of thy labours, is also known as Pentecost and the feast of weeks; and the feast of ingathering, in the end of the year, is also known as the feast of tabernacles and the feast of booths. Precepts: - Luke 22:1 The feast of unleavened bread drew nigh, which is called the Passover; the two names are one feast. Exodus 23:18-19 - Thou shalt not offer the blood of my sacrifice with leavened bread, neither shall the fat of my sacrifice remain until the morning. The first of the firstfruits of thy land thou shalt bring into the house of the Lord thy God. - Thou shalt not seethe a kid in his mother's milk: the Lord repeats what was read at Exodus 22:30, that the young one was not to be taken too young and too soon; it stayed its seven days with his dam before it was given. Exodus 23:20-22 - Behold, I send an Angel before thee, to keep thee in the way and to bring thee into the place which I have prepared. Beware of him, obey his voice, provoke him not, for he will not pardon your transgressions: for my name is in him. That Angel is speaking of Christ. - If thou indeed obey his voice, I will be an enemy unto thine enemies and an adversary unto thine adversaries. These enemies are not the same enemy of verse four: the enemy of verse four is your brother whom you must help and shew mercy; these enemies in verse 22 the Lord himself deals with and destroys for you. Exodus 23:23-31 - The Angel goes before Israel unto the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites, and Jebusites, to cut them off. Thou shalt not bow down to their gods nor serve them nor do after their works, but utterly overthrow them and quite break down their images. - Serve the Lord your God, and he shall bless thy bread and thy water, take sickness away from the midst of thee, none casting their young nor barren in the land, and the number of thy days he will fulfil. He drives the nations out by little and little, lest the land become desolate and the beasts multiply, until Israel be increased and inherit the land. - The bounds are set from the Red Sea even unto the sea of the Philistines, and from the desert unto the river, the river Euphrates. That little sliver on the map today is not how big Israel is supposed to be: the land was to encompass all the way out to the Euphrates by Babylon, taking in parts of what is Iraq and Iran, and it will be filled one day. Exodus 23:32-33 - Thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor with their gods. They shall not dwell in thy land, lest they make thee sin against me: for if thou serve their gods, it will surely be a snare unto thee. This is the third way the Lord states the command of verse 13 in this chapter: no learning their worship, no serving, no covenant. Exodus 24: The Blood of the Covenant Read the chapter → Exodus 24 Exodus 24:1-3 - Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel were called up to worship afar off, and Moses alone came near the Lord. - Moses told the people all the words of the Lord and all the judgments, and all the people answered with one voice: All the words which the Lord hath said will we do. That was us making a verbal agreement with the Lord; we are our ancestors back on the earth again. - All the hell we catch today, we have no excuse for: it is our fault, because we agreed to do all the words the Lord had spoken. The Lord hates for us to go through it, but where he said all of this would come back on us, God is not a man that he should lie. Exodus 24:4-8 - Moses wrote all the words of the Lord, rose up early, and builded an altar under the hill with twelve pillars according to the twelve tribes of Israel; young men offered burnt offerings and peace offerings of oxen. - Moses took half of the blood in basons and half he sprinkled on the altar; then he took the book of the covenant and read in the audience of the people, and they said, All that the Lord hath said will we do, and be obedient. And he sprinkled the blood on the people: Behold the blood of the covenant, which the Lord hath made with you concerning all these words. This sprinkling ties in later to the book of Hebrews and its teaching on sacrifice. - Notice verse seven: Moses had a book of the covenant written and read it before he ever went up into the mount for the forty days. It was more than ten commandments; a whole book of what was to be done was already broken down before he went up. - Because we swore the oath, all we can do now is pray the Lord have mercy on us and return to redeem us from those that hate us. Exodus 24:9-11 - Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and the seventy elders went up, and they saw the God of Israel: under his feet as it were a paved work of a sapphire stone, and as it were the body of heaven in his clearness. Sapphire is blue, and the blue flame is the hottest part of a flame. - Upon the nobles of the children of Israel he laid not his hand: also they saw God, and did eat and drink. Since no man hath seen God at any time, the one they saw and ate before was Christ, who is called the mighty God and the everlasting Father. - Paul confirms it: all our fathers were under the cloud and passed through the sea, and they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them, and that Rock was Christ. The Corinthians Paul wrote were Israelites, for Greece was not even a power on the earth in Moses' day. It was Christ dealing with Israel in the wilderness on behalf of the Most High. Precepts: - Isaiah 9:6-7 Unto us a child is born, and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace. - 1 Corinthians 10:1-4 All our fathers were under the cloud and drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them, and that Rock was Christ. Exodus 24:12 - The Lord said, Come up to me into the mount, and I will give thee tables of stone, and a law, and commandments which I have written, that thou mayest teach them. This lets you know the law and the commandments are one and the same; Christianity tries to separate the law from the commandments, but the commandment is a lamp and the law is light, lamp and light, one and the same. These are the things you build your faith on, tearing down imaginations in the minds of our people with the word of God. Precepts: - Proverbs 6:23 The commandment is a lamp, and the law is light; commandments and law are one and the same. Exodus 24:13-18 - Moses rose up with his minister Joshua and went up into the mount of God, leaving Aaron and Hur with the elders for any matters. A cloud covered the mount, the glory of the Lord abode upon Sinai six days, and on the seventh day he called unto Moses out of the midst of the cloud. - The sight of the glory of the Lord was like devouring fire on the top of the mount in the eyes of the children of Israel; and Moses was in the mount forty days and forty nights. - If you have been actively listening: Moses already had the book of the covenant written before he went up. In the forty days and forty nights he came down with even more; it was never just the ten commandments. Exodus 25: The Pattern of the Tabernacle Read the chapter → Exodus 25 Exodus 25:1-2 - Speak unto the children of Israel, that they bring me an offering: of every man that giveth it willingly with his heart ye shall take my offering. The Lord wants a willing heart in giving, not grudgingly or of necessity or only because the law says so, but because you know your giving benefits someone in need or the house of God, whatever it needs, the lights, the roof, the floor, the tables, the leadership's travel. Exodus 25:3-7 - The offering was gold, silver, brass, blue, purple, and scarlet, fine linen, goats' hair, rams' skins dyed red, badgers' skins, shittim wood, oil for the light, spices, and onyx stones for the ephod and the breastplate. Thank the Most High he requires no gold and silver now, for half of us would have nothing to give; under the new covenant the offering is the body presented a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable. - The badgers' skins settle a confusion: the Lord commanded Israel to handle animal skins and hair to build his own tabernacle. So the laws about not touching that which is defiled, the carcass of the unclean beast, go into the matter of sacrifice and coming into the temple, not into everyday handling. A boar-bristle brush is not sin; brush your hair, brothers. Precepts: - Romans 12:1 Present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God; that is the offering of him that has no gold nor silver. Exodus 25:8-9 - Let them make me a sanctuary, that I may dwell among them. According to all that I shew thee, after the pattern of the tabernacle and the pattern of all the instruments thereof, even so shall ye make it. Shew is the old English; everything was built after the pattern the Lord shewed. Exodus 25:10-16 - The ark of shittim wood: two cubits and a half the length, a cubit and a half the breadth and the height. A cubit as we know it is about eighteen inches, and it differed with the size of men in each time; when men were bigger the cubit was bigger. - It was overlaid with pure gold within and without, with a crown of gold round about, four rings of gold in the corners, and staves of shittim wood overlaid with gold to bear it; the staves were not to be taken from it. And into the ark was put the testimony which the Lord gave. Exodus 25:17-22 - The mercy seat of pure gold sat above upon the ark, with two cherubims of gold of beaten work on the two ends, stretching forth their wings on high, covering the mercy seat, their faces one to another looking toward the mercy seat. - There I will meet with thee, and I will commune with thee from above the mercy seat, from between the two cherubims which are upon the ark of the testimony, of all things which I will give thee in commandment unto the children of Israel. Exodus 25:23-30 - The table of shittim wood was overlaid with pure gold, with a crown of gold round about: the crown is the molding going around the table, like the crown molding some have in their houses today. It bore the dishes, spoons, covers, and bowls, all of pure gold, and the shewbread was set upon it before the Lord alway. - Understand how we lived: in our kingdom everything was overlaid with pure gold, clean and royal, with the order of kings, priests, counsellors, and the royal garments. Some nations do a good job in their films of bringing their old royal culture to remembrance for their people; that order and gold is how Israel used to live, and we are going back to it. Exodus 25:31-40 - The candlestick of pure gold is the menorah, one beaten work: his shaft, his branches, his bowls, his knops, and his flowers of the same. Six branches come out of the sides of it, three out of the one side and three out of the other, with the shaft in the middle: seven lamps in all. - A ten-candle candlestick is not the pattern given of God; the scripture gives seven, one in the middle and three coming out on each side, with bowls made like unto almonds with a knop and a flower. - The seven lamps were lit that they may give light over against it: it was not small, for it had to light up a whole section of the tabernacle. The tongs and the snuffdishes were of pure gold, of a talent of pure gold, and all these vessels were made after the pattern shewed in the mount. --- Topics: Clean and Unclean Meats · Idolatry · Sacrifice and Atonement · The Covenant · The Feasts of the Most High · The Priesthood · The Sabbath ← Exodus 18-21 · Exodus Study · Exodus 26-29 →

title: Exodus 26: The Pattern Shown in the Mount
text: ← Exodus 22-25 · Exodus Study · Exodus 30-33 → Exodus 26: The Pattern Shown in the Mount Read the chapter → Exodus 26 Introduction This reading covers Exodus 26 through 29: the curtains, boards, and veil of the tabernacle; the brasen altar, the court, and the oil for the lamp; the holy garments of Aaron the high priest; and the consecration of Aaron and his sons in the priest's office. This is a reading session; the chapters are read straight through with teaching at the key points, and the first two chapters move quickly since the tabernacle furniture was covered in the previous session on chapter 25. The recording begins in the middle of Exodus 26, at the comment on the cubit in verse 2, so the opening of the session is not on the tape. Exodus 26:1-6 - The ten curtains of the tabernacle are measured in cubits. A cubit is approximately eighteen inches when you look it up today, and it was probably bigger, because the men were of larger stature back then. - The curtains of fine twined linen with blue, purple, and scarlet are coupled with loops and taches of gold, that it may be one tabernacle. Exodus 26:7-14 - Eleven curtains of goats' hair cover the tabernacle, with a covering of rams' skins dyed red above, and a covering above that of badgers' skins. - The badgers' skins settle a doctrine question. Leviticus 11 says not to touch the carcase of the unclean beast, and the badger goes on paws, yet the tabernacle had to be built with badger skins by hand. The law goes into sacrificing the unclean thing and eating it, touching it with your mouth; it is not saying a dead animal in your path cannot be moved out of the way with your hands. Precepts: - Leviticus 11:8 The carcase not to be touched is spoken of the beasts as food; the command sits in the dietary law. - Leviticus 11:27 Whatsoever goeth upon his paws is unclean, which is what makes the badger an unclean beast. Exodus 26:15-30 - The boards of shittim wood, the sockets of silver, and the bars overlaid with gold are the physical structure of the tabernacle, how it would be put together and what it would consist of. - Rear up the tabernacle according to the fashion thereof which was shewed thee in the mount. The Most High showed Moses all of this in mount Sinai; the forty days and forty nights were not the ten commandments alone, Moses came down with a whole architectural layout based on what the Most High showed him. - What was built in the wilderness was a shadow of what is in the heavens. The Most High is the architect, and He showed Moses the pattern of a heavenly tabernacle to be made for Israel on earth; thy kingdom come, thy will be done in earth as it is in heaven, is an example of that same order. Precepts: - Hebrews 8:5 The priests serve unto the example and shadow of heavenly things, as Moses was admonished to make all things according to the pattern shewed to thee in the mount. - Matthew 6:10 Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven; the tabernacle on earth answered to the heavenly. Exodus 26:31-37 - The veil of blue, purple, and scarlet with cherubims divides between the holy place and the most holy; the ark of the testimony with the mercy seat goes within the veil, the table on the north side and the candlestick toward the south without it. - The Most High specifically included purple in the design of His heavenly tabernacle that was meant for us on earth; the color men talk down on today is a color the Most High chose for His own house. Exodus 27: The Altar, the Court, and the Oil for the Lamp Read the chapter → Exodus 27 Exodus 27:1-8 - Verses one through eight go into the altar in which the sacrifices were done in the tabernacle: the altar of shittim wood foursquare, its horns of the same, overlaid with brass, with its pans, shovels, basons, fleshhooks, and firepans, the grate of network of brass, and the staves to bear it. - As it was shewed thee in the mount, so shall they make it; the altar too follows the pattern. Exodus 27:9-19 - The court of the tabernacle: hangings of fine twined linen an hundred cubits on the south and north sides, fifty on the west and east, with pillars filleted with silver in sockets of brass, and the gate of the court a hanging of blue, purple, and scarlet wrought with needlework. The length of the court a hundred cubits, the breadth fifty every where, the height five cubits, and all the pins of brass. Exodus 27:20-21 - The Most High tells Moses to command the children of Israel to bring pure oil olive beaten for the light, to cause the lamp to burn always; Aaron and his sons order it from evening to morning before the Lord, a statute for ever unto their generations. - Though Israel is in captivity now without a temple, without lamps to bring oil for, and no longer under the Levitical priesthood, think about it spiritually: you have to keep your lamp lit and keep the oil in your life. Brotherhood and unity, and correction, which is an excellent oil that shall not break the head, are that oil; if you are not around a body being built up and corrected by teachers and peers, that is how people run out of oil, their lamp goes out, and they fall out of this truth and do not endure to the end. The ten virgins with their lamps and oil come to mind here, offered as a meditation. Precepts: - Leviticus 24:1-4 The same command word for word: pure oil olive beaten for the light, the lamps ordered from evening unto morning before the Lord continually, a statute for ever. - Psalms 133:1 Behold how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity; the brotherhood that keeps the oil in your life. - Psalms 141:5 Let the righteous smite me, it shall be an excellent oil which shall not break my head; correction is oil for the lamp. Exodus 28: Holy Garments for Glory and for Beauty Read the chapter → Exodus 28 Exodus 28:1-2 - Aaron and his sons Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar are taken from among the children of Israel to minister unto the Most High in the priest's office. - The Most High commanded holy garments to be made for Aaron for glory and for beauty. Garments were ordained for the men of Israel; when the world hears Deuteronomy 22:5 and asks why the men wear garments, the answer is here: the most holy and regarded men of the nation, the priests, were arrayed in long garments down to the foot. - The sealed of the Lord receive the same. The hundred forty and four thousand of Revelation 7 that must be sealed before destruction comes are read of again in 2 Esdras: they departed from the shadow of the world, leaving spiritual Egypt and the ways Babylon taught behind, and have received glorious garments of the Lord. In the kingdom of heaven the Most High will clothe His men in glorious garments as in ancient times, on another level than anything worn today. Precepts: - 1 Esdras 1:2 The priests were arrayed in long garments; old history of the garments ordained for the men. - 2 Esdras 2:38-39 The sealed that departed from the shadow of the world receive glorious garments of the Lord. - Revelation 7:4 The number of the sealed, an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel; the same company 2 Esdras 2 describes. Exodus 28:3 - Only the wise hearted, whom the Most High filled with the spirit of wisdom, could make Aaron's garments. The garment is heavenly, mapped out for Moses to create on earth; the Lord had to be dealing with a man in a certain way, putting the spirit within him, for him to be able to create that glory and beauty. It cannot be duplicated. Exodus 28:4-5 - The garments to be made: a breastplate, an ephod, a robe, a broidered coat, a mitre, and a girdle, holy garments for Aaron and his sons to minister in the priest's office. - The Most High is the fashion designer of Israel. He clothed Israel with broidered work, badgers' skin, fine linen and silk, decked His people with ornaments, bracelets, chains, jewels, earrings, and a beautiful crown; Israel prospered into a kingdom, and its renown went forth among the heathen for its beauty, for it was perfect through the comeliness the Most High put upon them. Israel was the standard of beauty and fashion among the nations, and no brand name of today can touch what the Most High designed. Precepts: - Ezekiel 16:10-14 Clothed with broidered work, shod with badgers' skin, decked with gold and silver; Israel prospered into a kingdom and was renowned among the heathen for beauty, perfect through His comeliness. Exodus 28:6-12 - The ephod of gold, of blue, purple, scarlet, and fine twined linen with cunning work, joined at the two shoulderpieces with its curious girdle of the same. - Two onyx stones are engraved with the names of the children of Israel, six names on one stone and six on the other according to their birth, set in ouches of gold upon the shoulders of the ephod; Aaron bare the names of the tribes before the Lord upon his two shoulders for a memorial. Exodus 28:13-21 - The breastplate of judgment, foursquare and doubled, of the same gold, blue, purple, scarlet, and fine twined linen as the ephod, is set with four rows of precious stones enclosed in gold: sardius, topaz, carbuncle; emerald, sapphire, diamond; ligure, agate, amethyst; beryl, onyx, jasper. - The twelve stones are with the names of the children of Israel, every one engraved like a signet according to the twelve tribes; as with the shoulder stones, the nation is written on the priest. - The Wisdom of Solomon says of this garment that in the long garment was the whole world, and in the four rows of the stones was the glory of the fathers. There was no Moabite stone, Jebusite stone, or Edomite stone in it; the whole world in the garment is the twelve tribes of Israel, and the glory of the fathers is written in their stones. - That settles 1 John 2:2 for the Christians who run to it. John was a Jew of the southern kingdom, so our sins means the southern kingdom; and not for ours only but also for the sins of the whole world means all twelve tribes, the whole world of Israel. Alongside Isaiah 45:17 and John 18:20, Wisdom of Solomon 18:24 is the precept that shows who the whole world is. Precepts: - Wisdom of Solomon 18:24 In the long garment was the whole world; the four rows of stones bearing the twelve tribes are called the whole world and the glory of the fathers. - 1 John 2:2 The propitiation for our sins, the southern kingdom, and also for the sins of the whole world, all twelve tribes of Israel. - Isaiah 45:17 Israel shall be saved in the Lord with an everlasting salvation; salvation is spoken to Israel. - John 18:20 Christ spake openly to the world, in the synagogue and in the temple, whither the Jews always resort; the world he spoke to was Israel. Exodus 28:22-29 - Chains of wreathen work of pure gold and rings of gold fasten the breastplate to the ephod with a lace of blue, that the breastplate be not loosed from the ephod. - Aaron shall bear the names of the children of Israel in the breastplate of judgment upon his heart when he goeth in unto the holy place, for a memorial before the Lord continually. The Most High was all about His nation being represented: put Israel on your chest when you go into the temple. Exodus 28:30 - The Urim and the Thummim go in the breastplate of judgment, upon Aaron's heart before the Lord; Aaron bears the judgment of the children of Israel upon his heart continually. - Urim and Thummim means lights and perfections: objects not specifically described in the scriptures, perhaps stones since they went in the breastplate, by which the high priest ascertained the will of the Most High in important matters affecting the nation. To ascertain is to find out for certain, a divine discerning beyond what a man can determine by his own thinking. - One theory holds they were cast as lots, but the apostles, who were not dealing with the Levitical priesthood, cast lots between Joseph called Barsabas and Matthias without any Urim and Thummim, which is an issue with that theory. The better theory: they served as a symbol of the high priest's authority to seek counsel of the Most High, His will being revealed to him through inner illumination. - The significance shows in Nehemiah's day: priests whose register was not found among those reckoned by genealogy were put from the priesthood as polluted, and the Tirshatha, who is Nehemiah the governor, said they should not eat of the most holy things till there stood up a priest with Urim and with Thummim; determining that lineage was outside human ability, so it waited on the priest with the divine discerner. - Joshua likewise was to stand before Eleazar the priest, who shall ask counsel for him after the judgment of Urim before the Lord; the Most High gave revelation through it. Precepts: - Leviticus 8:6-8 At the consecration Moses put the ephod and breastplate on Aaron, and he put in the breastplate the Urim and the Thummim. - Acts 1:23-26 The apostles cast lots between Joseph called Barsabas and Matthias, and the lot fell upon Matthias; lots were cast without the Urim and Thummim. - Nehemiah 7:63-65 Priests not found in the register were put from the priesthood as polluted, and were not to eat of the most holy things till there stood up a priest with Urim and Thummim. - Numbers 27:21 Joshua shall stand before Eleazar the priest, who shall ask counsel for him after the judgment of Urim before the Lord. Exodus 28:31-35 - The robe of the ephod all of blue, with a bound hole for the head that it be not rent, and upon the hem pomegranates of blue, purple, and scarlet round about, with bells of gold between them: a golden bell and a pomegranate round about the hem. - The bells meant the high priest could be heard: his sound shall be heard when he goeth in unto the holy place before the Lord, and when he cometh out, that he die not. That was serious; the Most High does not play about His instructions, and the noisy fringe was ordained on pain of death. Exodus 28:36-38 - A plate of pure gold engraved like a signet, HOLINESS TO THE LORD, on a blue lace upon the forefront of the mitre, always upon Aaron's forehead, that Aaron may bear the iniquity of the holy things of the children of Israel and that they may be accepted before the Lord. - No man today needs to walk around in a mitre bearing iniquity and claiming a high priest's office. Christ bore our iniquities and did that work; the priesthood has changed, which is why Paul wrote what he wrote in 1 Corinthians 11. Wearing it on your own time as heritage is one thing, but when you are dealing with the scriptures, teaching, reading, studying, or praying, take it off; that is not your office. Precepts: - 1 Corinthians 11:4 Every man praying or prophesying having his head covered dishonoureth his head; the priesthood that wore the mitre has changed. Exodus 28:39-43 - The broidered coat of fine linen, the mitre of fine linen, and the girdle of needlework; and for Aaron's sons coats, girdles, and bonnets, for glory and for beauty, to be anointed and consecrated in. - Linen breeches to cover their nakedness, from the loins even unto the thighs, upon Aaron and his sons when they come near the altar to minister, that they bear not iniquity and die: a statute for ever unto him and his seed after him. - Breeches are pants; the grandmothers of the south said pull your britches up, and the hosen of Daniel 3 is defined with one word, pants. This is where pants were ordained in the scriptures, and the statute for ever means that from beginning to end of time pants were created for men, period. Women are not to wear what pertaineth unto a man. - Why they would bear iniquity without the breeches: before the breeches were instituted, going up by steps unto the altar would have discovered their nakedness, so the Most High commanded the covering. - Ecclesiasticus gives the second account of these garments and confirms the breeches under the robe of glory. It also shows the pomegranates and bells compassed him, all around the hem and not four corners only, and that the crown of gold sat upon the mitre before Israel had any kings, because mediator between the Most High and His people is the highest honor; for the brothers given the honor to lead and teach among the nation, do not take it for granted or be slothful in it, for there is nothing more honorable to do on this earth. Precepts: - Daniel 3:21 The three were bound in their coats, their hosen, and their hats; hosen when you look up that word is pants. - Deuteronomy 22:5 The woman shall not wear that which pertaineth unto a man; the breeches were ordained a statute for ever for the men. - Exodus 20:26 Neither go up by steps unto mine altar, that thy nakedness be not discovered thereon; the breeches answered this. - Ecclesiasticus 45:6-13 The second account of Aaron's garments: rich garments with breeches, pomegranates and bells compassing him round about, the whole world in the writing of the tribes, and a crown of gold upon the mitre; no stranger ever put them on. Exodus 29: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons Read the chapter → Exodus 29 Exodus 29:1-4 - To hallow Aaron and his sons to minister in the priest's office: one young bullock and two rams without blemish, with unleavened bread, cakes tempered with oil, and wafers anointed with oil, brought in one basket to the door of the tabernacle of the congregation. - And shalt wash them with water: cleanliness and spotlessness were very important to the Most High in everything dealing with the temple, and He is real specific and detailed about how clean and sanctified a man must be before he enters the holy place. This thread runs all through the first five books, Leviticus especially. Exodus 29:5-9 - The garments are put upon Aaron, the coat, the robe of the ephod, the ephod, and the breastplate, with the curious girdle; the mitre upon his head and the holy crown upon the mitre; the anointing oil poured upon his head; and his sons in coats, girdles, and bonnets. The priest's office shall be theirs for a perpetual statute: thou shalt consecrate Aaron and his sons. - Ecclesiasticus records the same consecration: Moses anointed him with holy oil, an everlasting covenant to Aaron and to his seed so long as the heavens should remain, to minister unto Him, execute the office of the priesthood, offer the sacrifices, and teach Jacob the testimonies and inform Israel in His laws. The priest's job was the offerings and teaching the nation the law, statutes, and commandments. - What happened to that covenant is answered in Malachi, where the commandment is spoken to the priests: the covenant with Levi was of life and peace, the priest's lips should keep knowledge and they should seek the law at his mouth, for he is the messenger of the Lord of hosts; but ye are departed out of the way, ye have caused many to stumble at the law, ye have corrupted the covenant of Levi. The priests were finessing the offerings, keeping the best animals for themselves and sacrificing the blind and the broken, and they perverted the teachings of the law for their own benefit. - That is why leadership today is not walking around requiring Levite lineage of Aaron. Christ is the high priest now, and the nation is a whole nation of kings and priests; Malachi and Hebrews are two good books to study on the changing of the priesthood, against the doctrine that the Aaronic covenant could never change. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 45:15-17 The everlasting covenant of the priesthood with Aaron and his seed: to offer the sacrifices and to teach Jacob the testimonies and inform Israel in His laws. - Malachi 2:1 And now, O ye priests, this commandment is for you; the chapter is spoken to the priests. - Malachi 2:5-8 The covenant with Levi was of life and peace and the priest is the messenger of the Lord of hosts; but ye are departed out of the way, caused many to stumble at the law, and have corrupted the covenant of Levi. Exodus 29:10-14 - The bullock is killed before the Lord by the door of the tabernacle, its blood put upon the horns of the altar with the finger, the fat burnt upon the altar, and the flesh, skin, and dung burnt with fire without the camp: it is a sin offering. This is the introduction to the categories of offerings; there is the sin offering. Exodus 29:15-18 - The first ram is slain, its blood sprinkled round about upon the altar, and the whole ram burnt upon the altar: it is a burnt offering unto the Lord, a sweet savour, an offering made by fire. There is the second category, the burnt offering. Exodus 29:19-28 - The second ram is the ram of consecration: its blood is put upon the tip of the right ear of Aaron and of his sons, upon the thumb of their right hand and the great toe of their right foot, and sprinkled upon the altar round about; the blood and the anointing oil are sprinkled upon Aaron, his garments, his sons, and their garments, and he shall be hallowed. - The bread and the parts of the ram are put in the hands of Aaron and his sons and waved for a wave offering before the Lord, then burnt upon the altar; and the breast of the wave offering and the shoulder of the heave offering are sanctified for Aaron and his sons by a statute for ever. There go the wave offering and the heave offering, which you will read about throughout the first five books, Leviticus predominantly. - These ordinances belonged to the Levitical priesthood, and the doctrines that would put men back under pieces of that office today do not even keep what they claim; they sound right because they use scriptures strongly and confidently, but they are in error. Be not tossed to and fro with every wind of doctrine, nor carried about with strange doctrines; do not ever fall away from the Messiah. Precepts: - Ephesians 4:14 Be no more children tossed to and fro and carried about with every wind of doctrine, by the sleight of men. - Hebrews 13:9 Be not carried about with divers and strange doctrines; the heart is established with grace, not with meats. Exodus 29:29-34 - The holy garments of Aaron pass to his sons after him, to be anointed and consecrated in them; the son that is priest in his stead shall put them on seven days when he cometh into the tabernacle to minister. - Aaron and his sons eat the flesh of the ram and the bread at the door of the tabernacle, the things wherewith the atonement was made; a stranger shall not eat thereof, because they are holy. And whatever of the flesh or the bread remains unto the morning is burnt with fire and not eaten: no eating the leftovers of the offering, because it is holy. Exodus 29:35-42 - Seven days shalt thou consecrate them, offering every day a bullock for a sin offering for atonement, cleansing the altar and anointing it to sanctify it, that it be an altar most holy. - Then the continual offering: two lambs of the first year day by day continually, one lamb in the morning and the other at even, with the tenth deal of flour mingled with beaten oil and the drink offering of wine; a continual burnt offering throughout your generations at the door of the tabernacle, where the Lord meets and speaks with Israel. Exodus 29:43-46 - The tabernacle shall be sanctified by His glory, and Aaron and his sons sanctified to minister in the priest's office; for the Most High to enter and deal with Israel, everything had to be sanctified. That was serious. - I will dwell among the children of Israel, and will be their God. He was in no other nation's tabernacle, temple, or synagogue, and though there is no tabernacle today it is still the same case: He is in the midst of Israel and none else, which excludes everybody else from the benefits of having the Most High as their God. There is nothing to be ashamed of in the fact that He chose Israel only, and nothing changed across testaments: blessed be the Lord God of Israel, for he hath visited and redeemed his people, and that is the purpose of Christ, to redeem His people. - The other nations knew it. When the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin heard the temple was being rebuilt they came saying, Let us build with you, for we seek your God; and Zerubbabel, Jeshua, and the chief of the fathers answered, Ye have nothing to do with us to build an house unto our God, but we ourselves together will build unto the Lord God of Israel. That is the mindset for these last days: Israel does not need the other nations' assistance, but rebuilds one another spiritually as a nation while awaiting Christ's return to restore the kingdom. - He brought them forth out of the land of Egypt that He may dwell among them: I am the Lord their God. Israel should walk confident, special, and chosen above all nations of people, for the Most High is faithful and belongs to no one else; repent from spiritual fornication and return to the Most High. Precepts: - Joel 2:27 I am in the midst of Israel, and I am the Lord your God, and none else; everyone else is excluded, and my people shall never be ashamed. - Luke 1:68 Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, for he hath visited and redeemed his people; the God of the Bible is the God of Israel in both testaments. - Ezra 4:1-3 The adversaries said, Let us build with you, for we seek your God; the fathers answered, Ye have nothing to do with us, but we ourselves together will build unto the Lord God of Israel. --- Topics: Clean and Unclean Meats · Esau and Edom · Sacrifice and Atonement · The Covenant · The Feasts of the Most High · The Priesthood ← Exodus 22-25 · Exodus Study · Exodus 30-33 →

title: Exodus 30: The Altar of Incense and the Holy Anointing Oil
text: ← Exodus 26-29 · Exodus Study · Exodus 34-37 → Exodus 30: The Altar of Incense and the Holy Anointing Oil Read the chapter → Exodus 30 Introduction This reading covers Exodus 30 through 33: the altar of incense, the ransom of souls, the laver of brass, the holy anointing oil and perfume, Bezaleel and Aholiab filled with wisdom to build, the sabbath as a sign between the Most High and Israel, the golden calf at Horeb, and Moses pleading for the presence of the Lord and seeing his glory pass by. This was a reading session with teaching along the way; the questions answered at the end are merged under the verses they belong to. Exodus 30:1-5 - The altar to burn incense upon was made of shittim wood, a cubit in length and a cubit in breadth, foursquare, and two cubits high, with horns of the same. A cubit has been read to be about seventeen inches, so this stood about waist high. - It was overlaid with pure gold, the top, the sides round about, and the horns, with a crown of gold round about, two golden rings under the crown, and staves of shittim wood overlaid with gold. The staves through the rings were how the priests bore it as Israel moved through the wilderness. Exodus 30:6-9 - The altar was put before the vail that is by the ark of the testimony, before the mercy seat where the Most High would meet with Moses. - Aaron burned sweet incense on it every morning when he dressed the lamps, and again at even when he lighted the lamps, a perpetual incense before the Lord throughout the generations; it burned continually, morning and evening. - No strange incense went on it, and no burnt sacrifice, meat offering, or drink offering; this altar was for one specific incense only. The service had to be exactly as prescribed, and deviation carried death, which is a reason to thank the Lord for Christ. Exodus 30:10 - Aaron made an atonement upon the horns of it once in a year with the blood of the sin offering of atonements; it is most holy unto the Lord. This altar served the day of atonement. - On the tenth day of the seventh month Israel afflicted their souls and did no work at all, and the priest made an atonement for the sanctuary, the tabernacle, the altar, the priests, and all the people of the congregation, to cleanse them from all their sins before the Lord; an everlasting statute, once a year. - The priests went always into the first tabernacle accomplishing the service of God, but into the second went the high priest alone once every year, not without blood. Christ offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, so the day of atonement is still kept by afflicting the soul and doing no work, but without the animal sacrifice, because Christ took the place of the animal. Precepts: - Leviticus 16:29-34 On the tenth day of the seventh month ye shall afflict your souls, and the priest makes an atonement to cleanse the children of Israel from all their sins, an everlasting statute. - Hebrews 9:6-7 Into the second went the high priest alone once every year, not without blood, which he offered for himself and for the errors of the people. - Hebrews 10:10-12 The daily sacrifices can never take away sins, but this man offered one sacrifice for sins for ever and sat down on the right hand of God. Exodus 30:11-16 - Numbering the children of Israel was not done lightly; when they were counted, every man gave a ransom for his soul unto the Lord, that there be no plague among them when they were numbered. - The ransom was half a shekel after the shekel of the sanctuary, from every one that passed among them that were numbered, from twenty years old and above; the rich gave no more and the poor gave no less, to make an atonement for their souls. - The atonement money was appointed for the service of the tabernacle of the congregation.
