The gold, the wood, the curtains, and the fabrics all had to be bought and kept up, and the tabernacle moved with the nation through the wilderness; that is the same reason offerings are gathered in the congregation today, because the house of the Most High cannot be built or kept without it. Exodus 30:17-21 - The laver of brass, with his foot also of brass, stood between the tabernacle of the congregation and the altar, with water in it; a great brass bowl set on a brass base. - Aaron and his sons washed their hands and their feet thereat when they went into the tabernacle of the congregation and when they came near to the altar to minister, that they die not; the priests could not go in unclean. - It was a statute for ever to Aaron and to his seed throughout their generations. Exodus 30:22-33 - The holy anointing oil was compounded of principal spices, pure myrrh five hundred shekels, sweet cinnamon two hundred and fifty, sweet calamus two hundred and fifty, cassia five hundred after the shekel of the sanctuary, and oil olive an hin, an ointment compound after the art of the apothecary, which is a maker of perfume. - With it were anointed the tabernacle of the congregation, the ark of the testimony, the table and all his vessels, the candlestick and his vessels, the altar of incense, the altar of burnt offering with all his vessels, and the laver and his foot, that they be most holy; whatsoever toucheth them shall be holy. Aaron and his sons were anointed and consecrated with it to minister in the priest's office. - It was not poured upon man's flesh, and none was to be made like it after the composition of it; whosoever compounded any like it, or put any of it upon a stranger, was cut off from his people. - The Most High gave specific orders down to the spices and the weights, and none could deviate from them or they would die. Our forefathers carried out that tedious, exact work, yet we complain about the smallest things set in place for order, the uniform, the new moon, and not cooking on the sabbath; the spirit has to get right. Exodus 30:34-38 - The perfume was made of sweet spices, stacte, onycha, and galbanum, with pure frankincense, of each a like weight, tempered together, pure and holy, a confection after the art of the apothecary. - Part of it was beaten very small and put before the testimony in the tabernacle of the congregation; unto you it shall be most holy. The Most High wanted the tabernacle anointed and smelling sweet, everything done one specific way. - It was for the Lord alone; ye shall not make to yourselves according to the composition thereof, and whosoever made like unto it, to smell thereto, was cut off from his people. There were no knockoffs of the holy things; a copy carried death. Exodus 31: Bezaleel and Aholiab, and the Sabbath Sign Read the chapter → Exodus 31 Exodus 31:1-6 - The Lord called by name Bezaleel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, and filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom, in understanding, in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship, to devise cunning works, to work in gold, in silver, in brass, in cutting of stones, and in carving of timber. - With him the Lord gave Aholiab the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, and put wisdom in the hearts of all that were wise hearted, that they might make all that he had commanded. - The Most High still works the same way. Brothers and sisters come into the congregation who are carpenters, plumbers, electricians, builders, painters, cooks, and tech savvy, and he sets every one in the body as it pleases him; no one appoints himself over the camp or the kitchen. All the diverse gifts together build the work today the way the tabernacle was built then. Precepts: - 1 Corinthians 12:6-11 There are diversities of operations, but it is the same God which worketh all in all, and the manifestation of the Spirit is given to every man to profit withal. - 1 Corinthians 12:14 The body is not one member, but many; the nation cannot be all teachers. - 1 Corinthians 12:18 God hath set the members every one of them in the body, as it hath pleased him. Exodus 31:7-11 - The wise hearted made all that was commanded: the tabernacle of the congregation, the ark of the testimony, the mercy seat that is thereupon, all the furniture of the tabernacle, the table and his furniture, the pure candlestick with all his furniture, the altar of incense, the altar of burnt offering with all his furniture, and the laver and his foot. - They made the cloths of service, the holy garments for Aaron the priest and the garments of his sons to minister in the priest's office, the anointing oil, and the sweet incense for the holy place, according to all that the Lord commanded. - That spirit of workmanship on Israel is why the tabernacle, and later the house Solomon built for the Lord, outshined anything the world had seen; and though strangers shall build up our walls in the kingdom, it will be Israel directing how the Lord wants it done. Exodus 31:12-15 - Verily my sabbaths ye shall keep, for it is a sign between me and you throughout your generations, that ye may know that I am the LORD that doth sanctify you. Keeping the weekly sabbath and the feast days shows that Israel are his children and he is their God; the nations do not have this sabbath, and adopted Sunday worship is not the true sabbath given to the children of Israel. - Every one that defileth the sabbath shall surely be put to death. The stoning was done away in Christ, but the judgment for breaking the sabbath still stands, and people still die on the sabbath day, Friday sundown to Saturday sundown; the Most High is justified, because it is his sign between him and his people. - Six days may work be done, but in the seventh is the sabbath of rest, holy to the LORD. It is more than a day of rest and congregating; it is the sign of who Israel's God is, which is why saying the sabbath is done away takes away the very sign between Israel and God. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 33:7-9 Every day has the same sun, but by the knowledge of the Lord some days were made high days and hallowed; the sabbath is distinguished by God, not by man. - From the questions: eating is allowed on the sabbath, but not cooking. What is baked and seethed is prepared the day before and laid up, so the sabbath meal is leftovers or simple food; no microwaving, no coffee pots, no kindling the cooking fire. - There is no buying or selling on the sabbath or on the holy day, so gas and food are bought before sundown; no fishing either, for what could be called work opens the door to every man excusing his trade on the sabbath. - The Lord gives no man license to sin, but Christ is Lord of the sabbath and brought grace for necessities out of our control, a blown tire or an empty tank on the way to keep the sabbath, or medicine when the body is in danger; it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days. Precepts: - Exodus 35:3 Kindle no fire throughout your habitations upon the sabbath day; this speaks to the cooking fire, not to warming the household. - Exodus 16:23 Bake that which ye will bake to day, and that which remaineth is laid up until the morning; the sabbath food is cooked the day before. - Nehemiah 10:31 If the people of the land bring ware or victuals on the sabbath day to sell, we would not buy it of them on the sabbath, or on the holy day. - Matthew 12:11-12 A man is better than a sheep lifted out of the pit on the sabbath; wherefore it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days. - Matthew 12:8 The Son of man is Lord even of the sabbath day; grace covers what is out of our control, never license to sin. Exodus 31:16-17 - The children of Israel shall keep the sabbath, to observe the sabbath throughout their generations, for a perpetual covenant; it is a sign between the Most High and the children of Israel for ever, for in six days the LORD made heaven and earth, and on the seventh day he rested, and was refreshed. - Christians use Mark 2:27 to say the sabbath is done away, but that is not what Christ said. The sabbath was made for man, the children of Israel; man was not put on the earth for the sabbath, the sabbath was put on the earth for man, and the Son of man is Lord of the sabbath because Christ instituted it. He rested for our sakes, that we should rest after the same similitude. Precepts: - Mark 2:27-28 The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath; therefore the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath. Exodus 31:18 - When he had made an end of communing with Moses upon mount Sinai, he gave him two tables of testimony, tables of stone, written with the finger of God. God literally wrote the testimony with his finger, and we know that was Christ. Exodus 32: The Golden Calf at Horeb Read the chapter → Exodus 32 Exodus 32:1-6 - When the people saw that Moses delayed to come down out of the mount, they gathered unto Aaron: Up, make us gods, which shall go before us; for as for this Moses, we wot not what is become of him. Any time deliverance did not come when Israel wanted it, the nation rebelled, and Moses and the leadership got the blame; the same spirit is against the leadership of Israel to this day. - Aaron said break off the golden earrings which are in the ears of your wives, of your sons, and of your daughters. Men and women both wore earrings in the scriptures, and it is not sin. - Aaron received the gold, fashioned it with a graving tool, and made a molten calf, and they said, These be thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt. Aaron saw the miracles in Egypt and was set up as high priest, yet he succumbed to the pressure of the people; that is why the Lord chose Moses specifically to lead, because Moses could not be moved by any means. - Aaron built an altar before it and made proclamation, To morrow is a feast to the LORD; and the people rose up early, offered burnt offerings and peace offerings, sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to play. Israel kept provoking God, and the Lord still brought the nation into the promised land as he promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Precepts: - 1 Corinthians 10:1-7 All our fathers were under the cloud and were baptized unto Moses, and that Rock was Christ; the Corinthians were Israelites. Neither be ye idolaters, as it is written, the people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play. Exodus 32:7-10 - The Lord told Moses, Go, get thee down; for thy people, which thou broughtest out of the land of Egypt, have corrupted themselves. They turned aside quickly out of the way, made a molten calf, worshipped it, and sacrificed thereunto. Not forty days gone, and they had already left his commandments. - The spirit that was in Israel in Egypt was still in Israel when they left. It is the same coming into this truth: the evil carried in from the world will corrupt you and turn you from the Lord if it is not put off. - I have seen this people, and, behold, it is a stiffnecked people. That has been Israel's reputation with the Father from the beginning; without the laws of God we are a carnal, rebellious people, which is why these last days call for humbleness and repentance, not bringing the world's rhetoric into the congregation. - Now therefore let me alone, that my wrath may wax hot against them, and that I may consume them: and I will make of thee a great nation. Moses was of the tribe of Levi, of the seed of Jacob, so the Lord could have started over with him. Precepts: - Ecclesiastes 5:1 Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God; the evil still in a man from the world will corrupt him as it did our forefathers. Exodus 32:11-14 - Moses besought the LORD his God: LORD, why doth thy wrath wax hot against thy people, which thou hast brought forth out of the land of Egypt with great power, and with a mighty hand? Moses had compassion and stood in the middle, interceding and mediating between the people and God. - Wherefore should the Egyptians speak, and say, For mischief did he bring them out, to slay them in the mountains? And remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, to whom thou swarest by thine own self to multiply their seed as the stars of heaven, and to give the land to their seed for ever. - And the LORD repented of the evil which he thought to do unto his people. The Most High does not repent as a man; he has no one to answer to, he simply turned from the anger of that moment. He was never going to break his covenant, for consuming the people would have destroyed all the seed of Jacob except Moses; Moses was there to remind him of his own word. - From the questions: the Lord dealt with Moses on a level where Moses could speak to him so, but the outcome stood on what was declared from the beginning; had it been his pleasure to destroy, nothing Moses said could have stayed it. Precepts: - Isaiah 46:10 Declaring the end from the beginning; my counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure. Exodus 32:15-20 - Moses went down from the mount with the two tables of the testimony in his hand, written on both their sides; the tables were the work of God, and the writing was the writing of God, graven upon the tables. - Joshua heard the noise of the people and said, There is a noise of war in the camp; Moses answered, It is not the voice of them that shout for mastery, neither the voice of them that cry for being overcome, but the noise of them that sing do I hear. They were feasting and dancing around the idol. Joshua's loyalty at the mount is one of the main reasons the Lord chose him to succeed Moses. - As soon as he came nigh unto the camp and saw the calf and the dancing, Moses' anger waxed hot, and he cast the tables out of his hands and brake them beneath the mount. - He took the calf which they had made, burnt it in the fire, ground it to powder, strawed it upon the water, and made the children of Israel drink of it. Our forefathers were no joke about the law; Nehemiah likewise put hands on those who profaned the sabbath in his day. Exodus 32:21-24 - Moses said unto Aaron, What did this people unto thee, that thou hast brought so great a sin upon them? He had left Aaron in charge, and came back to a camp deep in wickedness. - Aaron answered, Let not the anger of my lord wax hot: thou knowest the people, that they are set on mischief; they said make us gods, I cast the gold into the fire, and there came out this calf. A leader cannot blame the congregation, the same excuse Saul gave; the charge has to be carried. - The psalm gives the depth of it: they soon forgat his works and waited not for his counsel, they made a calf in Horeb and changed their glory into the similitude of an ox that eateth grass, and they forgat God their saviour, which had done great things in Egypt, wondrous works in the land of Ham, and terrible things by the Red sea. Precepts: - Psalms 106:13-16 They soon forgat his works and waited not for his counsel, but lusted exceedingly in the wilderness, and tempted God in the desert. - Psalms 106:19-23 They made a calf in Horeb and forgat God their saviour; he said he would destroy them, had not Moses his chosen stood before him in the breach, to turn away his wrath. Exodus 32:25-29 - The people were naked, for Aaron had made them naked unto their shame among their enemies. That is the same nakedness of Genesis 3, the shame of sin uncovered. - Moses stood in the gate of the camp and said, Who is on the LORD's side? let him come unto me. And all the sons of Levi gathered themselves together unto him. - Every man put his sword by his side and went in and out from gate to gate throughout the camp, and there fell of the people that day about three thousand men. The Lord chose those particular ones to die; that spirit would have wrecked the nation down the road, so he moved it out of the congregation. Do not be broken when someone leaves the truth; the Lord moves spiritually. - Consecrate yourselves to day to the LORD, even every man upon his son, and upon his brother, that he may bestow upon you a blessing this day. Exodus 32:30-35 - Moses said unto the people, Ye have sinned a great sin. They had broken the first two commandments just given at Sinai: no other gods before him, and no graven image to bow down to and serve. - Moses returned unto the LORD to mediate: yet now, if thou wilt forgive their sin; and if not, blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book which thou hast written. That is a real leader, putting himself in the way of harm for his people. - The Lord answered, Whosoever hath sinned against me, him will I blot out of my book; therefore now go, lead the people, and mine Angel shall go before thee; nevertheless in the day when I visit I will visit their sin upon them. And the LORD plagued the people, because they made the calf, which Aaron made. Precepts: - Exodus 20:1-5 I am the LORD thy God; thou shalt have no other gods before me, nor make any graven image, nor bow down to them, for the iniquity of the fathers is visited upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate him; the calf broke these first commandments. Exodus 33: My Presence Shall Go with Thee Read the chapter → Exodus 33 Exodus 33:1-3 - The Lord said, Depart, and go up hence, thou and the people which thou hast brought up out of the land of Egypt, unto the land which I sware unto Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob; and I will send an angel before thee, and I will drive out the Canaanite, the Amorite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite. That Angel is Christ. - I will not go up in the midst of thee, for thou art a stiffnecked people, lest I consume thee in the way. - From the questions: a land flowing with milk and honey is not a magical land of milk. It means a plenteous, fertile land of great landscape, valleys, grass, and fields, with cattle and goats grazing for the milk, and flowers and plants in abundance for the bees to make the honey; a land blessed as the days of heaven upon the earth. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 11:13-15 Hearken diligently unto his commandments, and he gives the rain of your land in his due season and grass in thy fields for thy cattle, that thou mayest eat and be full. - Deuteronomy 11:21 That your days may be multiplied in the land which the LORD sware unto your fathers, as the days of heaven upon the earth. - Leviticus 26:3-6 Walk in his statutes and keep his commandments, and the rain comes in due season, the land yields her increase, the trees yield their fruit, ye shall eat your bread to the full, and none shall make you afraid. Exodus 33:4-6 - When the people heard these evil tidings, they mourned, and no man did put on him his ornaments; the Lord said, Put off thy ornaments from thee, that I may know what to do unto thee, and the children of Israel stripped themselves of their ornaments by the mount Horeb, while the Lord weighed whether to come up into the midst of them in a moment and consume them. Exodus 33:7-11 - Moses took the tabernacle and pitched it without the camp, afar off from the camp, and called it the Tabernacle of the congregation. The Lord dwelt there, and he would not sit in the midst of a camp that had corrupted itself; every one which sought the LORD went out unto the tabernacle without the camp. - When Moses went out unto the tabernacle, all the people rose up and stood every man at his tent door and looked after Moses until he was gone in; and the cloudy pillar descended and stood at the door of the tabernacle, and the LORD talked with Moses, and all the people rose up and worshipped, every man in his tent door. - The LORD spake unto Moses face to face, as a man speaketh unto his friend. That is not Moses looking eye to eye at the Lord; it means there was no mediator between Moses and the Lord, for Moses himself was the mediator between the Lord and the people, and the Lord spoke to him directly. - His servant Joshua, the son of Nun, a young man, departed not out of the tabernacle. Joshua was a true disciple, a learner, eager to stay by Moses' side and learn; the Lord knew his spirit. Exodus 33:12-17 - Moses pled with the Lord: thou hast said, I know thee by name, and thou hast also found grace in my sight; now therefore shew me now thy way, that I may know thee, that I may find grace in thy sight; and consider that this nation is thy people. - The Lord answered, My presence shall go with thee, and I will give thee rest. And Moses said, If thy presence go not with me, carry us not up hence; for wherein shall it be known here that I and thy people have found grace in thy sight? is it not in that thou goest with us? so shall we be separated, I and thy people, from all the people that are upon the face of the earth. - The presence of the Most High in the midst is how Israel is known to be separated from all the nations, and it ties back to the sabbath sign: when Israel keeps the sabbath and gathers in his name, the Lord and Christ are in the midst. Precepts: - Matthew 18:20 Where two or three are gathered together in his name, there he is in the midst of them; the presence in the midst is the separation from the nations. Exodus 33:18-23 - Moses said, I beseech thee, shew me thy glory. And he said, I will make all my goodness pass before thee, and I will proclaim the name of the LORD before thee, and will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and will shew mercy on whom I will shew mercy, then and in the future as well. - Thou canst not see my face: for there shall no man see me, and live. In verse 11 Christ spoke to Moses on the Lord's behalf, with Moses as the mediator to the people; here it is the Father of heaven and earth himself, and no man can see his face and live. - Behold, there is a place by me, and thou shalt stand upon a rock: I will put thee in a clift of the rock, and will cover thee with my hand while I pass by; and I will take away mine hand, and thou shalt see my back parts, but my face shall not be seen. Moses beheld the similitude of the LORD, the back parts of his glory, never his face. Precepts: - Numbers 12:8 With Moses the Lord spake mouth to mouth, even apparently, and not in dark speeches, and the similitude of the LORD shall he behold; Moses saw the back parts, not the face. --- Topics: Clean and Unclean Meats · Idolatry · Sacrifice and Atonement · The Covenant · The Feasts of the Most High · The Priesthood · The Sabbath ← Exodus 26-29 · Exodus Study · Exodus 34-37 →

title: Exodus 34: The Second Tables and the Covenant Renewed
text: ← Exodus 30-33 · Exodus Study · Exodus 38-40 → Exodus 34: The Second Tables and the Covenant Renewed Read the chapter → Exodus 34 Introduction This reading covers Exodus 34 through 37: the second tables of stone and the covenant renewed, Moses' shining face, the sabbath and the willing hearted offering for the tabernacle, the wise hearted building the tabernacle, and Bezaleel making the ark, the mercy seat, and the holy furniture. Exodus 34:1-4 - The Most High commanded Moses to hew, that is carve out or chisel, two tables of stone like unto the first, because Moses brake the first tables; the words were written in stone, and the Lord would write upon these tables the words that were in the first. - No man was to come up with Moses, neither was any man to be seen throughout all the mount, neither flocks nor herds feed before it; the Most High did not want man nor beast near mount Sinai. Exodus 34:5-7 - The Lord descended in the cloud and stood with him there. The clouds are His chariot, His vehicle, His way of traveling; the Most High, Christ, and the angels travel in these vehicles. - He proclaimed the name of the Lord, as He had promised Moses in the mount. No man can see the face of the Most High and live, so the Lord set Moses upon a rock, put him in a clift of the rock, and covered him with His hand while His glory passed by; Moses saw only His back parts. - Keeping mercy for thousands, forgiving iniquity and transgression and sin: this is spoken to Israel. Moses is speaking only to the children of Israel at this time; sin is the transgression of the law, and the word and the statutes were given to Israel only. - And that will by no means clear the guilty: He will forgive you, but you will still be judged; He still visits the iniquity of the fathers upon the children and upon the children's children, unto the third and to the fourth generation. Precepts: - Psalms 104:3 Who maketh the clouds his chariot; the cloud the Lord descended in is His vehicle of travel. - Exodus 33:19-23 I will proclaim the name of the LORD before thee; thou canst not see my face and live; Moses stood upon the rock, was covered in the clift, and saw the back parts. - Psalms 147:19-20 He sheweth his word unto Jacob; he hath not dealt so with any nation. The forgiveness proclaimed here belongs to Israel. - 1 John 3:4 Sin is the transgression of the law; the sin being forgiven is the breaking of the law given to Israel. Exodus 34:8-9 - Moses made haste, bowed his head toward the earth, and worshipped: let my Lord, I pray thee, go among us, for it is a stiffnecked people; and pardon our iniquity, meaning forgive our iniquity, and our sin, and take us for thine inheritance. Exodus 34:10 - The Most High made a covenant to do marvels such as have not been done in all the earth, nor in any nation, and all the people among which Israel dwells shall see the work of the Lord. One of those marvels is laid out in the Revelation. - Israel lay as dead bodies in the street of the great city which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt: a decayed state, a spiritually dead people. The people and kindreds and tongues and nations saw them in that dead state through the years of captivity, when they were slaves, and their bodies were not put in graves because the death is spiritual, not physical; the two witnesses go to the northern and southern kingdoms. - They that dwell upon the earth rejoiced over them, made merry, and sent gifts one to another, because these had tormented them. Then the Spirit of life from God entered into them: the people that were spiritually dead in captivity, that would not look their slave masters in the face, stood upon their feet, and great fear fell upon them which saw them; that same fear falls on the slave masters. Precepts: - Revelation 11:8-11 The dead bodies in the street of the great city spiritually called Sodom and Egypt are Israel spiritually dead in captivity; the Spirit of life enters them, they stand upon their feet, and great fear falls on them which see them. This is the marvel the Most High spoke of. Exodus 34:11-16 - Observe thou that which I command thee this day: behold, the Most High drives out before Israel the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites. - Take heed to thyself, lest thou make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land, lest it be for a snare, a trap, in the midst of thee. Ye shall destroy their altars, break their images, and cut down their groves, just as the law states it again in Deuteronomy; for the Lord, whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God. - The snare is spelled out: they go a whoring after their gods, they call thee, thou eat of their sacrifice and partake in serving their gods; thou take of their daughters unto thy sons, and their daughters go a whoring after their gods and make thy sons go a whoring after their gods. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 7:5 Destroy their altars, break down their images, and cut down their groves; the command of this chapter is written again in the law. Exodus 34:17 - Thou shalt make thee no molten gods. It had to be reiterated here, because in the chapter before Israel made a molten calf; that shall not be done. Exodus 34:18-20 - The feast of unleavened bread shalt thou keep seven days, in the time of the month Abib, for in the month Abib thou camest out from Egypt; this goes to the Passover season. - All that openeth the matrix is the Lord's, every firstling among thy cattle that is male, and the firstling of an ass redeemed with a lamb; all the firstborn of thy sons thou shalt redeem. This is symbolic of the Most High bringing Israel out of Egypt: He killed the firstborn of the Egyptians and kept His people alive. Exodus 34:21 - Six days thou shalt work, but on the seventh day thou shalt rest: in earing time and in harvest thou shalt rest. Even when it was the time of harvest and gathering, Israel still rested on the seventh day. Exodus 34:22-24 - The feast of weeks goes to Pentecost, and the feast of ingathering at the year's end goes to the feast of tabernacles. - Thrice in the year shall all your men children appear before the Lord GOD, the God of Israel. The law is written again in Deuteronomy: the feast of unleavened bread, which is the Passover season, the feast of weeks, which is Pentecost, and the feast of tabernacles; and they shall not appear before the Lord empty, for each had to bring his sacrifice. - Neither shall any man desire thy land when thou shalt go up to appear before the Lord thrice in the year: when the men left their land and went up to keep the three high holy days, the Most High promised no man would desire their land. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 16:16 Three times in a year shall all thy males appear before the LORD in the place which he shall choose, at the three feasts, and they shall not appear before the LORD empty. Exodus 34:25-26 - Thou shalt not offer the blood of my sacrifice with leaven; neither shall the sacrifice of the feast of the passover be left unto the morning: it had to be eaten up or burned. - The first of the firstfruits of thy land thou shalt bring unto the house of the LORD thy God. And thou shalt not seethe a kid in his mother's milk: a young one still in his mother's milk, as veal is taken for instance, is not ready to be eaten; it is unlawful. Exodus 34:27-28 - Write thou these words: for after the tenor of these words I have made a covenant with thee and with Israel. The words are the laws the Lord had just given. - Moses was there with the Lord forty days and forty nights; he did neither eat bread, nor drink water. And he wrote upon the tables the words of the covenant, the ten commandments; the words of the covenant take in the directions of the sacrifices, which animals were to be offered and how it was to be done, together with the commandments. Exodus 34:29-35 - When Moses came down from mount Sinai with the two tables of testimony in his hand, the skin of his face shone while he talked with him, and Moses wist it not; and when Aaron and all the children of Israel saw it, they were afraid to come nigh him. - A man's wisdom maketh his face to shine. This was no ordinary wisdom Moses was getting; he was getting the utmost wisdom. In the mount the Most High held him by Him a long season, told him many wondrous things, and shewed him the secrets of the times and the end; he saw the beginning of the creation, the middle, and the end of these times, and that is why his face shone. - Some of that wisdom Moses was commanded to hide and not declare; there is wisdom the Most High gave him that he was not to publish, that we do not even have right now. - Moses put a vail on his face until he had done speaking with the people; but when he went in before the Lord to speak with Him he took the vail off, to show respect to the Most High. Precepts: - Ecclesiastes 8:1 A man's wisdom maketh his face to shine, and the boldness of his face shall be changed; that is why Moses' face shone. - 2 Esdras 14:3-6 The Most High shewed Moses the secrets of the times and the end; that measure of wisdom made his face shine, and some of it he was commanded to hide. Exodus 35: The Sabbath and the Willing Hearted Offering Read the chapter → Exodus 35 Exodus 35:1-3 - Moses gathered all the congregation of the children of Israel: six days shall work be done, but on the seventh day there shall be to you an holy day, a sabbath of rest to the Lord; whosoever doeth work therein shall be put to death. - Ye shall kindle no fire throughout your habitations upon the sabbath day: kindling fire goes to cooking. Bake that which ye will bake today, and seethe that ye will seethe, and lay up what remains to be kept unto the morning; you could not cook on the sabbath, so the day before is the prep day, and what you prepare that day is what you eat. Precepts: - Exodus 16:23 Bake that which ye will bake today, and lay up what remaineth to be kept until the morning; kindling fire on the sabbath goes to cooking, so the cooking was done on the preparation day. Exodus 35:4-9 - Whosoever is of a willing heart, let him bring the Lord's offering: gold, silver, and brass; blue, purple, scarlet, fine linen, and goats' hair; rams' skins dyed red and badgers' skins; shittim wood; oil for the light and spices for the anointing oil and the sweet incense; and onyx stones and stones to be set for the ephod and the breastplate. These are the offerings the people would bring unto the Lord. Exodus 35:10-19 - Every wise hearted among you shall come and make all that the Lord hath commanded: those who had skill, the crafty ones. - The list runs through the whole work: the tabernacle, his tent, his covering, his taches, boards, bars, pillars, and sockets; the ark of the covenant with the staves and the mercy seat, and the vail of the covering; the table with his staves and vessels and the shewbread; the candlestick, which is the menorah, with his lamps and the oil for the light; the incense altar; the altar of burnt offering, where the burnt offering was burnt, with his brasen grate; the laver; the hangings of the court; and the cloths of service, the holy garments for Aaron the priest and the garments of his sons, to minister in the priest's office. Exodus 35:20-29 - The congregation departed from the presence of Moses, and they came, every one whose heart stirred him up and every one whom his spirit made willing, and brought the Lord's offering for the work of the tabernacle; the people brought the gold and silver and all the things listed willingly. - Both men and women, as many as were willing hearted, brought bracelets, and earrings, and rings, and tablets, all jewels of gold; and every man with whom was found blue, purple, scarlet, fine linen, goats' hair, red skins of rams, badgers' skins, silver, brass, or shittim wood brought it. - All the women that were wise hearted did spin with their hands; the women knew how to sew, and brought that which they had spun of blue, purple, scarlet, and fine linen, and the women whose heart stirred them up in wisdom spun goats' hair. The rulers brought onyx stones, stones for the ephod and breastplate, spice, and oil. Exodus 35:30-35 - The Lord called by name Bezaleel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, and filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom, in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship; the Most High put His spirit on him to be gifted in what he did, to devise curious works in gold, silver, and brass, in cutting of stones, and in carving of wood. - He hath put in his heart that he may teach, both he and Aholiab the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan; the two brothers the Most High was dealing with in workmanship trained and taught their fellow brethren how to do it. - It is the same today: the Most High puts His spirit on brothers and sisters with different talents, and they put their talents to use and teach others in the congregation; Israel was putting their talents together and building, showing each other how to do these works. Exodus 36: The Wise Hearted Build the Tabernacle Read the chapter → Exodus 36 Exodus 36:1-3 - Then wrought Bezaleel and Aholiab and every wise hearted man in whom the Lord put wisdom and understanding, according to all that the Lord had commanded; they were over the cunning work of the building and were leading the men among them in how the work was done. - They received of Moses all the offering which the children of Israel had brought for the work of the service of the sanctuary; and the people brought yet unto him free offerings every morning. Exodus 36:4-7 - The wise men that wrought the work came and spake unto Moses: the people bring much more than enough for the service of the work. That shows how willing they were; it was too much. - Moses gave commandment, and they caused it to be proclaimed throughout the camp that neither man nor woman make any more work for the offering of the sanctuary; the people were restrained from bringing, for the stuff they had was sufficient for all the work, and too much. Exodus 36:8-13 - Every wise hearted man among them made ten curtains of fine twined linen, and blue, and purple, and scarlet, with cherubims of cunning work; the cherubims were wrought into the curtains by the skilled craftsmen. - A cubit is eighteen inches: the length of one curtain, twenty and eight cubits, is forty two feet, and the breadth of one curtain, four cubits, is seventy two inches; the curtains were all of one size. - He coupled five curtains one unto another, and the other five likewise, with fifty loops on the edge of each coupling and fifty taches of gold to couple the curtains one unto another; so it became one tabernacle. Exodus 36:14-19 - He made eleven curtains of goats' hair for the tent over the tabernacle, coupled five by themselves and six by themselves, with fifty loops and fifty taches of brass to couple the tent together, that it might be one. - He made a covering for the tent of rams' skins dyed red, and a covering of badgers' skins above that; these are the materials used to make the covering of the tent for the tabernacle, all commanded by the Most High God to Moses. Exodus 36:20-34 - He made boards for the tabernacle of shittim wood standing up: this is the framework of the tabernacle that holds it up. The length of a board was ten cubits, which is one hundred and eighty inches, and the breadth of a board a cubit and a half, which is twenty seven inches. - Twenty boards for the south side and twenty for the north, with forty sockets of silver under each twenty, two sockets under every board for his two tenons; six boards westward and two for the corners; and bars of shittim wood, five for the boards of each side, with the middle bar shooting through the boards from the one end to the other. He overlaid the boards and the bars with gold, and made their rings of gold for the places of the bars. - The whole tent was built to be carried. Any time Israel moved through the wilderness, the men appointed as carriers would break everything down and travel with it toward the land of Canaan; wherever the Most High moved, Israel followed, and where the Most High stopped, they set up again. Exodus 36:35-38 - He made a vail of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen, with cherubims of cunning work, upon four pillars of shittim wood overlaid with gold, their hooks of gold, upon four sockets of silver. - He made an hanging for the tabernacle door of needlework, with five pillars, their chapiters and their fillets overlaid with gold, and their five sockets of brass. Exodus 37: Bezaleel Makes the Ark, the Mercy Seat, and the Holy Furniture Read the chapter → Exodus 37 Exodus 37:1-5 - Bezaleel made the ark of shittim wood: two cubits and a half was the length of it, which is forty five inches, and a cubit and a half, which is twenty seven inches, the breadth of it, and a cubit and a half the height of it. - It was wood overlaid with pure gold within and without, with a crown of gold round about it, and four rings of gold cast for the four corners; the staves of shittim wood overlaid with gold were put into the rings by the sides of the ark to bear the ark. The staves stick out from the sides; that is how the ark was carried, and the priesthood always carried it. Exodus 37:6-9 - He made the mercy seat of pure gold, and two cherubims of gold beaten out of one piece on the two ends of the mercy seat, one cherub on the end on this side and another cherub on the other end on that side; the cherubims spread out their wings on high and covered with their wings over the mercy seat, with their faces one to another. - The most holy place, where the ark of the covenant and the mercy seat sat, was the central focus of the entire tabernacle: there the Most High spoke to the high priest above the mercy seat, in the area where the wings of the cherubims faced each other; the tablets of the law were placed inside the ark. - Annually the high priest would sprinkle blood on the mercy seat to atone for the sins of all the people. The purpose and desire of the Most High is to dwell among His people and to commune with them; the layout of the tabernacle, with the steps of sacrifice and cleansing, is designed to bring sinful mankind to a loving and holy God. Exodus 37:10-16 - He made the table of shittim wood: two cubits was the length thereof, a cubit the breadth thereof, and a cubit and a half the height thereof; he overlaid it with pure gold, with a crown of gold round about and a border of an hand breadth, and cast four rings of gold for the four corners that were in the four feet thereof, the places for the staves of shittim wood overlaid with gold to bear the table. - This is the table of shewbread: on it Aaron and his sons placed twelve loaves of bread made from fine flour, and these twelve loaves represented the twelve tribes of Israel, a continual reminder of the everlasting promises, the covenant between the Most High and the children of Israel, and a memorial of His provision of food; the bread was eaten by Aaron and his sons and replaced every week on the sabbath. - He made the vessels which were upon the table, his dishes, his spoons, his bowls, and his covers, of pure gold. Exodus 37:17-24 - He made the candlestick of pure gold, which is the menorah, all of one beaten work: his shaft, his branches, his bowls, his knops, and his flowers were of the same, with six branches going out of the sides thereof, three out of the one side and three out of the other, the bowls made after the fashion of almonds, and his seven lamps. - The knops and the flowers are the designs wrought into the work; the almond shaped bowls at the top held the olive oil where the lamps continually burned, and the light could not go out. - Of a talent of pure gold made he it, and all the vessels thereof: a talent is close to eighty pounds. Exodus 37:25-29 - He made the incense altar of shittim wood: the length of it a cubit, and the breadth of it a cubit, foursquare, and two cubits the height of it, the horns thereof of the same. First it was made with wood, and then he overlaid it with pure gold, both the top of it, and the sides round about, and the horns, with a crown of gold round about, two rings of gold under the crown, and staves of shittim wood overlaid with gold to bear it withal. - He made the holy anointing oil and the pure incense of sweet spices, according to the work of the apothecary, one who compounded such mixtures. The Lord required that special incense, a special sweet mixture of spices to be used only for the tabernacle, be burned consistently on this altar; none other was to be burned on it, and it was a matter of life and death. - Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aaron, took either of them his censer, put fire therein and incense thereon, and offered strange fire before the Lord, which he commanded them not; and there went out fire from the Lord and devoured them, and they died before the Lord. They were not the ones authorized to burn the incense; in the tabernacle service you had to be appointed to do certain services, and you could not just take it upon yourself to do them. - Then Moses said unto Aaron, This is it that the Lord spake, saying, I will be sanctified in them that come nigh me, and before all the people I will be glorified. And Aaron held his peace. Precepts: - Leviticus 10:1-2 Nadab and Abihu offered strange fire before the LORD, which he commanded them not, and fire from the LORD devoured them; only the appointed could burn the incense on this altar. --- Topics: Idolatry · Sacrifice and Atonement · The Covenant · The Feasts of the Most High · The Priesthood · The Sabbath ← Exodus 30-33 · Exodus Study · Exodus 38-40 →

title: Exodus 38: The Altar, the Court, and the Sum of the Offering
text: ← Exodus 34-37 · Exodus Study · Leviticus 1 → Exodus 38: The Altar, the Court, and the Sum of the Offering Read the chapter → Exodus 38 Introduction This reading covers Exodus 38 through 40, with Leviticus 1 taken in the same session. These are the chapters men call the boring chapters, but skip past any page and you can miss a jewel; reading them teaches attention to detail. Here Moses follows through on the instructions of the earlier chapters: the tabernacle, the court, and the altar are built, the holy garments are made, and the tabernacle is reared up and filled with the glory of the Lord. Exodus 38:1-8 - This chapter is the application of the instructions already given for the tabernacle: the altar of burnt offering of shittim wood overlaid with brass, its vessels, and its staves were made exactly as commanded. - The laver of brass was made of the looking glasses of the women assembling at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation; even the women's own possessions went into the work. Exodus 38:21 - This is the sum of the tabernacle: a collection was taken in order to fund the building of the tabernacle and the service of building it, counted according to the commandment of Moses by the hand of Ithamar son to Aaron the priest. Exodus 38:24-26 - All the gold, silver, and brass occupied for the work was counted. The silver came a bekah for every man, half a shekel after the shekel of the sanctuary, from every one numbered from twenty years old and upward, six hundred thousand and three thousand and five hundred and fifty men. Thousands of men contributed to the cause of the sanctuary being built. - Israel in the wilderness was delivered, not in captivity; today we are waking up in our captivity, and the buildings we get for sanctuaries require work, wood, service, and labor. Yet many do not have the spirit to give. If you have trouble coming up out of your pocket to help the cause of the Lord, examine yourself whether ye be in the faith, whether you really believe and really study. - After Babylon invaded Jerusalem our fathers were captives, yet they still made a collection for the house of the Lord, not a required amount but according to every man's power. Likewise today the congregations do not push a ten percent; you give according to your power, and the Lord knows how much power you have to give. Sadly some give more than those who have more power to give than they. - He which soweth sparingly shall reap sparingly, and he which soweth bountifully shall reap bountifully; that does not mean the Most High blesses you with a three story house, for you may be storing up treasures in heaven. Give as you purpose in your heart, not grudgingly or of necessity, for God loveth a cheerful giver; giving with an attitude is worse than keeping the money. Precepts: - Baruch 1:5-6 In the Babylonian captivity our fathers still made a collection, according to every man's power, not a set amount. - 2 Corinthians 9:6-7 Sow bountifully and reap bountifully; give as you purpose in your heart, not grudgingly or of necessity, for God loveth a cheerful giver. - Matthew 6:20 The bountiful reaping may be treasures laid up in heaven rather than riches in this life. Exodus 38:29-31 - The brass of the offering, seventy talents and two thousand and four hundred shekels, made the sockets of the door, the brasen altar and its grate and vessels, the sockets of the court, and all the pins of the tabernacle and the court. Every material was accounted for; not everybody had the spirit to contribute physically, but everybody put their brick in and gave something for the cause. Exodus 39: The Holy Garments and the Names of the Children of Israel Read the chapter → Exodus 39 Exodus 39:1 - Chapter 39 is the application of the instructions of chapter 28: the holy garments for Aaron the priest, the clothes of service to do service in the holy place, made of the blue, purple, and scarlet as the Lord commanded Moses. Exodus 39:8-14 - The breastplate carried four rows of stones, and the stones were according to the names of the children of Israel, twelve according to their names, like the engravings of a signet, every one with his name according to the twelve tribes; the shoulders of the ephod carried onyx stones graven the same way, stones for a memorial to the children of Israel. - The Most High had us representing: when the priest stepped on the scene you already knew what nationality he was. Nationality is very important to the Lord, and he took it very seriously. Exodus 39:24-26 - The pomegranates and the bells of gold went upon the hem of the robe round about; the word keeps saying round about, because the fringes go all throughout the garment, round about, not gathered only at four corners. Old depictions show Israelites with the fringes all the way around, and it would not hurt to put them all throughout, out of the fear of God. Exodus 39:30-31 - They made the plate of the holy crown of pure gold, written like the engravings of a signet, HOLINESS TO THE LORD, fastened on high upon the mitre with a lace of blue. - Black man, this is your heritage: our forefathers the priests wore crowns of real pure gold. It is a blessing to come back to this knowledge; they will not teach you this anywhere else. Exodus 39:32-43 - Thus was all the work of the tabernacle finished, and the children of Israel did according to all that the Lord commanded Moses; they brought every piece to Moses, and he looked upon all the work, and behold, they had done it as the Lord had commanded, and Moses blessed them. - It is like getting a building today and doing all the painting, sanding, nailing, and screwing, and then standing back and seeing the finished product: all praises to the Most High, we did it; then the people are blessed. Exodus 40: The Tabernacle Reared Up and the Glory of the Lord Read the chapter → Exodus 40 Exodus 40:12-15 - Aaron and his sons were brought to the door of the tabernacle and washed with water; before they entered they were bathed, spotless. Then they were clothed and anointed to minister in the priest's office, for their anointing shall surely be an everlasting priesthood throughout their generations. The garments, the mitre, the sanctification, and the everlasting priesthood were opened at length in the Exodus 26 through 29 session. Exodus 40:16-33 - Thus did Moses according to all that the Lord commanded him. In the first month in the second year, on the first day of the month, the tabernacle was reared up: the ark with the testimony and the mercy seat, the table with the bread in order, the candlestick with the lamps, the golden altar with sweet incense, the altar of burnt offering, the laver for washing, and the court round about; so Moses finished the work. Exodus 40:34-38 - Then a cloud covered the tent of the congregation, and the glory of the Lord filled the tabernacle. Our forefathers were blessed to witness these things firsthand; it should be very exciting to read of the pillar and the glory that our ancestors saw in the wilderness. - Israel did not have to rely on maps; the cloud of the Lord upon the tabernacle by day and the fire by night were the navigation system. When the cloud was taken up they journeyed, and if it was not taken up they journeyed not until the day it was taken up. - The cloud led them in the day and the pillar of fire gave them light in the way by night; the Most High in His manifold mercies forsook them not in the wilderness. They had no need to create their own lamps; the Lord gave them light freely. - The cloud and the fire speak of spirits the Most High created, His angels: He maketh the clouds His chariot, and He maketh His angels spirits, His ministers a flaming fire. Fire is a spirit, created for vengeance, poured out in the time of destruction to appease the wrath of Him that made them. Precepts: - Nehemiah 9:12 Thou leddest them in the day by a cloudy pillar, and in the night by a pillar of fire, to give them light in the way. - Nehemiah 9:19 In thy manifold mercies thou forsookest them not in the wilderness; the pillar of cloud and the pillar of fire departed not from them. - Psalms 104:3-4 He maketh the clouds His chariot, and His angels spirits, His ministers a flaming fire; the cloud and fire were His created spirits. - Ecclesiasticus 39:28-29 Fire is one of the spirits created for vengeance; fire is a spirit. - Psalms 34:7 The angel of the Lord encampeth round about them that fear Him, and delivereth them; Israelites that fear the Most High are guarded by His angels. - The Most High sent an angel before Israel to keep them in the way and to bring them into the place He had prepared, warning them to obey his voice and provoke him not, for he will not pardon your transgressions, for my name is in him. That shows why the first generation did not make it to the promised land: they provoked the angel, transgressed, complained, worshipped idols, and wanted to go back into Egypt. - If Israel obeyed the angel's voice, the Lord would be an enemy unto their enemies and cut off the nations of the land before them. The scripture makes a distinction: the enemy whose ox or ass you must bring back and help is your brother that hates you, as the parallel law shows by using the word brother; the enemies of the nations are those the Most High said He would cut off. So love thine enemies does not mean the nation Israel was sold to; it speaks of your brother that you may be at odds with. Precepts: - Exodus 23:20-23 An angel went before Israel to keep them in the way; obey his voice and provoke him not, and the Lord will be an enemy unto thine enemies and cut off the nations. - Exodus 23:4-5 Bring back thine enemy's ox going astray and help him that hateth thee; this enemy is your brother. - Deuteronomy 22:4 The parallel law says thy brother's ass or his ox, showing the enemy of Exodus 23:4 is your brother. - Matthew 5:44 Love your enemies speaks of your brother you are at odds with, not the nations Israel was sold under. --- Topics: Sacrifice and Atonement · The Priesthood ← Exodus 34-37 · Exodus Study · Leviticus 1 →

title: Exodus 6: The Promise Renewed and the Generations of Moses and Aaron
text: ← Exodus 2-5 · Exodus Study · Exodus 10-13 → Exodus 6: The Promise Renewed and the Generations of Moses and Aaron Read the chapter → Exodus 6 Introduction This reading covers Exodus 6 through 9: the Most High renews His promise to bring Israel out of Egypt, the genealogy of Reuben, Simeon, and Levi of whom came Moses and Aaron, Aaron's rod turned serpent, and the first seven plagues upon Egypt. The thread of the session is that through each plague the Most High was mocking an idol god of Egypt: Sobek the god of the rivers, Heqet the god of the frogs, Beelzebub the lord of flies and uncleanness, Hathor the goddess of cattle, Sekhmet the goddess of health and beauty, and Nut and Geb the gods of the sky and the earth. Exodus 6:1 - The Lord renews His promise: Pharaoh will not merely let Israel go, but with a strong hand he shall drive them out of his land. Exodus 6:2-3 - The Most High appeared unto Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob by the name of God Almighty, but by His name JEHOVAH was He not known to them. Some say Jehovah and some say Yahawah; you can say whichever name you want to say. Exodus 6:4-5 - The covenant stands to give Israel the land of Canaan, the land of their pilgrimage wherein they were strangers; and the Most High heard the groaning of the children of Israel whom the Egyptians kept in bondage. - The land of Canaan is in the land of Ham. So when people say we are Africans, the answer is that we come from Northeast Africa, from that continent, but we are not Africans; our land sits on the continent, and we are the Israelites. Exodus 6:9-12 - The children of Israel hearkened not unto Moses for anguish of spirit and for cruel bondage. - Moses answered, Behold, the children of Israel have not hearkened unto me; how then shall Pharaoh hear me, who am of uncircumcised lips? This is why Aaron was given him for a mouthpiece in the next chapter. Exodus 6:16-20 - Chapter 6 is dealing with the genealogy: the families of Reuben, Simeon, and Levi, and out of Levi came Moses and Aaron. Levi begat Kohath, Kohath begat Amram, and Amram took Jochebed to wife, and she bare him Aaron and Moses. Exodus 6:26-27 - These are that Aaron and Moses to whom the Lord said, Bring out the children of Israel from the land of Egypt; these are they which spake to Pharaoh king of Egypt. Exodus 7: Aaron's Rod and the River Turned to Blood Read the chapter → Exodus 7 Exodus 7:1-2 - The Lord made Moses a god to Pharaoh, and Aaron his brother was his prophet. Moses was as God and Aaron was the mouthpiece, because Moses kept saying he was of uncircumcised lips. - This is why you do not move in a spirit of speaking against your leadership. Airing your complaints in front of everybody instead of bringing them in order only shows what type of spirit you are moving in; it is completely out of order. Exodus 7:8-12 - It was Aaron who cast down the rod before Pharaoh, and it became a serpent. A lot of people to this day say it was Moses with the rod, because they do not read the Bible; Moses was telling Aaron what to do, and it was Aaron's rod that turned into the serpent. - The magicians of Egypt did in like manner with their enchantments, and their rods became serpents; but Aaron's rod swallowed up their rods. Exodus 7:19-22 - All the waters of Egypt were turned to blood, in the streams, the rivers, the ponds, the pools, and in vessels of wood and vessels of stone; the fish died and the river stank. - With this first plague the Most High was mocking Sobek, the Egyptian idol god of the rivers, showing that he could not defend his own waters. - The magicians did so with their enchantments, but they could only copy the plague; they could not turn the water back clear. Seven days were fulfilled after the Lord had smitten the river. - Many Egyptologists claim this never happened, because to admit it happened is to admit that the idols they claim to be gods and goddesses were powerless before our God, and that those idols do not exist at all. Exodus 8: Frogs, Lice, and Swarms of Flies Read the chapter → Exodus 8 Exodus 8:5-8 - Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters, and the frogs came up and covered the land of Egypt. With this second plague the Most High was mocking Heqet, the Egyptian idol god of the frogs. - The magicians did so with their enchantments and brought up frogs, but just as with the water they could only add to the plague; they could not take the frogs away. - So Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron and said, Entreat the Lord that he may take away the frogs. Why did Pharaoh not call on Heqet, the god of frogs? He had to go to the Lord. Exodus 8:16-19 - All the dust of the land became lice in man and in beast throughout all the land of Egypt. Imagine that: the dust of the whole land of Egypt turned to lice. - The magicians did so with their enchantments to bring forth lice, but this time they could not; and the magicians said unto Pharaoh, This is the finger of God. Yet Pharaoh's heart was hardened. - With the third and fourth plagues, the lice and the swarms of flies, the Most High was mocking Beelzebub, the idol lord of flies and uncleanness. Exodus 8:21-24 - These were no ordinary flies. They were biting and killing men and animals; the scripture records that the bitings of flies killed and no remedy was found. - The Lord severed the land of Goshen, where His people dwelt, so that no swarms of flies were there, and put a division between His people and Pharaoh's people, to the end Pharaoh may know that the Lord is in the midst of the earth. - Goshen was Israel's own quarter in Egypt, where we had our own houses and our own cattle; it was given to us in the days of Joseph, as we read in the book of Genesis. Precepts: - Wisdom of Solomon 16:9 The bitings of flies killed and no remedy was found; these were no ordinary flies. - Genesis 47:6 Goshen, the best of the land, was given to Israel in Joseph's day; that is where the children of Israel dwelt apart from Egypt. Exodus 8:25-32 - Pharaoh said, Go sacrifice to your God in the land; but Moses answered, It is not meet, for we should sacrifice the abomination of the Egyptians before their eyes, and will they not stone us? Israel's sacrifices were the very animals Egypt held sacred, so Israel must go three days' journey into the wilderness. - Moses warned Pharaoh, Let not Pharaoh deal deceitfully any more. The Lord removed the swarms so that there remained not one; and Pharaoh hardened his heart at this time also, and would not let the people go. Exodus 9: Murrain, Boils, and Hail; Goshen Set Apart Read the chapter → Exodus 9 Exodus 9:1-7 - A grievous murrain fell upon the cattle of Egypt, upon the horses, asses, camels, oxen, and sheep; and with this fifth plague the Most High was mocking Hathor, the Egyptian idol goddess of cattle. - The Lord severed between the cattle of Israel and the cattle of Egypt: all the cattle of Egypt died, but of the cattle of the children of Israel died not one. Pharaoh sent, and behold, there was not one of the cattle of the Israelites dead; and his heart was hardened. - Picture what was taking place in the land: flies all over Egypt, but where Israel dwelt there were no flies; the water was blood, but where Israel dwelt the water was good; the cattle of Egypt died, but Israel's cattle lived. The plagues touched Pharaoh, his servants, and the Egyptians only; they did not touch the Israelites at all, because this was the Lord redeeming the Israelites. - The Egyptians could not pray to their idols to help them, because the Lord was mocking them, showing them that Hathor does not exist, Sobek does not exist, Heqet does not exist, and Beelzebub does not exist. Exodus 9:8-12 - Moses sprinkled ashes of the furnace toward heaven, and it became a boil breaking forth with blains upon man and upon beast throughout all the land of Egypt. - The magicians could not stand before Moses because of the boils, for the boils were upon the magicians themselves and upon all the Egyptians. With this sixth plague the Most High was mocking Sekhmet, the Egyptian idol goddess of health and beauty. Exodus 9:13-17 - Some mock and ask, What type of God says let my people go and then keeps hardening Pharaoh's heart so he will not let them go? That is exactly the God we serve, and the Lord tells you Himself why He did it: for this cause have I raised thee up, for to shew in thee my power, and that my name may be declared throughout all the earth. - The same thing is happening now, right here in this captivity. The powers of Babylon know what is being taught, yet the Lord hardens their hearts so that they keep passing laws and pressing against His people, so that the Most High can show His power again, just as He did in Egypt. Exodus 9:18-21 - Before the hail the Lord gave warning: gather thy cattle and all that thou hast in the field, for upon every man and beast found in the field the hail shall come down, and they shall die. - He that feared the word of the Lord among the servants of Pharaoh made his servants and his cattle flee into the houses; they began to recognize the God of heaven and earth, the God of the Israelites. - He that regarded not the word of the Lord left his servants and his cattle in the field. Many in Egypt held certain idols in more favor than others, and these trusted that Nut, the idol goddess of the sky, would keep them safe. Exodus 9:22-26 - This was no regular hail. There was hail, and fire mingled with the hail, very grievous, such as there was none like it in all the land of Egypt since it became a nation; the fire ran along upon the ground. - With this seventh plague the Most High was mocking Nut and Geb, the Egyptian idol gods of the sky and the earth, striking from the sky and burning along the ground they were supposed to rule. - Only in the land of Goshen, where the children of Israel were, was there no hail. The Lord does not play; our God is a terrible God. Exodus 9:27-30 - Pharaoh said, I have sinned this time: the Lord is righteous, and I and my people are wicked. This time? So all the other times, none of that was sin? Only now, under the thunder and hail, does he see it. - Moses answered that the thunder and hail would cease, that thou mayest know how that the earth is the Lord's; but as for thee and thy servants, I know that ye will not yet fear the Lord God. Exodus 9:31-32 - The flax and the barley were smitten, for the barley was in the ear and the flax was bolled; but the wheat and the rie were not smitten, for they were not grown up. Exodus 9:34-35 - When Pharaoh saw that the rain and the hail and the thunders were ceased, he sinned yet more and hardened his heart, he and his servants. He still had the wheat and the rie in the ground, because they were not grown up yet, and that is part of why he went right back to hardening himself. --- Topics: Idolatry · Sacrifice and Atonement · The Covenant · The Feasts of the Most High · The Priesthood ← Exodus 2-5 · Exodus Study · Exodus 10-13 →

title: Leviticus 1: The Law of the Burnt Offerings
text: ← Exodus 38-40 · Leviticus Study · Leviticus 2-5 → Leviticus 1: The Law of the Burnt Offerings Read the chapter → Leviticus 1 Introduction This chapter was read in the same session as Exodus 38 through 40. Leviticus comes from Levitical, whose root word is Levi: the Levites were given the priesthood of the Lord, so this book deals with the laws and the priesthood. Chapter 1 lays out the three categories of the burnt offering, of the herd, of the flocks, and of fowls. Knowing the distinctions of the offerings is not what saves you, but it is your heritage and your history, and you should not be ignorant of it. Leviticus 1:1-3 - The Lord called unto Moses out of the tabernacle of the congregation, the tent just reared up at the end of Exodus 40, and gave the law of the offerings brought of the cattle, of the herd and of the flock. - The burnt sacrifice of the herd is of the cattle, such as the bullock and the heifer. It had to be a male without blemish, offered of his own voluntary will at the door of the tabernacle. - In the book of Malachi the priests were finessing and corrupting this law: a man would bring a male without blemish, and the priest would keep it and sacrifice a blemished one, with a broken leg or a blind eye. That corruption is even more of a reason why Christ had to come and be the perfect sacrifice once and for all. Precepts: - Malachi 1:14 Cursed be the deceiver which hath in his flock a male, and sacrificeth unto the Lord a corrupt thing; the priests corrupted the law of the unblemished male. Leviticus 1:4-9 - He put his hand upon the head of the burnt offering, and it was accepted for him to make an atonement for him; the bullock was killed before the Lord, the blood sprinkled round about upon the altar by the priests, and the parts laid in order upon the wood on the fire. - Notice the fat is laid on the altar. Do not stumble when chapter 3 says not to eat fat: that deals with the fat of the sacrifice that the priest sent up in the offering, not the fat on a steak off your grill. - The offering made by fire is a sweet savour unto the Lord. Christ walked in love and gave himself for us an offering and a sacrifice to God for a sweetsmelling savour: he fulfilled and replaced all these offerings, once and for all, in his death and resurrection. - This is the context so much of Paul's letters sit in: he was convincing the congregations that they no longer had to sacrifice animals, because Pharisees were creeping in trying to turn them back to those things; therefore let no man judge you in meat or in drink. - In our captivity, with no Levitical priesthood and no temple, keeping the commandments is the offering and the reasonable service: he that keepeth the law bringeth offerings enough, and we present our bodies a living sacrifice, sacrificing the lusts and pleasures of the flesh to follow the footsteps of Christ. And Ezekiel 20 shows that when Israel is brought back through the wilderness, offerings will be required again in the holy mountain. Precepts: - Ephesians 5:2 Christ gave himself for us an offering and a sacrifice to God for a sweetsmelling savour; he is the sacrifice once for all. - Colossians 2:16 Let no man judge you in meat, or in drink; Paul defended the congregations from those pushing them back to the sacrifices. - Ecclesiasticus 35:1 Keeping the law brings offerings enough; that is our offering with no temple standing. - Romans 12:1 Present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service. - Ezekiel 20:40 In the holy mountain, at the return, all Israel shall serve the Most High, and there He will require the offerings again. Leviticus 1:10-13 - The second category is the burnt sacrifice of the flocks: the sheep and the goats, a male without blemish, killed on the side of the altar northward before the Lord, the pieces laid in order and washed, and all burnt upon the altar, a sweet savour unto the Lord. Leviticus 1:14-17 - The third category is the burnt sacrifice of fowls, meaning birds: turtledoves or young pigeons. That is the offering meant when a woman after childbirth brings two turtledoves or two young pigeons, as in Leviticus 12. Precepts: - Leviticus 12:8 If she be not able to bring a lamb, she shall bring two turtles or two young pigeons; the offering of fowls served her purifying. --- Topics: Sacrifice and Atonement · The Feasts of the Most High · The Priesthood · The Sabbath ← Exodus 38-40 · Leviticus Study · Leviticus 2-5 →

title: Leviticus 10: Strange Fire and the Charge of the Priesthood
text: ← Leviticus 6-9 · Leviticus Study · Leviticus 14-15 → Leviticus 10: Strange Fire and the Charge of the Priesthood Read the chapter → Leviticus 10 Introduction This reading covers Leviticus 10 through 13: the strange fire of Nadab and Abihu and the charge laid on the priesthood, the dietary law of clean and unclean beasts, the law of purification after childbirth, and the law of the plague of leprosy. Leviticus 10:1-2 - Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aaron, took either of them his censer, put fire therein and incense thereon, and offered strange fire before the Lord, which he commanded them not; and fire went out from the Lord and devoured them. - The instructions for the incense were already given: Aaron shall burn sweet incense every morning and at even, a perpetual incense before the Lord throughout your generations, and ye shall offer no strange incense thereon. There were instructions on what could be burned and what could not; the strange fire is that Nadab and Abihu put strange incense before the Lord. - When the Most High gave instructions through Moses on what to sacrifice and how, it was with specificity; you were to do it exactly the way he told you. - They were also not the ones authorized to burn the incense; in the tabernacle service you had to be appointed to certain services and could not take a service upon yourself. Zacharias shows the pattern throughout the generations: he executed the priest's office in the order of his course, and his lot, his appointed job, was to burn incense when he went into the temple of the Lord. - The fire that went out from the Lord was the same fire that came out from before the Lord in Leviticus 9 and consumed the burnt offering upon the altar. Precepts: - Exodus 30:7-9 Aaron shall burn a perpetual sweet incense throughout your generations, and no strange incense; the law of the incense was already set. - Luke 1:5-9 Zacharias, a righteous priest of the course of Abia, had the burning of incense as his lot; each Levite was appointed his own service. - Leviticus 9:24 There came a fire out from before the Lord that consumed the offering on the altar; that is the fire that devoured Nadab and Abihu. Leviticus 10:3 - Then Moses said unto Aaron, this is what the Lord spake: I will be sanctified in them that come nigh me, and before all the people I will be glorified. And Aaron held his peace. Leviticus 10:4-5 - Moses called Mishael and Elzaphan, the sons of Uzziel the uncle of Aaron, and they came near and carried them in their coats out of the camp, as Moses had said. Leviticus 10:6 - Aaron, Eleazar, and Ithamar were told, uncover not your heads, neither rend your clothes, lest ye die and wrath come upon all the people; basically they were told not to mourn for them, because Nadab and Abihu died in the midst of sin and what they did was abominable to the Most High. The whole house of Israel would bewail the burning which the Lord kindled. - Ezekiel is the example of that word: the Most High took away the desire of his eyes, his wife, with a stroke, and told him make no mourning for the dead, neither weep, and Ezekiel went and taught the people that morning, and at even his wife died. - The same standard fell on Jehoiakim the son of Josiah: they shall not lament for him, saying, Ah my brother, or, Ah lord. Precepts: - Ezekiel 24:16-18 Make no mourning for the dead; the Most High took Ezekiel's wife and he was not to weep for her. - Jeremiah 22:18 Concerning Jehoiakim king of Judah: they shall not lament for him. Leviticus 10:7 - They were not to go out from the door of the tabernacle, for the anointing oil of the Lord was upon them. The anointing oil had already been put on them, so they could not leave the sanctuary. Precepts: - Leviticus 21:12 Neither shall he go out of the sanctuary, for the crown of the anointing oil of his God is upon him; that is why they could not leave. Leviticus 10:8-11 - Some read this and think Aaron and his sons could never drink, but going precept upon precept, this speaks of when they went into the tabernacle of the congregation: they were at work doing the Lord's work, and there was no drinking on the job. - Ezekiel lays out the priests' work rules. The priests the Levites, the sons of Zadok, kept the charge of the sanctuary; when they entered the gates of the inner court they were clocking in, clothed in linen garments and linen bonnets, girded with nothing that causeth sweat; and going out to the people in the utter court they put off the garments wherein they ministered and put on other garments, like taking off a work uniform. - Neither shall any priest drink wine when they enter into the inner court; that is exactly what verse 9 speaks of. - They had to be sober minded because they taught the people the difference between the holy and profane and caused them to discern between the unclean and the clean, and in controversy they stood in judgment, judging according to the judgments of the Most High. - On the priests' hair: they were not to shave their heads nor suffer their locks to grow long, but only poll their heads. Polling the head means keeping the hair trimmed and maintained; you can grow it, but keep it up. Precepts: - Ezekiel 44:15-16 The sons of Zadok that kept the charge of the sanctuary shall come near to minister unto the Most High and keep his charge. - Ezekiel 44:17-19 In the inner court they wear linen and nothing that causeth sweat, and going out to the people they put off the garments wherein they minister; the priest's uniform for the Lord's work. - Ezekiel 44:20 Neither shave the head nor suffer locks to grow long, but poll the head; keep the hair trimmed and maintained. - Ezekiel 44:21 Neither shall any priest drink wine when they enter into the inner court; no drinking on the job. - Ezekiel 44:23-24 They teach the difference between the holy and profane and stand in judgment in controversy; the priest must be sober dealing with the people. Leviticus 10:12-15 - Moses told Aaron, Eleazar, and Ithamar to take the meat offering that remained of the offerings made by fire and eat it without leaven beside the altar, in the holy place, for it was their due; and the wave breast and heave shoulder were eaten in a clean place, the due of Aaron and his sons and his daughters by a statute for ever. - The wave offering is explained in chapter 7: his own hands shall bring the offerings of the Lord made by fire, the fat with the breast, that the breast may be waved for a wave offering before the Lord. Precepts: - Leviticus 7:30 The fat with the breast is brought and the breast waved for a wave offering before the Lord; that is the wave offering of this passage. Leviticus 10:16-18 - Moses diligently sought the goat of the sin offering, and behold, it was burnt; and he was angry with Eleazar and Ithamar, because the Most High had given it to them to bear the iniquity of the congregation, and seeing the blood of it was not brought in within the holy place, they should indeed have eaten it in the holy place, as he commanded. - Those were the instructions of the law of the sin offering: the priest that offereth it for sin shall eat it in the holy place, and all the males among the priests shall eat thereof; but no sin offering whereof any of the blood is brought into the tabernacle to reconcile withal shall be eaten, it shall be burnt in the fire. Precepts: - Leviticus 6:25-26 The law of the sin offering: the priest that offereth it for sin shall eat it in the holy place. - Leviticus 6:29-30 All the males among the priests shall eat thereof, but a sin offering whose blood is brought into the tabernacle is burnt, not eaten. Leviticus 10:19-20 - Aaron answered Moses: this day have they offered their sin offering and their burnt offering, and such things have befallen me; and if I had eaten the sin offering today, should it have been accepted in the sight of the Lord? And when Moses heard that, he was content. Leviticus 11: The Dietary Law of Clean and Unclean Beasts Read the chapter → Leviticus 11 Leviticus 11:1-3 - Leviticus 11 tells you what you can and cannot eat. Among all the beasts of the earth, ye shall eat whatsoever parteth the hoof, and is clovenfooted, and cheweth the cud. - A cloven hoof is a hoof split into two toes; mammals with this hoof include cattle, deer, antelopes, gazelles, goats, and sheep. - Chewing the cud means the animal has more than one stomach: it chews its food, brings it back up into its mouth to be chewed again, and then digests it through another stomach. Leviticus 11:4-8 - Both marks must be present. There are animals that chew the cud and animals that divide the hoof but do not have both; those are unclean. The camel cheweth the cud but divideth not the hoof: you cannot eat camel. - The coney is the pika, a small mountain dwelling mammal that resembles its close relative the rabbit, found at heights among the highest of any mammal. The scriptures already had it right: the rocks are a refuge for the conies, and the conies, a feeble folk, make their houses in the rocks. You cannot eat coney, and the hare likewise is unclean. - The swine has only the one mark: he divideth the hoof and is clovenfooted, yet he cheweth not the cud; he is unclean unto you. You cannot eat pork; leave it alone. - Their carcase shall ye not touch sits inside the dietary law: it goes into sacrificing the unclean thing and eating it, touching it with the mouth. It does not mean a dead animal in your path cannot be moved out of the way with the hands; the tabernacle itself had to be built by hand with badgers' skins. Precepts: - Psalms 104:18 The rocks are a refuge for the conies; the coney is the rock dwelling pika. - Proverbs 30:26 The conies are but a feeble folk, yet make they their houses in the rocks.
