Leviticus 11:9-12 - Of all that are in the waters, ye shall eat whatsoever hath fins and scales; whatever has not fins and scales is an abomination. No shrimp, no crab, no lobster, no bottom dwellers. - The Most High gave an excellent dietary law: high blood pressure and the like come from eating shellfish. He made these animals and knows what they do; if you eat what he allowed you will be fine. It is simple: if it does not have both fins and scales, leave it alone. - A fish must have both scales and fins. Tilapia has scales and fins, so it may be eaten if you want it; sardines do not show both, so it looks like sardines are a no. Leviticus 11:13-19 - These are the fowls in abomination that shall not be eaten: the eagle, the ossifrage, the osprey, the vulture and the kite after his kind, every raven after his kind, the owl, the nighthawk, the cuckow, the hawk, the little owl, the cormorant, the great owl, the swan, the pelican, the gier eagle, the stork, the heron after her kind, the lapwing, and the bat. - Look these up. The ossifrage, the bone breaker, is an older name for the bearded vulture, a scavenger famous for dropping bones on rocks to crack them open. The osprey is the seahawk or fishhawk, a fish eating bird of prey. The kite is a bird of prey in the family of the eagle. - What is interesting is that all of these are scavengers and hunters; even in the waters the Most High did not want you to have the scavengers, and no shark, a hunter. He gave you this diet because he made these animals and knows what they do. - After his kind: when the Most High made one, he made many of them, so the rule covers the whole family. - On duck: the swan's closest relatives include the geese and ducks. The swan is unclean, and duck falls in the family of the swan, so you cannot eat duck; they are related, and it is the same thing. Leviticus 11:20-23 - All fowls that creep, going upon all four, are an abomination, yet those which have legs above their feet to leap withal upon the earth may be eaten: the locust, the bald locust, the beetle, and the grasshopper after his kind. You can eat locusts; John the Baptist ate locusts. Leviticus 11:24-28 - The carcases of every beast which divideth the hoof and is not clovenfooted nor cheweth the cud are unclean; whoever touches them is unclean until the even, and whoever bears the carcase washes his clothes. - Whatsoever goeth upon his paws, among all manner of beasts that go on all four, is unclean: you cannot eat mountain lion, tiger, cougar, gorilla, dog, or cat; they have paws and walk on all fours. Leviticus 11:29-38 - These creeping things are unclean: the weasel, the mouse, the tortoise after his kind, the ferret, the chameleon, the lizard, the snail, and the mole. You cannot eat tortoise. - If you find a dead mouse in your house, do not touch it: sweep it into a bag and throw it out. - Whatever vessel one of them falls into when dead is unclean until the even and must be put into water; if it falls into one of your pots, clean that pot out and cook nothing in it until the even. An earthen vessel it falls into is broken and thrown out, and ovens and ranges for pots are broken down. - If any part of their carcase falls on sowing seed which is to be sown, the seed is clean; but if water be put upon the seed and the carcase fall thereon, it is unclean and no good. Leviticus 11:39-43 - Even of a beast which ye may eat, if it die of itself, he that toucheth, eateth of, or beareth the carcase is unclean until the even and washes his clothes. - Every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth is an abomination: whatsoever goeth upon the belly, whatsoever goeth upon all four, and whatsoever hath more feet. You cannot eat centipedes and millipedes. Leviticus 11:44-47 - Sanctify yourselves, and ye shall be holy, for I am holy: for I am the Lord that bringeth you up out of the land of Egypt to be your God. This is the law of the beast and of the fowl and of every living creature that moveth in the waters and of every creature that creepeth upon the earth; the Most High explained everything and then summed it all up, to make a difference between the unclean and the clean, and between the beast that may be eaten and the beast that may not be eaten. - Do not confuse yourself with 1 Timothy 4:4, that you can eat whatever you want. Every creature is good and nothing to be refused if it be received with thanksgiving, for it is sanctified by the word of God; so find what the word of God sanctified, and that is the law of the beast in Leviticus 11. What is sanctified is what he already made clean. - The law perisheth not, but remaineth in his force; that law did not change at all. Do not let anybody confuse you, especially if you are new in the truth: eat what the Most High instructed you to eat. Precepts: - 1 Timothy 4:4-5 Every creature received with thanksgiving is sanctified by the word of God; the word of God sanctified the clean beasts of Leviticus 11. - 2 Esdras 9:37 The law perisheth not but remaineth in his force; the dietary law did not change. Leviticus 12: The Law of Purification After Childbirth Read the chapter → Leviticus 12 Leviticus 12:1-2 - If a woman have conceived seed and born a man child, she shall be unclean seven days, according to the days of the separation for her infirmity. Conceived seed means the sperm has met the egg: at intercourse about 300 million sperm enter, most die on the journey, and fertilization is one sperm uniting with the egg to form new life. All of that has to happen; that is conceiving seed. - At the moment of fertilization a unique genetic code arises, instantly determining gender: an X with an X chromosome is a female, and an X with a Y chromosome is a male. Gender is determined at conception; you do not get to choose it, and there is no changing it afterward. - Even inside the woman it is a male and a female pronucleus that come together to form the baby: male and female, not two males. - The seven days match the law of the woman's issue: when her issue is blood, she is put apart seven days; those are the days of her separation spoken of here. Precepts: - Leviticus 15:19 If a woman have an issue of blood she shall be put apart seven days; those are the days of the separation. Leviticus 12:3 - In the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised. The law is Genesis 17: every man child among you shall be circumcised at eight days old, a token of the covenant, and my covenant shall be in your flesh for an everlasting covenant; the uncircumcised man child whose flesh is not circumcised, that soul shall be cut off from his people. Brothers coming into the truth must be circumcised. - That did not change. On the eighth day they came to circumcise John the Baptist, and when eight days were accomplished for the circumcising of the child, his name was called Jesus, which was so named of the angel before he was conceived in the womb. Precepts: - Genesis 17:10-14 Every man child eight days old shall be circumcised, an everlasting covenant in the flesh; the uncircumcised is cut off. - Luke 1:59-60 On the eighth day they came to circumcise the child, and he was called John; John the Baptist was circumcised. - Luke 2:21 When eight days were accomplished for the circumcising of the child, his name was called Jesus; Christ kept the same law. Leviticus 12:4 - She shall then continue in the blood of her purifying three and thirty days: seven days of separation plus thirty three days is forty days. If she has a male child she is unclean forty days, touching no hallowed thing and coming not into the sanctuary until the days of her purifying be fulfilled. - Mary is the fulfilment of that: when the days of her purification according to the law of Moses were accomplished, they brought him to Jerusalem to present him to the Lord; Mary had to do this law. Precepts: - Luke 2:22 When the days of her purification according to the law of Moses were accomplished; Mary kept the law of the forty days. Leviticus 12:5 - If she bear a maid child, she shall be unclean two weeks, as in her separation, and continue in the blood of her purifying threescore and six days: fourteen days plus sixty six days is eighty days for a daughter. - Solomon describes the birth every man has: he was a mortal man, fashioned to be flesh in his mother's womb in the time of ten months, compacted in blood of the seed of man. A full term pregnancy is forty weeks, which is ten months; they say nine months but forget the month of conception. - There is no king that had any other beginning of birth, and all men have one entrance into life. Christ was no exception: he was made of the seed of David according to the flesh, so it took seed to come through David's line. Precepts: - Wisdom of Solomon 7:1-6 No king had any other beginning of birth; every man is fashioned to be flesh in ten months of the seed of man. - Romans 1:3 Jesus Christ our Lord was made of the seed of David according to the flesh. Leviticus 12:6-8 - When the days of her purifying are fulfilled, for a son or for a daughter, she brings a lamb of the first year for a burnt offering and a young pigeon or a turtledove for a sin offering to the priest, who makes an atonement for her; and if she be not able to bring a lamb, she brings two turtles or two young pigeons. - What is heavy is how hard conception is: all the work the body does to create life, and then to take that life away in abortion is against everything the body labored to do. Leviticus 13: The Law of the Plague of Leprosy Read the chapter → Leviticus 13 Leviticus 13:1-8 - The plague of leprosy is discerned by the priest. When the hair in the plague is turned white and the plague in sight is deeper than the skin of the flesh, it is a plague of leprosy and the priest pronounces him unclean; if not, the priest shuts him up seven days, and seven days more if the plague is at a stay, and if the plague is somewhat dark and spread not, it is but a scab and he is pronounced clean; but a scab that spreads much abroad after his cleansing is a leprosy. Leviticus 13:12-13 - If the leprosy break out abroad and cover all the flesh from head to foot, and it be all turned white, the priest shall pronounce him clean. - That is the albino: if the leprosy covers all the skin, as in an albino, he is still clean. A man can be albino and still be Israel; if his father is Judah, he is clean. It is not about your skin, it is about your nationality. Leviticus 13:29-30 - For a plague upon the head or the beard, if it be in sight deeper than the skin, and there be in it a yellow thin hair, it is a dry scall, even a leprosy upon the head or beard, and the priest pronounces him unclean. - Yellow thin hair is called a plague. Our hair does not come like that; the nations that have blonde hair are naturally that way. When Israel, blacks, Hispanics, and Native Americans dye their hair blonde, they are taking after the customs of Esau, emulating who they want to be like, and the word calls that yellow thin hair a plague on our people. - There is no law against color as such: the scripture names yellow thin hair; but go with what the word says. Leviticus 13:40-41 - The man whose hair is fallen off his head is bald, yet is he clean; and he whose hair is fallen off toward his face is forehead bald, yet is he clean. - So do not assume against a brother: if he goes bald naturally, the word says the man is clean, and a brother may be forehead bald with hair further back you cannot see. Leviticus 13:45-46 - The leper in whom the plague is, his clothes shall be rent, his head bare, a covering upon his upper lip, and he shall cry, Unclean, unclean; all the days the plague is in him he is defiled, and he shall dwell alone, without the camp. - Miriam is the example. She and Aaron spake against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman whom he had married, Miriam trying to usurp authority over the man, and the Lord heard it; the cloud departed, and behold, Miriam became leprous, white as snow. - The Lord said, if her father had but spit in her face, should she not be ashamed seven days? Let her be shut out from the camp seven days, and after that let her be received in again. That is the same law working here: the leper is put without the camp. Precepts: - Numbers 12:1-2 Miriam and Aaron spake against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman, and the Lord heard it. - Numbers 12:10 The cloud departed from off the tabernacle, and Miriam became leprous, white as snow. - Numbers 12:14-15 Let her be shut out from the camp seven days, and after that received in again; the leper dwells without the camp. Leviticus 13:47-52 - The plague of leprosy can be in a garment, woollen or linen, in the warp or woof or in any thing made of skin, greenish or reddish; it is shewed unto the priest and shut up seven days, and if the plague be spread in the garment it is a fretting leprosy: the garment is burnt in the fire. As with Miriam, the clothing wherein the plague is had to be dealt with. Leviticus 13:53-59 - If the plague be not spread, the thing is washed and shut up seven days more; if the plague have not changed his colour it is burnt, and if it be somewhat dark after washing, the piece is rent out; if it appear still, it is a spreading plague and burnt with fire; and the garment that the plague departs from is washed the second time and shall be clean. This is the law of the plague of leprosy in a garment, to pronounce it clean or to pronounce it unclean. --- Topics: Clean and Unclean Meats · Esau and Edom · Sacrifice and Atonement · The Covenant · The Feasts of the Most High · The Priesthood · The Sabbath ← Leviticus 6-9 · Leviticus Study · Leviticus 14-15 →

title: Leviticus 14: The Law of the Leper in the Day of His Cleansing
text: ← Leviticus 10-13 · Leviticus Study · Leviticus 18-21 → Leviticus 14: The Law of the Leper in the Day of His Cleansing Read the chapter → Leviticus 14 Introduction This session is a reading-only recording covering Leviticus 14 and 15 only. The chapters were read straight through without exposition or question and answer, so these notes carry the reading itself with short breakdowns and no precepts. Chapter 14 gives the law of the leper in the day of his cleansing and the law of the plague of leprosy in a house; chapter 15 gives the law of issues, the running issues of the flesh and the separation of the woman, ending with the charge to separate the children of Israel from their uncleanness. Note a gap in the series: no session was ever recorded for Leviticus 16 and 17, so this book passes from chapter 15 to chapter 18. Leviticus 14:1-3 - This is the law of the leper in the day of his cleansing. The leper stays outside the camp; the priest goes forth out of the camp to him and looks whether the plague of leprosy be healed in the leper. - The priest does not heal the plague; he examines the man after the healing and carries out the cleansing the Most High commanded. Leviticus 14:4-7 - For him that is to be cleansed the priest commands two birds alive and clean, cedar wood, scarlet, and hyssop. One bird is killed in an earthen vessel over running water. - The living bird, with the cedar wood, the scarlet, and the hyssop, is dipped in the blood of the bird that was killed over the running water; the priest sprinkles him that is to be cleansed seven times, pronounces him clean, and lets the living bird loose into the open field. Leviticus 14:8-9 - He that is to be cleansed washes his clothes, shaves off all his hair, and washes himself in water, and comes into the camp; but he tarries abroad out of his tent seven days. - On the seventh day he shaves all his hair off his head, his beard, and his eyebrows, washes his clothes and his flesh in water, and is clean. Leviticus 14:10-13 - On the eighth day he brings two he lambs without blemish, one ewe lamb of the first year without blemish, three tenth deals of fine flour mingled with oil for a meat offering, and one log of oil. - The priest that makes him clean presents him with these things before the Most High at the door of the tabernacle. One he lamb is offered for a trespass offering with the log of oil, waved for a wave offering, and slain in the holy place: as the sin offering is the priest's, so is the trespass offering; it is most holy. Leviticus 14:14-18 - The priest takes of the blood of the trespass offering and puts it upon the tip of the right ear of him that is to be cleansed, upon the thumb of his right hand, and upon the great toe of his right foot. - Of the log of oil the priest pours into his own left hand, sprinkles of it with his finger seven times before the Lord, and puts oil upon the ear, the thumb, and the toe, upon the blood of the trespass offering; the remnant of the oil he pours upon the head of him that is to be cleansed, to make an atonement for him before the Lord. Leviticus 14:19-20 - The priest then offers the sin offering to make an atonement for him that is to be cleansed from his uncleanness, kills the burnt offering, and offers the burnt offering and the meat offering upon the altar; the priest makes an atonement for him, and he shall be clean. Leviticus 14:21-32 - If he be poor and cannot get so much, the law makes provision: one lamb for a trespass offering to be waved, one tenth deal of fine flour mingled with oil, a log of oil, and two turtledoves or two young pigeons, such as he is able to get, the one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering. - The same order is kept for the poor man: the blood of the trespass offering upon the right ear, the right thumb, and the right great toe, the oil sprinkled seven times and put upon the same places, and the rest of the oil upon his head. This is the law of him in whom is the plague of leprosy, whose hand is not able to get that which pertaineth to his cleansing. Leviticus 14:33-42 - The Most High tells Moses and Aaron that when Israel comes into the land of Canaan, and he puts the plague of leprosy in a house of the land of their possession, the owner shall come and tell the priest, saying, It seemeth to me there is as it were a plague in the house. - The priest commands that the house be emptied before he goes in, that all that is in it be not made unclean; then he looks on the plague, and if it be in the walls with hollow strakes, greenish or reddish, in sight lower than the wall, he shuts up the house seven days. - If at the seventh day the plague be spread in the walls, the stones in which the plague is are taken away and cast into an unclean place without the city; the house is scraped within round about, the dust poured out without the city into an unclean place, and other stones and other mortar are put in their place. Leviticus 14:43-47 - If the plague come again and break out in the house after the stones were taken away and the house scraped and plastered, the priest looks, and if the plague be spread, it is a fretting leprosy in the house: it is unclean. - He breaks down the house, the stones of it, the timber, and all the mortar, and carries them forth out of the city into an unclean place. He that goes into the house while it is shut up is unclean until the even, and he that lies or eats in the house washes his clothes. Leviticus 14:48-53 - If the priest comes in and looks, and the plague hath not spread in the house after it was plastered, the priest pronounces the house clean, because the plague is healed. - The house is cleansed the same way as the leper: two birds, cedar wood, scarlet, and hyssop; one bird killed in an earthen vessel over running water, the house sprinkled seven times, and the living bird let go out of the city into the open fields; so he makes an atonement for the house, and it shall be clean. Leviticus 14:54-57 - The chapter closes the summary: this is the law for all manner of plague of leprosy and scall, for the leprosy of a garment and of a house, for a rising, a scab, and a bright spot, to teach when it is unclean and when it is clean. This is the law of leprosy. Leviticus 15: The Law of Issues and Separation Read the chapter → Leviticus 15 Leviticus 15:1-12 - When any man hath a running issue out of his flesh, because of his issue he is unclean, whether his flesh run with his issue or be stopped from his issue. - Every bed whereon he lies and every thing whereon he sits is unclean. Whoever touches his bed, sits where he sat, touches his flesh, or is touched by him before he has rinsed his hands, washes his clothes, bathes himself in water, and is unclean until the even; the same goes for his spittle and his saddle. - The vessel of earth that he touches shall be broken, and every vessel of wood shall be rinsed in water. Leviticus 15:13-15 - When he that hath an issue is cleansed of his issue, he numbers to himself seven days for his cleansing, washes his clothes, and bathes his flesh in running water, and shall be clean. - On the eighth day he takes two turtledoves or two young pigeons and comes before the Lord unto the door of the tabernacle, and gives them unto the priest; the priest offers the one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering, and makes an atonement for him before the Lord for his issue. Leviticus 15:16-18 - If any man's seed of copulation go out from him, he washes all his flesh in water and is unclean until the even; every garment and every skin whereon is the seed is washed with water and unclean until the even. - The woman also with whom a man lies with seed of copulation: they both bathe themselves in water and are unclean until the even. Leviticus 15:19-24 - When a woman has an issue, and her issue in her flesh be blood, she is put apart seven days for her separation, and whosoever toucheth her is unclean until the even. - Every thing that she lies upon or sits upon in her separation is unclean; whoever touches her bed or any thing she sat upon washes his clothes, bathes himself in water, and is unclean until the even. - If any man lie with her at all, and her flowers be upon him, he is unclean seven days, and all the bed whereon he lies is unclean. Leviticus 15:25-27 - If a woman have an issue of her blood many days out of the time of her separation, or if it run beyond the time of her separation, all the days of the issue of her uncleanness are as the days of her separation: she is unclean. - Every bed she lies on and every thing she sits upon in those days is as the uncleanness of her separation, and whosoever touches those things washes his clothes, bathes in water, and is unclean until the even. Leviticus 15:28-30 - When she is cleansed of her issue, she numbers to herself seven days, and after that she shall be clean. - On the eighth day she takes two turtles or two young pigeons and brings them unto the priest to the door of the tabernacle; the priest offers the one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering, and makes an atonement for her before the Lord for the issue of her uncleanness. Leviticus 15:31-33 - The purpose of the whole chapter is stated plainly: thus shall ye separate the children of Israel from their uncleanness, that they die not in their uncleanness when they defile the tabernacle of the Most High that is among them. - This is the law of him that hath an issue, of him whose seed goeth from him, of her that is sick of her flowers, of him and her that have issues, and of him that lieth with her that is unclean. --- Topics: Clean and Unclean Meats · Sacrifice and Atonement · The Priesthood · The Sabbath ← Leviticus 10-13 · Leviticus Study · Leviticus 18-21 →

title: Leviticus 18: After the Doings of Egypt and Canaan Shall Ye Not Do
text: ← Leviticus 14-15 · Leviticus Study · Leviticus 22-25 → Leviticus 18: After the Doings of Egypt and Canaan Shall Ye Not Do Read the chapter → Leviticus 18 Introduction This reading covers Leviticus 18 through 21: the unlawful beds forbidden after the doings of Egypt and Canaan, the statutes of holiness for everyday life, the judgments appointed for the abominations, and the holiness required of the priests, the sons of Aaron. All four chapters were read and taught. Leviticus 18:1-3 - In Egypt the children of Israel served the gods of Egypt, dressed like Egyptians, and were fully engulfed in the Egyptian way of life; Moses himself was raised as an Egyptian in the house of Pharaoh. The Most High told them to leave all of that back in Egypt. - The same word stands for us: when the Most High redeems us out of this captivity, many of the customs we learned here will be cut off, because they are not coming into the kingdom. - The land of Canaan was full of idols. If Israel obeyed His voice the Most High would be an enemy to their enemies, bless their bread and water, and take sickness away; the charge in Canaan was not to bow to their gods nor do after their works, but to utterly overthrow them and break down their images. - Coming out of Egypt required a transformed mind: not conformed to the way of life of Egypt or Canaan, but renewed to the commandments of the Most High. Precepts: - Exodus 23:22-25 Obey His voice and He is an enemy to thine enemies; the nations of Canaan and their gods were to be overthrown, not learned from. - Romans 12:2 Be not conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind. Leviticus 18:4-6 - Keep the statutes and judgments of the Most High, which if a man do, he shall live in them. - The Ten Commandments are not the whole of the law but a summary. Under the Sabbath commandment sit sub-statutes such as no buying, no selling, no working; likewise under the law of adultery sit all the laws of this chapter, the ordinances of marriage and the forbidden beds. - None of you shall approach to any that is near of kin to uncover their nakedness; these laws name who a man may not lay down with. Leviticus 18:7-8 - The nakedness of thy father's wife is thy father's nakedness; that is the stepmother. The wicked mind reasons that she is not the biological mother, so it is fine to lust after her; the scripture says no, that is wicked. - This very sin was reported among the Corinthians, a fornication not so much as named among the Gentiles, that one should have his father's wife. The law had already forbidden it, and it was being done in Egypt and Canaan; that is why the Most High opened the chapter the way He did. Precepts: - 1 Corinthians 5:1 Fornication that one should have his father's wife; the law of Leviticus 18:8 was being broken in the days of the apostles. Leviticus 18:9-11 - The sister, whether born at home or born abroad, and the son's daughter and the daughter's daughter are all forbidden; the grandchildren's nakedness is thine own nakedness. - There are sick spirits out there, and some of them are grandfathers, uncles, and fathers. Be careful and mindful who you leave your children around; do not hand your children to just anybody for the sake of your own pleasure. Leviticus 18:12-14 - The father's sister, the mother's sister, and the wife of the father's brother, thine aunt, are all near kinswomen and off limits. - Incest is still practiced among the nations of this land, and children born of incestuous unions often carry defects and disabilities; the law guards the seed. Leviticus 18:15-18 - The daughter in law, the brother's wife, and a woman with her daughter or her granddaughter are all forbidden; it is wickedness. - Neither take a wife to her sister to vex her, to uncover her nakedness beside the other in her lifetime; that also shuts down what the world today calls threesomes. Leviticus 18:19 - A woman put apart for her uncleanness is a woman in her menstrual cycle. A man must wait the appointed seven days, and if the issue runs beyond, wait again; Leviticus 15 details these laws of uncleanness, taught in the previous class. Precepts: - Leviticus 15:19 The law of her separation: she shall be put apart seven days. Leviticus 18:20 - To lie carnally with thy neighbour's wife is adultery. This world even sings songs celebrating adultery; the law forbids defiling thyself with her. Leviticus 18:21 - Passing seed through the fire to Molech was child sacrifice: the nations slew their newborn children and offered them to that god, and Israel learned it from them, as Ezekiel testifies of Jerusalem slaying the children of the Most High. - The abortions of today are no different. The Most High is bringing spirits into the earth, and the child is slain so the parents can go on living as they please; that is the same sacrifice unto Molech, and it is wickedness. Precepts: - Ezekiel 16:20-21 Thou hast slain my children and delivered them to cause them to pass through the fire; that is what giving seed to Molech means. Leviticus 18:22 - Abomination means a thing that causes disgust or hatred. When a man lies with mankind as with womankind, the Most High calls it disgusting and hateful. - What a man hates and finds disgusting he removes far from himself; so we must teach our people to repent and come out of the things the Most High hates. Leviticus 18:23 - Lying with any beast is confusion, for man and for woman alike. The nations have set up places where these strange lusts are fulfilled, and the sin is found among every people; it is all wickedness. Leviticus 18:24-30 - In all these things the nations were defiled which the Most High cast out; the Egyptians and the Canaanites were doing these very abominations, and the land itself was defiled by them. - The land spews out the defiled. That is why Israel was put out of Jerusalem: we could not abide in the land with our sins, sacrificing to idol gods and working all manner of evil, so the Most High raised up an enemy to carry us into bondage and remove us out of the land. - Whosoever commits any of these abominations, the souls that commit them shall be cut off from among their people, meaning put to death. Leviticus 19: Ye Shall Be Holy, for I the Lord Your God Am Holy Read the chapter → Leviticus 19 Leviticus 19:1-3 - Ye shall be holy, for I the Lord your God am holy; this word went to all the congregation of the children of Israel. - Fear every man his mother and his father goes back to the commandment, honour thy father and thy mother. - Honour can be kept even at a distance: show respect, and do nothing that would bring shame on your mother. But there is a balance; if she asks for what is against the commandments of the Most High, the commandments come first. - Keep my sabbaths: the feast days are Sabbaths also. The Passover, the first and last days of the feast of Tabernacles, the day of atonement, and the memorial of blowing of trumpets are all Sabbaths; no servile work, no buying and selling, though cooking is permitted on the feast days. Precepts: - Exodus 20:12 Honour thy father and thy mother; fearing them in Leviticus 19 is the same commandment. Leviticus 19:4 - Turn not unto idols, nor make molten gods; this is the commandment against making any graven image. Precepts: - Exodus 20:4 Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image. Leviticus 19:5-8 - The peace offering was eaten the same day it was offered or on the morrow; whatever remained to the third day was burnt. Eaten on the third day it is abominable, and the eater bears his iniquity, for he has profaned the hallowed thing of the Lord. Leviticus 19:9-10 - The corners of the field, the gleanings of the harvest, and the leavings of the vineyard belonged to the poor and the stranger. The Most High is teaching, do not be selfish; love thy neighbour as thyself and look out for the poor of your people. - He that provides not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, has denied the faith. Those of his own house are his wife and children; his own is his nation. Care for your people. - Charge them that are rich that they be not highminded, but ready to distribute, willing to communicate. Most of us today have no fields or vineyards, but some have good jobs and blessed incomes; you cannot take it with you, so give of your substance. The scriptures also say no good can come to him that gives no alms. Precepts: - 1 Timothy 5:8 Provide for thine own and specially for those of thine own house; the own is the nation, the house is the family. - 1 Timothy 6:17-18 The rich are charged to be ready to distribute, willing to communicate; the law of the gleanings teaches the same giving. Leviticus 19:11 - Dealing falsely is any dishonesty: skewing the truth to get your way, or cheating. - Be honest. Have an honest job so you do not steal; run an honest business so you do not cheat people with foul practices, selling goods you know will fail or charging a customer for repairs he does not need. That honesty is owed even to the other nations. Leviticus 19:12 - Do not swear by His name falsely. Saying I swear to God over a lie profanes the name of the Most High. - Christ said swear not at all, neither by heaven, nor by the earth, nor by thy head; let your communication be yea, yea and nay, nay. The only reason a man swears is that he has lied before and no one believes him; in your repentance take swearing out of your speech, and do not put oaths on your own head or your family either. Precepts: - Matthew 5:33-37 Swear not at all; let your communication be yea, yea and nay, nay, for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil. Leviticus 19:13 - The wages of him that is hired shall not abide with thee all night until the morning: when a man works for you, pay him that same day. Holding back the wage is defrauding thy neighbour, so businesses in Israel should pay their people the way the scriptures say. - If both parties agree beforehand to payment the next day, that agreement is between you, the Lord, and that man; the scripture states the standard. Leviticus 19:14-15 - Curse not the deaf, put no stumblingblock before the blind, but fear thy God. - Do no unrighteousness in judgment; respect not the person of the poor nor honour the person of the mighty. The courts of this land do the opposite: our people receive far harsher sentences than others for the same crime with the same priors, sometimes before the very same judge. Leviticus 19:16 - A talebearer revealeth secrets, but he that is of a faithful spirit concealeth the matter. What a brother or sister tells you in confidence is not yours to spread; carrying it to the next person is talebearing, and it happens even in this truth. - Where no wood is, there the fire goeth out: much strife and contention comes from messy people. Repent of that messy spirit; it has no place in Israel. Precepts: - Proverbs 11:13 A talebearer revealeth secrets; the faithful spirit conceals the matter. - Proverbs 26:20 Where no talebearer is, the strife ceaseth; messy people feed the fire. Leviticus 19:17-18 - Hate not thy brother in thine heart; rebuke thy neighbour and suffer not sin upon him. If you love your brother or sister you correct them when they are going off into sin; that is real love. - Love thy neighbour as thyself: thy neighbour is the children of thy people. Get that right, against the teaching that makes the neighbour everybody. Leviticus 19:19 - Keep the statutes: no gendering cattle with a diverse kind, no sowing the field with mingled seed, and no garment mingled of linen and woollen; that is the law against mixed fabrics. Leviticus 19:20-22 - The bondmaid betrothed to an husband and not redeemed was scourged, not put to death, because she was not free; the man brought a ram for a trespass offering, and the priest made atonement, and the sin was forgiven him. Leviticus 19:23-25 - Fruit of a newly planted tree was counted as uncircumcised for three years and not eaten; in the fourth year all the fruit was holy to praise the Lord withal; only in the fifth year could the fruit be eaten, that it might yield its increase. Leviticus 19:26 - Eat nothing with the blood: cook the blood out of the meat. No rare or bloody meat, none of the raw-meat customs of the other nations. - Use no enchantments nor observe times; that goes into the horoscopes, astrology, and the rest of that nonsense. Leave it alone. Leviticus 19:27 - Round not the corners of your head, meaning do not bald your head; mar not the corners of thy beard, meaning do not shave off the beard. This is written to all the children of Israel, not to the priests only. Leviticus 19:28 - No cuttings in the flesh for the dead, nor any marks printed upon you: that is the tattoo. The RIP tattoo for a dead family member is both a cutting in the flesh for the dead and a mark printed upon you. - If you came into this truth already carrying tattoos, repent, ask the Most High for forgiveness, and get no more. - Ear and nose piercings are not forbidden by this verse; the cutting forbidden here is the cutting in the flesh for the dead. Leviticus 19:29 - Prostituting your daughter to cause her to be a whore takes several forms: letting her dress immodestly, letting a little girl wear makeup and grown attire, and letting her have a boyfriend. There are no boyfriends and girlfriends in the scriptures. - The father waketh for the daughter: his charge is to watch over her, know her clothes, her phone, her friends and their parents, and keep her under supervision, lest she pass away the flower of her age, which is her virginity being taken. Keeping a sure watch over her is not being too hard on her; it is the commandment, lest she make thee a laughingstock to thine enemies. - Many daughters go the way of the mother, as the proverb says, as is the mother, so is her daughter; but Israel is teaching the sisters self-respect again, with the scriptures on modest apparel and on not wearing that which pertaineth to a man. - When daughters are left without watch, the land falls into whoredom and fills with wickedness; the state of the community today shows the fruit of neglecting this law. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 42:9-11 The father waketh for the daughter when no man knoweth; keep a sure watch over a shameless daughter. - Ezekiel 16:44 As is the mother, so is her daughter; the pattern repeats unless it is broken. - 1 Timothy 2:9 Women adorn themselves in modest apparel, with shamefacedness and sobriety. - Deuteronomy 22:5 The woman shall not wear that which pertaineth unto a man; the dress code is law. Leviticus 19:30-32 - Keep my sabbaths and reverence my sanctuary. - Regard not them that have familiar spirits, neither seek after wizards to be defiled by them. - Rise up before the hoary head and honour the face of the old man: show respect unto your elders. Leviticus 19:33-34 - Vex not the stranger that sojourns with thee in the land; he shall be as one born among you, and thou shalt love him as thyself, for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt. - The stranger of this law is an Israelite of another tribe sojourning outside the allotment of his own tribe: a man of Judah dwelling in the land of Benjamin is a stranger to that land, because that was not the allotment the Most High gave him. When your brother the stranger falls into decay, relieve him and let him sojourn with you; give him work to deliver him out of his low state until he can stand again. - The bondmen laws show the contrast in how the word stranger is used. The bondmen and bondmaids were to be of the heathen round about, and in that context the children of the strangers sojourning among you are the heathen, a possession and an inheritance; but over your brethren the children of Israel ye shall not rule with rigour. Then the sojourner or stranger that waxeth rich by thee returns to the Israelite stranger, for the bondservant of the heathen did not wax rich. Precepts: - Exodus 22:21 Thou shalt neither vex a stranger nor oppress him, for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt. - Leviticus 25:35 Thy brother waxen poor is called a stranger or a sojourner, so the stranger of this law is your own brother outside his allotment. - Leviticus 25:43-46 In the bondmen context the stranger is the heathen round about, but over your brethren the children of Israel ye shall not rule with rigour. - Leviticus 25:47 The stranger who waxes rich by thee is again the Israelite stranger, for the bondservants of the heathen were a possession and did not wax rich. Leviticus 19:35-37 - Just balances, just weights, a just ephah and a just hin. Falsifying the balance is rigging the scale so that one pound weighs out as two and the buyer pays double; our people were doing that wickedness, and the Most High requires honest measure. - Therefore observe all my statutes and all my judgments and do them: the Lord which brought Israel out of the land of Egypt requires it. Leviticus 20: The Judgments Appointed for the Abominations Read the chapter → Leviticus 20 Leviticus 20:1-5 - Whosoever of Israel or of the strangers in the land gave of his seed unto Molech was surely put to death; the people of the land stoned him with stones. This is the child sacrifice shown in Ezekiel 16, slaying the children of the Most High and delivering them to pass through the fire. - If the people of the land hid their eyes from the man and killed him not, the Most High set His face against that man and against his family. When you see wickedness you must utter it and expose it; a witness that holds his peace bears iniquity. - Sin brings judgment on a whole house. Achan coveted the goodly Babylonish garment, the silver, and the wedge of gold, and he and his sons and his daughters and all that he had were stoned and burned in the valley of Achor. What you do is not just about you; your sin can bring judgment on your family. Precepts: - Ezekiel 16:20-21 Thou hast slain my children to cause them to pass through the fire; that is giving seed unto Molech. - Leviticus 5:1 If a soul hear swearing and is a witness and do not utter it, he shall bear his iniquity; wickedness seen must be exposed. - Joshua 7:20-25 Achan's covetousness brought stoning and fire on him and his whole house; one man's sin judged his family. Leviticus 20:6-9 - The soul that turns after such as have familiar spirits and after wizards, to go a whoring after them, is cut off from among his people. - Sanctify yourselves and be ye holy; keep the statutes of the Most High, for He is the Lord which sanctifieth you. - Every one that curseth his father or his mother shall surely be put to death; his blood shall be upon him. Disrespecting your mother and your father carried the death penalty. Leviticus 20:10 - The man that committeth adultery with another man's wife, the adulterer and the adulteress, shall surely be put to death. This world openly defends adultery and men even boast of committing it with another man's wife; the scriptures call for death upon both. Leviticus 20:11-16 - The man that lies with his father's wife, and the man that lies with his daughter in law, shall surely be put to death; they have wrought confusion. - If a man lie with mankind as he lieth with a woman, both have committed an abomination and shall surely be put to death; abomination means hateful and disgusting unto the Most High. - The man that takes a wife and her mother is burnt with fire, both he and they, that there be no wickedness among you. - The man or woman that lies with a beast is put to death, and the beast is slain also. All of these judgments fall under the laws of adultery, the sub-statutes of that commandment. Leviticus 20:17-21 - The man that takes his sister and sees her nakedness, it is a wicked thing; they are cut off in the sight of their people, and he bears his iniquity. - The man that lies with a woman having her sickness, her menstrual cycle, has discovered her fountain, and both are cut off from among their people; this goes with the laws of Leviticus 15. - The nakedness of the mother's sister and the father's sister is near kin; they bear their iniquity. He that lies with his uncle's wife or takes his brother's wife, they shall die childless. Precepts: - Leviticus 15:19 The law of the woman put apart in her issue; chapter 20 judges what chapter 15 defines. Leviticus 20:22-24 - Keep all my statutes and all my judgments, that the land whither I bring you spew you not out. Walk not in the manners of the nation cast out before you, for they committed all these things and therefore the Most High abhorred them. - I am the Lord your God, which have separated you from other people. The Most High separated Israel from the other people, so Israel is to walk differently; these laws are the separation. Leviticus 20:25-26 - Put difference between clean beasts and unclean, and between unclean fowls and clean; this goes back to Leviticus 11, the dietary laws. No shrimp, crab, lobster, pork, catfish, and the like; everything is not clean, whatever the church teaches. - If you eat whatever you please, you are not separating yourself from the other nations. Ye shall be holy unto me, for I the Lord am holy, and have severed you from other people, that ye should be mine. Leviticus 20:27 - A man or woman that hath a familiar spirit, or that is a wizard, was surely put to death by stoning. The tarot card readings, the fortune telling, and the horoscopes of today are that same dealing with familiar spirits; do not touch any of it. Leviticus 21: The Holiness of the Priests, the Sons of Aaron Read the chapter → Leviticus 21 Leviticus 21:1-4 - The priests, the sons of Aaron, were not to be defiled for the dead among their people, except for near kin: mother, father, son, daughter, brother, and a virgin sister that had no husband. - The priests had to remain clean to administer the priesthood, for anyone unclean that approached the sanctuary was put to death; a chief man among his people was not to profane himself. Leviticus 21:5-6 - The priests were not to make baldness upon their head, nor shave off the corner of their beard, nor make any cuttings in their flesh; they were to be holy unto their God, for they offer the offerings of the Lord made by fire. - Christians will read verse 1 and say this chapter speaks only to the priests, so shaving the head and beard has nothing to do with them. But go back to chapter 19: the Lord spake there to all the children of Israel and said the exact same thing, round not the corners of your head, neither mar the corners of thy beard. The law given to the priests here was already the law of the whole nation; do not isolate the priests to escape the commandment. Precepts: - Leviticus 19:1-2 The words of chapter 19 went to all the congregation of the children of Israel, not to the priests only. - Leviticus 19:27 Round not the corners of your head, neither mar the corners of thy beard; the same law binds every man of Israel. Leviticus 21:7-9 - The priests could not take a wife that was a whore, or profane, or put away from her husband; they were held to an even higher standard, for the priest is holy unto his God. - The daughter of any priest that profaned herself by playing the whore profaned her father and was burnt with fire. Under the law it was straight death, and we are all guilty of these things; this is why Christ had to come. Thank the Most High for the blood of Christ, that we can repent, correct ourselves, and keep moving, for a just man falleth and riseth up again. Precepts: - Proverbs 24:16 A just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again; under Christ there is room to repent and stand back up. Leviticus 21:10-12 - The high priest, upon whose head the anointing oil was poured, was not to uncover his head nor rend his clothes, nor go in to any dead body, nor go out of the sanctuary; the crown of the anointing oil of his God was upon him. Under the old covenant his head was covered with the mitre. - When Christ died the veil of the temple was rent and the priesthood was changed; the high priest now is Christ, for it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda. The sons of Levi no longer carry that office; Judah carries this work to the kingdom. Precepts: - Matthew 27:51 The veil of the temple was rent in twain when Christ died. - Hebrews 7:12-14 The priesthood being changed, there is a change also of the law; it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda. Leviticus 21:13-15 - The high priest took a wife in her virginity: not a widow, nor a divorced woman, nor profane, nor an harlot, but a virgin of his own people, that he profane not his seed among his people. Leviticus 21:16-24 - A blemish is a disability or birth defect: blind, lame in his walk, a flat nose, any thing superfluous, brokenfooted, brokenhanded, crookbackt, a dwarf, a blemish in the eye, scurvy, scabbed, or stones broken. No man of the seed of Aaron with a blemish could come nigh to offer the offerings of the Lord made by fire. - Yet the blemished priest still ate the bread of his God, both of the most holy and of the holy; he was provided for, only he went not in unto the vail nor came nigh unto the altar, that the sanctuaries be not profaned. - Moses told it unto Aaron, and to his sons, and unto all the children of Israel. --- Topics: Clean and Unclean Meats · Idolatry · Sacrifice and Atonement · The Covenant · The Feasts of the Most High · The Priesthood · The Sabbath ← Leviticus 14-15 · Leviticus Study · Leviticus 22-25 →

title: Leviticus 2: The Meat Offering of Fine Flour
text: ← Leviticus 1 · Leviticus Study · Leviticus 6-9 → Leviticus 2: The Meat Offering of Fine Flour Read the chapter → Leviticus 2 Introduction This reading covers Leviticus 2 through 5: the meat offering of fine flour, the peace offering without blemish, the sin offering for sins of ignorance, and the trespass offering. Blessed is he that readeth, and they that hear the words of this prophecy (Revelation 1:3); leadership was in the spirit to allow the reading of four chapters a day, recording it and touching on everything to break down the word. Leviticus goes into the Levitical laws: the laws of sacrifice, the moral laws, the civil laws, the ceremonial laws. Meditate on the milk, the first five books. The pastors of the world tell our people not to read the Old Testament, that it is done away with, but there is a lot of symbolic prophecy in these first five books that must be known in order to understand the New Testament and to understand Christ. Leviticus 2:1-3 - The meat offering is of fine flour, with oil poured upon it and frankincense put thereon; the priest burns his handful of it as a memorial upon the altar, an offering made by fire of a sweet savour unto the Lord, and the remnant belongs to Aaron and his sons. - Five primary offerings run through these chapters. The burnt offering, usually a male burnt at the altar, with the skin for the priests, was glorified by the Most High. The meal offering, the one read here, was made of fine flour with oil and frankincense; no leaven and no honey were permitted, it had to be seasoned with salt, and it was baked in an oven, a pan, or a frying pan. - The peace offering could be either male or female: the blood, the fat, and the kidneys were the Lord's, and the breast and the right shoulder were for the priest. The sin offering was blood and fat on the altar, with the bullock burned without the camp, for the judgment of sin. The trespass offering was for atonement and forgiveness, the blood and fat of a ram on the altar, with the principal restored and the fifth part added. There are also wave offerings and heave offerings, but these five are the primary offerings. Leviticus 2:4-7 - Leviticus 2:7 always goes viral on social media, as if the meat offering baken in the frying pan relates to fried chicken. That is not what it is talking about; be mindful of learning from posts instead of from the scriptures. - The chapter itself defines the meat: go back and read verse 1, and the offering is of fine flour, not of fried chicken. When you have questions, go back to the beginning verses of the chapter, and you get the true understanding. - Meat in the scriptures is not always talking about animals. Every tree yielding seed was given for meat; the inside of a fruit is called the meat of that fruit, the meat of an orange, an apple, a pear, a watermelon. Precepts: - Genesis 1:29 Every herb bearing seed and every tree yielding seed, to you it shall be for meat; meat does not have to be an animal. Leviticus 2:8-10 - The meat offering is presented unto the priest, who brings it unto the altar and burns the memorial of it, an offering made by fire of a sweet savour unto the Lord. - The Lord delighted in the offerings, the same way you walk inside a house and smell that good cooking; so it was when the Levites offered up the sacrifices for the people and for themselves. - That which is left of the meat offering is Aaron's and his sons', a thing most holy of the offerings of the Lord made by fire. Leviticus 2:11 - No meat offering brought unto the Lord shall be made with leaven, and no honey in any offering made by fire. This is where the Passover and Christ come in: it was all a shadow of things to come, just as all leaven is put out when the Passover comes around. The leaven is read about more in chapter 3. Leviticus 2:12 - The oblation of the firstfruits is offered unto the Lord but not burnt on the altar for a sweet savour. Firstfruits is another holy day, with the Pentecost; all of it was symbolic. - Cain and Abel show both kinds of offering. Cain was a tiller of the ground, part of the agriculture, and brought of the fruit of the ground, the firstfruits; Abel brought of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof. The Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering, but unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect. - Sacrifices are symbolic of your works. The Most High knows how much you can do for this truth, whether you are being slack, slothful, and cheap, or going above and beyond; Abel went above and beyond, and Cain was mediocre. Our sacrifices today are keeping the commandments, the work we put in, the alms we give, and the time we sacrifice. Precepts: - Genesis 4:1-5 Cain brought of the fruit of the ground and Abel of the firstlings of his flock; the Lord had respect unto Abel's offering and not to Cain's. - Ecclesiasticus 35:1 Keeping the law brings offerings enough; the work you put in is your offering, and the Lord extends the more mercy. Leviticus 2:13 - Every oblation of the meat offering had to be seasoned with salt, the salt of the covenant of thy God; with all thine offerings thou shalt offer salt. It is physical too: you offer something up, you whip something up, you better season that thing. - Israel has a covenant of salt with the Lord. When Abijah king of Judah stood on the mount to defuse the war between the northern kingdom and the southern kingdom, around the 900s BC, he told Jeroboam: ought ye not to know that the Lord God of Israel gave the kingdom over Israel to David for ever, even to him and to his sons by a covenant of salt? The northern kingdom far exceeded the southern in numbers, but the numbers did not matter. - Salt is a preservative; it keeps a thing fresh. The covenant of salt goes into the brotherhood: we are supposed to preserve our relationships, keep our alliance fresh, and grow together. Everything given to the Levites for sacrifice carried that symbolism. Precepts: - 2 Chronicles 13:1-5 Abijah told Jeroboam that the Lord gave the kingdom to David and his sons by a covenant of salt; the salt is the preserving of the bond. - Zechariah 12:7 The Lord shall save the tents of Judah first; that word is in effect, and the lesson of the war between the kingdoms is to stand down when it comes to Judah. Leviticus 2:14-16 - The meat offering of the firstfruits is green ears of corn dried by the fire, corn beaten out of full ears, with oil put upon it and frankincense thereon; the priest burns the memorial of it, an offering made by fire unto the Lord. Leviticus 3: The Peace Offering Without Blemish Read the chapter → Leviticus 3 Leviticus 3:1 - The peace offering of the herd, whether male or female, must be offered without blemish before the Lord: no bruise, no cut, no stain, nothing superfluous like an extra member. Whatever the sacrifice is for the Lord, it has to be the best of the best, a flawless sacrifice. - The Passover lamb shows how that was carried out. The lamb was without blemish, a male of the first year, taken out from the sheep and kept from the goats, because if it got in a fight it would take a blemish, a bruise, a cut. It was kept up to the fourteenth day, isolated and given nothing but water, so that it purified itself; and it was eaten roast with fire, not raw and not sodden with water, with the purtenance thereof, for after those days there was nothing left within it. Precepts: - Exodus 12:3-9 Your lamb shall be without blemish; it was taken out from the sheep, kept from the goats to the fourteenth day, and roasted with fire, not raw nor sodden. - The lamb that had no blemish was symbolic of Christ. A little leaven leaveneth the whole lump: a little sin in the spirit will get worse, so the old leaven is purged out, and that is the true resemblance of the Passover, purging out sin not one day a year but constantly, in prayer and fasting; for even Christ our Passover, our lamb without blemish, is sacrificed for us. - Christ gave himself for the church, that he might present it to himself a glorious church, not having spot or wrinkle, holy and without blemish, sanctified and cleansed with the washing of water by the word. - Christ did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth: without blemish physically was symbolic of no sin. He was the one and only flawless sacrifice. He also suffered wrongfully, and that is thankworthy with God; when you follow his steps and suffer wrongfully without adding a blot to your honor, that is acceptable with God. - John bore the record: behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world. That goes back to presenting a glorious church; the only way to be without blemish is through faith in Christ. - That is why the Levitical laws of sacrifice are no longer performed: the law had a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image; those sacrifices offered year by year could never make the comers thereunto perfect, for it is not possible that the blood of bulls and of goats should take away sins. We needed Christ, the ultimate sacrifice. Read verse 1 again with that understanding: the offerings went up without blemish because they were symbolic of Christ's coming. Precepts: - 1 Corinthians 5:6-7 A little leaven leaveneth the whole lump; purge out the old leaven, for even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us. - Ephesians 5:25-27 Christ gave himself for the church, to present it a glorious church, holy and without blemish, as the Levitical sacrifices figured. - 1 Peter 2:21-22 Christ suffered for us, who did no sin; no blemish means no sin, the one flawless sacrifice. - 1 Peter 2:19-20 Enduring grief, suffering wrongfully, is thankworthy; that is what Christ went through for us, and the pattern for us when we suffer for well doing. - John 1:29 Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world; Christ was that lamb. - Hebrews 10:1-4 The law had a shadow of good things to come; the blood of bulls and goats could never take away sins, so Christ had to be the ultimate sacrifice. Leviticus 3:2-16 - The peace offering could be of the herd or of the flock, a lamb or a goat, male or female without blemish, unlike the burnt offering of chapter 1, which was a male. The offerer laid his hand upon the head of his offering and killed it at the door of the tabernacle, and Aaron's sons sprinkled the blood upon the altar round about. - The blood, the fat that covers the inwards, the two kidneys with the fat upon them by the flanks, and the caul above the liver were the Lord's, burned upon the altar, the food of the offering made by fire for a sweet savour; the breast and the right shoulder were for the priest. All the fat is the Lord's. Leviticus 3:17 - It shall be a perpetual statute that ye eat neither fat nor blood. This is a controversial scripture: brothers and sisters ask whether we are cut off for eating fat. Having that question is a good thing; it means you are reading to understand, not reading just to say you read four chapters. - Leviticus 7 answers it in context: whosoever eateth the fat of the beast of which men offer an offering made by fire unto the Lord shall be cut off. This is the law of sacrifice, which we are no longer under; Christ is the end of the law for righteousness. The sacrifices stopped after 70 AD at the fall of Jerusalem, when there was no longer a temple. And there is no way to take off all the fat of the meat you eat; we are not koshering our meat. Precepts: - Leviticus 7:22-25 The fat forbidden is the fat of the beast of which men offer an offering made by fire; it belongs to the laws of sacrifice. - Romans 10:4 Christ is the end of the law for righteousness; that goes into the sacrificial law. - The blood was also for the altar of the Lord, but there is more to why the Lord had to say it. After Israel came out of Egypt, we had learned heathen practices there, such as drinking blood. The Lord said: after the doings of the land of Egypt, wherein ye dwelt, shall ye not do. Drinking the blood of animals was an Egyptian custom tied to their idols, and the blood-drinking customs of the Hamitic nations continue to this day. - The Lord put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel and sanctified his people with these laws; these laws make us special, going back to Deuteronomy 7 and 6, how he separated us. Do not follow the customs and fashions of the heathen. Precepts: - Leviticus 7:26-27 Ye shall eat no manner of blood; whatsoever soul eateth any manner of blood shall be cut off from his people. - Leviticus 18:1-3 After the doings of the land of Egypt, wherein ye dwelt, shall ye not do; Israel had to be commanded away from what was learned there. - Exodus 11:7 The Lord doth put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel; his laws sanctify his people. - Deuteronomy 7:6 Thou art an holy people chosen to be a special people; the dietary laws are part of that separation. - Israel fell into this sin in Saul's day: the people flew upon the spoil and ate with the blood, and Saul said, ye have transgressed. Eating with the blood is sin; that is why you make sure your food is thoroughly cooked, well done, cut open to the bone so it cooks through. Meat served rare is not running with juice, it is blood. - Serve the Lord and he shall bless thy bread and thy water, and take sickness away from the midst of thee: keep the dietary laws, what to eat and not eat, how to cook it and how to season it, and do not bow down to the gods of the heathen nor do after their works. Precepts: - 1 Samuel 14:33-34 The people sinned against the Lord in eating with the blood; Saul had every man slay his beast on the great stone so they sinned not. - Exodus 23:23-25 Do not do after the works of the heathen; serve the Lord, and he shall bless thy bread and thy water and take sickness away from the midst of thee. Leviticus 4: The Sin Offering for Sins of Ignorance Read the chapter → Leviticus 4 Leviticus 4:1-3 - The sin offering is for a soul that sins through ignorance against any of the commandments. You sin through ignorance when you get complacent: it was a double Sabbath and you forgot, and you bought or sold something you were not supposed to; an honest mistake. Even then it was not a verbal sorry; you literally brought an offering for your mistake. - The offering was your collateral in those times. There were no dollar bills; being rich meant land, cattle, flocks, and agriculture, what the scriptures call milk and honey, as with Job, who was rich in land and livestock. Your sins cost you out of that substance. - Even the priest that is anointed committed sin, according to the sin of the people, and had to bring a young bullock without blemish unto the Lord for a sin offering. The priests went always into the first tabernacle accomplishing the service of God, but the high priest went alone once every year into the second, not without blood, which he offered for himself and for the errors of the people. - The people got redundant with it: every priest stood daily offering oftentimes the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins. They kept sinning and kept bringing sacrifices instead of repenting, thinking it was okay to sin as long as the offerings kept coming. It is the same spirit today, wicked all weekend and a hundred dollars in the plate on Sunday; the Most High does not want your money, he wants you to repent. Only you can put away your sins, when you repent and stop sinning. - But this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God. Christ took away the first covenant to establish the second, and we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all. Men had been sacrificing since the days of Adam; when Christ came, one sacrifice ended it, because that lamb had no blemish. The law of sacrifice was always temporary, a shadow of good things to come, and the good thing that came was Christ. Precepts: - Hebrews 9:6-7 Into the second went the high priest alone once every year, not without blood, which he offered for himself and for the errors of the people; even the priests sinned. - Hebrews 10:7-12 Sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not; he taketh away the first covenant to establish the second, and this man offered one sacrifice for sins for ever and sat down. Leviticus 4:4-12 - The ritual of the priest's sin offering: the bullock killed before the Lord, the anointed priest dipping his finger and sprinkling the blood seven times before the vail of the sanctuary, blood put upon the horns of the altar of sweet incense, the rest poured at the bottom of the altar of the burnt offering, all the fat burned upon the altar, and the whole bullock carried forth without the camp unto a clean place where the ashes are poured out, and burned on wood with fire. Leviticus 4:13-21 - If the whole congregation sin through ignorance and the thing be hid from the eyes of the assembly, pay attention to the key word: they have done somewhat against the commandments. It says somewhat because the Lord knows your heart, and the heart is deceitful and wicked above all things; you say you sinned through ignorance, and the Lord knows whether that is so. - When the sin is known, the congregation offers a young bullock; the elders lay their hands upon its head before the Lord, the blood is sprinkled seven times before the vail and put on the horns of the altar, all the fat is burned, and the bullock is burned without the camp as the first: and the priest shall make an atonement for them, and it shall be forgiven them. Leviticus 4:22-26 - When a ruler hath sinned, there it is again: done somewhat through ignorance. Some of it is not ignorance; some of it is complacency, a lack of faith, a mind not in the spirit. His offering was a kid of the goats, a male without blemish, and the priest made atonement, which goes into reconciliation with the Lord and forgiveness of sins. - Saying we knew it not does not stand before the Most High. Doth not he that pondereth the heart consider it, and he that keepeth thy soul, doth not he know it? A lot of people say they never heard this truth when they heard it and did not want to apply it. The Most High knows the things that come into your mind, every one of them; he created us and knows us better than we know ourselves, and he knows whether you sinned through ignorance or willfully. Precepts: - Proverbs 24:12 If thou sayest, behold, we knew it not, doth not he that pondereth the heart consider it? The excuse of ignorance does not stand before him. - Ezekiel 11:5 I know the things that come into your mind, every one of them; the Lord knows the spirit behind the sin. - Numbers 15 lays the two ways side by side. If ought be committed by ignorance, the congregation and the soul that sinned bring their offerings, and it shall be forgiven them, one law both for him that is born among the children of Israel and for the stranger. But the soul that doeth ought presumptuously reproacheth the Lord, and that soul shall be cut off from among his people; he hath despised the word of the Lord, and his iniquity shall be upon him. - Presumptuously means impulsive and willful: no boundaries, doing things without seeking counsel, led by your own mind, your own opinion, your own emotions instead of leaning on the leadership the Most High set in place. Peter marks that spirit: they walk after the flesh in the lust of uncleanness, despise government, presumptuous are they, selfwilled, not afraid to speak evil of dignities. Despising government, gossiping and murmuring against leadership, and refusing to gather with the body is that same dangerous spirit; the Lord said gather yourselves together, O nation not desired, and he works through spiritual men as he did through Moses and Aaron. Precepts: - Numbers 15:22-29 Sin committed by ignorance was atoned and forgiven, one law for him that is born among Israel and for the stranger that sojourneth among them. - Numbers 15:30-31 The soul that doeth ought presumptuously reproacheth the Lord and shall be cut off; he hath despised the word of the Lord. - 2 Peter 2:10 They that walk after the flesh despise government; presumptuous are they, selfwilled, not afraid to speak evil of dignities. - The man found gathering sticks upon the Sabbath day shows the presumptuous side, immediately after that law was spoken. They did not kill him right away; they put him in ward, because it was not declared what should be done to him, and Moses got direction from the Lord. And the Lord said, the man shall be surely put to death, and all the congregation stoned him without the camp. - That is the judgment on the willful: if we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins. That man knew the law; it was not ignorance, it was blatant. The Lord knoweth all the works of men, their imaginations, their thoughts, and their hearts; he knoweth your inventions and what ye think in your heart, even them that sin and would hide their sin. Sin willfully and your grace period is up. Precepts: - Numbers 15:32-36 The man gathering sticks on the Sabbath was kept in ward until the mind of the Lord was declared, and the Lord said he shall surely be put to death. - Hebrews 10:26 If we sin wilfully after receiving the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins. - 2 Esdras 16:54-55 The Lord that made heaven and earth by the word knoweth all the works of men and their hearts. - 2 Esdras 16:63 He knoweth your inventions, even them that sin and would hide their sin; nothing willful is hid from him. Leviticus 4:27-35 - If any one of the common people sin through ignorance, his offering was a kid of the goats or a lamb, a female without blemish; he laid his hand upon the head of the sin offering, the blood went on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, the fat was burned for a sweet savour, and the priest made an atonement for him, and it shall be forgiven him. - Even the priests and the rulers had to offer for their own sins. That is the reason the law of sacrifice had to be done away with: the high priest, Christ, came and gave one offering, as Hebrews lays out, and he was done; he did not do it for millenniums, he came one time. Leviticus 5: The Trespass Offering and the Duty of the Witness Read the chapter → Leviticus 5 Leviticus 5:1 - If a soul sin, and hear the voice of swearing, and is a witness, whether he hath seen or known of it, if he do not utter it, then he shall bear his iniquity. Verse 4 defines the voice of swearing: a soul that swears, pronouncing with his lips to do evil or to do good. If you know and say nothing, your brother's blood is required because you did nothing about it. - We are to rebuke one another. Hear no evil, see no evil, speak no evil is a wicked saying; the scriptures say you renounce evil. The watchman does not cover his eyes, because he needs to see, and does not cover his mouth, because he gives the warning; hear the word at my mouth, and give them warning from me. - If you do not apply this verse, you hate your brother in your heart; keeping quiet at his sin, or trimming your ways for him, is hate too. Stand still for the laws of the Most High and do not turn your ways for anybody, even carnal family that puts you out over your beard or your fringes. - There is a way to correct: brethren, if a man be overtaken in a fault, ye which are spiritual, restore such an one in the spirit of meekness. A soft answer turneth away wrath; you do not render evil for evil and blast a brother, you build him up with a humble mind, and that is how souls are won. The man gathering sticks got the reproof that fit that willful case; meekness fits the brother overtaken in a fault. Precepts: - Ezekiel 3:17 I have made thee a watchman unto the house of Israel; hear the word at my mouth, and give them warning from me. - Leviticus 19:17 Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart; not uttering what you witnessed is hating your brother. - Galatians 6:1 If a man be overtaken in a fault, ye which are spiritual restore such an one in the spirit of meekness; that is how you win souls. - The witness law was written when Israel was in its own kingdom and everyone lived by the law; today it is applied among those in the body that understand the law, not to the world outside. The Most High judges them that are without, so the neighbor selling drugs on the corner is not your business; but when you see sin among Israel, do not hide it, bring it out, send it up to the leadership or correct it yourself. The land full of bloody crimes is what came upon Jerusalem when this law was not applied among the people. - A lot of people do not know how to apply this verse; the precept for Leviticus 5:1 is Deuteronomy 17:4. Whether the thing be told thee or thou hast heard of it, thou shalt enquire diligently, and only when it be true and the thing certain does judgment proceed: make sure you are certain of a thing before you bring somebody to judgment. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 17:4 Enquire diligently, and behold, if it be true and the thing certain; the diligent enquiry that governs how the witness law is applied. - 1 Corinthians 5:9-13 What have I to do to judge them also that are without? them that are without God judgeth; the law is applied among the body, not the world. - Proverbs 28:17 A man that doeth violence to the blood of any person shall flee to the pit; let no man stay him; do not hide sin among Israel, bring it out. - Ezekiel 7:21-23 Make a chain, for the land is full of bloody crimes; that is what came upon Jerusalem when this law was not applied among the people. Leviticus 5:2-3 - Touching any unclean thing, the carcase of an unclean beast or the uncleanness of man, leaves a soul unclean and guilty. This goes into eating, not mere contact; the classes have touched on this already, and it stands. - It is the same as telling your son or daughter, get your hand out of the cookie jar: you say do not touch it, not do not eat it, because you know what the intention is. The Lord deals with us the same way; do not be touching that stuff means do not eat it, do not defile yourself. - The touching itself pertained to the sacrifice: Israel was separated from their uncleanness that they die not when they defile the tabernacle, so a man that had touched the unclean thing could not come in to sacrifice. There is no more sacrifice, so the touching-defilement laws do not apply today; a brush of boar bristles is not sin. Precepts: - Leviticus 15:31 Thus shall ye separate the children of Israel from their uncleanness, that they die not, when they defile my tabernacle; the defilement laws guarded the sacrifice. Leviticus 5:4-6 - If a soul swear, pronouncing with his lips to do evil or to do good, and it be hid from him, when he knoweth of it he is guilty. Brothers say, I swear to God; watch your mouth. - When a man is guilty in one of these things, he shall confess that he hath sinned in that thing, and bring his trespass offering, a female from the flock, a lamb or a kid of the goats, and the priest shall make an atonement for him concerning his sin. - A man was held accountable for whatever came out of his mouth; pronouncing with his lips and not performing it was sin. When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it, for better is it that thou shouldest not vow than that thou shouldest vow and not pay; suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin. Christ set the same standard on the mouth: let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay. Precepts: - Ecclesiastes 5:4-6 Better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay; suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin. - Matthew 5:37 Let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil. Leviticus 5:7-13 - The offering scaled to what a man could bring: if he be not able to bring a lamb, two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering; and if he be not able to bring those, the tenth part of an ephah of fine flour, with no oil and no frankincense upon it, for it is a sin offering. - The offerings were the collateral of those times, and families felt the after-effects of always sacrificing: the livestock and the agriculture went for your sins, and the household lacked because of it. - Israel took the nourishment of the Lord for granted, and he grew tired of the empty offerings: put your burnt offerings unto your sacrifices, and eat flesh. He spake not unto our fathers concerning burnt offerings, but this thing commanded he: obey my voice, and I will be your God, and ye shall be my people. He never wanted the sacrifices above obedience; today he does not want an apology or money in the plate, he wants you to obey his voice and repent. Precepts: - Jeremiah 7:21-23 Put your burnt offerings unto your sacrifices; I commanded not burnt offerings, but this thing: obey my voice, and I will be your God. Leviticus 5:14-16 - If a soul commit a trespass and sin through ignorance in the holy things of the Lord, he brings a ram without blemish, with thy estimation by shekels of silver after the shekel of the sanctuary; he makes amends for the harm done in the holy thing and adds the fifth part thereto for the priest, and it shall be forgiven him. - The scripture that pops up again is the same one: if thou sayest, behold, we knew it not, doth not he that pondereth the heart consider it? Worldly family and coworkers that are not keeping the laws talk the same way, not understanding they condemn themselves because they are not repenting; that card cannot be pulled on the Messiah. Precepts: - Proverbs 24:12 Doth not he that pondereth the heart consider it? He that keepeth thy soul knoweth whether the ignorance is real. Leviticus 5:17-19 - If a soul sin against any of the commandments, though he wist it not, yet is he guilty, and shall bear his iniquity. Though he is ignorant of it, the iniquity is still there; saying I did not know does not remove sin, and everyone still appears before the judgment seat of Christ when it is all said and done. The priest made an atonement concerning his ignorance wherein he erred and wist it not, for he hath certainly trespassed against the Lord. - The remedy is to know the law: let thy mind be upon the ordinances of the Lord, and meditate continually in his commandments. The ordinances are found in the first five books; as these four chapters a day are conducted, meditate and study them continually. - As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby. The milk is the dos and the don'ts.
