Many want to run to Revelation and the parables, but the solutions for what is wrong in your spirit, for lust, covetousness, hatred, malice, and envy, sit in the ordinances and the commandments; look up the scriptures on patience, temperance, and how to treat your family correctly. - Stay humble with it: Lord, my heart is not haughty, nor mine eyes lofty; neither do I exercise myself in great matters, or in things too high for me; David behaved and quieted himself as a child that is weaned of his mother. Except ye be converted and become as little children, ye shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven; so behave yourselves humbly, and the Most High will establish thine heart and increase thy wisdom. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 6:37 Meditate continually in his commandments, and he shall establish thine heart and give thee wisdom. - 1 Peter 2:2 As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby; the milk is the first five books. - Psalms 131:1-2 My heart is not haughty; I have behaved and quieted myself as a child that is weaned of his mother. - Matthew 18:1-3 Except ye be converted and become as little children, ye shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven. --- Topics: Clean and Unclean Meats · Sacrifice and Atonement · The Covenant · The Feasts of the Most High · The Priesthood · The Sabbath ← Leviticus 1 · Leviticus Study · Leviticus 6-9 →

title: Leviticus 22: The Holy Things and Offerings Without Blemish
text: ← Leviticus 18-21 · Leviticus Study · Leviticus 26-27 → Leviticus 22: The Holy Things and Offerings Without Blemish Read the chapter → Leviticus 22 Introduction This reading covers Leviticus 22 through 25: the holy things of the priests and the law of offerings without blemish, the feasts of the Lord, the pure oil and the shewbread and the judgment of the blasphemer, and the sabbath of the land with the year of jubile. All four chapters were read, with precepts brought in along the way and questions answered after the reading. Leviticus 22:1-3 - The Levitical priesthood was established in Aaron and his sons. Certain things were consecrated that could not be touched by the rest of Israel, and a priest with his uncleanness upon him could not go unto the holy things, lest that soul be cut off from the presence of the Most High. - Aaron was consecrated and anointed to minister in the priest's office, and his sons were clothed and anointed as their father, an everlasting priesthood throughout their generations. Precepts: - Exodus 40:13-15 Aaron and his sons were anointed and sanctified to minister in the priest's office, an everlasting priesthood throughout their generations. Leviticus 22:4-9 - A man of the seed of Aaron that was a leper, had a running issue, or touched any unclean thing could not eat of the holy things until he was clean: he washed his flesh with water, and when the sun was down he was clean and could afterward eat. - That which dieth of itself, or is torn with beasts, he shall not eat to defile himself therewith. That same law elsewhere says to give such a thing unto the stranger or sell it to an alien, for thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God: these laws were given to Israel alone, and the other nations may eat those things because they are not the holy people. There is no equality in that. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 14:21 The thing that dieth of itself may be given to the stranger or sold to an alien, for thou art an holy people; the law marks the difference between Israel and the nations. Leviticus 22:10-16 - No stranger may eat of the holy thing, neither a sojourner of the priest nor an hired servant. But the soul the priest buys with his money, and he that is born in his house, they eat of his meat, because they are joined to the priest's household. - The priest's daughter married unto a stranger may not eat of the offering of the holy things; but if she is a widow or divorced and has no child, and is returned unto her father's house as in her youth, she eats of her father's meat, because she returns to her father's covering. - A woman was commonly under her father's covering until she came under a husband's. The independent woman was not birthed from the Bible; she was birthed from Babylon. - He that eats of the holy thing unwittingly adds the fifth part unto it and gives it to the priest with the holy thing; the priests must not suffer the children of Israel to bear the iniquity of trespass when they eat their holy things. Leviticus 22:17-25 - Whatever offering is brought for a vow or a freewill offering must be a male without blemish, of the beeves, of the sheep, or of the goats. Beeves goes to the ox and that family, the oxen and bulls. - Blind, broken, maimed, or having a wen, or scurvy, or scabbed, shall not be offered unto the Lord. Scurvy is just having scratches; these offerings could have no scratches and no bruises, nothing bruised or crushed or broken or cut. - Neither from a stranger's hand shall ye offer the bread of your God of any of these, because their corruption is in them and blemishes be in them; they shall not be accepted for you. Leviticus 22:26-30 - When a bullock or a sheep or a goat is brought forth, it shall be seven days under the dam. The dam is that animal's mother; the young must stay under its mother seven days, and from the eighth day it is accepted for an offering. - Whether it be cow or ewe, ye shall not kill it and her young both in one day. And the sacrifice of thanksgiving is eaten the same day; none of it is left until the morrow. Leviticus 22:31-33 - Therefore shall ye keep my commandments and do them: neither shall ye profane my holy name, but I will be hallowed among the children of Israel. - I am the Lord which brought you out of the land of Egypt, to be your God. The Most High brought Israel out of the land of Egypt to be their God; that is the foundation the commandments stand on. Leviticus 23: The Feasts of the Lord Read the chapter → Leviticus 23 Leviticus 23:1-3 - These are the feasts of the Lord, holy convocations which He Himself proclaimed. The Most High gave us holy days; a holiday not listed in this Bible and not ordained of the Most High has nothing holy about it. By the knowledge of the Lord the days were distinguished: some He made high days, as the Passover, Tabernacles, the new moon, and the Sabbath, and the days He did not name are ordinary days. - Six days shall work be done, but the seventh day is the sabbath of rest, an holy convocation. No matter where your dwelling is, Israel, North America, London, or Australia, the Sabbath is still the Sabbath: Friday sundown to Saturday sundown in whatever time zone you are in. - Keeping the Sabbath holy is more than no working. Ye shall kindle no fire throughout your habitations upon the sabbath day, so there is no cooking on the Sabbath; and if the people of the land bring ware or victuals on the sabbath day to sell, we would not buy it of them, so there is no buying and no selling. - It is a holy convocation, which means a gathering. Keeping the Sabbath sitting at home with your gerbil or your hamster is not keeping the Sabbath; you have to come out of your comfort zone and congregate. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 33:7-9 One day excels another by the knowledge of the Lord: some days He made high days and hallowed them, and some He made ordinary. - Exodus 35:1-3 On the holy sabbath day whosoever doeth work shall be put to death, and ye shall kindle no fire throughout your habitations; no cooking on the Sabbath. - Nehemiah 10:31 If the people of the land bring ware or victuals on the sabbath day to sell, we would not buy it of them; no buying and no selling on the Sabbath. Leviticus 23:4-8 - In the fourteenth day of the first month at even is the Lord's passover. The fourteenth day at even means the fifteenth day, so the verse about the fifteenth day is saying the same thing: the first day of the Passover is also the first day of the feast of unleavened bread. - On the first day and on the seventh day is an holy convocation: no buying, no selling, no servile work. But you can cook on the Passover, because there is no Passover without the Passover meal, the lamb, unleavened bread, and bitter herbs. - On the last day of unleavened bread you may also cook, unless it falls on the seventh day Sabbath. The only time you can cook on the seventh day Sabbath is when the Passover falls on that day, because you cannot have the Passover without the lamb roast with fire; no other high holy day gives you a set meal, and no other feast overrides the Sabbath cooking prohibition. Precepts: - Luke 22:1 The feast of unleavened bread is called the Passover; the two feasts run together as one. - 1 Esdras 1:17-19 In the days of Josias the feast of unleavened bread is called the feast of sweet bread, kept seven days with the passover. Leviticus 23:9-14 - When ye be come into the land, ye shall bring a sheaf of the firstfruits of your harvest unto the priest, and he shall wave the sheaf before the Lord on the morrow after the sabbath, with an he lamb without blemish for a burnt offering. - This wave sheaf day is what the New Testament calls the preparation: after the Passover was kept, the day following was the preparation, which prepared for this feast of the waving of the sheaf. - Ye shall eat neither bread nor parched corn nor green ears until the selfsame day that ye have brought an offering unto your God; it is a statute for ever throughout your generations. Leviticus 23:15-21 - From the morrow after the sabbath, from the day the sheaf of the wave offering was brought, count seven sabbaths complete, seven times seven which is forty and nine, and the morrow after the seventh sabbath is the fiftieth day. That is why the feast is called Pentecost, from fifty, as a pentagon has five sides; it is also called the feast of weeks, because of the seven weeks that are counted. - With the two wave loaves came burnt offerings, a sin offering, and peace offerings, meat offerings and drink offerings. That is what Colossians is talking about when it says let no man judge you in meat or in drink or in respect of an holyday: those who did not believe in Christ condemned the followers of Christ as wicked for not sacrificing on the holy days. We still keep the holy days, but we do not offer the offerings, because the body of Christ has been given. - The meat offerings and drink offerings and carnal ordinances were a figure for the time then present, imposed until the time of reformation; they could not make him that did the service perfect as pertaining to the conscience. But Christ being come, an high priest of good things to come, Christ is now in place of all those oblations and sacrifices. Precepts: - Tobit 2:1 Pentecost is the holy feast of the seven weeks, the seven sabbaths counted after the wave sheaf. - Colossians 2:16 Let no man judge you in meat or in drink or in respect of an holyday; no man may condemn you for keeping the holy days without the sacrifices, now that Christ is come. - Hebrews 9:9-11 The gifts and sacrifices were a figure for the time then present, carnal ordinances imposed until the time of reformation; Christ being come stands in place of them. Leviticus 23:22 - When ye reap the harvest of your land, thou shalt not make clean riddance of the corners of thy field, neither gather the gleaning of thy harvest: thou shalt leave them unto the poor and to the stranger. Leviticus 23:23-25 - In the seventh month, in the first day of the month, is a sabbath, a memorial of blowing of trumpets. The new moon starts the new month, so the memorial of blowing of trumpets is a new moon; the seventh new moon is the special one, and that one is called the memorial of blowing of trumpets. - The Most High made the moon to serve in her season for a declaration of times: from the moon is the sign of feasts, a light that decreaseth in her perfection. The moon is needed to calculate the feasts; the month is called after her name, because the new moon starts the new month, increasing wonderfully in her changing through the phases. - But the moon has nothing to do with the seventh day Sabbath. The day starts at evening, for the evening and the morning were the first day; darkness was here first and has seniority. The moon was not even created on the first day of the week but on the fourth day, and the heavens and the earth were finished and the Most High still rested on the seventh day. The seven day rotation has run since the first day and nothing changes it; the Sabbath will always be Friday sundown to Saturday sundown. - If the new moon falls on a seventh day Sabbath there is absolutely no cooking; the only day that permits cooking on the Sabbath is the Passover. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 43:6-8 The moon serves for a declaration of times, and from the moon is the sign of feasts; the month is called after her name. - Genesis 1:14-19 The lights in the firmament were made for signs and for seasons, the lesser light to rule the night, on the fourth day; the moon came after the week was already counting. - Genesis 2:1-3 The heavens and the earth were finished, and on the seventh day God ended his work and rested; the moon made on the fourth day did not dictate the seventh day Sabbath. Leviticus 23:26-32 - On the tenth day of this seventh month, the same month as the blowing of trumpets, is the day of atonement, an holy convocation; ye shall afflict your souls, and do no manner of work in that same day, for whatsoever soul does any work that same day, that soul will the Most High destroy from among his people. - To afflict your soul is to neither feed nor drink water nor taste anything, as Nineveh was commanded: no eating, no drinking, no tasting anything at all. That goes for gum, because you can taste gum, and even toothpaste; the last thing you do before the fast begins is brush your teeth before the sun goes down, and the first thing after it ends is brush them after the sun goes down. If you can taste it, keep it out of your mouth. - From even unto even shall ye celebrate your sabbath, the ninth day of the month at even. Even unto even is how days are numbered, one complete day of twenty-four hours, not sunrise to sunrise, for the evening and the morning were the first day. Precepts: - Jonah 3:7 Let neither man nor beast taste any thing, nor feed, nor drink water; that is the affliction of the soul, tasting nothing at all. - Genesis 1:5 The evening and the morning were the first day; the day starts at evening, so the sabbath runs from even unto even. Leviticus 23:33-44 - The fifteenth day of the seventh month is the feast of tabernacles for seven days unto the Lord. The first day is an holy convocation with no servile work, and on the eighth day is an holy convocation, a solemn assembly. - Ye shall take you on the first day the boughs of goodly trees, branches of palm trees, and the boughs of thick trees, and willows of the brook, and rejoice before the Lord your God seven days. Those branches may be collected and put together in a vase in the home for the feast. - Ye shall dwell in booths seven days, that your generations may know that the Most High made the children of Israel to dwell in booths when He brought them out of the land of Egypt, as when Israel was in the wilderness dwelling in tents. - These laws are our culture, our history, and our heritage. The Passover is kept because the Most High delivered Israel out of the land of Egypt, not just some date we do for the kids; we do what this Bible says because the Most High commanded it, and all of His laws reflect our history. Leviticus 24: The Pure Oil, the Shewbread, and the Blasphemer Read the chapter → Leviticus 24 Leviticus 24:1-4 - The children of Israel were commanded to bring pure oil olive beaten for the light, to cause the lamps to burn continually. Aaron ordered it from the evening unto the morning before the Lord continually, upon the pure candlestick, a statute for ever in your generations. Precepts: - Exodus 31:8 The pure candlestick with all his furniture was part of the tabernacle work; the lamps ordered on it burned before the Lord continually. Leviticus 24:5-9 - Twelve cakes of fine flour were set in two rows, six on a row, upon the pure table before the Lord, with pure frankincense upon each row, every sabbath, taken from the children of Israel by an everlasting covenant. - It shall be Aaron's and his sons', and they shall eat it in the holy place, for it is most holy unto him of the offerings of the Lord made by fire. Leviticus 24:10-16 - The son of an Israelitish woman, whose father was an Egyptian, went out among the children of Israel, and strove in the camp with a man of Israel, and blasphemed the name of the Lord, and cursed. His mother was Shelomith, the daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan. - They put him in ward, that the mind of the Lord might be shewed them; and the Lord commanded that he that had cursed be brought forth without the camp, that all that heard him lay their hands upon his head, and that all the congregation stone him. The strife in the camp likely arose from a man of Israel correcting him concerning the law. - His father being an Egyptian shows he was conceived while Israel was in captivity in the land of Egypt, dwelling among the Egyptians; in the same way Moses, outside of Egypt with Jethro the priest of Midian, took a wife there. And there is no such thing as being half Israelite or a fourth Israelite: if your parent is Israel, you are Israel. - Whosoever curseth his God shall bear his sin, and he that blasphemeth the name of the Lord, he shall surely be put to death, as well the stranger as he that is born in the land. Leviticus 24:17-23 - He that killeth any man shall surely be put to death, and he that killeth a beast shall make it good, beast for beast. If a man cause a blemish in his neighbour, as he hath done, so shall it be done to him: breach for breach, eye for eye, tooth for tooth. One manner of law stood for the stranger as for one of your own country. - When Christ came he taught the proper understanding of eye for eye for dealing inside the nation: ye have heard that it hath been said, an eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth, but I say unto you that ye resist not evil. As the Son of God he had authority to magnify the law: whosoever smites thee on thy right cheek, turn to him the other also; if any man sue thee and take away thy coat, let him have thy cloak also; whosoever compels thee to go a mile, go with him twain. - Inside our nation we must practice forgiveness, patience, and long-suffering; we are dealing with our own people, brothers with a conscience. We are the most forgiving people on the planet; the only time we do not know how to forgive is when it comes to each other, and Christ dealt with that. Precepts: - Matthew 5:38-42 Ye have heard that it hath been said, an eye for an eye; but I say unto you that ye resist not evil; Christ magnified the law for how brothers deal with brothers. Leviticus 25: The Sabbath of the Land and the Year of Jubile Read the chapter → Leviticus 25 Leviticus 25:1-7 - When ye come into the land which I give you, six years thou shalt sow thy field and prune thy vineyard, but in the seventh year shall be a sabbath of rest unto the land, a sabbath for the Lord: no sowing, no pruning, no reaping of that which groweth of its own accord. - As we rest on the seventh day, the land rests the seventh year. Letting the land rest is harmony and balance on the earth, and the sabbath of the land is meat for thee, thy servants, the stranger, thy cattle, and the beasts in thy land. - These land laws were given for the land of Israel; land bought in this captivity is not under the seventh year rest. Leviticus 25:8-13 - Thou shalt number seven sabbaths of years, seven times seven years, forty and nine years; then shall thou cause the trumpet of the jubile to sound on the tenth day of the seventh month, in the day of atonement, throughout all your land. - Ye shall hallow the fiftieth year, and proclaim liberty throughout all the land unto all the inhabitants thereof: it shall be a jubile unto you, and ye shall return every man unto his possession, and every man unto his family. Neither sow, nor reap that which groweth of itself, for it is the jubile; it shall be holy unto you. Leviticus 25:14-17 - If thou sell ought unto thy neighbour, or buyest ought of thy neighbour's hand, ye shall not oppress one another: according to the number of years after the jubile thou shalt buy, and according unto the fewness of years thou shalt diminish the price, for according to the number of the years of the fruits doth he sell unto thee. - Thou shalt fear thy God, for I am the Lord your God; the price was reckoned honestly to the jubile so no man was oppressed. Leviticus 25:18-22 - Wherefore ye shall do my statutes and keep my judgments, and ye shall dwell in the land in safety, and the land shall yield her fruit, and ye shall eat your fill. - If ye shall say, What shall we eat the seventh year? behold, we shall not sow nor gather in our increase: then I will command my blessing upon you in the sixth year, and it shall bring forth fruit for three years. The Most High answered the lack before it came: the sixth year would bring forth enough until the harvests of the ninth year came in, and ye shall sow the eighth year and eat yet of old fruit. Leviticus 25:23-28 - The land shall not be sold for ever, for the land is mine; for ye are strangers and sojourners with me. Israel was not able to sell away any of the land for ever, because it is the holy land of the Most High, and in all the land of your possession ye shall grant a redemption for the land. - If thy brother be waxen poor and hath sold away some of his possession, and any of his kin come to redeem it, then shall he redeem that which his brother sold; or if the man himself be able, he may redeem it, or it goes out in the jubile and he returns to his possession. - Redeem and buy are interchangeable words here: his kin come to redeem it meaning to buy it back. This is the prime example to reference for the curse that says no man shall buy you: no man shall redeem you. The other nations never came to say, we want to redeem Israel out of slavery and set them back to freedom; Israel has been in slavery for hundreds of years and no nation did that. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 28:68 Ye shall be sold unto your enemies for bondmen and bondwomen, and no man shall buy you; buy is interchangeable with redeem, and no nation redeemed Israel out of this captivity. Leviticus 25:29-34 - If a man sell a dwelling house in a walled city, he may redeem it within a whole year after it is sold; if it be not redeemed within the space of a full year, the house in the walled city is established for ever to him that bought it. But the houses of the villages which have no wall are counted as the fields of the country: they may be redeemed, and they go out in the jubile. - Notwithstanding, the cities of the Levites, the houses of the cities of their possession, may the Levites redeem at any time, for the houses of the cities of the Levites are their possession among the children of Israel. Levi was not given any land; his portion was the offerings of the Lord, and the fields of the suburbs of their cities are their perpetual possession and may not be sold. Leviticus 25:35-38 - If thy brother be waxen poor and fallen in decay with thee, then thou shalt relieve him, yea, though he be a stranger or a sojourner, that he may live with thee. The word stranger does not always mean a heathen; sometimes it is your own brother sojourning away from his land, and the context of the verse tells you which. - Thy brother is thy neighbour and the children of thy people: thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people, but thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. Brother, neighbour, and children of thy people all mean the same thing. - Take thou no usury of him, or increase, but fear thy God, that thy brother may live with thee. Usury is interest, a fee accumulating over time; thou shalt not give him thy money upon usury, nor lend him thy victuals for increase. Lending for the opportunity to make a profit off your own people is evil. - I am the Lord your God, which brought you forth out of the land of Egypt, to give you the land of Canaan. The Most High is not the God of everybody: to bring Israel out He judged Egypt, and to give Israel Canaan He cast out the seven nations, greater and mightier than Israel, delivered them before Israel to be smitten, with no covenant and no mercy shewed, during that time period. Precepts: - Leviticus 19:17-18 Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people, but thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself; brother, neighbour, and children of thy people are the same. - Isaiah 43:3-4 I gave Egypt for thy ransom, Ethiopia and Seba for thee; since thou wast precious in my sight, I have loved thee, therefore will I give men for thee. A ransom secures the safe exit of the victim; the Most High gave Egypt and Ethiopia their own lives to bring Israel out. - Deuteronomy 7:1-2 Seven nations greater and mightier than Israel were cast out and delivered before Israel to be utterly destroyed, with no covenant made and no mercy shewed; that is how the Most High gave the land of Canaan. Leviticus 25:39-43 - If thy brother that dwelleth by thee be waxen poor and be sold unto thee, thou shalt not compel him to serve as a bondservant, but as an hired servant and as a sojourner he shall be with thee, and shall serve thee unto the year of jubile; then shall he depart from thee, both he and his children with him, and shall return unto his own family and unto the possession of his fathers. - The Hebrew servant serves six years, and in the seventh he goes out free for nothing; if he came in by himself he goes out by himself, and if he were married his wife goes out with him. That seventh year of release is that servant's jubile: a servant taken in 2012 goes out free in 2019, and one taken in 2019 goes out free in 2026. - For they are my servants, which I brought forth out of the land of Egypt: they shall not be sold as bondmen. Thou shalt not rule over him with rigour, but shalt fear thy God; deal with him properly, for the Most High judges both the poor man and the one he serves. Precepts: - Exodus 21:2-3 If thou buy an Hebrew servant, six years he shall serve, and in the seventh he shall go out free for nothing; the brother sold to thee goes out at the release. Leviticus 25:44-46 - Both thy bondmen and thy bondmaids, which thou shalt have, shall be of the heathen that are round about you; of them shall ye buy bondmen and bondmaids, and of the children of the strangers that do sojourn among you, and they shall be your possession. - Ye shall take them as an inheritance for your children after you, to inherit them for a possession; they shall be your bondmen for ever. But over your brethren the children of Israel, ye shall not rule one over another with rigour. Leviticus 25:47-55 - If a sojourner or stranger wax rich by thee, and thy brother that dwelleth by him wax poor and sell himself unto the stranger, after that he is sold he may be redeemed again: one of his brethren may redeem him, either his uncle, or his uncle's son, or any that is nigh of kin unto him of his family; or if he be able, he may redeem himself, working as an hired servant and earning the price of his own freedom. - Here again redeem means buy, as in buying a man out of slavery back to the position of freedom; and the price of his redemption was reckoned with him that bought him, according to the number of years from the year he was sold unto the year of jubile, as the time of an hired servant. If he be not redeemed in these years, then he shall go out in the year of jubile, both he and his children with him. - For unto me the children of Israel are servants; they are my servants whom I brought forth out of the land of Egypt: I am the Lord your God. Everybody is not the servant of the Most High; the children of Israel are His servants, and this teaching identifies them today as the so-called Blacks, Hispanics, and Native Americans. --- Topics: Clean and Unclean Meats · Sacrifice and Atonement · The Covenant · The Feasts of the Most High · The Priesthood · The Sabbath ← Leviticus 18-21 · Leviticus Study · Leviticus 26-27 →

title: Leviticus 26: The Blessings and the Curses
text: ← Leviticus 22-25 · Leviticus Study · Numbers 1-2 → Leviticus 26: The Blessings and the Curses Read the chapter → Leviticus 26 Introduction This reading covers Leviticus 26 through Numbers 2: the blessings and the curses upon the children of Israel, the law of vows and estimations, the numbering of the armies of Israel, and the order of the camps about the tabernacle. Leviticus 26 goes in parallel with Deuteronomy the 28th chapter: the blessings for walking in the commandments of the Most High and the curses for breaking the covenant. Leviticus 26:1 - The children of Israel are to make no idols nor graven images, rear up no standing image, and set up no image of stone in the land to bow down to it. - That covers the images bowed to today: the cobblestone of Islam, the cross, and the relics and Egyptian heads that egyptologists worship. The Israelites are not to do that. Leviticus 26:2 - Keep the sabbaths of the Most High and reverence His sanctuary. When you came into the sanctuary you had better come with respect, because the Most High was putting men to death over it. - Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aaron, offered strange fire before the Lord which He commanded them not, and fire went out from the Lord and devoured them; that is what reverencing the sanctuary means. Precepts: - Leviticus 10:1-3 Nadab and Abihu offered strange fire which the Lord commanded them not, and fire from the Lord devoured them; I will be sanctified in them that come nigh me. Leviticus 26:3-4 - These are the blessings for walking in the statutes and keeping the commandments, the same blessings and curses read in Deuteronomy the 28th chapter. - If Israel kept the commandments there would be no famine: rain in due season, the crops continually growing, the harvest coming in on time, and rain in the land even in a drought. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 28:1-2 If thou shalt hearken diligently unto the voice of the Lord, all these blessings shall come on thee and overtake thee; the same covenant of blessing and curse. Leviticus 26:5 - The threshing is the corn and the vintage is the grapes for the wine. The threshing reaching to the vintage and the vintage to the sowing time means one season's plenty would carry into the next. - Israel would never be without wine, without crops, without food; each harvest would reach to the next season, and the bread would be eaten to the full in safety. Leviticus 26:6 - The Most High would give peace in the land: no enemies able to come against Israel, no war in the land, no one making the people afraid. That was fulfilled in the days of king Solomon, when there was rest on every side. - That is also how you know the people in the land of Israel today are not the real Jews: this prophecy of rest is not fulfilled on them. When the Most High saves Israel from captivity it will be the same again, and none shall make him afraid. Precepts: - Jeremiah 30:10 Jacob shall return, and shall be in rest, and be quiet, and none shall make him afraid; the future deliverance carries the same promise as this blessing. Leviticus 26:7-9 - Israel would chase their enemies, and the enemies would fall before them by the sword; the nations feared Israel when the nation kept this covenant, as the book of Joshua shows. - Five would chase an hundred, and an hundred put ten thousand to flight: that is how much power the Most High was going to bestow on His people, having respect unto them, making them fruitful, and establishing His covenant with them and their children. Leviticus 26:10-13 - Eating the old store and bringing forth the old because of the new means the storehouses would be so full that the old crop would have to be carried out to make room for the new; that is how plenteous the land would be. - The Most High would set His tabernacle among the people, walk among them, and be their God; He brought them out of Egypt so they should not be bondmen, and broke the bands of their yoke. Leviticus 26:14-16 - This is the flip side. If Israel would not hearken but despised the statutes and broke the covenant, the Most High would walk contrary to the people, standing in exact opposition so that nothing would prosper. - Terror is the terrorism lived under every single day: terrorized by wicked corrupt officers, by our own brothers and sisters, by the nations. Consumption is being consumed in the land, with diseases, oppression, financial mishaps, and the prison system; the burning ague goes into disease, harm to the eyes, and sorrow of heart in the mind. - Sowing seed in vain: vineyards planted that the enemies eat, and children sown in vain, born only to be killed, incarcerated, or raised up under the curse. Leviticus 26:17 - The Most High set His face against Israel, and the people are slain before their enemies; you see that every single day. - They that hate you shall reign over you: that is the clear explanation of why no laws will be passed to deliver this people and why there will be no reparations. No political party, Democratic or Republican, will be beneficial, because the curse stands and they that hate us now reign over us; and we flee when none pursueth. Leviticus 26:18-20 - Seven times more punishment for the sins, and the pride of Israel's power broken: the very power promised in the blessings, when enemies would flee, was taken away. - That is the explanation of how the slave masters could bring Israel into slavery: they are not bigger or stronger nations, but it was divine intervention; the Most High broke our power and took our strength so the enemies could prevail. We outnumbered them many times in the cotton fields, yet could do nothing. - The heaven as iron and the earth as brass also goes into the shackles on the neck and on the feet; and the strength is spent in vain, for the land yields no increase. Leviticus 26:21-22 - Walking contrary still brings seven times more plagues according to the sins. - Wild beasts sent among the people to rob them of their children, destroy their cattle, and make them few in number: wolves, coyotes, bears, whatever the Most High would allow to come upon the people for their wickedness. That is real evil brought for real rebellion. - It also goes into the pestilences and diseases loosed among the people in these last days, as Revelation 6 bears out with death by sword, hunger, and the beasts of the earth. Precepts: - Revelation 6:8 Power was given them to kill with sword, with hunger, with death, and with the beasts of the earth; the same instruments of judgment. Leviticus 26:23-26 - If the people would not be reformed by these things, the Most High would punish yet seven times more and bring a sword to avenge the quarrel of His covenant; gathered into their cities, the pestilence would be sent among them and they would be delivered into the hand of the enemy. - Breaking the staff of bread, with ten women baking bread in one oven and delivering bread again by weight, is straight poverty: a lack of resources and food. Many of us grew up literally knocking on the neighbor's door to borrow sugar, borrow the iron, borrow bread, use the grill at such and such house because our appliances did not work; that is this verse, the same thing to this day, eating and not being satisfied. Leviticus 26:27-29 - The Most High said He would walk contrary in fury, and He would be the one doing it: He would use the enemies, but it would be Him behind it. That is heavy. - Eating the flesh of sons and daughters goes into 70 AD, and it also happened in the days of the kings when the city was besieged and there was such famine that a woman's son was boiled and eaten. Precepts: - 2 Kings 6:25-29 In the siege of Samaria an ass's head sold for fourscore pieces of silver, and a woman said, Give thy son, that we may eat him to day; so we boiled my son, and did eat him. - Deuteronomy 28:52-53 The enemy shall besiege thee in all thy gates, and thou shalt eat the fruit of thine own body, the flesh of thy sons and daughters, in the siege and straitness. - Luke 21:20 When ye shall see Jerusalem compassed with armies, then know that the desolation thereof is nigh; the siege of 70 AD fulfilled this curse. Leviticus 26:30 - The high places destroyed, the images cut down, and the carcasses of the people cast upon the carcasses of their idols: our people dying in the christian church with a cross around the neck, our people dying up against the cobblestone, still worshipping while they die. - Even the high places themselves fall in judgment, as when a storm brought a church down on the congregation in Africa during a so-called easter program; that is what this verse reads about. Leviticus 26:31-33 - The Most High made the cities waste and brought the sanctuaries to desolation, and would not smell the savour of the sweet odours: He was not accepting the sacrifices, and He used the enemy to destroy the sanctuary. The Babylonians destroyed the temple, then the Greeks, then the Romans. - When Babylon came against Jerusalem, Esau stood on the side cheering it on to the foundation, as Psalms 137 records. - Scattered among the heathen with a sword drawn out after them: not only the scattering, but death and anguish sent among the people in the lands of the captivity. Precepts: - Psalms 137:7 Remember the children of Edom in the day of Jerusalem, who said, Rase it, rase it, even to the foundation thereof; Esau cheered the destruction on. Leviticus 26:34-35 - Then shall the land enjoy her sabbaths as long as it lieth desolate. The land was to rest every seventh year, and the sabbaths were not kept: no cooking or tilling on the sabbath, the land resting every seven years, none of it. - The Most High said the land could not rest while the people dwelt on it doing evil, so He rid the people out of the land so that the land could enjoy her sabbaths while it lay desolate without them. Leviticus 26:36-38 - Upon them that are left alive a faintness is sent into their hearts in the lands of their enemies, so that the sound of a shaken leaf chases them; the same trembling heart, failing of eyes, and sorrow of mind that Deuteronomy 28 describes for the land of the enemies. - Falling one upon another as it were before a sword when none pursueth: even at these protests, when the rubber bullets, the tear gas, the water hoses, and the dogs come out, the people stumble and fall over one another trying to get away. Still to this day the same thing. - And ye shall perish among the heathen: many of us die in this land and in all the lands where we are scattered, and the land of the enemies eats the people up in oppression. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 28:65-67 Among these nations shalt thou find no ease, but a trembling heart, and failing of eyes, and sorrow of mind, fearing day and night with no assurance of life. Leviticus 26:39 - They that are left pine away in their iniquity in the enemies' land, and in the iniquities of their fathers. You see people just decay in their sickness: the Most High may not judge a man right away but gives him space to repent, yet he keeps eating the defiled food, smoking his weed, doping, in and out of jail, and slowly pines away. - It is a miserable life to live; we have to get right with the Most High. Leviticus 26:40-41 - Confessing the iniquity of the fathers and their own trespass, with the uncircumcised heart humbled, is exactly what is being done right now: repenting, confessing the sins, remembering that the sins of the forefathers are ours, and turning the uncircumcised mind back to the Father. - Accepting the punishment of the iniquity means going through the trials without fighting the sentence: not marching for reparations or so-called equality, but accepting the punishment for the iniquities committed against the Most High. Leviticus 26:42-43 - When the people repent and turn back, the Most High remembers His covenant with Jacob, with Isaac, and with Abraham, the covenant passed down to their children, the children of Israel; and He remembers the land. - The land enjoys her sabbaths while she lieth desolate without them, and the people must accept that they were evil and wicked against the Most High, because they despised His judgments and their soul abhorred His statutes. Precepts: - 1 Kings 8:46-48 If they bethink themselves in the land of their captivity, and repent, and return unto thee with all their heart, the Most High hears; repentance in captivity brings the covenant back to remembrance. Leviticus 26:44-45 - Yet for all that, in the land of their enemies the Most High will not cast the people away, neither abhor them to destroy them utterly and break His covenant. He sent Israel into captivity not for all to die, but to be afflicted until they finally turn back to the Lord God of Israel. - So when you hear people say the Israelites are done away, that is a lie: the Most High promised He would not destroy the seed of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, but would give them a chance to repent and would remember the covenant of their ancestors whom He brought out of Egypt in the sight of the heathen. It also carries into the future tense. Leviticus 26:46 - These are the statutes and judgments and laws which the Most High made between Him and the children of Israel in mount Sinai by the hand of Moses. - The quick recap of the chapter: these are the blessings and the curses that come upon the children of Israel for obedience or disobedience, and the chapter runs parallel with Deuteronomy the 28th chapter. Leviticus 27: Vows and Estimations Read the chapter → Leviticus 27 Leviticus 27:1-2 - A singular vow is a man binding himself to the Most High: promising that in exchange for a blessing he will give himself, or what is his, to the service of the Lord. The persons vowed were valued by the estimation of the priest. - Hannah is the example: in bitterness of soul she vowed that if the Lord gave her a man child she would give him unto the Lord all the days of his life, and that is how the story of Samuel began. - Christ taught on this because a vow is dangerous: you must pay your vow. Better not to swear at all, but let your communication be yea, yea; that is why we just say Lord's will, Lord's will I get this done. Precepts: - 1 Samuel 1:10-11 Hannah vowed a vow: give unto thine handmaid a man child, and I will give him unto the Lord all the days of his life; the pattern of a singular vow. - Matthew 5:33-37 Perform unto the Lord thine oaths; but swear not at all, and let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay. Leviticus 27:3-8 - The estimation is the value set for redeeming a person out of the vow. A male from twenty to sixty years old, the prime of life, was fifty shekels of silver after the shekel of the sanctuary, and a female thirty shekels. - From five years to twenty years old the male was twenty shekels and the female ten; from a month old to five years the male was five shekels and the female three; and from sixty years old and above the male was fifteen shekels and the female ten. - If the man was poorer than the estimation and could not pay it, he presented himself before the priest, and the priest valued him according to the ability of him that vowed, his worth and what he was able to bring forth. Leviticus 27:9-13 - If a beast was brought as an offering to the Most High it had to be holy, not blemished; it could not be altered or changed, a good for a bad or a bad for a good, and if it was changed at all, both it and the exchange became holy. - An unclean beast, one with a blemish that could not be sacrificed, was presented before the priest and the priest valued it, good or bad; and to redeem it, a fifth part had to be added to the estimation to get that beast back. Leviticus 27:14-15 - A man could sanctify his house to be holy unto the Most High, and the priest estimated it, good or bad, and as the priest estimated it, so it stood. - To redeem the house he added the fifth part of the money of the estimation: if the house was worth a hundred thousand, he paid that hundred thousand plus the extra twenty thousand, and it was his again. Leviticus 27:16-25 - A field sanctified to the Most High was estimated according to the seed thereof, an homer of barley seed at fifty shekels of silver; from the year of jubile the estimation stood full, but after the jubile the priest reckoned the money according to the years that remained, and it was abated from the estimation. - The jubile was the year of release, when the land had to rest, so the value was reckoned by how close the jubile was: the fewer years left to reap the field, the lower the estimation. It is like trading in a car; a two year old car with twenty thousand miles brings more value than an old car with a hundred and fifty thousand miles on it. - To redeem a sanctified field the fifth part was added to the estimation. A field not redeemed, or sold to another man, could not be redeemed any more, but went out in the jubile holy unto the Lord, a devoted field, the possession of the priest; and in the year of jubile a bought field returned to him of whom it was bought. - All the estimations were according to the shekel of the sanctuary, twenty gerahs to the shekel; that was the standard, the set price. Leviticus 27:26-29 - The firstling of the beasts could not be sanctified by any man, because as a firstling it was the Lord's already, whether ox or sheep; an unclean firstling was redeemed by the estimation with the fifth part added, or sold according to the estimation. - No devoted thing that a man devoted unto the Most High, of man, beast, or field of his possession, could be sold or redeemed: every devoted thing is most holy unto the Lord, and a devoted man was surely put to death. Leviticus 27:30-34 - All the tithe of the land, of the seed of the land or the fruit of the tree, is the Lord's; it is holy unto the Lord. To redeem out of the tithes a man added the fifth part thereto. - The tithe of the herd and the flock, the tenth of whatsoever passeth under the rod, was holy unto the Lord; he was not to search whether it was good or bad or change it, and if he changed it at all, both it and the change were holy and could not be redeemed. - The quick recap of the chapter: when a brother or sister vowed themselves to the Most High, the redemption from that vow went according to the estimation, by age and by sex, and likewise a house or a field; all these things go into how the priest calculated the estimation of these particular things to release you from the vow. The chapter can be tricky, so read it over and over. --- Topics: Clean and Unclean Meats · Esau and Edom · Idolatry · Sacrifice and Atonement · The Covenant · The Priesthood · The Sabbath ← Leviticus 22-25 · Leviticus Study · Numbers 1-2 →

title: Leviticus 6: The Trespass Offering and the Fire That Shall Never Go Out
text: ← Leviticus 2-5 · Leviticus Study · Leviticus 10-13 → Leviticus 6: The Trespass Offering and the Fire That Shall Never Go Out Read the chapter → Leviticus 6 Introduction This reading covers Leviticus 6 through 9: the trespass offering and restitution, the laws of the burnt, meat, sin, trespass, and peace offerings, the consecration of Aaron and his sons, and the eighth day when the glory of the Lord appeared to all the people. Leviticus is straightforward like the rest of the law, and these chapters pertain heavily to the book of Hebrews: the law of sacrifice is the volume of the book that is written of Christ, and once you understand the law you begin to understand the letters of Paul. The session opened by backtracking into Leviticus 5 on the witness law, unclean things, and oaths; that teaching belongs to the Leviticus 5 chapter set and is logged there. Leviticus 6:1-5 - If a soul lie unto his neighbour in that which was delivered him to keep, or in fellowship, or deceive his neighbour, or find that which was lost and lie concerning it, and swear falsely, the Lord counts all of it as a thing taken away by violence: verse 4 says he shall restore that which he took violently away. Deceiving your neighbour, going into agreement and not holding up your end, or lying about what was given you to hold is a violent act toward your neighbour, and a Ponzi scheme or pyramid scheme sits right in that law. - He shall restore it in the principal: the value of what was taken had to be given back, with more added on top. A sorry would not settle it with the Lord; you could end up in debt for years over sticky fingers. - Stealing was not a sin unto death, but the Lord made the restitution heavy so you would never commit it again. It goes back to the commandment, thou shalt not steal, and to the civil law where an ox was restored fivefold and a sheep fourfold. Precepts: - Exodus 20:15 Thou shalt not steal; the trespass law enforces this commandment. - Exodus 22:1 Five oxen for an ox and four sheep for a sheep; the thief restored the principal many times over. Leviticus 6:6-7 - The trespass offering was a ram without blemish, perfect as the Most High made it, and the priest made an atonement for him before the Lord and it was forgiven him. The sacrifice stood in your place for your sin. - The whole law of sacrifice points to Christ, who came in the volume of the book. He is the offering without blemish and the atonement, and who has become the high priest is Jesus the Christ. - Israel became the enemy of the Most High by sin. There are two kinds of enemies: the nations that are the natural enemies of the Most High, and Israel, who rebelled and vexed his holy spirit, and he was turned to be their enemy. Through the death of his Son the nation is reconciled, brought back together with its God. - The letters of Paul were written to Israelites living in those lands and called by their names, Romans and Corinthians, the same way we are called American or Jamaican today; written today they would be the letter to the Jamaicans or the letter to the Puerto Ricans. Precepts: - Hebrews 10:7 Lo, I come in the volume of the book it is written of me; the whole book from Genesis to Revelation points to Christ. - Isaiah 63:7-10 The great goodness toward the house of Israel; but they rebelled, and he was turned to be their enemy. - Romans 5:10-11 When we were enemies we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, by whom we have now received the atonement. - Ezekiel 45:17 The sin offering, meat offering, burnt offering, and peace offerings were prepared to make reconciliation for the house of Israel; that is what reconciled means. - Acts 5:30-31 Him hath God exalted to be a Prince and a Saviour, for to give repentance to Israel, and forgiveness of sins; Christ died for the nation of Israel. Leviticus 6:8-9 - The burnt offering burned upon the altar all night unto the morning, and the fire of the altar was burning in it. When Exodus says kindle no fire on the sabbath day, that speaks of making food; the Levites were commanded to keep a fire burning on the altar continually, sabbath included. - Christ used this very law on the Pharisees: have ye not read how that on the sabbath days the priests in the temple profane the sabbath, and are blameless? The priests had fire going in the temple every sabbath by commandment. - I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: the Most High desired the knowledge of God and obedience more than burnt offerings. Israel leaned so heavily on the sacrifices instead of applying the commandments that they were confounded and could not see Christ as the Son of God when he came. - Jeremiah carries the same word: I spake not unto your fathers concerning burnt offerings or sacrifices, but this thing commanded I them, obey my voice. Yet they hearkened not, but walked in the counsels of their evil heart and went backward and not forward; speak all these words unto them, but they will not hearken. That is seen every sabbath on the streets. Precepts: - Exodus 35:3 Kindle no fire throughout your habitations upon the sabbath day; that is fire for cooking, not the altar fire. - Matthew 12:5-7 On the sabbath days the priests in the temple profane the sabbath and are blameless; if ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless. - Hosea 6:6 For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings. - Malachi 2:7 The priest's lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth; the knowledge the Most High desired is the law. - Jeremiah 7:21-23 Put your burnt offerings unto your sacrifices; I commanded obedience: obey my voice, and I will be your God, and ye shall be my people. Leviticus 6:10-11 - The priest put on his linen garment and his linen breeches upon his flesh. The priests were men, not women, and breeches are pants; they were made for the men. - The ashes of the burnt offering were carried forth without the camp unto a clean place. Christ fulfilled that figure: they led him away out of the city to crucify him at Golgotha, the place of a skull; he suffered without the gate. - Hebrews draws the lesson: let us go forth therefore unto him without the camp, bearing his reproach. Put away the sacrifice as it was carried outside the temple, and come out unto Christ. Precepts: - Exodus 28:42 Linen breeches to cover their nakedness were made for Aaron and his sons; the breeches belonged to the men. - Matthew 27:31-33 They led him away to crucify him, and came unto a place called Golgotha; led away is the same as carried without the camp. - Hebrews 13:10-14 The bodies of the beasts are burned without the camp; wherefore Jesus also suffered without the gate; let us go forth unto him without the camp. Leviticus 6:12-13 - The fire upon the altar shall be burning in it; it shall not be put out. The priest burnt wood on it every morning, and that included the sabbath; the fire shall ever be burning upon the altar, and it shall never go out. - This is exactly what Christ went into in Matthew 12: the priests profane the sabbath and are blameless, because the commanded altar fire never went out. Leviticus 6:14-18 - This is the law of the meat offering. The meat offering is not flesh; it is grain, fine flour with oil and frankincense. A handful was burnt upon the altar for a sweet savour, and the remainder Aaron and his sons ate unleavened in the holy place. - It shall be a statute for ever in your generations: the law is spiritual. To understand how a perpetual statute of sacrifice pointed to Christ, the Spirit of Christ had to dwell in you; Paul himself did not understand until Christ touched him on the way to Damascus. - Christ told the disciples the Comforter would teach them all things and bring all things to their remembrance. Unless the Spirit of the Lord deals with you, you will never understand the Bible or the laws; that is why there was such contention between Christ and the Pharisees, for the Spirit had not revealed to them who he was. Precepts: - Romans 7:14 For we know that the law is spiritual; the statute for ever is understood in the spirit. - John 14:26 The Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance; the spirit of the law is revealed by the Spirit. Leviticus 6:19-23 - This is the offering of Aaron and of his sons in the day when he is anointed: the tenth part of an ephah of fine flour for a meat offering perpetual, half in the morning and half at night, baked with oil in a pan. The meat offering is again actual flour, grain. - Every meat offering for the priest was wholly burnt; it was not eaten. The priest's own offering went completely to the Lord. Leviticus 6:24-30 - This is the law of the sin offering: in the place where the burnt offering is killed shall the sin offering be killed before the LORD; it is most holy. Christ was the sin offering, and he was most holy. - Christ did no sin, neither was guile, which is deceit, found in his mouth; when he was reviled, he reviled not again. He kept his Father's commandments and abode in his love, leaving us an example that we should follow his steps; if you do not keep the commandments of God you are not following his steps. - The blood was not eaten: the sin offering whose blood was brought into the tabernacle to reconcile was not eaten but burnt in the fire. Israel does not mess with the blood; Esau eats the blood, not us. Precepts: - 1 Peter 2:21-23 Christ suffered for us, leaving us an example, that ye should follow his steps: who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth. - John 15:10 If ye keep my commandments, ye shall abide in my love; even as I have kept my Father's commandments; that is how Christ walked. Leviticus 7: Christ Our Peace Offering Read the chapter → Leviticus 7 Leviticus 7:1-7 - Likewise this is the law of the trespass offering: it is most holy. The fat, the rump, the fat that covers the inwards, the kidneys, and the caul above the liver, basically the guts, were burnt upon the altar, and as the sin offering is, so is the trespass offering; there is one law for them. - Paul was a master of the law, and trespass in his letters goes back to this law: you hath he quickened, who were dead in trespasses and sins, when in time past we walked according to the course of this world, according to the prince of the power of the air, which is Satan. - By grace ye are saved means all of us deserve death for our sins, but through Christ we have grace and are saved from the destruction to come, if we endure to the end keeping the commandments. Precepts: - Ephesians 2:1-5 You hath he quickened, who were dead in trespasses and sins; God, who is rich in mercy, even when we were dead in sins, hath quickened us together with Christ; by grace ye are saved. - Romans 6:23 The wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ; that is the grace, that we are not killed for our sins. Leviticus 7:11-18 - This is the law of the sacrifice of peace offerings. If it was offered for a thanksgiving, the flesh was eaten the same day it was offered; none was left until the morning. - If the sacrifice was a vow or a voluntary offering, it was eaten the same day and the remainder on the morrow also; that is the difference between the two. But flesh remaining on the third day was burnt with fire, and if any was eaten on the third day it was an abomination, and the offering was not accepted. Leviticus 7:19-21 - The flesh that touched any unclean thing was not eaten but burnt with fire, and the soul that ate of the peace offerings having his uncleanness upon him was cut off from his people. An unclean man coming into the tabernacle to sacrifice or a priest eating unclean was facing death before the Lord. - All the touching of unclean and defiled things pertains to sacrifice: the point of the uncleanness laws was to separate the children of Israel from their uncleanness, that they die not when they defile the tabernacle. There is no more sacrifice, so those defilement laws do not apply today; a brother can brush his hair with a brush of boar bristles, because that law was about coming in to sacrifice. Precepts: - Leviticus 15:31 Thus shall ye separate the children of Israel from their uncleanness, that they die not, when they defile my tabernacle; the uncleanness laws guarded the sacrifice. Leviticus 7:22-27 - Ye shall eat no manner of fat, of ox, or of sheep, or of goat: this pertained to the sacrifices. The fat upon the sacrifices was either burnt completely or put to other uses; there is no sin in eating fat off an animal now, because what it pertained to was the sacrifice. - One of those other uses was soap: Israel took the fat and made soap with it. Jeremiah shows it, though thou wash thee with nitre, and take thee much soap; Israel had soap way back then and did not live filthy, and when the Moors ruled in Europe they introduced soap to Esau again. - But blood was different: no manner of blood, of fowl or of beast, in any of your dwellings, whether sacrificing or not. The soul that eats any manner of blood shall be cut off; cook the food well done, not rare, and that stands to this day. Precepts: - Jeremiah 2:22 Though thou wash thee with nitre, and take thee much soap, yet thine iniquity is marked before me; soap was known in Israel of old, made from the fat. Leviticus 7:28-34 - He that offered his peace offerings brought the oblation with his own hands: the fat with the breast, that the breast may be waved for a wave offering before the LORD. The wave offering was heaved up and waved before the Lord as a sign, proof of what he had brought. - The wave breast and the heave shoulder were given to Aaron the priest and his sons by a statute for ever; this is how the priests ate from the peace offerings. Leviticus 10 returns to these portions, the wave breast and heave shoulder given to Aaron and his sons and daughters; chapters 6 through 10 explain the offerings. Precepts: - Exodus 29:27 Sanctify the breast of the wave offering, and the shoulder of the heave offering, which is waved, and which is heaved up; the offering was lifted and waved before the Lord. Leviticus 7:35-38 - Verse 37 lists all the different offerings in one place: the burnt offering, the meat offering, the sin offering, the trespass offering, the consecrations, and the sacrifice of the peace offerings, which the LORD commanded Moses in mount Sinai. - Christ is our peace, our peace offering between us and the Most High. He abolished in his flesh the enmity, even the law of commandments contained in ordinances; the ordinances are the law of sacrifice, sprinkle the blood seven times, a lamb without blemish, eaten before the third day, carried without the camp, burnt to ashes with the garments changed. - Let no man therefore judge you in meat or in drink: add the word offering, the meat offering and drink offering we just read in Leviticus. No man can condemn you because you are not sacrificing animals any more, or for how you observe a holyday, new moon, or sabbath pertaining to sacrifice, for those are a shadow of things to come, but the body is of Christ. - The law of sacrifice was contrary to us because those sacrifices offered year by year continually could never make the comers thereunto perfect. It was a scapegoat so the law would not have to kill us; the Most High has been extending grace since Adam, for he had every right to kill Adam and Eve, and instead extended grace through the animal sacrifice. If the law of sacrifice still stood, there would be no sacrifice for worshipping other gods, and we would be done as a people; it was taken out of the way so Israel could come back to God. Precepts: - Ephesians 2:13-16 Ye who sometimes were far off are made nigh by the blood of Christ: for he is our peace, who hath abolished in his flesh the law of commandments contained in ordinances, and reconciled both unto God in one body. - Colossians 2:14-17 Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us, nailing it to his cross; let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days: which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ. - Hebrews 10:1 The law having a shadow of good things to come can never with those sacrifices year by year make the comers thereunto perfect; that is how it was contrary to us. Leviticus 8: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons Read the chapter → Leviticus 8 Leviticus 8:1-5 - Take Aaron and his sons with him, and the garments, and the anointing oil, and a bullock for the sin offering, and two rams, and a basket of unleavened bread; and all the congregation was gathered unto the door of the tabernacle. - Mark the list: if you want to live under the Old Covenant, you had better have a priest, the garments, the anointing oil, a bullock for the sin offering, two rams, a basket of unleavened bread, and a temple to gather at. The covenant of sacrifice cannot be kept today. Leviticus 8:6-9 - Moses washed Aaron and his sons with water, and put upon him the coat, the girdle, the robe, and the ephod, and he put the breastplate upon him, and in the breastplate the Urim and the Thummim. - He put the mitre upon his head, and upon the mitre, upon his forefront, the golden plate, the holy crown, as the LORD commanded Moses. Leviticus 8:10-13 - Moses anointed the tabernacle and all that was therein, sprinkled the altar seven times, and poured of the anointing oil upon Aaron's head, and anointed him, to sanctify him, to set him apart. - This is what David is going back to in the psalm: behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity; it is like the precious ointment upon the head, that ran down upon the beard, even Aaron's beard, down to the skirts of his garments. That oil could be poured on no one but the high priest; that is how precious unity among the people is to be. Precepts: - Psalms 133:1-3 Unity among brethren is like the precious ointment upon Aaron's head that ran down his beard to the skirts of his garments; for there the LORD commanded the blessing. Leviticus 8:14-17 - Aaron and his sons laid their hands upon the head of the bullock for the sin offering, and Moses put the blood upon the horns of the altar with his finger, purified the altar, and sanctified it, to make reconciliation upon it; reconciliation goes back to making reconciliation for the house of Israel. - The fat, the caul, and the kidneys, the guts, were burnt upon the altar, but the bullock with his hide and flesh was burnt with fire without the camp. Christ's crucifixion lines up with the law of sacrifice: he was taken outside Jerusalem to the place called Golgotha and crucified there. Precepts: - Ezekiel 45:17 The sin offering and the burnt offering were prepared to make reconciliation for the house of Israel; the purified altar carried that reconciliation. Leviticus 8:18-21 - The ram for the burnt offering was cut into pieces, the inwards and legs washed in water, and Moses burnt the whole ram upon the altar: a burnt sacrifice for a sweet savour, an offering made by fire unto the LORD. Leviticus 8:22-24 - Moses slew the other ram, the ram of consecration, and put the blood upon the tip of Aaron's right ear, upon the thumb of his right hand, and upon the great toe of his right foot, and the same for his sons. - The blood went on the right side. The right side is the favored side with the Most High, and the volume of the book bears the pattern: when Christ rose he went to his Father and sat on the right hand of God. Leviticus 8:25-29 - The fat, the right shoulder, and out of the basket one unleavened cake, a cake of oiled bread, and one wafer were put upon the hands of Aaron and his sons and waved for a wave offering before the LORD, then burnt on the altar for a sweet savour. - Moses took the breast and waved it for a wave offering before the LORD, lifting it up and waving it as in Exodus 29; it was Moses' part of the ram of consecration. Leviticus 8:30-36 - Moses sprinkled the anointing oil and the blood upon Aaron and his garments and upon his sons and their garments, and sanctified them. They boiled the flesh at the door of the tabernacle and ate it there with the bread of consecration, and abode at the door of the tabernacle day and night seven days, until the days of their consecration were at an end. - The blood, sprinkled again and again about the altar, is spiritual: they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony, which is the Bible, and they loved not their lives unto the death. That is how Satan and all the nations are overcome; the blood of the sacrifices went all the way back to Christ. Precepts: - Revelation 12:11 They overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony; the sprinkled blood of the law is the shadow of that blood. Leviticus 9: The Glory of the Lord Appears Read the chapter → Leviticus 9 Leviticus 9:1-6 - On the eighth day Moses called Aaron and his sons and the elders of Israel: a young calf for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering, without blemish; and for the people a kid of the goats for a sin offering, a calf and a lamb of the first year without blemish, a bullock and a ram for peace offerings, and a meat offering mingled with oil, the meat offering again being grain, not flesh. - For today the LORD will appear unto you: they brought what Moses commanded before the tabernacle, and all the congregation drew near and stood before the LORD, the whole nation gathered in front of the tabernacle. Leviticus 9:7-14 - Moses said unto Aaron, go unto the altar, and offer thy sin offering and thy burnt offering, and make an atonement for thyself, and for the people. The priest had to make an atonement for himself first, and then offer the offering of the people. - That is the order Hebrews opens up: the high priests of the law needed daily to offer up sacrifice first for their own sins and then for the people's; but Christ, the high priest after the order of Melchisedec, is holy, harmless, and undefiled, and offered up himself once. - Aaron dipped his finger in the blood and put it upon the horns of the altar, burnt the fat and kidneys and caul, the guts, upon the altar, and the flesh and the hide he burnt with fire without the camp; you keep reading it over and over, without the camp. Precepts: - Hebrews 7:26-27 Such an high priest, holy, harmless, undefiled, who needeth not daily, as those high priests, to offer up sacrifice, first for his own sins, and then for the people's: for this he did once, when he offered up himself. Leviticus 9:15-21 - Aaron brought the people's offering: the goat of the sin offering was slain and offered for sin as the first, the burnt offering was offered according to the manner, and he took an handful of the meat offering, the grain, and burnt it upon the altar. - He slew the bullock and the ram for a sacrifice of peace offerings for the people, the word read in Ephesians of Christ our peace, and the blood was sprinkled upon the altar round about, the blood the law keeps returning to. - The breasts and the right shoulder Aaron waved for a wave offering before the LORD, a washed piece lifted and waved, as Moses commanded. Leviticus 9:22-24 - Aaron lifted up his hand toward the people and blessed them, and came down from offering the sin offering, the burnt offering, and the peace offerings; and Moses and Aaron went into the tabernacle, and came out and blessed the people. - The glory of the LORD appeared unto all the people, and there came a fire out from before the LORD and consumed upon the altar the burnt offering and the fat; which when all the people saw, they shouted, and fell on their faces. The whole nation standing before the tabernacle saw the Most High answer the offering with fire. - To understand the priests and the sacrifices read Hebrews 7 on your own time; it goes into Melchisedec, who is Christ, and ties the whole priesthood together. --- Topics: Clean and Unclean Meats · Esau and Edom · Idolatry · Sacrifice and Atonement · The Covenant · The Feasts of the Most High · The Priesthood · The Sabbath ← Leviticus 2-5 · Leviticus Study · Leviticus 10-13 →

title: Numbers 1: The Numbering of the Armies of Israel
text: ← Leviticus 26-27 · Numbers Study · Numbers 3-6 → Numbers 1: The Numbering of the Armies of Israel Read the chapter → Numbers 1 Introduction This reading covers Numbers 1 and 2, read in the same session as Leviticus 26 and 27. The book of Numbers opens with the numbering of the armies of the Most High, the armies of the children of Israel: the census of the men of war in the wilderness of Sinai, and then the order of the camps about the tabernacle. Some think this reading is boring, but the Bible is not for them; there is beauty in everything read here, for the Most High was forming the armies of His people, and it is a beautiful thing that He found us fit and chose us to be His people. Numbers 1:1-3 - The book of Numbers is the numbering of the armies of the Lord, the armies of the children of Israel. Moses and the elders numbered the men from twenty years old and upward, every one able to go forth to war, by their armies. - Every man went to war unless the law released him: a man that had newly married, or built a house and not dedicated it, did not have to go; and a fearful man did not have to go, because that spirit of fear would jump on the other brothers. - The Most High chose able men. In the book of Judges He cut the army down from the thousands to three hundred; and when Moses held up his hands over the battle, mighty men had to hold his arms up. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 20:5-8 The officers released the man with a new house, a new vineyard, a new wife, and the fearful man, lest his brethren's heart faint as well as his heart. - Judges 7:7 By the three hundred men that lapped will I save you; the Most High cut the army down to able men of His choosing. - Exodus 17:11-12 When Moses held up his hand Israel prevailed, and Aaron and Hur stayed up his hands until the going down of the sun. Numbers 1:4-16 - With Moses and Aaron stood a man of every tribe, each one head of the house of his fathers: the renowned of the congregation, princes of the tribes, heads of thousands in Israel. - The Most High always chose the men He wanted. It is not up to us to choose who is going to be leadership or who will be in this or that position; it is never us. Promotion cometh neither from the east, nor from the west, nor from the south: God is the judge, He putteth down one and setteth up another, and He elected these men as renowned men. Precepts: - Psalms 75:6-7 Promotion cometh neither from the east, nor from the west, nor from the south; God is the judge: he putteth down one, and setteth up another. Numbers 1:17-19 - The congregation declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers. That is the Bible's rule of lineage: the line runs through the father, not the mother. - Those called Jewish today reckon you Jewish by your mother, but that is not what the Bible says. The father plants the seed; the woman is the soil, and the seed planted in the soil grows into the child. The Most High established the pedigrees of the children of Israel by the house of their fathers. Numbers 1:20-43 - Tribe by tribe, by their generations, after their families, by the house of their fathers, every male from twenty years old and upward able to go forth to war was numbered: Reuben 46,500; Simeon 59,300; Gad 45,650; Judah 74,600; Issachar 54,400; Zebulun 57,400; Ephraim 40,500; Manasseh 32,200; Benjamin 35,400; Dan 62,700; Asher 41,500; Naphtali 53,400. - The counting is by scores: a score is twenty, so two score is forty, threescore is sixty, and fourscore is twenty times four, which is eighty. Threescore and two thousand and seven hundred is 62,700. Numbers 1:44-46 - These are those whom Moses and Aaron numbered with the twelve princes of Israel, each one for the house of his fathers: all the men of war from twenty years old and upward came to six hundred thousand and three thousand and five hundred and fifty. - This was the forming of Israel's armies in the wilderness, because the nation was going to have to be prepared to go to war with the nations ahead of them. Numbers 1:47-54 - The Levites were not numbered among the men of war, for the Most High did not have Moses, Aaron, and the twelve princes number them; they were set apart to take care of the sanctuary, to minister unto the Lord and to the people. - The Levites were appointed over the tabernacle of testimony and all its vessels: they bore it, took it down when it set forward, and set it up when it was pitched; and the stranger that came nigh was put to death. - The Levites pitched round about the tabernacle, that there be no wrath upon the congregation of the children of Israel; and the children of Israel did according to all that the Most High commanded Moses. Numbers 2: The Order of the Camps About the Tabernacle Read the chapter → Numbers 2 Numbers 2:1-2 - Every man of the children of Israel pitched by his own standard, with the ensign of his father's house, far off about the tabernacle of the congregation. - This is the picture of the tribes set in their sections around the tabernacle, with the tabernacle in the middle and the pillar of fire coming down by night: the setting of the Lord's army in formation. That is how we are supposed to be set in formation; that is heavy. Numbers 2:3-9 - On the east side toward the rising of the sun pitched the standard of the camp of Judah, with Nahshon the son of Amminadab as captain, and next to him Issachar under Nethaneel the son of Zuar and Zebulun under Eliab the son of Helon. - All that were numbered in the camp of Judah were an hundred thousand and fourscore thousand and six thousand and four hundred, which is 186,400 throughout their armies; and these set forth first. Numbers 2:10-16 - On the south side was the standard of the camp of Reuben, with Elizur the son of Shedeur as captain, and by him Simeon under Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai and Gad under Eliasaph the son of Reuel. - All that were numbered in the camp of Reuben were an hundred thousand and fifty and one thousand and four hundred and fifty, which is 151,450 throughout their armies; and they set forth in the second rank. Numbers 2:17 - Then the tabernacle of the congregation set forward with the camp of the Levites in the midst of the camp: as they encamped, so they set forward, every man in his place by their standards. - The tabernacle stayed in the middle of the formation whether Israel was camped or marching; the order of the camp was the order of the march. Numbers 2:18-24 - On the west side was the standard of the camp of Ephraim, with Elishama the son of Ammihud as captain, and by him Manasseh under Gamaliel the son of Pedahzur and Benjamin under Abidan the son of Gideoni. - All that were numbered of the camp of Ephraim were an hundred thousand and eight thousand and an hundred, which is 108,100 throughout their armies; and they went forward in the third rank. Numbers 2:25-31 - On the north side was the standard of the camp of Dan, with Ahiezer the son of Ammishaddai as captain, and by him Asher under Pagiel the son of Ocran and Naphtali under Ahira the son of Enan. - All that were numbered of the camp of Dan were an hundred thousand and fifty and seven thousand and six hundred, which is 157,600; and they went hindmost with their standards. Numbers 2:32-34 - All those that were numbered of the camps throughout their hosts were six hundred thousand and three thousand and five hundred and fifty; but the Levites were not numbered among the children of Israel, as the Most High commanded Moses. - The children of Israel did according to all that the Most High commanded Moses: so they pitched by their standards, and so they set forward, every one after their families, according to the house of their fathers. --- Topics: The Feasts of the Most High · The Priesthood ← Leviticus 26-27 · Numbers Study · Numbers 3-6 →

title: Numbers 11: Beware of Murmuring
text: ← Numbers 7-10 · Numbers Study · Numbers 15-18 → Numbers 11: Beware of Murmuring Read the chapter → Numbers 11 Introduction This reading session covers Numbers 11 through 14: the fire at Taberah, the lusting for flesh, the seventy elders, and the murmuring of the people in the wilderness.
