These notes were transcribed from the session audio, because the video has no captions. The available transcription ends about thirty minutes in, partway through Numbers 11 at verse 25, so these notes cover the portion of the reading that was captured; Numbers 12 through 14 were read in the remainder of the session but are not in the transcript. Numbers 11:1 - The Most High hates it when His people complain. He had just destroyed Egypt for Israel, its land, its infrastructure, its firstborn, and drowned its army in the sea, all to save the people out; then on the other side of the wilderness, at the first trial or tribulation, the people jumped off His bandwagon, and the same is still being done to this day. - The Lord heard the complaining, and His anger was kindled, and the fire of the Lord burnt among them. Vengeance, when it punisheth, does not pass by him that speaketh unrighteous things; the murmurer receives the vengeance of the Lord. - Nothing spoken behind closed doors is hidden. Inquisition is made into the counsels of the ungodly, by the Lord and His angels, the same council seen when the Lord asked who shall persuade Ahab that he may fall at Ramothgilead; the sound of a man's words comes unto the Lord, for the ear of jealousy heareth all things. - Beware of murmuring and refrain the tongue from backbiting, for there is no word so secret that shall go for nought, and the mouth that belieth, that slandereth a brother, a sister, the leadership, or the Lord, slayeth the soul. - Many speak evil against leadership because they do not like when judgment comes out; a problem with the leadership the Most High set up is a problem with the Most High Himself. Precepts: - Wisdom of Solomon 1:8-11 The ear of jealousy heareth all things; beware of murmuring, for the mouth that belieth slayeth the soul. - 1 Kings 22:20 The Lord holds council with His angels; that is the inquisition made into the counsels of the ungodly. Numbers 11:2-3 - The people cried unto Moses, and when Moses prayed unto the Lord, the fire was quenched; the Most High quenched the fire because Moses prayed on behalf of the children of Israel. - The place was called Taberah, because the fire of the Lord burnt among them. Numbers 11:4-6 - The mixed multitude that fell a lusting were the other nations sprinkled in among Israel, the mixed multitude that went up with the people out of Egypt; the law in Leviticus tells what they were for, to be the bondmen and bondmaids of Israel. - It was not Israel complaining at first; it was the nations lusting after the food of Egypt, and the children of Israel, gullible and assimilated as always, followed right after them and murmured against their God. The same spirit is on the people now: whatever the other nations want to do, our people want to be part of it. - They wept for the fish they ate freely in Egypt, the cucumbers, the melons, the leeks, the onions, and the garlic, right after the Lord destroyed the Egyptians to bring them out of bondage. It is the same today with the entertainments and comforts of this captivity, and some will do the same thing again in the wilderness when the Most High brings the people back out. - They had just seen the Lord consume the complainers in the uttermost parts of the camp, and they went back and did the same thing. We are the same people today; there is nothing new under the sun, and these things were written aforetime for our learning, so we can read them and refuse to do as they did. Precepts: - Exodus 12:38 A mixed multitude of other nations went up with Israel out of Egypt. - Leviticus 25:44-45 The strangers sojourning among Israel were to be their bondmen and bondmaids. - Romans 15:4 Whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning. Numbers 11:7-9 - The manna was as coriander seed, the colour of bdellium; the people gathered it, ground it, baked it in pans, and the taste of it was as the taste of fresh oil. - Read precept upon precept to understand what they despised: manna is angels' food, the food the Lord feeds the angels, sent from heaven prepared without their labour; they only had to pick it up. - The manna was able to content every man's delight and agreed to every taste, tempering itself to every man's liking; whatever the tongue craved that day, the manna tasted like it. To complain about that provision, including the very garlic and onions and melons they wept for, was pure rebellion against the Lord God of heaven and earth. Precepts: - Wisdom of Solomon 16:20-21 Manna was angels' food, agreeing to every taste and tempering itself to every man's liking. Numbers 11:10 - Moses heard the people weep throughout their families, every man in the door of his tent; the anger of the Lord was kindled greatly, and Moses also was displeased. Numbers 11:11-15 - Moses asked the Most High why He had afflicted His servant and laid the burden of all this people on him: have I conceived all this people, that thou shouldest say, Carry them in thy bosom as a nursing father? He was carrying grown people who acted like children. - The people Moses bore are the same people today; this teaching identifies the children of Israel with the so-called Blacks, Hispanics, and Native American Indians, and the sheer rebellion and complaining in these chapters is one of the marks of the people. - Moses said, If thou deal thus with me, kill me, I pray thee, out of hand; he would rather die than bear so rebellious a people alone and look upon his own wretchedness. Numbers 11:16-17 - The Lord told Moses to gather seventy men of the elders of Israel to the tabernacle, and He would take of the spirit upon Moses and put it upon them, that they bear the burden of the people with him. - Leadership works the same way today. The spirit on the head, the willingness to put in work, the humility, the patience, is meant to trickle down to the men below him, and the spirit the lead sisters roll in sets the spirit of the sisters in the congregation. That is why the leaders must be right according to the scriptures, because the Most High takes their spirit and lets it come upon the others. Numbers 11:18-20 - The Lord said, Sanctify yourselves against to morrow, and ye shall eat flesh; ye have wept in the ears of the Lord, saying, It was well with us in Egypt, therefore the Lord will give you flesh. - Not one day, nor two, nor five, nor ten, nor twenty days, but a whole month, until it come out at your nostrils and it be loathsome unto you. He fed them so much of the flesh they begged for that they would grow sick of it and hate it. - The reason for the judgment is stated plainly: because ye have despised the Lord which is among you. They spoke evil of His manna and wept to go back among the oppressors He had just destroyed. Numbers 11:21-23 - Moses inquired how it could be done: the people are six hundred thousand footmen, and that count is not including women and children; there were millions in the wilderness. Shall the flocks and the herds be slain for them, or all the fish of the sea gathered together for them, to suffice them? - The Lord answered, Is the LORD'S hand waxed short? The One who destroyed Egypt asks whether His hand is short; thou shalt see now whether my word shall come to pass unto thee or not. Be patient and watch the word come to pass. Numbers 11:24-25 - Moses gathered the seventy elders round about the tabernacle, and the Lord came down in a cloud and took of the spirit that was upon Moses and gave it unto the seventy elders; and when the spirit rested upon them, they prophesied, and did not cease. - The same thing happened with Elijah and Elisha. Elisha, Elijah's right hand and disciple, asked for a double portion of his master's spirit before Elijah was taken up, and when the sons of the prophets saw Elisha smite Jordan with the mantle, they said, The spirit of Elijah doth rest on Elisha. - It was the same in the time of Christ: the apostles taught like Christ, and men could tell that spirit was on them, just as the elders carried the spirit of Moses. Precepts: - 2 Kings 2:9 Elisha asked for a double portion of Elijah's spirit before his master was taken from him. - 2 Kings 2:15 The sons of the prophets saw it and said, The spirit of Elijah doth rest on Elisha. --- ← Numbers 7-10 · Numbers Study · Numbers 15-18 →

title: Numbers 15: Offerings, Presumptuous Sin, and the Fringes
text: ← Numbers 11-14 · Numbers Study · Numbers 19-22 → Numbers 15: Offerings, Presumptuous Sin, and the Fringes Read the chapter → Numbers 15 Introduction This reading covers Numbers 15 through 18: the offerings to be made in the land and the one law for Israel and the stranger, the difference between sin of ignorance and presumptuous sin with the man that gathered sticks on the sabbath, the rebellion of Korah, Aaron's rod that budded, and the charge and portion of the priests and the Levites. This was a reading session with brief comment on the verses; no questions were raised at the end. Numbers 15:1-3 - When Israel came into the land of their habitations, they were to make an offering by fire unto the Lord: a burnt offering, a sacrifice in performing a vow, a freewill offering, or an offering in the solemn feasts, for a sweet savour unto the Lord. - These are all the accounts on which you would sacrifice to the Lord, taken of the herd or of the flock. Numbers 15:4-10 - Every sacrifice came with its measured meat offering of flour mingled with oil and its drink offering of wine, and the measures scaled up with the animal: a lamb, a ram, and then a bullock. - An hin is roughly a gallon to a gallon and a half, so the bullock, the greatest offering, carried half an hin of oil and half an hin of wine. Numbers 15:11-13 - Thus it was done for one bullock, one ram, one lamb, or a kid; the kid is the goat. Everyone did according to the number they prepared. - All that are born of the country did these things after this manner when offering an offering made by fire of a sweet savour unto the Lord. Numbers 15:14-16 - The scripture separates the two: the children of Israel and the stranger that sojourns with them. If a stranger joined himself to Israel, he had to keep the law to journey with them in the land. - One ordinance and one law stood both for the congregation and for the stranger that was joined with them, an ordinance for ever in their generations: as ye are, so shall the stranger be before the Lord. Numbers 15:17-21 - When Israel ate of the bread of the land, they offered up a cake of the first of their dough as an heave offering unto the Lord, as they did the heave offering of the threshingfloor. - The heave offering was a particular motion in presenting it: the offering was held up to the Most High and brought back down; that is why it was called the heave offering. Numbers 15:22-26 - If the whole congregation sinned through ignorance, without the knowledge of what they were doing, and the priest came behind them and corrected them on it, then all the congregation offered a young bullock for a burnt offering and a kid of the goats for a sin offering. - The priest made an atonement for all the congregation of the children of Israel, and it was forgiven them, for it was ignorance; the stranger among them was included in that forgiveness. Numbers 15:27-29 - If any single soul sinned through ignorance, he brought a she goat of the first year for a sin offering, and the priest made an atonement for him, and it was forgiven him. - One law covered him that sinned through ignorance, both for him born among the children of Israel and for the stranger that sojourned among them. Numbers 15:30-31 - But the soul that doeth ought presumptuously sinned willfully; he thought about what he was doing before he did it. Whether born in the land or a stranger, that soul reproached the Lord and was cut off from among his people. - Because he despised the word of the Lord and broke his commandment, that soul was utterly cut off, meaning put to death, and his iniquity was upon him. Numbers 15:32-36 - The man found gathering sticks on the sabbath day is the example of the presumptuous sin just described: someone who thought about the sin before he did it. He was not picking up sticks just to pick up sticks; he was gathering them to kindle a fire and cook on the sabbath. - They put him in ward, meaning they locked him up, because it was not declared what should be done to him; then the Lord commanded Moses that the man be surely put to death, and all the congregation stoned him with stones without the camp. - He did not even get to the act itself; he had the intention, and for that willful intent he was put to death. Numbers 15:37-41 - Because of that act, the Most High gave Israel the commandment to make fringes in the borders of their garments throughout their generations, and to put upon the fringe of the borders a ribband of blue. - The fringe is to look upon and remember all the commandments of the Lord and do them, and not to seek after your own heart and your own eyes; so that when we think of sin, we look at the fringes and remember the laws of the Most High instead of going and picking up sticks. - I am the Lord your God, which brought you out of the land of Egypt, to be your God. Numbers 16: The Rebellion of Korah Read the chapter → Numbers 16 Numbers 16:1-3 - Korah was of Levi, and Dathan, Abiram, and On were of Reuben. With them rose up two hundred and fifty princes of the assembly, famous in the congregation, men of renown; that is two hundred and fifty three in all against Moses and Aaron. - These were known and powerful men among the congregation, and their influence, because of who they were, is how they were able to persuade people. - They charged Moses and Aaron with taking too much upon themselves and lifting themselves above the congregation. They thought Moses and Aaron carried themselves as better than the rest, but the Most High is the one who chose them as leaders and was dealing with them; the accusers were jealous of them. Numbers 16:4-7 - When Moses heard it, he fell upon his face, and told Korah and all his company: even to morrow the Lord will shew who are his, and who is holy; the Most High himself would show whom he chose and whom he was dealing with. - The test was censers: take you censers, Korah and all his company, put fire therein and incense before the Lord, and the man whom the Lord doth choose, he shall be holy. Ye take too much upon you, ye sons of Levi. Numbers 16:8-11 - Moses exhorted Korah: seemeth it but a small thing that the God of Israel hath separated you from the congregation to bring you near to himself, to do the service of the tabernacle? Only Levi could do the service of the tabernacle, and that was a heavy job in itself. - You already stand before the congregation and minister unto them; the Most High is still dealing with you. But they sought the priesthood also, and for that cause Korah and all his company were gathered together against the Lord: and what is Aaron, that ye murmur against him? Numbers 16:12-14 - Dathan and Abiram would not come up when Moses called them. They were being rebellious against Moses because they wanted his spot, accusing him of bringing them out of a land flowing with milk and honey to kill them in the wilderness and of making himself a prince over them. - Those same spirits are around today; the same thing that went on in the old time goes on now. Numbers 16:15-19 - Moses was very wroth and said unto the Lord, respect not thou their offering: I have not taken one ass from them, neither have I hurt one of them. - Every man took his censer, two hundred and fifty censers, with Aaron and Korah also, put fire and incense in them, and stood in the door of the tabernacle of the congregation; and Korah gathered all the congregation against Moses and Aaron, and the glory of the Lord appeared unto all the congregation. Numbers 16:20-22 - The Lord told Moses and Aaron to separate themselves from among the congregation, that he might consume them in a moment: get away from them, because judgment is about to come. - Moses and Aaron fell upon their faces and pleaded: O God, the God of the spirits of all flesh, shall one man sin, and wilt thou be wroth with all the congregation? They still had that love for their people and pleaded with the Lord not to deal with the whole congregation over one man's sin. Numbers 16:23-27 - The Lord commanded the congregation to get up from about the tabernacle of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram; Moses warned them to depart from the tents of these wicked men and touch nothing of theirs, lest they be consumed in all their sins and put to death in all that wickedness. - The congregation got up from the tabernacle of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram on every side; and Dathan and Abiram came out and stood in the door of their tents with their wives, their sons, and their little children. Numbers 16:28-30 - Moses put the proof on the Most High: hereby ye shall know that the Lord hath sent me to do all these works, for I have not done them of mine own mind. If these men die the common death of all men, then the Lord hath not sent me; if the Most High does not do something out of the ordinary to put them to death, then the Lord had not sent him. - But if the Lord make a new thing, and the earth open her mouth and swallow them up, and they go down quick into the pit, then ye shall understand that these men have provoked the Lord. Numbers 16:31-34 - As he made an end of speaking, the ground clave asunder under them, and the earth opened her mouth and swallowed them up, their houses, all the men that appertained unto Korah, and all their goods; anybody that had something to do with them went down, with all they owned. - The earth just opened and closed upon them, and they perished from among the congregation; all Israel round about fled at the cry of them, for you could hear them crying as they were swallowed up, and they said, lest the earth swallow us up also. Numbers 16:35 - The other two hundred and fifty men that followed them and offered incense did not escape either: there came out a fire from the Lord and consumed them. Numbers 16:36-40 - The Lord told Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest to take up the censers out of the burning, for they are hallowed, and scatter the fire yonder; the censers of these sinners against their own souls were made broad plates for a covering of the altar, because they were offered before the Lord. - The plates were a memorial and a sign unto the children of Israel, that no stranger which is not of the seed of Aaron come near to offer incense before the Lord, that he be not as Korah and as his company. Numbers 16:41-45 - On the morrow, the very next day, all the congregation murmured against Moses and Aaron, saying, ye have killed the people of the Lord. After they had just seen the earth open up and swallow men, they still would not let it go and gathered against Moses again; that is just how rebellious we are. - The Most High saw what was going on, and the cloud covered the tabernacle and the glory of the Lord appeared; Moses and Aaron came before the tabernacle because they knew the Most High was ready to deal with them. - The Lord came down ready to put them to death again, saying get you up from among this congregation, that I may consume them as in a moment; and Moses and Aaron fell upon their faces, still pleading for their people because they loved them so much. Numbers 16:46-48 - Moses told Aaron to take a censer with fire from off the altar and incense, and go quickly unto the congregation and make an atonement for them, for wrath had gone out from the Lord and the plague was begun; the Most High was already putting them to death. - Aaron ran into the midst of the congregation, put on incense, made an atonement for the people, and stood between the dead and the living; and the plague was stayed. Numbers 16:49-50 - They that died in the plague were fourteen thousand and seven hundred, beside them that died about the matter of Korah; so beside the two hundred and fifty three that died with Korah, fourteen thousand seven hundred more were put to death. Numbers 17: Aaron's Rod That Budded Read the chapter → Numbers 17 Numbers 17:1-5 - Every tribe took a rod, a stick or staff, according to the house of their fathers, twelve rods, and the prince of every tribe wrote his name upon his rod; Aaron's name was written upon the rod of Levi. - The rods were laid up in the tabernacle of the congregation before the testimony, the ark of the covenant, where the Lord met with them; the man's rod whom the Lord chose would blossom and grow. - By this the Most High would make the murmurings of the children of Israel to cease from him, showing them that he was dealing with Moses and Aaron and them alone. Numbers 17:6-9 - Every prince gave Moses a rod, one for each according to their fathers' houses, twelve rods, and the rod of Aaron was among them, and Moses laid them up before the Lord in the tabernacle of witness. - On the morrow, the rod of Aaron for the house of Levi was budded, and brought forth buds, and bloomed blossoms, and yielded almonds; and every man took back his own rod. Numbers 17:10-11 - The Lord commanded Aaron's rod to be brought again before the testimony, to be kept for a token against the rebels, to take away their murmurings from the Lord, that they die not; so he would not have to put them to death again for murmuring. - And Moses did as the Lord commanded him. Numbers 17:12-13 - The children of Israel cried, behold, we die, we perish, we all perish: whosoever cometh any thing near unto the tabernacle of the Lord shall die. - You had to be of Levi to go near the tabernacle; that had to be your office. The next chapter explains who was to minister there. Numbers 18: The Charge and Portion of the Priests and Levites Read the chapter → Numbers 18 Numbers 18:1-7 - The Lord told Aaron that he and his sons and his father's house would bear the iniquity of the sanctuary and of their priesthood; that was their job. This explains who should minister in the tabernacle after Israel's cry in the last chapter. - The tribe of Levi was joined unto Aaron to minister unto him and keep the charge of the tabernacle, their jobs; only they were not to come nigh the vessels of the sanctuary and the altar, the ark of the covenant and the different vessels, that neither they nor the priests die. - The Levites were given to Aaron as a gift for the Lord, to do the service of the tabernacle; Aaron and his sons kept the priest's office for every thing of the altar and within the vail. The stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death: an Israelite not of Levi could not come near the tabernacle. Numbers 18:8-11 - The Lord gave Aaron the charge of the heave offerings of all the hallowed things of the children of Israel, by reason of the anointing, to him and his sons by an ordinance for ever. - Of the most holy things reserved from the fire, every oblation, meat offering, sin offering, and trespass offering was most holy for Aaron and his sons; the priests kept a portion of it and ate it in the most holy place. - The heave offering of their gift, with all the wave offerings of the children of Israel, was given to Aaron and his sons and his daughters by a statute for ever; every one that is clean in the house could eat of it. This is what the children of Israel gave for the Levites. Numbers 18:12-14 - All the best of the oil, the best of the wine, and the wheat, the firstfruits which they offered unto the Lord, were given to the priests; whatsoever is first ripe in the land was theirs, and every one that was clean in the house could eat of it. - Every thing devoted in Israel was theirs. Numbers 18:15-17 - Every thing that openeth the matrix in all flesh, whether of men or beasts, was the Lord's; the firstborn was to be offered. Nevertheless the firstborn of man was surely redeemed, because you would not sacrifice the firstborn of our people, and the firstling of unclean beasts was redeemed also. - Verse 16 explains how you redeem them: those to be redeemed from a month old were redeemed for the money of five shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary, which is twenty gerahs; twenty gerahs equal one shekel. - But the firstling of a cow, a sheep, or a goat was not redeemed, because those you could sacrifice: they are holy; their blood was sprinkled upon the altar and their fat burnt for an offering made by fire, for a sweet savour unto the Lord. Numbers 18:18-19 - The flesh of them was the priest's, as the wave breast and as the right shoulder; all the heave offerings of the holy things which the children of Israel offered unto the Lord were given to Aaron and his sons and his daughters by a statute for ever, to the lineage of the Levites. - Exodus 29 shows how the wave offering and the heave offering were done. The wave offering was put in the hands of Aaron and his sons and waved, meaning shaken, before the Lord; then it was received of their hands and burnt upon the altar. Each had a different way it was waved or lifted up to the Most High before it was actually burnt and offered to the Lord, and the breast of the ram of consecration was waved and became the priest's part. - It is a covenant of salt for ever before the Lord, unto Aaron and to his seed with him, the children that come after them. Precepts: - Exodus 29:24-28 The wave offering was waved in the hands of Aaron and his sons before the Lord and then burnt on the altar, and the wave breast and heave shoulder were the priests' part from the children of Israel for ever. Numbers 18:20-24 - The Lord told Aaron: thou shalt have no inheritance in their land, neither any part among them; I am thy part and thine inheritance among the children of Israel. The Levites had no inheritance of land to pass down; the Most High said, I will be taking care of you. - The Lord gave the children of Levi all the tenth in Israel for an inheritance. This is the tithe: the tenth part was given to the Levites for their service which they served, the service of the tabernacle of the congregation, their sacrificing and teaching of the laws. - That tenth went to the children of Levi, and it was done away with when Christ came and died and took that priesthood; we no longer give that tenth to Levi. - The children of Israel were not to come nigh the tabernacle of the congregation, lest they bear sin and die; it was a sin for the other tribes of Israel to come near the tabernacle, on pain of death. All the work to be done in the tabernacle was committed unto the Levites, and they bore their iniquity, a statute for ever. Numbers 18:25-32 - When the Levites took of the children of Israel the tithes given them for their inheritance, they offered up of it an heave offering for the Lord, even a tenth part of the tithe: after the Levites got their tenth, the Most High wanted his tenth part of that, which they had to offer up. - Their heave offering was reckoned unto them as though it were the corn of the threshingfloor and the fulness of the winepress, and the Lord's heave offering out of all their tithes was given to Aaron the priest; out of all their gifts they offered every heave offering of the Lord, of all the best thereof, even the hallowed part. - When they had heaved the best thereof from it, they could eat it in every place, they and their households, for it was their reward for their service in the tabernacle of the congregation; and they bore no sin by reason of it when they heaved the best of it, neither polluted the holy things of the children of Israel, lest they die. --- Topics: Clean and Unclean Meats · Sacrifice and Atonement · The Covenant · The Feasts of the Most High · The Priesthood · The Sabbath ← Numbers 11-14 · Numbers Study · Numbers 19-22 →

title: Numbers 19: The Water of Separation
text: ← Numbers 15-18 · Numbers Study · Numbers 23-26 → Numbers 19: The Water of Separation Read the chapter → Numbers 19 Introduction This reading covers Numbers 19 through 21: the water of separation made with the ashes of the red heifer, the strife at the water of Meribah, Edom refusing Israel passage, the death of Aaron, the fiery serpents and the serpent of brass lifted up on a pole, and Israel's journeys toward the border of Moab. The recording opens at Numbers 19:10 and cuts off during Numbers 21:18, so the earlier verses of chapter 19, the rest of chapter 21, and all of Numbers 22 were read without exposition captured in this session; only the taught portions are included here. Numbers 19:10 - After the priest burns the red heifer and sprinkles her blood, one that is clean gathers up her ashes; even that clean man must wash his clothes and be unclean until the evening. - This is a statute for ever, unto the children of Israel and unto the stranger that sojourneth among them. Numbers 19:11 - Any man that touches the dead body of any man is unclean seven days. There is history on this law: in Numbers 9 certain men were defiled by a dead body around the passover and could not keep it on that day because of this very statute. - The Most High answered through Moses with a second keeping: the man unclean by reason of a dead body, or far off on a journey, keeps the passover the fourteenth day of the second month at even, eating it with unleavened bread and bitter herbs. Precepts: - Numbers 9:6-7 Certain men defiled by the dead body of a man could not keep the passover that day; they asked Moses wherefore they were kept back. - Numbers 9:10-11 The unclean by a dead body or far off on a journey keep the passover the fourteenth day of the second month with unleavened bread and bitter herbs. Numbers 19:12-13 - The unclean man purifies himself with the water of separation on the third day and on the seventh day, and then he is clean; if he purifies not himself the third day, then the seventh day he shall not be clean. - Whoever touches the dead and purifies not himself defiles the tabernacle of the Most High, and that soul is cut off from Israel, because the water of separation was not sprinkled upon him; his uncleanness is yet upon him. Numbers 19:14-22 - This is the law when a man dies in a tent: all that come into the tent and all that is in the tent are unclean seven days, and every open vessel with no covering bound upon it is unclean. - For the unclean person they take of the ashes of the burnt heifer of purification for sin, with running water in a vessel; a clean person dips hyssop in the water and sprinkles the tent, the vessels, and the persons on the third day and on the seventh day, and on the seventh day he washes his clothes, bathes in water, and is clean at even. - The man that stays unclean and will not purify himself is cut off from among the congregation, because he has defiled the sanctuary of the Lord. - Chapter 19 as a whole gives the water of separation, which is the purification for sin: the first half gives the specifics of the sacrifice and what the priest must do, and the rest gives the examples of how a man becomes unclean, whether by sin, by touching the dead, or by being around the dead. Numbers 20: Strife at Meribah and Edom's Refusal Read the chapter → Numbers 20 Numbers 20:1 - The whole congregation came into the desert of Zin in the first month and abode in Kadesh, and Miriam died there and was buried there. Numbers 20:2-5 - There was no water for the congregation, and the people gathered together against Moses and against Aaron; this is another account of Israel coming against them. - When it says the people chode with Moses, they raised their voices; it was loud, angry, a shouting argument: would God that we had died when our brethren died; why have ye brought us into this evil place with no seed, figs, vines, pomegranates, or water to drink. - This is us, the blacks and Hispanics. We were taken out of Egypt by the hand of the Most High, headed to the promised land, and we forgot so quickly how we were brought out; anything out of the ordinary, we complained about it. That constant complaining is one of the marks that this book is speaking of this people. - Moses had to deal with all twelve tribes at once, twelve personalities and twelve attitudes; give that brother all the honor he deserves. Numbers 20:6-11 - Moses and Aaron fell upon their faces at the door of the tabernacle, and the glory of the Lord appeared. The command was to take the rod and speak unto the rock before their eyes, and it would give forth his water for the congregation and their beasts. - At this point Moses got out of the spirit; a stomach can only take so much of a rebellious people. He said, Hear now, ye rebels; must we fetch you water out of this rock? That we is how you know Moses was off: he forgot who was giving the water. It was the Lord giving it, not Moses and not Aaron. - Moses lifted up his hand and smote the rock twice with his rod, and the water still came out abundantly, and the congregation drank, and their beasts also. Numbers 20:12-13 - Because ye believed me not, to sanctify me in the eyes of the children of Israel: for this Moses and Aaron would not bring the congregation into the land given them. - This is the water of Meribah, which means strife, because the children of Israel strove with the Lord, and he was sanctified in them. Numbers 20:14-17 - Moses sent messengers to the king of Edom, saying, Thus saith thy brother Israel. Israel rehearsed the travail: our fathers went down into Egypt, the Egyptians vexed us, we cried unto the Lord and he heard our voice and sent an angel and brought us forth. - Edom is identified in this teaching with the people called the white man today, the Caucasians. This is Israel pleading with the brother nation: not sneaking in, not hiding, not touching the fields, the vineyards, or the water of the wells; only the king's highway, turning neither to the right hand nor to the left, until past the borders, to reach the promised land. Numbers 20:18-21 - Edom answered, Thou shalt not pass by me, lest I come out against thee with the sword. Israel stayed humble: we will go by the highway, and if I and my cattle drink of thy water, then I will pay for it; I will only go through on my feet. - Edom still refused and came out against Israel with much people and with a strong hand, and Israel turned away from him. - Why so harsh against a people asking only to pass through? That hatred stands from something: Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing wherewith his father blessed him, and purposed in his heart to slay his brother. Genesis 25 through 27 is the start of the two nations, and Israel was given the birthright and the kingdom while Esau was rejected. - The hatred is perpetual, everlasting, never ending. The forefather's hatred showed in Numbers 20 and it shows to this day in the nation of Edom still rejecting Israel; it will not stop until Christ stops it, and Israel's part is to repent and come back to the lost statutes and commandments. Precepts: - Genesis 27:41 Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing and said in his heart, then will I slay my brother Jacob; the refusal in Numbers 20 goes back to this. - Ezekiel 35:5 Thou hast had a perpetual hatred, and hast shed the blood of the children of Israel; perpetual means everlasting, never ending. Numbers 20:22-29 - At mount Hor, by the coast of the land of Edom, the Lord said Aaron shall be gathered unto his people; he could not enter the land because of the rebellion at the water of Meribah. - Moses stripped Aaron of his garments and put them upon Eleazar his son; the priesthood passed to Eleazar, and Aaron died there in the top of the mount. - When all the congregation saw that Aaron was dead, all the house of Israel mourned for Aaron thirty days. Numbers 21: The Fiery Serpents and the Serpent of Brass Read the chapter → Numbers 21 Numbers 21:1-3 - King Arad the Canaanite, which dwelt in the south, fought against Israel and took some of them prisoners. Israel vowed a vow unto the Lord, and the Lord hearkened and delivered up the Canaanites, and Israel utterly destroyed them and their cities. - The Canaanites are identified in this teaching with the people called Africans today. The place was called Hormah, which means utter destruction, because that is exactly what Israel did to them there. Numbers 21:4-5 - They journeyed from mount Hor by the way of the Red Sea to compass the land of Edom, and the soul of the people was much discouraged because of the way: since Edom refused passage, Israel had to go around, and the way was longer than they wanted it to be. - The people spake against God and against Moses: no bread, no water, and our soul loatheth this light bread. The bread they were loathing was angels' bread, and they complained about it anyway. - No other nation on this earth takes food as seriously as Israel; even the complaints over bread and water are a familiar mark of this people to this day. You cannot put another nation in these scriptures. Numbers 21:6-9 - The Lord sent fiery serpents among the people, and they bit the people, and much people of Israel died. Read it with the nation in view: the people being bitten, the people dying, all of it is Israel. - Once the serpents started biting and much people died, the people came back into the spirit: we have sinned, for we have spoken against the Lord and against thee; pray unto the Lord that he take away the serpents from us. And Moses prayed for the people. - Moses made a serpent of brass and set it upon a pole, and it came to pass that if a serpent had bitten any man, when he beheld the serpent of brass, he lived. The symbol on ambulances today, a snake wrapped around a pole, comes from this scripture. - That brass serpent on the pole was for the Israelites, to heal the Israelites, because it was the Israelites being bitten for rebelling against God and against Moses. - Christ brought this same passage to Nicodemus. Nicodemus was a Pharisee, a ruler of the Jews, and he came to Christ, who is also a Jew: two Israelites speaking together about the history of Israel. - As Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness to save Israel from death, even so must the Son of man be lifted up: the same way Israel beheld the serpent and did not perish, whosoever believes on Christ shall not perish but have eternal life. And the whosoever is defined in Acts: whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be saved; ye men of Israel, hear these words. The salvation spoken of is for Israel. Precepts: - John 3:1-2 Nicodemus, a Pharisee, a ruler of the Jews, came to Christ by night; an Israelite came to an Israelite. - John 3:14-15 As Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish. - Acts 2:21-22 Whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be saved; ye men of Israel, hear these words. The whosoever is spoken to Israel. Numbers 21:10-15 - The children of Israel set forward and pitched in Oboth, then in Ijeabarim, in the wilderness before Moab toward the sunrising, then in the valley of Zared, then on the other side of Arnon, which is the border of Moab, between Moab and the Amorites. - Now Israel comes among the Moabites and the Ammonites, identified in this teaching with the nations called the Chinese and the Japanese today. - It is said in the book of the wars of the Lord what he did in the Red Sea and in the brooks of Arnon. Numbers 21:16-18 - From thence they went to Beer: that is the well whereof the Lord spake unto Moses, Gather the people together, and I will give them water. - Then Israel sang this song: Spring up, O well. The princes digged the well, the nobles of the people digged it, by the direction of the lawgiver. The recording ends here, during this passage. --- Topics: Clean and Unclean Meats · Esau and Edom · Sacrifice and Atonement · The Feasts of the Most High · The Priesthood · The Sabbath ← Numbers 15-18 · Numbers Study · Numbers 23-26 →

title: Numbers 23: How Shall I Curse, Whom God Hath Not Cursed?
text: ← Numbers 19-22 · Numbers Study · Numbers 27-30 → Numbers 23: How Shall I Curse, Whom God Hath Not Cursed? Read the chapter → Numbers 23 Introduction This reading covers Numbers 23 through 26: Balaam's parables that bless Israel instead of cursing her, the star and sceptre prophecy of the latter days, Israel joined unto Baal-peor and the zeal of Phinehas, and the second census of the families of Israel in the plains of Moab. This is a reading session, with the chapters read straight through and teaching given along the way. Numbers 23:1-2 - Sacrificing animals was not solely a thing pertaining to Israel; sacrificing for sin is what pertained to Israel. All the ancient nations of old sacrificed animals when they worshipped their gods, so Balak and Balaam offering bullocks and rams on altars was nothing new to them. - Offering animals on altars had been done since the time of Adam. It was commonplace in that time, so do not be confused at why Balaam keeps calling for altars and offerings through this chapter. Numbers 23:7-8 - Balak the king of Moab brought Balaam from Aram to curse Jacob and defy Israel, and Balaam could not do it: how shall I curse, whom God hath not cursed? - Understand this: we are a blessed people, but we are living under the curses of God for our disobedience. We are the sons and daughters of God, above all nations, yet on the bottom for our sin, and we remain there until we repent as a nation. Numbers 23:9-10 - The people shall dwell alone and shall not be reckoned among the nations; who can count the dust of Jacob? Israel is as the sand of the sea. - Let me die the death of the righteous, and let my last end be like his. The last end of Israel is a crown of glory in the hand of the Lord: the land married, double for our shame, everlasting joy, and a seed acknowledged among the Gentiles as the seed which the Lord hath blessed. That is why we cannot wait for those days. Precepts: - Hosea 1:10 The number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea; that is the dust of Jacob no man can count. - Isaiah 62:3-5 Israel's last end is a crown of glory and a royal diadem, the land no more termed forsaken but married, and the Most High rejoicing over her as a bridegroom over the bride. - Isaiah 61:7-9 For your shame ye shall have double, an everlasting covenant, and a seed known among the Gentiles as the seed which the Lord hath blessed. Numbers 23:11-12 - Balak charged Balaam with blessing his enemies altogether, and Balaam answered: must I not take heed to speak that which the Lord hath put in my mouth? - That is the same charge given to Ezekiel, and it is what every man must do who speaks on behalf of the Most High, especially the brothers: go unto the house of Israel and speak with His words unto them. - The house of Israel is impudent and hardhearted, so the Lord makes the face and forehead strong, meaning the mind: whatever excuse the people raise, He gives an answer through the scriptures on the spot. The rebellious spirits on our people are only cast down by the word of God, which is why we speak what the Lord puts in our mouth. Precepts: - Ezekiel 3:4 Go, get thee unto the house of Israel, and speak with my words unto them. - Ezekiel 3:7-9 The house of Israel is impudent and hardhearted, but the Lord makes thy face strong against their faces; fear them not, though they be a rebellious house. Numbers 23:19 - God is not a man, that he should lie. Whatever the Lord speaks out of His mouth, once the judgment is passed there is no taking it back, whether in this life or the one to come. - The parable of Lazarus shows it: between us and you there is a great gulf fixed, so that none can pass. The judgment has been set and there is no changing it. - In the day of doom no man shall be able to save him that is destroyed. This present life is not the end, and asking the righteous to pray for those that outright despise God and His laws is praying for the weak; Esdras tried that with the Most High and was told to concern himself with the righteous. - That is what we doubted back in Deuteronomy when Moses read the curses over us; we thought the Lord would not make good on His word. But the Lord is longsuffering and patient and will in no wise acquit the wicked; we will not escape our sins. Precepts: - Luke 16:25-26 Between us and you there is a great gulf fixed; once judgment is passed there is no crossing it, because God is not a man that he should lie. - 2 Esdras 7:42-45 In the day of doom no man shall be able to save him that is destroyed; the sentence stands for ever. Numbers 23:20-21 - He hath received commandment to bless, and it cannot be reversed: he hath not beheld iniquity in Jacob, neither seen perverseness in Israel. Israel had done wickedly since Egypt, and princes rose up to overthrow Moses, but the Lord forgave us over and over again. - No nation could pull up before God and demand He do away with His people. In His eyes Israel was good compared to the accusers; the shout of a King is among them. Numbers 23:22-23 - God brought them out of Egypt; he hath as it were the strength of an unicorn. The unicorn in biblical times is the rhinoceros, the beast with the one great horn on the front. - Surely there is no enchantment against Jacob, neither is there any divination against Israel. For Levi and all the tribes, that voodoo stuff is nothing: once you repent, there is no hex, divination, or curse of bad luck anyone can put on you. Do not even worry about it. Numbers 23:24 - Behold, the people shall rise up as a great lion, and he shall not lie down until he eat of the prey and drink the blood of the slain: Israel shall destroy his enemies. Deuteronomy carries that same promise, and Genesis 49 touches it as well in the blessings of the tribes. Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days Read the chapter → Numbers 24 Numbers 24:1-2 - When Balaam saw that it pleased the Lord to bless Israel, he went not to seek enchantments, and the spirit of God came upon him. Do not be confused at the spirit of God coming on a man of another nation: all the spirits belong to the Most High, and He can do what He wants with any of them. - That does not make the other nations prophets. Prophets are raised up of the sons of Israel; the Lord used Balaam for one specific purpose, to show the nations there is nothing they can do against Israel when the Lord is on our side, and to have Moses write it down in a book. Precepts: - Amos 2:11 I raised up of your sons for prophets; the prophets come out of the children of Israel, not the nations. Numbers 24:3-4 - Balaam heard the words of God and saw the vision of the Almighty, falling into a trance, but having his eyes open. Picture a man staring off as if daydreaming: he is seeing visions with his eyes open while the Lord gives him what to say to the nations that are trying to do evil to Israel. Numbers 24:5-7 - He shall pour the water out of his buckets, and his seed shall be in many waters. The water is the word: Christ sanctifies and cleanses the church with the washing of water by the word, and a young man cleanses his way by taking heed thereto according to the word. That is how you cleanse your spirit. - His seed shall be in many waters means Israel scattered all over the earth, and his kingdom shall be exalted higher than Agag. Precepts: - Ephesians 5:26 Sanctified and cleansed with the washing of water by the word; the water is the word. - Psalms 119:9 Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? By taking heed thereto according to thy word. Numbers 24:8-9 - God brought him forth out of Egypt with as it were the strength of an unicorn; he shall eat up the nations his enemies, break their bones, and pierce them through with his arrows. That is the destruction coming on Israel's enemies when we rise back up. - He couched, he lay down as a great lion, and who shall stir him up? Blessed is he that blesseth thee, and cursed is he that curseth thee. Balaam is speaking the very prophecies and promises that belong to Israel throughout the scriptures. Numbers 24:10-11 - Balak's anger was kindled and he smote his hands together: I thought to promote thee unto great honour, but lo, the Lord hath kept thee back from honour. That was Satan speaking through Balak, trying to entice Balaam with honor to curse Israel. - Satan promotes with honor, riches, prestige, and lust; that is the deceitfulness of riches and the lust of other things that choke the word. When the word is sown, Satan comes immediately to take it away, using whatever device fits where you are. - He tried the same device on Christ, offering all the power and the glory of the kingdoms in exchange for worship, and Christ answered, Get thee behind me, Satan. Satan is an old spirit using the same tricks from the beginning of time. - We are not to be ignorant of his devices, lest he get an advantage of us. Many are falling to those devices at home in this quarantine, letting the old man rise back up; resist the devil and he will flee, but give in and he will use you until he destroys you. Precepts: - Mark 4:18-19 The cares of this world, the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things choke the word; those are the promotions Satan offers. - Mark 4:15 When they have heard, Satan cometh immediately and taketh away the word that was sown in their hearts. - Luke 4:6-8 The devil offered Christ all the power and glory of the kingdoms for worship; the same spirit offered Balaam honor through Balak. - 2 Corinthians 2:11 Lest Satan should get an advantage of us: for we are not ignorant of his devices. Numbers 24:12-13 - Balaam answered: if Balak would give me his house full of silver and gold, I cannot go beyond the commandment of the Lord, to do either good or bad of mine own mind; but what the Lord saith, that will I speak. Numbers 24:14 - Behold, I go unto my people: Balaam's people were the Midianites, for Israel later slew Balaam with the sword beside the five kings of Midian. - I will advertise thee what this people shall do to thy people in the latter days. The latter days are the last days, and the last days began when Christ came on the earth, was crucified, and resurrected: God, who spake in time past unto the fathers by the prophets, hath in these last days spoken unto us by His Son. - A thousand years is as a day to the Lord, and a day as a thousand years; as Hosea says, after two days He will revive us, and in the third day He will raise us up. The full teaching of that timing belongs to another class. Precepts: - Numbers 31:8 Balaam the son of Beor was slain with the sword beside the five kings of Midian; the Midianites were his people. - Hebrews 1:1-2 God hath in these last days spoken unto us by his Son; the last days began at Christ. - 2 Peter 3:8 One day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day. - Hosea 6:1-2 He hath torn, and he will heal us; after two days will he revive us, and in the third day raise us up. Numbers 24:17 - I shall see him, but not now: I shall behold him, but not nigh. Balaam is saying the Most High will raise him up again in the last days, but as a servant, far off from the King; he will behold him, but he will not be near him. - Compare that with Job, and the contrast shows Job was an Israelite and not of another nation: Job knew that his redeemer liveth, that in his flesh he shall see God, whom he shall see for himself and his eyes shall behold, and not another. Balaam has no such nearness, because the redeemer is not his. - There shall come a Star out of Jacob: the Star is Christ, the root and offspring of David, the bright and morning star. And a Sceptre shall rise out of Israel: the sceptre belongs to kings, so the prophecy is that the King shall rise out of Israel. Precepts: - Job 19:25-27 Job shall see his redeemer for himself and his eyes shall behold him; Balaam shall behold him, but not nigh. - Revelation 22:16 I am the root and the offspring of David, and the bright and morning star; the Star out of Jacob is Christ. - Wisdom of Solomon 6:1-2 The word to them that hold thrones is addressed to kings; the sceptre speaks of a king. - Wisdom of Solomon 6:21 Thrones and sceptres belong to kings; the Sceptre rising out of Israel is Christ the King. - And shall smite the corners of Moab, and destroy all the children of Sheth. Balaam is prophesying of the latter days: this teaching identifies Moab with the Chinese and Ammon with the Japanese, and Sheth goes into the Egyptian. Asia is partaker of the hope of Babylon, going through the earth buying up land, trying to become financially what America already is and to deal with all nations as she has. - The judgment on her is written: plagues, widowhood, poverty, famine, sword, and pestilence, and the glory of her power dried up as a flower when the heat arises that is sent over her. Moab shall be as Sodom and the children of Ammon as Gomorrah, the breeding of nettles and salt pits; the stinging nettle is a plant that burns, and the fire that fell on Sodom is coming again. - The residue of the Most High's people, the third that is left, shall spoil them, and the remnant shall possess them; this shall they have for their pride against the people of the Lord of hosts. - The Lord will be terrible unto them and famish all the gods of the earth, and men shall worship Him every one from his place, even all the isles of the heathen. That is why Balaam said he shall behold Him, but not nigh: the nations will worship from their own place and come up only at the appointed times of the year. Precepts: - 2 Esdras 15:46-50 Asia has made herself like Babylon, which is America; her plagues come, and her glory dries up as a flower when the heat arises. - 2 Esdras 16:1 Woe unto Babylon, Asia, Egypt, and Syria; destruction is coming on them all. - Zephaniah 2:8-11 For the reproach of Moab and the revilings of Ammon, Moab shall be as Sodom and Ammon as Gomorrah, the remnant of the Most High's people shall possess them, and men shall worship the Lord every one from his place. Numbers 24:18-19 - And Edom shall be a possession. Edom is nowhere named in the matter of Balak and Balaam in these chapters, but the Lord made sure Edom was written into the prophecy: Seir also shall be a possession for his enemies, and Israel shall do valiantly. The law of bondmen shows what a possession is: the heathen round about are bought for an inheritance, bondmen for ever, though over our own brethren we do not rule with rigour. - For Esau that servitude is not for ever, because Esau is the only nation on the earth with an expiration date. The house of Jacob, the twelve tribes of Israel, the blacks, Hispanics, and Native Indians, shall be a fire, the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for stubble; there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau, for the Lord hath spoken it. The rest of the nations go into servitude for ever, but the Lord can only bear with Esau so much longer. - Out of Jacob shall come he that shall have dominion: that is the one who cometh from Edom with dyed garments from Bozrah, glorious in his apparel, traveling in the greatness of his strength, which is the whole host of heaven, thousands upon thousands of angels. The day of vengeance is in his heart, for though Israel serves out her punishment in captivity, Esau went overboard and kept laying on punishment when our iniquity had an end. Precepts: - Leviticus 25:44-46 The heathen round about are bought for bondmen and taken for a possession for ever; that is what Edom becomes to Israel. - Obadiah 1:18 The house of Jacob shall be a fire, the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for stubble; there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau. - Isaiah 63:1-4 He that cometh from Edom with dyed garments from Bozrah treads the winepress in his fury, for the day of vengeance is in his heart and the year of his redeemed is come. Numbers 24:20 - Amalek was the first of the nations. That means Amalek was the first of the nations to come out and fight against Israel, when he met us at Rephidim as we came out of Egypt. - The Lord swore to utterly put out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven, and that the Lord would have war with Amalek from generation to generation. This teaching identifies Amalek, the seed of Esau through Eliphaz, with the people who call themselves Jewish in the land of Israel today: the war that has never left that land since they entered it is the war the Lord swore, and the prophecy that none shall remain of the house of Esau belongs to no other nation. - His latter end shall be that he perish for ever; precept upon precept, the scriptures show who Amalek is and what his end is. Precepts: - Exodus 17:8 Then came Amalek, and fought with Israel in Rephidim; that is why Amalek is called the first of the nations. - Exodus 17:14-16 The remembrance of Amalek shall be utterly put out from under heaven, for the Lord hath sworn to have war with Amalek from generation to generation. Numbers 24:21-22 - The Kenite's dwelling place was strong, his nest put in a rock; nevertheless the Kenite shall be wasted and go into captivity, until Asshur, which is the Assyrians, shall carry him away captive. Numbers 24:23-25 - Alas, who shall live when God doeth this! Ships shall come from the coast of Chittim, and Chittim is Italy; they shall afflict Asshur and afflict Eber, and he also shall perish for ever. Eber here is not speaking of Israel, for other peoples besides us came out of Eber, who is of Shem; the history of prophecy opens this up as the prophets are read. - And Balaam rose up and returned to his place, and Balak also went his way; they parted. Numbers 25: Baal-peor and the Zeal of Phinehas Read the chapter → Numbers 25 Numbers 25:1-3 - Israel abode in Shittim, and the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab. Why? Balaam could not curse us, because God said you cannot curse what is blessed; so his counsel was the best the enemy can ever do: throw another god in front of Israel and send the women, and let Israel bring the trespass on himself. That counsel is why the Lord put Balaam to death. - They called the people unto the sacrifices of their gods, and the people did eat and bowed down; Israel joined himself unto Baal-peor, and the anger of the Lord was kindled. The worship of Baal-peor went into whoredom, that orgy worship: we started worshipping another god and messing with the women together. Precepts: - Numbers 31:15-16 These caused the children of Israel, through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass against the Lord in the matter of Peor. Numbers 25:4-5 - The Lord said, take all the heads of the people and hang them up before the Lord against the sun, that His fierce anger be turned away; and Moses said unto the judges, slay ye every one his man that were joined unto Baal-peor. Every one his man means every judge by his rank: the officer over ten took ten, the officer over fifty took fifty, and so on. With the Most High it is two options only, life and death. - Under the old covenant there was no winking at ignorance; judgment was instant. The only reason we are not judged that way now for the gods we served is the grace and mercy given through Christ: the times of this ignorance God winked at, the Christianity with the white Jesus, the Islam, the Buddhism, the Hinduism, the Egyptology, the atheism; but now He commandeth all men every where to repent, because He hath appointed a day in which He will judge the world in righteousness by that man whom He hath ordained, Jesus the Christ. - Do not take that mercy lightly, and do not frustrate the grace of God until He is finished with you. He can cut a man's days down whenever He wants; do not press Him to it. Precepts: - Acts 17:29-31 The times of this ignorance God winked at, but now commandeth all men every where to repent, for He hath appointed a day of judgment by Christ. Numbers 25:6-9 - While the whole congregation wept before the door of the tabernacle, one of the children of Israel brought a Midianitish woman unto his brethren in the sight of Moses and all the congregation: a man that did not care about his people while everyone around him mourned. - When Phinehas the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, saw it, he rose up from among the congregation, took a javelin in his hand, went after the man of Israel into the tent, and thrust both of them through; so the plague was stayed from the children of Israel, and those that died in the plague were twenty and four thousand. - Let us now praise famous men: Phinehas stands third in glory, because he had zeal in the fear of the Lord and stood up with good courage of heart when the people were turned back, and made reconciliation for Israel; therefore a covenant of peace was made with him, that he and his posterity should have the dignity of the priesthood for ever. - These things were our examples, that we should not lust after evil things as they lusted. The people sat down to eat and drink and rose up to play, and that play means sex; that was the golden calf. Neither commit fornication as they did, when three and twenty thousand fell in one day; neither tempt Christ, for it was Christ with us in the wilderness. These things are written for our admonition, that we be warned: idolatry leads to whoredom, spiritual whoredom against the Most High and physical whoredom with it. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 44:1 The register of famous men opens the record in which Phinehas is honored. - Ecclesiasticus 45:23-24 Phinehas is third in glory for his zeal, and the covenant of peace and everlasting priesthood was his reward. - 1 Corinthians 10:6-11 These things happened unto them for ensamples and are written for our admonition; do not be idolaters, fornicators, or tempters of Christ as they were. Numbers 25:10-13 - Phinehas turned the wrath of the Most High away from the children of Israel, because he was zealous for his God's sake among them; wherefore the Lord gave him His covenant of peace, and to his seed after him the covenant of an everlasting priesthood, because he made an atonement for the children of Israel. - That covenant of peace is what all of us are striving for, rest from this servitude of bondage; but the wisdom in reading the acts of Phinehas is that you must be zealous for the law of the Most High to obtain it. Be ye zealous for the law, and give your lives for the covenant of your fathers; Phinehas our father, in being zealous and fervent, obtained the covenant of an everlasting priesthood. - Being zealous today is confessing Christ before men, and you confess him mainly through your actions. Christ suffered for us, leaving us an example that we should follow his steps, and his steps were keeping the commandments of God; the first way you deny Christ is by rejecting the commandments. - Christ came not to send peace on earth but a sword, setting a man at variance against his own household; he that loveth father or mother more than him is not worthy of him. We stay zealous by letting nothing separate us from following Christ in his steps: keeping the laws of God, teaching the gospel, and spreading the word with wisdom. Precepts: - 1 Peter 2:21 Christ left us an example that we should follow his steps; the steps are commandment keeping. - Matthew 10:32-33 Whosoever shall confess Christ before men, him will he confess before his Father; whosoever shall deny him, him will he also deny. - Matthew 10:34-37 Christ came not to send peace but a sword; he that loveth father or mother more than him is not worthy of him. - 1 Maccabees 2:50 Be zealous for the law and give your lives for the covenant of your fathers. - 1 Maccabees 2:54 Phinehas obtained the everlasting priesthood by being zealous and fervent. Numbers 25:14-18 - The man of Israel that was slain was Zimri the son of Salu, a prince of a chief house among the Simeonites; the woman was Cozbi the daughter of Zur, head over a people of a chief house in Midian. The charge stands to Simeon to get it together; Simeon is coming back with the rest of the tribes. - The Lord said unto Moses, vex the Midianites and smite them, for they vex you with their wiles, wherewith they have beguiled you in the matter of Peor and in the matter of Cozbi. Numbers 26: The Second Census of the Families of Israel Read the chapter → Numbers 26 Numbers 26:1-2 - After the plague the Lord commanded a new numbering of the congregation, from twenty years old and upward, all that are able to go to war in Israel. Twenty is the biblical age of a man: Israel sent men to war, not children, so the numbering of them able for war fixes the age of manhood at twenty years old. Numbers 26:5-7 - Of Hanoch, the family of the Hanochites; of Pallu, the family of the Palluites. The ending ites means the descendants of, the people you belong to: Israelites are the descendants of Israel, Edomites the descendants of Edom, and so it goes all down the line through the scriptures. - Reading these family names aloud loosens the tongue to say the names of the scriptures fluently and without hesitation. 1 Chronicles 1 serves the same practice, and it carries the names of Israel's families together with Edom and Ishmael, the nations that come out of Abraham's line. Precepts: - Isaiah 44:5 One shall call himself by the name of Jacob, and another surname himself by the name of Israel; the name tells whose people you are. Numbers 26:9-11 - Dathan and Abiram were famous in the congregation, who strove against Moses and against Aaron in the company of Korah, when they strove against the Lord; the account is back in Numbers 16. The earth opened her mouth and swallowed them up together with Korah, the fire devoured two hundred and fifty men, and they became a sign. - Notwithstanding, the children of Korah died not. Numbers 26:19-22 - Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan, and the families of Judah continued through Shelah, Pharez, and Zerah, threescore and sixteen thousand and five hundred numbered. - Do not hear Pharez and think the Pharisees came from the Pharzites; the Pharisees did not come out of that family. The rise of those sects is read of in the books of the Maccabees. Numbers 26:51-56 - The numbered of the children of Israel were six hundred thousand and a thousand seven hundred and thirty. Unto these the land shall be divided for an inheritance according to the number of names: to many the more inheritance, to few the less, and the land divided by lot according to the tribes of their fathers. - Land is how wealth is built, and Esau knows how important land is; that is why the land is kept in his generations and why Gad, the Native Indian, was never given one square inch of his land back, only the casinos and the little plots called reservations. Israel is getting the most fertile land back; as for this land here, let it burn. Numbers 26:59-61 - Jochebed the daughter of Levi bare unto Amram Aaron and Moses and Miriam their sister; and unto Aaron were born Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar. - Nadab and Abihu died when they offered strange fire before the Lord; go back and read that account. Precepts: - Leviticus 10:1-2 Nadab and Abihu offered strange fire before the Lord, which he commanded them not, and fire from the Lord devoured them. Numbers 26:63-65 - Among these numbered by Moses and Eleazar in the plains of Moab there was not a man of them that was numbered in the wilderness of Sinai, for the Lord had said of them, they shall surely die in the wilderness; and there was not left a man of them, save Caleb the son of Jephunneh and Joshua the son of Nun. - Why Caleb and Joshua? They had another spirit on them and did not doubt when the Lord sent them to spy out the land. My servant Caleb, because he had another spirit with him and hath followed me fully, him will I bring into the land; he let nobody keep him from serving the Most High. - Christ said the same thing: he that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me. If the Lord finds you lukewarm, choosing your kids, your parents, or your spouse over following God and Christ and keeping the commandments wholly, you will not enter into the land; you must follow fully like Caleb and zealously like Phinehas. - Let that be a lesson learned, for whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope. Precepts: - Numbers 14:23-24 None that provoked the Lord shall see the land, but Caleb, because he had another spirit with him and followed the Lord fully, shall possess it. - Matthew 10:37 He that loveth father or mother more than Christ is not worthy of him; nothing may keep you from following fully. - Romans 15:4 Things written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope. --- Topics: Esau and Edom · Idolatry · Sacrifice and Atonement · The Covenant · The Feasts of the Most High · The Priesthood ← Numbers 19-22 · Numbers Study · Numbers 27-30 →

title: Numbers 27: The Daughters of Zelophehad and the Ordination of Joshua
text: ← Numbers 23-26 · Numbers Study · Numbers 31-34 → Numbers 27: The Daughters of Zelophehad and the Ordination of Joshua Read the chapter → Numbers 27 Introduction This reading covers Numbers 27 through 30: the inheritance won by the daughters of Zelophehad, the ordination of Joshua to lead after Moses, the continual burnt offering and the offerings of every sabbath, new moon, and feast, the high holy days of the seventh month, and the law of vows. To answer the inheritance question the whole of Numbers 36 was also read, precept upon precept, and the Q&A after the reading is folded into the verses it belongs to. Numbers 27:1-4 - The daughters of Zelophehad, of the tribe of Manasseh, stood before Moses, Eleazar the priest, the princes, and all the congregation at the door of the tabernacle. - Their father died in the wilderness in his own sin; he was not in the company of Korah that gathered together against the Lord. He had no sons, only these five daughters. - Their question was the question of the lineage: since the man puts the seed in the woman, if a man had only daughters, why should his name be done away from among his family? So they asked for a possession among the brethren of their father. Numbers 27:5-7 - Moses brought their cause before the Lord. He did not do his own thing; he sought counsel and asked the Most High what to do in this instance. - The Lord said the daughters of Zelophehad speak right: give them a possession of an inheritance among their father's brethren, and cause the inheritance of their father to pass unto them. Numbers 27:8-11 - Here the Lord set the order of inheritance for all Israel: if a man die and have no son, it passes to his daughter; if no daughter, to his brethren; if no brethren, to his father's brethren; and if his father had no brethren, to the kinsman that is next to him of his family. Every angle was covered so the inheritance stayed within the tribe. - Israel always had questions, just as we do when we read, and the Lord put these statutes in place to answer them before they were asked. - But what if a daughter who received the inheritance married into another tribe? You have to go precept upon precept: Numbers 36 takes up that very case with these same daughters. The chief fathers of Gilead brought it to Moses, and the word came back that the daughters of Zelophehad may marry to whom they think best, only to the family of the tribe of their father shall they marry. Precepts: - Numbers 36:6-7 Let them marry to whom they think best, only within the tribe of their father, so the inheritance does not remove from tribe to tribe. - Numbers 36:8-9 Every daughter that possesses an inheritance shall be wife unto one of the family of the tribe of her father, that every man enjoy the inheritance of his fathers. - Numbers 36:10-12 The daughters of Zelophehad were married unto their father's brothers' sons, and the inheritance remained in the tribe of the family of their father. - This is not saying no one ever married from Judah to Benjamin or Levi to Ephraim; it is showing that where an inheritance rode on the marriage, the woman married within her father's tribe. - It also goes into marriage in the nation as a whole: there was never a case where an inheritance in Israel passed to an Edomite, an Ammonite, or a Moabite. The fathers from the beginning took wives of their own kindred, and interracial marriage is not of the scriptures. Precepts: - Tobit 4:12 Chiefly take a wife of the seed of thy fathers; our fathers from the beginning all married wives of their own kindred, and were blessed in their children. Numbers 27:12-14 - The Lord told Moses to get up into mount Abarim and see the land given to the children of Israel; he would see it but not enter it, and then be gathered unto his people as Aaron his brother was gathered. - The reason is written: Moses rebelled against the commandment of the Most High in the desert of Zin at the water of Meribah. The Lord gave a specific commandment to speak unto the rock before their eyes, and Moses instead smote the rock twice; the water still came out abundantly, but Moses and Aaron did not sanctify the Lord in the eyes of the children of Israel, and for that neither of them brought the congregation into the land. Precepts: - Numbers 20:7-12 The commandment was to speak unto the rock; Moses smote it twice, and because they believed not, to sanctify the Lord in the eyes of Israel, they did not bring the congregation into the land. Numbers 27:15-17 - Before his death Moses asked the Lord to set a man over the congregation, to go out before them and come in before them, to lead them out and bring them in, that the congregation of the Lord be not as sheep which have no shepherd. - Moses asked for a man because the leadership of the nation belongs to men. The woman was made to be an help meet unto the man, not to rule over him; she is the weaker vessel, and the congregation is not set up for her to lead it. - A sister helping to build up other sisters new in the congregation is right, and the sisters bless the nation with real talents, raising the children in the commandments, and the aged women teaching the young women. But teaching and leading the nation is not the place the Most High set for her. Precepts: - Isaiah 3:12 Children are their oppressors, and women rule over them; that condition is a mark of a people gone astray, not the order of the Most High. - 1 Timothy 2:11-14 I suffer not a woman to teach, nor to usurp authority over the man; for Adam was first formed, then Eve, and the woman being deceived was in the transgression. - Ezekiel 34:31 The flock of my pasture are men; the shepherds and saviors of the nation are men. - Proverbs 8:4 Unto you, O men, I call; and my voice is to the sons of man. - Titus 2:3-5 The aged women are to be teachers of good things, that they may teach the young women to love their husbands and children, to be discreet, chaste, keepers at home, obedient to their own husbands. Numbers 27:18-21 - The Lord answered: take thee Joshua the son of Nun, a man in whom is the spirit, and lay thine hand upon him. - Joshua was set before Eleazar the priest and before all the congregation and given his charge in their sight, and some of Moses' honour was put upon him, so all Israel could see with their own eyes the man the Most High ordained to lead the nation after the death of Moses. - Joshua was to stand before Eleazar the priest, who would ask counsel for him after the judgment of Urim before the Lord; at his word they would go out and come in, he and all the children of Israel with him. Numbers 27:22-23 - Moses did as the Lord commanded him: he took Joshua, set him before Eleazar the priest and all the congregation, laid his hands upon him, and gave him a charge, as the Lord commanded by the hand of Moses. Numbers 28: The Continual Burnt Offering and the Offerings of the Feasts Read the chapter → Numbers 28 Numbers 28:1-8 - The Lord commanded the offerings made by fire to be observed in their due season: two lambs of the first year without spot, day by day, one lamb in the morning and the other lamb at even, a continual burnt offering which was ordained in mount Sinai. - With it went a meat offering of a tenth deal of flour mingled with the fourth part of an hin of beaten oil, and a drink offering of the fourth part of an hin; in the holy place the strong wine was poured unto the Lord. - The fire and the sacrifice continued morning and evening; it burned through the day and through the night, every single day. Numbers 28:9-10 - On the sabbath day two more lambs were offered, with their meat and drink offerings, the burnt offering of every sabbath, beside the continual burnt offering. That is four lambs every sabbath, with the drink offerings attached. - Precept upon precept this answers what Christ told the Pharisees: the priests in the temple profane the sabbath and are blameless. Israel did not kindle fire for themselves on the sabbath, but this altar work was the ordinance of the Lord for every sabbath day. - This is also why Christ had to come. In captivity we have no lambs, no farms, no temple, no most holy place, no veil, no high priest; the handwriting of ordinances that was against us was taken out of the way and nailed to his cross. Those who deny Christ and claim the Old Testament only are not keeping these sacrifices, and without Christ the whole law, drink offering to meat offering, still stands over them. Precepts: - Matthew 12:5 The priests in the temple profane the sabbath, and are blameless; the sabbath offerings were commanded work. - Colossians 2:14-17 The handwriting of ordinances against us was nailed to the cross; let no man judge you in meat, or in drink, or of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days, which are a shadow of things to come, but the body is of Christ. Numbers 28:11-15 - In the beginnings of your months, the new moon, a burnt offering was made: two young bullocks, one ram, seven lambs of the first year without spot, with their meat offerings of flour mingled with oil and their drink offerings of wine. - A kid of the goats for a sin offering was added, and all of it was beside the continual burnt offering. This was the burnt offering of every month throughout the months of the year. Numbers 28:16-25 - The fourteenth day of the first month is the passover of the Lord, and the fifteenth day is the feast: seven days unleavened bread, bread without leaven, must be eaten. - The first day and the seventh day are holy convocations wherein no manner of servile work is done, and each of the seven days carried its own sacrifice by fire: two young bullocks, a ram, seven lambs without blemish, with the meat offering of flour mingled with oil and a goat for a sin offering to make an atonement, beside the continual burnt offering of the morning. - That is on top of the passover lamb itself, which was not dressed like these offerings but roast with fire and eaten with the bitter herbs. Count the lambs of that week and you see how much the sacrifice law carried. Numbers 28:26-31 - The day of the firstfruits, the feast of weeks, when the new meat offering was brought after your weeks be out, was also an holy convocation with no servile work, with two young bullocks, one ram, seven lambs, their meat and drink offerings, and a kid of the goats to make an atonement, beside the continual burnt offering. - Every feast carried offerings stacked upon the daily offering, and missing them was sin.
