The Lord said by David, sacrifice and offering and burnt offerings and offering for sin thou wouldest not; they could never make the comers thereunto perfect, for the people went right back to their sin. - He taketh away the first, that he may establish the second: Christ offered his body once for all, where the priests stood daily offering the same sacrifices which can never take away sins. Thank the Most High for Jesus Christ, because these ordinances cannot be fulfilled in captivity. Precepts: - Hebrews 10:8-11 He taketh away the first covenant of sacrifices to establish the second; we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all, while the priests stood daily offering sacrifices which can never take away sins. Numbers 29: The Feasts of the Seventh Month Read the chapter → Numbers 29 Numbers 29:1-6 - The first day of the seventh month is an holy convocation, a day of blowing the trumpets, the memorial of blowing of trumpets: no servile work, and a burnt offering of one young bullock, one ram, and seven lambs of the first year without blemish, with their meat offerings and a kid of the goats for a sin offering. - That day is also the new moon, so the offering of the trumpets came beside the burnt offering of the month, the daily burnt offering, and their meat and drink offerings. In a span of fifteen days this month holds the memorial of blowing of trumpets coupled with the new moon, the day of atonement, and the feast of tabernacles. Numbers 29:7-11 - The tenth day of the seventh month is an holy convocation, a large gathering, wherein ye shall afflict your souls and do no work at all: the day of atonement, instituted as a statute for ever, when the priest made an atonement to cleanse the people from all their sins before the Lord. - To afflict your soul is to fast. The fast the Lord has chosen is a day for a man to afflict his soul, to loose the bands of wickedness, to undo the heavy burdens, to let the oppressed go free, and to break every yoke; that is why we still fast on this day once a year, and why we go out and teach on the day of atonement. - We fast without the sacrifices, because the atonement is now Christ. He was brought as a lamb to the slaughter, wounded for our transgressions, and the Lord laid on him the iniquity of us all, just as the priest laid the sins of the nation on the sacrifice of Leviticus 16; that is why the veil rent in two when he died, and why John said, Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world. - Isaiah 53 cannot be speaking of David, who was already dead in Isaiah's day; it speaks of Jesus Christ, cut off out of the land of the living for the transgression of the people, the ultimate sacrifice. Precepts: - Leviticus 16:29-31 A statute for ever: in the seventh month, on the tenth day, ye shall afflict your souls, and the priest made an atonement to cleanse you from all your sins before the Lord. - Isaiah 58:5-6 The fast that the Lord has chosen is a day for a man to afflict his soul, to loose the bands of wickedness, and to break every yoke. - Isaiah 53:4-10 He was wounded for our transgressions and brought as a lamb to the slaughter; he was cut off for the transgression of my people, and his soul was made an offering for sin. - John 1:29 Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world; Christ is the atonement now. Numbers 29:12-16 - The fifteenth day of the seventh month is an holy convocation, the feast of tabernacles: no servile work, and a feast kept unto the Lord seven days. - The first day's offering was thirteen young bullocks, two rams, and fourteen lambs of the first year without blemish, with their meat offerings by number and a kid of the goats for a sin offering, beside the continual burnt offering. - Leviticus 23 shows what this feast is: all that are Israelites born shall dwell in booths seven days, that your generations may know that the Most High made the children of Israel to dwell in booths when he brought them out of the land of Egypt. That is why once a year, around October, you will see us out in the wilderness in tents, eight days counting the solemn assembly, those of us able to get the time off; all our feast days are memorials of what the Lord did for us. Precepts: - Leviticus 23:33-36 The fifteenth day of the seventh month shall be the feast of tabernacles for seven days; the first day an holy convocation, and the eighth day a solemn assembly with no servile work. - Leviticus 23:41-43 A statute for ever in your generations: ye shall dwell in booths seven days, that your generations may know that I made the children of Israel to dwell in booths when I brought them out of Egypt. Numbers 29:17-19 - On the second day the count came down to twelve young bullocks, with the same two rams, fourteen lambs of the first year without spot, their meat and drink offerings by number, and a goat for a sin offering, beside the continual burnt offering. - The pattern descends a bullock each day: eleven on the third day, ten on the fourth, nine on the fifth, eight on the sixth, and seven on the seventh day, every day with two rams, fourteen lambs, the meat and drink offerings after the manner, and the goat for a sin offering, all beside the continual burnt offering that never stopped. Numbers 29:35-38 - The eighth day is a solemn assembly, the last day, with no servile work; its offering was one bullock, one ram, and seven lambs of the first year without blemish, with their meat and drink offerings and a goat for a sin offering, beside the continual burnt offering. Numbers 29:39-40 - All these sacrifices were for the set feasts of the Lord, and they came beside your vows and your freewill offerings, which carried sacrifices of their own. This is why Paul wrote, let no man judge you in meat or in drink; the feast days of the Lord were wrapped in offerings from the sabbath to the solemn assemblies. - What is left for us is better: present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service. Keeping the feast days, telling your employer months ahead that you need the day of atonement or the tabernacles off, and helping supply the feasts is presenting the body a living sacrifice. - He that keepeth the law bringeth offerings enough; to depart from wickedness pleases the Lord, and to forsake unrighteousness is a propitiation. The prophets showed before that Christ should suffer, and he hath so fulfilled it, doing away with the law of animal sacrifice. - If ye love him, keep his commandments, and he will send the Comforter, the Spirit of truth, which the world cannot receive; the Holy Ghost teaches all things and brings all things to remembrance, and that spirit is how this truth is understood in these last days. Precepts: - Romans 12:1 Present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service. - Ecclesiasticus 35:1-3 Keeping the law brings offerings enough; departing from wickedness and forsaking unrighteousness is the propitiation now. - Acts 3:18 What God before had shewed by the mouth of all his prophets, that Christ should suffer, he hath so fulfilled. - John 14:15-17 If ye love me, keep my commandments; and the Father shall give you another Comforter, the Spirit of truth, whom the world cannot receive. - John 14:26 The Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance. Numbers 30: The Law of Vows Read the chapter → Numbers 30 Numbers 30:1-2 - If a man vow a vow unto the Lord, or swear an oath to bind his soul with a bond, he shall not break his word; he shall do according to all that proceedeth out of his mouth. - A vow is promising the Lord you will do a thing. Say a man vows, Lord, if you bring this to pass I will never eat swine again; he must keep that vow, and he cannot go back on it and simply ask forgiveness afterward. - If thou shalt forbear to vow, it shall be no sin in thee; but that which is gone out of thy lips thou shalt keep and perform. Do not suffer thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin, and do not say before the angel that it was an error. Precepts: - Leviticus 27:2 When a man shall make a singular vow, the persons shall be for the Lord by thy estimation; the law already valued what was vowed. - Deuteronomy 23:21-23 When thou shalt vow a vow, thou shalt not slack to pay it, for it would be sin in thee; but if thou forbear to vow, it shall be no sin in thee. - Ecclesiastes 5:3-7 Pay that which thou hast vowed; better not to vow than to vow and not pay; suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin, neither say before the angel that it was an error. - Christ took it further: swear not at all, neither by heaven, nor by the earth, nor by Jerusalem; let your communication be Yea, yea, Nay, nay, for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil. That is why we say the Lord's will: the Lord's will I will be there, the Lord's will I will teach that day. - A vow made before you came into this truth does not stand, for you were not vowing to the God of Israel then; if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature, and old things are passed away. And if you vowed ignorantly and could not fulfill it, all manner of sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven unto men; only blasphemy against the Holy Ghost, speaking evil of this truth after receiving it, shall not be forgiven. - Swearing on the Bible in the court system is another matter: be subject unto the higher powers, for the powers that be are ordained of God, and you also have the option to affirm; either way, tell the truth. Precepts: - Matthew 5:33-37 Swear not at all; let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil. - James 5:12 Above all things, swear not, neither by heaven, neither by the earth, neither by any other oath; lest ye fall into condemnation. - 2 Corinthians 5:17 If any man be in Christ, he is a new creature; old things are passed away, and a vow made while serving the world does not stand. - Matthew 12:31-32 All manner of sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven unto men, but the blasphemy against the Holy Ghost shall not be forgiven. - Romans 13:1-2 Be subject unto the higher powers, for there is no power but of God; whosoever resisteth the power resisteth the ordinance of God. - On the wedding day we do not make vows in the manner of Christianity, promising things the flesh may not perform; we pray as Tobias and Sara prayed, that the Lord mercifully ordain that husband and wife may become aged together, and we apply the scriptures to the marriage. - Marriage is not sin, but such shall have trouble in the flesh; trials will come up in a marriage that have to be fixed with the scriptures, so ask the Most High for the mercy and the strength to endure rather than vowing what you cannot uphold. Precepts: - Tobit 8:5-8 The prayer of the marriage bed: mercifully ordain that we may become aged together; that is the prayer, not a vow. - 1 Corinthians 7:28 If thou marry, thou hast not sinned; nevertheless such shall have trouble in the flesh. Numbers 30:3-5 - A daughter in her father's house in her youth who vows a vow is under her father's covering. If her father hears her vow and holds his peace, all her vows stand and every bond wherewith she hath bound her soul stands. - But if her father disallow her in the day that he heareth, not any of her vows or bonds shall stand, and the Lord shall forgive her, because her father disallowed her. That shows the power the Most High put in the man of the house: a father can hear his daughter bind herself and say no, and the Lord releases her. Numbers 30:6-8 - The same covering passes to the husband. If a woman with a husband vows, or utters ought out of her lips wherewith she binds her soul, and her husband hears it and holds his peace in the day that he hears it, her vows stand. - But if her husband disallow her on the day that he heard it, he makes her vow of none effect, and the Lord shall forgive her. A wife could be binding herself to something she cannot perform, and her husband can step in and say, Lord, do not hear that vow, and the Most High releases her because of her husband. - That is the power of the head of the house: the husband keeping the commandments stands between his wife and a bond that would jack her up. That is a reason to love your hedge, not to despise it. Numbers 30:9 - Every vow of a widow, and of her that is divorced, wherewith they have bound their souls, shall stand against her. She has no father or husband to disallow it, so what she vows she must perform. - The husband is a hedge of protection; where no hedge is, the possession is spoiled. The married woman has a covering that the widow and the divorced woman do not have. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 36:25 Where no hedge is, the possession is spoiled; the covering of the house is the hedge. Numbers 30:10-15 - If a wife vowed in her husband's house and her husband heard it and held his peace and disallowed her not, then all her vows stand. Her husband may establish every vow and every binding oath to afflict the soul, or her husband may make it void. - If he altogether holds his peace at her from day to day, then he establishes all her vows and confirms all her bonds, because he held his peace in the day that he heard them. Holding your peace is confirming it. - But if he shall any ways make them void after that he hath heard them, then he shall bear her iniquity. He cannot hear her vow, hold his peace day after day, and then come later to void it; he had the power to stop it and did not, so the iniquity falls to him. And this runs one way: a wife cannot disallow or nullify her husband's vow. - This is the order of the house: the husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church, and he is the saviour of the body; so let the wives be subject to their own husbands in every thing, even in what is vowed in prayer. Precepts: - Ephesians 5:22-24 The husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church; therefore let the wives be to their own husbands in every thing. Numbers 30:16 - These are the statutes which the Lord commanded Moses, between a man and his wife, and between the father and his daughter, being yet in her youth in her father's house. The whole chapter is the government of vows inside the house of Israel. --- Topics: Clean and Unclean Meats · Sacrifice and Atonement · The Covenant · The Feasts of the Most High · The Priesthood · The Sabbath ← Numbers 23-26 · Numbers Study · Numbers 31-34 →

title: Numbers 3: The Levites Taken Instead of the Firstborn
text: ← Numbers 1-2 · Numbers Study · Numbers 7-10 → Numbers 3: The Levites Taken Instead of the Firstborn Read the chapter → Numbers 3 Introduction This reading covers Numbers 3 through 6: the Levites taken for the Most High instead of all the firstborn of Israel, the service and burdens of the sons of Kohath, Gershon, and Merari, the law of putting the defiled out of the camp and the law of jealousies, and the law of the Nazarite with the blessing of the children of Israel. The session picks up at Numbers 3:11 after the reading of the earlier verses was interrupted; the recap of the stranger teaching from that portion is kept under Numbers 3:10. The word to remember through the whole reading is order: everything in the camp of Israel was set in order, and the Most High required it on pain of death. Numbers 3:10 - Aaron and his sons were appointed to wait on the priest's office, and the stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death. Anybody outside the tribe of Levi, when it came to doing the service of the Lord, was considered a stranger. Precepts: - Hebrews 7:13-14 Our Lord sprang out of Juda, of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood; no man of another tribe gave attendance at the altar. Numbers 3:11-13 - The Most High took the Levites from among the children of Israel instead of all the firstborn that openeth the matrix. The matrix is the womb; that is what the Lord calls it. - All the firstborn are his from the day he smote all the firstborn in the land of Egypt. Verse 13 proves the Most High does not love everybody; he killed all the firstborn of Egypt. Numbers 3:14-16 - The children of Levi were numbered after the houses of their fathers, by their families. Your lineage is determined by your father, not your mother. - The claim that identity passes through the mother is nowhere in the Bible; number the children of Levi after the house of their fathers is the standard of scripture. Numbers 3:21-26 - Of Gershon were the families of the Libnites and the Shimites, numbered 7,500 males from a month old and upward, and they pitched behind the tabernacle westward. Depending on your family lineage you had a specific side of the tabernacle that you and all your descendants had to be on. - The charge of the sons of Gershon was the tabernacle and the tent, the covering thereof, the hanging for the door, the hangings of the court, and the cords of it; that was their responsibility. Numbers 3:27-31 - The ending "ites" denotes the people of; the Kohathites are the people of Kohath. They numbered 8,600 and pitched on the side of the tabernacle southward. - Their charge was the ark, the table, the candlestick, the altars, and the vessels of the sanctuary. Only they were responsible for the ark; anybody outside of that suffered the judgment of the Most High, as Uzzah did generations later when he put forth his hand to the ark and God smote him on the spot. Precepts: - 2 Samuel 6:6-8 Uzzah took hold of the ark when his family was not chosen for that charge, and God smote him there for his error; he died by the ark of God. Numbers 3:32 - Eleazar the son of Aaron was chief over the chief of the Levites, with the oversight of them that keep the charge of the sanctuary. He was the manager of the tabernacle. Numbers 3:33-37 - Of Merari were the families of the Mahlites and the Mushites, numbered 6,200, and they pitched on the side of the tabernacle northward. - Their custody and charge was the boards of the tabernacle, the bars, the pillars, the sockets, the vessels, and the pillars of the court round about with their sockets, pins, and cords. Numbers 3:38 - Moses and Aaron and his sons encamped before the tabernacle toward the east, keeping the charge of the sanctuary; and the stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death. Anybody outside the tribe of Levi that approached unto the tabernacle was considered a stranger. Numbers 3:39-43 - All the Levites numbered from a month old and upward were 22,000; the Most High was separating the tribe of Levi unto himself instead of all the firstborn among the children of Israel. - The firstborn males of the children of Israel were twenty and two thousand two hundred and threescore and thirteen. A score is twenty, so threescore and thirteen is 73; the count is 22,273. Numbers 3:44-51 - The firstborn of Israel outnumbered the Levites by 273, and those odd ones were redeemed at five shekels apiece by the poll, after the shekel of the sanctuary, which is twenty gerahs. Moses took the redemption money, 1,365 shekels, and gave it unto Aaron and to his sons. - The money went to Aaron and the priests because they had to take care of the widows, the fatherless, and the strangers; the strangers are our people that come from different parts of the land down to Jerusalem needing help. That is how the Most High put money into the sanctuary to take care of those that could not take care of themselves. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 14:27-29 The Levite has no part nor inheritance with thee; the Levite, the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow within thy gates shall come and eat and be satisfied. Numbers 4: The Service of the Tabernacle Done in Order Read the chapter → Numbers 4 Numbers 4:1-3 - The sons of Kohath were numbered from thirty years old and upward even unto fifty years old, all that enter into the host to do the work in the tabernacle of the congregation. You took on that responsibility at thirty years old. - Fifty was basically the age of retirement from the service; the law elsewhere shows the elder then sat down to be a judge amongst his brethren. Numbers 4:4-6 - This is the service of the sons of Kohath about the most holy things. When the camp set forward, Aaron and his sons took down the covering vail and covered the ark of the testimony with it, with the covering of badgers' skins and a cloth wholly of blue. - The design of the ark and the tabernacle, the pure gold dishes, spoons, and vessels, was laid out back in Exodus 35 and 36; review it there. Numbers 4:7-14 - The table of shewbread, the candlestick, the golden altar, and all the instruments of ministry were each wrapped in cloths of blue, scarlet, or purple and covered with badgers' skins before they were put on the staves and bars. - Badger skin is something we would consider unclean today, yet the Lord had his holy things covered in it. Under the law of sacrifice, defilement came by touching unclean things to eat them; touching them to make something for the tabernacle still left you unclean until sundown, unable to sacrifice, but the skins themselves served the sanctuary. Numbers 4:15 - After Aaron and his sons made an end of covering the sanctuary, the sons of Kohath came to bear it, but they shall not touch any holy thing, lest they die. The Most High is very particular about the most holy things. - The Lord referred to all the tribes together as the camp. If you are not in a camp you are out of order; people avoid camps because a camp carries a certain level of order and subjection, and they want to do their own thing, which is to sit in the midst of sin. - All twelve tribes are not gathered together right now, but we are still commanded to rehearse the righteous acts of the Lord, and that takes gathering; the body must move in one unison, in one direction, as a camp. Precepts: - Judges 5:11 They that are delivered shall rehearse the righteous acts of the Lord in the places of drawing water; that duty stands even before all twelve tribes are gathered. - 1 Corinthians 1:10 Speak the same thing, no divisions, perfectly joined together in the same mind and the same judgment; that is the camp moving in one direction. Numbers 4:16 - To the office of Eleazar pertained the oil for the light, the sweet incense, the daily meat offering, the anointing oil, and the oversight of all the tabernacle. The burning of the sweet incense stayed in that priestly line: Zacharias, of the course of Abia, descended from the line of the Kohathites, and his lot was to burn incense in the temple of the Lord. - Luke 1:6 is the New Testament precept for what it means to be righteous: walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless. Highlight that and commit it to memory. - The son of Zacharias was John the Baptist, a Levite; and John the Baptist was Elijah back on the earth again, come to do what was prophesied of him. There is no reincarnation, coming back as a bird or such; there is regeneration, and we come back over and over again. Precepts: - Luke 1:5-9 Zacharias of the course of Abia was righteous, walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless, and his lot was to burn incense in the temple; he served in the Kohathite charge. - Matthew 17:12-13 Elias is come already, and they knew him not; the disciples understood that he spake unto them of John the Baptist. Numbers 4:17-20 - The Most High commanded that the families of the Kohathites not be cut off: Aaron and his sons appointed every one to his service and to his burden, but they shall not go in to see when the holy things are covered, lest they die. - It was a heavy responsibility; your life was on the line and you could not be out of order. One slip, one curious peek at the shiny gold before it was covered, and God put you to death on the spot. You had to be serious about your job and follow all instructions. - That is the God we are dealing with; that is why Christ came, to give us mercy and grace from that thing. Numbers 4:21-28 - The sons of Gershon were numbered from thirty to fifty years old for their service: bearing the curtains of the tabernacle, the coverings of badgers' skins, the hangings of the court and the doors, the cords, and all the instruments of their service. - Their charge was under the hand of Ithamar the son of Aaron the priest. Ithamar had to make sure the priests had covered all the most holy things before the Gershonites came in to bear them; he was responsible for the lives of all the Gershonites that served, and he had to be in order. Numbers 4:29-33 - The sons of Merari were numbered from thirty to fifty years old, charged with the boards, bars, pillars, sockets, pins, and cords of the tabernacle and the court, reckoned by name, under the hand of Ithamar the son of Aaron. - Only Eleazar and Ithamar were left to oversee, because Nadab and Abihu were killed by the Lord for offering strange fire; there were only two sons of Aaron remaining. Numbers 4:34-49 - The numbered for service were 2,750 Kohathites, 2,630 Gershonites, and 3,200 Merarites; the total of those from thirty to fifty years old that entered the service of the tabernacle was 8,580, eight thousand and five hundred and fourscore. - The Lord constantly repeats himself through these chapters to make sure you stay in order and do not go out of order, because going out of order cost your life. That is why you read the same thing in the Bible over and over again. Numbers 5: Put Out of the Camp, and the Law of Jealousies Read the chapter → Numbers 5 Numbers 5:1-4 - Every leper, every one that hath an issue, and whosoever is defiled by the dead, male and female, was put out without the camp, that they defile not their camps in the midst whereof the Most High dwelt. And the children of Israel did so. - Israel is referred to as a camp all through these chapters. The Lord is gathering his camp back together again to come and deliver us; if you are not in a camp, get in a camp. - Inside the camp we consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works; the stronger in faith exhort the weaker to keep striving and endure to the end. If you are not gathered you cannot do that, and you do a disservice to the Lord and to your people. - Separating yourself after receiving the knowledge of the truth is willful sin, and there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins, but a fearful looking for of judgment; that is doing despite unto the spirit of grace that woke us up in these last days. Precepts: - Hebrews 10:24-25 Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, but exhorting one another, and so much the more as ye see the day approaching. - Hebrews 10:26-29 Sinning willfully after receiving the knowledge of the truth leaves no more sacrifice for sins, only judgment; the despiser of the covenant is counted worthy of sorer punishment. - Zephaniah 2:1 Gather yourselves together, O nation not desired; there is nowhere to obey that except gathered in a camp. Numbers 5:5-8 - When a man or woman commits a trespass against the Lord, they shall confess their sin and recompense the trespass with the principal thereof plus the fifth part, given unto him against whom the trespass was done. Exodus 22 is the chapter of those civil matters and repayments; the Lord laid the payment on you so you would learn not to do it again. - If the man have no kinsman, the trespass was recompensed unto the Lord, even to the priest, beside the ram of the atonement. The atonement now is Christ; we no longer take a ram to a priest, because Christ became the atonement and we ask forgiveness through him. - Christ is the advocate and the propitiation, the mercy, for our sins; there is no more Levite priest sacrifice, for he is the mediator between us and the Most High now. The whole world in that verse is the whole world of the nation of Israel. Precepts: - 1 John 2:1-2 If any man sin, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous, the propitiation for our sins and for the sins of the whole world. - Isaiah 45:17 Israel shall be saved in the LORD with an everlasting salvation, world without end; that is the whole world the propitiation covers. Numbers 5:9-10 - Every offering of the holy things brought unto the priest was his, because the Levites had no inheritance of land as the other tribes did. Levi was scattered in every land, in Ephraim, in Dan, in Zebulun, in Judah, in Benjamin, so the people could bring the sacrifice to them; Levi had no plot to cultivate crops on, and was fed by the people of the Lord. Numbers 5:11-15 - If a man's wife go aside and lie with another carnally, hid from the eyes of her husband with no witness, and the spirit of jealousy come upon him, there is a law for it. The spirit of jealousy is the Lord putting it on the husband that something is not right: the routine changes, and he begins questioning and seeing things differently, whether she be defiled or not defiled. - The man brought his wife unto the priest with the tenth part of an ephah of barley meal, no oil and no frankincense upon it, for it is an offering of jealousy, an offering of memorial, bringing iniquity to remembrance; the Lord said do not make this offering sweet. Numbers 5:16-18 - The priest set the woman before the Lord, took holy water in an earthen vessel with the dust of the floor of the tabernacle, and uncovered the woman's head. - Verse 18 is a precept that our sisters had their heads covered. A wig is not the covering; the covered head is a custom, a tradition, and our heritage. Numbers 5:19-22 - The priest charged her by an oath: if no man have lain with thee, be thou free from this bitter water that causeth the curse; but if thou hast gone aside to another instead of thy husband, the Lord make thy thigh to rot and thy belly to swell. The Most High is hard on his daughters for a reason, and he was not playing with that judgment. - The woman had to answer Amen, amen. If you would not agree to drink the water, you showed yourself guilty already, and the guilty were stoned. Surely your sin shall find you out; there is nothing you can hide. Precepts: - Numbers 32:23 Be sure your sin will find you out; nothing done in the dark stays hid before the Most High. Numbers 5:23-28 - The priest wrote the curses in a book and blotted them out with the bitter water, waved the jealousy offering before the Lord, burnt the memorial upon the altar, and caused the woman to drink. - If she was defiled, the water became bitter, her belly swelled and her thigh rotted, and the woman became a curse among her people, a plague she could not get rid of. If she was not defiled, she was free and shall conceive seed; the husband was simply tripping, and she was clear. Numbers 5:29-31 - This is the law of jealousies, when a wife goeth aside or when the spirit of jealousy cometh upon a husband: the priest executed upon her all this law, the man was guiltless from iniquity, and the woman, if guilty, bore her iniquity. Numbers 6: The Law of the Nazarite and the Blessing of Israel Read the chapter → Numbers 6 Numbers 6:1-4 - When a man or woman vowed the vow of a Nazarite, to separate themselves unto the Lord, he separated himself from wine and strong drink, drank no vinegar of wine nor liquor of grapes, and ate nothing made of the vine tree, from the kernels even to the husk. - John the Baptist fell under that Nazarite vow: the angel told Zacharias his son shall drink neither wine nor strong drink, and shall be filled with the Holy Ghost even from his mother's womb. - John was filled with the Holy Spirit before he was born, and Elizabeth did not sleep with an angel; Zacharias was her husband. The same way Christ was filled with the Holy Spirit before birth; the immaculate conception is a Catholic doctrine, not the scriptures. Precepts: - Luke 1:13-17 John shall drink neither wine nor strong drink, filled with the Holy Ghost from the womb, going before the Lord in the spirit and power of Elias to make ready a people prepared for the Lord. Numbers 6:5 - All the days of the vow no razor came upon his head; he was holy, and let the locks of the hair of his head grow. - Samson was a Nazarite also, from the tribe of Dan; he got caught up in wickedness with the daughters of Ham, but he was a Nazarite, and his hair grew in seven locks. That description is not speaking of the people who call themselves Jews today, whatever the movies portray. Precepts: - Judges 16:13 Samson spoke of the seven locks of his head; the locks of the Nazarite mark the man the scripture describes. Numbers 6:6-8 - All the days of his separation he came at no dead body, and made not himself unclean even for his father, his mother, his brother, or his sister when they died, because the consecration of his God was upon his head. It was a heavy thing to fall under the Nazarite vow; you had to separate yourself from everybody, even family, so you would not be defiled. Numbers 6:9-12 - If any man died very suddenly by him, the head of his consecration was defiled: he shaved his head on the seventh day of his cleansing, brought two turtles or two young pigeons to the priest on the eighth day, and a lamb of the first year for a trespass offering; the days before were lost. - Paul partook in that Nazarite purification. Unto the Jews he became a Jew; he brought himself down to their level of understanding to win them over, not by breaking the law but by walking orderly and keeping it. - The elders at Jerusalem told Paul to purify himself with four men which had a vow on them and be at charges with them, that all may know thou thyself walkest orderly and keepest the law. And note it well: the thousands there that believed were Jews, all zealous of the law, and the Gentiles Paul taught among were Jews scattered among the Gentiles. Precepts: - 1 Corinthians 9:20 Unto the Jews I became as a Jew, that I might gain the Jews; that is why Paul took the charges of the vow. - Acts 21:20-24 Thousands of Jews which believe, all zealous of the law, and Jews among the Gentiles; Paul purified himself with the four men that had a vow, walking orderly and keeping the law. Numbers 6:13-20 - When the days of his separation were fulfilled, the Nazarite offered a he lamb without blemish for a burnt offering and a ewe lamb without blemish for a sin offering, with unleavened bread and the meat and drink offerings. Without blemish is the same thing going into Christ. - He shaved the head of his separation at the door of the tabernacle and put the hair in the fire under the sacrifice of the peace offerings; the priest put the sodden shoulder and the cakes on his hands and waved them for a wave offering, which we covered in Exodus: the priest picks it up and waves it before the Lord. - After that the Nazarite may drink wine; before that he could not. In our understanding today you cannot keep the vow of a Nazarite under Christ: you can let your hair grow as long as you want, but when we break bread and take the cup in remembrance of Christ, renewing that covenant, you have to drink that wine to be in covenant with him. Precepts: - 1 Corinthians 11:23-25 Take, eat, this is my body; this cup is the new testament in my blood, this do ye, as oft as ye drink it, in remembrance of me. The cup of the covenant is why the Nazarite vow cannot be kept under Christ. Numbers 6:22-27 - On this wise Aaron and his sons blessed the children of Israel: the Lord bless thee and keep thee, the Lord make his face shine upon thee and be gracious unto thee, the Lord lift up his countenance upon thee and give thee peace; and they shall put my name upon the children of Israel, and I will bless them. - All of that is a stipulation, a contract; it is not unconditional love with the Most High. Keep my commandments and live. - When the southern kingdom asked wherefore the Lord pronounced evil against them, the answer was because your fathers forsook me and walked after other gods, and ye have done worse than your fathers. Bring it up to today: Christianity, Islam, Buddhism, Hinduism, every denomination walking after the imagination of its own evil heart, cast out into a land we knew not, serving gods where the Lord shows no favor. That is why our people have no peace and no blessing. - The Most High has taken that blessing from us, and we have to work to get it back by repentance and enduring to the end. But it will happen again; the Lord is pulling his spirit back out on us, and the remnant is waking up. Precepts: - Jeremiah 16:10-13 Because your fathers have forsaken me and walked after other gods, and ye have done worse than your fathers, therefore will I cast you out of this land into a land that ye know not, where I will not shew you favour. --- Topics: Clean and Unclean Meats · Idolatry · Sacrifice and Atonement · The Covenant · The Feasts of the Most High · The Priesthood · The Sabbath ← Numbers 1-2 · Numbers Study · Numbers 7-10 →

title: Numbers 31: Vengeance on the Midianites
text: ← Numbers 27-30 · Numbers Study · Numbers 35-36 → Numbers 31: Vengeance on the Midianites Read the chapter → Numbers 31 Introduction This reading covers Numbers 31 through 34: the war of vengeance against Midian and the dividing of the prey, Reuben and Gad receiving their inheritance on this side Jordan, the journeys of Israel from Egypt to the plains of Moab, and the borders and dividers of the land of Canaan. This session is mostly reading with brief exposition; the counsel through the chapters of journeys and borders is to follow along with the maps in the back of the Bible, so the lands and cities being read take on life instead of putting the reader to sleep. Numbers 31:1-2 - The Most High told Israel to avenge the children of Israel of the Midianites. The reason for this vengeance is the history of Numbers 25; go back and read that chapter to see what Midian did. Precepts: - Numbers 25:1-3 The people began whoredom with the daughters of Moab and were joined unto Baal-peor; that history is the reason the Lord commanded the vengeance. Numbers 31:3-6 - A thousand of every tribe, twelve thousand armed for war, were sent with Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest, with the holy instruments and the trumpets to blow. - Phinehas is the one who killed the man of Israel that was fornicating with the woman of the other nation, in the history of Numbers 25. Precepts: - Numbers 25:7-8 Phinehas took a javelin and thrust the man of Israel and the Midianitish woman through, and the plague was stayed. Numbers 31:7-8 - They warred against the Midianites as the Lord commanded Moses, slew all the males, and slew the five kings of Midian: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba. - Balaam also the son of Beor they slew with the sword. Balaam was a soothsayer, a diviner; he was a witch, so to speak. Precepts: - Joshua 13:22 Balaam the son of Beor, the soothsayer, did the children of Israel slay with the sword among them that were slain by them. Numbers 31:9-12 - Israel took the women of Midian captives with their little ones, took the spoil of all their cattle, flocks, and goods, and burnt all their cities and all their goodly castles with fire. - Midian comes from the lineage of Ishmael, the people known today as the Arab man. This shows Esau was not the one who first came up with castles; the castles seen in the movies were conquered from other nations. - They took all the spoil and all the prey, both of men and of beasts: the Midianites had captives of their own, and Israel took over both the men and the beasts when they overcame them. Numbers 31:13-18 - Moses was wroth with the officers of the host, the leaders of the army of Israel, because they saved all the women alive. - These women caused the children of Israel, through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass against the Lord in the matter of Peor. Balaam took it upon himself to send the women of the other nations to Israel, and it caused the people to go into fornication, and the Lord began putting them to death, over twenty and four thousand, in the history of Numbers 25. - Therefore every male among the little ones was to be killed, and every woman that had known man by lying with him; but the women children that had not known a man they kept alive for themselves. - Moses allowed the men to keep those women so they would not commit sin and go raping the women, being out at war. That does not mean it is done today; it was a time that the Most High allowed it so the men would not be in the midst of sin. Precepts: - Numbers 25:9 Those that died in the plague were twenty and four thousand; that plague in the matter of Peor is why the women who had known man could not be kept. Numbers 31:19-24 - Whoever killed any person or touched any slain had to abide without the camp seven days and purify himself and his captives on the third day and on the seventh day. That is the law going back to Numbers 5:2, putting the defiled outside the camp. - Purifying the raiment, all that is made of skins, all work of goats' hair, and all things made of wood goes back to the law of purification in Numbers 19. - Eleazar the priest gave the ordinance: gold, silver, brass, iron, tin, and lead, everything that may abide the fire, goes through the fire and is purified with the water of separation; whatever abides not the fire goes through the water; and on the seventh day they wash their clothes, are clean, and come into the camp. Precepts: - Numbers 5:2 Put out of the camp every one defiled by the dead; the seven days without the camp keep that law. - Numbers 19:11-12 He that touches the dead purifies himself on the third day and on the seventh day; the men of war purified themselves by that law. Numbers 31:25-30 - Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the chief fathers of the congregation took the sum of the prey, both of man and of beast, adding up all that was taken from the Midianites. - The prey was divided into two parts: between the army who went out to battle and took the prey, and all the congregation that did not go to war. The nation looked out for each other. - A tribute was levied unto the Lord: of the men of war, one soul of five hundred, of persons, beeves, asses, and sheep, given to Eleazar the priest for a heave offering, because he was the priest; and of the children of Israel's half, one portion of fifty, given to the Levites which kept the charge of the tabernacle. Numbers 31:41 - Moses gave the tribute, the Lord's heave offering, unto Eleazar the priest, as the Lord commanded Moses. The heave offerings belong to the priesthood by statute forever, a covenant of salt, because Aaron and Levi have no inheritance in the land; the Most High is their part and their inheritance. Precepts: - Numbers 18:19 All the heave offerings of the holy things are given to the priest and his sons by a statute for ever; it is a covenant of salt before the Lord. - Numbers 18:20 Aaron has no inheritance in their land; the Lord is his part and his inheritance among the children of Israel. - Numbers 18:21 The children of Levi are given all the tenth in Israel for an inheritance, for the service of the tabernacle of the congregation. Numbers 32: The Inheritance of Reuben and Gad on This Side Jordan Read the chapter → Numbers 32 Numbers 32:1-5 - The children of Reuben and Gad had a very great multitude of cattle, and when they saw that Jazer and Gilead was a place for cattle, they asked Moses for that land and said, bring us not over Jordan. - They did not want to go forward any more; they were ready to set up shop before they crossed over Jordan, and they had not even finished the mission. Numbers 32:6-9 - Moses said unto them, shall your brethren go to war, and shall ye sit here and do nothing? - Wherefore discourage ye the heart of the children of Israel from going over into the land which the Lord hath given them: thus did your fathers when they were sent from Kadesh-barnea to see the land. That goes back into the history of the spies in Numbers 13; the fathers were not even in the land yet and were already getting comfortable. Precepts: - Numbers 13:31-33 The men that went up brought an evil report of the land and discouraged the people; that is the history Moses set before Reuben and Gad. Numbers 32:10-13 - The Lord's anger was kindled and he sware that none of the men that came up out of Egypt from twenty years old should see the land, save Caleb the son of Jephunneh and Joshua the son of Nun, for they wholly followed the Lord. - He made Israel wander in the wilderness forty years, until all the generation that had done evil in the sight of the Lord was consumed. Moses is giving Reuben and Gad the history of everything so they see what their request repeats. Numbers 32:14-15 - Behold, ye are risen up in your fathers' stead, an increase of sinful men, to augment yet the fierce anger of the Lord toward Israel; if ye turn away from after him, he will yet again leave them in the wilderness, and ye shall destroy all this people. Numbers 32:16-19 - They came near and answered: we will build sheepfolds for our cattle and cities for our little ones, but we ourselves will go ready armed before the children of Israel until we have brought them unto their place. Moses got them in the spirit this time. - They vowed not to return to their houses until the children of Israel had inherited every man his inheritance, since their own inheritance had fallen to them on this side Jordan eastward. Numbers 32:20-24 - Moses set the condition: if ye will go all of you armed over Jordan before the Lord until his enemies be driven out, then afterward ye shall return and be guiltless before the Lord and before Israel, and this land shall be your possession. - But if ye will not do so, behold, ye have sinned against the Lord: and be sure your sin will find you out. - Build you cities for your little ones and folds for your sheep, and do that which hath proceeded out of your mouth. Do not think only about yourself; look out for your children, the nation coming after you. Numbers 32:33-42 - Moses gave unto the children of Gad and of Reuben and unto half the tribe of Manasseh the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites and the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, the land with the cities thereof, and they built their cities and folds for sheep. - The children of Machir the son of Manasseh went to Gilead and took it, and dispossessed the Amorite which was in it: they took them out of the land. Numbers 33: The Journeys of Israel from Egypt to the Plains of Moab Read the chapter → Numbers 33 Numbers 33:1-4 - These are the journeys of the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt, and Moses wrote their goings out by the commandment of the Lord. - They departed from Rameses on the fifteenth day of the first month, on the morrow after the passover, with an high hand in the sight of all the Egyptians, while the Egyptians buried all their firstborn, which the Lord had smitten among them: upon their gods also the Lord executed judgments; he put them to death. Numbers 33:8-11 - They passed through the midst of the sea into the wilderness, pitched in Marah, came to Elim where there were twelve fountains of water and threescore and ten palm trees, encamped by the Red sea, and encamped in the wilderness of Sin. - Follow these journeys with the maps in the back of the Bible; most Bibles have them. Seeing the wilderness of Sin, the Red sea, and the route they were taking gives a better understanding of the lands and cities being read. Numbers 33:16-17 - They would walk a little and then set up camp wherever the Lord wanted them to stop. They were led by the cloud by day and the light by night; the light gave them sight at night, and when they saw it stop, they knew to pitch camp right there. Numbers 33:37-39 - They pitched in mount Hor, in the edge of the land of Edom; the map shows the land of Edom there. - Aaron the priest went up into mount Hor at the commandment of the Lord and died there, in the fortieth year after the children of Israel were come out of the land of Egypt, in the first day of the fifth month; and Aaron was an hundred and twenty and three years old when he died. The number is the fortieth year; read it carefully. Numbers 33:44-49 - They pitched in Ije-abarim, in the border of Moab; on the map Moab sits right above the land of Edom. - They departed from the mountains of Abarim and pitched in the plains of Moab by Jordan near Jericho; so they ended in the midst of the land of Moab, where the camp now sits. Numbers 33:50-53 - When ye are passed over Jordan into the land of Canaan, ye shall drive out all the inhabitants of the land from before you, destroy all their pictures and all their molten images, and quite pluck down all their high places: all the idols go. - Dispossess the inhabitants of the land and dwell therein, for the Most High has given the land to possess it. Numbers 33:54 - The land was to be divided by lot for an inheritance among the families, to the more the more inheritance and to the fewer the less, every man's inheritance in the place where his lot falleth, according to the tribes of the fathers. The map of the tribal lands, Simeon, Judah, Benjamin, Reuben and the rest with their cities, is the product of the tribes following what the Most High said to do. Numbers 33:55-56 - But if ye will not drive out the inhabitants of the land, those which ye let remain shall be pricks in your eyes and thorns in your sides, and shall vex you in the land wherein ye dwell. - They are going to be problems, because they are not following the Most High as Israel follows; if you allow them to stay in your land they will always cause problems. Precepts: - Joshua 23:13 The nations left remaining become snares and traps, scourges in your sides and thorns in your eyes, until ye perish from off the good land. Numbers 34: The Borders of the Land of Canaan Read the chapter → Numbers 34 Numbers 34:1-5 - This is the land of Canaan that falls to Israel for inheritance, with the coasts thereof; the south quarter runs from the wilderness of Zin along by the coast of Edom, the south border from the outmost coast of the salt sea eastward, fetching a compass unto the river of Egypt and out at the sea. - This is going into how far the land stretched. When reading these borders, look at the map and visualize how the land is stretched, border by border. Numbers 34:6-12 - The western border is the great sea; the north border runs from the great sea to mount Hor and the entrance of Hamath out to Hazar-enan; the east border goes down from Shepham to Riblah, reaches unto the side of the sea of Chinnereth eastward, and goes down Jordan out at the salt sea. Numbers 34:13-15 - Moses commanded that this is the land to be inherited by lot, which the Lord commanded to give unto the nine tribes and to the half tribe; for Reuben, Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh, the son of Joseph, had already received their inheritance on this side Jordan near Jericho eastward. - Levi did not get an inheritance of land, because Levi was scattered throughout all the other tribes' lands to do the service of the Lord. Numbers 34:16-29 - The Lord named the men which shall divide the land: Eleazar the priest and Joshua the son of Nun, and one prince of every tribe, Caleb the son of Jephunneh for Judah and the rest by name. - These are they whom the Lord commanded to divide the inheritance unto the children of Israel in the land of Canaan: the princes of all the twelve tribes that divided the land to all the tribes. --- Topics: Clean and Unclean Meats · Esau and Edom · Idolatry · Sacrifice and Atonement · The Covenant · The Feasts of the Most High · The Priesthood · The Sabbath ← Numbers 27-30 · Numbers Study · Numbers 35-36 →

title: Numbers 35: The Cities of the Levites and the Cities of Refuge
text: ← Numbers 31-34 · Numbers Study · Deuteronomy 1-2 → Numbers 35: The Cities of the Levites and the Cities of Refuge Read the chapter → Numbers 35 Introduction This session covered Numbers 35-36 together with Deuteronomy 1-2, closing the book of Numbers and opening the book of Deuteronomy; the Deuteronomy chapters sit in their own chapter set. Numbers 35 gives the cities of the Levites and one of the more interesting subjects in the books of Moses, the cities of refuge, where the Most High taught Israel how to discern murder from manslaughter. Numbers 36 settles the inheritance of the daughters of Zelophehad and the law of marrying within the tribe. Numbers 35:1-2 - Moses commands the tribes to separate cities out of their own inheritance for the Levites to dwell in, with suburbs round about them. - The Levites needed cities inside every tribe's territory because the Most High took them from among the children of Israel as a gift, to do the service of the tabernacle of the congregation. Every tribe needed that service done among them, so the Levites had to be spread out through all the children of Israel. - The commandment was fulfilled when Israel came into the land: the heads of the fathers of the Levites came to Eleazar the priest and Joshua at Shiloh and claimed the cities the Lord commanded by the hand of Moses. Precepts: - Numbers 18:6 The Levites are taken from among the children of Israel as a gift to do the service of the tabernacle; that is why every tribe gave them cities. - Joshua 21:1-3 When Israel reached the land, the Levites claimed the commandment of Numbers 35 and the children of Israel gave them cities and suburbs out of their inheritance. Numbers 35:3-5 - The cities were for the Levites to dwell in, and the suburbs were for their cattle, their goods, and all their beasts. - The suburbs were measured out: a thousand cubits from the wall of the city round about, and two thousand cubits on the east, south, west, and north sides, with the city in the midst. Numbers 35:6-8 - Among the Levite cities six were set apart for refuge, appointed for the manslayer to flee there, with forty and two more added: forty and eight cities in all, given from every tribe according to its inheritance, many from them that had many and few from them that had few. - Why would the Lord permit a manslayer refuge? The Most High gave Moses the understanding of how to discern manslaughter from murder. For murder there was no refuge, but for manslaughter cities of refuge were given. - The law itself was already instituted in Exodus 21; Numbers 35 answers where the manslayer goes: the Most High appointed him a place to flee. Precepts: - Exodus 21:12-14 He that smiteth a man that he die is put to death; but for him that lay not in wait, God delivering him into his hand, a place was appointed to flee; the presumptuous slayer is taken even from the altar to die. Numbers 35:9-12 - Killeth any person unawares means he did not mean to do it; it was an accident that resulted in a death. Accidental deaths are of the Lord, beyond our control. - Refuge means a condition of being safe or sheltered from pursuit, danger, or trouble. The cities of refuge exist because the manslayer is being pursued: someone has the right to avenge the death of the one who was killed. - The city of refuge keeps the manslayer alive until he stands before the congregation in judgment, so the trial can discern between murder and manslaughter before the avenger reaches him. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 19:6 The avenger pursues the slayer while his heart is hot; without refuge he would overtake and slay a man who was not worthy of death. Numbers 35:13-15 - Six cities of refuge stood, three on this side Jordan and three in the land of Canaan, and they served the children of Israel, the stranger, and the sojourner among them alike. - The chapter lays out three categories when someone dies by the hand of another: he meant to hurt him but not kill him, yet he died, and that is murder; he hated him and killed him with premeditation, and that is murder; or he had no quarrel and never meant it, and that is manslaughter, not worthy of death. Numbers 35:16-18 - Smite him with an instrument of iron, with a stone, or with a hand weapon of wood so that he die, and he is a murderer: even if the intent was only to hurt him and not to kill him, if he dies, the judgment is death. - This is a precept for the street: the music culture glorifies slinging an iron, but the word says if you sling that iron and the brother dies, you are a murderer and your judgment is to die. Numbers 35:19 - The revenger of blood himself slays the murderer when he meets him; there was no refuge and no mercy for murder. - This is the law given to Israel at that time, an understanding of those judgments; it is not license for anyone to go about killing today. Numbers 35:20-21 - Laying of wait means he was lurking and stalking, waiting to catch him slipping because of hatred between them; that is premeditated murder. - Even without a weapon, smiting him in enmity with the hand so that he dies is murder; he that smote him shall surely be put to death. Numbers 35:22-24 - The law repeats its key words on purpose, the way legal statutes do, because the details decide the case: suddenly, without enmity, without laying of wait, and seeing him not. - Seeing him not matters because it is nearly impossible to kill a man by accident while looking straight at him; the victim was out of sight when the thing flew and struck him. - He was not his enemy and sought not his harm: there could be no documented past hatred, and he could not even have been seeking to harm him, since seeking only to harm still makes the death murder. Then the congregation judges between the slayer and the revenger of blood according to these judgments. Numbers 35:25 - Once the congregation clears him of murder, it delivers the slayer out of the hand of the revenger and restores him to his city of refuge; he still must abide there. - He stays within the city until the death of the high priest which was anointed with the holy oil, whoever held that office when the incident happened. Numbers 35:26-28 - If the slayer steps outside the borders of his city of refuge before that high priest dies and the revenger of blood finds him there and kills him, the revenger is not guilty of blood, because the slayer was instructed to remain within the borders. - After the death of the high priest the slayer returns to the land of his possession, and the avenger can no longer touch him. Numbers 35:29-30 - The murderer is put to death by the mouth of witnesses, plural: multiple people must testify, and their stories must match in the details for the murder to be established. - One witness alone cannot cause a man to die, because a single witness could lie in the interest of the avenger and put an innocent man to death. - The rule stood first for sins worthy of death and then had to become the principle for every matter: two or three witnesses establish any accusation of iniquity or sin. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 17:6 At the mouth of two or three witnesses shall he that is worthy of death be put to death; one witness is never enough. - Deuteronomy 19:15 One witness shall not rise up against a man for any iniquity or any sin; at the mouth of two or three witnesses is the matter established. Numbers 35:31-32 - The judges could take no satisfaction for the life of a murderer guilty of death, and no satisfaction for the manslayer to come home before the death of the high priest; a guilty man cannot buy himself off. - No matter who stands before the judge or what money is offered, if they are guilty of death they are guilty of death; a gift blinds the eyes of the wise and perverts the words of the righteous. - Israel's judges later fell into exactly this: they became covetous and took bribes to clear the guilty and turn aside the poor in the gate. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 16:18-19 Judges in all thy gates must judge with just judgment, respect no persons, and take no gift, for a gift doth blind the eyes of the wise. - Amos 5:12 The judges of Israel came to afflict the just and take a bribe, turning aside the poor in the gate from their right. Numbers 35:33-34 - Blood defileth the land, and the land cannot be cleansed of the blood shed in it but by the blood of him that shed it; the murderer who escapes his judgment leaves the land polluted. - That judgment was instituted back in the days of Noah, and Moses carried it forward in the statutes given to Israel, for the Lord himself dwells among the children of Israel. Precepts: - Genesis 9:6 Whoso sheddeth man's blood, by man shall his blood be shed; the only cleansing of the land is the blood of the shedder. Numbers 36: The Inheritance of the Daughters of Zelophehad Read the chapter → Numbers 36 Numbers 36:1-4 - The chief fathers of the families of Gilead of the tribe of Manasseh bring an issue rising out of what was already ruled in Numbers 27: when Zelophehad died in the wilderness with no sons, the Lord ruled that his inheritance pass to his daughters. - Their concern is real: if the daughters marry men of another tribe, their father's inheritance passes with them to the husband's tribe, and at the jubilee it is fixed to that tribe, so the tribe of Manasseh loses that land forever. Precepts: - Numbers 27:3-4 The daughters of Zelophehad pleaded that their father died in his own sin with no son, and asked why his name should be done away from among his family. - Numbers 27:6-8 The Lord ruled the daughters spoke right: if a man die and have no son, his inheritance passes to his daughter; that ruling set up the question of Numbers 36. Numbers 36:5-7 - The Most High affirms the tribe of the sons of Joseph: they have said well. The solution: the daughters of Zelophehad may marry whom they think best, only within the family of the tribe of their father. - The purpose is stated plainly: so shall not the inheritance of the children of Israel remove from tribe to tribe; the marriage boundary here was instituted because of land inheritance. Numbers 36:8-9 - Every daughter that possessed an inheritance had to marry within her father's tribe, so every man of Israel would enjoy the inheritance of his fathers and no inheritance would remove from one tribe to another. - The tribal restriction belonged to the time when Israel dwelt in the land; it existed because of inheritance. Today Israel has no inheritance in the lands of captivity, so the rule that still applies is marrying within the nation of Israel, not tribe-only marriage. - No one today knows his exact tribe with certainty; a Judahite could have been dropped off anywhere in the captivity. Without the history of Numbers 36, Tobit 4:12 gets twisted into a doctrine that a man may only marry his own tribe, and that is a heresy born of not knowing why the law was given. Precepts: - Tobit 4:12 Take a wife of the seed of thy fathers and not a strange woman; the seed-of-thy-fathers command still stands, and the tribe clause belonged to the inheritance law of Numbers 36. Numbers 36:10-13 - The daughters of Zelophehad did as the Lord commanded Moses: Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Noah married their father's brothers' sons, within the families of Manasseh, and their inheritance remained in the tribe of the family of their father. - These are the commandments and the judgments which the Lord commanded by the hand of Moses in the plains of Moab by Jordan near Jericho; with this verse the book of Numbers is completed. --- Topics: The Feasts of the Most High · The Priesthood ← Numbers 31-34 · Numbers Study · Deuteronomy 1-2 →

title: Numbers 7: The Offering of the Princes at the Dedication of the Altar
text: ← Numbers 3-6 · Numbers Study · Numbers 11-14 → Numbers 7: The Offering of the Princes at the Dedication of the Altar Read the chapter → Numbers 7 Introduction This reading circles back to catch Numbers 7 through 10: the offerings of the twelve princes at the dedication of the altar, the cleansing of the Levites and the years of their service, the passover of the second month and the cloud over the tabernacle, and the two silver trumpets with the order of Israel's journeys. This is a reading session, so the teaching is brief precepts given along the reading, together with the questions answered after it. Numbers 7:1-3 - On the day that Moses had fully set up the tabernacle and anointed and sanctified it with all the instruments thereof, the princes of Israel, heads of the house of their fathers and over them that were numbered, brought their offering before the Lord: six covered wagons and twelve oxen, a wagon for two of the princes and for each one an ox. Numbers 7:4-9 - The Lord told Moses to take the wagons and oxen for the service of the tabernacle of the congregation and give them to the Levites, to every man according to his service: two wagons and four oxen to the sons of Gershon, and four wagons and eight oxen to the sons of Merari, under the hand of Ithamar the son of Aaron the priest. - Unto the sons of Kohath he gave none, because the service of the sanctuary belonging unto them was that they should bear upon their shoulders. Numbers 4 shows what that bearing was: Aaron and his sons covered the ark and the vessels first, and after that the sons of Kohath came to bear them, not touching any holy thing lest they die. - The Kohathites were in charge of carrying the sanctuary to and fro, and the reading further on shows them doing it once the camp moved. Precepts: - Numbers 4:4-6 The service of the sons of Kohath is about the most holy things; Aaron and his sons take down the covering vail and cover the ark before the camp sets forward. - Numbers 4:15 When Aaron has made an end of covering the sanctuary, the sons of Kohath come to bear it, but they shall not touch any holy thing, lest they die. Numbers 7:10-11 - The princes offered for the dedicating of the altar in the day that it was anointed, and the Lord said unto Moses, they shall offer their offering, each prince on his day. Numbers 7:12-17 - Nahshon the son of Amminadab of the tribe of Judah offered the first day. The charger is simply a plate or a platter, and the bowl and the golden spoon carried the fine flour mingled with oil and the incense. Numbers 7:18-23 - On the second day Nethaneel the son of Zuar, prince of Issachar, offered. Each prince on his day brought the very same offering as Nahshon, because this was the order that they had to do. - The twelve days went in the order of the camps: Judah, Issachar, Zebulun, Reuben, Simeon, Gad, Ephraim, Manasseh, Benjamin, Dan, Asher, and Naphtali, closing with Ahira the son of Enan on the twelfth day. Numbers 7:84-88 - This was the dedication of the altar in the day when it was anointed by the princes of Israel, and the totals are summed: twelve chargers of silver, twelve silver bowls, twelve spoons of gold, and all the bullocks, rams, lambs, and goats for the burnt offering, the sin offering, and the peace offerings. - Israel does not do the animal sacrifices anymore. When Christ came into the world he said, sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not; the Most High had no pleasure in them, because the people's minds were not changed when they offered them, and Christ was the ultimate sacrifice who took away the first that he might establish the second. - There is also no tabernacle today to do them at. The sacrifices had to be done at the tabernacle, and Israel is scattered everywhere in captivity, not able to go to Jerusalem to a temple that is not standing. Precepts: - Hebrews 10:5-9 When Christ cometh into the world he saith, sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not; he taketh away the first, that he may establish the second. Numbers 7:89 - When Moses was gone into the tabernacle of the congregation to speak with him, that is Moses going in to speak with the Most High. The voice came from off the mercy seat that was upon the ark of testimony, from between the two cherubims, exactly where the Lord said he would meet and commune with him. Precepts: - Exodus 25:21-22 There I will meet with thee, and I will commune with thee from above the mercy seat, from between the two cherubims. Numbers 8: The Levites Taken Instead of the Firstborn Read the chapter → Numbers 8 Numbers 8:1-4 - Aaron lighted the seven lamps to give light over against the candlestick, as the Lord commanded Moses; and the candlestick was of beaten gold, made according unto the pattern which the Lord had shewed Moses. Numbers 8:5-14 - The Levites were taken from among the children of Israel and cleansed: water of purifying sprinkled upon them, all their flesh shaven, and their clothes washed. - The whole assembly of the children of Israel was gathered, the children of Israel put their hands upon the Levites, and Aaron offered the Levites before the Lord for an offering of the children of Israel, with the two bullocks for a sin offering and a burnt offering to make an atonement for the Levites. - Thus were the Levites separated from among the children of Israel: and the Levites shall be mine. Numbers 8:15-19 - After the cleansing the Levites went in to do the service of the tabernacle of the congregation. Mark the word instead in verse 16: instead of such as open every womb, instead of the firstborn of all the children of Israel, the Most High took the Levites unto himself. - At the first, all the firstborn of all the tribes were sanctified for the office, from the day the Lord smote every firstborn in the land of Egypt. Here he makes it clear again, as he has done in multiple places, that the one tribe of Levi now performs the service of the tabernacle. - The Levites were given as a gift to Aaron and to his sons, to do the service of the children of Israel and to make an atonement for them, that there be no plague among the children of Israel when they come nigh unto the sanctuary. Precepts: - Exodus 13:1-2 Sanctify unto me all the firstborn, whatsoever openeth the womb among the children of Israel; that was the office before the Levites were taken instead. Numbers 8:20-22 - Moses, Aaron, and all the congregation of the children of Israel did to the Levites according unto all that the Lord commanded Moses; the Levites were purified, and after that they went in to do their service in the tabernacle of the congregation before Aaron and before his sons. Numbers 8:23-26 - The service of the Levites had an age: from twenty and five years old and upward they went in to wait upon the service of the tabernacle of the congregation, and up until that point they were not allowed to do the service. - From the age of fifty years they ceased waiting upon the service; it ran from twenty five to fifty. After fifty they ministered with their brethren in the tabernacle to keep the charge, but did no service. Numbers 9: The Second Passover and the Cloud over the Tabernacle Read the chapter → Numbers 9 Numbers 9:1-5 - In the first month of the second year after they were come out of the land of Egypt, the Lord commanded that the children of Israel keep the passover at his appointed season, the fourteenth day of the month at even; and they kept it in the wilderness of Sinai, according to all that the Lord commanded Moses. - The passover carried its rites and its ceremonies: there were things they had to sacrifice and do according to all the ordinances of it, to keep everything in order for the congregation. Numbers 9:6-8 - Certain men were defiled by the dead body of a man, so they could not keep the passover on that day. The law had already put out of the camp whosoever was defiled by the dead, so they could not come in with the congregation to make their offering. - They asked, wherefore are we kept back, that we may not offer an offering of the Lord in his appointed season? And Moses said, stand still, and I will hear what the Lord will command concerning you. Precepts: - Numbers 5:1-2 Put out of the camp every leper, every one that hath an issue, and whosoever is defiled by the dead; that is why those men could not come in. Numbers 9:9-12 - The answer came: if any man be unclean by reason of a dead body, or be in a journey afar off, he shall still keep the passover unto the Lord, on the fourteenth day of the second month at even, eating it with unleavened bread and bitter herbs. - Defilement by the dead and traveling afar off were the only two reasons given to miss the appointed day, and even then the passover was kept the following month, not neglected. - The same holds today: many drive trucks and work jobs they cannot get off, and the Most High understands the captivity, but that does not mean you neglect the passover; keep it the second month if it is possible. Numbers 9:13 - But the man that is clean, and is not in a journey, and forbeareth to keep the passover, shall be cut off from among his people; he brought not the offering of the Lord in his appointed season, and that man shall bear his sin. - This speaks to the one that likes to make excuses. There were no excuses then without being cut off, and there are none now when the holy days come around; if the reason is not according to the bible, it does not stand. Numbers 9:14 - The stranger that sojourns with Israel and will keep the passover keeps it according to the ordinance of the passover and the manner thereof: one ordinance both for the stranger and for him that was born in the land. - The stranger here is not unbelieving family; it is one of another nation that dwelt among Israel. Even the nations among us had to keep the laws just as we did; they were not getting a pass around us. Numbers 9:15-16 - On the day that the tabernacle was reared up the cloud covered it, and at even there was upon the tabernacle as it were the appearance of fire until the morning. - That cloud is the chariot of the Most High: he maketh the clouds his chariot, and that is what sat over the top of the tabernacle. Precepts: - Psalms 104:3 He maketh the clouds his chariot; the cloud over the tabernacle was his chariot. Numbers 9:17-23 - When the cloud was taken up from the tabernacle, the children of Israel journeyed; and in the place where the cloud abode, there they pitched their tents. Wherever the chariot went, Israel got up and followed it, the same way it led them across the Red Sea. - Whether it were two days, or a month, or a year that the cloud tarried upon the tabernacle, they abode in their tents and journeyed not; and when it was taken up, they journeyed, whether by day or by night. That is how they knew where they needed to stay and when to move. - At the commandment of the Lord they rested in the tents, and at the commandment of the Lord they journeyed; they kept the charge of the Lord by the hand of Moses. Precepts: - Exodus 40:36 When the cloud was taken up from over the tabernacle, the children of Israel went onward in all their journeys; Numbers revisits what Exodus recorded. Numbers 10: The Silver Trumpets and the Order of the Journeys Read the chapter → Numbers 10 Numbers 10:1-4 - Two trumpets of silver, of a whole piece, were made for the calling of the assembly and for the journeying of the camps. When they blew with both, all the assembly gathered to the door of the tabernacle of the congregation; when they blew but with one, the princes, the heads of the thousands of Israel, gathered. - There were different ways the Levites had to blow the trumpets: one way to call the whole congregation, another for just the leaders, and another to let everybody know it was war. Numbers 10:5-6 - When ye blow an alarm, the camps that lie on the east parts go forward first: that was Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun, under the standard of the camp of Judah. - When the alarm is blown the second time, the camps that lie on the south side take their journey: that was Reuben, Simeon, and Gad. The alarm for the journeys was short bursts. Precepts: - Numbers 2:3-7 On the east side toward the rising of the sun pitch the standard of the camp of Judah, with Issachar and Zebulun beside him. - Numbers 2:10-14 On the south side is the standard of the camp of Reuben, with Simeon and Gad beside him. Numbers 10:7-9 - When the congregation is to be gathered together, ye shall blow, but ye shall not sound an alarm: a longer sound, a different tone from the short alarm bursts, letting everybody know this is the gathering. - If the trumpet give an uncertain sound, who shall prepare himself to the battle? The sound had to be certain, or people would sit still or try to gather when it was time to go to war. - The sons of Aaron the priests blew the trumpets, an ordinance for ever throughout your generations. In war in your land against the enemy that oppresseth you, blow an alarm, and ye shall be remembered before the Lord your God and saved from your enemies. As Israel marched through the wilderness against the nations, the Most High remembered them and destroyed the enemy, as long as they were keeping the commandments. Precepts: - 1 Corinthians 14:8 For if the trumpet give an uncertain sound, who shall prepare himself to the battle? Numbers 10:10 - The trumpets were also blown in the day of your gladness, in your solemn days, and in the beginnings of your months, over the burnt offerings and the sacrifices of the peace offerings, for a memorial before your God. - The feast days must be a glad moment even to this day. Coming to congregate with your brothers and sisters grudgingly is one of the reasons Israel went into captivity: we were not glad to do what the Most High said. - The beginnings of the months are marked by the moon: the Most High made the moon to serve in her season for a declaration of times, a light that decreaseth in her perfection and then increaseth in her changing, and the month is called after her name. When the light is full again, that is the new moon. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 43:6-8 The moon declares the times and seasons and is the sign of feasts; her cycle marks the beginnings of the months. Numbers 10:11-13 - On the twentieth day of the second month in the second year the cloud was taken up from off the tabernacle of the testimony, and the children of Israel took their journeys out of the wilderness of Sinai; and the cloud rested in the wilderness of Paran. - The testimony is the commandments of the Most High. If the children keep his covenant and his testimony, their children shall sit upon the throne for evermore; and it is his testimony, not our own testimony, that is righteous and very faithful and that changes the people. Precepts: - Psalms 132:12 If thy children will keep my covenant and my testimony, their children shall also sit upon thy throne for evermore. - Psalms 119:138 Thy testimonies that thou hast commanded are righteous and very faithful. - Psalms 19:7 The testimony of the LORD is sure, making wise the simple; it is the laws of the Most High that must be taught, for his laws change the people, not our testimony. Numbers 10:14-28 - In the first place went the standard of the camp of the children of Judah. The standard is the banner, like the flags of the different tribes held up in the schools today. - The order of the march is given camp by camp: Judah with Issachar and Zebulun first; the tabernacle taken down and borne by the sons of Gershon and Merari; then Reuben with Simeon and Gad; then the Kohathites bearing the sanctuary, and the other did set up the tabernacle against they came; then Ephraim with Manasseh and Benjamin; and last Dan with Asher and Naphtali, the rereward of all the camps. - The tabernacle went ahead so that it would be set up before the whole congregation of the twelve tribes arrived where they were going. This was the order of the armies whenever they got up and moved. Numbers 10:29-32 - Moses said unto Hobab the son of Raguel the Midianite, his kinsman by marriage, we are journeying unto the place of which the Lord said, I will give it you: come thou with us, and we will do thee good.
