Deuteronomy 23:4-6 - The reason for the ban: Ammon and Moab met not Israel with bread and with water in the way when they came forth out of Egypt, and hired Balaam the son of Beor of Pethor to curse them. - The history is in Numbers: Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab, was sore afraid because the people were many, and sent the elders of Moab and Midian with the rewards of divination to call Balaam to curse Israel. - Nevertheless the Lord thy God would not hearken unto Balaam, but turned the curse into a blessing, because the Lord thy God loveth thee; therefore Israel was never to seek their peace nor their prosperity. Precepts: - Numbers 22:2-7 Balak king of Moab sent unto Balaam the son of Beor with the rewards of divination to curse Israel, for they were too mighty for him. Deuteronomy 23:7-8 - Thou shalt not abhor an Edomite, for he is thy brother: this was a temporary law. Edom broke the brotherly covenant; he did pursue his brother with the sword, did cast off all pity, his anger did tear perpetually, and he kept his wrath for ever. - Edom's hatred is a perpetual hatred: he shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword in the time of their calamity, and as we see our people being slaughtered by Esau, that anger continues even to this very day. - Thou shalt not abhor an Egyptian, because thou wast a stranger in his land: many brothers and sisters do not want to deal with that part and only want to deal with Edom, but Egypt likewise came under judgment for the violence against the children of Judah, because they shed innocent blood in their land. Precepts: - Amos 1:9 Tyrus delivered up the whole captivity to Edom and remembered not the brotherly covenant. - Amos 1:11 Edom did pursue his brother with the sword, cast off all pity, and his anger did tear perpetually. - Ezekiel 35:5 Edom had a perpetual hatred and shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword in the time of their calamity. - Joel 3:19 Egypt shall be a desolation and Edom a desolate wilderness, for the violence against the children of Judah, because they shed innocent blood in their land. Deuteronomy 23:9 - When the host goeth forth against thine enemies, then keep thee from every wicked thing: when Israel went to war, they were to keep themselves from every wicked thing. - The example is Achan: Israel was warned in any wise to keep from the accursed thing, lest they make the camp of Israel a curse and trouble it, and Achan the son of Carmi of the tribe of Judah took of the accursed thing, the Babylonish garment, and the anger of the Lord was kindled against the children of Israel. - Because of that trespass Israel could not stand before their enemies but turned their backs, for they were accursed; the Lord would not be with them any more except they destroyed the accursed from among them, and Achan and his family and all that belonged to him were destroyed and burned, and a heap set upon them, because he broke the covenant. Precepts: - Joshua 6:18 Keep yourselves from the accursed thing, lest ye make the camp of Israel a curse and trouble it. - Joshua 7:1 Achan took of the accursed thing, and the anger of the Lord was kindled against the children of Israel. - Joshua 7:11-13 Israel hath sinned and taken of the accursed thing; therefore they could not stand before their enemies until the accursed was destroyed from among them. Deuteronomy 23:10-11 - Any man that was not clean by reason of uncleanness that chanceth him by night went abroad out of the camp; when evening came he washed himself with water, and when the sun was down he came into the camp again. Precepts: - Leviticus 15:16 The law of the uncleanness that chanceth a man by night: he shall wash all his flesh in water and be unclean until the even. Deuteronomy 23:12-14 - There was a place without the camp to go forth abroad, and a paddle upon the weapon to dig and cover that which cometh from thee: to make it plain, if you had to ease yourself, you went outside the camp to do it. - Verse 14 explains why: the Lord thy God walketh in the midst of thy camp, to deliver thee and to give up thine enemies before thee; therefore shall thy camp be holy, that he see no unclean thing in thee and turn away from thee. - That is what we just read happened with Achan the son of Carmi: he brought an unclean thing into the camp, and the Most High turned from Israel in battle. - God says he is in the midst of Israel and none else; the Lord would go before us and fight our battles, and that is why he wanted no unclean thing in the camp, for we are holy and the camp was to be holy. Precepts: - Joel 2:27 Ye shall know that I am in the midst of Israel, and my people shall never be ashamed. - Deuteronomy 1:30 The Lord your God which goeth before you, he shall fight for you, according to all that he did for you in Egypt. Deuteronomy 23:17-18 - There shall be no whore of the daughters of Israel, nor a sodomite of the sons of Israel. A sodomite is the biblical word for a homosexual, and the whore of the daughters of Israel here is the same sin in the daughters, what we today would call lesbians. - There is a heavy push in the world today for our men to be homosexuals and our sisters to be lesbians; popular entertainers are used to influence the younger generation to sin, just as young rappers were dressed in skirts and dresses until it became cool to be gay. - This is what we have to bring our people back from: by being an example, the men being an example, the sisters being an example in the way they dress and carry themselves, and by having families, reinstituting a father and a mother in the divine order the Most High God established. - Thou shalt not bring the hire of a whore or the price of a dog into the house of the Lord thy God, for even both these are abomination unto the Lord. Without are dogs: that is not the four-legged barking kind, but the other nations. - Christ told a woman of another nation it is not meet to take the children's bread and cast it to dogs, and she said, Truth, Lord; and four-legged dogs did not pierce Christ's hands and feet, for the dogs that compassed him were the other nations, in that case the Romans. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 41:17 Be ashamed of whoredom before father and mother. - 1 Corinthians 11:3 The divine order the Most High established: the head of every man is Christ, and the head of the woman is the man. - Revelation 22:14-15 Blessed are they that do his commandments; for without are dogs, and sorcerers, and whoremongers. - Matthew 15:24-27 Christ, sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel, called the woman of another nation a dog, and she said, Truth, Lord. - Psalms 22:16 Dogs have compassed me; they pierced my hands and my feet: the other nations, the Romans, pierced Christ. Deuteronomy 23:19-20 - Thou shalt not lend upon usury to thy brother, usury of money, of victuals, of any thing: when you read the definition of usury, that is interest. We are not to charge interest to each other when we loan each other anything. - Unto a stranger thou mayest lend upon usury: the blessing is that Israel shall lend unto many nations and shall not borrow, the head and not the tail. That is our rightful place on the earth when we keep these commandments: we should lend unto them and may take usury upon what we lend to them, but we should not do that to our own people. - The same law was already read in Exodus: if thou lend money to any of my people that is poor by thee, thou shalt not be to him as an usurer. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 28:12-13 Thou shalt lend unto many nations and shalt not borrow, and the Lord shall make thee the head and not the tail. - Exodus 22:25 If thou lend money to any of my people that is poor by thee, thou shalt not be to him as an usurer. Deuteronomy 24: Divorcement, Pledges, and Mercy to the Poor Read the chapter → Deuteronomy 24 Deuteronomy 24:1 - When a man hath taken a wife and she find no favour in his eyes because he hath found some uncleanness in her, then let him write her a bill of divorcement, give it in her hand, and send her out of his house. - Christ magnified this law: when the Pharisees asked why Moses then commanded to give a writing of divorcement, he said, Moses because of the hardness of your hearts suffered you to put away your wives, but from the beginning it was not so. - Whosoever shall put away his wife, except it be for fornication, and shall marry another, committeth adultery; and whoso marrieth her which is put away doth commit adultery. Precepts: - Matthew 19:3-9 What God hath joined together, let not man put asunder; Moses suffered divorce for the hardness of your hearts, but from the beginning it was not so. Deuteronomy 24:3-4 - If the latter husband hate her and write her a bill of divorcement, or if the latter husband die, her former husband which sent her away may not take her again to be his wife after that she is defiled, for that is abomination before the Lord. - The question is whether a woman who leaves her husband and becomes another man's wife can be joined to the first again; the prophet asks the same thing: shall he return unto her again? shall not that land be greatly polluted? Precepts: - Jeremiah 3:1 If a man put away his wife and she become another man's, shall he return unto her again? shall not that land be greatly polluted? Deuteronomy 24:5 - When a man hath taken a new wife, he shall not go out to war, neither shall he be charged with any business; he shall be free at home one year and shall cheer up his wife which he hath taken. Make it plain: the first year, stay at home and make a baby. - Husband and wife render due benevolence to one another; benevolence means good, it is a good thing. - The war laws give the same understanding: the man that had betrothed a wife and not taken her was sent back to his house, lest he die in the battle and another man take her, for the Lord is the one that goeth with the host to fight against the enemies. Precepts: - Genesis 3:16 Thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee. - 1 Corinthians 7:2-3 Let every man have his own wife, and let the husband render unto the wife due benevolence, and likewise also the wife unto the husband. - Deuteronomy 20:1 When thou goest out to battle, be not afraid, for the Lord thy God is with thee. - Deuteronomy 20:4-5 The Lord your God is he that goeth with you, to fight for you against your enemies, to save you. - Deuteronomy 20:7 What man hath betrothed a wife and not taken her? let him go and return unto his house, lest he die in the battle and another man take her. Deuteronomy 24:6 - No man shall take the nether or the upper millstone to pledge, for he taketh a man's life to pledge. The millstone is a tool for grinding meal: the manna was gathered and ground in mills or beaten in a mortar and baked into cakes. - Taking a man's tool takes away his living, like somebody stealing your tools so you cannot make a living. It is better that they steal your money, because with your tools you can go back and make more money. Precepts: - Numbers 11:7-8 The people gathered the manna and ground it in mills, or beat it in a mortar, and made cakes of it. - Ecclesiasticus 34:22 He that taketh away his neighbour's living slayeth him. Deuteronomy 24:9 - Remember what the Lord thy God did unto Miriam by the way, after that ye were come forth out of Egypt: Miriam and Aaron spake against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman whom he had married, and Miriam was not supposed to be speaking against Moses. - The anger of the Lord was kindled against them, the cloud departed from off the tabernacle, and behold, Miriam became leprous, white as snow. - The Lord said, if her father had but spit in her face, should she not be ashamed seven days? Had her father chastised her and rebuked her sharply, she would not have had that tongue. That is for a lot of our sisters today who do not have that understanding. Precepts: - Numbers 12:1 Miriam and Aaron spake against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman whom he had married. - Numbers 12:9-10 The anger of the Lord was kindled, the cloud departed from off the tabernacle, and Miriam became leprous, white as snow. - Numbers 12:14 If her father had but spit in her face, should she not be ashamed seven days? Deuteronomy 24:10-13 - When thou dost lend thy brother any thing, thou shalt not go into his house to fetch his pledge; stand abroad, and let the man bring the pledge out unto thee. - If the man be poor, thou shalt not sleep with his pledge; deliver him the pledge again when the sun goeth down, that he may sleep in his own raiment and bless thee, and it shall be righteousness unto thee before the Lord thy God. - The law was already given: if thou at all take thy neighbour's raiment to pledge, deliver it by that the sun goeth down, for that is his covering only, and when he crieth unto the Most High, he will hear, for he is gracious. - The history shows how wicked we were to each other: Israel laid themselves down upon clothes laid to pledge by every altar, stacking up people's raiment like pallets and drinking the wine of the condemned in the house of their god, instead of returning the pledge before the sun went down as righteousness. That is why the Lord was judging us. Precepts: - Exodus 22:26-27 If thou take thy neighbour's raiment to pledge, deliver it by that the sun goeth down, for that is his covering only. - Amos 2:6-8 For three transgressions of Israel and for four: they lay themselves down upon clothes laid to pledge by every altar. Deuteronomy 24:16 - The fathers shall not be put to death for the children, neither shall the children be put to death for the fathers: every man shall be put to death for his own sin. - The example: as soon as the kingdom was confirmed in Amaziah's hand, he slew his servants which had slain the king his father, but the children of the murderers he slew not, according unto that which is written in the book of the law of Moses. - The soul that sinneth, it shall die: the son shall not bear the iniquity of the father, neither shall the father bear the iniquity of the son. Precepts: - 2 Kings 14:5-6 Amaziah slew his father's murderers, but their children he slew not, according to that which is written in the book of the law of Moses. - Ezekiel 18:20 The soul that sinneth, it shall die; the son shall not bear the iniquity of the father. Deuteronomy 25: Just Judgment, the Brother's Duty, and Amalek Read the chapter → Deuteronomy 25 Deuteronomy 25:1-3 - If there be a controversy between men, the judges justify the righteous and condemn the wicked; the wicked man worthy to be beaten was made to lie down and be beaten before the judge's face, according to his fault, by a certain number. - Forty stripes may he give him, and not exceed, lest thy brother should seem vile unto thee. Paul recounted receiving that beating under this law. Precepts: - 2 Corinthians 11:24-25 Of the Jews five times received I forty stripes save one; Paul recounted how he was beaten. Deuteronomy 25:4 - Thou shalt not muzzle the ox when he treadeth out the corn: the corn is the reward for the ox. - Paul applies this verse to how the elders are treated: let the elders that rule well be counted worthy of double honour, especially they who labour in the word and doctrine, for the labourer is worthy of his reward. - Giving double honour is not just saying the words to the leadership; it is true respect and reverence toward the leadership that labours in this word and doctrine. Precepts: - 1 Timothy 5:17-18 The elders that labour in the word and doctrine are worthy of double honour, for thou shalt not muzzle the ox that treadeth out the corn. Deuteronomy 25:5-10 - If brethren dwell together and one of them die and have no child, the wife of the dead was not to marry without unto a stranger; her husband's brother took her to wife, and the firstborn she bare succeeded in the name of the dead brother, that his name be not put out of Israel. - Check this out: this is no longer the law, so do not try to use it as an excuse toward your brother's wife. It stood for the name not being put out because of the land inheritance in Israel. - The man who refused was called before the elders; his brother's wife loosed his shoe from off his foot, spat in his face, and answered, So shall it be done unto that man that will not build up his brother's house; and his name was called in Israel, The house of him that hath his shoe loosed. Precepts: - Genesis 38:6-10 Onan refused to raise up seed to his brother Er, and the thing which he did displeased the Lord. - Ruth 3:10-13 Boaz answered Ruth that he would perform the kinsman's part, but there was a kinsman nearer than he. - Ruth 4:1-6 The nearer kinsman could not redeem it, lest he mar his own inheritance, and the right passed to Boaz. - Matthew 22:23-30 The Sadducees put to Christ the case of seven brethren who under this law took one wife. Deuteronomy 25:17-19 - Remember what Amalek did unto thee by the way, when ye were come forth out of Egypt: he met thee by the way and smote the hindmost of thee, all that were feeble behind thee, when thou wast faint and weary, and he feared not God. - Israel was later commanded through Samuel to repay it: I remember that which Amalek did to Israel; now go and smite Amalek, and utterly destroy all that they have, and spare them not. - At Rephidim, where Amalek first came and fought with Israel, the Lord told Moses to write this for a memorial in a book and rehearse it in the ears of Joshua, for the Lord hath sworn that the Lord will have war with Amalek from generation to generation; and that war is still going on even to this day. Precepts: - 1 Samuel 15:2-3 I remember that which Amalek did to Israel; now go and smite Amalek, and utterly destroy all that they have. - Exodus 17:8 Then came Amalek, and fought with Israel in Rephidim. - Exodus 17:14-16 Write this for a memorial in a book, for the Lord will have war with Amalek from generation to generation. Deuteronomy 26: The Firstfruits Confession and a Peculiar People Read the chapter → Deuteronomy 26 Deuteronomy 26:5 - The firstfruits confession spoken before the Lord begins: a Syrian ready to perish was my father, and he went down into Egypt and sojourned there with a few, and became there a nation, great, mighty, and populous. - The father is Jacob: Jacob fled into the country of Syria, and Israel served for a wife, and for a wife he kept sheep, as we read in Genesis. Precepts: - Hosea 12:12 Jacob fled into the country of Syria, and Israel served for a wife, and for a wife he kept sheep. Deuteronomy 26:6 - The Egyptians evil entreated us, and afflicted us, and laid upon us hard bondage. - There arose up a new king over Egypt which knew not Joseph; fearing that the children of Israel were more and mightier than they, Egypt set over them taskmasters to afflict them with their burdens, and they built for Pharaoh the treasure cities, Pithom and Raamses. Precepts: - Exodus 1:8-11 A new king which knew not Joseph set taskmasters over Israel to afflict them with their burdens, and they built for Pharaoh treasure cities. Deuteronomy 26:16-17 - This day the Lord thy God hath commanded thee to do these statutes and judgments: thou shalt keep and do them with all thine heart and with all thy soul. - Thou hast avouched the Lord this day to be thy God: avouch means affirm or confirm. We confirm, thou art our God and we are going to be thy people, walking in his ways and keeping his statutes, his commandments, and his judgments, and hearkening unto his voice. Deuteronomy 26:18 - The Lord hath avouched thee this day to be his peculiar people, as he hath promised thee: the Lord hath chosen Jacob unto himself, and Israel for his peculiar treasure. - Ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people, that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light: we were called out of our sins into the light, and the light is the commandments and the law. - Which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God: we were called by other names, African American, Dominican, Negro, but now we are coming into the understanding that we are actually the children of Israel. Precepts: - Psalms 135:4 The Lord hath chosen Jacob unto himself, and Israel for his peculiar treasure. - 1 Peter 2:9-10 A chosen generation, a royal priesthood, a peculiar people, which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God. - Proverbs 6:23 The commandment is a lamp, and the law is light: the marvellous light we were called into. - Exodus 19:5-6 If ye will obey my voice and keep my covenant, ye shall be a peculiar treasure unto me above all people. Deuteronomy 26:19 - And to make thee high above all nations which he hath made, in praise, and in name, and in honour, and that thou mayest be an holy people unto the Lord thy God, as he hath spoken. - This is the same word given earlier in Deuteronomy, among other scriptures: thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God, chosen to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 7:6 Thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God, chosen to be a special people unto himself, above all people upon the face of the earth. --- Topics: Clean and Unclean Meats · Esau and Edom · Sacrifice and Atonement · The Covenant · The Feasts of the Most High · The Priesthood ← Deuteronomy 19-22 · Deuteronomy Study · Deuteronomy 27-30 →

title: Deuteronomy 27: Write the Law upon Stones
text: ← Deuteronomy 23-26 · Deuteronomy Study · Deuteronomy 31-34 → Deuteronomy 27: Write the Law upon Stones Read the chapter → Deuteronomy 27 Introduction This session covers Deuteronomy 27 through 30, the heart of the covenant. Chapter 27 commands Israel to write the law very plainly upon great stones and sets half the tribes on mount Gerizim to bless and half on mount Ebal to curse, with the people answering Amen to every curse. Chapter 28 lays out the blessings for obedience and the curses for disobedience, the curses that identify who the true Israelites are to this day. Chapter 29 is the covenant made in the land of Moab, made not only with those who stood there that day but with us who were not there. Chapter 30 is the goodness of the Most High: the way back out of the curses, to call them to mind in captivity, return, keep the commandments, and choose life. Deuteronomy 27:2-3 - On the day Israel passed over Jordan into the land, they were to set up great stones, plaster them with plaster, and write upon them all the words of this law. - Here is the difference between the truth and Islam and every other religion. The stone is not to be worshipped or thought to be a god; you set it up and put the laws on it so you can remember the laws. Deuteronomy 27:4-8 - The stones were to be set up in mount Ebal, and an altar of whole stones built there unto the Most High; no iron tool was to be lifted upon them. - Burnt offerings and peace offerings were offered there, and the people were to eat and rejoice before the Most High. - Thou shalt write upon the stones all the words of this law very plainly. That is what the Most High wants remembered most: not the stone itself, but the law written on it. Deuteronomy 27:9-10 - Moses and the priests the Levites told all Israel: this day thou art become the people of the Lord thy God; therefore obey his voice and do his commandments and statutes. - Even the other nations' own books witness to it. The Martyrdom of Man says that "God made all men equal" is a fine sounding phrase but not a scientific fact, and that those who outlive hardships and sufferings which fall on all alike owe their existence to some superiority not only of body but of mind. - There is no way we could have lasted this long through what we have been through if we were not the people of the Most High: thousands of years run out of the homeland, living among our enemies, put on ships and transported all over the world, and still surviving from 1492 on up here in Babylon the great. Deuteronomy 27:11-13 - Moses charged the people that day: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph (which is Ephraim and Manasseh), and Benjamin were to stand upon mount Gerizim to bless the people. - Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali were to stand upon mount Ebal to curse. Half the tribes stood on one side and half on the other, one saying one thing and the other answering. Deuteronomy 27:14-15 - The Levites were to speak with a loud voice unto all the men of Israel: cursed be the man that maketh any graven or molten image, an abomination unto the Most High, the work of the hands of the craftsman, and putteth it in a secret place. - And all the people shall answer and say, Amen. Every curse that follows carried that same answer from the whole congregation. Deuteronomy 27:16 - Cursed be he that setteth light by his father or his mother. Setting light by them means disrespecting your parents and not obeying them. Deuteronomy 27:17 - Cursed be he that removeth his neighbour's landmark. Every man in Israel was allotted a certain plot of land for his inheritance individually. - If you moved that landmark trying to make your own land bigger, the Most High says cursed be upon you. The allotments are recorded in Joshua and in Numbers 27, where the inheritance laws are given. Deuteronomy 27:18 - Cursed be he that maketh the blind to wander out of the way. Do not mistreat those we call the disabled. Deuteronomy 27:19 - Cursed be he that perverteth the judgment of the stranger, fatherless, and widow. - This goes back to Deuteronomy chapter 1, where the judges were charged to judge righteously between every man and his brother and the stranger with him, and to respect no persons in judgment. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 1:16-17 Judge righteously between every man and his brother and the stranger; ye shall not respect persons in judgment. Deuteronomy 27:20 - Cursed be he that lieth with his father's wife, because he uncovereth his father's skirt. That is nasty stuff, and the curse of the whole congregation stood against it. Deuteronomy 27:21 - Cursed be he that lieth with any manner of beast. Bestiality is the practice of Esau, and Israel was cursed for touching it. Deuteronomy 27:22 - Cursed be he that lieth with his sister, the daughter of his father or the daughter of his mother. - This goes back to Leviticus chapter 18, where the nakedness laws were first given. Precepts: - Leviticus 18:9 The nakedness of thy sister thou shalt not uncover; the curse repeats the law already given. Deuteronomy 27:23-24 - Cursed be he that lieth with his mother in law, and all the people shall say, Amen. - Cursed be he that smiteth his neighbour secretly, and all the people shall say, Amen. Deuteronomy 27:25 - Cursed be he that taketh reward to slay an innocent person. That is your hitman right there in verse 25: taking payment to kill the innocent puts you under the curse. Deuteronomy 27:26 - Cursed be he that confirmeth not all the words of this law to do them. At that time this encompassed everything, including the law of sacrifice. - It also applies to us today, because sacrifice is alive and well; it just transformed. We still sacrifice, only it is no longer animals but our bodies. - Our bodies must be holy and without blemish before the Most High, because the law says you cannot bring anything with blemishes into the house of the Lord. If your sacrifice is not holy and acceptable, the Son is not taking you to present you before the Father. Christ magnified the law, as Isaiah says. Precepts: - Romans 12:1 Present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God; the animal no longer suffices, the sacrifice is your body. - Isaiah 42:21 He will magnify the law and make it honourable; Christ magnified the law, he did not do away with the sacrifice principle. Deuteronomy 28: The Blessings and the Curses That Identify Israel Read the chapter → Deuteronomy 28 Deuteronomy 28:1 - If thou shalt hearken diligently unto the voice of the Lord thy God to observe and to do all his commandments, the Most High will set thee on high above all nations of the earth. - Diligent means characterized by steady, earnest, and energetic effort. You have to be on fire for the laws of the Most High, standing fast. - You cannot be one foot in and one foot out, lukewarm, yawning through the classes. You cannot be tired of the word of the Lord; be excited to hear it. Deuteronomy 28:2 - All these blessings shall come on thee and overtake thee, if thou shalt hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God. Hearken means to listen. Deuteronomy 28:3-6 - Blessed in the city and blessed in the field; blessed shall be the fruit of thy body, which is your children, and the fruit of thy ground and cattle. - Blessed shall be thy basket and thy store: that is going into your surplus. - Blessed when thou comest in and blessed when thou goest out: it is twofold, but it is going into coming in and out of Jerusalem. Deuteronomy 28:7-14 - The enemies that rise up against thee shall flee before thee seven ways; the blessing is commanded on thy storehouses and on all thou settest thine hand unto. - The Most High shall establish thee an holy people unto himself, and all the people of the earth shall see that thou art called by the name of the Lord and be afraid of thee. - Thou shalt lend unto many nations and not borrow; the Lord shall make thee the head and not the tail, above only and not beneath, if thou hearken to the commandments and turn not aside after other gods. - Isaiah sums up Deuteronomy 28:1-14: we possessed it but a little while. Israel had the blessings to a point when they went into the land, but only about eighty years at the full level, under David and Solomon. How Solomon abounded in gold, ships, and plenty of food you can read in 1 Kings. Precepts: - Isaiah 63:18 The people of thy holiness have possessed it but a little while; our adversaries have trodden down thy sanctuary. Deuteronomy 28:15 - But if thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes, all these curses shall come upon thee and overtake thee. Now we do some precepting, word by word. - The voice of the Lord is his commandments; to hearken unto his voice means to keep his commandments. - Observe to DO all his commandments: do is the action word. The Most High is a God of doing, and by him actions are weighed. Do not talk proudly and arrogantly, saying God loves me no matter what and God knows my heart; he had a personal relationship with a few men like Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Samuel, and David, and talking like you are one of them is arrogancy coming out of your mouth. - Curses means evil: the Lord said, I will bring evil upon this people because they have not hearkened unto my words. Overtake thee means you shall not be able to escape them, and though they cry unto him, he will not hearken. Precepts: - Psalms 103:20 His angels do his commandments, hearkening unto the voice of his word; the voice of the Most High is his commandments. - 1 Samuel 2:3 Talk no more so exceeding proudly; the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed. - James 2:20 Faith without works is dead; the works are the action of doing the commandments. - James 2:26 As the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead also. - Jeremiah 6:19 I will bring evil upon this people because they have not hearkened unto my words nor to my law; evil is another way of saying curses. - Jeremiah 11:11 I will bring evil upon them which they shall not be able to escape; the curses shall overtake thee, meaning you will not escape them. Deuteronomy 28:16 - Cursed shalt thou be in the city: as when police fired on a car of siblings as young as nine years old in Georgia after the children panicked when a cruiser followed their vehicle. That is cursed in the city. - Cursed shalt thou be in the field: we came off the slave ship and went right to the field, picking cotton from sunup to sundown. We know that one. Deuteronomy 28:17 - Cursed shall be thy basket and thy store: that goes into your businesses and your holdings. It is hard enough for a black man or woman to start a business; we are left with side hustles while the major trades, the ships, the metals, and the timber belong to Esau. - These curses are on us as a nation. It is not about us individually; keep that in mind. Deuteronomy 28:18 - Cursed shall be the fruit of thy body: your children. The same children panicking in front of police, and the dozens of children killed by youth gun violence in Chicago in a matter of months. - Cursed shall be the fruit of thy land, thy kine, and thy sheep: the food we eat is cursed. Fast food fills our neighborhoods, and where there is no fast food there is a corner store selling unclean meat that causes diseases in us. - Ezekiel says it plainly: the children of Israel eat their defiled bread among the Gentiles. Others may eat that food, but it is foul for us because we are supposed to eat the best food on the planet, for we are an holy people as Deuteronomy 14 says. Precepts: - Ezekiel 4:13 Even thus shall the children of Israel eat their defiled bread among the Gentiles, whither I will drive them. - Deuteronomy 14:2 Thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God, chosen to be a peculiar people above all the nations upon the earth. Deuteronomy 28:19 - Cursed shalt thou be when thou comest in and cursed when thou goest out. He is talking about Jerusalem, but it is twofold: it is coming in and going out of life itself. - Ecclesiasticus, for you newer people in the Apocrypha, spells it out: we are born under the curses and we die still living under them. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 41:8-9 Born to a curse and dying with a curse for a portion; and the more we have increased as a people, the worse it has become. Deuteronomy 28:20 - The Lord shall send upon thee cursing, vexation, and rebuke in all that thou settest thine hand unto, until thou be destroyed. - Rebuke means sharp disapproval or criticism because of your behavior: no matter what you do, nobody will see the silver lining in it; even what you mean for good turns out bad. - Vexation means the state of being annoyed or a thing that causes annoyance: among these nations they do not love you, they tolerate you. Your marching for equal rights annoys them; they ask why you will not just accept what you were given. Deuteronomy 28:21-22 - The Lord shall make the pestilence cleave unto thee: diseases. He shall smite thee with a consumption, a fever, an inflammation, an extreme burning, the sword, blasting, and mildew. - Amos shows what the blasting and mildew go into: famine, pestilence after the manner of Egypt, young men slain with the sword, death and destruction. Precepts: - Amos 4:9 I have smitten you with blasting and mildew; your gardens, vineyards, fig trees, and olive trees the palmerworm devoured: famine. - Amos 4:10 I have sent among you the pestilence after the manner of Egypt; your young men have I slain with the sword; yet have ye not returned unto me. Deuteronomy 28:23-24 - Thy heaven over thy head shall be brass, and the earth under thee iron. It is twofold: rain not coming down and crops not coming up. - It also goes into the chains above your head and the shackles of iron on your feet. Look up the images of slavery and you see whose neck the chains were on. - The rain of thy land shall be powder and dust from heaven until thou be destroyed. Deuteronomy 28:25-26 - Thou shalt go out one way against thine enemies and flee seven ways before them, and shalt be removed into all the kingdoms of the earth: 1492 and 1619. - Thy carcase shall be meat unto the fowls of the air and the beasts of the earth, and no man shall fray them away. Look up Wounded Knee, where the United States cavalry killed the Native Americans, who are Gad in the Bible, and left their bodies in the snow. Deuteronomy 28:27 - The Lord will smite thee with the botch of Egypt, the emerods, the scab, and the itch, whereof thou canst not be healed. - The itch that cannot be healed: look up who has the highest rates of sexually transmitted diseases right now. It is us. Deuteronomy 28:28-29 - The Lord shall smite thee with madness, blindness, and astonishment of heart, and thou shalt grope at noonday as the blind gropeth in darkness. - Thou shalt not prosper in thy ways, and thou shalt be only oppressed and spoiled evermore, and no man shall save thee: going back into bondage. - Hosea shows the wandering of the blind: we fled from the Most High, we return but not to the Most High, and the end of it is derision in the land of Egypt, which means captivity. Precepts: - Hosea 7:12-14 Woe unto them, for they have fled from me; they have not cried unto me with their heart when they howled upon their beds. - Hosea 7:16 They return, but not to the most High; this shall be their derision in the land of Egypt, which means captivity. Deuteronomy 28:30-31 - Thou shalt betroth a wife and another man shall lie with her: our wives were taken away, raped, robbed, and murdered in the captivity. - Thou shalt build an house and not dwell therein: we built the master's house, we built the White House, and to this day our people frame the roofs of suburban houses they will never live in. - Thou shalt plant a vineyard and not gather the grapes: down south our people and the Haitians, who are Levi, are still in the fields picking beans and oranges, and none of it comes back to them; it is packaged and shipped somewhere else. - Thine ass shall be violently taken away from before thy face and shall not be restored to thee: no reparations. They just pulled the okey-doke in North Carolina, promising reparations and then saying it would not be paid in money but in infrastructure. The Most High said it would not be restored. Deuteronomy 28:32 - Thy sons and thy daughters shall be given unto another people, and thine eyes shall look and fail with longing for them all the day long, and there shall be no might in thine hand. - The slave narratives collected in When I Was a Slave back it up: slaves were treated like cattle, a speculator went about the country buying them up, and it was pitiful to see children taken from the mother's breast, mothers sold from children, husbands sold from wives. - Another narrative: slavery days were hell; babies were snatched from their mother's breast and sold to speculators, children separated from sisters and brothers and never saw each other again. The Bible is a true book, and our ancestors backed it up. Deuteronomy 28:33-34 - The fruit of thy land and all thy labours shall a nation which thou knowest not eat up, and thou shalt be only oppressed and crushed alway. - The record of the conquistadors says one Spaniard ate enough for seven of the Indians, the northern kingdom. They literally ate up the fruit of the land. - Thou shalt be mad for the sight of thine eyes which thou shalt see. Deuteronomy 28:35-37 - The Lord shall bring thee and thy king unto a nation which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, and there shalt thou serve other gods, wood and stone. - Thou shalt become an astonishment, a proverb, and a byword among all nations: Puerto Rican, Dominican, Haitian, Jamaican, African American, gentile. We lost our name and left it for a curse, like it says in Isaiah, while others wear the name and cry anti-Semitic. Precepts: - Isaiah 65:15 Ye shall leave your name for a curse unto my chosen; we became a byword and lost our name in the captivity. Deuteronomy 28:38-41 - Thou shalt carry much seed out into the field and gather but little in; thou shalt plant vineyards but neither drink the wine nor gather the grapes; olive trees through all thy coasts, but no oil to anoint thyself. - Thou shalt beget sons and daughters, but thou shalt not enjoy them, for they shall go into captivity: the same story the slave narratives tell. - It happened before the ships too. When we ruled in Spain, in what they call the Dark Ages, a shipload of our people cast out on the African coast had the men and youths sold into slavery, the defenseless women ravished, and the aged, the sick, and the infants tortured and murdered by the thousands. That is recorded in The Jews and Moors in Spain; get that book if you do not have it. Deuteronomy 28:42-44 - All thy trees and the fruit of thy land shall the locust consume. - The stranger that is within thee shall get up above thee very high, and thou shalt come down very low; he shall lend to thee, and thou shalt not lend to him; he shall be the head, and thou shalt be the tail. Basically, you will always be oppressed. - Their own book, New World Jewry, says the Jewish converts were so disseminated through all the trading parts of the world that they became the pegs and nails that keep the whole frame of commerce together, back in the 1600s. But the curse says Israel comes down very low and borrows from the stranger. The lender at the top of world trade and the cursed borrower cannot be the same people; somebody is lying, and now we caught it. Deuteronomy 28:45-46 - All these curses shall pursue thee and overtake thee till thou be destroyed, because thou hearkenedst not unto the voice of the Lord thy God. - They shall be upon thee for a sign and for a wonder, and upon thy seed for ever. There is no time limit on this thing; that is how we know we are the real Israelites, because these curses are still hitting us all over the earth in some shape, form, or fashion to this day. - The Most High said you would be the bottom, and he meant it until the kingdom comes. That is why they do not want to go to Deuteronomy 28. Deuteronomy 28:47 - Because thou servedst not the Lord thy God with joyfulness and with gladness of heart for the abundance of all things: we have to be happy keeping these commandments. - That means joyful at the new moon, joyful on the sabbath, joyful in the classes. The lack of joy in keeping the commandments is the very reason the captivity came. - Sisters, that includes the commandment to be obedient and in subjection to your husband. Do not act like it is bondage; your husband cannot save you on the day of judgment, and you must work out your own salvation and stand before Christ with a joyful spirit in the commandments. Deuteronomy 28:48 - Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies in hunger, in thirst, in nakedness, and in want of all things, and he shall put a yoke of iron upon thy neck until he have destroyed thee. - Here is one way we stay destroyed: Juneteenth. The slave narrative records the master telling his slaves, this is military law, but I am forced to tell you this law says you are now free; I cannot make you stay unless you want to. That June 19th announcement of the master's law is what is still celebrated in Texas. - Our people celebrate Juneteenth like it is something to be proud of, but it is the slave master's holiday, and we are still slaves under the curses. Deuteronomy 28:49-50 - The Lord shall bring a nation against thee from far, from the end of the earth, as swift as the eagle flieth: the eagle is the symbol of Esau's nation. - A nation whose tongue thou shalt not understand: we did not speak English, and our brothers in the islands and South America did not speak Spanish when the ships came. - New World Jewry itself records that many slaves were called ladino, which in that context means a negro slave who could speak Spanish. So the northern kingdom brother who says he is not black is simply a negro that speaks Spanish; welcome home, you are our brother. - A nation of fierce countenance, which shall not regard the person of the old nor shew favour to the young: they worked the old to death in the cotton fields, and today an old man dies with a knee held on his neck for over eight minutes, and children get fired on by police. Neither old nor young is spared. Deuteronomy 28:51 - He shall eat the fruit of thy cattle and the fruit of thy land until thou be destroyed, leaving thee neither corn, wine, nor oil. - The Native Americans lived off the land, following the buffalo and the deer and making coats of skins. Now Reuben stays by the casino and Gad lives on reservation lands like barren wasteland where nothing grows, with outdoor plumbing, and it has never been restored. Reparations is not a casino, and it is not being called sovereign while occupied by another nation. Deuteronomy 28:52-57 - He shall besiege thee in all thy gates until thy high and fenced walls come down. Verse 52 onward is going into the siege of Jerusalem by Babylon and by Rome, and Assyria did this also. This is NOT talking about black-on-black violence; do not use it for that. - Thou shalt eat the fruit of thine own body, the flesh of thy sons and daughters, in the siege and in the straitness wherewith thine enemies shall distress thee. The Most High starved our people out in the siege until they boiled and ate their own children. - The proof it is not street violence is in the text itself: the tender man's eye shall be evil toward the wife of his bosom and toward the remnant of his children, because he has nothing left in the siege. It describes a good, caring, delicate man broken by famine, not violence in the neighborhood. - The tender and delicate woman, which would not set the sole of her foot upon the ground for delicateness: our sisters have fallen a long way from that standard of tenderness and delicateness, and they need to return to it. Deuteronomy 28:58-61 - If thou wilt not observe to do all the words of this law written in this book, that thou mayest fear this glorious and fearful name, THE LORD THY GOD, then he will make thy plagues wonderful, plagues of thy seed, of long continuance, and sore sicknesses. - Verse 59 is saying the Most High will make up diseases to keep punishing you; he will even have Esau create them in a laboratory and make them affect you more than anybody else. - He will bring upon thee all the diseases of Egypt which thou wast afraid of, and also every sickness and every plague which is NOT written in the book of this law, until thou be destroyed. Deuteronomy 28:62-63 - Ye shall be left few in number, whereas ye were as the stars of heaven for multitude, because thou wouldest not obey the voice of the Lord thy God. - As the Lord rejoiced over you to do you good and to multiply you, so the Lord will rejoice over you to destroy you. We have to understand who we are dealing with: he is happy to bless you and happy to destroy you for breaking the commandments. - That is the God this Christianity needs to be teaching, to put some fear back in our people. Deuteronomy 28:64 - The Lord shall scatter thee among all people from the one end of the earth even unto the other, and there thou shalt serve other gods which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone: that is talking about Christianity and Islam. - The Handbook of Denominations records that as early as 1700 white slaveholders in the south provided religious teaching for their slaves, and the slaves identified with the faith of their owners: if your slave master was Baptist you were Baptist; if he was Catholic you were Catholic. - The same book says black Baptist doctrine runs quite parallel to that of white Baptist churches: it is the same exact thing, the slave master's religion with a black face on it. - The Most High is saying: wherever I scatter you, you will not know me; you will be caught up thinking you serve me, but you do not know me. The only time you will know him is when he puts his spirit back on the earth and reveals it in the last days. That is why there is so much turmoil in our life, because we were not serving God right. Deuteronomy 28:65 - Among these nations shalt thou find no ease, neither shall the sole of thy foot have rest, but the Lord shall give thee there a trembling heart, and failing of eyes, and sorrow of mind. - No ease: the northern kingdom is catching it right now, with migrant children taken from their families and detained in hotels not even registered with the government before deportation, and thousands of those children cannot be found. Deuteronomy 28:66-67 - Thy life shall hang in doubt before thee, and thou shalt fear day and night, and shalt have none assurance of thy life. That is why those children panicked when the police car pulled up behind them: no assurance of thy life. - In the morning thou shalt say, Would God it were even, and at even, Would God it were morning, for the fear of thine heart and the sight of thine eyes. Deuteronomy 28:68 - Here is the nail in the coffin: the Lord shall bring thee into Egypt again with ships. Egypt means bondage; the scripture defines it right in Deuteronomy 5, the land of Egypt, the house of bondage. He is saying: I will bring you into slavery again, with ships. - It is not the literal land of Egypt, because you can walk to Egypt; Isaiah shows Israel walked down to Egypt. The false pastors who say we were shipped back across the Red Sea are wrong; the ships went to a spiritual Egypt. - Revelation names it: the great city which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt. The greatest country on the face of the earth, America, Babylon the great, is the Egypt we were carried into with ships. - Even their own scholarship confirms who was there the first time: a treatise on physical geography admits that negroes existed in Egypt in the days of Rameses with the same national features they have now. The Bible says the negroes go INTO Egypt, bondage, AGAIN. - There ye shall be sold unto your enemies for bondmen and bondwomen, and no man shall buy you: buy means redeem. Under the servitude laws a poor brother sold to a stranger could be redeemed by his uncle, his uncle's son, or any of his kin; but in this captivity none of your brothers can redeem you, because they are in bondage right along with you, as verse 29 already said: no man shall save thee. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 5:6 I am the Lord thy God, which brought thee out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage; Egypt means bondage and slavery. - Isaiah 30:1-2 Woe to the rebellious children that walk to go down into Egypt; Israel could walk to literal Egypt, so the ships carry us to a spiritual Egypt. - Revelation 11:8 The great city which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt; the spiritual Egypt of the ships is Babylon the great, America. - Leviticus 25:47-49 A brother sold to a stranger may be redeemed by his kin; in this captivity no kinsman can redeem you, for all Israel is sold into bondage together. - Deuteronomy 28:29 Thou shalt be only oppressed and spoiled evermore, and no man shall save thee; the quick precept for no man shall buy you. Deuteronomy 29: The Covenant Made with Us Who Were Not There Read the chapter → Deuteronomy 29 Deuteronomy 29:1 - These are the words of the covenant which the Lord commanded Moses to make with the children of Israel in the land of Moab, beside the covenant which he made with them in Horeb. Deuteronomy 29:2-4 - Ye have seen all that the Lord did before your eyes in the land of Egypt, the great temptations, the signs, and those great miracles. - Yet the Lord hath not given you an heart to perceive, and eyes to see, and ears to hear, unto this day. Moses is telling them: you do not truly understand what Deuteronomy 28 means; you do not know how bad it is really going to get. Deuteronomy 29:5-9 - The Most High led Israel forty years in the wilderness; their clothes waxed not old upon them, nor their shoes upon their feet, that they might know that he is the Lord their God. - Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan came out against Israel, and Israel smote them and gave their land for an inheritance to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh. - Keep therefore the words of this covenant and do them, that ye may prosper in all that ye do. Deuteronomy 29:10-13 - All Israel stood that day before the Lord: captains, elders, officers, little ones, wives, and the stranger in the camp, from the hewer of wood unto the drawer of water. Even the servants among us heard this covenant. - But though those strangers were among us, Deuteronomy 28 did not apply to them. That is why no other nation on earth suffers the curses of the Most High the way we do; they live here in Babylon under the same judicial system, but they are not suffering from it like us. - The purpose: that he may establish thee to day for a people unto himself, as he sware unto thy fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob. That is who we come from. Deuteronomy 29:14-15 - Neither with you only do I make this covenant and this oath, but also with him that is not here with us this day. That is us: the Lord made this covenant with the generations which were to come. - This is how you know the covenant and the curses apply to our forefathers and to us to this day. If we do not hearken to his voice and obey his commandments diligently, all the curses of Deuteronomy 28 fall upon us; that is what is happening to us right now. Deuteronomy 29:16-19 - Ye have seen the abominations and idols of the nations, wood and stone, silver and gold; lest there should be among you man, woman, family, or tribe whose heart turneth away from the Lord to serve the gods of these nations. - Lest there should be among you a root that beareth gall and wormwood: destruction. - Verse 19 is Christianity 101: when he heareth the words of this curse, he blesseth himself in his heart, saying, I shall have peace, though I walk in the imagination of mine heart. He hears the whole of Deuteronomy 28, the ships, the children given away, the no rest and no ease, and says in his mind, I am an American, I live under the blessings of God, while he catches the bus, pays rent, and drinks dirty water in Flint. - To add drunkenness to thirst: the Most High says you are drunk with that dumb understanding, lying to yourself, and thirstier for it. Deuteronomy 29:20-21 - The Lord will not spare him; the anger of the Lord and his jealousy shall smoke against that man, and all the curses written in this book shall lie upon him, and the Lord shall blot out his name from under heaven: death. - Once you hear Deuteronomy 28, you cannot go back to living how you used to live. You heard the curses, even ten minutes of it on the street; you are marked, and if you go back, the Most High says, I am coming for you. Deuteronomy 29:22-28 - The generation to come and the stranger from a far land shall see the plagues of the land, the whole land brimstone, salt, and burning, like the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboim. - All nations shall say, Wherefore hath the Lord done thus unto this land? And men shall answer, Because they have forsaken the covenant of the Lord God of their fathers. - That is what they say when they look at our people: the ones who know we are the real Israelites say, they forsook God and now they are being punished; but we are not going to tell them who they are, because we are living good while they suffer. - The Lord rooted them out of their land in anger and cast them into another land, as it is this day. Welcome to Babylon the great. Deuteronomy 29:29 - The secret things belong unto the Lord our God: those are the prophecies, which Deuteronomy 30 goes into a little. - But those things which are revealed belong unto us and to our children for ever, that we may do all the words of this law. The revealed things, the milk, are the laws that are easy to be understood, and they belong to us; focus on those. Deuteronomy 30: Call the Curses to Mind and Choose Life Read the chapter → Deuteronomy 30 Deuteronomy 30:1-2 - With all that being said, here is the goodness of the Most High: he said, I am going to punish you, but he gave us the solution to get up out of the curses. - When all these things are come upon thee, the blessing and the curse, thou shalt call them to mind among all the nations whither the Lord thy God hath driven thee. Baruch tells you what calling them to mind is: in the land of their captivities they shall remember themselves. - We are remembering ourselves now: we know we got here on ships, we know we did not speak the white man's language when he came to the west coast of Africa, we know we rise when the alarm clock goes off and work for food, water, and drink, and we know Christianity is a slave religion forced on our ancestors. That is calling the curses to mind. - And shalt return unto the Lord thy God, and shalt obey his voice according to all that I command thee, thou and thy children, with all thine heart and with all thy soul. The stipulation of returning is keeping the commandments; you cannot just say I accept the Lord in my heart. That does not work. And your children must be in order under your household too; they cannot fake it either. Precepts: - Baruch 2:30 Calling the blessing and the curse to mind is Israel remembering themselves in the land of their captivities. Deuteronomy 30:3-5 - Then the Lord thy God will turn thy captivity and have compassion upon thee, and will return and gather thee from all the nations whither the Lord thy God hath scattered thee. - It did not say the League of Nations, NATO, or an airline jet will gather us. The Most High is sending Christ to come and get us and take us back to the land, the same way he delivered us out of Egypt himself, with the angel leading, and no Amorite, Greek, or Roman helping. - There is nothing new under the sun; that is how we know the people over in the land now are not the people of the book, because Israel returns by the hand of the Most High, not by planes. - If any of thine be driven out unto the outmost parts of heaven, from thence will he fetch thee: no matter where we are in the four corners of the earth, if we repent and endure to the end, Christ said, I am coming to get you. Precepts: - Matthew 24:31 He shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds; Christ gathers Israel, nobody else. Deuteronomy 30:6-7 - The Lord thy God will circumcise thine heart and the heart of thy seed, to love the Lord thy God with all thine heart and with all thy soul, that thou mayest live. - And the Lord thy God will put all these curses upon thine enemies and on them that hate thee, which persecuted thee. When the number of the 144,000 is fulfilled, every curse we just read in Deuteronomy 28 goes on every other nation on the face of the planet, double for what we received. And what we got was terrible; endure to those days. Deuteronomy 30:8-10 - Thou shalt return and obey the voice of the Lord, and do all his commandments; and the Lord will again rejoice over thee for good, as he rejoiced over thy fathers, making thee plenteous in every work of thine hand. - If thou hearken unto his voice, to keep his commandments and his statutes which are written in this book of the law: before it was called the Holy Bible, it was called the book of the law. That is what the Most High governs by: law. Deuteronomy 30:11-14 - This commandment is not hidden from thee, neither is it far off; it is not in heaven and not beyond the sea, that thou shouldest say, Who shall fetch it for us? - The word is very nigh unto thee, in thy mouth and in thy heart, that thou mayest do it. Look how close the word is now: the Most High put it on the spirit of even our oppressor to make Bible apps, so the judgments, the curses, the blessings, and what he requires sit in everybody's pocket. - There are no excuses on the day of judgment. None. Deuteronomy 30:15-16 - See, I have set before thee this day life and good, and death and evil. - How do you love the Most High? To walk in his ways, and to keep his commandments and his statutes and his judgments, that thou mayest live and multiply. That did not change from Old Testament to New: the only way we love God is by keeping his commandments. Deuteronomy 30:17-18 - You heard the IF at the top; now here comes the BUT. When you hear the word but, open your ears, because whatever follows you had better not walk outside the lines of. - But if thine heart turn away, and thou be drawn away to worship other gods and serve them: you want Christianity and whatever denomination feels good to you, or Islam with four and five wives worshipping a stone, or Buddhism, or Scientology? - I denounce unto you this day, that ye shall surely perish, and that ye shall not prolong your days upon the land, whither thou passest over Jordan to possess it. Deuteronomy 30:19 - Highlight verse 19 if you do not have it highlighted: I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live. - He already told you what is up. The life he is telling you to choose is in Proverbs: keep my commandments and live. The commandments give you life; they are your spiritual force field out on the streets in the land of wickedness. Precepts: - Proverbs 7:2 Keep my commandments, and live; and my law as the apple of thine eye; that is the life the Most High tells you to choose. Deuteronomy 30:20 - That thou mayest love the Lord thy God, and that thou mayest obey his voice, and that thou mayest cleave unto him: for he is thy life, and the length of thy days. - What is his voice again? Precept upon precept: the voice of the Lord is his commandments, so cleave unto him by doing them, that thou mayest dwell in the land which the Lord sware unto thy fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob. Precepts: - Psalms 103:20 His angels that do his commandments, hearkening unto the voice of his word; obeying his voice is keeping his commandments. --- Topics: Clean and Unclean Meats · Esau and Edom · Idolatry · Sacrifice and Atonement · The Covenant · The Feasts of the Most High · The Priesthood · The Sabbath ← Deuteronomy 23-26 · Deuteronomy Study · Deuteronomy 31-34 →

title: Deuteronomy 3: The Battle Is the Lord's
text: ← Deuteronomy 1-2 · Deuteronomy Study · Deuteronomy 7-10 → Deuteronomy 3: The Battle Is the Lord's Read the chapter → Deuteronomy 3 Introduction This session covered Deuteronomy 3-6. As Israel nears the end of the first five books, the thread of each is worth holding: Genesis is the beginning, the book of your genes and genealogy; Exodus is the grand exit from slavery in Egypt; Leviticus carries the levitical laws given through the Levites; Numbers is the numbering of the families and armies of Israel; and Deuteronomy is a reiteration, a repetition of the laws of the Most High and of everything that happened in the previous books. Chapters 1 and 2 retold how the Most High helped Moses by appointing leaders, so that one man would not carry the whole burden of a stiffnecked and rebellious people alone, and gave Israel instruction on which wars to take on, sparing Edom and the children of Moab. Chapter 3 opens with the war against Og king of Bashan. Deuteronomy 3:1-3 - Bashan is about to be conquered, and Og the king of Bashan came out with all his people to battle at Edrei. The Most High said fear him not, for I will deliver him and all his people and his land into thy hand, as was done to Sihon king of the Amorites at Heshbon. - Always remember, the battle is the Lord's; this fight is spiritual. Israel does not need weapons of mass destruction: the Bible is the weapon, and when Israel keeps the commandments the Most High fights for his people. - The Lord our God delivered into our hands also the king of Bashan: they were out there doing physical war, but they gave the praise, the glory, and the victory to the Most High. They did not boast in their own swords; that is how you sanctify the Most High. - The same order stands today: when you wake up you thank the Most High, and you thank him for the food even though you cooked it, because he is the one who allowed you to have it. You always put the Most High first. Deuteronomy 3:4-7 - Threescore cities were taken, all fenced with high walls, gates, and bars, beside unwalled towns a great many, and not one city was left untaken. - They utterly destroyed the men, women, and children of every city, as they did unto Sihon king of Heshbon. That command came from the Most High himself; this is the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, the God of the Bible, not the invented gospel that says he loves everybody no matter what. - Only the cattle and the spoil of the cities were taken for a prey; those were needed and were spared. Deuteronomy 3:8-11 - Israel took the land from the two kings of the Amorites on this side Jordan, from the river of Arnon unto mount Hermon. - Only Og king of Bashan remained of the remnant of giants. His bedstead was a bedstead of iron, nine cubits long and four cubits broad: about thirteen feet long and six feet wide, near the size of two king beds, showing how tall and big this man was. - Og was an Amorite, and the Amorites descend from Ham; Genesis 10 proves the lineage. The Hamitic nations were known for great stature, as Goliath the Philistine stood nine feet nine inches, and to this day the tallest peoples on earth, the Watusi, the Dinka, and the Nilotic tribes of Sudan, Ethiopia, and Kenya, are Hamites. - Ancient Palestine was first the land of the Philistines, Hamitic tribes, before the Arabs and later others took hold of it; the name goes back to those ancient Philistines. Precepts: - Genesis 10:5 The Most High divided the isles of the Gentiles, every one after his tongue, after their families, in their nations; the nations were never the same, he divided them by tongue and land. - Genesis 10:6 The sons of Ham: Cush is Ethiopia, Mizraim is Egypt, with Phut and Canaan; Ham, the youngest son of Noah, is the progenitor of these dark nations, and Kemet and Ham mean the same thing. - Genesis 10:16 The Jebusite and the Amorite are of the lineage of Canaan; the Amorites are a Hamitic tribe, so Og the Amorite descends from Ham. Deuteronomy 3:12-17 - The conquered land was divided: from Aroer by the river Arnon and half mount Gilead to the Reubenites and the Gadites, and the rest of Gilead and all Bashan, the kingdom of Og, to the half tribe of Manasseh. - All the region of Argob with all Bashan was called the land of giants, because the giants there were of Og's kin, of his family. - Jair the son of Manasseh took all the country of Argob and called it after his own name, Bashan-havoth-jair, unto this day. Deuteronomy 3:18-20 - All that were meet for the war were to pass over armed before their brethren, while the wives, the little ones, and the much cattle abode in the cities already given, until the Most High gave rest to their brethren and they also possessed their land beyond Jordan. - When you read these wars, put yourself in the position of the brothers going out. Being promised victory over the land did not mean every man would survive it; Israel still had casualties, and there were brothers that gave their lives for their people. - Read to understand, not just to say you read your four chapters: bring the scripture to life and visualize what was really going on. Deuteronomy 3:21-22 - Joshua was commanded at that time: thine eyes have seen all that the Lord your God hath done unto these two kings; so shall he do unto all the kingdoms whither thou passest. - Ye shall not fear them, for the Lord your God he shall fight for you; the victories over Sihon and Og were the proof set before Joshua's own eyes. Deuteronomy 3:23-24 - Moses besought the Most High: thou hast begun to shew thy servant thy greatness and thy mighty hand, for what God is there in heaven or in earth that can do according to thy works and according to thy might? - That greatness shown to Moses was more than the exodus. On Sinai he received the ten commandments and the six hundred plus commandments, ceremonial, civil, moral, dietary, and sacrificial, that the Most High ordained Israel to keep. - He was also told many wondrous things: the prophecies such as Deuteronomy 28, that the people would go into slave ships under yokes of iron, lose their nationality, become a byword and an astonishment, and that a small remnant would wake up in the end days and come back. - He was shown the secrets of the times, the understanding of the parables and allegories of the scriptures, and the end itself; all of that stands behind this thanksgiving in Deuteronomy. Precepts: - 2 Esdras 14:3-6 The Most High held Moses by him a long season, told him many wondrous things, and shewed him the secrets of the times and the end; that is the greatness and the mighty hand Moses praised. Deuteronomy 3:25-26 - Moses begged: I pray thee, let me go over and see the good land that is beyond Jordan. The Most High had already told him he would not see the promised land, and Moses was trying to get him to repent of the word he had given. - The sentence came from the water of Meribah: Moses said hear now, ye rebels, must we fetch you water out of this rock, and smote the rock twice. He took the credit and became high minded instead of sanctifying the Most High in the eyes of the children of Israel, so he was told he would not bring the congregation into the land. - The contrast is Deuteronomy 3:3: after the war with Og the people said the Lord our God delivered them into our hands. That is sanctifying the Most High; Moses at the rock did the opposite. - The Lord was wroth with me for your sakes: Moses laid it on stiffnecked Israel. And the answer was final, let it suffice thee, speak no more unto me of this matter, as a parent tells a child that keeps begging that the matter is closed and had better not be raised again. Precepts: - Numbers 20:10-12 Moses smote the rock twice and the water came out abundantly, but because he believed not, to sanctify the Most High in the eyes of the children of Israel, he and Aaron would not bring the congregation into the land. Deuteronomy 3:27-29 - Get thee up into the top of Pisgah and behold the land with thine eyes westward, northward, southward, and eastward, for thou shalt not go over this Jordan; seeing it from the mountain was all that was granted. - But charge Joshua, and encourage him, and strengthen him, for he shall go over before this people and cause them to inherit the land. The Most High said plainly whom he would deal with for the crossing. - Promotion comes from the Most High: he was dealing with Moses and declared who he wanted in charge, and Moses was to strengthen the man chosen to replace him. Deuteronomy 4: Neither Add nor Diminish Read the chapter → Deuteronomy 4 Deuteronomy 4:1 - Hearken, O Israel: hearken means listen, pay attention, and there is a difference between hearing and listening. - The statutes and judgments are taught for to do them; knowing you are an Israelite is only half the battle. The main thing is applying the scriptures, doing what the Most High is telling you to do, that ye may live. - The promise is to go in and possess the land, and possessing land is true wealth: your milk and honey, your cattle, your agriculture, where you cultivate and take care of your family. It is not the diamonds, the cars, the sneakers, or the newest phone; a big house with no land is not wealth, and that is why the heathen boxes our people into apartments. Deuteronomy 4:2 - Ye shall not add unto the word, neither diminish ought from it. This was spoken around 1500 BC, and on the last page of the Bible the same charge closes the book: the prophets across millenniums and captivities all speak the same thing, Moses, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Christ, and John, and that consistency proves the Bible is a true book, because twenty people cannot keep one story straight for five minutes. - The watered down versions such as the NIV and ESV show what taking away looks like: many of them remove Matthew 18:11 and other scriptures, and they have taken out the Apocrypha. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 12:32 What thing soever I command you, observe to do it; observing to do it is obligated, not optional, and thou shalt not add thereto nor diminish from it. - Revelation 22:18-19 If any man shall add unto these things, God shall add unto him the plagues written in this book, and if any man take away from the words, God shall take away his part out of the book of life. - 1 Corinthians 1:10 That ye all speak the same thing: John the Revelator and Moses were speaking the same thing, and Christ spoke out of the Old Testament. - Adding to the word sounds like god loves everybody: how many have been found liars saying it? Do not quote what the Most High has not said, and prove all things, because an opinion off the top of your head cannot be proven by scripture. - If any man speak, let him speak as the oracles of God. New brothers in this truth should not rush to debate before they have studied to shew themselves approved; uttering things that are not in the scriptures is not a good look. - From the beginning the Most High commanded the prophets to speak his words and diminish not a word: do not be afraid to tell the nations what the scripture actually says, that salvation is to Israel and that there is no female deity. Precepts: - Proverbs 30:6 Add thou not unto his words, lest he reprove thee, and thou be found a liar. - Proverbs 28:26 He that trusteth in his own heart is a fool; following your own mind instead of the scripture is folly. - 1 Thessalonians 5:21 Prove all things; if you cannot prove it, do not utter it. - 1 Peter 4:11 If any man speak, let him speak as the oracles of God, neither adding nor taking away. - Jeremiah 26:2 Speak all the words that I command thee to speak unto them; diminish not a word. Deuteronomy 4:3-4 - Your eyes have seen what the Lord did because of Baal-peor: all the men that followed Baal-peor were destroyed from among the people, and this recalls the history of Balaam. Balaam was a Midianite, an Ishmaelite. - But ye that did cleave unto the Lord your God are alive every one of you this day: those who said they would not go after that foolishness were saved alive. - The Bible is that simple, and it destroys the confusion of the world's religions: keep the commandments and live, or break them and die. Follow after the ways of the nations and be put to death; keep the laws, statutes, and commandments and have life. Precepts: - Numbers 31:16-18 These caused the children of Israel, through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass in the matter of Peor; that history stands behind this verse. - Deuteronomy 30:19 I call heaven and earth to record: life and death, blessing and cursing, are set before you, so choose life; everything is being recorded, every idle word. - Proverbs 13:21 Evil pursueth sinners, but to the righteous good shall be repayed; the Most High does not bless a man in his sins, and the trouble that keeps following is the pursuit of sin. Deuteronomy 4:5-6 - Keep therefore and do them, for this is your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the nations. Israel deals with the Almighty; having the omnipotent God on your side is the wisdom the nations do not have, and it is what they are mad at. - When Israel keeps the laws it makes them a peculiar nation: peculiar by definition means characteristic of only one person, group, or thing, and different from the usual or normal. The Most High made this people different and set them above the other nations. - Royal means of a kingly ancestry, and the King of kings is Christ; but rulership belongs to the lineage only when the laws are kept. When Israel is fallen into sin, the people look worse than the nations instead of wise and understanding. - Which shall hear all these statutes and say, surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people: they may not say it out loud today, but when they see Israel united in Christ and in order, that is what rises in their minds. Precepts: - 1 Peter 2:9 A chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people: Peter and Moses speak the same thing about the same people. - 2 Esdras 6:54 Of Adam come we all, and there is also the people whom the Most High hath chosen, the children of Israel. - Deuteronomy 14:2 Thou art an holy people, chosen to be a peculiar people unto himself, above all the nations upon the earth; Deuteronomy 7 likewise calls Israel special and above all nations. - Psalms 44:13-14 When the laws are broken Israel is made a reproach to the neighbours, a scorn and a derision, a byword among the heathen, and a shaking of the head among the people; calling ourselves colors and bywords instead of our nationality is part of that estate. Deuteronomy 4:7-8 - What nation is there so great, who hath God so nigh unto them? The Most High is near unto Israel in all things they call upon him for, and no nation has statutes and judgments so righteous as this law. - When Israel keeps the laws, statutes, and commandments, they are the light of the world; in the days when the brothers and sisters were in order, the nations looked on and marveled at what nation this was, so great and so beautiful. Deuteronomy 4:9-10 - Take heed to thyself and keep thy soul diligently, lest thou forget the things thine eyes have seen; and teach them thy sons, and thy sons' sons. These are generational commandments: children's children, cousins' cousins, so that no generation misses a beat. - Gather me the people together, and I will make them hear my words, that they may learn to fear me all the days that they shall live upon the earth, and that they may teach their children. - Why learn to fear the Most High? Verses 3 and 4 of this same chapter answer it: those that followed the idols were destroyed, and those that cleaved to him are alive. Follow after idols, after the nations and their religions, and he will destroy you. - Fear is the first spirit required, before love, before confession: fear and respect go hand in hand, and if you fear him you will do what he says, and do it with joyfulness and gladness for the reward no nation can touch. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 10:12 And now, Israel, what doth the Lord thy God require of thee? The first thing named is to fear the Lord thy God; that fear proves the love, the confession, and the spirit. - Psalms 111:10 The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom; a good understanding have all they that do his commandments. Deuteronomy 4:11-13 - The mountain burned with fire unto the midst of heaven, and the Most High spake out of the midst of the fire; ye heard the voice of the words, but saw no similitude. - He declared his covenant, even ten commandments: the ten are the umbrella over all the other commandments, the sub-laws and sub-statutes beneath them. - And he wrote them upon two tables of stone. The laws men call the mosaic laws did not belong to Moses; they were written with the finger of God and given to Israel by Christ, and they endure for ever. Precepts: - Exodus 31:18 Two tables of testimony, tables of stone, written with the finger of God; Deuteronomy 4:13 is the reiteration of this, for Deuteronomy means repetition. Deuteronomy 4:14-16 - The Most High commanded Moses at that time to teach the statutes and judgments, and Israel is charged to take good heed, for ye saw no manner of similitude on the day the Lord spake in Horeb. - No similitude means he spoke plainly and clearly, not in dark speeches: when the commandments were given there was no arguing over what they meant.
