Fringes on the borders of the garments, no swine, thou shalt not kill; it was simple and easy to understand. - Lest ye corrupt yourselves and make a graven image, the similitude of any figure, the likeness of male or female: Israel had come out of Egypt, where graven images filled the land and where the likeness of the female was worshipped. - Egypt is where feminism was already incorporated: Hathor the cattle goddess and Qetesh the goddess of beauty were among the idols learned there, so the Most High had to say plainly, no deity male or female. There is no goddess in the scriptures. Precepts: - Numbers 12:6-8 With Moses the Most High spake mouth to mouth, even apparently, and not in dark speeches; that is why Israel saw no similitude and heard plain commandments. - Exodus 15:3 The Lord is a man of war: a man. The scriptures give no ground to those who say God is a woman; he deals with the men of Israel, and no woman is to usurp authority over the man. Deuteronomy 4:17-19 - The likeness of any beast on the earth goes back to idols like Heqet the frog god and Sobek the god of the river; the likeness of any winged fowl to Horus the falcon; anything that creepeth on the ground to the beetles, flies, and locusts they deified; any fish in the waters to Sobek and to Dagon the fish god of the Babylonians, whose symbolism carries into pagan imagery to this day. - The eagle and the falcon symbols of the powers of this world trace back to the gods and goddesses of Egypt, because this present power is spiritual Egypt and takes after her. - Lest thou lift up thine eyes unto heaven and be driven to worship the sun, the moon, and the stars: that is Ra the sun god and Nut the sky goddess, and it is also astrology, the zodiac, and witchcraft today. Calling yourself a Gemini or a Taurus is the same star worship; none of it is the way to the kingdom, and it was filth learned in Egypt. - Why worship what the Most High created to serve you? The sun, moon, and stars are ordinances that keep their order and do their job, which is why the new moon can be kept; Israel is the one out of order when the commandments are not kept. Precepts: - Jeremiah 31:35-36 The Most High giveth the sun for a light by day and the ordinances of the moon and stars for a light by night; if those ordinances depart from before him, then the seed of Israel shall cease from being a nation. They serve his children, not the reverse. - Ecclesiastes 5:1 Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God, and be more ready to hear than to give the sacrifice of fools: put off the filth learned in this land and drop the prideful rebuttals of the lies you were taught. - Exodus 3:5 Put off thy shoes from off thy feet, for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground; Moses knew all the ways and deities of the Egyptians, and he was told to be quiet, humble himself, and receive the milk of the laws so he could grow. Deuteronomy 4:20-22 - The Lord hath taken you and brought you forth out of the iron furnace, even out of Egypt, to be unto him a people of inheritance. - Furthermore the Lord was angry with me for your sakes: again Moses lays his barred crossing on the people. It is how the workers feel when they go out to preach truth and catch anger for it; you are not arguing with the messenger, you are mad at the Bible, so speak the oracles and neither add nor diminish to please anybody. - Moses must die in this land and not go over Jordan, but ye shall go over and possess that good land; he kept repeating it, longing for what he would not see. Deuteronomy 4:23-26 - Take heed unto yourselves, lest ye forget the covenant and make a graven image, for the Lord thy God is a consuming fire, even a jealous God. - When children's children are begotten and the stay in the land grows long, corruption creeps in; make the graven image and do evil to provoke him, and ye shall soon utterly perish from off the land. - Heaven and earth are called to witness against Israel this day; the warning was on record before it ever came to pass. Deuteronomy 4:27-28 - And the Lord shall scatter you among the nations, and ye shall be left few in number among the heathen: this is future prophecy of the scattering to the four corners of the earth. - And there ye shall serve gods, the work of men's hands, wood and stone: the wood is the cross of christianity and the stone is the kaaba stone at Mecca. Israel would fall into the heathen religions, christianity and islam, in the lands of the scattering. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 28:64 The Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other, and there thou shalt serve other gods, wood and stone; the same prophecy in the curses. - 1 Peter 1:1 Peter writes to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia: the scattered ones are Israel. Deuteronomy 4:29-31 - But if from thence thou shalt seek the Lord thy God, thou shalt find him, if thou seek him with all thy heart and with all thy soul; the seeking begins with the spirit of fear, to get right with the Most High. - When thou art in tribulation, and all these things are come upon thee, even in the latter days: the latter days began when Christ came, for God who spake in time past by the prophets hath in these last days spoken by his Son. - And shalt be obedient unto his voice: the voice of the Most High tells you to keep his commandments. If someone claims God spoke to him in a dream and told him everything but obedience, that is not the voice of the Most High. - For the Lord thy God is a merciful God; he will not forsake thee, nor destroy thee, nor forget the covenant of thy fathers. Precepts: - Hebrews 1:1-2 God, who at sundry times and in divers manners spake unto the fathers by the prophets, hath in these last days spoken unto us by his Son; Christ's coming began the last days, and the Most High has always dealt through his prophets. - Deuteronomy 27:10 Thou shalt therefore obey the voice of the Lord thy God, and do his commandments and his statutes; that is what the voice of God tells a man to do. - Psalms 103:20 Bless the Lord, ye his angels, that do his commandments, hearkening unto the voice of the word; doing his commandments is hearkening to that voice. Deuteronomy 4:32-35 - Ask now of the days that are past, since the day that God created man upon the earth: you are supposed to search out your forefathers and look up your history, and not slavery only, but the reign under David and Solomon and the empires where Israel ruled, and slavery too, because failing to keep the laws is why the people went into it. - Did ever people hear the voice of God speaking out of the midst of the fire and live? Hath God assayed to take him a nation from the midst of another nation, by temptations, by signs, and by wonders, and by war, and by a mighty hand? There is no such history anywhere else; the Most High did this for Israel alone. - Unto thee it was shewed, that thou mightest know that the Lord he is God; there is none else beside him. Precepts: - Job 8:8 Enquire, I pray thee, of the former age, and prepare thyself to the search of their fathers; looking up the history is a command, not a fixation. Deuteronomy 4:36-39 - Out of heaven he made thee to hear his voice, that he might instruct thee; and because he loved thy fathers, therefore he chose their seed after them, and brought thee out of Egypt in his sight with his mighty power. - To drive out nations from before thee greater and mightier than thou art: they had more economic might and more military power, but the Most High delivered Israel out of their hands, and to this day the twelve tribes are still here. - Know therefore this day, and consider it in thine heart, that the Lord he is God in heaven above and upon the earth beneath; there is none else. Consider is the key word: really appreciate all of it, for Israel could have been born of any nation, but the Most High ordained this people, and the way to cash in is simply keeping the commandments. Precepts: - Isaiah 44:1 Yet now hear, O Jacob my servant, and Israel whom I have chosen; the chosen seed the whole passage speaks of. Deuteronomy 4:40 - Thou shalt keep therefore his statutes and his commandments, that it may go well with thee and with thy children after thee, and that thou mayest prolong thy days upon the earth. - This is the solution. The voting, protesting, and marching have never worked and never will; trust in the Most High and keep his laws, and he will take care of his people with long days, families, and the land. Deuteronomy 4:41-49 - Then Moses severed three cities on this side Jordan toward the sunrising, that the slayer which killed his neighbour unawares, and hated him not in times past, might flee thither and live: Bezer in the wilderness for the Reubenites, Ramoth in Gilead for the Gadites, and Golan in Bashan for the Manassites. - The chapter closes with the summary: this is the law, the testimonies, the statutes, and the judgments which Moses spake unto the children of Israel after they came forth out of Egypt, in the land of Sihon and of Og, the two kings of the Amorites. Deuteronomy 5: The Ten Commandments Reiterated Read the chapter → Deuteronomy 5 Deuteronomy 5:1-3 - Hear, O Israel, the statutes and judgments which I speak in your ears this day, that ye may learn them, and keep, and do them. Doing them is the key thing: it is not verbal, actions carry the weight, and the actions are the commandments. - The Lord made not this covenant with our fathers, but with us, even us, who are all of us here alive this day. Deuteronomy 5:4-6 - The Lord talked with you face to face in the mount out of the midst of the fire, and Moses stood between the Lord and the people to shew the word: Moses was the mediator for Israel. - I am the Lord thy God, which brought thee out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage: Egypt means slavery. This is a good scripture for the brothers who go out to prophesy, because the whole exodus claim can be shown from Deuteronomy 5 without ever leaving the book. Deuteronomy 5:7-10 - Thou shalt have none other gods before me, and thou shalt not make thee any graven image: the ten commandments are being reiterated and Israel reminded, because the graven images they knew came from Egypt. - The scriptures are twofold: the commandment still pertains today, against the false images of Christ, the virgin mary statues, the cobblestone at Mecca, buddha, and the gods of the east. - The Most High is a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate him, and shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love him and keep his commandments. Precepts: - Job 11:6 The secrets of wisdom are double to that which is; the scriptures are twofold, speaking to Egypt then and to spiritual Egypt now. Deuteronomy 5:11 - Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain: this is not about saying oh my god. Solomon shows how the name is taken in vain: lest I be poor, and steal, and take the name of my God in vain. Breaking the commandments, stealing, lying, bearing false witness, committing adultery, is how the name is taken in vain. - His name is called The Word of God, and the word of God is the book of the commandments; so to profane the commandments is to profane the name. - Solomon's prayer is the humble spirit: give me neither poverty nor riches, feed me with food convenient for me. Full riches make a man deny the Most High and forget the congregation and the work, and money has pulled people out of this walk; poverty drives a man to steal. The chief things for life are simple, water, bread, clothing, and an house to cover shame, and the Most High blessed Solomon with riches because riches were not his god. Precepts: - Proverbs 30:7-9 Remove far from me vanity and lies; give me neither poverty nor riches; lest I be full, and deny thee, and say, Who is the Lord? or lest I be poor, and steal, and take the name of my God in vain. - Ecclesiasticus 29:21-22 The chief things for life are simple; better a poor man's own mean cottage than delicate fare as a freeloader in another man's house. - Revelation 19:13 His name is called The Word of God; the name of the Most High is his word. - Baruch 4:1 The word of God is the book of the commandments of God, the law that endureth for ever; the name, the word, and the law go hand in hand. Deuteronomy 5:12-15 - Keep the sabbath day to sanctify it: six days shalt thou labour, but the seventh day is the sabbath of the Lord thy God, and no work is done by thee, thy children, thy servants, thy cattle, nor the stranger within thy gates, that all may rest. - And remember that thou wast a servant in the land of Egypt, and that the Lord thy God brought thee out thence through a mighty hand; therefore the sabbath was commanded. Deuteronomy 5:16-21 - Honour thy father and thy mother, that thy days may be prolonged; thou shalt not kill; neither shalt thou commit adultery; neither shalt thou steal; neither shalt thou bear false witness against thy neighbour, meaning lie. - The sexual laws of Leviticus 18 go with the adultery commandment, covering adultery and fornication. - Neither shalt thou covet: the word used today is jealousy. Being mad that a brother or sister drives better or earns better, keeping up with the Joneses, is an evil spirit that has to be purged. Deuteronomy 5:22-27 - These words the Lord spake unto all the assembly out of the midst of the fire, of the cloud, and of the thick darkness, with a great voice, and he added no more; and he wrote them in two tables of stone. - The people heard the voice out of the darkness while the mountain burned, and the heads of the tribes came near and said, we have seen this day that God doth talk with man, and he liveth; but why should we die? for this great fire will consume us. - So they asked Moses to go near, hear all that the Lord our God shall say, and speak it unto them: and we will hear it, and do it. Deuteronomy 5:28-29 - They have well said all that they have spoken: Israel always talked a good game. - O that there were such an heart in them, that they would fear me, and keep all my commandments always, that it might be well with them and with their children for ever. When it came to actions the people did not fear the judgments and the repercussions of breaking the commandments. - The Most High does not want to see his people die; the keeping of the commandments is the solution he keeps setting before them, not the protesting, marching, and voting. Deuteronomy 5:30-33 - Go say to them, get you into your tents again; but as for thee, stand thou here by me, and I will speak unto thee all the commandments which thou shalt teach them. - Ye shall walk in all the ways which the Lord your God hath commanded you, turning aside neither to the right hand nor to the left, that ye may live, and that it may be well with you, and that ye may prolong your days. Precepts: - Psalms 119:1 Blessed are the undefiled in the way, who walk in the law of the Lord; walking in the way of God is keeping his commandments. Deuteronomy 6: Teach Them Diligently unto Thy Children Read the chapter → Deuteronomy 6 Deuteronomy 6:1-3 - These are the commandments, the statutes, and the judgments, commanded to be taught, that thou mightest fear the Lord thy God: the fear always comes up first, thou, and thy son, and thy son's son, all the days of thy life. - Hear therefore, O Israel, and observe to do it, that ye may increase mightily. Increase and power are the desire of the people, and keeping the commandments is the one thing our people have not tried; assimilation, the gods of the nations, and politics, liberal or conservative, have all been tried and none of it has worked. - The land that floweth with milk and honey is the true riches: cattle, vegetation, agriculture, land to cultivate, the gift that keeps on giving. Deuteronomy 6:4-7 - Hear, O Israel: the Lord our God is one Lord: and thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might. - Thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children: diligently means you do not miss a beat. The children are not to be taught the dance challenges, halloween, and the satanic birthdays, and remember that you teach by your actions, so you fix yourself first. - Talk of them when thou sittest in thine house: go through the scriptures at home, the histories of Samson, Joseph, Solomon, and David. When thou walkest by the way: when you run into each other, ask, are you keeping the laws, what four chapters did you read today? - When thou liest down, and when thou risest up: the bedtime stories are biblical, the ten plagues of Egypt rather than the fairy tales, prayer before they sleep and when they rise, and even the coloring books painting the images brown, bringing it back to its true course. Deuteronomy 6:8-9 - Thou shalt bind them for a sign upon thine hand, and they shall be as frontlets between thine eyes: bind them in your mind. The commandments are the light, the torch that guides you and leads you in the correct path. - And thou shalt write them upon the posts of thy house, and on thy gates. Deuteronomy 6:10-16 - When the Lord brings thee into great and goodly cities which thou buildedst not, houses full of all good things which thou filledst not, wells digged which thou diggedst not, and thou shalt have eaten and be full, then beware lest thou forget the Lord which brought thee forth out of the house of bondage. - Thou shalt fear the Lord thy God, and serve him, and shalt swear by his name; ye shall not go after the gods of the people round about you, for the Lord thy God is a jealous God, lest his anger be kindled and destroy thee from off the face of the earth. - Ye shall not tempt the Lord your God, as ye tempted him in Massah. Deuteronomy 6:17-19 - Ye shall diligently keep the commandments of the Lord your God, and his testimonies, and his statutes. Testimony is one of the trigger words that confuses our people: the laws are what Moses gave, and the testimonies are the history of the forefathers and foremothers, what they went through and how it was handled according to the laws. - Everything correlates: when king David had Uriah killed, that goes back to thou shalt not kill, thou shalt not covet, and bearing false witness; he was dealing with much sin in that one matter. That is how you go precept upon precept, line upon line, to the law and to the testimony. - A personal testimony that cannot come back to the Bible is not biblical; if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light, no truth, in them. - Thou shalt do that which is right and good in the sight of the Lord: not by personal standards of what feels good in the heart, but by the standard set before us, for the scripture says plainly that the law is good. The reward is to go in and possess the good land, the real wealth, not the bags and rings and sneakers, which are vanity. Precepts: - Isaiah 8:20 To the law and to the testimony: if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light in them. - Proverbs 6:23 The commandment is a lamp, and the law is light; that is the light that is missing in them that speak not according to the word. - Psalms 119:105 Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path. - 1 John 2:4 He that saith, I know him, and keepeth not his commandments, is a liar, and the truth is not in him; the same measure as no light in them. - 1 Timothy 1:8 But we know that the law is good, if a man use it lawfully; what is good is what the Most High says is good. - Romans 7:12 The law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good. Deuteronomy 6:20-25 - When thy son asketh thee in time to come, saying, what mean the testimonies, and the statutes, and the judgments? The children will ask why David did what he did, why Samson, why Miriam was judged, why Moses was barred; the answer starts with the history. - Then thou shalt say unto thy son, we were Pharaoh's bondmen in Egypt, and the Lord brought us out with a mighty hand, and shewed signs and wonders upon Egypt and upon Pharaoh; he brought us out that he might bring us in, to give us the land which he sware unto our fathers. The Most High always keeps his covenant; he is not a man, that he should lie. - The Lord commanded us to do all these statutes, to fear the Lord our God, for our good always, that he might preserve us alive: the fear again stands first, and the commandments are for Israel's good and preservation, obligated and not optional, with punishment for breaking and reward for keeping. - And it shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments: keeping the commandments is what makes you righteous, and righteousness is kept at all times, the fringes worn seven days a week and not on the sabbath only. - Words like testimony, righteousness, grace, and faith must be defined out of the scripture itself: the Bible is a dictionary within itself. Egypt means slavery, righteousness means keeping the laws, and going by the Bible's own definitions destroys the private interpretations of the religions. Precepts: - Psalms 106:3 Blessed are they that keep judgment, and he that doeth righteousness at all times; at all times, not one day a week. - Psalms 119:172 My tongue shall speak of thy word: for all thy commandments are righteousness. --- Topics: Clean and Unclean Meats · Idolatry · Sacrifice and Atonement · The Covenant · The Feasts of the Most High · The Priesthood · The Sabbath ← Deuteronomy 1-2 · Deuteronomy Study · Deuteronomy 7-10 →

title: Deuteronomy 31: Moses' Final Charge and the Rebellion Foretold
text: ← Deuteronomy 27-30 · Deuteronomy Study · Joshua 1-4 → Deuteronomy 31: Moses' Final Charge and the Rebellion Foretold Read the chapter → Deuteronomy 31 Introduction This session covers Deuteronomy 31 through 34, the close of the Torah. These are some of the most monumental chapters for identifying who we are today: we have already been through Genesis 49, Deuteronomy 28, and Leviticus 26, and today we cover Deuteronomy 33, the blessing that shows where the tribes of Israel are geographically in these last days. Moses, barred from the promised land, spends his final days giving the children of Israel prophecy: chapter 31 is his charge and the warning of rebellion to come, chapter 32 is the song of Moses, chapter 33 is the blessing of the tribes, and chapter 34 is his death in the mount. Deuteronomy 31:1-2 - Moses is one hundred and twenty years old this day, and the Most High has told him he shall not go over this Jordan. After he was provoked by the people at the waters of strife, he did not sanctify the Most High before the children of Israel, so he was barred from entering the promised land. - The Most High lets him go up on the mountain to take a look at the land, but he will not enter into it. Before his farewell, chapters 31 through 33 give the children of Israel prophecy of what would happen to them. Deuteronomy 31:3-6 - The Most High himself goes over before Israel to destroy these nations, and Joshua goes over before the people, as he did to Sihon and Og, kings of the Amorites. - The nations are given up before Israel's face so that Israel may do to them according to all the commandments already given: when you enter the land, follow the guidelines of Deuteronomy 7. Do not take their daughters for wives or give your sons to theirs, do not worship their gods, but utterly burn their gods with fire. - Be strong and of a good courage, fear not, for the Most High goes with thee; he will not fail thee, nor forsake thee. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 7:3-5 Make no marriages with the nations of the land, but destroy their altars and burn their graven images with fire. Deuteronomy 31:7-8 - Moses calls Joshua in the sight of all Israel and charges him: be strong and of a good courage, for thou must go with this people into the land sworn to their fathers, and cause them to inherit it. - The Most High goes before Joshua; he will be with him and will not fail him. Fear not, neither be dismayed. Deuteronomy 31:9-13 - Moses wrote this law and delivered it to the priests, the sons of Levi that bear the ark of the covenant, and to all the elders of Israel. - At the end of every seven years, in the solemnity of the year of release, in the feast of tabernacles, the law was to be read before all Israel: gather the people together, men and women and children, that they may hear, learn, and fear the Most High, and observe to do all the words of this law. The law had to be taught over and over to remind the people what would befall them and what they must do. - Their children which have not known any thing must hear and learn to fear the Most High. The first thing you establish with your children, before they know anything else, is who they are and who their God is. Precepts: - Zephaniah 2:1 Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired. Precepts: - Exodus 13:2 Sanctify unto me all the firstborn: the firstling is the glory of the birthright. - Genesis 48:16 Let my name be named on them, and let them grow into a multitude in the midst of the earth. - 2 Esdras 13:40-41 The ten tribes were carried over the waters and took counsel to go forth into a further country. Deuteronomy 33:18-19 - And of Zebulun he said, Rejoice, Zebulun, in thy going out; and, Issachar, in thy tents. Notice the grouping: Zebulun and Issachar are blessed together because they would dwell very close, with linked cities at their borders. - They shall call the people unto the mountain; there they shall offer sacrifices of righteousness. In the promised land they linked up to make sacrifices of righteousness; but when they linked up on this side of the world as the Aztecs and the Mayans, they erected pyramids and eventually went off and sacrificed to other gods, even human sacrifice, as Hosea testifies of their sacrificing. - For they shall suck of the abundance of the seas, and of treasures hid in the sand: the gold and silver discovered in their land, which is why the conquistadors were so glad to stumble upon it. Precepts: - Hosea 8:13-14 They sacrifice flesh for the sacrifices of mine offerings, but the Lord accepteth them not; Israel hath forgotten his Maker. Deuteronomy 33:20-21 - And of Gad he said, Blessed be he that enlargeth Gad. Gad alone holds over three hundred Indian tribes within itself; it is a very large tribe. - He dwelleth as a lion, and teareth the arm with the crown of the head: Gad was a warlike, predator people, and the tearing of the arm goes into the blood brother pact they were known for making, the chief with the crown of feathers having a man tear his arm to be accepted into the tribe. - And he provided the first part for himself: that is North America, the mainland, the largest and best portion. Because there, in a portion of the lawgiver, was he seated: the tribe of Gad served as the lawgivers for the northern kingdom. - And he came with the heads of the people: the travel to this side of the earth was made with Ephraim and Manasseh, the horns, at the head, dealing with the so-called Hispanics and Indians together. He executed the justice of the Lord, and his judgments with Israel, before they went off. Deuteronomy 33:22 - And of Dan he said, Dan is a lion's whelp: he shall leap from Bashan. Dan is a warlike people; the Carib Indians did not play. - He shall leap from Bashan says a lot in a short verse: Bashan was in the most northern part of Israel, so leaping from Bashan lands Dan in the middle of all Israel. That is why Dan today is not their own tribe but is absorbed into all the other tribes, primarily Benjamin, dwelling in the Caribbean. - Amos says they shall fall, and never rise up again: Dan fell and never rose again as a tribe, which is why Dan is not mentioned among the tribes of the 144,000 in Revelation 7. And as Genesis 49 says, Dan is an adder in the path: look how the islands are shaped geographically, like a serpent. Precepts: - Genesis 49:17 Dan shall be a serpent by the way, an adder in the path. - Amos 8:14 They that swear by the sin of Samaria and say, The manner of Beersheba liveth; even they shall fall, and never rise up again. Deuteronomy 33:23 - And of Naphtali he said, O Naphtali, satisfied with favour: Naphtali is Argentina and Chile today. Satisfied with favour goes into the grapes they are able to produce in their land for wine, and coffee as well. - And full with the blessing of the Lord: to this day their land is rich with agriculture and cattle. - Possess thou the west and the south: the Most High gets geographic again. Look at a map of the world: what land sits in the southwestern region of the earth? Argentina and Chile. Stop playing with the prophets; we know who we are. Deuteronomy 33:24-25 - And of Asher he said, Let Asher be blessed with children. Asher is also a large tribe: the countries that make up Asher today include Brazil, Peru, Colombia, and Uruguay, and Brazil has the largest population of children in the world. - Let him be acceptable to his brethren: for a period of time they became so wild in their ways that they were not acceptable in the sight of their brethren. - And let him dip his foot in oil: one of the largest outputs of crude oil resources is Colombia. - Thy shoes shall be iron and brass: the Hebrew word for iron is barzel; say it fast and you hear Brazil. It goes into the mineral resources in that land, iron, copper, zinc. And as thy days, so shall thy strength be. Deuteronomy 33:26-29 - There is none like unto the God of Jeshurun, who rideth upon the heaven in thy help. The eternal God is thy refuge, and underneath are the everlasting arms: he shall thrust out the enemy from before thee. - Notice how the song and blessing have evolved: from Israel provoking the Most High and being punished, the teeth of beasts sent upon us, now it goes into our salvation, how the Most High will be our refuge. Israel then shall dwell in safety alone. - Happy art thou, O Israel: who is like unto thee, O people saved by the Lord! And thine enemies shall be found liars unto thee: after all these years of the crafty counsel, being told you are anything but Israel and that everybody else holds your heritage, the Most High said your enemies shall be found liars, and thou shalt tread upon their high places. - Never trust your enemy: your enemy will do everything in his power to keep you oppressed and subject to him, including lying to you about your history. As in the days of the Maccabees, the leaders show the people the falsehood of the heathen and the breach of their oaths, the covenants and treaties they broke with our people; after so long you learn that your enemies have been liars this whole time. Precepts: - 2 Maccabees 15:10 Judas stirred up their minds, shewing them the falsehood of the heathen and the breach of oaths. Deuteronomy 34: The Death of Moses Read the chapter → Deuteronomy 34 Deuteronomy 34:1-4 - Moses went up from the plains of Moab unto the mountain of Nebo, to the top of Pisgah, over against Jericho, and the Most High shewed him all the land: Gilead unto Dan, Naphtali, Ephraim and Manasseh, Judah unto the utmost sea, the south, and the plain of the valley of Jericho unto Zoar. - This is the land which I sware unto Abraham, unto Isaac, and unto Jacob, saying, I will give it unto thy seed: I have caused thee to see it with thine eyes, but thou shalt not go over thither. Moses could see it, but he could not go into it. Deuteronomy 34:5-7 - So Moses the servant of the Lord died there in the land of Moab, according to the word of the Lord, and he was buried in a valley in the land of Moab, over against Bethpeor: but no man knoweth of his sepulchre unto this day. So do not go trying to find it. - Moses was an hundred and twenty years old when he died: his eye was not dim, nor his natural force abated. He was not weak, old, and sickly like a man about to drop dead; he was in full strength, and still he had to go up and die because he could not enter the land. Deuteronomy 34:8-9 - The children of Israel wept for Moses in the plains of Moab thirty days, until the days of weeping and mourning for Moses were ended. - Joshua the son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom; for Moses had laid his hands upon him. Joshua was Moses' protege, and he carried the spirit Moses had, a great leader compassionate for the people; and the children of Israel hearkened unto him, and did as the Lord commanded Moses. Deuteronomy 34:10-12 - And there arose not a prophet since in Israel like unto Moses, whom the Lord knew face to face. This verse is heavy because of a doctrine: some say Joshua was the prophet of Deuteronomy 18:18, the prophet raised up like unto Moses, and therefore there is no Christ. - But the scripture that acknowledges Joshua rising up with the spirit upon him says in the same breath that there arose not a prophet since in Israel like unto Moses. Joshua was a mighty prophet, but he did not fit that word; Christ did. - None matched all the signs and the wonders which the Lord sent Moses to do in the land of Egypt, and all that mighty hand, and all the great terror which Moses shewed in the sight of all Israel. With this the Torah, the books of Moses, is finished. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 18:18 I will raise them up a Prophet from among their brethren, like unto thee: Christ, not Joshua, fulfilled this word. --- Topics: Esau and Edom · Idolatry · Sacrifice and Atonement · The Covenant · The Feasts of the Most High · The Priesthood ← Deuteronomy 27-30 · Deuteronomy Study · Joshua 1-4 →

title: Deuteronomy 7: A Holy People, Chosen Above All People
text: ← Deuteronomy 3-6 · Deuteronomy Study · Deuteronomy 11-14 → Deuteronomy 7: A Holy People, Chosen Above All People Read the chapter → Deuteronomy 7 Introduction This session covered Deuteronomy 7-10, precepting through as the chapters were read. The class opened sounding the alarm in the street, lifting up the voice like a trumpet, with Luke 13:3 and 5: except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish. Classroom order was set by 1 Corinthians 14:33 and 40, for God is not the author of confusion, and all things are to be done decently and in order. Chapter 7 lays out the destruction of the seven nations, the ban on marrying them, and Israel's election as a holy people; chapter 8 ties life to the commandments and warns against forgetting the Most High in prosperity; chapter 9 strips away self-righteousness and retells the molten calf; chapter 10 gives the second tables, the separation of Levi, and what the Most High requires of Israel. Deuteronomy 7:1-2 - The seven nations cast out before Israel, the Hittites, Girgashites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, greater and mightier than Israel, are Hamitic nations. - Thou shalt smite them and utterly destroy them; thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor shew mercy unto them. Since the days of old the Most High has never been about the love-of-the-world gospel; throw that doctrine in the trash. - This is why they do not want you reading the old covenant: verses like this correct the miseducation received through Christianity, and the mind begins to correct itself as you read. Deuteronomy 7:3-4 - Neither shalt thou make marriages with them: the Most High forbids marrying outside the nation. The seed of the fathers today is found among the so-called blacks, Hispanics, and Native Indians, who make up the twelve tribes of Israel; a spouse may come from any of the twelve tribes, but from within the tribes only. - Going outside your nation for a husband or wife is despising your brethren in your heart. Whom you marry is the greatest commitment you make in this life; if you truly loved your people, you would choose one of your own people to become aged together with. - They will turn away thy son from following me: the nations are strangers to the Most High and cannot come into this covenant, so they draw the Israelite spouse off to religions that accept everything. Christianity accepts that union, and that is how they turn you away from your God. Precepts: - Tobit 4:12-13 Take a wife of the seed of thy fathers; going outside the nation is despising thy brethren in thy heart. - Tobit 8:6-7 Marriage is taking a sister of thine own people, not for lust but uprightly, to become aged together. Deuteronomy 7:5 - Thus shall ye deal with them: destroy their altars, break down their images, cut down their groves, and burn their graven images with fire. Nothing of their worship was to be spared or adopted. Deuteronomy 7:6 - For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God: this is one of the most uplifting scriptures in the book, and it should be etched into your children's minds from the moment they begin to read, until it is implanted into their spirit. - The mind controls the body: what goes into the mind comes out through the body, so a people that knows it is holy and special above all people walks and carries itself differently. - Being chosen above all people keeps you out of the affairs of this world, their fashions, their hairstyles, their trends and challenges, and keeping up with the Joneses; you cannot flip-flop with every new wave and still carry the speciality the Most High put on you. Precepts: - Proverbs 23:7 As a man thinketh in his heart, so is he; the heart is the mind, and what is planted there comes out in how you carry yourself. Deuteronomy 7:7-8 - The Lord did not choose Israel for their number, for ye were the fewest of all people: only threescore and ten souls came out of the loins of Jacob when Israel first went down, as Genesis records, some places reading seventy and some counting seventy-five. - But because the Lord loved you: the Most High needs no other reason, he simply loved us, and we should never apologize for that. - He kept the oath sworn unto the fathers and redeemed Israel out of the house of bondmen, from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt; Israel came out from under Rameses. Precepts: - Numbers 33:3 They departed from Rameses with an high hand in the sight of all the Egyptians; this proves which Pharaoh Israel came out from under. Deuteronomy 7:9-11 - Know therefore that the Lord thy God, he is God, the faithful God, which keepeth covenant and mercy with them that love him and keep his commandments to a thousand generations, and repayeth them that hate him to their face. - This is the same teaching as the new testament: loving the Most High is keeping his commandments, and refusing his commandments shows him with your actions that you hate him, and then judgment comes. - From the jump it has always been the same: love God, keep the commandments; nothing changed between the covenants. Precepts: - 1 John 5:2-3 This is the love of God, that we keep his commandments, and his commandments are not grievous; the opposite of this is how you show him you hate him. Deuteronomy 7:12-15 - If ye hearken to these judgments and keep and do them, the Lord keeps the covenant and the mercy: he will love thee, bless thee, and multiply thee, blessing the fruit of thy womb, thy land, thy corn, wine, oil, kine, and sheep, blessed above all people, which goes right back to verse 6. - The Lord will take away from thee all sickness and put none of the evil diseases of Egypt upon thee, but will lay them upon all them that hate thee. That still reigns true today: keep the commandments and the Most High will keep you from the diseases of modern-day Egypt, and if you do catch something, he will revive you and bring you back to your health. Deuteronomy 7:16 - Thou shalt consume all the people which the Lord thy God shall deliver thee; thine eye shall have no pity upon them, neither shalt thou serve their gods, for that will be a snare unto thee. - Those days are coming back when Christ returns. Deuteronomy 7:17-24 - If thou shalt say in thine heart, these nations are more than I: fear them not, but remember what the Lord did unto Pharaoh and unto all Egypt, the signs, the wonders, the mighty hand and the stretched out arm; so shall he do unto all the people of whom thou art afraid. - The Lord will send the hornet among them until even those that hide themselves are destroyed, and he will put out those nations before thee by little and little, lest the beasts of the field increase upon thee. - He shall deliver their kings into thine hand, and thou shalt destroy their name from under heaven. There is no way to read Deuteronomy 7 and still say God loves everybody; that idea is being drunk on Christianity, not reading the book. Deuteronomy 7:25-26 - The graven images of their gods shall ye burn with fire: desire not the silver or gold that is on them, lest thou be snared therein, for it is an abomination to the Lord thy God. - Neither shalt thou bring an abomination into thine house, lest thou be a cursed thing like it. Bring it up to today: the Jesus pieces, the crosses, the ankhs, and the rosary beads wrapped around the neck and rubbed in prayer make the wearer an abomination and a cursed thing just like the idol. - The main abomination we bring into our house is the Christmas tree of Jeremiah 10: the tree cut down, fastened with nails and hammers, and decked with silver and with gold, whether cut from the forest or bought as a fake tree from the store. Precepts: - Jeremiah 10:1-5 Learn not the way of the heathen, and be not dismayed at the signs of heaven; the decked tree is the custom of the people and is vain, and the stargazing, the probes, and the planet colonies are the signs of heaven the heathen are dismayed at. Deuteronomy 8: Keep the Commandments and Live Read the chapter → Deuteronomy 8 Deuteronomy 8:1 - All the commandments shall ye observe to do, that ye may live and multiply and go in and possess the land. The commandments are life; everything else brings death to us. - This is why you must vacate and run from Christianity as fast as possible, not ease out over years of so-called research. Once you know the man-made religions teach no commandments while our people die by the thousands, you should run to this truth and start keeping the commandments, because this is your life. Precepts: - Proverbs 7:2 Keep my commandments and live, and my law as the apple of thine eye; it has been the same since the days of old, and the commandments ultimately lead to eternal life. Deuteronomy 8:2-3 - Remember all the way which the Lord led thee these forty years in the wilderness, to humble thee and to prove thee, to know whether thou wouldest keep his commandments or no. Trials and tribulations in this flesh are the Most High proving us the same way, whether a lost spouse, family separating from you, a lost job, or strife with friends. - He fed thee with manna to make thee know that man doth not live by bread only, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of the Lord. Christ quoted this very verse walking in the earth; he was pulling from the old covenant, which proves nothing has been done away with, for he would not quote something that was abolished. - Far too many tuck and run when the Most High is proving them; he never gives us something we are not able to overcome, and through Israel's schools, classes, and daily teaching he is giving you the way to bear the temptation. Prove to him that you will endure it, love him, and persevere; hard times are the perfect segue back into the vomit you came out of if you do not stand. Precepts: - 1 Corinthians 10:13 There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man; God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able, but will with the temptation also make a way to escape. Deuteronomy 8:4-5 - Thy raiment waxed not old upon thee, neither did thy foot swell, these forty years. - As a man chasteneth his son, so the Lord thy God chasteneth thee: you do wrong, you get punished, exactly as a father raises his children. Who is more experienced than the Most High, the Ancient of days? There is no way we can tell him through our actions that we know what is right for us. - This is why Esau has no judgment on him like Israel has: they are not the sons, so the Most High is not chastening them. You cannot do what the other nations do; when we get that in our heads we will be in a far better situation as a people. Precepts: - Hebrews 12:6-8 Whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth; if ye be without chastisement, then are ye bastards, and not sons. - Hebrews 12:11 No chastening for the present seemeth joyous, but grievous; nevertheless afterward it yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness unto them which are exercised thereby. Deuteronomy 8:6-9 - Verses 7 through 9 are the precept for describing the land of milk and honey: a good land of brooks of water, of fountains and depths, of wheat, barley, vines, fig trees, and pomegranates, a land of oil olive and honey, where thou shalt eat bread without scarceness, whose stones are iron and out of whose hills thou mayest dig brass. Write it down and use it. - Right now the land is not flowing with milk and honey: the place is desolate, full of desert places, and much of its food is imported, exactly as the prophecy requires until the Most High restores it. - The Most High says he will return the land to its original form, like the garden of Eden; that is a precept in itself, for the garden of Eden is Jerusalem, the land of Israel, the land of milk and honey. Precepts: - Ezekiel 36:29-36 The desolate land shall be tilled and become like the garden of Eden, and when Israel learns the law they shall lothe themselves in their own sight for their iniquities; I the Lord have spoken it, and I will do it. Deuteronomy 8:10-14 - When thou hast eaten and art full, then thou shalt bless the Lord thy God for the good land which he hath given thee. - Beware that thou forget not the Lord thy God, in not keeping his commandments: keeping the commandments is how you remember the Most High, and not keeping them is how you forget him. No wonder our families do not know God; forget the laws and you have forgotten him, for they go hand in hand. - Consider how the doctrine of Christianity works: an entire book, especially the old covenant, says keep the commandments over and over, Christ himself says keep the commandments, and Christianity says read only the letters of Paul and do away with the commandments. That is strong witchcraft, to make you disbelieve what the very book says; it is Satan's playground. - Lest when thy herds and thy silver and thy gold multiply, thine heart be lifted up, and thou forget the Lord thy God, which brought thee forth out of the house of bondage. Deuteronomy 8:15-16 - He led thee through that great and terrible wilderness, wherein were fiery serpents and scorpions and drought, brought thee water out of the rock of flint, and fed thee with manna, to humble thee and to prove thee, to do thee good at thy latter end. Precepts: - Numbers 21:6 The fiery serpents of the wilderness: the Lord sent fiery serpents among the people, and much people of Israel died. Deuteronomy 8:17-18 - Here is Christianity wrapped up in a few scriptures: and thou say in thine heart, my power and the might of mine hand hath gotten me this wealth. They keep no commandments and then boast, look what we have done, look at this job, look at all this stuff, as if the Most High gave them that power. - But thou shalt remember the Lord thy God, for it is he that giveth thee power to get wealth, that he may establish his covenant. The power to get wealth belongs to the covenant; if you forget God and keep no commandments, it was not God blessing you. - Who blesses everybody that does not keep the commandments and still gets everything they desire? Satan says come as you are; whoever wants power, fame, and money in this world without obeying God can have it from him, and you will pay the piper when you meet Christ. Share these precepts with your family. Precepts: - Luke 4:5-7 The devil shewed Christ all the kingdoms of the world and said, All this power will I give thee, for that is delivered unto me, and to whomsoever I will I give it: if thou therefore wilt worship me, all shall be thine. - Jeremiah 13:11 As the girdle cleaveth to the loins of a man, so have I caused to cleave unto me the whole house of Israel and the whole house of Judah, that they might be unto me for a people, and for a name, and for a praise, and for a glory: but they would not hear; our very life cleaves to the Most High, yet the people followed the religions instead. Deuteronomy 8:19-20 - If thou do at all forget the Lord thy God and walk after other gods, the religions, and serve them and worship them, I testify against you this day that ye shall surely perish. - Now you know why our people die, why the tribes were conquered and scattered: as the nations which the Lord destroyed before your face, so shall ye perish, because ye would not be obedient unto the voice of the Lord your God. We want thou shalt not, and we will not do thou shalt, therefore we perish. Deuteronomy 9: Not for Thy Righteousness Read the chapter → Deuteronomy 9 Deuteronomy 9:1-3 - Hear, O Israel: thou art to pass over Jordan this day, to possess nations greater and mightier than thyself, a people great and tall, the children of the Anakims, of whom it was said, who can stand before the children of Anak. - The Anakims are Hamites, scattered now in the land of Ham; do not ask which nation they are today, for the Most High has not told us. - The Lord thy God goeth over before thee as a consuming fire; he shall destroy them and bring them down before thy face, so shalt thou drive them out and destroy them quickly. Deuteronomy 9:4-6 - Speak not thou in thine heart, saying, for my righteousness the Lord hath brought me in to possess this land: here is more of the Christianity spirit corrected. Israel entered for the wickedness of those nations and to perform the word sworn unto Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, not for their own uprightness. - Understand that the only reason any of us have a roof over our head and food in our stomach right now is the mercy and righteousness of the Most High, for thou art a stiffnecked people; it is because of him that we survive every single day. Deuteronomy 9:7-9 - Remember, and forget not, how thou provokedst the Lord thy God to wrath in the wilderness: from the day of leaving Egypt unto this place, ye have been rebellious against the Lord. - Moses abode in the mount forty days and forty nights, neither eating bread nor drinking water, when he went up to receive the tables of the covenant. - What was he doing those forty days? He was receiving the understanding of the beginning of times, the midst of times, and the end of times; that is why some things Moses wrote, like Genesis 49 and Deuteronomy 32 and 33, are hard to understand, hidden in plain view, while keep the commandments is written easy. Precepts: - 2 Esdras 14:1-6 The Most High held Moses by him a long season on Sinai, shewed him the secrets of the times and the end, and commanded which words to declare and which to hide. Deuteronomy 9:10-11 - The Lord delivered unto me two tables of stone written with the finger of God: God took his time and wrote the ten commandments down himself, according to all the words which the Lord spake with you in the mount out of the midst of the fire. Deuteronomy 9:12-14 - Arise, get thee down quickly; thy people have corrupted themselves and made them a molten image. That molten image was the calf, the Egyptian goddess Hathor; you can look that up yourself. - Let me alone, that I may destroy them, and blot out their name from under heaven, and I will make of thee a nation mightier and greater than they. The Most High was ready to go back to the days of the flood and start over with one man; time means nothing to the Ancient of days. - Religion has tried to remove the fierceness, the wrath, and the severity of the Most High and push an effeminate white Jesus in front of us that loves everybody, forgives everything at the last breath with no commandments kept, and can do no wrong. We are suffering in all our cities, in Africa, in Europe, and in the Caribbean from that lack of fear of God before our eyes. Precepts: - Romans 3:18 There is no fear of God before their eyes; religion removed the fear and austerity of the Most High from before us, and this is the result. Deuteronomy 9:15-17 - Moses came down from the mount, the mount burning with fire, the two tables of the covenant in his two hands, and behold, ye had sinned against the Lord your God and made you a molten calf. - Ye had turned aside quickly out of the way which the Lord had commanded you: the Most High had been proving them through hard times, and they quickly turned back, just as many today go right back to their old ways the moment they are left alone. Brothers and sisters, check yourselves; we must endure to the end and rehearse the righteous acts now. - Moses took the two tables, cast them out of his two hands, and brake them before your eyes. Deuteronomy 9:18-21 - Moses fell down before the Lord, as at the first, forty days and forty nights, neither eating bread nor drinking water, because of all your sins; that is two forty-day fasts, for he was afraid of the anger and hot displeasure wherewith the Lord was wroth against the people. - The Lord was very angry with Aaron to have destroyed him, and Moses prayed for Aaron also at the same time. Moses prayed, and the Lord hearkened unto him; there arose no prophet like Moses, a mighty great man in the scriptures. - He took your sin, the calf which ye had made, burnt it with fire, stamped it, ground it very small until it was as small as dust, and cast the dust into the brook that descended out of the mount. Deuteronomy 9:22-24 - At Taberah, at Massah, and at Kibrothhattaavah ye provoked the Lord to wrath, and at Kadeshbarnea ye rebelled against the commandment of the Lord and believed him not. - Ye have been rebellious against the Lord from the day that I knew you: Moses called Israel out plainly, and it is real talk still. Deuteronomy 9:25-29 - Moses fell down before the Lord forty days and forty nights because the Lord had said he would destroy the people, and prayed: O Lord God, destroy not thy people and thine inheritance, which thou hast redeemed through thy greatness. - Remember thy servants, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; look not unto the stubbornness of this people, nor to their wickedness, lest the land whence thou broughtest us out say the Lord was not able to bring them in, and because he hated them he brought them out to slay them. - Esdras prayed the same prayer as Moses for the children of Israel, so precept these two prayers together: pay no attention to the fakers, for they remove themselves, but be merciful to us who have no works of righteousness, for by that mercy thou shalt be called merciful. When we are in the midst of sin we live worse than beasts, for a beast runs on instinct, but we consciously choose to go against the laws of the Most High. Precepts: - 2 Esdras 8:26-39 Esdras prayed the same prayer as Moses for Israel, and the Most High answered that the sinners are reserved to the end while he rejoices over the disposition of the righteous. Deuteronomy 10: What Doth the Lord Require of Thee Read the chapter → Deuteronomy 10 Deuteronomy 10:1-5 - Hew thee two tables of stone like unto the first, and make thee an ark of wood; Moses made the ark of shittim wood and went up with the two tables in his hand. - He wrote on the tables, according to the first writing, the ten commandments: twice the record says God wrote them, in Deuteronomy 9:10 written with the finger of God and here again. That is why the law is so important; these are not merely the commandments of Moses, they are the laws of God, and breaking them brings judgment if you do not repent. - We have to repent, keep the commandments, and be found blameless before the Lord when Christ returns. - Moses put the tables in the ark which he had made, and there they be, as the Lord commanded. Deuteronomy 10:6-9 - Aaron died and was buried, and Eleazar his son ministered in the priest's office in his stead. - At that time the Lord separated the tribe of Levi, to bear the ark of the covenant, to stand before the Lord to minister unto him, and to bless in his name; wherefore Levi hath no part nor inheritance with his brethren, the Lord is his inheritance. - Levi ate well through the sacrifices the Lord set up: the Levites dwelt in the best areas, the suburbs, and lived in castles, because the Lord was their provider. All they had to do was teach Israel the commandments of God. - But they corrupted the covenant of Levi, left off teaching the law, and were partial in it, so the Lord gave them a swift and mighty judgment. Now you understand why Levi, identified in the land of Haiti, has been the poorest in the western hemisphere and catches hell to this day: their provider was the Lord, and they departed out of the way. Precepts: - Malachi 2:6-9 The law of truth was in his mouth, and the priest's lips should keep knowledge, but ye are departed out of the way, ye have caused many to stumble at the law, ye have corrupted the covenant of Levi; therefore have I made you contemptible and base before all the people. Deuteronomy 10:10-11 - Moses stayed in the mount, according to the first time, forty days and forty nights, and the Lord hearkened unto him at that time also, and the Lord would not destroy thee. - Arise, take thy journey before the people, that they may go in and possess the land which I sware unto their fathers. Deuteronomy 10:12-13 - And now, Israel, what doth the Lord thy God require of thee: here is your purpose in life, the stipulations for the body the Most High gave you, and what you must do to please him as the children of Israel. - Fear the Lord thy God, walk in all his ways, love him, and serve him with all thy heart and with all thy soul: it all boils down to keeping the commandments of the Lord and his statutes, which he commands thee for thy good. That is how you love and serve God until the day we return to the dust or he sends his son to redeem us from the land of our captivity. - Do not just say you love God, put action behind it. Sisters, come out of the pants and mini skirts and put on a modest dress, and be in subjection to your own husbands; brothers, put on your fringes, stop dyeing your hair, and marry the mother of your children instead of leaving her a baby mama. When you will not do what he told you to do, no words out of your mouth can make you love him; your actions show you actually hate him. Precepts: - 1 Samuel 2:3 Talk no more so exceeding proudly, let not arrogancy come out of your mouth: for the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed; saying God knows my heart while breaking his laws is speaking proudly. - 2 John 1:6 And this is love, that we walk after his commandments; it never changed from old covenant to new. Deuteronomy 10:14-15 - Behold, the heaven and the heaven of heavens is the Lord's thy God, the earth also; yet only the Lord had a delight in thy fathers to love them, and he chose their seed after them, even you above all people, as it is this day. - No other nation can lay claim to this: our forefather Abraham was the friend of God, and the Most High took Israel from the chief men of the earth, for Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob were the best men walking the face of the earth when he made us a nation. Heavy scriptures right there. Precepts: - Isaiah 41:8-9 But thou, Israel, art my servant, Jacob whom I have chosen, the seed of Abraham my friend; I have taken thee from the ends of the earth, and called thee from the chief men thereof, and said, Thou art my servant; I have chosen thee, and not cast thee away. Deuteronomy 10:16-17 - Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart, and be no more stiffnecked. - For the Lord your God is God of gods, and Lord of lords, a great God, a mighty, and a terrible, which regardeth not persons, nor taketh reward: that is what needs to be taught in the church, who we are really dealing with. - Christ described his father the same way and forewarned us plainly: the Most High can destroy both the flesh and the spirit, disintegrate the spirit with no second chance at life, so make sure you are walking correct and keeping these laws before you come before him. Precepts: - Luke 12:4-5 Be not afraid of them that kill the body; but I will forewarn you whom ye shall fear: fear him, which after he hath killed hath power to cast into hell; yea, I say unto you, Fear him. Deuteronomy 10:18-19 - He doth execute the judgment of the fatherless and widow, and loveth the stranger, in giving him food and raiment; love ye therefore the stranger, for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt. - Which stranger is Moses telling Israel to love? He is prophesying of the day Israel's own brother would become a stranger: when the northern kingdom was cut off, the brother became the stranger who would come back. Love them, because they are coming back into the covenant. - The stranger of this commandment is thy brother fallen into decay, whom thou shalt relieve, not the nations Israel was commanded to drive out. Precepts: - Obadiah 1:12 Thou shouldest not have looked on the day of thy brother in the day that he became a stranger; the brother becoming a stranger is the key to who Moses means. - Leviticus 25:35 If thy brother be waxen poor, then thou shalt relieve him, yea, though he be a stranger or a sojourner, that he may live with thee. Deuteronomy 10:20-22 - Thou shalt fear the Lord thy God; him shalt thou serve, and to him shalt thou cleave, and swear by his name. He is thy praise, and he is thy God, that hath done for thee these great and terrible things which thine eyes have seen. - Thy fathers went down into Egypt with threescore and ten persons, and now the Lord thy God hath made thee as the stars of heaven for multitude. --- Topics: Esau and Edom · Idolatry · Sacrifice and Atonement · The Covenant · The Feasts of the Most High · The Priesthood ← Deuteronomy 3-6 · Deuteronomy Study · Deuteronomy 11-14 →

title: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success
text: ← Deuteronomy 31-34 · Joshua Study · Joshua 5-8 → Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success Read the chapter → Joshua 1 Introduction This session opens the book of Joshua, a mighty and action packed book of history. Moses delivered the children of Israel out of Egypt and led them through the wilderness; Joshua is the man anointed to rise up in his stead and lead them over Jordan into the promised land. The reading covers Joshua 1 through 4: the charge and commission to Joshua, the formula for success in Joshua 1:8, Rahab and the spies at Jericho, Israel crossing Jordan on dry ground, and the twelve stone memorial at Gilgal. Joshua 1:1-2 - Joshua is called Moses' minister because when Moses was the leader, Joshua was the one always cleaving to him. He was not close to Moses in age; he was one of the young men that cleaved unto his elder, and if Moses was a good leader, beloved among the children of Israel, who better to rise up in his stead than the man who has his spirit? Precepts: - Numbers 11:28 In the wilderness Joshua was the servant of Moses, one of his young men, his protege; those were his humble beginnings. - Exodus 33:10-11 All the people worshipped at their tent doors while the Lord spake unto Moses face to face, but his servant Joshua, a young man, departed not out of the tabernacle; he wanted to be right there with his leader. - That is the spirit the young men coming up in this truth should aspire to: cleave to your leadership. It is not being around the longest that qualifies a man to rise up in another's stead; it is being the diligent servant who learned the ins and outs of how his leader was successful, and even observed his leader's mistakes so he knows what not to do in that position. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 6:34 Do not spend your hours joking with your peers; cleave unto the wise men that sit over you, as Joshua did with Moses. - Ecclesiasticus 6:36 Get to him early, because you never know how long that brother will be around; wherever he is, be there to receive whatever knowledge he has to offer. - Why was Joshua the one anointed? When the Lord told Moses he would see the land but not enter it, Moses did not argue or justify himself. His humble response was to ask the Lord to set a man over the congregation, that the congregation of the Lord be not as sheep which have no shepherd. Moses brought no candidates; he let the Lord pick, and the Lord picked the young man who had cleaved to him: promotion comes from the Lord, and he selects the leaders over his people. Precepts: - Numbers 27:15-17 Moses asked the Lord to set a man over the congregation to lead them out and bring them in, that Israel be not as sheep without a shepherd. - Numbers 27:18-20 The Lord said, Take thee Joshua the son of Nun, a man in whom is the spirit; Moses laid his hand on him, set him before Eleazar and the congregation, and put some of his honour upon him so the people would give Joshua the same respect and be obedient. - Moses said set a man over the congregation, not a woman, because women were never ordained to lead the children of Israel; that does not fit the divine order of the Most High. Miriam was a prophetess and one of the chief women, and she led the women; women have a real role in the nation, but leading the body is not it. When Miriam got puffed up and spoke against Moses, she was judged. Precepts: - Exodus 15:20 Miriam the prophetess led the women with timbrels and dances; her place was over the women, not over the body. - Numbers 12:10 When Miriam spoke against Moses she was struck with leprosy, white as snow, and was shut out of the camp seven days. Joshua 1:3-5 - Every place that the sole of your foot shall tread upon, that have I given unto you: the Lord let Joshua know that everywhere his foot stepped on this path would belong to the children of Israel, from the wilderness and Lebanon unto the great river Euphrates and unto the great sea toward the going down of the sun. These are the borders of the journey he would lead them through. - As I was with Moses, so I will be with thee: not any man would be able to stand before Joshua all the days of his life. When the Lord tells you that, you carry the spirit that backs down from nothing. - This is the same word the Lord foretold to Moses that Joshua now fulfills. The promised land was meant to be as the days of heaven upon the earth, and the condition was diligently keeping all the commandments, to love the Lord, to walk in all his ways, and to cleave unto him; then the Lord would drive out nations greater and mightier than Israel. Heaven was never about everybody being equal and holding hands; heaven is Israel gaining possession and power over the nations, and that has always been the gospel. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 11:21-25 Days as the days of heaven upon the earth; if ye diligently keep the commandments, every place whereon the soles of your feet shall tread shall be yours, no man shall be able to stand before you, and the Lord shall lay the fear and dread of you upon all the land, the very promise repeated to Joshua. - Hebrews 4:2 The gospel was preached unto them in the wilderness as it is preached unto us: keep the commandments and inherit the kingdom prepared for Israel; under Christ the difference is an eternal reign, with our spirit changed so we cannot transgress. - The proof that we have not kept the commandments is that we own nothing today. Even land bought and paid for is not truly yours: fail to pay the real estate tax and it is taken by eminent domain and sold at auction. It was never meant to be that way; Israel was supposed to have ownership of the earth. Joshua 1:6-7 - The first thing the Lord commands the new leader is to be strong and of a good courage. This truth is not for the weak, not for people easily discouraged when trials and tribulations occur and people bring burdens of matters unto you; you have to be built for it. - He has to reiterate it: only be thou strong. You are dealing with the Israelites, a stiffnecked, rebellious, cold hearted people, so there is no room for mild moments or weak moments. - It takes strength to observe to do according to all the law; that is why the scriptures speak of building up your faith and being exercised in the things you learn. You have to be spiritually fit to survive in this truth, especially as a leader. The word for being strong and very courageous is fortitude, one of the virtues that comes with wisdom. Precepts: - Wisdom of Solomon 8:7 Wisdom teaches fortitude, the very strength and courage the Lord commanded Joshua to have. - 1 Samuel 15:9 Turn not to the right hand or to the left means no deviating from the word and no hunting loopholes; Saul was told to spare nothing, yet he spared Agag and the best of the animals, and it cost him the kingdom. Joshua 1:8 - This verse is the recipe for success, the formula for success, the true prosperity doctrine, and it has three steps: the law in your mouth, meditation day and night, and observing to do all that is written therein. - This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth: when you open your mouth, what comes out is supposed to be scriptural; your conversation has to be modeled after what this book says. When people leave this truth the Lord removes his words out of their mouth, and their whole conversation changes: nothing is left but slander, falsehood, strange doctrines, and flattering speech. Precepts: - Psalms 119:43 David prayed, take not the word of truth utterly out of my mouth; do not let me reach the point where I utter foolishness, hatred, and evil communications. - Psalms 51:11 It is the same prayer as take not thy holy spirit from me; when the Lord removes that spirit, the words of truth leave the conversation with it. - Romans 16:18 Those who serve their own belly deceive the hearts of the simple by good words and fair speeches; it is no longer the book and the straight commandments, just flattery and shade on the next man. - Psalms 71:24 My tongue shall talk of thy righteousness all the day long: solutions, building one another, correction and exhortation, not backbiting, gossip, and murmuring. - Ecclesiasticus 9:15 You cannot keep the law in your mouth while conversing with people who know nothing of it; talk with those who love the Lord and have wisdom. - Thou shalt meditate therein day and night: to meditate is to think deeply and carefully, to contemplate, consider, ponder, and muse. Many read their four chapters a day, listen to videos, and quote their precept lists, but never meditate on what they read. You cannot just slap the butter on the biscuit; you have to let it sink into every layer. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 22:17 Meditation is like a portrait in an art gallery: the one who loves it stands and examines a thousand details the surface look never sees; be settled on the scripture, the counsel, and the class the same way. - Psalms 143:5 I meditate on all thy works; I muse on the work of thy hands: to muse is to be absorbed in thought on what the Most High has done. - Solomon shows what a companion meditation makes of wisdom: when he came into his house he reposed himself with her, for her conversation has no bitterness and living with her has no sorrow, but mirth and joy. Get in the habit of chilling with wisdom when you get home. When you ponder the whole benefit package that comes with wisdom, you understand that to be allied unto wisdom is immortality; the wiser you get, the more spiritually invincible you become. Precepts: - Wisdom of Solomon 8:1 The chapter speaks of wisdom as a she who orders all things sweetly and mightily. - Wisdom of Solomon 8:16-17 Solomon pondered these things in his heart; that pondering is the meditation the Lord commanded Joshua. - Make meditation a daily custom, a holy habit, as our forefathers did: somewhere alone and peaceful where the mind can be clear, because you cannot meditate in the middle of activity and noise. When you meditate continually on the commandments, the Lord establishes your heart, and the evil thoughts you battle begin to flush out of your mind. Precepts: - Genesis 24:63 Isaac went out to meditate in the field at the eventide; he had an appointed place and time of day, alone at the going down of the sun, to reflect on the works of the Most High. - Ecclesiasticus 6:37 Meditate continually, as a habit, and he shall establish thine heart and give thee wisdom at thine own desire. - Isaiah 26:3 The mind has to stay on these things, and it will not stay there without continual meditation. - That thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: the end goal of talking about the commandments and meditating on the commandments is to do the commandments. Attending every class, hearing every breakdown, and keeping every precept list is all in vain if you never do thus saith the Lord; not doing the word of God is why we went into slavery and sit at the bottom of society. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 17:18-19 Every king of Israel had to write himself a copy of the law and read therein all the days of his life, not just on a sabbath, that he may learn to fear the Lord and keep the words of this law to do them; you are what you eat, and what you put within comes out in your conversation and your actions. - Ezekiel 33:31-32 Many hear the word as a lovely song, loving to hear the scriptures broken down, but they hear the words and do them not; hearing so much does not earn you credit for doing. - James 1:22 Be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves; it is applying what you heard that saves your soul, not attendance. - For then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success: only after the mouth, the meditation, and the doing does prosperity follow. Thus saith God, the second you transgress the commandments of the Lord you cannot prosper, so any pastor teaching prosperity while saying the law is done away with is teaching a lie. Real prosperity never came from sowing a seed into a basket; it comes from obeying the laws of the Most High, and that applies to us as a whole nation of people. Precepts: - 1 Chronicles 22:13 Then shalt thou prosper, if thou takest heed to fulfil the statutes and judgments which the Lord charged Moses with concerning Israel; the same charge, be strong and of good courage. - Psalms 1:1-3 Blessed is the man who walks not in the counsel of the ungodly but meditates in the law day and night; he brings forth fruit, meaning action, his spirit does not wither, and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper. - Job 36:11 As a nation of people, if they obey and serve him, they shall spend their days in prosperity. - Psalms 122:6 They shall prosper that love thee: the nation that loves Jerusalem, meaning keeps the commandments of her God, prospers. - 2 Chronicles 24:20 The spirit of God came upon Zechariah to ask, Why transgress ye the commandments of the Lord, that ye cannot prosper? The moment you transgress, the prosperity is over. Joshua 1:9 - Have not I commanded thee: not being afraid is a commandment. Fear does not come from the Most High; the only fear he deals with is fearing him and the judgments you suffer for disobeying him. Being scared of what man can do to you is a spirit from the devil, not from God. Precepts: - 2 Timothy 1:7 God hath not given us the spirit of fear, but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind; if the spirit of fear comes upon you, it is not of God. - Nehemiah 6:13 Nehemiah discerned the man urging him to hide in the temple was hired that he should be afraid, and do so, and sin; a leader who becomes afraid of what the heathen threaten is in the midst of sin, so if you carry a fearful spirit, repent. - Look at the end result of a fearful spirit that is never shaken: the fearful are the first named of those whose part is in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone. The Lord gave us the spirit of power; as long as you serve and obey him, there is nothing to be scared of. Precepts: - Revelation 21:8 The fearful head the list of those who take the dive into the lake of fire, before the unbelieving, the abominable, and the murderers. - Ephesians 6:10 Be strong in the Lord and in the power of his might; that is the spirit given in place of fear. Joshua 1:10-15 - Joshua immediately took up the charge: the officers passed through the host with the command, prepare you victuals, for within three days ye shall pass over this Jordan to possess the land which the Lord your God giveth you. - The word to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh goes back to Numbers 32. They had very much cattle, and when they saw the land on this side Jordan was a good place for it, they asked to dwell there. Moses charged them: before you settle, your armed men pass over before your brethren, all the mighty men of valour, and help them fight; when your brethren have rest and possession, then return to the land of your possession toward the sunrising and enjoy it. Precepts: - Numbers 32:20-22 The deal Moses made: go armed before the Lord to war until the land be subdued, and afterward ye shall return and be guiltless, and this land shall be your possession before the Lord. Joshua 1:16-18 - All that thou commandest us we will do, and whithersoever thou sendest us we will go: that is loyalty and the willingness to obey orders, something the Lord loves, and part of the spirit it takes to obtain the promised land. - The boundary stands: if an order breaks the commandments of God, no. But if it falls within the boundaries of the commandments, be willing without hesitation to do what your leader tells you. Whatever position you hold in the body, you are a servant, and when the opportunity comes to fulfill an order you need to be ready; that readiness is the spirit we lack in Israel. Precepts: - 2 Samuel 15:15 The king's servants said, Behold, thy servants are ready to do whatsoever my lord the king shall appoint; always ready, whatever is needed. - 1 Maccabees 13:8-9 When Judas fell and Simon rose up in his stead, the people vowed the same obedience to the new leader, just as Israel did with Joshua after Moses. - According as we hearkened unto Moses in all things, so we will hearken unto thee: when a leader falls and a new leader rises in his stead, that is who the Lord appointed over you, and he is owed the same respect the original leader had. Moses himself asked the Lord to select the man; the selection is spiritual. - Whosoever rebels against thy commandment and will not hearken unto thy words shall be put to death: that is how our forefathers rolled. Under Christ there is grace and mercy, but the order still works by delegation; instruction passes from Christ through the brothers he sets over you, and refusing the brother who carries the order is refusing the one who sent it. Rehearse these righteous acts of taking orders while you have grace. Joshua 2: Rahab and the Spies Read the chapter → Joshua 2 Joshua 2:1-7 - Joshua sent two men out of Shittim to spy secretly and view the land, even Jericho, and they came into the house of a harlot named Rahab and lodged there. - Word made its way to the king of Jericho that men of the children of Israel had come to search out the country, and he sent unto Rahab to bring them forth.
