She had taken the two men and hid them on the roof under the stalks of flax she had laid in order there. - She told the king's men the truth in part and misdirection in the rest: men came unto me, but I wist not whence they were, and they went out about the time of the shutting of the gate; pursue after them quickly. The pursuers chased toward Jordan after men who had gone nowhere, the gate was shut behind them, and the spies had clearance to escape. A heathen woman looked out for Israel, and she did it out of the fear of the Lord, as her own words show. Joshua 2:8-11 - Before the spies lay down, Rahab came up to the roof and confessed: I know that the Lord hath given you the land, and that your terror is fallen upon us, and that all the inhabitants of the land faint because of you. That is faith and belief; a heathen acknowledged that the God of Israel had ordained them to conquer her land. Precepts: - Matthew 15:27-28 Like the woman who answered, Truth, Lord: yet the dogs eat of the crumbs which fall from their masters' table, and Christ said, great is thy faith; Rahab is a heathen whose faith the Lord honoured. - Her faith came by report: we have heard how the Lord dried up the water of the Red Sea for you, and what ye did unto Sihon and Og, the two kings of the Amorites whom ye utterly destroyed; and as soon as we had heard it, our hearts did melt, neither did there remain any more courage in any man. The Lord had said he would put that spirit on the nations. Precepts: - Numbers 21:34-35 The destruction of Sihon and Og on the other side Jordan was the report that reached Jericho. - Deuteronomy 2:25 This day will I begin to put the dread of thee and the fear of thee upon the nations, who shall hear report of thee, and shall tremble and be in anguish because of thee; Rahab's melted heart is that word fulfilled. - Faith and fear go hand in hand. Rahab knew the Lord is not to be played with when it comes to this people, and that fear is what gave her the faith to put her life on the line. She might get caught by her king for hiding the spies, but what she really feared was the judgment of their God if she did not help them. Precepts: - Hebrews 11:31 By faith the harlot Rahab perished not with them that believed not, when she had received the spies with peace; her fear of the Lord worked faith, and that faith saved her. Joshua 2:12-21 - Rahab asked the spies to swear unto her by the Lord, since she had shewed them kindness, that they would shew kindness unto her father's house and give her a true token, saving her father, mother, brethren, and sisters alive. - The men answered, our life for yours, if ye utter not this our business: since she looked out for Israel, Israel would look out for her, on condition the plan stayed secret. If she uttered the business, the oath was null and void. - The token was the line of scarlet thread bound in the window by which she let them down, for her house was upon the town wall. That scarlet line marked her house so no one in it would be slain when Israel came into the land; the terms were that whosoever went out of the doors into the street, his blood would be on his own head, and whosoever stayed within, his blood on Israel's head if any hand touched him. - She sent them to the mountain to hide three days until the pursuers returned, said according unto your words, so be it, and bound the scarlet line in the window. Joshua 2:22-24 - The spies abode in the mountain three days until the pursuers returned, having sought them throughout all the way and found them not. - They came again to Joshua and reported: truly the Lord hath delivered into our hands all the land, for even all the inhabitants of the country do faint because of us. The land was theirs for the taking, exactly as the Lord had promised. Joshua 3: Jordan Driven Back Read the chapter → Joshua 3 Joshua 3:1-4 - Joshua rose early in the morning, and Israel removed from Shittim and came to Jordan and lodged there before passing over. After three days the officers went through the host to spread the orders and instructions the people had to abide by. - The instruction: when ye see the ark of the covenant and the priests the Levites bearing it, remove from your place and go after it, keeping a space of about two thousand cubits between you and it, for ye have not passed this way heretofore. - Officers passing through the host with orders is the same order we rehearse today, with officers and captains coming through the lines at the marches and the men's conferences. We are not reading these stories just to marvel at them; we observe them to do them, learning how to set the nation in order with ranks and delegation. We are rehearsing the righteous acts of our fathers and living the words of this Bible. Joshua 3:5-8 - Sanctify yourselves: for tomorrow the Lord will do wonders among you. Israel had to prepare themselves for miracles; the Lord announced ahead what he was about to do. - The Lord told Joshua, this day will I begin to magnify thee in the sight of all Israel, that they may know that as I was with Moses, so I will be with thee. The people were about to see the Lord rocking with Joshua the same way he rocked with Moses. - Joshua was to command the priests bearing the ark of the covenant: when ye are come to the brink of the water of Jordan, ye shall stand still in Jordan. Joshua 3:9-13 - Joshua called Israel to hear the words of the Lord: hereby ye shall know that the living God is among you, and that he will without fail drive out from before you the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Hivites, the Perizzites, the Girgashites, the Amorites, and the Jebusites. - Twelve men were to be taken out of the tribes of Israel, one man out of every tribe, prepared ahead for what would follow the crossing. - The sign given in advance: as soon as the soles of the feet of the priests that bear the ark of the Lord rest in the waters of Jordan, the waters coming down from above shall be cut off and stand upon an heap, and a riverbed becomes dry land for a whole nation to walk through. Hear a word like that today and men would call you crazy, but that is how the Lord dealt with Israel; they had to be ready for miracles. Joshua 3:14-17 - Jordan overflows all his banks all the time of harvest, yet the moment the feet of the priests bearing the ark were dipped in the brim of the water, the waters which came down from above rose up upon an heap very far from the city Adam beside Zaretan, and the waters coming down toward the salt sea failed and were cut off. - No man can stand in a river, but the priests that bare the ark of the covenant of the Lord stood firm on dry ground in the midst of Jordan, and all Israel passed over on dry ground right against Jericho, until all the people were passed clean over. - When the Lord is dwelling within Israel, the creation itself moves for them; only for the Israelites will a river fall back. You do not know the manner of love the Most High bestowed upon this people to call them the children of God. Precepts: - Psalms 114:1-3 When Israel went out of Egypt, Judah was his sanctuary and Israel his dominion; the sea saw it and fled, Jordan was driven back, because the Lord was dwelling within his people. Joshua 4: The Twelve Stone Memorial Read the chapter → Joshua 4 Joshua 4:1-9 - When all the people were clean passed over, the Lord commanded Joshua to take twelve men, one out of every tribe, and have each carry a stone upon his shoulder out of the midst of Jordan, from the very place where the priests' feet stood firm, over to the lodging place. - The stones are a sign and a memorial: when your children ask their fathers in time to come, What mean ye by these stones? ye shall answer them, that the waters of Jordan were cut off before the ark of the covenant of the Lord. These stones lay in the middle of a river that Israel walked through on dry ground, and they memorialize that forever. - Joshua also set up twelve stones in the midst of Jordan itself, in the place where the feet of the priests which bare the ark stood, and they are there unto this day. Joshua 4:10-14 - The priests which bare the ark stood in the midst of Jordan until every thing was finished that the Lord commanded Joshua to speak unto the people, and the people hasted and passed over. - The children of Reuben, the children of Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh passed over armed before the children of Israel, about forty thousand prepared for war, keeping the word they gave Moses: suited for battle with their brethren before returning to enjoy their own land on the other side. - On that day the Lord magnified Joshua in the sight of all Israel, and they feared him as they feared Moses all the days of his life. A man through whom the Lord makes a whole river stand up commands that reverence. Joshua 4:15-18 - The priests stayed firm at their post in the riverbed even after all the people had passed over, until the Lord spake to Joshua and Joshua gave the order: come ye up out of Jordan. That is discipline, order, fortitude, and faith; they held their place in the midst of a stopped river without wavering. Precepts: - Matthew 14:29-31 Peter walked on the water, but as soon as doubt came he began to sink; had the priests doubted and thought the water was about to fall, they could not have stood, but their feet stood firm. - As soon as the soles of the priests' feet were lifted up unto the dry land, the waters of Jordan returned unto their place and flowed over all his banks as they did before. Everything held its place exactly as long as Israel needed it to. Joshua 4:19-24 - The people came up out of Jordan on the tenth day of the first month and encamped in Gilgal, in the east border of Jericho, and there Joshua pitched the twelve stones they took out of Jordan. - The fathers were given the answer for their children: Israel came over this Jordan on dry land, for the Lord your God dried up the waters of Jordan from before you until ye were passed over, as the Lord your God did to the Red Sea. The later generation witnessed the same kind of miracle the previous generation saw, because Joshua carried the same spirit Moses had, and the Lord rocked with him the same way. - The purpose is written: that all the people of the earth might know the hand of the Lord, that it is mighty, that ye might fear the Lord your God for ever. The world was made for Israel's sake; the waters and everything else in the earth answer to what the Most High commands for his people, but when the Lord is not dwelling among Israel, that power is not there. Seeing what he does in the twinkling of an eye is faith building, and it teaches the fear of the Lord. --- Topics: The Covenant · The Feasts of the Most High · The Priesthood · The Sabbath ← Deuteronomy 31-34 · Joshua Study · Joshua 5-8 →

title: Joshua 13: Much Land Yet to Be Possessed
text: ← Joshua 9-12 · Joshua Study · Joshua 17-20 → Joshua 13: Much Land Yet to Be Possessed Read the chapter → Joshua 13 Introduction This session covers Joshua 13 through 16, where the dividing of the land begins. Joshua is now old, and the Most High names the land that still remains to be possessed, confirms the inheritance Moses gave the two tribes and a half on the other side Jordan, and commands the rest to be divided by lot. Caleb receives Hebron for wholly following the Most High, then the lot of the tribe of Judah and the lot of the children of Joseph are drawn out. These chapters carry a whole lot of names of cities and borders, so as you read and listen back through them, it does not hurt to pull up a map or look through your Bible atlas and find where these places were, to get a geographical sense of the land the children of Israel were moving through and conquering. Joshua 13:1 - Joshua is old and stricken in years, and there remaineth yet very much land to be possessed. The Most High had already said he was not going to drive out these nations in one year, but little and little as Israel increased, so much land still remained. - The nations were also left among Israel to prove them, whether they would keep the commandments of the Most High, and so that the generations which had not known the wars of Canaan might be taught war. We all know what ended up happening with that proving, and it comes later on as we read. Precepts: - Exodus 23:29-30 I will not drive them out before thee in one year, but by little and little, until thou be increased and inherit the land. - Judges 3:1-2 These are the nations the Most High left to prove Israel, that the generations might know, to teach them war. Joshua 13:2-5 - This is the land that yet remains: all the borders of the Philistines with their five lords, the Gazathites, the Ashdothites, the Eshkalonites, the Gittites, and the Ekronites, along with the Avites, the Canaanites, the Sidonians, the Amorites, the Giblites, and all Lebanon toward the sunrising. - These are the different peoples that still had to be driven out of these lands. Joshua 13:6-7 - The Most High himself will drive out the inhabitants of the hill country of Lebanon and all the Sidonians from before the children of Israel; Joshua's part is only to divide the land by lot unto the Israelites for an inheritance, as he was commanded. - The land is to be divided only unto the Israelites: unto the nine tribes and the half tribe of Manasseh, for the other two and a half tribes had already received theirs. It had already been told that these lands must be divided among our people. Precepts: - Numbers 33:54 Ye shall divide the land by lot for an inheritance among your families; the command was given long before. - Joshua 11:23 Joshua gave the land for an inheritance unto Israel according to their divisions by their tribes. Joshua 13:8-14 - The Reubenites and the Gadites had already received their inheritance with the half tribe of Manasseh, which Moses gave them beyond Jordan eastward: all the cities of Sihon king of the Amorites and all the kingdom of Og in Bashan, who remained of the remnant of the giants, for these did Moses smite and cast out. - Nevertheless the children of Israel expelled not the Geshurites nor the Maachathites, but they dwelt among the Israelites until this day. - Only unto the tribe of Levi he gave none inheritance; the sacrifices of the Lord God of Israel made by fire are their inheritance. The Most High had already said the same thing way back to Aaron, that Levi would have no inheritance in the land but would live among the people, and what was stated back then is being carried out in what we are reading now. Precepts: - Numbers 18:20 Thou shalt have no inheritance in their land; I am thy part and thine inheritance among the children of Israel. Joshua 13:15-23 - Moses gave the tribe of the children of Reuben their inheritance according to their families: from Aroer on the bank of the river Arnon, all the plain by Medeba, Heshbon and all her cities, unto Jordan and his border, the cities and the villages thereof. - With the princes of Midian, Balaam also the son of Beor, the soothsayer, did the children of Israel slay with the sword. This is the same Balaam from Numbers 22, the one whose ass saw the angel standing there to kill him when he could not see it himself. He was the one going after the lust of greed, and he ended up getting put to death. Precepts: - Numbers 22:5 The same Balaam the son of Beor that was sent for to curse Israel; he chased the reward and was slain. Joshua 13:24-28 - Moses gave inheritance unto the tribe of the children of Gad according to their families: Jazer and all the cities of Gilead, half the land of the children of Ammon, and the rest of the kingdom of Sihon king of Heshbon, unto the edge of the sea of Chinnereth on the other side Jordan eastward, the cities and their villages. Joshua 13:29-33 - Moses gave inheritance unto the half tribe of Manasseh by their families: from Mahanaim, all Bashan, all the kingdom of Og, and all the towns of Jair, threescore cities, pertaining unto the children of Machir the son of Manasseh. - These are the countries which Moses distributed for inheritance in the plains of Moab, on the other side Jordan by Jericho eastward. - But unto the tribe of Levi Moses gave not any inheritance: the Lord God of Israel was their inheritance, as he said unto them. It is the same thing that is said in verse 14. Joshua 14: Caleb Wholly Followed the Most High Read the chapter → Joshua 14 Joshua 14:1-5 - The countries in the land of Canaan were distributed by Eleazar the priest, Joshua the son of Nun, and the heads of the fathers of the tribes, by lot, as the Most High commanded by the hand of Moses, for the nine tribes and the half tribe; Moses had already given the two tribes and a half their inheritance on the other side Jordan. - The children of Joseph were two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim, therefore no part was given unto the Levites in the land, save cities to dwell in with their suburbs for their cattle and for their substance. - The Levites were living in the suburbs, which is the towns, right among the people. They did not have a land designated to themselves; they were spread throughout all the many tribes. Joshua 14:6-9 - Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenezite comes to Joshua in Gilgal and reminds him of the thing the Most High said unto Moses concerning them both in Kadeshbarnea: Caleb was forty years old when Moses sent him from Kadeshbarnea to spy out the land, and he brought word again as it was in his heart. - His brethren that went up with him made the heart of the people melt, but he wholly followed the Lord his God. The men that went with him brought up an evil report, made the people afraid, and made them doubt. - Caleb was not playing any games; he was about that business, ready to go and take the land, because he understood the Most High had already promised us the land, so he had no fear. That is the spirit that says, let us go up at once and possess it. - So Moses sware on that day that the land whereon Caleb's feet had trodden would be his inheritance and his children's for ever, because he wholly followed the Lord. Precepts: - Numbers 13:25-30 The spies returned after forty days, and Caleb stilled the people before Moses: let us go up at once and possess it, for we are well able to overcome it. - Numbers 13:31-33 The men that went up with him brought an evil report of giants, saying we were in our own sight as grasshoppers, and made the people afraid. Joshua 14:10-11 - The Most High has kept Caleb alive these forty and five years, and now at fourscore and five years old he is as strong this day as he was in the day Moses sent him; as his strength was then, even so is his strength now, for war, both to go out and to come in. This man is eighty-five years old and in perfect health. - Moses was the same way: a hundred and twenty years old with the strength and the vision of a young man. A lot of us are not living to a hundred and twenty, but at the same time we are making it to sixty and seventy, and at fifty we are hooked up on machines. We are all going to die at some point, but that does not mean you have to be miserable, sitting there hooked up to all kind of machines while you are here. - Leadership has been pushing that we all need to take care of our bodies and our health. A lot of us deal with gluttony even though it is not a topic we talk about all the time; cut down a little what you eat and eat better food. - The same way we make haste to stop the different sins, be quick to change the diet. If we make haste to change those things, the Most High will also keep away that continual sickness, the diabetes and everything causing our limbs to be cut off just to live. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 34:7 Moses was an hundred and twenty years old when he died: his eye was not dim, nor his natural force abated. - Ecclesiasticus 30:15-17 There is no riches above a sound body; do not spend your years on the earth in continual sickness. - Ecclesiasticus 31:22 Be quick in all thy works, including how you eat, so shall there no sickness come unto thee. Joshua 14:12-15 - Caleb asks for the very mountain the Anakims were in: now therefore give me this mountain, whereof the Lord spake in that day, for thou heardest how the Anakims were there and the cities were great and fenced; if so be the Lord will be with me, then I shall be able to drive them out. - Joshua blessed him and gave Caleb the son of Jephunneh Hebron for an inheritance, and it became his inheritance unto this day, because he wholly followed the Lord God of Israel. - The name of Hebron before was Kirjatharba, which Arba was a great man among the Anakims. And the land had rest from war. Joshua 15: The Lot of the Tribe of Judah Read the chapter → Joshua 15 Joshua 15:1-4 - This is the lot of the tribe of the children of Judah by their families, even to the border of Edom: the south border ran from the shore of the salt sea, up the south side of Kadeshbarnea, and out unto the river of Egypt, with the goings out of that coast at the sea. - We are not locating every one of these places as we read, but as you go back and listen, look these places up in your Bible atlas so you can see the actual areas being read about in the region. Joshua 15:5-12 - The east border was the salt sea unto the end of Jordan; the north border went up from the bay of the sea, by Bethhogla and the stone of Bohan the son of Reuben, and up by the valley of the son of Hinnom unto the south side of the Jebusite: the same is Jerusalem. - The border went to the top of the mountain before the valley of Hinnom westward, at the end of the valley of the giants northward, then out by Kirjathjearim, Bethshemesh, and Ekron, and the west border was to the great sea. This is the coast of the children of Judah round about according to their families. Joshua 15:13-19 - Unto Caleb the son of Jephunneh was given a part among the children of Judah according to the commandment of the Lord to Joshua: the city of Arba the father of Anak, which city is Hebron. And Caleb drove thence the three sons of Anak: Sheshai, and Ahiman, and Talmai, the children of Anak. - He went up thence to the inhabitants of Debir, whose name before was Kirjathsepher, and said, he that smiteth Kirjathsepher and taketh it, to him will I give Achsah my daughter to wife. Othniel the son of Kenaz, the brother of Caleb, took it, and got Achsah to wife. - Achsah moved him to ask of her father a field, and said, give me a blessing, for thou hast given me a south land; give me also springs of water. And Caleb gave her the upper springs and the nether springs. Joshua 15:20 - This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Judah according to their families, and the chapter counts out their cities district by district through verse 62: the uttermost cities toward the coast of Edom southward, twenty and nine cities with their villages; the cities in the valley in their groups of fourteen, sixteen, and nine; Ekron, Ashdod, and Gaza with their towns and villages unto the river of Egypt and the great sea; the cities in the mountains in their groups of eleven, nine, ten, six, and two; and six cities in the wilderness, all with their villages. Joshua 15:63 - As for the Jebusites, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the children of Judah could not drive them out, but the Jebusites dwell with the children of Judah at Jerusalem unto this day. - Later on David conquered this place. The Jebusites thought David could not come in, that he was not getting past those walls, saying except thou take away the blind and the lame thou shalt not come in hither; nevertheless David took the stronghold of Zion, the same is the city of David, and dwelt in the fort and built round about. - The people that were left of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, whom Israel was not able utterly to destroy, upon those did Solomon levy a tribute of bondservice unto this day. They were forced to become our bondservants. Precepts: - 2 Samuel 5:6-9 The Jebusites said David could not come in hither, but David took the stronghold of Zion, the same is the city of David. - 1 Kings 9:20-21 Upon the people left of those nations did Solomon levy a tribute of bondservice unto this day. Joshua 16: The Lot of the Children of Joseph Read the chapter → Joshua 16 Joshua 16:1-2 - The lot of the children of Joseph fell from Jordan by Jericho, unto the water of Jericho on the east, up through mount Bethel, and goeth out from Bethel to Luz. - This location is the same place where our forefather Jacob was, where he had the vision of the ladder that reached up into heaven. Jacob rose up early, took the stone he had put for his pillows, set it up for a pillar, and called the name of that place Bethel, but the name of that city was called Luz at the first. - We are reading about it in Joshua where our forefather had already been to that location, and we are just going back to take it back. That is what we are doing. Precepts: - Genesis 28:18-19 Jacob set up the stone for a pillar and called that place Bethel, but the name of that city was called Luz at the first. Joshua 16:3-9 - The children of Joseph, Manasseh and Ephraim, took their inheritance. The border of the children of Ephraim by their families ran from Ataroth on the east, about eastward unto Taanathshiloh, down to Jericho and out at Jordan, and from Tappuah westward unto the river Kanah, with the goings out thereof at the sea. - There were also separate cities for the children of Ephraim among the inheritance of the children of Manasseh, all the cities with their villages. Joshua 16:10 - They drave not out the Canaanites that dwelt in Gezer, but the Canaanites dwell among the Ephraimites unto this day, and serve under tribute. - Like the Jebusites among Judah, these were also forced to be under tribute, as our bondservants. --- Topics: Esau and Edom · Idolatry · Sacrifice and Atonement · The Priesthood ← Joshua 9-12 · Joshua Study · Joshua 17-20 →

title: Joshua 17: The Lot of Manasseh and the Blessing of Ephraim
text: ← Joshua 13-16 · Joshua Study · Joshua 21-24 → Joshua 17: The Lot of Manasseh and the Blessing of Ephraim Read the chapter → Joshua 17 Introduction This session covers Joshua 17 through 20 verse by verse: the lot of the tribe of Manasseh, the seven tribes still waiting for their inheritance and the lots cast at Shiloh, the portions of Benjamin, Simeon, Zebulun, Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and Dan, and the cities of refuge with the laws of the slayer. Bible maps of the conquest of the land of Canaan are used throughout to bring the scriptures to life, so we can see where our forefathers and foremothers, the real twelve tribes of Israel, lived in the land. Joshua 17:1 - A lot goes into an allotment, a portion; there was a portion for the tribe of Manasseh, for he was the firstborn of Joseph. Machir, the firstborn of Manasseh and the father of Gilead, was a man of war, therefore he had Gilead and Bashan. - Bashan was the kingdom of Og, one of the giants that Israel conquered under Joshua. Before the conquest all this territory was called the land of Canaan, with the Canaanites, the Perizzites, and the Jebusites and their families dwelling in it. - Prior to this chapter Judah received his inheritance in chapter 15 and the inheritance of Joseph, Ephraim, came in chapter 16; after the victories the Most High gave through Christ, the land was divided by lot so that every tribe had its portion. - The Bible maps that even the enemies of Israel put together according to the scriptures show this history: Manasseh held Bashan and a portion by Gilead on the other side of Jordan. The so-called Cubans come from this tribe; this is their history that their enemies do not want them to know. Joshua 17:2 - There was also a lot for the rest of the children of Manasseh by their families, Abiezer, Helek, Asriel, Shechem, Hepher, and Shemida: these were the male children of Manasseh the son of Joseph. - Remember that Manasseh was the son of Joseph; Joseph had two sons, Ephraim and Manasseh. Joshua 17:3-4 - Zelophehad the son of Hepher had no sons, but daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah. - They came near before Eleazar the priest, before Joshua the son of Nun, and before the princes, saying the Lord commanded Moses to give them an inheritance among their brethren; and according to the commandment of the Lord he gave them an inheritance among the brethren of their father. Joshua 17:5-6 - Ten portions fell to Manasseh, beside the land of Gilead and Bashan which were on the other side of Jordan. On the map the Jordan river flows down through the land, and across the river sat Gilead and Bashan, the lands Manasseh already held. - Down south the Jordan empties into the Dead Sea, and Sodom and Gomorrah sat south of the Dead Sea, by where Edom was residing; the maps give a good feel for what the Bible is talking about. - The daughters of Manasseh had an inheritance among his sons, just as the Lord commanded for the daughters of Zelophehad, and the rest of Manasseh's sons had the land of Gilead. Joshua 17:7-8 - The coast of Manasseh ran from Asher to Michmethah; Manasseh had the land of Tappuah, but Tappuah itself on the border of Manasseh belonged to the children of Ephraim. - We have to know where our forefathers came from and what the Bible is speaking about; that is why we search out these borders on the maps, where Tappuah sat on the southern border by Shechem. Joshua 17:9-11 - The coast descended to the river Kanah: southward of the river the cities were Ephraim's, and northward it was Manasseh's, the sea was his border, and they met together in Asher on the north and in Issachar on the east. - This land of Canaan is also known as Israel, and this is where our foremothers and forefathers lived: the so-called Mexicans, Guatemalans, and Hondurans lived here, and the so-called Brazilians, Colombians, and Venezuelans up in these coasts. A lot of times we read that Asher lived here and forget it is talking about us; our people need the visual. - Manasseh also had within Issachar and Asher the cities of Beth-shean, Ibleam, Dor, En-dor, Taanach, and Megiddo with their towns, even three countries. Joshua 17:12-13 - Even though Israel conquered the majority of the land of Canaan, there were still areas the Canaanites kept possession of; the children of Manasseh could not drive out the inhabitants of those cities, but the Canaanites would dwell in that land. - When the children of Israel were waxen strong, they put the Canaanites to tribute, but did not utterly drive them out; they kept them as servants and handmaids. Joshua 17:14-15 - The children of Joseph, led by Ephraim, asked Joshua why he gave them but one lot to inherit, seeing they are a great people; great here means numerous. Ephraim and Manasseh were among the most populated tribes, and Ephraim's own portion had already been given back in chapter 16. - Their fruitfulness was prophesied when Israel blessed Joseph; the very name Ephraim goes into being fruitful. Precepts: - Genesis 49:22 Joseph is a fruitful bough; the fruitfulness of Joseph's seed was prophesied by Israel. - Joshua answered without bias: if thou be a great people, then get thee up to the wood country, into the forest, and cut down there in the land of the Perizzites and of the giants, if mount Ephraim be too narrow for thee. Narrow means too small: if you are complaining that your lot is too small, then go to war and conquer more land. Joshua 17:16 - The children of Joseph answered that the hill is not enough for them, and the Canaanites that dwell in the land of the valley have chariots of iron; those nations had military power too. - On the map those Canaanites sat right north of Manasseh, in Beth-shean and her towns and in the valley of Jezreel, dwelling in the midst of our brothers with an army; they were a problem, and Manasseh was already having a hard time with them. Joshua 17:17-18 - Joshua told the house of Joseph, thou art a great people and hast great power; the mountain shall be thine, and thou shalt drive out the Canaanites, though they have iron chariots and though they be strong. Going through the wood means going through the dense forest; it would be a struggle, but at the end of the day they would overcome. - Manasseh had issues driving the Canaanites out, but Ephraim did it. The difference between the two brothers goes back to Genesis 48, where Israel blessed Joseph's sons and crossed his hands, guiding them wittingly, meaning he knew exactly what he was doing. Precepts: - Genesis 48:1-2 Joseph brought his two sons Manasseh and Ephraim to his sick father, and Israel strengthened himself and sat upon the bed, glad to see his son. - Genesis 48:8-11 Israel's eyes were dim for age; he kissed and embraced Joseph's sons, saying he had not thought to see Joseph's face, and lo, God had shewed him his seed also. - Genesis 48:12-14 Joseph set Manasseh toward Israel's right hand for the greater blessing of the firstborn, but Israel stretched his right hand upon Ephraim the younger, guiding his hands wittingly. - Genesis 48:17-19 It displeased Joseph and he held up his father's hand, but Israel refused, saying I know it, my son: Manasseh shall also be great, but his younger brother shall be greater, and his seed shall become a multitude of nations. - Ephraim being greater goes into Ephraim becoming the head of the ten tribes, the head of the kingdom of Samaria; and it was Ephraim that led the charge, with the help of Issachar and Manasseh, that brought the ten tribes from the eastern hemisphere to the western hemisphere. The unicorn there is not a fairy tale horse; the original etymology goes into the rhinoceros. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 33:17 Joseph's horns are the horns of unicorns, and with them he shall push the people together to the ends of the earth; they are the ten thousands of Ephraim and the thousands of Manasseh. - Isaiah 7:9 The head of Ephraim is Samaria; Ephraim became the ruler of the ten tribes. - Judges 8:1 The men of Ephraim chided sharply with Gideon for not calling them to the battle against the Midianites; that war-like spirit was always in Ephraim. - The Zondervan compact Bible dictionary, a tool to add to your arsenal, says Ephraim and Manasseh seem to have been bitter rivals, Manasseh being the larger group, but Ephraim asserting the more vigorous leadership, though they seem to have held their land in common for a time. Vigorous means very passionate, sometimes rough; that is the spirit the children of Ephraim have. - In Judges 7 Manasseh went to war with the three hundred men and destroyed the Midianites though they were lower in numbers, because Christ gave them the victory; then in Judges 8 Ephraim was upset that they were not called to help in that war. Ephraim always had that leadership attribute, that military spirit. Joshua 18: The Lots Cast at Shiloh Read the chapter → Joshua 18 Joshua 18:1-2 - The whole congregation of the children of Israel assembled together at Shiloh and set up the tabernacle of the congregation there, and the land was subdued before them: they won the war, and the land was now in their control. - There remained among the children of Israel seven tribes which had not yet received their inheritance. Joshua 18:3 - How long are ye slack to go possess the land which the Lord God of your fathers hath given you? The land was already given; they were waiting instead of going in to possess it. Slack means lazy, slothful, full of excuses. - It is the same spirit a lot of our brothers and sisters have today: you have gifts you bring to the table, but you exercise them for your boss at work and are slack when it comes to the necessities of your nation. This shows we are the children of Israel, because that is the spirit we have, and we have to come out of that thing. - We cannot sit back knowing Christ is coming and not do the work; the time is short, and this is not our rest. We have to bring our brothers and sisters to repentance. Precepts: - Proverbs 12:24 The hand of the diligent shall bear rule, but the slothful shall be under tribute; the other tribes were diligent and went and conquered their land. - Micah 4:10 Be in pain and labour to bring forth, O daughter of Zion; the daughter of Zion is the children of Israel. - Luke 17:21 The kingdom of God is within you; it is up to us to labour and bring forth the kingdom. Joshua 18:4-5 - Joshua asked for three men from each tribe, that he may send them to rise and go through the land and describe it according to the inheritance of them, dividing it into seven parts; he wanted a good description of the land. - Judah shall abide in their coast on the south, and the house of Joseph in their coasts on the north; when you look at the map you see Judah sitting south of Ephraim, exactly as it is written. Joshua 18:6-7 - The description of the seven parts was to be brought to Joshua, that he may cast lots for them before the Lord. Casting lots is like throwing dice or drawing straws: you may be the one throwing, but the Lord decides what comes up. Precepts: - Proverbs 16:33 The lot is cast into the lap, but the whole disposing thereof is of the Lord; the Lord decided the outcome of the inheritance of these lands. - Jonah 1:1-7 The mariners said, Come, and let us cast lots, that we may know for whose cause this evil is upon us; they cast lots, and the lot fell upon Jonah, because the lot belongs to the Lord. - Jonah is also the picture of the slack spirit: he wanted nothing to do with prophesying to wake his people up, and he lay fast asleep down in the sides of the ship while the tempest was ready to break it. America is that spiritual ship that is going to sink, and a lot of our people are asleep in the middle of the chaos, comfortable while a pestilence from the Lord is on the earth. - The Levites have no part among you, for the priesthood of the Lord is their inheritance. The Levites were well taken care of; they dwelt in the suburbs of the cities and had the best of everything. Precepts: - Numbers 18:23 The Levites do the service of the tabernacle, and among the children of Israel they have no inheritance. - Deuteronomy 10:9 Levi hath no part nor inheritance with his brethren; the Lord is his inheritance. - Gad and Reuben and the half tribe of Manasseh had already received their inheritance beyond Jordan on the east, which Moses the servant of the Lord gave them. Joshua 18:8-10 - The men arose and passed through the land and described it by cities into seven parts in a book, and came again to Joshua to the host at Shiloh. - Joshua cast lots for them in Shiloh before the Lord, and there divided the land unto the children of Israel according to their divisions; Shiloh, where the lots were cast, sat in the land of Ephraim. Joshua 18:11-20 - The lot of the tribe of the children of Benjamin came up, and the coast of their lot came between the children of Judah and the children of Joseph. - Their north border went from Jordan up the side of Jericho, through the mountains westward toward Luz, which is Bethel; the south quarter ran by the valley of the son of Hinnom, which is in the valley of the giants, down to En-rogel, and out to the north bay of the salt sea at the south end of Jordan. - To get actual depictions of what is being described, look up Bible maps from the time of Joshua's conquest of the land of Canaan; the Lord told Joshua to destroy those nations so that all Israel, his children, had an inheritance. Joshua 18:21-28 - These are the cities of the tribe of the children of Benjamin: Jericho, Beth-hoglah, Bethel, Gibeon, Ramah, Mizpeh, and the rest, twenty and six cities in all with their villages. - Among them is Jebusi, which is Jerusalem: Jerusalem sat in the portion of Benjamin. This was the inheritance of the children of Benjamin according to their families. Joshua 19: The Portions of the Remaining Tribes Read the chapter → Joshua 19 Joshua 19:1 - The second lot came forth to Simeon, and their inheritance was within the inheritance of the children of Judah. - On the map the whole land Judah possessed is marked as one, and within it sits the portion where Simeon resided, down by Beer-sheba. The so-called Dominicans, of Simeon, were living within the land of the so-called African Americans, of Judah; this is our history and where we lived. - It only sounds crazy because we are not taught anything prior to 1492; we are the real Jews, and these maps show where our forefathers and our foremothers were living. Joshua 19:8-9 - This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Simeon according to their families, out of the portion of the children of Judah: for the part of the children of Judah was too much for them. - Judah had a lot of area and was being his brother's keeper: come dwell with us, Simeon, we got you; therefore the children of Simeon had their inheritance within the inheritance of them. Joshua 19:10 - The third lot came up for the children of Zebulun according to their families, and the border of their inheritance was unto Sarid, twelve cities with their villages. - Zebulun sat north, together with Issachar and Asher; those three tribes would always reside together, just like today, and Naphtali stayed close to Asher. The same way, Reuben and Gad were always together on the map. - Today Gad and Reuben reside in the United States of America: Reubenites in Florida, Georgia, Mississippi, Louisiana, and Oklahoma, and Gad also in Idaho, North Dakota, South Dakota, Utah, Texas, and New Mexico; they are known today as the North American Indians or First Nations peoples, but according to the Bible they are Israelites. - Seminole is not a real nationality; seminole means runaway, and Indian goes into slave or servant. God calls you Reuben, God calls you Israel; the Most High gave you a holy, sanctified, powerful name. We are the twelve tribes, the so-called Blacks, Hispanics, and Native Americans. Joshua 19:17-18 - The fourth lot came out to Issachar according to their families, and their border was toward Jezreel; their coast reached to Tabor and went out at Jordan, sixteen cities with their villages. Joshua 19:24 - The fifth lot came out for the tribe of the children of Asher according to their families; their border reached to Carmel westward, up to great Zidon and to the strong city Tyre, twenty and two cities with their villages. Joshua 19:32-35 - The sixth lot came out to the children of Naphtali; their coast reached to Zebulun on the south side, to Asher on the west side, and to Judah upon Jordan toward the sunrising, meaning the east. - The fenced cities are cities with great walls; they were bordered and protected for military purposes, so that the land and the city would not be infiltrated. Joshua 19:40 - The seventh lot came out for the tribe of the children of Dan according to their families, with Zorah, Eshtaol, Ajalon, Ekron, and the border before Japho. Joshua 19:47 - The coast of the children of Dan went out too little for them: they lost their portion, they let it slip, and they had to go and conquer different territory. - Therefore the children of Dan went up to fight against Leshem, took it, smote it with the edge of the sword, possessed it, and dwelt therein, and called Leshem, Dan, after the name of Dan their father. Joshua 19:49-51 - When they had made an end of dividing the land, the children of Israel gave an inheritance to Joshua the son of Nun according to the word of the Lord: the city which he asked, Timnath-serah in mount Ephraim; and he built the city and dwelt therein. - Eleazar the priest, Joshua the son of Nun, and the heads of the fathers of the tribes divided the inheritances by lot in Shiloh before the Lord, at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation. So they made an end of dividing the country; everybody had their portion, and everyone was satisfied. Joshua 20: The Cities of Refuge Read the chapter → Joshua 20 Joshua 20:1-3 - Now that every tribe had its inheritance, cities of refuge had to be instituted, as the Lord spake by the hand of Moses: that the slayer that killeth any person unawares and unwittingly may flee thither, and they shall be your refuge from the avenger of blood. - Unwittingly means unknowingly; remember the word wittingly in Genesis 48, where Israel guided his hands knowing what he was doing. This is accidental death, not intentional murder, like leaving a co-worker shut in the freezer by mistake because you were focused on going home. - Notice the scripture says slayer, not murderer: a slayer may be innocent, it may have been a mistake or self-defense, so there are stipulations and laws for his case. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 19:1-3 Moses gave the instruction to separate cities of refuge in the midst of the land; in Joshua 20 Joshua is applying the law. - Deuteronomy 19:4-6 The case of the slayer: two neighbours go into the wood to hew wood, the axe head slips from the helve and lights upon his neighbour that he die; he hated him not in time past, so he was not worthy of death. - Numbers 35:11-12 The cities of refuge were appointed that the manslayer die not, until he stand before the congregation in judgment. - Exodus 21:12-13 The law goes back to Exodus: he that smiteth a man that he die shall surely be put to death, but if a man lie not in wait and God deliver him into his hand, a place is appointed whither he shall flee. - The avenger of blood is a family member of the one killed, and while his heart is hot he is not thinking logically; he is guided by his emotions, and that is how you end up rendering evil for evil. Heart is hot is the same way we talk today, I was hot, I am heated: our forefathers and foremothers spoke the same way. Precepts: - Nehemiah 13:21 Nehemiah said, if ye do so again, I will lay hands on you; the same spirit and speech is in our people to this day. - Deuteronomy 19:11-13 But if any man hate his neighbour and lie in wait and smite him mortally, the elders of his city shall fetch him from the refuge and deliver him to the avenger of blood; thine eye shall not pity him. - Deuteronomy 19:21 Life shall go for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth: that was the judgment instituted in that time; today we are under different laws of the land, and you forgive your brother seventy times seven. - Numbers 35:22-25 If he thrust him suddenly without enmity, or cast a stone seeing him not, the congregation shall judge between the slayer and the revenger of blood and deliver the innocent slayer back to his city of refuge. - The murderer cannot run to a city of refuge to lay low; those cities were not established for him. Even today a killer can cross the border into another jurisdiction and go free, and that is evil; but when Israel controlled the land you could not cross a border to get away with murder, for the elders would deliver you right back to the city you came from. Your sin will find you out. Joshua 20:6 - The slayer shall dwell in that city until he stand before the congregation for judgment: the congregation had to see whether it was a mistake or intentional, questioning him on what he was doing and why, just like a courtroom. - He also dwelt there until the death of the high priest of those days; then the slayer shall return to his own city and his own house, the city from whence he fled. Precepts: - Numbers 35:25 The congregation shall restore him to the city of his refuge, and he shall abide in it unto the death of the high priest, which was anointed with the holy oil. - Numbers 35:26-28 If the slayer comes outside the border of his city of refuge before the death of the high priest and the revenger of blood finds him and kills him, the revenger shall not be guilty of blood; the refuge is protective custody, and he was to remain in it. Joshua 20:7-9 - They appointed Kedesh in Galilee in mount Naphtali, Shechem in mount Ephraim, and Kirjath-arba, which is Hebron, in the mountain of Judah; and on the other side Jordan by Jericho they assigned Bezer out of the tribe of Reuben, Ramoth in Gilead out of the tribe of Gad, and Golan in Bashan out of the tribe of Manasseh. - These cities were appointed for all the children of Israel and for the stranger that sojourneth among them, that whosoever killeth any person at unawares might flee thither and not die by the hand of the avenger of blood, until he stood before the congregation: until he gets a fair trial. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 17:6 At the mouth of two witnesses or three witnesses shall he that is worthy of death be put to death; at the mouth of one witness he shall not be put to death. - Matthew 18:15-17 If thy brother trespass against thee, go and tell him his fault alone; if he will not hear, take one or two more, that in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established, and then tell it unto the church. - If your brother trespasses against you, you do not go and shoot, stab, or fight him; you speak to him alone, and if he hears you, you have gained your brother. This law of righteous judgment is what is missing in the cursed cities of our people, the so-called Blacks, Hispanics, and Native Americans, who have not learned to apply the scripture and await righteous trial. - Not everything is a Matthew 18: Matthew 18 goes into severe sin, a matter worthy of putting somebody out of the body, not a petty disagreement over a parking space, a stepped-on toe, or a mispronounced name. For the petty offenses the scripture says admonish a friend, because many times what you heard is just a tale. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 19:13-17 Admonish a friend, for many times it is a slander; believe not every tale, and do not threaten a Matthew 18 over what only needs a correction. - Luke 17:1 Offences will come, it is inevitable; we build stronger bonds with brothers and sisters through adversity, so endeavor to keep the unity. - 1 John 3:15 The spirit of anger and hatred transitions to murder; whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer. - When you are angry you are not thinking logically; precepts are not coming to your mind, only carnal solutions. Do not go and talk to a brother while you are upset, and do not cleave to another backbiter or gossiper to feed your anger; cleave to somebody positive that is a peacemaker and solution minded. - Give place to the law of the Most High: whatever situation you are going through, the solution is in the Bible, so do not let anger close the book on you. Sometimes the answer is to suffer wrongfully, and what matters is not who is right but what the right thing to do is according to the Bible. Precepts: - 1 Peter 2:19 This is thankworthy, if a man for conscience toward God endure grief, suffering wrongfully; but examine yourself before you use this precept to play the victim, for the Lord knows what is behind closed doors. --- Topics: Esau and Edom · Idolatry · The Feasts of the Most High · The Priesthood · The Sabbath ← Joshua 13-16 · Joshua Study · Joshua 21-24 →

title: Joshua 21: The Cities of the Levites
text: ← Joshua 17-20 · Joshua Study · Judges 1-4 → Joshua 21: The Cities of the Levites Read the chapter → Joshua 21 Introduction This reading closes out the book of Joshua, covering chapters 21 through 24: the cities and suburbs given to the Levites out of every tribe, the altar of witness built by the two and a half tribes on the other side Jordan, Joshua's farewell charge to cleave unto the Most High, and the covenant made at Shechem where all Israel chose to serve the Lord. The book of Joshua, like the books before it, is the history of the tribes; it goes further into how Israel got the land, and precept upon precept some things are more detailed in Numbers while Joshua carries the same history further. The Q&A after the reading is folded into the verses it belongs to. Joshua 21:1-3 - The heads of the fathers of the Levites came near to Eleazar the priest, to Joshua, and to the heads of the tribes at Shiloh, because the tribe of Levi had been appointed cities to dwell in with suburbs for their cattle, and the time had come to receive them. - This was not a new request; it was commanded of the Most High by the hand of Moses that all twelve tribes should give of their inheritance to the Levites. Precepts: - Numbers 35:2-3 The commandment by the hand of Moses: give unto the Levites cities to dwell in and suburbs round about them for their cattle, their goods, and all their beasts. Joshua 21:4-8 - The cities came out by lot family by family: the children of Aaron the priest, of the Kohathites, had thirteen cities out of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin; the rest of the children of Kohath had ten cities out of Ephraim, Dan, and the half tribe of Manasseh. - The children of Gershon had thirteen cities out of Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and the half tribe of Manasseh in Bashan, and the children of Merari had twelve cities out of Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun; all given by lot as the Most High commanded by the hand of Moses. Joshua 21:9-19 - Out of Judah and Simeon the children of Aaron received nine cities by name, and out of Benjamin four more, thirteen cities in all for the priests. - They received Hebron in the hill country of Judah, the city of Arba the father of Anak, to be a city of refuge for the slayer; but the fields and villages of the city belonged to Caleb the son of Jephunneh for his possession. - From the Q&A: not all the cities given to the Levites were cities of refuge. Only certain cities were designated for that, six in all, for the man that killed his brother accidentally. - The city of refuge worked like protective custody: the slayer that killed a person unawares fled there from the avenger of blood and stayed there until he stood before the congregation and his case was judged. Precepts: - Numbers 35:9-12 Cities of refuge were appointed that the slayer which killeth any person at unawares may flee there and not die by the avenger until he stand before the congregation in judgment. - Numbers 35:13-15 Six cities were for refuge, three on this side Jordan where the two and a half tribes were and three in the land of Canaan, for the children of Israel, the stranger, and the sojourner. - Numbers 35:16-19 If he smote him with an instrument of iron, a stone, or a hand weapon of wood so that he die, he is a murderer; the murderer shall surely be put to death, and the revenger of blood shall slay him. - Numbers 35:20-21 If he thrust him of hatred or smote him in enmity, he that smote him shall surely be put to death, for he is a murderer. - Numbers 35:22-24 But if he thrust him suddenly without enmity, seeing him not, and was not his enemy, then the congregation shall judge between the slayer and the revenger of blood according to these judgments. Joshua 21:20-26 - The families of the children of Kohath that remained had four cities out of Ephraim, including Shechem in mount Ephraim to be a city of refuge for the slayer, four cities out of Dan, and two out of the half tribe of Manasseh: ten cities in all. Joshua 21:27-33 - The children of Gershon received Golan in Bashan out of the other half tribe of Manasseh to be a city of refuge for the slayer, four cities out of Issachar, four out of Asher, and out of Naphtali three, including Kedesh in Galilee, a city of refuge: thirteen cities in all. Joshua 21:34-42 - The children of Merari, the rest of the Levites, received four cities out of Zebulun, four out of Reuben, and four out of Gad, including Ramoth in Gilead, a city of refuge for the slayer: twelve cities. - All the cities of the Levites within the possession of the children of Israel were forty and eight cities with their suburbs, every one with her suburbs round about her. Joshua 21:43 - All the different lands and places just named, everything the tribes inherited at that time, had been promised all the way back to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Israel was always promised to have that land, and now they possessed it and dwelt therein. Joshua 21:44-45 - The Most High gave Israel rest round about according to all that he sware unto their fathers; not a man of all their enemies stood before them, for the Lord delivered all their enemies into their hand. - There failed not ought of any good thing which the Lord had spoken unto the house of Israel; all came to pass. Everything the Most High said he would do and every good thing he promised, he did it, because God does not lie. Precepts: - 1 Kings 8:56 Solomon said the exact same thing: blessed be the Lord that hath given rest unto his people Israel; there hath not failed one word of all his good promise which he promised by the hand of Moses. Joshua 22: The Altar of Witness Read the chapter → Joshua 22 Joshua 22:1-3 - Joshua called the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh and told them they had kept all that Moses commanded them and obeyed his voice; they had not left their brethren these many days, but kept the charge of the commandment of the Most High. - The charge was the condition Moses set when these two and a half tribes asked to stay on the other side Jordan: whenever it was time to go to war they had to show up and fight with their brethren, not sit over there while Israel took the land. Precepts: - Numbers 32:20-22 Moses said if ye will go all of you armed over Jordan before the Lord until his enemies be driven out, then afterward ye shall return and be guiltless, and this land shall be your possession. - Numbers 32:23 But if ye will not do so, ye have sinned against the Lord, and be sure your sin will find you out. Joshua 22:4-6 - Now that the Most High had given rest to their brethren as he promised, there was no war going on, so Joshua sent them home: return ye unto your tents and unto the land of your possession which Moses gave you on the other side Jordan. - The release came with a charge: take diligent heed to do the commandment and the law, to love the Lord your God, to walk in all his ways, to keep his commandments, to cleave unto him, and to serve him with all your heart and all your soul. - Rest did not end the duty; if their brethren ever needed them again they had to show up, as all the tribes did show up later in this same chapter. Joshua 22:7-9 - Joshua blessed them and sent them away rich: return with much riches unto your tents, with very much cattle, with silver, gold, brass, iron, and very much raiment, and divide the spoil of your enemies with your brethren. - The children of Reuben, the children of Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh departed from Shiloh in the land of Canaan to go into the country of Gilead, the land of their possession according to the word of the Lord by the hand of Moses. Joshua 22:10-12 - When the two and a half tribes came to the borders of Jordan they built a great altar by Jordan, an altar great to see to. They hid nothing; they built it on purpose so that it could be seen. - When the children of Israel heard of it, the whole congregation gathered themselves together at Shiloh to go up to war against them. They thought the two and a half tribes had built the altar to worship idols and do their own thing, and they were ready to cleanse it before judgment fell on the whole nation like it had before. Joshua 22:13-14 - Israel sent Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest with ten princes, one head of a chief house from every tribe. When you send Phinehas it is a problem, because of the kind of man Phinehas was: where he showed up, the zeal of the Most High showed up with him. - At Baalpeor the men of Israel began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab, bowed down to their gods, and joined themselves unto Baalpeor, and the anger of the Most High was kindled against Israel. - One man of Israel was so bold he brought a Midianitish woman to his brethren in the sight of Moses and all the congregation while they wept before the door of the tabernacle. It was once a shameful thing for our men to be seen like that; today men and women of Israel walk boldly and proudly with the nations, that same spirit. - Phinehas saw it, rose up from among the congregation, took a javelin, went after the man of Israel into the tent, and thrust both of them through, and the plague was stayed from the children of Israel; those that died in the plague were twenty and four thousand. So when Phinehas showed up at Gilead, everybody knew it was about to go down. Precepts: - Numbers 25:1-3 Israel began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab, ate of the sacrifices of their gods and bowed down to them, and Israel joined himself unto Baalpeor, and the anger of the Lord was kindled. - Numbers 25:4-5 The Lord told Moses to take all the heads of the people that were joined to Baalpeor and hang them up before the Lord against the sun, that his fierce anger be turned away from Israel. - Numbers 25:6-9 Phinehas rose up from among the congregation, took a javelin, and thrust the man of Israel and the woman through, and the plague was stayed; those that died were twenty and four thousand. Joshua 22:15-18 - The delegation asked what trespass is this that ye have committed against the God of Israel, to build you an altar that ye might rebel this day against the Lord. They saw the altar and immediately thought the two and a half tribes were going into idolatry. - Is the iniquity of Peor too little for us? All those thousands died in that plague, and Israel had just gotten into the land and gotten peace; why would anyone bring that thing back on the nation again? - Their reasoning was national: if ye rebel today against the Lord, tomorrow he will be wroth with the whole congregation of Israel. Judgment does not fall on pieces of the nation; Deuteronomy 28 happened to all of us, and they understood that, so they showed up quick, fast, and in a hurry rather than sit around and let it happen. Joshua 22:19-20 - They even offered their own land: if the land of your possession be unclean, pass ye over unto the land of the possession of the Lord and take possession among us, close by where we can keep an eye on you; only rebel not against the Lord, nor build you an altar beside the altar of the Lord our God. - They cited the proof from their own history: did not Achan the son of Zerah commit a trespass in the accursed thing, and wrath fell on all the congregation of Israel, and that man perished not alone in his iniquity. One man trespassed and the whole nation felt it. Precepts: - Joshua 7:1 Achan of the tribe of Judah took of the accursed thing, and the anger of the Lord was kindled against all the children of Israel. - Joshua 7:15 He that is taken with the accursed thing shall be burnt with fire, he and all that he hath, because he hath transgressed the covenant of the Lord. Joshua 22:21-23 - The two and a half tribes answered: the LORD God of gods, the LORD God of gods, he knoweth, and Israel he shall know; if it be in rebellion or in transgression against the Lord, save us not this day. They put their own lives on the line: if we built this thing in rebellion, put us to death today. - If we built an altar to turn from following the Lord, or to offer burnt offerings, meat offerings, or peace offerings on it, let the Lord himself require it. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 18:19 Whosoever will not hearken unto the words of the Lord, he will require it of him; the Lord requires it whenever you go off. Joshua 22:24-25 - This is why they built it: for fear of this thing, that in time to come your children might speak unto our children, saying, What have ye to do with the LORD God of Israel? The Lord hath made Jordan a border between us and you; ye have no part in the LORD. - They feared that generations later the children on one side of Jordan would tell the children on the other side that they were not the children of Israel, shutting them out from fearing the Lord, from the temple, the feast days, and the sacrifices. Joshua 22:26-29 - The altar was not for burnt offering nor for sacrifice; it was a witness between us and you and our generations after us, a memorial, so the two and a half tribes could do the service of the Lord before him in the place he chose, along with the rest of the tribes, and nobody could stop them. - If anyone ever said to their generations, Ye have no part in the Lord, the answer would stand built in stone: behold the pattern of the altar of the LORD, which our fathers made, not for burnt offerings nor for sacrifices, but it is a witness between us and you. - The same thing is happening today with the northern kingdom. Our people left their own witnesses over here: the writings on the Los Lunas stone identify with the northern kingdom, and the traditions, artifacts, practices, laws, and books that are being brought out in the classes all prove our people were here long ago and that they are the children of Israel. Yet with all that proof out there, people still deny it, the very thing the two and a half tribes feared. - Nobody else could have built that altar to the pattern of the altar of the Lord, because no other nation was keeping the laws; only Israel keeps the precepts, not the heathen. That is why the memorial could stand as identification. Precepts: - 2 Esdras 3:36 Israel by name hath kept thy precepts, but not the heathen; only Israel could leave the pattern of the law behind as a witness. - God forbid that we should rebel against the Lord to build an altar for burnt offerings, meat offerings, or sacrifices, beside the altar of the LORD our God that is before his tabernacle: the sacrifices belonged in front of the altar the Most High set in his chosen place. Joshua 22:30-31 - When Phinehas and the princes heard the words of the children of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh, it pleased them. Phinehas said, This day we perceive that the LORD is among us, because ye have not committed this trespass against the Lord. - Now ye have delivered the children of Israel out of the hand of the LORD: because they were not going off, nobody had to die that day, and coming from Phinehas that meant everything, because if it had been rebellion he would have been the one to start it. Joshua 22:32-34 - Phinehas and the princes returned from Gilead to the land of Canaan and brought the children of Israel word again: all is good, the altar is a memorial so the generations after do not forget that our people are on that side Jordan too, and they can come in and keep the feasts and do their sacrifices with us. - The thing pleased the children of Israel; they blessed God, dismantled from war, and did not go up to destroy the land where the children of Reuben and Gad dwelt. - The children of Reuben and Gad called the altar Ed: for it shall be a witness between us that the LORD is God. Joshua 23: Cleave unto the Lord Your God Read the chapter → Joshua 23 Joshua 23:1-5 - A long time after the Most High had given rest unto Israel from all their enemies round about, Joshua waxed old and stricken in age, and he called for all Israel, their elders, heads, judges, and officers to give his last charge. - Ye have seen all that the LORD your God hath done unto all these nations because of you, for the LORD your God is he that hath fought for you. - The nations that remained were divided by lot unto the tribes for an inheritance, from Jordan unto the great sea westward, which is the Mediterranean Sea. Those remaining nations belonged to Israel, as in the earlier chapters where they were made tributaries and served Israel. - The promise still ran ahead of them: the LORD your God, he shall expel them from before you and drive them from out of your sight, and ye shall possess their land, as the LORD your God hath promised unto you. Joshua 23:6-8 - Be ye therefore very courageous to keep and to do all that is written in the book of the law of Moses, turning not aside therefrom to the right hand or to the left. - Come not among these nations that remain among you; neither make mention of the name of their gods, nor cause to swear by them, neither serve them, nor bow yourselves unto them. Israel was not to go off into idolatry and worship the gods of the nations round about; that is what those nations do, not what Israel does. - But cleave unto the LORD your God, as ye have done unto this day. Joshua 23:9-10 - The Most High drove out great and strong nations from before Israel; no man had been able to stand before them unto that day. - One man of you shall chase a thousand: for the LORD your God, he it is that fighteth for you, as he hath promised you. Picture one man beating up a thousand; you cannot do that unless God is with you, and that is what it looked like. Joshua 23:11-13 - Take good heed therefore unto yourselves, that ye love the LORD your God. - The warning is plain: if ye go back and cleave unto the remnant of these nations and make marriages with them, know for a certainty that the Most High will no more drive out any of these nations from before you; they shall be snares and traps unto you, scourges in your sides and thorns in your eyes, until ye perish from off this good land. - This is the same thing that happened at Baalpeor, when Israel went and mingled with the women of Moab and then worshipped their gods. The warning here is do not do that thing. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 7:2-4 Make no covenant with them, neither make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter take unto thy son, for they will turn away thy son from following the Most High to serve other gods, and his anger will destroy thee suddenly. Joshua 23:14-16 - Joshua, going the way of all the earth, made Israel acknowledge in all their hearts and souls that not one thing had failed of all the good things which the Lord spake concerning them; all came to pass. - The other side of that is a heavy scripture: therefore as all good things are come upon you, so shall the LORD bring upon you all evil things, until he have destroyed you from off this good land. Many come out of Christianity being told God is good all the time, yet the scripture says plainly that the Most High will destroy you when you go off, because that also is what he promised. - When ye have transgressed the covenant and served other gods, ye shall perish quickly from off the good land. That is exactly why Israel is not at home right now; we did exactly that. And that is what the waking up is for today: the classes going out all day, the teaching in the streets, trying to bring our people back to the laws of God. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 28:63 As the Lord rejoiced over you to do you good, so the Lord will rejoice over you to destroy you, and ye shall be plucked from off the land whither thou goest to possess it. Joshua 24: Choose You This Day Whom Ye Will Serve Read the chapter → Joshua 24 Joshua 24:1-3 - Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel to Shechem, with the elders, heads, judges, and officers, and they presented themselves before God for the covenant. - The history begins on the other side of the flood: your fathers dwelt on the other side of the flood in old time, even Terah the father of Abraham and the father of Nachor, and they served other gods. - Abraham was chosen out of his family: the Most High took him from the other side of the flood, led him throughout all the land of Canaan, multiplied his seed, and gave him Isaac. Abraham was told to get up and leave his family and follow God, and he did just that. Joshua 24:4-7 - Unto Isaac were given Jacob and Esau; Esau received mount Seir to possess it, but Jacob and his children went down into Egypt. A whole lot of time passes in just those few verses. - The Most High sent Moses and Aaron, plagued Egypt, and brought Israel out; and when the Egyptians pursued with chariots and horsemen unto the Red sea, he put darkness between Israel and the Egyptians and brought the sea upon them and covered them. - Your eyes have seen what I have done in Egypt: the ones under twenty years old who went in with Joshua and Caleb saw these things as children, and now they were grown with children of their own, being reminded of what they saw with their own eyes. - Ye dwelt in the wilderness a long season: that long season was the forty years. Joshua 24:8-10 - The Most High brought Israel into the land of the Amorites on the other side Jordan, and they fought with Israel, and he gave them into Israel's hand and destroyed them from before them; that history is in Numbers 21. - Then Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab, arose and warred against Israel, and sent and called Balaam the son of Beor to curse Israel; that is Numbers 22, read only days before this class. - But I would not hearken unto Balaam; therefore he blessed you still: so I delivered you out of his hand. Joshua 24:11-13 - Israel went over Jordan unto Jericho, and the men of Jericho and the seven nations fought against them, and the Most High delivered them into Israel's hand. - He sent the hornet before them, which drave out the two kings of the Amorites from before them, but not with thy sword, nor with thy bow. God was doing the fighting; great nations bigger and more than Israel fell because the Most High was with them. - I have given you a land for which ye did not labour, and cities which ye built not, and ye dwell in them; of the vineyards and oliveyards which ye planted not do ye eat. Israel took over everything the nations had in those lands, the ships, the vineyards, the merchandise, and became the merchants of the land; it was theirs, because it was promised. Precepts: - Exodus 23:28 I will send hornets before thee, which shall drive out the Hivite, the Canaanite, and the Hittite, from before thee. Joshua 24:14-15 - Now therefore fear the LORD, and serve him in sincerity and in truth, and put away the gods which your fathers served on the other side of the flood, and in Egypt. - Choose you this day whom ye will serve; but as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD. A lot of people hang that quote up in the house and do not keep one law; everybody reads this verse and reads nothing before it about being put to death for going off. Lord willing they have space and time to repent. - Moses said the same thing: he set life and death, blessing and cursing before Israel and said choose life. Deuteronomy 28 laid it out, blessings in verses 1 through 14 if Israel obeyed, to be above all people and rule; curses from 15 down to 68 if not. Israel chose the cursing and the death, and that is what we are in now, trying to come back and get out of it. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 30:19-20 I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing; therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live, that thou mayest love the Lord thy God, obey his voice, and cleave unto him. Joshua 24:16-18 - The people answered, God forbid that we should forsake the LORD, to serve other gods. - For the LORD our God, he it is that brought us up and our fathers out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage: Egypt is the house of bondage, and he did those great signs in Israel's sight and preserved them in all the way they went. - Therefore will we also serve the LORD; for he is our God. Joshua 24:19-20 - Joshua said unto the people, Ye cannot serve the LORD: for he is an holy God; he is a jealous God; he will not forgive your transgressions nor your sins. - If ye forsake the LORD, and serve strange gods, then he will turn and do you hurt, and consume you, after that he hath done you good. Everything he promised for good had come to pass and Israel was on top in the land; all they had to do was keep the commandments. Going off meant being taken out of that land into captivity, and because that is what Israel decided to do, that is the predicament we are in today. Joshua 24:21-25 - The people said unto Joshua, Nay; but we will serve the LORD. It is the same thing Israel told Moses back then; we came into that covenant again, this time without the blood. - Joshua said, Ye are witnesses against yourselves that ye have chosen you the LORD, to serve him; and they said, We are witnesses. Everybody was in full agreement. - Put away the strange gods which are among you, and incline your heart unto the LORD God of Israel; and the people said, The LORD our God will we serve, and his voice will we obey. - So Joshua made a covenant with the people that day, and set them a statute and an ordinance in Shechem, the same thing Moses his predecessor did at the mountain; Joshua was his successor and did the same, though without the blood. Precepts: - Exodus 24:3-8 All the people answered with one voice, All the words which the Lord hath said will we do; Moses wrote all the words of the Lord, built an altar and twelve pillars, read the book of the covenant in the audience of the people, and sprinkled the blood of the covenant on the people. Joshua 24:26-28 - Joshua wrote these words in the book of the law of God, and took a great stone, and set it up under an oak that was by the sanctuary of the LORD. - Behold, this stone shall be a witness unto us; for it hath heard all the words of the LORD which he spake unto us: it shall be therefore a witness unto you, lest ye deny your God. - So Joshua let the people depart, every man unto his inheritance. Joshua 24:29-30 - After these things Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of the LORD, died, being an hundred and ten years old. - They buried him in the border of his inheritance in Timnathserah, which is in mount Ephraim; he is buried in Ephraim because Joshua was of the tribe of Ephraim, the same tribe as Nun his father. Precepts: - Numbers 13:8 Of the tribe of Ephraim, Oshea the son of Nun: Joshua and his father Nun were of the tribe of Ephraim. Joshua 24:31-33 - Israel served the LORD all the days of Joshua, and all the days of the elders that overlived Joshua, which had known all the works of the LORD that he had done for Israel. - The bones of Joseph, which the children of Israel brought up out of Egypt, they buried in Shechem, in the parcel of ground which Jacob bought of the sons of Hamor the father of Shechem for an hundred pieces of silver, and it became the inheritance of the children of Joseph. - Eleazar the son of Aaron died, and they buried him in a hill that pertained to Phinehas his son, which was given him in mount Ephraim. --- Topics: Clean and Unclean Meats · Esau and Edom · Idolatry · Sacrifice and Atonement · The Covenant · The Feasts of the Most High · The Priesthood ← Joshua 17-20 · Joshua Study · Judges 1-4 →

title: Joshua 5: Circumcision of the Flesh and of the Heart
text: ← Joshua 1-4 · Joshua Study · Joshua 9-12 → Joshua 5: Circumcision of the Flesh and of the Heart Read the chapter → Joshua 5 Introduction This session covered Joshua 5 through 8: the circumcision of the wilderness generation at Gilgal and what the uncircumcised heart means, the Captain of the host of the Lord, the fall of Jericho and the faith of Rahab, the accursed thing and the sin of Achan, the taking of Ai, and the blessings and cursings read at mount Ebal. By way of recap of chapters 1 through 4: after the death of Moses, Joshua was set over the host of Israel, the Lord dried up the river Jordan so the people crossed on dry ground, and the spies Joshua sent had linked up with Rahab the harlot in Jericho. Rahab worked as counterintelligence for Israel; she dwelt on the side of the wall in the poor quarter of the city, and such people know the secret goings-on of a city, so she gave the spies information to carry back to Joshua. Joshua 5:1 - The kings of the Amorites and the Canaanites heard that the Lord had dried up the waters of Jordan from before the children of Israel, and their heart melted: they were paralyzed with fear. - They had heard how the Most High split the Red sea in Exodus, and now he had done it again at Jordan, so neither was there spirit in them any more because of the children of Israel.
