Joshua 5:2-3 - Circumcise again the children of Israel the second time: the children of Israel had not been keeping the commandments, being stiffnecked and hardheaded, and the Lord told Joshua to fix them. - Circumcision is the covenant the Most High instituted with our forefather Abraham: every man child circumcised at eight days old, and the servant born in the house or bought with money circumcised likewise and keeping the laws as well. - When Abraham received the commandment he performed it, circumcising every male of his house the selfsame day; he showed the Lord by his actions that he believed. So the men in Joshua who had not been circumcised showed a form of repentance by applying the law of circumcision. Precepts: - Genesis 17:10-12 The covenant with Abraham and his seed: every man child among you shall be circumcised, he that is eight days old, including the servant bought with money. - Genesis 17:23-24 Abraham circumcised every male of his house in the selfsame day, as God had said unto him; faith shown by doing. - The eighth day is the wisdom of the Most High for the body: before then a baby's blood has not begun to coagulate as it needs to, and the child could bleed out; by the eighth day he is strong enough to withstand the process and heal. - There are physical benefits to the law: when the foreskin remains, moisture gets trapped and creates an environment for bacteria, raising the risk of infection and urinary tract infections, and being circumcised even reduces a wife's risk of cervical cancer. This is the Most High as a Father giving his children counsel on how to live and stay clear of disease. - The physical circumcision is symbolic of spiritual circumcision. The heart in scripture is the mind, for out of the heart of men proceed evil thoughts; sin is what makes a man dirty, nasty, and filthy, so the uncircumcised heart is the mind that will not keep the commandments. - No surgery can circumcise the brain: circumcision of the heart is repentance. You wash you and make you clean by ceasing to do evil, and a young man cleanses his way by taking heed thereto according to the word of the Most High. Precepts: - Leviticus 26:41 If then their uncircumcised hearts be humbled, and they accept the punishment of their iniquity; the Lord speaks here of the heart, not the flesh. - Mark 7:21 From within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts; the heart is the mind. - Isaiah 1:16 Wash you, make you clean; cease to do evil is how you are made clean. - Psalms 119:9 A young man cleanses his way by taking heed thereto according to thy word. Joshua 5:4-6 - This is the cause of the circumcision: all the men of war that came out of Egypt died in the wilderness because they obeyed not the voice of the Lord, and the generation born by the way had not been circumcised. - That they had not circumcised themselves means they did not obey the voice of the Lord: they should have been circumcised physically and also mentally and spiritually. - The land that floweth with milk and honey is understood by the Bible's own dictionary, precept upon precept: the rebels in Numbers called Egypt the land flowing with milk and honey, and Israel was brought out of the land of Egypt, so the phrase describes a land abundant in food. The milk goes into your cattle and your meats, and the honey goes into your vegetation. - The mixed multitude and the children of Israel wept for the fish, cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions, and garlic they ate in Egypt: they were comfortable in their oppression and did not understand they were not free, the same mindset among our people in captivity today who say they are free and living their best life. - The honey teaching carries a dietary lesson: hast thou found honey, eat so much as is sufficient for thee. Do not overeat; balance your salts, sugars, meats, and dainties moderately. Precepts: - Numbers 16:13 The rebels called the land Israel came out of a land that floweth with milk and honey; that land was Egypt. - Exodus 20:2 I am the Lord thy God which have brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage. - Numbers 11:4-5 The mixed multitude fell a lusting, and Israel wept for the fish, cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions, and garlic of Egypt; comfortable in their oppression. - Proverbs 25:16 Hast thou found honey? eat so much as is sufficient for thee; the honey goes into your food, and the lesson is moderation. Joshua 5:7 - Their children raised up in their stead Joshua circumcised, for they had not circumcised them by the way. - A father can have his son circumcised in the flesh yet never circumcise him from the heart: if he never teaches him the laws and to obey the voice of the Lord, the physical circumcision alone profits him nothing. It is symbolic of obeying the voice of the Lord. Joshua 5:8 - They abode in their places in the camp till they were whole: these were grown men, not eight day old babies, so they had to remain in the camp until they healed from the circumcision. Joshua 5:9 - This day have I rolled away the reproach of Egypt from off you: they finally believed and obeyed, circumcising themselves and obeying the voice of the Lord, so they were no longer a reproach, an embarrassment, or a disgrace. - The children of Israel finally sanctified themselves, and the name of the place is called Gilgal unto this day. Joshua 5:10-12 - The children of Israel encamped in Gilgal and kept the passover on the fourteenth day of the month at even in the plains of Jericho; the passover was instituted by the Most High, and you can read about it in Exodus 12. - They did eat of the old corn of the land on the morrow after the passover, and the manna ceased; the children of Israel had manna no more, but ate of the fruit of the land of Canaan that year. Joshua 5:13-14 - Joshua lifted up his eyes by Jericho and saw a man standing over against him with his sword drawn, a warrior. Joshua did not run; he went straight to him and asked, Art thou for us, or for our adversaries? There was no fear in the heart of Joshua. - The man answered, Nay; but as captain of the host of the Lord am I now come. Host means army: he is the captain, the leader, of the army of the Lord. - When Joshua realized who stood before him, the fear came: he fell on his face to the earth and did worship, and the leader of Israel's army called himself a servant, saying, What saith my lord unto his servant? Joshua had cleaved to Moses and understood who the captain of the host is. - The captain of the host of the Lord is Christ, the captain of our salvation. This is why Joshua was afraid: the return of Christ is not the soft picture Christianity paints, for he is not coming back made like unto his brethren as at the first, but with the power of the living God, to take vengeance and destroy. No missiles or fighter jets will do anything against him. Precepts: - Hebrews 2:9-10 We see Jesus, made perfect through sufferings, the captain of their salvation; Christ is the captain of the host. - Isaiah 47:3 I will take vengeance, and I will not meet thee as a man; at his second coming Christ comes with the power of the living God. - Exodus 15:3 The Lord is a man of war: the Lord is his name. Joshua 5:15 - The captain of the Lord's host said, Loose thy shoe from off thy foot; for the place whereon thou standest is holy. And Joshua did so. Joshua 6: The Fall of Jericho and the Faith of Rahab Read the chapter → Joshua 6 Joshua 6:1-2 - Jericho was straitly shut up because of the children of Israel: none went out and none came in. Jericho had a military, and a garrison, a military base, was built there, with the walls shut so nobody could enter or leave. - The Lord said unto Joshua, See, I have given into thine hand Jericho, and the king thereof, and the mighty men of valour: the battle was already decided. Joshua 6:3-5 - The battle plan came from the Lord: compass the city with all the men of war once a day for six days, seven priests bearing seven trumpets of rams' horns before the ark; on the seventh day compass the city seven times, and at the long blast all the people shout with a great shout, and the wall shall fall down flat. - The blowing of the trumpets activates the armies of the Lord, the angels, to help in battle. Remember Elisha's servant: when his eyes were opened he saw the host of angels that were there warring and protecting Israel. - This is the spirit behind the men of Israel rehearsing the righteous acts with trumpets and shofars today, at the camps and at the new moons; it is spiritual and an act of faith. Precepts: - Numbers 10:9 If ye go to war against the enemy that oppresseth you, blow an alarm with the trumpets, and ye shall be remembered before the Lord and saved from your enemies. Joshua 6:6-11 - Joshua called the priests and gave the order: seven priests bear seven trumpets before the ark, the armed men pass on before the ark, and the rereward, the guards in the rear, came after the ark. - Joshua commanded the people, Ye shall not shout, nor make any noise with your voice, neither shall any word proceed out of your mouth, until the day I bid you shout; then shall ye shout. - The ark of the Lord compassed the city once, and they came into the camp and lodged there. Joshua 6:12-14 - They repeated the act six days back to back, rising early, the priests bearing the ark and blowing the trumpets, the armed men before and the rereward after, one compass of the city each day. - Every army in the world stole this from the Israelites: the pass and review of the militaries, with their battalions and units, their guidons with the eagle on the tip of the spear, marching round the field sounding off with cadences and trumpets, is patterned after what Israel did here. Joshua 6:15-16 - On the seventh day they rose about the dawning of the day and compassed the city seven times. There is something about the number seven that the Lord loves; you read about it in Revelation. - At the seventh time, when the priests blew with the trumpets, Joshua said unto the people, Shout; for the Lord hath given you the city. - The men apply Joshua 6 to this day: when a scoffer will not hear the word and thinks to outcry the truth, the brothers say the scripture together with one mind, one body, one spirit. That unity is spiritual, a rehearsal of the righteous acts. - Unity and order are what the enemies fear: not gangs and drug dealing, but the so-called Black man, Hispanic man, and Native American man unified in the order of a military, with structure and organization. That is what puts fear in the nations. Joshua 6:17-19 - The city shall be accursed, even it and all that are therein, to the Lord: only Rahab the harlot shall live, she and all that are with her in the house, because she hid the messengers. She made a covenant with the spies: she would conceal them and assist Israel, knowing the Lord was with Israel, as long as her family was saved when the city fell. - Rahab was a Canaanite, a heathen, yet the heathen can be blessed when they do it to benefit Israel; blessed is he that blesseth thee. - Rahab is the scripture's own example that a man is justified by works and not by faith only: faith and works go hand in hand, for your actions prove whether you believe. Was not Rahab the harlot justified by works, when she had received the messengers and sent them out another way? As the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead also. - Works by the Bible's own dictionary is keeping his commandments: set your hope in God, forget not his works, but keep his commandments. Words say a lot, but actions always speak louder, and by him actions are weighed. - Keep yourselves from the accursed thing, lest ye make yourselves accursed and make the camp of Israel a curse, and trouble it: your individual sins affect the whole nation of Israel, your brothers, your sisters, and the children. That is why we must examine ourselves whether we be in the faith. - All the silver and gold and vessels of brass and iron were consecrated unto the Lord, separated and sanctified for his treasury alone: nobody was to gain personally from this war. Precepts: - James 2:24-26 By works a man is justified, and not by faith only; Rahab the harlot was justified by works; faith without works is dead. - Psalms 78:7 Set their hope in God, and not forget the works of God, but keep his commandments; works means keeping the commandments. - 1 Samuel 2:3 The Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed. Joshua 6:20-21 - The people shouted when the priests blew with the trumpets, and the wall fell down flat. That shout is Isaiah 58:1 in action, cry aloud and spare not: the sound coming out of their mouths with the trumpets broke everything down, like thousands of lions roaring at once. - The people went up into the city, every man straight before him, and they took the city and utterly destroyed all that was in it, both man and woman, young and old, ox, sheep, and ass, with the edge of the sword. Precepts: - Isaiah 58:1 Cry aloud, spare not, lift up thy voice like a trumpet; the spirit of the great shout at the wall. Joshua 6:22-25 - Joshua sent the two spies into the harlot's house to bring out Rahab and all that she had, as they sware unto her; they brought out her father, mother, brethren, and all her kindred, and left them without the camp of Israel. - They burnt the city with fire and all that was therein; only the silver, gold, and vessels of brass and iron went into the treasury of the house of the Lord. - Joshua saved Rahab the harlot alive and her father's household, and she dwelleth in Israel even unto this day, because she hid the messengers. She helped the nation of Israel toward rulership, and that is the only help Israel wants from the other nations: not food stamps, welfare, or reparations, but tell our people who they are, the Israelites the Bible speaks of, the so-called Blacks, Hispanics, and Native Americans, and that we must keep the commandments of the Most High. Whoever does that will receive mercy just as Rahab did. Joshua 6:26-27 - Joshua adjured them at that time: cursed be the man before the Lord that riseth up and buildeth this city Jericho; he shall lay the foundation thereof in his firstborn, and in his youngest son shall he set up the gates of it. The city was not to be rebuilt. - So the Lord was with Joshua, and his fame was noised throughout all the country. Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan Read the chapter → Joshua 7 Joshua 7:1 - Who committed the trespass? Many will answer Achan, but read the first sentence: the children of Israel committed a trespass in the accursed thing. Achan the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took of the accursed thing, and the anger of the Lord was kindled against all the children of Israel. - Your individual sins can hurt the rest of the nation. You can be the hindrance to why your camp is not growing, why your family, your marriage, or your children have issues, when you have a spirit on you that you know about and keep secret, not praying, not fasting, not seeking counsel. That is the spirit of Achan, and the children of Israel pay for it; we are supposed to be one mind, one body, one spirit. Joshua 7:2-5 - The men who viewed Ai came back confident: let not all the people go up, but about two or three thousand men, for they are but few. The way Israel had been winning, they thought they could not lose; but what happened in verse 1 was about to play its part. - About three thousand went up, and they fled before the men of Ai, who smote about thirty and six men and chased them from before the gate; the hearts of the people melted and became as water. - The Lord is the one who wins the battles and gets the victory, not us. Pick out the weakest nation on earth: no matter how strong Israel is physically, if we are not spiritually right with the Lord, he will make us lose, for this fight is not carnal. - Hearts melting as water is the curse for disobedience: the Most High sends a faintness into the heart, so that the mighty flee as fleeing from a sword and fall when none pursueth, like the athlete in the scary movie suddenly stumbling from sheer fear. Precepts: - Leviticus 26:27-28 If ye walk contrary unto me, I will walk contrary unto you also in fury, and chastise you seven times for your sins. - Leviticus 26:36 I will send a faintness into their hearts; the sound of a shaken leaf shall chase them, and they shall flee as fleeing from a sword, and fall when none pursueth. - Ezekiel 21:7 For the tidings, because it cometh: every heart shall melt, all hands shall be feeble, every spirit shall faint, and all knees shall be weak as water. Joshua 7:6-9 - Joshua rent his clothes and fell to the earth upon his face before the ark until the eventide, he and the elders of Israel, and put dust upon their heads, grieving over the war just lost and the men that died. - Israel turning their backs means they were fleeing, retreating, defeated. Joshua understood what the nations do when they see Israel take a loss: the Canaanites would hear of it, environ us round, surround us, capitalize while we are down, and cut off our name from the earth. - And what wilt thou do unto thy great name? If Israel is cut off, who will be there to praise the Most High? Joshua 7:10-12 - The Lord said, Get thee up; wherefore liest thou upon thy face? Israel hath sinned. It does not say Achan sinned; it says Israel. This walk is not selfish or individual: when you are in sin you hurt your wife, your husband, your children, the congregation, and the leadership, for we are all our brother's keeper and responsible for one another. - They have taken of the accursed thing, and stolen, and dissembled, and put it among their own stuff: the Lord says they. As a father who finds mischief chastens all his children together when none confesses, so the Most High deals with his children as one house; we pay for one another's sins. - Therefore the children of Israel could not stand before their enemies: the Lord was not going to let them win, and he put a mightier warring spirit on the men of Ai. However well you train with your sword and shield, the Most High controls the outcome. - His power cannot be comprehended: great things doeth he, which we cannot comprehend; touching the Almighty, we cannot find him out. Stop trying to figure the Creator out and questioning why he created what he created; you are the creation, so keep the commandments and play your role. - Neither will I be with you any more, except ye destroy the accursed from among you: what is accursed must be destroyed; that is the only way to remove it. Precepts: - Job 37:5 God thundereth marvellously with his voice; great things doeth he, which we cannot comprehend. - Job 37:23 Touching the Almighty, we cannot find him out: he is excellent in power, and in judgment, and in plenty of justice. Joshua 7:13-15 - Up, sanctify the people against tomorrow: there is an accursed thing in the midst of thee, O Israel; thou canst not stand before thine enemies until ye take away the accursed thing from among you. - The search would narrow by the Lord's own taking: tribe, then family, then household, then man by man; and he that is taken with the accursed thing shall be burnt with fire, he and all that he hath. - The folly was wrought against a plain commandment: Joshua had already charged them in Joshua 6:18-19 to keep from the accursed thing lest they trouble the camp, and adjured them in Joshua 6:26; the transgressor troubled the camp, the army and congregation of Israel. Joshua 7:16-18 - Joshua rose up early and brought Israel by their tribes, and the tribe of Judah was taken; then the family of the Zarhites, then the household of Zabdi man by man, and Achan the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, was taken. Joshua 7:19 - My son, give, I pray thee, glory to the Lord God of Israel, and make confession unto him; and tell me now what thou hast done; hide it not from me. Joshua said hide it not from me because it was already not hidden from One mightier than he: we cannot hide what we do from the Lord. - The eyes of the Lord are in every place, beholding the evil and the good; he sees everything we do. If you are in this walk as a manpleaser, the Lord sees what you do away from the brotherhood and the sisterhood. - The Lord gives a dispensation of time and grace to get the mind right, to repent, pray, and fast over what we struggle with; the just man falleth seven times and riseth up again. When leadership corrects you, do not think evil of them: the Lord did not have to send leadership, he could have sent evil your way instead; correction is the warning and the mercy. Precepts: - Proverbs 15:3 The eyes of the Lord are in every place, beholding the evil and the good. - Jeremiah 23:24 Can any hide himself in secret places that I shall not see him? saith the Lord. Do not I fill heaven and earth? - Ecclesiasticus 23:19 The eyes of the Lord are ten thousand times brighter than the sun; you cannot hide from him. - Numbers 32:23 If ye will not do so, ye have sinned against the Lord: and be sure your sin will find you out. Joshua 7:20-21 - Achan confessed: indeed I have sinned against the Lord God of Israel. He saw among the spoils a goodly Babylonish garment, two hundred shekels of silver, and a wedge of gold of fifty shekels weight; he coveted them, took them, and hid them in the earth in the midst of his tent. - Joshua had said all the silver and gold and vessels were consecrated unto the Lord for his treasury, so Achan was not stealing from men; he was literally stealing from the Most High. - I coveted them: covetousness is the last of the ten commandments, and as a father saves the weightiest warning for last but not least, the Lord ends the ten with thou shalt not covet. - To covet is to carry the spirit of jealousy and envy, and there is not a more wicked thing than a covetous man: he sets his own soul to sale, selling out his dignity and self-respect to fulfil his desires no matter what it takes. Precepts: - Exodus 20:17 Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour's house, thy neighbour's wife, nor any thing that is thy neighbour's; the last commandment, last but not least. - Ecclesiasticus 10:9 There is not a more wicked thing than a covetous man; he sets his own soul to sale. Joshua 7:22-26 - Joshua sent messengers, and they ran unto the tent, and behold, it was hid in his tent, and the silver under it; they laid it all out before the Lord with the whole congregation present. The Lord revealed it, and the scripture cannot be broken: as Jericho was made a curse, so the one who took of it. - Joshua and all Israel took Achan, the silver, the garment, the wedge of gold, and his sons, and his daughters, and his oxen, asses, sheep, tent, and all that he had, unto the valley of Achor. His sons and daughters did not steal it, yet because he lacked knowledge and understanding they paid for the covetous spirit he carried. - Why hast thou troubled us? the Lord shall trouble thee this day. Achan was the reason men died in that battle and the nation was nearly overtaken; his selfish, individual spirit never weighed what his family would pay. - All Israel stoned him with stones, and burned them with fire, after they had stoned them with stones: them, because his household went with him. My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge: reject knowledge and the Lord will reject thee, and the end of Hosea 4:6 that we seldom quote says, I will also forget thy children. The Lord hits where it hurts, and your sin reaches your children, your wife, your husband, your brothers and sisters. - It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God, and that is where Achan fell, and unfortunately his sons and daughters and all he had with him. Some of our people in the islands and elsewhere still ignorantly carry out such public executions to this day; we do not condone it, for we are not under the law of sacrifice now but under grace, and the judgment is of the Lord. - Consider the contrast that closes these chapters: Achan, an Israelite of Judah, lacked faith and was put to death, while Rahab the Canaanite harlot was saved alive for her faith. When Israel will not obey his voice, the Lord likens the house of Judah unto all the heathen; so we must have the fear of the Lord in our hearts. - They raised over him a great heap of stones unto this day, and the Lord turned from the fierceness of his anger; wherefore the name of that place was called the valley of Achor unto this day. Precepts: - Hosea 4:6 My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge; seeing thou hast forgotten the law of thy God, I will also forget thy children. - Hebrews 10:31 It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God. - Ezekiel 25:8 Moab and Seir do say, Behold, the house of Judah is like unto all the heathen; disobedience makes the Lord liken Israel unto the heathen. Joshua 8: The Taking of Ai and the Blessings and Cursings Read the chapter → Joshua 8 Joshua 8:1-2 - With the accursed thing purged, the Lord said unto Joshua, Fear not, neither be thou dismayed: take all the people of war with thee and go up to Ai; see, I have given into thy hand the king of Ai, and his people, and his city, and his land. - This time the spoil thereof and the cattle shall ye take for a prey unto yourselves, unlike Jericho where everything was consecrated to the treasury of the Lord; and the command was to lay an ambush for the city behind it. Joshua 8:3-8 - Joshua chose out thirty thousand mighty men of valour and sent them away by night to lie in ambush behind the city, not very far from it, always ready. These were warriors, men of courage, but none of that matters unless the spirit is right with the Lord first. - The strategy: Joshua and the people with him approach the city, and when the men of Ai come out, Israel flees before them as at the first, drawing them away from the city; then the ambush rises up and seizes the city and sets it on fire, according to the commandment of the Lord. - Note the wording: for the Lord your God will deliver it into your hand. He did not say ye shall win the battle; the Most High is the one who delivers the enemy into Israel's hand. Joshua 8:9-13 - The ambush went and abode between Bethel and Ai, on the west side of Ai, while Joshua lodged that night among the people; he rose early, numbered the people, and went up with the elders of Israel and pitched on the north side of Ai, with a valley between them and the city. - He took about five thousand men and set them to lie in ambush between Bethel and Ai on the west side: every position was assigned, everything strategic. Joshua was carrying out the playbook, gifted in war strategy and technique. Joshua 8:14-17 - When the king of Ai saw it, the men of the city hasted and rose up early and went out against Israel to battle at a time appointed, not knowing there were liers in ambush behind the city. - Joshua and all Israel made as if they were beaten before them, and fled by the way of the wilderness: part of the strategy, feigning defeat so Ai would chase them straight into the ambush. - All the people in Ai were called together to pursue, and they were drawn away from the city: not a man was left in Ai or Bethel that went not out after Israel, and they left the city open. Joshua 8:18-19 - The Lord said unto Joshua, Stretch out the spear that is in thy hand toward Ai; for I will give it into thine hand. - As soon as he stretched out his hand, the ambush arose quickly out of their place, ran, entered into the city, took it, and hasted and set the city on fire. Joshua 8:20-23 - When the men of Ai looked behind them, the smoke of their city ascended up to heaven, and they had no power to flee this way or that way; the people that fled to the wilderness turned back upon the pursuers. - The men of Ai were in the midst of Israel, some on this side and some on that side, and Israel smote them until none remained or escaped; they were surrounded, exactly as drawn up. The king of Ai they took alive and brought him to Joshua. Joshua 8:24-26 - When Israel had made an end of slaying all the inhabitants of Ai in the field and in the wilderness, all that fell that day, both of men and women, were twelve thousand, even all the men of Ai. Women are casualties of war. - That point stands as a warning for the sisters serving unrepented in the militaries of the nations, standing stiffly for the oppressor: when Christ comes back he is coming to kill, and a uniform and a weapon will not save; men and women will be dying alike. It is best in these last days for a woman to stand by and support her own man and nation, not another nation. - Joshua drew not his hand back until he had utterly destroyed all the inhabitants of Ai, meaning the children were put to death also. This was not new: at Sihon's cities Israel utterly destroyed the men, the women, and the little ones. The children's song teaching that Christ loves all the children of every nation alike does not stand with these scriptures; the Lord's love is toward the children of Israel. Precepts: - Jeremiah 31:22 How long wilt thou go about, O thou backsliding daughter? the Lord hath created a new thing in the earth, A woman shall compass a man. - Deuteronomy 2:34 We took all his cities at that time, and utterly destroyed the men, and the women, and the little ones, of every city; we left none to remain. Joshua 8:27-29 - Only the cattle and the spoil of that city Israel took for a prey unto themselves, according unto the word of the Lord which he commanded Joshua: they carried out the order exactly as instructed. - Joshua burnt Ai and made it an heap for ever, even a desolation unto this day; the king of Ai he hanged on a tree until eventide, and as soon as the sun was down his carcase was taken down, cast at the entering of the gate of the city, and a great heap of stones raised thereon. Joshua 8:30-32 - Then Joshua built an altar unto the Lord God of Israel in mount Ebal, as Moses commanded and as it is written in the book of the law: an altar of whole stones, over which no man hath lift up any iron; and they offered burnt offerings and sacrificed peace offerings, and he wrote upon the stones a copy of the law of Moses. - We are still under the law of sacrifice today, but the sacrifice is your body, not the blood of bulls and goats: you sacrifice time, money, pain, and labor to push this truth and do the work, spiritual sacrifices through your works by keeping the laws. - The peace offering today is keeping the commandments: he that keepeth the law bringeth offerings enough, and he that taketh heed to the commandment offereth a peace offering. Under grace, peace is a dispensation: the more sin you commit, the less peace you will have, so keep the commandments and do not frustrate the grace and peace the Most High has with you. - The Most High hath a controversy with the inhabitants of the land; if you do not want the Lord to have a controversy with you, keep the laws. And keeping the laws is more than beards, fringes, borders of blue, and not eating pork: it is purging the unfruitful spirits you know dwell inside you, the jealousy, envy, covetousness, malice, hatred, grudging, backbiting, murmuring, and gossip. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 35:1 Today's peace offering is keeping the commandments. - Hosea 4:1 The Lord hath a controversy with the inhabitants of the land; keep the laws so the controversy is not with you. Joshua 8:33 - All Israel, and their elders, and officers, and their judges stood on this side the ark and on that side, before the priests the Levites, the stranger as well as he that was born among them, half over against mount Gerizim and half over against mount Ebal, as Moses commanded, that they should bless the people of Israel. - Why does the body set up rank instead of saying I only follow Christ? Because we are commanded to rehearse the righteous acts of the Lord: reading the wars and works of Joshua, Moses, and the officers, judges, and elders, we practice what our forefathers did, in order, as an organized army. - Rehearse means practice, and practice makes perfect: there are rehearsals every day, classes and meetings for the men, the women, and the children, because this is not our rest. Precepts: - Judges 5:11 There shall they rehearse the righteous acts of the Lord; the order of officers and judges is rehearsed in the body today. Joshua 8:34-35 - Afterward he read all the words of the law, the blessings and cursings, according to all that is written in the book of the law. We tell our neighbor God bless you, but by the same book the Most High and Christ will curse you too if you do not keep the laws. - Heaven and earth are called to record: everything we do is recorded, and life and death, blessing and cursing, are set before us. Life is the keeping of the commandments of the Most High, and death is the wages of sin; it is the one thing left optional, so choose life, for it is not just you that pays but thy seed as well. - How do you become blessed? Read the last page of the book: blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life. A few verses before your Bible says the end, it says keep the commandments, so no man in his right mind can say the laws are done away with; that is justifying wickedness. Keep the sabbath holy, leave the swine alone, dress in modesty, and keep the commandments if you want the blessings. - There was not a word of all that Moses commanded which Joshua read not before all the congregation, with the women, and the little ones, and the strangers that were conversant among them: those were the strangers that fell in line with Israel, with the fear of the Lord in them, as Rahab had. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 30:19 I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live. - Proverbs 7:2 Keep my commandments, and live; life is keeping the commandments. - Romans 6:23 The wages of sin is death; sin is what brings the cursing and the death. - Revelation 22:14 Blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life; the blessing at the last page of the book. --- Topics: Clean and Unclean Meats · Sacrifice and Atonement · The Covenant · The Feasts of the Most High · The Priesthood · The Sabbath ← Joshua 1-4 · Joshua Study · Joshua 9-12 →

title: Joshua 9: The Gibeonite Deception and the Weight of an Oath
text: ← Joshua 5-8 · Joshua Study · Joshua 13-16 → Joshua 9: The Gibeonite Deception and the Weight of an Oath Read the chapter → Joshua 9 Introduction This session covers Joshua 9 through 12, the heart of the conquest of the land. Chapter 9 is the wile of the Gibeonites, who beguile Israel into a league because the princes asked not counsel at the mouth of the Most High. Chapter 10 is the day the sun stood still: the Most High casts down hailstones from heaven, five kings are drawn out of their cave, and the whole south country is destroyed. Chapter 11 is the northern kings gathered as the sand of the sea and utterly destroyed, and chapter 12 is the roll of the thirty and one kings Joshua smote. What we read in Joshua will play out again when Christ returns, for there is nothing new under the sun. So study, pray, apply, endure to the end, and seek ye out of the book of the Lord and read. Joshua 9:1-2 - The kings on this side Jordan, in the hills, in the valleys, and in all the coasts of the great sea over against Lebanon: the Hittite, the Amorite, the Canaanite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite. These are Hamites, better known as Nilotic Africans. - When they heard what had been done, they gathered themselves together to fight with Joshua and with Israel with one accord. Joshua 9:3-6 - The inhabitants of Gibeon heard what Joshua had done to Jericho and to Ai, and they did work wilily: they made as if they had been ambassadors, with old sacks upon their asses, wine bottles old and rent and bound up, old shoes and old garments, and bread dry and mouldy. - They came to Joshua at the camp at Gilgal saying, We be come from a far country: now therefore make ye a league with us. Israel was commanded to destroy all the inhabitants of the land, the very nations listed in verse 1, so the Gibeonites' only hope was to pretend they were not of the land. Joshua 9:7-13 - The men of Israel were suspicious at first: peradventure ye dwell among us, and how shall we make a league with you? Joshua pressed them, Who are ye, and from whence come ye? - The Gibeonites leaned on the fame of the Most High: we have heard all that he did in Egypt, and to Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan, the two kings of the Amorites beyond Jordan. - Their props sold the story. In ancient times wine did not come in bottles like ours; wine came in bags, sometimes made of leather, and they would rend through wear and tear over time. Joshua 9:14-15 - The men took of their victuals, and asked not counsel at the mouth of the LORD. That is the first mistake, and not asking counsel of the Most High at this moment ended up being a snare and a trap to us as a people, as the rest of the scriptures show. - Let reason think on whether it is the right move, and even before you reason within yourself, the Most High says counsel, counsel, counsel before every action. - This type of ordeal will play out again in the times when Christ returns: the sons of strangers shall come to build up Israel's walls, their kings shall minister unto Israel, and the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish. There is nothing new under the sun. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 37:16 Counsel before every action; that is what our forefathers did not do here. - Isaiah 60:9-12 Future prophecy: the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls and their kings minister unto thee, and the nation that will not serve thee shall perish. Joshua 9:16-19 - At the end of three days Israel heard that they were their neighbours, dwelling among them. The children of Israel smote them not, because the princes of the congregation had sworn unto them by the LORD God of Israel. - All the congregation murmured against the princes, but the princes held the line: we have sworn unto them by the LORD God of Israel, now therefore we may not touch them. Our forefathers were wrong in one situation, but they were upright men in holding up to their word. Precepts: - Ecclesiastes 5:4-6 When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; what comes out of your mouth, be sure to do it. Joshua 9:20-21 - We will even let them live, lest wrath be upon us, because of the oath which we sware unto them. A vow made before the Most High stands, even one gotten by guile. - Let them be hewers of wood and drawers of water unto all the congregation. Hewers of wood and drawers of water means slaves. - This is according to the law of the Most High pertaining to other nations. If you just read the Old Testament, there was no equality among the nations, and there is still no equality among nations: they were made for a certain purpose. The reason they are not in that purpose now is because we have sinned and failed, and one day Israel will rise again to put them back in their rightful places. Precepts: - Leviticus 25:44-46 Thy bondmen and bondmaids shall be of the heathen round about you; the other nations were made to be Israel's servants, but over your brethren ye shall not rule with rigour. Joshua 9:22-23 - Joshua called for them: wherefore have ye beguiled us, saying, We are very far from you, when ye dwell among us? - Now therefore ye are cursed, and there shall none of you be freed from being bondmen, and hewers of wood and drawers of water for the house of my God. They were servants all the way up and through. Joshua 9:24-27 - The Gibeonites answered honestly: it was certainly told thy servants how the LORD thy God commanded his servant Moses to give you all the land and to destroy all the inhabitants, therefore we were sore afraid of our lives because of you. Behold, we are in thine hand. - So did he unto them, and delivered them out of the hand of the children of Israel, that they slew them not; and Joshua made them that day hewers of wood and drawers of water for the congregation and for the altar of the LORD, even unto this day. Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still Read the chapter → Joshua 10 Joshua 10:1-5 - Adoni-zedec king of Jerusalem heard how Joshua had taken Ai and utterly destroyed it. You might be confused why it says Jerusalem, since Jerusalem had not been set up as of yet because the land was not conquered: when the scribes wrote the history they left identifying location markers, so the reader knows visually where this is taking place. - They feared greatly, because Gibeon was a great city, as one of the royal cities, greater than Ai, and all the men thereof were mighty. So the five kings of the Amorites, the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon, gathered themselves, went up with all their hosts, and made war against Gibeon, because it had made peace with Joshua and with the children of Israel. Precepts: - Genesis 14:14 Abram pursued them unto Dan, yet the land of Dan was not established in Genesis and Israel was not even born yet; proof the scribes leave location markers for the reader. Joshua 10:6-9 - The men of Gibeon sent to Joshua at Gilgal: slack not thy hand from thy servants; come up to us quickly, and save us, for all the kings of the Amorites that dwell in the mountains are gathered together against us. - The LORD said unto Joshua, Fear them not: for I have delivered them into thine hand; there shall not a man of them stand before thee. So Joshua ascended from Gilgal all night with all the people of war and the mighty men of valour, and came unto them suddenly. Joshua 10:10-11 - The LORD discomfited them before Israel, slew them with a great slaughter at Gibeon, and chased them along the way that goeth up to Beth-horon. As they fled, the LORD cast down great stones from heaven upon them unto Azekah, and they died. - They were more which died with hailstones than they whom the children of Israel slew with the sword. The Most High was up in heaven aiming the hailstones right at the people, and nobody could escape. - He did the same thing in Egypt: the elements were changed in themselves to fight for Israel, and here he sends down hailstones to destroy the people again. Precepts: - Wisdom of Solomon 19:18-20 As in Egypt, the elements themselves were changed to fight against Israel's enemies. Joshua 10:12-14 - Joshua spake to the LORD in the sight of Israel: Sun, stand thou still upon Gibeon; and thou, Moon, in the valley of Ajalon. The sun stood still in the midst of heaven and hasted not to go down about a whole day, and there was no day like that before it or after it, that the LORD hearkened unto the voice of a man: for the LORD fought for Israel. - Is not this written in the book of Jasher? Why do we not have that book today? The mouth of the Most High commanded and his spirit gathered the books of the Bible for us in these last days; he left the book of Jasher out because we do not need it in this captivity. If he wanted us to read it, he would have left it in the book. - He put the Apocrypha in the 1611 version because he wanted us to read it in the last days; the Protestants and Catholics took it out of the modern Bible in the late 1700s, but you cannot stop the Most High. The Bible will always be with the children of Israel, and no, a white man did not write it: the Most High put it in the hands of our enemies to preserve it. That is the power of God. - Reading is fundamental. Listening to and watching videos is fine, but nothing takes the place of reading; the hearing of the word strengthens the understanding of what we have read. That is why the leadership set up the four chapters reading, so make sure reading is first and foremost in understanding and applying the words of the Most High. - Do not go seeking books he did not command us to read: the book of Jasher, the book of the wars, the made-up book of Enoch are unnecessary matters. There are enough deep mysteries in the eighty books he gave us, the sixty-six and the books of the Apocrypha, to stay focused on. Precepts: - Isaiah 34:16-17 Seek ye out of the book of the LORD, and read: no prophecy in it shall fail, and the land is divided to Israel from generation to generation, so the book follows the children of Israel forever. - Ecclesiastes 12:12 Of making many books there is no end, and much study of books he did not command is a weariness of the flesh. - Ecclesiasticus 3:21-24 Be not curious in unnecessary matters; think with reverence on what is commanded thee. Joshua 10:15-21 - The five kings fled and hid themselves in a cave at Makkedah. Joshua said, Roll great stones upon the mouth of the cave, set men by it to keep them, and stay ye not: pursue after your enemies and smite the hindmost of them, for the LORD your God hath delivered them into your hand. - Israel slew them with a very great slaughter till they were consumed, and none moved his tongue against any of the children of Israel. Those dogs equal nations. - Christ did not come for all nations; he came for one people. If in your Christian mind you decide to run to Paul to try to contradict Christ, that lets you know you are wicked, because Christ trumps everybody; and Paul did not teach opposite of Christ anyway, he taught the same thing and just used different names, Gentiles, heathen, the uncircumcised. Precepts: - Exodus 11:7 Against any of the children of Israel shall not a dog move his tongue, that ye may know how that the LORD doth put a difference between Egypt and Israel; underline it and put Joshua 10:20-21 next to it. - Matthew 15:24-26 I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel; it is not meet to take the children's bread and to cast it to dogs; Christ called the other nations dogs just as Exodus 11:7 and Joshua 10:21 do. Joshua 10:22-25 - Then said Joshua, Open the mouth of the cave, and bring out those five kings unto me: the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon. - Joshua called for all the men of Israel and said to the captains of the men of war, Come near, put your feet upon the necks of these kings. Fear not, nor be dismayed, be strong and of good courage: for thus shall the LORD do to all your enemies against whom ye fight. - They hid in caves, and that is what the nations are going to do again. What we read in Joshua is future prophecy: in the day of the Most High men shall go into the holes of the rocks and into the caves of the earth for fear of the LORD, when he ariseth to shake terribly the earth. Precepts: - Isaiah 2:10-12 Enter into the rock and hide thee in the dust for fear of the LORD; caves are made out of rock, and the day of the LORD is upon everyone that is proud and lofty. - Isaiah 2:19-21 They shall go into the holes of the rocks and into the caves of the earth for fear of the LORD, when he ariseth to shake terribly the earth; a future prophecy. Joshua 10:26-27 - Afterward Joshua smote them, slew them, and hanged them on five trees until the evening; at the going down of the sun they took them down, cast them into the cave wherein they had been hid, and laid great stones in the cave's mouth, which remain until this very day. - They took them down according to the law: he that is hanged is accursed of God, and the body shall not remain all night upon the tree, that thy land be not defiled. - Everybody that is hung from a tree is cursed. That lets you know all the nations are cursed, and Israel fell up under the curses also. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 21:22-23 His body shall not remain all night upon the tree, for he that is hanged is accursed of God; they took the kings down so the land would not be defiled. Joshua 10:28-39 - That day Joshua took Makkedah and smote it with the edge of the sword; he utterly destroyed all the souls that were therein, he let none remain, and did to the king of Makkedah as he did unto the king of Jericho. - The southern campaign rolled city by city: Libnah, then Lachish, which he took on the second day; Horam king of Gezer came up to help Lachish, and Joshua smote him and his people until he had left him none remaining. - From Lachish to Eglon, up to Hebron, and back to Debir: every city taken, its king slain, and all the souls therein utterly destroyed, none remaining, according to all that he had done to the cities before. Joshua 10:40-43 - So Joshua smote all the country of the hills, of the south, of the vale, and of the springs, and all their kings; he left none remaining, but utterly destroyed all that breathed, as the LORD God of Israel commanded, from Kadesh-barnea even unto Gaza. All these kings did Joshua take at one time, because the LORD God of Israel fought for Israel. - This is why they tell you not to read the Old Testament: the Most High is out there fighting through his people, giving them the spirit to destroy all that breathe, both young and old, leaving none alive. The LORD is a man of war: the LORD is his name. - Do not think the Most High is unjust in what he does. Nobody taught him or took counsel with him; you cannot show him anything, because he made you and you just got here. In his infinite wisdom he decreed in his own counsel that the nations are as a drop of a bucket, counted as the small dust of the balance that does not tip the scale at all. - Lebanon is not sufficient to burn, nor the beasts thereof sufficient for a burnt offering: you could not gather enough wood or sacrifice enough animals to change his mind about the other nations. All nations before him are as nothing, and they are counted to him less than nothing, and vanity. All means all: no nation is excluded. No wonder the Most High gave Moses and Joshua the green light to destroy everything that breathed. - He increaseth the nations and destroyeth them; the only reason they got big numbers is that they are being fattened for destruction. Precepts: - Exodus 15:3 The LORD is a man of war: the LORD is his name. - Isaiah 40:13-17 Who hath directed the spirit of the LORD, or taught him? The nations are as a drop of a bucket and counted to him less than nothing, and vanity. - Job 12:23 He increaseth the nations, and destroyeth them. Joshua 11: The Northern Kings Utterly Destroyed Read the chapter → Joshua 11 Joshua 11:1-5 - When Jabin king of Hazor heard those things, he sent to Jobab king of Madon, to the kings of Shimron and Achshaph, and to the kings of the north, to the Canaanite, the Amorite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Jebusite, and the Hivite under Hermon. - They went out, they and all their hosts, much people, even as the sand that is upon the sea shore in multitude, with horses and chariots very many. Their plan was to come against Israel in force and overcome them with sheer numbers, and they pitched together at the waters of Merom to fight against Israel. Joshua 11:6-9 - The LORD said unto Joshua, Be not afraid because of them: for to morrow about this time will I deliver them up all slain before Israel: thou shalt hough their horses, and burn their chariots with fire. - Joshua came against them by the waters of Merom suddenly, and the LORD delivered them into the hand of Israel, who smote them and chased them unto great Zidon and unto Misrephoth-maim, until they left them none remaining. Houghing the horses goes into binding up the horses' legs so they were finished as instruments of war. - Joshua did unto them as the LORD bade him: he houghed their horses and burnt their chariots with fire. Joshua 11:10-15 - Joshua turned back and took Hazor, for Hazor beforetime was the head of all those kingdoms, and smote all the souls therein with the edge of the sword; there was not any left to breathe, and he burnt Hazor with fire. But as for the cities that stood still in their strength, Israel burned none of them, save Hazor only. - All the spoil of these cities and the cattle the children of Israel took for a prey unto themselves, but every man they smote with the edge of the sword, neither left they any to breathe. As the LORD commanded Moses, so did Moses command Joshua, and so did Joshua: he left nothing undone of all that the LORD commanded Moses. - There is a law pertaining to war: when thou comest nigh unto a city to fight against it, proclaim peace unto it, and if it answers peace the people become tributaries and serve thee. But that applied to cities very far off. Of the cities of these people, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, thou shalt save alive nothing that breatheth, but shalt utterly destroy them. - The Most High is not unjust in what he does. It was already prophesied to Abram that his seed would be afflicted four hundred years and in the fourth generation come hither again, for the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet full. When Israel came back to establish the land, it was time for those nations to pay for their iniquities from way back when. - Genesis 15:13 is not talking about America. Judah has been here longer than four hundred years and the northern kingdom longer than six hundred, so this is not us coming up out of Babylon the great; and Israel was actually in Egypt four hundred and thirty years, free for the first thirty. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 20:10-17 The law of war: far-off cities that answer peace become tributaries, but of the cities of these nations save alive nothing that breatheth. - Genesis 15:13-16 Thy seed shall serve and be afflicted four hundred years and come hither again in the fourth generation, for the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet full; the destruction was prophesied and just. Joshua 11:16-20 - So Joshua took all that land, the hills, all the south country, all the land of Goshen, the valley, the plain, and the mountain of Israel; all their kings he took, and smote them, and slew them. Joshua made war a long time with all those kings. - There was not a city that made peace with the children of Israel, save the Hivites the inhabitants of Gibeon; that is why all of them went into destruction. It was of the LORD to harden their hearts, that they should come against Israel in battle, that he might destroy them utterly, and that they might have no favour. - There is nothing new under the sun; it shall happen again, and we are just waiting on it to unfold. The nation and kingdom that will not serve Israel shall perish, and those nations shall be utterly wasted; the sons of them that afflicted thee shall come bending unto thee. - We see the Most High setting it up right before our eyes: Israel is being made into warriors once again, so the days of Joshua can be once again when the Lord returns. He is setting us in order before our enemies' eyes. - Esau thinks the Most High is altogether such a one as himself, that the Most High looks like him and is happy with him punishing and oppressing us. He is not down for it; it is our punishment and it has to happen, but he will reprove Esau and set Israel in order before his eyes. - When Christ returns he will destroy all nations in the valley of Megiddo, and after Israel's spirits are changed he will thrust out the enemy from before us and say, Destroy them. Israel will lay the vengeance of the Most High upon Edom according to his anger and according to his fury. Brothers, you just have to endure to the end; this is how you read the Bible, precept upon precept, here a little and there a little. Precepts: - Isaiah 60:12-15 The nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish; the sons of them that afflicted thee shall come bending unto thee; it shall happen again. - Joel 2:7-11 They shall run like mighty men and climb the wall like men of war; the LORD shall utter his voice before his army; Israel made into warriors once again. - Psalms 50:21 Thou thoughtest that I was altogether such an one as thyself; but I will reprove thee, and set them in order before thine eyes. - Deuteronomy 33:27 He shall thrust out the enemy from before thee, and shall say, Destroy them. - Ezekiel 25:12-14 Edom revenged himself upon Judah over and above his charge; I will lay my vengeance upon Edom by the hand of my people Israel. - Micah 5:15 I will execute vengeance in anger and fury upon the heathen, such as they have not heard. Joshua 11:21-23 - At that time came Joshua and cut off the Anakims from the mountains, from Hebron, from Debir, from Anab, and from all the mountains of Judah and Israel; Joshua destroyed them utterly with their cities. None of the Anakims were left in the land of the children of Israel: only in Gaza, in Gath, and in Ashdod there remained. - So Joshua took the whole land, according to all that the LORD said unto Moses, and gave it for an inheritance unto Israel according to their divisions by their tribes. And the land rested from war. Joshua 12: The Thirty and One Kings Read the chapter → Joshua 12 Joshua 12:1-6 - These are the kings the children of Israel smote on the other side Jordan toward the rising of the sun: Sihon king of the Amorites, who dwelt in Heshbon, and Og king of Bashan, which was of the remnant of the giants, that dwelt at Ashtaroth and at Edrei. - Them did Moses the servant of the LORD and the children of Israel smite, and Moses gave their land for a possession unto the Reubenites, and the Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh. Look up a map of the Jordan river and the twelve tribes and you will see the split of where Reuben, Gad, and half Manasseh dwelt, on the east side of Jordan. - That region became known as the land of the Gentiles, as you read in the gospel. Precepts: - Matthew 4:15 The land beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles; the east-side territory became known as the land of the Gentiles. Joshua 12:7-24 - These are the kings of the country which Joshua and the children of Israel smote on this side Jordan on the west, which Joshua gave unto the tribes of Israel for a possession according to their divisions: the kings of Jericho, Ai, Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, Eglon, Gezer, Debir, Geder, Hormah, Arad, Libnah, Adullam, Makkedah, Bethel, Tappuah, Hepher, Aphek, Lasharon, Madon, Hazor, Shimron-meron, Achshaph, Taanach, Megiddo, Kedesh, Jokneam of Carmel, Dor, the nations of Gilgal, and Tirzah: all the kings thirty and one. - Practice reading these names aloud; it loosens up the tongue and helps you pronounce the names in the Bible that may run two or three syllables. - Joshua was a mighty man: thirty and one kings he took down in the power of the Most High. Let us now praise famous men and our fathers that begat us. In Ecclesiasticus he is called Jesus the son of Nave, for Joshua translated into the Greek is Jesus, and Nave is Nun: Joshua the son of Nun, valiant in the wars, the successor of Moses in prophecies, who according to his name was made great for the saving of the elect of God. - Did not the sun go back by his means, and was not one day as long as two? He said, Sun, be thou still, and there were two days of sunlight on the earth; and with hailstones of mighty power the Most High made the battle to fall violently upon the nations in the descent of Beth-horon. - His counterpart Caleb was a mighty man too: he and Caleb withstood the congregation and withheld the people from sin, and of six hundred thousand people on foot, they two were preserved to bring them into the heritage. The Most High gave Caleb strength unto his old age, fighting in his eighties like he was in his twenties, and you will read of his strength in the next few chapters. - Take pride in this: we are the descendants of the most famous men on the face of the earth. Our forefathers are mentioned in every single nation, and everybody wants to lay claim to them and to our book. That is why all nations hate us, and we will be famous again: the Most High will get Israel praise and fame in every land where they have been put to shame, when he turns back our captivity before our eyes. Remember, Jerusalem is a people before it is a place. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 44:1 We descend from the famous men of the book of the Lord. - Ecclesiasticus 46:1-6 The fame of Joshua: the sun stood by his means, and the great Lord heard him. - Ecclesiasticus 46:7-10 Joshua and Caleb, the two preserved of six hundred thousand, that all Israel might see it is good to follow the Lord. - Zephaniah 3:16-20 I will get them praise and fame in every land where they have been put to shame, when I turn back your captivity before your eyes; Israel will be famous again. --- Topics: Esau and Edom · Idolatry · Sacrifice and Atonement ← Joshua 5-8 · Joshua Study · Joshua 13-16 →

title: Judges 1: Judah Goes Up First, but the Inhabitants Are Not Driven Out
text: ← Joshua 21-24 · Judges Study · Judges 5-8 → Judges 1: Judah Goes Up First, but the Inhabitants Are Not Driven Out Read the chapter → Judges 1 Introduction This session covers Judges 1 through 4, reading through the Bible from Genesis through Revelation, four chapters a day, so the whole Bible is read in one year. It is not a class, but highlighted parts of the chapters are touched on with basic precepts to help with the understanding. Much of Judges reads straightforward: after the death of Joshua the tribes go up against the Canaanites, but tribe after tribe does not drive out the inhabitants of the land as the Most High commanded. Chapter 2 shows what dwelling among them cost Israel, chapter 3 opens the cycle of the judges with Othniel, Ehud, and Shamgar, and chapter 4 gives Deborah, Barak, and Jael. As you read, it helps to look at a map of the dividing of the land, such as the dividing-of-the-land map in the rear of the Zondervan's Compact Bible Dictionary, or an ancient twelve tribes chart, to see where these tribes and cities sat. Judges 1:1-3 - After the death of Joshua the children of Israel ask the Most High who shall go up first against the Canaanites, and the answer is Judah: behold, I have delivered the land into his hand. - Judah asks Simeon his brother to come up with him into his lot, and promises to go likewise with Simeon into his lot, so Simeon went with him. Judges 1:4-7 - The Most High delivers the Canaanites and the Perizzites into Judah's hand, and they slay ten thousand men in Bezek. - Adonibezek flees and is caught, and his thumbs and great toes are cut off. He confesses it himself: threescore and ten kings with their thumbs and great toes cut off gathered their meat under his table, and as he had done, so God requited him. Judges 1:8 - The children of Judah fought against Jerusalem, took it, smote it with the edge of the sword, and set the city on fire. This verse ties back into the history we just finished reading in Joshua. - Judah was supposed to drive the Jebusites, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, out of the land, but could not, and the Jebusites dwelt with the children of Judah at Jerusalem. Jerusalem sat right on Judah's border by the valley of the son of Hinnom. - The king of Jerusalem was already among the kings of the land which the children of Israel smote and whose land they possessed, so this fight in Judges is Judah taking the city itself. Precepts: - Joshua 15:63 The children of Judah could not drive out the Jebusites, but the Jebusites dwell with the children of Judah at Jerusalem unto this day. - Joshua 15:8 Judah's border went up by the valley of the son of Hinnom unto the south side of the Jebusite, the same is Jerusalem. - Joshua 12:1 These are the kings of the land which the children of Israel smote, and possessed their land. - Joshua 12:10 The king of Jerusalem, one; the king of Hebron, one; Jerusalem's king was already counted among the kings smitten. Judges 1:9-15 - Judah goes down against the Canaanites in the mountain, the south, and the valley, and against Hebron, which before was called Kirjath-arba, slaying Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai. - Caleb offers Achsah his daughter to wife to whoever smites Kirjath-sepher, and Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother, takes it. Achsah asks her father for a blessing, springs of water with the south land, and Caleb gives her the upper springs and the nether springs. - This is a review of the history we just read in Joshua; it was not that many days ago in the reading that we covered this, and it repeats again here at the opening of Judges. Precepts: - Joshua 15:16-17 The same account word for word: Caleb's offer, and Othniel the son of Kenaz taking Kirjath-sepher and receiving Achsah to wife. Judges 1:16-19 - The children of the Kenite, Moses' father in law, go up out of the city of palm trees with the children of Judah and dwell among the people in the wilderness of Judah. - Judah goes with Simeon his brother, slays the Canaanites in Zephath and utterly destroys it, calling the city Hormah, and takes Gaza, Askelon, and Ekron with their coasts. - The Most High was with Judah, and he drave out the inhabitants of the mountain, but could not drive out the inhabitants of the valley, because they had chariots of iron. Judges 1:20-21 - Hebron is given unto Caleb, as Moses said, and he expels thence the three sons of Anak. - The children of Benjamin did not drive out the Jebusites that inhabited Jerusalem, but the Jebusites dwell with the children of Benjamin in Jerusalem unto this day. Judges 1:22-26 - The house of Joseph goes up against Bethel, which before was called Luz, and the Most High was with them. - The spies see a man come out of the city and promise him mercy for showing the entrance. They smite the city with the edge of the sword, but let the man and all his family go, and he goes into the land of the Hittites and builds a city and calls it Luz. Judges 1:27-36 - Tribe after tribe repeats the same failure: neither did Manasseh, nor Ephraim, nor Zebulun, nor Asher, nor Naphtali drive out the inhabitants of their cities, and the Amorites forced the children of Dan into the mountain. - What we are reading is how we did not drive out all the inhabitants of the land, which the Most High had commanded us. Each tribe did not drive them out, and what did we do? We dwelt among them. - When Israel was strong, we put the Canaanites to tribute, but we still did not utterly drive them out; we still dwelt among them. Chapter 2 gets into what that dwelling among the inhabitants of the land brought upon us. Judges 2: No League with the Inhabitants of the Land Read the chapter → Judges 2 Judges 2:1-5 - An angel of the Most High comes up from Gilgal to Bochim and rehearses the covenant: I made you to go up out of Egypt, I brought you unto the land I sware unto your fathers, and I said I will never break my covenant with you. The command was plain: ye shall make no league with the inhabitants of this land, ye shall throw down their altars. But ye have not obeyed my voice. Why have ye done this? - The same is true today in the places where we are scattered: we have made leagues with the inhabitants of the land. We find ourselves in their sports leagues and bowling leagues, at their dinner parties, when the scripture says envy not the oppressor and choose none of his ways. - The Most High warned against letting them dwell in the land because they would make us sin against him. Dwelling among them breeds curiosity after their gods: how did these nations serve their gods, what is that thing they are doing with that tree, what are they hanging on the tree, why are they giving each other gifts? That curiosity is the snare, and we are not to add to his commandments or take away from them. - Throwing down their altars meant burning their graven images with fire, not even desiring the silver or gold on them, lest it become a snare. The Most High keeps reiterating that we will be snared and trapped by serving what these nations serve. - Because Israel disobeyed, the sentence falls: I will not drive them out from before you, but they shall be as thorns in your sides, and their gods shall be a snare unto you. The people lifted up their voice and wept, called the place Bochim, and sacrificed there unto the Most High. Precepts: - Exodus 23:32-33 Thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor with their gods; they shall not dwell in thy land, lest they make thee sin against me. - Proverbs 3:31 Envy thou not the oppressor, and choose none of his ways. - Deuteronomy 12:28-31 Take heed that thou be not snared by following them, and that thou enquire not after their gods, saying, How did these nations serve their gods? - Deuteronomy 12:32 What thing soever I command you, observe to do it: thou shalt not add thereto, nor diminish from it. - Deuteronomy 7:25 The graven images of their gods shall ye burn with fire; desire not the gold or silver on them, lest thou be snared therein, for it is an abomination to the Most High. Judges 2:6-9 - The people served the Most High all the days of Joshua, and all the days of the elders that outlived Joshua, who had seen all the great works he did for Israel. - Joshua the son of Nun dies at a hundred and ten years old and is buried in the border of his inheritance in Timnath-heres, in the mount of Ephraim, because Joshua was of the tribe of Ephraim; he was buried in the land of his own tribe's inheritance. Precepts: - Numbers 13:8 Of the tribe of Ephraim, Oshea the son of Nun; Oshea the son of Nun is Joshua, whom Moses called Jehoshua. Judges 2:10-13 - That whole generation is gathered unto their fathers, and there arises another generation which knew not the Most High, nor the works he had done for Israel, and the children of Israel do evil and serve Baalim and Ashtaroth. - Here a pattern starts to develop: when there is a judge in Israel and he dies, the people just go off. It shows we are a people that need leadership; that is why we are told to trust in the Most High and lean not to our own understanding, and he shall direct our paths. - We see the same today. Brothers and sisters come with theories they think are their own thoughts, but those thoughts were given to them, mostly by the television. You are either going to follow the one true living God of Israel or the prince of the power of the air, Satan the devil. Precepts: - Proverbs 3:5-6 Trust in the Lord with all thine heart, and lean not unto thine own understanding; in all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths. Judges 2:14-15 - Because Israel forsook the Most High, his anger was hot against them; he delivered them into the hands of spoilers and sold them into the hands of their enemies, so that they could not any longer stand before their enemies. Look at us today: Black Lives Matter, hands up don't shoot. We cannot stand before our enemies, so now we beg our enemies to see us as people, to see us as human. - Our offence is leaving off the commandments to serve other gods, and the Most High has gone and returned to his place until we acknowledge that offence; in our affliction we will seek him early. Judges is the record of that affliction beginning to come upon our people for turning our backs on the one true living God. - Whithersoever they went, the hand of the Most High was against them for evil, and they were greatly distressed. Is that not true today? We wonder why we cannot get anywhere as a people; we have individual millionaires, yet no infrastructure, no farms enough to set up our own stores and feed ourselves, no distribution, no hospitals, no textiles, none of the things a nation needs to sustain a nation. - The curse was to be cursed coming in and cursed going out, coming in from war and going out to war, and the same is happening to this very day. Our people do not think we are at war, but when the enemy gives you a false image, a false religion and a false education, slums and ghettos to live in, and bad foods, he is at war with you. Precepts: - Hosea 5:15 I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early. - Deuteronomy 28:19 Cursed shalt thou be when thou comest in, and cursed shalt thou be when thou goest out. Judges 2:16-19 - Nevertheless the Most High raised up judges which delivered them out of the hand of those that spoiled them, and yet they would not hearken unto their judges, but went a whoring after other gods and turned quickly out of the way their fathers walked in. - It repented the Most High because of their groanings by reason of them that oppressed them and vexed them. It was the same in Egypt: he said, I have surely seen the affliction of my people, I have heard their cry by reason of their taskmasters, I know their sorrows. - We are the apple of his eye; he that toucheth Israel toucheth the apple of his eye. The Most High does not want to see us on the bottom, but we trespassed against his commandments, so we have to be punished for it. - When the judge was dead, they returned and corrupted themselves more than their fathers, ceasing not from their own doings nor from their stubborn way. As soon as we got out of the condition we were in, we went right back to doing the same thing again, because this is a rebellious and stubborn people, even to this very day. Precepts: - Exodus 3:7 I have surely seen the affliction of my people which are in Egypt, and have heard their cry by reason of their taskmasters; for I know their sorrows. - Zechariah 2:8 He that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye. Judges 2:20-23 - Because this people transgressed the covenant and did not hearken, the Most High declares he will not henceforth drive out any of the nations which Joshua left when he died. This is exactly what Joshua warned before he died: if ye cleave unto the remnant of these nations and make marriages with them, know for a certainty the Most High will no more drive them out, but they shall be snares and traps, scourges in your sides and thorns in your eyes, until ye perish from off the good land. - In the course of making leagues with the inhabitants, what else did we do? We made marriages with them, the very thing the warning named. - The nations were left without being driven out hastily, that through them the Most High might prove Israel, whether they would keep his way to walk therein as their fathers did, or not. Precepts: - Joshua 23:12-13 If ye make marriages with the remnant of these nations, know for a certainty that the Lord will no more drive them out, but they shall be snares and traps unto you, until ye perish from off this good land. Judges 3: Nations Left to Prove Israel Read the chapter → Judges 3 Judges 3:1-4 - These are the nations the Most High left to prove Israel, even as many as had not known all the wars of Canaan, so that the generations of the children of Israel might know, to teach them war: five lords of the Philistines, and all the Canaanites, and the Sidonians, and the Hivites of mount Lebanon. - Who are all the Canaanites? Genesis 10 lists the families: Canaan begat Sidon his firstborn, and Heth, and the Jebusite, the Amorite, the Girgashite, the Hivite, the Arkite, the Sinite, the Arvadite, the Zemarite, and the Hamathite, and afterward the families of the Canaanites were spread abroad. - They were left to prove Israel, to know whether Israel would hearken unto the commandments of the Most High, which he commanded their fathers by the hand of Moses. Precepts: - Genesis 10:15-18 All the families of the Canaanites that spread abroad, begotten of Canaan. Judges 3:5-7 - The children of Israel dwelt among the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites. Stop: are those not the same people the Most High said to utterly destroy? But we are dwelling among them. - They took their daughters to be their wives, and gave their daughters to their sons, and served their gods. The law had said it plainly: thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor shew mercy unto them, neither shalt thou make marriages with them, for they will turn away thy son from following me, that they may serve other gods. - The law of war made a different stipulation for these people. For far off cities Israel was to proclaim peace first, and if they answered peace they became tributaries, just as we read the tribes putting the Canaanites to tribute. But of the cities of these people, the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, thou shalt save alive nothing that breatheth, total destruction, that they teach you not to do after all their abominations which they have done unto their gods. - Going out to battle against horses and chariots and people more than thou, Israel was told, be not afraid of them, for the Most High is with thee. He constantly repeats these things because he knew we were going to be a stubborn and rebellious people, and he wants us to acknowledge him and only him. Instead Israel did evil, forgat the Most High, and served Baalim and the groves. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 7:1-4 Seven nations greater and mightier than thou: make no covenant with them and no marriages with them, for they will turn away thy son from following me. - Deuteronomy 20:1 Be not afraid of horses and chariots and a people more than thou, for the Lord thy God is with thee. - Deuteronomy 20:10-13 The city that answers peace becomes tributary; the city that makes war is besieged and every male smitten. - Deuteronomy 20:16-18 But of the cities of these people thou shalt save alive nothing that breatheth, that they teach you not to do after all their abominations. Judges 3:8-11 - The anger of the Most High was hot against Israel, and he sold them into the hand of Chushan-rishathaim king of Mesopotamia, and Israel served him eight years. When they cried unto the Most High, he raised up a deliverer, Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother. - The spirit of the Most High came upon Othniel, and he judged Israel. But today our people say, you can't judge me. - He judged Israel and went out to war, because the Lord is a man of war. That answers those who ask, when we are out on the streets teaching, where are your women. They are not at war; the Lord is a man of war. - And for those who do not think we are at war now: though we walk in the flesh, we do not war after the flesh. It is a spiritual war, but we are still nonetheless at war, and the weapon of our warfare today is this Bible, mighty through God to the pulling down of strongholds, exposing all the lies on the earth. - The Most High delivered Chushan-rishathaim into Othniel's hand, and the land had rest forty years, until Othniel the son of Kenaz died. Precepts: - Exodus 15:3 The Lord is a man of war: the Lord is his name. - 2 Corinthians 10:3-6 We do not war after the flesh; the weapons of our warfare are not carnal, but mighty through God to the pulling down of strong holds. Judges 3:12-14 - The children of Israel did evil again in the sight of the Most High, and he strengthened Eglon the king of Moab against Israel because they had done evil. - Wait a minute: it says the Most High strengthened him. In Joshua, the hearts of the peoples melted because they heard of the things the Most High did for us; now he is strengthening them against us for breaking his commandments. - Eglon gathers the children of Ammon and Amalek, smites Israel, and possesses the city of palm trees, and the children of Israel serve Eglon the king of Moab eighteen years. Precepts: - Joshua 2:9-11 Your terror is fallen upon us; as soon as we had heard these things, our hearts did melt. The same nations whose hearts melted are now strengthened against disobedient Israel. Judges 3:15-23 - When the children of Israel cried unto the Most High, he raised them up a deliverer, Ehud the son of Gera, a Benjamite, a man lefthanded.
