Notice how the Most High raised up judges of different tribes also: Othniel of Judah, now Ehud of Benjamin. - Ehud makes a two edged dagger of a cubit length, girds it under his raiment on his right thigh, and brings the present to Eglon king of Moab, who was a very fat man. - Saying, I have a secret errand unto thee, O king, Ehud gets Eglon alone in his summer parlour, tells him, I have a message from God unto thee, and thrusts the dagger into his belly with his left hand, and the fat closes upon the blade so he cannot draw it out. Ehud goes forth and locks the doors of the parlour. Judges 3:24-30 - When the servants find the parlour doors locked, they say, surely he covereth his feet in his summer chamber; they wait outside because they think he is in there relieving himself, and they tarry till they are ashamed, then take a key and find their lord fallen down dead. - Ehud escapes to Seirath, blows a trumpet in the mountain of Ephraim, and leads the children of Israel down, saying, follow after me, for the Lord hath delivered your enemies the Moabites into your hand. They slay of Moab about ten thousand men, all lusty men of valour, and not a man escapes. - So Moab was subdued that day under the hand of Israel, and the land had rest fourscore years. Judges 3:31 - After Ehud was Shamgar the son of Anath, which slew of the Philistines six hundred men with an ox goad; and he also delivered Israel. Judges 4: Deborah, Barak, and Jael Read the chapter → Judges 4 This chapter was read through without stopping for exposition; the account itself carries the same cycle already laid out in chapter 2: Israel does evil, is sold into an oppressor's hand, cries unto the Most High, and a deliverer is raised up. Judges 4:1-3 - When Ehud was dead, the children of Israel again did evil, and the Most High sold them into the hand of Jabin king of Canaan, that reigned in Hazor, whose captain was Sisera, which dwelt in Harosheth of the Gentiles. - Sisera had nine hundred chariots of iron, and twenty years he mightily oppressed the children of Israel, and they cried unto the Most High. Judges 4:4-9 - Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lapidoth, judged Israel at that time, dwelling under the palm tree of Deborah between Ramah and Bethel in mount Ephraim, and the children of Israel came up to her for judgment. - She calls Barak the son of Abinoam and gives him the commandment of the Most High: draw toward mount Tabor with ten thousand men of Naphtali and Zebulun, and I will draw unto thee Sisera with his chariots and his multitude to the river Kishon, and deliver him into thine hand. - Barak answers, if thou wilt go with me, then I will go, but if thou wilt not go with me, then I will not go. Deborah agrees to go, but tells him the journey shall not be for his honour, for the Most High shall sell Sisera into the hand of a woman. Judges 4:10-16 - Barak calls Zebulun and Naphtali to Kedesh and goes up with ten thousand men at his feet, and Deborah goes up with him. Heber the Kenite, of the children of Hobab the father in law of Moses, had severed himself from the Kenites and pitched his tent by Kedesh. - Sisera gathers all nine hundred chariots of iron unto the river of Kishon, and Deborah says unto Barak, up, for this is the day in which the Lord hath delivered Sisera into thine hand; is not the Lord gone out before thee? - The Most High discomfits Sisera and all his chariots and all his host with the edge of the sword before Barak; Sisera lights down off his chariot and flees away on his feet, and all his host falls upon the edge of the sword; there was not a man left. Judges 4:17-24 - Sisera flees on foot to the tent of Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite, for there was peace between Jabin the king of Hazor and the house of Heber. Jael invites him in, covers him with a mantle, and gives him milk to drink when he asks for water. - He tells her to stand in the door and say no man is there; then Jael takes a nail of the tent and a hammer in her hand, goes softly unto him as he sleeps fast and weary, and smites the nail into his temples and fastens it into the ground, and he dies. The word through Deborah stands: Sisera was sold into the hand of a woman. - When Barak comes pursuing, Jael shows him Sisera lying dead with the nail in his temples. So God subdued that day Jabin the king of Canaan before the children of Israel, and their hand prospered and prevailed until they had destroyed him. --- Topics: Idolatry · The Covenant ← Joshua 21-24 · Judges Study · Judges 5-8 →

title: Judges 13: A Nazarite from the Womb
text: ← Judges 9-12 · Judges Study · Judges 17-20 → Judges 13: A Nazarite from the Womb Read the chapter → Judges 13 Introduction This session covers the whole history of Samson, one of the most famous forefathers and one of the most illustrated stories in the Bible: his birth announced by the angel of the Lord in chapter 13, his marriage among the Philistines and the riddle in chapter 14, the jawbone of an ass in chapter 15, and Delilah and his death in chapter 16. In the book of Judges, after Joshua led Israel into the promised land and died, Israel immediately started going off; before the major captivities of Assyria and Babylon came about, Israel was oppressed by the Moabites, the Philistines, and other nations round about. Here Israel is under the hand of the Philistines, and the Most High raises up a deliverer from the tribe of Dan. Judges 13:1 - The children of Israel did evil again in the sight of the Lord, and the Lord delivered them into the hand of the Philistines forty years. This is the pattern of the book of Judges: after Joshua's death Israel went off, and nation after nation was given power over them before the great captivities ever came. Judges 13:2 - There was a certain man of Zorah, of the family of the Danites, whose name was Manoah. He was married, but his wife was barren; she was not able to have any children. Judges 13:3 - The angel of the Lord appeared unto the woman and told her plainly: you are barren now, but you shall conceive and bear a son, a man child. - This is one of many examples in the Bible of our foremothers going through barrenness, and when the Most High was ready he enabled them to conceive. Sisters who have tried for years without children should in patience possess their souls, take comfort of the scriptures, meditate on the foremothers, and believe what the Bible says. Precepts: - Psalms 113:9 The Most High maketh the barren woman to keep house and to be a joyful mother of children. Judges 13:4-5 - The angel commanded the mother herself to drink no wine nor strong drink and to eat no unclean thing, because the child would be a Nazarite unto God from the womb; even in the womb he was to be kept pure. - No razor was to come on his head, for the child would be a Nazarite unto God from the womb, and he would begin to deliver Israel out of the hand of the Philistines. This is one of the first examples in scripture of somebody actually living the vow that was laid out in Numbers 6. - Understand the difference between a Nazarite and a Nazarene. Christ was a Nazarene because he was from the city of Nazareth, not a Nazarite; he drank wine, and Nazarites could not drink the blood of the grape at all. - The locks of the Nazarite also witness to who Israel is; the hair of Israel naturally grows into locks. Precepts: - Numbers 6:1-4 When a man or woman separates themselves to vow a vow of a Nazarite, they are on another level of dedication to the Lord: no wine, no strong drink, no vinegar, no liquor of grapes, nothing made of the vine tree from the kernels even to the husk. - Numbers 6:5 All the days of the vow no razor shall come upon his head; he shall be holy and shall let the locks of the hair of his head grow, which is why the angel gave Manoah's wife these instructions. Judges 13:6-7 - The woman came and told her husband that a man of God came unto her whose countenance was like the countenance of an angel of God, very terrible. In verse 3 the scripture says it was the angel of the Lord, but he did not tell her, so she was not sure; she only knew his face was terrible like an angel's. - The popular pictures of angels as cute babies with smooth cheeks and little white wings do not match the biblical descriptions at all. To see an angel of the Most High was a terrifying sight, not something to jump for joy about. - She repeated the message: the child shall be a Nazarite to God from the womb to the day of his death, and she was to drink no wine nor strong drink nor eat any unclean thing. Precepts: - Matthew 28:1-4 The angel of the Lord descended, rolled back the stone, and sat upon it; his countenance was like lightning and his raiment white as snow, and for fear of him the keepers did shake and became as dead men. Judges 13:8-10 - Manoah entreated the Lord: let the man of God which thou didst send come again unto us and teach us what we shall do unto the child that shall be born. - The Most High hearkened to the voice of Manoah, and the angel of God came again unto the woman as she sat in the field; she made haste and ran and showed her husband that the man was back. Judges 13:11-14 - Manoah arose and went after his wife, came to the man, and asked, art thou the man that spakest unto the woman? He said, I am. - Manoah asked how they should order the child and what they should do unto him, and the angel reiterated the instructions he had already given: of all that I said unto the woman let her beware, and all that I commanded her let her observe while she carries this son. Judges 13:15-16 - Manoah tried to detain the angel and make ready a kid for him, but the angel refused: though thou detain me, I will not eat of thy bread, and if thou wilt offer a burnt offering, thou must offer it unto the Lord. - The angel knew Manoah might try to offer it up to him, since he appeared like a god, so he directed the offering to the Lord. Israel is quick to worship anything that looks like it could be God because we cannot see the Most High, which is why the scriptures warn against the worshipping of angels. - Manoah still did not know that he was an angel of the Lord. Precepts: - Colossians 2:18 Let no man beguile you of your reward in a voluntary humility and worshipping of angels. - Revelation 22:8-9 John the revelator, the disciple whom Christ loved, fell down to worship before the feet of the angel, and the angel said, see thou do it not, for I am thy fellowservant and of thy brethren the prophets: worship God. Judges 13:17-18 - Manoah asked the angel his name, so that when his sayings came to pass they might do him honour. - The angel answered, why askest thou thus after my name, seeing it is secret? His name was too wonderful to be uttered to him. Judges 13:19-21 - Manoah took a kid with a meat offering and offered it upon a rock unto the Lord, and the angel did wondrously: when the flame went up toward heaven from off the altar, the angel of the Lord ascended in the flame and went out of their sight. - Manoah and his wife fell on their faces to the ground at the sight. This is the kind of thing Israel was able to see and witness with their own eyes. - The angel appeared no more, and then Manoah knew that he was an angel of the Lord. Judges 13:22-23 - Manoah said to his wife, we shall surely die, because we have seen God. This is a passage the contradictors point to, since the Bible says no man hath seen God; but God here is Elohim, which is plural and speaks of heavenly beings. They saw an angel, not the Most High God. - No flesh can look upon the Most High God; he is far too fierce and terrible. The furthest anybody got was Moses seeing his back parts. - His wife reasoned rightly: if the Lord were pleased to kill us, he would not have received a burnt offering and a meat offering at our hands, neither would he have shewed us all these things. Judges 13:24-25 - The woman bare a son and called his name Samson, and the child grew, and the Lord blessed him. - The spirit of the Lord began to move him at times in the camp of Dan between Zorah and Eshtaol; the Most High began to deal with him. Judges 14: An Occasion Against the Philistines Read the chapter → Judges 14 Judges 14:1-3 - Samson went down to Timnath and saw a woman of the daughters of the Philistines, and told his father and mother, get her for me to wife. As he grew up this brother had a lust issue with heathen women; that is the infamy the story of Samson is known for. - His parents answered him rightly: is there never a woman among the daughters of thy brethren, or among all my people, that thou goest to take a wife of the uncircumcised Philistines? There were twelve tribes; there was no shortage of women in all the coasts of Israel. - Samson insisted, get her for me, for she pleaseth me well. The forefathers always charged their sons not to do this. Precepts: - Genesis 28:1 Isaac called Jacob, blessed him, and charged him: thou shalt not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan; the fathers commanded their sons to choose from their own people. Judges 14:4 - His father and his mother knew not that it was of the Lord, that he sought an occasion against the Philistines, for at that time the Philistines had dominion over Israel. The Lord was moving Samson's spirit, and the parents did not understand, just as we often question the Most High when we have no idea the depths of his wisdom and what he is really doing. - The Most High was using Samson's flaw, his lust after Philistine women, as an occasion against the Philistines, to destroy them for oppressing his people. That is the basis of the whole story: the Lord was behind all of it, pulling the strings. - The Most High is in control of everything, good and evil alike. Even affliction that comes on his people is his tactic to make them seek him and repent; nothing anybody does can alter the outcome he has already ordained, for he declared the end from the beginning. Precepts: - Isaiah 55:8-9 His thoughts are not our thoughts, neither are our ways his ways; his thoughts are higher than our thoughts. - Job 12:16 With him is strength and wisdom; the deceived and the deceiver are his. The Most High used these heathen women, and later Delilah, to get Samson caught up with the Philistines so that he would end up destroying them. - Proverbs 21:30 There is no wisdom nor understanding nor counsel against the Lord; everything ultimately works within his plan. - Amos 3:6 Shall there be evil in a city, and the Lord hath not done it? The evil is wrong, but the Lord is behind it, working his purpose. - Hosea 5:15 In their affliction they will seek me early; affliction is how the Most High wakes his people up to repent. Judges 14:5-6 - As Samson went down to the vineyards of Timnath, a young lion roared against him, challenging him. Here you begin to see the divine power on Samson. - The spirit of the Lord came mightily upon him, and he rent the lion as he would have rent a kid, and he had nothing in his hand: no weapon, no sword, nothing. He tore up a young lion, a prince of the jungle, like it was a little goat. This is one of the forms of the spirit of the Lord, spiritual power. - He told not his father or his mother what he had done; he did not boast about it. Judges 14:7-9 - He went down and talked with the woman, and she pleased Samson well. - After a time he returned to take her, and he turned aside to see the carcase of the lion he had slain, and behold, there was a swarm of bees and honey in the carcase. - He took of the honey in his hands and went on eating, and gave to his father and mother and they did eat, but he told them not that he had taken the honey out of the carcase of the lion. Judges 14:10-14 - His father went down unto the woman, and Samson made there a feast, as the young men used to do, and when the Philistines saw him they brought thirty companions to be with him. - Samson put forth a riddle: if they could declare it within the seven days of the feast, he would give them thirty sheets and thirty change of garments, and if they could not, they would give him the same. - The riddle: out of the eater came forth meat, and out of the strong came forth sweetness. In three days they could not expound it. Judges 14:15-17 - On the seventh day they said unto Samson's wife, entice thy husband that he may declare unto us the riddle, lest we burn thee and thy father's house with fire. They threatened to burn their own countrywoman in her father's house over thirty outfits. - She turned to manipulation and wept before him: thou dost but hate me, and lovest me not; thou hast put forth a riddle unto the children of my people and hast not told it me. He answered, I have not told it my father nor my mother, and shall I tell it thee? - She wept before him the seven days while their feast lasted, and on the seventh day he told her, because she lay sore upon him. This big strong mighty brother caved in because of the tears of a woman. Judges 14:18 - She told the riddle to the children of her people, and the men of the city answered him before the sun went down: what is sweeter than honey, and what is stronger than a lion? - Samson knew exactly what happened: if ye had not plowed with my heifer, ye had not found out my riddle. - Never trust your enemy. That was his wife, and her loyalty belonged to him, but when she got the riddle out of him she went and told it to her heathen people, his enemy. That is why it makes no sense to marry the enemy. Judges 14:19-20 - The spirit of the Lord came upon him, and he went down to Ashkelon and slew thirty men of the Philistines, took their spoil, and gave the change of garments unto them which expounded the riddle; the spirit of the Lord came upon him even for this, against the nation that oppressed Israel. - His anger was kindled, and he went up to his father's house, and Samson's wife was given to his companion, whom he had used as his friend; she was his wife to be, for they had not yet consummated the marriage. Judges 15: The Jawbone of an Ass Read the chapter → Judges 15 Judges 15:1-3 - Within a while, in the time of wheat harvest, Samson visited his wife with a kid and said, I will go in to my wife into the chamber. He knew she had betrayed him and still went back to her; a weakness for a woman really does beat on Israelite men. - Her father would not suffer him to go in, saying, I verily thought that thou hadst utterly hated her, therefore I gave her to thy companion; is not her younger sister fairer than she? take her, I pray thee, instead of her. - Samson said concerning them, now shall I be more blameless than the Philistines, though I do them a displeasure; he was set to avenge himself. Judges 15:4-5 - Samson went and caught three hundred foxes by himself, took firebrands, turned the foxes tail to tail, and put a firebrand in the midst between two tails. - When he had set the brands on fire, he let them go into the standing corn of the Philistines and burnt up both the shocks and the standing corn, with the vineyards and olives; their food source and their wine source, all of it, because they crossed him. Judges 15:6 - The Philistines asked who had done this, and were told, Samson, the son in law of the Timnite, because he had taken his wife and given her to his companion. - The Philistines came up and burnt her and her father with fire; the very thing she betrayed her husband to escape came upon her from her own people. Judges 15:7-8 - Samson said unto them, though ye have done this, yet will I be avenged of you, and after that I will cease; he would get the last word. - He smote them hip and thigh with a great slaughter, dropping them like flies, and went down and dwelt in the top of the rock Etam. Judges 15:9-13 - The Philistines went up and pitched in Judah and spread themselves in Lehi, and the men of Judah asked, why are ye come up against us? We are already under tribute; what is the problem? They answered, to bind Samson are we come up, to do to him as he hath done to us. Samson was not even of Judah; he was a Danite. - Three thousand men of Judah went to the top of the rock Etam and said to Samson, knowest thou not that the Philistines are rulers over us? what is this that thou hast done unto us? Instead of standing with their brother, the whole tribe came to hand him over to the oppressor. - He answered, as they did unto me, so have I done unto them. He let them bind him, only making them swear that they would not fall upon him themselves, and they bound him with two new cords and brought him up from the rock. Judges 15:14-15 - When he came unto Lehi, the Philistines shouted against him, and the spirit of the Lord came mightily upon him: the cords that were upon his arms became as flax that was burnt with fire, and his bands loosed from off his hands. - He found a new jawbone of an ass, put forth his hand and took it, and slew a thousand men therewith. This is not normal; you have not seen this in any comic book. One man against a thousand, and all he had was the jawbone of a donkey, and he laid all of them down. - This is the superpower class of Israel's history, like walking with the giants; Israel really was nothing to play with when the Most High was dealing with us, and the nations knew it. Judges 15:16-17 - Samson said, with the jawbone of an ass, heaps upon heaps, with the jaw of an ass have I slain a thousand men. - When he had made an end of speaking, he cast away the jawbone out of his hand and called that place Ramath-lehi. Judges 15:18-19 - He was sore athirst and called on the Lord: thou hast given this great deliverance into the hand of thy servant, and now shall I die for thirst, and fall into the hand of the uncircumcised? You kill a thousand men with a jawbone, you are going to be parched. - God clave an hollow place that was in the jaw, and there came water thereout; and when he had drunk, his spirit came again, and he revived. It is the same as after a fast, when the first food and drink make you feel like a whole new person. - He called the name of that place En-hakkore, which is in Lehi unto this day. Precepts: - Acts 9:19 Paul went days without eating, and when he had received meat, he was strengthened; food and drink after the trial revive the servant of the Most High. Judges 15:20 - Samson judged Israel in the days of the Philistines twenty years; he ended up a leadership figure, a judge over Israel. Judges 16: Samson and Delilah Read the chapter → Judges 16 Judges 16:1-3 - Samson went to Gaza, the chief city of the Philistines, and saw there an harlot and went in unto her; once again the whoremongering spirit had hold of this brother. - It was told the Gazites that Samson was come, and they compassed him in and laid wait for him all night in the gate of the city, quiet all the night, saying, in the morning, when it is day, we shall kill him. - Samson lay till midnight, arose at midnight, and took the doors of the gate of the city and the two posts, and went away with them, bar and all, upon his shoulders, and carried them up to the top of an hill that is before Hebron. They wanted to wait at the gate for him, so he took the gates. Judges 16:4-5 - Afterward he loved a woman in the valley of Sorek whose name was Delilah; she was seductive and promiscuous, and Samson started leaning on this other heathen woman. - The lords of the Philistines came up unto her and said, entice him, and see wherein his great strength lieth, and by what means we may prevail against him, that we may bind him to afflict him; and we will give thee every one of us eleven hundred pieces of silver. - They knew what it took to get to Samson, just as the serpent knew what it took to get to Adam. The scheme never changed: when the devil wants to attack a strong Israelite man, he uses the woman. Judges 16:6-9 - Delilah asked Samson outright, tell me, I pray thee, wherein thy great strength lieth, and wherewith thou mightest be bound to afflict thee. She was literally asking him for the formula to get him killed. - He told her, if they bind me with seven green withs that were never dried, then shall I be weak and be as another man. The lords of the Philistines brought them up, she bound him, with liers in wait abiding in the chamber, and said, the Philistines be upon thee, Samson. - He brake the withs as a thread of tow is broken when it toucheth the fire, so his strength was not known. A man of war should have recognized right there that this was a setup, and cut her off, but he stayed. Judges 16:10-12 - Delilah pressed again: thou hast mocked me and told me lies, now tell me, I pray thee, wherewith thou mightest be bound. Think how backwards that is: she was openly complaining that he would not hand her the way to bind him. His instinct should have been to get away from her, but he stayed. - He said, if they bind me fast with new ropes that never were occupied, then shall I be weak; but he was playing with her, for he had already burst through new cords in chapter 15. - Delilah took new ropes and bound him, with liers in wait in the chamber, and said, the Philistines be upon thee, Samson; and he brake them from off his arms like a thread. Judges 16:13-14 - She pressed the third time, and he told her, if thou weavest the seven locks of my head with the web. She fastened it with the pin and said, the Philistines be upon thee, Samson; he awaked out of his sleep and went away with the pin of the beam and with the web. - Three times she had attempted to have his life taken, and he was still dealing with this harlot; it made no sense, but that is the strength of this snare. Judges 16:15-17 - She said, how canst thou say, I love thee, when thine heart is not with me? and she pressed him daily with her words and urged him, so that his soul was vexed unto death. Day after day she would not let up. - He told her all his heart, and that is where he messed up: there hath not come a razor upon mine head, for I have been a Nazarite unto God from my mother's womb; if I be shaven, then my strength will go from me, and I shall become weak and be like any other man. - This is a scriptural example of why a man cannot tell his wife every single thing in his heart. We do not go by the philosophies of men that say your wife is your best friend you tell everything to; we do what the Bible says. Precepts: - Micah 7:5 Trust ye not in a friend, put ye not confidence in a guide: keep the doors of thy mouth from her that lieth in thy bosom; you cannot share everything on your mind even with the woman you lie down with. Judges 16:18-20 - When Delilah saw that he had told her all his heart, she knew she had him, and sent and called for the lords of the Philistines, and they came up and brought the money in their hand. - She made him sleep upon her knees, and she called for a man and caused him to shave off the seven locks of his head, and she began to afflict him, and his strength went from him. - She said, the Philistines be upon thee, Samson; and he awoke out of his sleep and said, I will go out as at other times before, and shake myself. And he wist not that the Lord was departed from him. He thought he was going into beast mode like before, but it was over, because he had broken his vow; the hair was shaved from off his head. Judges 16:21-22 - The Philistines took him and put out his eyes, brought him down to Gaza, bound him with fetters of brass, and he did grind in the prison house: a blind slave, put on display like an exhibit, the man that had been slaying them now unable even to see. - Howbeit the hair of his head began to grow again after he was shaven; they did not keep it cut. Judges 16:23-25 - The lords of the Philistines gathered together to offer a great sacrifice unto Dagon their god, an idolatrous ritual, and to rejoice, for they said, our god hath delivered Samson our enemy into our hand. - They gave the praise and the glory to their idol, a devil that had not done a thing. Really it was Samson's own transgression that caused the Most High to allow the Philistines to bind and afflict him; that praise to a fake god did not please the Most High. - When their hearts were merry, they said, call for Samson, that he may make us sport; and they called for him out of the prison house and set him between the pillars, using the Israelite man for entertainment and mockery while they honoured their idol. Judges 16:26-27 - Samson said unto the lad that held him by the hand, suffer me that I may feel the pillars whereupon the house standeth, that I may lean upon them: the two main pillars that bore up the whole building, one at his right hand and one at his left. - Now the house was full of men and women, all the lords of the Philistines were there, and there were upon the roof about three thousand men and women that beheld while Samson made sport. Judges 16:28-30 - Samson called unto the Lord and said, O Lord God, remember me, I pray thee, and strengthen me, I pray thee, only this once, O God, that I may be at once avenged of the Philistines for my two eyes. - He took hold of the two middle pillars upon which the house stood, of the one with his right hand and of the other with his left, and said, let me die with the Philistines; and he bowed himself with all his might, and the house fell upon the lords and upon all the people that were therein. - So the dead which he slew at his death were more than they which he slew in his life. Remember Judges 14:4: the Lord sought an occasion against the Philistines, and even with Samson's failings and flaws the Most High used him as a vessel of vengeance on the heathen who oppressed his people and gave the glory of their victory to a fake god. - Israel's salvation in scripture is always joined with the destruction of the enemy. The avenging of what has been done to Israel does not come by striving for equality; the righteous justice and judgment is the destruction the Most High brings on the oppressor. Precepts: - Wisdom of Solomon 18:7 Of the Most High's people is accepted both the salvation of the righteous and the destruction of the enemies; the two always go together. Judges 16:31 - His brethren and all the house of his father came down and took him, and brought him up and buried him between Zorah and Eshtaol in the buryingplace of Manoah his father. And he judged Israel twenty years. --- Topics: Clean and Unclean Meats · Idolatry · Sacrifice and Atonement · The Sabbath ← Judges 9-12 · Judges Study · Judges 17-20 →

title: Judges 17: Micah's House of Idols and the Hired Levite
text: ← Judges 13-16 · Judges Study · Judges 21 → Judges 17: Micah's House of Idols and the Hired Levite Read the chapter → Judges 17 Introduction This session covers Judges 17 through 20, some of the wildest history in the book: Micah of mount Ephraim and his house of idols, the Levite he hired to be his personal priest, the Danites stealing Micah's gods and conquering Laish, the Levite's concubine and the sons of Belial at Gibeah, and the war of all Israel against Benjamin. The thread that ties these chapters together is stated four times: in those days there was no king in Israel, and every man did that which was right in his own eyes. Israel came out of the wilderness with the commandments, but without a leadership structure they were sheep without a shepherd, and the nation ran wild in all manner of wickedness, primarily idolatry. Judges 17:1-4 - A man of mount Ephraim named Micah stole eleven hundred shekels of silver from his own mother, and when he heard her cursing about the missing silver he confessed, I took it, and restored it to her. - Instead of rebuking her son, his mother said blessed be thou of the LORD, and told him she had wholly dedicated the silver for him to make a graven image and a molten image. She refused to keep what he returned, took two hundred shekels to the founder, and had idols made to set up in her son's house. - A mother buying her son idols was nothing new in Israel; there were mothers who steered a son down the wrong path. Precepts: - 2 Chronicles 22:3 Later in history king Ahaziah walked in the ways of the house of Ahab, for his mother was his counsellor to do wickedly; the same pattern seen with Micah's mother. Judges 17:5 - Micah had a whole house of gods. He made an ephod and teraphim and consecrated one of his own sons to be his priest, a counterfeit priesthood serving counterfeit gods. Judges 17:6 - This verse is the key to understanding the whole book of Judges. With no king and no government, Israel was sheep without a shepherd, and when you see how the people carry on in these chapters, that is why: every man did that which was right in his own eyes. - The same individual spirit is around today in those who say join no camp and let no man teach you. Every time the scripture shows Israel without a leadership structure, all manner of wickedness follows, primarily idolatry. Judges 17:7-10 - A young Levite of Bethlehemjudah departed to sojourn wherever he could find a place and came to mount Ephraim to the house of Micah. - When Micah learned the man was a Levite, of the tribe known for the priesthood and the knowledge of the sacrifices, he offered him a deal: dwell with me, be unto me a father and a priest, ten shekels of silver by the year, a suit of apparel, and thy victuals. He hired himself a personal priest for his idols. Judges 17:11-13 - The Levite was content to dwell with him and became as one of his sons. Nothing says the Levite was already in idolatry, but when money was offered he went right along with it; being corrupted for reward was always the Levites' weakness. - Then Micah said, now know I that the LORD will do me good, seeing I have a Levite to my priest. A house full of idols and a hired priest over them, yet he expected the Most High to bless him because a Levite was on the payroll. That is how sick in the mind Israel was without leadership. Judges 18: Dan Steals Micah's Gods and Takes Laish Read the chapter → Judges 18 Judges 18:1-2 - Again the scripture reiterates there was no king in Israel. In those days the tribe of the Danites was still seeking an inheritance to dwell in, because unto that day all their inheritance had not fallen unto them among the tribes; they had conquered in Joshua's day but never attained all their land. - The children of Dan sent five men of valour from Zorah and Eshtaol to spy out land to conquer, and on their way they came to mount Ephraim and lodged at the house of Micah. Precepts: - Joshua 19:47 The coast of the children of Dan went out too little for them, so Dan went up to fight against Leshem and took it; this campaign against Laish is that history. Judges 18:3-6 - By the house of Micah they knew the voice of the young man the Levite, and they turned in and questioned him: who brought thee hither? what makest thou in this place? A Levite serving in a house of idols raised questions. - He told them plainly, Micah hired me and I am his priest. They asked him to ask counsel of God whether their way would be prosperous, and the priest answered, go in peace: before the LORD is your way wherein ye go. Judges 18:7-10 - The five men came to Laish and saw the people that were therein, how they dwelt careless, quiet and secure, after the manner of the Zidonians, the nearby nation whose lifestyle they copied. They were a chill people with no worries, not even watching for anyone to come in and conquer them. - A magistrate is a judge: there was no judicial system in that land to put a man to shame or convict him for a crime. They were also far from the Zidonians, too far for Zidon to interfere, and had no business with any man, no allies. The spies peeped all of it. - Their report back at Zorah and Eshtaol: arise, that we may go up against them, for we have seen the land, and behold, it is very good; a place where there is no want of any thing that is in the earth, and God hath given it into your hands. Do not sit still; let us move now. Judges 18:11-14 - Six hundred men of the family of the Danites appointed with weapons of war went up from Zorah and Eshtaol, camped at Mahanehdan behind Kirjathjearim, and passed again unto mount Ephraim to the house of Micah. - The first time Micah let the five spies lodge in his house, they saw his expensive looking gods and got covetous. Now passing back through they tell their brethren, do ye know that there is in these houses an ephod, and teraphim, and a graven image, and a molten image? now therefore consider what ye have to do. On the way to the lick they spotted another lick. - The Bible addresses everything: do not bring just anybody into your house, even brethren, because the deceitful man has many tricks and approaches to finesse you out of the goods in your house. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 11:29 Micah brought every man into his house and lost everything in it; the deceitful man has many trains, many tricks and approaches. Judges 18:15-20 - They turned in to the house and saluted the Levite, a friendly greeting at the door; that is one of the deceitful man's many trains. While the six hundred armed men stood by the entering of the gate keeping the priest occupied, the five spies went up inside and took the graven image, the ephod, the teraphim, and the molten image. - When the priest saw them coming out with the gods and asked, what do ye? they told him hold thy peace, lay thine hand upon thy mouth: is it better for thee to be a priest unto the house of one man, or unto a tribe and a family in Israel? Do not snitch; roll with us and be the man over a whole tribe. - The priest's heart was glad, and he took the ephod, the teraphim, and the graven image and went in the midst of the people. His covetous spirit was plain: already sold out to serve idols for Micah's silver, he dropped the man who treated him as a son the moment a bigger position was offered. Disloyal through and through. Judges 18:21-26 - When Micah and the men near his house gathered and overtook the children of Dan, Dan asked, what aileth thee, that thou comest with such a company? He answered, ye have taken away my gods which I made, and the priest, and ye are gone away: and what have I more? - Examine how foolish that sounds: my gods which I made. How can a man make his own god? That is how simple we had become without leadership. - Dan's answer: let not thy voice be heard among us, lest angry fellows run upon thee, and thou lose thy life, with the lives of thy household. In plain terms, hush, because you are going to anger some of these brothers, they will run up on you, and you and your folks will not make it home. Micah saw they were too strong for him and turned back to his house. Dan was a problem. Judges 18:27-29 - The Danites took the things which Micah had made and the priest which he had, came unto Laish, unto a people quiet and secure, smote them with the edge of the sword, and burnt the city with fire. - There was no deliverer, because Laish was far from Zidon and had no business with any man, exactly what the spies had scoped out; no neighbor and no ally came to save them. - They built the city again, dwelt therein, and called the name of it Dan, after Dan their father which was born unto Israel; howbeit the name of the city was Laish at the first. Judges 18:30-31 - The first thing the children of Dan did in the land the Most High allowed them to take was set up the graven image, a god made by the hands of a man they had just robbed. Jonathan the son of Gershom, the son of Manasseh, he and his sons were priests to the tribe of Dan until the day of the captivity of the land, and they kept Micah's graven image all the time the house of God was in Shiloh. - Dan stayed heavy in idolatry all the way through history and never changed. After the kingdom split, Jeroboam feared that if the people kept going up to sacrifice at the house of the LORD in Jerusalem, their heart would turn again unto Rehoboam king of Judah and they would kill him; so he took counsel and made two calves of gold with his own hands, doubling the iniquity of the wilderness, and said, behold thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt. Precepts: - 1 Kings 12:27 Jeroboam's fear: if this people go up to sacrifice at Jerusalem, their heart shall turn again unto their lord Rehoboam, and they shall kill me. - 1 Kings 12:28-30 He made two calves of gold and set one in Bethel, and the other put he in Dan; and this thing became a sin, for the people went to worship before the one, even unto Dan. - Hear the word against Dan by the prophet: they that swear by the sin of Samaria and say, thy god, O Dan, liveth, shall fall and never rise up again. Mind you, it is an idol made with hands, yet they called it living. That is why Dan has no gate among the sealed tribes in Revelation 7; Dan was discontinued as a tribe of itself and intertwined with Benjamin for the most part. Precepts: - Amos 8:14 They that swear by the sin of Samaria, and say, Thy god, O Dan, liveth, shall fall, and never rise up again; the judgment on Dan's idolatry. - Revelation 7:5-8 When the tribes are sealed, Dan is not named among them; the tribe that set up the graven image never rose up again. Judges 19: The Levite's Concubine at Gibeah Read the chapter → Judges 19 Judges 19:1-2 - Once more, there was no king in Israel, no leadership structure, still sheep without a shepherd. A certain Levite sojourning on the side of mount Ephraim took to him a concubine out of Bethlehemjudah; a concubine was a woman dealt with on the level of a servant. - His concubine played the whore against him, laid with another man, then went away from him unto her father's house to Bethlehemjudah and was there four whole months. Judges 19:3 - Instead of letting her go, her husband arose and went after her to speak friendly unto her and to bring her again, with his servant and a couple of asses, and the damsel's father rejoiced to meet him. - By the law, a woman who is put away and becomes another man's is defiled to her former husband, and taking her back defiles the land. The Most High does not permit it, but with no king in the land and no enforcement of the law, this is what men did. Precepts: - Jeremiah 3:1 If a man put away his wife and she become another man's, shall he return unto her again? shall not that land be greatly polluted? - Deuteronomy 24:4 Her former husband may not take her again to be his wife after she is defiled, for that is abomination and causes the land to sin. Judges 19:4-9 - The damsel's father retained him: eat, drink, lodge, three days, then a fourth, then a fifth. Like an old man who never has anybody to talk to, he kept finding a reason not to let the Levite go, and a one night plan stretched into five days. - The father's words on the fifth day cut a popular doctrine. They tarried until afternoon, and he said, behold, the day draweth toward evening, and then, behold, the day groweth to an end. According to the Bible the day ends at evening; and if it ends at evening it begins at evening, so a day runs from evening to evening, including the sabbath. That buries the sunrise to sunrise doctrine, which has no works and no fruits to show it was ever right. Judges 19:10-13 - The man would not tarry that night; five days was enough and he had business to tend to. He rose up, departed, and came over against Jebus, which is Jerusalem, with two saddled asses and his concubine. - Jerusalem is called Jebus here because the Jebusites, the original inhabitants of Jerusalem, still dwelt in it; this is before David rose up and took it from them. When Israel came out of the wilderness, the promised land was inhabited primarily by Canaanites, and the children of Judah could not drive the Jebusites out. Precepts: - Joshua 15:63 As for the Jebusites, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the children of Judah could not drive them out, and the Jebusites dwelt with the children of Judah at Jerusalem unto this day. - 2 Samuel 5:6-7 Not until king David went up against the Jebusites was the strong hold of Zion taken; that is when Jebus became the city of David. - When the servant suggested turning in to lodge in this city of the Jebusites, his master refused: we will not turn aside hither into the city of a stranger, that is not of the children of Israel; we will pass over to Gibeah. Even in those wild days he would not lodge with heathens, only with his brothers. Judges 19:14-21 - The sun went down upon them by Gibeah, which belongeth to Benjamin, and when they went in and sat down in a street of the city, no man took them into his house to lodge. The Benjamites were not so friendly. - An old man from his work out of the field at even, a man of mount Ephraim sojourning in Gibeah, lifted up his eyes and questioned the wayfaring man: whither goest thou? and whence comest thou? The Levite explained he was passing toward the house of the LORD with straw, provender, bread, and wine of his own, lacking nothing, yet no man would receive him to house. - The old man said, peace be with thee; howsoever let all thy wants lie upon me; only lodge not in the street. He knew the manner of the men of that city and what the streets of Gibeah held at night. He brought them into his house, and they washed their feet and did eat and drink. Judges 19:22-24 - As they were making their hearts merry, certain sons of Belial, meaning children of the devil, demon seed, beset the house round about and beat at the door in the middle of the night, saying to the master of the house, bring forth the man that came into thine house, that we may know him. - To know in this context is sexual intercourse; the men of Gibeah were howling for the man himself. This is a rerun of a very familiar story of old, the men of Sodom at Lot's door, and the scripture names exactly what vile thing they were after. Precepts: - Genesis 19:4-5 The men of Sodom, old and young, all the people from every quarter, compassed Lot's house and said, bring them out unto us, that we may know them; the same words beaten at the door in Gibeah. - Genesis 19:7-8 Lot answered, do not so wickedly: behold now, I have two daughters which have not known man; to know means no man had lain with them, so the knowing the men of Sodom sought was sexual. - Genesis 19:9 They said, this one fellow came in to sojourn, and he will needs be a judge, and they pressed sore upon Lot and came near to break the door; sojourners in both cities were pressed the same way. - Romans 1:26-27 The vile thing named: God gave them up unto vile affections, the men leaving the natural use of the woman and burning in their lust one toward another, men with men working that which is unseemly. That is what Gibeah had on its mind. - The master of the house went out and pleaded, nay, my brethren, do not so wickedly; seeing this man is come into mine house, do not this folly. Like Lot he offered his maiden daughter and the concubine, humble ye them, but unto this man do not so vile a thing. All the tribes have some jacked up history somewhere down the line; this night is Benjamin's. Judges 19:25-28 - The men would not hearken, so the man brought his concubine forth unto them; and they knew her, and abused her all the night until the morning. They is plural: this was a gang rape, forced, nothing voluntary about it, done in the anger of men who could not get the man they wanted. - When the day began to spring they let her go, and the woman came in the dawning of the day and fell down at the door of the man's house where her lord was, her hands upon the threshold. In the morning he said, up, and let us be going; but none answered. There was no more spirit left in her; she was dead. He laid her upon an ass and got him unto his place. - What we witnessed is rape, and the scripture is plain that rape is a sin worthy of death; marriage is the only honorable bed. Men out here calling themselves Israelites and teaching otherwise give Israelites a bad name; we preach the laws of the Most High. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 22:25 If a man force a betrothed damsel in the field and lie with her, the man only that lay with her shall die; forced means against her will, and the Most High made it punishable by death. - Deuteronomy 22:26 Unto the damsel thou shalt do nothing, for as when a man riseth against his neighbour and slayeth him, even so is this matter; the Most High counts rape the equivalent of murder, and in this gang rape the victim was literally murdered. - Hebrews 13:4 Marriage is honourable in all, and the bed undefiled: but whoremongers and adulterers God will judge; there is no permission for rape anywhere in the word. Judges 19:29-30 - When he was come into his house he took a knife, laid hold on his concubine, and divided her, together with her bones, into twelve pieces, and sent her into all the coasts of Israel, to make the twelve tribes aware of what was done in Gibeah. - All that saw it said, there was no such deed done nor seen from the day that the children of Israel came up out of the land of Egypt unto this day: consider of it, take advice, and speak your minds. The nation had never seen a matter like this, and it called the whole congregation to counsel. Judges 20: Israel's War Against Benjamin Read the chapter → Judges 20 Judges 20:1-2 - All the children of Israel went out, and the congregation was gathered together as one man, from Dan even to Beersheba, with the land of Gilead, unto the LORD in Mizpeh: four hundred thousand footmen that drew sword. - Israel got ready for war behind one woman, one victim. There is no hatred of women in this truth; wicked women are rebuked, which is itself love, and here a crime against one sister moved the whole nation to arms. Judges 20:3-7 - The children of Benjamin heard that Israel was gone up to Mizpeh. The Levite, the husband of the woman that was slain, testified: I came into Gibeah that belongeth to Benjamin, and the men of Gibeah rose against me and beset the house round about upon me by night, and thought to have slain me; and my concubine have they forced, that she is dead. Forced is the Bible's word for rape. - He said they have committed lewdness and folly in Israel. Nowhere in the Bible can rape be called lawful; it is lewdness and folly, and whether the victim lives or dies the matter is counted as murder. Be very mindful of sick, perverted camps that teach otherwise. Judges 20:8-11 - All the people arose as one man, saying, we will not any of us go to his tent, neither will we any of us turn into his house; none of us are going home until this is answered. - They set an order for war, ten men of an hundred throughout all the tribes to fetch victual for the people, and all the men of Israel were gathered against the city, knit together as one man. Even wicked and without a king, Israel had some morals left; gang rape was intolerable. Judges 20:12-14 - The tribes of Israel sent men through all the tribe of Benjamin, saying, what wickedness is this that is done among you? Now deliver us the men, the children of Belial which are in Gibeah, that we may put them to death and put away evil from Israel; everything those men had going on was worthy of death. - But the children of Benjamin would not hearken to the voice of their brethren; instead they gathered themselves together out of the cities unto Gibeah to go out to battle against the children of Israel, riding for their own no matter the crime. Judges 20:15-17 - Benjamin numbered twenty and six thousand men that drew sword out of the cities, beside the inhabitants of Gibeah, seven hundred chosen men. Among all this people were seven hundred chosen men lefthanded, every one able to sling stones at an hair breadth and not miss: slinging with the velocity of a firearm and dead accurate. Benjamin was about that action. - The men of Israel beside Benjamin were four hundred thousand men of war that drew sword. Four hundred thousand against twenty and six thousand: you would think a landslide victory. Judges 20:18-21 - The children of Israel arose, went up to the house of God, and asked counsel of God: which of us shall go up first to the battle against the children of Benjamin? And the LORD said, Judah shall go up first. - Israel encamped against Gibeah and put themselves in array, and the children of Benjamin came forth out of Gibeah and destroyed down to the ground of the Israelites that day twenty and two thousand men. Benjamin opened the battle by giving Judah the business. Judges 20:22-25 - The men of Israel encouraged themselves; we cannot go out like that to the men of Gibeah. They set their battle again in array in the same place, went up and wept before the LORD until even, and asked, shall I go up again to battle against the children of Benjamin my brother? And the LORD said, go up against him. - The second day Benjamin came forth out of Gibeah and destroyed down to the ground eighteen thousand more, all men that drew the sword. Fresh legs came in against them and Benjamin still had the endurance and stamina to whip them. Judges 20:26-28 - Then all the children of Israel and all the people went up unto the house of God, wept, sat there before the LORD, fasted that day until even, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the LORD. This time the whole nation humbled itself. - The ark of the covenant of God was there in those days, and Phinehas the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron, stood before it. They asked, shall I yet again go out to battle against the children of Benjamin my brother, or shall I cease? And the LORD said, go up; for to morrow I will deliver them into thine hand: a direct promise of victory on the morrow. Judges 20:29-36 - Now Israel set liers in wait round about Gibeah. No more going head up against lefthanded slingers you cannot beat straight on; now there was a strategy, an ambush. - Part of Israel put themselves in array as at other times, and Benjamin was drawn away from the city, beginning to smite and kill about thirty men and saying, they are smitten down before us as at the first. Little did they know they were falling into the plan; Israel fled on purpose and drew them from the city onto the highways. - The liers in wait came forth out of their places, even out of the meadows of Gibeah, ten thousand chosen men out of all Israel, and the LORD smote Benjamin before Israel: the children of Israel destroyed of the Benjamites that day twenty and five thousand and an hundred men. The victory belonged to the Most High, as he had promised. Judges 20:37-46 - There was an appointed sign between the men of Israel and the liers in wait, that they should make a great flame with smoke rise up out of the city. That was the purpose of drawing the Benjamites out: while Benjamin smote about thirty men and thought they were winning as in the first battles, the liers in wait hasted, rushed upon Gibeah, smote all the city with the edge of the sword, and set the sign. - When the flame began to arise out of the city with a pillar of smoke, the Benjamites looked behind them, and behold, the flame of the city ascended up to heaven; and the men of Benjamin were amazed, for they saw that evil was come upon them. In that moment they knew it was over. - They turned their backs before the men of Israel unto the way of the wilderness, toward the rock of Rimmon, but the battle overtook them: eighteen thousand men of valour fell, five thousand were gleaned in the highways, and two thousand slain at Gidom, twenty and five thousand in all, including all those mighty lefthanded men of valour. Judges 20:47-48 - Six hundred men turned and fled to the wilderness unto the rock Rimmon and abode there four months; only that remnant kept the tribe from being utterly destroyed. The men of Israel turned again upon the children of Benjamin and smote them with the edge of the sword, men of every city, and beast, and all that came to hand, and set on fire all the cities they came to. - Benjamin was judged big time; the Most High pushed the reset button on the tribe for the sodomite and rape activity that came out of Gibeah. Chapter 21 shows the drastic measures that had to be taken so Benjamin could continue producing as a tribe. - That judgment is why Saul, in the days of the first king, calls himself a Benjamite of the smallest of the tribes of Israel; this war is what minimized the tribe. There have been mighty and righteous Benjamites since, Paul chief among them, but it is written, and we learn the history as it is written. Precepts: - 1 Samuel 9:21 Saul answered, am not I a Benjamite, of the smallest of the tribes of Israel? Benjamin was the smallest because of the judgment poured out in this war. --- Topics: Idolatry · Sacrifice and Atonement · The Covenant · The Feasts of the Most High · The Priesthood · The Sabbath ← Judges 13-16 · Judges Study · Judges 21 →

title: Judges 21: The Oath at Mizpeh and Wives for Benjamin
text: ← Judges 17-20 · Judges Study · Ruth 1-3 → Judges 21: The Oath at Mizpeh and Wives for Benjamin Read the chapter → Judges 21 Introduction This session covers Judges 21 together with Ruth chapters 1 through 3; these notes cover Judges 21, the closing chapter of the book. After the war against Benjamin in the previous chapters, Israel weeps that a whole tribe is nearly cut off, but the men of Israel had sworn at Mizpeh not to give their daughters to Benjamin to wife, and an oath sworn to the Most High had to be performed. The chapter shows how Israel provided wives for the remnant of Benjamin, first from Jabeshgilead and then from the daughters of Shiloh, and it closes the book on the key of the whole era: in those days there was no king in Israel, and every man did that which was right in his own eyes. Judges 21:1-6 - The men of Israel had sworn at Mizpeh that not one of them would give his daughter unto Benjamin to wife. This follows the previous chapter, where the tribes went to war against Benjamin. - The people came to the house of God and sat there till evening before God, lifted up their voices and wept sore, asking why it had come to pass that there should be one tribe lacking in Israel. The next day they rose early, built an altar, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. - The children of Israel repented them for Benjamin their brother, for there was one tribe cut off from Israel that day. They had also made a great oath that whoever came not up to the Lord at Mizpeh would surely be put to death. Judges 21:7 - The question of the chapter: how shall we do for wives for them that remain, seeing we have sworn by the Lord not to give them our daughters? They made a vow, they swore to the Lord, and the law says a sworn oath must be performed; that is why they could not simply turn around and give their daughters. Precepts: - Numbers 30:1-2 If a man vow a vow unto the Lord or swear an oath, he shall not break his word; he shall do according to all that proceedeth out of his mouth. This is the law Israel was bound by when they swore concerning their daughters. Judges 21:8-12 - They searched which tribe came not up to Mizpeh, and behold, none had come from Jabeshgilead to the assembly. So under the great oath the congregation sent twelve thousand of the valiantest men to smite Jabeshgilead with the edge of the sword, destroying every male and every woman that had lain by man. - Among the inhabitants of Jabeshgilead they found four hundred young virgins that had not known man by lying with any male, and brought them to the camp at Shiloh in the land of Canaan. - Verse 12 is the precept for what it means in scripture to know somebody: to lie with them, meaning to have sex with them. Judges 21:13-18 - The whole congregation sent to speak peaceably to the children of Benjamin at the rock Rimmon, and Benjamin came again. They gave them the wives saved alive of the women of Jabeshgilead, but they sufficed not; there were not enough for all the men that remained. - The people repented them for Benjamin because the Lord had made a breach in the tribes of Israel, and the elders said there must be an inheritance for them that be escaped of Benjamin, that a tribe be not destroyed out of Israel. - Verse 18 restates why they could not just give their own daughters: the children of Israel had sworn, saying, Cursed be he that giveth a wife to Benjamin. That is the same oath read in verse 7. Judges 21:19-23 - The solution: there was a yearly feast of the Lord in Shiloh, so they commanded the children of Benjamin to lie in wait in the vineyards, and when the daughters of Shiloh came out to dance in the dances, every man was to catch him a wife of the daughters of Shiloh and go to the land of Benjamin. - When the fathers or brethren came to complain, the elders would answer, Be favourable unto them for our sakes; because the fathers did not give their daughters, they would not be guilty of breaking the oath. - The children of Benjamin did so and took wives according to their number of them that danced, then returned to their inheritance, repaired the cities, and dwelt in them. Judges 21:24-25 - The children of Israel departed thence at that time, every man to his tribe, to his family, and to his inheritance. - In those days there was no king in Israel; every man did that which was right in his own eyes. We see that same thing today: most of our people are still in that state, doing what is right in their own eyes. There is nothing new under the sun. --- Topics: Sacrifice and Atonement · The Feasts of the Most High ← Judges 17-20 · Judges Study · Ruth 1-3 →

title: Judges 5: The Song of Deborah and Barak: A Willing People
text: ← Judges 1-4 · Judges Study · Judges 9-12 → Judges 5: The Song of Deborah and Barak: A Willing People Read the chapter → Judges 5 Introduction This session covers Judges 5 through 8: the song of Deborah and Barak after the victory over Sisera, the call of Gideon while Israel is wasted under Midian, the three hundred men by whom the Lord saves Israel, and Israel's return to Baal worship as soon as Gideon is dead. The class opens under the order of 1 Corinthians 14:34-35, that the women keep silence in the assembly, for it is not permitted unto them to speak, but they are commanded to be under obedience, as also saith the law. The running thread is that everything Israel does for the Most High must come from a willing heart, and that the victory of battle stands not in the multitude of an host, but strength comes from heaven. Judges 5:1-2 - Deborah and Barak sing praise to the Lord for the avenging of Israel, when the people willingly offered themselves. That is what the Most High wants from us: a willing heart in all that we do, in the keeping of the commandments, in the keeping of the feast days, and in the praise of him. Precepts: - Exodus 35:22 At the building of the tabernacle in the wilderness, both men and women as many as were willing hearted brought their gold unto the Lord; we have to have that same willing heart today. - How do we willingly offer ourselves to the Lord in the twenty-first century? By giving up whatever presents itself as an obstacle between us and the Lord. It may be father, mother, husband, wife, or children; it may be drugs, money, or working on the sabbath. If you willingly offer yourself, you will not let any stumbling block keep you from the Lord. Precepts: - Matthew 10:34-39 Christ came not to send peace but a sword, to set a man at variance against his own household; he that loveth father or mother more than him is not worthy of him, and he that loseth his life for his sake shall find it. - Galatians 6:5 Taking up your cross does not mean buying a cross from the pawn shop to wear around your neck; every man shall bear his own burden, enduring his own tests in this truth with prayer and fasting. Judges 5:3-5 - The Lord marching out of the field of Edom, the earth trembling, the heavens dropping, and the mountains melting from before the Lord God of Israel is future prophecy; this has not happened yet. Precepts: - Isaiah 63:1-4 The one who cometh from Edom with dyed garments, treading the winepress alone in the day of vengeance, is the same picture the song is singing of. Judges 5:6-9 - This passage is for all the closet feminists who think Deborah justifies women leading men. She did not lead men into any kind of war; she did not put on body armor and a breastplate, rise up on a horse, and lead the charge. She was the motivating factor to men that were shaky and fearful during that time, a mother in Israel, a guiding light. - Verse 9 proves it: my heart is toward the governors of Israel, the leaders who offered themselves willingly among the people. Her heart was with the men who led; she was not ruling over them. Precepts: - Numbers 27:15-17 Moses asked the Lord to set a man over the congregation, a man to go out before them and bring them in, that the congregation of the Lord be not as sheep which have no shepherd. - Numbers 27:18 The Lord answered in total agreement with what Moses spoke: take thee Joshua the son of Nun, a man in whom is the spirit; the Lord set a man over the congregation. - 1 Timothy 2:11-12 The order did not change in the New Testament: the woman is to learn in silence with all subjection, not to teach nor to usurp authority over the man. Judges 5:10-11 - They that are delivered from the noise of archers in the places of drawing water shall rehearse the righteous acts of the Lord. That is where we are right now: in the places of drawing water, rehearsing the righteous acts of the Most High while the arrows are still being shot. Precepts: - Baruch 3:8 We are yet this day in our captivity, subject unto payments for the iniquities of our fathers; we have to obey the laws of the land under the hand of our oppressor, endure, and exercise faith in the keeping of the commandments until Christ redeems us. Judges 5:12-18 - The song rehearses which tribes came out. Out of Ephraim, Benjamin, Machir, and Zebulun came governors and they that handle the pen of the writer, and the princes of Issachar were with Deborah and Barak in the valley. - For the divisions of Reuben there were great thoughts and great searchings of heart: they were second-guessing themselves. Gilead abode beyond Jordan, Dan remained in ships, and Asher continued on the seashore; the song is getting on the tribes that stayed home. - Zebulun and Naphtali were a people that jeoparded their lives unto the death in the high places of the field; those tribes are warriors. Judges 5:19-23 - The kings of Canaan fought by the waters of Megiddo and took no gain of money; they fought from heaven, and the stars in their courses fought against Sisera. Sisera is the general of the Canaanite host, not Syria; the river Kishon swept them away. - The angel of the Lord said curse ye Meroz, curse ye bitterly the inhabitants thereof, because they came not to the help of the Lord against the mighty. Sitting out the battle of the Lord brings a curse. Judges 5:24-27 - Blessed above women in the tent shall Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite be. Sisera asked water and she gave him milk; then she put her hand to the nail and her right hand to the workman's hammer, and where he bowed, there he fell down dead. Precepts: - Judges 4:18-22 The account itself: Jael covered him with a mantle, gave him milk when he asked water, and when he was fast asleep and weary she smote the nail into his temples and fastened it into the ground; when Barak came, Sisera lay dead with the nail in his temples. Judges 5:28-31 - The mother of Sisera looked out at a window and cried, why is his chariot so long in coming? Her wise ladies answer her with imaginations of victory, that they are dividing the prey and the needlework spoil. She is looking for a son who is never coming home; he lay dead in Jael's tent. - So let all thine enemies perish, O Lord: but let them that love him be as the sun when he goeth forth in his might. And the land had rest forty years. Judges 6: The Call of Gideon: Why Is All This Befallen Us Read the chapter → Judges 6 Judges 6:1-2 - Israel did evil in the sight of the Lord, and the Lord delivered them into the hand of Midian seven years. That is our manner: the Most High delivers us, we get a little bit of freedom, and we go right back to wickedness. The same thing goes on today; we get relaxed, and the Lord has to remind us, putting us right back into hard bondage, that this is not our rest. - Because of the Midianites, the children of Israel made them the dens in the mountains, and caves, and strongholds; Israel hid in the mountains of their own land. Judges 6:3-6 - When Israel had sown, the Midianites, the Amalekites, and the children of the east came up as grasshoppers for multitude, destroyed the increase of the earth, and left no sustenance for Israel, neither sheep, nor ox, nor ass, and Israel was greatly impoverished. That goes right into the curses. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 28:21-22 The Lord shall smite thee with blasting and with mildew; the blasting and the mildew go into famine, exactly what Midian and the children of the east worked on Israel by taking the crops. Judges 6:7-10 - When Israel cried unto the Lord, the Lord sent a prophet to remind them: I brought you up from Egypt out of the house of bondage, and I said, fear not the gods of the Amorites in whose land ye dwell, but ye have not obeyed my voice. The judgment came with a reason attached. Precepts: - Genesis 10:15-16 The Amorites go back into the Hamites: the lineage of the Amorites, the Jebusites, and the Perizzites all comes down from Ham through Canaan. Judges 6:11-12 - An angel of the Lord came and sat under an oak in Ophrah, while Gideon threshed wheat by the winepress to hide it from the Midianites; that is how hard the oppression sat on the land, that a man hid his own harvest to keep it. - The angel greets him: the Lord is with thee, thou mighty man of valour. The Most High already saw the warrior in the man hiding wheat. Precepts: - Hebrews 1:7 The angels are spirits and ministers made of the flame of fire that sits under the throne of heaven; they go and come as they please, change forms, vanish into thin air, and one of them can slay an hundred fourscore and five thousand men in a single night. - Hebrews 13:1-2 Be not forgetful to entertain strangers, for thereby some have entertained angels unawares, just as Tobias in the book of Tobit entertained Raphael and did not know it until the angel revealed himself. Judges 6:13 - Gideon answers, oh my Lord, if the Lord be with us, why then is all this befallen us, and where be all his miracles which our fathers told us of? A lot of us ask that same question today when we watch our people judged in the streets over and over: if we be the chosen people, why does all of this happen to us? Precepts: - Hebrews 12:6-8 Whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth; if ye be without chastisement, then are ye bastards and not sons. That is why the other nations never suffer the judgments we suffer: the chastening of the Most High does not pertain to them, but he chastens us because we are his sons. - Hebrews 12:9-11 No chastening for the present seemeth to be joyous but grievous, and it does look grievous to all of us; nevertheless afterward it yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness, which is the kingdom, eternal life, and everlasting peace for them which are exercised thereby. - Gideon says the Lord hath forsaken us, and that is the same thought our people carry today when you hit the streets teaching. But God has not forsaken us; it is actually we that have forsaken God. Precepts: - Jeremiah 2:31 Have I been a wilderness unto Israel, a land of darkness? The Lord asks, am I not able to be found, am I not right in front of you? Yet my people say, We are lords; we will come no more unto thee. - Jeremiah 2:13 My people have committed two evils: they have forsaken me the fountain of living waters, and hewed them out broken cisterns that can hold no water. The water is the word, and the broken cisterns are the religions we hewed out for ourselves, Christianity, Islam, and now politics, the newest religion our people put their faith in. Judges 6:14-15 - The Lord commissions him: go in this thy might, and thou shalt save Israel from the hand of the Midianites; have not I sent thee? Gideon answers with his pedigree: my family is poor in Manasseh, and I am the least in my father's house. That is a defeated mentality, and we all have to overcome it, because every one of us was called for a reason, to put a brick in for the kingdom. Precepts: - 1 Corinthians 1:26-28 Not many wise men after the flesh, not many mighty, not many noble are called; God hath chosen the foolish, the weak, the base, and the despised things of the world to confound the mighty. - James 2:5 Hath not God chosen the poor of this world, rich in faith, and heirs of the kingdom which he hath promised to them that love him? The Lord calls whom he will; money and status mean nothing to him. - Rich, poor, or middle class, none of it matters to the Most High; what man holds in high esteem, God calls abomination. The highest calling anyone can have on the face of the earth is to teach the word of God and compel the lost sheep of the house of Israel to come in, so do not think less of yourself because your name carries no prestige. Precepts: - Luke 16:15 Ye are they which justify yourselves before men, but that which is highly esteemed among men is abomination in the sight of God; you could be president, a general, the highest grossing rapper, or the leading scorer in the league, and none of it matters to the Lord. - Isaiah 49:5 The servant formed from the womb to bring Jacob again to the Lord is glorious in the eyes of the Lord; gathering Israel back is the highest honor on earth. - 1 Samuel 16:6-7 Samuel looked on Eliab and thought, surely the Lord's anointed is before him, but the Lord said, look not on his countenance or the height of his stature; man looketh on the outward appearance, but the Lord looketh on the heart. You short brothers can be great leaders. Judges 6:16-18 - The Lord promises, surely I will be with thee, and thou shalt smite the Midianites as one man. Gideon asks for a sign that it is really the Lord talking with him; the least in his father's house wanted to be sure he was not talking to himself. Judges 6:19-21 - Gideon brings a kid and unleavened cakes, and the angel touches the flesh and the cakes with the end of his staff; fire rises up out of the rock and consumes them, and the angel departs out of his sight, gone just like that. No lighter fluid existed on the earth; the angel made fire come out of the rock, because the angels are made out of that fire. Precepts: - 1 Corinthians 15:40 There are celestial bodies and bodies terrestrial; our earthly bodies are made of the ground, but the angels have celestial bodies, which is why they can appear, disappear, and stand all around us right now listening and recording without us knowing. - Matthew 18:10 Christ said of the little ones that in heaven their angels do always behold the face of his Father; every one of us that has repented has a guardian angel assigned to minister to us and nudge us in the way the Lord wants our life to go. Judges 6:22-24 - When Gideon perceived he had seen an angel of the Lord face to face, he feared death, but the Lord said, peace be unto thee; fear not: thou shalt not die. Gideon built an altar there and called it Jehovah-shalom, which is, the Lord is peace. Judges 6:25-27 - The same night the Lord tells him to throw down his own father's altar of Baal, cut down the grove by it, and build an altar unto the Lord in its place. Notice this: even before the split of the kingdom, the tribes that would become the northern kingdom were already dabbling with Baal, worshipping the Lord in some fashion while holding onto the idol. Precepts: - 1 Kings 12:28 That is why it was such an easy transition when Jeroboam set up the golden calves and said, behold thy gods, O Israel; the north had been dealing with Baal long before the split ever happened. - Gideon took ten of his servants and did as the Lord said, but by night, because he feared his father's household and the men of the city; they worshipped that idol and would have killed him in the daylight. Judges 6:28-32 - In the morning the men of the city found the altar of Baal cast down, and when they inquired, they said, Gideon the son of Joash hath done this thing. He crept at night, but somebody was peeping out a window; he was doing the right thing and still got told on. - The grove they worshipped was a carved tree stump, cut and shaped to look like a particular god; that is the idol Gideon cut down. - The men demand his death, but Joash stands up for his son: will ye plead for Baal? If he be a god, let him plead for himself, because one hath cast down his altar. Obviously he is no god; he is an idol. So that day Gideon was named Jerubbaal, saying, let Baal plead against him. Judges 6:33-35 - The Midianites, the Amalekites, and the children of the east gathered and pitched in the valley of Jezreel, but the Spirit of the Lord came upon Gideon; he blew a trumpet, and Abiezer, Manasseh, Asher, Zebulun, and Naphtali came up to meet him. - Those tribes are warriors; do not get it twisted. You see how Zebulun and Naphtali, who are in the south Americas right now, get down: that warrior spirit is still in them, only right now it has turned on each other, and the Most High is going to correct it and turn it right again. Judges 6:36-40 - Gideon asks the fleece signs: dew on the fleece only with dry earth beside, and then the reverse, dew on all the ground with the fleece dry. The Lord commands the dew, the condensation that falls through the night, to land exactly where he pleases; God can do whatever he wants, infinite power. Precepts: - Numbers 17:8 The same power made Aaron's rod bud, bloom blossoms, and yield almonds overnight. - 2 Kings 20:11 For Hezekiah he brought the shadow ten degrees backward on the sundial; time itself obeys him. - Matthew 12:39 But do not ask for signs like that anymore; an evil and adulterous generation seeketh after a sign. He gave us all the signs back in the day, he split the Red Sea and we still became rebellious, so the walk we are in now is by faith. Judges 7: The Three Hundred: The Victory Is the Lord's Read the chapter → Judges 7 Judges 7:1-3 - The Lord tells Gideon the people with him are too many for him to give Midian into their hands, lest Israel vaunt themselves against him, saying, mine own hand hath saved me. That is Israel: look at what I did. The Lord knows how we think. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 8:11 Beware that thou forget not the Lord thy God in not keeping his commandments; the warning was given before they ever entered the land. - Deuteronomy 8:14-18 Lest thine heart be lifted up and thou say in thine heart, my power and the might of mine hand hath gotten me this wealth; thou shalt remember the Lord thy God, for it is he that giveth thee power to get wealth. - Whosoever is fearful and afraid, let him return: twenty and two thousand bounced back to Gilead, and ten thousand remained. That is why God always lowered the numbers going into battle, so Israel would know it was by the Lord's strength that we overcame our enemies; and it is going to be the same thing again, few numbers going into battle against the nations when that time comes. Judges 7:4-6 - The people are yet too many; the Lord tries them at the water. Some lapped the water with their hand to their mouth as a dog lappeth, and all the rest bowed down upon their knees to drink; the lappers were three hundred men. - What can we learn from this? You have to be willing to let go of some people.
