The Lord said, of whom I say, this shall not go with thee, the same shall not go: some people are not going to be beneficial to the war ahead of you, and the Lord will move them out of the way, but you have to be ready to let them go. Precepts: - Genesis 12:1 The same word came to Abraham: get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred; there were things the Lord had to do for him that required letting go. - Matthew 10:34-36 Christ came to divide and separate, father, mother, husband, wife, family; let that ring in your mind, you have to be willing to let go of some people for the battle ahead. Judges 7:7-8 - By the three hundred men that lapped will I save you, and deliver the Midianites into thine hand. The Lord sent the rest of Israel every man unto his tent and retained the three hundred, with victuals and trumpets in their hands. - Now you know where the famous story of the three hundred came from: they got it from our ancestors, from Gideon. The nations take our history and make it entertainment, and even the artwork drew those three hundred with locks and braids and gave the other host the same, because the artist knew whose history he was drawing; those three hundred were Israelites. Judges 7:9-15 - The same night the Lord sends Gideon down to the outside of the enemy host with Phurah his servant: thou shalt hear what they say, and afterward shall thine hands be strengthened. There he hears a man telling his fellow a dream of a cake of barley bread tumbling into the host and overturning a tent, and his fellow interprets it: this is nothing else save the sword of Gideon, for into his hand hath God delivered Midian. - The Lord put that dream into the mind of the enemy and sent Gideon down to hear it, so he could go into the battle valiant and strong, without any doubt. When Gideon heard the dream and the interpretation, he worshipped, and returned to say, arise; for the Lord hath delivered into your hand the host of Midian. Judges 7:16-18 - Gideon divides the three hundred into three companies, a hundred to the left flank, a hundred down the middle, a hundred to the right, and puts a trumpet in every man's hand, with empty pitchers and lamps within the pitchers. Look on me, and do likewise: pay attention, and when I blow the trumpet, blow ye also on every side of the camp, and say, the sword of the Lord, and of Gideon. Precepts: - Numbers 10:9 If ye go to war in your land against the enemy that oppresseth you, then ye shall blow an alarm with the trumpets, and ye shall be remembered before the Lord your God, and saved from your enemies. This is the history behind the shofars we blow; those trumpets are not just for looks and thumbnails, there is a deep meaning behind them going into the memorial of blowing of trumpets. Judges 7:19-22 - Gideon and his hundred come to the outside of the camp in the beginning of the middle watch, when they had but newly set the watch; in war you always have watchmen taking first, second, and third watch, and Gideon struck right in between the changing of the watchmen. - The three companies blew the trumpets, brake the pitchers, held the lamps in their left hands and the trumpets in their right, and cried, the sword of the Lord, and of Gideon; and every man stood in his place round about the camp. Three hundred against thousands, you have to do something to mess with their mind: those horns blowing in unison put fear in the nations, and all the host ran, and cried, and fled. - And the Lord set every man's sword against his fellow, even throughout all the host. The enemy destroyed itself; that is the Lord fighting the battle. Judges 7:23-25 - The men of Naphtali, Asher, and all Manasseh gathered themselves and pursued after the Midianites, and Gideon sent messengers throughout all mount Ephraim to come down and take the waters before them; and Ephraim took two princes of Midian, slaying Oreb upon the rock Oreb and Zeeb at the winepress of Zeeb. - Ephraim, stand up; get this spirit back and come join your brothers in the war, because Judah is calling you right now. For those that may not know, that is you so-called Hispanics, you Puerto Ricans: you are Ephraim. Judges 8: Gideon's Pursuit and Israel's Return to Baal Read the chapter → Judges 8 Judges 8:1-3 - The men of Ephraim chode with Gideon sharply: why hast thou served us thus, that thou calledst us not when thou wentest to fight with the Midianites? Ephraim has an attitude because they got called late to the battle and wanted in from the beginning. - Gideon answers with wisdom: is not the gleaning of the grapes of Ephraim better than the vintage of Abiezer? God delivered into your hands the princes of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb; what was I able to do in comparison of you? He gave them the best possible situation, the enemy fed right into their hands with nowhere to go, and then their anger was abated toward him. Judges 8:4-9 - Gideon and the three hundred pass over Jordan, faint, yet pursuing Zebah and Zalmunna the kings of Midian. He asks the men of Succoth for loaves of bread for his men, and the princes of Succoth answer, are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna now in thine hand, that we should give bread unto thine army? They try to play neutral ground for fear the kings might come against them if they helped. - Gideon promises Succoth that when the Lord has delivered Zebah and Zalmunna into his hand, he will tear their flesh with the thorns of the wilderness and with briers; and when the men of Penuel answer him the same way, he promises to break down their tower when he comes again in peace. Judges 8:10-12 - Zebah and Zalmunna were in Karkor with about fifteen thousand men, all that were left of the host of the children of the east, for there fell an hundred and twenty thousand men that drew sword. Three hundred against those numbers: you know God was with them. - Gideon went up by the way of them that dwelt in tents and smote the host while it was secure, and when the two kings fled, he pursued and took them, and discomfited all the host. Judges 8:13-17 - Returning from battle, Gideon caught a young man of Succoth who described unto him the princes and elders of the city, and he came back to Succoth with Zebah and Zalmunna in hand: behold the kings with whom ye did upbraid me. Gideon and his men had finished off Midian on an empty stomach because of them. - He took the elders of the city, and thorns of the wilderness and briers, and with them he taught the men of Succoth; he taught them a lesson, that when the army of the Lord comes through faint and weary and asks for bread, you do not turn them away. And he beat down the tower of Penuel and slew the men of the city. Judges 8:18-21 - Zebah and Zalmunna describe the men they slew at Tabor: each one resembled the children of a king. Those were powerful men, and they were Gideon's brethren, the sons of his mother; as the Lord liveth, if ye had saved them alive, I would not slay you. - Gideon tells Jether his firstborn, up, and slay them, but the youth drew not his sword, for he feared, because he was yet a youth. We have all had that moment of getting the nudge from pops and being nervous; the son was young, and that is understandable, but you see Gideon being a father, taking his son to the war and teaching him the ways he must walk. Precepts: - Proverbs 22:6 Train up a child in the way he should go: Gideon is doing exactly what we have to do with our young men, teaching them how to walk in the ways of the Lord. - Zebah and Zalmunna say, rise thou, and fall upon us: for as the man is, so is his strength. They wanted to die quick at the hand of a warrior rather than suffer under the sword of a boy; so Gideon arose and slew them, and took away the ornaments that were on their camels' necks. Judges 8:22-23 - The men of Israel ask Gideon to rule over them, both he, his son, and his son's son, for delivering them from the hand of Midian. Israel has always needed a leader, because we are lost sheep; we need somebody to guide us in the way we must go, or we wander off the path of righteousness. It has always been that way, and you see it playing out right here. - Gideon refuses: I will not rule over you, neither shall my son rule over you; the Lord shall rule over you. Judges 8:24-27 - Gideon requests of every man the earrings of his prey, for the enemy had golden earrings because they were Ishmaelites; and they willingly gave them, a thousand and seven hundred shekels of gold, beside the ornaments, collars, purple raiment, and camel chains of the kings. - Gideon made an ephod thereof and put it in his city, even in Ophrah: and all Israel went thither a whoring after it, which thing became a snare unto Gideon, and to his house. Precepts: - 1 Timothy 6:10 The love of money is the root of all evil; the gold that Gideon gathered turned into the very snare that trapped his own house. Judges 8:28-32 - Thus was Midian subdued before the children of Israel, so that they lifted up their heads no more, and the country was in quietness forty years in the days of Gideon. Gideon had threescore and ten sons, for he had many wives, and his concubine in Shechem bare him a son whose name he called Abimelech; and Gideon the son of Joash died in a good old age. - The sum of the history of Gideon, who is also named Jerubbaal, is this: the victory does not come in the strength of numbers, in how many guns or how many bullets you have. The victory of battle comes from the Lord, and that is why we have to trust in the Lord with all our heart and endure to the end, keeping these commandments until the return of our King of kings. Precepts: - 1 Maccabees 3:16-22 Judas Maccabaeus with a small company answered just as the history of Gideon teaches: it is no hard matter for many to be shut up in the hands of a few, for strength cometh from heaven. Judges 8:33-35 - It came to pass, as soon as Gideon was dead, that the children of Israel turned again, and went a whoring after Baalim, and made Baal-berith their god, and remembered not the Lord their God, who had delivered them out of the hands of all their enemies on every side; neither shewed they kindness to the house of Jerubbaal. - The same cycle turns again the moment the judge is gone. That is the whole lesson of the book: our deliverance is never our own hand, and our downfall is always our own forgetting. --- Topics: Esau and Edom · Idolatry · Sacrifice and Atonement · The Covenant · The Priesthood ← Judges 1-4 · Judges Study · Judges 9-12 →

title: Judges 9: Abimelech and the Fire Out of the Bramble
text: ← Judges 5-8 · Judges Study · Judges 13-16 → Judges 9: Abimelech and the Fire Out of the Bramble Read the chapter → Judges 9 Introduction This session covers Judges 9 through 12: Abimelech's bloody rise and fall at Shechem, the judges Tola and Jair, Israel sold into the hands of the Philistines and Ammon for serving other gods, Jephthah the Gileadite and his answer to the king of Ammon, Jephthah's vow and his daughter, the slaughter of the Ephraimites at the passages of Jordan, and the judges Ibzan, Elon, and Abdon. The main threads of the teaching: the Most High is in the midst of every war and sends the spirits that stir them; your sin will find you out; and know your history, because Jephthah knew the scriptures and could not be deceived about what actually happened. Judges 9:1-2 - Abimelech was the son of Jerubbaal by his concubine in Shechem. He went to Shechem unto his mother's brethren, his uncles on his mother's side, and had them ask the men of Shechem whether it was better for all seventy sons of Jerubbaal to reign over them, or for one man to reign. - Remember also that I am your bone and your flesh: he reminded them that he was family. When people do that, they want you to remember that blood is thicker than water, so you will back them whether or not it is right. Precepts: - Judges 7:1 Jerubbaal, who is Gideon; the two names are the same man. - Judges 8:28-31 Midian was subdued and the country was in quietness forty years in the days of Gideon; Gideon had threescore and ten sons of his body begotten, for he had many wives, and his concubine that was in Shechem also bare him a son, whose name he called Abimelech. Judges 9:3-4 - His mother's brethren spake of him in the ears of all the men of Shechem, whispering for their nephew, and their hearts inclined to follow Abimelech, for they said, He is our brother. They chose him by kinship, not by righteousness. - They gave him threescore and ten pieces of silver out of the house of Baal-berith, money out of their idol's house to back his rise. Politics has always worked this way: people will put a man in office not because he is best for the job, but because he is family or because they know him. - Baal was the chief god of the Canaanites, worshipped as the god of the elements who brought rain and made the ground fruitful, and sometimes as the god of war. Baal-berith, also called El-berith, was the Canaanite god of Shechem in the twelfth century BC, a sub god under Baal. - With that money Abimelech hired vain and light persons, wicked and empty men, which followed him. Judges 9:5 - He went unto his father's house at Ophrah and slew his brethren the sons of Jerubbaal, threescore and ten persons, upon one stone. He killed his own family to clear his way to a throne. - Notwithstanding, Jotham the youngest son of Jerubbaal was left, for he hid himself. Judges 9:6 - All the men of Shechem and all the house of Millo gathered together and made Abimelech king by the plain of the pillar that was in Shechem. They endorsed the man who had just used their money and his hired men to murder his seventy brothers. Judges 9:7-15 - When they told it to Jotham, he went and stood in the top of mount Gerizim, lifted up his voice, and cried, Hearken unto me, ye men of Shechem, that God may hearken unto you. This young brother was fearless; he stood up alone and rebuked the men who had made his brothers' killer king. - In his parable the trees went forth on a time to anoint a king over them. The olive tree would not leave its fatness, wherewith by it they honour God and man; the fig tree would not forsake its sweetness and good fruit; the vine would not leave its wine, which cheereth God and man. The profitable trees refused to be promoted over the trees. - Only the bramble accepted: if in truth ye anoint me king over you, then come and put your trust in my shadow; and if not, let fire come out of the bramble and devour the cedars of Lebanon. The worthless bush took the crown, and its answer carried the threat of fire. Judges 9:16-20 - Jotham applied the parable: if ye have done truly and sincerely in that ye have made Abimelech king, and if ye have dealt well with Jerubbaal and his house, then rejoice ye in Abimelech, and let him also rejoice in you. - He reminded them of what they owed his father: my father fought for you, and adventured his life far, and delivered you out of the hand of Midian; and ye are risen up against my father's house this day, and have slain his sons, threescore and ten persons upon one stone, and have made Abimelech, the son of his maidservant, king over the men of Shechem, because he is your brother. They did it only because he was kin to them. - But if not, let fire come out from Abimelech and devour the men of Shechem and the house of Millo; and let fire come out from the men of Shechem and from the house of Millo, and devour Abimelech. That is what the parable of the bramble was about: he prophesied that they would destroy one another, and it came to pass. Judges 9:21 - Jotham ran away and fled to Beer and dwelt there, for fear of Abimelech his brother. His brother already had a reputation for killing; he knew he could be next. Judges 9:22-24 - When Abimelech had reigned three years over Israel, God sent an evil spirit between Abimelech and the men of Shechem, and the men of Shechem dealt treacherously with Abimelech. Read that carefully: the Lord sent the evil spirit. When somebody's spirit suddenly changes toward you, we tend to think it is just that person; the scripture shows the Most High is the one who stirs these things. - War and strife between nations are not coincidence, karma, or mother nature; those are the world's false ideas and idols. The Most High is in the midst of these things, mustering the host, the armies above and below, and he even puts it on the spirit of one wicked man to go against another. - The reason is given: that the cruelty done to the threescore and ten sons of Jerubbaal might come, and their blood be laid upon Abimelech their brother, which slew them, and upon the men of Shechem, which aided him in the killing of his brethren. The hired men and the backers carried the blood guilt too. Abimelech ran for three years and everything looked good, but you are not getting away with evil. Precepts: - Isaiah 13:3-4 The sanctified ones are the prophets and the mighty ones are the angels; the Lord of hosts mustereth the host of the battle, so the Most High himself is in the midst of the armies stirring up war among the kingdoms of nations. - Isaiah 45:7 The Most High forms the light and creates darkness, makes peace and creates evil; I the LORD do all these things. - Exodus 15:3-4 The LORD is a man of war, the LORD is his name; many who think they know God have no idea who they are dealing with. - 1 Esdras 1:25-27 Josiah put himself in the midst of a war the Most High had sent Pharaoh to fight, and it cost him his life; when the Lord is in the midst of a thing, it is best to get out of the way. - 1 Kings 22:22-23 The same way the Lord put a lying spirit in the mouth of all Ahab's prophets, that he should go up and fall at Ramoth-gilead. Judges 9:25 - The men of Shechem set liers in wait for him in the top of the mountains, and they robbed all that came along that way by them; and it was told Abimelech. The treachery the Most High sent had begun. Judges 9:26-29 - Gaal the son of Ebed came with his brethren and went over to Shechem, and the men of Shechem put their confidence in him. They went out into the fields, gathered their vineyards, trode the grapes, made merry, went into the house of their god, did eat and drink, and cursed Abimelech. - Gaal talked big: who is Abimelech, and who is Shechem, that we should serve him? is not he the son of Jerubbaal? and Zebul his officer? serve the men of Hamor the father of Shechem: for why should we serve him? He asked why they should be serving this Israelite at all. - Would to God this people were under my hand! then would I remove Abimelech. He was talking cash money with wine in him: increase thine army, and come out. Judges 9:30-33 - When Zebul the ruler of the city, Abimelech's officer, heard the words of Gaal the son of Ebed, his anger was kindled. He sent messengers unto Abimelech privily, saying, Behold, Gaal and his brethren fortify the city against thee. - Zebul counselled Abimelech to rise up by night with his people and lie in wait in the field, and in the morning, as soon as the sun was up, to set upon the city. This is the same hand we read of in verse 23; the Lord is in the midst of this whole treachery, turning it back on all of them. Judges 9:34-41 - Abimelech and all the people with him rose up by night and laid wait against Shechem in four companies. When Gaal saw the people coming down from the top of the mountains, Zebul told him, Thou seest the shadow of the mountains as if they were men, playing him until it was too late. - Then Zebul threw his own words back at him: where is now thy mouth, wherewith thou saidst, Who is Abimelech, that we should serve him? is not this the people that thou hast despised? go out, I pray now, and fight with them. All of that big talk disappeared when the fight showed up. - Gaal went out before the men of Shechem and fought with Abimelech, and Abimelech chased him, and he fled before him, and many were overthrown and wounded, even unto the entering of the gate. Abimelech dwelt at Arumah, and Zebul thrust out Gaal and his brethren, that they should not dwell in Shechem. Judges 9:42-45 - On the morrow the people went out into the field, and it was told Abimelech. He divided his men into three companies, laid wait in the field, rose up against the people, and smote them. - Abimelech fought against the city all that day; he took the city, slew the people that was therein, beat down the city, and sowed it with salt. Judges 9:46-49 - When all the men of the tower of Shechem heard that, they entered into an hold of the house of the god Berith. - Abimelech gat him up to mount Zalmon, cut down a bough from the trees with an axe, laid it on his shoulder, and said unto the people that were with him, What ye have seen me do, make haste, and do as I have done. They cut every man his bough, put them to the hold, and set the hold on fire upon them, so that all the men of the tower of Shechem died also, about a thousand men and women. - Remember, these are the people whose money and endorsement made him king: I am your brother, make me king. Now he turned on Shechem itself and burned them; the fire out of the bramble that Jotham prophesied was devouring the men of Shechem. Judges 9:50-55 - Then went Abimelech to Thebez, and there was a strong tower within the city, and all the men and women of the city fled to the top of it. Abimelech came unto the tower and went hard unto the door to burn it with fire, and a certain woman cast a piece of a millstone upon Abimelech's head, and all to brake his skull. A millstone is a heavy stone; it crushed his skull. - He called hastily unto the young man his armourbearer: draw thy sword, and slay me, that men say not of me, A woman slew him. It was counted a shame for a man of war to die by the hand of a woman, as when Jael put Sisera to death earlier in this book. His young man thrust him through, and he died. - He reigned only three years. Killing his seventy brothers bought him a three year reign and a crushed skull; it was to no profit. If you are doing wickedness behind closed doors and think the Most High does not see it, he sees it, and he brings swift judgment. Precepts: - Judges 4:21 Sisera the captain fled from the battle and died by the hand of a woman when Jael smote the nail into his temples. - Ecclesiasticus 1:30 God discovered the secret that he had slain his brothers and cast him down in the midst of the congregation; he took the throne as if he had earned it, but he came not in truth, and his heart was full of deceit. - Numbers 32:23 Be sure your sin will find you out; that is exactly what happened to Abimelech. Judges 9:56-57 - Thus God rendered the wickedness of Abimelech, which he did unto his father, in slaying his seventy brethren; and all the evil of the men of Shechem did God render upon their heads. Both sides were judged; for three years they reigned and everything looked good, then the Most High brought the judgment. - Upon them came the curse of Jotham the son of Jerubbaal. Our forefather Jotham, a young man at the time, prophesied their destruction, and it came to pass. - We read these accounts for the history, but look deeper and apply them to our lives: if there is evil being done behind closed doors, the Most High will judge it in front of everybody, like he judged Abimelech. Judges 10: Go and Cry unto the Gods Which Ye Have Chosen Read the chapter → Judges 10 Judges 10:1-2 - After Abimelech there arose to defend Israel Tola the son of Puah, a man of Issachar; he judged Israel twenty and three years, and died, and was buried in Shamir. - Notice it says to defend Israel. Israel was in the land, but do not forget that the Lord had left nations among us, so the judges had to defend the people. Precepts: - Judges 3:1-4 The Lord left nations to prove Israel, that the generations which had not known all the wars of Canaan might be taught war, and to know whether Israel would hearken unto the commandments which he commanded their fathers by the hand of Moses. Judges 10:3-5 - After him arose Jair, a Gileadite, and judged Israel twenty and two years. He had thirty sons that rode on thirty ass colts, and they had thirty cities in the land of Gilead, which are called Havoth-jair unto this day; and Jair died and was buried in Camon. Judges 10:6 - The children of Israel did evil again in the sight of the LORD. That is the cycle of this whole book: after a judge died and Israel had peace and safety for a while, the people went right back into their sin, just like always. - Israel served Baalim and Ashtaroth, and the gods of Syria, the gods of Zidon, the gods of Moab, the gods of the children of Ammon, and the gods of the Philistines, and forsook the LORD, and served not him. Ashtaroth is Ishtar or Astarte, the so called queen of heaven; the heathen carried the same goddess under different names, the same one the Greeks called Aphrodite. Judges 10:7-9 - The anger of the LORD was hot against Israel, and he sold them into the hands of the Philistines and into the hands of the children of Ammon. Israel was serving their gods, so the Lord sold Israel to them. - Eighteen years they vexed and oppressed all the children of Israel that were on the other side Jordan, in the land of the Amorites, which is in Gilead: that was Reuben, Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh in their allotments across the river. - Moreover the children of Ammon passed over Jordan to fight also against Judah, and against Benjamin, and against the house of Ephraim, which shows those tribes dwelling in their own allotments on the other side; so that Israel was sore distressed. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 28:32 One of the curses for breaking the laws: thy sons and thy daughters shall be given unto another people, and there shall be no might in thine hand. - Deuteronomy 28:41 Thou shalt beget sons and daughters, but thou shalt not enjoy them, for they shall go into captivity; the curse of the law was already working on Israel in the land. Judges 10:10-14 - The children of Israel cried unto the LORD, saying, We have sinned against thee, both because we have forsaken our God, and also served Baalim. The enemy had destroyed on one side of Jordan and was crossing over against Judah, Benjamin, and Ephraim, so now Israel wanted to confess. - The Lord answered by rehearsing the deliverances: did not I deliver you from the Egyptians, and from the Amorites, from the children of Ammon, and from the Philistines? the Zidonians also, and the Amalekites, and the Maonites did oppress you, and ye cried to me, and I delivered you out of their hand. All through the early chapters of this book he kept delivering us over and over. - Yet ye have forsaken me, and served other gods: wherefore I will deliver you no more. Go and cry unto the gods which ye have chosen; let them deliver you in the time of your tribulation. The Lord is not unrighteous; he gave a fair covenant: do right and he is with you above all nations, do wrong and you go into captivity. He will not break his word, and everybody's grace is not the same. Precepts: - Nehemiah 9:26-28 The whole cycle of the book of Judges in one passage: Israel was disobedient, cast thy law behind their backs, and slew the prophets; the Lord delivered them into the hand of their enemies; in the time of their trouble they cried, and he heard from heaven and gave them saviours who saved them; and after they had rest, they did evil again before thee. Judges 10:15-16 - The children of Israel said unto the LORD, We have sinned: do thou unto us whatsoever seemeth good unto thee; deliver us only, we pray thee, this day. And they put away the strange gods from among them and served the LORD. This time the repentance came with action. - And his soul was grieved for the misery of Israel. The Most High loves Israel; it grieved him to have his own children in captivity, but he cannot break his word, so the repentance had to come first. That is also why Christ was sent to die for our sins, so we could have a chance to return to him in the last days. Judges 10:17-18 - The children of Ammon were gathered together and encamped in Gilead, and the children of Israel assembled themselves together and encamped in Mizpeh. - The people and princes of Gilead said one to another, What man is he that will begin to fight against the children of Ammon? he shall be head over all the inhabitants of Gilead. That question is answered in chapter 11. Judges 11: Jephthah and the Search of the Fathers Read the chapter → Judges 11 Judges 11:1-3 - Now Jephthah the Gileadite was a mighty man of valour, and he was the son of an harlot: and Gilead begat Jephthah. His mother was a harlot, but he himself was a mighty man of valour. - Gilead's wife's sons grew up and thrust out Jephthah: thou shalt not inherit in our father's house, for thou art the son of a strange woman. Strange woman here does not mean his mother was of another nation; the scripture says only that she was a harlot. His brothers cast him out of his father's house over his mother, though he had as much right to that house as they did. - Jephthah fled from his brethren and dwelt in the land of Tob, and there were gathered vain men to Jephthah, and went out with him. Watch what that shows: when we do our brothers and sisters wrong, when the ones trying to do right do not get the love and support they need from their own family, they go looking for love in the wrong places, and you see the kind of men they gravitate to. Judges 11:4-11 - In process of time the children of Ammon made war against Israel, and the elders of Gilead went to fetch Jephthah out of the land of Tob: come and be our captain, that we may fight with the children of Ammon. Now they wanted the man of valour they had cast out. - Jephthah answered, Did not ye hate me, and expel me out of my father's house? and why are ye come unto me now when ye are in distress? You hated me, you put me out, and now that trouble has come, you need me. - He set the terms: if ye bring me home again to fight against the children of Ammon, and the LORD deliver them before me, shall I be your head? And the elders of Gilead said, The LORD be witness between us, if we do not so according to thy words; they called the Lord to judge them if they broke their word. - Jephthah went with the elders of Gilead, and the people made him head and captain over them: and Jephthah uttered all his words before the LORD in Mizpeh. Judges 11:12-13 - Jephthah sent messengers unto the king of the children of Ammon, saying, What hast thou to do with me, that thou art come against me to fight in my land? He wanted to know what Ammon had against Israel. - The king of Ammon answered, Because Israel took away my land, when they came up out of Egypt, from Arnon even unto Jabbok, and unto Jordan: now therefore restore those lands again peaceably. That claim was a lie, and Jephthah knew it. Judges 11:14-22 - Jephthah sent messengers again and broke down the whole history: Israel took not away the land of Moab, nor the land of the children of Ammon. He knew the record, so nobody could talk him out of it. - When Israel came up from Egypt and walked through the wilderness unto the Red sea and came to Kadesh, they sent messengers to the king of Edom and to the king of Moab asking passage, and both refused; so Israel went along through the wilderness, compassed the land of Edom and the land of Moab, came by the east side of the land of Moab, and pitched on the other side of Arnon; but they came not within the border of Moab, for Arnon was the border of Moab. - This is why we must know our history. The king of Ammon could have pulled that on somebody ignorant and been given the land; Jephthah said no, that is not what happened, the book of Numbers does not say that. People try to confuse us about the Bible in the street the same way, so prepare yourself to the search of the fathers. Precepts: - Job 8:8 Enquire, I pray thee, of the former age, and prepare thyself to the search of their fathers; we are supposed to know these things so nobody can pull the wool over our eyes. - Deuteronomy 32:7 Remember the days of old, consider the years of many generations: ask thy father, and he will shew thee; thy elders, and they will tell thee. - 1 Timothy 4:13 Till I come, give attendance to reading; Paul wrote it to Timothy, a young leader, because the study never stops. - Then Israel sent messengers unto Sihon king of the Amorites, the king of Heshbon: let us pass, we pray thee, through thy land into my place. But Sihon trusted not Israel to pass through his coast; he gathered all his people together, pitched in Jahaz, and fought against Israel. They came against Israel; Israel did nothing to them. - And the LORD God of Israel delivered Sihon and all his people into the hand of Israel, and they smote them: so Israel possessed all the land of the Amorites, from Arnon even unto Jabbok, and from the wilderness even unto Jordan. That is how Israel got the land of the Amorites: the Lord gave it in battle when they came out against his people. Precepts: - Numbers 20:21 Edom refused to give Israel passage through his border, just as Jephthah rehearsed it. - Exodus 23:20-23 The promise behind this history: the Most High sent an Angel before Israel, and we know that angel is Christ; obey his voice, and I will be an enemy unto thine enemies, for mine Angel shall go before thee and bring thee in unto the Amorites, and I will cut them off. - Deuteronomy 2:30 Sihon would not let us pass, for the LORD thy God hardened his spirit and made his heart obstinate, that he might deliver him into thy hand; go verse upon precept and you see the Most High in the midst of the battle. - Deuteronomy 2:33-36 The LORD our God delivered him before us, and we took all his cities at that time; from Aroer even unto Gilead, there was not one city too strong for us, because the Lord and his angels were in the midst of Israel. - Deuteronomy 2:37 Only unto the land of the children of Ammon thou camest not; Israel never touched Ammon's land, which proves the king's claim false. Judges 11:23-28 - So now the LORD God of Israel hath dispossessed the Amorites from before his people Israel, and shouldest thou possess it? The Lord moved the Amorites out by moving Israel in; why should Ammon possess what the Most High gave to Israel? - Wilt not thou possess that which Chemosh thy god giveth thee? So whomsoever the LORD our God shall drive out from before us, them will we possess. You take what your god gives you; we will possess whatever the Most High gives us, and we are not backing down from anybody. - Art thou any thing better than Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab? did he ever strive against Israel, or did he ever fight against them? While Israel dwelt in Heshbon and her towns, and in Aroer and her towns, and in all the cities along the coasts of Arnon, three hundred years, why did ye not recover them within that time? Three hundred years Israel held that land and nobody came to claim it. - Wherefore I have not sinned against thee, but thou doest me wrong to war against me: the LORD the Judge be judge this day between the children of Israel and the children of Ammon. The Lord is in the midst of every battle; nothing goes down without the Most High letting it go down. World War One, the Lord was in the midst; World War Two, the Lord was in the midst; whoever he has destined to win is going to win. - Howbeit the king of the children of Ammon hearkened not unto the words of Jephthah: the Lord had hardened their hearts not to listen, the same as he did with Sihon. - The Most High strengthens nations and weakens nations, and moves peoples in and out of lands to fulfil his word. In this last battle Israel cannot lose so long as we keep the commandments, have faith in Christ, and endure to the end; but if we stay in sin, we die with the heathen. Precepts: - Isaiah 46:10 Declaring the end from the beginning: my counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure; whoever the Most High wants to win a war is going to win it. - 2 Timothy 4:7-8 Paul could say, I have fought a good fight, because he knew a crown of righteousness was laid up for him; that is the fight Israel is in now. Judges 11:29-31 - Then the Spirit of the LORD came upon Jephthah, and he passed over Gilead and Manasseh, and passed over unto the children of Ammon. - Jephthah vowed a vow unto the LORD: if thou shalt without fail deliver the children of Ammon into mine hands, then whatsoever cometh forth of the doors of my house to meet me, when I return in peace, shall surely be the LORD'S, and I will offer it up for a burnt offering. The vow was made before the battle, an offering promised to the Lord for the victory: whatever came out of his doors first would be given over to the Lord. Judges 11:32-33 - Jephthah passed over unto the children of Ammon to fight against them, and the LORD delivered them into his hands. He smote them from Aroer even till thou come to Minnith, even twenty cities, with a very great slaughter. Thus the children of Ammon were subdued before the children of Israel. Judges 11:34-35 - Jephthah came to Mizpeh unto his house, and behold, his daughter came out to meet him with timbrels and with dances; and she was his only child; beside her he had neither son nor daughter. - He rent his clothes and said, Alas, my daughter! thou hast brought me very low; for I have opened my mouth unto the LORD, and I cannot go back. A vow made to the Most High could not be taken back. Judges 11:36-40 - His daughter answered, My father, if thou hast opened thy mouth unto the LORD, do to me according to that which hath proceeded out of thy mouth; forasmuch as the LORD hath taken vengeance for thee of thine enemies, even of the children of Ammon. She was not pleading for her life; she accepted that her life was now vowed to the Lord. - She asked one thing: let me alone two months, that I may go up and down upon the mountains, and bewail my virginity, I and my fellows. To bewail is to weep and mourn; she went with her companions and mourned her virginity, because being given over to the Lord she would never know a man. - Jephthah did not burn his daughter as a human sacrifice. Israel did not do human sacrifices; that was Molech worship among the Canaanites. Read the end of the passage: at the end of two months she returned unto her father, who did with her according to his vow which he had vowed, and she knew no man. If she had been put to death, there would be no reason for the scripture to say she knew no man; her life was committed to the Lord and she remained a virgin. - Why would she mourn her virginity if she were about to die? Because the sorrow was that she could never marry or bear children. In those days our women wanted to bring children into the world and continue the lineage; to be without children was counted a shame and a dishonour among the daughters of Israel. - A lot of people try to say Jephthah sacrificed his daughter, because our people do not understand the scriptures; keep reading and the text itself answers it. It is a translation difference around the word offering: she was presented to the Lord to serve him, not sent up as a burnt sacrifice. - And it was a custom in Israel, that the daughters of Israel went yearly to lament the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite four days in a year. Precepts: - Genesis 30:1-2 Rachel said to Jacob, Give me children, or else I die; that is how heavy childlessness sat upon our foremothers, and that is why Jephthah's daughter bewailed her virginity. Judges 12: Strife Amongst Brethren Read the chapter → Judges 12 Judges 12:1-3 - The men of Ephraim gathered themselves together and went northward and said unto Jephthah, Wherefore passedst thou over to fight against the children of Ammon, and didst not call us to go with thee? we will burn thine house upon thee with fire. They came at their own deliverer with a threat. - Jephthah answered, I and my people were at great strife with the children of Ammon; and when I called you, ye delivered me not out of their hands. When I saw that ye delivered me not, I put my life in my hands and passed over against the children of Ammon, and the LORD delivered them into my hand: wherefore then are ye come up unto me this day, to fight against me? Judges 12:4-6 - Jephthah gathered together all the men of Gilead and fought with Ephraim, and the men of Gilead smote Ephraim and took the passages of Jordan before the Ephraimites. - When the Ephraimites which were escaped said, Let me go over, the men of Gilead asked him, Art thou an Ephraimite? If he said nay, they said unto him, Say now Shibboleth; and he said Sibboleth, for he could not frame to pronounce it right. Then they took him and slew him at the passages of Jordan. They identified their brothers by their speech. - There fell at that time of the Ephraimites forty and two thousand. This right here was strife amongst brethren: Israel killed forty two thousand of their own brothers. Judges 12:7 - Jephthah judged Israel six years; then died Jephthah the Gileadite, and was buried in one of the cities of Gilead. Judges 12:8-10 - After him Ibzan of Bethlehem judged Israel. He had thirty sons and thirty daughters, whom he sent abroad, and took in thirty daughters from abroad for his sons. He judged Israel seven years, and died, and was buried at Bethlehem. Judges 12:11-12 - After him Elon, a Zebulonite, judged Israel ten years; and Elon the Zebulonite died, and was buried in Aijalon in the country of Zebulun. Judges 12:13-15 - After him Abdon the son of Hillel, a Pirathonite, judged Israel. He had forty sons and thirty nephews, that rode on threescore and ten ass colts; and he judged Israel eight years, and died, and was buried in Pirathon in the land of Ephraim, in the mount of the Amalekites. --- Topics: Esau and Edom · Idolatry · Sacrifice and Atonement · The Covenant ← Judges 5-8 · Judges Study · Judges 13-16 →

title: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab
text: ← Judges 21 · Ruth Study · Ruth 4 → Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab Read the chapter → Ruth 1 Introduction This session covers Judges 21 together with Ruth chapters 1 through 3; these notes cover Ruth 1 through 3. The book of Ruth opens in the days when the judges ruled, the same era Judges just closed with the words, there was no king in Israel, and every man did that which was right in his own eyes. That setting explains how the sons of Elimelech came to take wives of the women of Moab, which the law forbade. The teaching follows Naomi and Ruth from Moab back to Bethlehem and into the field of Boaz, and its main threads are the rest a widow finds in the house of her husband, the inheritance a man is supposed to leave behind, the law of raising up the name of the dead, the idol gods Orpah returned to, the place of the stranger who joins herself under Israel, and the near kinsman at the threshingfloor. Ruth 1:1-2 - It came to pass in the days when the judges ruled: the scripture is putting Ruth in a time frame. Ruth takes place in the same time as the book of Judges. - There was a famine in the land, and Elimelech of Bethlehemjudah went to sojourn in the country of Moab with his wife Naomi and his two sons Mahlon and Chilion, Ephrathites of Bethlehemjudah. Ruth 1:3-5 - Elimelech, Naomi's husband, died, and she was left with her two sons. The sons took them wives of the women of Moab, Orpah and Ruth, and after they dwelt there about ten years Mahlon and Chilion died also, leaving Naomi without her husband and without her sons. - Were the sons of Israel supposed to take wives of the women of Moab while sojourning there? No; but remember what was just read at the end of Judges, that every man did that which was right in his own eyes. And this was not the first time Israel dealt with the women of Moab. Precepts: - Judges 21:25 There was no king in Israel and every man did that which was right in his own eyes; that is the state Israel was in when these marriages happened. - Deuteronomy 23:3 An Ammonite or Moabite shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord for ever; Israel was not supposed to be marrying the women of Moab. - Numbers 25:1-2 Israel had already committed whoredom with the daughters of Moab at Shittim, and the people did eat and bowed down to their gods. - 1 Esdras 8:69 Even in the time of Ezra, Israel had not put away the strange people of the land, the Moabites among them; remember that it says the strange people of the land. Ruth 1:6-9 - Naomi heard in the country of Moab that the Lord had visited his people and given them bread, so she arose with her daughters in law to return unto the land of Judah, and told them, Go, return each to her mother's house; the Lord deal kindly with you, as ye have dealt with the dead and with me. - The Lord grant you that ye may find rest, each of you in the house of her husband: that rest is an inheritance. The man is supposed to leave an inheritance; you are not supposed to leave your wife and your children desolate with a gang of bills. To leave an inheritance you first have to work, and you have to be wise with how you deal with your money. Precepts: - Proverbs 13:22 A good man leaveth an inheritance to his children's children. - 1 Timothy 5:8 Providing for your own house is where leaving an inheritance begins; first you have to work. - Ruth 4:5 Reading ahead for understanding: whoever bought the field of Naomi had to buy it also of Ruth, the wife of the dead, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance. - Judith 8:4-7 The example of a widow finding rest in the house of her husband: Manasses left Judith gold, silver, servants, cattle, and lands, and she remained upon them. - Behind the words the wife of the dead stands the law of the husband's brother: if brethren dwell together and one dies having no child, his brother takes the widow to wife, and the firstborn she bears succeeds in the name of the dead brother, that his name be not put out of Israel. That first child is basically the dead brother's child; he gets the rights of inheritance as if the brother were still alive, so the brother's name stays in the earth and his house is built up. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 25:5-6 The wife of the dead shall not marry without unto a stranger; her husband's brother shall take her to wife, and the firstborn shall succeed in the name of his brother which is dead. - Deuteronomy 25:7-10 If the man refused, the widow loosed his shoe and spat in his face before the elders, because he would not build up his brother's house; keeping the name going was the whole purpose of the law. - Genesis 49:3 The firstborn is the might and the beginning of strength, the excellency of dignity and power; you want somebody to carry on your name. - 1 Chronicles 5:1 Reuben was the firstborn, but because he defiled his father's bed his birthright was given unto the sons of Joseph; the birthright shows why the firstborn and the inheritance mattered so much in Israel. - We are not under that law anymore; we do not have that land inheritance in captivity. It is wicked to pull that scripture today to try to get with your brother's wife after he passes away; do not be looking at your brother's wife. - It is important for us to build our legacy and pass it down; that is one of the things we lack in Israel today. Some of us use captivity as an excuse not to better ourselves or build, but that is not what the scriptures say: get the job, further your education, do more for yourself, your family, and the body. Building up your house also means spiritually building it, teaching your wife and children. Precepts: - Proverbs 19:14 Houses and riches are the inheritance of fathers, and a prudent wife is from the Lord. - Deuteronomy 28:43-44 The stranger gets up very high and Israel comes down very low, the head and the tail; this curse is why we find ourselves in this position, but it does not mean we throw in the towel. - Jeremiah 29:5-6 Even in the seventy years under Babylon the Lord said build ye houses, plant gardens, take wives, and beget sons and daughters, that ye may be increased there and not diminished; captivity was never a command to stop building your house. Ruth 1:10-13 - The daughters in law said, Surely we will return with thee unto thy people; but Naomi answered, Are there yet any more sons in my womb, that they may be your husbands? Even if she had a husband that night and bore sons, would they tarry until the boys were grown? They were grown women; they were not going to wait. - Naomi was free of her responsibility toward them: her husband had died, her sons their husbands had died, and their husbands had left them inheritances in Moab. She would not put them under an oath to stay and wait for sons that would likely never come. Precepts: - 1 Timothy 5:11 In Israel the younger widows are refused, for when they begin to wax wanton against Christ they will marry; a young widow still has years to bear children and that urge will most likely come upon her, which is why Naomi released them. Ruth 1:14-15 - They lifted up their voice and wept again; Orpah kissed her mother in law and went back, but Ruth clave unto her. - Naomi said, Thy sister in law is gone back unto her people and unto her gods. Those gods were idols; Chemosh was the god the Moabites served. Precepts: - Psalms 96:5 All the gods of the nations are idols, but the Lord made the heavens; what Orpah returned to were idols. - Numbers 21:29 Woe to thee, Moab; thou art undone, O people of Chemosh. Chemosh was the god Moab was serving. - 1 Kings 11:4-7 When Solomon was old his strange wives turned away his heart, and he built an high place for Chemosh, the abomination of Moab; the scripture shows numerous times that Chemosh was the god of the Moabites. Ruth 1:16-17 - Ruth was determined: Intreat me not to leave thee; whither thou goest, I will go; thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God; where thou diest, will I die. She was saying, do not put me away; Orpah may have gone back, but I am going to cleave unto you. - Does that mean she would inherit the kingdom as a Moabitess? No. She joined herself under Israel and acknowledged her place in the hierarchy under Israel, and the scriptures give examples of strangers who did the same. Precepts: - Matthew 15:24-28 Christ said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel, and the woman answered, Truth, Lord: yet the dogs eat of the crumbs which fall from their masters' table; because she acknowledged who he is, who she is, and who the children of Israel are, he said, O woman, great is thy faith, and her daughter was made whole. - Joshua 6:25 Rahab the harlot and her father's household were saved alive and she dwelt in Israel, because she knew the fame of what the God of Israel had done and that the hearts of her people had melted; she knew the Most High was the true living God. - Genesis 30:27 Laban said, I have learned by experience that the Lord hath blessed me for thy sake; Laban knew where his blessings came from, for he had little before Jacob arrived and increased while our forefather served him. Ruth 1:18-22 - When Naomi saw that Ruth was stedfastly minded to go with her, she left speaking unto her, and the two went until they came to Bethlehem, where all the city was moved about them and said, Is this Naomi? - She answered, Call me not Naomi, call me Mara: for the Almighty hath dealt very bitterly with me. I went out full, and the Lord hath brought me home again empty. - So Naomi returned, and Ruth the Moabitess her daughter in law with her, and they came to Bethlehem in the beginning of barley harvest. Ruth 2: Gleaning in the Field of Boaz Read the chapter → Ruth 2 Ruth 2:1-3 - Naomi had a kinsman of her husband, a mighty man of wealth of the family of Elimelech, and his name was Boaz. - Ruth asked Naomi, Let me now go to the field and glean ears of corn after him in whose sight I shall find grace; and her hap was to light on a part of the field belonging unto Boaz, who was of the kindred of Elimelech. Ruth 2:4-9 - Boaz came from Bethlehem and greeted his reapers, The Lord be with you; and they answered him, The Lord bless thee. When he asked whose damsel this was, the servant set over the reapers answered, It is the Moabitish damsel that came back with Naomi, and reported how she had asked to glean and had continued from the morning with only a little rest in the house. - Boaz told Ruth to glean in no other field but to abide fast by his maidens; he had charged the young men not to touch her, and when she was athirst she could drink of the vessels the young men had drawn. Ruth 2:10 - Ruth fell on her face and asked, Why have I found grace in thine eyes, that thou shouldest take knowledge of me, seeing I am a stranger? She acknowledged what she was to Israel: a stranger. Precepts: - 1 Esdras 8:69 The Moabites are counted among the strange people of the land; Ruth spoke of herself by that same word. - Leviticus 25:44-46 The bondmen and bondmaids of Israel shall be of the heathen round about and of the children of the strangers that sojourn among you; they shall be your possession. When we get into the kingdom this order will be in place. Ruth 2:11-13 - Boaz answered that it had fully been shewed him all she had done for her mother in law since the death of her husband, how she left her father, her mother, and the land of her nativity, and came unto a people she knew not before. - The Lord recompense thy work, and a full reward be given thee of the Lord God of Israel, under whose wings thou art come to trust. Ruth answered, Let me find favour in thy sight, my lord, for thou hast comforted me, though I be not like unto one of thine handmaidens. Ruth 2:14-17 - At mealtime Boaz told her to come and eat of the bread and dip her morsel in the vinegar; he reached her parched corn, and she did eat and was sufficed and left. - When she rose to glean, Boaz commanded his young men to let her glean even among the sheaves without reproach, and to let fall handfuls of purpose for her. She gleaned until evening and beat out about an ephah of barley. Ruth 2:18-23 - Ruth brought what she had gleaned into the city, gave Naomi what she had reserved, and told her, The man's name with whom I wrought to day is Boaz. - Naomi blessed him of the Lord, who hath not left off his kindness to the living and to the dead, and said, The man is near of kin unto us, one of our next kinsmen. - Naomi told her it was good to go out with his maidens, that they meet thee not in any other field; so Ruth kept fast by the maidens of Boaz to glean unto the end of barley harvest and of wheat harvest, and dwelt with her mother in law. Ruth 3: The Skirt of the Near Kinsman Read the chapter → Ruth 3 Ruth 3:1-5 - Naomi said, My daughter, shall I not seek rest for thee, that it may be well with thee? This is the same rest spoken of in chapter 1, rest in the house of a husband; and Boaz of their kindred was winnowing barley that night in the threshingfloor. - Her instructions: wash thyself, anoint thee, put thy raiment upon thee, get thee down to the floor, and make not thyself known unto the man until he has done eating and drinking; mark where he lies, uncover his feet, and lay thee down, and he will tell thee what thou shalt do. Ruth answered, All that thou sayest unto me I will do. Ruth 3:6-9 - Ruth did according to all her mother in law bade her. When Boaz had eaten and drunk and his heart was merry, he lay down at the end of the heap of corn, and she came softly, uncovered his feet, and laid her down. At midnight the man was afraid, turned himself, and behold, a woman lay at his feet. - She answered, I am Ruth thine handmaid: spread therefore thy skirt over thine handmaid; for thou art a near kinsman. - On the skirt: Zondervan's Compact Bible Dictionary, page 137, explains that the basic garments of the men of biblical times were the inner tunic, the tunic coat, the girdle, and the cloak, with the headdress and the shoes or sandals; the word skirt in the Bible usually refers to an article of male, not female, clothing, and carries meanings such as extremity, as in Ruth 3:9. Asking Boaz to spread his skirt over her was asking the near kinsman to take her under his covering. Ruth 3:10 - Boaz blessed her: thou hast shewed more kindness in the latter end than at the beginning, inasmuch as thou followedst not young men, whether poor or rich. Ruth could have gone after other men, but even as a Moabitess she was following the customs of Israel, trying to find someone to raise up seed for her dead lord and keep his name in the earth; she was trying to do the right thing and keep the laws of Israel. Precepts: - Ruth 1:12-13 Naomi had asked, Would ye tarry for sons till they were grown? Boaz's words point back to this: Ruth did what no young widow was expected to do, seeking the kinsman of her dead husband instead of following young men. Ruth 3:11-13 - Fear not, my daughter; I will do to thee all that thou requirest: for all the city of my people doth know that thou art a virtuous woman. - Boaz was honest: it is true that I am thy near kinsman, howbeit there is a kinsman nearer than I. Tarry this night, and in the morning, if he will perform unto thee the part of a kinsman, well; but if not, then will I do the part of a kinsman to thee, as the Lord liveth. Ruth 3:14-18 - She lay at his feet until the morning and rose up before one could know another; that is the same precept of knowing read in Judges 21, meaning in this case to lie down and have sex with each other. That is also why Boaz said, Let it not be known that a woman came into the floor. - Boaz measured six measures of barley into her vail and she went into the city; she told Naomi, These six measures of barley gave he me; for he said to me, Go not empty unto thy mother in law. - Naomi answered, Sit still, my daughter, until thou know how the matter will fall: for the man will not be in rest until he have finished the thing this day. Precepts: - Judges 21:12 The virgins of Jabeshgilead had not known man by lying with any male; to know somebody in scripture means to lie with them. --- Topics: Esau and Edom · Idolatry · Sacrifice and Atonement · The Feasts of the Most High · The Priesthood · The Sabbath ← Judges 21 · Ruth Study · Ruth 4 →

title: Ruth 4: Boaz Redeems the Inheritance
text: ← Ruth 1-3 · Ruth Study · 1 Samuel 1-3 → Ruth 4: Boaz Redeems the Inheritance Read the chapter → Ruth 4 Introduction This session covers Ruth 4 together with 1 Samuel 1-3; these notes cover Ruth 4, the end of the book of Ruth, before the class moves into the history of Israel in first Samuel. The chapter closes the book: Boaz goes up to the gate and conducts the laws of the land before witnesses, the law of inheritance is traced back to Numbers 36 and the law of the husband's brother back to Deuteronomy 25, the nearer kinsman refuses to redeem, Boaz buys the field and takes Ruth to raise up the name of the dead, Obed is born and Naomi becomes nurse unto him, and the generations of Pharez run down to David. Nothing too major happens in Ruth 4 beyond the laws of the land and the law of loving thy neighbour as thyself; that is what Boaz was exercising, and that is why he is mentioned in the scriptures. Ruth 4:1-2 - Boaz went up to the gate, called the kinsman of whom he had spoken to turn aside and sit down, and took ten men of the elders of the city to sit with them. - What he is doing is calling witnesses. He is about to make a purchase, so he calls witnesses, that it can be put in the books for the future that this is what was done. Ruth 4:3-4 - Boaz laid the matter before the kinsman: Naomi, that is come again out of the country of Moab, selleth a parcel of land which was our brother Elimelech's. If thou wilt redeem it, redeem it; but if not, tell me, for there is none to redeem it beside thee, and I am after thee. And the kinsman said, I will redeem it. - What is this going back to? The law of the land, the law of inheritance when it comes to land, read back in the book of Numbers. The husband died and the two sons died, and the only person left is the wife with the land; so she instinctively went to Boaz, and Boaz is now conducting the laws of the land of who it should be passed down to, going down the list of inheritance. Precepts: - Numbers 36:1-4 The chief fathers of Gilead brought the case of the daughters of Zelophehad: if the daughters married into another tribe, their inheritance would be taken from the inheritance of the fathers and put to the tribe wherein they were received, and fixed there at the jubile. - Numbers 36:5-9 The answer: let them marry to whom they think best, only to the family of the tribe of their father, so that no inheritance of the children of Israel remove from tribe to tribe. - Reading between the lines of verses two and three of Numbers 36: you are able to marry outside your particular tribe. You can be Judah and marry somebody from Manasseh; you can be Manasseh and marry somebody from Ephraim. Marrying outside the tribe was fine, and that is why they had this complaint; it just has to be within the twelve tribes of Israel, inside your nation, not outside the nation with the heathen. Ruth 4:5 - What day thou buyest the field of the hand of Naomi, thou must buy it also of Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of the dead, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance. Whoever took the land had to take the dead brother's wife with it; Ruth the Moabitess came along as a parcel of the land, to keep the name of Mahlon alive. - What law is that going back to? That law goes back to Deuteronomy 25, the duty of the husband's brother: the widow of the dead does not marry without unto a stranger, and the firstborn she bears succeeds in the name of the dead brother, that his name be not put out of Israel. This law was taught in full when it was read ahead at Ruth 1:6-9 in these notes: the firstborn carries the weight of the name, and the shoe was loosed from him that would not build up his brother's house. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 25:5-6 The wife of the dead shall not marry without unto a stranger; her husband's brother shall take her to wife, and the firstborn shall succeed in the name of his brother which is dead, that his name be not put out of Israel. - Deuteronomy 25:7-10 If the man refused, the widow loosed his shoe and spat in his face before the elders, because he would not build up his brother's house. - Genesis 49:3 The firstborn is the might and the beginning of strength, the excellency of dignity and power; you want somebody to carry on your name. - 1 Chronicles 5:1 Reuben was the firstborn, but because he defiled his father's bed his birthright was given unto the sons of Joseph; the birthright shows why the firstborn and the inheritance mattered so much in Israel. - Notice the bottom of verse 5: to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance. This law applies to inheritance; it went into the law of land being passed down. It does not apply today: your husband dying does not mean his brother now has to go in unto you and raise up children, because that duty was due to the law of inheritance, and Israel has no land inheritance in this captivity. It is wicked to pull that scripture today to try to get with your brother's widow. Ruth 4:6 - The kinsman said, I cannot redeem it for myself, lest I mar mine own inheritance: redeem thou my right to thyself, for I cannot redeem it. In other words, I already have kids in the way; I cannot do it, I am not doing it. Ruth 4:7-8 - Now this was the manner in former time in Israel concerning redeeming and concerning changing: for to confirm all things, a man plucked off his shoe and gave it to his neighbour, and this was a testimony in Israel. So the kinsman said unto Boaz, Buy it for thee, and he drew off his shoe. - You can read about that shoe back in Deuteronomy 25. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 25:9-10 The loosed shoe was the testimony in Israel against him that would not build up his brother's house; his name was called in Israel, The house of him that hath his shoe loosed. Ruth 4:9-10 - Boaz said unto the elders and unto all the people, Ye are witnesses this day that I have bought all that was Elimelech's, and all that was Chilion's and Mahlon's, of the hand of Naomi; moreover Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of Mahlon, have I purchased to be my wife, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance, that the name of the dead be not cut off from among his brethren, and from the gate of his place. - What law is Boaz exercising in this? Love thy neighbour as thyself. That is what Boaz was putting into place and applying, and that is why he is mentioned in the scriptures. Precepts: - Leviticus 19:18 Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself: the law Boaz was exercising toward his dead kinsman's house. Ruth 4:11-12 - All the people that were in the gate and the elders said, We are witnesses. They blessed the marriage: the Lord make the woman that is come into thine house like Rachel and like Leah, which two did build the house of Israel; and let thy house be like the house of Pharez, whom Tamar bare unto Judah, of the seed which the Lord shall give thee of this young woman. - In that blessing they are prophesying about David to come. Ruth 4:13-15 - So Boaz took Ruth, and she was his wife; and when he went in unto her, the Lord gave her conception, and she bare a son. - The women said unto Naomi, Blessed be the Lord, which hath not left thee this day without a kinsman, that his name may be famous in Israel; he shall be unto thee a restorer of thy life, and a nourisher of thine old age: for thy daughter in law, which loveth thee, which is better to thee than seven sons, hath born him. Ruth 4:16-17 - Naomi took the child, and laid it in her bosom, and became nurse unto it; and the women her neighbours gave it a name, saying, There is a son born to Naomi; and they called his name Obed: he is the father of Jesse, the father of David. - Why did Naomi take that child from Ruth the Moabitess? Because it is not the custom of Israel to allow a child to be raised up under the hand of a heathen. Although Ruth was used to keep Mahlon's name alive in Israel, and although she was brought in, she was a vessel; she did not have the same standing of rights as an Israelite woman, and she had no hand in raising the child. Naomi took it and raised it as her own, so that it could learn the ways of Israel. Precepts: - Nehemiah 13:23-24 Nehemiah saw Jews that had married wives of Ashdod, of Ammon, and of Moab, and Ruth was of Moab; their children spake half in the speech of Ashdod, and could not speak in the Jews' language. - A child's first teacher is the mother: she is the one who nurses him, he spends all his time with her, and he takes on her ways. So what Naomi did in the spirit, she did immediately after that child was born: she took it and raised it as her own. Notice the neighbours said, There is a son born to Naomi; Naomi did not bear that son, Ruth did, but she took it as her own. Ruth 4:18-22 - Now these are the generations of Pharez: Pharez is of Judah, so this is the lineage of Judah, how they came about right down to the king. Pharez begat Hezron, and Hezron begat Ram, and Ram begat Amminadab, and Amminadab begat Nahshon, and Nahshon begat Salmon, and Salmon begat Boaz, and Boaz begat Obed, and Obed begat Jesse, and Jesse begat David. - We read that lineage in Matthew chapter 1: how David came about, how Solomon came about, ultimately down to Christ. Precepts: - Matthew 1:5-6 Salmon begat Booz of Rachab, and Booz begat Obed of Ruth, and Obed begat Jesse, and Jesse begat David the king; the same lineage runs on down to Christ. --- Topics: Esau and Edom ← Ruth 1-3 · Ruth Study · 1 Samuel 1-3 →

title: 1 Samuel 1: Hannah's Vow and the Birth of Samuel
text: ← Ruth 4 · 1 Samuel Study · 1 Samuel 4-7 → 1 Samuel 1: Hannah's Vow and the Birth of Samuel Read the chapter → 1 Samuel 1 Introduction This session covers Ruth 4 together with 1 Samuel 1-3; these notes cover 1 Samuel 1 through 3. With first Samuel the class gets into the history of Israel, our people, as we move through the Bible. The main threads of the teaching: Hannah barren and provoked by her adversary, the vow of the Nazarite she vowed for a man child, the petition granted according to the will of the Most High, the vow paid when Samuel is lent to the Lord all the days of his life, Hannah's prophecy that they that stumbled are girded with strength, the sons of Eli who were sons of Belial and knew not the Lord, the judgment on the house of Eli for honouring his sons above the Most High, and the Lord coming and standing to reveal himself to Samuel, the same way he stands at the door of the spirit of all Israel and knocks. 1 Samuel 1:1-3 - There was a certain man of mount Ephraim named Elkanah, and he had two wives: the name of the one was Hannah, and the name of the other Peninnah. Peninnah had children, but Hannah had no children. - Elkanah went up out of his city yearly to worship and to sacrifice unto the Lord of hosts in Shiloh, where the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, the priests of the Lord, were. Shiloh is another name for Jerusalem. 1 Samuel 1:4-7 - When Elkanah offered, he gave to Peninnah his wife and to all her sons and her daughters portions; but unto Hannah he gave a worthy portion, for he loved Hannah: but the Lord had shut up her womb. - Her adversary provoked her sore, to make her fret, because the Lord had shut up her womb; year by year, when she went up to the house of the Lord, she provoked her, so that Hannah wept and did not eat. The women of Israel have not changed one bit: even back in the times of Samuel there was a sister vexing a barren woman and rubbing it in her face. Sisters of Israel have to get their spirits right; no doubt about it, you are Israel. 1 Samuel 1:8 - Elkanah her husband said to her, Hannah, why weepest thou? and why eatest thou not? and why is thy heart grieved? am not I better to thee than ten sons? 1 Samuel 1:9-11 - Hannah rose up after they had eaten in Shiloh, and in bitterness of soul she prayed unto the Lord and wept sore, while Eli the priest sat upon a seat by a post of the temple of the Lord. - She vowed a vow: O Lord of hosts, if thou wilt indeed look on the affliction of thine handmaid, and remember me, and give unto thine handmaid a man child, then I will give him unto the Lord all the days of his life, and there shall no rasor come upon his head. What law is that going back to? The law of the Nazarite. Put some things together as you read through Samuel about Samuel. Precepts: - Numbers 6:5 All the days of the vow of his separation no rasor comes upon his head; he shall be holy, and shall let the locks of the hair of his head grow. - The locks of a Nazarite are hair braided so that it locks into place as it grows long; when you braid your hair you are locking it in. You read of the locks of Samson's hair back in the book of Judges; Samson was under that same vow. Precepts: - Judges 16:13 Samson spoke of the seven locks of his head; the locks of the Nazarite vow. 1 Samuel 1:12-18 - As she continued praying before the Lord, Eli marked her mouth. Hannah spake in her heart; only her lips moved, but her voice was not heard: therefore Eli thought she had been drunken, and said, How long wilt thou be drunken? put away thy wine from thee. - Hannah answered, No, my lord, I am a woman of a sorrowful spirit: I have drunk neither wine nor strong drink, but have poured out my soul before the Lord; count not thine handmaid for a daughter of Belial. Then Eli answered, Go in peace: and the God of Israel grant thee thy petition that thou hast asked of him. - So the woman went her way, and did eat, and her countenance was no more sad. What did she do? She believed when she heard the word of Eli. - Why did the Lord grant her petition? It was the will of the Most High for Samuel to come through Hannah; it was just in his time. And she was granted it because of what she did before she even asked: she kept his commandments and did those things that are pleasing in his sight. Precepts: - 1 John 5:14-15 This is the confidence that we have in him: if we ask any thing according to his will, he heareth us, and we have the petitions that we desired of him. - 1 John 3:22 Whatsoever we ask, we receive of him, because we keep his commandments, and do those things that are pleasing in his sight. - Understand this: a lot of us pray for things that the Lord has not given to us. The Most High has the infinite and ultimate wisdom and knows what is best for us, so some things he keeps back from us; we have to accept that and know that. If we keep the commandments and it be his will, we receive whatsoever we ask, in his time; if it is not his will, we will not receive it. 1 Samuel 1:19-20 - They rose up in the morning early, worshipped before the Lord, and returned to their house to Ramah; they went back up north, for Elkanah came out of mount Ephraim. And Elkanah knew Hannah his wife: knew means he laid with her, they had laid down together; and the Lord remembered her. - When the time was come about after Hannah had conceived, she bare a son and called his name Samuel, saying, Because I have asked him of the Lord. Samuel means asked of the Lord. 1 Samuel 1:21 - The man Elkanah, and all his house, went up to offer unto the Lord the yearly sacrifice, and his vow. What is that yearly sacrifice going into? Deuteronomy 16:16. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 16:16 Three times in a year shall all thy males appear before the Lord: in the feast of unleavened bread, which is known as Passover; in the feast of weeks, which is known as Pentecost; and in the feast of tabernacles, which is also known as the feast of booths. Elkanah, who lived in mount Ephraim, was applying this law over and over again. 1 Samuel 1:22-23 - But Hannah went not up; she said unto her husband, I will not go up until the child be weaned, and then I will bring him, that he may appear before the Lord, and there abide for ever. A weaned child was three or four years old; that would be the last time he was under her care, so she said, I am not going up until that happens. - Elkanah said unto her, Do what seemeth thee good; tarry until thou have weaned him; only the Lord establish his word. She did not have to go up: the law said all thy males. So the woman abode, and gave her son suck until she weaned him. 1 Samuel 1:24-28 - When she had weaned him, she took him up with her, with three bullocks, and one ephah of flour, and a bottle of wine, and brought him unto the house of the Lord in Shiloh: and the child was young. - She said to Eli, I am the woman that stood by thee here, praying unto the Lord. For this child I prayed; and the Lord hath given me my petition which I asked of him: therefore also I have lent him to the Lord; as long as he liveth he shall be lent to the Lord. That is great faith right there that Hannah had, and she kept her promise: Hannah was an upright and honest woman. Precepts: - Ecclesiastes 5:4-6 When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay. The angel before whom you must not say it was an error is your personal angel, your guardian angel for lack of a better word, that watches over you and listens to you; do not say, I did not mean to say that. Yes you did; the angel recorded it and knew exactly what it was. - Matthew 5:37 That is why Christ went on to say, Let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay. Whatever comes out of your mouth, be upright and honest, and do that which comes out of thy mouth. 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed Read the chapter → 1 Samuel 2 1 Samuel 2:1-2 - Hannah prayed, and said, My heart rejoiceth in the Lord, mine horn is exalted in the Lord: I rejoice in thy salvation. There is none holy as the Lord: for there is none beside thee: neither is there any rock like our God. 1 Samuel 2:3 - Talk no more so exceeding proudly; let not arrogancy come out of your mouth: for the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed. What the Lord weighs is actions: if it came out of your mouth, are you going to do it? - All of us in this walk, keeping the commandments and the faith in Christ, have taken covenant and proclaimed out of our mouths that we are going to endure to the end; we broke the bread and drank the wine and took the covenant with the Lord. Now the Lord is judging you by your actions: are you going to endure to the end, whether to Christ's return or until you leave this earth, if you truly love him? Precepts: - Luke 6:46 Why call ye me, Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say? You cannot just say you love the Lord, that you believe in the God of Israel, and do nothing of what he says: not loving your neighbour, holding grudges and envy, respecting leadership above your own husband who is Christ in the house. - Hebrews 10:7 Lo, I come, in the volume of the book it is written of me, to do thy will, O God. The letters of Paul, the book of Samuel, the book of Genesis, the laws of Moses: everything we read ultimately leads up to the life of Christ and his return, and all of it is the spirit of Christ telling you to do those things. - Matthew 12:36-37 Every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment; by thy words thou shalt be justified, and by thy words thou shalt be condemned. Make sure what comes out of your mouth is calculated; that whole "we were arguing and it just slipped" will not fly on judgment day. Repent, and make a door and a bar for thy mouth, as the scriptures say. - "I have a personal relationship with God; God knows my heart; God loves me no matter what": that is arrogancy coming out of the mouth. The scripture says he loves you if you keep the commandments. 1 Samuel 2:4-5 - The bows of the mighty men are broken, and they that stumbled are girded with strength. The Lord is prophesying through Hannah here. Precepts: - Zechariah 12:7-8 The Lord shall save the tents of Judah first, that the inhabitants of Jerusalem, which were Benjamin and Levi in there with Judah, do not magnify themselves against Judah. That is why you see so many of Judah, Benjamin, and Levi in the truth right now, with the northern kingdom trickling in; the Most High gives the head tribes what is most important first, not worldly things but the truth of who they are, to raise up the twelve tribes of Jacob. And he that is feeble among them at that day shall be as David, and the house of David shall be as God: all twelve tribes, as the angel of the Lord before them. - Psalms 18:29 David said, by my God have I leaped over a wall; David was a mighty man of war. - Psalms 18:33-34 His feet like hinds' feet, fast like a deer, and a bow of steel broken by his arms: David bent steel, took down lions and bears, and killed a giant with a rock and a sling. He that is feeble shall be as David goes right back to they that stumbled are girded with strength; that is the house of Israel. - They that were full have hired out themselves for bread: so that the barren hath born seven, and she that hath many children is waxed feeble. Hannah is talking about herself there. 1 Samuel 2:6 - The Lord killeth, and maketh alive: he bringeth down to the grave, and bringeth up. The Lord decides who wakes up and the Lord decides who passes; that is all of the Lord. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 32:39 See now that I, even I, am he, and there is no god with me: I kill, and I make alive; I wound, and I heal: neither is there any that can deliver out of my hand. There is no Buddha, there is no Allah, there is no Krishna; all of that is made-up imaginations of men. 1 Samuel 2:7 - The Lord maketh poor, and maketh rich: he bringeth low, and lifteth up.
