Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 11:14 For your newer brothers and sisters, Ecclesiasticus is the book also called Sirach: prosperity and adversity, life and death, poverty and riches, all come of the Lord. 1 Samuel 2:8 - He raiseth up the poor out of the dust: out of the dust means out of confusion; he brings the poor out of confusion, and lifteth up the beggar from the dunghill, to set them among princes, and to make them inherit the throne of glory: for the pillars of the earth are the Lord's, and he hath set the world upon them. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 11:5 How is that possible? It is the Lord: he brings low, and he lifts up one that was never thought of. Like David: when Samuel looked at the older brother he thought, he has to be the one, he looks like a king; but the Lord chose the one sitting down upon the ground whom nobody thought of to be the king. 1 Samuel 2:9-10 - He will keep the feet of his saints, and the wicked shall be silent in darkness; for by strength shall no man prevail. The adversaries of the Lord shall be broken to pieces; and he shall give strength unto his king, which is Christ, and exalt the horn of his anointed. 1 Samuel 2:11-12 - Elkanah went to Ramah to his house, and the child did minister unto the Lord before Eli the priest. Now the sons of Eli were sons of Belial; they knew not the Lord. They were the devil. - They were Levites, priests in the house of the Lord doing the work of the Lord, and yet it says they knew not the Lord. Why? Because they did not keep the commandments true in their spirit; they kept it on the surface where you can see it. They looked the part: they had on the fringes, they had the beard, they showed up on the sabbath day; but their spirit was not right with the Lord, and they were really the sons of the devil. Do not let that be you, Israel. 1 Samuel 2:13-14 - The priests' custom with the people was that when any man offered sacrifice, the priest's servant came, while the flesh was in seething, with a fleshhook of three teeth in his hand, and struck it into the pan, or kettle, or caldron, or pot; all that the fleshhook brought up the priest took for himself. They would dip it in, and what came up was the priest's portion of meat for that day; all the Levites did that, based on the sacrifices Israel brought in. - This is how the Lord took care of Levi. He told Levi in the law that Levi would have no inheritance of land among the tribes; the Lord provided for them through the sacrifices that Israel brought, so they had need of nothing. 1 Samuel 2:15-17 - Also, before they burnt the fat, the priest's servant came and said to the man that sacrificed, Give flesh to roast for the priest; for he will not have sodden flesh of thee, but raw: I will cook it up my own way, give it to me now, before it is done. And if any man said, Let them not fail to burn the fat presently, and then take as much as thy soul desireth, he would answer, Nay; but thou shalt give it me now: and if not, I will take it by force. - These were devils serving in the house of the Lord, strong-arming the offerings. Wherefore the sin of the young men was very great before the Lord: for men abhorred the offering of the Lord. These priests were disrespecting the offering of the Lord. 1 Samuel 2:18-21 - But Samuel ministered before the Lord, being a child, girded with a linen ephod; moreover his mother made him a little coat, and brought it to him from year to year, when she came up with her husband to offer the yearly sacrifice. - Eli blessed Elkanah and his wife, saying, The Lord give thee seed of this woman for the loan which is lent to the Lord. And the Lord visited Hannah, so that she conceived and bare three sons and two daughters; and the child Samuel grew before the Lord. 1 Samuel 2:22-26 - Eli was very old, and heard all that his sons did unto all Israel, and how they lay with the women that assembled at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation: the harlots hanging around the temple, and Eli's sons dealing with them. - He said unto them, Why do ye such things? for I hear of your evil dealings by all this people; ye make the Lord's people to transgress. The Levites were the leaders, so the people followed their actions: what the priests did, the people did also. They saw the sons of Eli sleeping with the harlots and said, it must be all right, look what they have, look how they live in the temple; let us follow their lead. - Notwithstanding they hearkened not unto the voice of their father, because the Lord would slay them. And the child Samuel grew on, and was in favour both with the Lord, and also with men. - Eli might have said something to his children, but he did not remove them and put them out of the priesthood for their evil dealings; he said something, but he did not go further than words, he took no action with it. Watch what happened to his children. 1 Samuel 2:27-29 - There came a man of God unto Eli, saying, Thus saith the Lord, Did I plainly appear unto the house of thy father, when they were in Egypt in Pharaoh's house? That is talking about Levi, going into Moses. Did I choose him out of all the tribes of Israel to be my priest, to offer upon mine altar, to burn incense, to wear an ephod before me? and did I give unto the house of thy father all the offerings made by fire of the children of Israel? They had need of nothing; they were well taken care of. - Wherefore kick ye at my sacrifice and at mine offering, which I have commanded in my habitation; and honourest thy sons above me? You are disrespecting me, is what he is saying: I am supposed to be honoured in everything before the children of Israel, and you let your sons disrespect my offerings. - Take that into account: do you honour your children above what the Lord says to do? Can they do no wrong, even when they are doing real wrong against the Lord, keeping no commandments, never showing up on the sabbath day, and still living under your roof grown? If they are of age, they know right from wrong, and they are under your roof while you keep the commandments, then they had better be keeping the commandments: showing up to every feast day, the blowing of trumpets, the day of atonement, the passover, the same as you. When they are of age they can go their own way; but they should not be living under your roof and breaking the commandments of God. You honour your children above God when you allow that. Precepts: - Joshua 24:15 As for me and my house, we will serve the Lord. 1 Samuel 2:30 - Wherefore the Lord God of Israel saith, I said indeed that thy house, and the house of thy father, should walk before me for ever: but now the Lord saith, Be it far from me; for them that honour me I will honour, and they that despise me shall be lightly esteemed. Lightly esteemed means the Lord is not really looking out for you: you are not thinking about me, so I am not thinking about you; go ahead and see how it works out for yourself. - That is why the Lord dealt with Abraham the way he did: Abraham was not going to choose his kids above the Most High, and they were going to do all that he commanded. Precepts: - Genesis 18:19 I know him, that he will command his children and his household after him, and they shall keep the way of the Lord, to do justice and judgment. The Most High said, I know how Abraham gets down; he is not going to let his kids be out of order. - Genesis 26:5 Because that Abraham obeyed my voice, and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws. This is what was going on in the tent of Abraham as long as he lived: all the laws that applied to Abraham at that time, he kept them, the sabbath day included; other laws would apply after Israel came out of Egypt. 1 Samuel 2:31-33 - Behold, the days come, that I will cut off thine arm, and the arm of thy father's house, that there shall not be an old man in thine house. Cutting off the arm means cutting off thy strength: it was talking about his children. He was going to kill Eli's descendants young, and all the increase of his house would die in the flower of their age, in the full strength and peak of their youth. - Why would the Lord judge the children of future generations of Eli's house? The thought might be, he is killing them for the sins of their forefather; I thought the sons did not die for the fathers. Ezekiel 18 shows what it is talking about: the judgment falls on the son that continues in the sins of his father. Precepts: - Ezekiel 18:10-13 If he beget a son that is a robber, a shedder of blood, that lifts up his eyes to the idols and commits abomination, he shall not live: he hath done all these abominations; he shall surely die; his blood shall be upon him. The son that continues in the sins of his father dies for his own doings. - Ezekiel 18:14-17 But if he beget a son that seeth all his father's sins which he hath done, and considereth, and doeth not such like, he shall not die for the iniquity of his father; he shall surely live. Eating upon the mountains is partaking in the heathen's idol worship, the food and the drink that went into it, as when Israel rose up to eat and to play before the calf. - So why would the Lord cut off all those descendants of Eli in the strength of their youth? Because they were going to follow in the same way of their fathers, the sons of Belial, doing wickedness and evil; because Eli did not reprove his sons, the generations after would follow right in their footsteps. 1 Samuel 2:34-35 - And this shall be a sign unto thee, that shall come upon thy two sons, on Hophni and Phinehas: in one day they shall die both of them. And I will raise me up a faithful priest, that shall do according to that which is in mine heart and in my mind; and I will build him a sure house, and he shall walk before mine anointed for ever. - That is the same man we have to be: faithful unto the Lord, doing all that is in his heart and in his mind, not in our own. We cannot lean upon our own understanding, and we cannot lean upon our own emotions and how we feel; in whatever situation, at any given moment, it is what did the Lord say. Do not let the old man guide you and lead you; it should be the spirit of Christ which is in you, the hidden man. Precepts: - Proverbs 3:5 Trust in the Lord with all thine heart, and lean not unto thine own understanding. 1 Samuel 2:36 - It shall come to pass, that every one that is left in thine house shall come and crouch to him for a piece of silver and a morsel of bread. The Lord was going to make it hard on the descendants of Eli: he removed them from the priesthood, and it was written down that the descendants of Eli were not to be allowed into the house of the Lord any more. - Remember, Levi was given no inheritance of land; so how would they eat, how would they live, how would they survive? Receiving their inheritance and their goods was based on them doing what thus saith the Lord told them to do, teaching the laws. Cut off from the priesthood, Eli's house was left to beg. 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel Read the chapter → 1 Samuel 3 1 Samuel 3:1 - The child Samuel ministered unto the Lord before Eli. And the word of the Lord was precious in those days; there was no open vision. Precious means the Lord was not dealing with everybody: he was not dealing with the priests, and there were no prophets around saying, thus saith the Lord. The word was about to go only to Samuel. 1 Samuel 3:2-3 - Eli was laid down in his place, his eyes beginning to wax dim, and ere the lamp of God went out in the temple of the Lord, where the ark of God was, Samuel was laid down to sleep. Ere means before: before the lamp of God went out. That light in the temple by the ark was never to go out, though at a point in time it did go out. Precepts: - Exodus 27:20-21 The children of Israel brought pure oil olive beaten for the light, to cause the lamp to burn always; Aaron and his sons ordered it from evening to morning before the Lord, a statute for ever. - Christ spoke about that fire in the temple: on the sabbath days the priests in the temple profane the sabbath, and are blameless. Israel was not to kindle a fire on the sabbath when it comes to food, but the priests had to keep that fire burning, and they sacrificed on the sabbath days, a lamb in the morning and a lamb in the evening; they broke the sabbath yet are blameless, because they were doing thus saith the Lord. Precepts: - Matthew 12:5-7 Have ye not read in the law, how that on the sabbath days the priests in the temple profane the sabbath, and are blameless? In this place is one greater than the temple; and if ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless. - Numbers 28:9-10 The burnt offering of every sabbath: the priests sacrificed a lamb in the morning and in the evening on the sabbath because the Lord commanded it. - Sacrifice was never the most important thing to the Lord; not the blood of bulls and of goats, but mercy upon one another and the keeping of the commandments. The sacrifices were added because of transgression, the animal's blood taken in your place so the Most High would not have to kill you; you read of it from Genesis 3, where the Lord took the skins after Adam sinned. Yet there were some things you could not sacrifice for, abominations for which a man's own blood was required. Precepts: - Hosea 6:6 I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings. This is what Christ was quoting, for the New Testament was not yet written; the knowledge of God is the keeping of the commandments. - Jeremiah 7:21-23 I spake not unto your fathers, nor commanded them in the day that I brought them out of the land of Egypt, concerning burnt offerings or sacrifices: but this thing commanded I them, saying, Obey my voice, and I will be your God, and ye shall be my people. - Exodus 19:3-6 Before the Most High even gave the ten commandments he made this plain: if ye will obey my voice indeed, and keep my covenant, then ye shall be a peculiar treasure unto me above all people, a kingdom of priests, and an holy nation. Obedience is what he desired most from the beginning. 1 Samuel 3:4-7 - The Lord called Samuel, and he answered, Here am I, and ran unto Eli; and Eli said, I called not; lie down again. The Lord called yet again, and again Samuel went to Eli. Now Samuel did not yet know the Lord, neither was the word of the Lord yet revealed unto him. - Look at that. Samuel had been in the house of the Lord since he was weaned, three or four years old, and he still did not know the Lord. This goes in on those playing church with their children: just because your children come and sit and listen to the teaching does not mean they know the Lord; they are there because you brought them there. They can hear all the words they want, but until the Lord reveals himself to them, they do not know him. What makes your kid so special, greater than Samuel? - Do not have your children going into a covenant with Christ that he will judge them for if they break it; the scripture says, for this cause many are weak and sickly among you, and many sleep. You do not know if your kids are going to serve the Lord when they go out on their own, or what kind of lusts are in them that will draw them away into the world when they come of age. It is your job as a parent to train them up and pray they stay in it: kids learn by watching, so let them see you take that covenant over and over again until they are ready, and make them rehearse the righteous acts. When the child comes to the age of reasoning and knows the Lord for himself, and the Lord reveals himself to him, you will know it; do not rush it. Precepts: - Proverbs 22:6 Train up a child in the way he should go: your job is the training; the revealing belongs to the Most High. - 1 Corinthians 11:29-30 He that eateth and drinketh unworthily, eateth and drinketh damnation to himself; for this cause many are weak and sickly among you, and many sleep. That covenant is not to be forced on children who do not yet know the Lord. - No one knows the Father until Christ reveals him, because Christ is the mediator. That is why our brothers and sisters caught up in Christianity and Islam do not know the Most High: he has not been revealed to them, and they have not been shown who they are. The word comes down in order, from the Most High to Christ, to the angels, and into our spirit when it is time to wake up; the Most High does not deal with us directly right now, because we are too full of sin. Precepts: - Matthew 11:27 No man knoweth the Son, but the Father; neither knoweth any man the Father, save the Son, and he to whomsoever the Son will reveal him. - John 14:26 The Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance. - Revelation 1:1 The Revelation of Jesus Christ, which God gave unto him, and he sent and signified it by his angel unto his servant John: that is the order, from the Most High to Christ to the angels to the servants; that is how the word comes down and how Israel wakes up. 1 Samuel 3:8-9 - The Lord called Samuel again the third time, and Eli perceived that the Lord had called the child; therefore Eli said unto Samuel, Go, lie down: and it shall be, if he call thee, that thou shalt say, Speak, Lord; for thy servant heareth. - The Lord is merciful with us even in these days, in this wickedness: he calls out to us numerous times until we wake up. We do not know who is chosen, so we never know when we are going to wake up; it might be the first time, the second time, or the third time you hear the voice of the Lord calling. Some heard the call the first time because the Most High ordained them to be built up as leaders, to get the spirits of the world off of them so they could be a righteous example and a fit guide for you; you came in at the third call, after they were prepared. Your job is not to try to supersede those that came in before you, but to follow them; God set it up that way for a reason. 1 Samuel 3:10 - And the Lord came and stood, and called as at other times, Samuel, Samuel. The Lord did not just call from the heavens: the Lord came down and stood by Samuel and called out to him. That is cold-blooded. Samuel could not see him, but he heard him; that is what happens in the spirit to all of us. - Notice in the scriptures that the Most High calls the name two times: Moses, Moses; Samuel, Samuel. That may be a question to ask Christ, Lord's will, for him that endures to the end. - What was happening spiritually when the Most High was revealing himself to Samuel and about to pour his word into him? The same thing that happens to all Israel: he stands at the door and knocks. That door is your spirit. The knocking is the Lord calling out through the videos, the flyers, the four chapters a day, the classes; that is the Lord standing and knocking at the spirit of all Israel before he cuts you off. Precepts: - Revelation 3:20 Behold, I stand at the door, and knock: if any man hear my voice, and open the door, I will come in to him, and will sup with him, and he with me. Opening the door is repentance: put away the drugs, the whoredom, and the ways of the world, apply thus saith the Lord, and you will be full of the Lord. - John 10:7-9 I am the door of the sheep: by me if any man enter in, he shall be saved. This is the way the sheep go through; this is how they get to the Most High: they come through Christ. - Proverbs 1:23-26 Turn you at my reproof: behold, I will pour out my spirit unto you, I will make known my words unto you. That is exactly what was read of Samuel: the word of the Lord was not yet revealed to him, and when the Lord called and he turned, the word was made known to him. But because I have called, and ye refused, I also will laugh at your calamity. - Proverbs 1:27-31 Then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer; they shall seek me early, but they shall not find me: for they hated knowledge, the laws, and would none of my counsel: therefore shall they eat of the fruit of their own way. Refuse to turn from the drugs, and the drugs destroy you; refuse to stop fornicating, and the sex you love destroys you; refuse to give up the sabbath chasing money, and money destroys you. - So warn your brothers and sisters of the nation of Israel: when you hear the Lord calling, through this flyer, these scriptures, this video, turn at his reproof. We do not know when he will cut a man off and leave him to his own devices to destroy himself; and when he cries, the Lord will not hear. 1 Samuel 3:11-14 - The Lord said to Samuel, Behold, I will do a thing in Israel, at which both the ears of every one that heareth it shall tingle. In that day I will perform against Eli all things which I have spoken concerning his house: when I begin, I will also make an end. For I have told him that I will judge his house for ever for the iniquity which he knoweth; because his sons made themselves vile, and he restrained them not. Eli let his children break the commandments of the Lord and lead the people astray, and he restrained them not. - Therefore I have sworn unto the house of Eli, that the iniquity of Eli's house shall not be purged with sacrifice nor offering for ever. When the Lord is mad, the Lord is mad: thus we are in the lands of our captivity 400 years and counting, and you have heard the history of the Spanish Inquisition, how we were burned for keeping the commandments; his anger burns unto the lowest hell. - Do not let that be you. Do not let the Lord pass a judgment on your house where Christ prays for you and the Most High says, No, I will bring a judgment on his house for ever. Do not sin a sin so great that it cannot be prayed for, so that nothing is left but the fiery day of judgment. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 16:1-3 Desire not a multitude of unprofitable children: it is better to have none at all, and to die without children, than to have them that are ungodly and not be able to restrain them from doing evil. 1 Samuel 3:15-18 - Samuel lay until the morning, and opened the doors of the house of the Lord; and Samuel feared to shew Eli the vision. But Eli called him and said, What is the thing that the Lord hath said unto thee? I pray thee hide it not from me: God do so to thee, and more also, if thou hide any thing from me of all the things that he said unto thee. - Samuel was going to be a judge of Israel, and here is his first test as a judge: do not sugarcoat what the Lord has said, and do not trim your words to seek love. And Samuel told him every whit, and hid nothing from him. - Eli said, It is the Lord: let him do what seemeth him good. Eli had no control of his kids, but he accepted the judgment of the Lord: thy will be done. Maybe the Lord had mercy on Eli; that is of the Lord, and we will not know. Precepts: - Romans 9:15 I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy; whether mercy reached Eli is of the Lord. 1 Samuel 3:19-21 - Samuel grew, and the Lord was with him, and did let none of his words fall to the ground. What does that mean? What Samuel said, it came to pass. - All Israel from Dan even to Beersheba knew that Samuel was established to be a prophet of the Lord. And the Lord appeared again in Shiloh: for the Lord revealed himself to Samuel in Shiloh by the word of the Lord. - That is good history we read today about Samuel; take heed to what you have heard, and do not let it slip. Some of you may be in these same situations: putting other people before God, honouring your children above God and not restraining them, or hearing the Lord call once, twice, three times without answering the call. This history is here for us to learn from; use it, lest the judgments of God be passed upon us when he is angry, for whatever the Most High says, Christ follows, because that is the order: God, Christ, man, woman, children. Precepts: - Romans 15:4 Whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning. --- Topics: Idolatry · Sacrifice and Atonement · The Covenant · The Feasts of the Most High · The Priesthood · The Sabbath ← Ruth 4 · 1 Samuel Study · 1 Samuel 4-7 →

title: 1 Samuel 12: Turn Not Aside From Following the Lord
text: ← 1 Samuel 8-11 · 1 Samuel Study · 1 Samuel 16-19 → 1 Samuel 12: Turn Not Aside From Following the Lord Read the chapter → 1 Samuel 12 Introduction This session covers 1 Samuel 12 through 15, heavy chapters in the rise and fall of king Saul. In chapter 12 Samuel gives his farewell address: he establishes his own blamelessness, rehearses the righteous acts of the Most High from Egypt through the judges, rebukes Israel for demanding a king when the Lord was their king, and calls down thunder and rain in wheat harvest to prove the wickedness of that request. In chapter 13 Saul begins to show he is not fit to be king, making haste in time of trouble by offering the burnt offering instead of waiting for Samuel. In chapter 14 Jonathan and his armor bearer take on the Philistine garrison alone, showing there is no restraint to the Lord to save by many or by few. In chapter 15 the Lord commands Saul to utterly destroy Amalek; Saul obeys partially, and partial obedience is counted as rebellion: to obey is better than sacrifice, and rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft. 1 Samuel 12:1 - At the end of chapter 11 Israel crowned Saul at Gilgal. Back in chapter 8 the people had pressured Samuel because they wanted to be like the nations round about them, and the Most High led him to choose Saul the son of Kish. - This is the aftermath speech. Samuel is putting it on record: I hearkened unto your voice in all that ye said unto me and made a king over you; whatever happens from here came from what you asked for. 1 Samuel 12:2-5 - Samuel establishes his blamelessness before he reasons with them. He walked before Israel from his childhood unto this day; whose ox or ass has he taken, whom has he defrauded or oppressed, from whose hand has he taken any bribe? Speak up now and he will restore it. - The people answer that he has not defrauded nor oppressed them nor taken anything from any man's hand, and the Lord and his anointed are witness that day. Samuel was never a bad guy to the nation of Israel, and the whole congregation confirms it. 1 Samuel 12:6-7 - It is the Lord that advanced Moses and Aaron and brought your fathers up out of the land of Egypt. Now stand still, that Samuel may reason with them before the Lord of all the righteous acts of the Lord which he did to them and to their fathers. Precepts: - Psalms 103:7 He made known his ways unto Moses, his acts unto the children of Israel; the righteous acts Samuel rehearses are those acts. 1 Samuel 12:8-11 - When Jacob was come into Egypt and your fathers cried unto the Lord, the Lord sent Moses and Aaron and made Israel dwell in this place. When they forgat the Lord he sold them into the hand of Sisera, captain of the host of Hazor, and of the Philistines, and of the king of Moab; this is the history of the book of Judges, starting in chapter 4. - They cried unto the Lord and confessed they had sinned in forsaking him and serving Baalim and Ashtaroth. That is the same lesson Samuel taught in chapter 7: when the Philistines beat Israel, they went and got the ark of the covenant, got beat even worse, and lost the ark. It is not just about having the ark of the covenant among you; you have to put away the idols and stop serving Baalim and Ashtaroth. - So the Lord sent Jerubbaal, which is Gideon, and Bedan, and Jephthah, and Samuel, and delivered Israel out of the hand of their enemies on every side, and they dwelled safe. None of those saviors had to wear a crown. Precepts: - Judges 8:22 After Gideon led the three hundred, the men of Israel said, Rule thou over us, both thou and thy son and thy son's son also, for thou hast delivered us from the hand of Midian. - Judges 8:23 Gideon refused: I will not rule over you, neither shall my son rule over you; the Lord shall rule over you. He knew that if thrones were set up, the people would put their trust and faith in the king instead of the Most High; it was never the Lord's intention to set kings in the flesh over Israel, he was to be our king. 1 Samuel 12:12-15 - When Nahash king of the children of Ammon came against them, Israel said, Nay, but a king shall reign over us, when the Lord their God was their king. That demand exposed their disbelief in the Lord; they wanted a king they could see and touch, because all the nations around them had kings. - Now behold the king whom ye have chosen and whom ye have desired. If ye will fear the Lord and serve him and obey his voice and not rebel against the commandment of the Lord, then shall both ye and also the king that reigneth over you continue following the Lord your God. If you and your king do not rebel against the voice of the Lord, the ultimate king, you will be all right. - Moses, in the spirit of the Lord, knew exactly what Israel would do once they came into the land, and wrote the law of the king ahead of time. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 17:14 Moses prophesied Israel would come into the land and say, I will set a king over me, like as all the nations that are about me. - Deuteronomy 17:15 The king must be one whom the Lord thy God shall choose, one from among thy brethren; thou mayest not set a stranger over thee, which is not thy brother. - Deuteronomy 17:20 His heart must not be lifted up above his brethren, and he must not turn aside from the commandment to the right hand or to the left, to the end that he may prolong his days in his kingdom, he and his children in the midst of Israel; that is exactly what Samuel just told the people. - But if ye will not obey the voice of the Lord, but rebel against the commandment of the Lord, then shall the hand of the Lord be against you, as it was against your fathers. Samuel repeats it because Israelites require repetition. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 28:15 If thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes, all these curses shall come upon thee and overtake thee. - Deuteronomy 28:36 The Lord shall bring thee, and thy king which thou shalt set over thee, unto a nation which neither thou nor thy fathers have known; if you and your king disobey, the Lord sends you and your king into subjection to the other nations. 1 Samuel 12:16-18 - Is it not wheat harvest today? To demonstrate how wicked Israel was for asking a king, Samuel calls unto the Lord for thunder and rain on the very day they expected clear skies to gather the wheat. The Lord sent thunder and rain that day, and all the people greatly feared the Lord and Samuel. Precepts: - 2 Samuel 22:14 The Lord thundered from heaven, and the most High uttered his voice; imagine how terrified they were when that voice went off. - 2 Samuel 22:15 And he sent out arrows, and scattered them; lightning, and discomfited them; that is the power the Most High put on display. 1 Samuel 12:19 - Once the Lord thundered, the people acknowledged their folly: pray for thy servants unto the Lord thy God, that we die not, for we have added unto all our sins this evil, to ask us a king. Now they confess they were dead wrong for asking for a king. 1 Samuel 12:20 - Fear not: ye have done all this wickedness, yet turn not aside from following the Lord, but serve the Lord with all your heart. Yes, you did all this wickedness, but now you get it; after all the wickedness you have done, still serve the Lord. That is heavy. Precepts: - Proverbs 24:16 This is really a precept for the just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again; the fall does not end your service to the Most High. 1 Samuel 12:21 - Turn ye not aside, for then should ye go after vain things which cannot profit nor deliver, for they are vain. Something you make with your own hands is not going to make thunder and rain come on your harvest day to show you how wicked you are; idols cannot help you or save you. - Our people do the same thing today, icing out crosses and things of that nature that cannot do a thing for them; those are the vain things our people follow after. Samuel warned Israel not to do it, and over a span of time that is exactly what they ended up doing. Precepts: - Jeremiah 2:5 What iniquity have your fathers found in me, that they are gone far from me, and have walked after vanity, and are become vain? 1 Samuel 12:22 - The Lord will not forsake his people for his great name's sake, because it hath pleased the Lord to make you his people. That is part of the comfort of the scriptures: he may purge his people, but he will never exterminate the Israelites, for his name's sake. - Test that against the doctrine that says the Most High cast off Israel after Christ. Paul, whose writings that doctrine misinterprets, said the same thing Samuel said. Precepts: - Romans 11:1 Hath God cast away his people? God forbid. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin. - Romans 11:2 God hath not cast away his people which he foreknew; the Lord has not cast off Israel. 1 Samuel 12:23 - Marinate on this verse. God forbid that I should sin against the Lord in ceasing to pray for you; but I will teach you the good and the right way. Samuel says that as a leader who loved his nation, if he stopped praying for them, that itself would put him in sin. - For those who battle with prayer, meditate on that: ceasing to pray for your nation puts you in sin. Precepts: - Job 15:4 Yea, thou castest off fear, and restrainest prayer before God; restraining prayer shows you are starting to lack fear of the Most High. If you want him in your life, you cannot restrain prayer from him, any more than you would let communication die with someone you wanted to keep. 1 Samuel 12:24-25 - Only fear the Lord and serve him in truth with all your heart, and consider how great things he hath done for you. But if ye shall still do wickedly, after the speech, the warning, and the thunder, ye shall be consumed, both ye and your king. - That is what Deuteronomy 28:36 said: you and the king you set over you will be brought into subjection to the other nations. Samuel's exhortation was to get their minds on the right track: you asked for the wrong thing, but now that you have it, keep the commandments and you will be all right. 1 Samuel 13: Make Not Haste in Time of Trouble Read the chapter → 1 Samuel 13 1 Samuel 13:1-4 - Chapter 13 is the beginning of Saul showing his simplicity, the beginning of the proof that he is not fit to be king over Israel. - Saul chose three thousand men, two thousand with him in Michmash and mount Bethel and a thousand with Jonathan in Gibeah of Benjamin. Jonathan smote the garrison of the Philistines in Geba, and the Philistines heard of it; Saul blew the trumpet throughout all the land, and Israel was had in abomination with the Philistines. His son popped off the battle, so now it is war time. 1 Samuel 13:5-7 - The Philistines gathered thirty thousand chariots, six thousand horsemen, and people as the sand on the seashore, far deeper than the three thousand Israel had prepared. When the men of Israel saw they were in a strait, they hid themselves in caves, thickets, rocks, high places, and pits; some Hebrews fled over Jordan, and the people that followed Saul followed him trembling. - The sons of God, the mighty men of valor, saw the enemy coming and started hiding. As the chosen people, if we really have faith we should be fearless; the Lord had just defeated the Philistines for Israel in chapter 7. To still fear the enemy shows a lack of faith, that you really do not believe in your God. - Nehemiah shows the right spirit. In the Persian captivity he had liberty from the king to rebuild the walls of Jerusalem, and the enemies Sanballat, Tobiah, and Geshem plotted to scare him off the work. A hired man urged him to hide in the temple because they were coming to slay him, and Nehemiah refused; operating in the spirit of fear is sin according to the scripture. Precepts: - Nehemiah 6:10-11 Shemaiah counseled Nehemiah to hide in the temple because they will come to slay thee; Nehemiah answered, Should such a man as I flee? He was the governor the Most High set up for everybody to look up to, and he would not go in. - Nehemiah 6:12-13 Nehemiah perceived that God had not sent him, but that Tobiah and Sanballat had hired him, that he should be afraid, and do so, and sin, and that they might have matter for an evil report to reproach him; fear in the leader would let the enemy call him weak and unfit to lead. - 2 Timothy 1:7 The Lord did not give us the spirit of fear; for the people of the Most High, fearfulness before the enemy is unbelief. - Ecclesiasticus 10:2 If the ruler is a coward, so goes the rest of the nation; that is why the leader must be fearless, because the hearts of the people depend upon their leadership. - James 3:1 That is why the scriptures say the greater condemnation: if you aspire to leadership, make sure your spirit is right, because if you fold when you are tried, you are accountable for all the souls that fold right along with you. 1 Samuel 13:8-10 - Samuel had instructed Saul in chapter 10: when you get to Gilgal, tarry seven days, make no moves until I arrive. Saul tarried seven days according to the set time, but Samuel came not at the moment expected, and the people were scattered from him and acting frantic. - Saul said, Bring hither a burnt offering to me, and he offered the burnt offering, and Saul is not the priest; that is Samuel's office. And it came to pass that as soon as he had made an end of offering the burnt offering, behold, Samuel came. He was barely late, and Saul could not hold his patience. - Brothers do the same thing today: leadership said it would be here at ten, it is five past ten, so we cancel the plan and go home. Be humble and tarry like you were instructed; it may run some minutes over, and the Lord may be testing your patience. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 2:2 Saul made haste in a time of trouble; he panicked and did unadvisedly, and he is going to suffer consequences for it. 1 Samuel 13:11-12 - Samuel asks, What hast thou done? Saul answers with excuses: the people were scattered from me, thou camest not within the days appointed, the Philistines gathered at Michmash, so I forced myself and offered a burnt offering. This is part of Saul's pattern of behavior; he never wants to hold himself accountable, he always deflects onto whoever else. Precepts: - Isaiah 58:9 Then shalt thou call, and the Lord shall answer, if thou take away from the midst of thee the yoke and the putting forth of the finger; the Most High says stop playing the blame game if you want him to intervene on your behalf, but pointing the finger is exactly what Saul did. 1 Samuel 13:13-14 - Samuel does not entertain the excuses: thou hast done foolishly; thou hast not kept the commandment of the Lord thy God. Saul thought he was only bending Samuel's word, but disobeying the instruction was disobeying the commandment of the Lord. - For now would the Lord have established thy kingdom upon Israel for ever; but now thy kingdom shall not continue. For that one act of foolishness the Lord withdrew what he would have given: Saul's lineage ruling Israel. - The Lord wants to see whether you will perform what he told you to do even when things do not work out how you planned; that is what proves you faithful in temptation and worthy of being exalted. Saul failed that test in the time of his distress. - The Lord hath sought him a man after his own heart to be captain over his people. Samuel prophesied this without ever having met the replacement; that man is David, predestined before he is even introduced in the scriptures. Precepts: - 1 Maccabees 2:52-53 Abraham drew down with the knife even when it made no fleshly sense, and Joseph, betrayed and tempted, kept the commandment in the time of his distress and was exalted to be lord of Egypt; loyalty to the Lord regardless of circumstances is what the trial is for. - Acts 13:22 When he had removed Saul, he raised up unto them David to be their king: I have found David the son of Jesse, a man after mine own heart, which shall fulfil all my will. 1 Samuel 13:15-18 - Samuel went up from Gilgal to Gibeah of Benjamin, and Saul numbered the people present with him, about six hundred men. The Philistines encamped in Michmash, and the spoilers came out of their camp in three companies, toward Ophrah, toward Bethhoron, and toward the border overlooking the valley of Zeboim; three raiding parties sent out to invade Israel. 1 Samuel 13:19-23 - There was no smith found throughout all the land of Israel, for the Philistines said, Lest the Hebrews make them swords or spears. The Israelites had to go down to the Philistines to sharpen every man his share, his coulter, his axe, and his mattock, so the Philistines knew exactly how disarmed Israel was; all they had was a file for the tools. - This is heavy for today. A people that must depend on its adversary for weaponry cannot deliver itself by arms; talk of going to war means nothing when you have to buy your weapons from the very gun store of the ones you say you will fight. Same picture as the scriptures. - So in the day of battle there was neither sword nor spear in the hand of any of the people, but with Saul and with Jonathan his son was there found; only two men in the army had a blade. - In chapter 13 Saul blew the kingdom with his instability in a time of distress. The Most High said, You are not fit; I would have established you, but your replacement is already on the way. 1 Samuel 14: By Many or by Few Read the chapter → 1 Samuel 14 1 Samuel 14:1-3 - Jonathan said unto the young man that bare his armor, Come, let us go over to the Philistines' garrison on the other side; but he told not his father. Saul tarried under a pomegranate tree in Migron with about six hundred men, with Ahiah the priest wearing an ephod, and the people knew not that Jonathan was gone. 1 Samuel 14:4-6 - Between the passages were two sharp rocks, Bozez and Seneh, one facing Michmash and the other Gibeah. Jonathan said, Come, let us go over unto the garrison of these uncircumcised; it may be that the Lord will work for us: for there is no restraint to the Lord to save by many or by few. - The Lord put that spirit on Jonathan. That is how the Most High operates: he loves to show his power by having a small number defeat a very large number. That is why it will be the 144,000 taking over the whole world; that is just how he rolls. Precepts: - 1 Maccabees 3:18-19 Judas answered, It is no hard matter for many to be shut up in the hands of a few; and with the God of heaven it is all one to deliver with a great multitude or a small company; we do not have to come deep to get the victory. - 2 Chronicles 14:11 Asa cried unto the Lord, It is nothing with thee to help, whether with many, or with them that have no power: help us, O Lord our God, for we rest on thee, and in thy name we go against this multitude; that is the faith you see in Jonathan and this young servant, two men going against an army in the name of the Lord. 1 Samuel 14:7-10 - His armor bearer said, Do all that is in thine heart: behold, I am with thee according to thy heart. Jonathan set the sign: we will discover ourselves unto them; if they say, Tarry until we come to you, we will stand still in our place; but if they say, Come up unto us, then we will go up, for the Lord hath delivered them into our hand. That is how they would know the Lord had given the green light. 1 Samuel 14:11-14 - Both of them showed themselves to the garrison, and the Philistines said, Behold, the Hebrews come forth out of the holes where they had hid themselves; and the men of the garrison said, Come up to us, and we will shew you a thing. The sign came to pass exactly; the Lord had delivered them into the hand of Israel. - Jonathan climbed up upon his hands and upon his feet, his armor bearer after him, and that first slaughter was about twenty men within about half an acre of land. Two men against a garrison. - Some hold a doctrine that Jonathan was a homosexual; this act answers it. Scaling a rock face to rush a garrison two-deep is a bold, manly act of war that most men are not cut out for; he carried himself like a real man. 1 Samuel 14:15-16 - There was trembling in the host, in the field, and among all the people; the garrison and the spoilers also trembled, and the earth quaked, so it was a very great trembling. The Philistines got caught off guard and panicked. - The watchmen of Saul in Gibeah of Benjamin looked, and behold, the multitude melted away, and they went on beating down one another; in their panic and confusion the Philistines started beating on each other. 1 Samuel 14:17-23 - Saul numbered the people and found Jonathan and his armor bearer missing. While Saul talked with the priest, the noise in the host of the Philistines went on and increased, and when Israel came to the battle, behold, every man's sword was against his fellow, and there was a very great discomfiture; the enemies were destroying each other, and Israel did not have to put in the work. - The Hebrews that were with the Philistines from the country round about turned to be with the Israelites that were with Saul and Jonathan, and the men of Israel which had hid themselves in mount Ephraim followed hard after them in the battle when they heard the Philistines fled. - So the Lord saved Israel that day, and the battle passed over unto Bethaven. 1 Samuel 14:24-26 - Saul had adjured the people, saying, Cursed be the man that eateth any food until evening, that I may be avenged on mine enemies; so none of the people tasted any food. Saul put out a strange order, and the men of Israel were distressed that day. - All they of the land came to a wood, and there was honey upon the ground, and the honey dropped, but no man put his hand to his mouth, for the people feared the oath. - But Jonathan heard not when his father charged the people with the oath; he was not there when the order came out. 1 Samuel 14:27-30 - Jonathan dipped the end of his rod in an honeycomb and put his hand to his mouth, and his eyes were enlightened; like the first taste after a long fast, he felt like a whole new creature. Then one of the people told him his father straitly charged the people with an oath, and the people were faint. - Jonathan said, My father hath troubled the land: see how mine eyes have been enlightened, because I tasted a little of this honey; how much more, if haply the people had eaten freely of the spoil of their enemies, had there not been now a much greater slaughter among the Philistines? He began to convince the people that eating was the better idea and that the king's order was folly. Precepts: - Proverbs 24:21 My son, fear thou the Lord and the king, and meddle not with them that are given to change; Saul was the king and put out an order, and when someone among you tries to change the orders of the king, do not meddle with him, because he will lead you into error, which is exactly what happened next. 1 Samuel 14:31-35 - They smote the Philistines that day from Michmash to Aijalon, and the people were very faint. Then the people flew upon the spoil, took sheep, oxen, and calves, slew them on the ground, and did eat them with the blood; too faint to prepare the meat, they ate it raw with the blood, and that was the transgression Jonathan's talk led the people into. - When they told Saul, he said, Ye have transgressed: roll a great stone unto me this day; bring every man his ox and his sheep, slay them here, and eat, and sin not against the Lord in eating with the blood. And Saul built an altar unto the Lord, the first altar that he built unto the Lord. 1 Samuel 14:36-37 - Saul proposed going down after the Philistines by night to spoil them until morning, and the people agreed; then said the priest, Let us draw near hither unto God. And Saul asked counsel of God, Shall I go down after the Philistines? wilt thou deliver them into the hand of Israel? But he answered him not that day. - If you are spiritual, when the Lord ignores you, you understand at that point what it reveals: it is sin. It has to be; the scriptures give only that reason. Precepts: - Psalms 66:18 If I regard iniquity in my heart, the Lord will not hear me; somewhere in the camp there was iniquity, so the Lord did not hear Saul. - Isaiah 59:2 Your iniquities have separated between you and your God, and your sins have hid his face from you, that he will not hear; sin and iniquity are what cause the Most High not to hear you, plain and clear. 1 Samuel 14:38-44 - Saul said, Draw ye near, all the chief of the people, and know and see wherein this sin hath been this day; for as the Lord liveth, which saveth Israel, though it be in Jonathan my son, he shall surely die. But there was not a man among all the people that answered him. - Saul said unto the Lord God of Israel, Give a perfect lot; and Saul and Jonathan were taken, but the people escaped. Then they cast lots between Saul and Jonathan, and Jonathan was taken. - Jonathan told him, I did but taste a little honey with the end of the rod that was in mine hand, and, lo, I must die. And Saul answered, God do so and more also: for thou shalt surely die, Jonathan. Saul was ready to kill his own son over the oath. 1 Samuel 14:45 - The people said unto Saul, Shall Jonathan die, who hath wrought this great salvation in Israel? God forbid: as the Lord liveth, there shall not one hair of his head fall to the ground, for he hath wrought with God this day. So the people rescued Jonathan, that he died not; they kept him from the wrath of his father. - Think about the contrast, and why the scripture says to get the love of the congregation. In chapter 13 Saul was the one disobeying the voice of the Lord and getting rebuked, while Jonathan was brave and mighty and had just saved Israel out of the hand of its enemies; now the coward wants to kill the deliverer. - In some situations you have to weigh it like the people did: yes, he made a mistake and crossed the order, but he just saved all our lives. Precepts: - James 2:13 He shall have judgment without mercy, that hath shewed no mercy, and mercy rejoiceth against judgment; Saul had just been shown mercy for his own failure, so passing merciless judgment on his own son would have left no mercy for Saul the next time he fell. 1 Samuel 14:47-52 - Saul took the kingdom over Israel and fought against all his enemies on every side: Moab, the children of Ammon, Edom, the kings of Zobah, and the Philistines; and whithersoever he turned himself, he vexed them. He gathered an host, smote the Amalekites, and delivered Israel out of the hands of them that spoiled them. - The chapter closes with his house: his sons Jonathan, Ishui, and Melchishua; his daughters Merab and Michal, whom we will learn about later; his wife Ahinoam; and Abner the son of Ner, Saul's uncle, captain of his host. There was sore war against the Philistines all the days of Saul, and when Saul saw any strong man or any valiant man, he took him unto him. 1 Samuel 15: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice Read the chapter → 1 Samuel 15 1 Samuel 15:1-3 - Samuel said unto Saul, The Lord sent me to anoint thee to be king over his people; now therefore hearken thou unto the voice of the words of the Lord. Thus saith the Lord of hosts, I remember that which Amalek did to Israel, how he laid wait for him in the way when he came up from Egypt. Generations after the wilderness, the Most High still remembers; the generation of Amalekites had returned, and it was time to fulfil what was written. - Now go and smite Amalek, and utterly destroy all that they have, and spare them not; but slay both man and woman, infant and suckling, ox and sheep, camel and ass. This is a specific instruction: kill all of them, spare none. Note that the Most High commanded this against a generation that had not personally done the deed in the wilderness; that answers the argument, I never did anything to you, so why hold it against me? The Most High himself commanded recompense for what was done to the forefathers. - Christianity says forgive and forget, but the Most High God said remember; this is a righteous grudge, and it shows Leviticus 19:18 applies to the children of thy people. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 25:17-18 Remember what Amalek did unto thee by the way, how he met thee and smote the hindmost of thee, all that were feeble behind thee, when thou wast faint and weary; and he feared not God; the detail is written to stir you up: they preyed on the weak and the tired. - Deuteronomy 25:19 When the Lord thy God hath given thee rest from all thine enemies round about, thou shalt blot out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven; thou shalt not forget it. Israel now had rest and a king; the time had come. - Exodus 17:16 The Lord hath sworn that the Lord will have war with Amalek from generation to generation; that war did not end in the wilderness. - Leviticus 19:18 Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people; the grudge law is toward your own people, not toward the enemies of Israel whom the Most High has sworn against. - The teaching applies Exodus 17:16 to this day: the same war continues from generation to generation, and it is now more spiritual than ever, because the adversary has established the imagination that they are the Jews, and we go out and cast down that imagination every day. Edom cheered Babylon on when Jerusalem burned, and the scripture pronounces the payback. Precepts: - Psalms 137:7 Remember, O Lord, the children of Edom in the day of Jerusalem, who said, Rase it, rase it, even to the foundation thereof; they were the cheerleaders when Babylon destroyed the temple. - Psalms 137:8-9 O daughter of Babylon, who art to be destroyed, happy shall he be that rewardeth thee as thou hast served us; happy shall he be that taketh and dasheth thy little ones against the stones; the Most High calls him happy that pays her back for everything she has done. - Revelation 17:5 Edom grew up from being the daughter of Babylon into Mystery, Babylon the Great, the mother of harlots; that is why the great woman of Revelation carries Babylon's name. - Understand the frame: we live peaceably with all men and lay hands on no one; we do not incite or condone any violence, and if we hear of any we report it. The day of Psalms 137 has not yet come; it belongs to the return of the Lord, so chill out and relax, none of that is for now. Precepts: - Romans 12:18 If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men; that is the walk commanded now. - Leviticus 5:1 If a soul hear the voice of swearing and is a witness, he must utter it; hence if we hear of violence we make it known. 1 Samuel 15:4-6 - Saul gathered the people and numbered them in Telaim, two hundred thousand footmen and ten thousand men of Judah, and laid wait in the valley. - Saul said unto the Kenites, Go, depart, get you down from among the Amalekites, lest I destroy you with them: for ye shewed kindness to all the children of Israel when they came up out of Egypt. So the Kenites departed. The Most High discriminates righteously: the people who showed Israel kindness were spared out of the judgment. Precepts: - Judges 1:16 The children of the Kenite, Moses' father in law, went up with the children of Judah; these are the people of Jethro, whose counsel set up the ranking system over Israel and whose family was as eyes for Israel in the wilderness; they were always helpful to us. 1 Samuel 15:7-9 - Saul smote the Amalekites from Havilah until thou comest to Shur, and utterly destroyed the people with the edge of the sword; but he took Agag the king of the Amalekites alive. He halfway fulfilled the order, reasoning like the king might be valuable as a hostage, as if the Lord forgot that detail. - But Saul and the people spared Agag, and the best of the sheep, and of the oxen, and of the fatlings, and the lambs, and all that was good, and would not utterly destroy them; but every thing that was vile and refuse, that they destroyed utterly. They killed what looked like it deserved killing, so they could say they did some killing, and kept the healthy, good looking animals, telling themselves surely the Lord could not have meant these. 1 Samuel 15:10-11 - Then came the word of the Lord unto Samuel: It repenteth me that I have set up Saul to be king, for he is turned back from following me, and hath not performed my commandments. Mark the language: Saul did most of what was said, yet the Lord counts it as turning back and not performing his commandments at all. - For everybody who says, well, I did do this part, understand: whenever there is a but in your obedience, you did not perform the orders given unto you. That is what the Most High is showing us in this story. - And it grieved Samuel, and he cried unto the Lord all night. Pride had to be in operation for Saul to transgress on that level, and pride is where the throne is lost. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 10:12-14 That is exactly what happened: Saul's heart turned from his Maker, he poured out sin upon sin from there, and the Lord cast down the proud prince's throne and set up the meek in his stead; that is the whole story we are about to read. 1 Samuel 15:12-15 - Samuel rose early to meet Saul, and it was told him that Saul came to Carmel and set him up a place, a monument to himself, and is gone down to Gilgal. When your transgression becomes the lesson, be thankful when the correction comes quietly and nobody knows your name; do not take the spirit of bitterness, because you deserved a lot more. - Saul greets Samuel first with a cover: Blessed be thou of the Lord: I have performed the commandment of the Lord. The first thing out of his mouth is a fabrication, knowing full well he transgressed. - Samuel answers, What meaneth then this bleating of the sheep in mine ears, and the lowing of the oxen which I hear? If you performed the commandment, why do I hear animals? - Saul deflects again, the same blame game as chapter 13: They have brought them from the Amalekites, for the people spared the best of the sheep and of the oxen, to sacrifice unto the Lord thy God; and the rest we have utterly destroyed. Verse 9 already told us Saul and the people spared them; now suddenly it is only the people, and for a good reason, a sacrifice, as though the Lord ought to be pleased. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 12:32 What thing soever I command you, observe to do it: thou shalt not add thereto, nor diminish from it; the Most High made a law for the bright ideas that come along the way of following instructions, and it is plain. 1 Samuel 15:16-19 - Samuel said, Stay, and I will tell thee what the Lord hath said to me this night. When thou wast little in thine own sight, wast thou not made the head of the tribes of Israel, and the Lord anointed thee king over Israel? Samuel brings Saul back to his remembrance: when you thought nothing of yourself, with no confidence to be a ruler, the Most High still chose you. - And the Lord sent thee on a journey, and said, Go and utterly destroy the sinners the Amalekites, and fight against them until they be consumed; the errand was the vengeance written in Deuteronomy 25. Wherefore then didst thou not obey the voice of the Lord, but didst fly upon the spoil, and didst evil in the sight of the Lord? Keeping the orders partially is evil in the sight of the Lord. Precepts: - 1 Samuel 9:21 Saul had answered, Am not I a Benjamite, of the smallest of the tribes of Israel, and my family the least of all the families of the tribe of Benjamin? wherefore then speakest thou so to me? That was the little-in-his-own-sight attitude Saul started with. 1 Samuel 15:20-21 - Saul is in denial: Yea, I have obeyed the voice of the lord, and have gone the way which the Lord sent me, and have brought Agag the king of Amalek, and have utterly destroyed the Amalekites. Samuel breaks down the rebuke and Saul tells the prophet he is wrong. - In justifying himself over the animals, Saul volunteers even more of his rebellion, boasting that he spared the king, as if that was the smart move everyone really wanted; then he lays the spoil on the people again: the people took of the spoil, sheep and oxen, the chief of the things which should have been utterly destroyed, to sacrifice unto the Lord thy God in Gilgal. Precepts: - Job 9:20 If I justify myself, mine own mouth shall condemn me; when you plead your own righteousness against correction, you end up revealing more of your rebellion out of your own mouth, which is exactly what Saul did. 1 Samuel 15:22 - Samuel makes it plain: Hath the Lord as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the Lord? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams. Do you think the Lord prefers a sacrifice to atone for broken commandments over you simply keeping the commandments? That is a heavy verse. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 34:18-19 The spoil was wrongfully gotten, taken against the will of the Lord, so the offering is ridiculous; all those animals were not going to pacify his anger. - Proverbs 21:27 The sacrifice of the wicked is abomination: how much more, when he bringeth it with a wicked mind? It does not merely do nothing; it makes the Most High more angry, and Saul probably would have kept those animals to eat had it never been pointed out. - Psalms 51:16-17 Thou desirest not sacrifice, else would I give it: the sacrifices of God are a broken spirit; a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise. David wrote this in his repentance: the true sacrifice is being sorry and remorseful for what you did, not pleading why you were not wrong for doing wrong; that is the spirit Saul does not have. 1 Samuel 15:23 - For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness is as iniquity and idolatry. That is heavy. A brother who would never touch voodoo will sit through a whole counsel of do not do this, and call two weeks later saying he did it anyway; according to this verse, that rebellion is the same as witchcraft. - Stubbornness is idolatry because the instruction does not come from the man; it is the commandment of the Lord that leadership carries. When you are stubborn against it, you are saying what I want to do comes before what God wants me to do, and you have put yourself in the midst of idolatry as surely as circling the stone at Mecca or bowing before a cross. - Because thou hast rejected the word of the Lord, he hath also rejected thee from being king: you will lose whatever position the Most High put you in. - This stubborn heart is what fares evil at the last; we will read Saul's end in the last chapter of 1 Samuel, and in chapter 16 the evil spirit enters into him and the Spirit of the Lord departs. The plant of wickedness took root here. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 3:26-27 Obstinate is another word for stubborn: the mind set on doing what it wants contrary to counsel will be laden with sorrows, and Saul heaped sin upon sin, lying, justifying himself, and blaming the people, which is what carried him into the witchcraft and idolatry of rebellion. 1 Samuel 15:24-25 - Now the confession finally comes, and it is still not sincere: I have sinned, for I have transgressed the commandment of the Lord and thy words; because I feared the people, and obeyed their voice. Even in admitting it he deflects: it is the fault of the wicked people you put me over. - Then he asks, Pardon my sin, and turn again with me, that I may worship the Lord; take me back to the regular Saul and Samuel connection, as though a fearful excuse settles it. Precepts: - Proverbs 29:25 The fear of man bringeth a snare, but whoso putteth his trust in the Lord shall be safe; if you fear what the people will say, you will fall into the trap and transgress, which is why a leader cannot fold when the people become too much to handle; Saul would have been safe had he trusted the Lord. 1 Samuel 15:26 - Samuel refuses: I will not return with thee; for thou hast rejected the word of the Lord, and the Lord hath rejected thee from being king over Israel. Think it through: Samuel gave Saul the opening at the bleating of the sheep, and Saul would not humble down; he asked why Saul disobeyed the voice of the Lord, and Saul justified himself again. Two admonitions were given and refused before this rejection. Precepts: - Titus 3:10 A man that is an heretick after the first and second admonition reject; Saul had two chances to repent and confess and still justified himself, so Samuel did exactly what the scripture says and rejected him. - Titus 1:16 They profess that they know God, but in works they deny him, being abominable, and disobedient, and unto every good work reprobate; Saul professed, restore me that I may worship the Lord, while every work denied him; this is the starting point of Saul losing the Spirit and going reprobate. 1 Samuel 15:27-29 - As Samuel turned about to go away, Saul laid hold upon the skirt of his mantle, and it rent. And Samuel said, The Lord hath rent the kingdom of Israel from thee this day, and hath given it to a neighbour of thine, that is better than thou. Just as Saul tore the hem of the garment, so the Lord tore the throne from him; and Samuel says this still before he has ever met David, the same word he gave in chapter 13. - And also the Strength of Israel will not lie nor repent: for he is not a man, that he should repent. The Strength of Israel is the Most High. Understand the spirit of the title: whenever you go off on your own mind, pride has you departing from your strength, and once you have left your strength you are open to Satan; if a brother tells you that you are battling with pride, take heed and examine yourself. Precepts: - Numbers 23:19 God is not a man, that he should lie; neither the son of man, that he should repent: hath he said, and shall he not do it? - Judith 8:16 The Most High is not as man, that he may be threatened, neither does he waver; the sentence on Saul stood. 1 Samuel 15:30-31 - Then he said, I have sinned: yet honour me now, I pray thee, before the elders of my people, and before Israel. This spirit is very real: okay, you are right, but do not let the people see the demotion; make sure they still know I am the king. - That is the spirit of vanity, caught up in a rank and a title while forgetting that the title came for pleasing the Lord; once you discontinue pleasing the Lord, the title is going to leave as well. So Samuel turned again after Saul, and Saul worshipped the Lord. 1 Samuel 15:32-33 - Then said Samuel, Bring ye hither to me Agag the king of the Amalekites. And Agag came unto him delicately, and said, Surely the bitterness of death is past; with Saul under rebuke, Agag figured nobody was mad at the Amalekites anymore and he was safe. - And Samuel said, As thy sword hath made women childless, so shall thy mother be childless among women. And Samuel hewed Agag in pieces before the Lord in Gilgal. The old prophet did not play; he finished the commandment himself, measure for measure for what Amalek's sword had done. 1 Samuel 15:34-35 - Then Samuel went to Ramah, and Saul went up to his house in Gibeah, and Samuel came no more to see Saul until the day of his death: nevertheless Samuel mourned for Saul, and the Lord repented that he had made Saul king over Israel. - The mourning is what makes it sad: Samuel raised Saul up from nothing, saw his potential, and saw the Spirit come upon him in chapter 11 when he stood up as a savior for the people; he had hope in him, and it came to this. Samuel was grieved, and the Lord repented of the appointment. --- Topics: Esau and Edom · Idolatry · Sacrifice and Atonement · The Covenant · The Feasts of the Most High · The Priesthood ← 1 Samuel 8-11 · 1 Samuel Study · 1 Samuel 16-19 →

title: 1 Samuel 16: The Lord Looketh on the Heart
text: ← 1 Samuel 12-15 · 1 Samuel Study · 1 Samuel 20-23 → 1 Samuel 16: The Lord Looketh on the Heart Read the chapter → 1 Samuel 16 Introduction This session covers 1 Samuel chapters 16 through 19: David selected and anointed as Saul's replacement, his humble beginnings as a keeper of sheep and a player on the harp, his victory over Goliath, Saul's descent into envy and murder once the women sang David's praise, and the faithfulness of Jonathan and Michal in delivering David from Saul's snares. The thread that ties it together is the spirit: the Most High looks not on the outward appearance but on the heart, his spirit came upon David from the day of his anointing, and it departed from Saul, who was given over to his own ruin. 1 Samuel 16:1 - Recall the class on chapters 12 through 15: in chapter 15 Saul rebelled against the commandment, and after two admonitions he still would not humble down and repent, so the Most High rejected him from reigning over Israel and told him through Samuel that his kingdom would not continue. - Samuel had groomed Saul up and saw potential in the brother, so he mourned over him; the Most High asked how long he would keep crying over the man he had rejected. - Samuel is told to fill his horn with oil and go to Jesse the Bethlehemite, for the Most High had already provided himself a king from among Jesse's sons. 1 Samuel 16:2-3 - Samuel feared that Saul would kill him if he heard of it. Remember the influence and love Samuel had among the people; even so, this shows the power of the king. Saul raised no hand against Samuel yet, but a king had the authority to command a prophet's death. - The Most High told Samuel to go in with a heifer, as if coming only to sacrifice; he would go incognito, not letting it be known that he was coming to anoint Saul's replacement, and the Most High would show him whom to anoint. Precepts: - 1 Esdras 4:2-3 Men bear rule over sea and land, but yet the king is more mighty; this is the debate before the king of Persia over what is strongest. - 1 Esdras 4:7 The king is only one man, but if he command to kill, they kill; that is the power Saul held, and why Samuel had cause to be careful. 1 Samuel 16:4-5 - Samuel did what the Most High spake and came to Bethlehem, and the elders of the town trembled at his coming and asked, Comest thou peaceably? Everybody knew Samuel did not play; if he was coming to your town it was probably for some judgment. - Samuel answered peaceably: he came to sacrifice to the Lord, and he sanctified Jesse and his sons and called them to the sacrifice. 1 Samuel 16:6-7 - When Samuel looked on Eliab he judged through his own lens as a man: surely this is the Lord's anointed. The Most High corrected him: look not on his countenance or on the height of his stature, because I have refused him. Looking the mightiest and the tallest does not make a man the one the Most High picked. - The Lord seeth not as man seeth; man looketh on the outward appearance, but the Lord looketh on the heart. This scripture is heavy: it is showing the spirit of Christ before Christ walked the earth. The Pharisees could not understand why he dealt with the lower class instead of the mighty men; he was looking on the heart, and he knew the Pharisees' hearts were corrupt while the humble were willing to devote their lives to the Most High. - This still happens today: brothers will look at a group and assume the biggest one must be the leader, not knowing that brother might be the soldier while the leader is the slim one beside him. Precepts: - John 7:24 Judge not according to the appearance, but judge righteous judgment; the same standard the Most High gave Samuel in this verse. - Isaiah 11:1-3 The rod out of the stem of Jesse is prophecy of Christ, out of this same lineage; the word repeated all through the verses is spirit, and he shall not judge after the sight of his eyes nor reprove after the hearing of his ears. - Hebrews 12:9 We gave the fathers of our flesh reverence; how much rather should we be in subjection to the Father of spirits, for the Most High deals with the spirits of men, not the outside. - Numbers 27:16-17 In the context of selecting a leader over the congregation, the Most High is called the God of the spirits of all flesh; the selection is always spiritual. 1 Samuel 16:8-13 - Jesse made seven of his sons pass before Samuel, the older, bigger, more developed ones, and Samuel said of each, Neither hath the Lord chosen this; the Lord had not chosen any of these. - Asked whether these were all his children, Jesse answered that there remained yet the youngest, and behold, he keepeth the sheep. Samuel would not sit down until the young one was fetched. He was ruddy, of a beautiful countenance, and goodly to look to, a young handsome fella, and the Most High said, Arise, anoint him, for this is he. - Samuel anointed David in the midst of his brethren, and the spirit of the Lord came upon David from that day forward, from that young age, being the youngest son. - Taking a keeper of sheep and making him the shepherd of the nation is a pattern with the Most High; he took leaders and prophets from following literal flocks and set them to feed the flock of Israel. Precepts: - 2 Samuel 7:8 I took thee from the sheepcote, from following the sheep, to be ruler over my people, over Israel; from literal sheep to shepherd over the sheep of the house of Israel. - Psalms 78:70-71 He chose David his servant and took him from the sheepfolds, from following the ewes great with young, to feed Jacob his people; sheep in the backyard to feeding the nation. - Exodus 3:1 Moses kept the flock of Jethro his father in law, the priest of Midian, and led the flock to the mountain of God, where the Most High called him out of the midst of the bush. - Exodus 3:10 Moses was called from the flock of animals to bring forth the children of Israel out of Egypt, and he ended up feeding them with the laws of the Most High. - The same pattern continues through the prophets: Elisha was taken from the plow and Amos from the herd. Precepts: - 1 Kings 19:16 The Most High told Elijah to anoint Jehu to be king over Israel and Elisha the son of Shaphat to be prophet in his room. - 1 Kings 19:19-21 Elisha was plowing with twelve yoke of oxen when Elijah cast his mantle upon him; he left the care of the literal flock, ministered to Elijah, and eventually became the prophet in his place. - Amos 7:14-15 Amos was no prophet, neither a prophet's son, but an herdman and a gatherer of sycomore fruit, and the Lord took him as he followed the flock and said, Go, prophesy unto my people Israel. - David was also young when the spirit came on him, and that is nothing new either; the Most High does not choose the ones everybody expects, for the spirit of Christ was in the prophets he selected. Precepts: - Susanna 45 The Lord raised up the holy spirit of a young youth named Daniel; another example of the spirit put on a man at a very young age. - 1 Peter 1:10-11 The spirit that was in the prophets when they were selected to feed the flock of Israel was the spirit of Christ, which testified beforehand the sufferings of Christ. - 1 Corinthians 1:26-27 Not many mighty are called; the Most High did not choose the giants that were in the earth, he chose Israel, few in number; that is how he operates. 1 Samuel 16:14 - Simultaneously, as the Most High put his spirit on David, the spirit departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from the Lord troubled him. Note it well: the evil spirit came from the Lord; that is a teaching the church world leaves out. - Chapter 15 said rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and Saul is now headed down that downward spiral; the spirit is leaving him, and he will eventually become a reprobate and dabble in real witchcraft. Precepts: - 1 Samuel 15:23 Rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft; the road Saul took after the spirit departed ends with him literally at witchcraft. - Proverbs 17:11 An evil man seeketh only rebellion, which is what Saul did in chapter 15, therefore a cruel messenger shall be sent against him; a cruel spirit sent to trouble him is what we see on Saul. 1 Samuel 16:15 - Saul's servants could see it: behold now, an evil spirit from God troubleth thee. It was evident; whatever he was doing and saying, his servants could tell an evil spirit was on him. - Why did the spirit leave Saul? Wisdom walks with a man by crooked ways at the first and tries him by her laws. Saul was put through a trial, whether he would keep the commandment given through the mouth of the prophet, and he went wrong; so the spirit forsook him and he was given over to his own ruin, that abyss of jealousy, envy, and hatred. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 4:17-19 Saul was tried by the laws of the Most High and went wrong; had he passed the test he would have been elevated, but wisdom forsook him and gave him over to his own ruin. - Wisdom of Solomon 1:3-5 Froward means contrary; Saul set his mind on the contrary of what the Most High commanded, and the holy spirit of discipline fled the deceit and would not dwell in a body subject unto sin. 1 Samuel 16:16 - Saul's servants proposed the remedy: seek out a man who is a cunning player on an harp, that when the evil spirit from God is upon thee, he shall play with his hand and thou shalt be well. - Our people understood back then that music is spiritual. The right playing could relieve an evil spirit; and if a spiritual song can heal, think what an evil song can do to a good spirit. Evil communications corrupt good manners; be mindful when it comes to music. - The songs we make and listen to, now that we know the truth, should be spiritual songs; the psalms were the jams of that day, and every one of them is deep, teaching who the daughter of Babylon is, the crafty counsel taken against us, and that the law was given to Israel. Precepts: - 1 Chronicles 25:1 David and the captains of the host separated the sons of Asaph, of Heman, and of Jeduthun, who should prophesy with harps, with psalteries, and with cymbals; musicians prophesying with instruments of music. - Colossians 3:16 Teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord; the command is spiritual songs, sung to the Most High. - Psalms 137:3-4 They that carried us away captive required of us a song; how shall we sing the Lord's song in a strange land? In this captivity our people are paid fortunes to sing the opposite of spiritual songs, songs that help destroy one another. - 1 Corinthians 15:33 Evil communications corrupt good manners; what is played into the ears works on the spirit. 1 Samuel 16:18 - One of the servants had seen a son of Jesse the Bethlehemite that is cunning in playing, a mighty valiant man, a man of war, prudent in matters, a comely person, and the Lord is with him. He did not say the name, but this son of Jesse who went hard on the instruments was David. - David was also a singer; he praised the Most High with words of glory and sung songs with his whole heart, and he set up the singers before the altar, the same service we read of in 1 Chronicles 25. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 47:2 As the fat is taken from the peace offering, so was David chosen out of the children of Israel. - Ecclesiasticus 47:8-9 David sung songs with his whole heart and set singers before the altar to daily sing praises; praises in their songs, not filth. 1 Samuel 16:19-22 - Saul sent to Jesse: send me David thy son, which is with the sheep.
