Jesse sent David with bread, a bottle of wine, and a kid, and David came to Saul, stood before him, and Saul loved him greatly. - David became Saul's armourbearer; these are his humble beginnings, serving at the king's side. Even after the spirit had left Saul, David loved him and served him faithfully. - Saul asked Jesse to let David stand before him, for he hath found favour in my sight; Saul liked the spirit on that young brother, and every king keeps a young soldier always with him. Precepts: - Proverbs 14:35 The king's favour is toward a wise servant; that is what David was as armourbearer. We know him as a mighty king, but he started out a wise servant, and that is how he got the king's favour. 1 Samuel 16:23 - When the evil spirit from God was upon Saul, David took an harp and played with his hand, and Saul was refreshed and was well, and the evil spirit departed from him. - David was being his brother's keeper. He saw the evil spirit on his leader and helped him. That is the example to follow: brothers and sisters who come up in a congregation always trying to find fault in their leadership are not in the spirit; David did not roll in that spirit, he was faithful and loyal to the brother. 1 Samuel 17: Not by Sword and Spear Read the chapter → 1 Samuel 17 1 Samuel 17:1-3 - As we covered before, the Philistines always wanted smoke with the Israelites; they would not leave us alone. They gathered to battle at Shochoh and pitched between Shochoh and Azekah. - Saul and the men of Israel pitched by the valley of Elah and set the battle in array; the Philistines stood on a mountain on one side, Israel on a mountain on the other side, with a valley between them. 1 Samuel 17:4-7 - Out of the camp of the Philistines came a champion named Goliath of Gath, whose height was six cubits and a span; the heavyweight champion of the Philistines. - He wore a helmet of brass and a coat of mail weighing five thousand shekels of brass, greaves of brass on his legs, a target of brass between his shoulders, a spear like a weaver's beam with a head of six hundred shekels of iron; a big man in a mighty costume of armor. - He did not even carry his own shield; one bearing a shield went before him. 1 Samuel 17:8-11 - Goliath cried to the armies of Israel: choose you a man and let him come down to me. If he kills me, we will be your servants; if I prevail and kill him, ye shall be our servants. And he said, I defy the armies of Israel this day; give me a man that we may fight together. - When Saul and all Israel heard the words of the Philistine, they were dismayed and greatly afraid. They were in a carnal spirit, measuring his height, his armor, and his reach; the spirit had departed, and fear is not the spirit of the Most High. - The Most High put laws in the book about going to battle, and this fear showed that Saul and the people lacked faith; the same God that destroyed Pharaoh and the Egyptians who pursued Israel was with them, and a trial of faith was set before them in the form of one big intimidating man with a big mouth. Precepts: - 2 Timothy 1:7 The Most High hath not given us the spirit of fear, but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind; the fear in the camp was not his spirit. - Isaiah 51:12 I, even I, am he that comforteth you: who art thou, that thou shouldest be afraid of a man that shall die? The chosen people of the living God have no business fearing a man who will be made as grass. - Deuteronomy 20:1-4 When thou goest out to battle and seest a people more than thou, be not afraid of them, for the Lord thy God is with thee; the priest was to tell the people, let not your hearts faint, fear not, for the Lord your God goeth with you to fight for you against your enemies and to save you. 1 Samuel 17:12-16 - David was the son of that Ephrathite of Bethlehemjudah named Jesse, who had eight sons. The three eldest, Eliab, Abinadab, and Shammah, followed Saul to the battle; the same three the Most High refused in chapter 16. - David, the youngest, went and returned from Saul to feed his father's sheep at Bethlehem. - The Philistine drew near morning and evening and presented himself forty days; forty days straight of talking his big talk to try to scare Israel. 1 Samuel 17:17-19 - Jesse sent David to the camp with parched corn and ten loaves for his brethren and ten cheeses for their captain of the thousand, to see how his brethren fared and take their pledge. - Saul and all the men of Israel were in the valley of Elah, fighting with the Philistines; David was sent on an errand to get his brothers some supplies and check on them. 1 Samuel 17:20-24 - David rose early, left the sheep with a keeper, and came to the trench as the host was shouting for the battle; while he saluted his brethren, the champion came up and spake according to the same words, the same daily smack talk, and David heard them. - All the men of Israel, when they saw the man, fled from him and were sore afraid. Think on it: the whole nation's freedom, everything they possessed, was on the line, and they ran scared. - This is why the Most High said in chapter 16 that he had refused David's brothers: they were there and did not have the spirit to rise up; they were among the ones who fled. Precepts: - Psalms 94:16 Who will rise up for me against the evildoers? That is the spirit the Most High looks for, one who will stand up for his people against the workers of iniquity; he is not worried about outward appearance. 1 Samuel 17:25-27 - The men of Israel said that the man who killeth Goliath, the king will enrich with great riches, give him his daughter, and make his father's house free in Israel; a prize was on Goliath's head. Compare Caleb, who made a like offer in the book of Joshua. - David asked, What shall be done to the man that killeth this Philistine and taketh away the reproach from Israel? For who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living God? - The soldiers themselves did not understand that they were the armies of the living God; David, a sheep keeper sent on an errand, knew it. Israel is the army of the Most High, and every army requires order; that is why there are captains and officers, and despising that order is despising the army of the living God. Precepts: - Exodus 7:4 That I may lay my hand upon Egypt, and bring forth mine armies, and my people the children of Israel; the Most High calls his people, the children of Israel, his armies. - Joshua 15:16 Caleb said, He that smiteth Kirjathsepher, and taketh it, to him will I give Achsah my daughter to wife; the same kind of offer the king made over Goliath. 1 Samuel 17:28-30 - Eliab, the eldest brother, heard David and his anger was kindled: why camest thou down hither, and with whom hast thou left those few sheep in the wilderness? I know thy pride and the naughtiness of thine heart; thou art come down that thou mightest see the battle. A big brother talking down to a little brother, accusing him of sneaking out to watch. - David answered, What have I now done? Is there not a cause? The men are scared, nobody will step up; what is the problem? And he turned to another and spake after the same manner. 1 Samuel 17:31-33 - David's words were rehearsed before Saul, and Saul sent for him. David told Saul, Let no man's heart fail because of him; thy servant will go and fight with this Philistine. Nobody panic; I will handle it. - Saul answered, Thou art not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him, for thou art but a youth, and he a man of war from his youth. - Young people coming into this truth: if the Most High is dealing with you in a special way, do not let anybody discourage you or tell you that you are too young to be a mighty man of the Lord. Do not let it deter you. Precepts: - 1 Timothy 4:12 Let no man despise thy youth, but be thou an example of the believers, in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity; the nation had no example of faith that day, so a young youth had to be that example. 1 Samuel 17:34-37 - David gave Saul his resume: keeping his father's sheep, when a lion and a bear took a lamb out of the flock, he went out after him, smote him, and delivered it out of his mouth; when he arose against him, David caught him by his beard and slew him. He might have looked small, but he was killing lions and bears behind his sheep. - David said, The Lord that delivered me out of the paw of the lion and out of the paw of the bear, he will deliver me out of the hand of this Philistine. Same God, no difference. And Saul said, Go, and the Lord be with thee. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 47:3 David played with lions as with kids and with bears as with lambs; he was a mighty young man, and Saul did not know that about him. 1 Samuel 17:38-40 - Saul armed David with his own armor, a helmet of brass and a coat of mail, and David girded his sword upon the armor and assayed to go; but he had not proved it, and he said, I cannot go with these, and put them off him. - Instead of the helmet and the brass, David took his staff, chose him five smooth stones out of the brook, put them in a shepherd's bag, and took his sling in his hand. What he put on instead was the whole armour of God: the shield of faith, the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the spirit. Precepts: - Ephesians 6:16-17 Above all taking the shield of faith, and the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God; David went to the battle believing his God would fight for him, carrying the word instead of carnal armor. 1 Samuel 17:41-45 - When the Philistine looked about and saw David, he disdained him, for he was but a youth, ruddy and of a fair countenance: Am I a dog, that thou comest to me with staves? And the Philistine cursed David by his gods and promised to give his flesh to the fowls of the air and the beasts of the field. - David answered, Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of the Lord of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom thou hast defied. Again the record shows who the army of the Most High is: Israel. - David understood he did not need the sword, the spear, or the shield; he had the spirit of the living God. It is no amount of carnal firepower that overcomes the enemies of Israel; this is spiritual warfare, and our forefather David understood that. Precepts: - Zechariah 4:6 Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the Lord of hosts; the only way Israel overcomes. 1 Samuel 17:46-47 - David prophesied the outcome before the fight: this day will the Lord deliver thee into mine hand, and I will smite thee, and take thine head from thee, that all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel. - All this assembly shall know that the Lord saveth not with sword and spear: for the battle is the Lord's. The Most High fights how he wants to fight, not how man thinks it must be done. Precepts: - Hosea 1:7 I will have mercy upon the house of Judah, and will save them by the Lord their God, and will not save them by bow, nor by sword, nor by battle, by horses, nor by horsemen; prophecy that Judah would be saved without carnal weapons. - 2 Kings 19:34-35 The fulfillment in Hezekiah's day: the angel of the Lord went out and smote in the camp of the Assyrians an hundred fourscore and five thousand, and Judah woke up to the battle already won; that is how the Lord gets down. 1 Samuel 17:48-51 - David hasted and ran toward the army to meet the Philistine, took a stone from his bag, slang it, and smote the Philistine in his forehead, that the stone sunk into his forehead, and he fell upon his face to the earth. David had precise aim and power; that stone left the sling with the velocity of a bullet, and it took one shot. - David prevailed with a sling and with a stone, and there was no sword in the hand of David; he ran and stood upon the Philistine, drew Goliath's own sword out of the sheath, slew him, and cut off his head with it. - When the Philistines saw their champion was dead, they fled. They ran from a young youth because they knew something supernatural was going on; he was in the spirit of the Lord. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 47:4-5 David slew a giant when he was yet but young and took away reproach from the people; he called upon the Most High, and it was the Most High who gave his right hand strength to slay that mighty warrior. 1 Samuel 17:55-58 - When Saul saw David go forth against the Philistine, he asked Abner, the captain of the host, Whose son is this youth? And Abner could not tell; in the shock of it they forgot whose son the young man was. - As David returned from the slaughter of the Philistine with the head of the Philistine in his hand, Abner brought him before Saul, and David answered, I am the son of thy servant Jesse the Bethlehemite. - That is the history of David and Goliath: when the mighty men of Israel ran afraid, a young youth stood up bold in the spirit of the Lord and took the giant down. 1 Samuel 18: The Envious Eye of Saul Read the chapter → 1 Samuel 18 1 Samuel 18:1-4 - The soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul, and they made a covenant; Jonathan stripped himself of his robe and gave it to David, with his garments, his sword, his bow, and his girdle. - Address the perversion head on, as we did last class: souls being knit is not talking about anything unnatural between the two men. The same word describes the church: hearts knit together in love, as joints and bands in one body. Jonathan and David were on one accord; they had the same spirit. Precepts: - Colossians 2:2 That their hearts might be comforted, being knit together in love; the will of Christ for the church at Colosse, the same knitting of souls. - Colossians 2:19 The body, by joints and bands knit together, increaseth with the increase of God; as muscles and joints are knit into one body, so were Jonathan and David of one spirit. 1 Samuel 18:5-7 - David went whithersoever Saul sent him and behaved himself wisely, and Saul set him over the men of war, and he was accepted in the sight of all the people and of Saul's servants. - When they returned from the slaughter of the Philistine, the women came out of all cities of Israel singing and dancing to meet king Saul, with tabrets, with joy, and with instruments of musick. - The women answered one another as they played: Saul hath slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands. The first line honored Saul, but the song made David exponentially the greater warrior, and brothers catch spirits behind what women say and do. 1 Samuel 18:8-9 - Saul was very wroth and the saying displeased him: they have ascribed unto David ten thousands, and to me they have ascribed but thousands; and what can he have more but the kingdom? Wroth is the same word used in Genesis 4 of how Cain fell toward Abel, and Abel had done nothing to him but what the Lord required; David likewise did nothing to Saul but what Saul himself asked of him. - Instead of appreciating the song, give credit where it is due, for the labourer is worthy of his reward, Saul was displeased at his brother's praise; that is the same spirit of envy. - And Saul eyed David from that day and forward. What was behind that eye? Envy. The envious man is not satisfied with his own portion; Saul had his thousands and still had the kingdom, but his eye was on David's portion, and iniquity dried up his soul from that point forward. Precepts: - Genesis 4:5 Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell; the same word, the same spirit, kindled against a brother who had done nothing wrong. - Matthew 5:21-22 Whosoever is angry with his brother without a cause shall be in danger of the judgment, the same judgment as a murderer; anger without a cause is counted as murder in the spirit. - Ecclesiasticus 14:8-9 The envious man hath a wicked eye; that is the eye Saul eyed David with, and the iniquity of the wicked dried up his soul. 1 Samuel 18:10-12 - On the morrow the evil spirit from God came upon Saul, and this time it came back with more power: there was a javelin in Saul's hand, and he cast it, saying, I will smite David even to the wall with it. David avoided out of his presence twice. - Saul was afraid of David, because the Lord was with him and was departed from Saul. When Saul saw how quickly David escaped, that spirit on David made the hunter the scared one. Precepts: - James 2:19 The devils also believe, and tremble; when Saul saw the spirit on David, he who sought David's life became the one afraid. 1 Samuel 18:13-16 - Saul removed David from him and made him captain over a thousand; he basically demoted the brother, putting his own armourbearer away from his presence for no reason. - David behaved himself wisely in all his ways, and the Lord was with him, and when Saul saw it he was the more afraid. David's continued righteousness heaped coals of fire on Saul; when your righteousness makes the wicked afraid, that is how you know you are in the spirit. - But all Israel and Judah loved David, because he went out and came in before them; everybody knew he was the one really putting his life on the line and doing the work, even though he had no throne. Precepts: - Luke 6:22 Blessed are ye, when men shall hate you, and when they shall separate you from their company; Saul separated David from his company for no reason, a mark of blessing on David. - Romans 12:20 In so doing thou shalt heap coals of fire on his head; David's faithful service under a hateful king did exactly that. - 1 Peter 2:15 With well doing ye put to silence the ignorance of foolish men; David kept behaving wisely and left Saul nothing to charge him with. 1 Samuel 18:17-19 - Saul offered his elder daughter Merab to wife, only be thou valiant for me and fight the Lord's battles; for Saul said, Let not mine hand be upon him, but let the hand of the Philistines be upon him. Remember, the king's daughter was already the promise attached to killing Goliath; Saul aged him out of that and reattached conditions, thinking the Philistines would finish David. - David answered humbly: who am I, and what is my life, or my father's family in Israel, that I should be son in law to the king? - When the time came that Merab should have been given to David, she was given to Adriel the Meholathite; Saul tricked David out of her. 1 Samuel 18:20-27 - Michal, Saul's daughter, loved David, and the thing pleased Saul: I will give him her, that she may be a snare to him, and that the hand of the Philistines may be against him. He set his own daughter as a trap. - David again answered humbly, that he was a poor man and lightly esteemed; so Saul waived the dowry money and named his price: an hundred foreskins of the Philistines, thinking to make David fall by the hand of the Philistines, for there was no way he should survive that errand. - David arose with his men, slew two hundred Philistines, and brought their foreskins in full tale to the king; he doubled the order. That is how devoted a warrior he was for his king and his nation, and Saul gave him Michal his daughter to wife. 1 Samuel 18:28-30 - Saul saw and knew that the Lord was with David, and that Michal loved him, and Saul was yet the more afraid of David; and Saul became David's enemy continually. Put the verses together: he knew the Lord was with the man, and he chose to be that man's enemy anyway. If you know the Lord is with somebody and you make yourself their enemy, you have made yourself the adversary. - David was righteous, obedient, and humble; Saul was envious, wicked, and rebellious, and he could not stand him. As sin is an abomination to the Most High, so godliness is an abomination to a sinner; the sinner cannot bear to look at righteousness. - The princes of the Philistines went forth, and David behaved himself more wisely than all the servants of Saul, so that his name was much set by; harmless as a dove, wise as a serpent. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 1:25 Godliness is an abomination to a sinner; that is why Saul became David's enemy continually. - 1 John 3:12 Cain, who was of that wicked one, slew his brother because his own works were evil and his brother's righteous; the same spirit that was on Saul, the root of bitterness that says, I have to take that man's life. 1 Samuel 19: A Faithful Friend Is a Strong Defence Read the chapter → 1 Samuel 19 1 Samuel 19:1-3 - Saul spake to Jonathan his son and to all his servants that they should kill David. The Philistines could not get him, so now he wants Israelites to kill an Israelite; that is how far down the slope this man has gone. - But Jonathan delighted much in David and told him: my father seeketh to kill thee; take heed to thyself until the morning, abide in a secret place, and hide thyself. I will commune with my father of thee, and what I see, that I will tell thee. - Jonathan would have been next in line for the throne; you would think his loyalty lay with his daddy, but he saw the spirit was not on his father, it was on his brother David. His loyalty exceeded his own desires. That is the kind of friend to look for, and the lesson to learn from Jonathan. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 6:14 A faithful friend is a strong defence, and he that hath found such an one hath found a treasure; that is what Jonathan was to David. - Ecclesiasticus 22:25 I will not be ashamed to defend a friend, neither will I hide myself from him; even with his father the king gone crazy, Jonathan would not abandon David. 1 Samuel 19:4-7 - Jonathan spake good of David to Saul: let not the king sin against his servant, because he hath not sinned against thee, and his works have been to thee-ward very good; he put his life in his hand and slew the Philistine, and thou sawest it and didst rejoice. Why wilt thou sin against innocent blood, to slay David without a cause? - Without a cause: in chapter 18 it was just a feeling, wrath at David for nothing; as Christ explained in the spirit, that anger without a cause leads to actually wanting to murder, which is why it carries the same judgment. - Saul hearkened unto Jonathan and sware, As the Lord liveth, he shall not be slain; and Jonathan brought David back to Saul, and he was in his presence as in times past. Precepts: - Exodus 23:7 The innocent and righteous slay thou not; the law in the book that Saul was set on breaking. - Proverbs 6:16-17 Among the six things the Lord hates, yea seven that are an abomination unto him, are hands that shed innocent blood; that is the boat Saul put himself in. 1 Samuel 19:8-10 - There was war again, and David went out and fought with the Philistines and slew them with a great slaughter. Everything was back to normal until David's mighty spirit was displayed on the battlefield again. - The evil spirit from the Lord was upon Saul as he sat in his house with his javelin in his hand, and he sought to smite David even to the wall while David played with his hand. The evil spirit had leveled up: in times past the harp made it depart, now Saul throws the javelin at the man playing the music. - David slipped away out of Saul's presence, and the javelin smote into the wall, and David fled and escaped that night, just as in chapter 18. 1 Samuel 19:11-17 - Saul sent messengers unto David's house to watch him and to slay him in the morning. Having tried to turn his son against David, he now leans on his daughter, David's own wife; but Michal warned David, If thou save not thy life to night, to morrow thou shalt be slain. - Michal let David down through a window, and he fled and escaped; she laid an image in the bed with a pillow of goats' hair for his bolster and said, He is sick. Saul said, Bring him up to me in the bed, that I may slay him, and found the image; Michal covered herself, saying David threatened her, but she was looking out for her husband. - At this time Michal was a righteous example, a ride or die; she was a tower against death to her husband. She turns sour some chapters down the line, but here she saved his life. - Note Saul's words: why hast thou sent away mine enemy? Saul and David were brothers, both Israel, Benjamin and Judah; Saul made his brother his enemy, and David loved him anyway. That is the understanding of Christ's words on loving your enemy: David exemplified it with Saul. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 26:22 A married woman is a tower against death to her husband; that is what Michal was to David that night. - Matthew 5:44 Love your enemies; Saul was David's enemy, but David loved him, and that is the understanding Christ was going into. 1 Samuel 19:18-24 - David fled and escaped and came to Samuel to Ramah and told him all that Saul had done, and he and Samuel went and dwelt in Naioth. David was smart: he ran to the prophet, into the tower of the Lord. - Saul sent messengers to take David, and when they saw the company of the prophets prophesying and Samuel standing as appointed over them, the spirit of God was upon the messengers of Saul, and they also prophesied; a second and a third set of messengers were sent, and the same thing happened each time they entered that atmosphere. - Then Saul went himself, fully set in his mind to take David's life himself, and the spirit of God came upon him also; he prophesied before Samuel, stripped off his clothes, and lay down naked all that day and all that night, wherefore they say, Is Saul also among the prophets? - That is the close of the session: when you are fighting for the Most High, nothing can be done unto you; if the eyes of the wicked are against you and you are ordained and predestined, his enemies came to take David and the spirit of God shut the evil down every time. --- Topics: Idolatry · Sacrifice and Atonement · The Covenant · The Feasts of the Most High · The Priesthood ← 1 Samuel 12-15 · 1 Samuel Study · 1 Samuel 20-23 →

title: 1 Samuel 20: David's Empty Seat at the New Moon
text: ← 1 Samuel 16-19 · 1 Samuel Study · 1 Samuel 24-27 → 1 Samuel 20: David's Empty Seat at the New Moon Read the chapter → 1 Samuel 20 Introduction This session covers 1 Samuel chapters 20 through 23, the history of David fleeing from Saul: Jonathan's covenant with David and the sign of the arrows, David's empty seat at the new moon, the hallowed bread at Nob and the sword of Goliath, David feigning madness before Achish king of Gath, Doeg the Edomite slaying the priests of the Lord, and Saul pursuing David to Keilah and through the wilderness of Ziph and Maon. The history is pretty straightforward reading, so the teaching pulls in only a few precepts: Christ's own recounting of the shewbread, and the witness of scripture on trusting an enemy, shown in Doeg the Edomite. 1 Samuel 20:24-27 - David hid himself in the field, and when the new moon was come the king sat down to eat. David fled at the first of the month, and at the new moon meal his seat was empty. - That first day Saul spake not anything, for he thought something had befallen David, that surely he was not clean; but on the second day of the month, with David's place empty again, Saul asked Jonathan, Wherefore cometh not the son of Jesse to meat? 1 Samuel 20:30-33 - Saul got wind that his own son was hiding David out. When Jonathan covered for David, Saul's anger was kindled against Jonathan: as long as the son of Jesse liveth upon the ground, thou shalt not be established, nor thy kingdom. - Saul cast a javelin at Jonathan to smite him, whereby Jonathan knew that it was determined of his father to slay David; from here the history follows Saul pursuing David. 1 Samuel 21: The Hallowed Bread and the Feigned Madness Read the chapter → 1 Samuel 21 1 Samuel 21:6 - The priest gave David hallowed bread, for there was no bread there but the shewbread that was taken from before the Lord. Remember David had been out in the field three days, fearful of king Saul, when he came to Nob in need. - Link this history with the words of Christ: when the Pharisees challenged his disciples for plucking the ears of corn on the sabbath day, Christ recounted this very history of David and the shewbread. Precept this in your bibles if you do not have it already. Precepts: - Mark 2:23-24 The Pharisees challenged Christ's disciples for plucking the ears of corn on the sabbath day, saying it was not lawful. - Mark 2:25-26 Christ answered, Have ye never read what David did, when he had need, and was an hungred? This is that history, David eating the shewbread which is not lawful to eat but for the priests. 1 Samuel 21:10-15 - David fled that day for fear of Saul and went to Achish the king of Gath, and the servants of Achish knew him by the song, Saul hath slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands. - David laid up these words in his heart and was sore afraid of Achish, so he changed his behaviour and feigned himself mad, scrabbling on the doors of the gate and letting his spittle fall down upon his beard. David was playing crazy; he was fearful, and Achish dismissed him as a mad man. 1 Samuel 22: Never Trust Thine Enemy Read the chapter → 1 Samuel 22 1 Samuel 22:9-10 - Here you see that Saul had placed an Edomite over his servants: Doeg the Edomite, which was set over the servants of Saul, answered and reported that David had come to Nob and that Ahimelech had inquired of the Lord for him, given him victuals, and given him the sword of Goliath the Philistine. - The scriptures tell us we are never supposed to trust our enemies, yet what we are reading is Saul with an Edomite set over his servants. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 12:10 Never trust thine enemy; but Saul had placed an Edomite over his servants. 1 Samuel 22:17-19 - Saul commanded his footmen to turn and slay the priests of the Lord, but the servants of the king would not put forth their hand to fall upon the priests of the Lord. Saul was able to get the Edomite to do what his own men would not do: Doeg turned and fell upon the priests, and slew on that day fourscore and five persons that did wear a linen ephod, and smote Nob, the city of the priests, with the edge of the sword. - Go back to Genesis and see the spirit that has been placed on this man from the beginning: Esau comforted himself with the purpose of killing his brother Jacob. Just as in the time of Saul, even to this very day, when Israel suffers violence at the hands of the other nations, especially Esau, he gets comfort out of killing us; when Saul appointed Doeg to that task, you can best believe he was quite happy over it and most likely found much pleasure in killing the priests. Precepts: - Genesis 27:41-42 Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing, and purposed in his heart to slay his brother; Rebekah warned Jacob that Esau, as touching thee, doth comfort himself, purposing to kill thee. That comfort in killing is the spirit seen again in Doeg the Edomite. 1 Samuel 23: Saul Hunts David in the Wilderness Read the chapter → 1 Samuel 23 1 Samuel 23:21-23 - When the Ziphites offered to deliver David up, Saul blessed them and sent them back: go, prepare yet, and know and see his place where his haunt is, and who hath seen him there, and come ye again to me with the certainty. - Saul is asking the Ziphites for intel. He knows David is a man of war, and he wants to be absolutely sure David is exactly where they say he is before he comes down; for it was told him that David dealeth very subtilly. --- Topics: Esau and Edom · The Feasts of the Most High · The Priesthood · The Sabbath ← 1 Samuel 16-19 · 1 Samuel Study · 1 Samuel 24-27 →

title: 1 Samuel 24: David Spares Saul in the Cave at Engedi
text: ← 1 Samuel 20-23 · 1 Samuel Study · 1 Samuel 28-31 → 1 Samuel 24: David Spares Saul in the Cave at Engedi Read the chapter → 1 Samuel 24 Introduction This session covers 1 Samuel chapters 24 through 27. In the prior chapters Saul was chasing after David, hunting him to kill him; here David twice has Saul delivered into his hand and twice refuses to touch the Lord's anointed. The teaching follows David sparing Saul in the cave at Engedi, the folly of Nabal and the wisdom of Abigail who stayed David from shedding blood, David sparing Saul a second time in the wilderness of Ziph, and David's escape into the land of the Philistines, where Achish gave him Ziklag. The main threads are David's integrity, restraint, and fear of the Most High toward his elder and king, and the lesson of a wife of good understanding who protects her house with her behavior instead of her mouth. 1 Samuel 24:1-3 - Coming out of the prior chapters, Saul was hunting after David to kill him. When Saul returned from following the Philistines and was told David was in the wilderness of Engedi, he took three thousand chosen men out of all Israel to seek David and his men upon the rocks of the wild goats. - Saul went into the cave to cover his feet: that means he was in there relieving himself. See the vulnerable position Saul was in, and yet David spared his life; that is why David could say, thou wast delivered into my hand, but I did not take thy life. Precepts: - Judges 3:24-25 Eglon's servants saw the doors of the parlour locked and said, Surely he covereth his feet in his summer chamber, and tarried till they were ashamed; covering the feet is the scripture's phrase for relieving yourself. 1 Samuel 24:4-7 - Behold, I will deliver thine enemy into thine hand: who is being referred to as the enemy? His own people; Saul was of the tribe of Benjamin, and David was of the tribe of Judah. - On the skirt: the Zondervan Compact Bible Dictionary (page 136) shows the basic garments in general use among men of biblical times were the inner tunic, the tunic coat, the girdle, and the cloak, with the headdress and sandals. The word skirt in the KJV usually refers to an article of male, not female, clothing, with meanings of extremity and corner. Where we have our fringes attached to the borders of our garments, that is the bottom part of Saul's robe that David cut off privily. Precepts: - Ruth 3:9 The dictionary's own example of the skirt: spread therefore thy skirt over thine handmaid; the skirt is the extremity of the garment. - Exodus 28:33 The dictionary's other example: the hem of the priestly robe, the border of a male garment. - Afterward David's heart smote him because he had cut off Saul's skirt, and he said, The Lord forbid that I should do this thing unto my master, the Lord's anointed. So David stayed his servants with these words and suffered them not to rise against Saul. 1 Samuel 24:8-15 - When Saul rose out of the cave, David went out after him, cried, My lord the king, and stooped with his face to the earth and bowed himself. He reverenced Saul even though Saul was trying to kill him; that is why the Most High said David is a man after mine own heart. David maintained his integrity. - David laid the proof before Saul: this day thine eyes have seen how the Lord delivered thee into mine hand in the cave, and some bade me kill thee, but mine eye spared thee, for he is the Lord's anointed. See the skirt of thy robe in my hand: I cut off the skirt and killed thee not; there is neither evil nor transgression in mine hand, yet thou huntest my soul to take it. - David left the judgment with the Most High: the Lord judge between me and thee, and the Lord avenge me of thee, but mine hand shall not be upon thee; as saith the proverb of the ancients, Wickedness proceedeth from the wicked. After whom is the king of Israel come out? after a dead dog, after a flea. 1 Samuel 24:16-20 - Saul lifted up his voice and wept, and said to David, Thou art more righteous than I, for thou hast rewarded me good, whereas I have rewarded thee evil; if a man find his enemy, will he let him go well away? - Saul made an acknowledgement there because he saw the righteousness of David: I know well that thou shalt surely be king, and that the kingdom of Israel shall be established in thine hand. Precepts: - Isaiah 32:1 Behold, a king shall reign in righteousness; that is what Saul was acknowledging, that David was operating in righteousness. 1 Samuel 24:21-22 - Saul asked David to swear that he would not cut off his seed after him nor destroy his name out of his father's house, and David sware unto Saul; Saul went home, and David and his men gat them up unto the hold. - David showed so much restraint and respect unto his elder; that is something some of us struggle with today, and we need to use this as an example. The Most High was dealing with David: even though he saw Saul acting wickedly and strangely with him, when he had the opportunity to kill Saul he would not do it. 1 Samuel 25: Nabal's Folly and Abigail's Wisdom Read the chapter → 1 Samuel 25 1 Samuel 25:1-3 - Samuel died, and all the Israelites gathered together and lamented him and buried him in his house at Ramah; and David arose and went down to the wilderness of Paran. - There was a very great man in Maon whose possessions were in Carmel, three thousand sheep and a thousand goats, shearing his sheep in Carmel. His name was Nabal, and his wife was Abigail, a woman of good understanding and of a beautiful countenance; but the man was churlish and evil in his doings, and he was of the house of Caleb. 1 Samuel 25:4-9 - David heard in the wilderness that Nabal did shear his sheep and sent ten young men to greet him in peace: peace be to thee, to thine house, and to all that thou hast. - The request was righteous: thy shepherds were with us, we hurt them not, neither was there ought missing unto them all the while they were in Carmel; ask thy young men and they will shew thee. We come in a good day; give whatsoever cometh to thine hand unto thy servants and to thy son David. 1 Samuel 25:10-13 - Nabal answered, Who is David? and who is the son of Jesse? there be many servants now a days that break away every man from his master. He was talking much smack, as if he did not even know who David was, and refused to give of his bread, his water, and his flesh to men he knew not. - When his young men told David, he said, Gird ye on every man his sword; about four hundred men went up after David, and two hundred abode by the stuff. 1 Samuel 25:14-17 - One of the young men told Abigail: David sent messengers out of the wilderness to salute our master, and he railed on them. But the men were very good unto us; we were not hurt, neither missed we any thing as long as we were conversant with them; they were a wall unto us both by night and day while we were keeping the sheep. David's men had been giving Nabal's shepherds protection from their enemies. - Evil is determined against our master and against all his household, for he is such a son of Belial that a man cannot speak to him. Some of us know people like that: you cannot talk to them, they will not reason with you. Consider that Nabal was rich, a very wealthy man, and a lot of times what comes with that is an arrogant spirit. 1 Samuel 25:18-22 - Abigail made haste and took two hundred loaves, two bottles of wine, five sheep ready dressed, parched corn, clusters of raisins, and cakes of figs, laid them on asses, and sent her servants on before her; but she told not her husband Nabal. - David had said, Surely in vain have I kept all that this fellow hath in the wilderness; he hath requited me evil for good. He swore to leave Nabal none by the morning light of any that pisseth against the wall; David was coming with intent to destroy the men of that house. 1 Samuel 25:23-25 - When Abigail saw David she hasted, lighted off the ass, fell at his feet, and said, Upon me, my lord, upon me let this iniquity be. She was not the one who did anything wrong, but she took that iniquity upon herself; she was being that pillar of her house, using wisdom to protect it, for the scripture says she was a woman of good understanding. - She did not turn her lord over to be destroyed, as some women today would be ready to do; instead she pleaded, Let not my lord regard this man of Belial, even Nabal: for as his name is, so is he; Nabal is his name, and folly is with him. She had not seen the young men David sent, or she would have stepped in then to protect their house. Precepts: - 1 Peter 2:18-19 Servants, be subject to your masters with all fear, not only to the good and gentle but also to the froward, to those that are like Nabal; enduring grief wrongfully for conscience toward God is thankworthy. - 1 Peter 3:1-2 Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands, that if any obey not the word, they may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives, beholding your chaste conversation coupled with fear; this is what Abigail was putting in place. - Her chaste conversation was her behavior: when she heard David was coming she made that feast and brought it down to meet him, to spare her house. That is the lesson for wives: if your lord is out of the spirit, instead of going railing for railing with him, your behavior should be able to win him over, to make him say, I am tripping, I have a good wife keeping the commandments who stays in a humble spirit. Provoking with the mouth just leaves an unhappy household where people living under the same roof are set against each other. 1 Samuel 25:26-31 - Abigail said, The Lord hath withholden thee from coming to shed blood and from avenging thyself with thine own hand; now let thine enemies, and they that seek evil to my lord, be as Nabal. She asked, Forgive the trespass of thine handmaid; it was Nabal who was out of the spirit, but again that chaste conversation, stepping up for her household. - The soul of my lord shall be bound in the bundle of life with the Lord thy God, and the souls of thine enemies, them shall he sling out as out of the middle of a sling. When the Lord shall have appointed thee ruler over Israel, this shall be no grief unto thee, that thou hast shed blood causeless or that my lord hath avenged himself; then remember thine handmaid. 1 Samuel 25:32-35 - David said, Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, which sent thee this day to meet me, and blessed be thy advice, and blessed be thou, which hast kept me this day from coming to shed blood and from avenging myself with mine own hand. - David received of her hand that which she had brought him and said, Go up in peace to thine house; see, I have hearkened to thy voice and have accepted thy person. 1 Samuel 25:36-38 - Abigail came home and Nabal held a feast in his house like the feast of a king, and his heart was merry within him, for he was very drunken; so she told him nothing, less or more, until the morning light. - In the morning, when the wine was gone out of Nabal, his wife told him these things, and his heart died within him, and he became as a stone. Remember he had railed, Who is David? but when he sobered up and heard that the coming king had come down to destroy everybody in his house, his heart died within him. About ten days after, the Lord smote Nabal, that he died. 1 Samuel 25:39-42 - When David heard that Nabal was dead, he said, Blessed be the Lord, that hath pleaded the cause of my reproach from the hand of Nabal, and hath kept his servant from evil: for the Lord hath returned the wickedness of Nabal upon his own head. Then David sent and communed with Abigail, to take her to him to wife. - Abigail bowed herself on her face to the earth and said, Behold, let thine handmaid be a servant to wash the feet of the servants of my lord, and she arose and washed the feet of the servants who delivered the good tidings; that is a very humble act. - She was probably very joyous and glad to go: a woman living with a man who is hard to deal with, who will not listen, will not take advice, arrogant, maybe verbally abusive, was relieved of that thing when Nabal died, and she hasted and arose with five damsels of hers and became David's wife. 1 Samuel 25:43-44 - David also took Ahinoam of Jezreel, and they were also both of them his wives; but Saul had given Michal his daughter, David's wife, to Phalti the son of Laish, which was of Gallim. 1 Samuel 26: David Spares Saul a Second Time Read the chapter → 1 Samuel 26 1 Samuel 26:1-4 - The Ziphites came unto Saul to Gibeah, saying, Doth not David hide himself in the hill of Hachilah, which is before Jeshimon? Right here we are going back: chapter 26 is picking up on what we read in chapter 23, when the Ziphites first went up to Saul to deliver David into the king's hand. Precepts: - 1 Samuel 23:19-20 Then came up the Ziphites to Saul to Gibeah, saying, Doth not David hide himself with us in the strongholds, in the hill of Hachilah? come down, O king, and our part shall be to deliver him into the king's hand; chapter 26 picks this thread back up. - Saul arose and went down to the wilderness of Ziph, having three thousand chosen men of Israel with him, and pitched in the hill of Hachilah; but David abode in the wilderness, sent out spies, and understood that Saul was come in very deed. 1 Samuel 26:5-7 - David beheld the place where Saul lay, with Abner the son of Ner, the captain of his host; Saul lay in the trench with his spear stuck in the ground at his bolster, and the people pitched round about him as protection to the king. - David asked Ahimelech the Hittite and Abishai the son of Zeruiah, the brother of Joab, Who will go down with me to Saul to the camp? and Abishai said, I will go down with thee; and they came to the people by night, and all lay sleeping. 1 Samuel 26:8-12 - Abishai said, God hath delivered thine enemy into thine hand this day; let me smite him, I pray thee, with the spear even to the earth at once, and I will not smite him the second time. But David said, Destroy him not: for who can stretch forth his hand against the Lord's anointed, and be guiltless? - David left Saul's end with the Most High: as the Lord liveth, the Lord shall smite him, or his day shall come to die, or he shall descend into battle and perish; the Lord forbid that I should stretch forth mine hand against the Lord's anointed. - They took the spear and the cruse of water from Saul's bolster and got them away, and no man saw it, nor knew it, neither awaked, for they were all asleep, because a deep sleep from the Lord was fallen upon them. 1 Samuel 26:13-16 - David went over to the other side, stood on the top of an hill afar off, and cried to Abner: Art not thou a valiant man? and who is like to thee in Israel? wherefore then hast thou not kept thy lord the king? for there came one of the people in to destroy the king thy lord. - As the Lord liveth, ye are worthy to die, because ye have not kept your master, the Lord's anointed; and now see where the king's spear is, and the cruse of water that was at his bolster. 1 Samuel 26:17-20 - Saul knew David's voice and said, Is this thy voice, my son David? And David said, Wherefore doth my lord thus pursue after his servant? for what have I done? or what evil is in mine hand? - Let not my blood fall to the earth before the face of the Lord: for the king of Israel is come out to seek a flea, as when one doth hunt a partridge in the mountains. 1 Samuel 26:21-25 - Saul said, I have sinned: return, my son David, for I will no more do thee harm, because my soul was precious in thine eyes this day: behold, I have played the fool, and have erred exceedingly. Saul was acknowledging once more David's righteousness, because again David had an opportunity to kill Saul and did not put forth his hand. - David answered, The Lord render to every man his righteousness and his faithfulness: for the Lord delivered thee into my hand to day, but I would not stretch forth mine hand against the Lord's anointed. Again he showed compassion, restraint, and the fear of the Most High. - That is what we have to get to as far as brotherly love: when we see each other, we see Christ in each other. That is what our nation is lacking, and that is why we have to be that example, as David was in sparing Saul's life. 1 Samuel 27: David Dwells in the Land of the Philistines Read the chapter → 1 Samuel 27 1 Samuel 27:1-4 - David said in his heart, I shall now perish one day by the hand of Saul: there is nothing better for me than that I should speedily escape into the land of the Philistines, and Saul shall despair of me, to seek me any more in any coast of Israel. - David passed over with the six hundred men that were with him unto Achish the son of Maoch, king of Gath, every man with his household, David with his two wives, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess and Abigail the Carmelitess, Nabal's wife. When it was told Saul that David was fled to Gath, he sought no more again for him. 1 Samuel 27:5-7 - David said to Achish, If I have found grace in thine eyes, let them give me a place in some town in the country, that I may dwell there: for why should thy servant dwell in the royal city with thee? So Achish gave him Ziklag that day; wherefore Ziklag pertaineth unto the kings of Judah unto this day. - The time that David dwelt in the country of the Philistines was a full year and four months. 1 Samuel 27:8-12 - David and his men went up and invaded the Geshurites, and the Gezrites, and the Amalekites, for those nations were of old the inhabitants of the land, as thou goest to Shur, even unto the land of Egypt; and David smote the land, left neither man nor woman alive, took away the sheep, the oxen, the asses, the camels, and the apparel, and returned to Achish. - When Achish asked, Whither have ye made a road to day? David said, Against the south of Judah, and against the south of the Jerahmeelites, and against the south of the Kenites; and he saved neither man nor woman alive to bring tidings to Gath, saying, Lest they should tell on us. - Achish believed David, saying, He hath made his people Israel utterly to abhor him; therefore he shall be my servant for ever. So the session closes with David departed out of the presence of Saul, dwelling with Achish in the land of the Philistines at Gath. --- Topics: Idolatry · Sacrifice and Atonement · The Feasts of the Most High ← 1 Samuel 20-23 · 1 Samuel Study · 1 Samuel 28-31 →

title: 1 Samuel 28: Saul and the Woman with the Familiar Spirit
text: ← 1 Samuel 24-27 · 1 Samuel Study 1 Samuel 28: Saul and the Woman with the Familiar Spirit Read the chapter → 1 Samuel 28 Introduction This session covers 1 Samuel chapters 28 through 31, the closing chapters of the book and the end of the history of Saul. The recording rejoins the class at 1 Samuel 28:15, the opening of the chapter having been read before a connection break. Saul, cut off from the Most High for his disobedience, seeks out a woman with a familiar spirit and hears his own death prophesied; the Philistine lords send David home rather than trust an enemy in their ranks; David recovers all that the Amalekites carried away from Ziklag; and Saul and his sons fall on mount Gilboa exactly as Samuel spoke. With chapter 31 the history of Saul comes to an end, and the second book of Samuel takes up the rise and the history of King David. 1 Samuel 28:15 - What Saul was doing when he went to the woman with the familiar spirit is called necromancy. Look that word up: it is when you go to somebody that conjures up spirits. - Saul turned to this because the Lord was departed from him and answered him no more, neither by prophets nor by dreams, so he had Samuel conjured up to tell him what to do. 1 Samuel 28:16-18 - Samuel asks Saul why he inquires of him, seeing the Lord is departed from him and is become his enemy. The Lord did to Saul exactly as he spake by Samuel: he rent the kingdom out of Saul's hand and gave it to his neighbour, even to David. - The reason is stated plainly: because Saul obeyed not the voice of the Lord, nor executed his fierce wrath upon Amalek. The Most High gave a law concerning Amalek, and Saul did not carry it out; that history was read earlier in this book. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 25:17-19 This is the law concerning Amalek that Samuel was referencing: Israel was commanded to blot out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven, and Saul did not do it. 1 Samuel 28:19 - Tomorrow shalt thou and thy sons be with me means tomorrow you and your sons are going to die; you are going to be with me. Samuel prophesied from his grave, and he also declared that the Lord would deliver the host of Israel into the hand of the Philistines. 1 Samuel 28:20-25 - Saul fell straightway all along the earth, sore afraid because of the words of Samuel, and there was no strength in him, for he had eaten no bread all the day nor all the night. - The woman reminded Saul that she had put her life in her hand and obeyed his voice, and asked him to let her set a morsel of bread before him that he might have strength for his way. He refused at first, but his servants together with the woman compelled him; she killed the fat calf, baked unleavened bread, and they did eat and went away that night. - The chapter in sum: Saul inquired of the Lord and was not answered, so he turned to a woman with a familiar spirit and conjured up Samuel. Samuel told him that because of his disobedience the Lord was not dealing with him anymore, and prophesied that tomorrow Saul and his sons would be with him. 1 Samuel 29: Never Trust Thine Enemy Read the chapter → 1 Samuel 29 1 Samuel 29:1-5 - The Philistines gathered all their armies to Aphek, and Israel pitched by a fountain in Jezreel. David and his men passed on in the rearward with Achish, and the princes of the Philistines demanded, What do these Hebrews here? - Achish vouched for David: he has been with me these days, or these years, and I have found no fault in him since he fell unto me. But the princes were wroth and said, Make this fellow return to his place; let him not go down with us to the battle, lest in the battle he be an adversary to us. For wherewith should he reconcile himself unto his master? should it not be with the heads of these men? - The princes remembered the song: is not this David of whom they sang one to another in dances, saying, Saul slew his thousands, and David his ten thousands? 1 Samuel 29:6-11 - Achish told David, As the Lord liveth, thou hast been upright, and thy going out and thy coming in with me in the host is good in my sight; I have not found evil in thee. Nevertheless the lords favour thee not: return, and go in peace. David protested, What have I done, that I may not go fight against the enemies of my lord the king? But Achish answered that though David was good in his sight as an angel of God, the princes had said he shall not go up with us to the battle. So David and his men rose up early and returned into the land of the Philistines, and the Philistines went up to Jezreel. - One of the things to take from this reading is that they have more sense than we do. The lords of the Philistines told Achish, No, he cannot go to battle with us, because we will always be looking over our shoulders wondering if he is going to change his mind and go back unto his people. - This is the wisdom we have to apply today. There is always an outsider who dresses like us, talks like us, and gets himself accepted among our people; yet even the Philistines knew: he might be good to you, he might be serving you, but do not trust your enemy. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 12:10 The Philistine lords understood this even without the book; it is a lesson for us to apply today. 1 Samuel 30: David Recovers All at Ziklag Read the chapter → 1 Samuel 30 1 Samuel 30:1-6 - While David and his men were away with Achish, the Amalekites invaded the south and Ziklag, smote Ziklag and burned it with fire, and carried the women captive; they slew not any, great or small, but carried them away. David and his men came to the city on the third day, found it burned, and their wives and sons and daughters taken captive; they lifted up their voice and wept until they had no more power to weep. - David's two wives were taken, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess and Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite. David was greatly distressed, for the people spake of stoning him, because the soul of all the people was grieved, every man for his sons and his daughters; but David encouraged himself in the Lord his God. - Notice how this connects to yesterday's reading in chapter 27. Achish had given David Ziklag, and David and his men had gone up and invaded the Amalekites and the other old inhabitants of the land, leaving neither man nor woman alive. Now the Amalekites came back and smote Ziklag the same way, taking David's wives and the families of his men while they were gone up with Achish. Precepts: - 1 Samuel 27:5-6 David asked Achish for a place in some town in the country, and Achish gave him Ziklag that day; wherefore Ziklag pertaineth unto the kings of Judah unto this day. - 1 Samuel 27:8-9 David and his men had invaded the Geshurites, the Gezrites, and the Amalekites, and smote the land, leaving neither man nor woman alive; this is the raid the Amalekites answered at Ziklag. 1 Samuel 30:7-8 - David said to Abiathar the priest, Ahimelech's son, Bring hither the ephod, and David inquired at the Lord: shall I pursue after this troop? shall I overtake them? The answer came, Pursue: for thou shalt surely overtake them, and without fail recover all. - David sought the Lord first and asked whether this thing was so before he moved; the Lord said go down, and you will recover. 1 Samuel 30:9-10 - David went, he and the six hundred men that were with him, and came to the brook Besor, where those that were left behind stayed. David pursued with four hundred men, for two hundred abode behind, which were so faint that they could not go over the brook Besor. 1 Samuel 30:11-15 - They found an Egyptian in the field and brought him to David; they gave him bread, water, a piece of a cake of figs, and two clusters of raisins, and when he had eaten his spirit came again to him, for he had eaten no bread nor drunk any water three days and three nights. - A sidebar worth saying: this man was faint because he had gone without food three days and three nights. Some of our people are like that after fasting one day on the last Friday of the month; we have got to check our spirits. - He was a young man of Egypt, servant to an Amalekite, left behind because he fell sick three days before; his company had invaded the south of the Cherethites, the coast of Judah, and the south of Caleb, and burned Ziklag with fire. David asked, Canst thou bring me down to this company? He answered, Swear unto me by God that thou wilt neither kill me nor deliver me into the hands of my master, and I will bring thee down to this company. 1 Samuel 30:16-20 - When he had brought him down, behold, the Amalekites were spread abroad upon all the earth, eating and drinking and dancing because of all the great spoil they had taken out of the land of the Philistines and out of the land of Judah. - David smote them from the twilight even unto the evening of the next day, and there escaped not a man of them, save four hundred young men which rode upon camels and fled. - David recovered all that the Amalekites had carried away, and rescued his two wives; there was nothing lacking to them, neither small nor great, neither sons nor daughters, neither spoil nor any thing that they had taken. David took all the flocks and the herds, and they said, This is David's spoil. 1 Samuel 30:21-25 - When David came back to the two hundred men at the brook Besor, all the wicked men and men of Belial among those that went with David said, Because they went not with us, we will not give them ought of the spoil that we have recovered, save every man his wife and his children. Notice these were David's own men, yet the scripture calls them wicked men and men of Belial; David called that thinking of the devil, saying they had the devil on them for even thinking like that. - That is the same spirit a lot of our people have today: I went down there, my hands got me this, you have got to get your own. David said, Ye shall not do so, my brethren, with that which the Lord hath given us, who hath preserved us and delivered the company that came against us into our hand. - The ruling: as his part is that goeth down to the battle, so shall his part be that tarrieth by the stuff; they shall part alike. Those that went down into the battle split the spoil with those that stayed behind, and from that day forward David made it a statute and an ordinance for Israel unto this day. 1 Samuel 30:26-31 - When David came to Ziklag he sent of the spoil unto the elders of Judah, even to his friends, saying, Behold a present for you of the spoil of the enemies of the Lord. - The spoil went to them in Bethel, in south Ramoth, in Jattir, in Aroer, in Siphmoth, in Eshtemoa, in Rachal, in the cities of the Jerahmeelites, in the cities of the Kenites, in Hormah, in Chorashan, in Athach, in Hebron, and to all the places where David himself and his men were wont to haunt. - The chapter in sum: the Amalekites spoiled the city and took the families while the men were gone up with Achish; David sought the Lord first, was told to pursue and recover, and went down and recovered all; and when his men that fought did not want to share with the men that were too faint, David made everybody part alike. 1 Samuel 31: The Death of Saul Read the chapter → 1 Samuel 31 1 Samuel 31:1-3 - Now the Philistines fought against Israel, and the men of Israel fled from before the Philistines and fell down slain in mount Gilboa. The Philistines followed hard upon Saul and upon his sons, and slew Jonathan, and Abinadab, and Malchishua, Saul's sons. - The battle went sore against Saul, and the archers hit him, and he was sore wounded of the archers. 1 Samuel 31:4-6 - Saul said unto his armourbearer, Draw thy sword, and thrust me through therewith; lest these uncircumcised come and thrust me through, and abuse me. What Saul was fearful of is what you see in war, how men will abuse their captives, killing them and abusing their bodies. He was already wounded and could not get away, so instead of being taken captive he told his armourbearer to kill him. - His armourbearer would not, for he was sore afraid; therefore Saul took a sword and fell upon it, and when his armourbearer saw that Saul was dead, he fell likewise upon his sword and died with him. So Saul died, and his three sons, and his armourbearer, and all his men, that same day together. - Remember what we read in chapter 28: when Saul went and conjured up the spirit of Samuel, Samuel said to him, To morrow shalt thou and thy sons be with me. He prophesied unto Saul what was going to happen, and now we read the fulfillment of that prophecy. Precepts: - 1 Samuel 28:19 Samuel's prophecy from the grave, fulfilled to the letter on mount Gilboa: Saul and his sons died the next day, and Israel was delivered into the hand of the Philistines. 1 Samuel 31:7 - When the men of Israel that were on the other side of the valley, and they that were on the other side of Jordan, saw that the men of Israel fled and that Saul and his sons were dead, they forsook the cities and fled, and the Philistines came and dwelt in them. 1 Samuel 31:8-10 - On the morrow, when the Philistines came to strip the slain, they found Saul and his three sons fallen in mount Gilboa. They cut off his head and stripped off his armour, and sent into the land of the Philistines round about, to publish it in the house of their idols and among the people. - They put his armour in the house of Ashtaroth, and they fastened his body to the wall of Bethshan. 1 Samuel 31:11-13 - When the inhabitants of Jabeshgilead heard of that which the Philistines had done to Saul, all the valiant men arose and went all night, and took the body of Saul and the bodies of his sons from the wall of Bethshan, and came to Jabesh and burnt them there. They took their bones and buried them under a tree at Jabesh, and fasted seven days. - So in chapter 31 we read of Saul and his sons and his armourbearer dying at the hands of the Philistines. This concludes the history of Saul coming to an end; the second book of Samuel takes up the rise and much of the history concerning King David. --- Topics: Idolatry · The Feasts of the Most High · The Priesthood ← 1 Samuel 24-27 · 1 Samuel Study

title: 1 Samuel 4: The Ark of God Is Taken
text: ← 1 Samuel 1-3 · 1 Samuel Study · 1 Samuel 8-11 → 1 Samuel 4: The Ark of God Is Taken Read the chapter → 1 Samuel 4 Introduction This session covers 1 Samuel chapters 4 through 7, the war between Israel and one of our main enemies in the Old Testament, the Philistines, and their weak fake god Dagon. Samson had already crushed Dagon's house down on the Philistines in the book of Judges, yet they rebuilt him, and the prophets keep having to humiliate their gods. Here Israel loses the ark of the covenant in battle, the Most High plagues the Philistines from city to city until they send it back, and the prophet Samuel rises up for the nation of Israel, showing that prayer is a spiritual power: when a righteous man sends up prayer, the Most High will come down in thunder against the enemies of his people. Reading about our forefathers being attacked by the other nations prepares us for the same persecution today; as the works increase, so does the attack, so stay girded up and stay focused. 1 Samuel 4:1-2 - The word of Samuel came to all Israel, and Israel went out against the Philistines to battle, pitching beside Ebenezer while the Philistines pitched in Aphek. The Philistines never wanted to leave Israel alone. - When they joined battle, Israel was smitten before the Philistines, and about four thousand men of the army fell in the field. The Philistines came up against us and whooped us in this first battle. 1 Samuel 4:3-5 - The elders of Israel asked the right question, Wherefore hath the Lord smitten us to day before the Philistines? But instead of examining the nation, they had an idea: fetch the ark of the covenant out of Shiloh, and when it comes among us it will save us out of the hand of our enemies. - The two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, came with the ark, and when it entered the camp all Israel shouted with a great shout so that the earth rang again. That is how excited and ecstatic Israel was to have the ark of the covenant among them; they felt their enemies could not destroy them now. - So what is the ark of the covenant, and what does it contain? The Lord told Moses to hew two tables of stone like the first ones he broke, and the Lord rewrote the ten commandments on them with his own finger, and Moses put the tables in the ark. The ark of the covenant contained the commandments that God wrote. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 10:1-2 The Lord instructed Moses to hew two tables of stone like unto the first, make an ark of wood, and put in it the tables the Lord would write on. - Exodus 32:19 Moses broke the first tables when he came down from the mount and saw the people dancing before the golden calf they had made from their gold earrings. - Deuteronomy 10:3-5 Moses made an ark of shittim wood, the Lord wrote on the tables the ten commandments he spake out of the midst of the fire, and Moses put the tables in the ark, and there they be. - The law is spiritual, and the law has literal spiritual power; the commandments have always been our source of power as a nation. The church teaches that the laws are done away with, but watch in these chapters how seriously the Lord regarded the ark that contained his commandments. - Watch also why the ark did not have the effect Israel expected in this battle: there were still Israelites in the midst of idolatry with idols among them, and until those idols were put away we could not be delivered from our enemies. That is the lesson Samuel drives home in chapter 7. 1 Samuel 4:6-9 - When the Philistines heard the noise of the shout and understood that the ark of the Lord was come into the camp, they were afraid, saying, God is come into the camp; woe unto us, for there hath not been such a thing heretofore. They had never had to battle Israel with the ark of the covenant in the camp. - Think on what they said: Who shall deliver us out of the hand of these mighty Gods? These are the Gods that smote the Egyptians with all the plagues. The nations knew what the Most High did to Egypt; it was known throughout the earth, and to this day real history about what the Hebrews and their God did to the Egyptians is still taught on the other side of the earth. With the ark of the commandments among us, the nations understood they were dealing with something above a regular people. - Everything our people try to glory in about Kemet, the Lord smote down. The ten plagues humiliated ten plus different gods that the Egyptians served, all their power, all their magicians and wizards. Come out of that Kemet movement; the Lord destroyed it and said Egypt would not rise again as a power in the earth. - Still the Philistines rallied: be strong, and quit yourselves like men, O ye Philistines, that ye be not servants unto the Hebrews, as they have been to you. They remembered serving Israel in the days of the Judges and refused to be slaves again, so they got ready to fight. Precepts: - 2 Esdras 1:10 The Most High destroyed many kings for Israel's sake; Pharaoh and all his power is the most popular account, and the Philistines knew it. 1 Samuel 4:10-11 - The Philistines fought, Israel was smitten again, and every man fled into his tent; there was a very great slaughter, and thirty thousand footmen of Israel fell. A second loss, far worse than the first, even with the ark in the camp. - The ark of God was taken, and the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were slain. Those two were wicked as hell, sleeping with the women that assembled at the door of the congregation and finessing the people's offerings, so in this battle the Most High allowed their lives to be taken, exactly as had been prophesied against the house of Eli. 1 Samuel 4:12-18 - A man of Benjamin ran out of the army to Shiloh the same day with his clothes rent and earth upon his head, and found Eli sitting by the wayside watching, for his heart trembled for the ark of God. Eli was very protective of the ark; he did not want anything to happen to it. - Eli was the high priest who groomed Samuel up, and he was righteous as far as himself, but his sons were devils, and he honoured his sons above the Most High by not rebuking them like a true leader should have. - Eli was ninety and eight years old and his eyes were dim, and when the messenger told him Israel fled, the slaughter was great, thy two sons are dead, and the ark of God is taken, at the mention of the ark of God he fell from off the seat backward by the side of the gate, and his neck brake, and he died, for he was an old man, and heavy. The shock of the ark being taken is what took him off that seat. - He had judged Israel forty years, and his death was ultimately part of the judgment for how he dealt with his sons, in that he did not correct them as he should have. 1 Samuel 4:19-22 - Phinehas' wife was with child, near to be delivered, and when she heard the tidings that the ark of God was taken and that her father in law and her husband were dead, she bowed herself and travailed, giving birth before her time under all that misfortune. - Dying, she named the child Ichabod, saying, The glory is departed from Israel: for the ark of God is taken. Remember what the ark contained, the commandments; with the ark gone, she said the glory of Israel was gone. It was a very sad time for the nation of Israel: thirty thousand mighty men lost, Eli dead, and the ark in the hands of the Philistines. 1 Samuel 5: Dagon Falls Before the Ark Read the chapter → 1 Samuel 5 1 Samuel 5:1-5 - The Philistines took the ark of God from Ebenezer to Ashdod, and had the audacity to bring it into the house of Dagon and set it by Dagon, a fake god the Lord had already exposed. Now watch what the ark did to their idol. - When they of Ashdod arose early on the morrow, Dagon was fallen upon his face to the earth before the ark of the Lord. This was no little souvenir you could knock over; it was a large statue, and nobody had been in there to touch it. - They set him in his place again, as if maybe the wind blew a little harder, and the next morning Dagon was fallen on his face again before the ark, with the head of Dagon and both the palms of his hands cut off upon the threshold; only the stump of Dagon was left to him. No man did this: that is the power of the ark of God. Therefore the priests of Dagon tread not on the threshold of Dagon in Ashdod unto this day. Precepts: - Judges 16:29-30 Samson had already taken hold of the two middle pillars and brought Dagon's house down on the lords of the Philistines; they rebuilt this fake god, and the Most High humiliated him again. 1 Samuel 5:6 - The hand of the Lord was heavy upon them of Ashdod, and he destroyed them, and smote them with emerods. Emerods are what we know today as hemorrhoids: swollen veins in the lower rectum that bleed and cause pain. The Most High was not playing games with the heathen; he literally afflicted them in their behinds for stealing the ark. Precepts: - Psalms 78:66 He smote his enemies in the hinder parts, and put them to a perpetual reproach; a perpetual embarrassment for taking the ark of the Lord and sitting it beside their idol. 1 Samuel 5:7-9 - The men of Ashdod said, The ark of the God of Israel shall not abide with us: for his hand is sore upon us, and upon Dagon our god. So the lords of the Philistines gathered and decided to carry the ark about unto Gath, a different location in Philistia. - The punishment followed the ark: the hand of the Lord was against Gath with a very great destruction, and he smote the men of the city, both small and great, and they had emerods in their secret parts. Moving it to another city changed nothing; the affliction went with it. 1 Samuel 5:10-12 - By the time they sent the ark to Ekron, the third location, the Ekronites had already heard what was happening and cried out, They have brought about the ark of the God of Israel to us, to slay us and our people. - The lords of the Philistines were told, Send away the ark of the God of Israel, and let it go again to his own place; for there was a deadly destruction throughout all the city, and the hand of God was very heavy there. The men that died not were smitten with the emerods, and the cry of the city went up to heaven. That was the great suffering and affliction the Philistines earned for thinking they had done something by taking the ark. 1 Samuel 6: The Ark Returned with a Trespass Offering Read the chapter → 1 Samuel 6 1 Samuel 6:1-6 - The ark of the Lord was in the country of the Philistines seven months, and the Philistines called for the priests and the diviners, asking how to send it back to his place. Seven months of that plague and they had to get it out of the land. - The priests answered, send it not empty, but in any wise return him a trespass offering; then ye shall be healed. A trespass offering acknowledges you did wrong. The offering was five golden emerods and five golden mice, according to the number of the lords of the Philistines, images of the very things that marred the land, and ye shall give glory unto the God of Israel; peradventure he will lighten his hand from off you, and from off your gods, and from off your land. - Their own priests warned them from Israel's history: wherefore then do ye harden your hearts, as the Egyptians and Pharaoh hardened their hearts? They did not want to end up like Egypt, so they said, let us learn the lesson and get this ark back. 1 Samuel 6:7-12 - The test: make a new cart, take two milch kine on which there hath come no yoke, shut up their calves at home, lay the ark on the cart with the jewels of gold in a coffer, and send it away. If it goeth up by the way of his own coast to Beth-shemesh, then he hath done us this great evil: but if not, we shall know it was a chance that happened to us, maybe just a disease spreading through the nation. - The kine took the straight way to the way of Beth-shemesh, lowing as they went, and turned not aside to the right hand or to the left, with the lords of the Philistines following to the border. Cows with no yoke, separated from their calves, walking a straight line home to Israel: that settled that it was the hand of the Lord. 1 Samuel 6:13-18 - They of Beth-shemesh were reaping their wheat harvest in the valley, and when they lifted up their eyes and saw the ark, they rejoiced to see it. As soon as the ark crossed that border coming home, it was rejoicing time in Israel. - The cart came into the field of Joshua, a Beth-shemite, and stood by a great stone; they clave the wood of the cart and offered the kine a burnt offering unto the Lord, and the Levites took down the ark and the coffer with the jewels of gold. - The golden emerods were one for each lord's city, Ashdod, Gaza, Askelon, Gath, and Ekron, and when the five lords of the Philistines had seen it, they returned to Ekron the same day. The Philistines understood it really was the Lord that had afflicted them. 1 Samuel 6:19-21 - He smote the men of Beth-shemesh, because they had looked into the ark of the Lord, even fifty thousand and threescore and ten men. It was not just the other nations that had to keep discretion with the ark of the covenant; it was forbidden to touch it or look into it unless the Lord gave you authority, no matter what tribe you were, even Levi. - They got too excited and got nosy, taking a peek to see what the writing of God looked like, and the Lord smote fifty thousand and seventy of them just for peeking. That shows us we have to have a level of discipline over our eyes; with these devices today it is very easy to take a two second look at what you know you should not be looking at. Guard your eyes. - The people lamented and said, Who is able to stand before this holy Lord God? So they sent messengers to Kirjath-jearim to come fetch the ark up. The Bible acknowledges the Most High God as the king of terrors: he was killing thousands at a time, and his judgments are terrifying. Precepts: - Job 18:14 The confidence of the wicked shall be rooted out of his tabernacle, and it shall bring him to the king of terrors; scripture owns the Most High as the king of terrors. - Psalms 66:5 Come and see the works of God: he is terrible in his doing toward the children of men, heathen and wicked Israelite alike. 1 Samuel 7: Put Away the Strange Gods, and the Lord Thundered Read the chapter → 1 Samuel 7 1 Samuel 7:1-2 - The men of Kirjath-jearim fetched up the ark of the Lord into the house of Abinadab in the hill, and sanctified Eleazar his son to keep it. While the ark abode in Kirjath-jearim the time was long, twenty years, and all the house of Israel lamented after the Lord. 1 Samuel 7:3-4 - Samuel spake unto all the house of Israel: If ye do return unto the Lord with all your hearts, then put away the strange gods and Ashtaroth from among you, and prepare your hearts unto the Lord, and serve him only, and he will deliver you out of the hand of the Philistines. Go back to how we lost the battle even with the ark of God among us: we had strange gods among us. Deliverance is not just having the ark, it is applying the commandments that are in the ark, thou shalt have no other gods before me. - Who is Ashtoreth? Astaroth in demonology is a chief figure of hell, named after the Near Eastern goddess Astarte, and Astarte is the Hellenized form of Ashtoreth, a form of Ishtar, the goddess called the queen of heaven, associated with love, beauty, sex, and war. Samuel was exhorting the people to depart from these fake gods and goddesses of the nations, and to this day there are Israelites that have not put away Ashtoreth from among them. - Easter is at its roots the celebration of Ishtar, the goddess of fertility and sex.
