When Constantine set out to merge paganism with the faith of the apostles to bring everything under one empire, pagan rituals like Easter and Saturnalia were dressed up as honoring Christ, and that was the birth of Roman Catholicism. Nothing about it mathematically adds up to Christ rising, the apostles never celebrated it or taught it, and a bunny laying eggs has nothing to do with your Lord and Saviour; it is not of Christ. - Then the children of Israel did put away Baalim and Ashtaroth, and served the Lord only. That is repentance. Precepts: - Exodus 20:3 Thou shalt have no other gods before me; the first commandment in the very ark they had been trusting in. - Jeremiah 44:15-16 The men knew that their wives burned incense unto other gods, and the people told Jeremiah plainly, we will not hearken unto thee; the same spirit is on brothers today who know their wives are in the midst of evil and will not check them. - Jeremiah 44:17-18 We will burn incense unto the queen of heaven, for then had we plenty of victuals; since we left off, we have wanted all things. That is Ishtar worship, and it is the same spirit that says, when I was in the world celebrating her holidays I was good, and now in the truth I am catching hell. 1 Samuel 7:5-8 - Samuel said, Gather all Israel to Mizpeh, and I will pray for you unto the Lord. They gathered, drew water and poured it out before the Lord, fasted that day, and said, We have sinned against the Lord; and Samuel judged the children of Israel in Mizpeh. - When the lords of the Philistines heard Israel was gathered at Mizpeh, they came up against Israel again, and Israel was afraid. But this time, instead of running for the ark, the children of Israel charged Samuel, Cease not to cry unto the Lord our God for us, that he will save us out of the hand of the Philistines. They knew the prayer of a righteous man reaches the ears of the Most High. Precepts: - James 5:16 The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much; that is why they told Samuel, do not stop praying for us. - 1 Samuel 12:23 Samuel's mentality as a leader: God forbid that I should sin against the Lord in ceasing to pray for you; for a leader of Israel to stop praying for the nation is a transgression. 1 Samuel 7:9-12 - Samuel took a sucking lamb and offered it for a burnt offering wholly unto the Lord, and Samuel cried unto the Lord for Israel, and the Lord heard him. - As Samuel was offering up the burnt offering, the Philistines drew near to battle, but the Lord thundered with a great thunder on that day upon the Philistines, and discomfited them, and they were smitten before Israel. That was no regular thunder; it was the Lord entering the battle himself. They had repented, put away the false gods, and the prayer of the righteous man reached his ears, so now the Philistines had to deal with the Most High. - The Philistines were so terrified they put up no fight; the men of Israel went out of Mizpeh and pursued them, smiting them until they came under Beth-car. Then Samuel took a stone, set it between Mizpeh and Shen, and called the name of it Ebenezer, saying, Hitherto hath the Lord helped us. - Samuel was one of the most respected prophets in the whole history of the prophets: he established the kingdom and anointed Saul, and by his faithfulness he was found a true prophet. Faithfulness translates loyalty. He came up under Eli, watched Eli's sons go wicked, Eli die, and the nation take losses, but Samuel stayed loyal to the Most High, just as Abraham's faith was tried again and again and he remained faithful. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 46:13-15 Samuel established the kingdom, judged the congregation by the law, and by his loyalty was found a true prophet. - Ecclesiasticus 46:16-17 The Apocrypha records this very history: the sucking lamb offered, the enemies pressing on every side, and the Lord thundering from heaven. - Genesis 22:1 God did tempt Abraham; the Lord tries his servants to see if they will remain faithful, and that tried loyalty is what marked Samuel as a true prophet. - Isaiah 29:6 Thou shalt be visited of the Lord of hosts with thunder, and with earthquake, and great noise, with storm and tempest; when that thunder hit, the Philistines knew who had entered the battle. - 2 Samuel 22:14-15 The Lord thundered from heaven, and the most High uttered his voice; he sent out arrows, and scattered them; lightning, and discomfited them, the same word used of the Philistines at Mizpeh. 1 Samuel 7:13-14 - So the Philistines were subdued, and they came no more into the coast of Israel: and the hand of the Lord was against the Philistines all the days of Samuel. As long as Samuel lived, the Lord kept them down. - The cities the Philistines had taken from Israel were restored, from Ekron even unto Gath, and Israel delivered the coasts out of the hands of the Philistines; and there was peace between Israel and the Amorites. 1 Samuel 7:15-17 - Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life, and went from year to year in circuit to Bethel, and Gilgal, and Mizpeh, and judged Israel in all those places; and his return was to Ramah, for there was his house, and there he built an altar unto the Lord. Ramah was his headquarters. - That yearly circuit is leadership making its rounds, establishing the people and coming back to check on them, the same example Paul followed with the churches. These chapters close with the ark lost and regained, and Samuel rising up for the nation: prayer is a superpower, and that is how our mighty forefathers rolled, from Moses to Samuel to Judas Maccabeus all the way to Christ. Keep the commandments and send up that prayer, and the Most High will come down in thunder against your enemies. Precepts: - Acts 15:36 Paul said to Barnabas, Let us go again and visit our brethren in every city where we have preached the word of the Lord, and see how they do; the same circuit the leaders of old, like Samuel, kept every year. --- Topics: Idolatry · Sacrifice and Atonement · The Covenant · The Priesthood ← 1 Samuel 1-3 · 1 Samuel Study · 1 Samuel 8-11 →

title: 1 Samuel 8: Give Us a King Like All the Nations
text: ← 1 Samuel 4-7 · 1 Samuel Study · 1 Samuel 12-15 → 1 Samuel 8: Give Us a King Like All the Nations Read the chapter → 1 Samuel 8 Introduction This session covers 1 Samuel 8 through 11: the first king of Israel. Samuel's sons pervert judgment for bribes, and the elders demand a king to judge them like all the nations; the Most High tells Samuel that Israel has not rejected the prophet but rejected him, that he should not reign over them. Samuel warns the people of the manner of the king that shall reign over them, a warning later fulfilled in Solomon and Rehoboam. Then Saul is led to Samuel the seer while seeking his father's asses, is anointed captain over the Lord's inheritance, receives another heart, is chosen at Mizpeh, and after the victory over the Ammonites at Jabeshgilead the kingdom is renewed at Gilgal. The running thread is Israel putting its trust in a man instead of the Most High, the same spirit we walk in today. 1 Samuel 8:1-3 - When Samuel was old he made his sons judges over Israel: Joel the firstborn and Abiah his second, judges in Beersheba. But his sons walked not in his ways; they turned aside after lucre, took bribes, and perverted judgment. Precepts: - Exodus 23:8 Thou shalt take no gift, for the gift blindeth the wise and perverteth the words of the righteous; that gift is what goes into bribes. - Ecclesiastes 5:8 If thou seest the oppression of the poor and violent perverting of judgment in a province, marvel not at the matter, for he that is higher than the highest regardeth; what Samuel's sons did is what we see today. - We see that same thing going on now in this political climate, and even in the church system. This is why the churches will not teach us who we are or teach the commandments of the Most High; when riots and unrest break out, it is those same pastors who go out to calm the people down. 1 Samuel 8:4-5 - All the elders of Israel gathered themselves together and came to Samuel unto Ramah: thou art old, and thy sons walk not in thy ways; now make us a king to judge us like all the nations. Your sons are not righteous like you, so instead of them judging us, give us a king like the other nations have. - Where do we see that today? Voting. We are saying the same thing today when we vote, looking to a ruler like the nations instead of to the Most High. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 17:14 Moses prophesied that Israel would come into the land and say, I will set a king over me, like as all the nations that are about me; Moses was shown from the beginning to the end, he saw Israel rejecting the Lord, and he wrote it for us to read. - Deuteronomy 17:15 The king was to be one whom the Lord thy God shall choose, one from among thy brethren; thou mayest not set a stranger over thee, which is not thy brother. - When we rejected the Lord in our own land, that also set us up to be taken out of our own land and set in a land we did not know, under oppressors. Now you hear people say, well, this one is the lesser of two evils; but they are both evil. We look at our condition now because this is what we sought: we rejected the Lord and said we want a king over us, we want to be like all the other nations. 1 Samuel 8:6-9 - The thing displeased Samuel when they said, Give us a king to judge us, and Samuel prayed unto the Lord. The Lord said, Hearken unto the voice of the people, for they have not rejected thee, but they have rejected me, that I should not reign over them; according to all the works they have done since the day I brought them up out of Egypt, forsaking me and serving other gods, so do they also unto thee. Just as they rejected the Most High, they were rejecting Samuel and his counsel. - Joshua warned us about this. At Shechem, Israel made the covenant with its own mouth to serve the Lord and obey his voice; asking for a king was breaking the choice we ourselves made. Precepts: - Joshua 24:1-4 Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel to Shechem: your fathers dwelt on the other side of the flood in old time and served other gods, and the Most High took Abraham, multiplied his seed, and Jacob and his children went down into Egypt, where we served four hundred years. - Joshua 24:14 Now therefore fear the Lord, and serve him in sincerity and in truth, and put away the gods which your fathers served; if you are sincere about serving the Lord, you are going to keep the commandments. - Joshua 24:15 Choose you this day whom ye will serve; but as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord. - Joshua 24:16-18 The people answered, God forbid that we should forsake the Lord to serve other gods, for the Lord our God brought us up out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage; therefore will we also serve the Lord, for he is our God. - Joshua 24:19-20 Joshua said, Ye cannot serve the Lord, for he is an holy God, he is a jealous God; if ye forsake the Lord and serve strange gods, he will turn and do you hurt, and consume you, after that he hath done you good. - Joshua 24:21-24 The people said, Nay, but we will serve the Lord; ye are witnesses against yourselves that ye have chosen you the Lord; the Lord our God will we serve, and his voice will we obey. We made that covenant. - How do we serve the Lord in sincerity and in truth? A lot of people today say they love the Lord, yet they do not do any of his commandments; they do not truly show they have the faith of Christ, because they do not keep the commandments. Precepts: - John 4:24 God is a Spirit, and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth. - John 6:63 The spirit is the word: the words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life. - Psalms 119:142 The truth is the law: thy law is the truth. - A lot of us grew up with that plaque in the house, as for me and my house we will serve the Lord, and the house kept not one commandment: still eating pork, still keeping Sunday, still keeping the wicked pagan holidays of our oppressors. - Christ gave the same picture: a nobleman went into a far country to receive for himself a kingdom, and his citizens hated him. This is speaking about Christ; the same spirit that said set a king over us says, We will not have Christ to reign over us. When we read Samuel again, that is why the Lord said, they did not reject you, they have rejected me. Precepts: - Luke 19:12-14 His citizens hated him and sent a message after him, saying, We will not have this man to reign over us. - Luke 19:27 But those mine enemies, which would not that I should reign over them, bring hither, and slay them before me; that is how Christ deals with them that reject his reign when he returns. 1 Samuel 8:10-18 - Samuel told all the words of the Lord unto the people that asked of him a king: this will be the manner of the king that shall reign over you. He will take your sons for his chariots and to be his horsemen; he will appoint him captains over thousands and captains over fifties, and set them to ear his ground, to reap his harvest, and to make his instruments of war. - He will take your daughters to be confectionaries, cooks, and bakers; your fields, your vineyards, and your oliveyards, even the best of them, and give them to his servants; the tenth of your seed and of your vineyards for his officers; your menservants, your maidservants, your goodliest young men, and your asses to his work; the tenth of your sheep: and ye shall be his servants. - And ye shall cry out in that day because of your king which ye shall have chosen you, and the Lord will not hear you in that day. - The manner of the king came to pass under Solomon: he levied a tax, and the tax was men. Just as men go off to war, he sent them a month on and two months off to Lebanon, to prepare the timber and stones to build the house of the Lord. Precepts: - 1 Kings 5:13-14 King Solomon raised a levy out of all Israel, thirty thousand men, and sent them to Lebanon ten thousand a month by courses: a month in Lebanon, two months at home. - 1 Kings 6:1 In the four hundred and eightieth year after the children of Israel were come out of Egypt, in the fourth year of Solomon's reign, he began to build the house of the Lord. - 1 Kings 9:22-23 Of the children of Israel did Solomon make no bondmen, but they were men of war, his servants, his princes, his captains, and rulers of his chariots and his horsemen; five hundred and fifty chief officers bare rule over the people that wrought in the work. - Under Rehoboam the yoke grew heavier still. He passed over the old men's counsel and went to the young men he came up with, and answered the people roughly. We rejected the Lord and wanted a king like all the other nations, and this is what we got; and look at our condition today, ruler after ruler and things do not get any better for us. We are getting what we deserve, because we rejected the Lord. Precepts: - 1 Kings 12:3-4 Jeroboam and all the congregation of Israel said to Rehoboam, Thy father made our yoke grievous; make his heavy yoke lighter, and we will serve thee. - 1 Kings 12:10-11 The young men counselled him to say, My little finger shall be thicker than my father's loins; my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions. - 1 Kings 12:13 The king answered the people roughly, and forsook the old men's counsel that they gave him. 1 Samuel 8:19-22 - Nevertheless the people refused to obey the voice of Samuel; and they said, Nay, but we will have a king over us, that we also may be like all the nations, and that our king may judge us, and go out before us, and fight our battles. - Samuel heard all the words of the people and rehearsed them in the ears of the Lord, and the Lord said, Hearken unto their voice, and make them a king; and Samuel sent every man unto his city. 1 Samuel 9: Saul Is Led to Samuel the Seer Read the chapter → 1 Samuel 9 1 Samuel 9:1-2 - There was a man of Benjamin named Kish, a mighty man of power, and he had a son named Saul, a choice young man and a goodly: there was not among the children of Israel a goodlier person than he, and from his shoulders and upward he was higher than any of the people. 1 Samuel 9:3-5 - The asses of Kish were lost, and Kish told Saul to take one of the servants and go seek them. They passed through mount Ephraim, the land of Shalisha, the land of Shalim, and the land of the Benjamites, and found them not; when they were come to the land of Zuph, Saul said, Come, let us return, lest my father leave caring for the asses and take thought for us. 1 Samuel 9:6-10 - The servant said, Behold, there is in this city a man of God, and he is an honourable man; all that he saith cometh surely to pass. Saul asked what they had to bring the man of God, for the bread was spent in their vessels, and the servant had at hand the fourth part of a shekel of silver to give him to tell them their way. - Beforetime in Israel, when a man went to enquire of God, thus he spake, Come, and let us go to the seer: for he that is now called a Prophet was beforetime called a Seer. Precepts: - Genesis 25:21-22 When the children struggled together within Rebekah, she went to enquire of the Lord; in that time, going to enquire of the Lord meant going to a seer. 1 Samuel 9:11-14 - Going up the hill to the city they found young maidens going out to draw water, who told them the seer had come that day, for there was a sacrifice of the people in the high place; the people would not eat until he came, because he blessed the sacrifice. As they came into the city, Samuel came out toward them, going up to the high place. 1 Samuel 9:15-17 - The Lord had told Samuel in his ear a day before Saul came: tomorrow about this time I will send thee a man out of the land of Benjamin, and thou shalt anoint him to be captain over my people Israel, that he may save my people out of the hand of the Philistines: for I have looked upon my people, because their cry is come unto me. - Saul thought he was going out to fetch his father's asses, but his purpose was to be led unto Samuel; the Lord had already told Samuel he was sending him. Precepts: - Proverbs 20:24 Man's goings are of the Lord; how can a man then understand his own way? - When Samuel saw Saul, the Lord said unto him, Behold the man whom I spake to thee of; this same shall reign over my people. 1 Samuel 9:18-21 - Saul drew near to Samuel in the gate and asked where the seer's house was, and Samuel answered, I am the seer: go up before me unto the high place, for ye shall eat with me to day. As for the asses that were lost three days ago, set not thy mind on them, for they are found. And on whom is all the desire of Israel? Is it not on thee, and on all thy father's house? - Saul answered, Am not I a Benjamite, of the smallest of the tribes of Israel, and my family the least of all the families of the tribe of Benjamin? wherefore then speakest thou so to me? 1 Samuel 9:22-24 - Samuel took Saul and his servant into the parlour and made them sit in the chiefest place among them that were bidden, about thirty persons, and had the cook set before Saul the shoulder which had been kept for him: unto this time hath it been kept for thee since I said, I have invited the people. So Saul did eat with Samuel that day. 1 Samuel 9:25-27 - Samuel communed with Saul upon the top of the house, and they arose early. As they were going down to the end of the city, Samuel said to Saul, Bid the servant pass on before us, but stand thou still a while, that I may shew thee the word of God. 1 Samuel 10: Saul Anointed Captain and Chosen King Read the chapter → 1 Samuel 10 1 Samuel 10:1 - Samuel took a vial of oil and poured it upon Saul's head, and kissed him, and said, Is it not because the Lord hath anointed thee to be captain over his inheritance? 1 Samuel 10:2-8 - Samuel gave Saul the signs that would confirm the word: two men by Rachel's sepulchre saying the asses are found and thy father sorroweth for you; three men at the plain of Tabor going up to God to Bethel, who would give him two loaves of bread; and at the hill of God, where the garrison of the Philistines is, a company of prophets coming down from the high place, and the Spirit of the Lord will come upon thee, and thou shalt prophesy with them, and shalt be turned into another man. - When these signs are come unto thee, do as occasion serve thee, for God is with thee; and go down before me to Gilgal, and seven days shalt thou tarry, till I come to thee and shew thee what thou shalt do. 1 Samuel 10:9 - When Saul had turned his back to go from Samuel, God gave him another heart, and all those signs came to pass that day. Precepts: - Ezekiel 36:26-27 A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you; I will put my spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes; that is what the Most High did for Saul. 1 Samuel 10:10-13 - When they came to the hill, the company of prophets met him, and the Spirit of God came upon him, and he prophesied among them. The people that knew him beforetime said one to another, What is this that is come unto the son of Kish? and it became a proverb, Is Saul also among the prophets? 1 Samuel 10:14-16 - Saul's uncle asked him where they went and what Samuel said unto them. Saul told him plainly that the asses were found, but of the matter of the kingdom, whereof Samuel spake, he told him not. 1 Samuel 10:17-19 - Samuel called the people together unto the Lord to Mizpeh: thus saith the Lord God of Israel, I brought up Israel out of Egypt, and delivered you out of the hand of the Egyptians, and out of the hand of all kingdoms, and of them that oppressed you. - Remember, we just came out of reading Judges, and we were oppressed by many nations there. Every time one of our judges rose up and delivered us from oppression, we would get right during the life of that judge, and when that judge died we went right back into our falling. - And ye have this day rejected your God, who himself saved you out of all your adversities and your tribulations; and ye have said unto him, Nay, but set a king over us. 1 Samuel 10:20-24 - When all the tribes came near, the tribe of Benjamin was taken, then the family of Matri, and Saul the son of Kish was taken; and when they sought him he could not be found, for the Lord answered, Behold, he hath hid himself among the stuff. They ran and fetched him thence, and when he stood among the people he was higher than any of the people from his shoulders and upward; he was real tall, taller than everybody. - Samuel said unto all the people, See ye him whom the Lord hath chosen, that there is none like him among all the people; and all the people shouted, and said, God save the king. 1 Samuel 10:25 - Samuel told the people the manner of the kingdom, and wrote it in a book, and laid it up before the Lord; and Samuel sent all the people away, every man to his house. 1 Samuel 10:26-27 - Saul went home to Gibeah, and there went with him a band of men whose hearts God had touched. But the children of Belial said, How shall this man save us? and they despised him, and brought him no presents; but he held his peace. - That is just like us today. When a man gets raised up, instead of brothers being happy for him, a brother may feel that should have been me, not knowing he has things to work on in his own spirit, and not realizing that with rank comes responsibility; you should already be doing the work. Men are being raised up for order's sake in Israel, to help set the nation in order, and we should bless them. - That is why the scriptures call the ones who despised him the children of Belial, the children of the devil: the haters. 1 Samuel 11: Saul Delivers Jabeshgilead Read the chapter → 1 Samuel 11 1 Samuel 11:1-3 - Nahash the Ammonite came up and encamped against Jabeshgilead, and all the men of Jabesh said, Make a covenant with us, and we will serve thee. Nahash answered, On this condition will I make a covenant with you, that I may thrust out all your right eyes, and lay it for a reproach upon all Israel; he wanted to blind every man in one eye. - The elders of Jabesh asked seven days' respite to send messengers unto all the coasts of Israel: if there be no man to save us, we will come out to thee. You see that? We keep putting our trust in man, even to the point of contemplating letting a man thrust our eye out. That is a destroyed people. 1 Samuel 11:4-7 - The messengers came to Gibeah of Saul and told the tidings in the ears of the people, and all the people lifted up their voices and wept. Saul came after the herd out of the field, and when he heard those tidings the Spirit of God came upon Saul, and his anger was kindled greatly. - He took a yoke of oxen and hewed them in pieces and sent them throughout all the coasts of Israel by the hands of messengers, saying, Whosoever cometh not forth after Saul and after Samuel, so shall it be done unto his oxen. And the fear of the Lord fell on the people, and they came out with one consent. 1 Samuel 11:8-11 - When he numbered them in Bezek, the children of Israel were three hundred thousand, and the men of Judah thirty thousand. They said unto the messengers, Tomorrow, by that time the sun be hot, ye shall have help; and the messengers shewed it to the men of Jabesh, and they were glad. - On the morrow Saul put the people in three companies, and they came into the midst of the host in the morning watch, and slew the Ammonites until the heat of the day; and they which remained were scattered, so that two of them were not left together. 1 Samuel 11:12-13 - The people said unto Samuel, Who is he that said, Shall Saul reign over us? bring the men, that we may put them to death. But Saul said, There shall not a man be put to death this day: for to day the Lord hath wrought salvation in Israel. 1 Samuel 11:14-15 - Then said Samuel to the people, Come, and let us go to Gilgal, and renew the kingdom there. All the people went to Gilgal, and there they made Saul king before the Lord in Gilgal, and there they sacrificed sacrifices of peace offerings before the Lord; and there Saul and all the men of Israel rejoiced greatly. --- Topics: Esau and Edom · Idolatry · Sacrifice and Atonement · The Covenant ← 1 Samuel 4-7 · 1 Samuel Study · 1 Samuel 12-15 →

title: WORLDWIDE UPHEAVAL: THE COMING CRISIS
text: Introduction Opening prayer: Heavenly Father, the God of our father Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, we thank you for another Sabbath and for the unity of the brotherhood, for a place where we can come together in fellowship in one spirit. We pray for those who are sick in the midst of us, and for our people who are in need of food, clothes and shelter; as times get harder and harder, we ask you for mercy on your people. Do not forget the promise you made to our forefathers. As we can see, the prophecy is coming to pass day by day, and we are living in the greatest time. Thank you for taking us out of nothing and making us into something, for calling us into thy marvelous light. We know it is only the beginning; strengthen our mind and our spirit, and give us the spirit to endure and to overcome, no matter what. Let all Israel say hallelujah. The deacon holds class before the bishop comes in. Deacon Malachi's class showed the history of Islam and how the Arab world and Iran are going to play a major part in these last days, how they will come together and unite. As we talk about how the Arab world is going to unite, we also have to talk about us: how should we unite under what is about to happen. So today we are going to talk about betrayal, and about the unity of the brotherhood. Thumbnail video played. Then a map of the Middle East on the screen: you can see the war going on right now with America and Israel against Iran. Iran is attacking American bases in Iraq, in Saudi Arabia and across the Gulf; it is not attacking the countries or the governments, it is attacking the military bases America has all over the Middle East, and America has them there for one reason, to control the Arabs. Stop listening to the media; it is all propaganda. Israel is killing many people right now in Lebanon, and the plan is to take Lebanon. A second map shown, the greater Israel map they drew themselves: Iraq, the whole of Syria, part of Turkey, Lebanon, part of Kuwait, part of Saudi Arabia, Egypt on the left, and the whole of Jordan. The population of Jordan today is around twelve million; to take Jordan they would have to kill twelve million people, and that is what they want to do. But we know the scriptures say they shall fail. Brothers, put your thinking cap on. Do not think for a second that these events are happening and they are not going to affect us. Some of you say, I want the prophecy fulfilled; it is good to be happy to see it, because that is how your deliverance comes. However, you had better be right. What is the purpose of jumping up and down for the prophecies when you yourself are not right? In The News Video played, NATO explained: nobody should need to explain to the president of the United States what NATO is, but it seems he does not know. NATO is a defensive alliance; if any member is attacked, everybody responds. All week since the war started the president has been talking down NATO. Second video: NATO is a military pact between 32 countries, its core rule Article 5, an attack on one is an attack on all. It was created after World War II to control Russia, and over time it kept expanding right up to Russia's borders. If Mexico ever made an alliance with Russia, the US would instantly make them choose. The push to bring Ukraine into NATO put the alliance on Moscow's doorstep, which is the reason for Russia's invasion. Ukraine used to be part of the Soviet Union; it is in Russia's backyard. Remember the missile crisis in Cuba: America did not want Russia putting weapons two hours from America. It is the same thing. Third video, what just happened: keep in mind Iran did not attack America; America and Israel decided to attack Iran, and this is why NATO does not want to help. Three NATO allies told America to use someone else's airbase, and the president responded by threatening to leave NATO entirely. Day 33 of the bombing of Iran, Operation Epic Fury. Spain closed its airspace and blocked Rota and Moron for Iran operations and called the strikes unjustifiable. Italy on March 27 denied US bombers already in the air permission to land at Sigonella in Sicily; Italy's defense minister said, Trump goes his own way without listening to anyone, we go our own way without subservience. France had quietly banned US warplanes from its airspace since February 28, the first day of bombing. Poland refused to send its Patriot systems to the Gulf: Poland's security is an absolute priority. Five NATO allies asked, five refused; the media reports them as separate stories, but it is one story, a coalition of the unwilling inside NATO itself. Iran shut the Strait of Hormuz, the choke point for twenty percent of the world's oil: oil above one hundred dollars a barrel, Europe facing fuel shortages in April, the Philippines in a state of emergency, countries from Zimbabwe to Bangladesh running out of fuel. The president told Europe to build up some delayed courage and go take the Strait themselves. So Britain's Keir Starmer organized a meeting of 35 countries, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, Canada, the UAE, Australia, South Korea and the Netherlands, a coalition to reopen the Strait of Hormuz without the United States; America was not invited and did not attend. Phase one, mine hunting with British drones; phase two, military escorts for tankers. Starmer said the UK's long term national interest requires closer partnership with its allies in Europe. NATO is not dying because of Russia, China or Iran; the video says America broke it: calling allies cowards, threatening to seize Greenland, a tariff war on Europe, a Middle East conflict started without consulting a single NATO partner, then demanding their bases, missiles and soldiers. The president is now publicly floating withdrawing from NATO after the Iran war ends. Trump says the war is nearing completion, two to three more weeks; but the world that existed on February 27 will not be the world when the bombs stop. This is not turbulence inside an alliance; it is structural collapse. This is a divorce, and the whole world is watching who gets the house. - Deacon: they organized a meeting and did not invite America. That has never happened before. You are watching a divorce take place. That is the prophecy. Later in class, videos on the cost of living: seven dollars for ten slices of cheese, seventy five dollars for three steaks that were seventy the week before, thirty dollars for ground beef, a bag of chips at six dollars, a case of soda at twenty nine. A second video: more and more people sleeping in cars, vans and tents across wealthy nations, not because they are unemployed but because the price of simply existing has exploded; rent consuming sixty to seventy percent of paychecks; entire streets in Los Angeles glowing with van windows at night, families in Australia sleeping near beaches, van dwellers in the UK hiding from council fines. A third video: people charging a thousand dollars a month to rent a single room, and homeowners telling their friends not to buy a house because of property taxes, insurance and repairs. Scriptures Opened Romans 15:4 16:56 - We open with this because everything you are seeing was written aforetime for our learning. It is through the scriptures that we get our comfort and our patience, that we might have hope. What we are showing you here, mind your business; this is not your war. If you are here and you do not know what is going to happen, I feel sorry for you. You should have already prepared your mind to know what is going to happen, because the bishop brings many classes, the deacons teach many classes, the captains teach many classes, but for some of you it goes in one ear and out the other. Revelation 17:16 33:00 - The ten horns shall hate the whore, that is America here, and shall make her desolate and naked, and burn her with fire. They will turn against America. What we are seeing right now, the beginning of NATO and America splitting, has never happened before, and that is just the beginning. That is the prophecy. - This is why I said we are living in the greatest time. You cannot tell me the Bible is not a true book. The day you tell me the Bible is a white man's book is over. The prophecy is coming to pass exactly as it is written. Amos 3:7 34:52 - The Most High does nothing unless he reveals it to his servants the prophets. We are the prophets. Six years ago the bishop broke down the book of Revelation to the teeth and connected Revelation with Daniel; those classes are still up. Now we are seeing it. - Some of you brothers do not understand what you have in your hand, the connection you have with the Messiah. Ask a mega church pastor with thousands of people what is going to happen with the war and the American army; he has no idea. Your fourteen year old son understands what is about to happen. Why? Because the Most High reveals his secret unto his servants the prophets. This Bible has secrets that nobody knows except the prophets of the Messiah, so I laugh at brothers who say there is nothing else to learn in this Bible. Baruch 3:36 37:33 - The Most High found out all the way of knowledge and gave it to Jacob his servant and to Israel his beloved. So when events happen, you should not be shocked. If you study like you are supposed to, if you take notes in class like you are supposed to, nothing that happens in these last days should surprise you. - Stop listening to the Western news. Last week when the president gave Iran forty eight hours and talked about wiping out a whole population and sending them back to the stone age, people were panicking on social media. He is not doing that; that is not what the scripture says. The prophet should know not to listen to that. The Western media wants you to believe Iran is weak and has no weapons, and some of you believe it. The scripture says they are going to come with great power. They thought right now was the best time to attack Iran because Hezbollah, Hamas and the Houthis were weak; now they found out the hard way. The youngest men in here could have told them, you do not want to do this. Obadiah 1:3 41:33 - The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee. They went into Venezuela, not one soldier was killed, and they took a president; so now, in that pride, they thought, let us do it again, go into Iran, kill the top men, and the whole government will fall. Surprise of a lifetime. Jeremiah 28:8 42:26 - The prophets that have been before of old prophesied against many countries and against great kingdoms, of war, of evil and of pestilence. Those prophets that have come back are us. America is a great kingdom, and what you see right now, we have done before; this is not our first time. We always prophesy against evil. - We might look small, but keep in mind what the Bible says about the Israelites; do not let the numbers fool you. The Most High is looking for 144,000 leaders, and you are looking at them. Some of you have low self esteem, and that is why you let your house disrespect you; we are going to talk about that too. Isaiah 47:11 46:23 - Evil shall come upon thee; thou shalt not know from whence it riseth. We know evil is coming to America. Right now they say Iran does not have missiles that can reach here, and I bet you believe that; that is why you think you are safe. Stop being a fool. Sisters keep twerking, people keep fighting at the airport, a girls trip to Ghana was twerking on Elmina Castle. Brothers, there is going to be a lot of betrayal in these last days, and some of it is going to come from inside your own house; I hope you are prepared for that. - Captain: the media has lied to our people and given them a false sense of comfort, that what is going on abroad is never going to touch us here. It is going to. Our people are still in all manner of debauchery, kids ransacking cities and running into stores, because of the witchcraft of this place. Know for certain it is coming here. Matthew 24:4-8 50:56 - Take heed that no man deceive you: do not let the media deceive you, do not let the pastors deceive you. Many shall come in my name and shall deceive many. A lot of you will get deceived; some of you will walk out of this truth and go back to the Christian church when it gets hot. Some of you brothers are going to leave when your wife says, I did not sign up for this, let's go, and you will follow her right out the door. - Ye shall hear of wars and rumours of wars. What is a rumour? I am going to send them back to the stone age; I am going to wipe out a whole population. See that ye be not troubled, for all these things must come to pass. Millions of people are going to die, brothers; it is through that that your deliverance comes. I am not praying for it to stop. There will be no peace on earth until the Israelites take over. - But the end is not yet. What you see in the Middle East right now is not even the beginning of World War III yet; I see it as the beginning of the gathering into the valley of Jehoshaphat in the book of Joel. Nation shall rise against nation: America against Iran, Iran against Israel, Russia against Ukraine, people dying in Sudan and the DR Congo. And there shall be famines. - Videos played on the price of food. You might say, deacon, that is not fair, there is food in the store. There are two types of famine: a famine where you cannot find it, and a famine where it is there and you cannot afford it. It is still famine either way; you still die hungry. A hundred dollars used to shop for the whole week; now it cannot shop for two days. And they did not give you a raise; they cut your hours. Go to your boss Monday and ask for a raise because a pound of beef is thirty dollars; he will laugh in your face. - Six years ago the bishop told you to buy these things and put them in storage, and you laughed him to scorn: this is America, this will never happen here. Six years ago that item was two dollars; now it is fifteen. The problem is some of you think you are smarter than everybody else. Fine, brother, I cannot teach you anything; I will teach the humble brother next to you. - The video on people sleeping in cars: I am showing you the connection between the war and what is happening to the whole world. This kingdom is falling. After all they put our people through, payback time has not even started yet; this is very small. - And pestilences, and earthquakes in divers places. All these are the beginning of sorrows. Matthew 24:10 1:07:17 - Then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another. Some of you are going to get offended: your wife, your husband, your children. Christ already told you some of you are going to betray each other. All these things must come to pass, brothers. Psalms 41:7 1:08:15 - All that hate me whisper together against me; against me do they devise my hurt. - Zikanabiel taught twice on marriage in the last two weeks, and in one of those classes a sister told her husband, you had better find yourself another wife, because I am not doing anything a man tells me to do. Brothers, some of you are married to broken women, and a broken woman is unlovable. Video played of a young sister: I am angry, I am mad, I care more about you than you care about me, I am tired of feeling so much. She is broken. Now picture her walking in here. - Second video played, on trauma: the person who has been traumatized wants nothing more than love, but because it is so unfamiliar, when they get it they are suspicious of it, they reject it, they test it, and they punish the person trying to love them; but somebody who is neglectful and abusive feels familiar, and that one they love endlessly. Here you are, in this truth for a while, you get your life together, you tell the bishop, deacon and captain, I want to build a family; you prove her, you marry her, you try to love her the best you can, and she cannot accept it, because all her relationships have been chaos after chaos and you are trying to bring peace. She rejects the peace because she is not used to peace. I have seen this in Israel: why are you nice to me, why did you put me in a home, I am used to a broken home. That is a dangerous spirit, and brothers, that type of woman is the one who is going to betray you in these last days. Mark my words. - I know we jump from war to famine to relationships. Listen: they all come together. This is one event unfolding right in front of your eyes, like a chessboard, and as a man of God, a prophet, a leader, you cannot afford to miss anything; the minute you miss something, you are done. - Some of our people are the only people who do not understand honor. There was a woman upset that we clap when the bishop comes in; that same woman will clap for the president, clap for her boss, and clapped in the church, but now she is in Israel she has a problem. Just leave. We do not have time for that in these last days. Micah 7:5-6 1:18:08 - Trust ye not in a friend, put ye not confidence in a guide; keep the doors of thy mouth from her that lieth in thy bosom. Do not tell her everything; she will use what you say to destroy you. This is for you emotional brothers who think, I have to tell my wife everything. That is not what the scripture says. - A man's enemies are the men of his own house. You know your enemy; keep your friends close and your enemies closer, and you keep your eyes on them. But the woman sleeping in your bed, you are not keeping your eyes on her. Every time we talk about betrayal we look at the men, Judas Iscariot; but that same Judas spirit is in some of these sisters too. When you talk about agents being sent in among us, you always think about the men and never the women. - Article read in class: the story of Izola Ware Curry, the woman who nearly assassinated Martin Luther King Jr. A decade before his assassination, a black woman stabbed him with a letter opener at a Harlem book signing and nearly killed him. Most of you have never heard of her. Imagine if it had been a real knife. He did not expect that, from a black woman. You think Esau is going to walk in here or come to your house and stab you? I do not think so. Your enemy, brothers, is in your own house, eating your food, wearing your clothes, in your bed; those are the ones you are not paying attention to because you are too busy with other things. - Captain: what the deacon is bringing out is heavy because it is not obvious. It is the subtleties, the things in the blind spot of your spirit, and now she has crept up closest to you and you are out of the spirit or you are dead. Matthew 10:35-36 1:24:31 - Christ repeats the same thing Micah said: a man's foes shall be they of his own household. Your blind spot, like the captain said, the one you are not going to see coming. - I am not only talking about sisters; brothers are going to betray too, because of what is coming. Remember Matthew 24 said some of us are going to be offended. Offended about what? The word of God. Christ is black? I am offended. Esau cannot get the kingdom? I am offended. The white man is Esau? Esau is the Arab; I am offended you even said that. Revelation 14:4 1:26:15 - These are they which were not defiled with women. The bishop always says, if you really want to know a brother, wait until after he gets married; everything about that brother changes. You do not really know a brother until after he gets married; you see him change right in front of your eyes. Numbers 30:6-8 1:27:12 - Sisters, this is about your prayers. I am showing you the power of the men you think are nothing. We might look like nothing right now, but trust me when I tell you, we are the sons of the living God; there are no greater men on the planet. It is okay that you look down on us now; there is going to be a time when every mouth is shut when you see the men of God. - Sisters, look at the man you are married to, real good; if he is not here, think about him hard. If you decide to leave him, you will never find another man of that caliber again. You will die before you find another man like that. That man is the prophets of the Bible; they do not come better than him. So be very mindful how you talk about him, what you think about him, and what you say about him to your family in the world. There is a God. - If she vowed and her husband heard it and held his peace, her vow shall stand; the Most High will honor your prayer. But if her husband disallowed her on the day he heard it, he makes her vow of none effect. If your husband hears the foolishness coming out of your mouth, praying against him, and says, Lord, do not listen to that, it is of none effect. This is the power the Most High gave the husband over the wife. This is for the woman telling her husband, find yourself another wife because I am not doing what you say. Do not get mad at us; we are reading the Bible. Precepts: - Numbers 30:3-5 For those of you with no husband: if a woman vows in her father's house in her youth and her father disallows her, her vow does not stand, and the Lord shall forgive her because her father disallowed her. The Most High also gave the father power over the daughter. 1 Corinthians 12:4-26 1:35:08 - We talked about war, betrayal and family; now the unity of the brotherhood, which is very important now. There are diversities of gifts, but the same Spirit; differences of administrations, but the same Lord. The body is one and has many members. All of us play a part in the body of Christ, and in the end we are all one under Christ; that is the unity we have. Northern kingdom, southern kingdom, we all unify under Christ. - The members which seem to be more feeble are necessary. We do not all play the same part; some play a bigger part than others, but that does not mean you are not important. Cut one finger off a hand and you see the effect. - There should be no schism in the body, but the members should have the same care one for another. Whether one member suffer, all the members suffer with it. You are wearing a purple shirt; I am wearing a purple shirt. We are on the same team; you should not come against me and I should not come against you. That is what people in the world do; when you come into Israel there should be none of that, no I am going to do my own thing. We are all one under Christ. - Or one member be honoured, all the members rejoice with it. Sisters, let that sink in. One of us wins, it is a win for us all; one of us is honored, it is an honor for us all. At my age this is the first time in my life I am in something bigger than me, fighting for something bigger than me; for the first time in my life I am somebody, and people treat me with respect. I grew up in a society where I never saw one black man honor another black man. When I came into this truth I saw men like Bishop Nathanyel, Bishop Canaan and Bishop Yaushua, men I could learn from and look at as my father. I grew up in a house with a father and did not learn a thing from him; I did not become a man until I came into IUIC. I did not know that when things get hard in a marriage you are supposed to stick with it and work it out; it takes a man to fix it and a little boy to walk away. I learned that from these men, and they did not just talk it, they showed me the example; they were living it. That is the type of men I want to honor. So you think I am going to listen to you and not honor that man? You have lost your mind. - Video played, a black man on unity: that is why you all cannot get ahead, because you do not play as a team; you play as individuals. Even if you do not like something the group is going to do, you should play along with the team; that is team power. Wealth and power follow the numbers; if you are not pooling your money, your votes, your attention, your labor, other people will pick you clean and you will stay in the same spot. He is in the world and understands being a team player; some of you in the truth do not. You walk in here and try to challenge men who have been in this truth thirty years before you. - Some of you go to camp teaching, with brothers sitting right next to you, and you forget where a scripture is; you are so prideful you will not ask the brother next to you, hey, cap, where is that scripture again? Because you do not look at this as a team. That brother next to you is wearing purple; if you win, he wins; if you embarrass yourself, you embarrass everybody. Brothers, unity brings strength. Leviticus 19:32 1:46:36 - Captain: going back to the honor we lack as a people, there are laws in the Bible that tell us how to govern ourselves with our leaders and elders. Thou shalt rise up before the hoary head and honour the face of the old man. The Bible says you are to stand on your feet in their presence. When you hear bishop on deck, deacon on deck, it should not grieve your spirit if you are keeping the laws of God; the Most High is commanding us to show honor to our leaders. That word honor is a hard thing for our people; we have fallen far from the glory the Lord created us in. Romans and Ephesians say prefer one another, endeavor to keep the unity; the Lord has to tell us to work at what should come naturally. - And fear thy God: if you have an issue rising before the elders, the bishops, the deacons, there is a lack of fear in you, because this is a commandment of God. I am the Lord. Job 29:7-8 1:49:21 - When Job went out to the gate, the place where the leaders sat to judge matters, the young men saw him and hid themselves, and the aged arose and stood up. As Job made his entry, as leaders make their entry, it is a law to rise up before them. They thought we made that up, bishop on deck, IUIC doing their own thing; no, we are following the commandments of God. - Deacon: brothers, write this down. Unity is not just agreement. Unity is oneness in purpose, in spirit and in truth. There is protection in unity, there is strength in unity, and there is power in unity. 1 Peter 2:17 1:51:31 - Peter repeats what the captain just read: honour all men, love the brotherhood, fear God, honour the king. This is the brotherhood right here; if you love the brotherhood you are not going to shame the brotherhood. Hebrews 10:25 1:52:43 - Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, but exhorting one another. Why would the Most High put it in there if we were already doing it? Exhorting means to honor one another. If a brother does something good there is nothing wrong with honoring him and letting him know. If you have two kids, one with a bad grade and one with a good grade, you do not honor both; the one with the bad grade should be ashamed so next time he works harder. That is what our people cannot do. In the world we are crabs in a barrel; we do not honor the young man who works hard and is the first in his family to go to college, but we throw a big party for the one coming out of jail who was destroying the community. Now that you are in the truth you should have a different mindset: every chance we get, we should honor and exhort each other. - And so much the more as ye see the day approaching. It is going to get harder and harder; as you see the day approaching you should exhort and honor each other more and more. A win for you is a win for us all. 1 Timothy 5:17 1:55:55 - Let the elders that rule well be counted worthy of double honour, especially they who labour in the word and doctrine. What does it mean to rule well? To be an example to the men, to the women, and especially to the young men. The bishop has been in this truth over twenty years, putting his brick in, longer than some of you have been alive; do you think we are going to allow you to come in here and disrespect these men? That is not going to happen. You might as well go back to that church. - One thing I hate is disrespect. The same way I will not allow young men to disrespect the officers, I will not allow you to disrespect the officer next to you. We come from a society where it is okay to disrespect the black man; we cannot allow that here. If you are that person, we will give you a warning, maybe two, and after that you have to go, especially when it comes to our elders. Matthew 18:19-20 1:59:54 - This is for those asking why IUIC does not join with other camps. If two of you shall agree on earth as touching any thing, it shall be done for them. What does agree mean? We have to agree in doctrine, in spirit, in the teaching, and in judgment. Some of you do not like our judgment; I do not know why you are still sitting here. IUIC does not agree in doctrine with those camps: we do not agree with the doctrine of two thirds, and we do not agree with abusing young girls; there is a lot we do not agree with. - Where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them. Verse 20 is talking about verse 19. Why would I gather with you in Christ's name if I do not agree with you? Are we gathered here in Christ's name? Yes, because we agree; that is why. When we gather and do not agree, Christ is not in the midst of it. It also says every time we come together we should be talking about the scriptures, because that is where you find Christ's name. - Captain: another thing we do not agree on is that they do not honor our elders, and that is one of the main components of the growth of a nation, the order and structure of a body. If they disrespect our elders, we have nothing to discuss; close your Bible and we will see you when we see you. Wisdom of Solomon 4:8-9 2:04:32 - Honourable age is not that which standeth in length of time, nor measured by number of years. It is not about how old you are. I heard some of you say, I am too old for these young men to tell me what to do. The Most High does not care how old you are; you can be old and be an old fool nobody wants to listen to. - Video played of an older woman with gray hair who has been married three times and does not think she is the problem, and her advice to young sisters is to have sex and live with a man before marriage. You would think a sister with gray hair should be able to guide the younger sisters; look at the advice she gives. This is why the community is the way it is. - But wisdom is the gray hair unto men, and an unspotted life is old age. There is a reason the Messiah called you in your old age so the younger men can teach you; some of you in your old age are no good, your mind is gone, and the Messiah sent the young men to help you. Instead of embracing it you say, you cannot teach me anything. Then you are going to die in your sin, brother. Precepts: - Job 12:20 Captain: he removeth away the speech of the trusty, and taketh away the understanding of the aged. Just because you think you are wise in your older years, the Lord will take away your understanding, so no one should trust what an old fool says. Daniel's wisdom was called upon as a young man; Paul told Timothy to let no man despise his youth, a younger man who became an elder over the church. Many of the prophets were called young and set over congregations because the aged, who were supposed to have the wisdom, did not; they judged incorrectly, took bribes, and were engulfed in their lust like the elders in the history of Susanna. Our leaders here in Israel United in Christ have proven themselves through time and through the rigorous scriptures, and that is why we give them the honor they deserve. Jeremiah 30:7 2:12:28 - Alas, for that day is great, so that none is like it; it is even the time of Jacob's trouble. Believe it or not, we have been talking about Jacob's trouble all day. Some of you think Jacob's trouble is just some hard times; no, Jacob's trouble comes with everything: the war, the famine, the betrayal. We are all going to go through it, brothers. Revelation 3:10 2:13:21 - Because thou hast kept the word of my patience, I also will keep thee from the hour of temptation, which shall come upon all the world, to try them that dwell upon the earth. This is going to be our trial. Jacob's trouble is going to be our trial; the Most High is going to test you to see if you are worthy of the kingdom. It is going to get hard, not easy. What I showed you today about famine, food and gas rising, is only the beginning. In the midst of all this, make sure your spirit is right with the Messiah. 2 Corinthians 13:5 2:14:07 - Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves. Examine yourself does not mean you are in sin; it means stop and see yourself, because the one thing brothers cannot do is examine their own selves; they want to examine everybody else. Are you in the midst of watching porn? Things keep happening to you, a car accident, you lost your car, you lost your job, your wife is about to leave; why you and not everybody else? Stop and examine yourself. You are doing something you have no business doing, and then you lie to yourself and lie to us: I did not do anything. - Know ye not your own selves? Nobody here knows you more than you. Do not call me asking what I think you should change about yourself; you know you more than I know you. When a brother asks that question, he knows exactly what he should change. Maybe stop watching porn. Brothers, stop it. Nahum 1:7 2:17:26 - The Lord is good, a stronghold in the day of trouble; and he knoweth them that trust in him. We all know trouble is coming; our trial is coming; and the Lord is good in the day of trouble, if you keep the law. - We are moving into a place where you will have no choice but to depend on the brother sitting next to you and the sister sitting next to you. One thing about our people, we do not work well together; the Most High is going to change that whether you like it or not. It is going to come to a point where we have no choice but to work together, or neither of us makes it. Psalms 37:25 2:19:21 - I have been young, and now am old; yet have I not seen the righteous forsaken, nor his seed begging bread. That verse will not work if we do not work together. Every Sabbath we point to the donation screen: IUIC is helping a lot of brothers and sisters, especially outside of America. Passover is about to happen, and every school outside America has to hold Passover: they have to get lambs, garments, and rent a hall, and it costs money. That verse comes to pass because we work together to make sure the brothers and sisters have what they need. For that, we have to trust each other and depend on each other. - I am not talking about the brother who was supposed to save food six years ago and said the hell with the bishop's counsel; do not come to my house. Bishop has been teaching this for seven years. If every year you had bought a hundred dollars of groceries and saved it, think how much rice and beans you would have right now. But some of you are not serious. America has spoiled some of you, and I feel sorry for some of you for what is about to happen; you have never seen famine before, so you thought we did not know what we were talking about. Now a bag of rice you cannot even afford, and you have a wife and kids. Some of you cry because they cut your electricity and there is no hot water to shower. Is there cold water? Then you can shower. In the islands many houses have no water heater. Last year in Sierra Leone the captain went two weeks without hot water and showered every day. You have been spoiled, brother. 2 Esdras 15:27 2:24:15 - For now are the plagues come upon the whole earth, and ye shall remain in them; for God shall not deliver you, because ye have sinned against him. The plagues are coming on the whole earth, and what you see right now is the beginning; there is nothing you can do about it. A lot of us are going to be alive to see it. - That is a very powerful verse. Everything we talked about today, the war, the famine, the disease, the chaos all around us; imagine all these things happen, and that verse is talking about you. You saw it, but you did not get delivered. Why? You are not right. You never took the time to get yourself right, to repent, to keep the laws of the Most High. Some of you are still breaking his laws right now as we speak; some of you cannot wait for the Sabbath to be over to break his laws. The Most High says he is not going to deliver you; you are going to die right here. After all Esau put you through in this captivity, you end up not making the kingdom; that is a terrible card to be dealt, all because you refuse to change. In Closing Twelve tribes? Twelve tribes? Twelve tribes? With that we say shalom. The bishop is next. Announcements & References Deacon Malachi's class on the history of Islam, how the Arab world and Iran will unite in the last days, and how they took our prophecy and made it their own with the Mahdi; watch it if you missed it. Zikanabiel taught twice on marriage in the last two weeks; the wife is to submit to her husband. The bishop's Revelation series from six years ago, connecting Revelation with Daniel, is still available; what was taught then is what you are seeing now. Article read in class: the story of Izola Ware Curry, who stabbed Martin Luther King Jr. with a letter opener at a Harlem book signing in 1958. Dates: Passover is about to happen; the schools outside America need lambs, garments and halls, so give at the donation screen. --- Class Notes Index Transcript: full session

title: AMERICA: THE NEW ROMAN EMPIRE
text: Introduction Opening reading, Psalm 30: I will extol thee, O Lord, for thou hast lifted me up, and hast not made my foes to rejoice over me. Weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning. Thou hast turned for me my mourning into dancing. Opening prayer: Heavenly Father, the God of our father Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, we thank you for another Sabbath and for a place where we can come together in fellowship. We pray for those who are sick in the midst of us, and for every brother that is traveling for Passover; be with these men and protect them. The work is great and we still have a long way to go; send more laborers. Watch over the bishops, the deacons, the captains and the officers you have put on the forefront to wake up thy people. As we see the prophecies coming to pass day by day, help us to prepare mentally, spiritually and physically for what is coming; no man can prepare fully, but if we put our trust in thee we can overcome. We pray for our brothers and sisters scattered to the four corners of the earth who die every day under the hand of the enemy, especially our people in the Sudan, the forgotten ones the media has a blackout on, and for our people in Palestine and Iran. Have mercy on thy people in these last days, and let the enemy be used to destroy each other for what they did to thy people. As for us, we ask for mercy and compassion; be patient with us. Let all Israel say hallelujah. Today's lesson is entitled America, the New Roman Empire. Get out your pens and papers and take notes. Thumbnail video: a mock news bulletin. The US, Israel and Iran have come to an agreement, a ceasefire for the next two weeks. Reporting live, the tension between Iran and the US is now escalating. Then a Latin declaration and the caption: it is time for Rome to perish. Shout out to the ad department; you brothers and sisters are on fire. Scriptures Opened Romans 15:4 21:51 - We open with this because it says the same thing Ecclesiastes 1:9 said last week: there is no new thing under the sun. Whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope. So it behooves us to read, read, and read more. Everything America does is written already; we are going to show you the pattern in Rome. Book read in class: The Story of Civilization, Caesar and Christ, by Will Durant (page 566): "The revolution he sought was a far deeper one, without which reforms could only be superficial and transitory. If he could cleanse the human heart of selfish desire, cruelty, and lust, utopia would come of itself, and all those institutions that rise out of human greed and violence, and the consequent need for law, would disappear. Since this would be the profoundest of all revolutions, beside which all others would be mere coups d'etat of class ousting class, Christ was in this spiritual sense the greatest revolutionist in history." - Christ was the greatest revolutionist in history; greater than Marcus Garvey. Roman law would have to disappear for his revolution. - Page 39 of the same book: the Latins gave the name Africa to the region around Carthage and Utica, and followed the Greeks in calling its Semitic population Poeni, that is, Phoenicians. The Latins became known as the Roman Empire. They are the ones that put the name Africa on the continent; do not say you never saw proof. The Latins were Edom, and they took over Japheth's Roman Republic. Some of you got that and some of you do not know what I am talking about yet; hold that thought. 2 Esdras 11:1-6 25:21 - Ezra saw a dream: an eagle came up from the sea with twelve feathered wings and three heads. She spread her wings over all the earth, and all the winds of the air blew on her. Out of her feathers grew other contrary feathers, little and small, but her heads were at rest, and the head in the midst was greater than the others. - The eagle flew with her feathers and reigned upon the earth, and all things under heaven were subject unto her; no man spake against her, not one creature upon earth could come against this eagle. It was so powerful. This is the fourth empire. 2 Esdras 12:10-11 26:45 - Listen good: 2 Esdras 11 is answered in 2 Esdras 12. The two chapters go together; chapter 11 is the vision, chapter 12 is the interpretation. The eagle that came up from the sea is the kingdom which was seen in the vision of Daniel, but it was not expounded unto him. So let us read Daniel 7 and see what Daniel saw that was never explained to him. Daniel 7:3-7 27:28 - Four great beasts came up from the sea, diverse one from another. The first was like a lion with eagle's wings: that is the Babylonian Empire. The second, like a bear raised up on one side with three ribs in its mouth: that is the Medo-Persian Empire, first called Medo-Persian and later Persia-Media because the Persians became greater than the Medes; the three ribs were Egypt, Ethiopia and Sheba. - The third, like a leopard with four wings of a fowl and four heads: that is the Greeks. The four wings are the four major armies of Alexander's four generals, and the four heads are the generals who divided the kingdom: Lysimachus, Ptolemy, Cassander and Seleucus. - Then the fourth beast, dreadful and terrible and strong exceedingly, with great iron teeth; it devoured and brake in pieces and stamped the residue with its feet, diverse from all the beasts before it, and it had ten horns. Notice it does not give you an animal symbol for the fourth beast the way it gave the lion, the bear and the leopard. Daniel never understood that the fourth kingdom would be represented by the eagle; the Most High declared that to Ezra. 2 Esdras 12:14-15 30:54 - In the same shall twelve kings reign, one after another; the twelve wings, or feathers, are twelve kings. Whereof the second shall begin to reign and shall have more time than any of the twelve: that is Augustus Caesar, who reigned the longest. Shown on screen: Birth of an Empire, coins of the twelve Caesars. We are going to go through them slowly. 2 Esdras 11:12-19 32:16 - On the right side there arose one feather and reigned over all the earth: that is Julius Caesar, circa 100 BC to 44 BC, reign 49 BC to 44 BC, dictator of the Roman Republic and among history's greatest military commanders. Notice it says dictator of the Roman Republic, not of the Roman Empire. The Roman Republic and the Roman Empire are two separate things: the Roman Republic was Japheth, the Roman Empire is Esau. - Book read in class: Dr. William Smith's Dictionary of the Bible (1896), under Obadiah: "I have several times shown that from Edom proceeded the kings who reigned in Italy, and who built up Rome to be great among the nations and chief among the provinces; and in this way Italy and Greece and all the western provinces became filled with Idumeans. Thus it is that the prophets call the whole of that nation by the name of Edom." And: "Kimchi on Joel 3 says that Julius Caesar was an Idumean. The Jews, both those who are comparatively ancient and those who are modern, believe that Titus was an Edomite; and when the prophets denounce Edom, they frequently refer it to Titus." So Julius Caesar was not Japheth; he was an Idumean, an Edomite. When you look him up he is the last dictator of the Roman Republic, but he was also the beginning of the Roman Empire. - And so it was that when it reigned, the end of it came: Julius was assassinated. The next following stood up and reigned and had a great time: Augustus, born 63 BC, died AD 14, reign 27 BC to AD 14, founder of the Roman Empire, about 41 years. Notice history has Julius as the last dictator of the Republic and Augustus as the founder of the Empire; the Bible tells you Julius was the beginning of it. - Then came a voice: Hear thou that hast borne rule over the earth so long, before thou beginnest to appear no more, there shall none after thee attain unto thy time, neither unto the half thereof. No Caesar after Augustus would reign as long as his 41 years. - Then arose the third and reigned as the other before, and appeared no more also: Tiberius, born 42 BC, died AD 37, reign AD 14 to 37, stepson of Augustus, reclusive yet an effective military general. So went it with all the residue one after another: every one reigned and then appeared no more. There were twelve in total. Luke 2:1-5 38:28 - There went out a decree from Caesar Augustus that all the world should be taxed. You thought taxation started with America; it started with Rome. Everything America does is based on ancient Rome. - Joseph went up from Nazareth to Bethlehem, because he was of the house and lineage of David, to be taxed with Mary his espoused wife. To be taxed with Mary means they filed jointly. So I do not know where brothers and sisters get this idea that we are sovereign and do not have to pay taxes; you are going to get yourself jacked up, and anybody who listens to you. - Read from the screen: Tiberius Caesar (reign AD 14 to 37) was the Roman emperor during the events covering approximately Acts 1 through Acts 10: the establishment of the church at Pentecost, the early growth of the community in Jerusalem, and the initial persecution leading to the dispersion of believers. Tiberius was emperor during the crucifixion (AD 30 or 33) and the opening chapters of Acts, and reigned until his death in AD 37, around the events of Acts 9 or 10. Luke 3:1 40:31 - Luke 2:1 names Caesar Augustus; Luke 3:1 names Tiberius. These are the feathers we are reading about in Esdras. When you read the four gospels, Tiberius is the Caesar of the time Christ was an adult. - The fourth feather: Caligula, born AD 12, died AD 41, reign AD 37 to 41, the first Roman emperor to be assassinated; initiated construction of Roman aqueducts. Within the book of Acts his reign roughly corresponds to Acts 7 (the death of Stephen) through early Acts 12: the persecution following Stephen's death and Saul's conversion (circa AD 35 to 36), Peter's vision and ministry in Acts 10 and 11 around the time Caligula's persecution of Jews in Alexandria prompted a crisis, and Acts 12 (the death of James and the imprisonment of Peter under Herod Agrippa I) just after Caligula's assassination. Acts 18:2 43:16 - The fifth feather: Claudius, born 10 BC, died AD 54, reign AD 41 to 54; began the conquest of Britain, presided at public trials. He is explicitly mentioned in Acts: he commanded all Jews to depart from Rome, which is why Aquila and Priscilla had lately come from Italy, historically dated around AD 49 to 50. Acts 11:28 45:20 - Agabus signified by the spirit that there should be great dearth throughout all the world, which came to pass in the days of Claudius Caesar. Understand that Caligula was Caesar when this was prophesied; Claudius came into power four or five years later, and that is when the famine hit, around AD 45 to 46. This is why, when we tell you to prepare, black people say it did not happen this year or next, so it is not going to happen. This did not occur for five years. Just listen closely when we tell you things. - So I do not know why people say the Bible is not a history book. It gives you the Caesars all in there. Acts 25:10-12 48:07 - The sixth feather: Nero, born AD 37, died AD 68, reign AD 54 to 68; the great fire of Rome, which he started and blamed on the black Christians (the old CD burning software was named Nero after him, with Rome on fire for its symbol); built theaters and promoted cultural activities. His reign covers the latter part of Acts, Paul's trials in Caesarea and his journey to Rome, roughly Acts 25 through 28. His name is not found in the scriptures, but Nero is the Caesar to whom Paul appeals. - Paul said, I stand at Caesar's judgment seat, where I ought to be judged. If I be an offender, or have committed anything worthy of death, I refuse not to die; but if there be none of these things whereof these accuse me, no man may deliver me unto them. I appeal unto Caesar. Festus answered, Hast thou appealed unto Caesar? Unto Caesar shalt thou go. So Paul found it better to be judged by the Romans than by the wicked Israelites, because those Pharisees wanted Paul put to death. Acts 28:30 49:30 - Paul dwelt two whole years in his own hired house in Rome and received all that came in unto him. This takes place under Nero. - The seventh feather: Galba, born 3 BC, died AD 69, reign AD 68 to 69, first in the year of the four emperors; imposed heavy taxes on districts opposing his rule. The eighth: Otho, born AD 32, died AD 69, reign January to April AD 69, only about three months, reckless and extravagant. The ninth: Vitellius, born AD 15, died AD 69, reign April to December AD 69, unambitious and self-indulgent, executed by Vespasian's soldiers. - The tenth: Vespasian, born AD 9, died AD 79, reign AD 69 to 79, founded the Flavian dynasty. What happened in AD 70? The fall of Jerusalem; he was the Caesar of the time.
