The reason that thought came to their mind was Satan. - The same way on your job: a thought comes into your mind out of nowhere and you wonder, why did that thought come to me? Satan will play with those things. The war we are fighting you cannot see; it is in your mind. Satan will play with your emotions, play with people you care about, and put thoughts in your mind that were not there, to get you to go against God. That is how the root of bitterness destroys brothers. You have to learn to control your thoughts. James 1:13-15 1:56:28 - Let no man say when he is tempted, I am tempted of God: for God cannot be tempted with evil, neither tempteth he any man. When you get wicked thoughts in your mind, that is not God; that is Satan. - But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed. What does Satan tempt you with? Your own lust, the things that you like. Your lusts and enticements are your weaknesses; that is what he is going to try to get you with. That is why you got to put on the whole armour and examine yourself to know your weakness. Do not ask anybody else what your weakness is; you know it. Figure out what you need to strengthen so Satan does not destroy you. - Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin. Where is lust conceived? In your mind. The teacher put a picture of an immodestly dressed woman on the screen and asked the brothers one by one what they saw, to teach this: we all see beautiful women, but you have to train yourself to hate evil. It does not come naturally; you cannot come to the truth and all of a sudden hate what you see out there. You train your mind, when you see it, to reject it and turn away. The older brothers with experience have matured past it; the young brothers dealing with youthful lusts have to train. Sisters too: before you came to this truth a lot of you dressed the same way, and now you have changed how you dress. When Christ returns there will be a modesty law set up. - If the thought comes and you shake it off and rebuke it, lust is not conceived. But if you sit down and entertain it, it brings forth sin. That is why Christ said adultery does not start when you lie down with the woman; adultery starts in the mind. - And sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death. Some of you say, I fornicated and I did not die. That death is talking about damnation, your soul being destroyed. God will judge you. Precepts: - Matthew 5:28 Whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart. That is exactly how lust is conceived: it starts with the look, and then the thought, in your heart, before anything physical ever happens. Mark 7:21-23 2:14:57 - For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders, thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness. An evil eye is jealousy. - All these evil things come from within, and defile the man. The thoughts you be having, the things you be hearing in your mind, a lot of times those things are Satan putting things there that are not there, that are not real, because Satan wants to defile you and put the root of bitterness inside of you. It comes from within, it forms a root, and it defiles you. Proverbs 15:10 2:17:04 - Correction is grievous unto him that forsaketh the way. One of the key points in the root of bitterness is correction: people become bitter a lot of times when they are corrected. Brothers get corrected, and in their mind Satan enters and says, they hate you, they never liked you, they are not right. And you are listening to all these thoughts, which is Satan. Like Wormtongue whispering in the king's ear: it is either Satan in your mind, or the person next to you speaking evil in your ears and you listening to it. - Before bitterness becomes a root, it must be a seed first. Something gets whispered in your mind, and once that seed starts growing into roots inside of you, you change, and you change for the worse. You might think nobody sees your change; you come to class and try to play it off, but everybody sees it, because you cannot hide bitterness. - Did Cain forsake the way? Was Cain corrected? Yes. The Lord corrected him and said, if you do well I will accept you, and Cain refused the correction; it was grievous to him, he became bitter against his brother, and he went and killed him. - He that hateth reproof shall die. If you hate when you are corrected, and you do not want anybody to tell you anything, you are going to die. Some of you might get corrected harshly, and you get offended and say, I am not coming to the school anymore. Come on, man: what shall separate you from the love of God? You are going to let a brother speaking to you in a way you did not like separate you from Christ? - A lot of sisters, after they have been corrected by their husband, become bitter against their husband. I have seen sisters become bitter and leave the truth because their husband corrected them. Sisters do not want to take accountability; if they do something wrong, they do not want to say I am sorry, and everything has to be a fight. That is Satan doing a job on our sisters. Correction from your husband is part of him ruling over you, and to rule does not mean slavery or abuse: it means to provide for her, to guide her, to teach her, to correct her, all the things a man is supposed to do for a woman he loves. Adam's flaw was that he did not correct his wife; Eve was deceived, and Adam went along with it willingly. Genesis 30:1-2 2:28:21 - When Rachel saw that she bare Jacob no children, Rachel envied her sister. Envy: that is Satan. And she said unto Jacob, Give me children, or else I die: give me a baby or I am going to kill myself. A very beautiful woman can be very manipulative and use her beauty to control you; Eve did that to Adam, and here the same thing is being done to Jacob. When a woman knows you love her more than God, she will try to use certain things against you. Brothers, never put a woman above your God: God comes first. - And Jacob's anger was kindled against Rachel: and he said, Am I in God's stead, who hath withheld from thee the fruit of the womb? This is an argument Moses saw between Jacob and his wife, and he wrote it down in a kosher way for us. Jacob was angry, and when a man is angry he lifts his voice. That is not abuse. Sisters, when your husband gets angry and yells and corrects you, that is not abuse; take the correction, see what he is saying, and fix it, instead of trying to justify yourself. Because when a woman tries to justify herself, Satan comes in her mind saying, he was wrong for what he said to you, that is abuse right there; and if you listen to Satan, you end up divorced. A sister called the teacher this same week saying her husband was abusive; when she explained, it was arguments, and some things the brother should not have said, but it was still not abuse. Abuse is abuse, and correction is not it. In Closing I did not even fully get into the root of bitterness as yet. Lord's will, part two of leaven, the root of bitterness, continues on Sunday, so tune in. If we can keep the schools open for all these feast days, we are going to keep them open and give you the things you need to get your spirit together. Now let us break some unleavened bread and bring in the Sabbath. Announcements & References The teacher rocked an Original Royalty jacket in class: this is Israelite fashion, our own unique culture. We are literally creating our culture back, because we lost our culture; when the scripture says let your light shine, it is also talking about how you dress and carry yourself. If you brothers want to look fly, hit up Original Royalty. The schools are aiming to stay open for the full seven days of the feast of unleavened bread, with fellowship each night; come together and make the feast joyous. Closing reading: 1 Corinthians 11:23-29, the bread and the cup, in remembrance of the Lord's death till he come; let a man examine himself, for he that eateth and drinketh unworthily eateth and drinketh damnation to himself. --- Class Notes Index Transcript: full session

title: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau
text: Introduction Happy Passover. Happy Sabbath. All praises to the Most High. Captain Matt is teaching with the island congregation, joined at the table by Captain Select Micah, Officer Matt, Officer Malachi, and Officer Caleb. The class opens with Psalms 30 read in full and prayer: this week of Passover we celebrate the memorial of our enemies being destroyed; continue to purge us of our impurities and the bitterness, the envy, the hatred, and malice, and any manner of uncleanness. Today's class: Bitterness, the hidden leaven from Cain to Esau. The motivation for the class: coming down to the islands, the Lord revealed that the spirit of bitterness is here, and the deacon did not get a chance to get into his class yesterday, but his topic was going into the same thing. When classes go out you will see the same talking points from the 9am class and what is going on during the week, and these things are not rehearsed. Bitterness is the hidden leaven that must be purged. We are in the midst of Passover, and if you do not purge it, that bitterness will grow into a root that will defile the soul. You see it with brothers dealing with it; many brothers have left the body and come up with crazy videos, and it all started with a root of bitterness. Scriptures Opened Psalms 30:1-12 9:38 - The chapter read to open the class before prayer: I will extol thee, O Lord; for thou hast lifted me up, and hast not made my foes to rejoice over me. Weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning. Thou hast turned for me my mourning into dancing. Ephesians 4:4 15:36 - There is one body, and one Spirit: what is going on here is going on elsewhere. The Lord puts the spirit on the leadership to bring out the class that addresses the prevalent issue at the time. We are dealing with bitterness in the midst of Passover, and the Lord reveals it is not just here but throughout the congregations. Precepts: - 1 Corinthians 10:13 There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: if we see a spirit here, as leaders we have to understand that spirit is elsewhere. But God is faithful, and will with the temptation also make a way to escape. What is the way to escape? Put a class on. Call a brother; speak to your brother, to get that spirit off of you. A lot of times the devil jumps on us and we start battling in our own mind and create a whole other reality that does not even exist. You talk to the brother and realize all that mess you were thinking and rehearsing is not even the case. 1 Corinthians 5:1-8 18:09 - Fornication was a common thing going on in Corinth; Paul is dealing with the same kind of common spirit we are dealing with. - Know ye not that a little leaven leaveneth the whole lump? That leaven is a reference to sin. A little bit of sin ruins the entire lump. - Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump: at Passover in particular you have to examine the spirit, purge out the old leaven, and become a new creature in Christ. For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us. - Therefore let us keep the feast, not with old leaven, neither with the leaven of malice and wickedness: that malice is the bitterness. The thing creeps up in your spirit; a dumb thought jumps in, the seed gets planted, then it gets nourished, and the next thing you know you have malice and hatred toward your brother. - But with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth: meaning, I have got the bitter spirit; I have to talk to my brother in sincerity and truth. You have to go to your brother. Precepts: - 1 Peter 2:21 Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that ye should follow his steps: as a believer in Christ you must follow the steps of Christ. Christ came to bring peace; bitterness does not do that. Exodus 12:15 21:19 - Seven days shall ye eat unleavened bread; even the first day ye shall put away leaven out of your houses. We had to physically do that, but it is something spiritual today. What is your house today? - Brothers are dumping out the toaster, sweeping under the floor mats and in the corners; there is not one grain of yeast in the house. Meanwhile the brother has an evil eye toward another brother, or is bitter toward his wife. We sweep our houses with diligence; we must do the same thing with our spirit, because we are the temple of God. - Whosoever eateth leavened bread, that soul shall be cut off from Israel: how do we eat the leaven today? A dumb thought jumps in your mind and you say, I do not like that brother; you are spiritually consuming it. That is how you get cut off from your people. This is a serious thing. Precepts: - 1 Corinthians 3:16-17 Know ye not that ye are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you? You will pull this out on a brother in the street about his tattoos, and meanwhile you have a whole yeast factory in your spirit. If any man defile the temple of God, him shall God destroy: if you are out there with the leaven in your spirit, you are out of order too, and you will be destroyed just like that brother if you both do not repent. - Romans 6:23 The wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord, who is our Passover, who set the example. That is the promise made to Abraham, for us to get repentance for sins. - 1 Corinthians 6:19-20 Ye are not your own; ye are bought with a price, with Christ's blood. When we hide hatred, bitterness, malice, we are throwing that back in Christ's face. He bought us back; when a brother lends you something, you take extra care of it. So glorify God in your body, and in your spirit, which are God's. Exodus 13:7 25:01 - There shall no leavened bread be seen with thee, neither shall there be leaven seen with thee in all thy quarters: we do not want to be seen in the midst of sin, whether we are in Passover or not. The brother does not throw the bread out; he puts it in the storage closet and brings it back after the feast. The storage closet is where you put that sin for now, and as soon as you are out of the season you pick the sin back up. Brother, you are not in the spirit. Do not lay the bitterness aside for the season and pick right back up hating the brother; let it go totally. - Spiritually, brothers say, I am going to tuck away my hatred, tuck away my bitterness and save it for later. You tuck it in when the bishop comes around, and when he leaves you are evil again. They see through all that. Deuteronomy 16:3 28:00 - Seven days shalt thou eat unleavened bread therewith, even the bread of affliction: eating this bread, the Lord wants us mindful that we came forth out of the land of Egypt in haste. We got delivered when we were unleavened, when we were not in the midst of sin. - That thou mayest remember the day when thou camest forth out of the land of Egypt all the days of thy life: the unleavened bread is a reminder that we were catching hell in Egypt and got delivered. If we want to be delivered again, we have to move in the same spirit. Matthew 16:6 29:17 - Take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees. Precepts: - Matthew 23:1-3 The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses' seat: whatsoever they bid you observe, that observe and do; but do not ye after their works: for they say, and do not. They were hypocrites. - Mark 8:15 Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, and of the leaven of Herod: letting you know whose manner they were following. They were not just hypocrites; they were following after the manner of the wicked. - John 11:45-48 Many of the Jews believed on him, but some went their way to the Pharisees: wherever there is good, evil has to be there. If we let him alone, all men will believe on him, and the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation: that lets you know who their masters were. Leaven is an influence that spreads, and that bitterness is on the inside and corrupts the spirit. Genesis 4:1-8 33:55 - Cain was born first; make a mental note of that, just like Esau. Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground, out working the field. Who else was a man of the field? It is already letting you know what is going on. - In process of time Cain brought of the fruit of the ground an offering: he already knew right from wrong, because his father taught him sacrifice. But in a process of time Cain got evil; he did not do what the Lord commanded. - The Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering, but unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect: Abel did what was right, and Cain saw it. What do you think that builds? Envy. It is the same spirit in Esau and Jacob; it is already there in the beginning. - Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell: what really got this thing started? Correction. The correction became grievous, and that grievous spirit nourished the bitterness until it grew into murder. - If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door: the Lord told him plainly. - And Cain talked with Abel his brother: this is the deception. He acted like his friend, talked with him over a period of time, and lured him out to the field. And when they were in the field, Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him. That is the spirit you are rolling in when you move with that bitter spirit; in that wrath you will slay a brother, or in that bitterness you might betray a brother. Precepts: - Proverbs 15:10 Correction is grievous unto him that forsaketh the way: Cain forsook the way over a process of time, and the correction became grievous. And he that hateth reproof shall die, because the wages of sin is death. - Proverbs 13:10 Only by pride cometh contention: he was contending because pride was on him. I am not going to make it right with my brother; matter of fact, I have to put him to death because he is making me look bad. That is pride. But with the well advised is wisdom: let me get my spirit right; I cannot have an evil eye toward my brother. - James 3:16 For where envying and strife is, there is confusion and every evil work. Now Cain did not know right from wrong; he slew his brother. Confusion is Satan's playground; that is why his children throw all types of confusion into the media wherever they go, because every evil work is behind that cloud of confusion. - Galatians 5:26 Let us not be desirous of vain glory, provoking one another, envying one another: you try to agitate the brother to play him out of position because you are envious, to provoke him to do evil to justify your position against him. We see it even in marriage: a brother provokes his wife, she leaves out of the house and does something foolish, and he says, I told you the sister was off. No, brother; you provoked your wife. - Romans 7:11 For sin, taking occasion by the commandment, deceived me, and by it slew me: you can only acknowledge sin through the commandments of God. The law says thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart; when you meditate on it you realize, I have the evil spirit toward the brother. The law is the light, like fog lights piercing through the cloud of confusion, and what you see on the other side is yourself in the mirror of the Bible. - Psalms 37:8 Cease from anger, and forsake wrath: that bitterness is the spirit of Cain, and in that wrathful spirit you might slay a brother. None of us is above this. Do not sit in the congregation thinking such and such is getting cut with the scriptures; brother, that is you. Every lesson the leadership brings out is for us. As soon as you think, I am not dealing with that, Satan already has you lined up. 1 John 3:12-15 46:17 - Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother: if you are rolling in the bitter spirit, you are moving in the spirit of Cain, of Esau, today. This is the same spirit of the scribes and Pharisees: you read about them and say they were wicked, they were following the Romans, and here you are with an evil eye toward your brother. They were bitter toward Christ and wanted to put him to death; being bitter toward your brother is the same position. - And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother's righteous: Cain was the first recorded hater in the scriptures. - We know that we have passed from death unto life, because we love the brethren: that is why Christ said, a new commandment I give unto you. This is how you know. - He that loveth not his brother abideth in death: that brother's home is death. Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer: and ye know that no murderer hath eternal life abiding in him. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 21:27 When the ungodly curseth Satan, he curseth his own soul: you will have brothers and sisters say the wicked are going to be destroyed, and meanwhile you are moving in the same spirit. You curse Satan and curse your own soul, because when you become overcome with it you take on the same attributes Cain did. We have to exercise ourselves to have a conscience void of offense, and deal with our brother and sister uprightly according to the laws of God; do not let it fester and resonate in your spirit. Proverbs 26:24-28 51:06 - He that hateth dissembleth with his lips, and layeth up deceit within him: the brother calls talking all sweet, and you think everything is all good. When he speaketh fair, believe him not: for there are seven abominations in his heart. We read about murder, envy, pride; covetousness is in there. - Whose hatred is covered by deceit: that is why the Bible calls it the root of bitterness. What are roots covered by? Soil, meaning you cannot see them. His wickedness shall be shewed before the whole congregation: it starts where nobody can see it, but the Lord always brings it to the surface. - Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein: you try to set your brother up, you fall in it yourself. - A lying tongue hateth those that are afflicted by it, and a flattering mouth worketh ruin: when you have the spirit of bitterness you have to have a lying tongue, because you mask your true feelings. Even in your flatteries there is hatred according to the scripture. Ecclesiastes 7:9 53:25 - Be not hasty in thy spirit to be angry: for anger resteth in the bosom of fools. The bitter spirit resides in the bosom of foolish brothers and sisters. - Bitterness has a progression: it starts with correction or an offense; then pride comes in and you do not want to speak to the brother, and when you do speak, you speak in deceit, masking envy, anger, hatred. Ultimately it leads to your destruction and the destruction of those around you. Galatians 5:9 54:29 - A little leaven leaveneth the whole lump: just a little bit of bitterness defiles your entire soul. It could be one thing. Luke 12:1-2 54:58 - Beware ye of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy. For there is nothing covered, that shall not be revealed: remember, roots are covered, but the Bible says there is nothing covered. The bitterness will be revealed. - The deacon was about to get into his class last night; we had no idea when we got the call to do this broadcast. The first night we got down here there was a heavy spirit of bitterness on brothers, and we dealt with it for several hours. You come down to the island thinking everything is island vibes, and the Lord reveals all manner of bitterness. That is why these classes are coming out. James 1:14-15 56:47 - Every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed: a lot of times we think lust is just sexual. People have lust for money, for power, for other brothers' things, and also a lust for hatred, for keeping that strife and envy. Definition read in class: lust is an intense longing; enthusiasm, eagerness. Some people are eager to hate; that is their whole lifelong mission. And when you are eager about something you want to tell somebody: you want to spread that bitterness in the congregation. - Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: it has been festering, baking, growing, and now the root is revealed. It is out of the concrete, and the whole foundation is destroyed. - Illustration discussed in class: a tree near your house will send roots down into your sewage line and defile your plumbing, literally defiling your house. A freshly paved walkway looks smooth, but roots growing underneath will buckle a concrete slab that weighs a ton, and the smooth way becomes trips and bumps; some people trip and die. No matter how strong the foundation you lay, that is how dangerous bitterness is: it can uproot a solid foundation. Hebrews 3:12-13 1:00:37 - Take heed, brethren, lest there be in any of you an evil heart of unbelief, in departing from the living God. But exhort one another daily, while it is called To day: while we have the opportunity, because our life is but a vapor. We have to be genuine and deal real with the brother. Psalms 19:12-13 1:01:29 - Who can understand his errors? cleanse thou me from secret faults. Keep back thy servant also from presumptuous sins: you might have a particular lust that suits your fancy; you are the brother that likes to murmur. You have to tame that spirit: fast and pray, study, and say, Lord, get this demon off of me. - Let them not have dominion over me: if you do not, that thing will have dominion over you like the spirit had dominion over Cain, and he slew his brother. Then shall I be upright, and I shall be innocent from the great transgression. Reading shared in class on what bitterness is: bitterness in a person is more than just being upset; it is a deep, lingering resentment that settles into the heart and starts shaping how someone thinks, speaks, and reacts. Biblically it is addressed directly in Hebrews 12:15, which warns about a root of bitterness; that wording is important, because bitterness does not stay small. It grows underground and eventually shows up in visible ways: holding on to past wrongs instead of releasing them, constant replaying of hurt or betrayal, harsh or cynical speech, difficulty trusting others, quiet anger that does not go away. A bitter person may not always be loud or aggressive; sometimes it is subtle, like coldness, distance, or a critical spirit. It usually comes from unforgiveness, repeated hurt or disappointment, feeling wronged or treated unfairly, and pride; it is unresolved pain that was never properly dealt with. Spiritually it defiles not just the person but those around them, blocks peace and spiritual growth, opens the door to anger, malice, and division, and distorts perception: everything starts to look negative. - Brothers hold on to grudges for years, day of atonement after day of atonement, never telling the brother what they did not like. That thing stays on rerun in your mind. You see a brother or sister behave one way, and the minute correction comes, now they separate: I do not want to be in this office; I have to fall back; I need a break. You do not need a break; you want a break because you want to sin. - Nothing good is going to be perceived by a bitter person. That distorted perception is what happened to Cain: he thought his offering was good. Genesis 25:24-34 1:08:41 - The first came out red, all over like an hairy garment: Esau was the firstborn like Cain was the firstborn, and his birth had to be documented. Jacob was not described; he looked like everybody else. When the bishop brought out that Cain's spirit is Esau's, that is the proper understanding. - Esau was a cunning hunter, a man of the field: working the field, like Genesis 4. Crystal clear. - Feed me, I pray thee, with that same red pottage: he wanted the carnal thing. This man was carnal minded; he said to hell with the birthright, which is from above, which is spiritual. Right off the jump this is an earthly man. - And Jacob said, Sell me this day thy birthright: he told him straight up. Esau said, Behold, I am at the point to die: and what profit shall this birthright do to me? And he sware unto him, and sold his birthright unto Jacob. Jacob made him swear because a bare word was not going to hold; he needed the thing certified. - Thus Esau despised his birthright: he threw it in the garbage himself. Genesis 27:34-41 1:12:39 - He cried with a great and exceeding bitter cry: now all of a sudden he is worried about the birthright. Why do you think they want to stand in our place claiming to be the Jews? It is the same spirit. Where was that energy when he threw it away for something to eat? - Is not he rightly named Jacob? for he hath supplanted me these two times: he is lying and playing the victim. We read it: Jacob dealt with no deceit over the birthright; he asked him straight and it was up to Esau to say no. That is the false accusation the Psalms speak of, slandering his own mother's son. And that is how it goes today: throw the rock, hide the hand, and when the other side hits back, run to the council as the victim. - And Esau lifted up his voice and wept: the same worldly sorrow. - By thy sword shalt thou live: that is how the best places of the earth were gotten, by the sword, not by voting. Conquered, destroyed, decimated, and then replaced. - And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing, and Esau said in his heart, The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Jacob: in a process of time, the same thing we read in Genesis 4. Cain slew Abel; Esau wanted to kill Jacob. Cain was the firstborn; Esau was the firstborn. Same spirit. Precepts: - Genesis 33:4 And Esau ran to meet him, and embraced him, and fell on his neck, and kissed him: this is after he already said he hated his brother. Somebody who hates you can play the long game, pretend to be your friend and on your side, waiting to catch you at your worst. Jacob knew it; that is why he sent the gifts ahead. - Psalms 50:19-20 Thou givest thy mouth to evil, and thy tongue frameth deceit. Thou sittest and speakest against thy brother; thou slanderest thine own mother's son: did we not just read the slander? He tricked me two times. They were liars from the beginning, because they moved in the same spirit of Cain, who was of the wicked one. Hebrews 12:15-17 1:17:24 - Looking diligently: it is not talking about looking over the horizon; you have to look within yourself. Lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you: that is the subterranean sin that no one can see. Over time it springs up and troubles you: it distorts your thoughts and alters your perception of reality. To the pure all things are pure; when that root comes in, the things that were once pure are no longer pure. And thereby many be defiled. - Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau: definition read in class: profane means relating or devoted to that which is not sacred or biblical; secular rather than religious. This lets you know the man is carnal minded; his religion is sin. That is why he is called the man of sin, the son of perdition. When the Pharisees followed him, they were devoted to that which was not sacred. - Who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright: when we roll after the spirit of Esau, the carnal mind, we throw away our birthright. Your birthright is the kingdom; when you follow after the ways of the wicked, you throw it away. - When he would have inherited the blessing, he was rejected: and if you roll in the spirit of bitterness, you are a spiritual Edomite. Brothers talk about being a spiritual Israelite; with the bitter spirit you are the opposite on the inside, and always the victim. - For he found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears: hold on to that bitter spirit and you will find that same place of no repentance. In that day it will be too late; the judgment is set. Precepts: - 1 John 3:8-10 He that committeth sin is of the devil; for the devil sinneth from the beginning. For this purpose the Son of God was manifested, that he might destroy the works of the devil: so why do we move in the spirit of the devil and think we are moving in the spirit of Christ? In this the children of God are manifest, and the children of the devil: whosoever doeth not righteousness is not of God, neither he that loveth not his brother. If there is an offense, Matthew 18:15: you do not sow discord and murmur in the midst of the congregation and spread that spirit. - Romans 8:6-7 To be carnally minded is death; but to be spiritually minded is life and peace. The carnal mind is enmity against God: for it is not subject to the law of God. When you are spiritually minded you say, I have to gain my brother. That does not mean always being buddy-buddy, but the scripture says instead of a friend become not an enemy. Brothers want to hold on to that rival feeling, waiting to get back at the brother; that is the carnal mind. - Psalms 50:16-17 But unto the wicked God saith, What hast thou to do to declare my statutes? You are talking about in God we trust, swearing in on the Bible, and doing nothing according to the scriptures. Seeing thou hatest instruction, and castest my words behind thee: the carnal mind is at war with God. This is the battle of the spirit and the flesh, and that inner battle is within us too. Philippians 3:18-20 1:26:50 - A lot of times we go for the low hanging fruit: that brother is watching this, that brother is looking at that. We do not like to talk about the bitterness, because that thing cuts deep. - For many walk, of whom I have told you often, and now tell you even weeping, that they are the enemies of the cross of Christ: these are men with the mind of Cain and Esau. Carnal minded, earthly, of the field. - Whose end is destruction, whose God is their belly: feed me with that red pottage; to hell with the inheritance. Whose glory is in their shame, who mind earthly things: that is the man of the field. - For our conversation is in heaven: the brother that is spiritual, his conversation is the scriptures, from whence also we look for the Saviour, the Lord Jesus Christ. 2 Corinthians 7:10 1:33:18 - For godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation not to be repented of: to our inheritance. But the sorrow of the world worketh death: that is the sorrow of the man of the field, the bitter cry over what he himself threw away. We have to be sincere when we come to the Lord and have that godly sorrow; we cannot be faking it. Precepts: - Proverbs 1:28-31 Then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer: here is the worldly sorrow. When the affliction increases, after being wicked the whole time, now you are calling on the Lord, and the line is no longer available. For that they hated knowledge, and did not choose the fear of the Lord: they would none of my counsel; they despised all my reproof. Therefore shall they eat of the fruit of their own way: if you are out there sowing sin, that is what you are going to reap. Psalms 55:20-21 1:36:31 - He hath put forth his hands against such as be at peace with him: he hath broken his covenant: violence toward people who are not even bothering him, and every promise, treaty, and paper he signed, broken; hundreds of treaties broken on this land alone. They even have a saying, Indian giver, which is itself the deceit: what did the natives give? It was taken through lies, like the child that hands over the toy and then cries, he stole that from me. - The words of his mouth were smoother than butter, but war was in his heart: his words were softer than oil, yet were they drawn swords. He talks a good game: we will establish a country, give you schools. War is always behind the peaceful words. We have seen it with Jacob, in the Greek captivity, and today: peace negotiators invited to talk while their country is bombed. - And is that not the same thing when you have the bitter spirit? A brother offers peace: hey man, I think you have something against me. Nah, brother, we are good. That is you destroying any opportunity for peace negotiation, and then you turn around and call the wicked man wicked for doing the same thing to his negotiators. Thou art the man. Matthew 25:1-13 1:38:41 - The kingdom of heaven is like unto ten virgins; five were wise, and five were foolish. They that were foolish took their lamps, and took no oil with them: no wisdom with them. - At midnight there was a cry made, Behold, the bridegroom cometh: Christ returns. The foolish said unto the wise, Give us of your oil; but the wise answered, Not so; lest there be not enough for us and you: meaning you are on your own in that day. - And while they went to buy, the bridegroom came; and they that were ready went in with him to the marriage: and the door was shut. Afterward came also the other virgins, saying, Lord, Lord, open to us. But he answered, Verily I say unto you, I know you not: you are not on the guest list. - Watch therefore: we have to watch ourselves. We do not want that door shutting; we have to stay in the spirit. Leviticus 19:17-18 1:41:32 - Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart: we cannot move in the spirit of Cain; we cannot move in the spirit of Esau. Cain hated Abel; Esau hates Jacob. - Thou shalt in any wise rebuke thy neighbour, and not suffer sin upon him: if I love a brother, if I have love for a sister, I have to correct them, because the wages of sin is death. This is how we know we have passed from death unto life: we love the brethren. - Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people: that is my neighbor, my brother; we are all going through the same thing, oppressed by the same nations. What sense does it make to hate the man next to me who is oppressed like me? That is like blocking your own teammate's layup; if we watched that in a game we would say the man is crazy, and brothers do the same thing in the school. - But thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself: I am the Lord. You would not want a brother doing that to you, so do not do it to the brother. We have to have charity one for another. Matthew 5:21-24 1:44:18 - Whosoever is angry with his brother without a cause shall be in danger of the judgment: whosoever is bitter with his brother without a cause. Esau was guilty of murder according to what Christ says here, because he had the hatred in his heart even before the act. - Therefore if thou bring thy gift to the altar, and there rememberest that thy brother hath ought against thee; leave there thy gift before the altar, and go thy way; first be reconciled to thy brother: the first step. If you do not do it in that order, the Lord is not hearing what you are saying. Make amends with your brother before you come, or the gift gets rejected like Cain's offering was rejected. Ecclesiasticus 28:2-8 1:46:26 - Forgive thy neighbour the hurt that he hath done unto thee, so shall thy sins also be forgiven when thou prayest: first that, then your prayers are heard. - One man beareth hatred against another, and doth he seek pardon from the Lord? You have hatred for your brother, for your wife, for the leadership, and you are asking the Lord for forgiveness? It is not going to work. He sheweth no mercy to a man, which is like himself: who falls like you, who sins like you; and doth he ask forgiveness of his own sins? - If he that is but flesh nourish hatred, who will intreat for pardon of his sins? You cannot forgive your brother or your sister, Christ is not going to forgive you. Christ forgave us out of many idolatrous things and many sins, outside and inside this truth; we have to forgive our brothers the same way if we want that forgiveness. - Remember thy end, and let enmity cease: at the end we are judged by what is in this Bible and what we did on this earth. Remember the commandments, and bear no malice to thy neighbour; remember the covenant of the Highest, and wink at ignorance: if somebody offends you, brush it off your shoulders and let it go. - Abstain from strife, and thou shalt diminish thy sins: for a furious man will kindle strife. A sinful man disquieteth friends, and maketh debate among them that be at peace: wherever the bitter brother goes he brings debate and chaos, vain arguments with no fruit. When it says disquiet, that is the feeling when the brother comes around and your defenses go up, because only bitter brothers come with strife; the brothers with peace come with the fruit of the spirit. Ecclesiasticus 10:6-7 1:50:18 - Bear not hatred to thy neighbour for every wrong; and do nothing at all by injurious practices: remember, a bitter person's perception is negative; they cannot see right because they want to abide in darkness. The brother is bringing solutions and advice, and they do not see it; they just want to see the brother hurt, the sister hurt, slumped down and aching. - Pride is hateful before God and man: and by both doth one commit iniquity: with the bitter spirit comes pride, and when you commit iniquity you put yourself out of the kingdom of God. Proverbs 8:36 1:52:10 - But he that sinneth against me wrongeth his own soul: all they that hate me love death. Operating in the bitter spirit is loving death; you are blinded and continuing in that iniquity. Titus 3:3 1:53:06 - For we ourselves also were sometimes foolish, disobedient, deceived, serving divers lusts and pleasures: bitterness is one of those lusts. Living in malice and envy, hateful, and hating one another: when you have the root of bitterness you are literally living in malice. Do not be a hater; stop the hate. We learned that spirit here in this captivity. Deuteronomy 29:16-18 1:54:00 - Ye know how we have dwelt in the land of Egypt: the land of our captivity, the gross darkness. And ye have seen their abominations, and their idols: the false religion, the politics, the influences, all abominable in the sight of the Lord. And Babylon has you deceived: you are not out there worshipping Diana; they set yourself up as the idol. I got to do me, it is my birthday: we go after our own lust. That is the trickery of Babylon: make them their own gods, their own idols. - Lest there should be among you man, or woman, or family, or tribe, whose heart turneth away this day from the Lord our God; lest there should be among you a root that beareth gall and wormwood: that is the bitterness right there. The idols defile the mind, and now you have picked up that carnal mindset, hypnotized by the witchcraft of this place, with an evil eye toward your brother. We cannot roll like that. Acts 8:18-23 1:56:17 - When Simon saw that through laying on of the apostles' hands the Holy Ghost was given, he offered them money: a carnal minded man. Or you come into this truth saying, I want to be a captain, I want to be the deacon, I want to be the bishop. - But Peter said, Thy money perish with thee: that was covetousness and envy. I want to do what they are doing; that spirit ferments bitterness. You think because you have money and connections you are supposed to have an office, and that you are above correction. No: the Lord is the one raising up the men. - Thy heart is not right in the sight of God. Repent therefore of this thy wickedness, and pray God, if perhaps the thought of thine heart may be forgiven thee. - For I perceive that thou art in the gall of bitterness, and in the bond of iniquity: Peter saw the bitterness in the spirit. He did not want the gift to heal people; he had the bitter envy spirit: I can do it better. That is the same spirit today: that brother up there teaching does not know as many precepts as me. Brother, stay in the spirit. - Bitterness becomes a root; it is hidden, and those roots uproot concrete: they uproot relationships, uproot the congregation, uproot your marriage. If they get too deep it is almost impossible to remove them: like a big tree stump, you need heavy equipment and a chainsaw, and the whole thing becomes a construction site. Ecclesiasticus 13:15-17 2:03:37 - Every beast loveth his like, and every man loveth his neighbour: all flesh consorteth according to kind, and a man will cleave to his like. That is why you see a whole group of bitter brothers clinging together in the back of the room. - What fellowship hath the wolf with the lamb? so the sinner with the godly: that is why they separate themselves. It is all evil meant to destroy. Isaiah 29:21 2:04:32 - That make a man an offender for a word: the first sign of a bitter brother is that he is easily offended, looking for offense in anything that is said. That brother said this; I am offended. Brother, you are not in the right spirit. - They hold grudges, as we read in Leviticus 19; they revisit past wrongs; they lack forgiveness, as Ecclesiasticus 28 showed; and there is the quiet resentment, sitting back stewing in silence. Precepts: - Proverbs 16:27 An ungodly man diggeth up evil: and in his lips there is as a burning fire. That is the bitter brother always digging up the old things. - Ecclesiasticus 20:22 There is that destroyeth his own soul through bashfulness: the bitter bashful brother. He says yes sir to your face, and the whole time he has no intention in his heart of doing it. 2 Esdras 16:77-78 2:07:50 - Woe be unto them that are bound with their sins, and covered with their iniquities, like as a field is covered over with bushes, and the path thereof covered with thorns, that no man may travel through: once that bitterness becomes the overgrown field, nobody can reach you. The bitterness has overtaken your soul; you have found no place of repentance because you have hatred for the brother. The brother giving you scriptures, showing you charity, heaping coals of fire: not good enough, because you are overgrown. And it is even dangerous for a brother to reach his hand in there, because that bitter brother will cut you up and sell you out. - It is left undressed, and is cast into the fire to be consumed therewith: like you read in Revelation, hell and death were cast into the lake of fire. That is where that path ends. 1 Corinthians 15:33 2:10:00 - Be not deceived: evil communications corrupt good manners. Bitterness spreads like leaven through words: the yeast makes the thing rise, and the angry influence spreads to others through words and attitude. Precepts: - Proverbs 22:24-25 Make no friendship with an angry man; and with a furious man thou shalt not go: lest thou learn his ways, and get a snare to thy soul. The bitter brother is like that dangerous brush; there could be a viper in there. Get too close and the bitter spirit gets on you. Matthew 18:6-7 2:11:16 - Whoso shall offend one of these little ones which believe in me, it were better for him that a millstone were hanged about his neck, and that he were drowned in the depth of the sea: brothers think offense is only about a brother out in the street. No: the first offense, brother, is in your house. I have seen brothers offend their wives. - Woe unto the world because of offences! for it must needs be that offences come. Colossians 3:19 2:11:58 - Husbands, love your wives, and be not bitter against them: with that bitterness your whole family gets destroyed. Just like the root from the tree destroyed the concrete, your house was a strong foundation, and the root of bitterness came in and uprooted all of it. Now you have inherited the wind. Ephesians 4:30-32 2:12:49 - Grieve not the holy Spirit of God, whereby ye are sealed unto the day of redemption: do not be the bitter brother grieving the spirit. - Let all bitterness, and wrath, and anger, and clamour, and evil speaking, be put away from you, with all malice: notice bitterness comes first, and the rest accompany it. You have to put that thing away with extreme hatred for it. - And be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ's sake hath forgiven you: you want to seek pardon from the Lord while you hold hatred toward your brother? We read what that gets. Precepts: - Colossians 3:12-13 Put on therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved, bowels of mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness, longsuffering; forbearing one another, and forgiving one another, if any man have a quarrel against any: even as Christ forgave you, so also do ye. 2 Corinthians 13:5 2:15:38 - Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves: not your neighbor. Yourself. Precepts: - Proverbs 14:10 The heart knoweth his own bitterness: you cannot play confused when somebody asks where the bitterness is coming from. Nobody else can get in and decipher exactly what it is; we can tell you, brother, you are off, there is sin in there, but you know the specifics of what you are dealing with. - Psalms 139:23-24 Search me, O God, and know my heart: try me, and know my thoughts: and see if there be any wicked way in me. We ask the Lord to reveal the iniquity in us and not leave us blind to our own folly. And how does he search you? You have to search the scriptures. Proverbs 28:13 2:17:37 - He that covereth his sins shall not prosper: when you try to cover that bitterness, the roots keep growing; you are just hauling in more soil to dump on top of the stump. But whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall have mercy: that is what we all want. Precepts: - 1 John 1:9 If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins. That goes all the way back to Leviticus: when you brought your sacrifice before the priest, that was a public confession; you walked through the midst of all Israel with your offering. Today we hide behind walls and technology and think nobody knows; the Lord sees right through it. - James 5:16 Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed. We should be comfortable confessing our faults, because no temptation has taken you but such as is common to man. You confess to a brother and he says, brother, I was dealing with the same spirit, and you feel a lot better. Everybody deals with a level of bitterness, of lust, of lack of faith. That is not getting on the public announcement; it is finding a godly man and saying, I have this going on, I need help. They are going to help you. Matthew 6:14-15 2:20:22 - For if ye forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you: but if ye forgive not men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses. As we come into this truth, offenses are going to come; we have to forgive one another. - We are all sick, in the same hospital, walking in through the same emergency room door. If the brother next to you coughs on you, you do not get to rebuke him while you are coughing yourself. Everybody is sick in here; forgive the brother. Romans 12:2 2:22:06 - And be not conformed to this world: why? Because of who rules over this world. Do not take the mind of Cain. But be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind: after Christ; that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God. Precepts: - Psalms 119:9 Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? by taking heed thereto according to thy word. - 1 Peter 2:1-2 Wherefore laying aside all malice, and all guile: that is the fake talk because you are bitter; and hypocrisies, and envies, and all evil speakings, as newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby. - James 1:21-24 Lay apart all filthiness and superfluity of naughtiness, and receive with meekness the engrafted word, which is able to save your souls. But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves: we hear the class about putting away all bitterness, and then do not do it. That is the man beholding his natural face in a glass who goeth his way and straightway forgetteth what manner of man he was. We do not want that: we want to examine ourselves and say, Lord, thank you for revealing that evil in me and showing me I have a bitter spirit. In Closing This is a heavy topic. A lot of brothers and sisters are bitter. It came up in our congregation with a brother dealing with his wife; then we came down here and saw the same thing, and it destroyed a household. We cannot play with it. The reason these classes are coming out is that this is the spirit going on in the body right now, and if it is left unchecked it can destroy the congregation. Examine yourself, whether you are bitter toward your wife, toward the leadership, toward your brother; confess that thing and pray to the Lord to remove that spirit from you. All praise to the Most High. Lord willing, you brothers and sisters were edified, and with that we say shalom. Most High and Christ bless. Announcements & References - The class was broadcast with the island congregation during the week of Passover, with Captain Matt teaching alongside Captain Select Micah and the officers. - The deacon's class on the same root-of-bitterness topic, planned for the previous evening, is referenced throughout; the same subject continues in the leaven classes brought this Passover season. - Reading shared in class on what bitterness is, its signs, its causes, and what it does spiritually and mentally (summarized above under the Psalms 19 section). --- Class Notes Index Transcript: full session

title: Edom: The Greatly Despised
text: Introduction Early morning Sabbath class from Captain Abiel, live from San Diego at 9:00 a.m. East Coast time, during the season of Passover while the worldwide blitz covers the four corners of the earth. The class opens with a mini movie built on Obadiah: I have made thee small among the nations, thou art greatly despised; though thou exalt thyself as the eagle, thence will I bring thee down; as thou hast done, it shall be done unto thee; but upon Mount Zion shall be deliverance, and the kingdom shall be the Lord's. The question that drives the whole class: who is Esau, how did he become the greatly despised, and why? The class walks from the birth of Jacob and Esau through the birthright and the blessing, then through the receipts of history, decade by decade, asking one question over and over: why is Esau greatly despised? This class is the companion to Captain Zephaniah's class Puerto Rico: The Flame of Resistance, which follows it the same morning. Scriptures Opened Genesis 25:19-26 9:27 - Isaac entreated the Lord for his wife because she was barren, as all husbands should do: pray for your wives. The Lord was entreated of him, and Rebekah conceived. - The children struggled together within her, and she went to inquire of the Lord. The Lord said unto her: two nations are in thy womb, and two manner of people shall be separated from thy bowels. With that alone you know these children are not the same. They are in the same womb, but they are two different nations. - The one people shall be stronger than the other people: that one people is us, the so-called blacks, Latinos, and Native Americans under the line of Jacob. And the elder shall serve the younger. - The first came out red, all over like an hairy garment, and they called his name Esau. The second child is not described, because Jacob was a normal child. Only Rebekah knew the prophecy, because the Lord had told her. 2 Esdras 6:7-10 13:10 - Esdras asked, what shall be the parting asunder of the times? When is the end of what we are going through, and the beginning of your kingdom, Lord? - The answer points back to that birth: Jacob's hand held first the heel of Esau. For Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth. Esau is the last ruling empire; after Esau gets his run of the blessings, our blessings take place, and they are forever, the everlasting kingdom under Christ. - The hand of man is betwixt the heel and the hand: there is a stretch of things that must go down between Esau's end and the kingdom. And then the angel said, other question, Esdras, ask thou not. Genesis 25:27-34 15:51 - Esau was a cunning hunter, a man of the field; Jacob was a plain man, dwelling in tents. Isaac loved Esau because he did eat of his venison; but Rebekah loved Jacob, because Rebekah knew what the Lord had told her. - Feed me, I pray thee, with that same red pottage: red pottage with red meat in it, not cooked all the way. Therefore was his name called Edom, which means red. - Esau said, behold, I am at the point to die: and what profit shall this birthright do to me? He swore and sold his birthright unto Jacob for bread and pottage of lentils. Thus Esau despised his birthright. It was not taken; he sold it. - Book read in class, Modern Judaism by John Allen: the descendants of Esau, sworn enemies of the descendants of Jacob even to the end of the world, were at first a small nation inhabiting Mount Seir; after the republic of the twelve tribes was destroyed by the Assyrians and Babylonians, they increased in number, extended their dominion toward the west, subjugated Italy, founded Rome and the Roman Empire, and at length overturned the Jewish state, the second temple destroyed by Titus Vespasian. They hold dominion over all Europe, Esau detaining in captivity his brother Jacob. The prophecies of Isaiah, Jeremiah, and Obadiah against Esau, Edom, Seir, and the cities of Edom, which all belong to Rome and the Christians, have not yet received their full accomplishment; and of the Christians, Obadiah says there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau. That is future judgment. - Sworn enemies even to the end of the world means they will never be your friend. Remember Mount Seir; that name comes back. Genesis 27:1-29 23:51 - Isaac, old and dim of sight, asked Esau to take his weapons and bring him savory venison, that my soul may bless thee before I die. Rebekah heard, and commanded Jacob: fetch me two good kids of the goats, and I will make savory meat for thy father. - Christians read this and blame Jacob: he stole Esau's blessing, he lied. No. Esau had already despised and sold his birthright. And Jacob himself objected: Esau is a hairy man, I am a smooth man; my father will feel me, and I shall seem to him as a deceiver, and bring a curse on me. His mother said, upon me be thy curse. Why would she say that? Because she knew the prophecy. She said, this is the moment where the elder shall serve the younger; this is what God told me when the babies were born. I will take the sin; just do what I say. - She put Esau's raiment on Jacob so he would smell like the field, that earthy hunting smell, and the goat skins on his hands and neck. - Isaac is not stupid. How is it that thou hast found it so quickly, my son? Hunting venison takes time: find the tracks, track it, wait. Jacob answered, because the Lord thy God brought it to me. Isaac felt him: the voice is Jacob's voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau. He asked again, art thou my very son Esau? He ate, he drank, and then, come near now and kiss me, my son, because he wanted to smell him. He smelled the smell of his raiment: yes, the smell of my son is as the smell of a field which the Lord hath blessed. - Here the prophecy goes according to what God wanted. How is the elder going to serve the younger if the elder gets all of the blessings? The Lord let Isaac's eyes go dim so he could not discern, and Rebekah put the younger in to receive the elder's blessing: God give thee of the dew of heaven, and the fatness of the earth, and plenty of corn and wine. Let people serve thee, and nations bow down to thee. Be lord over thy brethren. Cursed be every one that curseth thee, and blessed be he that blesseth thee. - All of us have this blessing, but our blessing does not come into fruition until the appointed time. Genesis 27:30-41 33:42 - Esau came in from his hunting, and Isaac trembled very exceedingly: who? Where is he that hath taken venison? I have eaten of all before thou camest, and have blessed him; yea, and he shall be blessed. Whatever I told that man, he is going to get blessed. - Esau cried with a great and exceeding bitter cry: bless me, even me also, O my father. Thy brother came with subtilty, and hath taken away thy blessing. Is not he rightly named Jacob? For he hath supplanted me these two times: the birthright, and this moment right here. - Isaac answered: behold, I have made him thy lord, and all his brethren have I given to him for servants. That is how the elder shall serve the younger. - Then comes the blessing Esau has today: behold, thy dwelling shall be the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above. They would conquer nations and have the best lands, and whatever lands were not in their possession, they would find a way to get them. And by thy sword shalt thou live: Esau, Edom, Idumea lives fighting. And shalt serve thy brother: at the end of everything, the blessing is limited, and it returns to Jacob forever. - And it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, when you become the world superpower, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck: after you take him out of slavery. - And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing. He said in his heart, the days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Jacob. This is the beginning of the perpetual hatred. Hebrews 12:15-17 37:42 - How can a man fail of the grace of God? When God says something and you refuse to do it. Esau despised his birthright; that is when you fall from the grace of God. - Lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you: Esau became bitter after that, and thereby many were defiled. - Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright. When he would have inherited the blessing, he was rejected: for he found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears. He wept before his father, but the deed was already done and the Lord's will was done. Genesis 36:1 44:36 - Now these are the generations of Esau, who is Edom. That is all this verse is for: Esau is Edom. - Reading shown on Edom: an ancient kingdom that stretched across the area in the south of present-day Israel, Jordan, and Palestine. Once pushed out of their territories, the Edomites settled during the Persian period in the southern hills of Judea down to the area north of Beersheba, and the people appeared under a Greek form of their old name as Idumaeans, their new territory called Idumaea, a term used in the Hellenistic and Roman periods and mentioned in the New Testament. - Image shown: the Treasury carved into the rock at Mount Seir, an Edomite stronghold. 2 Esdras 3:12-16 46:33 - When they that dwelt upon the earth began to multiply, they began again to be more ungodly than the first; they multiplied so heavy that the Most High flooded the earth. - Thou didst choose thee a man from among them, whose name was Abraham; him thou lovedst, and unto him only thou showedst thy will, and madest an everlasting covenant with him, promising that thou wouldest never forsake his seed. He was a friend of God. - And unto him thou gavest Isaac, and unto Isaac also thou gavest Jacob and Esau. As for Jacob, thou didst choose him to thee, and put by Esau: and so Jacob became a great multitude. That is us. God chose Jacob; the younger one is the stronger one, and the elder shall serve him. It was all prophesied. Romans 9:9-13 48:47 - The children being not yet born, neither having done any good or evil: these babies did nothing wrong; they were in their mother's womb doing nothing but fighting. People ask, how can God just choose like that? Because he is God. He will have mercy on whom he will have mercy. - That the purpose of God according to election might stand, not of works, but of him that calleth. - It was said unto her: not unto him. God told Rebekah how he wanted this thing to go down. The elder shall serve the younger. - As it is written, Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated. It is not of anything good or evil that was done; it is through election. Malachi 1:2-4 51:19 - I have loved you, saith the Lord. Yet ye say, wherein hast thou loved us? That is us right now: police brutality, ICE, what is going on in Sudan, the Jones Act in Puerto Rico and the massacres in Ponce and Utuado, the atrocities in the Congo under Belgium, Shark Island in Namibia, and now the trafficking scandals of our day. How does God love us with all this garbage happening around us? - All these things have to happen, and while they are happening we are supposed to be going to the Lord, repenting, looking in our book, and doing what God says, because the reason we are in these conditions is that we broke God's commandments. - Was not Esau Jacob's brother? saith the Lord: yet I loved Jacob, and I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste. He is the eldest; he should have had the blessings, but God did not set it up that way. He set it up so we get the blessings forever. That is how he loves us. - Whereas Edom saith, we are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places: they were driven into the mountains, they rebuilt, and now they are the superpower in the world. But how they became the superpower is a record of abuse. - They shall build, but I will throw down; and they shall call them the border of wickedness, and the people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever. Obadiah 1:1-2 57:20 - The vision of Obadiah: thus saith the Lord God concerning Edom. Behold, I have made thee small among the heathen: thou art greatly despised. That is the title of this class. - How is Esau greatly despised? They seem nice: good morning, good afternoon, sometimes they give you food, some advice, a motivational speech. But the record answers the question. - Document read in class, the papal bull Dum Diversas, issued June 18, 1452 by Pope Nicholas V, the first document of the doctrine of discovery: it granted King Alfonso V of Portugal permission to invade, search out, capture, vanquish, and subdue all Saracens and pagans whatsoever, and other enemies of Christ wheresoever placed, and to take their kingdoms, dominions, possessions, and goods, and to reduce their persons to perpetual slavery. Perpetual slavery is perpetual hatred. - Definition read: the word Saracen was commonly used in medieval Europe for the peoples of Arabia, and by the medieval period it stretched to cover anybody who was not European. - The bull Romanus Pontifex came right after Dum Diversas and amplified it: the same language, to reduce their persons to perpetual slavery. Deuteronomy 28:68 1:05:56 - The Lord shall bring thee into Egypt again with ships: cargo slave ships. We went into slavery again with ships because we broke God's commandments, and God put Esau over us; it is part of Esau's blessing and our curse. - There ye shall be sold unto your enemies: not only to the white man but to other nations, through the transatlantic slave trade, the trans-Saharan slave trade, and along the Silk Road, all the way to China, Japan, and the Philippine islands; parts of Issachar are in the Philippines, and the tribe of Ephraim is in Hawaii. - And no man shall buy you: no revolutionary will save us, no matter how eloquently they speak or how hard they fight. - Trip report from Puerto Rico: the brothers visited Heriberto Marin Torres, the last survivor of the Puerto Rican Nationalist Party, 97 years old and strong, labeled a terrorist and a communist when all he loved was his people. He knew Pedro Albizu Campos personally, and his memoir covers the Ponce and Utuado massacres. They are going to say the same things about us. - At the library that week the brothers went through the original identification documents of the slaves held on the island. Books found in Puerto Rico were shown: Puerto Rico Negro, Fotografias para la Historia de Puerto Rico, a study of the decline of the slave trade in Puerto Rico from 1820 to 1860, and Sugar, Slavery, and Freedom in Nineteenth Century Puerto Rico. Yes, Puerto Ricans are black. - Film referenced: El Resplandor, a short Puerto Rican film on slavery on the island; slow paced, but it gets the message sent. - Posters shown from the Wayland Rudd Collection, Soviet era artwork about our people: he carried Africa in his heart, Lumumba; the end of colonialism; no to colonialism; colonialism is doomed; we mourn for Lumumba, Africa must live; colonizers must answer, that is where caught red-handed comes from; freedom to all the peoples of Africa, meaning freedom to all the peoples of the Israelites; a soldier receiving a medal from the ghost of the Third Reich for services in Vietnam; and I used to hold the whip in my hands, on how they colonize minds and make us taskmasters over our own, no different than in the days of Moses. During the Cold War they made us believe that side was pure evil, but those posters were depicting what was happening over here. Colonialism is only doomed when we wake up and realize our minds have been colonized; our souls should belong to the Most High. Obadiah 1:3 1:23:55 - The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee, thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, whose habitation is high; that saith in his heart, who shall bring me down to the ground? The clefts of the rock are the governments, the high places, the skyscrapers, all the richness and fatness of the earth Esau lives in. - Reading on the Force Publique, the military of the Congo Free State and the Belgian Congo from 1885 to 1960, founded on Leopold's orders and heavily involved in atrocities. A photograph from 1904 was shown and summarized in one line in class: a Congolese father looking at what the Force Publique had done to his little daughter, the record read as proof of who shall bring me down to the ground pride. - Reading on the Utuado Uprising, El Grito de Utuado, October 30, 1950: revolts against the United States government in Utuado, San Juan, Mayaguez, and Arecibo, with major confrontations in Ponce, Penuelas, and Adjuntas. The Puerto Rican Nationalist Party was formed September 17, 1922, under Jose Coll y Cuchi; Pedro Albizu Campos, the first Puerto Rican graduate of Harvard Law School and a World War I veteran, joined in 1924 and was elected president in 1930. The appointed governor Blanton Winship and Colonel Riggs applied harsh repressive measures; in 1936 Albizu Campos and the leaders were jailed in La Princesa and sent to the federal prison in Atlanta. America had already cut the value of the Puerto Rican peso in half, wiping out the people's savings. - Reading on the Jones Act, section 27 of the Merchant Marine Act of 1920: all goods moved by water between US ports must be carried on ships built, flagged, owned, and crewed American. The seamen's rights it defined never reached the Merchant Marine veterans; they were denied benefits. News read in class: the president extended a Jones Act waiver another 90 days to ease fuel prices as the war with Iran cut off a fifth of the world's oil supply. It was not kindness; Puerto Rico is a cash cow, and the waiver protects the US and global economies, not the island. - Video shown from Havana: the oil blockade on top of decades of economic mismanagement crippling life in Cuba. Why would you cut oil going to a country 90 miles away from yours? But the Cuban people are innovative; it is a country full of engineers. - Video and book shown on the 1950s: racism woven into housing, education, employment, and travel, and the Green Book, compiled by Victor Green, a black postman from Harlem, an annual guide of safe hotels, restaurants, and gas stations. The teacher bought a copy: a treasure map of places where black people could be safe. - J. Edgar Hoover was asked what the number one threat to America is, and he said the organization of Negroes. What happens when the diaspora organizes not in theory but in execution? A new economic force emerges: Tulsa, Oklahoma; Rosewood. That is what they did not want. Deuteronomy 28:48 1:46:26 - Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies, which the Lord shall send against thee: that is not a suggestion, that is the curse. In hunger, in thirst, in nakedness, and in want of all things; and he shall put a yoke of iron upon thy neck, until he have destroyed thee. We are so destroyed as a people that we cannot even organize. - To hell with organized crime; we are organizing the truth. We are an organized nation, looking for like-minded brothers and sisters willing to wake up, keep God's commandments, and see this thing to the end. - Reading on the Greensboro Four: the sit-in at the Woolworth lunch counter, meticulously planned; by February 5th about 300 students had joined, and the protest spread to 55 cities in 13 states. The Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee was founded in Raleigh in April 1960, vital in the Freedom Rides of 1961 and the 1963 March on Washington. - When you try to do things peacefully, then things get more radical: the Black Panther Party bore arms because the law said they could, and they did not like that black people had guns. Then the Young Lords: what Hoover feared, Negroes and Latinos and Native Americans together in the Rainbow Coalition. - Huey Newton quote read: the oppressor must be harassed until his doom; the enslaved have always outnumbered the enslavers; the power of the oppressor rests upon the submission of the people. - The one element missing from the Black Panthers, the Young Lords, and the American Indian Movement was the Bible. That is it. Had they had the Bible, we would probably be in the kingdom by now. Obadiah 1:4-6 1:53:21 - Though thou exalt thyself as the eagle, and though thou set thy nest among the stars, thence will I bring thee down, saith the Lord. That goes into space travel: the satellites literally look like nests. You can exalt yourself like the eagle, but you are not God. - Image shown: the Susan B. Anthony dollar of 1981, the eagle landed with branches, nesting on the moon with the earth in the background. They set their nest among the stars. - If thieves came to thee, would they not have stolen till they had enough? People who steal, steal until they have enough. Esau is greatly despised because they continue to steal and steal and steal. If the grapegatherers came, would they not leave some grapes? The law says leave grapes at the edges of the field for the poor. - How are the things of Esau searched out! How are his hidden things sought up! We are going to find out; the class goes back through the decades. 1 Maccabees 3:48 1:56:45 - And laid open the book of the law, wherein the heathen had sought to paint the likeness of their images. The heathen did exactly that. - Book read in class, In the Pillory: The Tale of the Borgia Pope: the bust of the Savior posed for by Cesare Borgia, the son of Pope Alexander VI. It was removed from the church of San Salvatore in Termis, now destroyed, to the monumental morgue of the Saint Louis church, where it is shown by the guide as the bust of the relative of a famous pope. It is an open secret that Cesare Borgia had posed for it. - The new lie in the earth right now is that there is no proof Cesare Borgia posed as the image of Christ. They are trying hard to discredit what we teach and to disconnect themselves from the atrocities. But the hidden things of Esau are sought up. Daniel 7:25 2:05:28 - Movie clips played from an exorcism film set around the Spanish Inquisition, paused every few moments for the history behind it. The friar in the film is Alonso de Ojeda, the real Dominican prior of the San Pablo convent who convinced Queen Isabella of Castile, during her stay in Seville between 1477 and 1478, of Judaizing practices among the Andalusian converts; a report by Cardinal Mendoza and the friar Tomas de Torquemada confirmed the suspicions, and in January 1481 the Inquisition tribunal was established in the San Pablo convent. The Inquisition prosecuted whatever indicated someone was Judaizing or Moorish, meaning anything that had to do with the Israelites. Earlier still, Pope Gregory IX created a pontifical Inquisition through the bull Excommunicamus in the 1230s. - The film's own line: centuries of persecution and torture, the abuses of the Inquisition, all started by the friar and done in the name of God, by the devil. They put the truth in a horror movie so you would disavow it, but we pause and look it up: Dum Diversas, Romanus Pontifex, the slavery they did. Hollywood knows the truth. - The early church was of the Israelites; when Rome, Edom, came into power, they took it over, ran the Renaissance, and changed the Sabbath to Sunday. He shall speak great words against the Most High: the Sabbath is now Sunday; Christ is now painted in their image by Leonardo, Michelangelo, and Donatello, the artists. - And shall wear out the saints of the Most High: in slavery we were worn out, so tired we stopped questioning anything the slave master threw at us. That is why so many of us do not want to read. - And think to change times and laws: they changed the calendar, some calendars now start the week on Monday, and they moved the new moon to the dark moon to keep the lie going and hide the high holy days. - And they shall be given into his hand until a time and times and the dividing of time: that is what Esau has been given, and his time is coming to an end. At the end of that is the heel and the hand, the beginning of the kingdom. Psalms 64:8 2:11:21 - So they shall make their own tongue to fall upon themselves: all that see them shall flee away. They wrote everything down with the expectation that we would never learn to read. Now we know how to read. Isaiah 23:1-8 2:11:55 - The burden of Tyre: this is a prophecy of Esau. She is a mart of nations: that is America, a marketplace of nations. Is this your joyous city, whose antiquity is of ancient days? America is an extension of Rome. - The crowning city, whose merchants are princes: the corporations here are like royalty. Whose traffickers are the honourable of the earth: that sounds like the trafficking scandals of our day, businessmen and celebrities, the honorable of the earth as the traffickers. And before that, we had the transatlantic slave trade; and slave trading still goes on in parts of Arabia, in Sudan, in the Congo. - Video played from a mission field report: sitting on the ruins of a synagogue built in 1685, the first completed synagogue built in the Americas, beside a coffee plantation where our northern and southern kingdom brothers were enslaved, and a cemetery where our people were buried after being worked to death. The traffickers were counted the honorable of the earth. Ezekiel 28:1-5 2:15:08 - Say unto the prince of Tyrus: because thine heart is lifted up, and thou hast said, I am a God, I sit in the seat of God, in the midst of the seas. You sit in the seat of God because you are in space, in rulership, the superpower in the midst of the nations, like the woman in Revelation that sits upon many waters. Yet thou art a man, and not God: a man made of dust, water, and blood, no matter the crown and the seal. Even the president talking reckless is only fulfilling the prophecy of making himself small among the heathen. - Behold, thou art wiser than Daniel; there is no secret that they can hide from thee: with wisdom and understanding they got riches, gold and silver into their treasures. Look at the Native American treaties the United States made and broke, like the Treaty of Fort Laramie of 1868, violated the minute gold was discovered. They know geology; they know where the gold is, and that is why the forts sit where they sit.
