They are confederate against thee: the tabernacles of Edom, the so-called white man, the number one oppressor and colonizer; the Ishmaelites, the Arabs; Moab; the Hagarenes; Gebal, Ammon, and Amalek; the Philistines with the inhabitants of Tyre. Psalms 81:8-9 29:08 - Hear, O my people, and I will testify unto thee: O Israel, if thou wilt hearken unto me. There shall no strange god be in thee; neither shalt thou worship any strange god. - Black man, Hispanic man, have you been given a strange god? Yes, you have. The Lord said no strange god: no Cesare Borgia white Jesus, no Allah, no Buddha. Through the Berlin Conference and the white Christian missionaries, the strange god went all over the world. And it is here in America too; your mama has white Jesus hanging on her wall right now. Daniel 11:39 29:42 - Thus shall he do in the most strong holds with a strange god: the he is the so-called white man, and the most strong holds is the land of Africa, the land of Ham, where all the resources are. The Western powers cannot survive without that continent. - With a strange god, whom he shall acknowledge and increase with glory: the so-called white Jesus. Testimony from the trip to Kenya: white Jesus is everywhere; it is on their buses, their billboards, the storefronts, in their schools, their churches, and in their minds, without one scripture saying Jesus is a white man. The so-called white man does not have to be physically there; his doctrine is there, and the love for him is there. - And he shall cause them to rule over many: they rule that land so thoroughly that they extract the resources and the people are not even upset about it. Testimony read in class: brothers in Kenya found a gold nugget in a stream, and it was worthless to them, because in Kenya you need a license to do anything with it; if they try to sell it they can go to jail. But a merchant can come from overseas, refine that same nugget, and it is worth thousands. - And shall divide the land for gain: before the 1884 Berlin Conference, Africa did not have these borders. That is where they divided up the continent: the French with the majority, Belgium with the Congo, the British with Kenya, the Germans in Tanzania, the Portuguese in Angola, the Italians in Eritrea and Somalia. All the Caucasian nations got wealthy and continue to get wealthy, because today it is called neo-colonialism. It is not over just because they physically left; the resources are still getting extracted. Psalms 81:11-14 41:30 - But my people would not hearken to my voice; and Israel would none of me. So I gave them up unto their own hearts' lust: and they walked in their own counsels. The Lord said, go ahead, do what you do. - Oh that my people had hearkened unto me: I should soon have subdued their enemies, and turned my hand against their adversaries. If we had done what the Lord told us to do, he would have put our enemies under our foot. Leviticus 26:17-19 42:40 - Because we did not hearken, the Lord said, I will set my face against you, and ye shall be slain before your enemies: they that hate you shall reign over you; and ye shall flee when none pursueth you. Instead of subduing your enemies, your enemies subdue you. - What is the major sign you have been subdued before your enemies? When you worship their god, black man, it is a sign you have been subdued. You are in subjection; you have total reverence for your enemies. - And I will break the pride of your power: I am going to break your spirit, and I will use the other nations to do it. Now you are bashful; now you have low self-esteem; now you have no confidence. Precepts: - Leviticus 26:36-37 I will send a faintness into their hearts in the lands of their enemies: mentally and spiritually you are going to be broken down. The sound of a shaken leaf shall chase them: no courage. And ye shall have no power to stand before your enemies. Think about that spiritually in 2026: when black people get mad at other black people, we show no mercy; we came up with terms for it, turning up, crashing out. But do we have that same level of aggression toward the nations that oppress us? Not at all. We will stand aggressive with each other all day long, but we will not stand before the other nations. And to be clear, we do not advocate violence on anybody; the point is the spirit is not the same. Proverbs 23:7 55:31 - For as he thinketh in his heart, so is he. You are what you think of yourself, brothers and sisters. If you think you are nothing, you become what you think you are. I am just here, I have no purpose, I am just going to blend in and cruise by and hope nobody sees me: you are in the wrong spirit. - The characteristics you take on are based on what you have practiced. If you are a brother with low self-esteem, you have been grooming that for years and years, and it has become your character. Now you have to fight that spirit. Isaiah 13:12 57:13 - I will make a man more precious than fine gold; even a man than the golden wedge of Ophir. Which one of you brothers is fine gold? Even if we put it to the test and you fail, you still have to believe it; you work on it until you are that fine gold. 1 Samuel 9:1-2 58:55 - Now we go into a case study of King Saul: was he a good king or a bad king, what did he do right, what did he do wrong? - Kish was a mighty man of power, and he had a son whose name was Saul, a choice young man, and a goodly: and there was not among the children of Israel a goodlier person than he. From his shoulders and upward he was higher than any of the people. Saul was the top of the food chain, the cream of the crop, thus saith the Lord. 1 Samuel 9:15-17 1:00:39 - The Lord told Samuel in his ear a day before Saul came: tomorrow about this time I will send thee a man out of the land of Benjamin, and thou shalt anoint him to be captain over my people Israel, that he may save my people out of the hand of the Philistines. - When Samuel saw Saul, the Lord said unto him, Behold the man whom I spake to thee of; this same shall reign over my people. Saul was the man the Lord himself chose. 1 Samuel 9:21 1:01:50 - And Saul answered, Am not I a Benjamite, of the smallest of the tribes of Israel, and my family the least of all the families of the tribe of Benjamin? Wherefore then speakest thou so to me? What did Saul think of himself? - Notice something, brothers: the leadership will see the best in you, and you will not even see it for yourself, because you have that low self-esteem. We will see greatness in you, and you say, I am just a soldier, I am just an officer of ten, I cannot do anything, I am just going to blend in and not maximize my potential. Some of you are in this Saul spirit right here: bashfulness, lack of confidence, low self-esteem, scared to make a mistake, scared of correction and rebuke. But how did the Lord see King Saul? Go back to verse 2: there was not a goodlier person than he. 1 Samuel 15:17-24 1:04:40 - In this chapter the Lord commanded Saul to utterly destroy the Amalekites and everything they have, and he did not do it. Samuel said, When thou wast little in thine own sight, wast thou not made the head of the tribes of Israel? When you thought you were a nobody, the Lord anointed you king over all Israel. - Wherefore then didst thou not obey the voice of the Lord? Saul answered, Yea, I have obeyed the voice of the Lord, and have brought Agag the king of Amalek. Wait a minute: the king is still alive. Saul is playing the defensive, justifying his actions, making excuses. - But the people took of the spoil: it was not me, it was the people, it was their fault. This goes into bashfulness: you do not take accountability. - Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams. To do what you were told is better than coming back afterward saying, my bad, I thought I understood, I decided to do it this way. You fulfill the commandment you were given, and if there is a problem, you say something. - For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness is as iniquity and idolatry. Because thou hast rejected the word of the Lord, he hath also rejected thee from being king. When you are in that spirit, the Lord cannot use you. Leadership may put you in a position, and when we question you on certain things, you make excuses, or you separate yourself into a bubble with the men under you. You are bashful, and you are bringing up a bunch of bashful brothers under you; you are keeping the brothers under you hostage. - And Saul said, I have sinned: because I feared the people, and obeyed their voice. If you are a leader and you are in fear of your people, what can those people do to you? Manipulate you. You are a pushover; they can sway you left and right. Who is supposed to move you? The Lord, not the people you are supposed to lead. You are not leading the people; you are being led by the people. Precepts: - 1 Samuel 15:3 The commandment was total: utterly destroy all that they have, and spare them not. All means everything. - 1 Samuel 15:28 And Samuel said unto him, The Lord hath rent the kingdom of Israel from thee this day, and hath given it to a neighbour of thine, that is better than thou. 1 Samuel 10:1-8 1:14:08 - Going back: after chapter 9, Samuel took a vial of oil and poured it upon Saul's head and kissed him: is it not because the Lord hath anointed thee to be captain over his inheritance? - Samuel gave Saul the signs: the two men by Rachel's sepulchre, the three men going up to God to Bethel who would give him two loaves of bread, and the company of prophets with a psaltery, a tabret, a pipe, and a harp. The Spirit of the Lord will come upon thee, and thou shalt prophesy with them, and shalt be turned into another man. God is with thee. Brothers, God is with you; you have to believe that. - And the instruction: thou shalt go down before me to Gilgal; seven days shalt thou tarry, till I come to thee, and shew thee what thou shalt do. That is the commandment. Let us see what King Saul does in his bashfulness. 1 Samuel 13:8-13 1:18:05 - Saul tarried seven days, but Samuel came not yet to Gilgal, and the people were scattered from him. And Saul said, Bring hither a burnt offering to me, and he offered the burnt offering. Samuel was supposed to make the offering, not Saul. Not only was he bashful; that bashful spirit made him self-willed. You do your own thing, and when somebody checks you on it, you make excuses. - As soon as he had made an end of offering, behold, Samuel came. And Saul went out to meet him, that he might salute him. When you are dead wrong and you try to cover it up, you meet him over there before he gets to where you messed up; you deflect and maneuver around. That is what brothers do. - Saul said, Because I saw that the people were scattered from me, and thou camest not within the days appointed, and the Philistines gathered themselves together, I forced myself therefore, and offered a burnt offering. I did it on my own; I am self-willed; I was scared; you were not around. - And Samuel said to Saul, Thou hast done foolishly: thou hast not kept the commandment of the Lord thy God: for now would the Lord have established thy kingdom upon Israel for ever. 1 Samuel 28:3-5 1:23:02 - Samuel was dead, and Saul had put away those that had familiar spirits and the wizards out of the land. The Philistines gathered themselves together, and when Saul saw the host of the Philistines, he was afraid, and his heart greatly trembled. - This is the king. If the king is scared, what is that going to do to the men under him? If the officer is fearful, it spreads to the soldiers under him. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 10:2 As the judge of the people is himself, so are his officers. Take the young men in regular clothes six months in the truth: they are going to follow the example of the officers that have been here eight, nine, ten years. If you are bashful, afraid, timid, and shy, your spirit is telling those brothers it is okay to be like this. It shall not be so in here. - Wisdom of Solomon 17:12 For fear is nothing else but a betraying of the succours which reason offereth. A soldier broke it down: you trick yourself into being scared because you make up things in your mind which are not really there. And you also have a lack of faith: your faith is supposed to be in the Lord, but a lot of the time your faith is only in what you can see with your eyes. - 2 Corinthians 5:7 For we walk by faith, not by sight. We fear what we physically see, but we do not fear breaking God's commandments. That we should fear. - 2 Timothy 1:7-8 For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind. The Lord never gave us that spirit. Be not thou therefore ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, but be thou partaker of the afflictions of the gospel according to the power of God. - Matthew 10:28 And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell. This is the level we have to get to: fear the Most High, not man. 1 Samuel 28:6-9 1:30:51 - And when Saul enquired of the Lord, the Lord answered him not, neither by dreams, nor by Urim, nor by prophets. The Lord was not dealing with Saul anymore. - Then said Saul unto his servants, Seek me a woman that hath a familiar spirit. Saul just rid the land of all the soothsayers, the familiar spirits, and the wizards; now he says find me one so I can know what is going on. His mind is all over the place; he is double-minded. - And Saul disguised himself, and put on other raiment, and came to the woman by night. And the woman said, Behold, thou knowest what Saul hath done: wherefore then layest thou a snare for my life, to cause me to die? Precepts: - Deuteronomy 18:10-11 There shall not be found among you any one that useth divination, or an observer of times, or an enchanter, or a witch, or a charmer, or a consulter with familiar spirits. This is the commandment Saul turned around and broke. 1 Samuel 28:16-19 1:35:47 - Then said Samuel, Wherefore then dost thou ask of me, seeing the Lord is departed from thee, and is become thine enemy? Imagine that: the Lord is your enemy now, Saul. Because you were bashful, you were self-willed, you broke the commandments of the Lord, you were deceitful, you lied, you made excuses, you were easily manipulated. It all went back to Saul being bashful. - The Lord hath rent the kingdom out of thine hand, and given it to thy neighbour, even to David: because thou obeyedst not the voice of the Lord, nor executedst his fierce wrath upon Amalek. - Moreover the Lord will also deliver Israel with thee into the hand of the Philistines: and to morrow shalt thou and thy sons be with me. Your day is over, Saul: no more kingdom, no more life. Cut off. Ecclesiasticus 20:22 1:39:11 - There is that destroyeth his own soul through bashfulness, and by accepting of persons overthroweth himself. That is the perfect scripture for King Saul. - A brother broke it down: by being bashful, by not being a leader, by not obeying God's commandments, we are destroying ourselves. God is not destroying us; he gave us the plan, and we will not follow it because we are scared. Saul never believed in himself from the start. God said he was the greatest among Israel, but when he looked in the mirror he did not see the lion, he saw the kitty cat. He did not believe God. And he had help the whole time: the prophet Samuel was there to guide him, and he never listened. Had he listened to Samuel while he was there, he could have stood on his own when Samuel was gone. - Another attribute in that bashfulness is lack of counsel, because you do not want to seem stupid, uninformed, or wrong. It is one thing to make a mistake from lack of understanding; you can learn from that. It is another thing to completely forego the counsel. All Saul had to do was ask, or be patient enough to wait. That timidness causes us not to reach out or ask for help, and that compounds the bashfulness that destroys us. Why do brothers and sisters not reach out? I did not want to bother you, Cap; I know you are busy, so I just decided to do it on my own. We get that at least three times a week. - Video played on four keys to strengthening your self-esteem: one, do not speak to yourself like an enemy; your inner voice must be your refuge, never your punishment. Two, stop comparing yourself; measure only against who you were yesterday. Three, set boundaries, not because you lack love, but because you have dignity. Four, keep promises to yourself; every commitment you honor in private becomes unshakable confidence in public. When you respect yourself, the world will mirror that respect back; if you do not respect yourself, the world will pick that up and treat you as such. - Video played on shyness: everything a great communicator does is just a series of behaviors. When people say, I am shy, it is because you have been practicing the shy behaviors for 15, 20, 30 years. Confidence is another series of behaviors you can practice. It becomes part of your identity and you feel stuck, but you are not. - Video played on being uncomfortable: everything you want in life is on the other side of being uncomfortable. Break yourself of your weaknesses. It takes a man to look in the mirror and say, I have problems, and then you do not put your head down; you put your head up and start fixing them one by one. You have been comforted in your vices and your timidness for years; you have to go to war with that spirit. 2 Esdras 14:14 1:50:51 - Let go from thee mortal thoughts, cast away the burdens of man, put off now the weak nature. Those mortal thoughts are the old habits you created: old thoughts that turned into actions, that turned into habits, that turned into characteristics. - The weak nature is your comfortability. I am used to doing it like this; that is just me. That is the lie you tell yourself. That weak nature is stopping you from being the Proverbs 31 woman that listens to her husband, or the husband that guides his house manfully. Some take the easy way out: no, you are scared to lead your own house. Being nice, brothers will tolerate you, but they will not respect you. You have to break the cycle of comfortability and make yourself uncomfortable doing what you are not used to, because you are trying to get somewhere you have never been. If you are not trying to get there, you will end up destroying yourself through bashfulness. - As we grow in the body, we grow in the truth. Sometimes the Lord brings you to a certain place, and now is the time you get taught: I let you get this far, but you cannot go further until you are okay with getting uncomfortable to break those weaknesses. Isaiah 51:20-23 1:53:38 - Thy sons have fainted: the gods on the earth have laid down. They lie at the head of all the streets, as a wild bull in a net: they are full of the fury of the Lord, the curses of Deuteronomy 28. - Thou afflicted, and drunken, but not with wine: what have we been afflicted and drunken with? White Jesus, Christianity, the philosophies of the world, society. - Behold, I have taken out of thine hand the cup of trembling: there is going to come a time when the Lord takes the cup of his fury out of our hand, and we shall no more drink it again. But I will put it into the hand of them that afflict thee: the nations that afflicted us. - Which have said to thy soul, Bow down, that we may go over: that is the position the other nations have put us in and still have us in. Your soul is subdued, not just your physical. And thou hast laid thy body as the ground: we lay down and they walk all over us. - Videos played from the trip: in South Africa, crowds giving Afrikaner descendants of the colonizers a hero's welcome while African migrants from Nigeria, Ghana, and Zimbabwe face xenophobic attacks in places like Durban and Pretoria; the descendants of the settlers, about 7 percent of the population, still hold about 90 percent of the land, and the people have no problem with it. This is what happens when you are subdued. - Video played of an African man saying the colonizers left too early, that they should have stayed longer to raise us to a certain level, that we are not prepared to rule ourselves. Look at the brother's face: defeated, subdued, low self-esteem, no faith in his own people. These are the minds we have to change, and the Lord is going to use you brothers to change them. - Testimony from the trip: the mall in Kenya was immaculate, like a mall in Atlanta, built under foreign direction with Kenyan labor; but where the people build for themselves, with no confidence and no standard, the steps are uneven and the houses are lopsided. That comes from low self-esteem. A whole country they can do anything with, and they wait for foreign aid, IMF loans, handouts, a dependence on the colonizer to save them. - Video played of the president of France, the top colonizing power in Africa, being celebrated on the east coast of Africa after the west African nations of Burkina Faso, Mali, and Niger expelled French influence; at a conference in Kenya he interrupted the room and told the audience to be quiet while he was talking, and they clapped for him. His country is responsible for coups, destabilization, and death across Africa; a commentator read in class noted Kenya has already paid millions to French companies for roads that were never constructed. That is the real relationship. - Video summarized in one line: a native doctor in Ghana died testing his own claimed bulletproof charm at a funeral ritual; the teaching point is that superstition in place of the word of God is part of the same broken mind. - The nations use our people because we invite them to use us. We are bashful; we do not think we can do it ourselves, so we reach out to the colonizers to be our daddies. The leader is supposed to have the people's best interest at heart. - Video played: a bishop teaching in Kenya said as soon as the church heard Jesus was black, they were infuriated and threw rocks, just from reading the scripture, because a people taught to hate themselves hate anything black. Matthew 17:20-21 2:12:43 - How do we get out of this bashful spirit? Jesus said unto them, Because of your unbelief: for verily I say unto you, If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye shall say unto this mountain, Remove hence to yonder place; and it shall remove; and nothing shall be impossible unto you. If you have faith, you will have confidence; you will speak strong; you will not be bashful. - Howbeit this kind goeth not out but by prayer and fasting. If you have the bashful spirit, pray and fast about it. If you see your leader is lacking confidence, pray and fast for him. Has anybody tried that? The leadership did not grow up in this truth; we were all dealing with the same things, and we have to make ourselves uncomfortable and fight that spirit to be men of God. Romans 10:17-21 2:14:56 - So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God. You have to constantly hear the word and constantly be around men that know the Bible; that grows your faith. - Have they not heard? Yes verily, their sound went into all the earth. We just did this in the worldwide blitz: the purple and gold went all over the planet spreading the word of God. That shows we are in the right place, and we are on the right side of history. - First Moses saith, I will provoke you to jealousy by them that are no people, and by a foolish nation I will anger you: the northern kingdom. Esaias is very bold, and saith, I was found of them that sought me not. How many of you were seeking the Lord in the world? You were in church on a Sunday banging a tambourine; you were doing Mother's Day last week. - But to Israel he saith, All day long I have stretched forth my hands unto a disobedient and gainsaying people. That disobedient people now has to receive the word of God and change their lives. Wisdom of Solomon 5:1 2:18:21 - Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him. You are supposed to be bold with the word of God. When you are bold with the word, the people can see this brother believes what he is saying, and they can follow him. - But if you are bashful, unsure, lacking confidence, speaking with your head in your chest, who is going to follow you? Sisters, who wants to follow a man like that? Nobody wants to follow a timid, shy man. They are going to manipulate you and run over you. If you are bashful and a leader, you are not the leader; you are the one being led. You just have a title. 2 Corinthians 12:1-4 2:20:37 - Paul is speaking of himself: I knew a man in Christ above fourteen years ago, caught up to the third heaven, caught up into paradise, and heard unspeakable words, which it is not lawful for a man to utter. Who is in the third heaven? The Father. Hold that thought for what happens to Paul at Lystra. Acts 14:1-7 2:21:43 - In Iconium, Paul and Barnabas so spake that a great multitude both of the Jews and also of the Greeks believed. Paul was not stationary; he was not local; he was traveling, moving around and around. - Long time therefore abode they speaking boldly in the Lord. They were not bashful. When an assault was made to stone them, they were ware of it, and fled unto Lystra and Derbe, cities of Lycaonia. And there they preached the gospel. How did they preach it? Boldly. Acts 14:11-21 2:23:28 - The people of Lystra saw what Paul had done and called Barnabas, Jupiter; and Paul, Mercurius, because he was the chief speaker, and the priest of Jupiter brought oxen and garlands to do sacrifice unto them. The apostles rent their clothes and ran in among the people, crying out, We also are men of like passions with you, and preach unto you that ye should turn from these vanities unto the living God. Stop this nonsense; turn to the living God and keep the commandments. - Then certain Jews from Antioch and Iconium persuaded the people, and having stoned Paul, drew him out of the city, supposing he had been dead. They knocked Paul upside the head with stones, and he went to the third heavens: that is the vision he spoke of in 2 Corinthians 12. - Howbeit, as the disciples stood round about him, he rose up, and came into the city: and the next day he departed with Barnabas to Derbe. And when they had preached the gospel to that city, and had taught many, they returned again to Lystra, and to Iconium, and Antioch. They went right back. Just like the team in Kenya: when they stoned us, we went right back. We took those stones, brothers got hit in the jaw, and we came right back. We are not going anywhere. Acts 15:25-26 2:26:22 - It seemed good unto us, being assembled with one accord, to send chosen men unto you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul: men that have hazarded their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. - Brothers, you are not here to be a professional student. You are not here to sit forever on a Saturday with a notebook hearing breakdowns. Your job is to learn this gospel, build your spirit up, go forth and teach. Acts 5:34-42 2:27:30 - Gamaliel, a doctor of the law, had in reputation among all the people, told the council: before these days rose up Theudas, boasting himself to be somebody, and all that obeyed him were scattered and brought to nought. After him rose up Judas of Galilee, and he also perished. We have that today: brothers come to the body, learn the scriptures a little bit, then go forth and heap men unto themselves, and when they leave, the men come to nought. - Refrain from these men, and let them alone: for if this counsel or this work be of men, it will come to nought: but if it be of God, ye cannot overthrow it; lest haply ye be found even to fight against God. If this movement is of God, you cannot do a thing about it. You are not fighting us; you are fighting God. - And when they had called the apostles, and beaten them, they departed from the presence of the council, rejoicing that they were counted worthy to suffer shame for his name. That is the level we have to get to: taking a beating for the Lord and rejoicing. How many of you could rejoice in that? Not many of us are there yet. - And daily in the temple, and in every house, they ceased not to teach and preach Jesus Christ. They did not go get their lick back; they kept teaching. 2 Esdras 10:33 2:32:03 - And he said unto me, Stand up manfully, and I will advise thee. How are we supposed to stand up, brothers? Manfully. And the Lord will advise us when we stand up manfully. Hebrews 11:6 2:32:37 - But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him. If you have faith, you cannot be bashful; brothers will know where you stand. - One more thing on the quiet, shy, timid brother: you do not know what he is thinking. When you are at war next to a brother like that, holding sentry, how do you know he is not going to run on you when trouble comes? You do not. So it is a deceitful spirit; they hide in the cut. If you have faith, you will not be shy or timid, and the brothers around you will know exactly where you stand. Ephesians 6:16 2:36:05 - Above all, taking the shield of faith, wherewith ye shall be able to quench all the fiery darts of the wicked. If you have no faith, you are quenching no darts; you will be taken away with the wicked. James 5:12-16 2:36:41 - Let your yea be yea; and your nay, nay; lest ye fall into condemnation. Is any among you afflicted? Let him pray. Is any merry? Let him sing psalms. - Is any sick among you? Let him call for the elders of the church; and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord: and the prayer of faith shall save the sick, and the Lord shall raise him up. - Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed. The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much. 1 Samuel 10:6-7 2:37:49 - The last scripture: this is when you go from a bashful sinner to a righteous man. And the Spirit of the Lord will come upon thee, and thou shalt prophesy with them, and shalt be turned into another man. You are not going to be that bashful little boy in a man's body anymore. - And let it be, when these signs are come unto thee, that thou do as occasion serve thee; for God is with thee. Brothers and sisters, you have to believe that. Stop being bashful. In Closing Bashfulness goes into lack of confidence, low self-esteem, self-consciousness, timidity, and shyness. Because Saul was all those things, he was self-willed, he made excuses, he feared the people and was manipulated by them, and he lost the kingdom and the Lord departed from him. The Lord cannot use a bashful leader. But the righteous man stands in great boldness: faith brings confidence, faith comes by hearing the word of God, and this kind goes out by prayer and fasting. Be willing to be uncomfortable, break yourself of your weaknesses, stand up manfully, and be turned into another man. Announcements & References Reports and testimony from the recent trips to Kenya and Tanzania ran through the class: the IUIC worldwide blitz carried the word into all the earth, the team taught outside a church in Kenya and kept teaching after being attacked with stones, and observations from the trip framed the teaching on the subdued spirit and the strange god in the motherland. --- Class Notes Index Transcript: full session

title: THE DEVELOPMENTAL PSYCHOLOGY OF BEING HATED
text: Introduction Shalom, my brothers and sisters. We are here in Miami, Florida. In this truth, those of us in leadership come across members of our congregation that suffer many different things, and our job is to help them. Our job is to administer the medicine of the Bible to them, to clean them up. None of us come into this truth because we are whole; people that are whole do not need a physician. Going back many years in New York, at the end of The Book of Our Fathers we would put up the stencil that said the Bible has the solution to our people's problems. That is the reason we still use it today. The Bible is the medicine cabinet: all of the ingredients of the healing are in this chest. We as the doctors, teachers, guides, and leaders assess, counsel, and as we hear the situations it is up to us to go inside the medicine cabinet and find the scriptures that deal with the problems, just like a doctor would do. We are dealing with a whole nation of people that are sick, spiritually sick and psychologically sick. Some subjects get much attention, and there are other subjects that do not get quite so much. This class deals with the ones we do not talk about a lot: the developmental psychology of being hated, and the escapes our people run to, especially alcohol. It is going to be ugly in places, but there is a way out, and we are going to see it in the scriptures. Scriptures Opened Isaiah 34:16 15:31 - Captain's opening: the scriptures are the solution to the problem, and that is also why the Bible is under attack. Do not have just one Bible in your house; have multiple Bibles, because it is going to come under attack. But do not only have the Bible, read the Bible. There is no point in having a manual that you do not know how to use. - Seek ye out of the book of the Lord, and read: you must open the book. A lot of people buy books and never read them. - No one of these shall fail: nothing that is written in the scriptures is going to fail. A lot of times we parallel that with prophecy, but that is also true of the healing elements the scriptures offer. All those scriptures that deal with mental health, they are true, and they are not going to fail when you properly apply them. 2 Peter 3:9 16:55 - Each one of you brothers and sisters that come inside this truth, you are special to the Most High. The Most High did not waste his time calling you if he did not mean for you to make it. - The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, but is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish. Any one of us that comes into this truth, the desire is for you to make it, so we need to try to help you get there. 2 Peter 1:10 17:43 - Give diligence to make your calling and election sure. The Most High called you in here, and that was not a waste. Things were decided in the heavens the day you woke up. Just as there was a conversation going on about Job, conversations were also happening about you repenting. When you come in, understand that sacred calling. - For if ye do these things, ye shall never fall: that is the guarantee of keeping God's commandments. It is up to us. You have the opportunity and the chance to wake up; why would we squander that because of some bad habits and temptations, and lose what Christ promised you? - Every one of your spirits is precious to the Most High. It is a hurtful thing for leadership to see you get weak in this truth, to see you lose the faith. As this lesson goes on, you will see that you do not really have a good excuse for not staying steadfast. - Video played: the old United Negro College Fund commercial, "A mind is a terrible thing to waste." The mind of the Israelites, men and women, is a precious thing. For the Lord to call you out of darkness into his marvelous light is because you have a mind to do great things. We have known many brothers and sisters that came in with good gifts they could have dedicated to the Lord's nation, then got weak hearted, went back out into the world, and are doing nothing. This was the time to shine. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 2:1 My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation. As you are preparing your soul, that is the Lord trying you to make sure you are worthy of that calling. It was already discussed in the heavens to bring you in; it is up to us to stay diligent and steadfast, and not get pulled off by sin, because we are a chosen vessel. You have to see yourselves that way. Hebrews 11:1 29:23 - If we are going to allow the little tribulations to take us off the mark, think about our forefathers in chattel slavery, and think about if they would have given up. They did not have anything near the opportunities you have today. It took a great level of faith for them to persevere through years of slavery and evil treatment, with a vision in mind that one day we are going to get out of this. - Record recounted in class: the husband and wife in the slave quarters who could not protect one another from the slave master's abuse, and still had to console each other and keep going. That is trauma upon trauma, and they endured it sober, without a bottle, and still preserved a generation. - Now faith is the substance of things hoped for: our people in slavery were hoping for freedom, and faith helped them persevere through tunnels of darkness where they saw no light in sight. Faith is also the evidence of things not seen: what they hoped for was not even in their reachable grasp, but it pulled them through, like Joseph in captivity. Joseph did not know that after nearly fourteen years he would be brought out, but he knew that there is a God, and said I will stay here until he decides when to deal with me. - They persevered not knowing when the deliverance was going to come. But here we are. We get a little bit of trouble here and there and all of a sudden we cannot cope; we need alcohol, we need drugs, we need illicit things to take our mind off our problems. Our brothers and sisters could not do that. This is how we have to start putting ourselves in discipline. That is the word: discipline. Deuteronomy 28:65-67 33:25 - Among these nations shalt thou find no ease, neither shall the sole of thy foot have rest: everywhere we go, we are not quite home. We are always being pushed on: move on, get from here, get from there. We have never experienced being home at all. The only time I got some experience of that is when I came to this truth and the brothers told me, welcome home. That felt like home, because I knew I was in the right ship that is going to take us all home. - The Lord shall give thee there a trembling heart, and failing of eyes, and sorrow of mind. Failing of eyes means you cannot envision how you are going to end up; you cannot envision a future for your children, where you will be next month, next year. No hope. Sorrow of mind is experiencing a terrible situation you cannot do anything to change, and you just have to experience the sorrow in it. - And thy life shall hang in doubt before thee: in chattel slavery our lives were in doubt every day. Every day there was a chance we would be killed. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 28:32 Thy sons and thy daughters shall be given unto another people. That could have happened at any moment: your son ripped out of your arms and sold, and you will never see your children again, and there shall be no might in thine hand. A bottle of whiskey would not stop that. They did not have that. They had to endure this thing sober, knowing the Lord is still going to be with us somehow, so I cannot off myself, because a generation is going to come from me. - Record recounted in class: the mother made to wash the master's clothes stained with her lynched son's blood, and even she could not give up. So what excuse do we have today? - In the morning thou shalt say, would God it were even, and at even, would God it were morning. What helped our brothers and sisters make it from night to morning each day with the uncertainty of their lives? Faith. They sang swing low, sweet chariot in the fields and believed those spirituals, not knowing when deliverance would come. And they did not even have the truth like we know it today; whatever little bit they learned, they gleaned from the back of the white man's lying churches, until we got brothers like Nat Turner that started teaching. The title: the developmental psychology of being hated. Definition read in class: the developmental psychology of being hated examines how consistent rejection and hostility warp a child's psychological and biological development. Not periods of hatred, but consistent rejection. Experiencing chronic ill will forces individuals to internalize feelings of worthlessness, alters their brain stress responses, and heavily shapes their approach to future relationships. This is the reason a lot of marriages fall apart and the families are jacked up: these things transmute into every stage of your life; they graduate with you. Constant exposure to hostility triggers a chronic stress response, flooding the developing brain with cortisol. Our kids are hypervigilant in the schools. The amygdala, the brain's fear center, becomes enlarged and overactive, and the prefrontal cortex, responsible for emotional regulation, shows reduced activity. They call it ADHD and put all kinds of stigmas on us, but it is because we are going through things like this. These things affect how we move, how we govern, how we love each other, how we organize. We have to deal with them while at the same time organizing the nation, and we are men; that should never scare men. We should be honored the Lord put us in position to help our people. Books read in class: The Developmental Psychology of the Black Child by Amos Wilson, on how each stage of development builds into the next. Trauma Letters: Healing the Child Within, on going into the levels of the traumas we went through and how we carry them into how we live today. Jawanza Kunjufu's Countering the Conspiracy to Destroy Black Boys, on the fourth grade failure syndrome. Haki Madhubuti's account of two mothers in Dearborn, Michigan: the white family bought model kits that taught their son labor, patience, organizing his time, envisioning how to make it work, and the black son was bought a finished toy plane to pull across the floor. One child was learning to be a manager, an organizer, a thinker, a creator, a builder, and the other was learning to be a consumer in the white man's world. Reading from Erik Erikson's stages of development: human development occurs across eight sequential stages, each presenting a critical psychological challenge. When a child successfully navigates each stage, they build the emotional and psychological foundation for the next. However, when stages are disrupted by absence, neglect, trauma, or instability, the unresolved tension carries forward into every subsequent phase of life. This could be the absence of a father or a mother, or the instability of not knowing if he is coming home at all. The body gets older but the mind does not grow with the body, and people take advantage of that ignorance; that is how our sons and daughters get messed up. So we are really the psychologists with the Bible, the medicine cabinet. Regardless of how messed up it is, we cannot punk out; we still have to get in the game and fix the people. Our forefathers had to get ready regardless of the ugliness before them day and night. Who are we to give up? Video played in class: Malcolm X speaking in 1962 after the Los Angeles police attack on the temple that left Ronald Stokes dead, recounting officers and attendants callously dismissing wounded black men; the teaching point is the climate of virulent hatred our people had to endure, and that was just in the sixties. Imagine living in a climate with that kind of hatred, knowing you are not desired, like the Bible says. And there is no way we could punk out and drown ourselves in alcohol and not pay attention to what is going on with us. If I sound spirited, it is because I hate that disease; I have seen what it did to my family and my people. - Alcohol is a problem when it comes to the point where you can no longer properly function, when it is messing up your family, your relationships, your jobs, and the things you are charged with. You have been put in position to be an asset to the nation, and you cannot be an asset when you are a slave to the bottle. - Your conscience gets on you when you know you should be doing better. Your mind will chastise you: when are you going to stand up? And you do not want to hear that, so you want to silence the conscience, drown the conscience in whiskey and booze. And every time you come back down, the situation is actually worse, because you never did anything to make it better. Then the wife starts voicing the same thing your own mind was telling you, and you want to silence her as well: this is where domestic violence comes in. It is up to us to be men and put an end to that. If we ourselves do not elect to fix our own problems, what other people is supposed to come into your space and do for you what you are too weak to do for yourselves? News story shown in class: the case of Rashawn Carter, a young brother found dead months after going missing, his last trail camera image showing him fleeing in fear; the teaching point is that his mother has to endure every day with no justice and no answers, the way our mothers in slavery endured, and we have no excuse to drown ourselves while our people go through this. Locals were angry at the man who turned in the photo evidence. You owe five dollars to the IRS, they will find you, but they cannot find who did this. Because we know this, we need to stop the cop out business. We have to be our brother's keeper: if you see a brother struggling with that thing, you jump on it. Others knew and said nothing; that is not love, that is the kisses of an enemy. And it is not just alcohol: pornography, adultery, and fornication destroy whole households the same way. Proverbs 13:12 1:31:11 - When you believe you have to just accept this life and suffer peacefully, the psychology you develop is one of hopelessness and despair. Our forefathers did not feel that way; every move they made was met with cruelty, but that still did not stop them from pushing to the point where we are born as a result of them. - Hope deferred maketh the heart sick: the heart meaning the mind. Hope is supposed to be attainable. Many of our people on the ships dove overboard because they saw no way out; they checked out mentally. But there was still a group, the elite of us, that had enough courage in the face of all that ugliness to still reproduce so that we could be here today. That took courage, faith, and hope. - When our people begin to feel that hope is out of their reach, they shortchange their own aspirations. You begin to retract into nothingness, comfortably numb with mediocrity, unproductiveness, laziness, drugs, and alcohol. - But when the desire cometh, it is a tree of life. We are not looking for a nation to save us; we are looking towards the Most High, and that is where our faith is supposed to be, even in the face of virulent hatred. Why would you even fight if you do not have a victory in your mind? Because our people do not believe, they do not even fight anymore; they say just give me the bottle because I am nothing. That is a destroyed state of mind, and we cannot allow it among ourselves or our brothers and sisters. If you see our brothers and sisters carrying that kind of spirit, it is your job to find a way to pull them out of it. We are going to be our brother's and our sister's keeper; we are going to look out for each other. Video discussed in class: Dr. Martin Luther King's lawyer, Dr. William Pepper, gave sworn deposition testimony alleging that King survived the shooting and was deliberately killed at the hospital; the teaching point is the depth of the hatred our leaders faced. A deposition is formal out of court sworn testimony, part of the discovery process, so what he said is on record. King gave the mountaintop speech the night before he was assassinated, saying I may not get there with you, but we as a people will get to the promised land, and I am not fearing any man. He knew death was imminent, yet he still went forward with the weight of all the people on his shoulders. Same with Malcolm, and with sisters that were just as rough when it came to liberation, and they were not even in the truth like we are. So I do not want to hear anybody say anything negative about these brothers, especially not with a bottle in your hand talking about you cannot take it anymore. Psalms 83:2-8 1:46:43 - They that hate thee have lifted up their head: our enemies hate God and hate the Israelites, because our Father chose us to be a special people unto himself above all people on the planet earth. What are you doing with your head in the bottle with that kind of love coming from the Father? - They have taken crafty counsel against thy people: and the counsel is so crafty that we may be thinking we can never get out of this, which is exactly what it is designed to make you think. The hatred and the oppression are designed to break black men down, to make you believe the order is fixed and you can only succumb. And if they cannot keep you subservient, they want to make your life so crazy it drives you to drugs, to alcohol, to fornication and adultery, destroying your nation and your family. - And consulted against thy hidden ones: they make us the hidden ones. We are God's people, and they do not like that. But we have to relish the fact that we are the children of God and act accordingly. The bodies we have, God gave us; we are not supposed to abuse them with alcohol, drugs, or overeating. Ye are gods; but yet we are looking like something else. As a man thinketh, his whole life, his body, and his family will reflect it. - On the body: being fat is not normal, and you are not supposed to be happy with it. The young men of valor come out of the streets with all that temptation around them and take the discipline programs seriously, and their objective is to meet the standards of the men above them. When they look up and see the next tier going backwards, what does that do for their aspirations? You can be whatever you are today, but get better; that is the standard. Many brothers and sisters have burned the fat off and now they can look back and say, I did it. That is achievement. - Let us cut them off from being a nation: the way they cut us off from being a nation is to get between you and what is actually going to save you, between you and your salvation, your God, your nation, your family. - For they have consulted together with one consent: all of the nations are in agreement to make sure we stay ignorant, drunk, and drugged. Look at the music they give us, and the liquor stores all over the place, and ask where the library is. - They are confederate against thee: the tabernacles of Edom, that is the white man leading all the rest of the nations in this; the Ishmaelites, the Arabs with shops all through our communities; Moab, and the rest. You go to Africa and see the same hands: during the scramble for Africa they made sure Africa could not manufacture its own materials, so colonizers take the raw materials, manufacture them, and sell the goods back at prices the people cannot pay, and the IMF loans finish the takeover. That is a brief hit list in this psalm; God is going to deal with all of them. - But the question is, what do we do? Do we walk away from the job of fixing it and go to a bottle? Regardless of how bleak you think the future is, you are still obligated as a man to seek to fix the problem. Seek for the answers. Organize. Discipline yourselves. Change your mental state, change your conversations, change your circle. Get with brothers and sisters that understand the mission, and the Most High will intervene and begin to show you the way. The Lord did not bring us this far to leave us here. Ezekiel 35:5 2:05:10 - This chapter is literally speaking about Esau himself. Thou hast had a perpetual hatred, and hast shed the blood of the children of Israel: perpetual meaning never ending. It was created that way from the womb, Esau and Jacob. That spirit was put in them. - We need to understand that we are a hated people. It is not for us to loathe ourselves and start wallowing because of the hatred; we need to operate in spite of it. Esau's hatred is rooted deep in their spirit from the womb, Genesis 25:23. The current administration is in our faces as a reminding wake up call from God, to agitate us through oppression. Isaiah 51:20 2:07:06 - Thy sons have fainted: our sons have fainted because there is no guidance for our children in the streets. They lie at the head of all the streets, on the corners with no direction and no aim. Their minds are totally wasted, and a mind is a terrible thing to waste. - As a wild bull in a net: that is our young sons in the streets. They are full of the fury of the Lord and the rebuke of thy God, because we broke God's commandments. That is judgment. - What is the rebuke supposed to do? It is not for our destruction; it is to agitate us to organize, to agitate us into keeping God's commandments and coming together like the Bible says: gather together, O nation not desired. Romans 13:3-4 2:09:24 - The Most High put this power over us because we refused to keep his commandments. The rebuke is being sent on us by God through Esau, because we refuse to return. Why would the Lord put his own people in a climate of hate? To agitate us, to cause us to ask God what we did wrong. And once you recognize it, he says, now you have it; let me show you the blueprint on how to get out. - Rulers are not a terror to good works: we are going to go through persecution and trials, but it is our faith in knowing there is a day of restitution, a day when we do not have to deal with this anymore, that is a comfort while we are in our captivity, just like our brothers and sisters in slavery. They had that perseverance without knowing the Bible the way we do; we are much more equipped to know what is coming, and we act like we do not know. Jeremiah 30:11 2:12:12 - For I am with thee, saith the Lord, to save thee: though I make a full end of all nations whither I have scattered thee, yet will I not make a full end of thee. That whole group we read in Psalms 83, every nation is ultimately going to be destroyed. Not the Israelites; we are going to be here. No other nation can claim that. We are in God's plans to be on this earth forever. - Us knowing this, all of this is temporary. The only way you would really go indulge in sin and in a bottle is because you do not believe. But if you believe, you will persevere through this. The Lord is not going to put more on us than we can handle; he said, I want you to make it, but I want to try you to make sure you are serious about keeping my commandments. - I will not make a full end of the righteous: some of our people are going to be destroyed, because they are going to choose the bottle, fornication, and debauchery over the Lord. But the ones that stay in righteousness will inherit the kingdom forever. If our brothers and sisters could endure slavery, we can endure this. And do not say, Lord, will I make it to the kingdom, that is up to you; that is a cop out. The Bible says give diligence to make your calling and election sure. That is on you. - But I will correct thee in measure: he is going to cause us to pass under the rod and teach us his commandments properly. We have some good days coming if we are steadfast. The way this system is set up is to make you believe you cannot escape it, to drive you into drugs, alcoholism, and evil; and if you succumb to that, you will be destroyed by it. The Lord said, fear not thou, O Jacob, for the Lord is our redeemer. We need to remember that. Matthew 5:16 2:19:08 - The Most High is telling us how to operate right now, today. Let your light so shine before men: you cannot let your light shine drunk, and you cannot let your light shine showing the world you do not even know how to control your eating. They call it overweight for a reason: over the weight. If you are comfortable being called overweight, or comfortable depending on a chemical to have a good time, something is wrong. It is a disease, all of it, and we have to cure ourselves from it, and you have the ability to do it. - Examine yourself: there is a part of you, your conscience, that has to step outside of yourself and look at you and say, you have a problem here; when are we going to work together to fix it? That is psychology right there. You do not need to wait for somebody else to tell you; you can evaluate yourself, take the initiative, start right there, and watch the results. Many brothers and sisters have lost the weight and can say, I did it. - We are the ones that are supposed to set the standard on how the world is supposed to move. We are the stars of God, the trendsetters; we only do it in evil now, but we are supposed to set the whole planet up in righteousness. Our job as the nation of Israel and as IUIC is to be the city on a hill, the organized nation, so that our brothers on the corners and the sisters out there see our good works and come and ask about the reason of our hope. And we will tell them: we used to be in your spot, but we repented, and if we can do it, you can do it. They are not going to learn it out here; society wants to take our people into destruction, with junk food and liquor stores on tap on every corner, because a people living with no hope will gravitate toward the crutch. - The same escapism shows up in grown men living in a fantasy virtual world of video games all day long, some so addicted they wear gamer diapers to eliminate bathroom breaks; definition read in class: they are used so players can stay continuously focused on extended gaming sessions without stepping away. Is that not a drug? It is the same thing as alcohol: we use it to escape reality, and reality is going right past you. - Everything you see in IUIC, the departments, the missions overseas, the outreach, none of it existed at the beginning. There had to be vision where it was not seen. That means we had to think like men and think ahead, preparing for the bad times and the famines. All of us have the capacity to think; why is it a surprise when we do it? We used the medicine that is in the Bible, applied it, and got things done. - Video played in class of a man arguing with an artificial girlfriend about cooking: envy thou not the oppressor, and choose none of his ways. That thing is designed to take the place of dealing with a real woman. Getting yourself together so you can properly acquire a wife and cultivate her takes work, time, and dedication, and some men would rather cheat and go around the bend. We have been warned. Wisdom of Solomon 17:12 2:45:46 - For fear is nothing else but a betraying of the succours which reason offereth. Succour means comfort, to run to the rescue, to provide relief in a time of extreme distress. We would choose the easier way out rather than challenge something that causes us to employ discipline, and it is a betraying comfort to do nothing. - Definition read in class: this passage addresses the danger of abandoning logical, structured thought in moments of panic. In times of crisis, fear tempts us to abandon sound judgment for an easier, often false sense of emotional safety. Fear causes us to betray our own capacity for logic, because it feels safer in the moment to panic than to face reality with reason. Sound judgment means making a real effort to correct alcoholic behavior, or doing the disciplined thing to curb the fat, instead of finding an excuse, or a scripture to abuse so you can say the Bible told me I could do this. - Document read in class: the 1883 letter of King Leopold II of Belgium to the colonial missionaries being sent into the Congo. Your principal objective is never to teach the Africans to know God, for this they know already; your essential role is to facilitate the task of administrators and industrials, and interpret the gospel the way that will best protect your interests. Keep watch on disinteresting the people from the richness that is plenty in their underground, lest they dream one day to overthrow you. Find texts encouraging your followers to love poverty, like happier are the poor, for they will inherit heaven. Make them disrespect everything which gives courage to affront us. Direct your action essentially to the younger ones, so the children learn to obey the missionary rather than their parents. Insist on total submission and obedience. And: teach students to read and not to reason. - Teach them to read but not to reason: up to this point many of us did not think there was a difference between the two. Definition read in class: reasoning is the cognitive process of using existing knowledge, facts, and logic to draw conclusions, make decisions, or solve problems; it bridges the gap between raw information and rational action, allowing you to move from one idea to a related idea. Our colonizers do not want us to have this ability, because reasoning is work: the mental work of sitting down, organizing, assessing, the work of a manager, an organizer, a builder. - This is what the stewardship program was: we canvassed the congregation to find out who knew what, who was skilled where, and organized the doctors, nurses, lawyers, paralegals, engineers, electricians, and building specialists into the pie chart. The reasonable solutions were available, right around us; we did not have to go out into the world to get them. That is not selling out; that is organizing exactly what the definition said, and now when people come in with problems, we meet problems with solutions, like Hope and Healing and the doula program. Real people are getting real help because an organizational effort was made. - Because of our inability to reason, we become frustrated and flustered in our thoughts. We know we should do things, but because we are not educated as a collective to reason and organize the elements around us, we act like we cannot, we begin to believe we cannot, and we are frustrated. There is a danger in not reasoning; that is why Leopold said do not teach them to reason, because if they ever learn, we are in trouble. - Example of the fear that runs from reasoning: the fear of acknowledging boldly the black Christ of the Holy Bible. Family members in the church will tell you to get that Bible away from them rather than read what is written. Because of this fear we seek a false and betraying comfort, a cognitive dissonance that normalizes sedative behavior and leaves us comfortably numb in our non-productivity. We say the color of Christ does not matter. Reasoning, if actually applied, would cause us to lay out the elements of our immediate existence and envision a solution to our problems; instead we look for excuses to be docile, for alcohol and getting drunk. - News video played in class: South African leader Julius Malema, long targeted by the AfriForum lobby over the liberation chant a court had ruled protected political speech, was sentenced to prison, and the video connected AfriForum's lobbying of the American administration to aid cuts projected to cost hundreds of thousands of lives. The nations protect the economic inequality apartheid built, and a white minority that lost political control used foreign power to punish a nation into submission. What is happening to our people in South Africa is connected to us from Soweto to Harlem: a collective exploitation of us all. Like Malcolm said, four fifths of the world is not white; they hold it by making us think we are all different while they pillage everybody. - Video played in class: an economist stating plainly that sub-Saharan Africa has been fundamental to global prosperity as a raw material producer, that the economic structures and institutions are designed to keep Africa impoverished, and that whether it is Europe, the US, or China, they need those materials dirt cheap. That is reality, and it can look insurmountable. You cannot get weak and say the order is fixed. Get that thinking out of your mind: we have God behind us, and with God behind us there is no doubt. - So because we feel trapped in so many psychological problems, and feel we could never solve them, we resort to the bottle, to drugs, to promiscuity, to domestic violence and misplaced aggression that affects our youth. Rather than reasoning with your brothers, we turn to violence against those closest to us. And alcohol itself is a huge influence toward violence and self destruction; that is why it is readily available to our people. We use the excuse that we are ready to perish as a reason to feed the disease. If our ancestors had used that excuse to get drunk, none of us would be here today. Habakkuk 2:15-18 3:37:37 - Video played in class: the old Bill Cosby stand up routine on drinking, the man who announces he deserves to go out and get drunk, ignores his own body telling him not to take another drink, and ends the night sick over the toilet vowing never to drink again. The comic relief carries the point: this is what we do to ourselves, and some go through it often. - Woe unto him that giveth his neighbour drink, that puttest thy bottle to him, and makest him drunken also. The alcohol lawyers will say this chapter is about idolatry, and in context it is illuminating other things; but the fact that it uses those words is true. Why would it compare the other evils in the chapter to the effects of alcohol if alcohol itself were not in view? It is speaking of those who press the bottle on their neighbors, the chug chug chug peer pressure you see in college, and the Lord pronounces woe on it. - Personal testimony: getting sick from cheap wine at seventeen, my mother quoting this very scripture over me, and vowing that day never to do it again. The hell with your friends; let them continue that thing. - We have the teaching videos on alcoholism, cup of confusion, overcoming drunkenness, drunken bondage, and more, but videos like that sit at a thousand views while alcohol destroys thousands and millions of homes. Reading shown in class: excessive alcohol use costs the US economy nearly 250 billion dollars annually, driven by lost workplace productivity, health care expenses, and criminal justice and property damage costs. That quarter trillion dollar problem absolutely affects the Israelite community, and the commandments fix all of it. - Reading shown in class: people abuse alcohol to cope with stress, trauma, or mental health issues, using it as a temporary escape to blunt negative emotions; over time the behavior transitions from conscious choice to habit. Alcohol causes the brain to release dopamine and endorphins, rewiring the brain's reward system and leading to cravings; what begins as voluntary use becomes compulsive drinking because of brain changes, making it difficult to stop. Individuals get caught in a cycle where they drink to deal with stress, but the alcohol increases the negative emotional states between drinks, prompting more drinking. We could not mask emotional pain in slavery, so do not use that as an excuse; this will kill you. - Reading shown in class: an alcogenic culture is a societal environment where alcohol consumption is normalized, encouraged, and ingrained in social rituals, where alcohol is highly accessible, heavily advertised, and perceived as essential for socializing, making it difficult for those seeking to drink less or remain sober. There is a line between social and drunkenness, and that line gets blurred; then the incident reports come up, intoxication, and we have to protect the body. We have to be careful, because some of us cannot deal with this thing at all. Romans 12:21 3:51:46 - Captain's teaching: it is not a sin to drink, but when we use drinking as an outlet for our problems, that is when we fall into condemnation. When we are dealing with issues, we always have to rely on the scriptures and build our faith to overcome. Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good, which is God's laws. Precepts: - Romans 8:13-14 If ye live after the flesh, ye shall die: when we obey the elements of the flesh and make the bottle an outlet, the end of that road is always death. But if ye through the Spirit do mortify the deeds of the body, ye shall live; for as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God. - Ecclesiasticus 31:28-29 Wine measurably drunk and in season bringeth gladness of the heart and cheerfulness of the mind; but wine drunken with excess maketh bitterness of the mind. The Lord cannot use you if you do not have that balance. Every element the Lord created has its function and purpose, but if you abuse it you cannot be useful to the nation. It goes for food as well; that is why they put the fast food across the street from more fast food in our neighborhoods. They are depending on you to fall into that destruction. Ecclesiasticus 36:22-23 4:18:24 - Letter read in class from a brother: my wife of thirty plus years only supports me when I bring it up; no meal prep, she would rather eat out; I work twelve hours a day and it is hard at times to even cook and pack my own lunch; over ten years in the truth, I am drained, but she is still my rib. Please help. - Video played in class: a bus driver pushed past his limit by an abusive passenger; the teaching point is that a man carrying stress on all ends with no relief at home can be ticked into ruin by one more provocation. Brothers, do not get to that point; control yourself, because our elders taught us, we need you brothers out here, not in jail. - The beauty of a woman cheereth the countenance, and a man loveth nothing better. He can do twelve hours if you deal with him right. If a man would go down into a pit and fight lions and bring the spoils to his wife, like Zerubbabel brought out in Esdras, what could some kind words do for a brother? He would say, I could do twelve more hours if I get treated like this. - If there be kindness, meekness, and comfort in her tongue, then is not her husband like other men. We kept answering that part with learned response, so hear the other side of it: the wife that does these things turns her husband into a man not like other men. He would have the confidence and the fortitude to do anything, because you are his comfort, his aid, his cheerleader, the help meet that is right for him. Look at what men will risk in wickedness for women that mean them no good; imagine what a man would do for a woman dealing with him right, in righteousness. When you have that support, that woman in your corner, there is no stopping us. In Closing We are definitely a traumatized people, and everything in this class is a disease we have to cure ourselves from. The Bible is the medicine cabinet, and the healing elements in it will not fail when they are properly applied. Our forefathers endured what we cannot imagine, sober, with faith in a deliverance they never saw; so we have no excuse to leave our post for a betraying comfort. Examine yourself. Give diligence to make your calling and election sure, because the Most High did not call you to waste you, and the Lord did not bring us this far to leave us here. Announcements & References Field reports played: - The prophets led by Captain Shem hit the Rolling Loud festival in Orlando, teaching the people their nationality according to the Bible. - IUIC Austin taught at the Crawfest in Killeen, Texas, on repentance and the dietary law in Leviticus 11 and Deuteronomy 14. - IUIC Indiana completed an adopt-a-block community cleanup on the west side of Indianapolis, leading by example in taking care of our own community. - Brothers were invited to teach a local community Bible study group about the twelve tribes and our history in the Bible; the group was very receptive and wants to continue learning. - IUIC Miami hosted its first annual YMOD and YDOS youth career fair, presenting careers and trades from members of the body to give the children a vision of what they can be for the nation. - A first congregation wedding was celebrated: a righteous union built on the word of God, two years of proving, and countless counsel. Dates: the Day of Simon feast is May 23rd at sundown. The next congregational fast is May 29th. The Feast of Pentecost is June 6th at sundown, with the Texas Pentecost 2026 gathering. Men's Conference 2026 registration closes Sunday, May 31st. Music and media: vote for the Israel Live top five countdown, Mondays at 9:00 pm Eastern. New single and apparel releases at originalroyalty.com; if you have one song in you, the label wants your single. Books and documents referenced in class: - The Developmental Psychology of the Black Child, by Amos Wilson - Trauma Letters: Healing the Child Within, by Captain Galayah - Countering the Conspiracy to Destroy Black Boys, by Jawanza Kunjufu (the fourth grade failure syndrome) - Black Men, by Haki Madhubuti (the Dearborn model plane account) - Letter from King Leopold II of Belgium to colonial missionaries, 1883 (teach students to read and not to reason) Closing reading: 1 Corinthians 11:23-29, the bread and the cup, in remembrance of the Lord's death till he come; let a man examine himself. --- Class Notes Index Transcript: full session

title: 70 TIMES 7: THE PERFECTION OF MERCY THROUGH CHRIST
text: Introduction All praise to the Most High for another Sabbath day, another opportunity, another day to receive forgiveness of our sins. The title of the class is 70 times 7, the perfection of mercy through Christ, and the deacon is taking us into some deep waters. Shout out to Deacon Malachi for his class going over the hatred that these nations have for our people; today's opening segues right out of it. Set the frame first: the only reason we are in this building is because of Jesus Christ. All of us have done things worthy of death. Every class we bring on the Sabbath is to glorify the Lord, not ourselves; we are ambassadors of Christ, preparing the way of the King of kings. In The News - Video shown of an influencer who goes around Tennessee harassing black men and women, calling them out of their name to provoke them to anger while he carries a pistol in an open carry state; he recently shot a brother he had been insulting. In the clip, a sister who knew him from years back greets him warmly and tells him, "You're not racist, I know that," because he used to be the neighborhood plug and all his friends were black. - It baffles me how, from the slave ships until now, our people are still in the illusion that we can change the minds of our oppressors if we feed them, work with them, and get into relationships with them. She saw all the videos and still stuck her hand out to dap up the enemy. And notice the cross on her neck: this is what Christianity does to our people, polluting the mind with assimilation, integration, and turn the other cheek nonsense, which is not biblical. Scriptures Opened Ecclesiasticus 12:10-11 14:23 - Never trust thine enemy: for like as iron rusteth, so is his wickedness. Not sometimes; never. Back then he was cool with everybody; give him time, and the rust shows. Though he humble himself and go crouching, yet take good heed and beware of him: thou shalt know that his rust hath not been altogether wiped away. - The Most High asks, can a leopard change his spots? You cannot change Esau, and you were never commissioned to try. Genesis 15:13 16:33 - Christ speaking to Abram: know of a surety that thy seed shall be a stranger in a land that is not theirs, and shall serve them, and they shall afflict them four hundred years. That seed runs through Isaac and Jacob; this first affliction is ancient Egypt, not America. - Why did God allow it? Because the sons of God broke God's law before it. Precepts: - Genesis 6:1-6 The sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair, and took them wives of all which they chose. The wickedness in verse 5 is that mixing the Most High said not to do; it grieved him at his heart, and judgment followed the chosen line into Egypt. - Luke 3:38 Which was the son of Enos, which was the son of Seth, which was the son of Adam, which was the son of God. That is the lineage of the sons of God: the chosen line comes through Seth, who replaced Abel. Write that down so the question never confuses you again. Exodus 1:1-11 22:58 - Seventy souls came into Egypt with Jacob, and the children of Israel were fruitful and increased abundantly, like we do here in America: they call us the minority, but in power only, not in number. - A new king arose which knew not Joseph, and said, Come on, let us deal wisely with them. How does modern day Egypt deal wisely with us now? Brothers answered: keeping us in the ghettos ringed with liquor stores and bad food, think tanks designing propaganda, and above all religion and politics. Those are the two main tools, because the keeping of God's commandments is what unifies us as a nation, and Esau knows it; that is why billions are pumped into religions and politics to keep the Israelites divided. - They set over us taskmasters to afflict us with burdens, and we built Pharaoh's treasure cities. We built the pyramids and the great cities of Egypt the same way we built up America; when the Israelites left Egypt, no new pyramid ever popped up. Exodus 3:1-14 28:04 - Put off thy shoes from off thy feet, for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground. Moses was a great man in Egypt, second to Pharaoh, and God required humility of him anyway. The shoes were symbolic: the same thing the Most High requires of us coming into this truth. The Christian garbage, the Islam garbage, the black power philosophy: leave it all outside and reform your mind as an Israelite in these scriptures. - I have surely seen the affliction of my people which are in Egypt, and have heard their cry by reason of their taskmasters. The Most High sees us oppressed here in America and expects us to cry unto him the same way, like the prayer before class: we pray for the destruction of our enemies, not the turn the other cheek prayer of the church. And the land he promised is the land of Canaan, which becomes Jerusalem when Messiah brings us back; the people in that land right now are not the real Jews. - God said unto Moses, I AM THAT I AM: thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel, I AM hath sent me unto you. Precepts: - Ecclesiastes 5:1 Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God, and be more ready to hear than to give the sacrifice of fools. Some come into the sanctuary with pride and contention, thinking they know much when they do not; keep your foot means keep your mouth shut and hear, the same charge God gave Moses at the bush. - John 8:58 Verily, verily, I say unto you, before Abraham was, I am. That is who spoke to Moses out of the bush: Christ. 1 Corinthians 10:1-11 34:47 - All our fathers were under the cloud, and all passed through the sea. Our fathers, possessive: through Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. The cloud is the chariots of God, what the world now calls UFOs or UAPs. All were baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea: Moses teaching us the laws of God and the gospel, because Moses spoke with Christ. They drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them, and that Rock was Christ. - With many of them God was not well pleased, for they were overthrown in the wilderness. These things were our examples, that we should not lust after evil things as they lusted. The people sat down to eat and drink and rose up to play: fornication in the wilderness, and three and twenty thousand fell in one day. Neither murmur ye: murmuring is not a light thing just because it is speech. The brother next to you cannot hear you, but the angels write it down and report it. - All these things happened unto them for ensamples, and are written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the world are come.
