The acts of the apostles continue; we are learning from our forefathers the same way the congregations in Asia Minor did. Precepts: - 2 Esdras 14:4-9 I led my people out of Egypt, and brought him up to mount Sinai, where I held him by me a long season: the forty days and forty nights. He told Moses many wondrous things and showed him the secrets of the times, the beginning, the middle, and the end; that is how Moses wrote the first five books, and how he saw even his own end before the promised land. Isaiah 1:4 41:52 - A sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity, a seed of evildoers, children that are corrupters. We have to be honest and sincere with ourselves, even in prayer: do not go to the Most High acting righteous when you are full of dead bones and guile. Open your mouth and confess the things you are battling. - They have forsaken the Lord, they have provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger, they are gone away backward. That is why we went into captivity: Deuteronomy 28:15 through 68 laid out the curses for breaking the commandments, and many of us are still moonwalking away from the Most High. Now is our time to get our minds right and repent. Precepts: - Matthew 11:28 Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Heavy laden with sin, and the rest is not a good night's sleep: it is the kingdom, rulership for a thousand years under Christ. This is why we need a saviour; we cannot do it without Christ. Numbers 13:1-3 45:26 - The Lord spake unto Moses: send thou men, that they may search the land of Canaan, which I give unto the children of Israel. Which I give: the fight was already the Lord's, and the land already given. - The men sent were not regular brothers; every one a ruler among them, heads of the children of Israel, men of renown who could lead other men. Numbers 13:25-33 47:20 - They returned after forty days and agreed the land flowed with milk and honey; then verse 28 turns on one word: nevertheless. The people be strong, the cities are walled, we saw the children of Anak. Doubt entered on the heels of the promise. - Caleb stilled the people and said, Let us go up at once and possess it, for we are well able to overcome it. Caleb showed faith and courage: the Most High already said he would deliver the enemy into our hands, so their stature did not matter. - But the men that went up with him brought an evil report: we were in our own sight as grasshoppers. Rulers and leaders, shook with doubt and fear; and doubt and fear are Satan's playground. Numbers 14:1-4 50:31 - The spirit of fear jumped from the leaders onto everybody: all the congregation lifted up their voice and cried, and all the children of Israel murmured against Moses and against Aaron. When they murmured against Moses and Aaron, who were they truly murmuring against? The instruction came from the Most High. - Would God that we had died in Egypt; were it not better for us to return into Egypt? In chapter one of this history they were crying to the Most High under the taskmasters; now they are in the wilderness and want to go back to master. Remember Harriet Tubman: I could have saved thousands more if they had known they were slaves. Our people still want to stay with master in Babylon America; it is the same thought. - And they said one to another, Let us make a captain. No to the leaders God appointed; they wanted somebody to give heed unto their itching ears. Numbers 14:11-12 54:45 - The Lord said unto Moses, How long will this people provoke me? and how long will it be ere they believe me, for all the signs which I have shewed among them? The Most High is showing longsuffering: all the plagues, all the miracles, and they are still moved by unbelief. Numbers 14:18-23 55:27 - The Lord is longsuffering, and of great mercy, forgiving iniquity and transgression, and by no means clearing the guilty. Moses stood as the mediator between us and God, and the Lord said, I have pardoned according to thy word. That is how much the Most High loved Israel and loved Moses. - Because all those men which have seen my glory and my miracles have tempted me now these ten times, and have not hearkened to my voice. Write the ten down; the Most High deals in numbers, and nothing in the Bible is insignificant. Precepts: - Exodus 14:11-12 One: at the Red Sea. Because there were no graves in Egypt, hast thou taken us away to die in the wilderness? It had been better for us to serve the Egyptians. - Exodus 15:23-24 Two: at Marah. The waters were bitter, and the people murmured against Moses, saying, What shall we drink? - Exodus 16:2-3 Three: the wilderness of Sin. The whole congregation murmured: would to God we had died by the hand of the Lord in Egypt, when we sat by the flesh pots. - Exodus 16:19-20 Four: hoarding the manna. Moses gave specific instruction, let no man leave of it till the morning; notwithstanding they hearkened not, and it bred worms and stank. - Exodus 16:27-29 Five: gathering on the Sabbath. The Lord gave two days of bread on the sixth day, and they went out on the seventh anyway. How long refuse ye to keep my commandments? No gratitude at all. - Exodus 17:2-7 Six: Massah and Meribah. Chide means to be contentious, to go back and forth. They were almost ready to stone Moses over water, and the place was named for the chiding of the children of Israel, because they tempted the Lord, saying, Is the Lord among us, or not? - Exodus 32:1-10 Seven: the golden calf. As for this Moses, we wot not what is become of him: listen to the disrespect toward the man who led them out. Aaron made the calf out of fear, knowing better as high priest, and the people sat down to eat and drink and rose up to play in honour of a god that cannot talk. No difference from our people today who prefer white Jesus or run to a stone in the east that cannot answer prayers. - Numbers 11:1-6 Eight: Taberah. When the people complained, it displeased the Lord, and the fire of the Lord burnt among them; the same thing he is going to do in America. Nine: the lusting for flesh. We remember the fish, the cucumbers, the melons, the leeks, the onions, and the garlick; ungrateful, complaining about the manna of heaven. - Numbers 11:34 And he called the name of that place Kibrothhattaavah: because there they buried the people that lusted. Numbers 14:26-35 1:13:02 - The tenth provocation was the report of the spies, and it was the last: how long shall I bear with this evil congregation, which murmur against me? Doubtless ye shall not come into the land, save Caleb the son of Jephunneh and Joshua the son of Nun, because Caleb had another spirit with him and followed the Lord fully. - Those twenty years old and upward did not enter in; the little ones the doubters said would be a prey were the ones brought in to know the land their fathers despised. - After the number of the days in which ye searched the land, even forty days, each day for a year, shall ye bear your iniquities, even forty years. That is how the Most High gets down with numbers: the forty years matched the forty days exactly. Judges 2:11-19 1:16:35 - In the land the pattern repeated: Israel forsook the Lord, served Baal and Ashtaroth, and provoked the Lord to anger; he sold them into the hands of their enemies; they cried out; he raised up judges and delivered them. Israel sins, we cry out, God delivers, again and again. - And when the judge was dead, they returned and corrupted themselves more than their fathers. That is why we are in need of a shepherd: left to ourselves, we destroy ourselves. 2 Chronicles 36:15-21 1:19:32 - The Lord God of their fathers sent to them by his messengers, rising up betimes and sending, because he had compassion on his people; but they mocked the messengers of God and despised his words, until the wrath of the Lord arose against his people, till there was no remedy. - The Babylonians burnt the house of God and brake down the wall of Jerusalem. With the temple destroyed, what could no longer take place? Sacrifice. The prophet Jeremiah called Israel a homeborn slave: from captivity to captivity there was no atonement to be had, and that is exactly why we needed a saviour, an ultimate sacrifice. Matthew 1:17 1:22:06 - Fourteen generations from Abraham to David, fourteen from David to the carrying away into Babylon, and fourteen from Babylon unto Christ. The line ran through slavery the whole way down. Matthew 1:21 1:22:36 - Thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins. His people; that is who the sacrifice was for. Precepts: - John 1:29 Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world. Christ was the perfect, ultimate sacrifice. - Hebrews 10:5-8 Sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not, but a body hast thou prepared me. The animal sacrifices were temporary, a shadow training us for what was to come; the good thing that came was the body of Jesus Christ. Lo, I come in the volume of the book: the whole book, because Christ is present in the Old Testament and before it. - John 1:3 All things were made by him, and without him was not any thing made that was made. Christ was always the plan. Genesis 2:1-3 1:25:51 - On the seventh day God ended his work which he had made, and he rested on the seventh day. The seventh day is not Sunday. Seven represents completion, perfection; hold that, because the whole class hangs on it. Precepts: - Exodus 20:8-10 Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy. Six days shalt thou labour; the seventh is the sabbath of the Lord thy God: no servile work. - Exodus 16:23 Bake that which ye will bake today: lay up your food before Friday sundown, because there is no cooking on the Sabbath. - Exodus 35:3 Ye shall kindle no fire throughout your habitations upon the sabbath day: that is the cooking fire, not the heat in winter. And stop following the additions of the Talmud from people who are not the real Jews. - Exodus 31:14 Ye shall keep the sabbath, for it is holy unto you: the penalty written on defiling it shows how seriously the Most High takes his sign. - Exodus 31:16-17 It is a sign between me and the children of Israel for ever, a perpetual covenant. Not the nations: the children of Israel only. When Christ returns, all nations will be made to keep it, but it was created for one people. Hebrews 3:15-19 1:30:19 - Harden not your hearts, as in the provocation. Paul takes us right back to the history we just read: with whom was he grieved forty years? them whose carcases fell in the wilderness. And to whom sware he that they should not enter into his rest, but to them that believed not? - So we see that they could not enter in because of unbelief. Unbelief is what kept a delivered people out of the promise. Hebrews 4:1-11 1:31:24 - Let us therefore fear, lest, a promise being left us of entering into his rest, any of you should seem to come short of it. For unto us was the gospel preached, as well as unto them: the gospel did not begin in Matthew; it was preached to our forefathers, and it did not profit them, not being mixed with faith. - For if Jesus had given them rest: that Jesus is Joshua. Joshua was mighty and smote the nations of Canaan, but there were enemies on every side, so the land was not the true rest. There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God: the seventh day Sabbath is the similitude, and the substance is the kingdom, reigning with Christ. - Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief. Rest is entered by labour; that is the paradox the wilderness generation never accepted. Precepts: - 2 Esdras 8:52 For unto you is paradise opened, the tree of life is planted, the time to come is prepared, a city is builded, and rest is allowed. Spoken to Israel, not to all nations. - 2 Esdras 3:5-6 Thou leddest Adam into paradise, which thy right hand had planted, before ever the earth came forward. Paradise was already here before the foundation of the earth; that is the rest prepared from the foundation of the world. - Micah 4:10 Be in pain, and labour to bring forth, O daughter of Zion, like a woman in travail. No matter what we are going through, we must be in pain and do this work to bring forth the kingdom. - Revelation 14:13 Blessed are the dead which die in the Lord, that they may rest from their labours; and their works do follow them. Your works are what follow you through those gates. - Isaiah 14:1-3 The Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel; the strangers shall be joined to the house of Jacob, and Israel shall rule over their oppressors. And it shall come to pass in the day that the Lord shall give thee rest from thy sorrow, and from thy fear, and from the hard bondage wherein thou wast made to serve. That is the true rest: after the Sabbath we go back to labouring in Esau's system Monday morning, but that day ends the bondage itself. - 2 Peter 3:7-8 Be not ignorant of this one thing, that one day is with the Lord as a thousand years. The seventh day maps to the thousand years. - Revelation 20:4 And they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years. The seventh day Sabbath represents us resting and reigning with Christ; that is what every seventh day is rehearsing. 2 Kings 5:10-14 1:43:37 - Elisha sent a messenger to Naaman: go and wash in Jordan seven times, and thy flesh shall come again to thee. Seven again: completion. Naaman was wroth at first, full of pride, wanting the clean rivers of Damascus instead of the muddy Jordan; his servants humbled him, and when he dipped seven times according to the saying of the man of God, his flesh came again like the flesh of a little child. - Who did the healing? The spirit of Christ, working through Elisha. What healed Naaman was his belief and his obedience to the word of the prophet. Precepts: - Isaiah 1:16-20 Wash you, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings. That is the true washing: cease to do evil, learn to do well. Action, not speech. Though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; if ye be willing and obedient, ye shall eat the good of the land, but if ye refuse and rebel, ye shall be devoured with the sword. - Psalms 51:6-7 Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean: wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow. The word of God is what really cleanses us of our sins. - Luke 3:3-4 John came into all the country about Jordan, preaching the baptism of repentance for the remission of sins: the same river Naaman was cleansed in. - Matthew 3:13 Then cometh Jesus from Galilee to Jordan unto John, to be baptized of him. The same Jordan, the number and the river pointing to the same Christ. - Luke 4:25-27 Many lepers were in Israel in the time of Eliseus the prophet, and none of them was cleansed, saving Naaman the Syrian. Christ himself reached back and referenced this exact history. Joshua 6:1-16 1:51:02 - Seven priests bearing seven trumpets of rams' horns before the ark; six days one circuit, and on the seventh day seven circuits, and at the seventh blast Joshua said, Shout; for the Lord hath given you the city. Seven also represents complete deliverance. - On the seventh day, because of their faith, the Most High brought down the walls of Jericho flat. Nothing is accidental with the Most High: the seventh day rest, Naaman dipped seven times, Jericho compassed seven times by seven priests with seven trumpets. Precepts: - Revelation 11:15 And the seventh angel sounded; and there were great voices in heaven, saying, The kingdoms of this world are become the kingdoms of our Lord, and of his Christ. The seventh trump brings forth completion, the same way the seventh circuit brought down Jericho. Leviticus 23:1-8 1:56:36 - These are the feasts of the Lord, holy convocations. In Leviticus 23 there are seven appointed feasts, and every single one of them represents Jesus Christ. We know there are other appointed days, Purim, Nicanor, Hanukkah; right now we are in this chapter's seven. - First the weekly Sabbath, whose true meaning we just read: rest going into the kingdom. Then the fourteenth day of the first month at even is the Lord's passover, which we just finished celebrating, and the fifteenth day begins the feast of unleavened bread: seven days ye must eat unleavened bread. The unleavened bread is Christ's sinless life, and the haste out of Egypt besides. Precepts: - Exodus 12:5 Your lamb shall be without blemish, a male of the first year. - 1 Peter 1:18-20 Ye were not redeemed with corruptible things, as silver and gold, but with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot. Christ was that lamb. - Exodus 12:46 Neither shall ye break a bone thereof: the instruction for slaughtering the passover lamb. - Psalms 34:20 He keepeth all his bones: not one of them is broken. The prophecy written of Christ. - John 19:31-33 The soldiers brake the legs of the two crucified with him, but when they came to Jesus and saw that he was dead already, they brake not his legs: thus fulfilling the prophecy of Psalms 34:20. - Micah 5:2 But thou, Bethlehem Ephratah, out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel. Article read in class: the unblemished passover lambs were raised at Migdal Eder, the tower of the flock by Bethlehem, wrapped in cloths, and brought to Jerusalem for sacrifice; the same road Christ walked, born in Bethlehem and offered at Jerusalem during Passover. - Luke 2:4-7 She brought forth her firstborn son, and wrapped him in swaddling clothes: the same handling our forefathers gave the lambs brought to Jerusalem. Thus fulfilling prophecy; Christ is our passover. - John 6:35 I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger. - 1 Corinthians 5:7 Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened. For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us. The old leaven is sin. Leviticus 23:15-17 2:07:57 - The feast of firstfruits: count seven sabbaths complete from the wave offering, and number fifty days. Seven sabbaths again, complete. Precepts: - 1 Corinthians 15:20-23 Now is Christ risen from the dead, and become the firstfruits of them that slept. Every man in his own order: Christ the firstfruits; afterward they that are Christ's at his coming. The same promise stands for us if we believe and keep the commandments in the faith of Christ. - Romans 8:23 Ourselves also, which have the firstfruits of the Spirit, waiting for the adoption, the redemption of our body. - James 1:18 Of his own will begat he us with the word of truth, that we should be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures. - Revelation 14:4 These are they which were not defiled with women: not defiled with false doctrine and philosophy, and not defiled literally. These follow the Lamb whithersoever he goeth, being the firstfruits unto God and to the Lamb. Leviticus 23:24-25 2:11:04 - The feast of trumpets: in the seventh month, a memorial of blowing of trumpets, an holy convocation. Precepts: - Matthew 24:31 He shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds. The elect is Israel, the only people scattered from one end of heaven to the other. - Zechariah 9:14-16 The Lord shall be seen over them, and his arrow shall go forth as the lightning, and the Lord GOD shall blow the trumpet. The Lord of hosts shall defend them, and the Lord their God shall save them in that day as the flock of his people: as the stones of a crown, lifted up as an ensign upon his land. - 2 Esdras 6:23 And the trumpet shall give a sound, which when every man heareth, they shall be suddenly afraid. That trumpet is no flute; it is a frightening sound. Leviticus 23:27 2:14:05 - The day of atonement: on the tenth day of the seventh month ye shall afflict your souls. Christ was that atonement. Precepts: - Hebrews 7:22-25 The priests under the law were many, because they were not suffered to continue by reason of death; but this man, because he continueth ever, hath an unchangeable priesthood. That is how Christ is able to save to the uttermost and atone continually: there is no death in him. - Hebrews 9:11-18 Not by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us. He is the mediator of the new testament, as Moses was mediator when we came out of Egypt; and where a testament is, there must of necessity be the death of the testator. That is why Christ had to die: a testament is of force after men are dead, and while the testator lives it can still change. - Romans 3:25 Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood. Propitiation means atonement. - 1 John 2:2 He is the propitiation for our sins: and not for ours only, but also for the sins of the whole world. That world is scattered Israel, all Israel, that they might have time to repent. - Wisdom of Solomon 18:24 For in the long garment was the whole world: the high priest's ephod carried a stone for each tribe. The world on Aaron's chest was Israel, and Christ is the new high priest. Leviticus 23:34 2:19:45 - The feast of tabernacles, seven days unto the Lord. Tabernacle, sukkot, booth: it means to dwell. Precepts: - John 1:14 And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us: Christ pitched his tent among us. - John 2:19-21 Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up. They thought he meant the building of forty six years; but he spake of the temple of his body. His body was the greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands. - Revelation 21:3 Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be his people, and God himself shall be with them, and be their God. He is the God of Israel; that is the completion every feast was pointing to. Proverbs 9:1 2:22:56 - Wisdom hath builded her house, she hath hewn out her seven pillars. Seven pillars: complete wisdom. Precepts: - Proverbs 8:22-23 The Lord possessed me in the beginning of his way, before his works of old; I was set up from everlasting. Wisdom and Christ are interchangeable here, because Christ is the ultimate wisdom. - Isaiah 11:1-2 There shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse: count the seven upon him. The spirit of the Lord, wisdom, understanding, counsel, might, knowledge, and the fear of the Lord: the seven pillars, complete spiritual perfection, which is what Christ operated in. Genesis 4:15 2:25:09 - Now the flip side: the devil's seven. Whosoever slayeth Cain, vengeance shall be taken on him sevenfold. Cain was the first murderer, and the teaching is that his spirit runs through Esau: complete, unquenchable vengeance, murder and bloodshed to the epitome. - He tells the so called blacks to forget about slavery, but every September 11th it is "never forget," and the Holocaust is kept before the world perpetually while our four hundred years are waved away. That is vengeance kept alive on their terms and denied on ours. Genesis 4:23-24 2:27:10 - Lamech, of Cain's line, boasted to his wives: I have slain a man to my wounding. If Cain shall be avenged sevenfold, truly Lamech seventy and sevenfold. There it is: 70 times 7 in the mouth of a murderer means complete, total, utter vengeance. - That is why we read in Ecclesiasticus, never trust thine enemy. You think he forgot how we handled them under King David, or the dark ages? He has not forgotten; he is still acting out his vengeance on the so called blacks and Hispanics to this day. Precepts: - Ezekiel 35:5 Because thou hast had a perpetual hatred, and hast shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword. Perpetual: great, ongoing, fiery hatred. - Amos 1:11 For three transgressions of Edom, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because he did pursue his brother with the sword, and did cast off all pity, and his anger did tear perpetually, and he kept his wrath for ever. - Obadiah 1:10 For thy violence against thy brother Jacob shame shall cover thee, and thou shalt be cut off for ever. Matthew 18:21-22 2:31:06 - Now the true flip side. Peter asked, Lord, how oft shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? till seven times? Jesus saith unto him, I say not unto thee, Until seven times: but, Until seventy times seven. - Lamech's seventy and sevenfold was complete vengeance; Christ's seventy times seven is complete, boundless, endless mercy to the Israelites who believe, and he told Peter to extend the same. Precepts: - Luke 17:3-4 If thy brother trespass against thee, rebuke him; and if he repent, forgive him. And if he trespass against thee seven times in a day, and seven times in a day turn again to thee, saying, I repent; thou shalt forgive him. That brother is the children of thy people, per Leviticus 19:17. - Colossians 3:12-13 Put on therefore, as the elect of God, bowels of mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness, longsuffering; forbearing one another, and forgiving one another, even as Christ forgave you. Some of us hold grudges like there is no tomorrow; imagine if Christ held on to grudges toward us. We would not be here. Forgiveness is something to pray for. Daniel 9:24-27 2:35:12 - What is 70 times 7 in the math? Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city: 490 years, from the commandment to restore and build Jerusalem in Nehemiah's day unto the Messiah the Prince, to finish the transgression, to make an end of sins, to make reconciliation for iniquity, and to anoint the most Holy. - After threescore and two weeks shall Messiah be cut off, but not for himself: cut off for the children of Israel. The people of the prince that shall come destroyed the city and the sanctuary: that is Titus and the Roman armies, 70 AD, the flood of desolation and the captivity that followed. - So Christ's seventy times seven is the 490: the prophecy completed, the perfection of mercy delivered exactly on schedule, because we could not sacrifice in our captivities and needed him. Precepts: - Hebrews 1:9 Thou hast loved righteousness, and hated iniquity; therefore God, even thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows. That is the anointing of the most Holy: Christ. - Luke 21:20 And when ye shall see Jerusalem compassed with armies, then know that the desolation thereof is nigh. The Roman armies: the desolation Daniel determined. Acts 5:29-31 2:39:14 - We ought to obey God rather than men. The God of our fathers raised up Jesus; him hath God exalted with his right hand to be a Prince and a Saviour, for to give repentance to Israel, and forgiveness of sins. - Now Matthew 18 lands in full: forgive your brother seventy times seven, because I forgave you seventy times seven. All those captivities where we could not sacrifice, going from one bondage to the next in the midst of sin: the only reason we are here is Christ. Revelation 7:14 2:40:15 - These are they which came out of great tribulation, and have washed their robes, and made them white in the blood of the Lamb. That is the Israelites, and that washing is the only thing that brings us through to perfection. Hebrews 10:26-30 2:40:45 - But do not take him for granted. If we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins, but a certain fearful looking for of judgment. Sinning wilfully is learning this truth and walking back into the world saying, put me back to sleep. - He that despised Moses' law died without mercy under two or three witnesses: of how much sorer punishment shall he be thought worthy, who hath trodden under foot the Son of God, and hath counted the blood of the covenant an unholy thing? Vengeance belongeth unto me, I will recompense, saith the Lord; the Lord shall judge his people. 2 Corinthians 5:14-15 2:42:24 - For the love of Christ constraineth us: it puts a brake on our impulses. He died for all, that they which live should not henceforth live unto themselves, but unto him which died for them, and rose again. - We owe Christ. We owe him a major price, brothers. That is the whole class in one line. In Closing Christ is the complete perfection. Lamech's seventy and sevenfold was the completion of vengeance, and that spirit of perpetual hatred is still working in the earth: a video was shown of one of the officers responsible for Patrice Lumumba's death laughing about it decades later; his body was destroyed with acid and a gold tooth kept, only recently returned to his family in the Congo, the same way Nat Turner's skull was passed down as a trophy. That is the record of the seventy times seven of hatred. Against it stands the seventy times seven of the Lord: boundless mercy, the 490 years fulfilled, the Lamb without blemish cut off not for himself but for us. The only reason we are here is Jesus Christ. Do not take him for granted, and forgive your brother the way he forgave you. Stay tuned for Bishop Nathaniel. Shalom, sign of Christ, bless. Announcements & References Videos and materials referenced in class: - Instagram video of an armed influencer harassing black people in Tennessee, and the sister who greeted him as a friend (opening teaching on Ecclesiasticus 12:10). - Article read in class on the passover lambs of Migdal Eder, the tower of the flock: raised in Bethlehem, wrapped in cloths, and brought to Jerusalem for sacrifice, as Christ was. - Translated interview clip of a Belgian officer involved in Patrice Lumumba's 1961 death, sent in by Officer Aaron from Midlands (closing teaching on Esau's perpetual vengeance). --- Class Notes Index Transcript: full session

title: CHARACTER & INTEGRITY: THE HIDDEN STRENGTH BEHIND WISDOM
text: Introduction Shalom, Israel. Most High and Christ bless. Happy Sabbath. I know it is bright and early, but it is time to get it in; we got classes all day. The Captain brings the class from his phone after his laptop with the whole class on it went down: it seems like when I go live, something bad happens. That is not IT's fault; it is Satan, trying to get you off your grip. This is the opening session of the class; the teaching continues in the second session under the same title. Today's topic: character and integrity, the hidden strength behind wisdom. We just finished Passover, and after Passover things get shaken up; that tree is shaking hard. Coming back from the Marriage is Honorable retreat, with the sit-downs every night around the leadership, one thing stood out: a lot of people lack integrity, and it shows in their character. Your character is the representation of you; that is what you are. Integrity is the action that fed that character. Real wisdom shows up in your character, your discipline, your honesty, your consistency, and how you move when nobody is watching. Wisdom leaves its footprints: you see a brother has wisdom and discernment based off how he moves, how he deals with people, how he deals with his wife and children, and how he takes correction. A person can know the scriptures, pull them left and right, and still have terrible character: secretly battling pride and lust, a lying spirit, lazy, selfish, a hypocrite, bitterness. You know where the scriptures are, but you do not apply any of it. That shows you lack integrity and character. Definitions read in class: - Character fundamentally refers to the distinctive combination of mental, moral, and ethical traits that make an individual unique. In psychology and ethics, it is the aggregate of moral and ethical qualities, such as integrity, courage, and honesty, that dictate how a person thinks, feels, and behaves. Notice the first quality listed is integrity. - Integrity is the quality of being honest and having strong moral or ethical principles. It involves aligning your actions with your values consistently, regardless of the circumstances or whether anyone is watching. Key aspect: consistency, practicing what you preach; your words and actions match up even when it is difficult or inconvenient. - The difference: think of character as the sum of your moral habits and values, and integrity as the unwavering consistency of acting in alignment with those values, especially when it is difficult. When you get corrected, when it is not convenient, when your back is against the wall: that is when integrity kicks in. - Integrity guides your life. Without integrity, emotions guide you; lust guides you if you are not disciplined; pride, anger, and impulse guide you. Integrity keeps you grounded. If you missed the retreat sit-downs, you missed hundreds of years of wisdom that was right there in your face: how to deal with your marriage, how to deal with your family, how to grow as a man in this truth. Some brothers were there but were not there, because they did not want their character on blast. You have to be around these men to grow; your mind plays tricks on you, and the scripture says woe to him that is alone. God did not design us to be by ourselves; he set up leaders when we came out of Egypt and when Christ walked the earth. The integrity of the laws of the Most High is what separates us from the nations; the Most High has been trying to teach us integrity since creation, and the Christian church is fighting against it right now. Scriptures Opened Proverbs 11:1-3 19:21 - A false balance is abomination to the Lord: falsifying something is not good character. But a just weight is his delight. When pride cometh, then cometh shame: but with the lowly is wisdom. - The integrity of the upright shall guide them: the upright is the person keeping the commandments, practicing what they preach. Your integrity is going to guide you into doing the right thing, no matter the circumstances. - But the perverseness of transgressors shall destroy them: the person that lacks integrity and character is destroyed by that same lack. - Discussion in class: a prison interview clip was recalled where a man convicted of multiple murders said he had no reason, felt nothing, and did not think he had any feelings of humanity, and that only a tenth of what he had done was ever found. That shows what the scripture says of the enemy: his soul is not upright in him. Many of the nations lack the ethics, empathy, and sympathy the Lord gave us; that is why we had the rule as a nation, because we showed the example of morals and ethics in the world. Without us in power, the world is in shambles. Interactive question 1, put on the screen 27:36 : you are alone online late at night, and temptation hits; nobody from the congregation would know. What shows integrity? A, entertain the temptation privately. B, watch a little and justify it later. C, cut it off immediately and fight temptation. D, convince yourself grace covers everything. - This is a moment of trial; this is what you call battling. You are fighting your war against yourself: you do not want to push play, but you want to push play, and nobody is there to tell you a thing. - The answer is C. The questions are easy and the answers are easy; the problem is when it actually comes to fruition in real time. That is when C gets blurred out. - Correct answer read: the real battlefield is private. A lot of people fall spiritually in secret long before they fall publicly. The representative shows up at the Sabbath; the real you shows up when you are at home, when you are alone, when you are with your family. Your wife knows exactly who you are. You cannot come up here saluting hard like you are over righteous and then go home and verbally, financially, or physically abuse your wife: you lack integrity and you have poor character. And vice versa, sisters: you cannot bow all the way down at the door and then go home and curse your husband out and keep nothing. You lack integrity in that area too. Precepts: - Romans 6:1 Answer D is a scary mindset to have. What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound? That is the mindset of the Christian church: I found grace, grace covers me, I can do what I want as long as I believe; I do not have to do what Christ says. That is a terrible mindset, and it is exactly what this verse is warning against. Proverbs 20:11 34:29 - Even a child is known by his doings, whether his work be pure, and whether it be right. Everybody is going to be accounted for their works, period. The works you choose to get into are dictated by the type of integrity and character you have: how you make decisions, how you give counsel, how you deal with your brother and sister. 1 Samuel 2:3 35:21 - Talk no more so exceeding proudly; let not arrogancy come out of your mouth: for the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed. - Your actions will be weighed. We are going to be judged off our actions, our works, period. You have to prove yourself to the Lord: that you are studying, the works you do in this body, constantly growing, constantly consistent. - We are the representation of this truth. When they look at the Israelites as a face, who do they look toward? The brothers in the purple and gold, Israel United in Christ. Why? Because our leadership is heavy on integrity, character, structure, and order: traits we were never taught growing up and have to be taught now, around men who have built themselves up. Psalms 15:1-5 38:25 - Lord, who shall abide in thy tabernacle? Who shall dwell in thy holy hill? He that walketh uprightly, and worketh righteousness: that worketh is an action; you are putting your hand to the plow. - And speaketh the truth in his heart: that means he is the same all the time; he shows the integrity behind his thoughts. - He that backbiteth not with his tongue, nor doeth evil to his neighbour: a person working toward righteousness is not going to do evil to his neighbor, because he has great moral character. He honoureth them that fear the Lord; he that sweareth to his own hurt, and changeth not. He that doeth these things shall never be moved. - It comes with consistency, and it also comes with the company you keep. If you are the smartest person in the room, you are in the wrong room. I want to be around men I can learn from, men that will tell me, no, that is not right, that will tell me where I am in error. But a lot of you like yes men and yes women, because that gives you the opportunity for murmuring and backbiting, like the scripture just said. A lot of you are not putting in any action; you lack integrity. Interactive question 2, put on the screen 41:57 : a brother corrects you and you feel embarrassed. What shows wisdom? A, get defensive immediately. B, talk about them afterward. C, examine yourself honestly. D, leave emotionally. - You got corrected, and you were wrong. A lot of brothers shut down, or explode and cannot control their emotions, because they got corrected. - The answer is C: examine yourself honestly. Everybody says C when they are looking at the screen, but when it actually happens in real time, C is blurred out; they do not even consider it. - A, getting defensive: people do not like being told they are wrong, but how can you fix something if you are never corrected? B, talking about them afterward: taking the correction to the face, then going behind his back to minimize it as if the brother was out of the spirit. D, leaving emotionally: you have no emotional strength to deal with correction; that is that 2018 spirit; you cannot take it. - Correct answer read: strong character can handle correction without collapsing emotionally. Pride hates correction, but wisdom loves instruction. - At the Marriage is Honorable sit-downs we saw the same thing: really only one sister answered honestly. It was not correct, but she answered honestly, and we can deal with that; we can grow from that. A lot of people were being politically correct, and you could tell they were not answering right at all. - Couples that went: keep the same energy you built down there. Do not come back and slide into the negative because you got the kids back; that is backtracking and not upholding your integrity. Proverbs 12:1 45:53 - Whoso loveth instruction loveth knowledge: being corrected is a good thing; that is how you grow. A lot of people do not like being around leadership because they know they will get stood up and asked questions, to see where their biblical knowledge and moral knowledge is. The elders and bishops are trying to build real strong righteous men, and you have to get corrected, because a lot of us lack these abilities. - But he that hateth reproof is brutish. Proverbs 15:10 46:58 - Correction is grievous unto him that forsaketh the way: and he that hateth reproof shall die. Proverbs 15:32 47:15 - He that refuseth instruction despiseth his own soul. He does not want to hear it, he is always right, but he is wrong. You are destroying your own soul, because you cannot be corrected, which means you cannot grow. - That is why some have been here 10 or 15 years and are still a soldier or an officer of 10. You cannot say you have been held back: you know everything else, but the wisdom cannot take hold and exalt you like it exalts the rest that take hold of it. That is when it is time to take stock in yourself, and a lot of people do not want to do that. Precepts: - Proverbs 17:10 A reproof entereth more into a wise man than an hundred stripes into a fool. A foolish person cannot allow wisdom to enter in; you sit around the men, you are in the school with all these men, you see everybody growing around you, but the wisdom cannot take hold because you are fighting against it. James 3:13-16 50:03 - Who is a wise man and endued with knowledge among you? Let him shew out of a good conversation his works with meekness of wisdom. These are actions; this is great moral character. - But if ye have bitter envying and strife in your hearts, glory not: this wisdom descendeth not from above, but is earthly, sensual, devilish. The Lord did not put that spirit in us; those are traits people picked up through life in the world, and that is why their name is always in some mess. - For where envying and strife is, there is confusion and every evil work. These are not the characteristics we want associated with us. This is why we have to be around men who have been through these things and can teach us to be better men, better leaders, better husbands, better fathers. If you are not around those type of people, how can you learn these moral and ethical traits? Ecclesiasticus 1:26-27 54:59 - If thou desire wisdom, keep the commandments, and the Lord shall give her unto thee. Keeping the commandments is an action. This is our foundation; this is the integrity we roll by. - When you are keeping the commandments with all your heart and all your soul, you really have no choice but to have very good integrity, and a person keeping them willfully will have very good character. You cannot keep the commandments with all your heart and have horrible character; it makes no sense. - For the fear of the Lord is wisdom and instruction. Ecclesiasticus 1:18-21 56:15 - The fear of the Lord is a crown of wisdom, making peace and perfect health to flourish: both which are the gifts of God. Wisdom raineth down skill and knowledge of understanding, and exalteth them to honour that hold her fast. - The root of wisdom is to fear the Lord, and the branches thereof are long life. - The fear of the Lord driveth away sins: and where it is present, it turneth away wrath. Why? Because a person that fears God is going to keep the commandments and uphold the integrity to do the right thing. Regardless of the situation, regardless of the inconvenience, you are going to continue to uphold the integrity of the commandments, because you are working it over and over again. - Captain's point: our integrity and our moral character are directly tied to our fear toward God. It is one and the same. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 18:27 A wise man will fear in every thing, and in the day of sinning he will beware of offence: but a fool will not observe time. That is integrity guiding you in every step: is this the right move, is this in alignment with the laws of God? In moments of correction, whether you can digest it and receive it is a sign of where your faith is at. Proverbs 11:3 59:28 - Back to where we started: the integrity of the upright shall guide them. Your integrity is going to guide you into doing the right thing; it is going to put you in position. The session ends here and the class continues in the second recording under the same title. In Closing The opening session lays the foundation: character is what you are, and integrity is the consistent action that builds it. Wisdom is hidden behind both; it shows up in your discipline, your honesty, and how you move when nobody is watching. Keep the commandments, love instruction, stay around men you can learn from, and let your integrity guide you. The class continues in the second session, going deeper into fixing the spirit. Announcements & References - The class follows the Marriage is Honorable retreat; couples who attended are charged to keep the same energy they built there in their marriages. - Definitions of character and integrity, and the difference between them, were read in class from reference material on screen. - The teaching continues in the companion session: Character & Integrity, The Hidden Strength Behind Wisdom. --- Class Notes Index Transcript: full session

title: Character & Integrity: The Hidden Strength Behind Wisdom
text: Introduction Integrity is a decision that has to be made every time. If you are not reading your four chapters a day, you are not studying, you don't give the Most High nothing to work with; how can you apply when it is time to apply if you are not reading and studying the scriptures? This is a fix your spirit class. We all got to fix our spirit; Satan is coming, and we got to tighten up our spirit, because people are going to get put in compromising positions where you have to use that integrity and have good character to get out of it. Scriptures Opened Wisdom of Solomon 1:3-8 1:05 - A froward thought means it is your worldly thought. You want to do what you want to do; you don't want to do what the Lord is telling you to do. You think you know better than the Lord, you think you know better than the men that rule over you. That means your mind ain't on the Lord at all; you're separating yourself by your own thoughts, which means ultimately you lack character, you lack integrity. - Wisdom cannot enter somebody with a malicious soul: a person that can't be corrected, that don't have good moral character. Some brothers know all the scriptures, but they can't keep rank, they always having issues. You know all these scriptures, why are you not applying them? That is because you have bad judgment, bad moral character. - When you have discipline, the Holy Spirit of discipline is going to flee deceit, and will not abide when unrighteousness cometh in. - He that speaketh unrighteous things cannot be hid. When you lack character, when you lack integrity, you do something that you know is wrong, eventually those things are going to come out; there is no getting around it. The Lord will reveal that stuff, and it comes out when it is supposed to come out. Joshua 1:16-17 12:21 - When Moses died, the mantle passed to Joshua, and the men should follow the leaders and everybody else behind them. All certain things is not going to come straight from the Lord; it's going to come as "I need you to do this, I need you to do that, straighten this up." - Moses led the people with integrity and character, and with Joshua ministering underneath Moses, they seen the same characteristics in him. That is why it wasn't a hard transition: we going to follow you just like we did Moses, whatever you tell us to do, we going to do, because they seen how he moved. It is the company you kept; Joshua was under Moses, and Caleb did the same thing. - Some elders from other camps say that Moses left the truth. It says right there in verse 17, only the Lord thy God be with thee, as he was with Moses. Shame on you for not reading the scriptures, and shame on the men that follow you. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 4:27 Camps like that have made themselves students and underlings to foolish men. Genesis 39:1-12 14:30 - The Lord was with Joseph, and he was a prosperous man. His master saw that the Lord was with him and made him overseer over his house, and the Lord blessed the Egyptian's house for Joseph's sake. - Joseph was a goodly person, and well favoured. He had a very good reputation; people looked at him as a man with integrity and good character. - His master's wife cast her eyes upon Joseph and said, lie with me. But he refused: he committed all that he hath to my hand, but he didn't give me you. How then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God? - Ain't nobody watching him. He could have did what he did, but he said no. This is where integrity come from: this is where you make the right decisions when nobody is watching. - She caught him by his garment when none of the men of the house was there, and he left his garment in her hand and fled. He know this is wickedness; this thing will destroy everything, my reputation, everything that I have worked so hard for. I ain't sinning against her, I'm sinning against the Lord ultimately. - Read on in Genesis 39: he end up going to prison behind this, because she lied on him. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 9:9 Sit not at all with another man's wife; don't play with it. Don't be drinking around somebody else's wife, lest thine heart incline unto her, and through thy desire thou fall into destruction. Both of y'all are going to destroy everything. Job 2:3-13 22:40 - This is a man that have integrity, very good moral character and ethics. The Lord said there wasn't nobody on the earth like him; that is the standard he had. - He lost his kids, he lost everything that he had, he had boils all over his body, and still he holdeth fast his integrity. - Listen how Satan would go into the woman. When things ain't right, when a woman feel uncomfortable, Satan try to go in there and infiltrate the woman. Women like to be comfortable in the security of that house; things is in shambles, so Satan creeping. She said, dost thou still retain thine integrity? Curse God, and die. - But he said, thou speakest as one of the foolish women speaketh. Shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil? In all this did not Job sin with his lips. He upheld his integrity even through trials and tribulations, when things are inconvenient. - His three friends came every one from his own place to mourn with him and to comfort him, and sat down with him upon the ground seven days and seven nights, and none spake a word unto him, for they saw that his grief was very great. Now you see the type of men that you're around; that is true friendship. Precepts: - Galatians 6:1-2 If a man be overtaken in a fault, ye which are spiritual restore such an one in the spirit of meekness. You got to build and restore this man back to life, speak life into that brother to get him back on track. Bear ye one another's burdens; if we was in that same situation, we would want our brothers to come and get us out of it. Daniel 6:4 33:00 - The presidents and princes sought to find occasion against Daniel, but there was no error or fault found in him. This man lived up to a name integrity, even when they tried to force them to worship other gods, and the Lord showed favor to Daniel. John 12:4-6 33:45 - Judas Iscariot said, why was not this ointment sold and given to the poor? This he said, not that he cared for the poor, but because he was a thief. This man walked with Christ, seen many miracles, and still betrayed the savior, and betrayed the disciples and everybody else around him. - It is people like that that they around, but they really not around; they just taking up space. This is not the type of character you need. Money was the root and the god of Judas: greed. Y'all casting out demons, y'all doing miracles; what more do you want? - This is how they infiltrate organizations, through money. Organizations fail because of money: they infiltrate, they come in, offer money, and they give up their organization. That mean they lacked integrity; they let money come in and dictate and control the movement. That ain't happening here. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 4:6 When your coworkers wondering why this brother don't murmur with them and don't ever work the Sabbath: keep therefore and do them, for this is your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the nations, which shall say, surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people. The other nations are expecting you to be that greedy individual that lacks integrity, but we give them this right here. 1 Samuel 15:13-24 38:02 - King Saul is a very good example of not upkeeping the integrity and lacking character when it came down to it. He wanted to please men more than he wanted to please God, and the Most High dealt with him. - I have sinned, for I have transgressed the commandment of the Lord, because I feared the people. He chose to disobey the Lord because he feared the people more than the Most High God. That is a problem a lot of people deal with even here: you worried about pleasing other people, but you not worried about pleasing the Lord. - What did the Lord say to do to Amalek? Kill everything; nothing should be alive when you leave there. But he wanted to do his own thing, and the people spared the best of the sheep. Pride, not listening, self-will. The Lord stopped dealing with Saul. 1 Samuel 18:8-11 - They have ascribed unto David ten thousands, and to me they have ascribed but thousands. You the king, but you jealous? Jealousy and envy is a lack of character. - Saul eyed David from that day and forward, and cast the javelin to smite David even to the wall. By not obtaining the integrity and not having good moral character, Saul continued to wax worse; his character begins to decline even more over time. - When you don't listen to the Lord, when you try to please other people and not the Lord, you're going to destroy yourself. It is only a matter of time, and it's going to be open to the public; everybody saw the decline of Saul. Philippians 2:12 44:30 - As ye have always obeyed, not as in my presence only, but now much more in my absence. Some people just show themselves to be that guy in front of everybody; you need to be like that in the absence of everybody. This is the perfect biblical example of integrity. Psalms 7:8 46:20 - Judge me by my integrity and my righteousness, Lord. Judge me by the decisions that I make when times are hard, because that is our works; we're going to be accounted for our actions and our works in righteousness. - The commandments and the wisdom of the Lord is the foundation of your integrity. When you upholding that, you're going to accumulate a very strong character that people can be proud to be around. You want to be known by the leadership with very good character and integrity, not for trying to portray something that you're not in front of the people while you sinning against the Lord. Hebrews 2:1 52:30 - We ought to give the more earnest heed to the things which we have heard, lest at any time we should let them slip. - Examine if you have been moving with integrity, if you're lacking moral and ethical character. These things matter in your walk: the type of husband you are, the type of father you are, the leader you are, the type of mother you are. We got to be around those people that not going to just be yes men and women, but those that's going to challenge your integrity and your character by helping you build it. Class Questions - Leadership gives instruction you don't personally agree with, but it's not against the commandments; what shows integrity? Answer: follow respectfully and maintain order. It is not sin what this person is asking you. Complain quietly afterwards means you did it with malice and no effort. Ignore the instruction means I don't agree with it, I ain't doing it. Pretend outwardly while causing division privately means now you're sowing discord and bringing somebody else into your lack of judgment and character. - A lot of times that complaining spirit, that doubtful spirit, is that you don't have faith. You don't believe that the bishops, the deacons, the men over you are put in place by God. You're not denying them, you're denying God, and that evil spirit of unbelief is hindering your understanding. - A person acts righteous around leadership, but differently everywhere else; what does that reveal? Answer: fear of men more than fear of God. That is image management, not integrity; you're trying to manage a false image of yourself. Integrity means being consistent everywhere, in any moment, when things are hard and inconvenient for you. You still uphold your vows, your values, your morals, and your ethics. - What's harder for most people? Answer: actually changing privately. Many people know truth but struggle with transformation; it's easier to look righteous publicly than to change privately. Until you apply what the Bible says, it's just words on the page. You got to believe what you're reading to be able to put it into action; you ain't reading it just to remember it, you're reading it so you can apply it. - A brother or sister apologizes sincerely after wrongdoing; what shows good character? Answer: forgive wisely and allow room for repentance and growth. You really see the sincerity over time; your actions have to show that you sincerely apologize for the wrong you did. And let the bitterness go: a brother held on to anger years after the other person apologized, when the brother thought it was over with. Let it go. - Which matters more to the Most High? Answer: true integrity from the heart. The Most High always gave us the answer; he said, I set before you death and life, choose life. He repeated himself over and over, and you still going to choose the wrong answer. - Integrity also means you're not going to get everything right. When you mess up: I got to say something. That is integrity too. - If you struggling with porn, a lot of brothers struggling with that; tell someone. Get someone who has integrity, go to that person and let them know, look, I'm struggling with this. That hatred, that envy will come out and show itself, I don't care if it's five years later. - Murmuring is a lack of integrity and character, and we have a lot of it; murmuring is big in the body. We got to shut that down. In Closing Wisdom is not proven by how deep you sound, how many scriptures you know, how spiritual you appear. Wisdom is revealed through consistency, discipline, humility, honesty, and integrity. ---

title: In Vain Do They Worship Me! Religious Syncretism
text: Introduction The early morning captain's class, taught from Phoenix, Arizona. Happy Sabbath: this is a double Sabbath, going into the feast of Pentecost, and the bishop will teach the Pentecost class tomorrow. Today's title is In Vain Do They Worship Me: Religious Syncretism. People ask what religious syncretism means; that is what we are going to find out. We are also less than two months from blitzing the earth to wake up and recover the lost sheep. The same conditions are all over the earth: wherever you see our people, the curses of Deuteronomy 28 are there, and if you can read with spiritual eyes it is almost impossible not to know who the biblical Jews, the real Israelites, are. The same lies we get over here, our brothers and sisters are getting wherever they are; the difference is the spirit the Lord put on the men here in America to go to the four corners of the earth and teach. Scriptures Opened Isaiah 34:16 13:45 - Seek ye out of the book of the Lord, and read: no one of these shall fail. This goes into the prophecies: whatever the Lord spake, it shall come to pass. Many of them have come to pass, but there are many more yet to come. Deuteronomy 16:16 16:43 - A few Pentecost scriptures for those that may be new, because this word is going out and daily new people are tuning in and finding out who they are. Three times in a year shall all thy males appear before the Lord thy God: in the feast of unleavened bread, and in the feast of weeks, and in the feast of tabernacles. This coming feast is the feast of weeks. 2 Chronicles 8:13 17:27 - Again we see that we are supposed to gather and give an offering three times in the year: the feast of unleavened bread, the feast of weeks, and the feast of tabernacles. - Do we give a physical offering today? No. So what do we offer? We offer ourselves, we offer obedience. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 35:1 He that keepeth the law bringeth offerings enough: he that taketh heed to the commandment offereth a peace offering. Tobit 2:1 18:54 - This scripture explains what Pentecost is: the feast of Pentecost, which is the holy feast of the seven weeks. Acts 2:1 19:53 - And when the day of Pentecost was fully come, they were all with one accord in one place. That feast of Pentecost was the feast of weeks. Definitions read in class: syncretism in religion is the blending of diverse religious beliefs, traditions, or practices into a new or combined system. It often happens organically when different cultures interact, exchange ideas, or are assimilated through historical events like trade, migration, or conquest. Notice how it jumps from exchanging ideas to being assimilated: another word for conquest is slavery. The Wikipedia entry adds that syncretism is the combining of distinct beliefs or schools of thought, particularly religious ones, where features of one religion are incorporated and absorbed into another, asserting an underlying unity and allowing an inclusive approach to multiple faiths. Inclusivism asserts there is beauty in the variety of different schools of thought and that they can coexist; it stands in contrast to exclusivism, which asserts that only one way is true and all others are erroneous. The entry also mentioned anthropology, the scientific study of humanity, of cultures, societies, norms, and values. Psalms 64:4-6 25:20 - That they may shoot in secret at the perfect: we are the perfect. They encourage themselves in an evil matter; they say, who shall see them? - They search out iniquities; they accomplish a diligent search. This is when they go and do their studies and research. The other nations, especially Esau, get to go out and dig up the historical artifacts, and when they find out about our history, they know. Cultural anthropology means they study us so they can figure out what drives us and what motivates us, and ultimately how to keep us in the midst of sin. Deuteronomy 32:8-9 28:32 - Let us see what exclusivism is. When the Most High divided to the nations their inheritance, he set the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Israel. - For the Lord's portion is his people; Jacob is the lot of his inheritance. And no one else. Everyone else is excluded. Matthew 15:24 29:32 - Reading it in the New Testament: I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel. That is exclusive; no one else is included in that. They do not like to hear that; they run to "neither Jew nor Greek." But it is what it is. Acts 7:43 31:53 - The coexist image was shown: an image created by a Warsaw based Polish graphic designer in 2000 as an entry in an international art competition sponsored by the Museum on the Seam for dialogue, understanding, and coexistence. In the lettering you have the crescent and star of Islam, the peace sign, the male and female sign, a star they label Judaism, the wicca pentagram, the yin and yang of Taoism, and the cross of Christianity, and they are saying all of these are supposed to coexist. - That star is not the star of David. Ye took up the tabernacle of Moloch, and the star of your god Remphan, figures which ye made to worship them: and I will carry you away beyond Babylon. Matthew 15:1-9 41:24 - The scribes and Pharisees asked why the disciples transgress the tradition of the elders. Christ answered, why do ye also transgress the commandment of God by your tradition? That is what we ask Christians all the time: why are you not keeping the Sabbath day? Why are the women not dressing modestly? Why do you eat unclean foods? These are just some of the basic laws. - God commanded, honour thy father and mother: and he that curseth father or mother, let him die the death. You children at home putting your hands on your mama or your daddy, Christ said let him die the death. - Thus have ye made the commandment of God of none effect by your tradition. That is modern day Christianity: they make the commandments of God null and void by their traditions, like the Sabbath day. - This people draweth nigh unto me with their mouth, and honoureth me with their lips; but their heart is far from me. They are very good at quoting scriptures and talking about the love of Jesus, but their minds are far from the Lord. - But in vain they do worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men. That is where the class title comes from. - Chart shown in class of man made religions and their founders: John Smyth and the Baptists, Joseph Smith and the Mormons, William Miller and the Seventh Day Adventists, Charles Taze Russell and the Jehovah's Witnesses, Charles Parham and the Pentecostals, and Friedrich Schleiermacher, the father of modern hermeneutics. These are the doctrines of men that our Christian brothers and sisters are following. Proverbs 4:2 44:56 - What are they supposed to be teaching? For I give you good doctrine, forsake ye not my law. You are supposed to be keeping the laws of God; that is the doctrine. Further reading from the article: contextualization, or enculturation, is the practice of making Christianity relevant to a culture; it does not address the doctrine but affects a change in the styles or expression of worship. Is that not where our people fall off the horse? Christianity is all about the praise and worship team. Christians took their European music and building styles into churches in other parts of the world, and in a contextualization approach they would build churches, sing songs, and pray in a local ethnic style to appeal to the ones they are trying to win over. That is why they are always in our neighborhoods: you do not have sinners in your own neighborhood? Some Jesuit missionaries adapted local systems and images to teach Christianity, as the Portuguese did in China, leading to the Chinese Rites controversy. Exclusivist systems see syncretism as a betrayal of their pure truth: adding an incompatible belief corrupts the original religion. That exclusivist approach is keeping the laws in the faith of Christ. Our forefathers fought to keep it separate. 1 Maccabees 2:19-22 50:38 - Mattathias answered with a loud voice: though all the nations under the king's dominion obey him, and fall away every one from the religion of their fathers, yet will I and my sons and my brethren walk in the covenant of our fathers. - God forbid that we should forsake the law and the ordinances. We will not hearken to the king's words, to go from our religion, either on the right hand or the left. Our religion is keeping the commandments. 2 Maccabees 6:23-24 51:30 - Eleazar considered his age, the honor of his gray head, and his honest education from a child in the holy law made and given by God, and willed them straightway to send him to the grave. - For it becometh not our age, said he, in any wise to dissemble, whereby many young persons might think that Eleazar, being fourscore years old and ten, were now gone to a strange religion. Ninety years old, and he would not pretend, because we have to be examples to the younger generation. 2 Esdras 2:42-47 52:43 - Esdras saw upon mount Sion a great multitude that praised the Lord with songs, and in the midst of them a young man of high stature, taller than all the rest, setting crowns upon their heads: it is the Son of God, whom they have confessed in the world. - These be they that have put off the mortal clothing and put on the immortal. Then began I greatly to commend them that stood so stiffly for the name of the Lord. That is what Eleazar was doing: he was not going to go against the commandments of God, which is our religion. 2 Maccabees 8:1-2 54:08 - Judas Maccabeus and they that were with him went privily into the towns, called their kinsfolk together, and took unto them all such as continued in the Jews' religion. There it is again: the Jews' religion. - They called upon the Lord to look upon the people that was trodden down of all, and to pity the temple profaned of ungodly men. Those other nations are ungodly men. 2 Maccabees 7:1-23 55:26 - The record read: seven brethren with their mother were taken and compelled by the king, against the law, to taste swine's flesh, and each brother chose a martyr's death rather than transgress the laws of the fathers. Why is it that swine's flesh is all throughout the black church today? These are those that stand stiffly. - We are ready to die rather than to transgress the laws of our fathers: do you know what level of faith that is? You truly cannot desire anything left in this world. And the bishop used to say it all the time: we are already captives. You have bills, you work fourteen hours a day. What are you leaving? There has to be something better. - The king and they that were with him marveled at the young man's courage. They marvel because they have to understand there is a certain spirit in them; there is something they know. - The fourth said, it is good, being put to death by men, to look for hope from God to be raised up again by him: as for thee, thou shalt have no resurrection to life. The sixth said, be not deceived without cause: for we suffer these things for ourselves, having sinned against our God; but think not thou that strivest against God that thou shalt escape unpunished. - The mother was marvelous above all and worthy of honorable memory: she saw her seven sons slain in one day, and bare it with good courage because of her hope in the Lord. The Creator of the world, who formed the generation of man, will also of his own mercy give you breath and life again. And what kind of mercy would it be for the same people that torment us to get an equal reward in the kingdom? That is not a merciful God, if he allows them to do that to us and then they get the same portion. Precepts: - Psalms 96:5 All the gods of the nations are idols: but the Lord made the heavens. They have no living God. - 1 Corinthians 8:5-6 Though there be that are called gods, whether in heaven or in earth, to us there is but one God, the Father, and one Lord Jesus Christ. Because we understand there is only one living God, that is why the king was marveling. 2 Maccabees 14:37-38 1:05:30 - Razis, one of the elders of Jerusalem, a lover of his countrymen: that is nationalism, that is loving your race. For his kindness he was called a father of the Jews. - For in the former times, when they mingled not themselves with the Gentiles, he had been accused of Judaism, and did boldly jeopard his body and life with all vehemency for the religion of the Jews. That is religious exclusivism. Galatians 1:13-14 1:07:07 - You may think that changed in the New Testament with Jesus. They love Galatians. Ye have heard of my conversation in time past in the Jews' religion. So we are reading about the Jews' religion in the New Testament: nothing changed. - And profited in the Jews' religion above many my equals in mine own nation, being more exceedingly zealous of the traditions of my fathers. Acts 26:5-7 1:08:21 - After the most straitest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee. And now I stand and am judged for the hope of the promise made of God unto our fathers: unto which promise our twelve tribes, instantly serving God day and night, hope to come. - Pause there, because the Christians come up to us on the street talking about Jews and Gentiles. Where do you read about the other tribes in the New Testament? You read about Anna of Aser in Luke, and Nephthalim and Zabulon, but all the tribes are not listed. Yet Paul says our twelve tribes. James 1:1-8 1:10:19 - James, a servant of God, to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad. So Paul and James are on one accord. Then how is it that they claim Paul taught not to keep the commandments, but they never accuse James of that? - Count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations, knowing that the trying of your faith worketh patience. If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, but let him ask in faith, nothing wavering. - Let not that man that has a wavering spirit think that he shall receive any thing of the Lord. A double minded man is unstable in all his ways. Video segment on Our Lady of Guadalupe: Catholicism in Central and South America has been integrated with elements from the cultures of the indigenous peoples of the Americas and enslaved Africans. The Catholic Church allows some symbols and traditions to be carried over from older belief systems so long as they are remade to conform to a Christian worldview, while syncretism with systems like Vodun and Santeria is expressly condemned. The image of Our Lady of Guadalupe and the devotion to her are seen as assimilating elements of native Mexican culture into Christianity, and Santa Muerte, a female deity of death, emerged as a combination of the indigenous goddess Mictecacihuatl and the Lady of Guadalupe, worshiped as of 2012 by about five percent of the Mexican population. A prayer video was played: they open in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, so they believe in the Trinity, and they pray to Our Lady of Guadalupe to make intercession for the holy church, calling her the ever virgin. That is woman worship, no different from Diana in Acts 19; the same spirits keep coming back up. A brother raised Catholic explained it evolved from Juan Diego, who claimed her image appeared on his cloak, and the same thing continues today with claimed appearances on tortillas and trees that people build altars around. This is what happened to our brothers of the northern kingdom: they got conquered, and this is the modern form of Christianity they are under. Hebrews 7:24-25 1:17:20 - If she makes intercession, that would make her the mediator. But this man, because he continueth ever, hath an unchangeable priesthood. Wherefore he is able also to save them to the uttermost that come unto God by him, seeing he ever liveth to make intercession for them. Christ is the intercessor, not Mary. Matthew 13:55-56 1:18:39 - Is not this the carpenter's son? is not his mother called Mary? and his brethren, James, and Joses, and Simon, and Judas, and his sisters, are they not all with us? Mary did not just have Jesus; she had other children. The Zondervan compact Bible dictionary entry on Mary lists the distinctive Roman Catholic doctrines about her, the immaculate conception and the assumption of Mary, and we just showed in the scriptures that the perpetual virginity claim is a lie. Video played of a man leaving Christianity: "One reason I'm done with Christianity is because I can no longer support the idea that if you don't accept Jesus Christ as Lord and Savior, you're going to burn forever in eternal hellfire." That is apostasy: the formal disaffiliation from, abandonment, or total rejection of a religion or previously held set of beliefs. A lot of times it is because you are not being taught, and because of the things you see going on in the church. The Latter Day Saint movement holds that truth in other sources can be identified via personal revelation. That is the "this is my truth" spirit: I am not religious, I am spiritual; that is your interpretation; the Bible says this to me. That personal revelation is what you get in a Christian church: the Lord told me, only me; twenty people are going to give two thousand dollars in the next twenty minutes. Psalms 119:142 1:30:31 - Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth. There is no private truth; the law is the truth. John 17:17 1:30:50 - Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth. Isaiah 8:20 1:31:14 - To the law and to the testimony: if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light in them. That is what the word of God is. 2 Peter 1:20-21 1:32:25 - No prophecy of the scripture is of any private interpretation. The prophecy came not in old time by the will of man: but holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost. So much for personal revelation. 1 Peter 1:10-11 1:33:09 - The prophets inquired and searched diligently, searching what, or what manner of time the Spirit of Christ which was in them did signify, when it testified beforehand the sufferings of Christ, and the glory that should follow. What was in the prophets? The Spirit of Christ. Luke 24:44 1:34:19 - All things must be fulfilled, which were written in the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms, concerning me. All those things were written by men who had the Spirit of Christ on them. So why do they ask, why are you reading out of the Old Testament? Because that is the effect of Christianity and that blending of religions. You are practicing a modern form of Christianity that is going to lead you straight to damnation. Exodus 20:1-11 1:35:51 - All of what we have been dealing with goes into serving other gods: idolatry. Thou shalt have no other gods before me. But what we have been reading is a mix or a blending of religions and other gods from the beginning. - Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image, nor bow down thyself to them, nor serve them: for I the Lord thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me; and shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love me, and keep my commandments. That means there are going to be those like us that repent in these last days. - Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy. What we just read was the first four commandments, and they go into loving the Lord thy God. All of this blending of religions is meant to take you away from serving the Lord thy God. How many of these religions honor the Sabbath day? How many of these Christians are going to keep the feast of tabernacles, the feast of weeks, the Passover? It is meant to keep you in sin. Precepts: - Proverbs 30:7-9 Give me neither poverty nor riches; lest I be full, and deny thee, and say, Who is the Lord? or lest I be poor, and steal, and take the name of my God in vain. He put his spirit in us; we are a holy people. When they say you cannot keep the commandments, that is because they want to remain in their sins. That does not mean we have never sinned; if anybody says they have not sinned, they lie. Matthew 22:37-40 1:41:23 - Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind. This is the first and great commandment. And the second is like unto it: thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets. We are focusing on the first one, because all the other commandments flow from these two. Deuteronomy 6:4-6 1:42:21 - Hear, O Israel: the Lord our God is one Lord. And thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might. And these words which I command thee this day shall be in thine heart. Numbers 25:1-3 1:43:38 - Now some biblical examples of syncretism.
