The stars of heaven shall not give their light; the sun shall be darkened: there is going to be so much war that the sun and the moon are blacked out. - I will punish the world for their evil, and the wicked for their iniquity; I will make a man more precious than fine gold: that is going to be us. - Therefore I will shake the heavens: the heavens are the nations; he is going to shake them and cause them to fight against each other. They shall every man turn to his own people, and flee every one into his own land. All that democracy talk about being one people is done in that day: everybody is going to turn to his own people and his own land. - Every one that is found shall be thrust through: this is talking about the destruction of America, and also the destruction of those over there calling themselves Jews. Their children also shall be dashed to pieces before their eyes; their houses shall be spoiled: that is what is going to happen over there in that land. - Behold, I will stir up the Medes against them. God says he is going to stir up the Medes and the Persians: that is Iran. Stir them up against whom? Against America and Israel. That is what you see taking place right now. It is so ironic: ancient Babylon was destroyed by the Persians and the Medes, and today the Persians and the Medes are going to play a role in destroying Babylon again. - Which shall not regard silver; and as for gold, they shall not delight in it. The Iranians do not care about your money. You cannot pay them off like you pay off other nations. You killed a man's father, his child, his wife; now you want to bargain with gold? He wants vengeance. And God is behind all of that. - Their bows also shall dash the young men to pieces. Their bows is talking about missiles. News clip read: Iran's missiles are hitting with growing precision, and US officials are questioning how; reports say the increasing accuracy has sparked concerns that hostile actors could be helping Tehran locate and target US military personnel and CIA facilities. - And Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, the beauty of the Chaldees' excellency, shall be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah. How was Sodom and Gomorrah destroyed? With brimstone and fire. Was ancient Babylon destroyed with fire? No, it fell from within. So which Babylon is this talking about? America. And what is it telling you about Iran? Eventually they are going to develop nuclear weapons. The same way God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah with brimstone and fire, it is going to be the same thing with Israel and America. In Closing Brothers and sisters, the time we are living in is the beginning of sorrows and great pain. The Lord has begun to visit the earth that he made, and everything you see taking place is him making preparation to deliver his people. The end is not yet, but the pains are going to increase like a woman in travail. Do not sit down and think everything is going to stay good like it is right now. Watch the signs of the time; get your mind together; stop worrying about the wrong things; keep the commandments, have faith and works so you are preserved from the perils that are coming; make you ready to the battle, and prepare your mind, your spirit, and your house for what is coming. With that, Shalom, Most High and Christ bless; Bishop is coming up next. --- Class Notes Index Transcript: full session

title: NOLAN WELLS: THE PERPETUAL HATRED WE NEVER LEARNED
text: Introduction Today's topic is entitled Nolan Wells: The Perpetual Hatred, We Never Learn. We never learn. Now, today's class is going to be kind of triggering, so I hope you guys have a strong stomach and a strong mind. I was getting mad as I was putting it together; I was getting upset just putting the class together. Real quick, write this down: Wars of the Jews, page 195. All right, let's jump into Genesis chapter 4 and verse one. The opening prayer remembered the families of Rasheem Carter, Kendrick Johnson, Nolan Wells, and Erskin Jenkins, and all those being oppressed. In The News - The Nolan Wells case frames the whole class. As read in class: Nolan Xavier Wells, 2026, an eighteen year old college freshman who disappeared and was later found dead following a July 4th boat trip to Horn Island, Mississippi, with a group of white high school friends. The class set the case beside Zechariah 11:5, whose possessors slay them, and hold themselves not guilty: they kill us and lawyer up. We do not know what happened; get my mom, she is a judge. - A list was read in class of our people found dead after trusting themselves alone among white friends: - Tamla Horsford, 2018: a forty year old mother of five found dead in a backyard after an overnight birthday sleepover in Forsyth County, Georgia, where she was the only black attendee among a group of white friends. - Quawan Charles, 2020: a boy from Louisiana who went missing after leaving his home with a white friend and the friend's mother, and was later found dead in a nearby sugarcane field. - Alonzo Brooks, 2004: a young man who attended a large party with mostly white acquaintances in Kansas and never came home. - Peter Spencer, December 2021: a twenty nine year old Jamaican immigrant invited to a weekend getaway at a cabin in Venango County, Pennsylvania, by a white former coworker; found dead with multiple gunshot wounds, and they called it suicide. - Daniel Irvin, Texas: an eighteen year old honor student and swimmer who went to Lake Ray Hubbard near Dallas with white acquaintances and never returned home. His death was first looked at as an accidental drowning, but police later arrested two individuals for allegedly tampering with evidence, including hiding his clothes and deleting messages. That was in Bishop's class last week; same kid. - That is six people. We don't learn, man. We don't learn. We never learn. Scriptures Opened Genesis 4:1-22 8:15 - Cain already knew from the beginning to offer up sacrifices of animals. In process of time he got tired of doing it and brought fruit instead, being disrespectful to the Lord. Abel maintained his integrity and righteousness and brought the right thing, the firstlings of his flock; and the Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering, but unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect, and Cain's countenance fell. - If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? If you do what I tell you to do, like your brother, will your offering not be acceptable? But if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door: Satan is waiting for you; and unto thee shall be his desire: and Satan shall rule over you. You will become a vessel for the devil. - You would think he got checked and learned. No: Cain rose up against Abel his brother and slew him. When he offered that fruit, Satan already had him; now he confirms it by murdering his brother violently. - The Lord asked, where is Abel thy brother? Testing whether there was any part of Cain left that was righteous. And he said, I know not: am I my brother's keeper? Am I his babysitter? Being more disrespectful. You are going to see am I my brother's keeper in numerous places today, because Cain is back today; Cain and his babies are alive and well today, and Abel's are too. - Now art thou cursed from the earth, which hath opened her mouth to receive thy brother's blood from thy hand: the class taught that the Lord removed that color from him so that he would match the very blood he spilled into that ground. Now you match your brother's blood. - And from thy face shall I be hid: meaning from God's face. God would never again deal with that spirit; he will not hear his prayers, there is no repentance and no salvation for it. That is a perpetual inheritance, to be hid from the eyes of the Lord. - A fugitive and a vagabond shalt thou be in the earth: a fugitive is an outlaw, committing crimes and getting away with them; a vagabond is found in the most unlikely places, in lands that do not belong to him, taking upon himself nationalities and lands that are not his, and leaving destruction behind him. The class applied this line all the way through today's cases: no arrest, no conviction, no consequence. - Video game parallel taught in class: in God of War the main character Kratos, a Spartan, is tricked by the gods into killing his wife and child, and the gods place their ashes upon his skin and turn him white. The class drew the parallel to Cain being made to match the blood he spilled. They put these hints in games here and there. - And Cain went out from the presence of the Lord, and dwelt in the land of Nod, on the east of Eden: write this down; that area is Babylonia. Cain built a city and called it Enoch after his son; it was later known as Unuk. Nimrod came behind him, another class, and built upon the ruins of that city, that tower, and it is the same region today: Iraq, Sumer, Shinar. The older archaeologists came to this understanding; the modern consensus view calls it unfounded, trying to wash away any biblical validation. - Cain did not build a metropolis for one wife and one child. There were many people around at this time, because Adam and Eve had many children, inside and outside of the Garden of Eden. - Cain's line and what it held: Jabal, the father of such as dwell in tents and of such as have cattle: power over resources and produce. Jubal, the father of all such as handle the harp and organ: musical influence, like the record label owners today. Tubal-cain, an instructor of every artificer in brass and iron: weapons, and not regular weapons; high level weaponry. He was an instructor, meaning he taught men how to create weapons of mass destruction in his day, just as his line creates them today. - Power over resources, power over music, and power over weapons. What is that one word? Influence: power and dominance over the world. That is what Cain had back then, and that is what he has today. The righteous at this point were pretty much gone; Abel was dead, and evil began to grow and dominate the earth. - Tubal-cain is reverenced and admired by the Freemasons, who honor builders; there is a masonic hall right here in Philadelphia with the portraits, the hands held a certain way. The teacher also passed on, flagged as possible internet folklore, the claim that the 007 symbol goes back to two balls and a cane. Genesis 25:20-34 23:40 - Isaac entreated the Lord for his wife, because she was barren; the Lord was intreated of him, and Rebekah conceived. And the children struggled together within her: there was a battle, a fight, a conflict in her womb. There were no sonograms back then; she was in pain and went to inquire of the Lord. - Two nations are in thy womb: nations goes back to races. God placed two different kinds of people in her womb. Most of the time a child is the same kind as its parents; the Lord said, no, this is different. He is a Hebrew, yes, but he is not the same as his brother. These are two distinct people. - And two manner of people shall be separated from thy bowels: one will look a certain way, behave a certain way, think a certain way, act a certain way; not the same. The teacher has twins: twins normally share looks, voices, mannerisms. Not these two: different thought process, different look, everything. - The one people shall be stronger than the other people; and the elder shall serve the younger. - And the first came out red, all over like an hairy garment; and they called his name Esau. The first thing Moses records is what the Lord showed him: this child is red, and hairy all over like he was wearing a carpet. Notice Moses never describes Jacob's features: because Jacob looked like his parents, like everybody else on the planet at that time. The class taught this as the nativity of the first Caucasian man, Esau, carrying the appearance that entered with Cain's curse. - And the boys grew: and Esau was a cunning hunter, a man of the field, just like Cain was a tiller of the ground. And Jacob was a plain man, dwelling in tents: he stayed home and tended the cattle. - And Isaac loved Esau, because he did eat of his venison: Esau brought home the best meat, and Isaac favored him. But Rebekah loved Jacob, because the Lord had told her what he did not tell Isaac. - Feed me, I pray thee, with that same red pottage: therefore was his name called Edom, meaning red, because he sought food that matched him. Sometimes a baby comes out pink and the color comes in later; the Lord said, no, he stayed the same: still red, still hairy. - Sell me this day thy birthright. And Esau said, behold, I am at the point to die: and what profit shall this birthright do to me? He was the eldest, the heir of Abraham's inheritance, and he did not care, because he was evil and did not care about God's blessings. He sware unto Jacob and sold it; and when he had eaten, he rose up and went his way: thus Esau despised his birthright. Genesis 27:1-45 30:27 - Isaac was old and his eyes were dim; he asked Esau to take his weapons, hunt venison, and make savory meat, that my soul may bless thee before I die. The father would bless the children before he passed on. Esau sold the birthright, but he figured, I can still bank on the blessing. - Rebekah heard, and commanded Jacob: go fetch me two good kids of the goats, and I will make the savory meat for thy father, such as he loveth, and thou shalt bring it to him, that he may bless thee before his death. - Jacob protested: Esau my brother is a hairy man, and I am a smooth man; my father peradventure will feel me, and I shall seem to him as a deceiver, and I shall bring a curse upon me, and not a blessing. His mother answered, upon me be thy curse, my son: because the Lord already told her while they were yet in the womb, the elder shall serve the younger. If Esau got the blessing, that word could not stand; she was following God's instructions from the beginning. This is all predestination. It was not Jacob's trickery and it was not his plan; the Most High moved her to do it. - She put the skins of the kids of the goats upon his hands and upon the smooth of his neck: because Esau had hairy hands and a hairy neck, which means a hairy back, hairy chest, hairy arms; a hairy man from the womb. And note the texture: goat hair, straight and long, not sheep's wool. The mother knows her son. - The voice is Jacob's voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau: they had different voices. Even twins' voices usually sound alike; not these two. Two manner of people, down to the voice. And he discerned him not, because his hands were hairy, as his brother Esau's hands: so he blessed him. - The blessing itself: God give thee of the dew of heaven: wherever dew falls, and dew falls everywhere; and the fatness of the earth: the best of the earth, the milk, the honey, the crops; and plenty of corn and wine. Let people serve thee, and nations bow down to thee: not be equal to thee; bow down. Be lord over thy brethren, and let thy mother's sons bow down to thee: Esau's children serving Jacob's. Cursed be every one that curseth thee, and blessed be he that blesseth thee. - Jacob was yet scarce gone out from the presence of Isaac, and Esau came in from his hunting. Look at God. And Isaac trembled very exceedingly: who? where is he that hath taken venison? I have blessed him: yea, and he shall be blessed. It could not be undone. - Esau cried with a great and exceeding bitter cry. Is not he rightly named Jacob? for he hath supplanted me these two times. Did Jacob supplant him twice? No. He supplanted him once; Esau sold the birthright himself and despised it, but he told his father a pity story: he took away my birthright. No, he did not; he sold it. - Isaac's answer to Esau: behold, thy dwelling shall be the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above: the same agriculture repeated. And by thy sword shalt thou live: how would he acquire it? By the sword. That is not from God; that goes back to what the Lord told Cain: from thy face shall I be hid. Isaac handed him back the same inheritance from Genesis 4: the power to destroy and to make weapons. - And thou shalt serve thy brother; and it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck: because our people went into sin, Israel was conquered and overthrown, and that is what gave Esau the chance to come out from under dominion and build up his power. And we have served him since: the Greeks, the Romans, the Spanish, the French, the Dutch, the Germans, the Israelis. - And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing, and Esau said in his heart, the days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Jacob. He said it internally, in his mind, and the scripture says those words were told to Rebekah: God was talking to Rebekah; the Lord was dealing with her on a high level. - Flee thou to Laban my brother to Haran, and tarry with him a few days, until thy brother's fury turn away. And Esau's anger did turn away; but his children's did not. That hatred he had for Jacob remained dormant in him, and he passed it on to his children. That is the perpetual hatred of today's title. Exodus 17:8-16 49:43 - Then came Amalek, and fought with Israel in Rephidim: Amalek is the children of Esau, the dukes, the elite of Esau's line. The battle continues into the next generation. - Moses stood on the top of the hill with the rod of God in his hand: when Moses held up his hand, Israel prevailed; when he let down his hand, Amalek prevailed. His hands were heavy, so they set a stone under him, and Aaron and Hur stayed up his hands, the one on the one side and the other on the other side, steady until the going down of the sun; and Joshua discomfited Amalek and his people with the edge of the sword. - Write this for a memorial in a book, and rehearse it in the ears of Joshua: for I will utterly put out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven. - Because the Lord hath sworn that the Lord will have war with Amalek from generation to generation: meaning for ever. It is the same thing Malachi said; we read Malachi 1 all the time, but this is in the law. God will war with Esau for ever, through us, and eventually himself when Christ returns. Deuteronomy 23:7 52:34 - Thou shalt not abhor an Edomite; for he is thy brother: thou shalt not abhor an Egyptian; because thou wast a stranger in his land. The apologists love to pull this verse on us, and it is actually in our favor: if you pull it, you are agreeing about who Esau is. - Why does the Lord speak of the Edomite and the Egyptian in the same breath? The Egyptians were our oppressors. Moses saw the beginning of time, the middle, and the end; he saw who was going to be our Egypt in this time and what they did to us back in Exodus. He is saying, do not carry hatred, because you are going to end up serving under them; if it be possible, be at peace with all men. That is the instruction, not amnesia. Deuteronomy 25:17-19 53:44 - Remember what Amalek did unto thee by the way: God does not forget, and God said remember. Exodus 17 gives the battle; here he gives the detail of how they attacked us. - How he met thee by the way, and smote the hindmost of thee, even all that were feeble behind thee, when thou wast faint and weary: in a caravan the strong men walk in the front. Who is in the back? The elderly, the women, the babies, the lame. Rather than attack head on, Amalek crept up and attacked from behind, killing the feeble, and waited until we were tired to do it. And he feared not God: they knew exactly who we were; those are our cousins. - When the Lord thy God hath given thee rest in the land, thou shalt blot out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven; thou shalt not forget it. God said do not forget what they did to you. God does not forget; we do. Christianity trains our people to be very forgetful, willfully. - Picture shown in class: at the trial of Botham Jean's killer, the judge embracing her, his own brother coming behind to hug her, and a court officer combing her hair. God said do not forget. Numbers 24:20 56:58 - When he looked on Amalek, he took up his parable, and said, Amalek was the first of the nations: the first nation Israel had to war with when we came out of Egypt. - But his latter end shall be that he perish for ever: the Lord wars with him from generation to generation, and his end is to be destroyed out of existence for ever. 1 Samuel 15:1-9, 32-33 57:44 - This is generations later. Moses is dead and gone; Israel is in the land. And the Lord of hosts says, I remember that which Amalek did to Israel, how he laid wait for him in the way, when he came up from Egypt. The Lord still remembers the sneak attack from Exodus. - Now go and smite Amalek, and utterly destroy all that they have, and spare them not. You may ask, but this is not the same generation that attacked them. That is the argument you hear today: that was not me; I never held anyone in slavery. But the Lord said destroy them for what their forefathers did in Exodus. The nations pay for the sins of their fathers, the same way we are paying for the sins of ours: our fathers refused God's commandments, the curses fell on them and their seed, and here we are generations of oppression later. We do not get a pass, so nobody else gets a pass either. - Slay both man and woman, infant and suckling, ox and sheep, camel and ass: because they did the same to us when they smote the hindmost, the feeble, the young and the old. - Saul gathered two hundred thousand footmen and ten thousand men of Judah. He told the Kenites, get you down from among the Amalekites, lest I destroy you with them: for ye shewed kindness to all the children of Israel when they came up out of Egypt. You did right by us; move away from them. - But Saul and the people spared Agag, the king of the Amalekites, and the best of the sheep and the oxen, being presumptuous and covetous; and every thing that was vile and refuse, that they destroyed utterly. He kept the tough one, their king, alive. - Then said Samuel, bring ye hither to me Agag. And Agag came unto him delicately, and said, surely the bitterness of death is past. And Samuel said, as thy sword hath made women childless, so shall thy mother be childless among women. And Samuel hewed Agag in pieces before the Lord in Gilgal. Samuel followed instructions; Saul played games. Remember Agag; he comes back up in this class. Esther 2:5-23 1:03:49 - Now in Shushan the palace there was a certain Jew, whose name was Mordecai, the son of Jair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish, a Benjamite: Mordecai and Esther were of the tribe of Benjamin. Precepts: - 1 Samuel 9:1-2 There was a man of Benjamin, whose name was Kish, a mighty man of power; and he had a son, whose name was Saul. So Saul and Mordecai come out of the same line. This was not a regular line; this was a mighty Benjamite line. Keep that in mind for what follows. - Esther was the daughter of Mordecai's uncle: they were cousins, not uncle and niece; do not say that. Her parents died, and Mordecai took her for his own daughter and raised her up. - Esther had not shewed her people nor her kindred: for Mordecai had charged her that she should not shew it. Do not tell anyone that you are an Israelite. The Persians are a dark people themselves, and from Esther's look you could not tell what she was; she could pass, and she kept the commandment of Mordecai, like as when she was brought up with him. - Two of the king's chamberlains, of those which kept the door, were wroth, and sought to lay hand on the king Ahasuerus. And the thing was known to Mordecai, who told it unto Esther the queen; and Esther certified the king thereof in Mordecai's name. Inquisition was made; both were hanged on a tree; and it was written in the book of the chronicles before the king. Mordecai saved the king's life, and it went on record. Esther 3:1-6 1:08:04 - After these things did king Ahasuerus promote Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite. Sound familiar? This is a descendant of the same Agag that Samuel hewed in pieces. Haman is an Amalekite, an Edomite, and the king set his seat above all the princes: the right hand of the king over Persia. - All the king's servants bowed and reverenced Haman, for the king had so commanded; but Mordecai bowed not, nor did him reverence. It is not our custom to bow to any man. - They spake daily unto him, and he hearkened not; and they told Haman, to see whether Mordecai's matters would stand: for he had told them that he was a Jew. And when Haman saw that Mordecai bowed not, Haman was full of wrath. - And he thought scorn to lay hands on Mordecai alone: Haman sought to destroy all the Jews that were throughout the whole kingdom of Ahasuerus, for what one Jew would not do. Why all of them? Remember what king Saul was sent to do to Amalek. Haman's people kept the records; he knew Mordecai's line, the line of Kish, was the line sent to destroy his forefathers. Esau forgave Jacob, but his children hold the grudge from generation to generation. They do not forget; we do. 1 Samuel 15:32-33 1:12:12 - The scriptures say the things that were written aforetime were written for our learning. Esau does not forget, but we do. Why? Because we are not tapped into the scriptures. - Agag was not supposed to be kept alive in the first place. King Saul trusted the enemy; Samuel did not. Agag came unto him delicately, crouching and speaking softly, and Samuel still carried out the word of the Lord. Precepts: - Ecclesiasticus 12:10-11 This is the wisdom Samuel applied, and the wisdom we have to learn to apply. Never trust thine enemy: for like as iron rusteth, so is his wickedness. Though he humble himself and go crouching: is that not exactly what Agag did, coming delicately? Yet take good heed and beware of him; thou shalt know that his rust hath not been altogether wiped away. When we apply what the scriptures show us, we learn that our enemies have been the same from day one, and they are not going to change. Esther 13:3-5 (Additions to Esther) 1:14:33 - This is the decree written against the Jews in the king's name. Aman, that excelled in wisdom among us, and was approved for his constant good will and steadfast fidelity, and had the honour of the second place in the kingdom: that is Haman. - Declared unto us, that in all nations throughout the world there was scattered a certain malicious people, that had laws contrary to all nations, and continually despised the commandments of kings: there is Haman slandering us, the same slander used on us today: they are malicious, they are violent, they are a problem. - So as the uniting of our kingdoms cannot go forward: Haman was a Macedonian Edomite in Persia, saying the kingdoms cannot unite as long as these Jews are around, this people alone, continually in opposition unto all men, working all the mischief they can that our kingdom may not be firmly established. The accuser's argument has not changed in all these ages. Psalms 50:16-22 1:17:07 - But unto the wicked God saith, what hast thou to do to declare my statutes, or that thou shouldest take my covenant in thy mouth? seeing thou hatest instruction, and castest my words behind thee. This whole passage is God speaking to the wicked. - When thou sawest a thief, then thou consentedst with him: when Columbus went out, the European nations all gave consent: go conquer, colonize, take. The Berlin Conference carved Africa up in pieces: you take your piece, I take my piece. They all got together and stole together. And hast been partaker with adulterers. - Thou givest thy mouth to evil, and thy tongue frameth deceit: by law, through the judicial system, through the legislatures, through executive orders. - Thou sittest and speakest against thy brother; thou slanderest thine own mother's son: this is Esau and Jacob, Cain and Abel. They sit and slander us as the violent ones and the criminals. The class answered the slander with the record: most white murder victims die at the hands of other white people; and count the nuclear bombs dropped, the peoples and animals driven to extinction, Black Wall Street bombed, Rosewood burned down, Gaza bombed. The slander does not match the record. - Video answered in class: a commentator dismissed reparations, claiming white taxpayer dollars already fund EBT, DEI, and scholarships. The guest answered with numbers: white women are the main beneficiaries of DEI programs; over sixty percent of SNAP beneficiaries are white; over fifty percent of tax fraud is committed by whites; over eighty percent of tax cuts go to white families and about one percent to black families. That is thou sittest and speakest against thy brother; the class added that welfare programs stay in place because they are heavily used by the very people who slander us over them. - These things hast thou done, and I kept silence: God allowed it, because we are in sin. Thou thoughtest that I was altogether such an one as thyself: because God sat back and allowed this man to conquer the earth by blood and warfare, he concludes that God is with him, that God looks like him, that Christ and the angels look like him, that everything good and divine is him. No. But I will reprove thee, and set them in order before thine eyes: and you are watching that order being set now. - Now consider this, ye that forget God, lest I tear you in pieces, and there be none to deliver. 1 John 3:10-12 1:21:06 - In this the children of God are manifest, and the children of the devil: the devil has children. That was Cain's children back then, and it is Esau's children today. Whosoever doeth not righteousness is not of God, neither he that loveth not his brother: did Cain love his brother? Does Esau? - For this is the message that ye heard from the beginning, that we should love one another. Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother. And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother's righteous. John 8:44 1:22:33 - Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do. Christ said this to leaders of his own people, the Pharisees who were in bed with Rome, in allegiance to Rome; the class taught that the same spirit rides on those of our people today who defend the oppressor against their own. - He was a murderer from the beginning: who was a murderer from the beginning? Cain. John said he was of that wicked one; Christ calls him the devil. - And abode not in the truth, because there is no truth in him: in process of time Cain stopped abiding in the truth with his offering; Esau did the same. Isaac taught Esau the laws and the commandments, and he cast them off. Wisdom of Solomon 10:1-3 1:24:42 - Wisdom preserved the first formed father of the world, that was created alone: Adam; and brought him out of his fall, and gave him power to rule all things. - But when the unrighteous went away from her in his anger, he perished also in the fury wherewith he murdered his brother: Cain went away from wisdom, and he was killed the same violent way that he killed Abel. Live by the sword, die by the sword. Amos 1:11 1:29:34 - Thus saith the Lord; for three transgressions of Edom, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because he did pursue his brother with the sword, and did cast off all pity. - And his anger did tear perpetually, and he kept his wrath for ever: the anger Esau had for Jacob back then passed on into his children. The hatred is generational; it remained, and it does not change. This is the perpetual hatred of the class title. - The class contrasted the footage we all keep seeing: unarmed brothers shot again and again, a man pinned down and shot in the face while an officer was calling for a taser, a seven year old boy shot dozens of times; set against armed white suspects wrestled down, talked down, taken alive. Two manner of people, as Genesis 25 said. Ezekiel 35:1-5 1:31:47 - Son of man, set thy face against mount Seir: Seir is Edom. Behold, O mount Seir, I am against thee; I will make thee most desolate; I will lay thy cities waste; and thou shalt know that I am the Lord. - Because thou hast had a perpetual hatred: the same word Amos used; Amos says his anger did tear perpetually, Ezekiel says a perpetual hatred. And hast shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword in the time of their calamity, in the time that their iniquity had an end: brought to modern time, the time our iniquity had an end points to the so-called emancipation. So what continued after it had an end? The class then read the record: - James Byrd Jr., 1998, Jasper, Texas: forty nine years old, walking home late at night, he accepted a ride from three white men in a pickup truck. They beat him, chained him by the ankles to the truck with a logging chain, and dragged him three miles along the asphalt; he was conscious for most of it, until he hit a culvert; they kept driving another mile and a half and dumped what was left in front of a black cemetery. The killers were white supremacists with Klan and Nazi tattoos who bragged about it afterward; two were sentenced to death and executed, and the driver's first parole eligibility is 2038. A modern lynching. Their hatred did tear perpetually. - Thomas Thistlewood, read in class: an Englishman who came to Savanna la Mar, Jamaica, in 1750 as a plantation overseer and later bought his own plantation. He kept a meticulous diary of ten to fourteen thousand pages documenting over thirty eight hundred rapes of over one hundred thirty eight enslaved women, branding, public whippings, starvation, a severed head kept on a pole, and the torture he named Derby's dose. He documented his own atrocities for over thirty six years until he died in 1786. - Mary Turner, May 1918, Valdosta, Georgia: after a plantation owner known for abusing his black workers was shot, white mobs began lynching black men without evidence; one was Hayes Turner. His wife Mary, twenty one years old and eight months pregnant, said publicly that she would press charges; the newspapers said she made unwise remarks. On May 19, 1918 the mob hung her upside down from a tree, set her on fire, cut her open so that her unborn child fell to the ground and was stomped to death, and shot her body dozens of times. Not one person was arrested or named; Georgia did not acknowledge her murder until a historical marker in 2008, ninety years later, and that marker has been shot at, vandalized, and torn down. - A fugitive and a vagabond in the earth: no one arrested, no one served time. That is Cain all over again; that is what the class means by we never learn who we are dealing with. Obadiah 1:1-10 1:43:51 - The vision of Obadiah. Thus saith the Lord God concerning Edom: behold, I have made thee small among the heathen: thou art greatly despised. The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee, thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock: that saith in his heart, who shall bring me down to the ground? - Though thou exalt thyself as the eagle: Edom's nations take the eagle for their symbol: Rome, Greece, Spain, France, Britain, Russia, America; a violent bird of prey that they themselves nearly killed off. And though thou set thy nest among the stars: he landed in space; the eagle has landed; now the space programs, the space force, the satellites. - Thence will I bring thee down, saith the Lord: once you reach that height, the bringing down begins. America is now officially two hundred fifty years old, inside its age of decadence, unraveling. - If thieves came to thee, would they not have stolen till they had enough? if the grapegatherers came, would they not leave some grapes? How are the things of Esau searched out! A thief takes enough and leaves; Esau takes everything: the house, the people inside the house, the land, the race, and the identity. - All the men of thy confederacy have brought thee even to the border: the men that were at peace with thee have deceived thee, and prevailed against thee. That is happening right now; eventually his own confederacy turns on him, as it did in the world wars. - Shall I not in that day destroy the wise men out of Edom, and understanding out of the mount of Esau? to the end that every one of the mount of Esau may be cut off by slaughter. For thy violence against thy brother Jacob shame shall cover thee, and thou shalt be cut off for ever. The judgment is written, and the charge on it is the violence against Jacob. 1 Peter 5:8 1:47:30 - Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour. The Bible speaks of the adversary as a lion; hold on to that image for the next scriptures. 2 Timothy 4:17 1:48:08 - Notwithstanding the Lord stood with me, and strengthened me; that by me the preaching might be fully known, and that all the Gentiles might hear: all of us scattered abroad. And I was delivered out of the mouth of the lion. - Many Bibles carry the margin note on this verse: the lion is Caesar Nero. Commentary read in class: scholars take the lion of 2 Timothy 4:17 as Nero and the Roman authorities who held the power of life and death, or as Satan, echoing 1 Peter 5:8. The class taught it is the same picture: Paul called the Roman power the lion, and the scriptures call the lion the devil. Psalms 22:20-21 1:50:10 - Deliver my soul from the sword; my darling from the power of the dog: the dog is the wicked elders of our own people. Save me from the lion's mouth: this is Christ on the cross. On that cross Christ is in the lion's mouth: the Roman, Edomite authority, with the evil ones of our own people who were in bed with that authority. Revelation 12:3-10 1:51:09 - And behold a great red dragon: why red? This red dragon is Edom, going back to Genesis 25 and Esau who came out red. Seven heads: the succession of European powers; ten horns: the ten common markets that made up the original European Union; seven crowns: each head gained power and authority on the earth at its point in time. - And there was war in heaven: Michael and his angels fought against the dragon; and the dragon fought and his angels, and prevailed not; neither was their place found any more in heaven. As the law says, the Lord has war with Amalek from generation to generation; the dragon's place is lost, and the European power structure will be destroyed. - And the great dragon was cast out, that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan, which deceiveth the whole world: the serpent that deceived the woman, and the murderer from the beginning of John 8:44. The class taught the two lines side by side, as 1 John 3:10 puts it: the children of God are manifest, and the children of the devil. - The captivity loop taught in class: the first captivity, Babylon, carried the lion as its symbol; Paul calls the Roman power the lion; and the lion is called the devil. We were in the hands of the lion in Babylon, and we are in the hands of the lion now. Judgment is a loop. - Now is come salvation, and strength, and the kingdom of our God, and the power of his Christ: for the accuser of our brethren is cast down, which accused them before our God day and night. The accuser goes right back to Psalms 50: thou slanderest thine own mother's son. They are violent; they are on welfare; they are criminals: the same accusation in every generation. - Am I my brother's keeper comes back around here: give them drugs, give them guns, and then blame them for it. They ask why we are violent: who made the guns, and how did they get there? They call us addicts: how did the drugs get there? They call us poor: who made us poor? Any people placed under our conditions do the same things; the studies have been done. - The class taught the accuser's aim: God did not choose Esau, he chose Jacob; so the adversary labors to make Jacob behave like him, believing that if Jacob falls he can stand up in Jacob's place. If you cannot beat them, become them: destroy you, and become you. Jeremiah 50:7 1:55:52 - All that found them have devoured them: all that found us in our sin devoured us. And their adversaries said, we offend not: and that is not only Edom; that is all the nations that partook, the Arabs too. - Because they have sinned against the Lord, the habitation of justice, even the Lord, the hope of their fathers: the nations excuse themselves with our sin: they went against their own God, so we are not wrong. They set the conditions, and then they point at the results. Zechariah 11:5 1:57:47 - Whose possessors slay them, and hold themselves not guilty: they kill us and lawyer up. Nolan Wells: we do not know what happened to him; get my mom, she is a judge. This verse is the Nolan Wells case in one line. - And they that sell them say, blessed be the Lord; for I am rich: every seller blesses his own god off of our destruction. - And their own shepherds pity them not: our own shepherds in allegiance with the powers make their living defending the system against their own people. The class named the media personalities who do this for a career; the scripture already described them. Revelation 13:1-2 1:59:00 - And I stood upon the sand of the sea, and saw a beast rise up out of the sea, having seven heads and ten horns: the same dragon system from chapter 12, with crowns now on the horns, and upon his heads the name of blasphemy. - The beast was like unto a leopard: it took on the Greek doctrine, democracy, born in Greece; his feet were as the feet of a bear: Persia; and his mouth as the mouth of a lion: Babylon, and back to the devil again. This last empire incorporates all the ancient empires before it to strengthen itself; America became this powerful in only two hundred fifty years. - And the dragon gave him his power, and his seat, and great authority: that is the source of the dominance. Not intelligence, not IQ: the dragon gave him his power, and he lives by the sword, exactly as the blessing of Genesis 27 said: the fatness of the earth, obtained by the sword. Ecclesiasticus 12:10-11 2:01:11 - Never trust thine enemy: for like as iron rusteth, so is his wickedness. As he was in the beginning, so is he now; he hides the rust for a season, but rust always comes back up through the surface, in any sword, over time. - James Byrd made that mistake and trusted a truck full of white men. Nolan Wells trusted a boat full of white high school friends. The list read in class, from Tamla Horsford to Peter Spencer to Daniel Irvin, is what this verse looks like when it is ignored. The scriptures already gave us the wisdom; the class charge is that we never learn it. - Book read in class, Columbus's journal remarks: in his October 14, 1492 entry Columbus wrote that the indigenous people he encountered lacked modern weapons and could easily be subjugated; they did not bear arms, were unfamiliar with them, cutting themselves on swords out of ignorance, and had no iron. He famously wrote that with fifty men they could all be subjugated and made to do what is required of them: which is what? Slavery. That was his first calculation on arrival. - Book read in class, The Conquest of America (page 22): the interpretation of nature's signs as practiced by Columbus is determined by the result that must be arrived at. He does not discover America; he finds it where he knew it would be. And how did he know? He had read Toscanelli, and the prophecies of Esdras: 2 Esdras places the ten tribes across the water. He knew exactly who he was going to find here, and he came to enslave them. - Book read in class, Sails of Hope: to what extent Columbus hoped that Jewish people would be found there was a concern he locked away in the innermost recesses of his soul; but among his contemporaries the belief was slow to die, and the first voyagers and colonists looked for whatever signs might link the Indians with the ten lost tribes of Israel. When the Spaniards conquered Peru they were again disposed to look for evidence that the Peruvians were of Jewish origin. In 1607 Gregorio Garcia expressed the view that the first inhabitants of the Americas had been Jewish; in 1650 the same opinion was put forward in England; Menasseh Ben Israel, the Portuguese rabbi who persuaded Cromwell to readmit the Jews to England, shared the conviction; and Montezinos, under the name Aaron Levi, reported that in South America he had associated with Jews of the ten tribes of Israel. Scholars noted the parallels between the Indians and the ancient Hebrews: belief in a life after death, the organization of the priesthood, prophecies and dream interpretation, religious sacrifices, and the appointment of a day of rest, a Sabbath. - Also from the reading: the greatest auto da fe in the new world was staged in Lima, Peru, on January 23, 1639: they burned people alive under the Inquisition. The Indians were regarded as subhuman; they were held to have no property rights at all; their land, their possessions, and their women belonged to the Spanish conquerors; and new instruments of torture unknown in Spain were devised and tried out on the Indians. If they proved refractory, they were slaughtered. - Columbus owned the travels of Marco Polo and had read it with great care, and he studied Esdras; Vasco da Gama sailed around the Cape of Good Hope to India; both were familiar with the reports about Jews in India. Wherever the Israelites are found, the wealth is found: remember the blessing, the dew of heaven and the fatness of the earth. - Luis de Torres: Columbus's interpreter spoke Aramaic, Arabic, Chaldee, and Hebrew, and Columbus sent him with Rodrigo de Xeres on shore to communicate with the natives; so after the landfall in America, the first words addressed to the natives were words of Hebrew. Ask yourself why you bring a Hebrew speaker to meet the people you claim you think are in India. Ezekiel 35:5-11 2:17:10 - Therefore, as I live, saith the Lord God, I will prepare thee unto blood, and blood shall pursue thee: sith thou hast not hated blood, even blood shall pursue thee. I will kill you the way you killed others. I will make thee perpetual desolations, and thy cities shall not return: perpetual hatred answered with perpetual desolation. - Because thou hast said, these two nations and these two countries shall be mine, and we will possess it; whereas the Lord was there. In the old time that was Judah and Samaria; brought forward, it is the land of Israel and the Americas: I will be a Jew in Israel and a Christian in America, possessing the people and the lands where the Lord's people are. The class connected this to Columbus, to the Balfour Declaration, and to the edicts Dum Diversas and Inter Caetera issued under Rodrigo Borgia for the crown, authorizing the enslavement of the peoples on this side of the world. - I will even do according to thine anger, and according to thine envy which thou hast used out of thy hatred against them. Where is the envy from? God did not choose them. The hatred runs from Cain and Abel all the way to now; and what God hath made crooked, no man can make straight. - Book read in class, Wars of the Jews (page 195): Queen Kahina, an Israelite queen, was resisting the Arab conquest of Africa; the historians write that the Muslims would have it, largely due to the peculiar Jewish weakness of compassion for the enemy. The historians themselves call our compassion for the enemy a peculiar Jewish weakness. Compassion without remembrance is how we keep being destroyed; that is what happened with James Byrd, and that is what happened with Nolan Wells: our people keep turning a blind eye to evil and extending trust where the scriptures say beware. - Video read in class, Sam Hose, 1899, Newnan, Georgia: the local newspaper announced the lynching in advance, and special trains from Atlanta offered discounted tickets. Two thousand white men, women, and children watched as his ears and fingers were cut off one by one and he was burned alive, and afterward pieces of his bones and organs were sold as souvenirs. Between 1877 and 1950 over four thousand black people were lynched in America, most as advertised public spectacles printed into postcards and mailed with notes. In 1916, fifteen thousand people gathered in Waco, Texas, to watch seventeen year old Jesse Washington burned alive, with the mayor and the chief of police present. A federal anti lynching bill failed some two hundred times between 1882 and 1968; the Emmett Till Antilynching Act was finally signed on March 29, 2022; and not one person was ever prosecuted for a lynching. Not one. Matthew 11:12 2:24:43 - From the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force. The kingdom of heaven here is the children of Israel; we are the kingdom of heaven. The violent at that time were the Romans, and the violent have taken the kingdom by force. Psalms 140:1-4 2:25:21 - Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man: preserve me from the violent man. The Bible calls him the evil man, the violent man, the wicked: that is Edom. - Which imagine mischiefs in their heart: to destroy, to take over lands and identities; continually are they gathered together for war. - They have sharpened their tongues like a serpent; adders' poison is under their lips: propaganda, lies, whitewashed history, old books destroyed, false doctrines poured out. - Preserve me from the violent man, who have purposed to overthrow my goings: the same violence Christ described in Matthew 11:12. Matthew 22:7 2:26:28 - But when the king heard thereof, he was wroth: and he sent forth his armies, and destroyed those murderers, and burned up their city. The king sent the Roman armies against the wicked elders of our people who had Christ killed, and burned up their city: that is 70 AD. Luke 21:20-24 2:26:59 - And when ye shall see Jerusalem compassed with armies, then know that the desolation thereof is nigh. Then let them which are in Judaea flee to the mountains: flee further into Africa for safety; let them which are in the midst of it depart out; and let not them that are in the countries enter thereinto. - For these be the days of vengeance, that all things which are written may be fulfilled. - And they shall fall by the edge of the sword: the sword of the violent man, the Romans; and shall be led away captive into all nations: and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled. Our land is now walked upon by imposters until their time in that land is up, and we are slowly approaching that time now, all thanks to America and Israel's alliance. - Image shown in class, the destroyed black towns and districts: Tulsa and the Osage country in Oklahoma, an hour apart, conquered like the northern and southern kingdoms at the same time; Wilmington, Atlanta, Rosewood, Elaine, Slocum, Colfax, Opelousas, Thibodaux, New Orleans, St. Bernard Parish, Vicksburg, Seneca Falls, Black Bottom in Detroit, and more; and that is a fraction of the list. The Pentagon itself was built on a former black town called Queen City. This is domestic terrorism built upon hatred and murder, and when they could not call it what it was, they renamed the massacres riots. 2 Esdras 11:40-46 2:29:36 - The fourth came, and overcame all the beasts that were past, and held the world with great fearfulness, and over the whole compass of the earth with much wicked oppression. Under the Greeks and Romans it was the old world; as Spain, Portugal, France, and Britain he gained dominion over the fourth part of the earth, the Americas: the whole compass of the earth. - For the earth hast thou not judged with truth: lies and corruption. Thou hast afflicted the meek, thou hast hurt the peaceable: the peaceable are the Native Americans, who meant him no harm; the same peaceable people Columbus reckoned fifty men could subjugate. Thou hast loved liars, going back to Psalms 50; and destroyed the dwellings of them that brought forth fruit, and hast cast down the walls of such as did thee no harm: the walls of Jerusalem, 70 AD. - Therefore is thy wrongful dealing come up unto the Highest, and thy pride unto the Mighty. The Highest also hath looked upon the proud times: the injustices, the massacres renamed riots, the lynchings; and behold, they are ended, and his abominations are fulfilled. Your time is up; the times of the Gentiles are being fulfilled. - And therefore appear no more, thou eagle: the same eagle from Obadiah that exalted itself and set its nest among the stars. Nor thy horrible wings: his kind; nor thy wicked feathers: the European powers; nor thy malicious heads: the leaders; nor thy hurtful claws: the military; nor all thy vain body. - That all the earth may be refreshed, and may return, being delivered from thy violence, and that she may hope for the judgment and mercy of him that made her. And with that the class closed: twelve tribes. Announcements & References Opening reading at the trumpets: Psalms 149, the high praises of God in their mouth, and a twoedged sword in their hand, to execute vengeance upon the heathen; the opening prayer lifted up the families of Rasheem Carter, Kendrick Johnson, Nolan Wells, and Erskin Jenkins. Books and materials read in class: - Wars of the Jews, page 195 (Queen Kahina and the peculiar Jewish weakness of compassion for the enemy); the teacher opened the class saying to write this reference down - Christopher Columbus's journal, the October 14, 1492 entry (fifty men could subjugate them all) - The Conquest of America, page 22 (Columbus does not discover America; he finds it where he knew it would be, having read the prophecies of Esdras) - Sails of Hope (Columbus, Luis de Torres, the Inquisition in the new world, and the accounts linking the Indians with the ten lost tribes of Israel) - Videos: the reparations exchange answered with the record; the atrocity records of James Byrd Jr., Thomas Thistlewood, Mary Turner, Sam Hose, and Jesse Washington; the list of black deaths among white friends, including Nolan Wells; the image of the destroyed black towns --- Class Notes Index Transcript: full session

title: THIS WOMAN'S WORK
text: Introduction Sabbath class from Captain Yadain with IUIC Birmingham, Alabama, fresh off the trip to Birmingham, UK. The class is titled This Woman's Work. A couple weeks ago the class dealt with marriage issues from the other side of the room, the things the woman has to fix about herself, and the men were all happy. Now it gets switched up. With the Marriage on the Roll event about to take place in LA, this class gives the other perspective. The title comes from the song This Woman's Work, recorded in 1988 by Kate Bush and featured in the movie She's Having a Baby; most of us know it from Maxwell and from Love & Basketball. Most people never heard the words. When you read the lyrics, it is a husband whose wife is in a life-threatening childbirth, and he is dealing with fear, helplessness, guilt, and regret: thinking about the things he should have done with his wife and how he took her for granted. Disclaimer from the start: this class is not for the wicked sisters, the ones that do not clean, do not cook, are disrespectful, and are not taking care of their wifely duties. This class is about the righteous wives, the virtuous wives that do what they are supposed to do. Scriptures Opened Ecclesiasticus 25:19-24 12:34 - A little heat from the beginning, so the wicked sisters do not feel like they got a W this Sabbath. All wickedness is but little to the wickedness of a woman. As the climbing up a sandy way is to the feet of the aged, so is a wife full of words to a quiet man. If you are that type of wife, this class is not talking about you; you can listen, but this is not for you. - A wicked woman abateth the courage, maketh an heavy countenance and a wounded heart. A woman that will not comfort her husband in distress maketh weak hands and feeble knees. Of the woman came the beginning of sin, and through her we all die. Genesis 1:28 15:50 - Having kids is God's plan. You get married young, the first thing you want to do is have kids. God blessed them and said be fruitful and multiply. That is what a husband and a wife do when you go into the scriptures. Psalms 127:3-5 16:24 - Children are an heritage of the Lord, and the fruit of the womb is his reward. Happy is the man that hath his quiver full of them, meaning a man that has a lot of kids is happy. - In the world, having a lot of kids is looked at as a bad thing when it comes to us, but then you have shows with 14 or 15 kids and everybody hyping them up. In our community we get looked at bad if we have a lot of kids. The reason is they do not want us to multiply. Read Exodus 1: when the children of Israel multiplied, they understood that when there is more of us, we have more power. So they make having a lot of kids look negative when it comes to the Israelites, the Hispanics, the northern kingdom. The nations do not want that. Psalms 128:3-4 17:45 - Thy wife shall be as a fruitful vine by the sides of thine house, meaning bring forth a lot of kids; thy children like olive plants round about thy table. Behold, that thus shall the man be blessed that feareth the Lord. You fear the Lord, you are going to be blessed with a lot of kids. Proverbs 17:6 18:17 - Children's children are the crown of old men, and the glory of children are their fathers. Ecclesiasticus 30:6 19:08 - He left behind him an avenger against his enemies. When you get older and pass on, the mind of a man is to leave behind an avenger: a kid that finishes fighting the war we were already fighting, that goes out there and wakes up our people and teaches our people who we are according to the scriptures. - We saw that in South Africa: young men out there teaching like young lions, young prophets bringing out the word. That is a crown to a man. Deuteronomy 28:15 20:14 - Even though children are blessings for us, we always have to consider that we are under the curses. If thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God to observe to do all his commandments, all these curses shall come upon thee and overtake thee. Genesis 3:16 20:42 - Unto the woman he said, I will greatly multiply thy sorrow and thy conception; in sorrow thou shalt bring forth children. That is one of the curses women deal with when they go into having children. Jeremiah 4:31 21:15 - Throughout the scriptures, any kind of trouble or travail is usually compared to a woman giving birth: a voice of a woman in travail, the anguish as of her that bringeth forth her first child, the daughter of Zion saying woe is me now. - We know the labor pains women go through, the contractions that come and go and come back stronger and stronger. They say when women have kids, that is the closest they ever get to passing away. And we know that under the curses, the mortality rate of Israelite women when it comes to having a baby is a lot higher than any other nation. - The class is really not about childbirth; that was brought out to use the song. The deeper meaning is what that man is saying when he sings it: a husband dealing with emotions. Whenever we talk about emotions we always talk about the women's side of the room, but men in leadership know it is the men's side that is very emotional. Brothers get corrected and do not know how to deal with it: they leave, they stop talking, they sit in the back of the classroom, they get attitude. We talk about women murmuring, but there is maybe more murmuring on the men's side than the women's side. The difference is that men were never taught how to handle their emotions. Psalms 32:3-4 24:28 - When I kept silence, my bones waxed old through my roaring all the day long. That is what happens with a lot of men: when they are dealing with stuff, they keep silence. Men may come for counsel on how to study better or break down scriptures, but the classes we really need, dealing with what goes on inside our households, our families, our personal lives, we do not really like those classes. Those are the best classes; that is what we need to build ourselves up as a nation. - Movies show it: Fences with Denzel Washington, a man not knowing how to deal with his emotions, so he takes it out on his wife and his son. Antwone Fisher, a young man not knowing how to deal with his past. - Day and night thy hand was heavy upon me. This is really dealing with holding your sin in, but a lot of times we hold our emotions in too. Then you start dealing with regret: what if, why didn't I. You think about how you treat your wife. In that song the brother is thinking about his wife not making it, and hindsight is 20/20. - Neglect is part of it. Some of you brothers do not take your wives anywhere but the bedroom, the kitchen, and the school. And some wives in this truth sit at home feeling like slaves. It is not supposed to be like that. - You also start to understand the weight that a righteous wife has to carry. She deals with the kids and the bringing forth of the kids. The leadership wives are expected to go fix the problems on the women's side, where sisters hold grudges and will not talk to each other. She has to order her house right. And she has to deal with you: your problems, your issues, the trauma you dump on her. Then you reflect and realize, she deals with all that, and I do not take her anywhere; I make her walk on eggshells in the household. Ecclesiasticus 26:13-17 29:23 - The grace of a wife delighteth her husband. No matter what, you have financial issues, he cannot find a job, the car broke, the insurance lapsed, everything happens in threes: a good wife still delights her husband. That is the job of a wife, to make her husband happy. - A silent and loving woman is a gift of the Lord. Every husband has at least five things he has been supposed to do for a month or a year, the honey-do projects, the picture never hung, the raised garden bed. A righteous wife knows that whining over and over is what the scriptures call a continual drip, so a lot of times she just sits back and does not say anything, even if on the inside she is a little upset. - A shamefaced and faithful woman is a double grace, and her continent mind cannot be valued. That is self-restraint: she could go off about the clothes left everywhere, but she does not. - As the sun when it ariseth in the high heaven, so is the beauty of a good wife in the ordering of her house. If your wife goes out of town for a week, every cabinet door is open, cereal boxes on the counter, no clothes washed. You do not realize the stuff that gets done automatically. It works the other way too: women who think they are independent, as soon as that man leaves they start to realize who used to do this and that. And if there is a baby, somebody has to stay up all night; if the man has to go to work, it is going to be her. Ecclesiasticus 26:22 33:30 - A married woman is a tower against death to her husband. How is that? Because your wife knows you probably better than anybody on this planet. She knows the real you. We go out saying shalom Israel, Christ bless, but she knows you are lazy, she knows you procrastinate, she knows if you really do not believe. Some wives watch more classes and study more than their husbands. - Some women go to leadership and talk about their husbands, but the majority of good sisters sit back and hide all that. She holds it in. And a lot of times we take that for granted as men, 100 percent, until you are faced with what the brother in the song is facing. - Video played in class from James Baldwin: a wife tells her husband that everybody else gets the best of him and she gets the very minimum. He grins at the white man on the job all day, greets strangers, smiles at his boss; she catches the frowns and the anger. She says, fake it with me; is that too much for the black woman to ask of the black man, for ten years, so we can get a child on his feet that says father smiled at mother. - How many of your wives probably feel that way, that they get the worst part of you and everybody else gets the best part? All our anger and built-up aggression, we come home and dump it on our wives. Everybody else gets the patience, respect, and kindness. Ephesians 5:31-32 37:22 - For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother, and shall be joined unto his wife, and they two shall be one flesh. This is a great mystery, but I speak concerning Christ and the church. The relationship a husband has with his wife is the same kind of relationship he should have with the church. - As leaders, when there are issues in the church, we counsel for an hour, two hours, trying to work it out: a husband and wife with an issue, two brothers with an issue, sisters with issues. We work hard to fix it even when we are tired and sleepy. When we teach on the streets we see the issues our people are going through, and we plead with the people and sorrow with the people. Then we come home and do the exact opposite. James 1:8 39:27 - A double minded man is unstable in all his ways. A lot of us as men are one way on the outside, how the world sees us, and a completely different person at home. That is another way of being double minded. - Everybody sees you with the kids around; you walk into the school and the kids are happy to see you, the brothers salute you, the sisters say shalom officer. And your wife is sitting there thinking, he just cussed me out for 45 minutes on the way to the school. Why is everybody else happy and I am not happy? Because we are double minded and we trauma dump on our wives. Job 4:1-6 40:48 - Behold, thou hast instructed many, and thou hast strengthened the weak hands. We go out and teach: camp 30 days in a row, 100 days in a row, 365 days in a row. People come into the body sick and needing help; marriages come in messed up; we dedicate our time to fixing them. - Thy words have upholden him that was falling, and thou hast strengthened the feeble knees. How many times has a brother come to you and you said, let me go to the scripture right here, the Bible says this, put the cigarettes down, stop smoking weed. As a leader in this truth your phone rings all day: can I counsel with you, I have a question. We even go get counsel for our counsel. - But now it is come upon thee, and thou faintest; it toucheth thee, and thou art troubled. All the things you have been dedicating your life to help and fix and build up, and now you have something going on in your own household and you do not know what to do. You freeze up; you fold up. You spend months and years building up other people's households with ease, scriptures coming from everywhere, but when it comes on you, you go against your own counsel, because most men do not counsel about issues in their own household. - Is not this thy fear, thy confidence, thy hope, and the uprightness of thy ways? A lot of men walk around saying I am not scared, I will die for this truth. But the real fear goes into unresolved trauma, unresolved issues, things in our past we have not overcome. When we get faced with a challenge, we turn back into that little kid, that boy, that boyfriend that got cheated on, that past marriage. Precepts: - Galatians 6:1 Brethren, if a man be overtaken in a fault, ye which are spiritual, restore such an one in the spirit of meekness. We spend a lot of time restoring brothers and sisters that fall, bringing them back up, making them better than they used to be. We do it for everybody else. Book read in class: Trauma Letters: Healing the Child Within, by Captain Galayah, number one on Amazon right now. From the introduction: trauma is not just what happened to you; trauma is what happened inside of you when what happened to you went unresolved. Clinically, trauma is an emotional and physiological response to an event or series of events that overwhelm an individual's ability to cope. It is not measured by the severity of the event alone but by the internal impact it leaves behind. Trauma reshapes neural pathways, alters attachment patterns, influences decision making, and distorts identity formation. Developmental trauma in childhood is particularly powerful because it occurs during the years when the brain is still forming its internal working models of safety, love, authority, and belonging: a father's absence, a father's neglect, a parent's betrayal, a moment of abandonment. - These are not just issues; they are blueprints, written upon your code. That is why certain things your wife says take you right back to when you were a child, to not having your father around, to when somebody left you. These things do not just go away; they are imprinted into our mental DNA. Isaiah 3:12 50:51 - As for my people, children are their oppressors. Think about who is breaking into houses and cars and pulling on door handles: children. They are the ones oppressing the neighborhood. - And women rule over them. When young men are born in single parent households, women rule over them, and they which lead thee cause thee to err. The emotional side gets pushed onto the young men: you stepped on my shoe, why are you looking at me, and they end up killing one another. You see young men fighting their mother's battles even when she is wrong; a woman gets into it in a store, the son shows up as a defender, and he ends up dead. The Ja Morant story was the same pattern: his mom got into an issue in a shoe store, and he showed up with his crew to defend her, and she was wrong. - Having a man in the house matters. Statistically, a child raised by just a father comes up almost as good as if he had both parents. Some women make it work, but the single parent household is not the ideal situation. And not having a father in the house means other men coming in and out of the house, so the young man ends up with an issue with his father for leaving and an issue with his mother for how she carries herself; it leaves a hatred for women and for men, the worst of both worlds. 2 Esdras 5:8 53:46 - Monstrous women shall bring forth monsters. You see the videos: the kids going crazy, the police show up, and then the mom shows up even worse, cussing everybody out. She is training her kids to be just like that. James 5:16 56:31 - From Trauma Letters, letter six, a son writing to his father: your absence affected my emotional intelligence. No one taught me how to process emotion. Men are often frowned upon in society for expressing how they feel. We are told to suppress, to be strong, to not break down. So I buried sadness, I converted fear into anger, I wore a mask so convincing even I forgot what was underneath. In order to be relieved of this internal pain we must learn to process and channel it through God's word, but I never learned this type of emotional stability; in your absence I learned to just not deal with it, not knowing the emotional and spiritual toll it was taking on me. - Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed. Men do not like doing that. Brothers will name you as their counselor of a thousand and never actually call you to counsel about anything they are dealing with. They do not want to say they do not have a counselor, but they do not have one. - We do not know how to process what happened to us in our past, so we keep it bottled up, and we do not take it out on our boss or the congregation. We take it out on our spouse. Ecclesiasticus 9:1 58:51 - You have to counsel about the issues you are dealing with, but there is somebody you should not be counseling with about these emotional issues: your wife. Be not jealous over the wife of thy bosom, and teach her not an evil lesson against thyself. That jealousy goes into resentment: you unloaded all your emotional issues on her, and now you get into an argument and she throws them in your face, hitting below the belt. Everything you told her about being called stupid in school because you could not read, it comes back out when you get mad. And now you are sitting there saying, I am never telling anybody anything. - When women get mad, the gloves are off; there is a whole song about busting the windows out your car. Do not teach her things about you that she can use against you. Micah 7:5 1:00:39 - Keep the doors of thy mouth from her that lieth in thy bosom. Do not be like Samson: he dealt with Delilah, and after a glorious time he just told her all his secrets. Do not counsel with your wife about stuff like that. Proverbs 27:17 1:01:22 - Who do you need to counsel with? The brothers. Iron sharpeneth iron; so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend. Men need correction from other men. You have something from your past you are dealing with, go to a righteous counselor, go to your brother. Proverbs 11:14 1:01:52 - Where no counsel is, the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety. The scripture says have one counselor of a thousand, and that is true for the real personal things. But sometimes issues of the past should be brought up amongst a lot of men, because we start to find out we all have those same issues. There was a class on covert incest, where mothers treat their sons like a substitute companion, and a lot of men have been through that; you think it is just you, and then you start talking and hear, that same thing happened to me. - If you do not counsel about what you are going through, you bottle it all up, it explodes, and you push it out on your rib. That is how you get situations where a husband puts hands on his wife: bottled up over and over until she pushes the button, and he does something he regrets forever. - Video played in class: a man with narcissistic personality disorder explaining why the people closest to a narcissist get treated the worst. A normal person's emotional capacity is like a cup; a narcissist's cup has holes in it, so it drains all day, and when he comes home the cup is empty, and the people closest to him get the remnants and become his emotional punching bag. - That is a lot of us. You get up mad in the car, mad at every driver, everything leaking out all day, and guess who gets it when you get home? Your wife gets the trauma dump. But the narcissist in the video also said there is something he can do: he can plug the holes up. You can fix it. You get counsel, you talk about the issues. A lot of us ignore it and act like it is not a big deal, and the holes get bigger, until it goes from how you deal with your wife to how you deal with your brothers in the truth and the congregation. 2 Timothy 3:1-5 1:12:28 - In the last days perilous times shall come, for men shall be lovers of their own selves. That is a narcissist: all you care about is yourself. You come home not thinking about anybody but you. - Unthankful, unholy, without natural affection. It should be natural to be affectionate toward your wife, to come home and want to hug your wife and kiss your wife. But we come home mad from the whole day, emotional capacity at zero, sometimes negative ten: do not bother me, leave me alone. Then the phone rings and a brother says come through, and suddenly you are in the shower and on your way. You just spent 30 minutes telling your wife to leave you alone. - Some of you come home to a clean house and never say the house looks good, it smells good in here. That goes into that unthankful part. - Having a form of godliness, but denying the power thereof. That is the double mindedness: like the Pharisees, cleaning the outside of the cup, whited sepulchres. You sit down and teach brothers for hours, giving breakdowns from everywhere in the book, and your wife does not know basic scriptures, cannot counsel a depressed sister without asking you what to tell her. Why? Because you do not teach her anything. She asks a question, you get mad and tell her to go watch a class. Ecclesiasticus 7:26 1:15:57 - Hast thou a wife after thy mind? Forsake her not. Your wife is supposed to be after your mind, a representative of you; you two are supposed to be one flesh. If you are a brother that is good in the scriptures, good in history, a great counselor, your wife should be a great counselor. - But give not thyself over to a light woman. You should not want your wife not understanding the Bible. Is she going to break down the book of Daniel or 2 Esdras? No, but she should have a good basic understanding of scriptures, able to counsel a sister that calls and says I am depressed. Philippians 2:3 1:18:55 - Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory; but in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves. A lot of you run your household on strife and vainglory. You cannot run your household on ego. - Some of you do not teach your wives because you do not want her to know something you do not know, do not want her to study, because one day she may ask a question you cannot answer and your pride and ego take over. There was a brother whose wife could not do anything, could not leave the house without him, did not know how to drive; he was not pouring into her at all. If she is supposed to be that tower against death, how is she going to guide you with the scriptures when you are going through something if you never built the tower up? Instead of counseling with us about how you do not build your wife up, you come and say, my wife does not know anything. Were you studying with her? No. Ecclesiasticus 26:5-6 1:23:44 - Some of us still live life in the past. We get on the sisters about not forgiving and not forgetting, but this side of the room is the exact same way. We hold on to old arguments: here we go again, you are about to bring that up. We hold on to issues from past relationships, being cheated on, an ex-wife. Instead of a bag lady, you are a bag brother, carrying all of it, and you take it out on your wife. You do not trust her, not for something she did, but because of something somebody else did to you. - The comparison game works both ways. The worst thing a woman can do is compare her husband to a man from her past or to her father. But a woman does not want to be compared to another woman either. There be three things that mine heart feareth, and for the fourth I was sore afraid: the slander of a city, the gathering together of an unruly multitude, and a false accusation; all these are worse than death. But a grief of heart and sorrow is a woman that is jealous over another woman. The wisdom here is that this fourth thing is worse than the things that are worse than death. And a scourge of the tongue which communicateth with all: you will not have a silent and loving woman if she is jealous over another woman. Philippians 3:13 1:26:53 - Brothers, you have to follow the scripture too: forgetting those things which are behind, and reaching forth unto those things which are before. Let the past go: the issues with your father not being around, how your father treated your mom, how your mom treated you, the ex-girlfriend, the ex-marriage. If you do not let it go and move forward with what you have, you are going to be in a worse situation. Ecclesiastes 7:10 1:28:10 - Say not thou, What is the cause that the former days were better than these? for thou dost not enquire wisely concerning this. Do not sit back thinking about how everything was good with the ex: the bathwater was ready, the food was always ready. Well, you should have stayed with her. But she did not believe in God and did not want to keep the commandments, so you left and found a woman that believes she is an Israelite, that keeps the commandments and has the faith of Jesus Christ. And now you are comparing her to a wicked woman. - It is the children of Israel in the wilderness: 40 years marching around because they kept looking back at Egypt. We were slaves, but the food was good.
