The manna even tasted how they wanted it to taste, and they still were not happy; they wanted meat, and when the Most High gave them so much quail they could not take it, they complained again. They kept looking back at their worst condition while the Most High was trying to free them. That is us with the exes in the past. That was not a good situation; you were unequally yoked with a nonbeliever. Now you have a believer, so build her up, teach her, raise her in the scriptures. If you keep going back to how stuff was before, how are you encouraging her to be godly? - Video played in class, a preacher making the point: we treat strangers better than we treat those that we love. We will be rude, disrespectful, mean, cutting, thoughtless, and hateful to those that love us, because we can get away with it. We will give a stranger a compliment, but when was the last time you told your spouse how great they are, how well they are doing, how good they look? - With brothers we do it: bro, I see you, I can tell you have been studying. A brother cuts his hair and lines his beard up and it is a whole celebration in the school. But your wife sits in the salon chair for eight hours, comes home, and asks, can you tell I cut it? And you say, I don't know, yeah, it looks good. We compliment men on their hair more than we compliment our wives on theirs. 1 Corinthians 7:29 1:35:59 - This is not a simp-out class. Do not go home, stop going to camp, stop traveling, and rub feet all day. The time is short: it remaineth that both they that have wives be as though they had none. You have to be about the Lord's business. Brothers have had a baby and been in Africa the next week. The work has to be done no matter what. 1 Corinthians 7:33 1:37:01 - But he that is married careth for the things that are of the world, how he may please his wife. When you are not doing the work, you have to take care of your responsibilities at home, your prized possession, your pillar of rest. If you do not build her up, she is going to be a pillar of stress. - Why does it matter? Because she is teaching your kids. Do you want an unhappy, mean, angry, bitter, emotional woman bringing up your kids while you are not around? Your son is going to pick up those traits, and your daughter too. Take care of that possession at home or you will destroy it. Hebrews 10:24 1:41:14 - Let us consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works. In the congregation we do that: a brother in sadness, a brother that suffered loss, we provoke him to love and good works. Then we go home and provoke our wives to nothing but to be angry at us. - Think about what we tolerate from strangers. Brothers on the street get berated and mocked by disrespectful people and restrain themselves through the word of God. You get shoulder-bumped by Esau in public and keep walking, because we are trying to fix our people, not destroy them. But at home, let your wife forget to do something and you are ready for war, ready to cuss out your wife. You treat a stranger better than the person you are one flesh with. Something is not right about that. Hebrews 3:13 1:43:41 - Exhort one another daily, while it is called To day. How do you exhort your wife daily? Exhorting is encouraging one to do what is right. Some of you wake up, leave for nine or ten hours, come back, shower, go to Care 101, and the whole relationship with your wife is, hey, what's up though. Five words a day, while you are on Telegram getting on brothers about how we have to communicate. - From the index cards the women fill out in different congregations, leadership hears things that do not make sense: a husband that does not even want his wife to say good morning to him. There was a brother who demanded his wife read chapters every day, come up with ten questions a day for him, while she was homeschooling their five or six kids and he was never there. You do not even do that yourself. That is a militant mindset about our household, and it comes from fear, misplaced anger, and thinking we have to rule our houses with ego. - If you do not teach your wife, you are not teaching your daughters, and you are not teaching your sons. You get a breakdown, an epiphany, something off the chain, and you do not tell your wife. Then she misreads a scripture and gets embarrassed, or she quotes Bishop, a captain, an officer, a mother in the truth, because that is the only biblical words she hears. When she references things, she references the people she hears teaching the Bible. She should hear you teaching the Bible. Why not? Malachi 1:6 1:52:17 - A son honoureth his father, and a servant his master. A lot of times men only give honor where they think it matters: to the boss in the world because there are consequences, to the men in the truth, double honor to the elders. In your household you think, it does not matter, she is not going to do anything, I can do whatever I want here. - That is familiarity. You respect strangers because there are consequences and you care how other people see you. At home you feel like there are no consequences. A good woman does not want to embarrass her husband, so you know you can get away with it. And the question and answer read in class said it: we are often nicer to strangers than family due to impression management, assumed unconditional love, and accumulated history. You look at your wife and think, no matter what, you are bound to me until I die, so I can treat you how I want. That is not scriptural. - Videos played in class: a husband kept singing a love song while his wife struck him, and a wife described the abuse she was suffering at home; the teaching point is that some of you have good, righteous women and treat them in reverse, and stories like these are real in this truth too. 1 Peter 3:7 1:53:02 - Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honour unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel. If something is weak, you have to build it up. Proverbs 12:18 1:54:24 - There is that speaketh like the piercings of a sword: but the tongue of the wise is health. A lot of us are mad about something and go home and speak to our wives like the piercing of a sword. Ecclesiasticus 4:30 1:54:48 - Be not as a lion in thy house, nor frantick among thy servants. Especially if you are a weakling in the streets: out camping, sin walks right by, and you are afraid to go into the scriptures and call it out. Then you go in the house and roar. Proverbs 6:13 1:55:50 - He winketh with his eyes, he speaketh with his feet, he teacheth with his fingers. Some of you go home and speak to your wives with your feet and teach with your fingers, meaning you put hands and feet on your wife. You are abusive to your wives, while out in the streets you take every disrespect and say, next teacher. 1 Timothy 5:8 1:56:54 - Problems come in our households because we keep score: I provide, I pay all the bills, I take care of this and that. But if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel. You are supposed to do that. That is your reasonable service, a commandment of God. Congratulations for doing your job. You cannot throw in your wife's face that you do what you are supposed to do. Ephesians 5:28-29 1:57:38 - So ought men to love their wives as their own bodies. He that loveth his wife loveth himself. For no man ever yet hated his own flesh; but nourisheth and cherisheth it, even as the Lord the church. How you deal with the church should be the same way you deal with your wife and how you deal with yourself. Colossians 3:19 1:58:30 - Husbands, love your wives, and be not bitter against them. Bitterness is nothing but unresolved issues with unmet expectations. And our expectations are not going to be fully met until we get into the kingdom. Until then we are laboring to enter into that rest. This is not our rest; like 1 Corinthians 7:28 says, you shall have trouble in the flesh. There will be issues, but do not be bitter toward your wife. Proverbs 16:32 1:59:42 - He that is slow to anger is better than the mighty; and he that ruleth his spirit than he that taketh a city. In the household you have to be slow to anger and deal with your wife as the weaker vessel. You figure out how to control your spirit at camp when a man twice your size is standing in front of you; control it at home too. - Now, if you have a wife that is unruly, stand up for yourself. But if you have a sister that does what she is supposed to do for the most part, there has to be a balance. Your wife cannot always see the worst part of you. 1 Corinthians 7:3-4 2:00:29 - Sisters, how can you help? Let the husband render unto the wife due benevolence: and likewise also the wife unto the husband. The wife hath not power of her own body. It is strange to hear of men that do not want to render due benevolence to their own wives; that one is hard to understand. Ephesians 5:33 2:01:49 - Let every one of you in particular so love his wife even as himself; and the wife see that she reverence her husband. Respect and tone matter when we are addressing issues. Sisters, speak to your husband the right way; Proverbs 15:1, a soft answer turneth away wrath. Your timing and how you approach things matters as a woman. Proverbs 14:1 2:02:22 - Every wise woman buildeth her house: but the foolish plucketh it down with her hands. You pluck it down by complaining, yelling, arguing, and being disrespectful. Ecclesiasticus 25:1 2:03:06 - In three things I was beautified, and stood up beautiful both before God and men: the unity of brethren, the love of neighbours, a man and a wife that agree together. A man and a wife that agree together is beautiful before God. Ephesians 5:21 2:03:37 - How do they agree together? Submitting yourselves one to another in the fear of God. You both agree that you are going to follow the Bible, the scriptures, the word of God. Matthew 7:12 2:04:16 - A captain once gave this counsel: you do not have a daughter, so you counsel one way, but those of us with daughters deal with this differently, because you do not want your daughter going through it. Therefore all things whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them. - Men, ask yourself the question: the way you are treating your wife, is that the way you want your daughter's husband to treat her? If the answer is no, then you have to fix it. Fix yourself: deal with your past, drop the pride, do not deal with misplaced anger, and do not dominate with control. 1 Corinthians 16:13-14 2:05:03 - Watch ye, stand fast in the faith, quit you like men, be strong. Let all your things be done with charity. Quit you like men means conduct yourself like a man: keeping the commandments, with maturity, courage, discipline, and responsibility. That is how you have to deal as a man, and that is how you have to deal with your wife in your household. In Closing I pray this message did not go out void. If you are having a situation in your household, this can fix it. Brothers, we have to fix ourselves. Sisters, if you are a good wife, continue to be a good wife. Shalom, Most High and Christ bless. Happy Sabbath, happy new moon. Announcements & References - The Marriage on the Roll event is about to take place in LA; if you are going, make sure you get your payments in. - Book read in class: Trauma Letters: Healing the Child Within, by Captain Galayah (number one on Amazon); the introduction and letter six were read at length above. - The Better Halves on Facebook: a couple whose skits deal with real life situations that go on in households that people do not talk about. - Media referenced: This Woman's Work (Kate Bush, 1988; Maxwell's cover; Love & Basketball), a James Baldwin scene on giving your wife the best of you, a narcissism explainer on emotional capacity, and a preacher's clip on treating strangers better than family. --- Class Notes Index Transcript: full session

title: WE ARE BORN IN BABYLON
text: Introduction Thumbnail video: "In the beginning, there was a struggle in the womb. Two nations, two manner of people. One who despised his birthright, one who wrestled with God and prevailed. Babylon rose, the temple fell, and the stones were scattered. But from the ashes, a promise remained. Out of three, there was one wise. Through his wisdom, the temple of God would rise again, and from his line a branch. And I saw a new heaven and a new earth. And I saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven. The struggle began in the womb. It ends at the throne." We are born in Babylon: that is today's lesson title. You know how this thing is spiritual: the thumbnail opened up with Jacob and Esau, and Deacon just happened to touch on the same topic today in his class, and neither of us spoke about our classes beforehand. That is how you know it is a spirit. Get your Bible and your notebook and take some good notes, because some of this stuff you are not going to remember; when you go home, write those precepts next to the verse. Scriptures Opened Genesis 25:21-28 17:25 - Isaac intreated the Lord for his wife, because she was barren, meaning she could not have babies; and the Lord was intreated of him, and Rebekah conceived. The children struggled together within her, and she said, if I be blessed by God, why am I having so much trouble in this childbirth? And she went to inquire of the Lord. - Two nations are in thy womb: this is the beginning of two nations. The word Genesis means beginning. Two manner of people shall be separated from thy bowels: two different types. The one people shall be stronger than the other people, stronger mentally and physically; and the elder shall serve the younger: the elder was prophesied to be a servant to the younger. - There were twins in her womb, but those twins were not identical, because it said two manner of people shall be separated. They looked different. - The first came out red, all over like an hairy garment, and they called his name Esau. Write this down: Esau means wasted away, meaning his melanin was wasted away. Clip shown from the heat wave in France: when they are in the sun they get red. Down south we call them rednecks, but it is not just their neck that gets red. Look how red them people are; do not tell me they are white. They are Esau; these are their children. - And after that came his brother out, and his hand took hold on Esau's heel. That is very important, because there is a lot of symbolism behind that. Precepts: - 2 Esdras 6:7-10 What shall be the parting asunder of the times? or when shall be the end of the first, and the beginning of it that followeth? Meaning when shall be the end of this world, and when shall the new world come in? From Abraham unto Isaac, when Jacob and Esau were born of him, Jacob's hand held first the heel of Esau. For Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth: that is what it symbolized when Jacob was holding Esau's heel. The hand of man is betwixt the heel and the hand: all the other nations are like extras in the movie. Moab is an extra; Ishmael is an extra. Christians do not know what that means at all. - His name was called Jacob, and Isaac was threescore years old when she bare them: Isaac was 60 when Rebekah gave birth to Esau and Jacob. They did not mention Jacob's color, because Jacob looked just like his mother and father; in fact Jacob looked like everybody from the time of Adam. The only color differential was Esau; that is why the scribes had to write down Esau's color: he was starkly different. Precepts: - Genesis 2:7 The Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground: the dust of the ground is different shades of brown; the deeper you dig, the darker it gets. That is what Adam looked like, and Eve, and everybody that came from them. Cain's line was cursed with a lack of melanin; the flood came and killed them all off, and God brought them all back through Noah's three sons. So when you move up the generational line to Isaac and Rebekah, Esau is the return of Cain's lineage, and Jacob is the return of Seth. - And the boys grew: and Esau was a cunning hunter, a man of the field; and Jacob was a plain man, dwelling in tents. When you examine the two, remember it said two manner of people: Jacob was plain, he dwelt in tents, he herded the sheep and the goats. Esau was not like that; he liked to go out and hunt, he liked that adrenaline rush. - And Isaac loved Esau, because he did eat of his venison: he hunted the food and learned how to cook it from Rebekah. But Rebekah loved Jacob. Hebrews 12:16-17 25:14 - Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright. In that pottage was meat: feed me, I pray thee, with that same red pottage, raw, bloody meat. And you have brothers today lusting after these same people. Many times brothers ask what it means that Esau was profane or a fornicator; the scriptures explain it. Precepts: - Genesis 26:34-35 Esau was forty years old when he took to wife Judith the daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Bashemath the daughter of Elon the Hittite: which were a grief of mind unto Isaac and to Rebekah. His parents did not like his marriage choices of those Hittites. Listen: you have unlearned Israelites that use these verses to say Esau was black because his kids mixed with the Hittites. No. God kept that line the way it is. Even today, no matter how black you are, if you marry a white woman you can tell that child is hybrid: high yellow, sometimes yellow hair, green eyes. Photos shown of Drake as a boy and his family: his hair is like his father, but his complexion is closer to the mother. So you mean back then God could not maintain that same lighter red complexion in Esau's line? These hybrid children look more like Esau. - Genesis 28:8-9 Esau, seeing that the daughters of Canaan pleased not Isaac his father, went unto Ishmael, and took Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael Abraham's son to be his wife. So now he married Arab kids too; that is what Esau was doing. - Tobit 4:12 Beware of all whoredom, my son, and chiefly take a wife of the seed of thy fathers, and take not a strange woman to wife, which is not of thy father's tribe. Whoredom falls under fornication; this is what made Esau a fornicator: he married Hittite women and Ishmaelite women, and Ishmael was the beginning of another race; Genesis is the beginning of races. For we are the children of the prophets, Noe, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob: our fathers from the beginning all married wives of their own kindred, and were blessed in their children, and their seed shall inherit the land. - For ye know how that afterward, when he would have inherited the blessing, he was rejected: rejected by God; for he found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears. Genesis 25:30-34 32:01 - Feed me, I pray thee, with that same red pottage; for I am faint: he came from the field faint from hunting in that hot sun, saying I feel like I am about to die. Therefore was his name called Edom: Edom meaning red. So his name was also called Edom. - And Jacob said, Sell me this day thy birthright. And Esau said, Behold, I am at the point to die: and what profit shall this birthright do to me? I do not give a damn about a birthright if I am about to die. And he sware unto him: and he sold his birthright unto Jacob. This is what made him profane: the birthright meant a lot, and he could not care less about it. - Then Jacob gave Esau bread and pottage of lentiles, and in those lentiles was raw meat; and he did eat and drink, and rose up, and went his way: thus Esau despised his birthright. Genesis 27:38-40 33:03 - Remember the history of this chapter: Rebekah told Jacob, your father is half blind; go in there and make believe you are your brother Esau. Jacob said, but I will get cursed. She said, whatever curse there be, let it fall on me. Why did she say that? Because she remembered what God told her when she was giving birth: the elder shall serve the younger. So she said to her younger son, put goats' hair on your hands and the back of your neck, so when your father feels you, you feel hairy like your brother. Isaac said, you sound like Jacob, but you feel and smell like Esau; and Isaac blessed Jacob with the major blessing, thinking it was Esau. - When you listen to Christians about those two boys, they say Jacob was the evil son and Esau was the good one, and you have black people in church echoing those same sentiments. No: Jacob was the good one. Esau was the profane one, the fornicating one, the one that despised his birthright. What Jacob did was due to his mama, and she was being obedient to God; she said, I remember what God said. - And Esau said unto his father, Hast thou but one blessing, my father? bless me, even me also, O my father. And Esau lifted up his voice, and wept. - And Isaac his father answered and said unto him, Behold, thy dwelling shall be the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above. Dew falls everywhere, and wherever the dew falls, that is where you are going to live: you are going to live where you want, and you are going to have the best places on the planet. - And by thy sword shalt thou live: Esau lives by the sword, meaning war. That is how they would get the lands, and that is how they would get the fatness of the earth: through war. So God through Isaac blessed Esau with the art of war, which, like Deacon brought up, was the same blessing Cain's line had: Tubalcain made all kinds of weapons. Precepts: - 1 Esdras 5:72-73 But the heathen of the land, lying heavy upon the inhabitants of Judea, and holding them strait, hindered their building; and by their secret plots, and popular persuasions and commotions, they hindered the finishing of the building all the time that king Cyrus lived: so they were hindered from building for the space of two years, until the reign of Darius. See that: secret plots, persuading the multitude against them, causing commotions. - Is it time for you, O ye, to dwell in your cieled houses, and this house lie waste? Hey Zerubbabel, is it time for you to live in your nice house with the new roof, while the Lord's house is a shambles? - Now therefore thus saith the Lord of hosts; Consider your ways. You know what consider your ways means? Examine yourself. And do not say that is only for Zerubbabel; it is not. Precepts: - 2 Corinthians 13:5 Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves. Know ye not your own selves, how that Jesus Christ is in you, except ye be reprobates? If you do not know Christ is in you, you are reprobate. That is what all of us have to do: examine ourselves day by day. - Ye have sown much, and bring in little: you have worked a lot with little profit to show for it. Ye eat, but ye have not enough; ye drink, but ye are not filled with drink; ye clothe you, but there is none warm; and he that earneth wages earneth wages to put it into a bag with holes. I just worked 48, 52 hours and I do not have enough money to show for it. Not only was that going on with Zerubbabel: that is why many of us in here are always struggling, because God is always second or third in your life, just like Zerubbabel. - Go up to the mountain, and bring wood, and build the house; and I will take pleasure in it, and I will be glorified, saith the Lord. - Ye looked for much, and, lo, it came to little; and when ye brought it home, I did blow upon it. Why? saith the Lord of hosts. Because of mine house that is waste, and ye run every man unto his own house. You are not looking after God's house first. - Therefore the heaven over you is stayed from dew, and the earth is stayed from her fruit: you are not getting blessings in your crops. And I called for a drought upon the land, and upon the mountains, and upon the corn, and upon the new wine, and upon the oil, and upon men, and upon cattle, and upon all the labour of the hands. Haggai 1:12-15 2:13:02 - Then Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Joshua the son of Josedech the high priest, with all the remnant of the people, obeyed the voice of the Lord their God, and the words of Haggai the prophet, and the people did fear before the Lord. - Notice: Joshua was the high priest, Zerubbabel was the governor; Haggai was not in those positions. But Joshua and Zerubbabel humbled themselves, because they knew it was the word of the Lord; they knew Haggai and Zechariah were sent of God. Zerubbabel could have said, arrest him, lock him up; or he could have punched a hole in his chest. He did none of that. He said, I recognize the word of the Lord; I am going to humble myself. - That is how we have to be. We will get on brothers and they take it personal, like we just stabbed his mama; we are just telling you to fix your life. That is love. You correct a brother's wife, and he says you are trying to destroy my marriage; no, we are trying to help your marriage. - Then spake Haggai the Lord's messenger in the Lord's message unto the people, saying, I am with you, saith the Lord. And the Lord stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel, and the spirit of Joshua, and the spirit of all the remnant of the people; and they came and did work in the house of the Lord of hosts, their God. Haggai 2:1-3 2:14:48 - Who is left among you that saw this house in her first glory? and how do ye see it now? is it not in your eyes in comparison of it as nothing? Remember, they were in Babylon for 70 years; Cyrus came in at the end of the 70 years, then Darius. So the question is, who is still alive that saw the temple that Solomon built? When they rebuilt the temple, it did not look half as good as what Solomon had built. Precepts: - Ezra 3:12-13 Many of the priests and Levites and chief of the fathers, who were ancient men that had seen the first house, when the foundation of this house was laid before their eyes, wept with a loud voice; and many shouted aloud for joy: so that the people could not discern the noise of the shout of joy from the noise of the weeping of the people; and the noise was heard afar off. - Reading shown on Herod: the temple Zerubbabel rebuilt was completed around 515 BC, but it did not compare to Solomon's. King Herod the Great began a massive expansion and renovation of the second temple around 20 to 19 BC, to beautify the site, impress the Roman world, and win favor with his Jewish subjects: he doubled the area of the Temple Mount platform to about 35 acres with giant retaining walls; workers used enormous carved white limestone blocks, some weighing over 500 tons; the main temple building was covered in bright white stone trimmed with gold; and he added grand colonnades, magnificent entry gates, and spacious public spaces for worshippers and pilgrims. - You see that last sentence: spacious public spaces for worshippers and pilgrims. Meaning the other nations had a place now; they could come and look at what was going on in the temple. That was not in the original design that God gave us. Herod added it. Herod was an Idumean, an Edomite, and this Edomite wanted favor with the Jews. Precepts: - Jeremiah 22:13 Woe unto him that buildeth his house by unrighteousness, and his chambers by wrong; that useth his neighbour's service without wages, and giveth him not for his work. - Matthew 11:12 From the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force. Who are the violent that Christ was talking about? Rome. - John 10:10 The thief cometh not, but for to steal, and to kill, and to destroy. Who is he talking about? Rome. Remember Herod was an Idumean, and Rome were Idumeans; they were the same race. Book read in class: Who Is Esau-Edom?, by Charles A. Weisman. Esau wrote this book; this is not a negro writing this: - "Herod was a shrewd and unscrupulous tyrant and was despised by the Judahites because he was an Idumean, and not one of their own stock. Herod hated the people of Judah, and one of his first acts was to execute forty-five of their leaders of the old aristocracy, to eliminate any rivalry for leadership. Having secured the kingship, Herod next destroyed the priestly line of Hyrcanus, the last being Antigonus, who taunted Herod with his Idumean origin, and asserted that the kingdom should fall on one of the royal family." Idumean means Edomite; that is why he did all that building, to get in good graces. - "We thus find that in the years just before the time of Christ, Judea was controlled by an Edomite faction who usurped the Judahite name, land, and heritage. Historically, the Edomites became known as Jews, derived from Judea, which was derived from the name Judah, being the royal line of Israel, though they were never of Judah or Israel." Usurped the name meaning they became Jewish: we are converts, we are Jews now. That is what Herod was doing. - "The Jews of today fall within two main types: the Sephardic Jew, also known as the Spanish Jews, who constitute about 5 percent of the Jews in the world; and the Ashkenazi Jew, the East European Jews found in Poland, Russia, Germany, and western Asia, who make up 90 percent." Initially we were the Sephardim in Spain; when they conquered us and cast us out, Esau became the Sephardic ones in Spain. - "Many reference and historical sources have unequivocally identified that the bulk of the Ashkenazi Jews were derived from a people known as Khazars. The original Jewish Encyclopedia of 1905 revealed that the main stock came from this Asiatic people: Chazars, a people of Turkish origin whose life and history are interwoven with the very beginnings of the history of the Jews of Russia. The Khazars are also of Edomite stock, and both stocks make up the present day Jews. According to the Jewish Encyclopedia, the original stock of the Khazars came from the land of Edom." We had to find out whether the Khazars were Japheth or Esau; their own encyclopedia says Edomite stock. Do not tell us we do not know what we are talking about: we have second, third, and fourth book sources, and the Bible is always our main source. - "As it is written, Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated (Romans 9:13). God not only hates Esau-Edom, but refers to them as the people of my curse (Isaiah 34:5). There is not one favorable or positive statement in the Bible in relation to Esau-Edom. If God hated you and your ancestors, how would you react? By natural reaction you would be against God and his people, and try to prevent them from finding out you are Esau. Who is it that tries to conceal their identity as Edom, the one hated by God, by claiming to be Israel, the one loved by God? Why do you suppose the Jews form organizations such as the Anti-Defamation League, to monitor and combat hate and to identify hate groups? If you were Esau-Edom, would you not do the same? An Edomite would also want to infiltrate churches." - That is the game now against the truth: they go into the churches and say, hate in Romans 9:13 does not really mean hate, it just means displeased; you have to go into the Hebrew. That is what they are doing now. Mark 13:1-4 2:28:11 - Master, see what manner of stones and what buildings are here: Herod made that thing look so good the disciples marveled at it. And Jesus answering said unto him, Seest thou these great buildings? there shall not be left one stone upon another, that shall not be thrown down. - And as he sat upon the mount of Olives over against the temple, Peter and James and John and Andrew asked him privately, Tell us, when shall these things be? and what shall be the sign when all these things shall be fulfilled? Their question was: when will this temple be destroyed, when shall the end come? - Book read: The Temples That Jerusalem Forgot, by Ernest L. Martin: "When Jesus said the temple and the city of Jerusalem would be obliterated, his prophecies were accurate to a T. The historical records show that when the Romans got through with their fury in dismantling Jerusalem and the temple, no stones were left in place that would make one believe there was once a city or a holy sanctuary in the area. So thorough was the ruin of the temple, and also of Jewish Jerusalem, that scholars cannot find any stone of the temple still in place in its original location. My conclusions show that the Bible and history reveal the wailing wall was not a wall of the temple, but is the western wall of Herod's fort Antonia." - Everybody in the world thinks that western wall was part of the temple. Christ said there would not be one stone left, and now Esau himself is revealing that wall was Herod's fortress. Diagram shown of the Temple Mount with fort Antonia: that is the wall that was left, not the temple; the temple was totally destroyed. Every year masses of people go to that wailing wall to pray at Herod's fort. Revelation 11:1-2 2:31:42 - And there was given me a reed like unto a rod: and the angel stood, saying, Rise, and measure the temple of God, and the altar, and them that worship therein. - But the court which is without the temple leave out, and measure it not; for it is given unto the Gentiles. Diagram shown with the courts color coded: the court of the Gentiles, the women's court, the men's court, the priests' court. That outer court is where the other nations went; Herod added it in, and it was not part of the original temple. - The argument is always, God is for everybody. God said do not even measure the Gentile court. God is not for everybody. Everybody see that. John 2:19-20 2:33:28 - Jesus answered and said unto them, Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up. Then said the Jews, Forty and six years was this temple in building, and wilt thou rear it up in three days? Precepts: - Mark 14:58 We heard him say, I will destroy this temple that is made with hands, and within three days I will build another made without hands. Those were the false witnesses; they overheard his teachings and lied on him. - Mark 15:29-30 And they that passed by railed on him, wagging their heads, and saying, Ah, thou that destroyest the temple, and buildest it in three days, save thyself, and come down from the cross. This is Christ on the cross. - Matthew 27:63 Sir, we remember that that deceiver said, while he was yet alive, After three days I will rise again. So that is what he meant when he said in three days I will rebuild this temple. - Matthew 16:21 From that time forth began Jesus to shew unto his disciples, how that he must go unto Jerusalem, and suffer many things of the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and be raised again the third day. He was talking about raising up himself the third day: Christ's body was the temple, and his temple today is us. 1 Peter 2:1-5 2:35:55 - Question to the class: how do we grow in this truth? How do we grow individually, as a congregation, in our marriage? Everybody jumps to the milk and misses verse one: wherefore laying aside all malice, and all guile (guile means deceit), and hypocrisies, and envies (jealousies), and all evil speakings (murmurings and complainings). You have to put away first all that is within you. - As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby. The sincere milk of the word is God's laws. What is Peter saying? We have to be drinking the laws of God like a baby drinks milk: that is not once a month, that is not once a week; that is every other hour, be in that Bible study. That is the only way you are going to grow. - A lot of brothers get demoted. We had a brother demoted last week for lying over a simple thing. Most of the time when we ask, we already know the answer; when you give another answer and we have witnesses, we call the brother and verify. Now you are found out to be a liar and deceitful, not worthy of your rank. That is why some brothers do not come to the war room. - If so be ye have tasted that the Lord is gracious: if you know this word is true. To whom coming, as unto a living stone, disallowed indeed of men: rejected of men, the scribes and Pharisees; but chosen of God, and precious. - Ye also, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house: that is the real temple right there; wherever our congregation is, that is a spiritual house. An holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices, acceptable to God by Jesus Christ. Lively meaning the laws percolate within you, meaning have some kind of zeal and passion about yourself. We need men with fire when they teach; I do not have to speak the language to read a boring spirit on a screen. - Remember, Zerubbabel got to that position not just for his fighting skills; it said he was of noble character, understanding truth and moral discipline. We all should walk in the footsteps of Zerubbabel: not deceitful with one another, not envious, not hateful, not filled with guile. - Frederick Douglass said, it is easier to build strong children than to repair broken men. All of us come in broken, broken with sins. So in order for us to grow mentally and spiritually and improve our character: verse one, lay it all aside, then desire the sincere milk of the word. Precepts: - Ephesians 2:21-22 In whom all the building fitly framed together (that is you and me) groweth unto an holy temple in the Lord. You know what fitly framed together means? Stones have to come together. Brothers, we must merge together: whatever your position is, play that position; do not try to change positions through deceit. In whom ye also are builded together for an habitation of God through the Spirit. - 1 Corinthians 3:16-17 Know ye not that ye are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you? If any man defile the temple of God, him shall God destroy; for the temple of God is holy, which temple ye are. That is why we have to change the way we conduct ourselves; our communications must change. 2 Timothy 2:19-21 2:46:35 - Nevertheless the foundation of God standeth sure, having this seal, The Lord knoweth them that are his. And, Let every one that nameth the name of Christ depart from iniquity. We must depart from iniquity. - But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver, but also of wood and of earth; and some to honour, and some to dishonour. This great house is the nation of Israel, the real nation of Israel. There are brothers and sisters who are gold and silver material: they are applying what we just read in 1 Peter 2:1-2. But also of wood and of earth: there are brothers and sisters here with fringes and a border of blue who are no good; they have not changed their lives; they are the same as they were two, three years ago. I am not talking about new people that just came in; I am talking about people who have been with us for years and are still that secret adulterer, that liar, complainer, murmurer. You are that wood and that earth. - In every IUIC school there are brothers and sisters of honor and dishonor, and the captains must be able to identify in their school who are the honorable men and women and who are the dishonorable. If you cannot do that, there is a problem. - If a man therefore purge himself from these, he shall be a vessel unto honour, sanctified, and meet for the master's use, and prepared unto every good work. When you purge a plant you are pruning it, taking away the bad elements. Likewise with us: the bad elements among us, you have to cut off. I knew which brothers I always used to get in trouble with; I had to cut them off and hang out with leadership. Precepts: - 2 Timothy 3:1-5 This know also, that in the last days perilous times shall come. For men shall be lovers of their own selves, covetous, boasters, proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, unthankful, unholy, without natural affection, trucebreakers, false accusers, incontinent, fierce, despisers of those that are good, traitors, heady, highminded, lovers of pleasures more than lovers of God; having a form of godliness, but denying the power thereof. You know why it says a form of godliness? That is the fringes and the border of blue, walking around with your Bible saying all the greetings, but you are really not keeping the commandments in your heart. From such turn away: the same thing he said in the chapter before, purge yourself from these. Isaiah 30:12-13 2:50:35 - Wherefore thus saith the Holy One of Israel, Because ye despise this word, and trust in oppression and perverseness. Our people despise God's laws and trust in oppression. You know what oppression is? For an example, democracy is an oppressive system. You know what perverseness is? Christianity: come as you are, stay as you be. That is what I learned in church; there was no change. - Therefore this iniquity shall be to you as a breach ready to fall, swelling out in a high wall, whose breaking cometh suddenly at an instant. - Video played: Harriet Tubman said, I would have freed so many more of my people, if only they knew they were slaves. All our people want is comfortable oppression: as long as it is comfortable, they are all right with it. The system understands that: we will feed them false hope, give them one or two to idolize and put on a pedestal to chase; but the system is not meant for everybody to win, because if it was, everybody would be winning. - That is trusting in oppression: I am not oppressed, I make millions a year. That is comfortable oppression; that is all it is. - Documentary recommended: Exterminate All the Brutes, on HBO Max, loosely based on Sven Lindqvist's book: it explores colonialism, white supremacy, and the brutality carried across the world, with reenactments and commentary from historians. Very good documentary; watch it when you get a chance. Zechariah 4:6-7 2:54:48 - Everything we do, brothers and sisters, must be according to the spirit of the Most High God; it has nothing to do with our physical powers and our skills. - Who art thou, O great mountain? Remember, Zerubbabel was in the Persian captivity; Babylon was already destroyed by Persia. So this great mountain is Babylon to come: Babylon the great. Does everybody understand that? Precepts: - Jeremiah 51:24-26 And I will render unto Babylon and to all the inhabitants of Chaldea all their evil that they have done in Zion in your sight, saith the Lord. Watch what he calls Babylon: Behold, I am against thee, O destroying mountain, which destroyest all the earth: and I will stretch out mine hand upon thee, and roll thee down from the rocks, and will make thee a burnt mountain. And they shall not take of thee a stone for a corner, nor a stone for foundations; but thou shalt be desolate for ever. That right there lets you know it is not Iraq: are people still living in Iraq today? Yes. This says thou shalt be desolate for ever; so it is not talking about ancient Babylon. - Isaiah 19:18-20 In that day shall five cities in the land of Egypt speak the language of Canaan: the language of Canaan is referring to the scriptures. In that day shall there be an altar to the Lord in the midst of the land of Egypt: it is talking about where the Israelites are, here in Babylon the great, the spiritual Egypt. And it shall be for a sign and for a witness unto the Lord of hosts: for they shall cry unto the Lord because of the oppressors, and he shall send them a saviour, and a great one, and he shall deliver them. Who is that saviour? Christ. - Before Zerubbabel thou shalt become a plain: flattened, destroyed. And he shall bring forth the headstone thereof with shoutings, crying, Grace, grace unto it. Why is he crying grace, grace? It said in Isaiah: because of the oppressors. This is showing you Zerubbabel is in these last days as well. Haggai 2:4-9 2:59:23 - Yet now be strong, O Zerubbabel, saith the Lord; and be strong, O Joshua, son of Josedech, the high priest; and be strong, all ye people of the land, saith the Lord, and work: for I am with you, saith the Lord of hosts. - According to the word that I covenanted with you when ye came out of Egypt, so my spirit remaineth among you: fear ye not. That is why Christ said, I will never leave you nor forsake you, even unto the end of the world. - For thus saith the Lord of hosts; Yet once, it is a little while, and I will shake the heavens, and the earth, and the sea, and the dry land; and I will shake all nations, and the desire of all nations shall come: and I will fill this house with glory. The silver is mine, and the gold is mine, saith the Lord of hosts. - The glory of this latter house shall be greater than of the former: the house that Christ builds is going to be greater than the former house that Solomon built. Malachi 3:1-4 3:00:47 - Behold, I will send my messenger, and he shall prepare the way before me: and the Lord, whom ye seek, shall suddenly come to his temple, even the messenger of the covenant, whom ye delight in. Now, you may think initially it is talking about John the Baptist; that is a good thought, but it is actually talking about the John the Baptist work in the last days. Precepts: - Malachi 4:4-6 Remember ye the law of Moses my servant, which I commanded unto him in Horeb for all Israel, with the statutes and judgments. Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord: and he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers. Why? Because we would forget who we are; we would lose our way; and he is going to turn us back to our forefathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; lest I come and smite the earth with a curse. - But who may abide the day of his coming? and who shall stand when he appeareth? for he is like a refiner's fire, and like fullers' soap. That is how you know it is the last days. Precepts: - Zechariah 13:8-9 This is what the refiner's fire and the soap mean. And it shall come to pass, that in all the land, saith the Lord, two parts therein shall be cut off and die: two out of every three of our people shall be cut off. But the third shall be left therein; and I will bring the third part through the fire, and will refine them as silver is refined, and will try them as gold is tried: they shall call on my name, and I will hear them: I will say, It is my people; and they shall say, The Lord is my God. That is the wilderness right there. - And he shall sit as a refiner and purifier of silver: and he shall purify the sons of Levi, and purge them as gold and silver, that they may offer unto the Lord an offering in righteousness. Then shall the offering of Judah and Jerusalem be pleasant unto the Lord, as in the days of old, and as in former years. Precepts: - Malachi 1:11 For from the rising of the sun even unto the going down of the same my name shall be great among the Gentiles; and in every place incense shall be offered unto my name, and a pure offering: for my name shall be great among the heathen, saith the Lord of hosts. That is the offering of Judah and Jerusalem. Malachi 3:5-6 3:04:22 - And I will come near to you to judgment; and I will be a swift witness against the sorcerers. Precepts: - Exodus 22:18 Thou shalt not suffer a witch to live. - News video played: growing numbers of black women in Maryland and across the nation are leaving traditional church worship for ancient forms of spiritual contact; some call it witchcraft, a term they accept and embrace, offering prayers to spirits and deities like Oshun; more than 200 witches gathered at a recent convention in Baltimore. They grew up Christian, Baptist, Episcopal; now they call themselves witches. God said he is going to be a swift witness against the sorcerers. - Testimony video on crystals: instead of healing you, it entices you and traps you into depending on it for every little thing; it is a placebo effect. So brothers, be careful: sisters come in with these crystals saying it is just spirituality. It is witchcraft; do not fall for it, or you are going to have demons all up in your house. - And against the adulterers. Precepts: - Deuteronomy 22:22 If a man be found lying with a woman married to an husband, then they shall both of them die: so shalt thou put away evil from Israel. At the sit down, the Christian pastors could not explain adultery. - Reading shown from a "swingers of color" site connecting black swingers in the lifestyle: this is adultery. True story told from one of our congregations: two couples switched partners for months before it came out; the brother who revealed it only revealed it because he was angry, not because a spirit told him to; and we had to put him out. He is on YouTube and TikTok now like an all knowing teacher, teaching everything we teach, but he is not going to reveal that he was that swinger brother. - And against false swearers. Precepts: - Leviticus 19:12 And ye shall not swear by my name falsely, neither shalt thou profane the name of thy God: I am the Lord. That goes into perjury and false statements. - And against those that oppress the hireling in his wages. You might say to yourself, this does not apply to us, nobody among us oppresses the hireling in his wages. Oh, you would be shocked; it took place right here. Brothers with their own trucking authority hired the brothers, then gave the good, high paying jobs to the ones they liked, gave the others little work, and paid brothers late and unequal. Everything was unjust. Precepts: - Leviticus 19:13 Thou shalt not defraud thy neighbour, neither rob him: the wages of him that is hired shall not abide with thee all night until the morning. - The widow, and the fatherless. Precepts: - Exodus 22:22-24 Ye shall not afflict any widow, or fatherless child. If thou afflict them in any wise, and they cry at all unto me, I will surely hear their cry; and my wrath shall wax hot, and I will kill you with the sword; and your wives shall be widows, and your children fatherless. - And that turn aside the stranger from his right, and fear not me, saith the Lord of hosts. - For I am the Lord, I change not; therefore ye sons of Jacob are not consumed. That is why we are still in existence today. And with that, twelve tribes, we say shalom. Announcements & References Books and readings referenced in class: - Light and Truth: Collected from the Bible and Ancient and Modern History, by R. B. Lewis (1844): the Moors and the definitions of negro (read at length above) - The Story of Civilization: Caesar and Christ, by Will Durant: the Latins gave the name Africa to the region around Carthage and Utica - Hearings before the Subcommittee on Constitutional Rights, United States Senate (1959), "American Negro problems": the American negro is the most advanced section and the destined vanguard - American Economic Association reading: the Negro stock landed in America was physically superior to the average of that left behind - Who Is Esau-Edom?, by Charles A. Weisman: Herod the Idumean, the Edomite usurping of the Judahite name, and the Khazars of Edomite stock - The Temples That Jerusalem Forgot, by Ernest L. Martin: no stone of the temple left; the wailing wall is the western wall of Herod's fort Antonia - Documentary: Exterminate All the Brutes (HBO Max), based on Sven Lindqvist's book Field reports played: - IUIC stood with the family of Kendrick Johnson in Washington DC, marching on the Supreme Court to bring awareness to his murder, going live on Fox News with the holy scriptures, then hitting the streets to teach. - The prophets of IUIC Denver, led by Captain Gad, blazed the cities of Colorado for 30 days of camp; through much tribulation and pushback, the word went out and God got the victory. - IUIC Montreal blitzed the Carimas parade with the word, giving our people love, correction, and the warning of Luke 13:3. - Community cleanup: picking up litter and planting hope; more than a cleanup, a movement of healing, unity, and spiritual growth for the community. - Officers finished a successful radio sit down at 8 Rebel Squad radio in New York and New Jersey, bringing out the prophecies against the accusations of the ADL and SPLC. - IUIC Sacramento held a family fun day: brothers in the scriptures, sisters serving in the spirit of unity, kids running around. - Missions report: brothers left Japan headed toward Indonesia and China, seeking the lost sheep on that side of the world where our people have taken on the features of the nations; the mission is to find the twelve tribes. Subscribe to IUIC Diaspora 2.0. - Captain Abiel led the prophets to deliver about 500 gallons of water, spiritual and physical, to a community in Mexico in the midst of a water shortage; send up prayers for the Lord to send rain. Dates and events: - The next voluntary fast is coming up on August 7th; stay in the spirit. - The Acts 2 program is here: to donate or make IUIC a beneficiary, email acts2@israelunite.org. - Dropping tonight on Original Royalty Records: the video Curse of the Cipher, the second video off the album 12 Tribes Worldwide by Four Corners News, available at originalroyalty.com. - The Sons of Thunder sixth studio album, The Souls of the Saints, drops August 29th on originalroyalty.com and all streaming platforms; pre-order now. The official album release party is August 30th in North Carolina; registration is open with your Royal Event Planning rep. - Israel Live top five: scan the QR code and cast your vote for next week's episode, Monday nights at 9:00 pm. - Northeast Region Tabernacles and Original Royalty concert registration is now open. - The Until All Is Served 2.0 fundraiser is taking place tonight; last year's winner was New York; place your orders. Closing reading: 1 Corinthians 11:23-29, the bread and the cup, in remembrance of the Lord's death till he come; let a man examine himself. --- Class Notes Index Transcript: full session

title: Clean and Unclean Meats
text: Clean and Unclean Meats The dietary laws: what may be eaten, what is an abomination, and the precepts behind them. Genesis Genesis 1:26-27 taught in Genesis 1-4 - Notice it says let them have dominion. The Most High did not create just one man; the man spoken of here is mankind. - The words created he him point to a particular person, who begins to be described in Genesis 2. Male and female created he them is mankind. Genesis 5:1-2 taught in Genesis 5-8 - The words made he him speak of the first Adam. This Adam was made in the likeness of God, a direct descendant of the Most High. - Male and female created he them, and called their name Adam: they were not that Adam; these were the other people on the earth. When the Most High creates a fish He does not create only a salmon; there is mackerel and tuna and all types of fish. In the same way, He created Adam and He created the other people. - Chapter 5 is the direct lineage of Adam. That lineage is the sons of God you read of in chapter 6, and the later chapters of Genesis tie the Israelites directly to the lineage of Adam through Shem. - When Christ said, Ye are gods, He was saying we come from that line of Adam. - Precept Genesis 1:26-27 : The man made in our image, created he him, is the first Adam; male and female created he them is the other people. Genesis 7:2-3 taught in Genesis 5-8 - The dietary law was not yet instituted, but the Most High had already defined what was a clean beast and what was an unclean beast, all the way back in Genesis; Moses reiterated that law to the children of Israel. - Today this gets confused with the doctrine that says I can eat all things through Christ who strengthens me, and that is not true; the laws were instituted for us to discern between the unclean and the clean. - Precept Leviticus 11:45-47 : The law of the beasts makes a difference between the unclean and the clean, the beast that may be eaten and the beast that may not be eaten. - Precept Ezekiel 44:23 : The people are taught to discern between the unclean and the clean; that is what the laws were instituted for. Genesis 7:21-23 taught in Genesis 5-8 - This was the first time the Most High destroyed the earth for the wickedness that was being done. The flood came because they despised the commandments; destruction came because of sin. - Of them that dwelt in the world only Noah and his household were left, of whom came all righteous men: through Shem's seed to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and through their line the Israelites. - The breath of life is twofold. One is the commandments, which were given to Adam; the other is the breathing life, the oxygen. Here everything on the dry land that breathed died; the fish were not touched. Genesis 8:20-22 taught in Genesis 5-8 - Noah built an altar and offered burnt offerings of every clean beast and every clean fowl, and the Most High smelled a sweet savour and said He would not again curse the ground any more for man's sake. Genesis 9:3 taught in Genesis 9-12 - This is the introduction of man eating meat. The Most High did not give man a new stomach; the body was already made for it and it lay dormant until after the flood. - Having the liberty to eat meat does not mean eating without balance; be not too greedy upon meats, for excess of meats brings sickness. - The law of what may be eaten was already understood; you could not eat everything. The doctrine that says you can pray over anything and eat it is a seducing spirit and a doctrine of devils. - Fish is meat; all flesh is not the same flesh, but the flesh of beasts, of fishes, and of birds are all flesh. Every creature of God is good for what it was made for, and it is sanctified by the word of God, and the word that sanctifies what may be eaten is the dietary law. - Precept Leviticus 11:46-47 : The law of the beasts makes a difference between the beast that may be eaten and the beast that may not be eaten. Genesis 9:4 taught in Genesis 9-12 - The law against eating flesh with the blood was given to Adam and is still in place with Noah; the word is true from the beginning. Exodus Exodus 4:24-26 taught in Exodus 2-5 - By the way in the inn, the LORD met him, and sought to kill him, because Moses had not circumcised his son. Zipporah took a sharp stone, cut off the foreskin of her son, and said, Surely a bloody husband art thou to me: bloody because of the circumcision she had to perform herself. - This shows the laws did not begin at Sinai. Circumcision was the covenant given to Abraham for every man child in his generations, on the eighth day, and the uncircumcised man child whose flesh is not circumcised, that soul shall be cut off from his people: he hath broken my covenant. That is why Moses was worthy of death. - The covenant still stands. A son of Israel must be circumcised; and a man that comes to the truth grown must still be circumcised, even at forty, fifty, or sixty years, as Abraham himself was circumcised at ninety and nine, and as Paul circumcised Timothy, whose father was a Greek. Nothing that defileth enters the kingdom. - The Egyptians did not practice circumcision; they were a nation of uncleanness, and the covenant was between the Lord and Israel: after the doings of the land of Egypt, wherein ye dwelt, shall ye not do. - Romans 2 does not do away with circumcision of the flesh. Circumcision verily profiteth if thou keep the law: the Jews who grew up circumcised and keeping the law, yet broke it, made their circumcision uncircumcision; and the uncircumcised of the cast-off northern kingdom who keep the righteousness of the law are counted as circumcised. Circumcision of the heart is putting away the evil of the doings, as the prophets say, take away the foreskins of your heart; the scribes and Pharisees were clean on the outside of the cup but full of iniquity within. - Precept Leviticus 12:1-3 : In the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised; the law Moses himself later carried to Israel. - Precept Revelation 21:27 : There shall in no wise enter into it any thing that defileth; the unclean do not enter the kingdom. Exodus 21:28-29 taught in Exodus 18-21 - If an ox gore a man or a woman that they die, the ox is stoned and his flesh not eaten, and the owner is quit. But if the ox were wont to push with his horns in time past, and it hath been testified to his owner, and he hath not kept him in, and it kill a man or a woman, the ox is stoned and his owner also put to death. - Most do not have oxen today, but the same judgment reaches the yard dogs, the pit bulls, German shepherds, and rottweilers. If the dog has bitten before and it was reported to you, and it gets out again through a snapped chain or a breach in the fence and mauls or kills somebody, the scripture holds the owner responsible unto death; that is why animal control writes the ticket and warns you to keep your dogs in. - The law is slack right now, as Habakkuk says, so many punishments worthy of death in the scriptures, like rape or this judgment, come out today as a fine or a slap on the hand. Exodus 25:3-7 taught in Exodus 22-25 - The badgers' skins settle a confusion: the Lord commanded Israel to handle animal skins and hair to build his own tabernacle. So the laws about not touching that which is defiled, the carcass of the unclean beast, go into the matter of sacrifice and coming into the temple, not into everyday handling. A boar-bristle brush is not sin; brush your hair, brothers. Exodus 26:7-14 taught in Exodus 26-29 - The badgers' skins settle a doctrine question. Leviticus 11 says not to touch the carcase of the unclean beast, and the badger goes on paws, yet the tabernacle had to be built with badger skins by hand. The law goes into sacrificing the unclean thing and eating it, touching it with your mouth; it is not saying a dead animal in your path cannot be moved out of the way with your hands. - Precept Leviticus 11:8 : The carcase not to be touched is spoken of the beasts as food; the command sits in the dietary law. - Precept Leviticus 11:27 : Whatsoever goeth upon his paws is unclean, which is what makes the badger an unclean beast. Exodus 29:29-34 taught in Exodus 26-29 - The holy garments of Aaron pass to his sons after him, to be anointed and consecrated in them; the son that is priest in his stead shall put them on seven days when he cometh into the tabernacle to minister. - Aaron and his sons eat the flesh of the ram and the bread at the door of the tabernacle, the things wherewith the atonement was made; a stranger shall not eat thereof, because they are holy. And whatever of the flesh or the bread remains unto the morning is burnt with fire and not eaten: no eating the leftovers of the offering, because it is holy. Exodus 30:17-21 taught in Exodus 30-33 - Aaron and his sons washed their hands and their feet thereat when they went into the tabernacle of the congregation and when they came near to the altar to minister, that they die not; the priests could not go in unclean. Leviticus Leviticus 5:2-3 taught in Leviticus 2-5 - Touching any unclean thing, the carcase of an unclean beast or the uncleanness of man, leaves a soul unclean and guilty. This goes into eating, not mere contact; the classes have touched on this already, and it stands. - The touching itself pertained to the sacrifice: Israel was separated from their uncleanness that they die not when they defile the tabernacle, so a man that had touched the unclean thing could not come in to sacrifice. There is no more sacrifice, so the touching-defilement laws do not apply today; a brush of boar bristles is not sin. Leviticus 6:19-23 taught in Leviticus 6-9 - This is the offering of Aaron and of his sons in the day when he is anointed: the tenth part of an ephah of fine flour for a meat offering perpetual, half in the morning and half at night, baked with oil in a pan. The meat offering is again actual flour, grain. - Every meat offering for the priest was wholly burnt; it was not eaten. The priest's own offering went completely to the Lord. Leviticus 7:19-21 taught in Leviticus 6-9 - The flesh that touched any unclean thing was not eaten but burnt with fire, and the soul that ate of the peace offerings having his uncleanness upon him was cut off from his people. An unclean man coming into the tabernacle to sacrifice or a priest eating unclean was facing death before the Lord. - All the touching of unclean and defiled things pertains to sacrifice: the point of the uncleanness laws was to separate the children of Israel from their uncleanness, that they die not when they defile the tabernacle. There is no more sacrifice, so those defilement laws do not apply today; a brother can brush his hair with a brush of boar bristles, because that law was about coming in to sacrifice. Leviticus 10:8-11 taught in Leviticus 10-13 - They had to be sober minded because they taught the people the difference between the holy and profane and caused them to discern between the unclean and the clean, and in controversy they stood in judgment, judging according to the judgments of the Most High. - Precept Ezekiel 44:23-24 : They teach the difference between the holy and profane and stand in judgment in controversy; the priest must be sober dealing with the people. Leviticus 11:1-3 taught in Leviticus 10-13 - Leviticus 11 tells you what you can and cannot eat. Among all the beasts of the earth, ye shall eat whatsoever parteth the hoof, and is clovenfooted, and cheweth the cud. - Chewing the cud means the animal has more than one stomach: it chews its food, brings it back up into its mouth to be chewed again, and then digests it through another stomach. Leviticus 11:4-8 taught in Leviticus 10-13 - Both marks must be present. There are animals that chew the cud and animals that divide the hoof but do not have both; those are unclean. The camel cheweth the cud but divideth not the hoof: you cannot eat camel. - The coney is the pika, a small mountain dwelling mammal that resembles its close relative the rabbit, found at heights among the highest of any mammal. The scriptures already had it right: the rocks are a refuge for the conies, and the conies, a feeble folk, make their houses in the rocks. You cannot eat coney, and the hare likewise is unclean. - The swine has only the one mark: he divideth the hoof and is clovenfooted, yet he cheweth not the cud; he is unclean unto you. You cannot eat pork; leave it alone. - Their carcase shall ye not touch sits inside the dietary law: it goes into sacrificing the unclean thing and eating it, touching it with the mouth. It does not mean a dead animal in your path cannot be moved out of the way with the hands; the tabernacle itself had to be built by hand with badgers' skins. Leviticus 11:9-12 taught in Leviticus 10-13 - Of all that are in the waters, ye shall eat whatsoever hath fins and scales; whatever has not fins and scales is an abomination. No shrimp, no crab, no lobster, no bottom dwellers. - The Most High gave an excellent dietary law: high blood pressure and the like come from eating shellfish. He made these animals and knows what they do; if you eat what he allowed you will be fine. It is simple: if it does not have both fins and scales, leave it alone. Leviticus 11:13-19 taught in Leviticus 10-13 - These are the fowls in abomination that shall not be eaten: the eagle, the ossifrage, the osprey, the vulture and the kite after his kind, every raven after his kind, the owl, the nighthawk, the cuckow, the hawk, the little owl, the cormorant, the great owl, the swan, the pelican, the gier eagle, the stork, the heron after her kind, the lapwing, and the bat. - On duck: the swan's closest relatives include the geese and ducks. The swan is unclean, and duck falls in the family of the swan, so you cannot eat duck; they are related, and it is the same thing. Leviticus 11:20-23 taught in Leviticus 10-13 - All fowls that creep, going upon all four, are an abomination, yet those which have legs above their feet to leap withal upon the earth may be eaten: the locust, the bald locust, the beetle, and the grasshopper after his kind. You can eat locusts; John the Baptist ate locusts. Leviticus 11:24-28 taught in Leviticus 10-13 - The carcases of every beast which divideth the hoof and is not clovenfooted nor cheweth the cud are unclean; whoever touches them is unclean until the even, and whoever bears the carcase washes his clothes. - Whatsoever goeth upon his paws, among all manner of beasts that go on all four, is unclean: you cannot eat mountain lion, tiger, cougar, gorilla, dog, or cat; they have paws and walk on all fours. Leviticus 11:29-38 taught in Leviticus 10-13 - These creeping things are unclean: the weasel, the mouse, the tortoise after his kind, the ferret, the chameleon, the lizard, the snail, and the mole. You cannot eat tortoise. - Whatever vessel one of them falls into when dead is unclean until the even and must be put into water; if it falls into one of your pots, clean that pot out and cook nothing in it until the even. An earthen vessel it falls into is broken and thrown out, and ovens and ranges for pots are broken down. - If any part of their carcase falls on sowing seed which is to be sown, the seed is clean; but if water be put upon the seed and the carcase fall thereon, it is unclean and no good. Leviticus 11:39-43 taught in Leviticus 10-13 - Even of a beast which ye may eat, if it die of itself, he that toucheth, eateth of, or beareth the carcase is unclean until the even and washes his clothes. - Every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth is an abomination: whatsoever goeth upon the belly, whatsoever goeth upon all four, and whatsoever hath more feet. You cannot eat centipedes and millipedes. Leviticus 11:44-47 taught in Leviticus 10-13 - Sanctify yourselves, and ye shall be holy, for I am holy: for I am the Lord that bringeth you up out of the land of Egypt to be your God. This is the law of the beast and of the fowl and of every living creature that moveth in the waters and of every creature that creepeth upon the earth; the Most High explained everything and then summed it all up, to make a difference between the unclean and the clean, and between the beast that may be eaten and the beast that may not be eaten. - Precept 1 Timothy 4:4-5 : Every creature received with thanksgiving is sanctified by the word of God; the word of God sanctified the clean beasts of Leviticus 11. Leviticus 12:1-2 taught in Leviticus 10-13 - If a woman have conceived seed and born a man child, she shall be unclean seven days, according to the days of the separation for her infirmity. Conceived seed means the sperm has met the egg: at intercourse about 300 million sperm enter, most die on the journey, and fertilization is one sperm uniting with the egg to form new life. All of that has to happen; that is conceiving seed. - Precept Leviticus 15:19 : If a woman have an issue of blood she shall be put apart seven days; those are the days of the separation. Leviticus 12:4 taught in Leviticus 10-13 - She shall then continue in the blood of her purifying three and thirty days: seven days of separation plus thirty three days is forty days. If she has a male child she is unclean forty days, touching no hallowed thing and coming not into the sanctuary until the days of her purifying be fulfilled. Leviticus 12:5 taught in Leviticus 10-13 - If she bear a maid child, she shall be unclean two weeks, as in her separation, and continue in the blood of her purifying threescore and six days: fourteen days plus sixty six days is eighty days for a daughter. Leviticus 13:1-8 taught in Leviticus 10-13 - The plague of leprosy is discerned by the priest. When the hair in the plague is turned white and the plague in sight is deeper than the skin of the flesh, it is a plague of leprosy and the priest pronounces him unclean; if not, the priest shuts him up seven days, and seven days more if the plague is at a stay, and if the plague is somewhat dark and spread not, it is but a scab and he is pronounced clean; but a scab that spreads much abroad after his cleansing is a leprosy. Leviticus 13:29-30 taught in Leviticus 10-13 - For a plague upon the head or the beard, if it be in sight deeper than the skin, and there be in it a yellow thin hair, it is a dry scall, even a leprosy upon the head or beard, and the priest pronounces him unclean. Leviticus 13:45-46 taught in Leviticus 10-13 - The leper in whom the plague is, his clothes shall be rent, his head bare, a covering upon his upper lip, and he shall cry, Unclean, unclean; all the days the plague is in him he is defiled, and he shall dwell alone, without the camp. Leviticus 13:47-52 taught in Leviticus 10-13 - The plague of leprosy can be in a garment, woollen or linen, in the warp or woof or in any thing made of skin, greenish or reddish; it is shewed unto the priest and shut up seven days, and if the plague be spread in the garment it is a fretting leprosy: the garment is burnt in the fire. As with Miriam, the clothing wherein the plague is had to be dealt with. Leviticus 13:53-59 taught in Leviticus 10-13 - If the plague be not spread, the thing is washed and shut up seven days more; if the plague have not changed his colour it is burnt, and if it be somewhat dark after washing, the piece is rent out; if it appear still, it is a spreading plague and burnt with fire; and the garment that the plague departs from is washed the second time and shall be clean. This is the law of the plague of leprosy in a garment, to pronounce it clean or to pronounce it unclean. Leviticus 14:33-42 taught in Leviticus 14-15 - The priest commands that the house be emptied before he goes in, that all that is in it be not made unclean; then he looks on the plague, and if it be in the walls with hollow strakes, greenish or reddish, in sight lower than the wall, he shuts up the house seven days. - If at the seventh day the plague be spread in the walls, the stones in which the plague is are taken away and cast into an unclean place without the city; the house is scraped within round about, the dust poured out without the city into an unclean place, and other stones and other mortar are put in their place. Leviticus 14:43-47 taught in Leviticus 14-15 - If the plague come again and break out in the house after the stones were taken away and the house scraped and plastered, the priest looks, and if the plague be spread, it is a fretting leprosy in the house: it is unclean. - He breaks down the house, the stones of it, the timber, and all the mortar, and carries them forth out of the city into an unclean place. He that goes into the house while it is shut up is unclean until the even, and he that lies or eats in the house washes his clothes. Leviticus 14:54-57 taught in Leviticus 14-15 - The chapter closes the summary: this is the law for all manner of plague of leprosy and scall, for the leprosy of a garment and of a house, for a rising, a scab, and a bright spot, to teach when it is unclean and when it is clean. This is the law of leprosy. Leviticus 15:1-12 taught in Leviticus 14-15 - When any man hath a running issue out of his flesh, because of his issue he is unclean, whether his flesh run with his issue or be stopped from his issue. - Every bed whereon he lies and every thing whereon he sits is unclean. Whoever touches his bed, sits where he sat, touches his flesh, or is touched by him before he has rinsed his hands, washes his clothes, bathes himself in water, and is unclean until the even; the same goes for his spittle and his saddle. Leviticus 15:16-18 taught in Leviticus 14-15 - If any man's seed of copulation go out from him, he washes all his flesh in water and is unclean until the even; every garment and every skin whereon is the seed is washed with water and unclean until the even. - The woman also with whom a man lies with seed of copulation: they both bathe themselves in water and are unclean until the even. Leviticus 15:19-24 taught in Leviticus 14-15 - When a woman has an issue, and her issue in her flesh be blood, she is put apart seven days for her separation, and whosoever toucheth her is unclean until the even. - Every thing that she lies upon or sits upon in her separation is unclean; whoever touches her bed or any thing she sat upon washes his clothes, bathes himself in water, and is unclean until the even. - If any man lie with her at all, and her flowers be upon him, he is unclean seven days, and all the bed whereon he lies is unclean. Leviticus 15:25-27 taught in Leviticus 14-15 - If a woman have an issue of her blood many days out of the time of her separation, or if it run beyond the time of her separation, all the days of the issue of her uncleanness are as the days of her separation: she is unclean. - Every bed she lies on and every thing she sits upon in those days is as the uncleanness of her separation, and whosoever touches those things washes his clothes, bathes in water, and is unclean until the even. Leviticus 15:31-33 taught in Leviticus 14-15 - This is the law of him that hath an issue, of him whose seed goeth from him, of her that is sick of her flowers, of him and her that have issues, and of him that lieth with her that is unclean. Leviticus 18:19 taught in Leviticus 18-21 - A woman put apart for her uncleanness is a woman in her menstrual cycle. A man must wait the appointed seven days, and if the issue runs beyond, wait again; Leviticus 15 details these laws of uncleanness, taught in the previous class. - Precept Leviticus 15:19 : The law of her separation: she shall be put apart seven days. Leviticus 19:23-25 taught in Leviticus 18-21 - Fruit of a newly planted tree was counted as uncircumcised for three years and not eaten; in the fourth year all the fruit was holy to praise the Lord withal; only in the fifth year could the fruit be eaten, that it might yield its increase. Leviticus 20:17-21 taught in Leviticus 18-21 - The man that takes his sister and sees her nakedness, it is a wicked thing; they are cut off in the sight of their people, and he bears his iniquity. - The man that lies with a woman having her sickness, her menstrual cycle, has discovered her fountain, and both are cut off from among their people; this goes with the laws of Leviticus 15. - The nakedness of the mother's sister and the father's sister is near kin; they bear their iniquity. He that lies with his uncle's wife or takes his brother's wife, they shall die childless. - Precept Leviticus 15:19 : The law of the woman put apart in her issue; chapter 20 judges what chapter 15 defines. Leviticus 20:25-26 taught in Leviticus 18-21 - Put difference between clean beasts and unclean, and between unclean fowls and clean; this goes back to Leviticus 11, the dietary laws. No shrimp, crab, lobster, pork, catfish, and the like; everything is not clean, whatever the church teaches. Leviticus 21:1-4 taught in Leviticus 18-21 - The priests had to remain clean to administer the priesthood, for anyone unclean that approached the sanctuary was put to death; a chief man among his people was not to profane himself. Leviticus 22:4-9 taught in Leviticus 22-25 - A man of the seed of Aaron that was a leper, had a running issue, or touched any unclean thing could not eat of the holy things until he was clean: he washed his flesh with water, and when the sun was down he was clean and could afterward eat. Leviticus 27:9-13 taught in Leviticus 26-27 - An unclean beast, one with a blemish that could not be sacrificed, was presented before the priest and the priest valued it, good or bad; and to redeem it, a fifth part had to be added to the estimation to get that beast back. Leviticus 27:26-29 taught in Leviticus 26-27 - The firstling of the beasts could not be sanctified by any man, because as a firstling it was the Lord's already, whether ox or sheep; an unclean firstling was redeemed by the estimation with the fifth part added, or sold according to the estimation.
