Numbers Numbers 4:7-14 taught in Numbers 3-6 - Badger skin is something we would consider unclean today, yet the Lord had his holy things covered in it. Under the law of sacrifice, defilement came by touching unclean things to eat them; touching them to make something for the tabernacle still left you unclean until sundown, unable to sacrifice, but the skins themselves served the sanctuary. Numbers 6:6-8 taught in Numbers 3-6 - All the days of his separation he came at no dead body, and made not himself unclean even for his father, his mother, his brother, or his sister when they died, because the consecration of his God was upon his head. It was a heavy thing to fall under the Nazarite vow; you had to separate yourself from everybody, even family, so you would not be defiled. Numbers 9:9-12 taught in Numbers 7-10 - The answer came: if any man be unclean by reason of a dead body, or be in a journey afar off, he shall still keep the passover unto the Lord, on the fourteenth day of the second month at even, eating it with unleavened bread and bitter herbs. Numbers 18:15-17 taught in Numbers 15-18 - Every thing that openeth the matrix in all flesh, whether of men or beasts, was the Lord's; the firstborn was to be offered. Nevertheless the firstborn of man was surely redeemed, because you would not sacrifice the firstborn of our people, and the firstling of unclean beasts was redeemed also. Numbers 19:10 taught in Numbers 19-22 - After the priest burns the red heifer and sprinkles her blood, one that is clean gathers up her ashes; even that clean man must wash his clothes and be unclean until the evening. Numbers 19:11 taught in Numbers 19-22 - Any man that touches the dead body of any man is unclean seven days. There is history on this law: in Numbers 9 certain men were defiled by a dead body around the passover and could not keep it on that day because of this very statute. - The Most High answered through Moses with a second keeping: the man unclean by reason of a dead body, or far off on a journey, keeps the passover the fourteenth day of the second month at even, eating it with unleavened bread and bitter herbs. - Precept Numbers 9:10-11 : The unclean by a dead body or far off on a journey keep the passover the fourteenth day of the second month with unleavened bread and bitter herbs. Numbers 19:12-13 taught in Numbers 19-22 - The unclean man purifies himself with the water of separation on the third day and on the seventh day, and then he is clean; if he purifies not himself the third day, then the seventh day he shall not be clean. Numbers 19:14-22 taught in Numbers 19-22 - This is the law when a man dies in a tent: all that come into the tent and all that is in the tent are unclean seven days, and every open vessel with no covering bound upon it is unclean. - For the unclean person they take of the ashes of the burnt heifer of purification for sin, with running water in a vessel; a clean person dips hyssop in the water and sprinkles the tent, the vessels, and the persons on the third day and on the seventh day, and on the seventh day he washes his clothes, bathes in water, and is clean at even. - The man that stays unclean and will not purify himself is cut off from among the congregation, because he has defiled the sanctuary of the Lord. - Chapter 19 as a whole gives the water of separation, which is the purification for sin: the first half gives the specifics of the sacrifice and what the priest must do, and the rest gives the examples of how a man becomes unclean, whether by sin, by touching the dead, or by being around the dead. Numbers 30:1-2 taught in Numbers 27-30 - A vow is promising the Lord you will do a thing. Say a man vows, Lord, if you bring this to pass I will never eat swine again; he must keep that vow, and he cannot go back on it and simply ask forgiveness afterward. Numbers 31:19-24 taught in Numbers 31-34 - Whoever killed any person or touched any slain had to abide without the camp seven days and purify himself and his captives on the third day and on the seventh day. That is the law going back to Numbers 5:2, putting the defiled outside the camp. - Purifying the raiment, all that is made of skins, all work of goats' hair, and all things made of wood goes back to the law of purification in Numbers 19. - Eleazar the priest gave the ordinance: gold, silver, brass, iron, tin, and lead, everything that may abide the fire, goes through the fire and is purified with the water of separation; whatever abides not the fire goes through the water; and on the seventh day they wash their clothes, are clean, and come into the camp. - Precept Numbers 19:11-12 : He that touches the dead purifies himself on the third day and on the seventh day; the men of war purified themselves by that law. Deuteronomy Deuteronomy 4:14-16 taught in Deuteronomy 3-6 - No similitude means he spoke plainly and clearly, not in dark speeches: when the commandments were given there was no arguing over what they meant. Fringes on the borders of the garments, no swine, thou shalt not kill; it was simple and easy to understand. Deuteronomy 12:15 taught in Deuteronomy 11-14 - The unclean and the clean that may eat thereof are unclean and clean persons, not unclean meats; Israel had servants then and will have servants again. - Precept Deuteronomy 15:22 : The unclean and the clean person shall eat it alike, as the roebuck and as the hart; the unclean and clean here are persons. Deuteronomy 14:3 taught in Deuteronomy 11-14 - The chapter then lists the clean beasts, the beasts that part the hoof and chew the cud, the fish with fins and scales, and the clean fowls; the rest of chapter 14 is clear cut on the laws of the clean and the unclean foods. - Precept Deuteronomy 12:15 : Whatsoever thy soul lusteth after, as of the roebuck and as of the hart: the lusting of the soul is bounded by the clean beasts of this chapter. Deuteronomy 15:19-23 taught in Deuteronomy 15-18 - If there be any blemish therein, as if it be lame or blind, thou shalt not sacrifice it unto the Lord thy God; thou shalt eat it within thy gates, the unclean and the clean person alike, as the roebuck and as the hart. Deuteronomy 23:10-11 taught in Deuteronomy 23-26 - Any man that was not clean by reason of uncleanness that chanceth him by night went abroad out of the camp; when evening came he washed himself with water, and when the sun was down he came into the camp again. - Precept Leviticus 15:16 : The law of the uncleanness that chanceth a man by night: he shall wash all his flesh in water and be unclean until the even. Deuteronomy 23:12-14 taught in Deuteronomy 23-26 - Verse 14 explains why: the Lord thy God walketh in the midst of thy camp, to deliver thee and to give up thine enemies before thee; therefore shall thy camp be holy, that he see no unclean thing in thee and turn away from thee. - That is what we just read happened with Achan the son of Carmi: he brought an unclean thing into the camp, and the Most High turned from Israel in battle. - God says he is in the midst of Israel and none else; the Lord would go before us and fight our battles, and that is why he wanted no unclean thing in the camp, for we are holy and the camp was to be holy. Deuteronomy 28:18 taught in Deuteronomy 27-30 - Cursed shall be the fruit of thy land, thy kine, and thy sheep: the food we eat is cursed. Fast food fills our neighborhoods, and where there is no fast food there is a corner store selling unclean meat that causes diseases in us. Joshua Joshua 8:34-35 taught in Joshua 5-8 - How do you become blessed? Read the last page of the book: blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life. A few verses before your Bible says the end, it says keep the commandments, so no man in his right mind can say the laws are done away with; that is justifying wickedness. Keep the sabbath holy, leave the swine alone, dress in modesty, and keep the commandments if you want the blessings. Joshua 22:19-20 taught in Joshua 21-24 - They even offered their own land: if the land of your possession be unclean, pass ye over unto the land of the possession of the Lord and take possession among us, close by where we can keep an eye on you; only rebel not against the Lord, nor build you an altar beside the altar of the Lord our God. Judges Judges 13:4-5 taught in Judges 13-16 - The angel commanded the mother herself to drink no wine nor strong drink and to eat no unclean thing, because the child would be a Nazarite unto God from the womb; even in the womb he was to be kept pure. Judges 13:6-7 taught in Judges 13-16 - She repeated the message: the child shall be a Nazarite to God from the womb to the day of his death, and she was to drink no wine nor strong drink nor eat any unclean thing. Judges 13:11-14 taught in Judges 13-16 - Manoah arose and went after his wife, came to the man, and asked, art thou the man that spakest unto the woman? He said, I am. - Manoah asked how they should order the child and what they should do unto him, and the angel reiterated the instructions he had already given: of all that I said unto the woman let her beware, and all that I commanded her let her observe while she carries this son.

title: Esau and Edom
text: Esau and Edom The lineage teaching on Esau and his descendants, from the birthright through the kings of Edom. Genesis Genesis 3:14 taught in Genesis 1-4 - Going on the belly and eating dust means the serpent was brought to a very low estate, made like a vagabond upon the earth. Cain became a vagabond upon the earth, and so did Esau. Genesis 14:4-11 taught in Genesis 13-16 - The five kings served Chedorlaomer twelve years and rebelled in the thirteenth; the four kings defeated them and took the goods of Sodom and Gomorrah. - The vale of Siddim was full of slimepits: bitumen, tar, petroleum. The same region is rich in oil to this day. Genesis 22:15-18 taught in Genesis 21-24 - The seed possessing the gate of his enemies is part of the covenant: the seed of Jacob shall possess the remnant of Edom and of all the heathen, and Edom shall be a possession. That is why all nations cannot be inside this covenant; the covenant has Israel possessing their enemies. - Precept Amos 9:11-12 : The tabernacle of David is raised up, that they may possess the remnant of Edom and of all the heathen. - Precept Numbers 24:17-18 : A Star out of Jacob and a Sceptre out of Israel; Edom shall be a possession, and Israel shall do valiantly. Genesis 24:58-60 taught in Genesis 21-24 - The covenant narrows again here: it runs through Rebekah's children, and of her two sons it is Jacob who carries it, for Esau sold his birthright. The covenants in Genesis cannot be broken. Genesis 25:22-23 taught in Genesis 24-27 - The whole scripture is good set against evil: the godly against the sinner, Jacob against Esau, righteousness against sin. Two powerful forces were being born into the earth, and the struggle began in the womb. Genesis 25:24-26 taught in Genesis 24-27 - The first came out red, all over like an hairy garment, and they called his name Esau. The scriptures describe the man because a nation comes from him; this teaching identifies Esau's seed with the red, hairy, melanin-lacking people of the world today. - Jacob's hand took hold on Esau's heel, and that is prophecy: Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth. When Esau's rulership is done, Jacob comes into power; that is how we know the times. - Precept 2 Esdras 6:7-9 : Jacob's hand held first the heel of Esau; Esau is the end of the world and Jacob the beginning of it that followeth. Genesis 25:27-28 taught in Genesis 24-27 - Esau was a cunning hunter, a man of the field; Jacob was a plain man, dwelling in tents. The Most High gives you the characteristics of the man so the nation can be known. - Isaac loved Esau because he did eat of his venison, but Rebekah loved Jacob, because the Lord had told her the prophecy that the younger was the chosen. Genesis 25:29-34 taught in Genesis 24-27 - Esau sold his birthright for red pottage; therefore was his name called Edom, red. He said, What profit shall this birthright do to me, and sware it away for a meal. - Thus Esau despised his birthright. Jacob is called a supplanter, but the supplanting was of the Holy Ghost; Esau gave the birthright away himself. Genesis 26:34-35 taught in Genesis 24-27 - Esau at forty took wives of the Hittites, and they were a grief of mind unto Isaac and to Rebekah. He went straight against the fathers' law of marrying within the kindred; that is the nature of the vessel. Genesis 27:1-4 taught in Genesis 24-27 - Isaac's eyes were dim so that he could not see, and the Lord allowed that blindness for a purpose: so that the blessing could pass to Jacob. What looks like evil can be for good, as Joseph's slavery in Egypt was for good. Genesis 27:5-13 taught in Genesis 24-27 - Rebekah heard and moved for Jacob because she carried the word from the Lord: the elder shall serve the younger. She knew the blessing belonged to Jacob by prophecy, and she took the curse upon herself: Upon me be thy curse, my son; only obey my voice. Genesis 27:15-23 taught in Genesis 24-27 - Rebekah put Esau's raiment on Jacob and the skins of the kids of the goats upon his hands and neck, and Isaac discerned him not: the voice is Jacob's voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau. Genesis 27:34-38 taught in Genesis 24-27 - Esau cried with a great and exceeding bitter cry and begged, Bless me, even me also, O my father. But he had already sold the birthright and never dealt rightly with Jacob about it; he wanted the blessing anyway. - Esau found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears. He that despised the birthright for one morsel of meat was rejected when he would have inherited the blessing. - Precept Hebrews 12:16-17 : Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright, was rejected and found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears. Genesis 27:39-40 taught in Genesis 24-27 - Esau's portion: the fatness of the earth and the dew of heaven from above, and by thy sword shalt thou live. Esau's kingdoms have gotten what they have through war; his living is by the sword, by ever more advanced weaponry, and the nations are overcome and awed by it. - And it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck: this is the time period now, where Esau has the dominion and rules first, and when his rule is done, Jacob comes into power. - Precept Revelation 13:13-14 : He maketh fire come down from heaven in the sight of men and deceiveth them that dwell on the earth by those wonders; the sword Esau lives by. Genesis 27:41-46 taught in Genesis 24-27 - Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing and purposed in his heart to slay him, the same hatred Cain had for Abel. Good against evil runs from the beginning of the book to the end. - Rebekah sent Jacob to Laban her brother until Esau's fury turned away, and said she was weary of her life because of the daughters of Heth: if Jacob take a wife of the daughters of the land, what good shall my life do me? Marrying the sons and daughters within the kindred is a weighty matter to the mothers of Israel. Genesis 28:5 taught in Genesis 28-31 - Jacob was sent to Laban, the son of Bethuel the Syrian, the brother of Rebekah. Rebekah herself was born to Bethuel, son of Milcah, the wife of Nahor, Abraham's brother; the family line was kept in place, generation after generation going back to their own kindred. Genesis 28:6-9 taught in Genesis 28-31 - Esau saw that the daughters of Canaan pleased not Isaac his father, but instead of following Jacob's path he went to Ishmael and took Mahalath to add to the wives he had. He answered his father's grief by doing his own thing. - Esau had already taken Hittite wives that were a grief of mind unto Isaac and Rebekah, and his generations show wives of the daughters of Canaan. He was hardheaded from the beginning; that is the spirit of the wicked, who hate instruction and cast the words of the Most High behind them. - Precept Genesis 26:34-35 : Esau's Hittite wives were a grief of mind unto Isaac and Rebekah. - Precept Genesis 36:2-3 : Esau's generations confirm he took wives of the daughters of Canaan and of Ishmael. - Precept Psalms 50:16-17 : Unto the wicked God saith, Thou hatest instruction, and castest my words behind thee; that is Esau's spirit. Genesis 32:3-7 taught in Genesis 32-35 - Jacob sent messengers to Esau, and they returned saying Esau was coming with four hundred men, and Jacob was greatly afraid and distressed. - His fear was rightful: the last word he had of Esau was that Esau purposed in his heart to slay him once their father's mourning came. The hatred began at the blessing, and the scriptures show in Ezekiel that the hatred never ended. - Precept Genesis 27:41-42 : Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing and said in his heart, I will slay my brother Jacob; that was the last report Jacob had. Genesis 32:9-12 taught in Genesis 32-35 - Jacob prayed humbly: I am not worthy of the least of all the mercies; deliver me from the hand of my brother. He was not too proud to confess his fear to the Most High. - He pleaded the covenant: thou saidst, I will make thy seed as the sand of the sea. That is the pattern for our prayers; plead the promise made to the fathers and ask the Most High to remember His covenant. Genesis 32:13-20 taught in Genesis 32-35 - Jacob sent droves of livestock ahead as a present, spaced apart, each servant instructed what to say. He said, I will appease him with the present that goeth before me. He moved strategically to soften Esau before they met face to face. Genesis 33:1-4 taught in Genesis 32-35 - Jacob bowed himself to the ground seven times as he came near, and Esau ran, embraced him, fell on his neck, and kissed him, and they wept. - That embrace is not proof that the hatred was gone. Jacob had prayed for deliverance, and when a man's ways please the Lord, He maketh even his enemies to be at peace with him; the Most High put that peace on Esau in that moment. - Precept Proverbs 16:7 : When a man's ways please the Lord, He maketh even his enemies to be at peace with him; that is what happened with Esau. Genesis 33:5-11 taught in Genesis 32-35 - Jacob presented the children which God graciously gave thy servant, and urged the present on Esau until he took it. Receiving the gift sealed the peace; Jacob wanted the assurance. Genesis 33:12-16 taught in Genesis 32-35 - Esau offered to travel together and to leave some of his four hundred men, and Jacob declined both, pleading the tender children and the young flocks: I will lead on softly. He stayed wise and kept his distance, and Esau returned that day to Seir. Genesis 35:1-4 taught in Genesis 32-35 - Before going up to Bethel, Jacob told his household, Put away the strange gods that are among you, and be clean. The strange gods were there because Rachel had stolen her father's images and hidden them, sitting on them when Laban searched. - Idolatry hidden in the household must be put away before you can stand at Bethel. Rachel finally gave up the images, and Jacob hid them under the oak by Shechem. - From Eve to Rachel the scriptures warn how sin enters through the household; of the woman came the beginning of sin. Sisters, stay in the spirit and guard against the serpent's beguiling as the mothers were beguiled. Genesis 35:22 taught in Genesis 32-35 - The judgment followed him: forasmuch as he defiled his father's bed, his birthright was given unto the sons of Joseph, and the genealogy is not reckoned after the birthright. The firstborn lost the birthright over it. - Precept 1 Chronicles 5:1 : Reuben was the firstborn, but because he defiled his father's bed his birthright was given unto the sons of Joseph. Genesis 35:27-29 taught in Genesis 32-35 - Isaac gave up the ghost at an hundred and fourscore years, old and full of days, and his sons Esau and Jacob together buried him. Genesis 36:1 taught in Genesis 36-39 - Now these are the generations of Esau, who is Edom. Esau is Edom, and this teaching identifies Edom with the people called the white man today. - Esau came out of the womb red, all over like an hairy garment; his blood could be seen through his skin for lack of melanin, and his name Esau goes into wasted away. Jacob was not described, because Jacob looked like everyone from Adam down to his time; the man of melanin needed no description. - Esau was called Edom, which means red, because he sold his birthright for that same red pottage. - Precept Genesis 25:24-26 : The first came out red, all over like an hairy garment; the twins were two nations, polar opposites. - Precept Genesis 25:30 : Feed me with that same red pottage; therefore was his name called Edom, which is red. Genesis 36:2-5 taught in Genesis 36-39 - Esau took his wives of the daughters of Canaan and of Ishmael. He was the first of the Edomites; there were no women of his nation yet, so his lineage began through those wives. Genesis is Bereshith, the beginning of nations. Genesis 36:6-8 taught in Genesis 36-39 - Esau went from the face of his brother because their riches were more than that they might dwell together, the same as with Abram and Lot in Genesis 13. Esau was rich at this time, out of the house of Isaac and Abraham. - Thus dwelt Esau in mount Seir. Mount Seir is the clefts of the rock; the vision of Obadiah speaks to Edom as thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, whose pride hath deceived him. - Precept Obadiah 1:3 : The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee, thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock; that is Edom in mount Seir. Genesis 36:9-11 taught in Genesis 36-39 - Esau is the father of the Edomites in mount Seir, and his grandson Teman, son of Eliphaz, is identified in this teaching with Germany; the reference work Edom and Germany lays that connection out. - The prophecy over Teman stands: the wise men shall be destroyed out of Edom and understanding out of the mount of Esau, and the mighty men of Teman shall be dismayed. Much of the world's science and weapons technology has come out of Germany, and the word says that wisdom will be destroyed. - Precept Obadiah 1:8-9 : The wise men of Edom and the mighty men of Teman shall be destroyed, that every one of the mount of Esau may be cut off. Genesis 36:12 taught in Genesis 36-39 - Timna was concubine to Eliphaz, and she bare Amalek. Amalek came of a concubine, a lesser wife, which is why the word bastard is studied here: in the scriptures it means a child of incest or one born outside the proper marriage. - The word says a bastard shall dwell in Ashdod, and Ashdod is the area of modern day Tel Aviv; this teaching places the line of Amalek dwelling there today. Genesis 36:15-19 taught in Genesis 36-39 - These were the dukes of the sons of Esau: dukes are the chiefs of their tribes, the leaders of the families of Edom. Genesis 36:20-30 taught in Genesis 36-39 - The sons of Seir the Horite inhabited the land before Esau; the Horites were the original dwellers of mount Seir. - The Lord destroyed the Horims from before the children of Esau, and they succeeded them and dwelt in their stead, as Deuteronomy records. - Precept Genesis 14:6 : The Horites were in their mount Seir already in Abraham's day. - Precept Deuteronomy 2:22 : The Lord destroyed the Horims from before the children of Esau, and they dwelt in their stead. Genesis 36:31 taught in Genesis 36-39 - These are the kings that reigned in the land of Edom before there reigned any king over the children of Israel. Israel had no king until Saul, whom the Lord sought out when Israel asked for a king like the nations, in 1 Samuel 8 and 9. Genesis 37:18-20 taught in Genesis 36-39 - When they saw him afar off, they conspired against him to slay him: Behold, this dreamer cometh. That is the same spirit Cain had, and the same spirit Esau had. Genesis 43:32 taught in Genesis 40-43 - Esau patterns himself after the former kingdoms. He learns how to govern and oppress by studying the kingdoms that were before him: ancient Babylon, ancient Greece, ancient Rome, ancient Egypt. They search out iniquities and accomplish a diligent search; nothing they do is accidental, everything follows the blueprint of the kingdoms that came before them. Genesis 43:33-34 taught in Genesis 40-43 - They sat before him, the firstborn according to his birthright and the youngest according to his youth, and the men marvelled one at another. Genesis 49:3-4 taught in Genesis 48-50 - Thou shalt not excel: Reuben would not excel as the firstborn, because he went up to his father's couch. His birthright was given unto the sons of Joseph because he defiled his father's bed, and the genealogy is not to be reckoned after the birthright. - Precept 1 Chronicles 5:1 : Reuben's birthright was given unto the sons of Joseph because he defiled his father's bed. Genesis 49:8-12 taught in Genesis 48-50 - Thy hand shall be in the neck of thine enemies: Judah sits right in the neck of the enemy's kingdom, right up under Esau here in America, in his politics and his government, always in a key position. - Precept Isaiah 63:1-3 : He that cometh from Bozrah with dyed garments has trodden the winepress alone; the garments washed in the blood of grapes look ahead to that day. Genesis 49:22-26 taught in Genesis 48-50 - Whose branches run over the wall: the Spaniards built a wall in Puerto Rico to keep themselves separate, but the daughters went over the wall and mixed themselves among the people; interracial marriage ran high, and that is why a great part of them favor Esau today. Exodus Exodus 10:1 taught in Exodus 10-13 - The potter has power over the clay, of the same lump to make one vessel unto honour and another unto dishonour. Some nations are honourable, which are the Israelites, and some are dishonourable; Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated. The vessels of wrath were fitted to destruction, endured with much longsuffering so the Most High could show how powerful he is; that is why Esau had to be set on such a high level, so that when he brings these people down all will know God is truly all powerful. - Precept Romans 9:13 : Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated; Jacob is the honourable vessel and Esau the dishonourable. Exodus 15:14-16 taught in Exodus 14-17 - The people shall hear and be afraid; the dukes of Edom shall be amazed, trembling shall take hold of the mighty men of Moab, and the inhabitants of Canaan shall melt away. This goes into the future, when the nations would hear what the Lord had done for Israel. Exodus 16:31-36 taught in Exodus 14-17 - Stop reading over the power in these books with the colonizer's picture of the fathers in mind. Esau paints our fathers as a backward people in rags, but the Most High shewed mighty wonders through Genesis and Exodus; stop believing that image. Exodus 17:8-13 taught in Exodus 14-17 - Then came Amalek, and fought with Israel in Rephidim. Amalek was the first nation to come against Israel after Egypt; Amalek was Esau's grandson, born to Eliphaz of Timna the concubine, a duke in the land of Edom. - Precept Genesis 36:12 : Timna bare to Eliphaz Amalek; Amalek is the grandson of Esau, a duke of Edom. Exodus 17:14-16 taught in Exodus 14-17 - The whole world is set up between Jacob and Esau, and Esau is the end of this world, the so-called white man, with Amalek leading; it is not speaking of the Arab man, for if Ishmael had a rulership still to come, Israel would have another captivity to enter, and Christ has already redeemed us from the curse of the law. - Precept 2 Esdras 6:7-9 : Jacob's hand held first the heel of Esau; for Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth. - Precept 2 Esdras 6:10 : Nothing stands between the heel and the hand; the world passes straight from Esau's end to Jacob's beginning. - Precept Genesis 3:15 : Enmity is set between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed; the battle between Esau's seed and Israel stands until the end. Exodus 28:13-21 taught in Exodus 26-29 - The Wisdom of Solomon says of this garment that in the long garment was the whole world, and in the four rows of the stones was the glory of the fathers. There was no Moabite stone, Jebusite stone, or Edomite stone in it; the whole world in the garment is the twelve tribes of Israel, and the glory of the fathers is written in their stones. Leviticus Leviticus 6:24-30 taught in Leviticus 6-9 - The blood was not eaten: the sin offering whose blood was brought into the tabernacle to reconcile was not eaten but burnt in the fire. Israel does not mess with the blood; Esau eats the blood, not us. Leviticus 7:22-27 taught in Leviticus 6-9 - One of those other uses was soap: Israel took the fat and made soap with it. Jeremiah shows it, though thou wash thee with nitre, and take thee much soap; Israel had soap way back then and did not live filthy, and when the Moors ruled in Europe they introduced soap to Esau again. Leviticus 13:29-30 taught in Leviticus 10-13 - Yellow thin hair is called a plague. Our hair does not come like that; the nations that have blonde hair are naturally that way. When Israel, blacks, Hispanics, and Native Americans dye their hair blonde, they are taking after the customs of Esau, emulating who they want to be like, and the word calls that yellow thin hair a plague on our people. Leviticus 26:31-33 taught in Leviticus 26-27 - When Babylon came against Jerusalem, Esau stood on the side cheering it on to the foundation, as Psalms 137 records. - Precept Psalms 137:7 : Remember the children of Edom in the day of Jerusalem, who said, Rase it, rase it, even to the foundation thereof; Esau cheered the destruction on. Numbers Numbers 20:14-17 taught in Numbers 19-22 - Moses sent messengers to the king of Edom, saying, Thus saith thy brother Israel. Israel rehearsed the travail: our fathers went down into Egypt, the Egyptians vexed us, we cried unto the Lord and he heard our voice and sent an angel and brought us forth. - Edom is identified in this teaching with the people called the white man today, the Caucasians. This is Israel pleading with the brother nation: not sneaking in, not hiding, not touching the fields, the vineyards, or the water of the wells; only the king's highway, turning neither to the right hand nor to the left, until past the borders, to reach the promised land. Numbers 20:18-21 taught in Numbers 19-22 - Edom answered, Thou shalt not pass by me, lest I come out against thee with the sword. Israel stayed humble: we will go by the highway, and if I and my cattle drink of thy water, then I will pay for it; I will only go through on my feet. - Edom still refused and came out against Israel with much people and with a strong hand, and Israel turned away from him. - Why so harsh against a people asking only to pass through? That hatred stands from something: Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing wherewith his father blessed him, and purposed in his heart to slay his brother. Genesis 25 through 27 is the start of the two nations, and Israel was given the birthright and the kingdom while Esau was rejected. - The hatred is perpetual, everlasting, never ending. The forefather's hatred showed in Numbers 20 and it shows to this day in the nation of Edom still rejecting Israel; it will not stop until Christ stops it, and Israel's part is to repent and come back to the lost statutes and commandments. - Precept Genesis 27:41 : Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing and said in his heart, then will I slay my brother Jacob; the refusal in Numbers 20 goes back to this. Numbers 20:22-29 taught in Numbers 19-22 - At mount Hor, by the coast of the land of Edom, the Lord said Aaron shall be gathered unto his people; he could not enter the land because of the rebellion at the water of Meribah. Numbers 21:4-5 taught in Numbers 19-22 - They journeyed from mount Hor by the way of the Red Sea to compass the land of Edom, and the soul of the people was much discouraged because of the way: since Edom refused passage, Israel had to go around, and the way was longer than they wanted it to be. Numbers 24:18-19 taught in Numbers 23-26 - And Edom shall be a possession. Edom is nowhere named in the matter of Balak and Balaam in these chapters, but the Lord made sure Edom was written into the prophecy: Seir also shall be a possession for his enemies, and Israel shall do valiantly. The law of bondmen shows what a possession is: the heathen round about are bought for an inheritance, bondmen for ever, though over our own brethren we do not rule with rigour. - For Esau that servitude is not for ever, because Esau is the only nation on the earth with an expiration date. The house of Jacob, the twelve tribes of Israel, the blacks, Hispanics, and Native Indians, shall be a fire, the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for stubble; there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau, for the Lord hath spoken it. The rest of the nations go into servitude for ever, but the Lord can only bear with Esau so much longer. - Out of Jacob shall come he that shall have dominion: that is the one who cometh from Edom with dyed garments from Bozrah, glorious in his apparel, traveling in the greatness of his strength, which is the whole host of heaven, thousands upon thousands of angels. The day of vengeance is in his heart, for though Israel serves out her punishment in captivity, Esau went overboard and kept laying on punishment when our iniquity had an end. - Precept Leviticus 25:44-46 : The heathen round about are bought for bondmen and taken for a possession for ever; that is what Edom becomes to Israel. - Precept Obadiah 1:18 : The house of Jacob shall be a fire, the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for stubble; there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau. - Precept Isaiah 63:1-4 : He that cometh from Edom with dyed garments from Bozrah treads the winepress in his fury, for the day of vengeance is in his heart and the year of his redeemed is come. Numbers 24:20 taught in Numbers 23-26 - The Lord swore to utterly put out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven, and that the Lord would have war with Amalek from generation to generation. This teaching identifies Amalek, the seed of Esau through Eliphaz, with the people who call themselves Jewish in the land of Israel today: the war that has never left that land since they entered it is the war the Lord swore, and the prophecy that none shall remain of the house of Esau belongs to no other nation. Numbers 26:5-7 taught in Numbers 23-26 - Of Hanoch, the family of the Hanochites; of Pallu, the family of the Palluites. The ending ites means the descendants of, the people you belong to: Israelites are the descendants of Israel, Edomites the descendants of Edom, and so it goes all down the line through the scriptures. - Reading these family names aloud loosens the tongue to say the names of the scriptures fluently and without hesitation. 1 Chronicles 1 serves the same practice, and it carries the names of Israel's families together with Edom and Ishmael, the nations that come out of Abraham's line. Numbers 26:51-56 taught in Numbers 23-26 - Land is how wealth is built, and Esau knows how important land is; that is why the land is kept in his generations and why Gad, the Native Indian, was never given one square inch of his land back, only the casinos and the little plots called reservations. Israel is getting the most fertile land back; as for this land here, let it burn. Numbers 27:8-11 taught in Numbers 27-30 - It also goes into marriage in the nation as a whole: there was never a case where an inheritance in Israel passed to an Edomite, an Ammonite, or a Moabite. The fathers from the beginning took wives of their own kindred, and interracial marriage is not of the scriptures. Numbers 31:9-12 taught in Numbers 31-34 - Midian comes from the lineage of Ishmael, the people known today as the Arab man. This shows Esau was not the one who first came up with castles; the castles seen in the movies were conquered from other nations. Numbers 33:37-39 taught in Numbers 31-34 - They pitched in mount Hor, in the edge of the land of Edom; the map shows the land of Edom there. Numbers 33:44-49 taught in Numbers 31-34 - They pitched in Ije-abarim, in the border of Moab; on the map Moab sits right above the land of Edom. Numbers 34:1-5 taught in Numbers 31-34 - This is the land of Canaan that falls to Israel for inheritance, with the coasts thereof; the south quarter runs from the wilderness of Zin along by the coast of Edom, the south border from the outmost coast of the salt sea eastward, fetching a compass unto the river of Egypt and out at the sea. Deuteronomy Deuteronomy 1:1-3 taught in Deuteronomy 1-2 - These be the words which Moses spake unto all Israel on this side Jordan in the wilderness: the audience of the entire book of Deuteronomy is the Israelites. - Moses spake in the fortieth year, in the eleventh month, on the first day of the month, according unto all that the Lord had given him in commandment unto them. Deuteronomy 2:1-7 taught in Deuteronomy 1-2 - Israel compassed mount Seir many days, and the Lord said, ye have compassed this mountain long enough; turn you northward and pass through the coast of your brethren the children of Esau, which dwell in Seir, the people called the white man today. - They shall be afraid of you: the Most High put fear upon Esau so they would not trouble Israel, because he did not want a war; take ye good heed unto yourselves therefore, and meddle not with them. - Mount Seir was given unto Esau for a possession, not so much as a foot breadth of it for Israel; the promise to Israel was the land of Canaan. Israel could buy meat and water of them for money, but take nothing. Deuteronomy 2:8-9 taught in Deuteronomy 1-2 - Passing from the children of Esau, the same order came concerning Moab: distress not the Moabites, neither contend with them in battle, for Ar was given unto the children of Lot for a possession. Deuteronomy 2:10-12 taught in Deuteronomy 1-2 - The Emims dwelt in that land in times past, a people great and many and tall as the Anakims, accounted giants; and the Horims dwelt in Seir beforetime, and the children of Esau succeeded them and dwelt in their stead. Deuteronomy 2:17-19 taught in Deuteronomy 1-2 - Esau, Moab, and Ammon were all off limits; the Most High appointed their possessions, and Israel was to pick no fight with them. Deuteronomy 2:22-23 taught in Deuteronomy 1-2 - As he did to the children of Esau when he destroyed the Horims from before them, so these nations succeeded the giants and dwelt in their stead even unto this day. Deuteronomy 2:26-30 taught in Deuteronomy 1-2 - Moses sent messengers unto Sihon with words of peace: let me pass through thy land by the highway, buying meat and water of thee for money, only passing through on my feet, as was done passing Esau in Seir and Moab in Ar. Deuteronomy 8:4-5 taught in Deuteronomy 7-10 - This is why Esau has no judgment on him like Israel has: they are not the sons, so the Most High is not chastening them. You cannot do what the other nations do; when we get that in our heads we will be in a far better situation as a people. Deuteronomy 15:9-11 taught in Deuteronomy 15-18 - Notice that Esau had this Bible, these commandments and these laws, yet worked us to death for over four hundred years, and when they released us we did not go out with anything. They had these laws written before them and did not do them. Deuteronomy 23:2 taught in Deuteronomy 23-26 - A bastard shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord, even to his tenth generation: the children begotten of forbidden unions with the nations were shut out of the congregation. - The prophets tie the bastard to Ashdod: a bastard shall dwell in Ashdod. Ashdod was one of the cities given to the tribe of Judah in the inheritance, but Israel did not drive out all the inhabitants and lost it. - In the days of Nehemiah, Jews had married wives of Ashdod, of Ammon, and of Moab, and their children spake half in the speech of Ashdod and could not speak in the Jews' language. Why is that? Because the mothers do the raising of the children. - Precept Joshua 15:20-21 : This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Judah according to their families. Deuteronomy 23:7-8 taught in Deuteronomy 23-26 - Thou shalt not abhor an Edomite, for he is thy brother: this was a temporary law. Edom broke the brotherly covenant; he did pursue his brother with the sword, did cast off all pity, his anger did tear perpetually, and he kept his wrath for ever. - Edom's hatred is a perpetual hatred: he shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword in the time of their calamity, and as we see our people being slaughtered by Esau, that anger continues even to this very day. - Thou shalt not abhor an Egyptian, because thou wast a stranger in his land: many brothers and sisters do not want to deal with that part and only want to deal with Edom, but Egypt likewise came under judgment for the violence against the children of Judah, because they shed innocent blood in their land. - Precept Amos 1:9 : Tyrus delivered up the whole captivity to Edom and remembered not the brotherly covenant. - Precept Amos 1:11 : Edom did pursue his brother with the sword, cast off all pity, and his anger did tear perpetually. - Precept Ezekiel 35:5 : Edom had a perpetual hatred and shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword in the time of their calamity. - Precept Joel 3:19 : Egypt shall be a desolation and Edom a desolate wilderness, for the violence against the children of Judah, because they shed innocent blood in their land. Deuteronomy 27:21 taught in Deuteronomy 27-30 - Cursed be he that lieth with any manner of beast. Bestiality is the practice of Esau, and Israel was cursed for touching it. Deuteronomy 28:17 taught in Deuteronomy 27-30 - Cursed shall be thy basket and thy store: that goes into your businesses and your holdings. It is hard enough for a black man or woman to start a business; we are left with side hustles while the major trades, the ships, the metals, and the timber belong to Esau. Deuteronomy 28:49-50 taught in Deuteronomy 27-30 - The Lord shall bring a nation against thee from far, from the end of the earth, as swift as the eagle flieth: the eagle is the symbol of Esau's nation. Deuteronomy 28:58-61 taught in Deuteronomy 27-30 - Verse 59 is saying the Most High will make up diseases to keep punishing you; he will even have Esau create them in a laboratory and make them affect you more than anybody else. Deuteronomy 32:10 taught in Deuteronomy 31-34 - He found him in a desert land, and in the waste howling wilderness; he led him about, he instructed him, he kept him as the apple of his eye. The same people the world counted as three fifths of a man are the apple of the Most High's eye. - Zechariah shows who that people is: deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon. Who was held captive in the land of the north, in North America, but the so-called blacks, Hispanics, and Native Americans? We are Zion, and we must deliver ourselves from the ways we were taught there. - He that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye: the nations that spoiled Israel and did her harm have a grand payback coming when Christ returns. - Precept Psalms 137:7-8 : Edom is remembered against the day of Jerusalem, and the daughter of Babylon is to be destroyed; this shows who Zion dwells with. Deuteronomy 33:17 taught in Deuteronomy 31-34 - His glory is like the firstling of his bullock: as in the law that sanctified the firstborn unto the Most High, that is the glory of the birthright given to Joseph. - Precept Exodus 13:2 : Sanctify unto me all the firstborn: the firstling is the glory of the birthright. Joshua Joshua 11:16-20 taught in Joshua 9-12 - Esau thinks the Most High is altogether such a one as himself, that the Most High looks like him and is happy with him punishing and oppressing us. He is not down for it; it is our punishment and it has to happen, but he will reprove Esau and set Israel in order before his eyes. - When Christ returns he will destroy all nations in the valley of Megiddo, and after Israel's spirits are changed he will thrust out the enemy from before us and say, Destroy them. Israel will lay the vengeance of the Most High upon Edom according to his anger and according to his fury. Brothers, you just have to endure to the end; this is how you read the Bible, precept upon precept, here a little and there a little. - Precept Ezekiel 25:12-14 : Edom revenged himself upon Judah over and above his charge; I will lay my vengeance upon Edom by the hand of my people Israel. Joshua 15:1-4 taught in Joshua 13-16 - This is the lot of the tribe of the children of Judah by their families, even to the border of Edom: the south border ran from the shore of the salt sea, up the south side of Kadeshbarnea, and out unto the river of Egypt, with the goings out of that coast at the sea. Joshua 15:5-12 taught in Joshua 13-16 - The east border was the salt sea unto the end of Jordan; the north border went up from the bay of the sea, by Bethhogla and the stone of Bohan the son of Reuben, and up by the valley of the son of Hinnom unto the south side of the Jebusite: the same is Jerusalem. - The border went to the top of the mountain before the valley of Hinnom westward, at the end of the valley of the giants northward, then out by Kirjathjearim, Bethshemesh, and Ekron, and the west border was to the great sea. This is the coast of the children of Judah round about according to their families. Joshua 15:20 taught in Joshua 13-16 - This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Judah according to their families, and the chapter counts out their cities district by district through verse 62: the uttermost cities toward the coast of Edom southward, twenty and nine cities with their villages; the cities in the valley in their groups of fourteen, sixteen, and nine; Ekron, Ashdod, and Gaza with their towns and villages unto the river of Egypt and the great sea; the cities in the mountains in their groups of eleven, nine, ten, six, and two; and six cities in the wilderness, all with their villages. Joshua 17:5-6 taught in Joshua 17-20 - Down south the Jordan empties into the Dead Sea, and Sodom and Gomorrah sat south of the Dead Sea, by where Edom was residing; the maps give a good feel for what the Bible is talking about. Joshua 24:4-7 taught in Joshua 21-24 - Unto Isaac were given Jacob and Esau; Esau received mount Seir to possess it, but Jacob and his children went down into Egypt. A whole lot of time passes in just those few verses. Judges Judges 5:3-5 taught in Judges 5-8 - The Lord marching out of the field of Edom, the earth trembling, the heavens dropping, and the mountains melting from before the Lord God of Israel is future prophecy; this has not happened yet. - Precept Isaiah 63:1-4 : The one who cometh from Edom with dyed garments, treading the winepress alone in the day of vengeance, is the same picture the song is singing of. Judges 11:14-22 taught in Judges 9-12 - When Israel came up from Egypt and walked through the wilderness unto the Red sea and came to Kadesh, they sent messengers to the king of Edom and to the king of Moab asking passage, and both refused; so Israel went along through the wilderness, compassed the land of Edom and the land of Moab, came by the east side of the land of Moab, and pitched on the other side of Arnon; but they came not within the border of Moab, for Arnon was the border of Moab. - Precept Numbers 20:21 : Edom refused to give Israel passage through his border, just as Jephthah rehearsed it. Ruth Ruth 1:3-5 taught in Ruth 1-3 - Elimelech, Naomi's husband, died, and she was left with her two sons. The sons took them wives of the women of Moab, Orpah and Ruth, and after they dwelt there about ten years Mahlon and Chilion died also, leaving Naomi without her husband and without her sons. - Were the sons of Israel supposed to take wives of the women of Moab while sojourning there? No; but remember what was just read at the end of Judges, that every man did that which was right in his own eyes. And this was not the first time Israel dealt with the women of Moab. - Precept 1 Esdras 8:69 : Even in the time of Ezra, Israel had not put away the strange people of the land, the Moabites among them; remember that it says the strange people of the land. Ruth 1:6-9 taught in Ruth 1-3 - Naomi heard in the country of Moab that the Lord had visited his people and given them bread, so she arose with her daughters in law to return unto the land of Judah, and told them, Go, return each to her mother's house; the Lord deal kindly with you, as ye have dealt with the dead and with me. - The Lord grant you that ye may find rest, each of you in the house of her husband: that rest is an inheritance. The man is supposed to leave an inheritance; you are not supposed to leave your wife and your children desolate with a gang of bills. To leave an inheritance you first have to work, and you have to be wise with how you deal with your money. - Behind the words the wife of the dead stands the law of the husband's brother: if brethren dwell together and one dies having no child, his brother takes the widow to wife, and the firstborn she bears succeeds in the name of the dead brother, that his name be not put out of Israel. That first child is basically the dead brother's child; he gets the rights of inheritance as if the brother were still alive, so the brother's name stays in the earth and his house is built up. - We are not under that law anymore; we do not have that land inheritance in captivity. It is wicked to pull that scripture today to try to get with your brother's wife after he passes away; do not be looking at your brother's wife. - It is important for us to build our legacy and pass it down; that is one of the things we lack in Israel today. Some of us use captivity as an excuse not to better ourselves or build, but that is not what the scriptures say: get the job, further your education, do more for yourself, your family, and the body. Building up your house also means spiritually building it, teaching your wife and children. - Precept 1 Chronicles 5:1 : Reuben was the firstborn, but because he defiled his father's bed his birthright was given unto the sons of Joseph; the birthright shows why the firstborn and the inheritance mattered so much in Israel. Ruth 2:10 taught in Ruth 1-3 - Ruth fell on her face and asked, Why have I found grace in thine eyes, that thou shouldest take knowledge of me, seeing I am a stranger? She acknowledged what she was to Israel: a stranger. - Precept 1 Esdras 8:69 : The Moabites are counted among the strange people of the land; Ruth spoke of herself by that same word. Ruth 4:5 taught in Ruth 4 - What day thou buyest the field of the hand of Naomi, thou must buy it also of Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of the dead, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance. Whoever took the land had to take the dead brother's wife with it; Ruth the Moabitess came along as a parcel of the land, to keep the name of Mahlon alive. - What law is that going back to? That law goes back to Deuteronomy 25, the duty of the husband's brother: the widow of the dead does not marry without unto a stranger, and the firstborn she bears succeeds in the name of the dead brother, that his name be not put out of Israel. This law was taught in full when it was read ahead at Ruth 1:6-9 in these notes: the firstborn carries the weight of the name, and the shoe was loosed from him that would not build up his brother's house. - Notice the bottom of verse 5: to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance. This law applies to inheritance; it went into the law of land being passed down. It does not apply today: your husband dying does not mean his brother now has to go in unto you and raise up children, because that duty was due to the law of inheritance, and Israel has no land inheritance in this captivity. It is wicked to pull that scripture today to try to get with your brother's widow. - Precept 1 Chronicles 5:1 : Reuben was the firstborn, but because he defiled his father's bed his birthright was given unto the sons of Joseph; the birthright shows why the firstborn and the inheritance mattered so much in Israel. 1 Samuel 1 Samuel 8:6-9 taught in 1 Samuel 8-11 - The thing displeased Samuel when they said, Give us a king to judge us, and Samuel prayed unto the Lord. The Lord said, Hearken unto the voice of the people, for they have not rejected thee, but they have rejected me, that I should not reign over them; according to all the works they have done since the day I brought them up out of Egypt, forsaking me and serving other gods, so do they also unto thee. Just as they rejected the Most High, they were rejecting Samuel and his counsel. - Joshua warned us about this. At Shechem, Israel made the covenant with its own mouth to serve the Lord and obey his voice; asking for a king was breaking the choice we ourselves made. - How do we serve the Lord in sincerity and in truth? A lot of people today say they love the Lord, yet they do not do any of his commandments; they do not truly show they have the faith of Christ, because they do not keep the commandments. - A lot of us grew up with that plaque in the house, as for me and my house we will serve the Lord, and the house kept not one commandment: still eating pork, still keeping Sunday, still keeping the wicked pagan holidays of our oppressors. - Christ gave the same picture: a nobleman went into a far country to receive for himself a kingdom, and his citizens hated him. This is speaking about Christ; the same spirit that said set a king over us says, We will not have Christ to reign over us. When we read Samuel again, that is why the Lord said, they did not reject you, they have rejected me. - Precept Joshua 24:1-4 : Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel to Shechem: your fathers dwelt on the other side of the flood in old time and served other gods, and the Most High took Abraham, multiplied his seed, and Jacob and his children went down into Egypt, where we served four hundred years. 1 Samuel 14:47-52 taught in 1 Samuel 12-15 - Saul took the kingdom over Israel and fought against all his enemies on every side: Moab, the children of Ammon, Edom, the kings of Zobah, and the Philistines; and whithersoever he turned himself, he vexed them. He gathered an host, smote the Amalekites, and delivered Israel out of the hands of them that spoiled them. 1 Samuel 15:1-3 taught in 1 Samuel 12-15 - The teaching applies Exodus 17:16 to this day: the same war continues from generation to generation, and it is now more spiritual than ever, because the adversary has established the imagination that they are the Jews, and we go out and cast down that imagination every day. Edom cheered Babylon on when Jerusalem burned, and the scripture pronounces the payback. - Precept Psalms 137:7 : Remember, O Lord, the children of Edom in the day of Jerusalem, who said, Rase it, rase it, even to the foundation thereof; they were the cheerleaders when Babylon destroyed the temple. - Precept Revelation 17:5 : Edom grew up from being the daughter of Babylon into Mystery, Babylon the Great, the mother of harlots; that is why the great woman of Revelation carries Babylon's name. 1 Samuel 22:9-10 taught in 1 Samuel 20-23 - Here you see that Saul had placed an Edomite over his servants: Doeg the Edomite, which was set over the servants of Saul, answered and reported that David had come to Nob and that Ahimelech had inquired of the Lord for him, given him victuals, and given him the sword of Goliath the Philistine. - The scriptures tell us we are never supposed to trust our enemies, yet what we are reading is Saul with an Edomite set over his servants. - Precept Ecclesiasticus 12:10 : Never trust thine enemy; but Saul had placed an Edomite over his servants. 1 Samuel 22:17-19 taught in 1 Samuel 20-23 - Saul commanded his footmen to turn and slay the priests of the Lord, but the servants of the king would not put forth their hand to fall upon the priests of the Lord. Saul was able to get the Edomite to do what his own men would not do: Doeg turned and fell upon the priests, and slew on that day fourscore and five persons that did wear a linen ephod, and smote Nob, the city of the priests, with the edge of the sword. - Go back to Genesis and see the spirit that has been placed on this man from the beginning: Esau comforted himself with the purpose of killing his brother Jacob. Just as in the time of Saul, even to this very day, when Israel suffers violence at the hands of the other nations, especially Esau, he gets comfort out of killing us; when Saul appointed Doeg to that task, you can best believe he was quite happy over it and most likely found much pleasure in killing the priests. - Precept Genesis 27:41-42 : Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing, and purposed in his heart to slay his brother; Rebekah warned Jacob that Esau, as touching thee, doth comfort himself, purposing to kill thee. That comfort in killing is the spirit seen again in Doeg the Edomite.

title: Idolatry
text: Idolatry The golden calf, the groves, Baalim, and every warning against serving other gods. Genesis Genesis 10:8-11 taught in Genesis 9-12 - Nimrod, his queen Semiramis, and her child Tammuz became the first pagan trinity, and their worship spread under different names through every nation: Baal, Bel, Zeus, Jupiter, Ra, Thor; Ishtar, Ashtaroth, Isis, Diana. Genesis 24:3-4 taught in Genesis 24-27 - The reason is given in the law itself: they will turn away thy son from following me, that they may serve other gods. Solomon is the prime example; he loved women of the other nations, went into their gods, and had to repent and bring it back. - Precept Deuteronomy 7:3-4 : Make no marriages with the nations, for they will turn away thy son from following the Most High to serve other gods. Genesis 31:30-32 taught in Genesis 28-31 - The scriptures prove it. Your fathers dwelt on the other side of the flood in old time, even Terah, the father of Abraham and the father of Nachor, and they served other gods. Laban was of the house of Nahor, an idolater just like his fathers. That is why the Most High told Abram to get out from his country and from his kindred: he separated Abram because of what he had set up for Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and for us, that we not be idolaters. - Precept Joshua 24:2 : Your fathers dwelt on the other side of the flood in old time, even Terah the father of Abraham and the father of Nachor, and they served other gods; Laban came of that idolatrous house. Genesis 32:27-28 taught in Genesis 32-35 - The God of Israel is He that giveth strength and power unto His people; He is the power source. When Israel went astray and served other gods, the name and the power were taken, and the nations called the people by every other name. Returning to the Most High is how the power returns, not carnal weapons of warfare. Genesis 35:1-4 taught in Genesis 32-35 - Before going up to Bethel, Jacob told his household, Put away the strange gods that are among you, and be clean. The strange gods were there because Rachel had stolen her father's images and hidden them, sitting on them when Laban searched. - Idolatry hidden in the household must be put away before you can stand at Bethel. Rachel finally gave up the images, and Jacob hid them under the oak by Shechem. - Precept Genesis 31:19 : Rachel had stolen the images that were her father's; that is where the strange gods in the household came from. Exodus Exodus 3:19-20 taught in Exodus 2-5 - I am sure that the king of Egypt will not let you go, no, not by a mighty hand; and I will stretch out my hand, and smite Egypt with all my wonders. The Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart so that the deliverance would come with wonders, destroying the idols of Egypt in the sight of Israel and of Egypt; the Most High is not one to be played with. Exodus 4:24-26 taught in Exodus 2-5 - By the way in the inn, the LORD met him, and sought to kill him, because Moses had not circumcised his son. Zipporah took a sharp stone, cut off the foreskin of her son, and said, Surely a bloody husband art thou to me: bloody because of the circumcision she had to perform herself. - This shows the laws did not begin at Sinai. Circumcision was the covenant given to Abraham for every man child in his generations, on the eighth day, and the uncircumcised man child whose flesh is not circumcised, that soul shall be cut off from his people: he hath broken my covenant. That is why Moses was worthy of death. - The covenant still stands. A son of Israel must be circumcised; and a man that comes to the truth grown must still be circumcised, even at forty, fifty, or sixty years, as Abraham himself was circumcised at ninety and nine, and as Paul circumcised Timothy, whose father was a Greek. Nothing that defileth enters the kingdom. - The Egyptians did not practice circumcision; they were a nation of uncleanness, and the covenant was between the Lord and Israel: after the doings of the land of Egypt, wherein ye dwelt, shall ye not do. - Romans 2 does not do away with circumcision of the flesh. Circumcision verily profiteth if thou keep the law: the Jews who grew up circumcised and keeping the law, yet broke it, made their circumcision uncircumcision; and the uncircumcised of the cast-off northern kingdom who keep the righteousness of the law are counted as circumcised. Circumcision of the heart is putting away the evil of the doings, as the prophets say, take away the foreskins of your heart; the scribes and Pharisees were clean on the outside of the cup but full of iniquity within. - Precept Colossians 3:5-6 : Mortify therefore your members, fornication, uncleanness; for which things' sake the wrath of God cometh on the children of disobedience. Exodus 7:19-22 taught in Exodus 6-9 - With this first plague the Most High was mocking Sobek, the Egyptian idol god of the rivers, showing that he could not defend his own waters. - Many Egyptologists claim this never happened, because to admit it happened is to admit that the idols they claim to be gods and goddesses were powerless before our God, and that those idols do not exist at all. Exodus 8:5-8 taught in Exodus 6-9 - Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters, and the frogs came up and covered the land of Egypt. With this second plague the Most High was mocking Heqet, the Egyptian idol god of the frogs. Exodus 8:16-19 taught in Exodus 6-9 - With the third and fourth plagues, the lice and the swarms of flies, the Most High was mocking Beelzebub, the idol lord of flies and uncleanness. Exodus 9:1-7 taught in Exodus 6-9 - A grievous murrain fell upon the cattle of Egypt, upon the horses, asses, camels, oxen, and sheep; and with this fifth plague the Most High was mocking Hathor, the Egyptian idol goddess of cattle. - The Egyptians could not pray to their idols to help them, because the Lord was mocking them, showing them that Hathor does not exist, Sobek does not exist, Heqet does not exist, and Beelzebub does not exist. Exodus 9:8-12 taught in Exodus 6-9 - The magicians could not stand before Moses because of the boils, for the boils were upon the magicians themselves and upon all the Egyptians. With this sixth plague the Most High was mocking Sekhmet, the Egyptian idol goddess of health and beauty. Exodus 9:18-21 taught in Exodus 6-9 - He that regarded not the word of the Lord left his servants and his cattle in the field. Many in Egypt held certain idols in more favor than others, and these trusted that Nut, the idol goddess of the sky, would keep them safe. Exodus 9:22-26 taught in Exodus 6-9 - With this seventh plague the Most High was mocking Nut and Geb, the Egyptian idol gods of the sky and the earth, striking from the sky and burning along the ground they were supposed to rule. Exodus 12:29 taught in Exodus 10-13 - At midnight the Lord smote all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh that sat on his throne unto the firstborn of the captive in the dungeon, and all the firstborn of cattle. Even the prisoners' firstborn died, and Pharaoh's own son died. - In this Christ showed that Osiris and Isis, the supposed Egyptian gods of life and death, control neither life nor death. Unto God the Lord belong the issues from death; the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob is the God of salvation, and he alone brings forth death. - Precept Psalm 68:20 : He that is our God is the God of salvation; and unto God the Lord belong the issues from death, not to the idols of Egypt. Exodus 14:1-5 taught in Exodus 14-17 - The Most High is not done with the Egyptians. He destroyed their firstborn and brought Israel out, but He kept one more judgment in store for that wicked nation, and He will do the same to the wicked nation that has done the same things to Israel today. - The heart of Pharaoh and of his servants turned as soon as the people were gone: why have we done this, that we have let Israel go from serving us? The oppressor does not release his slaves gladly. Exodus 18:9-11 taught in Exodus 18-21 - Other non-Israelites came to that same knowledge. All the gods of the nations are idols, but the Lord made the heavens; give unto the Lord the glory due unto his name. - Naaman the Syrian, healed of his leprosy in Jordan, confessed that there is no God in all the earth but in Israel. His faith was so strong he vowed to offer neither burnt offering nor sacrifice unto other gods, and asked pardon for even bowing in the house of Rimmon with his master. - Nebuchadnezzar came to praise and extol and honour the King of heaven, for those that walk in pride he is able to abase. The heathen understand that the Most High is greater than all other gods; it is our people that want a god that does not look like them. - Precept Psalms 96:5-8 : All the gods of the nations are idols, but the Lord made the heavens; give unto the Lord the glory due unto his name. - Precept 2 Kings 5:14-18 : Naaman dipped seven times in Jordan and was clean, and confessed there is no God in all the earth but in Israel; a heathen vowed to sacrifice to no other god but the Lord. Exodus 20:4-5 taught in Exodus 18-21 - An image in itself is not the sin, except for that white image of the beast; making images to bow down to them and serve them is the transgression, for the Lord thy God is a jealous God. - Visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation: Israel is yet this day in captivity, scattered for a reproach and a curse, according to all the iniquities of the fathers which departed from the Lord. Right now Israel is paying for the sins of the fathers; that is why the people are scattered to the four corners of the earth. Exodus 20:6 taught in Exodus 18-21 - And shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love me, and keep my commandments. Judith recounted how the Most High tried the fathers for the examination of their hearts: he tried Abraham and Isaac, and Jacob in Mesopotamia of Syria keeping the sheep of Laban, serving twenty years with his wages changed and given Leah when he looked for Rachel. - In Judith's day there was no tribe, family, people, nor city that worshipped gods made with hands, as had been aforetime; for that cause she trusted the Lord would not despise the nation. Mercy rests on them that know none other God, not Allah, not Buddha, not a white Jesus. - Precept Judith 8:18-20 : The fathers were given to the sword for idolatry, but a generation that knows none other god can trust he will not despise the nation. Exodus 20:8-11 taught in Exodus 18-21 - Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy. The word says remember because Israel would forget it: in this captivity the people were forced to serve other gods and their religions, and the Sabbath was lost through forced conversion. - Precept Jeremiah 17:4 : Thou shalt serve thine enemies in the land which thou knowest not; the captivity brought forced service to other gods. - Precept Deuteronomy 28:64 : Scattered among all people, there shalt thou serve other gods, wood and stone; that is how the Sabbath was forgotten.
