A brother who would never touch voodoo will sit through a whole counsel of do not do this, and call two weeks later saying he did it anyway; according to this verse, that rebellion is the same as witchcraft. - Stubbornness is idolatry because the instruction does not come from the man; it is the commandment of the Lord that leadership carries. When you are stubborn against it, you are saying what I want to do comes before what God wants me to do, and you have put yourself in the midst of idolatry as surely as circling the stone at Mecca or bowing before a cross. - Precept Ecclesiasticus 3:26-27 : Obstinate is another word for stubborn: the mind set on doing what it wants contrary to counsel will be laden with sorrows, and Saul heaped sin upon sin, lying, justifying himself, and blaming the people, which is what carried him into the witchcraft and idolatry of rebellion. 1 Samuel 16:14 taught in 1 Samuel 16-19 - Simultaneously, as the Most High put his spirit on David, the spirit departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from the Lord troubled him. Note it well: the evil spirit came from the Lord; that is a teaching the church world leaves out. - Chapter 15 said rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and Saul is now headed down that downward spiral; the spirit is leaving him, and he will eventually become a reprobate and dabble in real witchcraft. - Precept 1 Samuel 15:23 : Rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft; the road Saul took after the spirit departed ends with him literally at witchcraft. 1 Samuel 26:17-20 taught in 1 Samuel 24-27 - Saul knew David's voice and said, Is this thy voice, my son David? And David said, Wherefore doth my lord thus pursue after his servant? for what have I done? or what evil is in mine hand? - Let not my blood fall to the earth before the face of the Lord: for the king of Israel is come out to seek a flea, as when one doth hunt a partridge in the mountains. 1 Samuel 31:8-10 taught in 1 Samuel 28-31 - On the morrow, when the Philistines came to strip the slain, they found Saul and his three sons fallen in mount Gilboa. They cut off his head and stripped off his armour, and sent into the land of the Philistines round about, to publish it in the house of their idols and among the people. - They put his armour in the house of Ashtaroth, and they fastened his body to the wall of Bethshan.

title: Sacrifice and Atonement
text: Sacrifice and Atonement The offerings and what each one means: burnt, sin, trespass, peace, and the day of atonement. Genesis Genesis 3:21 taught in Genesis 1-4 - This is animal sacrifice to cover the sins. This is where the Most High ordained the sacrificial law; this is when they started to sacrifice. - The first sacrifice is twofold. A literal lamb was slain here to clothe Adam and his wife, and that lamb slain from the foundation of the world represents Christ, slain for our sins. - Precept Leviticus 16:27 : The sin offering yields skins, as the Most High made coats of skins to cover sin. Genesis 4:3-5 taught in Genesis 1-4 - The Most High had respect to Abel's offering and not to Cain's, and Cain was wroth. Genesis 4:7 taught in Genesis 1-4 - The Most High is calling Cain to repent. Cain knew that the Most High required animal sacrifice, because the sacrificial law was ordained at Genesis 3:21. Genesis 8:20-22 taught in Genesis 5-8 - Noah built an altar and offered burnt offerings of every clean beast and every clean fowl, and the Most High smelled a sweet savour and said He would not again curse the ground any more for man's sake. Genesis 9:5 taught in Genesis 9-12 - The Most High requiring blood at the hand of every beast is animal sacrifice, still in place with Noah, passed down generation to generation. - That is the scapegoat: it takes the wrongdoings, mistakes, and faults of others and places them on the animal. That is why Cain and Abel were bringing offerings, because they knew of the sacrifice from Genesis 3. - Precept Genesis 3:21 : The coats of skins were the first sacrifice; the beast stood in place of Adam and Eve. - Precept Genesis 4:3-5 : Cain and Abel brought offerings, proving the sacrifice was known and passed down. - Precept Leviticus 16:8-10 : The scapegoat is presented alive to make an atonement, standing in for the faults of others. Genesis 15:9-12 taught in Genesis 13-16 - Abram divided the heifer, the goat, and the ram, and drove the fowls from the carcases; he was offering sacrifice. Genesis 20:9-13 taught in Genesis 17-20 - Abimelech called it what it is: a great sin. Adultery is one of the weightier matters; there is no animal sacrifice that atones for it. Genesis 22:1-3 taught in Genesis 21-24 - God did tempt Abraham: Take now thy son, thine only son Isaac. Ishmael was alive, but the Most High counted Isaac the only son, because Ishmael was born of the flesh, of a plan the Lord never spoke, while Isaac was the child of the promise. - Abraham rose up early in the morning and went. No hesitation, no debating with the word; that is obedience. Genesis 22:7-8 taught in Genesis 21-24 - Isaac asked, Where is the lamb for a burnt offering? Abraham answered, My son, God will provide himself a lamb. He trusted the Most High with what was missing. Genesis 22:13-14 taught in Genesis 21-24 - Once the obedience was fulfilled, God provided the sacrifice: a ram caught in a thicket by his horns, offered in the stead of his son, just as Abraham had told Isaac. Abraham called the place Jehovahjireh: in the mount of the Lord it shall be seen. Exodus Exodus 3:16-18 taught in Exodus 2-5 - They shall hearken to thy voice; and thou and the elders shall say unto the king of Egypt, The LORD God of the Hebrews hath met with us: let us go, we beseech thee, three days' journey into the wilderness, that we may sacrifice to the LORD our God. Exodus 5:3 taught in Exodus 2-5 - They said, The God of the Hebrews hath met with us: let us go, we pray thee, three days' journey into the desert, and sacrifice unto the LORD our God; lest he fall upon us with pestilence, or with the sword. Exodus 5:6-9 taught in Exodus 2-5 - Pharaoh commanded the taskmasters the same day: ye shall no more give the people straw to make brick; let them go and gather straw for themselves; and the tale of the bricks ye shall lay upon them, ye shall not diminish ought thereof. For they be idle; therefore they cry, saying, Let us go and sacrifice to our God. Exodus 5:15-19 taught in Exodus 2-5 - Pharaoh answered, Ye are idle, ye are idle: therefore ye say, Let us go and do sacrifice to the LORD. The charge of idleness is the standing answer to any who would go serve God, whether it is the three days' journey or keeping the Sabbath and the new moons now. Exodus 8:5-8 taught in Exodus 6-9 - Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters, and the frogs came up and covered the land of Egypt. With this second plague the Most High was mocking Heqet, the Egyptian idol god of the frogs. - The magicians did so with their enchantments and brought up frogs, but just as with the water they could only add to the plague; they could not take the frogs away. - So Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron and said, Entreat the Lord that he may take away the frogs. Why did Pharaoh not call on Heqet, the god of frogs? He had to go to the Lord. Exodus 8:25-32 taught in Exodus 6-9 - Pharaoh said, Go sacrifice to your God in the land; but Moses answered, It is not meet, for we should sacrifice the abomination of the Egyptians before their eyes, and will they not stone us? Israel's sacrifices were the very animals Egypt held sacred, so Israel must go three days' journey into the wilderness. Exodus 10:24-26 taught in Exodus 10-13 - After three days of darkness Pharaoh called for Moses: go, serve the Lord, only let your flocks and your herds be stayed. Go, but leave all your possessions in Egypt. - Moses refused: our cattle also shall go with us, there shall not an hoof be left behind. Not a hoof, a hair, or a heifer would stay in Egypt, for thereof must Israel take to serve the Lord, and we know not with what we must serve the Lord until we come thither. Exodus 12:3-5 taught in Exodus 10-13 - The lamb was to be without blemish, a male of the first year, taken from the sheep or from the goats. This is a foreshadowing: the feast days and sacrifices are a shadow of things to come, but the body is of Christ. - The lamb without blemish and without spot points to Christ, who was sinless, verily foreordained before the foundation of the world but manifest in these last times for the nation of Israel. - Precept 1 Peter 1:19-20 : The precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot, foreordained before the foundation of the world. Exodus 12:24-28 taught in Exodus 10-13 - This thing is an ordinance to thee and to thy sons for ever, kept even when Israel comes into the land the Lord promised. When the children ask, What mean ye by this service? the answer is, It is the sacrifice of the Lord's passover, who passed over the houses of the children of Israel in Egypt when he smote the Egyptians and delivered our houses. Exodus 13:14-16 taught in Exodus 10-13 - When thy son asketh thee in time to come, saying, What is this? thou shalt say, By strength of hand the Lord brought us out from Egypt, from the house of bondage: when Pharaoh would hardly let us go, the Lord slew all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, therefore the firstborn are sacrificed or redeemed. - The children must be taught the righteousness of why the feast is kept. Ask the children of this land why they keep Christmas and they answer that Santa Claus is coming down the chimney; Israel's children are to be taught the works of the Most High instead. - It is for a token upon thine hand and for frontlets between thine eyes, for by strength of hand the Lord brought us forth out of Egypt. Exodus 16:22-30 taught in Exodus 14-17 - For the brothers and sisters far from a congregation: you may have to travel and you may have to be the firstfruits in your area. The first assemblies met in houses, and that is how camps start; a man will drive hours to a club, so drive for the truth, and the Lord honors that faith. - Precept Romans 16:3-5 : Greet the church that is in their house, and Epaenetus the firstfruits of Achaia; congregations begin with the diligent few. - Precept Matthew 6:33 : Seek ye first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things shall be added; the Lord sees the sacrifice it takes to get to the congregation. Exodus 18:9-11 taught in Exodus 18-21 - Naaman the Syrian, healed of his leprosy in Jordan, confessed that there is no God in all the earth but in Israel. His faith was so strong he vowed to offer neither burnt offering nor sacrifice unto other gods, and asked pardon for even bowing in the house of Rimmon with his master. - Precept Psalms 96:5-8 : All the gods of the nations are idols, but the Lord made the heavens; give unto the Lord the glory due unto his name. - Precept 2 Kings 5:14-18 : Naaman dipped seven times in Jordan and was clean, and confessed there is no God in all the earth but in Israel; a heathen vowed to sacrifice to no other god but the Lord. Exodus 23:14-17 taught in Exodus 22-25 - The feast of harvest, the firstfruits of thy labours, is also known as Pentecost and the feast of weeks; and the feast of ingathering, in the end of the year, is also known as the feast of tabernacles and the feast of booths. Exodus 23:18-19 taught in Exodus 22-25 - Thou shalt not offer the blood of my sacrifice with leavened bread, neither shall the fat of my sacrifice remain until the morning. The first of the firstfruits of thy land thou shalt bring into the house of the Lord thy God. Exodus 24:4-8 taught in Exodus 22-25 - Moses wrote all the words of the Lord, rose up early, and builded an altar under the hill with twelve pillars according to the twelve tribes of Israel; young men offered burnt offerings and peace offerings of oxen. - Moses took half of the blood in basons and half he sprinkled on the altar; then he took the book of the covenant and read in the audience of the people, and they said, All that the Lord hath said will we do, and be obedient. And he sprinkled the blood on the people: Behold the blood of the covenant, which the Lord hath made with you concerning all these words. This sprinkling ties in later to the book of Hebrews and its teaching on sacrifice. Exodus 25:1-2 taught in Exodus 22-25 - Speak unto the children of Israel, that they bring me an offering: of every man that giveth it willingly with his heart ye shall take my offering. The Lord wants a willing heart in giving, not grudgingly or of necessity or only because the law says so, but because you know your giving benefits someone in need or the house of God, whatever it needs, the lights, the roof, the floor, the tables, the leadership's travel. Exodus 25:3-7 taught in Exodus 22-25 - The offering was gold, silver, brass, blue, purple, and scarlet, fine linen, goats' hair, rams' skins dyed red, badgers' skins, shittim wood, oil for the light, spices, and onyx stones for the ephod and the breastplate. Thank the Most High he requires no gold and silver now, for half of us would have nothing to give; under the new covenant the offering is the body presented a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable. - The badgers' skins settle a confusion: the Lord commanded Israel to handle animal skins and hair to build his own tabernacle. So the laws about not touching that which is defiled, the carcass of the unclean beast, go into the matter of sacrifice and coming into the temple, not into everyday handling. A boar-bristle brush is not sin; brush your hair, brothers. - Precept Romans 12:1 : Present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God; that is the offering of him that has no gold nor silver. Exodus 27:1-8 taught in Exodus 26-29 - Verses one through eight go into the altar in which the sacrifices were done in the tabernacle: the altar of shittim wood foursquare, its horns of the same, overlaid with brass, with its pans, shovels, basons, fleshhooks, and firepans, the grate of network of brass, and the staves to bear it. Exodus 29:1-4 taught in Exodus 26-29 - To hallow Aaron and his sons to minister in the priest's office: one young bullock and two rams without blemish, with unleavened bread, cakes tempered with oil, and wafers anointed with oil, brought in one basket to the door of the tabernacle of the congregation. Exodus 29:5-9 taught in Exodus 26-29 - Ecclesiasticus records the same consecration: Moses anointed him with holy oil, an everlasting covenant to Aaron and to his seed so long as the heavens should remain, to minister unto Him, execute the office of the priesthood, offer the sacrifices, and teach Jacob the testimonies and inform Israel in His laws. The priest's job was the offerings and teaching the nation the law, statutes, and commandments. - What happened to that covenant is answered in Malachi, where the commandment is spoken to the priests: the covenant with Levi was of life and peace, the priest's lips should keep knowledge and they should seek the law at his mouth, for he is the messenger of the Lord of hosts; but ye are departed out of the way, ye have caused many to stumble at the law, ye have corrupted the covenant of Levi. The priests were finessing the offerings, keeping the best animals for themselves and sacrificing the blind and the broken, and they perverted the teachings of the law for their own benefit. - Precept Ecclesiasticus 45:15-17 : The everlasting covenant of the priesthood with Aaron and his seed: to offer the sacrifices and to teach Jacob the testimonies and inform Israel in His laws. Exodus 29:10-14 taught in Exodus 26-29 - The bullock is killed before the Lord by the door of the tabernacle, its blood put upon the horns of the altar with the finger, the fat burnt upon the altar, and the flesh, skin, and dung burnt with fire without the camp: it is a sin offering. This is the introduction to the categories of offerings; there is the sin offering. Exodus 29:15-18 taught in Exodus 26-29 - The first ram is slain, its blood sprinkled round about upon the altar, and the whole ram burnt upon the altar: it is a burnt offering unto the Lord, a sweet savour, an offering made by fire. There is the second category, the burnt offering. Exodus 29:19-28 taught in Exodus 26-29 - The bread and the parts of the ram are put in the hands of Aaron and his sons and waved for a wave offering before the Lord, then burnt upon the altar; and the breast of the wave offering and the shoulder of the heave offering are sanctified for Aaron and his sons by a statute for ever. There go the wave offering and the heave offering, which you will read about throughout the first five books, Leviticus predominantly. Exodus 29:29-34 taught in Exodus 26-29 - Aaron and his sons eat the flesh of the ram and the bread at the door of the tabernacle, the things wherewith the atonement was made; a stranger shall not eat thereof, because they are holy. And whatever of the flesh or the bread remains unto the morning is burnt with fire and not eaten: no eating the leftovers of the offering, because it is holy. Exodus 29:35-42 taught in Exodus 26-29 - Seven days shalt thou consecrate them, offering every day a bullock for a sin offering for atonement, cleansing the altar and anointing it to sanctify it, that it be an altar most holy. - Then the continual offering: two lambs of the first year day by day continually, one lamb in the morning and the other at even, with the tenth deal of flour mingled with beaten oil and the drink offering of wine; a continual burnt offering throughout your generations at the door of the tabernacle, where the Lord meets and speaks with Israel. Exodus 29:43-46 taught in Exodus 26-29 - The tabernacle shall be sanctified by His glory, and Aaron and his sons sanctified to minister in the priest's office; for the Most High to enter and deal with Israel, everything had to be sanctified. That was serious. - I will dwell among the children of Israel, and will be their God. He was in no other nation's tabernacle, temple, or synagogue, and though there is no tabernacle today it is still the same case: He is in the midst of Israel and none else, which excludes everybody else from the benefits of having the Most High as their God. There is nothing to be ashamed of in the fact that He chose Israel only, and nothing changed across testaments: blessed be the Lord God of Israel, for he hath visited and redeemed his people, and that is the purpose of Christ, to redeem His people. - The other nations knew it. When the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin heard the temple was being rebuilt they came saying, Let us build with you, for we seek your God; and Zerubbabel, Jeshua, and the chief of the fathers answered, Ye have nothing to do with us to build an house unto our God, but we ourselves together will build unto the Lord God of Israel. That is the mindset for these last days: Israel does not need the other nations' assistance, but rebuilds one another spiritually as a nation while awaiting Christ's return to restore the kingdom. - He brought them forth out of the land of Egypt that He may dwell among them: I am the Lord their God. Israel should walk confident, special, and chosen above all nations of people, for the Most High is faithful and belongs to no one else; repent from spiritual fornication and return to the Most High. - Precept Ezra 4:1-3 : The adversaries said, Let us build with you, for we seek your God; the fathers answered, Ye have nothing to do with us, but we ourselves together will build unto the Lord God of Israel. Exodus 30:6-9 taught in Exodus 30-33 - No strange incense went on it, and no burnt sacrifice, meat offering, or drink offering; this altar was for one specific incense only. The service had to be exactly as prescribed, and deviation carried death, which is a reason to thank the Lord for Christ. Exodus 30:10 taught in Exodus 30-33 - Aaron made an atonement upon the horns of it once in a year with the blood of the sin offering of atonements; it is most holy unto the Lord. This altar served the day of atonement. - On the tenth day of the seventh month Israel afflicted their souls and did no work at all, and the priest made an atonement for the sanctuary, the tabernacle, the altar, the priests, and all the people of the congregation, to cleanse them from all their sins before the Lord; an everlasting statute, once a year. - The priests went always into the first tabernacle accomplishing the service of God, but into the second went the high priest alone once every year, not without blood. Christ offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, so the day of atonement is still kept by afflicting the soul and doing no work, but without the animal sacrifice, because Christ took the place of the animal. - Precept Leviticus 16:29-34 : On the tenth day of the seventh month ye shall afflict your souls, and the priest makes an atonement to cleanse the children of Israel from all their sins, an everlasting statute. - Precept Hebrews 10:10-12 : The daily sacrifices can never take away sins, but this man offered one sacrifice for sins for ever and sat down on the right hand of God. Exodus 30:11-16 taught in Exodus 30-33 - The ransom was half a shekel after the shekel of the sanctuary, from every one that passed among them that were numbered, from twenty years old and above; the rich gave no more and the poor gave no less, to make an atonement for their souls. - The atonement money was appointed for the service of the tabernacle of the congregation. The gold, the wood, the curtains, and the fabrics all had to be bought and kept up, and the tabernacle moved with the nation through the wilderness; that is the same reason offerings are gathered in the congregation today, because the house of the Most High cannot be built or kept without it. Exodus 30:17-21 taught in Exodus 30-33 - The laver of brass, with his foot also of brass, stood between the tabernacle of the congregation and the altar, with water in it; a great brass bowl set on a brass base. - Aaron and his sons washed their hands and their feet thereat when they went into the tabernacle of the congregation and when they came near to the altar to minister, that they die not; the priests could not go in unclean. - It was a statute for ever to Aaron and to his seed throughout their generations. Exodus 30:22-33 taught in Exodus 30-33 - With it were anointed the tabernacle of the congregation, the ark of the testimony, the table and all his vessels, the candlestick and his vessels, the altar of incense, the altar of burnt offering with all his vessels, and the laver and his foot, that they be most holy; whatsoever toucheth them shall be holy. Aaron and his sons were anointed and consecrated with it to minister in the priest's office. Exodus 31:7-11 taught in Exodus 30-33 - The wise hearted made all that was commanded: the tabernacle of the congregation, the ark of the testimony, the mercy seat that is thereupon, all the furniture of the tabernacle, the table and his furniture, the pure candlestick with all his furniture, the altar of incense, the altar of burnt offering with all his furniture, and the laver and his foot. Exodus 32:1-6 taught in Exodus 30-33 - Aaron built an altar before it and made proclamation, To morrow is a feast to the LORD; and the people rose up early, offered burnt offerings and peace offerings, sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to play. Israel kept provoking God, and the Lord still brought the nation into the promised land as he promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Exodus 32:7-10 taught in Exodus 30-33 - The Lord told Moses, Go, get thee down; for thy people, which thou broughtest out of the land of Egypt, have corrupted themselves. They turned aside quickly out of the way, made a molten calf, worshipped it, and sacrificed thereunto. Not forty days gone, and they had already left his commandments. - The spirit that was in Israel in Egypt was still in Israel when they left. It is the same coming into this truth: the evil carried in from the world will corrupt you and turn you from the Lord if it is not put off. - I have seen this people, and, behold, it is a stiffnecked people. That has been Israel's reputation with the Father from the beginning; without the laws of God we are a carnal, rebellious people, which is why these last days call for humbleness and repentance, not bringing the world's rhetoric into the congregation. - Now therefore let me alone, that my wrath may wax hot against them, and that I may consume them: and I will make of thee a great nation. Moses was of the tribe of Levi, of the seed of Jacob, so the Lord could have started over with him. - Precept Ecclesiastes 5:1 : Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God; the evil still in a man from the world will corrupt him as it did our forefathers. Exodus 32:30-35 taught in Exodus 30-33 - Moses said unto the people, Ye have sinned a great sin. They had broken the first two commandments just given at Sinai: no other gods before him, and no graven image to bow down to and serve. - Moses returned unto the LORD to mediate: yet now, if thou wilt forgive their sin; and if not, blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book which thou hast written. That is a real leader, putting himself in the way of harm for his people. - The Lord answered, Whosoever hath sinned against me, him will I blot out of my book; therefore now go, lead the people, and mine Angel shall go before thee; nevertheless in the day when I visit I will visit their sin upon them. And the LORD plagued the people, because they made the calf, which Aaron made. Exodus 34:11-16 taught in Exodus 34-37 - The snare is spelled out: they go a whoring after their gods, they call thee, thou eat of their sacrifice and partake in serving their gods; thou take of their daughters unto thy sons, and their daughters go a whoring after their gods and make thy sons go a whoring after their gods. Exodus 34:22-24 taught in Exodus 34-37 - Thrice in the year shall all your men children appear before the Lord GOD, the God of Israel. The law is written again in Deuteronomy: the feast of unleavened bread, which is the Passover season, the feast of weeks, which is Pentecost, and the feast of tabernacles; and they shall not appear before the Lord empty, for each had to bring his sacrifice. Exodus 34:25-26 taught in Exodus 34-37 - Thou shalt not offer the blood of my sacrifice with leaven; neither shall the sacrifice of the feast of the passover be left unto the morning: it had to be eaten up or burned. - The first of the firstfruits of thy land thou shalt bring unto the house of the LORD thy God. And thou shalt not seethe a kid in his mother's milk: a young one still in his mother's milk, as veal is taken for instance, is not ready to be eaten; it is unlawful. Exodus 34:27-28 taught in Exodus 34-37 - Moses was there with the Lord forty days and forty nights; he did neither eat bread, nor drink water. And he wrote upon the tables the words of the covenant, the ten commandments; the words of the covenant take in the directions of the sacrifices, which animals were to be offered and how it was to be done, together with the commandments. Exodus 35:4-9 taught in Exodus 34-37 - Whosoever is of a willing heart, let him bring the Lord's offering: gold, silver, and brass; blue, purple, scarlet, fine linen, and goats' hair; rams' skins dyed red and badgers' skins; shittim wood; oil for the light and spices for the anointing oil and the sweet incense; and onyx stones and stones to be set for the ephod and the breastplate. These are the offerings the people would bring unto the Lord. Exodus 35:10-19 taught in Exodus 34-37 - The list runs through the whole work: the tabernacle, his tent, his covering, his taches, boards, bars, pillars, and sockets; the ark of the covenant with the staves and the mercy seat, and the vail of the covering; the table with his staves and vessels and the shewbread; the candlestick, which is the menorah, with his lamps and the oil for the light; the incense altar; the altar of burnt offering, where the burnt offering was burnt, with his brasen grate; the laver; the hangings of the court; and the cloths of service, the holy garments for Aaron the priest and the garments of his sons, to minister in the priest's office. Exodus 35:20-29 taught in Exodus 34-37 - The congregation departed from the presence of Moses, and they came, every one whose heart stirred him up and every one whom his spirit made willing, and brought the Lord's offering for the work of the tabernacle; the people brought the gold and silver and all the things listed willingly. Exodus 36:1-3 taught in Exodus 34-37 - They received of Moses all the offering which the children of Israel had brought for the work of the service of the sanctuary; and the people brought yet unto him free offerings every morning. Exodus 36:4-7 taught in Exodus 34-37 - Moses gave commandment, and they caused it to be proclaimed throughout the camp that neither man nor woman make any more work for the offering of the sanctuary; the people were restrained from bringing, for the stuff they had was sufficient for all the work, and too much. Exodus 37:6-9 taught in Exodus 34-37 - Annually the high priest would sprinkle blood on the mercy seat to atone for the sins of all the people. The purpose and desire of the Most High is to dwell among His people and to commune with them; the layout of the tabernacle, with the steps of sacrifice and cleansing, is designed to bring sinful mankind to a loving and holy God. Exodus 38:1-8 taught in Exodus 38-40 - This chapter is the application of the instructions already given for the tabernacle: the altar of burnt offering of shittim wood overlaid with brass, its vessels, and its staves were made exactly as commanded. Exodus 38:24-26 taught in Exodus 38-40 - All the gold, silver, and brass occupied for the work was counted. The silver came a bekah for every man, half a shekel after the shekel of the sanctuary, from every one numbered from twenty years old and upward, six hundred thousand and three thousand and five hundred and fifty men. Thousands of men contributed to the cause of the sanctuary being built. - Israel in the wilderness was delivered, not in captivity; today we are waking up in our captivity, and the buildings we get for sanctuaries require work, wood, service, and labor. Yet many do not have the spirit to give. If you have trouble coming up out of your pocket to help the cause of the Lord, examine yourself whether ye be in the faith, whether you really believe and really study. - After Babylon invaded Jerusalem our fathers were captives, yet they still made a collection for the house of the Lord, not a required amount but according to every man's power. Likewise today the congregations do not push a ten percent; you give according to your power, and the Lord knows how much power you have to give. Sadly some give more than those who have more power to give than they. - He which soweth sparingly shall reap sparingly, and he which soweth bountifully shall reap bountifully; that does not mean the Most High blesses you with a three story house, for you may be storing up treasures in heaven. Give as you purpose in your heart, not grudgingly or of necessity, for God loveth a cheerful giver; giving with an attitude is worse than keeping the money. Exodus 38:29-31 taught in Exodus 38-40 - The brass of the offering, seventy talents and two thousand and four hundred shekels, made the sockets of the door, the brasen altar and its grate and vessels, the sockets of the court, and all the pins of the tabernacle and the court. Every material was accounted for; not everybody had the spirit to contribute physically, but everybody put their brick in and gave something for the cause. Exodus 40:16-33 taught in Exodus 38-40 - Thus did Moses according to all that the Lord commanded him. In the first month in the second year, on the first day of the month, the tabernacle was reared up: the ark with the testimony and the mercy seat, the table with the bread in order, the candlestick with the lamps, the golden altar with sweet incense, the altar of burnt offering, the laver for washing, and the court round about; so Moses finished the work. Leviticus Leviticus 1:1-3 taught in Leviticus 1 - The Lord called unto Moses out of the tabernacle of the congregation, the tent just reared up at the end of Exodus 40, and gave the law of the offerings brought of the cattle, of the herd and of the flock. - The burnt sacrifice of the herd is of the cattle, such as the bullock and the heifer. Numbers 18:18-19 taught in Numbers 15-18 - The flesh of them was the priest's, as the wave breast and as the right shoulder; all the heave offerings of the holy things which the children of Israel offered unto the Lord were given to Aaron and his sons and his daughters by a statute for ever, to the lineage of the Levites. - Exodus 29 shows how the wave offering and the heave offering were done. Numbers 29:12-16 taught in Numbers 27-30 - The first day's offering was thirteen young bullocks, two rams, and fourteen lambs of the first year without blemish, with their meat offerings by number and a kid of the goats for a sin offering, beside the continual burnt offering. - Precept Leviticus 23:33-36 : The fifteenth day of the seventh month shall be the feast of tabernacles for seven days; the first day an holy convocation, and the eighth day a solemn assembly with no servile work. Numbers 29:35-38 taught in Numbers 27-30 - The eighth day is a solemn assembly, the last day, with no servile work; its offering was one bullock, one ram, and seven lambs of the first year without blemish, with their meat and drink offerings and a goat for a sin offering, beside the continual burnt offering. Numbers 30:1-2 taught in Numbers 27-30 - If a man vow a vow unto the Lord, or swear an oath to bind his soul with a bond, he shall not break his word; he shall do according to all that proceedeth out of his mouth. - A vow is promising the Lord you will do a thing. That is why we say the Lord's will: the Lord's will I will be there, the Lord's will I will teach that day. - A vow made before you came into this truth does not stand, for you were not vowing to the God of Israel then; if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature, and old things are passed away. Deuteronomy Deuteronomy 4:17-19 taught in Deuteronomy 3-6 - The likeness of any beast on the earth goes back to idols like Heqet the frog god and Sobek the god of the river; the likeness of any winged fowl to Horus the falcon; anything that creepeth on the ground to the beetles, flies, and locusts they deified; any fish in the waters to Sobek and to Dagon the fish god of the Babylonians, whose symbolism carries into pagan imagery to this day. - The eagle and the falcon symbols of the powers of this world trace back to the gods and goddesses of Egypt, because this present power is spiritual Egypt and takes after her. - Lest thou lift up thine eyes unto heaven and be driven to worship the sun, the moon, and the stars: that is Ra the sun god and Nut the sky goddess, and it is also astrology, the zodiac, and witchcraft today. Deuteronomy 33:11 taught in Deuteronomy 31-34 - Bless, Lord, his substance, and accept the work of his hands. Joshua 22:13-14 taught in Joshua 21-24 - Israel sent Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest with ten princes, one head of a chief house from every tribe. When you send Phinehas it is a problem, because of the kind of man Phinehas was: where he showed up, the zeal of the Most High showed up with him. - At Baalpeor the men of Israel began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab, bowed down to their gods, and joined themselves unto Baalpeor, and the anger of the Most High was kindled against Israel. - One man of Israel was so bold he brought a Midianitish woman to his brethren in the sight of Moses and all the congregation while they wept before the door of the tabernacle. It was once a shameful thing for our men to be seen like that; today men and women of Israel walk boldly and proudly with the nations, that same spirit. - Phinehas saw it, rose up from among the congregation, took a javelin, went after the man of Israel into the tent, and thrust both of them through, and the plague was stayed from the children of Israel; those that died in the plague were twenty and four thousand. So when Phinehas showed up at Gilead, everybody knew it was about to go down. - Precept Numbers 25:1-3 : Israel began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab, ate of the sacrifices of their gods and bowed down to them, and Israel joined himself unto Baalpeor, and the anger of the Lord was kindled. Joshua 22:21-23 taught in Joshua 21-24 - If we built an altar to turn from following the Lord, or to offer burnt offerings, meat offerings, or peace offerings on it, let the Lord himself require it. Joshua 22:24-25 taught in Joshua 21-24 - They feared that generations later the children on one side of Jordan would tell the children on the other side that they were not the children of Israel, shutting them out from fearing the Lord, from the temple, the feast days, and the sacrifices. Joshua 22:26-29 taught in Joshua 21-24 - The altar was not for burnt offering nor for sacrifice; it was a witness between us and you and our generations after us, a memorial, so the two and a half tribes could do the service of the Lord before him in the place he chose, along with the rest of the tribes, and nobody could stop them. - If anyone ever said to their generations, Ye have no part in the Lord, the answer would stand built in stone: behold the pattern of the altar of the LORD, which our fathers made, not for burnt offerings nor for sacrifices, but it is a witness between us and you. - God forbid that we should rebel against the Lord to build an altar for burnt offerings, meat offerings, or sacrifices, beside the altar of the LORD our God that is before his tabernacle: the sacrifices belonged in front of the altar the Most High set in his chosen place. Joshua 22:32-34 taught in Joshua 21-24 - Phinehas and the princes returned from Gilead to the land of Canaan and brought the children of Israel word again: all is good, the altar is a memorial so the generations after do not forget that our people are on that side Jordan too, and they can come in and keep the feasts and do their sacrifices with us. Joshua 24:21-25 taught in Joshua 21-24 - The people said unto Joshua, Nay; but we will serve the LORD. It is the same thing Israel told Moses back then; we came into that covenant again, this time without the blood. - Joshua said, Ye are witnesses against yourselves that ye have chosen you the LORD, to serve him; and they said, We are witnesses. Everybody was in full agreement. - Put away the strange gods which are among you, and incline your heart unto the LORD God of Israel; and the people said, The LORD our God will we serve, and his voice will we obey. - So Joshua made a covenant with the people that day, and set them a statute and an ordinance in Shechem, the same thing Moses his predecessor did at the mountain; Joshua was his successor and did the same, though without the blood. - Precept Exodus 24:3-8 : All the people answered with one voice, All the words which the Lord hath said will we do; Moses wrote all the words of the Lord, built an altar and twelve pillars, read the book of the covenant in the audience of the people, and sprinkled the blood of the covenant on the people. Judges Judges 5:1-2 taught in Judges 5-8 - Deborah and Barak sing praise to the Lord for the avenging of Israel, when the people willingly offered themselves. That is what the Most High wants from us: a willing heart in all that we do, in the keeping of the commandments, in the keeping of the feast days, and in the praise of him. - How do we willingly offer ourselves to the Lord in the twenty-first century? By giving up whatever presents itself as an obstacle between us and the Lord. It may be father, mother, husband, wife, or children; it may be drugs, money, or working on the sabbath. If you willingly offer yourself, you will not let any stumbling block keep you from the Lord. - Precept Exodus 35:22 : At the building of the tabernacle in the wilderness, both men and women as many as were willing hearted brought their gold unto the Lord; we have to have that same willing heart today. Judges 6:25-27 taught in Judges 5-8 - The same night the Lord tells him to throw down his own father's altar of Baal, cut down the grove by it, and build an altar unto the Lord in its place. Notice this: even before the split of the kingdom, the tribes that would become the northern kingdom were already dabbling with Baal, worshipping the Lord in some fashion while holding onto the idol. - Gideon took ten of his servants and did as the Lord said, but by night, because he feared his father's household and the men of the city; they worshipped that idol and would have killed him in the daylight. Judges 11:29-31 taught in Judges 9-12 - Jephthah vowed a vow unto the LORD: if thou shalt without fail deliver the children of Ammon into mine hands, then whatsoever cometh forth of the doors of my house to meet me, when I return in peace, shall surely be the LORD'S, and I will offer it up for a burnt offering. The vow was made before the battle, an offering promised to the Lord for the victory: whatever came out of his doors first would be given over to the Lord. Judges 11:36-40 taught in Judges 9-12 - Jephthah did not burn his daughter as a human sacrifice. Israel did not do human sacrifices; that was Molech worship among the Canaanites. Read the end of the passage: at the end of two months she returned unto her father, who did with her according to his vow which he had vowed, and she knew no man. If she had been put to death, there would be no reason for the scripture to say she knew no man; her life was committed to the Lord and she remained a virgin. - A lot of people try to say Jephthah sacrificed his daughter, because our people do not understand the scriptures; keep reading and the text itself answers it. It is a translation difference around the word offering: she was presented to the Lord to serve him, not sent up as a burnt sacrifice. Judges 13:15-16 taught in Judges 13-16 - Manoah tried to detain the angel and make ready a kid for him, but the angel refused: though thou detain me, I will not eat of thy bread, and if thou wilt offer a burnt offering, thou must offer it unto the Lord. - The angel knew Manoah might try to offer it up to him, since he appeared like a god, so he directed the offering to the Lord. Israel is quick to worship anything that looks like it could be God because we cannot see the Most High, which is why the scriptures warn against the worshipping of angels. Judges 13:19-21 taught in Judges 13-16 - Manoah took a kid with a meat offering and offered it upon a rock unto the Lord, and the angel did wondrously: when the flame went up toward heaven from off the altar, the angel of the Lord ascended in the flame and went out of their sight. Judges 13:22-23 taught in Judges 13-16 - His wife reasoned rightly: if the Lord were pleased to kill us, he would not have received a burnt offering and a meat offering at our hands, neither would he have shewed us all these things. Judges 16:23-25 taught in Judges 13-16 - The lords of the Philistines gathered together to offer a great sacrifice unto Dagon their god, an idolatrous ritual, and to rejoice, for they said, our god hath delivered Samson our enemy into our hand. Judges 17:7-10 taught in Judges 17-20 - When Micah learned the man was a Levite, of the tribe known for the priesthood and the knowledge of the sacrifices, he offered him a deal: dwell with me, be unto me a father and a priest, ten shekels of silver by the year, a suit of apparel, and thy victuals. He hired himself a personal priest for his idols. Judges 18:30-31 taught in Judges 17-20 - Dan stayed heavy in idolatry all the way through history and never changed. After the kingdom split, Jeroboam feared that if the people kept going up to sacrifice at the house of the LORD in Jerusalem, their heart would turn again unto Rehoboam king of Judah and they would kill him; so he took counsel and made two calves of gold with his own hands, doubling the iniquity of the wilderness, and said, behold thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt. - Precept 1 Kings 12:27 : Jeroboam's fear: if this people go up to sacrifice at Jerusalem, their heart shall turn again unto their lord Rehoboam, and they shall kill me. Judges 20:26-28 taught in Judges 17-20 - Then all the children of Israel and all the people went up unto the house of God, wept, sat there before the LORD, fasted that day until even, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the LORD. This time the whole nation humbled itself. Judges 21:1-6 taught in Judges 21 - The people came to the house of God and sat there till evening before God, lifted up their voices and wept sore, asking why it had come to pass that there should be one tribe lacking in Israel. The next day they rose early, built an altar, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. Ruth Ruth 1:3-5 taught in Ruth 1-3 - Elimelech, Naomi's husband, died, and she was left with her two sons. The sons took them wives of the women of Moab, Orpah and Ruth, and after they dwelt there about ten years Mahlon and Chilion died also, leaving Naomi without her husband and without her sons. - Were the sons of Israel supposed to take wives of the women of Moab while sojourning there? No; but remember what was just read at the end of Judges, that every man did that which was right in his own eyes. And this was not the first time Israel dealt with the women of Moab. - Precept Numbers 25:1-2 : Israel had already committed whoredom with the daughters of Moab at Shittim, and the people did eat and bowed down to their gods. 1 Samuel 1 Samuel 1:1-3 taught in 1 Samuel 1-3 - Elkanah went up out of his city yearly to worship and to sacrifice unto the Lord of hosts in Shiloh, where the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, the priests of the Lord, were. Shiloh is another name for Jerusalem. 1 Samuel 1:21 taught in 1 Samuel 1-3 - The man Elkanah, and all his house, went up to offer unto the Lord the yearly sacrifice, and his vow. What is that yearly sacrifice going into? Deuteronomy 16:16. 1 Samuel 2:13-14 taught in 1 Samuel 1-3 - The priests' custom with the people was that when any man offered sacrifice, the priest's servant came, while the flesh was in seething, with a fleshhook of three teeth in his hand, and struck it into the pan, or kettle, or caldron, or pot; all that the fleshhook brought up the priest took for himself. They would dip it in, and what came up was the priest's portion of meat for that day; all the Levites did that, based on the sacrifices Israel brought in. - This is how the Lord took care of Levi. He told Levi in the law that Levi would have no inheritance of land among the tribes; the Lord provided for them through the sacrifices that Israel brought, so they had need of nothing. 1 Samuel 2:15-17 taught in 1 Samuel 1-3 - These were devils serving in the house of the Lord, strong-arming the offerings. Wherefore the sin of the young men was very great before the Lord: for men abhorred the offering of the Lord. These priests were disrespecting the offering of the Lord. 1 Samuel 2:18-21 taught in 1 Samuel 1-3 - But Samuel ministered before the Lord, being a child, girded with a linen ephod; moreover his mother made him a little coat, and brought it to him from year to year, when she came up with her husband to offer the yearly sacrifice. 1 Samuel 2:27-29 taught in 1 Samuel 1-3 - There came a man of God unto Eli, saying, Thus saith the Lord, Did I plainly appear unto the house of thy father, when they were in Egypt in Pharaoh's house? That is talking about Levi, going into Moses. Did I choose him out of all the tribes of Israel to be my priest, to offer upon mine altar, to burn incense, to wear an ephod before me? and did I give unto the house of thy father all the offerings made by fire of the children of Israel? They had need of nothing; they were well taken care of. - Wherefore kick ye at my sacrifice and at mine offering, which I have commanded in my habitation; and honourest thy sons above me? You are disrespecting me, is what he is saying: I am supposed to be honoured in everything before the children of Israel, and you let your sons disrespect my offerings. - Take that into account: do you honour your children above what the Lord says to do? Can they do no wrong, even when they are doing real wrong against the Lord, keeping no commandments, never showing up on the sabbath day, and still living under your roof grown? If they are of age, they know right from wrong, and they are under your roof while you keep the commandments, then they had better be keeping the commandments: showing up to every feast day, the blowing of trumpets, the day of atonement, the passover, the same as you. When they are of age they can go their own way; but they should not be living under your roof and breaking the commandments of God. You honour your children above God when you allow that. 1 Samuel 3:2-3 taught in 1 Samuel 1-3 - Sacrifice was never the most important thing to the Lord; not the blood of bulls and of goats, but mercy upon one another and the keeping of the commandments. The sacrifices were added because of transgression, the animal's blood taken in your place so the Most High would not have to kill you; you read of it from Genesis 3, where the Lord took the skins after Adam sinned. Yet there were some things you could not sacrifice for, abominations for which a man's own blood was required. - Precept Matthew 12:5-7 : Have ye not read in the law, how that on the sabbath days the priests in the temple profane the sabbath, and are blameless? In this place is one greater than the temple; and if ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless. - Precept Numbers 28:9-10 : The burnt offering of every sabbath: the priests sacrificed a lamb in the morning and in the evening on the sabbath because the Lord commanded it. - Precept Hosea 6:6 : I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings. This is what Christ was quoting, for the New Testament was not yet written; the knowledge of God is the keeping of the commandments. - Precept Jeremiah 7:21-23 : I spake not unto your fathers, nor commanded them in the day that I brought them out of the land of Egypt, concerning burnt offerings or sacrifices: but this thing commanded I them, saying, Obey my voice, and I will be your God, and ye shall be my people. 1 Samuel 3:11-14 taught in 1 Samuel 1-3 - Therefore I have sworn unto the house of Eli, that the iniquity of Eli's house shall not be purged with sacrifice nor offering for ever. When the Lord is mad, the Lord is mad: thus we are in the lands of our captivity 400 years and counting, and you have heard the history of the Spanish Inquisition, how we were burned for keeping the commandments; his anger burns unto the lowest hell. 1 Samuel 4:10-11 taught in 1 Samuel 4-7 - The ark of God was taken, and the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were slain. Those two were wicked as hell, sleeping with the women that assembled at the door of the congregation and finessing the people's offerings, so in this battle the Most High allowed their lives to be taken, exactly as had been prophesied against the house of Eli. 1 Samuel 6:1-6 taught in 1 Samuel 4-7 - The priests answered, send it not empty, but in any wise return him a trespass offering; then ye shall be healed. A trespass offering acknowledges you did wrong. The offering was five golden emerods and five golden mice, according to the number of the lords of the Philistines, images of the very things that marred the land, and ye shall give glory unto the God of Israel; peradventure he will lighten his hand from off you, and from off your gods, and from off your land. 1 Samuel 6:7-12 taught in 1 Samuel 4-7 - The test: make a new cart, take two milch kine on which there hath come no yoke, shut up their calves at home, lay the ark on the cart with the jewels of gold in a coffer, and send it away. If it goeth up by the way of his own coast to Beth-shemesh, then he hath done us this great evil: but if not, we shall know it was a chance that happened to us, maybe just a disease spreading through the nation. - The kine took the straight way to the way of Beth-shemesh, lowing as they went, and turned not aside to the right hand or to the left, with the lords of the Philistines following to the border. Cows with no yoke, separated from their calves, walking a straight line home to Israel: that settled that it was the hand of the Lord. 1 Samuel 6:13-18 taught in 1 Samuel 4-7 - The cart came into the field of Joshua, a Beth-shemite, and stood by a great stone; they clave the wood of the cart and offered the kine a burnt offering unto the Lord, and the Levites took down the ark and the coffer with the jewels of gold. 1 Samuel 7:3-4 taught in 1 Samuel 4-7 - Samuel spake unto all the house of Israel: If ye do return unto the Lord with all your hearts, then put away the strange gods and Ashtaroth from among you, and prepare your hearts unto the Lord, and serve him only, and he will deliver you out of the hand of the Philistines. Go back to how we lost the battle even with the ark of God among us: we had strange gods among us. Deliverance is not just having the ark, it is applying the commandments that are in the ark, thou shalt have no other gods before me. - Who is Ashtoreth? Astaroth in demonology is a chief figure of hell, named after the Near Eastern goddess Astarte, and Astarte is the Hellenized form of Ashtoreth, a form of Ishtar, the goddess called the queen of heaven, associated with love, beauty, sex, and war. Samuel was exhorting the people to depart from these fake gods and goddesses of the nations, and to this day there are Israelites that have not put away Ashtoreth from among them. - Easter is at its roots the celebration of Ishtar, the goddess of fertility and sex. When Constantine set out to merge paganism with the faith of the apostles to bring everything under one empire, pagan rituals like Easter and Saturnalia were dressed up as honoring Christ, and that was the birth of Roman Catholicism. Nothing about it mathematically adds up to Christ rising, the apostles never celebrated it or taught it, and a bunny laying eggs has nothing to do with your Lord and Saviour; it is not of Christ. - Then the children of Israel did put away Baalim and Ashtaroth, and served the Lord only. That is repentance. - Precept Jeremiah 44:17-18 : We will burn incense unto the queen of heaven, for then had we plenty of victuals; since we left off, we have wanted all things. That is Ishtar worship, and it is the same spirit that says, when I was in the world celebrating her holidays I was good, and now in the truth I am catching hell. 1 Samuel 7:9-12 taught in 1 Samuel 4-7 - Samuel took a sucking lamb and offered it for a burnt offering wholly unto the Lord, and Samuel cried unto the Lord for Israel, and the Lord heard him. - As Samuel was offering up the burnt offering, the Philistines drew near to battle, but the Lord thundered with a great thunder on that day upon the Philistines, and discomfited them, and they were smitten before Israel. That was no regular thunder; it was the Lord entering the battle himself. They had repented, put away the false gods, and the prayer of the righteous man reached his ears, so now the Philistines had to deal with the Most High. 1 Samuel 9:11-14 taught in 1 Samuel 8-11 - Going up the hill to the city they found young maidens going out to draw water, who told them the seer had come that day, for there was a sacrifice of the people in the high place; the people would not eat until he came, because he blessed the sacrifice. As they came into the city, Samuel came out toward them, going up to the high place. 1 Samuel 10:2-8 taught in 1 Samuel 8-11 - Samuel gave Saul the signs that would confirm the word: two men by Rachel's sepulchre saying the asses are found and thy father sorroweth for you; three men at the plain of Tabor going up to God to Bethel, who would give him two loaves of bread; and at the hill of God, where the garrison of the Philistines is, a company of prophets coming down from the high place, and the Spirit of the Lord will come upon thee, and thou shalt prophesy with them, and shalt be turned into another man. - When these signs are come unto thee, do as occasion serve thee, for God is with thee; and go down before me to Gilgal, and seven days shalt thou tarry, till I come to thee and shew thee what thou shalt do. 1 Samuel 11:14-15 taught in 1 Samuel 8-11 - Then said Samuel to the people, Come, and let us go to Gilgal, and renew the kingdom there. All the people went to Gilgal, and there they made Saul king before the Lord in Gilgal, and there they sacrificed sacrifices of peace offerings before the Lord; and there Saul and all the men of Israel rejoiced greatly. 1 Samuel 13:8-10 taught in 1 Samuel 12-15 - Saul said, Bring hither a burnt offering to me, and he offered the burnt offering, and Saul is not the priest; that is Samuel's office. And it came to pass that as soon as he had made an end of offering the burnt offering, behold, Samuel came. He was barely late, and Saul could not hold his patience. 1 Samuel 13:11-12 taught in 1 Samuel 12-15 - Samuel asks, What hast thou done? Saul answers with excuses: the people were scattered from me, thou camest not within the days appointed, the Philistines gathered at Michmash, so I forced myself and offered a burnt offering. This is part of Saul's pattern of behavior; he never wants to hold himself accountable, he always deflects onto whoever else. 1 Samuel 15:12-15 taught in 1 Samuel 12-15 - Saul deflects again, the same blame game as chapter 13: They have brought them from the Amalekites, for the people spared the best of the sheep and of the oxen, to sacrifice unto the Lord thy God; and the rest we have utterly destroyed. Verse 9 already told us Saul and the people spared them; now suddenly it is only the people, and for a good reason, a sacrifice, as though the Lord ought to be pleased. 1 Samuel 15:20-21 taught in 1 Samuel 12-15 - In justifying himself over the animals, Saul volunteers even more of his rebellion, boasting that he spared the king, as if that was the smart move everyone really wanted; then he lays the spoil on the people again: the people took of the spoil, sheep and oxen, the chief of the things which should have been utterly destroyed, to sacrifice unto the Lord thy God in Gilgal. 1 Samuel 15:22 taught in 1 Samuel 12-15 - Samuel makes it plain: Hath the Lord as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the Lord? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams. Do you think the Lord prefers a sacrifice to atone for broken commandments over you simply keeping the commandments? That is a heavy verse. - Precept Ecclesiasticus 34:18-19 : The spoil was wrongfully gotten, taken against the will of the Lord, so the offering is ridiculous; all those animals were not going to pacify his anger. - Precept Proverbs 21:27 : The sacrifice of the wicked is abomination: how much more, when he bringeth it with a wicked mind? It does not merely do nothing; it makes the Most High more angry, and Saul probably would have kept those animals to eat had it never been pointed out. - Precept Psalms 51:16-17 : Thou desirest not sacrifice, else would I give it: the sacrifices of God are a broken spirit; a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise. David wrote this in his repentance: the true sacrifice is being sorry and remorseful for what you did, not pleading why you were not wrong for doing wrong; that is the spirit Saul does not have. 1 Samuel 16:2-3 taught in 1 Samuel 16-19 - The Most High told Samuel to go in with a heifer, as if coming only to sacrifice; he would go incognito, not letting it be known that he was coming to anoint Saul's replacement, and the Most High would show him whom to anoint. 1 Samuel 16:4-5 taught in 1 Samuel 16-19 - Samuel answered peaceably: he came to sacrifice to the Lord, and he sanctified Jesse and his sons and called them to the sacrifice. 1 Samuel 16:18 taught in 1 Samuel 16-19 - One of the servants had seen a son of Jesse the Bethlehemite that is cunning in playing, a mighty valiant man, a man of war, prudent in matters, a comely person, and the Lord is with him. He did not say the name, but this son of Jesse who went hard on the instruments was David. - David was also a singer; he praised the Most High with words of glory and sung songs with his whole heart, and he set up the singers before the altar, the same service we read of in 1 Chronicles 25. - Precept Ecclesiasticus 47:2 : As the fat is taken from the peace offering, so was David chosen out of the children of Israel. 1 Samuel 18:8-9 taught in 1 Samuel 16-19 - Saul was very wroth and the saying displeased him: they have ascribed unto David ten thousands, and to me they have ascribed but thousands; and what can he have more but the kingdom? Wroth is the same word used in Genesis 4 of how Cain fell toward Abel, and Abel had done nothing to him but what the Lord required; David likewise did nothing to Saul but what Saul himself asked of him. - Instead of appreciating the song, give credit where it is due, for the labourer is worthy of his reward, Saul was displeased at his brother's praise; that is the same spirit of envy. - And Saul eyed David from that day and forward. What was behind that eye? Envy. The envious man is not satisfied with his own portion; Saul had his thousands and still had the kingdom, but his eye was on David's portion, and iniquity dried up his soul from that point forward. - Precept Genesis 4:5 : Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell; the same word, the same spirit, kindled against a brother who had done nothing wrong. 1 Samuel 26:17-20 taught in 1 Samuel 24-27 - Saul knew David's voice and said, Is this thy voice, my son David? And David said, Wherefore doth my lord thus pursue after his servant? for what have I done? or what evil is in mine hand? - Let not my blood fall to the earth before the face of the Lord: for the king of Israel is come out to seek a flea, as when one doth hunt a partridge in the mountains.

title: The Covenant
text: The Covenant The covenants of the Most High from Noah and Abraham through Sinai and the plains of Moab. Genesis Genesis 6:8-9 taught in Genesis 5-8 - Noah found grace in the eyes of the Lord; he was a just man and perfect in his generations, and Noah walked with God. - Without Noah none of us would be here; Shem, Ham, and Japheth repopulated the earth after the flood. - Precept Ecclesiasticus 44:17-18 : Noah was found perfect and righteous and was left as a remnant unto the earth when the flood came. Genesis 8:20-22 taught in Genesis 5-8 - An everlasting covenant was made with Noah that all flesh should perish no more by a flood. Before it was water; the next time it is going to be fire, so let us get our minds right. Genesis 9:9-11 taught in Genesis 9-12 - The covenant established here is with Noah, his seed, and every living creature: all flesh shall never again be cut off by the waters of a flood. - This is a general covenant with all flesh. The covenant with Israel is found in Jeremiah 31. Genesis 9:12-13 taught in Genesis 9-12 - The bow in the cloud, the rainbow, is the token of the covenant between the Most High and the earth; it compasses the heaven about with a glorious circle, and His hands bended it. - The world has taken that same bow, the token of the covenant, and turned it into the symbol of sodomy. The spiritual eyes will see what that means: the great city is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt. Genesis 9:14-15 taught in Genesis 9-12 - The waters shall no more become a flood to destroy all flesh. The next time the destruction is not water but fire, when the day of the Lord comes and the elements melt with fervent heat. Genesis 9:20-23 taught in Genesis 9-12 - Noah was still perfect and righteous. A just man falleth seven times and riseth up again; one fall does not undo righteousness. - Understand Noah's heart: he preached repentance for around a hundred years, and everyone he knew outside his house drowned. Strong drink is for him that is ready to perish and wine for those of heavy hearts; Noah drank too much, but he remained righteous in the eyes of the Most High. - Ham saw the nakedness of his father and did not cover him; Shem and Japheth went backward and covered their father without looking. The commandments concerning nakedness were being applied; Leviticus 18 opens those laws. - Precept Ecclesiasticus 44:17-18 : Noah was found perfect and righteous and was left as a remnant unto the earth. Genesis 12:2-3 taught in Genesis 9-12 - In thee shall all families of the earth be blessed is not talking about everybody. The children of the prophets and of the covenant are Israel, and Israel would be scattered into all nations of the earth; through Abraham's seed the kindreds of the earth are blessed because scattered Israel gets the chance to repent and return, circumcised or not. - Precept Acts 3:25-26 : Ye are the children of the prophets and of the covenant made with Abraham; unto you first God sent His Son to bless you in turning you from your iniquities. Genesis 13:14-17 taught in Genesis 13-16 - This is the same covenant language spoken over the children of Israel: as the sand of the sea which cannot be measured nor numbered. Genesis 15:13-16 taught in Genesis 13-16 - The twelve tribes scattered among the nations today, the people called Blacks, Hispanics, and Native Americans, are the seed this covenant history belongs to. Genesis 16:15-16 taught in Genesis 13-16 - Abram was fourscore and six years old, eighty six, when Hagar bare Ishmael. Ishmael was Abram's firstborn, but the covenant did not go to Ishmael; the covenant goes through the twelve tribes of Israel. Genesis 17:4-6 taught in Genesis 17-20 - When the Most High began dealing with Abram on a covenant level, his name was changed: Abram became Abraham, a father of many nations, and kings would come out of him. - The blessing of all men and the covenant were made to rest upon the head of Jacob and divided among the twelve tribes. Kings come out of that seed, including Christ, the King of kings. - Precept Genesis 35:10-11 : The same covenant words passed to Jacob, named Israel: nations and kings out of his loins. - Precept Ecclesiasticus 44:19-23 : The blessing of all men and the covenant rested on the head of Jacob and was divided among the twelve tribes. Genesis 17:7 taught in Genesis 17-20 - The covenant is with Abraham's seed after him, and seed is literal offspring, not a spiritual metaphor. The Most High promised to be a God to Abraham and to his seed after him. Genesis 17:10-14 taught in Genesis 17-20 - Circumcision is the token of the covenant: every man child circumcised at eight days, and the uncircumcised soul cut off from his people. - It still has to be done. A covenant is a contract with terms; the covenant was confirmed to Jacob for a law, and circumcision is one of the laws within the covenant. - Precept 1 Chronicles 16:15-17 : Be mindful always of His covenant, confirmed to Jacob for a law; the covenant carries terms. Genesis 17:15-19 taught in Genesis 17-20 - Sarai's name was changed to Sarah, and she shall be a mother of nations; those are the same nations of the covenant, and she and Abraham had one child together, Isaac. Genesis 17:20-21 taught in Genesis 17-20 - Ishmael received a blessing: fruitful, multiplied exceedingly, twelve princes, a great nation. But the word to Abraham was kings shall come out of thee, and the covenant passes to Isaac: my covenant will I establish with Isaac.
