Since the days of old the Most High has never been about the love-of-the-world gospel; throw that doctrine in the trash. - This is why they do not want you reading the old covenant: verses like this correct the miseducation received through Christianity, and the mind begins to correct itself as you read. Deuteronomy 7:3-4 taught in Deuteronomy 7-10 - They will turn away thy son from following me: the nations are strangers to the Most High and cannot come into this covenant, so they draw the Israelite spouse off to religions that accept everything. Christianity accepts that union, and that is how they turn you away from your God. Deuteronomy 7:9-11 taught in Deuteronomy 7-10 - Know therefore that the Lord thy God, he is God, the faithful God, which keepeth covenant and mercy with them that love him and keep his commandments to a thousand generations, and repayeth them that hate him to their face. - From the jump it has always been the same: love God, keep the commandments; nothing changed between the covenants. Deuteronomy 7:12-15 taught in Deuteronomy 7-10 - If ye hearken to these judgments and keep and do them, the Lord keeps the covenant and the mercy: he will love thee, bless thee, and multiply thee, blessing the fruit of thy womb, thy land, thy corn, wine, oil, kine, and sheep, blessed above all people, which goes right back to verse 6. Deuteronomy 8:2-3 taught in Deuteronomy 7-10 - He fed thee with manna to make thee know that man doth not live by bread only, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of the Lord. Christ quoted this very verse walking in the earth; he was pulling from the old covenant, which proves nothing has been done away with, for he would not quote something that was abolished. Deuteronomy 8:10-14 taught in Deuteronomy 7-10 - Consider how the doctrine of Christianity works: an entire book, especially the old covenant, says keep the commandments over and over, Christ himself says keep the commandments, and Christianity says read only the letters of Paul and do away with the commandments. That is strong witchcraft, to make you disbelieve what the very book says; it is Satan's playground. Deuteronomy 8:17-18 taught in Deuteronomy 7-10 - But thou shalt remember the Lord thy God, for it is he that giveth thee power to get wealth, that he may establish his covenant. The power to get wealth belongs to the covenant; if you forget God and keep no commandments, it was not God blessing you. Deuteronomy 9:7-9 taught in Deuteronomy 7-10 - Moses abode in the mount forty days and forty nights, neither eating bread nor drinking water, when he went up to receive the tables of the covenant. Deuteronomy 9:10-11 taught in Deuteronomy 7-10 - The Lord delivered unto me two tables of stone written with the finger of God: God took his time and wrote the ten commandments down himself, according to all the words which the Lord spake with you in the mount out of the midst of the fire. Deuteronomy 9:15-17 taught in Deuteronomy 7-10 - Moses came down from the mount, the mount burning with fire, the two tables of the covenant in his two hands, and behold, ye had sinned against the Lord your God and made you a molten calf. Deuteronomy 10:6-9 taught in Deuteronomy 7-10 - At that time the Lord separated the tribe of Levi, to bear the ark of the covenant, to stand before the Lord to minister unto him, and to bless in his name; wherefore Levi hath no part nor inheritance with his brethren, the Lord is his inheritance. - But they corrupted the covenant of Levi, left off teaching the law, and were partial in it, so the Lord gave them a swift and mighty judgment. Now you understand why Levi, identified in the land of Haiti, has been the poorest in the western hemisphere and catches hell to this day: their provider was the Lord, and they departed out of the way. - Precept Malachi 2:6-9 : The law of truth was in his mouth, and the priest's lips should keep knowledge, but ye are departed out of the way, ye have caused many to stumble at the law, ye have corrupted the covenant of Levi; therefore have I made you contemptible and base before all the people. Deuteronomy 10:12-13 taught in Deuteronomy 7-10 - And now, Israel, what doth the Lord thy God require of thee: here is your purpose in life, the stipulations for the body the Most High gave you, and what you must do to please him as the children of Israel. - Fear the Lord thy God, walk in all his ways, love him, and serve him with all thy heart and with all thy soul: it all boils down to keeping the commandments of the Lord and his statutes, which he commands thee for thy good. That is how you love and serve God until the day we return to the dust or he sends his son to redeem us from the land of our captivity. - Do not just say you love God, put action behind it. Sisters, come out of the pants and mini skirts and put on a modest dress, and be in subjection to your own husbands; brothers, put on your fringes, stop dyeing your hair, and marry the mother of your children instead of leaving her a baby mama. When you will not do what he told you to do, no words out of your mouth can make you love him; your actions show you actually hate him. - Precept 2 John 1:6 : And this is love, that we walk after his commandments; it never changed from old covenant to new. Deuteronomy 10:18-19 taught in Deuteronomy 7-10 - Which stranger is Moses telling Israel to love? He is prophesying of the day Israel's own brother would become a stranger: when the northern kingdom was cut off, the brother became the stranger who would come back. Love them, because they are coming back into the covenant. Deuteronomy 17:2-5 taught in Deuteronomy 15-18 - If there be found among you man or woman that hath wrought wickedness, transgressed the covenant, and gone and served other gods, the sun or moon or any of the host of heaven, which the Most High commanded not, the matter had to be established first. Deuteronomy 23:7-8 taught in Deuteronomy 23-26 - Thou shalt not abhor an Edomite, for he is thy brother: this was a temporary law. Edom broke the brotherly covenant; he did pursue his brother with the sword, did cast off all pity, his anger did tear perpetually, and he kept his wrath for ever. - Precept Amos 1:9 : Tyrus delivered up the whole captivity to Edom and remembered not the brotherly covenant. Deuteronomy 23:9 taught in Deuteronomy 23-26 - Because of that trespass Israel could not stand before their enemies but turned their backs, for they were accursed; the Lord would not be with them any more except they destroyed the accursed from among them, and Achan and his family and all that belonged to him were destroyed and burned, and a heap set upon them, because he broke the covenant. - Precept Joshua 7:11-13 : Israel hath sinned and taken of the accursed thing; therefore they could not stand before their enemies until the accursed was destroyed from among them. Deuteronomy 26:18 taught in Deuteronomy 23-26 - The Lord hath avouched thee this day to be his peculiar people, as he hath promised thee: the Lord hath chosen Jacob unto himself, and Israel for his peculiar treasure. - Ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people, that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light: we were called out of our sins into the light, and the light is the commandments and the law. - Which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God: we were called by other names, African American, Dominican, Negro, but now we are coming into the understanding that we are actually the children of Israel. - Precept Exodus 19:5-6 : If ye will obey my voice and keep my covenant, ye shall be a peculiar treasure unto me above all people. Deuteronomy 29:1 taught in Deuteronomy 27-30 - These are the words of the covenant which the Lord commanded Moses to make with the children of Israel in the land of Moab, beside the covenant which he made with them in Horeb. Deuteronomy 29:5-9 taught in Deuteronomy 27-30 - Keep therefore the words of this covenant and do them, that ye may prosper in all that ye do. Deuteronomy 29:10-13 taught in Deuteronomy 27-30 - All Israel stood that day before the Lord: captains, elders, officers, little ones, wives, and the stranger in the camp, from the hewer of wood unto the drawer of water. Even the servants among us heard this covenant. Deuteronomy 29:14-15 taught in Deuteronomy 27-30 - Neither with you only do I make this covenant and this oath, but also with him that is not here with us this day. That is us: the Lord made this covenant with the generations which were to come. - This is how you know the covenant and the curses apply to our forefathers and to us to this day. If we do not hearken to his voice and obey his commandments diligently, all the curses of Deuteronomy 28 fall upon us; that is what is happening to us right now. Deuteronomy 29:20-21 taught in Deuteronomy 27-30 - The Lord will not spare him; the anger of the Lord and his jealousy shall smoke against that man, and all the curses written in this book shall lie upon him, and the Lord shall blot out his name from under heaven: death. - Once you hear Deuteronomy 28, you cannot go back to living how you used to live. You heard the curses, even ten minutes of it on the street; you are marked, and if you go back, the Most High says, I am coming for you. Deuteronomy 29:22-28 taught in Deuteronomy 27-30 - All nations shall say, Wherefore hath the Lord done thus unto this land? And men shall answer, Because they have forsaken the covenant of the Lord God of their fathers. Deuteronomy 31:9-13 taught in Deuteronomy 31-34 - Moses wrote this law and delivered it to the priests, the sons of Levi that bear the ark of the covenant, and to all the elders of Israel. Deuteronomy 31:14-18 taught in Deuteronomy 31-34 - The Most High tells Moses straight out: after you sleep with thy fathers, this people will rise up and go a whoring after the gods of the strangers of the land. The people Moses spent forty years tending will forsake the covenant, and instead of utterly destroying the nations and their gods, they will mingle with the nations and serve their gods. Deuteronomy 31:19-21 taught in Deuteronomy 31-34 - Write ye this song and teach it the children of israel, put it in their mouths, that this song may be a witness against them. We read chapter 32 as verses, but it was really given as a song, because what is in the form of a song is easily remembered and retained. - When they come into the land that floweth with milk and honey and have eaten and waxen fat, they will turn unto other gods and serve them; then this song shall testify against them as a witness, for it shall not be forgotten out of the mouths of their seed. - The Most High says, I know their imagination which they go about, even now, before I have brought them into the land. He already knew how they would forsake him when they got there. Deuteronomy 31:22-26 taught in Deuteronomy 31-34 - When Moses made an end of writing the words of this law in a book, he commanded the Levites that bear the ark to put the book of the law in the side of the ark of the covenant, that it may be there for a witness against thee. Deuteronomy 33:8-9 taught in Deuteronomy 31-34 - Who said unto his father and to his mother, I have not seen him; neither did he acknowledge his brethren, nor knew his own children: for they have observed thy word, and kept thy covenant. This is the zeal Levi had for the Most High. - At the golden calf, when Moses stood in the gate of the camp and said, Who is on the Lord's side? let him come unto me, only the sons of Levi gathered themselves unto him. They took every man his sword and did according to the word of Moses without hesitating, and there fell of the people that day about three thousand men. That is why the blessing says they saw not father or mother nor acknowledged their brethren: that is the devotion they had for the covenant. Deuteronomy 33:26-29 taught in Deuteronomy 31-34 - Never trust your enemy: your enemy will do everything in his power to keep you oppressed and subject to him, including lying to you about your history. As in the days of the Maccabees, the leaders show the people the falsehood of the heathen and the breach of their oaths, the covenants and treaties they broke with our people; after so long you learn that your enemies have been liars this whole time. Joshua Joshua 3:1-4 taught in Joshua 1-4 - The instruction: when ye see the ark of the covenant and the priests the Levites bearing it, remove from your place and go after it, keeping a space of about two thousand cubits between you and it, for ye have not passed this way heretofore. Joshua 3:5-8 taught in Joshua 1-4 - Joshua was to command the priests bearing the ark of the covenant: when ye are come to the brink of the water of Jordan, ye shall stand still in Jordan. Joshua 3:9-13 taught in Joshua 1-4 - Joshua called Israel to hear the words of the Lord: hereby ye shall know that the living God is among you, and that he will without fail drive out from before you the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Hivites, the Perizzites, the Girgashites, the Amorites, and the Jebusites. - Twelve men were to be taken out of the tribes of Israel, one man out of every tribe, prepared ahead for what would follow the crossing. - The sign given in advance: as soon as the soles of the feet of the priests that bear the ark of the Lord rest in the waters of Jordan, the waters coming down from above shall be cut off and stand upon an heap, and a riverbed becomes dry land for a whole nation to walk through. Hear a word like that today and men would call you crazy, but that is how the Lord dealt with Israel; they had to be ready for miracles. Joshua 3:14-17 taught in Joshua 1-4 - No man can stand in a river, but the priests that bare the ark of the covenant of the Lord stood firm on dry ground in the midst of Jordan, and all Israel passed over on dry ground right against Jericho, until all the people were passed clean over. Joshua 4:1-9 taught in Joshua 1-4 - The stones are a sign and a memorial: when your children ask their fathers in time to come, What mean ye by these stones? ye shall answer them, that the waters of Jordan were cut off before the ark of the covenant of the Lord. These stones lay in the middle of a river that Israel walked through on dry ground, and they memorialize that forever. Joshua 4:15-18 taught in Joshua 1-4 - The priests stayed firm at their post in the riverbed even after all the people had passed over, until the Lord spake to Joshua and Joshua gave the order: come ye up out of Jordan. That is discipline, order, fortitude, and faith; they held their place in the midst of a stopped river without wavering. - As soon as the soles of the priests' feet were lifted up unto the dry land, the waters of Jordan returned unto their place and flowed over all his banks as they did before. Everything held its place exactly as long as Israel needed it to. Joshua 5:2-3 taught in Joshua 5-8 - Circumcision is the covenant the Most High instituted with our forefather Abraham: every man child circumcised at eight days old, and the servant born in the house or bought with money circumcised likewise and keeping the laws as well. - Precept Genesis 17:10-12 : The covenant with Abraham and his seed: every man child among you shall be circumcised, he that is eight days old, including the servant bought with money. Joshua 6:6-11 taught in Joshua 5-8 - Joshua called the priests and gave the order: seven priests bear seven trumpets before the ark, the armed men pass on before the ark, and the rereward, the guards in the rear, came after the ark. - Joshua commanded the people, Ye shall not shout, nor make any noise with your voice, neither shall any word proceed out of your mouth, until the day I bid you shout; then shall ye shout. - The ark of the Lord compassed the city once, and they came into the camp and lodged there. Joshua 6:17-19 taught in Joshua 5-8 - The city shall be accursed, even it and all that are therein, to the Lord: only Rahab the harlot shall live, she and all that are with her in the house, because she hid the messengers. She made a covenant with the spies: she would conceal them and assist Israel, knowing the Lord was with Israel, as long as her family was saved when the city fell. Joshua 7:10-12 taught in Joshua 5-8 - The Lord said, Get thee up; wherefore liest thou upon thy face? Israel hath sinned. It does not say Achan sinned; it says Israel. This walk is not selfish or individual: when you are in sin you hurt your wife, your husband, your children, the congregation, and the leadership, for we are all our brother's keeper and responsible for one another. - They have taken of the accursed thing, and stolen, and dissembled, and put it among their own stuff: the Lord says they. As a father who finds mischief chastens all his children together when none confesses, so the Most High deals with his children as one house; we pay for one another's sins. - Therefore the children of Israel could not stand before their enemies: the Lord was not going to let them win, and he put a mightier warring spirit on the men of Ai. However well you train with your sword and shield, the Most High controls the outcome. - His power cannot be comprehended: great things doeth he, which we cannot comprehend; touching the Almighty, we cannot find him out. Stop trying to figure the Creator out and questioning why he created what he created; you are the creation, so keep the commandments and play your role. - Neither will I be with you any more, except ye destroy the accursed from among you: what is accursed must be destroyed; that is the only way to remove it. Joshua 7:13-15 taught in Joshua 5-8 - Up, sanctify the people against tomorrow: there is an accursed thing in the midst of thee, O Israel; thou canst not stand before thine enemies until ye take away the accursed thing from among you. - The search would narrow by the Lord's own taking: tribe, then family, then household, then man by man; and he that is taken with the accursed thing shall be burnt with fire, he and all that he hath. - The folly was wrought against a plain commandment: Joshua had already charged them in Joshua 6:18-19 to keep from the accursed thing lest they trouble the camp, and adjured them in Joshua 6:26; the transgressor troubled the camp, the army and congregation of Israel. Joshua 8:33 taught in Joshua 5-8 - All Israel, and their elders, and officers, and their judges stood on this side the ark and on that side, before the priests the Levites, the stranger as well as he that was born among them, half over against mount Gerizim and half over against mount Ebal, as Moses commanded, that they should bless the people of Israel. - Why does the body set up rank instead of saying I only follow Christ? Because we are commanded to rehearse the righteous acts of the Lord: reading the wars and works of Joshua, Moses, and the officers, judges, and elders, we practice what our forefathers did, in order, as an organized army. - Rehearse means practice, and practice makes perfect: there are rehearsals every day, classes and meetings for the men, the women, and the children, because this is not our rest. Joshua 22:19-20 taught in Joshua 21-24 - They even offered their own land: if the land of your possession be unclean, pass ye over unto the land of the possession of the Lord and take possession among us, close by where we can keep an eye on you; only rebel not against the Lord, nor build you an altar beside the altar of the Lord our God. - They cited the proof from their own history: did not Achan the son of Zerah commit a trespass in the accursed thing, and wrath fell on all the congregation of Israel, and that man perished not alone in his iniquity. One man trespassed and the whole nation felt it. - Precept Joshua 7:15 : He that is taken with the accursed thing shall be burnt with fire, he and all that he hath, because he hath transgressed the covenant of the Lord. Joshua 23:11-13 taught in Joshua 21-24 - Take good heed therefore unto yourselves, that ye love the LORD your God. - The warning is plain: if ye go back and cleave unto the remnant of these nations and make marriages with them, know for a certainty that the Most High will no more drive out any of these nations from before you; they shall be snares and traps unto you, scourges in your sides and thorns in your eyes, until ye perish from off this good land. - This is the same thing that happened at Baalpeor, when Israel went and mingled with the women of Moab and then worshipped their gods. The warning here is do not do that thing. - Precept Deuteronomy 7:2-4 : Make no covenant with them, neither make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter take unto thy son, for they will turn away thy son from following the Most High to serve other gods, and his anger will destroy thee suddenly. Joshua 23:14-16 taught in Joshua 21-24 - When ye have transgressed the covenant and served other gods, ye shall perish quickly from off the good land. That is exactly why Israel is not at home right now; we did exactly that. And that is what the waking up is for today: the classes going out all day, the teaching in the streets, trying to bring our people back to the laws of God. Joshua 24:1-3 taught in Joshua 21-24 - Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel to Shechem, with the elders, heads, judges, and officers, and they presented themselves before God for the covenant. Joshua 24:21-25 taught in Joshua 21-24 - The people said unto Joshua, Nay; but we will serve the LORD. It is the same thing Israel told Moses back then; we came into that covenant again, this time without the blood. - So Joshua made a covenant with the people that day, and set them a statute and an ordinance in Shechem, the same thing Moses his predecessor did at the mountain; Joshua was his successor and did the same, though without the blood. - Precept Exodus 24:3-8 : All the people answered with one voice, All the words which the Lord hath said will we do; Moses wrote all the words of the Lord, built an altar and twelve pillars, read the book of the covenant in the audience of the people, and sprinkled the blood of the covenant on the people. Judges Judges 2:1-5 taught in Judges 1-4 - An angel of the Most High comes up from Gilgal to Bochim and rehearses the covenant: I made you to go up out of Egypt, I brought you unto the land I sware unto your fathers, and I said I will never break my covenant with you. The command was plain: ye shall make no league with the inhabitants of this land, ye shall throw down their altars. But ye have not obeyed my voice. Why have ye done this? - Precept Exodus 23:32-33 : Thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor with their gods; they shall not dwell in thy land, lest they make thee sin against me. Judges 2:20-23 taught in Judges 1-4 - Because this people transgressed the covenant and did not hearken, the Most High declares he will not henceforth drive out any of the nations which Joshua left when he died. This is exactly what Joshua warned before he died: if ye cleave unto the remnant of these nations and make marriages with them, know for a certainty the Most High will no more drive them out, but they shall be snares and traps, scourges in your sides and thorns in your eyes, until ye perish from off the good land. Judges 3:5-7 taught in Judges 1-4 - They took their daughters to be their wives, and gave their daughters to their sons, and served their gods. The law had said it plainly: thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor shew mercy unto them, neither shalt thou make marriages with them, for they will turn away thy son from following me, that they may serve other gods. - Precept Deuteronomy 7:1-4 : Seven nations greater and mightier than thou: make no covenant with them and no marriages with them, for they will turn away thy son from following me. Judges 7:1-3 taught in Judges 5-8 - The Lord tells Gideon the people with him are too many for him to give Midian into their hands, lest Israel vaunt themselves against him, saying, mine own hand hath saved me. That is Israel: look at what I did. The Lord knows how we think. - Whosoever is fearful and afraid, let him return: twenty and two thousand bounced back to Gilead, and ten thousand remained. That is why God always lowered the numbers going into battle, so Israel would know it was by the Lord's strength that we overcame our enemies; and it is going to be the same thing again, few numbers going into battle against the nations when that time comes. - Precept Deuteronomy 8:14-18 : Lest thine heart be lifted up and thou say in thine heart, my power and the might of mine hand hath gotten me this wealth; thou shalt remember the Lord thy God, for it is he that giveth thee power to get wealth. Judges 10:10-14 taught in Judges 9-12 - Yet ye have forsaken me, and served other gods: wherefore I will deliver you no more. Go and cry unto the gods which ye have chosen; let them deliver you in the time of your tribulation. The Lord is not unrighteous; he gave a fair covenant: do right and he is with you above all nations, do wrong and you go into captivity. He will not break his word, and everybody's grace is not the same. Judges 20:26-28 taught in Judges 17-20 - The ark of the covenant of God was there in those days, and Phinehas the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron, stood before it. They asked, shall I yet again go out to battle against the children of Benjamin my brother, or shall I cease? And the LORD said, go up; for to morrow I will deliver them into thine hand: a direct promise of victory on the morrow. 1 Samuel 1 Samuel 2:3 taught in 1 Samuel 1-3 - All of us in this walk, keeping the commandments and the faith in Christ, have taken covenant and proclaimed out of our mouths that we are going to endure to the end; we broke the bread and drank the wine and took the covenant with the Lord. Now the Lord is judging you by your actions: are you going to endure to the end, whether to Christ's return or until you leave this earth, if you truly love him? 1 Samuel 3:2-3 taught in 1 Samuel 1-3 - Eli was laid down in his place, his eyes beginning to wax dim, and ere the lamp of God went out in the temple of the Lord, where the ark of God was, Samuel was laid down to sleep. Ere means before: before the lamp of God went out. That light in the temple by the ark was never to go out, though at a point in time it did go out. - Christ spoke about that fire in the temple: on the sabbath days the priests in the temple profane the sabbath, and are blameless. Israel was not to kindle a fire on the sabbath when it comes to food, but the priests had to keep that fire burning, and they sacrificed on the sabbath days, a lamb in the morning and a lamb in the evening; they broke the sabbath yet are blameless, because they were doing thus saith the Lord. - Sacrifice was never the most important thing to the Lord; not the blood of bulls and of goats, but mercy upon one another and the keeping of the commandments. The sacrifices were added because of transgression, the animal's blood taken in your place so the Most High would not have to kill you; you read of it from Genesis 3, where the Lord took the skins after Adam sinned. Yet there were some things you could not sacrifice for, abominations for which a man's own blood was required. - Precept Exodus 19:3-6 : Before the Most High even gave the ten commandments he made this plain: if ye will obey my voice indeed, and keep my covenant, then ye shall be a peculiar treasure unto me above all people, a kingdom of priests, and an holy nation. Obedience is what he desired most from the beginning. 1 Samuel 3:4-7 taught in 1 Samuel 1-3 - Do not have your children going into a covenant with Christ that he will judge them for if they break it; the scripture says, for this cause many are weak and sickly among you, and many sleep. You do not know if your kids are going to serve the Lord when they go out on their own, or what kind of lusts are in them that will draw them away into the world when they come of age. It is your job as a parent to train them up and pray they stay in it: kids learn by watching, so let them see you take that covenant over and over again until they are ready, and make them rehearse the righteous acts. When the child comes to the age of reasoning and knows the Lord for himself, and the Lord reveals himself to him, you will know it; do not rush it. - Precept 1 Corinthians 11:29-30 : He that eateth and drinketh unworthily, eateth and drinketh damnation to himself; for this cause many are weak and sickly among you, and many sleep. That covenant is not to be forced on children who do not yet know the Lord. 1 Samuel 4:3-5 taught in 1 Samuel 4-7 - The elders of Israel asked the right question, Wherefore hath the Lord smitten us to day before the Philistines? But instead of examining the nation, they had an idea: fetch the ark of the covenant out of Shiloh, and when it comes among us it will save us out of the hand of our enemies. - The two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, came with the ark, and when it entered the camp all Israel shouted with a great shout so that the earth rang again. That is how excited and ecstatic Israel was to have the ark of the covenant among them; they felt their enemies could not destroy them now. - So what is the ark of the covenant, and what does it contain? The Lord told Moses to hew two tables of stone like the first ones he broke, and the Lord rewrote the ten commandments on them with his own finger, and Moses put the tables in the ark. The ark of the covenant contained the commandments that God wrote. 1 Samuel 4:6-9 taught in 1 Samuel 4-7 - When the Philistines heard the noise of the shout and understood that the ark of the Lord was come into the camp, they were afraid, saying, God is come into the camp; woe unto us, for there hath not been such a thing heretofore. They had never had to battle Israel with the ark of the covenant in the camp. 1 Samuel 6:19-21 taught in 1 Samuel 4-7 - He smote the men of Beth-shemesh, because they had looked into the ark of the Lord, even fifty thousand and threescore and ten men. It was not just the other nations that had to keep discretion with the ark of the covenant; it was forbidden to touch it or look into it unless the Lord gave you authority, no matter what tribe you were, even Levi. 1 Samuel 8:6-9 taught in 1 Samuel 8-11 - Joshua warned us about this. At Shechem, Israel made the covenant with its own mouth to serve the Lord and obey his voice; asking for a king was breaking the choice we ourselves made. - Precept Joshua 24:21-24 : The people said, Nay, but we will serve the Lord; ye are witnesses against yourselves that ye have chosen you the Lord; the Lord our God will we serve, and his voice will we obey. We made that covenant. 1 Samuel 11:1-3 taught in 1 Samuel 8-11 - Nahash the Ammonite came up and encamped against Jabeshgilead, and all the men of Jabesh said, Make a covenant with us, and we will serve thee. Nahash answered, On this condition will I make a covenant with you, that I may thrust out all your right eyes, and lay it for a reproach upon all Israel; he wanted to blind every man in one eye. 1 Samuel 12:8-11 taught in 1 Samuel 12-15 - They cried unto the Lord and confessed they had sinned in forsaking him and serving Baalim and Ashtaroth. That is the same lesson Samuel taught in chapter 7: when the Philistines beat Israel, they went and got the ark of the covenant, got beat even worse, and lost the ark. It is not just about having the ark of the covenant among you; you have to put away the idols and stop serving Baalim and Ashtaroth. 1 Samuel 18:1-4 taught in 1 Samuel 16-19 - The soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul, and they made a covenant; Jonathan stripped himself of his robe and gave it to David, with his garments, his sword, his bow, and his girdle.

title: The Feasts of the Most High
text: The Feasts of the Most High Passover and the appointed times: the holy convocations and how they are kept. Genesis Genesis 4:25-26 taught in Genesis 1-4 - Seth was appointed another seed instead of Abel. Through Seth men began to call upon the name of the Lord; they started to worship the Most High and keep the commandments, while the line of Cain went on in evil and wickedness. That is why the Most High chose the line of Seth. Genesis 18:9-15 taught in Genesis 17-20 - Sarah was barren from the beginning and it had ceased to be with her after the manner of women; she laughed within herself at the promise of a son. - The Lord answered the thought she never spoke: Wherefore did Sarah laugh? She denied it out of fear, and He said, Nay, but thou didst laugh. The Most High sees what is within the mind. - Is any thing too hard for the Lord? The barren woman is made a joyful mother of children. Through faith Sarah received strength to conceive when she was past age, and Abraham, as good as dead at a hundred, staggered not at the promise but was strong in faith, fully persuaded that what He had promised He was able to perform. Genesis 19:1-3 taught in Genesis 17-20 - Lot sat in the gate and pressed the two angels into his house, because he knew the men of Sodom. He made them a feast, and they did eat; angels have bodies and functions like men. Genesis 24:12-16 taught in Genesis 21-24 - The servant prayed for a sign at the well: the damsel who offers to draw for the camels also is the one appointed. Before he had done speaking, Rebekah came out. Genesis 24:12-20 taught in Genesis 24-27 - The servant asked a sign, and before he had done speaking Rebekah came out: very fair, a virgin, and kind. She gave a stranger drink and drew for all his camels; that kind and easily entreated spirit is the pattern for the daughters of Israel. Genesis 25:20-21 taught in Genesis 24-27 - Isaac was forty years old when he took Rebekah to wife. Exodus Exodus 5:1-2 taught in Exodus 2-5 - Moses and Aaron went in and told Pharaoh, Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, Let my people go, that they may hold a feast unto me in the wilderness. Exodus 9:1-7 taught in Exodus 6-9 - A grievous murrain fell upon the cattle of Egypt, upon the horses, asses, camels, oxen, and sheep; and with this fifth plague the Most High was mocking Hathor, the Egyptian idol goddess of cattle. - The Lord severed between the cattle of Israel and the cattle of Egypt: all the cattle of Egypt died, but of the cattle of the children of Israel died not one. Exodus 10:2 taught in Exodus 10-13 - The fathers are to tell in the ears of their sons and their sons' sons what things the Most High wrought in Egypt. Exodus 10:7-11 taught in Exodus 10-13 - Pharaoh's own servants pleaded with him: how long shall this man be a snare unto us? Exodus 10:27-29 taught in Exodus 10-13 - The same delusion falls on Israel when the people go reprobate in their sins: believing the Sabbath begins when the sun comes up, that anything can be eaten on Passover, or that the leaven to be put away is only the heart. Sin blinds. Exodus 12:3-5 taught in Exodus 10-13 - In the tenth day of the month every man was to take a lamb according to the house of his fathers; if the household was too little for the lamb, he and his neighbour next unto his house were to take it according to the number of the souls. - The lamb was to be without blemish, a male of the first year, taken from the sheep or from the goats. Exodus 12:6-8 taught in Exodus 10-13 - The flesh was to be eaten that night, roast with fire, with unleavened bread and with bitter herbs. Exodus 12:9-11 taught in Exodus 10-13 - It was to be eaten with loins girded, shoes on the feet, and staff in hand, in haste: it is the Lord's passover, and that very night Israel was leaving Egypt. Exodus 12:12-13 taught in Exodus 10-13 - The blood was a token upon the houses: when I see the blood, I will pass over you. Exodus 12:14 taught in Exodus 10-13 - This day is a memorial, a feast to the Lord throughout your generations, kept by an ordinance for ever. Exodus 12:15-17 taught in Exodus 10-13 - Seven days shall ye eat unleavened bread; even the first day the leaven is put out of the houses, and whosoever eats leavened bread from the first day until the seventh, that soul shall be cut off from Israel. - The feast of unleavened bread is observed because in this selfsame day the Most High brought the armies of Israel out of Egypt. Exodus 12:18-20 taught in Exodus 10-13 - In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month at even, ye shall eat unleavened bread, until the one and twentieth day of the month at even. The Passover begins and ends at even because the day begins and ends at even; it is not difficult. Exodus 12:21-23 taught in Exodus 10-13 - The elders were to draw out a lamb for their families and kill the passover, take a bunch of hyssop, dip it in the blood in the bason, and strike the lintel and the two side posts; the hyssop bush was used like a paintbrush to paint the blood of the lamb over the doorposts. Exodus 12:24-28 taught in Exodus 10-13 - This thing is an ordinance to thee and to thy sons for ever, kept even when Israel comes into the land the Lord promised. Exodus 12:39-42 taught in Exodus 10-13 - It is a night to be much observed unto the Lord for bringing them out from the land of Egypt: this is the Passover night, which all the children of Israel are to observe in their generations. Exodus 13:3-4 taught in Exodus 10-13 - This day came ye out in the month Abib: the first month of the year, falling at the first new moon of the spring. Exodus 16:22-30 taught in Exodus 14-17 - Abide ye every man in his place on the seventh day is about not going out to gather food on the sabbath. Exodus 19:1-2 taught in Exodus 18-21 - In the third month after going forth out of Egypt, Israel departed from Rephidim, came into the wilderness of Sinai, and camped before the mount. Exodus 21:2-6 taught in Exodus 18-21 - Zedekiah's covenant in Jeremiah confirms the law in the prophets: every man was to let his Hebrew manservant and maidservant go free at the appointed release. Exodus 21:13-14 taught in Exodus 18-21 - If a man lie not in wait, but God deliver him into his hand, a place was appointed whither he shall flee. Exodus 22:29-30 taught in Exodus 22-25 - Likewise with the oxen and the sheep: seven days the firstling stayed with his dam, his mother, and on the eighth day it was given. Exodus 23:14-17 taught in Exodus 22-25 - The feast of unleavened bread is the Passover, kept in the time appointed of the month Abib, the first month of the year, as it is written, the feast of unleavened bread drew nigh, which is called the Passover. - The feast of harvest, the firstfruits of thy labours, is also known as Pentecost and the feast of weeks; and the feast of ingathering, in the end of the year, is also known as the feast of tabernacles and the feast of booths. - Precept Luke 22:1 : The feast of unleavened bread drew nigh, which is called the Passover; the two names are one feast. Exodus 23:18-19 taught in Exodus 22-25 - Thou shalt not offer the blood of my sacrifice with leavened bread, neither shall the fat of my sacrifice remain until the morning. Exodus 28:1-2 taught in Exodus 26-29 - Aaron and his sons Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar are taken from among the children of Israel to minister unto the Most High in the priest's office. - The Most High commanded holy garments to be made for Aaron for glory and for beauty. The hundred forty and four thousand of Revelation 7 that must be sealed before destruction comes are read of again in 2 Esdras: they departed from the shadow of the world, leaving spiritual Egypt and the ways Babylon taught behind, and have received glorious garments of the Lord. In the kingdom of heaven the Most High will clothe His men in glorious garments as in ancient times, on another level than anything worn today. - Precept 2 Esdras 2:38-39 : The sealed that departed from the shadow of the world receive glorious garments of the Lord. Exodus 28:30 taught in Exodus 26-29 - The Urim and the Thummim go in the breastplate of judgment, upon Aaron's heart before the Lord; Aaron bears the judgment of the children of Israel upon his heart continually. - Urim and Thummim means lights and perfections: objects not specifically described in the scriptures, perhaps stones since they went in the breastplate, by which the high priest ascertained the will of the Most High in important matters affecting the nation. To ascertain is to find out for certain, a divine discerning beyond what a man can determine by his own thinking. - One theory holds they were cast as lots, but the apostles, who were not dealing with the Levitical priesthood, cast lots between Joseph called Barsabas and Matthias without any Urim and Thummim, which is an issue with that theory. Exodus 29:1-4 taught in Exodus 26-29 - To hallow Aaron and his sons to minister in the priest's office: one young bullock and two rams without blemish, with unleavened bread, cakes tempered with oil, and wafers anointed with oil, brought in one basket to the door of the tabernacle of the congregation. Exodus 29:5-9 taught in Exodus 26-29 - The garments are put upon Aaron, the coat, the robe of the ephod, the ephod, and the breastplate, with the curious girdle; the mitre upon his head and the holy crown upon the mitre; the anointing oil poured upon his head; and his sons in coats, girdles, and bonnets. The priest's office shall be theirs for a perpetual statute: thou shalt consecrate Aaron and his sons. - Ecclesiasticus records the same consecration: Moses anointed him with holy oil, an everlasting covenant to Aaron and to his seed so long as the heavens should remain, to minister unto Him, execute the office of the priesthood, offer the sacrifices, and teach Jacob the testimonies and inform Israel in His laws. The priest's job was the offerings and teaching the nation the law, statutes, and commandments. - What happened to that covenant is answered in Malachi, where the commandment is spoken to the priests: the covenant with Levi was of life and peace, the priest's lips should keep knowledge and they should seek the law at his mouth, for he is the messenger of the Lord of hosts; but ye are departed out of the way, ye have caused many to stumble at the law, ye have corrupted the covenant of Levi. The priests were finessing the offerings, keeping the best animals for themselves and sacrificing the blind and the broken, and they perverted the teachings of the law for their own benefit. - That is why leadership today is not walking around requiring Levite lineage of Aaron. Exodus 29:19-28 taught in Exodus 26-29 - The second ram is the ram of consecration: its blood is put upon the tip of the right ear of Aaron and of his sons, upon the thumb of their right hand and the great toe of their right foot, and sprinkled upon the altar round about; the blood and the anointing oil are sprinkled upon Aaron, his garments, his sons, and their garments, and he shall be hallowed. - The bread and the parts of the ram are put in the hands of Aaron and his sons and waved for a wave offering before the Lord, then burnt upon the altar; and the breast of the wave offering and the shoulder of the heave offering are sanctified for Aaron and his sons by a statute for ever. There go the wave offering and the heave offering, which you will read about throughout the first five books, Leviticus predominantly. - These ordinances belonged to the Levitical priesthood, and the doctrines that would put men back under pieces of that office today do not even keep what they claim; they sound right because they use scriptures strongly and confidently, but they are in error. Be not tossed to and fro with every wind of doctrine, nor carried about with strange doctrines; do not ever fall away from the Messiah. Exodus 30:11-16 taught in Exodus 30-33 - The atonement money was appointed for the service of the tabernacle of the congregation. Exodus 30:22-33 taught in Exodus 30-33 - The Most High gave specific orders down to the spices and the weights, and none could deviate from them or they would die. Our forefathers carried out that tedious, exact work, yet we complain about the smallest things set in place for order, the uniform, the new moon, and not cooking on the sabbath; the spirit has to get right. Exodus 31:12-15 taught in Exodus 30-33 - Verily my sabbaths ye shall keep, for it is a sign between me and you throughout your generations, that ye may know that I am the LORD that doth sanctify you. Keeping the weekly sabbath and the feast days shows that Israel are his children and he is their God; the nations do not have this sabbath, and adopted Sunday worship is not the true sabbath given to the children of Israel. - Every one that defileth the sabbath shall surely be put to death. The stoning was done away in Christ, but the judgment for breaking the sabbath still stands, and people still die on the sabbath day, Friday sundown to Saturday sundown; the Most High is justified, because it is his sign between him and his people. - Six days may work be done, but in the seventh is the sabbath of rest, holy to the LORD. It is more than a day of rest and congregating; it is the sign of who Israel's God is, which is why saying the sabbath is done away takes away the very sign between Israel and God. - From the questions: eating is allowed on the sabbath, but not cooking. What is baked and seethed is prepared the day before and laid up, so the sabbath meal is leftovers or simple food; no microwaving, no coffee pots, no kindling the cooking fire. - There is no buying or selling on the sabbath or on the holy day, so gas and food are bought before sundown; no fishing either, for what could be called work opens the door to every man excusing his trade on the sabbath. - The Lord gives no man license to sin, but Christ is Lord of the sabbath and brought grace for necessities out of our control, a blown tire or an empty tank on the way to keep the sabbath, or medicine when the body is in danger; it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days. - Precept Ecclesiasticus 33:7-9 : Every day has the same sun, but by the knowledge of the Lord some days were made high days and hallowed; the sabbath is distinguished by God, not by man. Exodus 34:18-20 taught in Exodus 34-37 - The feast of unleavened bread shalt thou keep seven days, in the time of the month Abib, for in the month Abib thou camest out from Egypt; this goes to the Passover season. Exodus 34:22-24 taught in Exodus 34-37 - The feast of weeks goes to Pentecost, and the feast of ingathering at the year's end goes to the feast of tabernacles. - Thrice in the year shall all your men children appear before the Lord GOD, the God of Israel. Exodus 34:25-26 taught in Exodus 34-37 - Thou shalt not offer the blood of my sacrifice with leaven; neither shall the sacrifice of the feast of the passover be left unto the morning: it had to be eaten up or burned. - The first of the firstfruits of thy land thou shalt bring unto the house of the LORD thy God. Exodus 36:20-34 taught in Exodus 34-37 - The whole tent was built to be carried. Exodus 37:25-29 taught in Exodus 34-37 - Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aaron, took either of them his censer, put fire therein and incense thereon, and offered strange fire before the Lord, which he commanded them not; and there went out fire from the Lord and devoured them, and they died before the Lord. Leviticus 2:12 taught in Leviticus 2-5 - The oblation of the firstfruits is offered unto the Lord but not burnt on the altar for a sweet savour. Leviticus 2:14-16 taught in Leviticus 2-5 - The meat offering of the firstfruits is green ears of corn dried by the fire, corn beaten out of full ears, with oil put upon it and frankincense thereon; the priest burns the memorial of it, an offering made by fire unto the Lord. Leviticus 7:35-38 taught in Leviticus 6-9 - Let no man therefore judge you in meat or in drink: add the word offering, the meat offering and drink offering we just read in Leviticus. Leviticus 8:1-5 taught in Leviticus 6-9 - Take Aaron and his sons with him, and the garments, and the anointing oil, and a bullock for the sin offering, and two rams, and a basket of unleavened bread; and all the congregation was gathered unto the door of the tabernacle. - Mark the list: if you want to live under the Old Covenant, you had better have a priest, the garments, the anointing oil, a bullock for the sin offering, two rams, a basket of unleavened bread, and a temple to gather at. Leviticus 19:1-3 taught in Leviticus 18-21 - Keep my sabbaths: the feast days are Sabbaths also. Leviticus 23:1-3 taught in Leviticus 22-25 - These are the feasts of the Lord, holy convocations which He Himself proclaimed. The Most High gave us holy days; a holiday not listed in this Bible and not ordained of the Most High has nothing holy about it. Leviticus 23:23-25 taught in Leviticus 22-25 - In the seventh month, in the first day of the month, is a sabbath, a memorial of blowing of trumpets. Joshua Joshua 1:8 taught in Joshua 1-4 - This verse is the recipe for success, the formula for success, the true prosperity doctrine, and it has three steps: the law in your mouth, meditation day and night, and observing to do all that is written therein. - This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth: when you open your mouth, what comes out is supposed to be scriptural; your conversation has to be modeled after what this book says. When people leave this truth the Lord removes his words out of their mouth, and their whole conversation changes: nothing is left but slander, falsehood, strange doctrines, and flattering speech. - Thou shalt meditate therein day and night: to meditate is to think deeply and carefully, to contemplate, consider, ponder, and muse. Many read their four chapters a day, listen to videos, and quote their precept lists, but never meditate on what they read. You cannot just slap the butter on the biscuit; you have to let it sink into every layer. - Solomon shows what a companion meditation makes of wisdom: when he came into his house he reposed himself with her, for her conversation has no bitterness and living with her has no sorrow, but mirth and joy. Get in the habit of chilling with wisdom when you get home. When you ponder the whole benefit package that comes with wisdom, you understand that to be allied unto wisdom is immortality; the wiser you get, the more spiritually invincible you become. - Make meditation a daily custom, a holy habit, as our forefathers did: somewhere alone and peaceful where the mind can be clear, because you cannot meditate in the middle of activity and noise. When you meditate continually on the commandments, the Lord establishes your heart, and the evil thoughts you battle begin to flush out of your mind. - That thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: the end goal of talking about the commandments and meditating on the commandments is to do the commandments. Joshua 20:1-3 taught in Joshua 17-20 - Now that every tribe had its inheritance, cities of refuge had to be instituted, as the Lord spake by the hand of Moses: that the slayer that killeth any person unawares and unwittingly may flee thither, and they shall be your refuge from the avenger of blood. - Unwittingly means unknowingly; remember the word wittingly in Genesis 48, where Israel guided his hands knowing what he was doing.
