Even today a killer can cross the border into another jurisdiction and go free, and that is evil; but when Israel controlled the land you could not cross a border to get away with murder, for the elders would deliver you right back to the city you came from. Your sin will find you out. - Precept Numbers 35:11-12 : The cities of refuge were appointed that the manslayer die not, until he stand before the congregation in judgment. - Precept Exodus 21:12-13 : The law goes back to Exodus: he that smiteth a man that he die shall surely be put to death, but if a man lie not in wait and God deliver him into his hand, a place is appointed whither he shall flee. Joshua 20:7-9 taught in Joshua 17-20 - They appointed Kedesh in Galilee in mount Naphtali, Shechem in mount Ephraim, and Kirjath-arba, which is Hebron, in the mountain of Judah; and on the other side Jordan by Jericho they assigned Bezer out of the tribe of Reuben, Ramoth in Gilead out of the tribe of Gad, and Golan in Bashan out of the tribe of Manasseh. - These cities were appointed for all the children of Israel and for the stranger that sojourneth among them, that whosoever killeth any person at unawares might flee thither and not die by the hand of the avenger of blood, until he stood before the congregation: until he gets a fair trial. Joshua 21:1-3 taught in Joshua 21-24 - The heads of the fathers of the Levites came near to Eleazar the priest, to Joshua, and to the heads of the tribes at Shiloh, because the tribe of Levi had been appointed cities to dwell in with suburbs for their cattle, and the time had come to receive them. Joshua 21:9-19 taught in Joshua 21-24 - Out of Judah and Simeon the children of Aaron received nine cities by name, and out of Benjamin four more, thirteen cities in all for the priests. - They received Hebron in the hill country of Judah, the city of Arba the father of Anak, to be a city of refuge for the slayer; but the fields and villages of the city belonged to Caleb the son of Jephunneh for his possession. - From the Q&A: not all the cities given to the Levites were cities of refuge. Only certain cities were designated for that, six in all, for the man that killed his brother accidentally. - The city of refuge worked like protective custody: the slayer that killed a person unawares fled there from the avenger of blood and stayed there until he stood before the congregation and his case was judged. - Precept Numbers 35:9-12 : Cities of refuge were appointed that the slayer which killeth any person at unawares may flee there and not die by the avenger until he stand before the congregation in judgment. Joshua 22:32-34 taught in Joshua 21-24 - Phinehas and the princes returned from Gilead to the land of Canaan and brought the children of Israel word again: all is good, the altar is a memorial so the generations after do not forget that our people are on that side Jordan too, and they can come in and keep the feasts and do their sacrifices with us. Judges Judges 18:11-14 taught in Judges 17-20 - Six hundred men of the family of the Danites appointed with weapons of war went up from Zorah and Eshtaol, camped at Mahanehdan behind Kirjathjearim, and passed again unto mount Ephraim to the house of Micah. Judges 18:15-20 taught in Judges 17-20 - They turned in to the house and saluted the Levite, a friendly greeting at the door; that is one of the deceitful man's many trains. While the six hundred armed men stood by the entering of the gate keeping the priest occupied, the five spies went up inside and took the graven image, the ephod, the teraphim, and the molten image. - When the priest saw them coming out with the gods and asked, what do ye? they told him hold thy peace, lay thine hand upon thy mouth: is it better for thee to be a priest unto the house of one man, or unto a tribe and a family in Israel? Do not snitch; roll with us and be the man over a whole tribe. - The priest's heart was glad, and he took the ephod, the teraphim, and the graven image and went in the midst of the people. His covetous spirit was plain: already sold out to serve idols for Micah's silver, he dropped the man who treated him as a son the moment a bigger position was offered. Disloyal through and through. Judges 20:37-46 taught in Judges 17-20 - There was an appointed sign between the men of Israel and the liers in wait, that they should make a great flame with smoke rise up out of the city. That was the purpose of drawing the Benjamites out: while Benjamin smote about thirty men and thought they were winning as in the first battles, the liers in wait hasted, rushed upon Gibeah, smote all the city with the edge of the sword, and set the sign. Judges 21:19-23 taught in Judges 21 - The solution: there was a yearly feast of the Lord in Shiloh, so they commanded the children of Benjamin to lie in wait in the vineyards, and when the daughters of Shiloh came out to dance in the dances, every man was to catch him a wife of the daughters of Shiloh and go to the land of Benjamin. Ruth Ruth 1:6-9 taught in Ruth 1-3 - Naomi heard in the country of Moab that the Lord had visited his people and given them bread, so she arose with her daughters in law to return unto the land of Judah, and told them, Go, return each to her mother's house; the Lord deal kindly with you, as ye have dealt with the dead and with me. - The Lord grant you that ye may find rest, each of you in the house of her husband: that rest is an inheritance. The man is supposed to leave an inheritance; you are not supposed to leave your wife and your children desolate with a gang of bills. To leave an inheritance you first have to work, and you have to be wise with how you deal with your money. - Behind the words the wife of the dead stands the law of the husband's brother: if brethren dwell together and one dies having no child, his brother takes the widow to wife, and the firstborn she bears succeeds in the name of the dead brother, that his name be not put out of Israel. That first child is basically the dead brother's child; he gets the rights of inheritance as if the brother were still alive, so the brother's name stays in the earth and his house is built up. - We are not under that law anymore; we do not have that land inheritance in captivity. It is wicked to pull that scripture today to try to get with your brother's wife after he passes away; do not be looking at your brother's wife. - It is important for us to build our legacy and pass it down; that is one of the things we lack in Israel today. Some of us use captivity as an excuse not to better ourselves or build, but that is not what the scriptures say: get the job, further your education, do more for yourself, your family, and the body. Building up your house also means spiritually building it, teaching your wife and children. - Precept Judith 8:4-7 : The example of a widow finding rest in the house of her husband: Manasses left Judith gold, silver, servants, cattle, and lands, and she remained upon them. 1 Samuel 1 Samuel 1:21 taught in 1 Samuel 1-3 - The man Elkanah, and all his house, went up to offer unto the Lord the yearly sacrifice, and his vow. What is that yearly sacrifice going into? Deuteronomy 16:16. - Precept Deuteronomy 16:16 : Three times in a year shall all thy males appear before the Lord: in the feast of unleavened bread, which is known as Passover; in the feast of weeks, which is known as Pentecost; and in the feast of tabernacles, which is also known as the feast of booths. Elkanah, who lived in mount Ephraim, was applying this law over and over again. 1 Samuel 2:27-29 taught in 1 Samuel 1-3 - Take that into account: do you honour your children above what the Lord says to do? Can they do no wrong, even when they are doing real wrong against the Lord, keeping no commandments, never showing up on the sabbath day, and still living under your roof grown? If they are of age, they know right from wrong, and they are under your roof while you keep the commandments, then they had better be keeping the commandments: showing up to every feast day, the blowing of trumpets, the day of atonement, the passover, the same as you. When they are of age they can go their own way; but they should not be living under your roof and breaking the commandments of God. You honour your children above God when you allow that. 1 Samuel 13:8-10 taught in 1 Samuel 12-15 - Samuel had instructed Saul in chapter 10: when you get to Gilgal, tarry seven days, make no moves until I arrive. Saul tarried seven days according to the set time, but Samuel came not at the moment expected, and the people were scattered from him and acting frantic. - Saul said, Bring hither a burnt offering to me, and he offered the burnt offering, and Saul is not the priest; that is Samuel's office. And it came to pass that as soon as he had made an end of offering the burnt offering, behold, Samuel came. He was barely late, and Saul could not hold his patience. - Brothers do the same thing today: leadership said it would be here at ten, it is five past ten, so we cancel the plan and go home. Be humble and tarry like you were instructed; it may run some minutes over, and the Lord may be testing your patience. 1 Samuel 13:11-12 taught in 1 Samuel 12-15 - Samuel asks, What hast thou done? Saul answers with excuses: the people were scattered from me, thou camest not within the days appointed, the Philistines gathered at Michmash, so I forced myself and offered a burnt offering. This is part of Saul's pattern of behavior; he never wants to hold himself accountable, he always deflects onto whoever else. 1 Samuel 19:18-24 taught in 1 Samuel 16-19 - Saul sent messengers to take David, and when they saw the company of the prophets prophesying and Samuel standing as appointed over them, the spirit of God was upon the messengers of Saul, and they also prophesied; a second and a third set of messengers were sent, and the same thing happened each time they entered that atmosphere. 1 Samuel 20:24-27 taught in 1 Samuel 20-23 - David hid himself in the field, and when the new moon was come the king sat down to eat. David fled at the first of the month, and at the new moon meal his seat was empty. 1 Samuel 22:17-19 taught in 1 Samuel 20-23 - Go back to Genesis and see the spirit that has been placed on this man from the beginning: Esau comforted himself with the purpose of killing his brother Jacob. Just as in the time of Saul, even to this very day, when Israel suffers violence at the hands of the other nations, especially Esau, he gets comfort out of killing us; when Saul appointed Doeg to that task, you can best believe he was quite happy over it and most likely found much pleasure in killing the priests. 1 Samuel 25:26-31 taught in 1 Samuel 24-27 - The soul of my lord shall be bound in the bundle of life with the Lord thy God, and the souls of thine enemies, them shall he sling out as out of the middle of a sling. When the Lord shall have appointed thee ruler over Israel, this shall be no grief unto thee, that thou hast shed blood causeless or that my lord hath avenged himself; then remember thine handmaid. 1 Samuel 25:36-38 taught in 1 Samuel 24-27 - Abigail came home and Nabal held a feast in his house like the feast of a king, and his heart was merry within him, for he was very drunken; so she told him nothing, less or more, until the morning light. 1 Samuel 28:20-25 taught in 1 Samuel 28-31 - The woman reminded Saul that she had put her life in her hand and obeyed his voice, and asked him to let her set a morsel of bread before him that he might have strength for his way. He refused at first, but his servants together with the woman compelled him; she killed the fat calf, baked unleavened bread, and they did eat and went away that night. 1 Samuel 29:1-5 taught in 1 Samuel 28-31 - The Philistines gathered all their armies to Aphek, and Israel pitched by a fountain in Jezreel. David and his men passed on in the rearward with Achish, and the princes of the Philistines demanded, What do these Hebrews here? - Achish vouched for David: he has been with me these days, or these years, and I have found no fault in him since he fell unto me. But the princes were wroth and said, Make this fellow return to his place; let him not go down with us to the battle, lest in the battle he be an adversary to us. For wherewith should he reconcile himself unto his master? should it not be with the heads of these men? - The princes remembered the song: is not this David of whom they sang one to another in dances, saying, Saul slew his thousands, and David his ten thousands?

title: The Priesthood
text: The Priesthood Aaron, his sons, and the Levites: the garments, the duties, the anointing, and the order of the priesthood. Genesis Genesis 9:5 taught in Genesis 9-12 - The Most High requiring blood at the hand of every beast is animal sacrifice, still in place with Noah, passed down generation to generation. - The judgment for sin has always been death. When Eve sinned and caused Adam to sin, either they had to die, or something had to stand in their place; the blood of the animal stood in for them. - That is the scapegoat: it takes the wrongdoings, mistakes, and faults of others and places them on the animal. That is why Cain and Abel were bringing offerings, because they knew of the sacrifice from Genesis 3. - Precept Leviticus 16:8-10 : The scapegoat is presented alive to make an atonement, standing in for the faults of others. Genesis 14:18-20 taught in Genesis 13-16 - Melchizedek king of Salem brought forth bread and wine; Salem goes into Shalom, peace, so he is the king of peace, and he was the priest of the Most High God. - Abram paid tithes to Melchizedek. This is way before the Levitical priesthood; the twelve tribes were not yet born. For the order of Melchisedec, study Hebrews 7 and John 8:56. Genesis 35:9-11 taught in Genesis 32-35 - The nation and company of nations of Abraham's covenant is Israel, plain and clear, and kings come out of Israel's loins. Christ washed us from our sins and made us kings and priests unto God; the men of Israel are kings in the sight of the Most High. - Precept Revelation 1:5-6 : Christ washed us from our sins and hath made us kings and priests unto God. Genesis 41:45 taught in Genesis 40-43 - Pharaoh called Joseph's name Zaphnathpaaneah and gave him Asenath the daughter of Potipherah priest of On to wife. These heathens always like to change our names; that is one reason America is called spiritual Egypt, because they do the same thing that ancient Egypt did. Genesis 41:50-52 taught in Genesis 40-43 - Joseph called the firstborn Manasseh, forgetting, for God had made him forget all his toil and all his father's house; and the second called he Ephraim, fruitful, for God had caused him to be fruitful in the land of his affliction. - Ephraim was the second born, yet Ephraim possessed the kingship: the first king of the Northern Kingdom, Jeroboam, was of the tribe of Ephraim, not of Manasseh. Ephraim is the head tribe of the Northern Kingdom. - Jacob set that in place. When Joseph saw his father lay his right hand upon Ephraim's head it displeased him, and he tried to move it to Manasseh's head; but Jacob refused and said, his younger brother shall be greater than he; and he set Ephraim before Manasseh. Genesis 47:23-26 taught in Genesis 44-47 - Joseph gave the people seed and made it a law over Egypt: give the fifth part unto Pharaoh, and four parts are your own for seed of the field, for your food, and for your households and little ones. - Joseph teaches how to save money: pay the fifth part, and lay up for the years of trouble. That wisdom is how Egypt got through the famine, and it is the same perseverance to practice now in times of tribulation. Exodus Exodus 2:1 taught in Exodus 2-5 - A man of the house of Levi took to wife a daughter of Levi. These are Amram and Jochebed, the father and mother of Moses, Aaron, and Miriam. - Precept Exodus 6:20 : Amram took him Jochebed to wife, and she bare him Aaron and Moses; the scripture names the parents of Moses. Exodus 2:16-20 taught in Exodus 2-5 - The priest of Midian had seven daughters, and the shepherds drove them from the troughs; but Moses stood up and helped them, and watered their flock. Moses was a man of war, not a weak man. - Reuel the priest of Midian is the same man called Jethro, the father in law of Moses. Exodus 3:1-6 taught in Exodus 2-5 - Moses kept the flock of Jethro his father in law and led it to the backside of the desert, to Horeb the mountain of God; and the angel of the LORD appeared unto him in a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush, and the bush was not consumed. - The voice out of the bush said, Draw not nigh hither: put off thy shoes from off thy feet, for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground; I am the God of thy father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob. - The precepts identify that angel. Stephen recounts that the angel which appeared in the bush sent Moses to be a ruler and a deliverer; Joshua met the captain of the host of the LORD, who gave him the same command, Loose thy shoe from off thy foot; and the captain of their salvation, made perfect through sufferings, is Jesus Christ. Precept upon precept, the angel in the burning bush was Christ. - The same angel went before Israel out of Egypt: Behold, I send an Angel before thee; beware of him, and obey his voice, provoke him not, for my name is in him. - God is a Spirit, and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth; yet He has a celestial, angelic body, not flesh of this earth. The Ancient of days has a garment and the hair of his head like the pure wool; that is how man could be made in His image. - Christ was not reincarnated when he came in the flesh. He took not on him the nature of angels, but the seed of Abraham, made like unto his brethren, born a man so that he could die for the nation of Israel, for an angel cannot die. - Precept Hebrews 2:16-17 : He took not on him the nature of angels; but he took on him the seed of Abraham, and in all things it behoved him to be made like unto his brethren. Exodus 4:6-8 taught in Exodus 2-5 - This was a miracle precisely because Moses was a very dark-skinned man; the daughters of the priest of Midian had taken him for an Egyptian. The hand came out white as snow and went back to his natural dark skin; had he been white already there would have been no sign in it. Exodus 4:13-17 taught in Exodus 2-5 - Moses pressed, Send, I pray thee, by the hand of him whom thou wilt send; and the anger of the LORD was kindled against Moses. Is not Aaron the Levite thy brother? I know that he can speak well; he spoke the Hebrew of the people fluently. - Aaron shall be thy spokesman unto the people: he shall be to thee instead of a mouth, and thou shalt be to him instead of God. Moses stood as God in this instance, speaking through Aaron his prophet, who interpreted to the people. Exodus 4:27-31 taught in Exodus 2-5 - The LORD sent Aaron into the wilderness to meet Moses, and he met him in the mount of God and kissed him; Aaron believed right away. Moses told Aaron all the words of the LORD and all the signs. - Aaron spake all the words which the LORD had spoken unto Moses and did the signs in the sight of the people, and the people believed: and when they heard that the LORD had visited the children of Israel, and that he had looked upon their affliction, they bowed their heads and worshipped. After a long time in which the Lord had not been dealing with them, He finally heard their prayers. Exodus 5:1-2 taught in Exodus 2-5 - Moses and Aaron went in and told Pharaoh, Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, Let my people go, that they may hold a feast unto me in the wilderness. That feast was the Passover. Exodus 5:4-5 taught in Exodus 2-5 - The king of Egypt said, Wherefore do ye, Moses and Aaron, let the people from their works? get you unto your burdens. That is the standing complaint of the oppressor: the prophets are pulling the people from their labor and getting their hopes up that their God will deliver them. Exodus 5:6-9 taught in Exodus 2-5 - The work of the Lord is the true calling over any occupation held in Babylon: consider the Apostle and High Priest of our profession, Christ Jesus; fight the good fight of faith, lay hold on eternal life, whereunto thou art also called, and hast professed a good profession before many witnesses. - Precept Hebrews 3:1 : Consider the Apostle and High Priest of our profession, Christ Jesus; the work of the Lord is the profession of the called. Exodus 5:15-19 taught in Exodus 2-5 - The officers of the children of Israel came and cried unto Pharaoh, saying, Wherefore dealest thou thus with thy servants? There is no straw given unto thy servants, and they say to us, Make brick: and, behold, thy servants are beaten; but the fault is in thine own people. - Pharaoh answered, Ye are idle, ye are idle: therefore ye say, Let us go and do sacrifice to the LORD. The charge of idleness is the standing answer to any who would go serve God, whether it is the three days' journey or keeping the Sabbath and the new moons now. - The officers did see that they were in evil case. That is when they realized no appeal to Pharaoh would deliver them; deliverance was not coming from Egypt. - Precept John 11:47-48 : The chief priests and Pharisees said, If we let him thus alone, the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation; men set over the people fear losing their place more than they love the deliverer. Exodus 5:20-21 taught in Exodus 2-5 - They met Moses and Aaron and said, The LORD look upon you, and judge; because ye have made our savour to be abhorred in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of his servants, to put a sword in their hand to slay us. Exodus 6:9-12 taught in Exodus 6-9 - Moses answered, Behold, the children of Israel have not hearkened unto me; how then shall Pharaoh hear me, who am of uncircumcised lips? This is why Aaron was given him for a mouthpiece in the next chapter. Exodus 6:16-20 taught in Exodus 6-9 - Chapter 6 is dealing with the genealogy: the families of Reuben, Simeon, and Levi, and out of Levi came Moses and Aaron. Levi begat Kohath, Kohath begat Amram, and Amram took Jochebed to wife, and she bare him Aaron and Moses. Exodus 6:26-27 taught in Exodus 6-9 - These are that Aaron and Moses to whom the Lord said, Bring out the children of Israel from the land of Egypt; these are they which spake to Pharaoh king of Egypt. Exodus 7:1-2 taught in Exodus 6-9 - The Lord made Moses a god to Pharaoh, and Aaron his brother was his prophet. Moses was as God and Aaron was the mouthpiece, because Moses kept saying he was of uncircumcised lips. Exodus 7:8-12 taught in Exodus 6-9 - It was Aaron who cast down the rod before Pharaoh, and it became a serpent. A lot of people to this day say it was Moses with the rod, because they do not read the Bible; Moses was telling Aaron what to do, and it was Aaron's rod that turned into the serpent. - The magicians of Egypt did in like manner with their enchantments, and their rods became serpents; but Aaron's rod swallowed up their rods. Exodus 7:19-22 taught in Exodus 6-9 - All the waters of Egypt were turned to blood, in the streams, the rivers, the ponds, the pools, and in vessels of wood and vessels of stone; the fish died and the river stank. - With this first plague the Most High was mocking Sobek, the Egyptian idol god of the rivers, showing that he could not defend his own waters. - The magicians did so with their enchantments, but they could only copy the plague; they could not turn the water back clear. Seven days were fulfilled after the Lord had smitten the river. - Many Egyptologists claim this never happened, because to admit it happened is to admit that the idols they claim to be gods and goddesses were powerless before our God, and that those idols do not exist at all. Exodus 8:5-8 taught in Exodus 6-9 - Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters, and the frogs came up and covered the land of Egypt. With this second plague the Most High was mocking Heqet, the Egyptian idol god of the frogs. - So Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron and said, Entreat the Lord that he may take away the frogs. Why did Pharaoh not call on Heqet, the god of frogs? He had to go to the Lord. Exodus 8:16-19 taught in Exodus 6-9 - All the dust of the land became lice in man and in beast throughout all the land of Egypt. Imagine that: the dust of the whole land of Egypt turned to lice. - The magicians did so with their enchantments to bring forth lice, but this time they could not; and the magicians said unto Pharaoh, This is the finger of God. Yet Pharaoh's heart was hardened. - With the third and fourth plagues, the lice and the swarms of flies, the Most High was mocking Beelzebub, the idol lord of flies and uncleanness. Exodus 8:25-32 taught in Exodus 6-9 - Pharaoh said, Go sacrifice to your God in the land; but Moses answered, It is not meet, for we should sacrifice the abomination of the Egyptians before their eyes, and will they not stone us? Israel's sacrifices were the very animals Egypt held sacred, so Israel must go three days' journey into the wilderness. - Moses warned Pharaoh, Let not Pharaoh deal deceitfully any more. The Lord removed the swarms so that there remained not one; and Pharaoh hardened his heart at this time also, and would not let the people go. Exodus 9:8-12 taught in Exodus 6-9 - Moses sprinkled ashes of the furnace toward heaven, and it became a boil breaking forth with blains upon man and upon beast throughout all the land of Egypt. - The magicians could not stand before Moses because of the boils, for the boils were upon the magicians themselves and upon all the Egyptians. With this sixth plague the Most High was mocking Sekhmet, the Egyptian idol goddess of health and beauty. Exodus 9:27-30 taught in Exodus 6-9 - Pharaoh said, I have sinned this time: the Lord is righteous, and I and my people are wicked. This time? So all the other times, none of that was sin? Only now, under the thunder and hail, does he see it. - Moses answered that the thunder and hail would cease, that thou mayest know how that the earth is the Lord's; but as for thee and thy servants, I know that ye will not yet fear the Lord God. Exodus 10:3-6 taught in Exodus 10-13 - Moses went in to Pharaoh with a staff and an ultimatum: how long wilt thou refuse to humble thyself? Let my people go, or tomorrow, in twenty four hours, the locusts come into thy coast. - The locusts would cover the face of the earth so no one could see the ground, eat the residue that escaped the hail, and fill the houses of Pharaoh, of his servants, and of all the Egyptians, such as neither their fathers nor their fathers' fathers had seen. Exodus 10:7-11 taught in Exodus 10-13 - Pharaoh offered to let only the men go, and Moses and Aaron were driven out from his presence. Exodus 10:16-17 taught in Exodus 10-13 - When the judgment got real, Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron in haste and confessed, I have sinned against the Lord your God and against you. Everything had been eaten by the locusts, and now he begged that this death only be taken from him. Exodus 11:8-10 taught in Exodus 10-13 - All Pharaoh's servants would come down and bow to Moses, saying, Get thee out, and all the people that follow thee; and Moses went out from Pharaoh in a great anger. - Pharaoh would not hearken, that the wonders of the Most High might be multiplied in the land of Egypt. He is in control of the leaders of every country, presidents, governors, senators, congressmen, and mayors alike; whoever gets in the seat, he twists and turns them about like the river. Exodus 12:1-2 taught in Exodus 10-13 - This month shall be unto you the beginning of months, the first month of the year. The month is Abib, the month in which Israel came out of Egypt. - Abib in the Bible dictionary is the pre-exilic name for the first month of the year; after the exile the name was changed to Nisan, and it falls between March and April. So the new year begins in the springtime, around March and April, not on January the first in the dead of winter; that is another lie taught in Babylon. Exodus 12:24-28 taught in Exodus 10-13 - The feast days commemorate the Most High delivering his people and bringing judgment on their enemies; that is the same pattern the feast of dedication commemorates. The people bowed the head and worshipped, and the children of Israel went and did as the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron. Exodus 12:30-33 taught in Exodus 10-13 - The last time Pharaoh saw Moses he threatened to kill him if he ever saw his face again; now he called for Moses and Aaron by night, saying, Rise up, get you forth from among my people, go, serve the Lord as ye have said, take your flocks and your herds, and bless me also. Touch not mine anointed, and do my prophets no harm; the man who thought he could threaten the servant of the Most High had a complete change of tone. Exodus 12:43-51 taught in Exodus 10-13 - Thus did all the children of Israel as the Lord commanded Moses and Aaron, and the selfsame day the Lord brought them out of the land of Egypt by their armies. Exodus 14:10-12 taught in Exodus 14-17 - At the first sight of the Egyptians marching, Israel lost all faith. The Lord had done miracle after miracle before their eyes and brought them out with an high hand, yet at the first sign of danger they said He brought them out to die. Our people have always been a rebellious people of little faith: a very froward generation, children in whom is no faith. - Let us alone, that we may serve the Egyptians: that is the same word our people speak today. Why are you stirring up trouble, why tell us to come out of the ways of Babylon; let us alone to serve the slave master, because serving him feels easier than having faith in the Most High. - The same spirit was in Israel in the days of Christ: if we let him thus alone, all men will believe on him, and the Romans shall come. The fear of the oppressor outweighed belief in the miracles. - In captivity the people wax old in mind and will not depart: woe to the bloody city, the prey departed not. Israel was the prey in Egypt and did not want to leave, the same as now. - Precept John 11:47-48 : If we let him thus alone the Romans shall come; the same spirit feared the oppressor more than the Most High. Exodus 15:20-21 taught in Exodus 14-17 - Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took a timbrel, and all the women went out after her with timbrels and with dances, answering the song: sing ye to the Lord, for he hath triumphed gloriously. Exodus 16:1-3 taught in Exodus 14-17 - The whole congregation murmured against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness: would to God we had died by the hand of the Lord in Egypt, when we sat by the flesh pots. The Lord commanded Moses to bring the people out, and when things got tough they made it his fault. Exodus 16:6-8 taught in Exodus 14-17 - Your murmurings are not against us, but against the Lord. Moses and Aaron were nobody of themselves; complaining against the leadership the Most High sets is murmuring against the Most High Himself. Exodus 16:31-36 taught in Exodus 14-17 - Aaron laid up an omer of manna before the Testimony, to be kept for generations, that they may see the bread wherewith the Lord fed Israel in the wilderness. The manna that spoiled overnight on other days was preserved for generations; that is the power of the Most High. Exodus 17:8-13 taught in Exodus 14-17 - When Moses held up his hand, Israel prevailed; when he let down his hand, Amalek prevailed. Aaron and Hur stayed up his hands until the going down of the sun. Moses was about eighty years old holding a rod above his head all day; the fathers were mighty men, stronger than we are today. Exodus 18:1-6 taught in Exodus 18-21 - Jethro the priest of Midian, Moses' father in law, heard all that God had done for Moses and for Israel, and came to Moses in the wilderness with Zipporah and her two sons, Gershom and Eliezer. - Jethro is the same man called Reuel in Exodus 2: the priest of Midian whose seven daughters Moses helped at the well, and who gave Moses Zipporah his daughter. Exodus 19:1-2 taught in Exodus 18-21 - In the third month after going forth out of Egypt, Israel departed from Rephidim, came into the wilderness of Sinai, and camped before the mount. Exodus 19:5-8 taught in Exodus 18-21 - If ye will obey my voice indeed, and keep my covenant, then ye shall be a peculiar treasure unto me above all people, a kingdom of priests, and an holy nation. Exodus 19:12-13 taught in Exodus 18-21 - The Most High is serious about that charge. Exodus 20:25-26 taught in Exodus 18-21 - This scripture helps explain pants, precept upon precept. Exodus 22:28 taught in Exodus 22-25 - Acts 23 is the example: when Paul spoke against the high priest, they that stood by said, Revilest thou God's high priest? Exodus 22:29-30 taught in Exodus 22-25 - Thou shalt not delay to offer the first of thy ripe fruits and of thy liquors, and the firstborn of thy sons shalt thou give unto me. Exodus 23:14-17 taught in Exodus 22-25 - None shall appear before me empty: you could not come empty-handed. Exodus 24:13-18 taught in Exodus 22-25 - Moses rose up with his minister Joshua and went up into the mount of God, leaving Aaron and Hur with the elders for any matters. Exodus 25:3-7 taught in Exodus 22-25 - The offering was gold, silver, brass, blue, purple, and scarlet, fine linen, goats' hair, rams' skins dyed red, badgers' skins, shittim wood, oil for the light, spices, and onyx stones for the ephod and the breastplate. Exodus 25:23-30 taught in Exodus 22-25 - Understand how we lived: in our kingdom everything was overlaid with pure gold, clean and royal, with the order of kings, priests, counsellors, and the royal garments. Exodus 26:15-30 taught in Exodus 26-29 - The boards of shittim wood, the sockets of silver, and the bars overlaid with gold are the physical structure of the tabernacle, how it would be put together and what it would consist of. - Rear up the tabernacle according to the fashion thereof which was shewed thee in the mount. Exodus 27:20-21 taught in Exodus 26-29 - The Most High tells Moses to command the children of Israel to bring pure oil olive beaten for the light, to cause the lamp to burn always; Aaron and his sons order it from evening to morning before the Lord, a statute for ever unto their generations. - Though Israel is in captivity now without a temple, without lamps to bring oil for, and no longer under the Levitical priesthood, think about it spiritually: you have to keep your lamp lit and keep the oil in your life. Exodus 28:1-2 taught in Exodus 26-29 - Aaron and his sons Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar are taken from among the children of Israel to minister unto the Most High in the priest's office. - The Most High commanded holy garments to be made for Aaron for glory and for beauty. Exodus 28:30 taught in Exodus 26-29 - The Urim and the Thummim go in the breastplate of judgment, upon Aaron's heart before the Lord; Aaron bears the judgment of the children of Israel upon his heart continually. - Urim and Thummim means lights and perfections: objects not specifically described in the scriptures, perhaps stones since they went in the breastplate, by which the high priest ascertained the will of the Most High in important matters affecting the nation. Exodus 28:39-43 taught in Exodus 26-29 - The broidered coat of fine linen, the mitre of fine linen, and the girdle of needlework; and for Aaron's sons coats, girdles, and bonnets, for glory and for beauty, to be anointed and consecrated in. - Linen breeches to cover their nakedness, from the loins even unto the thighs, upon Aaron and his sons when they come near the altar to minister, that they bear not iniquity and die: a statute for ever unto him and his seed after him. - Precept Ecclesiasticus 45:6-13 : The second account of Aaron's garments: rich garments with breeches, pomegranates and bells compassing him round about, the whole world in the writing of the tribes, and a crown of gold upon the mitre; no stranger ever put them on. Exodus 29:43-46 taught in Exodus 26-29 - The tabernacle shall be sanctified by His glory, and Aaron and his sons sanctified to minister in the priest's office; for the Most High to enter and deal with Israel, everything had to be sanctified. Exodus 30:6-9 taught in Exodus 30-33 - Aaron burned sweet incense on it every morning when he dressed the lamps, and again at even when he lighted the lamps, a perpetual incense before the Lord throughout the generations; it burned continually, morning and evening. The Most High is hard on his daughters for a reason, and he was not playing with that judgment. Numbers 5:23-28 taught in Numbers 3-6 - The priest wrote the curses in a book and blotted them out with the bitter water, waved the jealousy offering before the Lord, burnt the memorial upon the altar, and caused the woman to drink. Numbers 5:29-31 taught in Numbers 3-6 - This is the law of jealousies, when a wife goeth aside or when the spirit of jealousy cometh upon a husband: the priest executed upon her all this law, the man was guiltless from iniquity, and the woman, if guilty, bore her iniquity. Numbers 6:9-12 taught in Numbers 3-6 - If any man died very suddenly by him, the head of his consecration was defiled: he shaved his head on the seventh day of his cleansing, brought two turtles or two young pigeons to the priest on the eighth day, and a lamb of the first year for a trespass offering; the days before were lost. Numbers 6:13-20 taught in Numbers 3-6 - He shaved the head of his separation at the door of the tabernacle and put the hair in the fire under the sacrifice of the peace offerings; the priest put the sodden shoulder and the cakes on his hands and waved them for a wave offering, which we covered in Exodus: the priest picks it up and waves it before the Lord. Numbers 6:22-27 taught in Numbers 3-6 - On this wise Aaron and his sons blessed the children of Israel: the Lord bless thee and keep thee, the Lord make his face shine upon thee and be gracious unto thee, the Lord lift up his countenance upon thee and give thee peace; and they shall put my name upon the children of Israel, and I will bless them. Numbers 7:4-9 taught in Numbers 7-10 - The Lord told Moses to take the wagons and oxen for the service of the tabernacle of the congregation and give them to the Levites, to every man according to his service: two wagons and four oxen to the sons of Gershon, and four wagons and eight oxen to the sons of Merari, under the hand of Ithamar the son of Aaron the priest. - Unto the sons of Kohath he gave none, because the service of the sanctuary belonging unto them was that they should bear upon their shoulders. Numbers 4 shows what that bearing was: Aaron and his sons covered the ark and the vessels first, and after that the sons of Kohath came to bear them, not touching any holy thing lest they die. - Precept Numbers 4:4-6 : The service of the sons of Kohath is about the most holy things; Aaron and his sons take down the covering vail and cover the ark before the camp sets forward. - Precept Numbers 4:15 : When Aaron has made an end of covering the sanctuary, the sons of Kohath come to bear it, but they shall not touch any holy thing, lest they die. Numbers 8:1-4 taught in Numbers 7-10 - Aaron lighted the seven lamps to give light over against the candlestick, as the Lord commanded Moses; and the candlestick was of beaten gold, made according unto the pattern which the Lord had shewed Moses. Numbers 8:5-14 taught in Numbers 7-10 - The Levites were taken from among the children of Israel and cleansed: water of purifying sprinkled upon them, all their flesh shaven, and their clothes washed. - The whole assembly of the children of Israel was gathered, the children of Israel put their hands upon the Levites, and Aaron offered the Levites before the Lord for an offering of the children of Israel, with the two bullocks for a sin offering and a burnt offering to make an atonement for the Levites. - Thus were the Levites separated from among the children of Israel: and the Levites shall be mine. Numbers 8:15-19 taught in Numbers 7-10 - After the cleansing the Levites went in to do the service of the tabernacle of the congregation. Mark the word instead in verse 16: instead of such as open every womb, instead of the firstborn of all the children of Israel, the Most High took the Levites unto himself. - The Levites were given as a gift to Aaron and to his sons, to do the service of the children of Israel and to make an atonement for them, that there be no plague among the children of Israel when they come nigh unto the sanctuary. - Precept Exodus 13:1-2 : Sanctify unto me all the firstborn, whatsoever openeth the womb among the children of Israel; that was the office before the Levites were taken instead. Numbers 8:20-22 taught in Numbers 7-10 - Moses, Aaron, and all the congregation of the children of Israel did to the Levites according unto all that the Lord commanded Moses; the Levites were purified, and after that they went in to do their service in the tabernacle of the congregation before Aaron and before his sons. Numbers 8:23-26 taught in Numbers 7-10 - The service of the Levites had an age: from twenty and five years old and upward they went in to wait upon the service of the tabernacle of the congregation, and up until that point they were not allowed to do the service. Numbers 9:6-8 taught in Numbers 7-10 - Certain men were defiled by the dead body of a man, so they could not keep the passover on that day. The law had already put out of the camp whosoever was defiled by the dead, so they could not come in with the congregation to make their offering. - They asked, wherefore are we kept back, that we may not offer an offering of the Lord in his appointed season? And Moses said, stand still, and I will hear what the Lord will command concerning you. Numbers 10:1-4 taught in Numbers 7-10 - There were different ways the Levites had to blow the trumpets: one way to call the whole congregation, another for just the leaders, and another to let everybody know it was war. Numbers 10:7-9 taught in Numbers 7-10 - The sons of Aaron the priests blew the trumpets, an ordinance for ever throughout your generations. In war in your land against the enemy that oppresseth you, blow an alarm, and ye shall be remembered before the Lord your God and saved from your enemies. As Israel marched through the wilderness against the nations, the Most High remembered them and destroyed the enemy, as long as they were keeping the commandments. Numbers 15:22-26 taught in Numbers 15-18 - If the whole congregation sinned through ignorance, without the knowledge of what they were doing, and the priest came behind them and corrected them on it, then all the congregation offered a young bullock for a burnt offering and a kid of the goats for a sin offering. - The priest made an atonement for all the congregation of the children of Israel, and it was forgiven them, for it was ignorance; the stranger among them was included in that forgiveness. Numbers 15:27-29 taught in Numbers 15-18 - If any single soul sinned through ignorance, he brought a she goat of the first year for a sin offering, and the priest made an atonement for him, and it was forgiven him. Numbers 15:32-36 taught in Numbers 15-18 - The man found gathering sticks on the sabbath day is the example of the presumptuous sin just described: someone who thought about the sin before he did it. He was not picking up sticks just to pick up sticks; he was gathering them to kindle a fire and cook on the sabbath. - They put him in ward, meaning they locked him up, because it was not declared what should be done to him; then the Lord commanded Moses that the man be surely put to death, and all the congregation stoned him with stones without the camp. - He did not even get to the act itself; he had the intention, and for that willful intent he was put to death. Numbers 16:1-3 taught in Numbers 15-18 - Korah was of Levi, and Dathan, Abiram, and On were of Reuben. With them rose up two hundred and fifty princes of the assembly, famous in the congregation, men of renown; that is two hundred and fifty three in all against Moses and Aaron. - They charged Moses and Aaron with taking too much upon themselves and lifting themselves above the congregation. They thought Moses and Aaron carried themselves as better than the rest, but the Most High is the one who chose them as leaders and was dealing with them; the accusers were jealous of them. Numbers 16:8-11 taught in Numbers 15-18 - You already stand before the congregation and minister unto them; the Most High is still dealing with you. But they sought the priesthood also, and for that cause Korah and all his company were gathered together against the Lord: and what is Aaron, that ye murmur against him? Numbers 16:15-19 taught in Numbers 15-18 - Every man took his censer, two hundred and fifty censers, with Aaron and Korah also, put fire and incense in them, and stood in the door of the tabernacle of the congregation; and Korah gathered all the congregation against Moses and Aaron, and the glory of the Lord appeared unto all the congregation. Numbers 16:20-22 taught in Numbers 15-18 - The Lord told Moses and Aaron to separate themselves from among the congregation, that he might consume them in a moment: get away from them, because judgment is about to come. - Moses and Aaron fell upon their faces and pleaded: O God, the God of the spirits of all flesh, shall one man sin, and wilt thou be wroth with all the congregation? They still had that love for their people and pleaded with the Lord not to deal with the whole congregation over one man's sin. Numbers 16:36-40 taught in Numbers 15-18 - The Lord told Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest to take up the censers out of the burning, for they are hallowed, and scatter the fire yonder; the censers of these sinners against their own souls were made broad plates for a covering of the altar, because they were offered before the Lord. - The plates were a memorial and a sign unto the children of Israel, that no stranger which is not of the seed of Aaron come near to offer incense before the Lord, that he be not as Korah and as his company. Numbers 16:41-45 taught in Numbers 15-18 - On the morrow, the very next day, all the congregation murmured against Moses and Aaron, saying, ye have killed the people of the Lord. After they had just seen the earth open up and swallow men, they still would not let it go and gathered against Moses again; that is just how rebellious we are. - The Most High saw what was going on, and the cloud covered the tabernacle and the glory of the Lord appeared; Moses and Aaron came before the tabernacle because they knew the Most High was ready to deal with them. - The Lord came down ready to put them to death again, saying get you up from among this congregation, that I may consume them as in a moment; and Moses and Aaron fell upon their faces, still pleading for their people because they loved them so much. Numbers 16:46-48 taught in Numbers 15-18 - Moses told Aaron to take a censer with fire from off the altar and incense, and go quickly unto the congregation and make an atonement for them, for wrath had gone out from the Lord and the plague was begun; the Most High was already putting them to death. - Aaron ran into the midst of the congregation, put on incense, made an atonement for the people, and stood between the dead and the living; and the plague was stayed. Numbers 16:49-50 taught in Numbers 15-18 - They that died in the plague were fourteen thousand and seven hundred, beside them that died about the matter of Korah; so beside the two hundred and fifty three that died with Korah, fourteen thousand seven hundred more were put to death. Numbers 17:1-5 taught in Numbers 15-18 - Every tribe took a rod, a stick or staff, according to the house of their fathers, twelve rods, and the prince of every tribe wrote his name upon his rod; Aaron's name was written upon the rod of Levi. - By this the Most High would make the murmurings of the children of Israel to cease from him, showing them that he was dealing with Moses and Aaron and them alone. Numbers 17:6-9 taught in Numbers 15-18 - Every prince gave Moses a rod, one for each according to their fathers' houses, twelve rods, and the rod of Aaron was among them, and Moses laid them up before the Lord in the tabernacle of witness. - On the morrow, the rod of Aaron for the house of Levi was budded, and brought forth buds, and bloomed blossoms, and yielded almonds; and every man took back his own rod. Numbers 17:10-11 taught in Numbers 15-18 - The Lord commanded Aaron's rod to be brought again before the testimony, to be kept for a token against the rebels, to take away their murmurings from the Lord, that they die not; so he would not have to put them to death again for murmuring. Numbers 18:1-7 taught in Numbers 15-18 - The Lord told Aaron that he and his sons and his father's house would bear the iniquity of the sanctuary and of their priesthood; that was their job. This explains who should minister in the tabernacle after Israel's cry in the last chapter. - The tribe of Levi was joined unto Aaron to minister unto him and keep the charge of the tabernacle, their jobs; only they were not to come nigh the vessels of the sanctuary and the altar, the ark of the covenant and the different vessels, that neither they nor the priests die. - The Levites were given to Aaron as a gift for the Lord, to do the service of the tabernacle; Aaron and his sons kept the priest's office for every thing of the altar and within the vail. The stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death: an Israelite not of Levi could not come near the tabernacle. Numbers 18:8-11 taught in Numbers 15-18 - The Lord gave Aaron the charge of the heave offerings of all the hallowed things of the children of Israel, by reason of the anointing, to him and his sons by an ordinance for ever. - Of the most holy things reserved from the fire, every oblation, meat offering, sin offering, and trespass offering was most holy for Aaron and his sons; the priests kept a portion of it and ate it in the most holy place. - The heave offering of their gift, with all the wave offerings of the children of Israel, was given to Aaron and his sons and his daughters by a statute for ever; every one that is clean in the house could eat of it. This is what the children of Israel gave for the Levites. Numbers 18:12-14 taught in Numbers 15-18 - All the best of the oil, the best of the wine, and the wheat, the firstfruits which they offered unto the Lord, were given to the priests; whatsoever is first ripe in the land was theirs, and every one that was clean in the house could eat of it. Numbers 18:18-19 taught in Numbers 15-18 - The flesh of them was the priest's, as the wave breast and as the right shoulder; all the heave offerings of the holy things which the children of Israel offered unto the Lord were given to Aaron and his sons and his daughters by a statute for ever, to the lineage of the Levites. - Exodus 29 shows how the wave offering and the heave offering were done. The wave offering was put in the hands of Aaron and his sons and waved, meaning shaken, before the Lord; then it was received of their hands and burnt upon the altar. Each had a different way it was waved or lifted up to the Most High before it was actually burnt and offered to the Lord, and the breast of the ram of consecration was waved and became the priest's part. - It is a covenant of salt for ever before the Lord, unto Aaron and to his seed with him, the children that come after them. - Precept Exodus 29:24-28 : The wave offering was waved in the hands of Aaron and his sons before the Lord and then burnt on the altar, and the wave breast and heave shoulder were the priests' part from the children of Israel for ever. Numbers 18:20-24 taught in Numbers 15-18 - The Lord told Aaron: thou shalt have no inheritance in their land, neither any part among them; I am thy part and thine inheritance among the children of Israel. The Levites had no inheritance of land to pass down; the Most High said, I will be taking care of you. - The Lord gave the children of Levi all the tenth in Israel for an inheritance. This is the tithe: the tenth part was given to the Levites for their service which they served, the service of the tabernacle of the congregation, their sacrificing and teaching of the laws. - That tenth went to the children of Levi, and it was done away with when Christ came and died and took that priesthood; we no longer give that tenth to Levi. - The children of Israel were not to come nigh the tabernacle of the congregation, lest they bear sin and die; it was a sin for the other tribes of Israel to come near the tabernacle, on pain of death. All the work to be done in the tabernacle was committed unto the Levites, and they bore their iniquity, a statute for ever. Numbers 18:25-32 taught in Numbers 15-18 - When the Levites took of the children of Israel the tithes given them for their inheritance, they offered up of it an heave offering for the Lord, even a tenth part of the tithe: after the Levites got their tenth, the Most High wanted his tenth part of that, which they had to offer up. - Their heave offering was reckoned unto them as though it were the corn of the threshingfloor and the fulness of the winepress, and the Lord's heave offering out of all their tithes was given to Aaron the priest; out of all their gifts they offered every heave offering of the Lord, of all the best thereof, even the hallowed part. Numbers 19:10 taught in Numbers 19-22 - After the priest burns the red heifer and sprinkles her blood, one that is clean gathers up her ashes; even that clean man must wash his clothes and be unclean until the evening. Numbers 19:11 taught in Numbers 19-22 - Any man that touches the dead body of any man is unclean seven days. There is history on this law: in Numbers 9 certain men were defiled by a dead body around the passover and could not keep it on that day because of this very statute. - The Most High answered through Moses with a second keeping: the man unclean by reason of a dead body, or far off on a journey, keeps the passover the fourteenth day of the second month at even, eating it with unleavened bread and bitter herbs. - Precept Numbers 9:6-7 : Certain men defiled by the dead body of a man could not keep the passover that day; they asked Moses wherefore they were kept back. Numbers 19:14-22 taught in Numbers 19-22 - Chapter 19 as a whole gives the water of separation, which is the purification for sin: the first half gives the specifics of the sacrifice and what the priest must do, and the rest gives the examples of how a man becomes unclean, whether by sin, by touching the dead, or by being around the dead. Numbers 20:2-5 taught in Numbers 19-22 - There was no water for the congregation, and the people gathered together against Moses and against Aaron; this is another account of Israel coming against them. Numbers 20:6-11 taught in Numbers 19-22 - Moses and Aaron fell upon their faces at the door of the tabernacle, and the glory of the Lord appeared. The command was to take the rod and speak unto the rock before their eyes, and it would give forth his water for the congregation and their beasts. - At this point Moses got out of the spirit; a stomach can only take so much of a rebellious people. He said, Hear now, ye rebels; must we fetch you water out of this rock? That we is how you know Moses was off: he forgot who was giving the water. It was the Lord giving it, not Moses and not Aaron. Numbers 20:12-13 taught in Numbers 19-22 - Because ye believed me not, to sanctify me in the eyes of the children of Israel: for this Moses and Aaron would not bring the congregation into the land given them. Numbers 20:22-29 taught in Numbers 19-22 - At mount Hor, by the coast of the land of Edom, the Lord said Aaron shall be gathered unto his people; he could not enter the land because of the rebellion at the water of Meribah. - Moses stripped Aaron of his garments and put them upon Eleazar his son; the priesthood passed to Eleazar, and Aaron died there in the top of the mount. - When all the congregation saw that Aaron was dead, all the house of Israel mourned for Aaron thirty days. Numbers 25:6-9 taught in Numbers 23-26 - When Phinehas the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, saw it, he rose up from among the congregation, took a javelin in his hand, went after the man of Israel into the tent, and thrust both of them through; so the plague was stayed from the children of Israel, and those that died in the plague were twenty and four thousand. - Let us now praise famous men: Phinehas stands third in glory, because he had zeal in the fear of the Lord and stood up with good courage of heart when the people were turned back, and made reconciliation for Israel; therefore a covenant of peace was made with him, that he and his posterity should have the dignity of the priesthood for ever. - Precept Ecclesiasticus 45:23-24 : Phinehas is third in glory for his zeal, and the covenant of peace and everlasting priesthood was his reward. Numbers 25:10-13 taught in Numbers 23-26 - Phinehas turned the wrath of the Most High away from the children of Israel, because he was zealous for his God's sake among them; wherefore the Lord gave him His covenant of peace, and to his seed after him the covenant of an everlasting priesthood, because he made an atonement for the children of Israel. - That covenant of peace is what all of us are striving for, rest from this servitude of bondage; but the wisdom in reading the acts of Phinehas is that you must be zealous for the law of the Most High to obtain it. Be ye zealous for the law, and give your lives for the covenant of your fathers; Phinehas our father, in being zealous and fervent, obtained the covenant of an everlasting priesthood. - Precept 1 Maccabees 2:54 : Phinehas obtained the everlasting priesthood by being zealous and fervent. Numbers 26:1-2 taught in Numbers 23-26 - After the plague the Lord commanded a new numbering of the congregation, from twenty years old and upward, all that are able to go to war in Israel. Twenty is the biblical age of a man: Israel sent men to war, not children, so the numbering of them able for war fixes the age of manhood at twenty years old. Numbers 26:9-11 taught in Numbers 23-26 - Dathan and Abiram were famous in the congregation, who strove against Moses and against Aaron in the company of Korah, when they strove against the Lord; the account is back in Numbers 16. The earth opened her mouth and swallowed them up together with Korah, the fire devoured two hundred and fifty men, and they became a sign. Numbers 26:59-61 taught in Numbers 23-26 - Jochebed the daughter of Levi bare unto Amram Aaron and Moses and Miriam their sister; and unto Aaron were born Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar. - Precept Leviticus 10:1-2 : Nadab and Abihu offered strange fire before the Lord, which he commanded them not, and fire from the Lord devoured them. Numbers 26:63-65 taught in Numbers 23-26 - Among these numbered by Moses and Eleazar in the plains of Moab there was not a man of them that was numbered in the wilderness of Sinai, for the Lord had said of them, they shall surely die in the wilderness; and there was not left a man of them, save Caleb the son of Jephunneh and Joshua the son of Nun. - Why Caleb and Joshua? They had another spirit on them and did not doubt when the Lord sent them to spy out the land. My servant Caleb, because he had another spirit with him and hath followed me fully, him will I bring into the land; he let nobody keep him from serving the Most High. - Christ said the same thing: he that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me. If the Lord finds you lukewarm, choosing your kids, your parents, or your spouse over following God and Christ and keeping the commandments wholly, you will not enter into the land; you must follow fully like Caleb and zealously like Phinehas. - Let that be a lesson learned, for whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope. Numbers 27:1-4 taught in Numbers 27-30 - The daughters of Zelophehad, of the tribe of Manasseh, stood before Moses, Eleazar the priest, the princes, and all the congregation at the door of the tabernacle. Numbers 27:12-14 taught in Numbers 27-30 - The Lord told Moses to get up into mount Abarim and see the land given to the children of Israel; he would see it but not enter it, and then be gathered unto his people as Aaron his brother was gathered. - The reason is written: Moses rebelled against the commandment of the Most High in the desert of Zin at the water of Meribah. The Lord gave a specific commandment to speak unto the rock before their eyes, and Moses instead smote the rock twice; the water still came out abundantly, but Moses and Aaron did not sanctify the Lord in the eyes of the children of Israel, and for that neither of them brought the congregation into the land. - Precept Numbers 20:7-12 : The commandment was to speak unto the rock; Moses smote it twice, and because they believed not, to sanctify the Lord in the eyes of Israel, they did not bring the congregation into the land. Numbers 27:18-21 taught in Numbers 27-30 - Joshua was set before Eleazar the priest and before all the congregation and given his charge in their sight, and some of Moses' honour was put upon him, so all Israel could see with their own eyes the man the Most High ordained to lead the nation after the death of Moses. - Joshua was to stand before Eleazar the priest, who would ask counsel for him after the judgment of Urim before the Lord; at his word they would go out and come in, he and all the children of Israel with him. Numbers 27:22-23 taught in Numbers 27-30 - Moses did as the Lord commanded him: he took Joshua, set him before Eleazar the priest and all the congregation, laid his hands upon him, and gave him a charge, as the Lord commanded by the hand of Moses. Numbers 28:9-10 taught in Numbers 27-30 - Precept upon precept this answers what Christ told the Pharisees: the priests in the temple profane the sabbath and are blameless. Israel did not kindle fire for themselves on the sabbath, but this altar work was the ordinance of the Lord for every sabbath day. - This is also why Christ had to come. In captivity we have no lambs, no farms, no temple, no most holy place, no veil, no high priest; the handwriting of ordinances that was against us was taken out of the way and nailed to his cross. Those who deny Christ and claim the Old Testament only are not keeping these sacrifices, and without Christ the whole law, drink offering to meat offering, still stands over them. - Precept Matthew 12:5 : The priests in the temple profane the sabbath, and are blameless; the sabbath offerings were commanded work. Numbers 28:26-31 taught in Numbers 27-30 - He taketh away the first, that he may establish the second: Christ offered his body once for all, where the priests stood daily offering the same sacrifices which can never take away sins. Thank the Most High for Jesus Christ, because these ordinances cannot be fulfilled in captivity. - Precept Hebrews 10:8-11 : He taketh away the first covenant of sacrifices to establish the second; we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all, while the priests stood daily offering sacrifices which can never take away sins. Numbers 29:7-11 taught in Numbers 27-30 - The tenth day of the seventh month is an holy convocation, a large gathering, wherein ye shall afflict your souls and do no work at all: the day of atonement, instituted as a statute for ever, when the priest made an atonement to cleanse the people from all their sins before the Lord. - We fast without the sacrifices, because the atonement is now Christ. He was brought as a lamb to the slaughter, wounded for our transgressions, and the Lord laid on him the iniquity of us all, just as the priest laid the sins of the nation on the sacrifice of Leviticus 16; that is why the veil rent in two when he died, and why John said, Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world. - Precept Leviticus 16:29-31 : A statute for ever: in the seventh month, on the tenth day, ye shall afflict your souls, and the priest made an atonement to cleanse you from all your sins before the Lord. Numbers 31:3-6 taught in Numbers 31-34 - A thousand of every tribe, twelve thousand armed for war, were sent with Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest, with the holy instruments and the trumpets to blow. - Precept Numbers 25:7-8 : Phinehas took a javelin and thrust the man of Israel and the Midianitish woman through, and the plague was stayed. Numbers 31:9-12 taught in Numbers 31-34 - Israel took the women of Midian captives with their little ones, took the spoil of all their cattle, flocks, and goods, and burnt all their cities and all their goodly castles with fire. - Midian comes from the lineage of Ishmael, the people known today as the Arab man. This shows Esau was not the one who first came up with castles; the castles seen in the movies were conquered from other nations. - They took all the spoil and all the prey, both of men and of beasts: the Midianites had captives of their own, and Israel took over both the men and the beasts when they overcame them. Numbers 31:13-18 taught in Numbers 31-34 - Moses was wroth with the officers of the host, the leaders of the army of Israel, because they saved all the women alive. - These women caused the children of Israel, through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass against the Lord in the matter of Peor. Balaam took it upon himself to send the women of the other nations to Israel, and it caused the people to go into fornication, and the Lord began putting them to death, over twenty and four thousand, in the history of Numbers 25. - Therefore every male among the little ones was to be killed, and every woman that had known man by lying with him; but the women children that had not known a man they kept alive for themselves. - Moses allowed the men to keep those women so they would not commit sin and go raping the women, being out at war. That does not mean it is done today; it was a time that the Most High allowed it so the men would not be in the midst of sin. Numbers 31:19-24 taught in Numbers 31-34 - Eleazar the priest gave the ordinance: gold, silver, brass, iron, tin, and lead, everything that may abide the fire, goes through the fire and is purified with the water of separation; whatever abides not the fire goes through the water; and on the seventh day they wash their clothes, are clean, and come into the camp. Numbers 31:25-30 taught in Numbers 31-34 - Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the chief fathers of the congregation took the sum of the prey, both of man and of beast, adding up all that was taken from the Midianites. - A tribute was levied unto the Lord: of the men of war, one soul of five hundred, of persons, beeves, asses, and sheep, given to Eleazar the priest for a heave offering, because he was the priest; and of the children of Israel's half, one portion of fifty, given to the Levites which kept the charge of the tabernacle. Numbers 31:41 taught in Numbers 31-34 - Moses gave the tribute, the Lord's heave offering, unto Eleazar the priest, as the Lord commanded Moses. The heave offerings belong to the priesthood by statute forever, a covenant of salt, because Aaron and Levi have no inheritance in the land; the Most High is their part and their inheritance. - Precept Numbers 18:19 : All the heave offerings of the holy things are given to the priest and his sons by a statute for ever; it is a covenant of salt before the Lord. - Precept Numbers 18:20 : Aaron has no inheritance in their land; the Lord is his part and his inheritance among the children of Israel. Numbers 32:1-5 taught in Numbers 31-34 - The children of Reuben and Gad had a very great multitude of cattle, and when they saw that Jazer and Gilead was a place for cattle, they asked Moses for that land and said, bring us not over Jordan. - They did not want to go forward any more; they were ready to set up shop before they crossed over Jordan, and they had not even finished the mission. Numbers 33:1-4 taught in Numbers 31-34 - These are the journeys of the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt, and Moses wrote their goings out by the commandment of the Lord. - They departed from Rameses on the fifteenth day of the first month, on the morrow after the passover, with an high hand in the sight of all the Egyptians, while the Egyptians buried all their firstborn, which the Lord had smitten among them: upon their gods also the Lord executed judgments; he put them to death. Numbers 33:37-39 taught in Numbers 31-34 - Aaron the priest went up into mount Hor at the commandment of the Lord and died there, in the fortieth year after the children of Israel were come out of the land of Egypt, in the first day of the fifth month; and Aaron was an hundred and twenty and three years old when he died. The number is the fortieth year; read it carefully. Numbers 34:16-29 taught in Numbers 31-34 - The Lord named the men which shall divide the land: Eleazar the priest and Joshua the son of Nun, and one prince of every tribe, Caleb the son of Jephunneh for Judah and the rest by name. Numbers 35:1-2 taught in Numbers 35-36 - Moses commands the tribes to separate cities out of their own inheritance for the Levites to dwell in, with suburbs round about them. - The Levites needed cities inside every tribe's territory because the Most High took them from among the children of Israel as a gift, to do the service of the tabernacle of the congregation.
