Even today a killer can cross the border into another jurisdiction and go free, and that is evil; but when Israel controlled the land you could not cross a border to get away with murder, for the elders would deliver you right back to the city you came from. Your sin will find you out. - Precept Numbers 35:22-25 : If he thrust him suddenly without enmity, or cast a stone seeing him not, the congregation shall judge between the slayer and the revenger of blood and deliver the innocent slayer back to his city of refuge. Joshua 20:6 taught in Joshua 17-20 - He also dwelt there until the death of the high priest of those days; then the slayer shall return to his own city and his own house, the city from whence he fled. - Precept Numbers 35:25 : The congregation shall restore him to the city of his refuge, and he shall abide in it unto the death of the high priest, which was anointed with the holy oil. - Precept Numbers 35:26-28 : If the slayer comes outside the border of his city of refuge before the death of the high priest and the revenger of blood finds him and kills him, the revenger shall not be guilty of blood; the refuge is protective custody, and he was to remain in it. Joshua 21:1-3 taught in Joshua 21-24 - The heads of the fathers of the Levites came near to Eleazar the priest, to Joshua, and to the heads of the tribes at Shiloh, because the tribe of Levi had been appointed cities to dwell in with suburbs for their cattle, and the time had come to receive them. - This was not a new request; it was commanded of the Most High by the hand of Moses that all twelve tribes should give of their inheritance to the Levites. - Precept Numbers 35:2-3 : The commandment by the hand of Moses: give unto the Levites cities to dwell in and suburbs round about them for their cattle, their goods, and all their beasts. Joshua 21:4-8 taught in Joshua 21-24 - The cities came out by lot family by family: the children of Aaron the priest, of the Kohathites, had thirteen cities out of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin; the rest of the children of Kohath had ten cities out of Ephraim, Dan, and the half tribe of Manasseh. Joshua 21:9-19 taught in Joshua 21-24 - Out of Judah and Simeon the children of Aaron received nine cities by name, and out of Benjamin four more, thirteen cities in all for the priests. - From the Q&A: not all the cities given to the Levites were cities of refuge. Only certain cities were designated for that, six in all, for the man that killed his brother accidentally. Joshua 21:20-26 taught in Joshua 21-24 - The families of the children of Kohath that remained had four cities out of Ephraim, including Shechem in mount Ephraim to be a city of refuge for the slayer, four cities out of Dan, and two out of the half tribe of Manasseh: ten cities in all. Joshua 21:27-33 taught in Joshua 21-24 - The children of Gershon received Golan in Bashan out of the other half tribe of Manasseh to be a city of refuge for the slayer, four cities out of Issachar, four out of Asher, and out of Naphtali three, including Kedesh in Galilee, a city of refuge: thirteen cities in all. Joshua 21:34-42 taught in Joshua 21-24 - The children of Merari, the rest of the Levites, received four cities out of Zebulun, four out of Reuben, and four out of Gad, including Ramoth in Gilead, a city of refuge for the slayer: twelve cities. - All the cities of the Levites within the possession of the children of Israel were forty and eight cities with their suburbs, every one with her suburbs round about her. Joshua 22:13-14 taught in Joshua 21-24 - Israel sent Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest with ten princes, one head of a chief house from every tribe. When you send Phinehas it is a problem, because of the kind of man Phinehas was: where he showed up, the zeal of the Most High showed up with him. - Precept Numbers 25:6-9 : Phinehas rose up from among the congregation, took a javelin, and thrust the man of Israel and the woman through, and the plague was stayed; those that died were twenty and four thousand. Joshua 22:30-31 taught in Joshua 21-24 - When Phinehas and the princes heard the words of the children of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh, it pleased them. Phinehas said, This day we perceive that the LORD is among us, because ye have not committed this trespass against the Lord. - Now ye have delivered the children of Israel out of the hand of the LORD: because they were not going off, nobody had to die that day, and coming from Phinehas that meant everything, because if it had been rebellion he would have been the one to start it. Joshua 22:32-34 taught in Joshua 21-24 - Phinehas and the princes returned from Gilead to the land of Canaan and brought the children of Israel word again: all is good, the altar is a memorial so the generations after do not forget that our people are on that side Jordan too, and they can come in and keep the feasts and do their sacrifices with us. - The thing pleased the children of Israel; they blessed God, dismantled from war, and did not go up to destroy the land where the children of Reuben and Gad dwelt. - The children of Reuben and Gad called the altar Ed: for it shall be a witness between us that the LORD is God. Joshua 24:4-7 taught in Joshua 21-24 - The Most High sent Moses and Aaron, plagued Egypt, and brought Israel out; and when the Egyptians pursued with chariots and horsemen unto the Red sea, he put darkness between Israel and the Egyptians and brought the sea upon them and covered them. Joshua 24:31-33 taught in Joshua 21-24 - Eleazar the son of Aaron died, and they buried him in a hill that pertained to Phinehas his son, which was given him in mount Ephraim. Judges Judges 6:36-40 taught in Judges 5-8 - Gideon asks the fleece signs: dew on the fleece only with dry earth beside, and then the reverse, dew on all the ground with the fleece dry. The Lord commands the dew, the condensation that falls through the night, to land exactly where he pleases; God can do whatever he wants, infinite power. - Precept Numbers 17:8 : The same power made Aaron's rod bud, bloom blossoms, and yield almonds overnight. Judges 8:24-27 taught in Judges 5-8 - Gideon made an ephod thereof and put it in his city, even in Ophrah: and all Israel went thither a whoring after it, which thing became a snare unto Gideon, and to his house. Judges 17:5 taught in Judges 17-20 - Micah had a whole house of gods. He made an ephod and teraphim and consecrated one of his own sons to be his priest, a counterfeit priesthood serving counterfeit gods. Judges 17:7-10 taught in Judges 17-20 - A young Levite of Bethlehemjudah departed to sojourn wherever he could find a place and came to mount Ephraim to the house of Micah. - When Micah learned the man was a Levite, of the tribe known for the priesthood and the knowledge of the sacrifices, he offered him a deal: dwell with me, be unto me a father and a priest, ten shekels of silver by the year, a suit of apparel, and thy victuals. He hired himself a personal priest for his idols. Judges 17:11-13 taught in Judges 17-20 - The Levite was content to dwell with him and became as one of his sons. Nothing says the Levite was already in idolatry, but when money was offered he went right along with it; being corrupted for reward was always the Levites' weakness. - Then Micah said, now know I that the LORD will do me good, seeing I have a Levite to my priest. A house full of idols and a hired priest over them, yet he expected the Most High to bless him because a Levite was on the payroll. That is how sick in the mind Israel was without leadership. Judges 18:3-6 taught in Judges 17-20 - By the house of Micah they knew the voice of the young man the Levite, and they turned in and questioned him: who brought thee hither? what makest thou in this place? A Levite serving in a house of idols raised questions. - He told them plainly, Micah hired me and I am his priest. They asked him to ask counsel of God whether their way would be prosperous, and the priest answered, go in peace: before the LORD is your way wherein ye go. Judges 18:11-14 taught in Judges 17-20 - The first time Micah let the five spies lodge in his house, they saw his expensive looking gods and got covetous. Now passing back through they tell their brethren, do ye know that there is in these houses an ephod, and teraphim, and a graven image, and a molten image? now therefore consider what ye have to do. On the way to the lick they spotted another lick. Judges 18:15-20 taught in Judges 17-20 - They turned in to the house and saluted the Levite, a friendly greeting at the door; that is one of the deceitful man's many trains. While the six hundred armed men stood by the entering of the gate keeping the priest occupied, the five spies went up inside and took the graven image, the ephod, the teraphim, and the molten image. - When the priest saw them coming out with the gods and asked, what do ye? they told him hold thy peace, lay thine hand upon thy mouth: is it better for thee to be a priest unto the house of one man, or unto a tribe and a family in Israel? Do not snitch; roll with us and be the man over a whole tribe. - The priest's heart was glad, and he took the ephod, the teraphim, and the graven image and went in the midst of the people. His covetous spirit was plain: already sold out to serve idols for Micah's silver, he dropped the man who treated him as a son the moment a bigger position was offered. Disloyal through and through. Judges 18:21-26 taught in Judges 17-20 - When Micah and the men near his house gathered and overtook the children of Dan, Dan asked, what aileth thee, that thou comest with such a company? He answered, ye have taken away my gods which I made, and the priest, and ye are gone away: and what have I more? Judges 18:27-29 taught in Judges 17-20 - The Danites took the things which Micah had made and the priest which he had, came unto Laish, unto a people quiet and secure, smote them with the edge of the sword, and burnt the city with fire. Judges 18:30-31 taught in Judges 17-20 - The first thing the children of Dan did in the land the Most High allowed them to take was set up the graven image, a god made by the hands of a man they had just robbed. Jonathan the son of Gershom, the son of Manasseh, he and his sons were priests to the tribe of Dan until the day of the captivity of the land, and they kept Micah's graven image all the time the house of God was in Shiloh. Judges 19:1-2 taught in Judges 17-20 - Once more, there was no king in Israel, no leadership structure, still sheep without a shepherd. A certain Levite sojourning on the side of mount Ephraim took to him a concubine out of Bethlehemjudah; a concubine was a woman dealt with on the level of a servant. Judges 19:4-9 taught in Judges 17-20 - The damsel's father retained him: eat, drink, lodge, three days, then a fourth, then a fifth. Like an old man who never has anybody to talk to, he kept finding a reason not to let the Levite go, and a one night plan stretched into five days. Judges 19:14-21 taught in Judges 17-20 - An old man from his work out of the field at even, a man of mount Ephraim sojourning in Gibeah, lifted up his eyes and questioned the wayfaring man: whither goest thou? and whence comest thou? The Levite explained he was passing toward the house of the LORD with straw, provender, bread, and wine of his own, lacking nothing, yet no man would receive him to house. Judges 20:3-7 taught in Judges 17-20 - The children of Benjamin heard that Israel was gone up to Mizpeh. The Levite, the husband of the woman that was slain, testified: I came into Gibeah that belongeth to Benjamin, and the men of Gibeah rose against me and beset the house round about upon me by night, and thought to have slain me; and my concubine have they forced, that she is dead. Forced is the Bible's word for rape. Judges 20:26-28 taught in Judges 17-20 - The ark of the covenant of God was there in those days, and Phinehas the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron, stood before it. They asked, shall I yet again go out to battle against the children of Benjamin my brother, or shall I cease? And the LORD said, go up; for to morrow I will deliver them into thine hand: a direct promise of victory on the morrow. Ruth Ruth 1:3-5 taught in Ruth 1-3 - Elimelech, Naomi's husband, died, and she was left with her two sons. The sons took them wives of the women of Moab, Orpah and Ruth, and after they dwelt there about ten years Mahlon and Chilion died also, leaving Naomi without her husband and without her sons. - Were the sons of Israel supposed to take wives of the women of Moab while sojourning there? No; but remember what was just read at the end of Judges, that every man did that which was right in his own eyes. And this was not the first time Israel dealt with the women of Moab. - Precept 1 Esdras 8:69 : Even in the time of Ezra, Israel had not put away the strange people of the land, the Moabites among them; remember that it says the strange people of the land. Ruth 2:10 taught in Ruth 1-3 - Ruth fell on her face and asked, Why have I found grace in thine eyes, that thou shouldest take knowledge of me, seeing I am a stranger? She acknowledged what she was to Israel: a stranger. - Precept 1 Esdras 8:69 : The Moabites are counted among the strange people of the land; Ruth spoke of herself by that same word. 1 Samuel 1 Samuel 1:1-3 taught in 1 Samuel 1-3 - Elkanah went up out of his city yearly to worship and to sacrifice unto the Lord of hosts in Shiloh, where the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, the priests of the Lord, were. Shiloh is another name for Jerusalem. 1 Samuel 1:9-11 taught in 1 Samuel 1-3 - Hannah rose up after they had eaten in Shiloh, and in bitterness of soul she prayed unto the Lord and wept sore, while Eli the priest sat upon a seat by a post of the temple of the Lord. 1 Samuel 2:11-12 taught in 1 Samuel 1-3 - Elkanah went to Ramah to his house, and the child did minister unto the Lord before Eli the priest. Now the sons of Eli were sons of Belial; they knew not the Lord. They were the devil. - They were Levites, priests in the house of the Lord doing the work of the Lord, and yet it says they knew not the Lord. Why? Because they did not keep the commandments true in their spirit; they kept it on the surface where you can see it. They looked the part: they had on the fringes, they had the beard, they showed up on the sabbath day; but their spirit was not right with the Lord, and they were really the sons of the devil. Do not let that be you, Israel. 1 Samuel 2:13-14 taught in 1 Samuel 1-3 - The priests' custom with the people was that when any man offered sacrifice, the priest's servant came, while the flesh was in seething, with a fleshhook of three teeth in his hand, and struck it into the pan, or kettle, or caldron, or pot; all that the fleshhook brought up the priest took for himself. They would dip it in, and what came up was the priest's portion of meat for that day; all the Levites did that, based on the sacrifices Israel brought in. 1 Samuel 2:15-17 taught in 1 Samuel 1-3 - Also, before they burnt the fat, the priest's servant came and said to the man that sacrificed, Give flesh to roast for the priest; for he will not have sodden flesh of thee, but raw: I will cook it up my own way, give it to me now, before it is done. And if any man said, Let them not fail to burn the fat presently, and then take as much as thy soul desireth, he would answer, Nay; but thou shalt give it me now: and if not, I will take it by force. - These were devils serving in the house of the Lord, strong-arming the offerings. Wherefore the sin of the young men was very great before the Lord: for men abhorred the offering of the Lord. These priests were disrespecting the offering of the Lord. 1 Samuel 2:18-21 taught in 1 Samuel 1-3 - But Samuel ministered before the Lord, being a child, girded with a linen ephod; moreover his mother made him a little coat, and brought it to him from year to year, when she came up with her husband to offer the yearly sacrifice. 1 Samuel 2:22-26 taught in 1 Samuel 1-3 - He said unto them, Why do ye such things? for I hear of your evil dealings by all this people; ye make the Lord's people to transgress. The Levites were the leaders, so the people followed their actions: what the priests did, the people did also. They saw the sons of Eli sleeping with the harlots and said, it must be all right, look what they have, look how they live in the temple; let us follow their lead. - Eli might have said something to his children, but he did not remove them and put them out of the priesthood for their evil dealings; he said something, but he did not go further than words, he took no action with it. Watch what happened to his children. 1 Samuel 2:27-29 taught in 1 Samuel 1-3 - There came a man of God unto Eli, saying, Thus saith the Lord, Did I plainly appear unto the house of thy father, when they were in Egypt in Pharaoh's house? That is talking about Levi, going into Moses. Did I choose him out of all the tribes of Israel to be my priest, to offer upon mine altar, to burn incense, to wear an ephod before me? and did I give unto the house of thy father all the offerings made by fire of the children of Israel? They had need of nothing; they were well taken care of. 1 Samuel 2:34-35 taught in 1 Samuel 1-3 - And this shall be a sign unto thee, that shall come upon thy two sons, on Hophni and Phinehas: in one day they shall die both of them. And I will raise me up a faithful priest, that shall do according to that which is in mine heart and in my mind; and I will build him a sure house, and he shall walk before mine anointed for ever. 1 Samuel 2:36 taught in 1 Samuel 1-3 - It shall come to pass, that every one that is left in thine house shall come and crouch to him for a piece of silver and a morsel of bread. The Lord was going to make it hard on the descendants of Eli: he removed them from the priesthood, and it was written down that the descendants of Eli were not to be allowed into the house of the Lord any more. - Remember, Levi was given no inheritance of land; so how would they eat, how would they live, how would they survive? Receiving their inheritance and their goods was based on them doing what thus saith the Lord told them to do, teaching the laws. Cut off from the priesthood, Eli's house was left to beg. 1 Samuel 3:1 taught in 1 Samuel 1-3 - The child Samuel ministered unto the Lord before Eli. And the word of the Lord was precious in those days; there was no open vision. Precious means the Lord was not dealing with everybody: he was not dealing with the priests, and there were no prophets around saying, thus saith the Lord. The word was about to go only to Samuel. 1 Samuel 3:2-3 taught in 1 Samuel 1-3 - Christ spoke about that fire in the temple: on the sabbath days the priests in the temple profane the sabbath, and are blameless. Israel was not to kindle a fire on the sabbath when it comes to food, but the priests had to keep that fire burning, and they sacrificed on the sabbath days, a lamb in the morning and a lamb in the evening; they broke the sabbath yet are blameless, because they were doing thus saith the Lord. - Precept Exodus 27:20-21 : The children of Israel brought pure oil olive beaten for the light, to cause the lamp to burn always; Aaron and his sons ordered it from evening to morning before the Lord, a statute for ever. - Precept Matthew 12:5-7 : Have ye not read in the law, how that on the sabbath days the priests in the temple profane the sabbath, and are blameless? In this place is one greater than the temple; and if ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless. - Precept Numbers 28:9-10 : The burnt offering of every sabbath: the priests sacrificed a lamb in the morning and in the evening on the sabbath because the Lord commanded it. - Precept Exodus 19:3-6 : Before the Most High even gave the ten commandments he made this plain: if ye will obey my voice indeed, and keep my covenant, then ye shall be a peculiar treasure unto me above all people, a kingdom of priests, and an holy nation. Obedience is what he desired most from the beginning. 1 Samuel 4:12-18 taught in 1 Samuel 4-7 - Eli was the high priest who groomed Samuel up, and he was righteous as far as himself, but his sons were devils, and he honoured his sons above the Most High by not rebuking them like a true leader should have. 1 Samuel 5:1-5 taught in 1 Samuel 4-7 - They set him in his place again, as if maybe the wind blew a little harder, and the next morning Dagon was fallen on his face again before the ark, with the head of Dagon and both the palms of his hands cut off upon the threshold; only the stump of Dagon was left to him. No man did this: that is the power of the ark of God. Therefore the priests of Dagon tread not on the threshold of Dagon in Ashdod unto this day. 1 Samuel 6:1-6 taught in 1 Samuel 4-7 - The ark of the Lord was in the country of the Philistines seven months, and the Philistines called for the priests and the diviners, asking how to send it back to his place. Seven months of that plague and they had to get it out of the land. - The priests answered, send it not empty, but in any wise return him a trespass offering; then ye shall be healed. A trespass offering acknowledges you did wrong. The offering was five golden emerods and five golden mice, according to the number of the lords of the Philistines, images of the very things that marred the land, and ye shall give glory unto the God of Israel; peradventure he will lighten his hand from off you, and from off your gods, and from off your land. - Their own priests warned them from Israel's history: wherefore then do ye harden your hearts, as the Egyptians and Pharaoh hardened their hearts? They did not want to end up like Egypt, so they said, let us learn the lesson and get this ark back. 1 Samuel 6:13-18 taught in 1 Samuel 4-7 - The cart came into the field of Joshua, a Beth-shemite, and stood by a great stone; they clave the wood of the cart and offered the kine a burnt offering unto the Lord, and the Levites took down the ark and the coffer with the jewels of gold. 1 Samuel 12:6-7 taught in 1 Samuel 12-15 - It is the Lord that advanced Moses and Aaron and brought your fathers up out of the land of Egypt. Now stand still, that Samuel may reason with them before the Lord of all the righteous acts of the Lord which he did to them and to their fathers. 1 Samuel 12:8-11 taught in 1 Samuel 12-15 - When Jacob was come into Egypt and your fathers cried unto the Lord, the Lord sent Moses and Aaron and made Israel dwell in this place. When they forgat the Lord he sold them into the hand of Sisera, captain of the host of Hazor, and of the Philistines, and of the king of Moab; this is the history of the book of Judges, starting in chapter 4. 1 Samuel 13:8-10 taught in 1 Samuel 12-15 - Saul said, Bring hither a burnt offering to me, and he offered the burnt offering, and Saul is not the priest; that is Samuel's office. And it came to pass that as soon as he had made an end of offering the burnt offering, behold, Samuel came. He was barely late, and Saul could not hold his patience. 1 Samuel 14:1-3 taught in 1 Samuel 12-15 - Jonathan said unto the young man that bare his armor, Come, let us go over to the Philistines' garrison on the other side; but he told not his father. Saul tarried under a pomegranate tree in Migron with about six hundred men, with Ahiah the priest wearing an ephod, and the people knew not that Jonathan was gone. 1 Samuel 14:17-23 taught in 1 Samuel 12-15 - Saul numbered the people and found Jonathan and his armor bearer missing. While Saul talked with the priest, the noise in the host of the Philistines went on and increased, and when Israel came to the battle, behold, every man's sword was against his fellow, and there was a very great discomfiture; the enemies were destroying each other, and Israel did not have to put in the work. 1 Samuel 14:36-37 taught in 1 Samuel 12-15 - Saul proposed going down after the Philistines by night to spoil them until morning, and the people agreed; then said the priest, Let us draw near hither unto God. And Saul asked counsel of God, Shall I go down after the Philistines? wilt thou deliver them into the hand of Israel? But he answered him not that day. 1 Samuel 16:8-13 taught in 1 Samuel 16-19 - Jesse made seven of his sons pass before Samuel, the older, bigger, more developed ones, and Samuel said of each, Neither hath the Lord chosen this; the Lord had not chosen any of these. - Asked whether these were all his children, Jesse answered that there remained yet the youngest, and behold, he keepeth the sheep. Samuel would not sit down until the young one was fetched. He was ruddy, of a beautiful countenance, and goodly to look to, a young handsome fella, and the Most High said, Arise, anoint him, for this is he. - Samuel anointed David in the midst of his brethren, and the spirit of the Lord came upon David from that day forward, from that young age, being the youngest son. - Taking a keeper of sheep and making him the shepherd of the nation is a pattern with the Most High; he took leaders and prophets from following literal flocks and set them to feed the flock of Israel. - The same pattern continues through the prophets: Elisha was taken from the plow and Amos from the herd. - David was also young when the spirit came on him, and that is nothing new either; the Most High does not choose the ones everybody expects, for the spirit of Christ was in the prophets he selected. - Precept Exodus 3:1 : Moses kept the flock of Jethro his father in law, the priest of Midian, and led the flock to the mountain of God, where the Most High called him out of the midst of the bush. 1 Samuel 17:8-11 taught in 1 Samuel 16-19 - Goliath cried to the armies of Israel: choose you a man and let him come down to me. If he kills me, we will be your servants; if I prevail and kill him, ye shall be our servants. And he said, I defy the armies of Israel this day; give me a man that we may fight together. - When Saul and all Israel heard the words of the Philistine, they were dismayed and greatly afraid. They were in a carnal spirit, measuring his height, his armor, and his reach; the spirit had departed, and fear is not the spirit of the Most High. - The Most High put laws in the book about going to battle, and this fear showed that Saul and the people lacked faith; the same God that destroyed Pharaoh and the Egyptians who pursued Israel was with them, and a trial of faith was set before them in the form of one big intimidating man with a big mouth. - Precept Deuteronomy 20:1-4 : When thou goest out to battle and seest a people more than thou, be not afraid of them, for the Lord thy God is with thee; the priest was to tell the people, let not your hearts faint, fear not, for the Lord your God goeth with you to fight for you against your enemies and to save you. 1 Samuel 21:6 taught in 1 Samuel 20-23 - The priest gave David hallowed bread, for there was no bread there but the shewbread that was taken from before the Lord. Remember David had been out in the field three days, fearful of king Saul, when he came to Nob in need. - Precept Mark 2:25-26 : Christ answered, Have ye never read what David did, when he had need, and was an hungred? This is that history, David eating the shewbread which is not lawful to eat but for the priests. 1 Samuel 22:17-19 taught in 1 Samuel 20-23 - Saul commanded his footmen to turn and slay the priests of the Lord, but the servants of the king would not put forth their hand to fall upon the priests of the Lord. Saul was able to get the Edomite to do what his own men would not do: Doeg turned and fell upon the priests, and slew on that day fourscore and five persons that did wear a linen ephod, and smote Nob, the city of the priests, with the edge of the sword. - Go back to Genesis and see the spirit that has been placed on this man from the beginning: Esau comforted himself with the purpose of killing his brother Jacob. Just as in the time of Saul, even to this very day, when Israel suffers violence at the hands of the other nations, especially Esau, he gets comfort out of killing us; when Saul appointed Doeg to that task, you can best believe he was quite happy over it and most likely found much pleasure in killing the priests. 1 Samuel 30:7-8 taught in 1 Samuel 28-31 - David said to Abiathar the priest, Ahimelech's son, Bring hither the ephod, and David inquired at the Lord: shall I pursue after this troop? shall I overtake them? The answer came, Pursue: for thou shalt surely overtake them, and without fail recover all.

title: The Sabbath
text: The Sabbath Every place the study notes teach the sabbath, from the seventh day of creation through the wilderness laws. Genesis Genesis 2:1-3 taught in Genesis 1-4 - This is the first Sabbath that you read about in the scriptures. The Most High blessed the seventh day and sanctified it. Genesis 3:16 taught in Genesis 1-4 - This is one of the first commandments given, alongside be fruitful and multiply, the Sabbath, and the commandment not to eat of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. Exodus Exodus 5:6-9 taught in Exodus 2-5 - Let there more work be laid upon the men, that they may labour therein; and let them not regard vain words. The same tactic runs in this captivity: burdens are increased and extra wages dangled for working the Sabbath and the feast days, to wear the people down so they will not regard the words of the Most High. Exodus 5:15-19 taught in Exodus 2-5 - Pharaoh answered, Ye are idle, ye are idle: therefore ye say, Let us go and do sacrifice to the LORD. The charge of idleness is the standing answer to any who would go serve God, whether it is the three days' journey or keeping the Sabbath and the new moons now. Exodus 10:27-29 taught in Exodus 10-13 - The same delusion falls on Israel when the people go reprobate in their sins: believing the Sabbath begins when the sun comes up, that anything can be eaten on Passover, or that the leaven to be put away is only the heart. Sin blinds. Exodus 12:3-5 taught in Exodus 10-13 - In the tenth day of the month every man was to take a lamb according to the house of his fathers; if the household was too little for the lamb, he and his neighbour next unto his house were to take it according to the number of the souls. - The lamb was to be without blemish, a male of the first year, taken from the sheep or from the goats. This is a foreshadowing: the feast days and sacrifices are a shadow of things to come, but the body is of Christ. - The lamb without blemish and without spot points to Christ, who was sinless, verily foreordained before the foundation of the world but manifest in these last times for the nation of Israel. - Precept Colossians 2:16-17 : The meat, drink, holydays, and sabbaths are a shadow of things to come, but the body is of Christ; the Passover lamb was a precursor of him. Exodus 12:15-17 taught in Exodus 10-13 - The first day and the seventh day are holy convocations; no manner of work is done in them save that which every man must eat, meaning the food may be cooked. Exodus 13:5-10 taught in Exodus 10-13 - When the Lord brings Israel into the land of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, a land flowing with milk and honey, this service is kept in this month: seven days of unleavened bread, and in the seventh day a feast to the Lord, with no leaven seen in all thy quarters. Exodus 16:22-30 taught in Exodus 14-17 - On the sixth day they gathered twice as much, and Moses said, Tomorrow is the rest of the holy sabbath unto the Lord: bake that which ye will bake today.
